title: Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence in Natural Product-Based Drug Discovery
abstract: Background: Natural products remain an important source of therapeutic agents, but their discovery is constrained by chemical complexity, time-consuming isolation, difficult structure elucidation, and high attrition rates. abstract: Soil salinity, driven by climate change and human activities, threatens global food security across over 412 million hectares, requiring precise monitoring. title: Coupling Artificial Neural Networks and high-resolution hydrodynamic models for an Early-Warning System for coastal flooding
abstract: Coastal regions are increasingly vulnerable to flooding due to extreme events and sea-level rise driven by climate change. Effective Early Warning Systems (EWSs) are essential for enhancing resilience and enabling proactive disaster management. Traditional EWSs often rely on physically-based numerical models to simulate flood scenarios. abstract: Concrete breakwaters, piers, and offshore foundations deteriorate under the combined action of saltwater, temperature cycling, and biological growth. Many of these structures lie in waters too deep, too contaminated, or too dangerous for human divers, and the same inspection problem occurs inland in dams and hydraulic structures. title: AQUAVERSE-AC: a machine learning-based atmospheric correction framework for inland and coastal waters
abstract: Accurately deriving remote sensing reflectance ( R r s ) from satellite imagery in optically complex inland and coastal waters is critical for water quality monitoring and management. This study presents AQUAVERSE-AC, the atmospheric correction component of the AQUAVERSE (Aquatic inversion scheme for remote sensing of fresh and coastal waters) platform, an innovative machine learning-based atmospheric correction (AC) framework, that leverages Mixture Density Networks (MDNs) to retrieve high-quality R r s from multispectral data acquired by Landsat-8/9 (OLI) and Sentinel-2A/B (MSI) satellites.

Over time, significant advancements in technology, particularly in image processing and machine learning, have revolutionized fingerprint analysis. abstract: The article analyzes the impact of artificial intelligence on political elections. abstract: Abstract Antibiotics are continuously released into aquatic environments from municipal, hospital, pharmaceutical, livestock, and aquaculture sources. abstract: ABSTRACT Chlorine (Cl) is an important tracer of mantle geodynamics, but seawater alteration and secondary contamination obscure primary mantle Cl signatures. abstract: Antarctic sea ice extent increased gradually over recent decades but has declined rapidly since 2016, including in the Ross Sea. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding the chemical and formulation space explored for nucleic acid lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), but accurate assay prediction does not by itself establish useful delivery in vivo . This critical narrative review examines how evidence links molecular design, complete formulation identity, and biological context to cell-resolved function, with a focus on mRNA. We distinguish tissue accumulation from functional cargo delivery, membrane damage from productive release, and target-cell coverage from panel-restricted on-target precision. title: Neural network-based finite-sample transmission coefficient estimation and uncertainty quantification in satellite-to-ground CV-QKD
abstract: Abstract Satellite-to-ground continuous variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is constrained by rapidly varying free-space channels and short transmission windows, which limit the amount of data available for parameter estimation within each channel interval. Under finite-sample conditions, parameter point estimates are subject to statistical uncertainty and may even yield an overly favorable description of the true channel state, while errors in the estimated transmission coefficient directly affect the covariance matrix used in the security analysis. title: Artificial Intelligence and Agricultural Supply Chain Resilience: Empirical Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) technology on agricultural supply chain resilience (ASCR) using provincial panel data from China between 2012 and 2023. We construct a comprehensive ASCR index based on resistance, recovery, and adaptability dimensions and employ fixed‐effects, mediation, moderation, and threshold models for empirical analysis. The results indicate that AI significantly enhances ASCR, with every 1% increase in AI application level improving resilience by 0.158%. title: A machine learning framework based on multibeam bathymetry for predicting submarine dune migration rates
abstract: Predicting submarine dune migration rates is important for understanding seabed evolution and supporting marine engineering safety. This study develops a machine learning framework using two-period multibeam bathymetric data. A dataset of 111 samples was constructed using seven input features: dune wavelength, height, water depth, gentle and steep slope lengths, and gentle and steep slope angles. Eight models were evaluated: EO-Stacking, Stacking, XGBoost, LightGBM, MLP, BPNN, SVR, and RF. title: Artificial Intelligence in Source Seismology: Potential Issues and Future Directions
abstract: Artificial Intelligence and machine learning have transformed the field of seismology over the past decade. Fueled by advances in high-performance computing, the availability of large seismic and labeled datasets, and breakthroughs in deep neural network architectures, the seismological community has developed many machine learning models for seismic phase detection and association, enabling the construction of high-resolution earthquake catalogs around the globe. abstract: Purpose This conceptual article revisits Heinz von Foerster's Doomsday calculation as a provocation about the authority of formal description and uses it to examine artificial intelligence (AI) as a new condition for second-order cybernetics. Design/methodology/approach The article develops a theoretical argument through von Foerster's observing systems, non-trivial machines, constructed realities and ethical imperatives. abstract: Smart Physiotherapy: Artificial Intelligence, Emerging Technologies, and Digital Transformation in Human Rehabilitation explores the intersection of rehabilitation sciences and technological innovation. The book examines the evolution of physical therapy toward digital health ecosystems, emphasizing the integration of artificial intelligence, computer vision, and machine learning for biomechanical assessment and clinical decision-making. abstract: As Saudi Arabia makes a significant transition towards renewable energy, solar energy have emerged as a feasible alternative owing to the country's favorable geographical conditions. However, this transition poses critical challenges that necessitate careful consideration. Due to the current energy mix's predominance of oil, the integration and management of solar power plants into the existing grid necessitate accurate forecasting. abstract: Coseismic landslide susceptibility mapping plays a critical role in disaster risk mitigation, infrastructure protection, and territorial spatial planning, particularly in tectonically active mountain belts such as the Tianshan Mountains. Conventional machine learning models often suffer from overfitting and inadequate generalization capability due to their homogeneous structures and inflexible modeling strategies. title: Prediction of Local Scour Depth Around Cylindrical Bridge Piers in Cohesive Soils Using Advanced Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Abstract Reliable prediction of local scour around cylindrical bridge piers in cohesive beds remains challenging because hydraulic forcing and soil resistance interact nonlinearly. title: Intelligent High-Resolution Marine Seismic Survey Using Machine Learning and Adaptive Acquisition Optimization
abstract: Conventional high-resolution marine seismic surveys often face challenges in detecting small features in the shallow subsurface because acquisition parameters involve trade-offs among spatial resolution, penetration, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and operational efficiency. This study presents an intelligent marine seismic acquisition framework that integrates selectable acquisition hardware with modified ML Real domain adaptation, deep learning reconstruction, quantitative quality-control (QC) evaluation, and a human-supervised adaptive agent. title: Extreme weather events and energy system resilience: Policy lessons from Brazil
abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events (EWEs) pose growing challenges to electricity systems worldwide, raising critical policy questions about how power systems operate and adapt under climate stress. This study assesses the impacts of EWEs on electricity generation in Brazil, a country with one of the world’s largest interconnected power system and a generation mix largely based on renewable sources. abstract: Rapid sea-ice loss and expanding shipping activity are increasing ship-generated underwater radiated noise (URN) across Arctic waters, with implications for acoustically dependent marine species and Indigenous subsistence and cultural practices. This Policy and Practice Review examines why existing mitigation measures produce uneven outcomes in the Arctic and how governance arrangements can better align spatial and ecological fit, legal and institutional coordination, and implementation and verification incentives. abstract: Additive manufacturing enables the design of lattice metamaterials by combining different unit-cell architectures, but exhaustive evaluation of large design spaces is computationally expensive. This study develops a machine-learning surrogate framework for lattices comprising six unit-cell types arranged at four positions. Stratified index sampling (SIS) selected configurations for finite-element (FE) analysis, and the FE model was validated through quasi-static compression experiments. title: From diagnosis to prognosis: machine learning-based survival prediction in breast cancer patients
abstract: Prognostication is important in personalising oncological care for breast cancer patients. Although conventional approaches, such as Cox regression, may be used to predict breast cancer outcomes, they may have limitations in capturing the complex interactions among multiple variables. As such, machine learning (ML) approaches, such as extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), have the potential to provide satisfactory predictions for survival outcomes. abstract: Abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains one of the most diagnostically complex malignancies because accurate diagnosis requires the integration of heterogeneous evidence from imaging, endoscopy, histopathology, molecular testing, and clinical evaluation rather than interpretation of any single modality in isolation. Artificial intelligence (AI) has shown promising performance across individual diagnostic tasks, including lesion detection, lymph node assessment, digital pathology, and biomarker prediction. title: Smart biodiesel systems in integrating nano-additives and artificial intelligence for cleaner internal combustion engines
abstract: The transition toward sustainable transport and energy systems requires integrated innovations that address both technical performance and environmental sustainability. This review examines the synergistic roles of biodiesel, nano additives, and artificial intelligence as enablers of clean energy adoption. Biodiesel derived from first- to fourth-generation feedstocks offers a renewable alternative to fossil diesel, with life cycle assessments reporting reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, improved air quality, and comparable engine efficiency. abstract: For applications in geophysical research, coastal hazard forecasting, and marine navigation, accurate bathymetry estimation is essential. Even though they work well, conventional methods like satellite remote sensing and shipborne sonar are still costly and restricted in areas with few measurements. In this work, we assess an inverse problem of bathymetry reconstruction from two-dimensional shallow water equations using a Self-Adaptive Physics-Informed Neural Network (SA-PINN) framework. title: Kriging and Neural Network models for pressure losses across perforated plates
abstract: In this paper, two novel data-driven models based on Kriging and neural networks (NN) are proposed to predict pressure losses across perforated plates with circular perforations in turbulent flows. The models are developed using two sets of experimental data available in the literature. The predictive performance of the proposed models is assessed and compared against widely used empirical formulae. title: Advancing spatial hurricane storm surge risk assessment using machine learning and simulations under changing climate scenarios
abstract: Hurricane risk assessments under climate change are essential for resilient infrastructure planning, yet they remain constrained by limited and inconsistent historical damage records. This study develops a spatial framework for assessing storm surge-induced hurricane building damage under future climate scenarios. Ten thousand years of synthetic hurricane tracks and storm-surge simulations were generated and overlaid with building-level insurance data. abstract: Abstract Deep learning based benthic substrate mapping is essential for large scale marine monitoring and automated seafloor analysis. However, model performance degrades in real underwater environments due to noise, mixed substrates, overlapping classes, variations in depth, illumination, and sensing conditions. Conventional deep learning models typically assume clean, well separated classes. title: Artificial Intelligence as a Cultural Adaptation Scaffold: Experiences of Asian International Students at Chinese Universities
abstract: Growing international student mobility, particularly intra-Asian flows to China, has intensified the need to support Asian international students’ cultural adaptation amid linguistic, academic, sociocultural, and psychological challenges. This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is used and perceived as a resource for such adaptation in Chinese higher education. Drawing on Berry’s acculturation framework, Ward and Kennedy’s dual-process model, and Deardorff’s and Byram’s intercultural competence theories, the study employed a qualitative interpretivist design. title: Smart Microneedle Platforms: Integrating Biosensing, Artificial Intelligence, and Targeted Drug Delivery for Better Therapeutic Outcome
abstract: Smart microneedle platforms are innovative biomedical systems that integrate biosensing, artificial intelligence (AI), and targeted drug delivery into a single minimally invasive technology. These micro-scale needle arrays can painlessly penetrate the outer skin layer to access interstitial fluid, enabling continuous and real-time monitoring of key biochemical markers such as glucose, metabolites, and disease-related biomarkers. title: 3D-ReSE-VN: Advanced Deep Learning for Protein Ligand Affinity Prediction in Cancer-Associated Targets
abstract: Accurate protein-ligand binding affinity prediction is important for structure-based anticancer drug discovery. This study presents 3D-ReSE-VN, a three-dimensional residual attention network that combines voxelized docking-derived complexes with residual learning, squeeze-and-excitation channel attention, and spatial attention. The model was evaluated on 4,620 protein-ligand complexes using random five-fold cross-validation and a predefined train/validation/test split. This study analysed 1,706 Web of Science Core Collection articles published from 2017 to 2025 using CiteSpace and VOSviewer, and applied Task–Data–Model (T–D–M) coding to a publication-year-stratified random sample of 500 articles. abstract: Abstract Arctic marginal ice zone (MIZ) is a key summertime source of elevated atmospheric gaseous elemental mercury (GEM), but controls on its spatial variability remain unclear. title: Disentangling Environmental Drivers of Marine Primary Production Using Explainable Machine Learning
abstract: Marine primary production is regulated by interacting environmental processes, making it challenging to distinguish biomass-associated variability from changes in production independent of phytoplankton biomass. We combined Random Forest models with SHAP-based explainable artificial intelligence in comparison with linear regression model to investigate the influence of environmental drivers on chlorophyll-a (Chl-a, used as a proxy of phytoplankton biomass) and primary production (PP) in a coastal marine ecosystem. abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into the field of cultural heritage presents new opportunities for research, conservation and the dissemination of knowledge. This contribution reflects on the potential of these technologies to facilitate access to specialised tools, process large volumes of information and develop new working methodologies. title: Advances in 3D-printed acoustic panels: experimental investigations, numerical modelling, and machine learning applications
abstract: Additive manufacturing provides a flexible route for fabricating acoustic panels with controlled porous, lattice, micro-perforated, resonant, and metamaterial architectures that are difficult to realize using conventional manufacturing. This review combines a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed literature spanning 1980–2026 with a critical synthesis of relevant experimental, analytical, numerical, and machine-learning studies addressing the design, fabrication, modelling, and acoustic performance of 3D-printed structures. title: Machine learning-based PM2.5 estimation using NASA’s MERRA-2 and comparison of ML- and SHAP-based meteorological normalization in Thailand
abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) poses severe health risks in Thailand; however, sparse ground monitoring has left long-term trends poorly quantified. This study utilizes NASA’s MERRA-2 reanalysis to estimate historical PM 2.5 levels across Thailand through two approaches: an empirical formulation based on PM 2.5 chemical components (MERRA2_EF) and a machine-learning model (MERRA2_ML) utilizing the Light Gradient Boosting Machine algorithm. title: Artificial intelligence promotes urban green innovation in China with regional spillovers and asymmetric climate-risk thresholds
abstract: We systematically examine the impact of artificial intelligence on urban green innovation in the context of climate risk. The results demonstrate that artificial intelligence substantially promotes green innovation, an effect primarily transmitted through expanded openness to trade and enhanced scientific-research investment, with the digital economy playing a positive moderating role. Spatial analysis reveals that artificial intelligence advances in one city generate significant positive spillovers that enhance the green innovation performance of neighboring cities. title: Artificial intelligence for sustainable and resilient infrastructure systems: a review of innovations across energy, water, transportation, and urban development
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to infrastructure systems to improve efficiency, resilience, sustainability, and decision-making in rapidly changing, uncertain environments. This study presents a systematic literature review and analytical synthesis of AI applications in sustainable and resilient infrastructure systems, focusing on energy, water, transportation, and urban development. title: Metabolism-Based Bacterial Detection in Water Using First-Principles Modeling and Predictive Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Bacterial contamination in water remains a global health concern. This study introduces a simplified and scalable approach for detecting Escherichia coli by coupling bacterial metabolism with predictive modeling. We developed a first-principle model to examine how E. coli consumes glucose as growth and metabolic rates vary over time. Detection time was primarily governed by bacterial growth rates, which exerted a substantially greater influence than variations in glucose consumption. title: A multi-source artificial intelligence framework for understanding climate effects on quality of agricultural products and supporting sustainable food systems
abstract: Quality of agricultural products (QAP) underpins global food systems, economic value, and public health. Climate change is altering QAP with significant implications for global food security. Understanding how climate shapes QAP is central to meeting rising demand for nutritious, flavourful, sustainable diets, and supporting food security. Artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated progress in these areas through data fusion, non-linear modelling, and improved interpretability. title: Computer vision-based detection of wind turbine surface defects: Methods, performance evaluation, and offshore applicability
abstract: Offshore wind turbine blades and towers are persistently exposed to strong winds, rain erosion, salt spray, high humidity, and intense ultraviolet radiation. These conditions promote leading-edge erosion, cracking, coating failure, and corrosion, thereby compromising operational safety, service reliability, and maintenance economics. Conventional manual inspection and some nondestructive testing methods remain constrained by operational risk, limited efficiency and coverage, and insufficient automation. title: Integrating spatial and temporal parameters for Landslide Hazard Prediction: A Machine Learning Framework with SHAP Interpretation in Campania, Italy
abstract: Rapid flow-like landslides triggered by intense or prolonged rainfall represent a severe and recurrent geohazard in Campania, Southern Italy, where steep slopes mantled by pyroclastic deposits exhibit high probability to sudden mobilization. Despite extensive research motivated by catastrophic historical events, the reliable spatio-temporal prediction of landslide hazards at the territorial scale remains a significant scientific challenge, particularly under dynamic climatic conditions. title: Linking the evolution of floe sizes to the sea-ice deformation history using SAR imagery
abstract: Arctic sea ice is a mosaic of ice floes whose distribution, sizes, and thicknesses greatly impact the interaction of sea ice with the atmosphere and the ocean. However, we are still lacking knowledge of the physics to describe the complex interplay of ice floes that are a key characteristic of sea ice. Here, we outline a framework to characterize sea-ice deformation at the floe-scale from observational data by studying the mechanical interactions of multiple identifiable floes. abstract: Based on the double-diagonal enhanced structure of deep-sea glass sponges, this study proposes a bio-inspired lattice metamaterial, aiming to enhance the impact resistance protection performance of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) through lightweight design. A three-dimensional hollow cylindrical lattice configuration was developed, and a systematic study was conducted by combining experimental tests, finite element analysis, and multi-condition drop simulation. abstract: Monitoring excess pore water pressure (EPWP) during and after soil improvement is essential under certain ground conditions. In some cases, ground monitoring may be required throughout the service life of a structure, particularly in areas where the subsoil is susceptible to environmental changes. However, installing sensors at every location across a construction site and its surrounding area is often impractical due to various site-specific constraints. title: Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Ensembles for Daily Maximum Temperature Prediction in Bangladesh: An Applied Meteorological Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Daily maximum temperature prediction plays an important role in climate‐risk management, agriculture, public health and energy planning and disaster preparedness in climate vulnerable country like Bangladesh. This study assesses the individual and ensemble predictive power of machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL) and hybrid ensemble‐based frameworks for daily maximum temperature prediction using 2013–2022 daily records from meteorological stations. abstract: Maritime search-and-rescue (SAR) operations typically involve scanning vast sea areas for sparse targets with often unknown appearances, making the process highly labour- and capital-intensive. Automating this task using reconnaissance drones and computer vision offers a significant operational advantage. This study investigates the detection of man-made objects in marine backgrounds without prior knowledge of their specific appearance, relying instead on characteristic visual patterns and shape primitives. abstract: Because of their strongly heterogeneous permeability, karst aquifers exhibit nonlinear relations between their outputs (discharge or groundwater level) and inputs (rain, temperature, etc.). Three main types of models are commonly used to simulate karst aquifers: physical models, pipe-flow models and conceptual models. title: Vibration energy absorption characteristics of porous and functionally graded biomechanical implants
abstract: The long-term success of hip and dental implants is often compromised by stress shielding and poor energy dissipation, leading to aseptic loosening. Viscoelastic Functionally Graded Bio-inspired Materials (VFGBM) with tailored porosity provide a potential solution by aligning the implant’s stiffness with local bone quality. title: Sliding Window–Neural Network and Round-Robin Framework: A Cloud-Based Data-Driven Energy Load Scheduling for Household Renewable Energy Systems
abstract: This study proposed a data-driven framework for real-time battery load scheduling that uses a sliding window and an artificial neural network (ANN) integrated with a round-robin switching mechanism. The system utilizes voltage-only measurements from multiple lead-acid batteries and processes real-time data using a 36-lag sliding window to capture nonlinear temporal discharge behavior. title: Two decades of kilometer-scale daily PM 2.5 from satellite observations and machine learning reveal geographically diverging exposure in Ghana
abstract: Exposure to fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) is a major contributor to the global burden of disease, yet air quality data remain sparse in many low- and middle-income countries, limiting nationwide monitoring and effective policy development. We address this gap by developing a high-resolution (1 km×1 km) gridded dataset of daily surface PM 2.5 concentrations across Ghana from 2005 to 2025 by training multiple machine learning (ML) models built on ground-based monitoring, satellite observations, and reanalysis products of atmospheric composition and meteorology. abstract: Contemporary foreign trade requires end-to-end visibility and maximum efficiency at modal transfer nodes. This article analyzes the development and application of electronic systems based on the Internet of Things (IoT), low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, subaquatic acoustic telemetry, and Artificial Intelligence algorithms applied to Terminal Operating Systems (TOS). abstract: The knowledge of land-surface variables (LSVs) is essential for an accurate description of the carbon cycle and, hence, for deriving the fraction of anthropogenic CO 2 emissions contributing to global warming. For a better representation of LSVs like the leaf-area index (LAI), we assimilate the observations of the satellite microwave sensors SMAP and AMSR2 with our land-data assimilation system (LDAS) on global cropland. abstract: Abstract Fundamental limits to predictability are central to our understanding of many physical and computational systems. In deep learning, training outcomes are often difficult to predict and reproduce even when extrinsic sources of randomness are controlled, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. abstract: Abstract. The differentiable programming paradigm is a cornerstone of modern scientific computing. It refers to numerical methods for computing the gradient of a numerical model’s output. Many scientific models are based on differential equations, in which differentiable programming plays a crucial role in calculating model sensitivities, inverting model parameters, and training hybrid models that combine differential equations with data-driven approaches. title: Neighborhood-aware retrieval of a spatial floe fragmentation index for Arctic sea ice using Sentinel-1 SAR and AMSR2
abstract: Arctic sea ice fragmentation involves changes in floe area composition, spatial separation, and geometric complexity, which affect lateral melt rates and ice–ocean heat fluxes. Existing metrics primarily characterize floe size distributions or area fractions, limiting their capacity to resolve variations in the spatial arrangement of floes. We propose a spatial floe fragmentation index (SFFI) that jointly quantifies floe area composition, spatial separation, and geometric complexity. title: MLAWind: a monthly sea surface wind dataset derived from an interpretable machine learning approach integrating in-situ observations and satellite data
abstract: A gridded sea surface wind dataset with long temporal coverage is crucial for understanding atmospheric circulation changes and air–sea interactions at different time scales. This study employs an interpretable machine learning model based on random forest algorithm to generate a 1° × 1° monthly sea surface wind dataset (MLAWind) from 1950 to 2023, covering the near-global ocean within 60° S–60° N. title: From the sky to the deep sea: ecosystem structure and ecological integrity across the National Marine Sanctuaries of Bikar and Bokak, Marshall Islands
abstract: Remote oceanic atolls provide increasingly rare opportunities to examine relatively intact tropical marine ecosystems in the Anthropocene. However, most ecological studies remain focused on individual habitats, limiting understanding of cross-habitat linkages across terrestrial, pelagic, mesophotic, and deep-sea systems. title: eDNA metabarcoding and random forest identify super-connector fish species across mangrove–seagrass–coral reef continuums in the South China Sea
abstract: Background Tropical coastal seascapes rely on ecological connectivity between mangrove, seagrass, and coral reef habitats to sustain fish biodiversity and fisheries productivity. However, identifying key fish species that facilitate cross-habitat energy flows remains challenging due to limitations of traditional survey methods in turbid, structurally complex environments. title: Compact FFT-based machine-learning model for efficient short-range forecasting of unidirectional waves
abstract: This paper presents a data-driven method using neural networks to forecast unidirectional irregular waves. The approach predicts downstream wave elevation based on a single upstream probe measurement. Operating in the frequency domain, the model applies a Sliding Fast Fourier Transform (SFFT) to decompose the signal into the temporal evolution of its modal components. A Softmax kernel serves as a temporal attention gate to adaptively weight past measurements of the decomposed modes (amplitude and phase). title: Ecosystem Based Environmental Control for Sustainable Coastal Zone Climate Mitigation
abstract: The development of sustainable coastal tourism is essential for promoting regional growth while preserving marine ecosystems. Emissions of Greenhouse Gases (GHG) are a primary cause of global warming, which disturbs the balance of marine ecosystems and threatens biodiversity. This research proposes a model to reduce GHG levels through Mangrove Planting and Nutrient Waste Management in coastal zones, which serve as the main control strategies for addressing the environmental challenges. title: A review on denoising methods for underwater explosion shockwave pressure signals
abstract: Abstract Underwater explosion shockwave pressure signals are critical for assessing damage effects of weapons. However, noise contamination renders these signals non-stationary, broadband, and transient characteristics, making high-fidelity denoising a bottleneck for accurate parameter extraction. This paper reviews recent denoising advances, classifying mainstream approaches into three categories: traditional filtering and transform-based methods, adaptive decomposition, and deep learning. title: Generative AI in Southeast Asian TVET: A Systematic Review of Learning Outcomes, Ethics and Research Directions
abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT entered technical and vocational education and training faster than evidence on their effects. Objective: This review synthesized empirical evidence on the applications, learning outcomes and ethical challenges of generative artificial intelligence in Southeast Asian vocational education. Method: Following PRISMA 2020, ten search strings were run in OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar for 2022–2026, which yielded 254 unique records, of which 25 primary studies met the eligibility criteria. title: AquaGuard: AI-Assisted Underwater Marine Debris Detection and Reporting — A Literature Review and System Design
abstract: Underwater marine debris is hard to monitor because observations are gathered with different tools, judged by different people and stored in formats that cannot be compared. Deep-learning detectors have been applied to sonar, remotely operated vehicle (ROV) and towed-camera imagery, yet the work reviewed here concentrates on detection models and annotated datasets rather than on the workflow that surrounds a detection. title: Daily global sea surface ageostrophic current dataset from 1993–2023 via physics-informed deep learning
abstract: Surface ocean circulation shapes climate, air–sea exchange, and the transport of heat, carbon, and other tracers, yet most long-term global datasets rely primarily on geostrophic balance and therefore miss important ageostrophic motions. Here, we reconstruct global daily sea surface circulation at 0.25° resolution from 1993 to 2023 using a physics-informed framework that integrates satellite altimetry with momentum constraints from geostrophic balance, wind stress, and nonlinear advection (Cui, 2026; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19966716). title: From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
abstract: Abstract Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behavior of CaCO3 in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. title: Internationalizing Pre-Service Student Teachers through the SEA-Teacher Program: Narratives of Development and Challenges
abstract: Background: One way to develop the quality of pre-service student teachers is by joining a student exchange overseas. So, the Indonesian Ministry of Education includes student mobility as a core component of tertiary education accreditation. Objectives: This study aims (1) to elaborate the SEA-Teacher participants' experiences and narrate their educational and personal development through the program and (2) to find out the challenges encountered during the program. title: dendRoAnalyst 2.0: an expanded R package for preprocessing, integrating, modeling, and analyzing dendrometer data with climate time series
abstract: Electronic dendrometers generate long, high-frequency records of stem diameter variations and growth that are increasingly analyzed together with meteorological data, event windows, and seasonal growth curves. Since our first description of dendRoAnalyst in 2020, the package has expanded from a compact set of preprocessing and phase-analysis tools into a substantially broader workflow for dendrometer research. title: Advances in technologies across the marine plastic value chain in Europe: A critical review
abstract: Marine Plastic Pollution (MPP) is widely recognised as a significant global challenge, driven by unsustainable plastic production, ineffective waste management, and the long-term persistence of plastics in marine environments. MPP has become increasingly widespread across oceans, along coastlines and on the seafloor, resulting in an urgent need for the development of technologies capable of advancing a Circular Economy (CE) for marine-derived products. title: Integrating Multi‐Group Microbial eDNA Data With Machine Learning for Large‐Scale Coastal Ecological Quality Assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT Among the many statistical methods for elucidating the complex relationships between microbial communities and specific environmental conditions, machine learning‐based methods are considered the most promising. The application of machine learning in the field of ecological quality assessment has been well documented; however, there is a paucity of research in the marine domain at a multi‐region scale. title: La inteligencia artificial y la protección constitucional de la propiedad intelectual en el Ecuador
abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed intellectual creation processes, creating new challenges for legal systems in the field of intellectual property. In Ecuador, the Constitution of the Republic and the Organic Code of the Social Economy of Knowledge, Creativity and Innovation (COESCCI) recognize and protect copyright and other intellectual property rights; however, they do not specifically regulate works generated through artificial intelligence systems. title: Graded-twist TPMS metamaterial with twist-locking mechanism and non-monotonic stiffness
abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces (TPMS) are increasingly exploited in additively manufactured metamaterials due to their smooth, continuous topologies that enable unusual mechanical behaviours. This paper proposes a graded-twist TPMS structure that undergoes continuous rotation along the height direction, leveraging its continuous topology to introduce a spatial gradient while preserving structural integrity. title: Scan-to-BIM Information Foundations and a Digital Twin Architecture for the Urban Tiber River Corridor in Rome
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly being proposed for urban river management, but their usefulness depends on the information available for specific applications. This study applies the DT methodology developed within the Agenzia del Demanio guidelines prepared by CITERA to approximately 8 km of the urban Tiber River in Rome, under an AUBAC-CITERA research agreement. The objectives concern maintenance of riverbed and bank hydraulic works, hydraulic condition monitoring and hydro-pluviometric monitoring. title: Chloride Resilient Recycled Aggregate Concrete: Optimising Marine Durability through Age Enhanced SCM Integration
abstract: The demand for sustainable construction materials is rising, and Recycled Aggregate Concrete (RAC) is one of the most discussed alternatives to conventional concrete. RAC, however, performs poorly in marine environments because chloride ions from seawater enter through the recycled aggregate and reach the reinforcement faster than in concrete made with natural aggregate, causing corrosion and shortening service life. title: EARTHQUAKE FORECASTING MODEL IN AZERBAIJAN BASED ON A NEURAL NETWORK
abstract: The paper presents a mathematical model for binary classification—"earthquake" vs. "no earthquake"—designed to estimate the probability of an earthquake occurring in Azerbaijan. The model is based on a fully connected neural network (multilayer perceptron, MLP). A sigmoid function strictly maps the network's output to the [0,1] range, mathematically allowing the result to be interpreted as the earthquake probability P. title: Memory-Efficient Deep-Learning-Matching Full Waveform Inversion for Field-Scale Datasets

The recently developed deep-learning-matching FWI (DLM-FWI) framework mitigates this by dynamically bridging the phase gap between synthetic and observed data, utilizing a convolutional neural network (CNN) within the inversion loop as a robust kinematic preconditioner. Estimating compound coastal flooding in response to combined fluvial and marine effects in the Seine Bay
abstract: In the context of climate change, low-lying coastal and estuarine environments are highly vulnerable to the combined effects of climate drivers and anthropogenic activities, resulting in destructive flooding and compound flooding events. Assessing these hazards is essential for supporting adaptive coastal management and enhancing coastal resilience. This study investigates compound flooding in the macrotidal Seine Estuary, where flooding is governed by the interaction between Seine River discharge and marine surges along the Normandy coast. title: Ecological Catastrophe Unveiled: A Comprehensive Review of the Impacts of Oil Spills on Marine Ecosystems
abstract: Oil spills are among the most serious forms of marine pollution and result from offshore oil exploration, tanker transport and other shipping activities. This review synthesises the current literature on the biological impacts of oil spills across trophic levels, from primary producers, corals and invertebrates to fishes, amphibians, reptiles, seabirds and marine mammals. title: A Deep‐Learning Model Cascade for Automating Large‐Scale Shoreline Mapping From Satellite Imagery
abstract: Abstract This study describes a machine learning model cascade for automating large‐scale shoreline mapping from time‐series of coastal satellite imagery. Our model cascade consists of independent supervised deep learning models for image suitability, image segmentation, and image segmentation suitability. The segmentation model determines shoreline locations, while the other models in this cascade filter imagery not suitable for segmentation or segmentations not suitable for shoreline detection. abstract: ABSTRACT Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) based lattice structures have attracted considerable interest due to their high strength‐to‐weight ratio and adaptability for functional applications with their continuous topology. This paper presents a framework to generate TPMS lattice structures with tailored surface characteristics on Gyroid, Diamond, and Schwarz P lattices. title: Prediction of Corrosion Rates in Iron-Based Materials Using Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This study investigates the capability of supervised machine learning models to predict corrosion rates in iron-based materials using heterogeneous descriptors obtained from the CORR-DATA repository. The original dataset containing 24,721 records and 15 variables was filtered to retain only iron-based materials, after which duplicate observations and extreme outliers were removed using a three-times interquartile range criterion. title: Simultaneous retrieval of sea-surface waves and winds from high-frequency radar using a convolutional neural network
abstract: High-frequency (HF) ocean radar is a powerful land-based remote sensing technique, yet extracting wave and wind parameters from Doppler spectra remains challenging. Conventional inversions struggle with spectral saturation, low signal-to-noise ratios, and directional ambiguity, traditionally necessitating dual-station networks. This study proposes a unified Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) framework to concurrently extract directional wave spectra and sea-surface wind vectors directly from entire Doppler spectra. abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous photocatalysis has been studied for the treatment of recalcitrant compounds for half a century, but one of the severe limitations for practical oxidation treatment continues to be the inhibitory effect of salt found in real water matrices. The negative impact of Na+, K+, Cl–, and other ionic species is rarely quantified, as there has been no systematic way to discuss salt effects, making the evaluation of photocatalysis performance across studies difficult and imprecise. abstract: Abstract We present an ensemble of five artificial neural network (ANN) models, extending and upgrading a previous model that reconstructs >30 keV equatorial electron flux measurements from low‐Earth‐orbit (LEO) satellite observations. abstract: Abstract The light attenuation coefficient controls underwater light availability and strongly influences marine biogeochemical dynamics. Despite its importance, most ocean biogeochemical models prescribe static climatologies of , neglecting its spatiotemporal variability and observational uncertainty. abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass (LCB)-based biorefineries offer a renewable alternative to first-generation biofuel production systems and petroleum-based refineries. However, their industrial-scale development is constrained by high freshwater consumption and the extensive use of costly chemical and nutrient inputs during biomass pretreatment, enzymatic saccharification, and microbial fermentation, which compromise both process economics and environmental sustainability. abstract: This study characterizes the long-term variability of five major aerosol types: desert dust, urban industrial, clean marine, continental, and mixed, at five Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) sites in Northeast Asia (Beijing, Seoul, Jeju, Hong Kong, and Fukuoka) from 2012 to 2024. title: IoUT-enabled multi-AUV network architecture with edge intelligence and multi-sensor fusion for autonomous hydrographic surveying in dynamic underwater environments
abstract: The integration of Internet of underwater things (IoUT) technologies with autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) is transforming traditional hydrographic surveying by enabling collaborative, intelligent, and networked underwater observation systems. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of recent advancements in IoUT-enabled Multi-AUV network architectures, edge intelligence, and multi-sensor fusion approaches for autonomous hydrographic surveying in dynamic underwater environments. title: Spatial patterns in phytoplankton community composition and their relationship to carbon export on the northwest Weddell Sea continental shelf
abstract: Typically, diatoms, haptophytes, and cryptophytes dominate phytoplankton biomass and abundance in the Southern Ocean, determining bloom dynamics and carbon transfer and responding to physical factors such as sea ice concentration and mixing. However, phytoplankton community composition remains understudied in many regions of the Southern Ocean. Here, we present pigment-based phytoplankton community-composition data from a summer cruise to the northwest Weddell Sea continental shelf. title: Data-driven lithology prediction as a framework for shallow geothermal resource evaluation
abstract: Reliable lithological characterization is essential for preliminary shallow geothermal assessment because ground composition strongly influences thermal and hydraulic behavior, yet borehole information is commonly sparse and unevenly distributed. This study aims to develop a geologically informed, data-driven framework for predicting shallow lithology across Cyprus and to evaluate whether improvements arise primarily from increased neural-network complexity or from better representation of geological information. abstract: The contemporary world is experiencing increasingly complex challenges that affect environmental sustainability, economic stability, public health, social equality, and technological development. Issues such as climate change, environmental degradation, emerging infectious diseases, food insecurity, water scarcity, poverty, digital inequality, and rapid urbanization require comprehensive solutions that cannot be achieved through isolated scientific or technological interventions. title: Influence of oceanic and atmospheric drivers and nonlinear vertical land motion correction on Mediterranean Sea level predictions
abstract: Accurate Mediterranean coastal sea-level prediction requires accounting for vertical land motion (VLM) in tide-gauge (TG) records and selecting predictors appropriate to regional conditions. abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the way we work, and the field of cultural heritage is no exception to this shift. Its integration presents significant opportunities, yet it also raises questions regarding the future of the professions involved, the quality of work, and the responsibility of those utilizing these tools. title: Web-Based and Mobile AI Tools in Southeast Asian Higher Education: A Systematic Review and Thematic Synthesis
abstract: Web-based and mobile artificial intelligence tools have spread rapidly in Southeast Asian universities, yet evidence on what they achieved in real learning remained fragmented. This systematic review synthesised empirical studies that implemented or evaluated such tools in degree-level higher education in Southeast Asia between 2021 and 2026. Following the PRISMA 2020 guideline, 642 Scopus records were screened, 79 full texts were assessed and 59 studies were included. title: A framework for genome-wide characterization of DNA methylation and variant effect prediction
abstract: DNA methylation plays a critical role in many essential biological processes, including transcriptional regulation, genomic imprinting, chromosomal maintenance, genomic stability and development, and has phenotypic and disease impacts. However, genome-wide characterization of methylation patterns across cell types and tissues remains a major challenge. abstract: The sustainable management of small-scale fisheries is key for the well-being of coastal communities. Environmental conditions are known to influence the ecology of the coastal zone, yet their interactions with fisheries management regimes remains poorly understood. We examined spatial changes in the structure of benthic communities under distinct management regimes (TURF or Territorial Use Rights for Fisheries, and OA or open access areas) located in areas with different temperature patterns (warm and cold). abstract: Introduction The bivalve Brachidontes pharaonis (Fisher, 1871) is a filter-feeding mussel widely used as a coastal bioindicator and may accumulate Vibrio alginolyticus , a ubiquitous marine bacterium with pathogenic potential, from surrounding seawater. Despite its ecological relevance in the Gulf of Suez, the dynamics of this host–bacterium association remain poorly characterized. title: AI Readiness, Digital Literacy and Digital Capability: Rethinking Educational Equity in Southeast Asia
abstract: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming digital environments and educational systems across Southeast Asia, while creating challenges for information credibility and digital inequality. This study examines the relationship between government AI readiness and population-level digital literacy across six Southeast Asian countries—Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam—and discusses its implications for digital capability and educational equity. title: Repurposed smart tuna-fishing buoys provide real-time intelligence for marine conservation and ocean observation
abstract: Abstract End-of-use echosounder buoys developed for industrial tuna fishing offer a largely untapped opportunity to expand ocean monitoring using existing fisheries technology. Here we present a technology-transfer and pilot feasibility study testing whether repurposed smart-buoys can operate as short-term autonomous platforms for marine conservation monitoring and ocean observation. abstract: Spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System reflectometry (GNSS-R) sea surface wind speed retrieval commonly relies on the normalized bistatic radar cross section (NBRCS), whose response depends on observation geometry, link conditions, signal quality, and sea state. abstract: Collaborative mapping has emerged as a key approach for collecting, analysing, and sharing geospatial information on natural hazards and risks. abstract: Accurate species assignments using (e)DNA (meta)barcoding depend on the reliability of DNA barcode reference libraries. abstract: The deep learning revolution cultivated the emergence of predictive tools, known as oracles, that do not directly improve understanding of predicted phenomena. The rise of oracles conjures an alarming vision of a new physics devoid of understanding. abstract: Soil is one of the most common forms of trace evidence in forensic investigations. Traditional forensic analyses rely on physical and chemical soil characteristics, which often lack sufficient discriminatory power in complex environments. abstract: The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally transforming the landscape of international relations and diplomatic practice worldwide. This article explores the concept of algorithmic statecraft and its potential implications for Ethiopian diplomacy in an increasingly digitalized global order. abstract: Nature is understood as a part of human life through sacred narratives to sustain the environmental resources. When nature is exposed to environmental disturbances such as climate change, it adapts to these imbalances and restructures itself to maintain a stable state. This article employs the idea of ‘isomorphism’ to investigate self-regulation and transformation of marine ecology through mythological narratives. title: Dust momentum as a metric linking atmospheric dynamics to ocean nutrient delivery
abstract: Dust deposition is a critical nutrient supply route for ocean ecosystems, yet the ecological implications of vertical transport polarity (updraft vs. downdraft) have not been systematically quantified. abstract: This paper analyzes the considerable impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and digitalization on energy markets and trading systems, as well as the expanding electric vehicle (EV) industry and its challenges. abstract: Abstract Currently, more and more machine learning (ML) surrogates are being developed for computationally expensive physical models. abstract: Purpose: This review asks whether, and under what conditions, combining satellite remote sensing with machine learning, and ensemble learning in particular, improves the mapping of illegal-dumpsite susceptibility, and where the evidence for that claim is still missing, with emphasis on sub-Saharan Africa and Nigeria. title: Mapping multidimensional artificial intelligence anxiety among academic librarians in the United Arab Emirates: An exploratory survey
abstract: This exploratory study examines artificial intelligence anxiety among academic librarians in the United Arab Emirates, a multilingual context undergoing rapid digital transformation. abstract: Phase-field simulations of liquid metal dealloying (LMD) capture complex microstructural evolution but become prohibitively expensive over large domains and long time horizons. We introduce a fully convolutional, conditionally parameterized U-Net surrogate designed to extrapolate far beyond its training data in both space and time. abstract: Brachyura taxa serve as key bioindicators of tidal flat ecosystems, yet traditional monitoring methods are labor-intensive, ecologically invasive, and subject to access constraints. Here, we present a non-invasive monitoring approach combining unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery with a U-Net semantic segmentation model to detect and classify Brachyura species directly on the tidal flat surface. abstract: Accurate localization is essential for the Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT), where underwater sensors, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), and surface gateways operate under dynamic acoustic conditions and strict energy constraints. This paper proposes Digital Twin-Reinforcement Learning (DT-RL), an observable-state localization-control framework that combines two-way acoustic ranging with Weighted Least Squares (WLS) position estimation. abstract: Depreciation has been and remains a source of confusion and dispute amongst economists. abstract: MurB, a key enzyme involved in bacterial cell wall biosynthesis, represents a promising target for antibacterial drug discovery. In this study, a machine learning assay was employed to identify potential inhibitors targeting E. coli MurB. title: An Ensemble of Small Convolutional Neural Networks for Identifying Monogeneans of the Order Dactylogyridea from Digital Photographs
abstract: Fish diseases pose a serious obstacle to the economic stability of aquaculture. Correct and timely identification of the causative agent is a necessary condition for carrying out veterinary and sanitary measures, making it possible to prevent mass fish mortality. However, many fish farms lack the laboratory infrastructure and specialists required for detailed analysis. This paper proposes an ensemble of three compact convolutional neural networks for identifying monogeneans of the order Dactylogyridea in photographs obtained through the eyepiece of a light microscope using a smartphone camera.

abstract: Abstract Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs) have attracted attention recently as an alternative to multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) for scientific machine learning. However, KANs can be expensive to train, even for relatively small networks. Inspired by finite basis physics-informed neural networks (FBPINNs), in this work, we develop a domain decomposition-based architecture for KANs that allows for several small KANs to be trained in parallel to give accurate solutions for multiscale problems. abstract: The success of precision fishing methods using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) heavily relies on the sensor's accuracy in detecting thermal anomalies on the water surface. The dynamic characteristics of coastal airspace present mechanical challenges in the form of turbulent flow, which affects vehicle stability and the reading accuracy of the drone's thermal radiation sensors. title: Capítulo 13. Portfolio profesional, empleabilidad y emprendimiento audiovisual
abstract: La transición de la formación universitaria al ejercicio profesional se aborda mediante estrategias para demostrar competencias y construir una identidad reconocible en el sector audiovisual. El capítulo desarrolla criterios para seleccionar, organizar y presentar proyectos en un portfolio, diferenciando sus modalidades y explicando la función del reel como muestra breve del trabajo realizado. title: A Graph Neural Network and Keypoint‐Guided Fitting Based Method for 3D Weld Seam Trajectory Extraction
abstract: To address inaccurate keypoint recognition and noise‐sensitive trajectory fitting in automated 3D weld seam extraction, a learning‐to‐fitting framework combining 3DSeamNet and KGC‐LO‐RANSAC is proposed. 3DSeamNet jointly predicts weld regions, centerline offsets, local tangential directions, and keypoint confidence from workpiece point clouds, providing structured geometric priors for subsequent trajectory fitting. abstract: Rhythmic lunar and solar cycles are well recognised to influence the biology, behaviour, physiology, and ecological adaptations of many terrestrial organisms, yet their effects on marine organisms remain poorly understood. abstract: We present a multi-platform, data-driven framework to reconstruct depth-resolved acoustic scattering profiles in the Northwest Pacific by integrating shipboard acoustics, satellite remote sensing, and Argo/BGC Argo observations. This study evaluates flood susceptibility in the Lower Niger Basin using a geospatial modelling approach. Ten flood-conditioning factors; rainfall, drainage density, slope, elevation, soil texture, land use/land cover (LULC), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and proximity to rivers were integrated within a Random Forest (RF) framework. Monitoring vegetation structure and habitats in restored floodplains is critically important to support evidence‐based NbS implementation and biodiversity conservation interventions. title: Spectral-driven estimation of surface roughness with machine learning for shallow-water modeling
abstract: This work investigates a simplified framework for the parameterisation of two-dimensional hydrodynamic models (2D-SWE) under controlled synthetic conditions. Given the strong influence of Manning’s roughness coefficient on model accuracy, the study explores how spatial variations in this parameter affect the resulting hydraulic response. To this end, a synthetic test case is constructed and analysed using Machine Learning techniques to relate roughness parameterisation to spatial patterns of model discrepancy.

abstract: Virtual sensing reconstructs structural responses at uninstrumented locations from a sparse set of physical measurements, enabling structural health monitoring where dense sensor networks are impractical. abstract: Accurate and low-latency 6D pose estimation is a key requirement for natural interaction in virtual reality systems, yet existing methods often struggle to simultaneously satisfy precision, real-time performance, and robustness in multi-user or interference-prone environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a deep learning-based dual-modal 6D pose estimation framework that integrates RGB and depth sensing for real-time virtual reality interaction. abstract: Introduction Precise mapping of sugarcane varieties is crucial for precision agriculture, yield evaluation, protection of breeders’ rights, efficient supply chain management and policy formulation. Previous studies highlighted that remote sensing techniques suffered issues such as low spatial resolution and inadequate field-validated ground truth data. title: A survey of routing protocols for internet of underwater things from a performance evaluation perspective
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we present a review of IoUT routing protocols, categorizing them into four groups: geographic, opportunistic, void-handling, and clustering routing protocols. We compare and evaluate these routing categories using various performance metrics. Furthermore, we analyze the strengths, limitations, applications, and performance trade-offs of existing IoUT routing protocols across the evaluation scenarios considered. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future research directions for the development of IoUT routing protocols.

abstract: Reliable motion prediction of Floating Offshore Wind Turbine (FOWT) platforms under stochastic metocean conditions is critical for structural safety, fatigue assessment, and operational control. abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in the Western Ghats, frequently causing substantial loss of life, infrastructure damage and environmental degradation. Wayanad District, Kerala, is particularly vulnerable because of its rugged topography, intense monsoon rainfall and complex geological conditions. title: Soil Salinity Mapping using Remote Sensing and Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Review of Methods and Applications
abstract: Soil salinity is a critical environmental issue affecting agricultural productivity and land sustainability, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. This study aims to assess and map soil salinity using remote sensing-based spectral indices integrated with geospatial techniques. A comprehensive set of salinity and vegetation indices including SI, NDSI, VSSI, NDVI and SAVI, was derived from multispectral satellite data to enhance the detection of saline-affected areas. title: Soil Salinisation in Irrigated Drylands of the Middle East and North Africa: Drivers, Extent, Crop Impacts and Reclamation Strategies
abstract: Salt-affected soils cover an estimated 8–12 million km² worldwide, and secondary salinisation caused by irrigation threatens a large share of the irrigated land on which food security in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) depends. This review synthesises evidence on the processes, extent, agronomic impacts, economic costs and management of soil salinity, with emphasis on Egypt and the wider MENA region. title: Integrating machine-learning-based landslide susceptibility and vulnerability for slope-unit risk assessment
abstract: Landslide susceptibility identifies terrain associated with landslide occurrence, whereas risk prioritization also requires information on the vulnerability of threatened elements. This letter presents a slope-unit framework linking machine-learning susceptibility prediction, SHAP-based interpretation, and vulnerability-based relative risk classification. Four models were evaluated using a regional test dataset, and the selected model was applied to 393 slope units. abstract: Abstract Sponges host phylogenetically highly diverse yet stable microbial symbiont communities that underpin the ecological success of the holobiont through functions such as nutrient cycling and secondary metabolite production. Here we describe 17 MAGs recovered from deep-sea sponges that belong to an uncultivated and previously uncharacterised, globally distributed microbial clade historically assigned a variety of placeholder names (AncK6, SAUL, PAUC34f and JAAXHH01). abstract: In Antarctica, two plausible tipping points have been suggested: an ocean tipping point involving a cold-to-warm transition of ice-shelf cavities, and an ice-sheet tipping point associated with the marine ice-sheet instability. abstract: Climate change has become one of the most pressing global challenges, particularly for coastal regions vulnerable to sea level rise, coastal erosion, and ecological degradation. In Indonesia, environmental adaptation is influenced not only by technical and policy approaches but also by cultural and religious values. abstract: Abstract Turbulent mixing may become increasingly important in a changing Arctic Ocean, influencing regional dynamics and global overturning. Arctic turbulence remains poorly characterized due to sparse observations, limitations of conventional parameterizations, and incomplete understanding. title: Machine Learning Calibration of Sentinel-3 Significant Wave Height Using Level-2 Features Only: A Two-Stage Approach Validated at 83 NDBC Buoys
abstract: Satellite radar altimetry provides the only global, all-weather record of significant wave height (SWH), but Sentinel-3 Level-2 retrievals retain systematic, context-dependent errors near coasts and at low sea states. We present a two-stage calibration that uses only Level-2 variables: a buoy-weighted isotonic regression removes the scale-dependent bias, and a LightGBM model predicts the residual from waveform-quality and along-track descriptors, with quantile models supplying a per-sample uncertainty. abstract: Estuarine delta wetlands are relatively fragile ecosystems, and soil ecological stoichiometry plays an important role in understanding wetland ecological conditions and developing effective restoration and sustainable management strategies. However, the spatial patterns of soil ecological stoichiometric characteristics and their relationships with environmental factors in estuarine delta wetlands remain insufficiently understood. abstract: Abstract Equatorial plasma bubbles (EPBs) are major low‐latitude ionospheric irregularities that can cause scintillation and degrade Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) performance. Existing amplitude‐scintillation prediction methods primarily use historical GNSS observations and ionospheric parameters, but rarely incorporate the evolving spatial morphology of EPBs. This study develops an airglow‐enhanced framework for regional EPB monitoring, short‐term airglow forecasting, and minute‐resolution scintillation prediction. abstract: Freshwater salinization is an increasing concern in colder regions where road-salt application, watershed development, hydroclimatic factors, and anthropogenic activities influence river salinity. This study evaluated winter freshwater salinization across six rivers in New York and New Jersey. abstract: Escherichia coli is one measure of fecal contamination in water, which is expected to correlate with the presence of fecal pathogens, such as pathogenic E. coli or Salmonella. abstract: Satellite-based wildfire spread studies differ in data organization and evaluation procedures, making model performance difficult to compare. Infrared brightness temperatures from geostationary satellites offer excellent temporal coverage over continental-scale domains. abstract: Abstract Eukaryotic microalgae fundamentally contribute to marine primary production throughout the year. abstract: Machine learning methods, particularly Random Forest (RF), present an effective solution for predicting urban pluvial flood water depth, especially in data-scarce regions where traditional hydrological and hydraulic observations are lacking. abstract: Background Coastal oxygen depletion is a major driver of changes in sediment biogeochemistry and microbial functioning. This study examined three sites with differing oxygen regimes across a year to investigate how temporal oxygen variability shapes surface sediment microbial communities and activity. abstract: Sugarcane is one of the major commercial crops cultivated in Andhra Pradesh, India, and accurate yield estimation is essential for agricultural planning, crop management, and food security. Conventional yield estimation methods are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and often limited in spatial coverage. Recent advancements in remote sensing, cloud computing, and machine learning have provided efficient alternatives for large-scale agricultural monitoring and crop yield prediction. abstract: Accurate fertilizer recommendation is fundamental to precision agriculture, yet many machine learning models rely on static soil nutrient measurements without adequately incorporating environmental factors that influence nutrient availability. This study proposes a hybrid machine learning framework that integrates soil chemical, physical, and climatic variables into a Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-derived Soil Quality Index (SQI) for crop-specific fertilizer recommendation. title: Spread spectrum orthogonal time-frequency space underwater acoustic communication based on second-order differential encoding
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation has been widely applied in underwater acoustic communication due to its superior adaptability in handling Doppler frequency shifts in high-speed mobile channels. abstract: Background Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) increasingly draw on artificial intelligence for prediction, classification, and control tasks. abstract: Abstract South America experiences recurrent precipitation variability and hydroclimatic anomalies, yet two questions remain unresolved: whether joint climate-mode states add information beyond individual-mode effects and how predictably their associated regional anomalies can be recovered out of sample. abstract: Abstract Developing desalination membranes that combine high water permeance with high ion rejection remains important for freshwater production. abstract: The ability to learn continuously in artificial neural networks is often limited by catastrophic forgetting, a phenomenon in which new knowledge becomes dominant. By taking mechanisms of memory encoding in neuroscience (i.e., engrams) as inspiration, we propose a novel approach that integrates stochastically activated engrams as a gating mechanism for metaplastic binarized neural networks (mBNNs). abstract: To achieve Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) Target 3, the selection of protected areas must consider the condition of ecosystems at sites in addition to the GBF 30% area target. Implementing this consideration for coral reef ecosystems is challenging because data describing condition are patchy and limited. abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) has a substantial mortality rate among urologic cancers today, and our current knowledge of the disease includes few distinct biomarkers, making early diagnosis particularly difficult. In this study, we utilized digital holographic microscopy (DHM) and quantitative phase imaging (QPI) to investigate trends in cell morphology and optical properties across 38 morphological and optical features in renal carcinoma cell lines UO-31 and SN12C, and renal epithelial cell line HK2. abstract: Applications of lightweight, wear-resistant polymer composites in automobile and engineering fields require an effective method for predicting and optimizing their wear performance, which will also curtail the time for designing new materials. Therefore, the present work employs L25 orthogonal array, machine learning (ML) techniques and wear mapping to study the dry sliding wear behavior of short carbon fiber–reinforced polypropylene (CF/PP) composites. abstract: This study investigates the electroactive, microstructural, and immersion behaviors of as-cast and heat-treated Al alloy anodes in 1 M KOH and 1 M NaCl solutions, aiming to enhance aluminum battery performance. abstract: Abstract Reliable fault diagnosis is essential for improving the safety, reliability, and operational efficiency of wind turbines. This study presents a machine learning (ML) framework for multi-class classification of wind turbine blade faults using vibration signals. The proposed approach combines statistical features and wavelet packet energy features to characterize the dynamic response of the blades under five health conditions: healthy, crack, erosion, twist, and unbalance. abstract: This study evaluates the hydrochemical characteristics and extent of saltwater intrusion in selected coastal communities of Rivers State, Niger Delta, Nigeria, with particular emphasis on groundwater vulnerability, salinity distribution and suitability for domestic and agricultural applications. Groundwater samples were collected from six (6) boreholes and six(6) hand-dug wells across Sama, Tema, Abalama, Buguma, Ido and Obuama communities and analysed for physicochemical parameters, major ions and selected heavy metals using standard laboratory procedures. title: Exploring marine conservation futures to inform systematic conservation planning
abstract: Marine conservation must advance towards global biodiversity targets despite significant climatic and geopolitical uncertainties. We present an expert-informed scenario framework to support systematic conservation planning in marine environments in the face of such unpredictable conditions. title: A lag-informed deep learning framework for real-time downstream water-level forecasting and flood decision support in the Kalu Ganga Basin, Sri Lanka
abstract: Floods are among the most damaging hazards in Sri Lanka's wet-zone river basins, where short warning lead times constrain preparedness and physically based hydrodynamic models are often impractical under limited data. This study develops a lag-informed deep-learning framework for 10-h-ahead downstream water-level forecasting in the flood-prone Kalu Ganga Basin, Sri Lanka. title: Analysis of Environmental Factors Influencing Regional Yellowfin Tuna Fishing Using Multi‐Strategy Generalized Additive Model
abstract: ABSTRACT Yellowfin tuna ( Thunnus albacares ) distribution is regulated by multidimensional oceanic environmental factors. However, the biophysical mechanisms associated with subsurface ocean parameters remain unclear. Here, we elucidated environmental factors influencing catch per unit effort in the South China Sea and adjacent waters, evaluated hyperparameter optimization for generalized additive models, and provided recommendations for fisheries management. abstract: Abstract The accurate detection and mapping of underground pipelines are critical for urban planning and infrastructure resilience. This process is critical to prevent catastrophic failures, minimize service disruptions, and maintain the structural integrity of public works projects. title: Multi-Image Sampling for Soil Particle Size Distribution Prediction Using Multiple Instance Learning
abstract: Predicting particle size distributions (PSD) from soil images is challenging because segmentation approaches fail to resolve sub-pixel fine particles and standard convolutional neural network architectures cannot efficiently process images at the high resolution required to capture fine-scale information. title: Assessing urban metro station flood resilience under extreme rainfall using an integrated machine learning–MCDM framework
abstract: Against the backdrop of climate change and rapid urbanisation, frequent extreme rainfall events have exposed urban underground rail transit systems to increasingly severe flood risks. Metro stations exhibit substantial differences in flood susceptibility, vulnerability, and recovery capacity, making it difficult for conventional risk assessment methods to accurately characterise their flood resilience. abstract: ABSTRACT Improving the fatigue life of advanced composites and accurately predicting their fatigue life are crucial because composites are increasingly used in applications involving repeated loading, including automotive chassis, wind turbine blades, aircraft structures, and bridges. Graphene‐modified glass fiber‐reinforced polymer (GFRP) composites were fabricated using the vacuum resin infusion method. title: Projecting the potential distribution of sea buckthorn in the Hindu Kush Himalaya under climate change using ensemble species distribution modelling
abstract: Sea Buckthorn is a multipurpose shrub valued for its nutrient-rich berries, land aggradation ability, and support to livelihoods in high-altitude regions. However, rapid environmental changes are threatening its habitats. Despite its climatic vulnerability, the impact of climate change on its habitats is poorly understood in the Hindu Kush Himalayas (HKH), a region spanning across eight countries. title: Reconstructing ancient ecosystems: guanaco and marine carrion as drivers of predator-prey networks in Southern South America
abstract: Understanding ancient trophic dynamics and human integration in terrestrial high-latitude ecosystems requires moving beyond traditional taxonomic lists to evaluate structural biological interactions. This study presents the first probabilistic, trait-based bipartite network reconstruction of ancient predator-prey assemblages in northern Tierra del Fuego, Southern South America, based on archeological records. title: Toward Multi-Fidelity optimization with transfer learning and parallel mechanisms
abstract: Multi-fidelity (MF) surrogate model optimization, as a cost-effective strategy that balances accuracy and efficiency, is increasingly employed in expensive black-box optimization. To enhance approximation capability and robustness of multi-fidelity surrogate model on heterogeneous high-fidelity (HF) and low-fidelity (LF) data, this paper proposes a robust MF model, termed Transfer-Learning-based Multi-Fidelity Neural Network (TL-MFNN).
