title: PCB Fault Detection AI-Based Inspection of Printed Circuit Boards
abstract: Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) are essential components of electronic devices, and even minor defects can affect their performance and reliability. Traditional manual inspection is time-consuming and may fail to identify small defects such as missing components, broken copper tracks, soldering errors, and incorrect component placement. To overcome these limitations, the proposed AI-Based PCB Fault Detection System uses computer vision and image processing techniques to analyze PCB images and identify potentially defective regions. title: CNN on ‘Top’: In search of scalable and lightweight image-based jet taggers
abstract: Abstract While Transformer-based and standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven to be the best performers in classifying different types of jets, they require substantial computational power. We explore the scope of using a lightweight and scalable version of EfficientNet architecture, along with global features of the jet. title: ML-assisted intra-salt interpretation of the Zechstein Group in the Norwegian North Sea: Implications for salt caverns
abstract: Abstract Salt formations often consist of layered evaporite sequences (LES) with mechanically distinct lithologies, which generate complex internal structures during deformation. Interpreting these structures in seismic data is challenging because of poor imaging, discontinuous reflectors, and strong velocity contrasts. While machine learning (ML) has been increasingly applied to salt boundary detection, its potential for resolving intra-salt structures remains underexplored. abstract: Abstract Nearshore ocean currents are characterized by complex structures and spatial heterogeneity. Conventional measurement techniques are either inefficient or offer low spatial resolution, while image velocimetry (a low-cost, high-resolution method) is limited in marine applications due to the trade-off between large-area coverage and high resolution, as well as the lack of ground control points for calibration. abstract: ABSTRACT Seawater electrolysis has been identified as a sustainable approach for the industrialization of green hydrogen. However, this process is hindered by two significant factors: the sluggish anodic kinetics and chloride‐induced corrosion. title: A CNN-Based Fault Diagnosis Method for AUV Thrusters Integrating Multidomain Data Sequence Reconstruction and Data Channel Extension
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are increasingly used in marine exploration and underwater operations, where unexpected thruster faults may hinder mission execution and compromise operational safety. Therefore, efficient and reliable fault diagnosis methods are essential for improving the safety and autonomy of AUV operations. Data-driven fault diagnosis approaches provide an efficient way for detecting thruster faults in autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). title: Interactions of large pelagic sharks (Elasmobranchii) with capture-based tuna aquaculture and salmon farming in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Interactions between large pelagic sharks and marine aquaculture remain poorly documented in the Mediterranean Sea. We report six cage-entry events involving blue sharks, Prionace glauca (Linnaeus, 1758), and shortfin makos, Isurus oxyrinchus Rafinesque, 1810, associated with capture-based Atlantic bluefin tuna aquaculture and Atlantic salmon farming between 2018 and 2026. title: An autonomous imaging system for reef fish monitoring in the southern Gulf of Mexico
abstract: Introduction Reef fish assemblages are widely used as indicators of coral reef condition. Yet, diver-based surveys provide limited temporal resolution and are constrained by logistical demands. We evaluated an autonomous underwater imaging system based on cameras programmed for unattended image acquisition to monitor reef fish assemblages in the southern Gulf of Mexico. Methods Five terrestrial trail cameras adapted for underwater deployment were operated at Bajo de Diez reef during two seasonal deployments in 2024 and 2025, yielding 191,758 valid underwater images at a nominal 3-min interval.

title: Hybrid GWO–GA optimized LSTM–MLP framework for highly accurate palmer drought severity index prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of the Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) is essential for drought monitoring, climate-risk assessment, and the effective management of water resources. This study proposes a hybrid Long Short-Term Memory–Multilayer Perceptron (LSTM–MLP) model for PDSI prediction, integrated with a Grey Wolf Optimizer–Genetic Algorithm (GWO–GA) optimization framework. title: Strategic Opportunities and Key Challenges for China's Marine Energy Resource Development under the Framework of the 15th Five‑Year Plan
abstract: The 15th Five‑Year Plan period represents a critical window for China's transition from a maritime nation to a maritime power. This paper, guided by the outline of the 15th Five‑Year Plan and related policy documents, employs a combination of policy text analysis and industrial empirical analysis to systematically explore pathways and strategies for the efficient development and utilization of marine energy resources. title: Sideswiping Typhoons Exacerbate Autumn Ozone Pollution in Coastal China
abstract: Abstract Ozone (O 3 ) pollution in coastal China exhibits a widespread increasing trend in autumn, coinciding with the active period of typhoons. Yet, the role of typhoons in autumn O 3 variations remains unclear. Here, we analyze autumn O 3 evolution during 63 typhoon episodes over 2014–2023, and illustrate diverse impacts of typhoons on O 3 variations over different coastal regions. title: AI-powered rapid detection of meat adulteration with terahertz spectroscopy in food and drug control
abstract: Introduction Meat adulteration is an increasing problem in food and drug law enforcement, where existing identification methods are inefficient and of limited scope. Methods This study proposes a detection scheme that combines terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) with artificial intelligence. Time-domain spectra of five common meat species (chicken, beef, duck, mutton and pork) were collected in the 0.2–2.0 THz band, and the absorption coefficient, refractive index and dielectric constant were calculated. title: Retrieving mangrove biochemical traits under oil pollution using hyperspectral data and transfer learning
abstract: Mangrove forests are essential in improving coastal resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration. However, they are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic pressures, particularly pollution such as oil contamination, which can induce long-term physiological stress in mangrove vegetation. Yet, monitoring the health of such ecosystems across large areas is difficult due to the scarcity of ground-based data and the spatial resolution–coverage trade-off. abstract: Tracking submerged targets in shallow-water acoustic environments poses severe operational challenges due to low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), ambient clutter, and range unobservability in passive bearings-only tracking. abstract: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) remains a leading environmental risk to global health, yet projections of future PM 2.5 ‐attributable mortality remain uncertain because of coarse model resolution and difficulty disentangling the effects of emissions, climate change, and land use. Here, we present a high‐resolution assessment of present‐day (2010) and future (2050) PM 2.5 ‐related mortality by integrating Earth system modeling, machine learning, and epidemiological analysis within a factorial forcing framework. abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable climate projections are essential for climate-risk assessment and planning. Yet, uncertainty in Global Climate Models (GCMs) and ensemble construction remains a major challenge. This study developed a machine learning-based selective multimodel ensemble framework to project precipitation, maximum temperature (Tmax), and minimum temperature (Tmin) over the Kangsabati, Keliaghai, Silabati, and Dwarkeswar (KKSD) river basin in eastern India. abstract: Abstract To address the inherent limitations of the YOLOv12n model in complex underwater environments, such as insufficient global context capture, restricted detection accuracy, and feature information loss during downsampling, this paper proposes a lightweight enhanced model named WDF-YOLO. title: Reducing false alarms in crackmeter-based early warning of small-scale slope deformation via deep learning-driven asynchronous displacement–rainfall data fusion
abstract: Real-time crackmeter-based deformation monitoring systems for small-scale rainfall-affected slopes suffer from high false alarm rates. Across multi-slope monitoring settings, threshold-based alerts are vulnerable to noise, while conventional denoising and prediction-based validation methods remain limited in automated warning discrimination and cross-site generalization. abstract: Coastal soil salinization driven by sea-level rise and changing climate patterns is a serious threat to agricultural productivity and wetland ecosystems worldwide. This study evaluated temporal variations in soil salinity across seven coastal locations, namely low saline (Sites 6 and 7), moderately saline (Site 3), very saline (Sites 4 and 5), and strongly saline (Sites 1 and 2). In this study, we leveraged machine learning (ML) to improve void fraction prediction across different combinations of liquids, gases, and flow orientations. abstract: This work investigates the potential of using a bio-based epoxy resin (Sicomin Infugreen 810) as an alternative to a conventional synthetic resin system (Gurit Prime 37) for marine applications. Carbon fibre reinforced polymer composites were manufactured and surface properties were characterised. abstract: Large eddy simulation (LES) on a cylindrical grid consisting of approximately 7 billion points is used to analyse the wake flow of a marine propeller equipped with propeller boss cap fins (PBCFs). abstract: Acute mountain sickness (AMS) poses a significant threat to individuals ascending to high-altitude regions, yet early identification of susceptible populations remains challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model for estimating AMS risk from exercise-induced physiological responses measured at low altitude. abstract: Coral reef limestone (CRL) originating from biogenic sedimentation is the main geomaterial widespread on the remote oceanic islands and reefs. title: From pixel-level retrievals to bay-scale nutrient dynamics in Pärnu Bay using Sentinel-3 OLCI
abstract: Monitoring nutrient dynamics is essential for assessing eutrophication in coastal waters, yet conventional in situ observations provide limited spatial coverage. This study evaluated the capability of Sentinel-3 Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI)-derived nutrient products to represent seasonal and interannual dynamics of total nitrogen (TN) and total phosphorus (TP) in Pärnu Bay, Gulf of Riga, during 2016–2024. title: Early warning system for non-seismic gravity driven tsunamis
abstract: Gravity-driven mass flows represent a significant near-field hazard in volcanic environments and, increasingly, in coastal regions affected by climate-driven slope instability. Despite their destructive potential, quantitative assessments of real-time detection systems operating under natural conditions remain scarce. abstract: Ovarian cancer classification based on histopathological images is complicated by the wide range of morphological patterns and the similarity of cancer types. The article describes a hybrid ResNet50–Vision Transformer–XGBoost ovarian cancer classification model that improves classification accuracy using multiple deep learning approaches. abstract: Abstract Chloride-induced corrosion is the dominant cause of durability degradation in concrete structures, and numerical modeling is an effective approach to reveal chloride transport mechanisms and predict structural long-term service performance. abstract: Air pollution, especially in Asia, poses a serious threat to public health and the environment, highlighting the need for accurate urban air pollution prediction models for better management and health protection. abstract: While biological rhythms are crucial to life, the deep sea has long been considered an arrhythmic exception. abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid progress of deep learning has been driven in part by general principles of biological information processing, yet current AI systems still fall short of biological intelligence in critical ways such as integration of the computational and physical domains, i.e., embodied AI, and achieving autonomy in complex environments. abstract: Routine swimming-pool surveillance may support detection-oriented screening, but rare positives and repeated sampling complicate model validation. This retrospective study analyzed 453 samples (37 occurrence-positive) from four chlorinated pools in two Greek facilities (2022-2025). This issue is particularly critical for ship hulls, offshore structures, and welded components exposed to long-term seawater attack, mechanical loading, and localized corrosion damage. Conventional surface treatments often compromise corrosion resistance, mechanical properties, and processing scalability, limiting their use for large marine components and on-site maintenance. title: Integrating Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Gut Microbiome Analysis, and Structural Analysis to Reveal the Molecular Mechanisms Linking PFOA and PFOS Exposure to Age-Related Macular Degeneration
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) are persistent environmental contaminants with potential adverse effects on human health, but their involvement in age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomics, network toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization (MR), gut microbiome analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate potential molecular targets linking PFOA/PFOS exposure to AMD. title: Phase prediction of high-entropy alloys via transfer learning with domain adaptation and oversampling
abstract: Accurate phase prediction is critical for customized high-entropy alloys (HEAs) design. Machine learning has been widely adopted to improve their phase classification accuracy, but limited samples and phase imbalance remain challenging. Herein, we developed a deep learning-based transfer learning scheme from sputtered-state to as-cast alloys. title: Spatial Prediction of Opisthorchis viverrini Infection Risk Using Multi‐Source Remote Sensing, Hexagonal Grid Optimization, and Ensemble Machine Learning: A Case Study From Northeastern Thailand
abstract: Abstract Opisthorchis viverrini (OV) infection is a major public health problem in northeastern Thailand, where it causes cholangiocarcinoma. This study developed a spatial prediction model for OV infection risk in Sakon Nakhon Province by integrating Sentinel‐2, Sentinel‐3, and CHIRPS data with hexagonal grid optimization and ensemble machine learning. Eleven environmental indices were aggregated using a newly developed Hd index, which identified an optimal hexagonal grid size of d = 2,100 m. title: Empirical screening of sesamol, melatonin, and spermidine combinations on growth, biochemical composition, and antioxidant responses of Nitzschia closterium under low-salinity stress
abstract: Low-salinity stress, frequently caused by spring rainfall and estuarine fluctuations, is a major constraint on the large-scale cultivation of marine diatoms and can disrupt their growth, photosynthesis, and carbon metabolism. Nitzschia closterium is a marine diatom with high nutritional value and strong potential for producing PUFAs such as EPA and DHA, and it is also widely used as a live feed in aquaculture. abstract: Background Dietary ingestion is a major exposure pathway for environmental radionuclides, and the radiological safety of seafood, an important component of the global diet, has attracted increasing public concern. As a Chinese coastal city where seafood is a traditional part of local residents’ daily diet, Ningbo lacks systematic baseline data on radionuclide levels in locally common edible seafood and associated dietary radiological risks for local residents. title: From sea turtle rehabilitation to verifiable conservation outcomes: an evidence-based framework for aquariums
abstract: Zoos and aquariums increasingly identify conservation as a central institutional commitment, but their contributions require evaluation through verifiable outcomes. Sea turtle rehabilitation provides a useful context because appropriately managed rescue and rehabilitation can support individual welfare and generate information on health, disease, anthropogenic threats, and post-release recovery, yet release alone does not demonstrate population-level benefit. abstract: Computational drug discovery is increasingly transforming the way therapeutic candidates are identified, prioritized, and optimized, with advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, molecular modelling, cheminformatics, and data-driven approaches expanding the possibilities for early-stage drug discovery. title: Genetic diversity and population structure of Metapenaeus ensis in the South China Sea determined via genotyping-by-sequencing
abstract: Metapenaeus ensis is a commercially important penaeid shrimp widely distributed across the Indo-West Pacific. However, the population genetic characteristics of its wild stocks along the Chinese coast remain poorly understood. This study employed genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) to assess genetic diversity, population structure, and historical gene flow in six wild M. ensis populations collected along the Chinese coast, including Beibu Gulf (BB), Lingao (LG), Raoping (RP), Shanwei (SW), Sanya (SY), and Zhuhai (ZH). title: BOILER ASH REINFORCED HDPE/NATURAL RUBBER COMPOSITES FOR OTEC COLD WATER PIPES
abstract: The development of lightweight materials for Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) cold-water pipes requires an appropriate balance of mechanical strength and flexibility. This study investigated the mechanical properties of high-density polyethylene (HDPE) composites containing natural rubber (NR), polypropylene-graft-maleic anhydride (PP-g-MA), and palm oil boiler ash (POBA) to identify a promising formulation for further development. journal: Jurnal Ilmiah Ilmu Terapan Universitas Jambi|JIITUJ|

title: An institutional analysis and development perspective of Taiwan’s oceanographic data management: an orderly chaos
abstract: Using the Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) framework, this research evaluates Taiwan’s oceanographic data management and identifies issues for the prospect of its development. Six databanks were interviewed. Taiwan’s oceanographic data management remains in an orderly chaos. On one hand, it is chaotic because there exist multiple actors with their own data management rules. title: Defining in plain language: towards an accessible dictionary
abstract: This paper explores the use of plain language in lexicographic definitions, supported by artificial intelligence, specifically ChatGPT, as a tool to improve dictionary accessibility. After a conceptual review of the evolution of definitions and their central role in dictionaries, the study analyzes a sample of 18 definitions from the Diccionario de la lengua española (DLE), reformulated by ChatGPT according to clarity criteria. title: Blue Economy Practices in Muslim-Majority Countries: Are They Sharia-Compliant?
abstract: The expansion of the Blue Economy in Muslim-majority countries has intensified debates over marine economic development, environmental sustainability, and Islamic economic principles, yet whether sustainable marine practices satisfy Sharia requirements remains insufficiently examined. This study investigates the alignment of Blue Economy practices with Sharia principles through a comparative analysis of coastal contexts in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia. An exploratory sequential mixed-methods design was employed, integrating qualitative cross-case analysis with Delphi expert validation
journal: BALANCA Jurnal Ekonomi dan Bisnis Islam

title: Generative assimilation and prediction for weather and climate
abstract: Machine learning models have shown great success in predicting weather up to two weeks ahead, outperforming process-based benchmarks 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 . However, most existing approaches do not fully integrate data assimilation into the prediction workflow 6 , 7 , and often suffer from error accumulation in autoregressive computation, limiting their applicability to predictions beyond the medium range 8 and climate projections 9 . title: Uncovering new antibiofilm roseabols from marine Clonostachys rosea through structural and multiomics approaches
abstract: Through a combined approach, that involved the one-strain-many-compounds (OSMAC) culturing approach, metabolomic and genomic studies, and bioassay-guided purification we disclose the marine fungus Clonostachys rosea as producer of a family of peptaibols with new structural features. HRMS/MS, NMR, and advanced Marfey's analysis enabled the structural elucidation of two major compounds of the roseabol family, named roseabols B (1) and C (2). title: Tangible AI in the Elementary Classroom: Effects on AI Literacy, Computational Thinking, and Learner Dispositions
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly ubiquitous, yet AI literacy remains underdeveloped in elementary education, where young learners often view AI in anthropomorphic or magical terms. This study examined changes in computational thinking (CT), AI concept mastery, learning motivation, and programming self-efficacy following a tangible AI intervention, and explored the teacher's implementation experience. Guided by a framework integrating the AI Literacy Framework and the SEAME Model, a four-week intervention (4 × 60 minutes) was implemented with 36 fifth-grade students and one teacher
journal: Journal of General Education and Humanities

title: Submarine groundwater discharge and nutrient enrichment in Kingston Harbour, Jamaica: geochemical evidence and spatial and seasonal dynamics
abstract: Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) constitutes a critical but systematically underquantified pathway for nutrient delivery to coastal waters, particularly in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) where coastal aquifers may be contaminated by wastewater and urban runoff. This study evaluated spatial and temporal variability in nutrients, chlorophyll a and physicochemical conditions in Kingston Harbour, Jamaica, a coastal water body that has experienced decades of eutrophication and declining biodiversity. title: Resilient substation design for 500-year storm events—Current state-of-the-art and challenges for floodplain management and infrastructure hardening
abstract: Electrical substations are critical but flood-sensitive power-system assets. This paper presents an integrated engineering framework for improving substation resilience to the 0.2% annual exceedance flood probability, commonly referred to as the 500-year flood, while recognizing that historical flood frequencies may not represent future climate conditions. title: A data-driven predictive system for shellfish biotoxin risk assessment
abstract: Diarrhetic shellfish poisoning (DSP) toxins pose a major threat to the aquaculture industry and public health. Traditional monitoring methods suffer from delays and high costs, and intelligent early warning systems are urgently needed. The study utilised machine learning to predict shellfish biotoxin levels in shellfish by integrating multiple data sources, including phytoplankton monitoring, climatic variables, and historical toxin records. title: Genomic mechanisms underlying Bombay duck's rapid population surge
abstract: Bombay duck (Harpadon nehereus), once a minor by-catch in the East China Sea, has bloomed into a dominant species, altering marine ecosystems. This study explored the genomic basis of its mysterious recent success via chromosome-level genome assembly, comparative and population genomics. The genome assemblies of H. nehereus and its closely related outgroup species Saurida undosquamis were of good quality, showing a 96.7-96.8% Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologues completeness. title: Self-evolving Embodied AI
abstract: Abstract Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) is an intelligent system formed by agents and their environment through active perception, embodied cognition, and action interaction. Existing embodied AI remains confined to human-crafted setting, in which agents are trained on given memories and construct models for given tasks, enabling fixed physical embodiments to interact with relatively static environments. However, for machine-learning surrogate climate models (emulators), we show that the low structural diversity in existing scenarios commonly used to generate training data places a ceiling on predictive skill. Owing to their stable line-spectrum characteristics and spatial directional information related to target bearing, they provide an important information source for non-acoustic passive ship localization and continuous trajectory estimation. title: Life in a sea urchin esophagus: a new endosymbiotic bivalve (Galeommatida, Galeommatoidea) from abyssal depths off southern Australia
abstract: During a large deep-sea survey off the southern coast of Australia, an unusual galeommatid bivalve was discovered living in the esophagus of the abyssal irregular urchin Carnarechinus clypeatus (Agassiz, 1879). We have determined that the bivalve, found from approximately 4000–5000 m depth, is a new species in the poorly documented genus Vaticinaria Dall, 1901. We reinstate the genus Vaticinaria and compare it with other genera that have been associated with it in the literature. abstract: The Chela (Barremian) and Kinkasi (Cenomanian) formations contain important hydrocarbon-bearing reservoir intervals within the onshore Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Coastal Basin. However, despite favorable geological conditions and the recognized hydrocarbon prospectivity of these reservoirs, hydrocarbon production remains limited and restricted to the Lindu-1 well. abstract: Aquaculture and fisheries are important contributors to global food supply but are highly energy and water-intensive, relying heavily on fossil fuels and contributing substantially to greenhouse-gas emissions. The Water-Energy-Food (WEF) nexus provides a framework for managing these interdependencies, and integrating Renewable Energy Sources (RES) is a key pathway towards more sustainable production. title: AI-Assisted Decision-Support Framework for Food Waste Compost Quality Assessment in Coastal Communities: A Case Study of KEEA Municipality, Ghana
abstract: Food waste management remains a major challenge in rapidly urbanising African coastal communities with limited waste infrastructure. This study developed an exploratory AI-assisted decision-support framework for assessing food-waste compost quality in selected coastal communities in Ghana. Organic waste generation was monitored for four weeks across 85 households in four communities, followed by laboratory evaluation of feedstock characteristics, compost physicochemical properties, germination-based maturity, microbial safety, and contaminant indicators. abstract: The conservation of the coastal built environment faces critical challenges, ranging from capillary moisture rise, particularly in land reclaimed from the sea, and marine aerosol degradation, to cyclic salt crystallization–dissolution processes driven by relative humidity fluctuations. title: Advanced Corrosion Monitoring and Predictive Integrity Assessment of Oil and Gas Pipelines in Saudi Arabia: Integrating Risk-Based Inspection, Degradation Modeling, and Preventive Maintenance
abstract: Saudi Arabia's oil and gas pipeline systems operate across environments where saline soils, coastal exposure, variable water handling, and long asset lives can complicate corrosion control. Although inspection, corrosion prediction, and maintenance optimisation have each progressed, their integration into defensible operational decisions remains uneven. This critical review evaluates evidence published between 2020 and 2025 on pipeline monitoring, degradation modelling, risk-based inspection, and preventive maintenance, with emphasis on transferability to Saudi operating conditions. title: Conservation-focused digital twins: the current landscape and lessons learned from the Dangermond Preserve
abstract: As conservation challenges intensify, digital twins—virtual models that integrate real-time data and simulations—offer a powerful new approach to understanding and managing natural systems. In this paper, we explore how digital twin technologies, widely used in industry, can be adapted to meet the unique needs of conservation. We introduce a technical maturity framework tailored to conservation contexts, outlining stages from foundational data collection to Artificial Intelligence (AI) augmented management. title: A decision support framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration through process-based ecosystem modeling and optimization
abstract: Wetland restoration is increasingly recognized as a nature-based climate solution, but effective planning requires balancing nonlinear ecological responses with economic and implementation constraints. We propose a conceptual and computational framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration that embeds process-based ecosystem modeling within restoration optimization. abstract: Equitable access to quality English Language Teaching (ELT) in remote, outermost, and underdeveloped (3T) island regions remains constrained by geographical isolation, severe textbook shortages, and an acute deficit of educators holding linear academic degrees in English education At SMA Negeri 5 Kepulauan Aru in Kabalsiang Benjuring Village, English instruction is conducted by non-EFL teachers facing pedagogical and instructional design barriers. title: Desenvolvimento de algoritmo de k-nearest neighbors (vizinhos mais próximos) para classificação de imagens de organismos do plâncton.
abstract: This study aimed to develop a k-nearest neighbors (KNN)-based algorithm for the automated recognition of planktonic organisms from digital images. Image datasets were used to train and evaluate the classifier, and its performance was assessed based on classification accuracy. The KNN approach achieved accuracy rates comparable to those obtained through conventional image identification by non-specialist observers, suggesting its potential as an alternative computational tool for plankton ecological analyses.

title: Re-specifying hydrocide: governance reproduction and cost externalisation in the Aral Sea basin
abstract: The Aral Sea crisis raises a question beyond environmental-governance failure: how can governance institutions persist alongside serious ecological degradation? This article assesses the proposition that displacement of water-related costs can help sustain such institutions. abstract: Cooperation on the continental shelf beyond 200 nautical miles can contribute to the blue economy by making scientific investment useful across successive stages of offshore development. This article compares developments in the East and South China Seas through submissions to and progress reports of the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS), diplomatic notes, government documents, and judicial decisions. abstract: Self-adhesive dry epidermal electrodes can be used to accurately monitor epidermal biopotentials even during physical movement. For continuous health monitoring, they should adhere to skin in both dry and underwater conditions. But the dry electrodes reported in literature cannot keep good adhesion under water. Here, we report fully organic blends that exhibit good adhesion to skin in both dry and underwater conditions, high conductivity, and mechanical stretchability and their application as conformal electrodes to accurately detect epidermal biopotentials under all conditions. title: Cross-border ocean governance under legal plurality: evidence from the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area
abstract: Cross-border ocean governance in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area involves three distinct legal, judicial and administrative systems. This study examines how governance outputs produced in one jurisdiction become lawfully usable in another. Combining doctrinal legal analysis, qualitative institutional document analysis and public-record case analysis, the study develops an exploratory legal–institutional interface framework. title: What Sets the AMOC's Sensitivity to CO 2 Forcing? The Role of Background Mean‐State and Density Balance
abstract: Abstract The future evolution of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) under anthropogenic forcing remains highly uncertain, partly because the role of the background ocean state in conditioning AMOC sensitivity is not fully understood. Using CMIP6 simulations under abrupt‐4 × CO 2 and SSP‐585 forcing, we investigate how mean‐state thermal and haline density compensation in the western subpolar North Atlantic influences AMOC decline. abstract: This study aims to analyze the disharmonization of social security arrangements and termination of employment for crew members in the Indonesian legal system and formulate an integrative legal harmonization model. The method used is normative legal research with a legislative, conceptual, and comparative approach to the legal regime of employment, shipping, and social security. title: Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
abstract: Shallow marine carbonates are recognized as key agents in deep carbon cycling. abstract: .– Eleutherodactylus juanariveroi (hereafter coquí llanero) is an endangered frog endemic to Puerto Rico. abstract: Climate change and anthropogenic pressures are increasing risks to coastal systems, feeding the need for adaptation strategies that are both effective and socially accepted. Nature-based solutions (NBS) are gaining prominence for reducing risks while strengthening ecosystem resilience, but their implementation depends heavily on stakeholder acceptance. The policy challenge is to connect joint invention with cooperation and sustained use in marine operations. abstract: Green-synthesized bioactive nanocomposites have emerged as promising multifunctional materials that combine sustainable fabrication with enhanced biological performance. This review critically examines recent advances in the green synthesis of bioactive nanocomposites and their antioxidant potential, with particular emphasis on applications relevant to adolescent health. title: Slip Detection for Robotic Grasping with LSTM and TCN: Edge AI Evaluation on Embedded Platforms
abstract: Abstract Reliable object grasping is essential for robotic manipulation in real-world environments, such as manufacturing and assembly. Undetected slips can lead to task failure, while effective slip detection enables robots to adapt their grip in real time, improving robustness and safety. In earlier work, we showed that Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks can be deployed on edge devices for real-time slip detection, but that study used a manually labelled dataset and reported only accuracy and F 1 scores, which limited comparisons of model–hardware combinations. title: Unveiling the subsurface: deep-penetrating geochemical methods and anomaly mechanisms in the Gobi Desert, China
abstract: The Gobi Desert of northwestern China represents a highly prospective yet critically under-explored metallogenic province, where thick, transported overburden and extreme aridity have rendered conventional geochemical surveys largely ineffective. Deep-penetrating geochemistry (DPG) has emerged as a suite of specialized surface methods designed to detect concealed mineralization beneath such exotic cover by targeting mobile forms of ore-forming elements that migrate from depth to the surface. title: Antimicrobial peptide–drug conjugates: rational design, pharmacological evaluation, and translational perspectives
abstract: Antimicrobial peptide–drug conjugates (APDCs) combine peptide and antibiotic functions within a single covalent construct. APDCs share design features with antibody–drug conjugates, but the field lacks an integrated account of how such conjugates should be designed and evaluated. This review examines that process from scaffold selection to translational precedent. abstract: This research analyzes the flood risk level of Yola North LGA, Adamawa State, Nigeria, by analyzing the Land Use Land Cover and Digital Elevation Model (DEM) of Yola North, identifying flood risk level, and areas vulnerable to flood risk level in the study area using geospatial techniques. abstract: Abstract Urban trees moderate city climates, yet how their leaf-area density relates to projected future climates is poorly constrained globally. We fitted a Random Forest model to monthly temperature and precipitation normals and the multi-year mean leaf area index (LAI) derived from a satellite-informed machine-learning urban tree product across 21,590 urban cells, then projected end-of-century change under six Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. title: Large language models for tech mining and technology opportunity analysis: A diffusion of innovation perspective on detecting evolutionary stages of innovative practices using ChatGPT
abstract: Technology opportunity analysis (TOA) traditionally examines technological developments to identify opportunities, but typically conceptualizes these opportunities at the level of technologies or fields. This study advances practice-level TOA by conceptualizing technology-enabled innovative practices as technology-process-industry configurations and using their evolution to identify technology opportunities. abstract: Machine-learning models for engine fault detection are usually judged by predictive accuracy, although a model can score well while learning relationships that contradict engine physics. This study proposes a physical-consistency audit that combines domain-informed monotonic constraints in XGBoost with the glass-box Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM). abstract: In this paper, we construct a dataset consisting of paired diffuser-plate images and thickness-distribution images, and evaluate the computational cost and prediction accuracy of an image-to-image translation surrogate model that directly pre-dicts thickness-distribution images from diffuser-plate drawings. title: Bridging the integrity gap: Strategies for fostering intellectual property awareness and research ethics in rural higher education institutions
abstract: Rural higher education institutions (HEIs) in India are expected to meet the same standards of research integrity and intellectual property (IP) governance as metropolitan universities, yet they often have fewer specialist services, less training and thinner support systems. This paper develops an evidence-informed framework for strengthening IP awareness and research ethics in such institutions. abstract: This study presents an experimental assessment of a compression-ignition internal combustion engine (CI-ICE) operating in dual-fuel mode with diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), without fuel preheating or combustion enhancers. The objective is to evaluate the effect of LPG substitution on engine performance, emissions, and operational fuel costs under electric power generation conditions. To address the limitations of the original Artificial Rabbits Optimization (ARO) algorithm—such as insufficient population diversity, loss of high-quality historical solutions, inadequate local search accuracy, and susceptibility to premature convergence—this paper proposes a Memory-enhanced Artificial Rabbits Optimization (MARO) algorithm. title: Pengaruh Pemahaman AI Dan Inovasi Digital Serta Literasi Pasar Modal Terhadap Niat Berwirausaha Digital Dengan Efikasi Diri Sebagai Variabel Mediasi
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital capital markets creates new business opportunities, yet little is known about how students' understanding of both domains shapes their digital entrepreneurial intention. This study examines the effect of understanding of AI and digital innovation and of capital market literacy on digital entrepreneurial intention, with self-efficacy as a mediating variable. A quantitative survey of 153 students attending a public lecture was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap

title: MFDNet: A Lightweight Mobile Mamba-based Detector for Real-Time Aviation Casting Defect Detection
abstract: Abstract Detecting defects in aviation castings is critical for ensuring the structural reliability and manufacturing safety of aircrafts. However, traditional manual inspection is time-consuming and prone to human error, whereas existing deep learning-based methods struggle to accurately detect subtle defects, such as microcracks and fine scratches, under resource-constrained industrial conditions. title: Sustainable soil practices for improving soil health, greenhouse gas mitigation and climate resilience of rice cropping systems
abstract: Climate change is threatening rice yields more and more, which undermines global food security. Traditional agricultural practices further endanger the ecosystem by causing carbon emissions, soil degradation and wasteful water usage. Despite some progress in this area, local adaptation, soil quality improvement and mitigation remain insufficient. This review emphasises the importance of sustainable soil management in enhancing the climate resilience of ecosystems. title: A multi-step and multivariate financial time series forecasting framework based on ConvLSTM optimized by Island Algorithm
abstract: Multi-scale and multi-indicator financial time series forecasting is a valuable requirement of quantitative analysis and intelligent decision-making. Nevertheless, the current research concentrates on single-step or univariate prediction, which is unable to completely meet the real-life needs of multi-step and multivariate prediction problems in complex financial time-series situations. title: The next frontier of peptide therapeutics: from targeted conjugates (PDC/ODC) to AI-driven safety-by-design
abstract: The pharmaceutical landscape is witnessing a profound “Peptide Renaissance,” driven primarily by the clinical success of GLP-1 receptor agonists and reinforced by engineering advanced drug delivery platforms. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of current trends in peptide-based drug development, using a target-localization framework that distinguishes molecular recognition from pharmacological action. title: The impact of green funds on the carbon emission intensity of listed companies
abstract: Background As the global climate change crisis intensifies, advancing the low-carbon transition has become a core strategy for sustainable development. Green finance is increasingly a key driver of corporate pollution reduction and carbon mitigation, yet how equity-based green funds shape corporate carbon emission intensity remains underexplored. Objective This paper investigates the impact of green fund shareholdings on the carbon emission intensity of listed companies, and examines the underlying mechanisms, heterogeneity and boundary conditions. abstract: This review examines more than 150 recent metaheuristics introduced between 2019 and 2026, emphasizing their significant impact and performance in solving complex optimization problems. In the past three decades, more than 500 metaheuristic algorithms have been proposed, with no sign of deceleration, resulting in a vast and growing landscape that makes it increasingly difficult to select, compare, and evaluate the most suitable methods for specific challenges. title: SAM 3-guided mask tracking with complementary two-stream refinement for vision-based vehicle speed prediction in highway traffic scenes
abstract: Accurate vehicle speed estimation is essential for Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) and autonomous driving applications. However, conventional vision-based methods commonly rely on bounding-box-based tracking, which is sensitive to environmental interference, object-boundary instability, and trajectory discontinuity. title: Quantile Regression for Power Grid Damage Prediction
abstract: This article addresses the challenge of predicting electrical grid damage in the Latvian regions of Zemgale and Kurzeme using machine learning and quantile regression techniques. The study leverages a comprehensive dataset spanning 2009–2025, incorporating environmental, infrastructure, seasonal, and weather-related features. abstract: While Enterprise sales systems have dashboards to track revenue, customers, and buying trends, reports often require reading between the lines to determine what's good and what's bad before deciding which accounts to focus on. In this research, an explainable Sales Intelligence framework is proposed that transforms transaction-level information into analytical evidence at the customer level and converts it into conversations to support decision-making. abstract: Trait evolution and lineage diversification are thought to be driven by selection on the phenotypes of individuals. However, many important phenotypes are only manifested when individuals interact. Collective behavior is one such phenotype. During collective behavior, interactions among individuals lead to emergent group-level phenotypes that can govern individual fitness. abstract: BACKGROUND: Keloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. title: Engineering resilient environmental microbiomes: from multi-omics early-warning signals to predictive control and functional recovery
abstract: Microbial consortia are used in environmental bioprocesses, particularly wastewater treatment and anaerobic digestion. High performance under controlled conditions does not ensure stability or functional recovery after disturbance or scale-up. This review examines disturbance, destabilization, detection, prediction, intervention, and functional recovery in engineered microbiomes. abstract: Bangladesh has completed most REDD+ readiness requirements and drafted a Carbon Market Framework, but lacks an evidence-based pathway for turning forest and coastal ecosystems into high-integrity carbon projects. Using secondary data from national policy instruments, the Forest Reference Level (FRL), the third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), crediting standards and published literature, this study synthesised a 23-step project development pathway and modelled mitigation potential and economic value under three scenarios. abstract: Introduction Orthopedic implant-associated infections are difficult to treat due to bacterial persistence in biofilms on implant surfaces and in surrounding tissues. Bioactive glass S53P4 (BAG) is a clinically used bone graft substitute with antibacterial properties resulting from surface reactivity and dissolution-mediated changes in the local microenvironment; however, its antibacterial efficacy against established infections with a high bacterial burden is limited. abstract: Green synthesis of nanoparticles has emerged as an environmentally sustainable and economically viable alternative to conventional physical and chemical synthesis methods. This approach utilizes biological resources, including plant extracts, bacteria, fungi, algae, and other naturally derived biomolecules, as reducing, stabilizing, and capping agents for nanoparticle fabrication. abstract: Abstract Global Red List assessments suggest that approximately 25% of freshwater animal species are at risk of extinction. However, these estimates remain tentative due to insufficient assessments of numerous species-rich invertebrate groups in neglected ecosystems, such as springs and subterranean waters. abstract: Robots need to be able to understand their surroundings in order to operate safely and robustly, and to interact with the surrounding environment. Robots deployed in unconstrained real-world scenarios must additionally be able to deal with novel situations and objects that have never been seen before. abstract: Introduction Where Late Quaternary extinctions were severe, archaeological, climatic, and extinction signals are compressed into short intervals, which makes their causes difficult to infer. abstract: Coastal deltaic road networks in India experience compounding hazards of monsoon flooding, prolonged soil-moisture saturation, and heat stress. However, many graph-learning approaches to network vulnerability assessment validate with random train–test splits that do not account for spatial dependence between adjacent road segments leading to insufficient quantification of failure probability without any spatially calibrated uncertainty. abstract: Magma-rich continental rifts comprise en-echelon magmatic segments where magmatism and extension are localised, similar to slow and ultra-slow spreading centres. abstract: Abstract Saline-alkaline soils severely constrain wheat production and have become a major threat to food security, especially in regions experiencing secondary salinization and climate change. As a glycophytic crop, wheat is highly sensitive to excessive salt and alkaline stresses, which disrupt ion balance, osmotic homeostasis, nutrient uptake, photosynthesis, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) metabolism, ultimately reducing plant growth, yield, and grain quality. abstract: Saudi Arabia’s extensive hydrocarbon transport infrastructure requires integrity decisions that simultaneously protect containment, sustain delivery reliability and allocate inspection expenditure efficiently. This critical review evaluates research published between 2020 and 2025 on corrosion prediction, in-line inspection, probabilistic failure assessment, risk-based inspection and lifecycle intervention planning. This study proposes a local structural enhancement-based precipitation data fusion (LSE-PDF) framework. abstract: Abstract Microbial communities are essential components of aquatic ecosystems, yet a stark contrast persists between the vast diversity revealed by environmental sequencing and the limited taxa recoverable by culturing. This disparity has contributed to a shift toward sequencing due to its cost‐effectiveness and broad applicability to ecological questions. abstract: Abstract Single-modal terahertz nondestructive testing faces inherent bottlenecks in quantifying thin concealed air gaps inside layered composite materials widely used in aerospace and advanced manufacturing. abstract: Heavy rainfall and the resulting floods are prominent manifestations of climate variability in low-lying coastal urban areas, with significant implications for environmental quality and public health. This study assessed the environmental and health effects of heavy rainfall on residents of Eti-Osa Local Government Area (LGA), Lagos State, Nigeria. abstract: Abstract Snow water equivalent (SWE), which quantifies the amount of water in a snowpack, is critical for water supply forecasting. This study explores machine learning (ML) models' capability of representing the spatial distribution of SWE across the western United States. abstract: Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) is an important variable for irrigation scheduling, agricultural water management, and hydrological applications. This study examines a Physics–Regularized Autoencoder (PRAE): a neural network that compresses daily weather variables into a small set of learned features while being encouraged to keep air temperature, relative humidity, and dew point temperature consistent with one another. While conventional cellular cores offer favorable stiffness-to-weight ratios, their flexural load-bearing capacity and structural integrity are often constrained by geometric limitations and complex, costly manufacturing processes. abstract: Two specimens of a dory were recently collected from Taiwan, representing the first specimen-based record of the species in the region. abstract: Abstract Accurate characterization of land–atmosphere interactions over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) is hindered by fragmented measurements, inconsistent data-processing standards, and a scarcity of integrated, multi-component observations. abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence is increasingly used in engineering education, but self-reported literacy may not establish whether students can evaluate its outputs. The distinction between perceived competence and performance on engineering-specific AI scenarios remains insufficiently examined. abstract: Abstract Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is a crucial task in modern communication systems, enabling the identification of modulation schemes in received signals. abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) enters higher education within established hierarchies of knowledge and expertise, becoming entangled with judgments about who sounds authoritative and which forms of writing carry weight. abstract: Machine-learning models for electromagnetic and magnetotelluric (EM/MT) interpretation are commonly trained on synthetic or historical data and then applied to new surveys. Standard validation, however, does not establish whether a deployment survey is represented by the development domain. abstract: Small-for-gestational-age (SGA) neonates face health risks when undetected, yet machine learning (ML) models are difficult to apply across sites with heterogeneous feature availability. title: Enhancing neural automatic short answer grading with attention masking, WordNet-based semantic enrichment, and ordinal regression
abstract: Automatic Short Answer Grading (ASAG) is an important task in educational technology and natural language processing (NLP), enabling efficient and consistent evaluation of open-ended student responses. Although recent neural architectures have achieved strong performance, further improvements are possible in model focus, semantic understanding, and score consistency. This study builds upon the hybrid convolutional neural network–bidirectional long short-term memory (CNN-BiLSTM) Siamese model by Chen et al. (2023) and introduces three complementary extensions. title: AVISNet: An edge-computing model for acoustic identification of species from the Doñana bird community
abstract: The global decline in biodiversity calls for scalable and efficient species monitoring. Birds, as sensitive ecological indicators with rich vocal activity, are particularly well suited for passive acoustic monitoring (PAM), which enables extensive, non-invasive data collection. Yet the large volumes of audio generated by PAM require automated and efficient processing pipelines to extract meaningful biological information in real time. To address this challenge, we integrated automated acoustic species identification directly into embedded devices (i.e., at the edge), enabling autonomous on-sit

title: A physics-guided uncertainty calibration framework for reliable probabilistic rainfall forecasting under heavy and extreme rainfall conditions
abstract: Reliable rainfall forecasting requires not only accurate point predictions but also well-calibrated estimates of predictive uncertainty, particularly during heavy and extreme events where forecast errors carry the greatest operational consequence. Deterministic machine learning models provide point forecasts without quantifying uncertainty, while existing probabilistic methods generally derive uncertainty from statistical relationships in the available data without explicitly conditioning it on the physical state of the atmosphere. Integrated metabolomics, network pharmacology and molecular docking to characterize differences associated with geographical origin and subspecies on the antioxidant and α-glucosidase inhibition activity of sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.)
abstract: Introduction Sea buckthorn ( Hippophae rhamnoides L.) (SB) is a food-medicine homologous berry with well-recognized antioxidant and hypoglycemic potential. However, the influence of geographical origin and subspecies on its chemical composition and bioactivity remains incompletely understood. Methods In this study, untargeted metabolomics, network pharmacology, and molecular docking were integrated to characterize the metabolite profiles of SB berries harvested from Shanxi, Inner Mongolia, and Xinjiang, China, and to elucidate the mechanisms underlying their differential bioactivities. Enhancing Tourist Loyalty Through Service Quality and Digital Communication: The Mediating Role of Destination Image at Matahari Lobuk Beach
abstract: This study examines the direct and indirect effects of service quality and digital communication on tourist loyalty through the mediating role of destination image at Matahari Lobuk Beach, a village-managed (BUMDes) marine tourism destination in Sumenep Regency, Madura. A quantitative causal-explanatory design was applied using Partial Least Squares - Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Data from 154 tourists, selected through purposive sampling, were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed with SmartPLS 4 through one-tailed bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples. title: MF-EFLJD: Multi-faceted ensemble federated learning for jamming detection in private 5G-enabled IIoT networks
abstract: Wireless network security is a growing concern in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) as jamming attacks disrupt communication of IIoT entities in Private 5G networks. While machine learning (ML) algorithms detect jamming attacks effectively, centralized data collection from entities compromises sensitive information and privacy in distributed IIoT environment. This article presents a multi-faceted ensemble federated learning-based jamming detection framework, MF-EFLJD, to detect and further improve detection performance. title: Multi-Omics Mendelian Randomization Identifies DDX17 as a Potential Mediator Linking Gut Microbiota-Immune-Metabolism Axis to Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: Introduction: The gut microbiota-immune-metabolism axis has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis; however, the key host molecular targets linking peripheral dysregulation to central neurodegeneration remain elusive. Methods: In this study, we systematically integrated large-scale GWAS data covering 1,903 gut microbiota taxa, 14,696 immune cell features, and 34,843 metabolite features with AD GWAS summary statistics, using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to identify causal genes. These genes were intersected with differentially expressed genes from three GEO datasets
institutions: Affiliated Hospital of Youjiang Medical University for Nationalities

title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF HYBRID LSTM MODELS FOR MULTIVARIATE WATER QUALITY PREDICTION
abstract: Accurate multivariate water-quality forecasting is essential for environmental monitoring and early-warning systems. However, the comparative performance of different Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based architectures across water-quality parameters with different temporal characteristics remains insufficiently established. This study quantitatively compares five deep-learning architectures: standard LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), LSTM-GRU, CNN-LSTM, and Attention-based LSTM (AT-LSTM). The analysis uses 30,894 observations of seven water-quality parameters—chlorophyll, temperature, dissolv
journal: Jurnal Ilmiah Ilmu Terapan Universitas Jambi|JIITUJ|

title: A hierarchical ensemble learning framework for cyberthreat detection in IoT platforms
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) and Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices has dramatically escalated the risk of cyberattacks, necessitating robust and highly responsive Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). However, existing solutions frequently struggle with severe class imbalance and high-dimensional data, leading to a suboptimal trade-off between detection accuracy and computational efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel hierarchical machine learning-based IDS optimized for real-time multiclass attack detection. We construct a comprehensive un

title: Integrating tower-based camera observations with time-series Sentinel-1/2 images for parcel-level crop yield estimation over large areas
abstract: Accurate parcel-level rice yield estimation is important for agricultural management and disaster loss assessment. This study developed a framework integrating tower-based camera observations with time-series satellite remote sensing to extend yield estimation from locally observed fields to regional rice parcels in Hengyang City, China. RGB-derived features were used for tower-camera modeling, while Sentinel-1/2, meteorological, soil, and cropping-type variables supported regional modeling. Tower-derived yield information and available field records were linked to parcel polygons through appr
institutions: Changsha University of Science and Technology

title: Advancing Biomass Valorization via Electrocatalytic Oxidation: Design Principles, Emerging Challenges, and Future Perspectives
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic oxidation enables the sustainable conversion of biomass into high‐value chemicals and fuels. However, the field lacks a unified framework linking substrate molecular structures to catalyst design. Herein, biomass substrates are categorized by carbon chain length and structural complexity: C 2 –C 3 alcohols, C 5 –C 7 cyclic compounds, and C n biopolymers. title: Design Review and Long-Term Thermomechanical Behavior of GSHP Energy Piles
abstract: Ground source heat pump (GSHP) energy piles serve dual functions, simultaneously providing structural support and acting as ground-coupled heat exchangers through built-in pipe circuits. This study synthesizes evidence from field monitoring, laboratory experiments, and numerical simulations to examine the design methodologies and long-term thermomechanical behavior of such foundation systems. Design parameters, such as heat exchanger layout, pile material, and operational strategy, have considerable influence, yet the primary concern remains the pile response under repeated heating and cooling
journal: International Journal of Concrete Structures and Materials
institutions: North China University of Science and Technology

title: Learning-enhanced rolling-horizon optimisation for port-centric freight systems
abstract: This paper presents a centralised rolling-horizon framework for dynamic freight matching in port-centric supply chains. Rather than solving one large static assignment, the framework advances through the planning horizon in short steps, splitting the dynamic many-to-many problem over time into a sequence of small per-step assignments. Within each step, a Graph Neural Network makes the real-time match or wait decisions. The Hungarian algorithm then solves that step’s assignment optimally. title: Data-driven Space Object Re-entry Simulation and Model Calibration with Sparse Observations
abstract: Atmospheric re-entry simulation and prediction for uncontrolled spacecraft and debris is challenging because nonlinear coupled dynamics and uncertain environmental and physical conditions can produce non-Gaussian and weakly identifiable behavior, while post-event reconstruction is often based only on sparse outcome information. To address this problem, this paper develops a simulator-consistent amortized posterior inference framework for a compact spherical body re-entry benchmark using a conditional normalizing flow based on Real-valued Non-Volume Preserving (RealNVP) invertible transformatio
journal: Journal of Reliability Science and Engineering

title: China’s revised Maritime Code and vessel-source oil pollution liability: innovations, gaps, and reform pathways
abstract: Vessel-source oil pollution remains a central concern in marine environmental governance because oil spills may spread rapidly, persist in the marine environment, and cause serious ecological and socio-economic harm. China has traditionally regulated vessel-source oil pollution through rules dispersed across civil, environmental, maritime, insurance, and administrative law. The revised Maritime Code of the People’s Republic of China, adopted in 2025 and effective from 1 May 2026, introduces China’s first dedicated chapter on Liability for Oil Pollution Damage from Ships. title: Comparative analysis of ensemble and linear models for geophysical Delta-T compressional (DTC) well log imputation and reconstruction
abstract: Delta-T Compressional (DTC) well logs provide important sonic information for formation evaluation and subsurface characterization, but incomplete or unavailable sonic-log measurements can limit subsequent interpretation. This study evaluates six supervised machine-learning models Multiple Linear Regression, SGD Regressor, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Random Forest, and XGBoost for DTC log reconstruction using well-log data from the Taranaki Basin, New Zealand. The dataset was cleaned, depth-aligned, and divided into an 80% training set and a 20% internal test set.
institutions: University of Petroleum and Energy Studies

title: Computational aerodynamics for leading-edge inflatable kite design
abstract: Soft-wing kites are morphing, bridled, tensile lifting surfaces used for wind-assisted ship propulsion and airborne wind energy applications. Their swept-back planform, pronounced anhedral, and unconventional leading-edge geometry induce complex aerodynamic behaviour that challenges conventional modelling approaches. For leading-edge inflatable (LEI) kites, pressure-side separation induced by the inflated tubular leading edge renders classical inviscid methods insufficient, thereby necessitating sectional input from higher-fidelity approaches. title: Utilization of support vector-based techniques for prediction of compressive strength for graphene oxide based self- compacting concrete
abstract: In the present work, the machine learning methods were used to develop the predictive models for the Compressive Strength (CS) of the graphene oxide-enhanced self-compacting concrete. The models were built and analysed using a comprehensive database of 76 samples extracted from the literature. The model uses water content, ground granulated blast furnace slag, fly ash, fine aggregates, coarse aggregates, superplasticizer and cement quantity as input parameters and concrete CS as output. The predictive modelling methods used are linear regression, genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization,

title: End-to-End 1D-CNN Leakage Detection in Low-Density Oil-Flow Pipelines Using Raw Simulated Vibration Signals
abstract: Background: Leakage detection in low-density oil-flow pipelines remains challenging because leakage-induced vibrations can be masked by pump harmonics, flow-dependent vibrations, and background disturbances. This study investigates an end-to-end one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) that learns directly from raw vibration waveforms without handcrafted feature extraction. institutions: B.S. Abdur Rahman Crescent Institute of Science & Technology

title: Lignin‐Based Supramolecular Dynamic Networks: A General Platform for Energy Harvesting and Sensing
abstract: Lignin- based ionogels are promising sustainable materials for flexible electronics, yet their development is limited by a persistent tradeoff between mechanical robustness and dynamic multifunctionality. Here, we report a rigid flexible supramolecular design strategy that transforms lignin from a rigid bio-based component into an active network building block for dynamic ionogels. By coupling rigid lignin derived domains with flexible dynamic polymer segments, the resulting ionogel achieves efficient energy dissipation, reversible network reconstruction, and stable ionic transport. institutions: Institute of Chemical Industry of Forest Products

title: Development of a Maintenance Management Cost-Effectiveness Prediction Model for Ageing Bridge Infrastructure: A Case of TARURA, Tanga Region, Tanzania
abstract: Bridges managed by the Tanzania Rural and Urban Roads Agency (TARURA) in Tanga Region are maintained largely reactively. About 78% of the annual bridge maintenance budget of TZS 850 million is spent on emergency repairs that cost 2.5 to 4 times more than equivalent preventive work. Existing bridge prediction models mostly predict condition rather than cost, require long inspection histories or large datasets, and omit institutional factors such as budget adequacy. This study therefore developed a maintenance management cost-effectiveness prediction model for ageing bridges in Tanga Region. It
institutions: Dar es Salaam Institute of Technology

title: Forecasting Culex pipiens/restuans abundance in Ontario, Canada using surveillance and weather data
abstract: Reliable short-term forecasting of vector abundance is critical for guiding localized mosquito control, yet week-ahead prediction at the Public Health Unit (PHU) scale remains challenging. We developed and evaluated a week-ahead forecasting framework for Culex pipiens/restuans abundance using 22 years of routine surveillance and meteorological data from 34 PHUs across Ontario, Canada. title: Robust acoustic event classification for environmental monitoring through CLAP-based transfer learning
abstract: Environmental noise monitoring requires reliable tools for acoustic source attribution and automatic screening of complex sound environments. Sound event classification systems may operate as black-box decision modules, but their predictions must remain trustworthy in practical monitoring workflows. Contrastive Language–Audio Pretraining (CLAP) provides general-purpose audio representations with strong zero-shot capabilities, but its direct application to environmental monitoring may lead to unbalanced class-wise performance and limited reliability for rare or critical events. title: Equation of State for Warm Neutron Star Outer Crusts
abstract: Abstract We describe the equation of state (EoS) of a warm ion plasma as obtained by performing microscopic many-body simulations using molecular dynamics computational techniques. Using the cold one-component plasma (OCP) composition in the neutron star (NS) outer crust assumed in U. Murarka et al. with a representative heavy nucleus for each density, we refine previous calculations. title: Self-supervised temporal reconstruction of reanalysis fields at subhourly scales
abstract: Fast-evolving weather events develop on 5–15-min timescales and can influence human activities and planning. However, most atmospheric reanalyses provide data every 1–3 h, making rapid changes difficult to capture. Traditional machine-learning approaches require high-frequency supervision labels, which limits their use when such data are unavailable. Here we present a token-guided self-supervised framework that learns temporal relationships directly from coarse archives and reconstructs subhourly fields without subhourly labels. title: Biohydrogen 2.0: Emerging Innovations from Waste Valorisation to Intelligent Bioprocess Design
abstract: The growing requirement for sustainable energy, coupled with greenhouse gas emissions reduction, have resulted in increased research efforts towards the production of hydrogen via biohydrogen as an alternative to fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production methods, though environmentally friendly, have limitations in terms of hydrogen yield and other operational issues. The objective of this literature review is to introduce Biohydrogen 2.0 and discuss recent advancements which make biohydrogen production technologically feasible for its incorporation into future energy generation. Special focus will

title: ESTUDO DESCRITIVO DAS FERRAMENTAS PARA ANÁLISE GENÔMICA: CARACTERÍSTICAS, POTENCIALIDADES E DESAFIOS
abstract: The expansion of data generated by next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies has increased the importance of bioinformatics in genomic analysis. This study aimed to characterize bioinformatics tools according to their applications, functionalities, limitations, interfaces, and access conditions. A qualitative, exploratory, descriptive, systematized literature review was conducted in Scopus. The search identified 14,051 records; after applying the Brazil geographic filter and eligibility criteria, 212 studies were included, of which 34 described new tools. title: United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 2026: Tracking Performance and Progress Towards UN 2030 Agenda
abstract: Purpose: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UNSDGs), adopted under the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development in 2015, provide a universal framework comprising 17 Goals and 169 targets to promote sustainable development across economic, social and environmental dimensions. With only four years remaining until the 2030 deadline, the aim of this paper is to analyse and assess the global performance and progress according to the the UN SDGs Report 2026. title: Water footprint of large AI models: risks to global water security and sustainable optimization strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT Diagram linking AI model training and inference to lifecycle water use, estimated at 4.2–6.6 billion m³ annually by 2027, and showing water reuse, efficient cooling, smarter workloads, and standardized reporting as strategies to protect global water security. The rapid proliferation of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) models has introduced a significant yet underexamined environmental challenge: freshwater consumption. title: Finite-time robust motion control of intelligent vehicles based on neural approximation and disturbance estimation
abstract: This paper addresses the inherent trade off between rapid convergence and high‑precision disturbance rejection in intelligent vehicle motion control under severe nonlinearities, parametric uncertainties, and time varying external perturbations. A composite finite‑time robust control strategy is proposed by synergistically integrating a nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode (NFTSM) surface, radial basis function neural networks (RBFNN), and a finite time disturbance observer (FTDO). title: CORROSION-RESILIENT UNDERGROUND PIPELINE SYSTEMS IN SAUDI ARABIAN DESERT ENVIRONMENTS: ADVANCED MATERIAL SELECTION, PROTECTIVE DESIGN, AND RISK-BASED INTEGRITY MANAGEMENT
abstract: Underground pipelines in Saudi Arabia cross environments that appear uniformly arid but differ sharply in electrolyte availability, salt accumulation, groundwater exposure and electrical interference. This critical review evaluates how those contrasts affect corrosion initiation, protective design and long-term integrity decisions. Recent peer-reviewed evidence published between 2020 and 2025 is synthesised through four linked themes: ground aggressiveness, pipeline material behaviour, coating-cathodic protection compatibility and risk-based asset management. title: Will Europe be able to align and accelerate global cooperation in S&T to foster a new knowledge-based global order ?
abstract: Amid the fragmentation of multilateralism and the securitisation of science, Europe must decide whether international research cooperation can still be organised rather than left to drift. Drawing on securitisation theory and scholarship on research internationalisation, the paper asks whether securitisation ends international scientific collaboration or reallocates it, advancing three propositions: securitisation contracts collaboration in strategically sensitive fields (P1); collaboration persists or expands in politically legible, mission-defined domains (P2); and securitisation reallocates

title: Wildfire detection near transmission lines using geostationary meteorological satellite data
abstract: Wildfires pose a severe threat to both ecological systems and critical infrastructure, particularly power transmission lines traversing high-risk areas such as forests and grasslands. We focus on wildfire detection near transmission lines in Yunnan Province, China, using geostationary meteorological satellite data from Himawari-8 and Geo-Kompsat-2A (GK2A). A machine learning-based approach is proposed that integrates spectral, spatial, and temporal features to improve detection accuracy. title: Modeling Decadal Organosulfates in Particulate Matter to Improve Estimations of Aerosol Hygroscopicity in the United States
abstract: Organosulfates (OSs) can comprise a substantial fraction of secondary organic aerosol and exhibit significantly different hygroscopicity than inorganic sulfates, yet their spatiotemporal prevalence and climatic impacts remain poorly constrained because speciated measurements are sparse and common chemical transport models do not explicitly represent OS formation. This study develops a flexible and robust modeling framework to quantify isoprene-derived OS (iOS) concentrations and OS impacts on aerosol hygroscopicity (κ) across the contiguous United States (U.S.) for summers spanning 2013-2022.

title: Intelligent bioprinting of biomimetic hemostatic constructs: From bioink design and programmable fabrication to preclinical validation for non-compressible hemorrhage
abstract: Non-compressible hemorrhage (NCH) remains a leading cause of preventable trauma mortality because conventional gauze and oxidized cellulose act as passive barriers, whereas fibrin sealants depend on patient-derived fibrinogen; neither is reliable in coagulopathic patients. Recent convergence of bioink engineering, 3D/4D bioprinting, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted material design enables the fabrication of biomimetic hemostatic constructs with programmable composition, multiscale architecture, and dynamic responsiveness. title: The state at the tip of the arrow: archery in Ottoman society and bureaucracy between 1567 and 1574
abstract: This study analyzes the role of archery in Ottoman military and society between 1567 and 1574 through archival documents from the Mühimme Registers. It aims to demonstrate that archery was not an obsolete practice but a complex institution vital for imperial administration. The findings reveal a highly organized system for arrow production, a pragmatic policy of accepting cash substitutes (bedel) for military service, and the crucial role of archery in coastal defense, as evidenced by orders countermanding the disarming of guards.
