title: Comparing watershed-based spatial units and administrative boundaries for malaria prediction in the Peruvian Amazon
abstract: Malaria continues to pose a major public health threat in the Peruvian Amazon, where climate variability influences transmission patterns. This study assessed whether watershed-based spatial units (hydrobasins) outperform traditional administrative boundaries in predicting P. vivax and P. falciparum cases in Loreto, Peru. A retrospective ecological analysis was conducted using village-level geocoded malaria case data from 2009 to 2018, aggregated at the district level and three hydrobasin levels (levels 6, 7, and ANA). Environmental and meteorological variables were derived from satellite data
institutions: Instituto de Medicina Tropical Alexander von Humboldt

title: Cross-City Transfer Learning for Daily Rainfall Forecasting at Pune, India
abstract: Data-driven rainfall models normally need long local records, which many stations lack. This study asks whether a transformer pre-trained on data-rich coastal Mumbai can cut both the local data and the computation needed to forecast daily rainfall at Pune, a rain-shadow city 120 km inland. RainFormer, a transformer encoder-decoder, first trained on Pune’s full record, gave a reference test RMSE of 12.522 mm. title: Rhino Optimiser Algorithm: A Novel Bio-Inspired Algorithm
abstract: The Rhino Optimiser is a novel bio-inspired optimisation algorithm inspired by the adaptive movement behaviour of solitary rhinoceroses. Unlike conventional swarm-based metaheuristics, the proposed algorithm employs a single-agent adaptive behavioural framework designed to improve optimisation efficiency and reduce search stagnation and premature convergence in high-dimensional search spaces. institutions: Botswana International University of Science and Technology

title: The Influence of Changes in Land Use on the Concentration of Carbon Monoxide (CO) as an Indicator of Climate Change in Bugesera District
abstract: In this comprehensive study, researcher investigate the complex interplay between land use changes, vegetation health as measured by NDVI, and carbon monoxide (CO) concentration in the Bugesera District from 2019 to 2022 using Google Earth Engine. The introduction sets the context by highlighting the environmental significance of understanding this relationship in a region marked by rapid urbanization and shifting land use patterns. journal: Journal of Chemical Environmental and Biological Engineering

title: Salivary glands auto-segmentation in head and neck radiotherapy: imaging modalities, models, and clinical relevance
abstract: Radiotherapy-induced salivary gland injury is a major contributor to xerostomia and impaired quality of life in patients with head and neck cancer, making accurate organ-at-risk delineation clinically important. Deep learning-based auto-segmentation has the potential to improve contouring efficiency and consistency, but reported performance is heterogeneous and its clinical significance is not always clear. title: A Multifunctional Surface for Microplastic Trapping, SERS‐Based Molecular Sensing, and PFAS Breakdown Through Microdroplet Deposition
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs) and per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) co‐occur in natural and drinking waters, where they persist, accumulate, and pose risks to ecological and human health. Their mitigation demands integrated detection and remediation beyond single‐function platforms. Here, we report Ag@TiO 2 nanobrushes (NBs), fabricated entirely by ambient charged microdroplet deposition, as a unified substrate for MP capture, SERS‐based sensing, and photocatalytic PFAS degradation. title: Photo‐Activated Nano‐Compatibilized Two‐Phase Polymer Blends: Dynamics of Morphology‐Mechanics Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT Light‐activated polymers (LAPs) are shape‐shifting materials capable of transforming their shapes in response to photoinduced chemical reactions, such as cis‐trans isomerization and dimerization. Owing to these reactions, LAPs often exhibit behavior analogous to multicomponent, multiphase polymer blends, where phase separation and interfacial effects play a critical role in governing mechanical performance. title: An explainable and transferable framework for multimodal flame image restoration with physics-smoothed stochastic interpolant
abstract: Abstract To address the severe degradation of imaging quality in optical combustion diagnostics under extreme operational environments characterized by high background noise and strong aerodynamic turbulence, this paper proposes a physically explainable and general framework for multimodal flame image restoration featuring exceptional cross-domain transferability. Existing deep learning models for flame enhancement frequently suffer from a critical lack of physical interpretability and poor generalization when deployed across different experimental setups. title: A new inland centre for Dicranomyia (Erostrata) (Diptera, Limoniidae): first record of the subgenus in mainland China, with three species including one new species
abstract: The subgenus Dicranomyia (Erostrata) Savchenko, 1976 is recorded from mainland China for the first time with the documentation of three species. One species new to science, D. (E.) serrata sp. nov ., and two species newly recorded from China, D. (E.) globulithorax Alexander, 1924 and D. (E.) koreana Kim & Bae, 2023, are reported. title: TPU Accelerated Multi-Resolution and Occupancy based Performance Analysis of Embedded Real-Time Traffic Sign Detection on Raspberry Pi 5
abstract: Embedded traffic-sign detection must balance accuracy against the compute, memory and power limits of the target platform. This study evaluates YOLOv8n on TT100K at six independently trained input resolutions (640×640, 512×512, 480×480, 320×320, 224×224 and 160×160) and on three platform configurations: an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 laptop GPU, a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU and a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Google Coral USB Edge TPU. title: Seaweed Traceability of Geographic Origin and Detection of Species-Mislabeling: Trends, Methods, Challenges, and Implications for the EU Industry
abstract: Diverse seaweed species constitute sustainable marine bioresources with widespread applications. Seaweed production can contribute significantly to achieving United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those related to food security and sustainability. While demand for seaweed-based products continues to increase in the European Union (EU), production capacity remains limited. title: Predicting early EGFR-TKI treatment response in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma from H&E histopathology with weakly supervised multiple-instance learning
abstract: Abstract Background This study sought to construct a deep-learning pipeline using an attention mechanism and multiple-instance learning (MIL) to predict early treatment response to epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) directly from routinely available hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) of pretreatment tissue in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). title: Study on the Polishing Mechanism of SiC Textured Surfaces Under Water‐Lubricated Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon carbide (SiC) is indispensable for high‐temperature and semiconductor applications, but its extreme hardness and chemical inertness impede precision polishing. Surface texturing has become an effective strategy for reducing friction and wear, which is widely used in high‐temperature kiln furniture and wear‐resistant sealing rings. This study investigates the polishing process of diamond grits on SiC textures in a water‐lubricated environment via molecular dynamics simulations. journal: Journal of the American Ceramic Society

title: Securing Africa’s digital backbone: Subsea cable vulnerability and the case for an African critical infrastructure protection regime
abstract: Africa's participation in the digital economy rests on a small number of subsea cables whose ownership, routing, repair and protection largely escape African control. Three disruption episodes in 2024 – in the Red Sea, off Côte d'Ivoire and off KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa – exposed the continent’s vulnerability to chokepoints, foreign-owned infrastructure and scarce repair capacity, a pattern confirmed again in September 2025. title: Cross-vector flexibility in sector-coupled low-carbon energy systems
abstract: This paper holistically assesses the current literature by examining how cross-vector flexibility is observed, coordinated, and verified in low-carbon energy systems based on sector coupling. To this end, the interplay between cross-vector flexibility, digital twins and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled observability, predictive control approaches, local coordination mechanisms, and flexibility markets is addressed within a common analytical framework. title: An AI ‐driven soil extractor for high‐throughput measurement of soil microarthropod taxon densities using live individuals
abstract: Abstract Soil invertebrates play a key role in ecosystem functioning, yet their monitoring remains constrained by labour‐intensive extraction and taxonomic identification procedures. Consequently, large‐scale and high‐frequency assessments of soil biodiversity remain difficult despite increasing demand for standardized monitoring tools. abstract: Tulu is a Dravidian language of coastal Karnataka and northern Kerala. It is normally written in Kannada script, and very little of it exists as digital text. Here, a data-driven screening workflow is proposed to identify lunar-based oxides (Si-Al-Mg-Ca-Fe-Ti-Na-O) that can retain solar-wind-implanted H and promote H 2 O production. Machine-learning (ML) models trained on spin-polarized electronic-structure metrics, local geometries, and magnetic moments predict reaction energies for H insertion (HIR) and H 2 O formation (WFR) with high accuracy. title: Vision-Based Self-Mapping for Autonomous Indoor Drones
abstract: Objectives: Without GPS signals the problem of self-autonomous navigation of indoor drones is greatly complicated and consequently there has been a recent surge of interest in Visual SLAM. Such systems enable the localization of a drone in an environment and the building of a map of it using only camera data. However indoor environments generally pose severe problems for these systems such as low illumination, motion blur due to rapid motion and featureless surfaces that do not offer the reliable features required for tracking. title: Segmentasi Pelanggan Berbasis Rfm dan K-Means pada Sistem Analitik Penjualan
abstract: The growth of daily transaction data volumes in the retail sector often ends up as passive digital archives due to resource limitations in manual analysis. This condition makes it difficult for management to map consumer loyalty objectively, causing marketing strategies to miss the target. This study aims to design a web-based analytical information system using Python to automate customer segmentation. abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Curcuma longa L. (turmeric) is an important medicinal and culinary plant and a major source of curcuminoids and volatile oils with diverse pharmacological activities. title: Monetary policy and the green paradox
abstract: We exploit three distinct monetary policy tools, monetary tightening shocks, central bank announcements and a machine-learning measure of climate-specific forward guidance to assess how they shape corporate climate risk exposure. Monetary tightening increases firms’ climate risk exposure, with the effect being more pronounced among high-emission firms. The effect is stronger in Europe than in the United States. title: IMU-Guided Adaptive Video Stabilization for Unmanned Surface Vehicles
abstract: This study addresses the critical challenge of video stabilization in Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) operating under high-wave and harsh maritime conditions. Conventional stabilization methods often struggle to distinguish erratic vessel motions caused by waves from intentional camera maneuvers, leading to significant image distortion, horizon tilt, and loss of visual data. title: Comparative assessment of pumped hydro and battery storage in a hybrid renewable energy system with excess-energy-driven desalination
abstract: Off grid renewable systems on remote coasts lean on storage to bridge long spells of weak solar and wind, yet mechanical and electrochemical storage are rarely tested side by side under the same conditions. This work assesses seawater pumped hydro storage (PHS) and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries inside a standalone system for Rangabali, Bangladesh, and routes surplus renewable energy that would otherwise be dumped into a reverse osmosis plant treated as a priority-dispatched, shiftable load. abstract: In recent years, cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) has gained considerable attention as an emerging non-thermal food processing method, but its interaction with food proteins remains poorly understood. title: Status and perspective on mechanical and protective properties of PVD MeSiN nitride nanocomposite coatings
abstract: MeSiN nanocomposite coatings have attracted growing interest due to their exceptional combination of high hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance. However, existing studies still lack a comprehensive analysis of their microstructural characteristics, performance metrics, and optimization strategies. This review critically examines recent advances in the fabrication techniques, structure–property relationships, and potential optimization strategies of MeSiN coatings. title: Soroll-IA: a weakly labeled audio dataset for real-world industrial port monitoring
abstract: Soroll-IA is a weakly labeled environmental audio dataset recorded in a real-world industrial port environment in Valencia (Spain) using two fixed sensing nodes. The dataset comprises approximately 22 h of audio segmented into 7396 clips and covers 26 sound event classes representative of industrial port acoustic activity commonly observed in such environments, such as crane sirens, train movements, traffic, and other logistical and industrial sounds. title: Lithium extraction from ore and waste streams with molten salts – A review
abstract: The growing demand for electric vehicles has intensified the need for Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries, yet Li remains a limited resource, sourced from mineral ores and seawater brines. Conventional acid- and alkali-based extraction methods rely on elevated temperatures and harmful chemicals, raising environmental and economic concerns. Molten salt technology has emerged as a promising alternative due to its high thermal stability, conductivity, and resistance to extreme processing conditions. title: Scaling inference with remote-sensing foundation models on large datacubes
abstract: High-resolution satellite constellations have grown Earth Observation (EO) archives to petabyte scale. While remote-sensing foundation models offer powerful capabilities for analysing this data, scaling inference across a variety of models to inputs far larger than memory, particularly on modest hardware, remains a challenge. abstract: Accurate simulation of microwave oxygen absorption is critical for upper atmospheric remote sensing, yet traditional models suffer from biases due to simplified Zeeman splitting calculations. This study presents the channel parameters of a hyperspectral microwave sounder for near space temperature profiling, built upon the updated microwave Line-by-Line (LBL) model with Larsson et al. title: AnnelidaDB: a comprehensive platform of taxonomic and multi-omic resources across annelids
abstract: Annelids inhabit marine, freshwater, and terrestrial ecosystems and are important models for studying animal evolution, regeneration, and host-microbe interactions, yet their rapidly growing omics resources remain dispersed across repositories and publications. We developed AnnelidaDB (www.annelidadb.com), a species-centred database built on an updated phylogenetic framework that integrates genomes, mitochondrial genomes, transcriptomes, proteomes, epigenomes, single-cell datasets, host-associated symbiont genomes, and comparative synteny for Annelida. title: Urban Water Use in the CONUS: Evolution From Deterministic to Chaotic Dynamics
abstract: Abstract Historical records show that urban water use in the Contiguous United States has evolved from early steady levels (pre‐1960s), to rapid growth (1970s–1980s), and to a recent phase marked by gradual decline, but along with significant inter‐annual variability (post‐1980s). Past studies have relied on statistical or machine learning models to link water use with climatic drivers such as precipitation, temperature, and humidity; and socioeconomic drivers such as population, income, and employment. title: A novel satellite embedding-driven SWOT framework for river discharge estimation: a case study of the Yangtze river
abstract: Accurate river discharge estimation is essential for water cycle modeling, water hazards prevention, water ecosystem protection and water resource management. However, conventional ground-based gauging networks are often sparsely distributed and insufficient to capture the complex hydrodynamic characteristics within large and heterogeneous river basins. With the rapid advancement of remote sensing technologies, particularly the launch of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission, new opportunities have emerged for large-scale and continuous river discharge estimation. title: Stage equilibrium and spatial differentiation: Characteristics of meteorological disaster emergency management policies in China
abstract: With intensifying global climate change and frequent extreme weather events posing severe challenges to emergency management systems, the quality of policy design directly affects operating efficiency. This study establishes a scientific, quantitative policy evaluation system for meteorological disaster emergency management to provide evidence for enhancing emergency management capabilities. title: The Broad Ecological Range of Salmonella enterica Serotype Typhimurium Is Associated With Genomic Diversification
abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium is a versatile foodborne pathogen with a broad ecological range, making it an ideal model to better understand pathogen adaptations that allow them to infect multiple hosts and persist across environments. Here, we analysed 595 genomes of S. Typhimurium representing three food animal sources (bovine, swine, and poultry) and one non-food animal source (wild birds). We found that S. title: Adaptive confidence-aware deep authentication framework for secure industrial Internet of Things
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) deployments authenticate an increasing volume of heterogeneous device traffic under adversarial conditions, and single-stage classifiers—whether shallow or deep—tend to commit to a label at every operating point, including the ambiguous region where the decision boundary is least reliable. This behaviour inflates both the False Acceptance Rate (FAR) and the False Rejection Rate (FRR) precisely where an authentication system can least afford it. title: Advancing sustainable financing through pandemic bond: a Bayesian model averaging approach to liquidity premia
abstract: Pandemic bonds, as a subtype of catastrophe (CAT) bonds, are designed to transfer public health risks to capital markets, yet they face substantial liquidity risk due to their nascent market structure and limited risk design. Using a relatively small sample from 2020 to 2024, we apply Bayesian model averaging (BMA) and interpretable machine learning (IML) to examine the associations of macroeconomic and bond-specific characteristics with liquidity premia across market phases. title: Seafood processing: a vital yet overlooked aspect of seafood systems
abstract: We argue in this paper that we cannot understand or change seafood systems if we do not look specifically at the history of industrial seafood processing in the U.S. Seafood is a vital part of human food systems that are imbricated with economic, social, and ecological processes, all of which have consequences for individual and collective culture, nutrition and health. Fisheries render seafood into food by capturing/harvesting, processing, and transporting it for human consumption, all within the context of policy and regulatory regimes and market imperatives. title: A Bagging-Initialised Residual Gradient-Boosting Framework for Predicting Malaria Infection Among Children Under Five Years in Kenya
abstract: Background: Malaria remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality among children younger than five years in Kenya. Although machine-learning models can capture complex relationships in population-based data, bias–variance trade-offs and limited geographical transportability may constrain their performance. This study developed and evaluated a bagging-initialised residual gradient-boosting (BIRGB) framework to predict microscopy-confirmed malaria infection in children under five years in Kenya. abstract: Abstract Climate change and rapid urbanization are intensifying flood risks, making unequal gray‐green infrastructure (GGI) provision a growing concern for extreme rainfall‐flood resilience (ERFR). However, how GGI inequality corresponds with ERFR differences between mainstream and tributary cities remains insufficiently understood. Using the 2025 Typhoon Wutip period as a fixed regional extreme‐event observation window, this study quantified GGI inequality and examined basin‐scale ERFR differentiation in southern China's Pearl River Basin (PRB). title: An adaptive bio-inspired secure routing framework with ECC encryption and intrusion detection for MANET communication
abstract: This research addresses a critical gap in MANET security, where secure routing, trust management, energy efficiency, and IDS are often treated separately, leading to suboptimal performance under dynamic and adversarial conditions. Conventional cryptographic methods introduce high computational overhead, while trust- and learning-based approaches often overlook end-to-end security, adaptive routing, and receiver-side intrusion validation. Integrating Information From Hydrologic Models and SWOT Remote Sensing Measurements to Estimate Discharge Across River Networks
abstract: Abstract The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite has the potential to improve knowledge of river discharge globally. However, SWOT discharge algorithms are informed by global hydrological model data, and a portion of the model's systematic bias is passed along to the SWOT discharge time series. To address this issue, we present a new algorithm designed to reduce systematic bias in SWOT discharge. title: Molecular surveillance of drug resistance markers in Plasmodium falciparum isolates from Ghana
abstract: The emergence and spread of Plasmodium falciparum drug-resistant parasites remain a significant hurdle to malaria control and elimination. However, how changes in transmission affect the evolution of drug resistance remains incompletely understood. We investigated the spatiotemporal prevalence of drug resistance across three distinct eco-epidemiological zones of Ghana (Guinea Savannah, Forest and Coastal) by characterizing genetic polymorphisms in five drug resistance genes ( pfdhfr, pfdhps, pfmdr1, pfk13 and pfmdr2 ). title: Using shear‐wave resonances induced by earthquakes for cost‐effective CO 2 ‐monitoring
abstract: Abstract We show how CO 2 ‐storage sites could be monitored using fibre‐optic cables as sensors and local earthquakes as natural sources. The method uses shear‐wave resonances, which are observable in sedimentary layers with strong shear‐wave velocity contrasts often occurring for shallow sand layers embedded in shale. title: TurboMeter: an attribution framework for aviation turbulence events in a changing climate
abstract: Understanding the influence of climate change on aviation turbulence is critical for ensuring flight safety and developing adaptive strategies. Thus, we present TurboMeter, a circulation-conditioned attribution framework that combines objectively observed aircraft turbulence reports with atmospheric analogues to quantify how turbulence-favourable environments evolve under comparable large-scale synoptic circulation conditions. abstract: Brackish groundwater is a strategic supply buffer for arid states reliant on energy-intensive seawater desalination, yet the operational condition of legacy well fields and the distribution-side limits on dispatchable volume remain understudied. Both are addressed here for Kuwait, where desalination supplies ∼ 92% of municipal water. title: Characterizing growth patterns of bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) in Sarasota Bay
abstract: Growth patterns of specific body structures provide insight into the physiological and developmental processes underlying their function; however, collecting morphological data on these body structures is challenging for large animals in the marine environment due to the logistics of collecting hands-on measurements and the limitations of data provided by other methods (e.g., photogrammetry). abstract: This study examines the pirate and maritime cultural heritage of Alonnisos, Lesvos, and Kos, three islands that, despite their geographical distance, share a long-standing historical relationship with the sea and the risks associated with maritime activity. It explores how pirate raids, privateering, and maritime rivalries influenced the organization of settlements, the construction of fortifications, economic activity, and the collective memory of local communities. title: Assessing Carbon Storage Potential in the Mediterranean Forests: A Review of Morocco’s Ecosystems
abstract: Climate change poses a major global challenge, and forests are increasingly recognized for their role in carbon sequestration. This review employs a dual analytical framework, integrating a systematic bibliometric analysis with a structured thematic synthesis, to assess the carbon storage potential of Morocco’s forest ecosystems across both biomass and soil organic carbon pools. abstract: The high Andean basins of Peru and Ecuador supply freshwater to approximately 60% and 70% of their respective national populations. However, these systems are increasingly threatened by glacier retreat, land-use transformation, and climate variability, which jeopardize long-term water security. abstract: Abstract High-risk AI systems distributed as software or embedded in connected hardware are simultaneously subject to two horizontal security rulebooks: the accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirements of Art. 15 of the AI Act and the essential cybersecurity requirements of the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). title: The silent storm: How climate, food commodity prices, and political stability fuel Somalia’s inflation crisis
abstract: In fragile economies, inflation is a critical macroeconomic issue for household well-being in vulnerable nations. As prices increase, at-risk families are forced to diminish essential consumption, remove children from formal education, and forsake long-term developmental goals to satisfy immediate survival requirements. In this regard, this study examines the impact of climate change, food commodity prices, and political stability on inflation in Somalia. title: Implementation Gap in Global Power Capacity Expansion to meet Paris Agreement Climate Targets
abstract: Abstract Meeting the Paris Agreement’s climate targets demands an unprecedented expansion of renewable energy. Despite global commitments, significant implementation gaps persist due to economic, policy, and technical uncertainties. Here, we develop a Global Power Capacity Dynamics Framework, integrating facility-level data, machine learning and transition modeling to assess the feasibility of global power expansion. title: The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria
abstract: Metabolic traits mediate microbial interactions and underpin mechanistic models of community assembly. With the rapid expansion of genomic data and bioinformatic tools, it is widely assumed that metabolic traits such as substrate utilization can be reliably inferred from genomes alone. Here, we systematically evaluate this assumption by comparing genome-based predictions from four commonly used tools to high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria. abstract: Shipboard operational decision making requires seafarers to interpret numerical information, identify operational risks, apply procedures, use onboard technology, and coordinate actions under changing conditions. This study evaluated predictive mathematical models of shipboard operational decision-making performance using scenario-based assessment. abstract: Introduction Groundwater is the primary dependable freshwater source in the arid coastal catchments of western Saudi Arabia, where natural recharge is limited and occurs mainly through episodic rainfall and flash‐flood infiltration along wadi systems. This study assesses groundwater potential in the Wadi Marwani basin (≈2,347 km 2 ), a major tributary of the Khulais system southeast of Rabigh, by integrating multi‐source remote sensing, GIS, and aeromagnetic data. title: Initial failure morphology of shallow loess containing millimeter-scale cracks: Insights from CT 3d imaging
abstract: Frequent shallow loess slope failures in loess regions pose significant threats to both linear infrastructure and local communities. Millimeter-scale initial cracks induced by water, temperature, and weathering are key factors controlling such loess failures. abstract: Rapid land subsidence is commonly experienced along the northern coast of Java, Indonesia, and this geological natural hazard tends to severely threaten infrastructure, including environmental degradation. title: The architecture and behavioral phenotype of microbial cells housed in citadel-like biofilms
abstract: Understanding how biofilms came to be recognized as spatially organized, three-dimensional (3D) communities (rather than isolated planktonic cells) requires tracing the conceptual shift that redefined bacterial life as architecturally structured. Biofilms, defined as surface-attached communities of microbial cells, represent the dominant mode of life for microorganisms, creating favorable microenvironments for their constituent cells that promote antimicrobial tolerance and persistence, ultimately contributing to the emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). title: Tropospheric Circulations Modulating the Arctic Stratospheric Polar Vortex in Winter
abstract: Here we present an observational study of the variations in the stratospheric polar vortex (SPV) associated with the main tropospheric circulation patterns in the Northern Hemisphere in winter (November to March). The circulation patterns are based on the empirical orthogonal function analysis of daily geopotential height anomalies at 500 hPa. We focus our analysis of the SPV at 100 hPa and 10 hPa. abstract: Structure from Motion photogrammetry has become an increasingly relevant method for digital data acquisition in construction and civil engineering. By using overlapping images, three - dimensional point clouds, digital terrain models, meshes and visual documentation can be generated without the need for expensive scanning equipment. abstract: Understanding the geochemical behavior of dissolved rare earth elements (REEs) in large tropical rivers is critical for tracing global silicate weathering and anthropogenic fluxes to the oceans. This study investigates REE dynamics in two major river systems, the Godavari and the Mahanadi, which drain contrasting lithologies (Deccan basalt vs. heterogeneous metamorphic terrains) and discharge into the Bay of Bengal. title: Ophelia yangi sp. nov. (Annelida, Opheliidae), a new species from Chinese waters, with comments on the taxonomic characters of the genus
abstract: Ophelia limacina (Rathke, 1843), originally described from Norway, is the only species of Ophelia Savigny, 1822 recorded from Chinese waters, but these records have never been verified. abstract: ABSTRACT Vegetation restoration is widely promoted to enhance ecosystem services in water‐limited regions, yet its hydrological consequences remain uncertain, particularly in large semi‐arid river basins. abstract: Abstract Predictive conservation for tropical built heritage is hindered by the persistent separation of continuous environmental sensing from computational deterioration diagnostics. abstract: Two competing models have been proposed for the formation of rare-metal brines in the southern Siberian Platform. abstract: Background Drawing on conservation of resources (COR) theory, this study examines the associations of job continuance insecurity (JCI) and job conditions insecurity (JCO) with proactive work behavior (PWB) and employee innovative behavior (EIB), including age and education profiles. title: A UAV-LiDAR based paradigm for rapid forest-vegetation health screening using canopy structural indicators
abstract: Forest health assessment is essential for ecosystem conservation and climate-change adaptation, yet existing approaches often rely on labor-intensive field surveys or complex multi-source remote-sensing workflows. This study developed a rapid structural screening framework for forest health based on unmanned aerial vehicle light detection and ranging (UAV-LiDAR). abstract: Abstract Land surface hydrological processes influence climate predictability through soil moisture persistence and coupling efficiency, the capacity of surface flux anomalies to generate spatially coherent atmospheric forcing at large scales. We examine coupling efficiency using century‐long free‐running simulations of a fully coupled Earth system model, comparing two configurations that differ only in land surface parameterizations. abstract: Climate change is altering precipitation across the full spectrum of intensity categories, with potentially profound consequences for the spatial distribution of seasonal rainfall and for regional drought–flood patterns. However, conventional metrics of extreme precipitation focus on its frequency, intensity, or total amount, leaving a critical question unanswered: how does the changing contribution of high-intensity events shape the spatial structure of seasonal precipitation? title: Identifying Snow-Covered Areas from Unoccupied Aerial Systems (UAS) Visible Imagery and Lidar: A Comparison of Methods
abstract: High-resolution imagery from Unoccupied aerial systems (UAS) offers new opportunities for mapping snow cover at fine spatial scales, particularly in regions with ephemeral and variable snow conditions. This study evaluates a range of classification strategies for generating snow-covered area (SCA) maps from UAS RGB imagery and lidar-derived snow depth collected over open areas in southern New Hampshire, USA and offers practical recommendations for producing UAS-derived SCA maps. abstract: Leveraging the promulgation of the Green Credit Guidelines as a quasi-exogenous policy shock, this study establishes a rigorous quasi-natural experimental framework to empirically examine the causal nexus between green credit policy and green innovation outcomes in renewable energy enterprises. title: Impact of Wildfire‐Emitted Black Carbon on Snowmelt Across Western North America
abstract: Abstract Wildfires are a major source of black carbon (BC) and their increasing frequency and intensity have enhanced BC deposition onto snowpack across western North America, which accelerates snowmelt and triggers multiple feedbacks that can substantially alter atmospheric composition and regional hydrology. abstract: Azospirillum baldaniorum Sp245 is a plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium (PGPR) whose ability to benefit host crops depends on robust root colonization, a process driven by the transition from a planktonic state to a sessile, biofilm-associated lifestyle. This study investigated the capacity of A. baldaniorum Sp245 to form Red, Dry, and Rough (RDAR) morphotype biofilms. title: Vacuum tamping preforming of low-density epoxy syntactic foam: Through-thickness structural evolution during compression molding and thermal curing
abstract: Deep-sea vehicles require low-density solid buoyancy materials combining load-bearing capacity and hydrostatic stability. In large blocks with densities below 0.45 g·cm -3 , restricted flow in highly filled systems can cause through-thickness heterogeneity, whose evolution during forming remains unclear. abstract: This study sought to evaluate the progress made over a decade of implementing the Primary Healthcare Under One Roof (PHCUOR) policy in Nigeria. A longitudinal study design using predefined scorecard was used. The scorecards are Scorecard 2 (2014) to Scorecard 6 (2022); Scorecard 1 (2012), corresponding to the programme’s inaugural year, was unavailable and therefore excluded. title: China’s Consumption Geography: A County-level Estimation of Daily Consumption Using Big Data
abstract: Abstract Residents’ daily consumption (RDC) levels provide an important indicator of regional development. However, existing research has largely examined consumption patterns either at coarse spatial scales or through localized case studies owing to data constraints, limiting our understanding of fine-grained spatial disparities in consumption. Using Baidu Population Profiling data, this study systematically examines the geography of RDC levels across county-level units in China and explores the socioeconomic factors underlying regional variation in consumption levels. title: Ovarian Structure, Function, and Asymmetry in Sexually Immature Small Cetaceans: Histological Analysis of Follicle Classes and Early Follicle Development
abstract: Small cetaceans serve as sentinel species for monitoring marine ecosystem health due to their vulnerability to bioaccumulative contaminants that may disrupt reproductive development. Despite this, there is a lack of validated reproductive toxicity markers, most notably for sexually immature individuals. abstract: This article introduces a proprietary methodology for identifying urban problem areas related to rainwater retention using open-source spatial data and advanced GIS tools, with Katowice selected as the pilot city. The research presents an integrated approach combining geospatial analysis, remote sensing indicators, and open data sources to generate synthetic maps highlighting zones most vulnerable to heavy rainfall and low water retention. title: The Aftermath of Almost: Communicating Risk Amid Community Narratives of Near Misses
abstract: Unpredictable weather means that serious threats do not always unfold as forecast. Hurricane near misses create an especially challenging communication context: The absence of harm may invite community explanations that make the event feel less threatening, even as future risk persists. abstract: Higher learning institutions (HLIs) are essential bases for a knowledge economy by developing human capital and technology. The HLIs fuel developing countries such as Tanzania to remain competitive in the current global economy. This paper explores the relationship between perceived transparency, trust in an HLI and student satisfaction. title: A chromosome-level genome of the king penguin ( Aptenodytes patagonicus ): a resource for linking genotype to fitness in a long-lived vertebrate
abstract: The king penguin (Aptenodytes patagonicus) is a long-lived seabird of the Southern Ocean that is emerging as a promising model in the wild for studying evolution. We present a high-quality, haplotype-resolved 1.35 Gb chromosome-level genome of an adult female king penguin - 'Pen/Se-guin' - assembled using PacBio HiFi long-reads and Hi-C proximity data. abstract: Mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) occur frequently throughout the Asian monsoon region (AMR) and exhibit distinct spatial distribution patterns, often associated with extreme weather events, including heavy rainfall, hail and tornadoes. To assess the hazardous impacts of MCSs and enhance disaster warning and response strategies, this study develops a database of MCSs across the AMR study domain from 2001 to 2023 using half-hourly infrared brightness temperature data and further examines their relationships with weather hazards based on observational data. abstract: ABSTRACT Gas sensors are increasingly required for distributed and unattended applications, where low power consumption, reliable calibration, and environmental robustness are as important as sensitivity. title: Connecting landscapes, communities and knowledge: lessons from organizing the INSAKA symposium on participatory conservation
abstract: Participatory conservation is widely endorsed as policy, yet the deliberative platforms through which it is enacted are seldom examined as research objects. This article studies a three-phase international symposium convened in Namibia in November 2025 by the University of Namibia under the INSAKA Consortium. title: Impact of climate change on surface temperature projections in Colombia’s principal natural regions
abstract: Abstract Climate change poses an increasing threat to Colombia, whose five principal natural regions (Andean, Caribbean, Orinoquia, Pacific, and Amazon) exhibit marked climatic and geographical diversity, increasing their vulnerability to rising surface temperatures. abstract: Building on research linking personality to financial behavior and market participation (Brown & Taylor, 2014; Conlin et al., 2015), this study examines whether personality traits influence simulated trading performance and whether this influence operates through trading intensity. abstract: The timing and geodynamic processes of the transition from oceanic subduction to continental collision along the Heihe–Hegenshan Suture remain debated, particularly the relationship between initial collision and final amalgamation of the Xing’an and Songliao-Xilinhot blocks. abstract: Abstract Photo-identification, which involves the recognition of individuals based on their natural markings, has become an increasingly valuable tool for studying elasmobranchs, offering a non-invasive alternative to traditional tagging methods. Despite this, its application in ray research remains limited and biased towards a small number of species. abstract: Background Rodent eradication on oceanic islands is essential for the conservation of endemic species. abstract: Water pollution is becoming an increasingly significant issue in both developed and developing countries. Land use change within a watershed directly affects water quality and aquatic ecosystems, making it essential to evaluate its impacts. title: Lower agricultural drought predictability in canal-irrigated districts of Pakistan
abstract: Agricultural drought threatens food security in irrigated and rainfed regions worldwide, and early warning is especially difficult in large irrigated basins, where canal water partly decouples crop condition from local climate. Machine learning forecasts often claim multi-month skill, yet few are tested over multiple years against simple benchmarks, and few examine irrigation's effect on predictability. abstract: _ The maritime technology and shipbuilding sector, encompassing yachts, leisure vessels, and marine structures, is undergoing rapid technological transformation, increasing environmental pressures, and heightened global competition. These dynamics emphasize the urgent need to modernize maritime education and training programs. abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetric (SDB) retrieval in shallow hypersaline waters is challenging because complex hydro-optical conditions and bottom heterogeneity can produce nonlinear spectral–depth relationships that limit conventional linear approaches. Marine seaweeds, renowned for their bioactive compounds, offer a promising avenue for the discovery of compounds targeting these pathways. abstract: Cities depend on infrastructural lifelines that extend far beyond their territorial boundaries, yet urban resilience is often conceptualized through capacities located within cities themselves. This Perspective uses disruptions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz to reconsider how urban resilience is shaped by geographically dispersed infrastructure networks operating across multiple spatial and institutional scales. abstract: Groundwater is vital for drinking, agriculture and industrial uses. abstract: Climate change is expected to affect the distribution of Mediterranean plant species, including Olea europaea var. sylvestris (wild olive), a keystone species for regional biodiversity and an important genetic resource for cultivated olives. abstract: Background Congenital heart defects are reported less often in non-domestic than in domestic species, although reports now span felids, primates, ungulates, and marine mammals. Atrioventricular septal defects (AVSDs), which arise from abnormal development of the endocardial cushions, are among the less frequently reported congenital heart defects in animals. abstract: Abstract Reliable road-puddle detection is important for intelligent road inspection and traffic-scene perception, yet remains challenging because puddles exhibit irregular shapes, weak boundaries, strong reflections, and high visual similarity to shadows, wet pavement, and road markings. This paper proposes PuddleSIFNet, a lightweight and robust road-puddle detector built on YOLOv13n. abstract: Paraquat (PQ) is an environmentally relevant herbicide associated with neurotoxicity and Parkinson’s disease (PD) risk, yet the key molecular determinants linking PQ exposure to PD and the cellular states in which these alterations occur remain incompletely understood. We integrated network toxicology, human PD transcriptomics, machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, spatial metabolomics, virtual perturbation, model-inferred protein analysis, molecular docking, and tissue validation to characterize PQ-associated molecular and cellular remodeling. title: Environmentally conditioned paired difference learning with field residual preservation for recovering controlled mooring response parameters from nonstationary buoy observations
abstract: Introduction Long-term motion records from aids-to-navigation buoys combine nonstationary environmental responses, mooring-state variations, and positioning errors. These components are difficult to separate when tension measurements and damage labels are unavailable. Methods We propose field-residual-preserving environment-conditioned paired-difference learning. title: Multiple eruptive events at Etna volcano in a short time (Dec 2025 – Jan 2026) captured by high-precision borehole strain and tilt
abstract: Between late 2025 and early 2026, Mt. Etna exhibited a highly diversified eruptive activity characterized by shifting eruptive styles. Occurring during a period of severe weather conditions, these different eruptive phases were captured by high-resolution signals recorded by borehole strainmeters and tiltmeters, whose joint analysis enabled the precise tracking of the evolving volcanic processes and the constraining of the related magmatic sources. title: Enhancing Maritime Supply Chain Performance Through Digital Technology, Supplier Collaboration, and Logistics Capability: A Moderated Mediation Approach
abstract: This study investigates how digital technology adoption, supplier collaboration, and logistics capability collectively enhance maritime supply chain performance through the mediating role of maritime supply chain agility and the moderating effect of environmental uncertainty. Positioned within the context of ports, shipping companies, and maritime logistics service providers, the research integrates the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Contingency Theory to explain how internal capabilities and external conditions interact in modern maritime ecosystems. abstract: Background and Aim: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health concern affecting humans, animals, and the environment. Although surveillance has traditionally focused on healthcare settings and livestock, wildlife is increasingly recognized as a potential reservoir, carrier, and indicator of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria and resistance genes. abstract: The gut microbiota functions as an active organ that produces enzymes which directly affect host adiposity, insulin sensitivity and systemic inflammation. However, the ability to convert multi-omics profiles to evidence-informed metabolic decision making is still complicated because it is difficult to determine which enzymes from commensal bacteria correlate to specific perturbed circulating and faecal metabolites. title: Hydrothermal Liquefaction and Catalytic Hydrotreating of Food-Waste
abstract: Institutional catering facilities generate large, continuous streams of food waste whose disposal carries environmental and economic costs, particularly in Mediterranean settings where landfill capacity and waste-management infrastructure are increasingly constrained. This work reports an integrated, experimentally grounded waste-valorization pathway that converts pre-sorted food waste from a Greek military academy canteen into a hydrotreated bio-oil, developed within the MARINES project. abstract: Evidence on dengue, chikungunya and West Nile virus (WNV) in North Africa has been synthesised one virus at a time or at continental scale. This narrative review with a structured search brings all three together for Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt and Sudan, and asks whether few reported cases reflect under-detection or low transmission. title: Efficiency Estimation of Oscillating Water Column Wave Energy Device Accounting for Multi-Parameter Coupling Effects
abstract: The development of Oscillating Water Column (OWC) devices is hindered by a critical gap in understanding: the neglect of coupling effects between key parameters in the estimation of energy conversion efficiency. This study introduces a novel experimental framework to address this issue. abstract: Abstract In the decades following the introduction of EU modal shift policy in 1992, modal shift targets intending to decarbonize transport have been set at varying levels of governance. Shifting cargo from road transport to more sustainable modes with fewer negative externalities, such as rail, inland navigation, and short sea shipping, has become a central policy objective throughout Europe and beyond. abstract: Spatial omics enables the integration of high-dimensional molecular organization with clinical outcomes, yet incorporating spatial single-cell information into predictive models at the population scale remains challenging. Here, we adapted BSNMani, Bayesian scalar-on-network regression with manifold learning, to integrate subject-specific, spatially informed co-expression networks into clinical prediction. title: Open multi-year UAV surveys establish a reproducible seabird baseline for the Destruction Bay–North Foreland region, King George Island, Antarctica
abstract: Large sectors of the Antarctic Peninsula remain incompletely surveyed for breeding seabirds, while historical records often lack the spatial and methodological detail required to assess change. We combined broad uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) reconnaissance with targeted high-resolution mapping and repeated surveys to establish a spatially explicit contemporary baseline for surface-nesting seabirds in the Destruction Bay–North Foreland region of King George Island during the 2022/23–2025/26 breeding seasons. title: NSFA AQE CenterOBB detects oriented SAR ships using frequency domain noise suppression and angle quality estimation
abstract: Ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery underpins maritime surveillance, traffic monitoring, and safety-of-navigation applications, yet high-quality detection in real-world SAR remains difficult. Multiplicative speckle and sensor-dependent noise degrade contrast, sea clutter and strong land or shore backscatter confuse inshore scenes, and elongated ships need reliable orientation estimates that a horizontal bounding box simply cannot give. abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid advancement of wearable electronics places ever‐increasing demands on the electrical and mechanical properties of materials. title: Evolving energy-water infrastructure strengthens drought resilience in the U.S. Northeast and Midwest
abstract: Abstract Strategies to strengthen regional water security will be essential for navigating a critical 21st-century environmental challenge: securing freshwater supplies against growing demands and increasingly severe climate extremes. This paper assesses the evolution of water security in the historically water-rich U.S. Northeast (NE) and Midwest (MW) to quantify their resilience to severe drought now and in the future. title: Phenotypic screening in ALS motor neurons identifies SIRT1 activation as a genotype-independent neuroprotective strategy
abstract: Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease, characterised by motor neuron degeneration and intrinsic neuronal hyperexcitability, with a lack of disease modifying treatments. One of the major challenges in therapeutic development for ALS is the genetic heterogeneity. abstract: AIM: To estimate RSV hospitalisation rates among children ≤ 2 years in New South Wales (NSW), Australia over two decades; to examine how rates varied by age, prematurity and selected co-morbidities and to describe temporal, seasonal and geographic patterns in RSV hospitalisation across NSW. abstract: Purpose – This article examines how the Bahtsul Masa’il formulation associated with LBM MWCNU Paciran frames mangrove planting as an Islamic legal responsibility and how this locally articulated norm relates to Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 14, particularly Target 14.2. title: Analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution of agricultural production efficiency and its determinants in China
abstract: China faces regional disparities in agricultural development. Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution of agricultural production efficiency and its driving factors is essential for advancing sustainable agricultural development. Using panel data from China’s 31 provinces from 2013 to 2023, we constructed an input–output indicator system and applied the super-efficiency slacks-based measure (SBM) model to evaluate agricultural production efficiency. abstract: Abstract Probabilistic tsunami hazard assessment (PTHA) at the inundation level over large spatial scales remains computationally challenging, requiring many scenarios, fine-resolution modelling, and high-quality digital elevation models (DEMs). abstract: Thermokarst lakes are critical components of Arctic carbon cycling, yet their ice phenology remains poorly characterized at regional scales. abstract: Introduction To address the growing global type 2 diabetes mellitus burden, dietary intervention via dipeptidyl peptidase‐4 (DPP‐4) inhibition provides a viable approach for glycemic control. Takifugu bimaculatus skin hydrolysates exhibit favorable hypoglycemic efficacy; however, the core active components remain uncharacterized. title: Leakage-Aware Cross-Dataset Multi-Task Learning for Shrimp Disease Recognition and Biomass Estimation
abstract: Public shrimp image collections are reused to train disease classifiers and non-invasive biomass estimators, yet they mix originals with published augmentations, byte-identical copies, and repeated views of the same animal, potentially inflating performance through data leakage. This study examines what these collections support once leakage is controlled: how protocol and acquisition conditions, rather than architecture alone, influence performance; whether disease recognition transfers to an independently collected dataset; and whether monocular imagery supports individual-weight estimation.

abstract: Abstract Sudden tropical cyclone (TC) track turns remain a major source of short range forecast error over the western North Pacific because small environmental differences can shift both the turning time and the turning location, rapidly amplifying cross track displacement. abstract: Introduction Seagrass restoration efforts have been motivated by global decreases in coverage associated with anthropogenic influences on the environment. In the Indian River Lagoon (IRL), FL, USA, seagrass declined by 75% between 2011 and 2021. During this time, abundance of the native macroalga Caulerpa prolifera increased substantially in this system. As restoration efforts began in the IRL, it became apparent that varying abundance of C. prolifera could impact the recovery of seagrass. abstract: Introduction The intestinal microbiota is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to host digestive physiology; however, its potential contribution to digestive capacity during fish larval development remains largely unknown. Satellite-derived fire hotspot products are widely used for this purpose; however, differences among sensor and the occurrence of redundant hotspot detections may affect the consistency and interpretation of these datasets. abstract: Understanding the bacterial diversity present in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) is essential for identifying potential pathogens and taxa with bioremediation and biotechnological relevance, particularly as these artificial environments remain largely unexplored bioresources with untapped microbial potential. abstract: This study aimed to describe the distribution and conservation status of Dipterocarpus retusus in Gunung Tilu Forest, West Java, Indonesia, using secondary data from the Forum Pohon Langka Indonesia (FPLI). title: A stochastic framework to investigate the stability of bridges subjected to local scour under a changing climate
abstract: Climate change poses significant risks to transportation infrastructure, increasing maintenance demands and reducing service lifespans due to more frequent and intense extreme events. One critical impact is the alteration of scouring patterns around bridge piers, driven by higher river discharge events, which can undermine foundation stability and lead to premature structural failures. abstract: Amidst maritime tensions in the South China Sea, the intersection of national identity and economic pragmatism has created a complex landscape for foreign language education and human capital development in Vietnam. Grounded in the geopolitical economy of higher education framework, this interpretative phenomenological study investigates how regional diplomatic volatility (re)shapes the career trajectories and academic mobility intentions of final-year Chinese language majors at a Vietnamese public university. abstract: Flexible tactile sensors must resolve not only the magnitude but also the direction, position, and mode of mechanical stimuli to support reliable perception of complex contacts. This Review critically examines how material selection, microstructural anisotropy, device architecture, and signal processing jointly enable multidirectional tactile sensing. title: Updated occurrence, habitat associations, and genomic resources of syngnathids in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia
abstract: Syngnathid fishes, including seahorses and pipefishes, are ecologically and economically important but remain vulnerable to overfishing, habitat degradation, and trade-driven exploitation. This study documents syngnathid occurrence, habitat associations, body-size observations, and genomic resources in the Sembilan Archipelago, Malaysia, using SCUBA-based visual surveys and high-resolution photographic analysis. abstract: Natural products remain an important source of bioactive molecules. title: Influence of IG waves on rock armour stability in shallow water
abstract: ABSTRACT Rock armour stability of rubble mound breakwaters in shallow water is strongly influenced by depth-limited wave breaking and spectral transformations over the foreshore. abstract: Abstract Reservoirs provide water supply, clean energy, and numerous functions for human well‐being. abstract: Las actitudes hacia las matemáticas constituyen un elemento relevante en la formación inicial docente, ya que influyen en la manera en que el futuro profesorado valora y utiliza esa disciplina en contextos educativos. abstract: Satellite-derived photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) products provide valuable information for environmental monitoring and agricultural applications, but residual fluctuations may remain even after bias correction, potentially affecting predictive reliability. abstract: Abstract The rise of the Generative Pre-Trained Transformer(GPT) language model, more commonly used as ChatGPT, has brought a spotlight on the ever-developing field of Generative AI (GAI). abstract: Near-real-time flood depth prediction demands surrogate models that are accurate, fast, and transferable across watersheds. title: FusionXNet edge for predictive maintenance under cross domain deployment shift
abstract: Abstract Industrial predictive maintenance (PdM) requires models that remain computationally manageable while handling heterogeneous sensor data and changing operating conditions. This study evaluates FusionXNet-Edge, a compact multi-branch architecture that combines CNN, BiLSTM, GRU, and MLP components, with an auxiliary branch that receives physically motivated engineered features. title: From detections to demography: methodological challenges and opportunities in survival estimation from automated telemetry networks
abstract: Survival is a fundamental demographic process influencing individual fitness and population dynamics. Automated telemetry systems offer unprecedented opportunities to estimate survival of highly mobile organisms across broad spatial and temporal scales. However, the structure of these tracking networks creates systematic biases that render standard survival models inadequate. Receiver stations are distributed unevenly across landscapes and over time, meaning that individuals taking different movement paths encounter vastly different opportunities for detection. title: Strict liability for maritime autonomous surface ships: rethinking tortious accountability in the age of autonomy
abstract: The commercialization of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) poses a fundamental challenge to the traditional maritime tort liability system, which centers on human fault. To address this challenge, a three-pronged institutional framework centered on the shipowner, comprising strict liability, liability limitations, and compulsory insurance, should be established. title: Evaluation of transfer learning in hydrological forecasting using ensemble LSTM models: a statistical approach to uncertainty and accuracy
abstract: Global change poses significant challenges to water resource management. Water Table Depth (WTD) is a critical variable linking subsurface dynamics to land-surface processes; however, real-world observations remain sparse. Transfer learning can support WTD monitoring, but assessing prediction quality in locations without observations is challenging. This contribution explores a method using an assessment tool to estimate prediction quality in such locations. title: The Overlooked Role of Alongshore Beach Non‐Uniformity in Short‐Term Shoreline Variability
abstract: Abstract Long‐term beach monitoring and satellite‐derived shoreline products are typically validated, and shoreline models calibrated, along cross‐shore transects. Open sandy beaches, however, are rarely uniform alongshore, because crescentic megacusps migrate past fixed transects, and their effect on single‐transect records remains unquantified. title: Privacy‐Preserving Agentic AR : A Fully Localized Edge‐ AI Architecture for Consumer Smart Glasses
abstract: ABSTRACT Consumer AR smart glasses are evolving from passive displays into proactive, intelligent assistants. Currently, these ‘Agentic AR’ systems rely heavily on cloud‐based AI. They continuously upload First‐Person View (FPV) video streams and multimodal sensor data. However, this massive data offloading creates severe problems. It introduces critical privacy vulnerabilities, unacceptable network latency and major security risks. title: Seasonal and Environmental Influences on Microbial Community Dynamics in the Dunk River Watershed, Prince Edward Island, Canada
abstract: Riverine ecosystems are crucial biogeochemical hubs, with their microbial communities playing a key role in nutrient cycling and overall ecosystem health. title: Nitrous Oxide Accumulation in Braided Rivers Is Controlled by Interactions Between Seasons, Nitrate Availability, and Flow
abstract: Abstract Human activities have increased reactive nitrogen inputs to rivers, intensifying the emissions of nitrous oxide (N 2 O). However, riverine N 2 O saturation is difficult to predict because it is influenced by both reactive nitrogen availability, particularly nitrate (NO 3 − ), and hydrology. title: The multi-USV mission management problem: Formalization and literature review
abstract: Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) have gained prominence in recent years due to their versatility and their ability to operate in hazardous maritime environments, thereby reducing human exposure to risk. As mission complexity increases, the deployment of multiple USVs becomes necessary to achieve scalability, robustness, and operational efficiency. abstract: Outliers are commonly present in frequency spectrum data from CSEM exploration, which often cause errors in amplitude calculation, especially when the outliers are huge, with a high proportion, and/or the sample size is small, making the effect significant and difficult to suppress. Based on principles of measurement statistics, we proposed an Elimination-Feedback-Function (EFF) based outlier-handling method in this paper. abstract: Tropical cloud prediction over the Maritime Continent remains challenging for numerical weather prediction models, largely due to uncertainties in cloud microphysics parameterizations under complex topography and multiscale convective conditions. abstract: The deep biosphere harbors diverse microbial communities amounting to a substantial fraction of Earth's biomass for much of its history. abstract: Background: Automated cervical cell image classification can support cytological screening by helping identify different cervical cell types. abstract: ABSTRACT Gamma‐ray log motifs provide useful descriptors of vertical grain‐size trends and stacking architecture, but their ability to discriminate reservoir quality is nonunique and requires quantitative testing. This study evaluated whether bell, cylindrical, funnel, serrated, and symmetrical motifs are associated with systematic differences in the petrophysical quality of Agbada Formation reservoirs in six wells from the Central Swamp Depobelt, Niger Delta Basin. title: Nonlinear interpretation of fall-cone tests in K0-consolidated clay
abstract: The fall-cone test is widely used for estimating the undrained shear strength of soft clays, yet its conventional interpretation is largely based on an empirical proportional relationship between soil strength and cone penetration. The applicability of this relationship to clays formed under one-dimensional stress histories remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Introduction Connected healthcare networks link medical sensors, gateways, electronic health record systems and cloud services, which enlarges their exposure to cyberattacks. Centralized intrusion detection systems (IDSs) require traffic from all sites to be pooled in one repository, which conflicts with data-residency constraints and creates a single high-value target, and their alerts are often not interpretable. abstract: The increasing digitalisation of maritime systems has raised concerns about cyber threats to shipping operations, port infrastructure and maritime safety. However, existing approaches often examine cyber-risk scenarios, geographical patterns and dependencies among risk factors separately. abstract: Ultra-shallow gas and hydrate-bearing systems in deep-water Quaternary strata are important exploration targets, but their geological controls and seismic responses remain difficult to quantify because the reservoirs are weakly consolidated, laterally heterogeneous, and commonly occur near the base of the gas-hydrate stability zone. This study presents an integrated geological and rock-physics seismic interpretation of the Lingshui 36-1 (LS36-1) ultra-shallow gas reservoir in the Qiongdongnan Basin. title: Data-driven risk assessment framework for railway operation accidents based on an improved Bayesian network
abstract: As a cornerstone national infrastructure, railway systems have faced increasingly intensive operational demands, escalating accident risks that threat socio-economic stability and public welfare. Therefore, ensuring operational safety is of paramount importance. This study develops an effective framework for assessing railway operational accident risks by integrating an improved Bayesian network. abstract: Abstract Forecasting irregularly sampled multivariate time series (IMTS) remains a fundamental challenge in contemporary time series analysis, owing to the inherent non-uniformity of sampling and pronounced inter-variable asynchrony. abstract: Microalgal cultivation generates continuous and diverse data streams, including physicochemical sensor measurements, optical and spectroscopic signals, and episodic molecular tests. Together, these data characterize cultivation conditions at different biological scales. abstract: Climate change can redistribute environmentally suitable conditions for Phlebotomus vectors in semi-arid regions, but conventional habitat-suitability models provide limited information on the broader environmental dimensions of future expansion. This study developed a Climate-Driven Environmental Sustainability Indicator (ESI) to assess spatial patterns of future Phlebotomus expansion risk in semi-arid Iran. abstract: Ensemble-based modelling of the atmospheric dispersal of volcanic clouds enables more realistic forecasts by explicitly accounting for uncertainties in eruption source parameters, meteorological data, and systematic errors in transport models. Many ensemble applications, including forecast uncertainty quantification, data assimilation, and probabilistic hazard assessment, require large ensembles to reduce sampling errors and adequately represent probability distributions. abstract: Bearing fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions is challenged by domain distribution shifts and the high computational cost of deep models on resource-constrained edge devices. abstract: Traditional corporate credit evaluation models often treat enterprises as isolated entities and rely on static financial data, making it difficult to capture dynamic risk evolution and inter-enterprise risk transmission. This study proposes a Graph-fused Multi-Modal Dynamic Gating Network (GMDG-Net) that integrates three information modalities: internal financial and market data, external online public opinion text, and an enterprise association graph constructed from equity pledge relationships. abstract: “Non-sulfide” Zn-Pb deposits are comprised of a series of non-sulfide minerals and are of crucial economic importance. abstract: This study develops an interpretable supervisory energy management strategy for a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle, combining deterministic safety and feasibility checks with a genetic-algorithm-tuned multi-criteria mode selector. abstract: Abstract Large-scale CO2 geological storage is evolving from stand-alone sites toward million-tonne-scale, clustered, and basin-coordinated deployment, making basin-scale heterogeneity a key constraint on capacity utilization, sustained injection, and long-term storage security. title: Distinct intraseasonal pathways driving rapidly escalating heat extremes in North China and their subseasonal predictability
abstract: Rapidly escalating heat extremes, characterized by abrupt onset and limited preparation time, pose disproportionate risks to public health, agriculture, and regional economies, yet their governing mechanisms and subseasonal predictability remain poorly understood. Here we identify 107 such events over North China during the summers of 1940–2024 and classify them into four spatial types. title: Beyond illegal fishing: strengthening Somalia’s domestic fishing capacity to realize its fisheries potential
abstract: Somalia’s fisheries are characterized by substantial but largely unrealized development potential, yet domestic benefits remain limited. We introduce a Protection-Production–Value (PPV) framework that treats fisheries development as an integrated system of three interdependent pillars. In this framework, Protection ensures sustainable resource opportunity, Production converts that opportunity into harvest capacity, and Value determines how much of the resulting fisheries value is retained domestically. title: Soil reclamation induced salinity decline is associated with shifts in bacterial, fungal and protistan communities and higher wheat yield in saline-alkali fields
abstract: Soil reclamation is widely practiced in saline–alkali land areas. However, limited research has focused on how reclamation duration regulates soil microbial communities and crop yield via modifying soil environmental conditions. In this study, high-throughput sequencing, ecological network analysis, and soil physicochemical characterization were integrated to investigate variations in soil properties, microbial community composition, and crop yield across saline–alkali fields with different reclamation durations (1, 5, and 10 years). abstract: Industrial fire protection machinery has a very particular reliability requirement in that it has to be capable of performing when required, even though it will be in standby for the vast majority of its life. The conventional approach of scheduled inspection is still absolutely vital, though periodic testing may well miss the gradual degradation that occurs between inspections. abstract: Acoustic recording can be a very interesting way of monitoring cetaceans for conservation purposes. abstract: Although 3D shape completion facilitates robotic grasping from partial observations, deterministic completion models overlook regional uncertainty, which can result in suboptimal grasp poses. abstract: Climate change has led to more frequent occurrences of extreme weather conditions and irregular rainfall patterns, making accurate prediction of rainfall amounts essential. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate long-horizon streamflow forecasting is crucial for water resource management, but existing models often face efficiency and interpretability challenges. abstract: Introduction The Bashijiqike Formation in the northern Kuqa Depression of the Tarim Basin is critical for Cretaceous petroleum exploration, yet its high-resolution stratigraphic framework remains poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract Accurate dietary intake assessment is essential for research in nutritional epidemiology, public health, and sustainable nutrition. Integrating new processed foods into databases often remains a time-consuming manual task for dietitians. abstract: Abstract Compound flooding threatens communities along the coastline of the Laurentian Great Lakes, where intense rainfall and high lake levels can occur simultaneously, creating large flood impacts. abstract: ABSTRACT Text‐to‐3D scene generation has emerged as a promising approach for enabling natural and intuitive 3D content creation through language. title: Tree Periderm‐Inspired Roughening via a Sacrificial Surface Layer for Ultradurable Multifunctional Protective Aramid Fabrics
abstract: Fire, water, and ice pose persistent challenges to personal protective materials used in harsh environments. Integrating water repellency, ice resistance, antimicrobial activity, and flame retardancy into a single fabric remains particularly difficult for chemically inert aramid fabrics widely employed in firefighting protective clothing. abstract: Transformative Technologies (TTs) and Anticipated Radical Technologies (ARTs) are frequently discussed as drivers of sustainability transitions, but their conceptual boundaries and the evidence supporting their systemic effects remain inconsistent. title: A TCN-KANformer-MDN model for engine remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of the remaining useful life of aircraft engines is critical to the safety of aircraft operations. abstract: Student behavior recognition is an important part in smart classrooms. There are two main problems with existing student behavior recognition methods. Firstly, it is easy to overlook the behavior of students who are seated densely; Secondly, it is difficult to recognize the behavior of students who sitting in the back row or being partially obstructed by the students in front row. abstract: Abstract This paper provides a proof of concept comparative study of four autoencoder architectures for compressing acceleration signals collected from a real railway tunnel under realistic and noisy conditions. The evaluated models include a Single-layer Sparse Autoencoder (SAE), a Fully Connected Autoencoder (FC), a Convolutional Autoencoder (CAE), and a hybrid architecture that combines convolutional (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers. abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible multimodal sensors capable of simultaneously monitoring pressure and temperature are highly desirable for wearable healthcare, physiological monitoring, and human–machine interaction. abstract: Sulfur metabolism, one of the oldest metabolic systems in the biosphere, plays a central role in coordinating elemental cycling in natural ecosystems. However, modern wastewater engineering has traditionally treated sulfur species as nuisance pollutants, relying predominantly on energy-intensive, carbon-driven aerobic processes. abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Small Language Models (SLMs) as autonomous agents at the network edge marks a shift in cyber–physical systems and the Internet of Things (IoT). abstract: Flooding remains the most frequent and damaging natural hazard worldwide, accounting for 35–40% of weather‑related disasters and affecting nearly two billion people. abstract: Reliable length–age relationships are essential for the effective management of elasmobranchs. abstract: Introduction Rice price volatility in India is driven by temporal dependence, climatic variability and supply-side uncertainties, creating continuous challenges for farmers, traders and policymakers. abstract: Microfibers (MFs) are among the most widespread forms of pollution in the environment. abstract: Maritime decarbonisation requires a shift towards low- and zero-emission energy systems, while the viability of electrified vessels depends on how voyage energy is provided onboard and replenished externally.
