abstract: Battery safety remains the primary bottleneck for mass electric vehicle (EV) adoption, yet field monitoring is hamstrung by a fundamental asymmetry: complex electrochemical faults must be diagnosed via sparse, low-frequency voltage measurements. Existing methods struggle to resolve the signal ambiguity between overlapping fault modes without hardware upgrades. abstract: Ports already share data, and system-to-system port-clearance APIs and practical port-to-port trials show that digital exchange is feasible. abstract: Student satisfaction is an indicator for evaluating the quality of the university experience and guiding institutional improvement efforts. This study aimed to predict university student satisfaction using data mining techniques and to identify the factors that contributed most to its classification. abstract: Reliable image-quality assessment is important in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle surveys because degraded frames can compromise mapping and downstream visual analysis. abstract: Reliable detection and mapping of burned areas are critical for managing the growing impact of fires on agricultural land and natural ecosystems. abstract: This study applied synthetic biology principles to engineer Saccharomyces cerevisiae with a heterologous astaxanthin pathway, creating a high-yield strain. title: A linear‐transformer hybrid for single‐nucleotide polymorphism‐based genotype‐to‐phenotype prediction in grapevine
abstract: Robust genotype-to-phenotype (G2P) prediction is essential for accelerating grapevine (Vitis spp.) breeding decisions and genetic gain. However, it remains challenging to measure complex traits under variable field conditions and across years. In this study, we propose a linear-Transformer (LiT)-G2P, an automated predictive framework that integrates additive genetic variance effects with Transformer-based nonlinear interactions using genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) data. title: Towards high-capacity and robust free-space optical communications
abstract: Free-space optical communication is emerging as a cornerstone technology for next-generation wireless networks, driven by the escalating demand for fiber-optic-level data rates in applications ranging from data center interconnects to satellite and deep-space communications. Despite its substantial theoretical capacity advantage, reliable long-distance optical links remain challenging because of atmospheric turbulence, pointing and tracking inaccuracies, and stringent power budgets. title: Transport and retention of microplastics during riverbank filtration
abstract: Introduction Riverbank filtration (RBF) is a widely used natural water treatment process; however, the fate and attenuation of microplastics (MPs), within river–aquifer systems is not well understood. This study investigated the occurrence and characteristics of MPs within an RBF system to comprehend the MPs transport behaviour. abstract: Context recognition and rare event classification in unlabeled audio represent critical challenges in both academic and industrial domains. These technologies hold significant potential for applications such as IoT-based predictive maintenance, surveillance systems (e.g., crime scene analysis or aviation incident investigations), and urban management (e.g., traffic monitoring). abstract: China’s consolidated maritime enforcement system connects dispersed domestic powers with new obligations under the Ecological and Environmental Code (EEC) and the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement. This study examines the relationship between China’s implementation responsibility and the legality of a specified China Coast Guard (CCG) measure. abstract: Hydrogeological studies with a focus on the cryosphere became numerous during the last years due to the sensitivity of snowfalls to the climate variations. This study investigated the Gran Sasso Range in central Italy, which is a carbonate mountain characterized by rainfalls and snowfalls. A study of stable water isotopes (δ 2 H and δ 18 O) of rainfall, snow, ephemeral and perennial streams and groundwater is proposed to constrain the principal processes involved in the aquifer recharge. title: International Migration and Poverty in Indonesia: The Dominant Role of Structural Factors
abstract: International migration is considered a strategy for households to exit from poverty as it provides opportunities for them to earn a higher income, expand access to economic opportunities, and offer better financial stability. However, it remains unclear whether these economic gains translate into meaningful reductions in poverty or whether poverty outcomes are primarily driven by underlying structural factors. This study examines the relationship between international migration experience and poverty status in Indonesia. The data used are from the 2021 Indonesian National Labour Force Survey

title: Forecasting Freight Flows and Mitigating Disruption Risks in the China–Europe Multimodal Transport Corridor: A Physics/Economics-Informed Spatiotemporal Diffusion Bi-LSTM Approach
abstract: We develop ST-Diff-BiLSTM to forecast node-level freight flows and classify disruption risk in the China–Europe multimodal corridor. The model combines geographic, trade, and flow-based graph links with feature and temporal attention. Its loss includes capacity and flow-balance penalties. In the reported test split, MAE was 8.4 TEU, compared with 17.8 TEU for baseline LSTM; the capacity-overrun rate was 0.1%, compared with 4.8%. The disruption classifier reached an AUC of 0.941. title: Development of a precision irrigation strategy based on sap-flow sensor
abstract: Water scarcity is an escalating global challenge, and agriculture accounts for roughly 70% of freshwater consumption worldwide. Greenhouse irrigation is usually scheduled by timers or by accumulated solar radiation, both of which estimate crop water demand indirectly. Substrate moisture sensors measure root-zone water content directly, but they do not show how the plant itself responds. abstract: Abstract Speckle-based sensing exploits the rich environmental information of its high-dimensional spatial intensity patterns. However, the requirement for camera-based acquisition and subsequent electronic digitization introduces significant latency and bandwidth bottlenecks that forbid real-time operation and higher temporal resolutions. abstract: Microbial symbionts may enhance adaptation to environmental stress, yet their role in nutrient-enriched freshwater habitats remains unclear. abstract: Abstract Forecasting snowfall accumulation is a challenging process that utilizes predicted variables usually from the microphysics parameterization of a numerical weather model, and evaluating these forecasts can be difficult with scarce quality observations. abstract: Saudi chemical manufacturing depends on reliable water supplies for reaction media, steam generation, cooling, cleaning and utility services, yet conventional wastewater management often treats these interconnected demands as separate engineering problems. abstract: Abstract Extending previous work focused on tropical cyclone (TC) rainband distinctions, this study employs polarimetric radar observations to examine the multiscale microphysical characteristics of Typhoon Doksuri (2023). abstract: Abstract Fengyun-3E (FY-3E) Microwave Temperature Sounder-III (MWTS-III) provides critical early-morning-orbit observations for global numerical weather prediction (NWP). abstract: The rising incidence and impact of natural disasters have thus increased the need for efficient risk transfer solutions. Conventional indemnity insurance contracts tend to inadequately address financial risks associated with natural disasters due to transaction costs, time-consuming claims settlement, and moral hazard. abstract: Accurate grid-to-site height correction of tropospheric mapping functions is essential for space geodesy. abstract: Abstract The growing variety of flight data, the expanding scope of its applications, and the continuous improvement in data quality have collectively accelerated the digital transformation of the aviation industry. title: Incertidumbre algorítmica y agencia moral en la UCI: comunicar los límites de la predicción clínica.
abstract: Introducción: Los sistemas de inteligencia artificial (IA) pueden apoyar la interpretación de datos y la estimación de riesgos en las unidades de cuidados intensivos (UCI), pero una probabilidad calculada no elimina la incertidumbre ni determina por sí sola qué decisión es adecuada para una persona. Objetivo: Proponer un marco conceptual que distinga entre incertidumbre de los datos, incertidumbre algorítmica e incertidumbre biográfica u ontológica, y examinar sus consecuencias para el juicio clínico y la agencia moral. title: Comparison of ConvLSTM, ConvLSTM with Temporal Embedding, and 3D CNN for Monthly Rainfall Prediction in Bekasi and Surroundings Areas
abstract: Monthly rainfall in tropical regions exhibits complex spatiotemporal variability, requiring models to simultaneously capture spatial heterogeneity and temporal patterns. This study compares ConvLSTM, ConvLSTM with Temporal Embedding (ConvLSTM-TE), and 3D CNN for monthly rainfall prediction using CHIRPS v2.0 data (1990–2025) over a 20 × 20 grid domain (5.75°–6.75° S; 106.5°–107.5° E) covering Bekasi and its surrounding areas. title: A ROS-based Simulation Framework for Industrial Robotics Pick-and-Place Application: Integration of Vision-based Pose Estimation and 3-DOF Inverse Kinematics
abstract: The efficiency of industrial automation depends heavily on the precision and reliability of robotic pick-and-place applications. This paper presents a complete simulation framework designed to develop and validate such applications in the ROS (Robot Operating System) environment. We perform a closed-form inverse kinematics analysis for the 3-degree-of-freedom OpenManipulator-X, providing the critical transformation from task-oriented Cartesian space to the manipulator's joint space. title: Dynamic spatiotemporal graph network with a temporal masked transformer for traffic flow forecasting
abstract: Accurate traffic flow forecasting requires a model to capture time-varying spatial correlations, nonlocal temporal dependencies, and recurring traffic patterns simultaneously. Existing spatiotemporal models often rely on fixed relational graphs or local temporal operators, which limits their ability to represent evolving dependencies in traffic networks. To address these limitations, we propose a Dynamic Spatiotemporal Graph Network with a Temporal Masked Transformer (DSGN-TMT). abstract: Afghanistan's geopolitical position at the crossroads of Central Asia and South sia gives it significant strategic importance in regional energy transit and connectivity. Bordering the energy-rich republics of Central Asia while providing access to the energy-deficient markets of South Asia. Thereby, Afghanistan plays a connecting role and serves as a natural land bridge for the transportation of natural gas, electricity, and other energy resources.

title: Sediment Transport Simulation under Flood Propagation by 2D HEC-RAS for Tigris River, Iraq
abstract: Changes in the hydrological regime significantly affect water quality and sediment delivery in all river systems. Sediment transport analysis aids in better understanding fluvial dynamics. This paper focuses on river dynamics, which maintain the environment and support low-cost training activities and flood control constructions. The work aims to evaluate the total load sediment transport rate in the case of unsteady non-equilibrium under the condition of flood in 2D waves adopted within the 2D HEC-RAS model. title: De la autonomía emergente a la personalidad instrumental: reconstrucción dogmática de la responsabilidad en agentes inteligentes de frontera
abstract: Este artículo analiza las tensiones estructurales que la opacidad epistémica inherente a los modelos de frontera empleados en agentes inteligentes produce sobre las garantías constitucionales de motivación, trazabilidad y control jurisdiccional. La investigación parte de la constatación de que la autonomía emergente e imposibilidad técnica de reconstruir cadenas causales en la operatividad de estos sistemas hacen inviable el paradigma del control humano significativo, convirtiéndolo en una ficción normativa incapaz de asegurar una responsabilidad efectiva. title: MASHI: Multi-Agent Vision-Language System for Home Inspection
abstract: Home inspection evaluates the visible components of a residential building and reports their deficiencies, safety concerns, and recommended actions. Vision–language models (VLMs) can describe what a photograph shows, but inspection findings also require regulatory knowledge, system-level assessment, and familiarity with inspection practice. We present MASHI, a multi-agent vision–language system that answers home inspection questions across the ten systems of the ASHI Standard of Practice. title: Integrated Sensing and Communication for 6G Networks: From Information-Theoretic Foundations to Standardization and AI-Enabled Applications
abstract: Sixth-generation (6 G) wireless networks are expected to merge communication and sensing into a single function known as integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). ISAC performs data transmission and environmental sensing at the same time, using the same hardware, signal processing and spectrum. This capability supports future intelligent networks in applications such as industrial automation, smart cities and extended reality. title: Adopting a Fuzzy C-Means Clustering Method to Evaluate Soil Liquefaction from SPT Measurements
abstract: Soil liquefaction occurs during major earthquakes in saturated, relatively shallow soils and is the primary cause of building foundation failures. Hence, assessing the likelihood of soil liquefaction has become one of the most important areas of study in geotechnical and earthquake engineering. However, the complex nonlinear behavior of liquefiable soils and the nondeterministic nature of earthquakes make liquefaction analysis difficult and uncertain. GIS-Based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) in Batang Kali, Selangor, Malaysia
abstract: Landslides are a prevalent environmental risk in Malaysia, occurring mainly in hilly and tropical locations, often during the optimum time for heavy downpours. This study aims to assess the landslide susceptibility in Batang Kali, Selangor, Malaysia, utilizing the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) based on Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Based on historical records, aerial image interpretation, and remote sensing data, in combination with field verification, a landslide database of 46 identified landslide locations was produced. title: Ensemble Kalman Filter Optimization for Convection-Permitting Forecasts in Complex Terrain
abstract: Weather forecasting in complex terrain remains challenging due to mountainous topography, which generates high spatial variability, local atmospheric circulations, and rapidly evolving convective systems. This paper focuses on the optimization of the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) to enhance convection-permitting numerical weather prediction in complex terrain. A high-resolution ensemble forecasting framework is used to analyze the effects of key EnKF parameters, including ensemble size, covariance localization, and inflation. journal: International Journal of Environmental and Agriculture Research

title: A context-aware risk assessment framework for critical shipboard operations: Application to bunkering
abstract: Critical shipboard operations such as bunkering, cargo handling, mooring, and enclosed-space entry are carried out under conditions that differ from one execution to the other, yet the risk score recorded for a hazard remains fixed for a set of procedures. This study develops a context-aware risk assessment framework in which the assessed severity of a hazard is conditioned on the circumstances of its execution. title: Multi-Objective Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Spatial Optimization of Green Infrastructure in Rapidly Densifying Cities: A Case Study of Ghorahi, Dang, Nepal
abstract: Urban microclimatic degradation is compounded by the rate of rapid urban expansion and rapidly increasing urban density in rapidly densifying metropolitan areas, which increase the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect and worsen the disruption of ecological connectivity. Two-dimensional (2D) spatial planning currently existing in the planning framework has not considered the vertical aspect of urban densification and the vertical dimension also influences the sub-optimal location of Green Infrastructure (GI) and Blue-Green Infrastructure (BGI). journal: Research Journal in Civil Industrial and Mechanical Engineering

title: Exploring flexible sensing strategies toward embodied intelligence
abstract: The field of embodied intelligence emphasizes the adaptive development of systems through interactions with their environments, with perceptual capabilities acting as a core enabler. Accordingly, flexible sensors are increasingly integrated into embodied intelligence systems, owing to their conformability to complex morphologies and adaptability to dynamic movements. Despite the great potential of such sensors, improving their performance to further advance embodied intelligence presents cross-disciplinary challenges. title: Assessing response strategies for maritime chokepoint disruptions: An integrated routing–simulation framework with application to the Suez Canal
abstract: This study presents an integrated routing–simulation framework to evaluate response strategies to maritime chokepoint disruptions. The framework combines disruption-route generation using the A-star algorithm with stochastic modeling of canal queuing, demand, and shipping dynamics through Monte Carlo and discrete-event simulation. The framework examines the disruption and operating conditions under which waiting, normal-speed rerouting, or increased-speed rerouting becomes the preferred response strategy. journal: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice

title: Integrated Drought Vulnerability Assessment and Mapping of Bangalore City, India
abstract: Drought vulnerability mapping is essential for understanding the spatial distribution of water scarcity and its associated socio-environmental impacts. The present study assesses the overall drought vulnerability of Bangalore urban district, Karnataka, India, through an integrated approach combining the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Geographic Information System. Four thematic components: meteorological, agricultural, hydrological and socio-economic were selected, standardized and weighted using AHP to develop individual and composite vulnerability maps. title: Floating Solar Photovoltaics and the Sustainable Development Goals: A Global Review of Technical, Environmental, and Socioeconomic Impacts
abstract: ABSTRACT Floating solar photovoltaics (FSPV) have emerged as a promising alternative to traditional ground‐mounted photovoltaic (GPV) systems. By deploying solar panels over water bodies such as lakes and reservoirs, FSPV systems mitigate land‐use constraints while enhancing energy performance and contributing to more effective water‐resource management. This paper presents a comprehensive review of FSPV technology, including its operational principles, technological developments, techno‐economic feasibility, environmental impacts, system reliability, and sustainability implications. Read-reference voltage adaptation for 3D NAND flash memory via RBER-aware few-shot transfer learning
abstract: Program/erase (P/E) cycling and retention drift alter the threshold-voltage distributions of 3D NAND flash, causing previously calibrated read-reference voltages to become mismatched to new operating conditions. To update read references when target measurements are limited, we propose a raw bit error rate (RBER)-aware few-shot transfer framework that adapts a Gaussian-parameter predictor from a single characterized source condition without requiring a pre-calibrated multi-condition voltage grid. title: Evaluation of Gridded Data Sets for Representing Precipitation Event Properties Across 20 U.S. Gulf Coast Locations
abstract: Abstract The skill of gridded sub‐daily precipitation products to represent rainfall event properties remains uncertain. Here, we evaluate four gauge‐influenced (AORC, MRMS, MSWEP, and Stage IV) and four gauge‐independent (PERSIANN, IMERG, ERA5, and MERRA2) products using 128,141 events across 20 U.S. Gulf Coast locations during 2015–2024. We assess event intensity (minimum, average, and maximum), duration, and volume. title: A PSO-Optimized Non-Linear Channel Capacity Enhancement Framework for CSI-based and MIMO Wireless Communications
abstract: Optimization of channel capacity in Channel State Information (CSI)-assisted Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems is a critical need for beyond 5G and future 6G wireless communication systems, in which non-linear propagation and time-varying fading channels significantly affect the channel capacity. Traditional approaches based on linear channel models and complex optimization algorithms often face challenges in terms of robustness, Scalability, and global optimality. journal: International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering

title: Mini review of multimodal intelligence for air quality modeling
abstract: Single data sources can miss important information needed for air quality modeling. Ground stations provide accurate local measurements. Satellites, IoT sensors, traffic records, meteorology, and land-use data describe different parts of the same environmental process. These sources improve coverage and representation if they are combined. However, this combination does not guarantee better forecasting performance. title: Addressing the challenge of missing remote sensing data in cold and high-altitude regions: A Dual-branch Spatiotemporal Fusion GAN based on incomplete images
abstract: Continuous monitoring of surface dynamics in cold and high-altitude regions is of vital strategic importance. However, sensor limitations hinder the acquisition of complete high-spatiotemporal resolution images. Traditional spatiotemporal fusion models rely on cloud-free reference pairs, struggling with incomplete observations. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Dual-branch Spatiotemporal Fusion Generative Adversarial Network (DSTF-GAN) for incomplete images. institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Calculation of the impacts of aerosols on cloud microphysical properties by combining ground- and space-based measurements
abstract: The effect of aerosols on cloud properties remains poorly constrained, in part because ground-based measurements are highly local while space-based retrievals are spatially imprecise representing averages over large footprints. Here, we show how the two viewpoints can be combined using colocated surface aerosol measurements and thermodynamic profiling from the peri-urban ATOLL (ATmospheric Observatory in LiLLe) site and geostationary-satellite cloud microphysical retrievals from the SEVIRI instrument. title: Modeling leakage current in naturally contaminated insulators using linear regression for transmission line diagnostics
abstract: Natural contamination can significantly influence the surface conductivity of high-voltage ceramic insulators and increase the risk of flashover. This study proposes a modeling framework based on multivariate linear regression to characterize leakage current behavior induced by three contamination types: dust, moss, and flashover residues. Experimental data were obtained from controlled laboratory tests with three replications for each contamination type. title: Spatial proteomics reveals lipid droplet reorganization in symbiotic Paramecium bursaria cells
abstract: Endosymbiosis is an important adaptive mechanism allowing organisms to exploit previously inaccessible niches. The flexible relationship between the ciliate Paramecium bursaria and green algae represents a model system for studying early endosymbiosis evolution. However, the mechanisms underlying how P. bursaria cells maintain this endosymbiotic relationship remain unclear. Here, we use mass spectrometry–based proteomics to generate a spatial proteomic atlas of the host P. bursaria cells with and without endosymbionts. title: AI optimized fertilization and irrigation improve wheat yield and quality in semi-arid calcareous soils
abstract: Traditional wheat farming in calcareous, low-organic-carbon, semi-arid environments relies on blanket fertilization and calendar-based irrigation, causing low nitrogen use efficiency and poor grain quality. We compared traditional practice with an AI-optimized system using soil test-based fertilization and tensiometer-guided irrigation for winter wheat in Khuzestan, Iran. The AI system reduced water use by 12.5% and nitrogen fertilizer by 28% while increasing grain yield by 8.5%. title: Robust distance perception for construction machinery via spatial-semantic LiDAR-camera fusion
abstract: Reliable distance perception for intelligent construction equipment in unstructured work sites is challenged by illumination variation, occlusion, and background clutter, which hinder LiDAR–camera feature association. We propose a spatial-semantic association framework integrating visual detection, point-cloud processing, and cross-modal matching. The visual branch employs a lightweight scalable detection head (SS-Head), with EIoU and Focal Loss to improve localisation in dense scenes and hard-sample recall. title: Microplastics and emerging chemical contaminants in indoor dust: potential human exposure pathways and implications for food and human health
abstract: Introduction Indoor dust is increasingly recognised as an important medium for human exposure to microplastics and associated chemical contaminants. This study investigated the occurrence and characteristics of microplastics and emerging chemical contaminants in non-residential indoor environments and explored their potential implications for human exposure and food-chain transfer. title: Social–ecological dual-network patterns and coupling characteristics in Gannan Prefecture from a complex network perspective
abstract: Under the tide of globalization, ecological fragmentation and imbalanced urban development have emerged as two major global challenges. In recent years, facing dual pressures of social governance and ecological protection, Gannan Prefecture has encountered separate issues in both social and ecological systems, further impeding their coordinated coupling development. This study proposes an optimization method integrating social-ecological dual networks with coupling coordination to achieve balanced eco-social integrated development. title: Flash flood resilience in rural communities of the Sylhet Basin Region, Bangladesh
abstract: Flash floods present a recurrent and severe hydrometeorological threat to the Sylhet Basin of Bangladesh, severely compromising rural livelihoods, ecosystem integrity, and physical infrastructure. This study presents a diagnostic evaluation of community resilience across four representative unions ( Sukhair , Sachna Bazar , Raniganj , and Jagadal ) using an integrated Rural Resilience Index (RRI) framework to assess baseline conditions (2025) and prospective trajectories (2030). title: From digital to green: the effect of corporate digital transformation on pollution emission intensity
abstract: Digital transformation is a key driver of the optimization and upgrading of China’s economic structure and a core element in the transition of China’s economic and social development towards green growth. This paper empirically analyzes the impact of corporate digital transformation on pollution emission intensity and its mechanisms. The results indicate that digital transformation significantly enhances corporate pollution emission intensity. title: Co-occurrence, interactions, and combined ecological and human health risks of microplastics, pharmaceuticals and personal care products, antibiotics, and pesticides in aquatic environments: a critical review with evidence grading and quantitative synthesis
abstract: Microplastics (MPs), pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs), antibiotics and pesticides share sources and receiving waters, yet evidence on their co-occurrence, interactions and combined risks is fragmented and often over-generalised. We conducted a critical review with a PRISMA 2020-guided search of Web of Science, ScienceDirect and PubMed (397 database records, plus citation and update searches; 77 included studies) and classified each study as Level 1 (field co-occurrence), Level 2 (laboratory interaction: sorption, desorption, ageing, biofouling) or Level 3 (laboratory exposure

title: Low-overhead trust mechanism for efficient cross-domain authentication in internet of vehicles based on blockchain sharding
abstract: Introduction To solve the problems of inadequate scalability, sluggish synchronization of authentication information, and high authentication overhead, an efficient authentication strategy based on a double-layer shard blockchain was presented for the cross-trust domain of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). A double-layer shard blockchain architecture was developed for multiple cross-trust domain message authentication by constructing blockchains on different entity levels in all domains in order to boost system scalability and provide secure and efficient cross-domain information flow. title: Non‐Linear Epigenetic Aging Clocks: A Case Study in Atlantic Halibut ( Hippoglossus hippoglossus )
abstract: Age information is fundamental in population biology. In fisheries management, robust and effective stock assessment models depend on accurate estimates of fecundity, survival rates, and other life-history traits, many of which vary with age. Consequently, reliable age determination is essential for understanding population dynamics and supporting informed management and conservation decisions. Age in fish is generally estimated by counting otolith growth rings, a labor- and time-intensive approach that requires lethal sampling and highly specialized, species-specific expertise. title: A Bibliometric and Thematic Analysis of LLM ‐Based Agents for Clinical Decision Support: Comparative Topic Modelling and a Five‐Axis Taxonomy
abstract: ABSTRACT Large language model (LLM)‐based agents combine reasoning, external knowledge access, tool use and multiagent coordination in emerging clinical decision support systems. This study maps both the knowledge structure of this literature and the expert‐system design choices represented within it. A PRISMA‐2020‐guided search of the Web of Science Core Collection yielded 40 publications from 2024 to 2025. title: Decarbonizing Aviation and Maritime Transport: Comparative Assessment of Clean Fuel Pathways, Life Cycle Greenhouse Gas Performance, and Deployment Strategies
abstract: Decarbonizing aviation and shipping requires low-carbon fuels whose climate performance depends on production route, electricity source, feedstock, conversion efficiency, infrastructure, and end-use conditions. This review compares hydrogen, ammonia, methanol, sustainable aviation fuels (SAF), power-to-liquid (PtL)/e-fuel pathways, and biomethane/bio-liquefied natural gas (bio-LNG) using a structured evidence-mapping approach and critical comparative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature and authoritative institutional evidence available through 2026. abstract: Over the past decade, the number of articles on the detection and analysis of pharmaceuticals in water has increased significantly due to improved methods and new, more accurate measurement tools. Antibiotics, painkillers, heart drugs, oral contraceptives and antidepressants are just some of the pharmaceuticals which concentrations is slowly increasing to disturbing level in river systems and underground water. title: Latent Autoencoder Ensemble Kalman Filter for Nonlinear Data Assimilation
abstract: Abstract. The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) is widely used for data assimilation in high-dimensional systems, but its performance often deteriorates for strongly nonlinear dynamics due to the structural mismatch between the Kalman update and the underlying system behavior. In this work, we propose a latent autoencoder ensemble Kalman filter (LAE-EnKF) that mitigates this limitation by reformulating the assimilation problem in a learned latent space with stable linear dynamics. title: Multiscale damage evolution mechanisms and life-cycle performance prediction modeling of asphalt pavement for resilient infrastructure
abstract: Asphalt pavements deteriorate under heavy loading, thermal extremes and freeze–thaw cycling, yet damage physics, life-cycle prediction and resilience assessment are still handled as separate problems. This study joins them. We define damage at the micro, meso and macro scales through a single effective-bearing-area variable, and we link the scales with viscoelastic-damage constitutive relations, a cohesive interfacial criterion and representative volume element homogenisation. title: Moisture content modulates DOM thermodynamic regulation of oxygen consumption in drying streambed sediments
abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic matter (DOM) thermodynamic properties regulate biogeochemical processes (e.g., O 2 consumption rates) in riverbed sediments. This connection has been established under saturated conditions, yet most streams and rivers experience variable inundation in parafluvial zones and go dry at least one day per year. title: Structural Drivers of Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Decarbonisation Pathways Across Income Groups in Asia
abstract: This study examines the structural correlates of changes in per-capita greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across 41 Asian countries from 2000 to 2023, with particular attention to income-group heterogeneity. Two-way fixed-effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors evaluate meat production, energy consumption, fertiliser use, urbanisation, trade openness, internet use and mobile cellular subscriptions. title: AdaFusionNet: Adaptive Trajectory Prediction of Group Two-wheelers in Interactive Conflict Scenarios for Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: Abstract The accurate prediction of two-wheeler motion trajectories is essential for ensuring the safety of autonomous vehicles (AVs), particularly at crowded intersections in China. Existing trajectory prediction approaches face limitations in representing the diverse motion patterns, dynamic constraints, and group-level behavioral characteristics of two-wheeler riders. This paper proposes an adaptive trajectory prediction framework for two-wheelers by integrating the revised social force model (RSFM) and a spatiotemporal Transformer (STTransformer) module. title: Long-term asset planning for port facilities: utilising asset service life variation to facilitate smooth replacement efforts and reduce costs
abstract: Many assets deteriorate gradually over time. Their condition is monitored throughout this period. An asset is replaced when it reaches the end of its useful life. This study looks at assets that form part of a larger population and can share functions. These assets are for example found in ports and are used for quay wall facilities. Their service life is shorter than that of the quay wall itself. As assets do not all age at the same rate, this study investigated how these differences in service life could inform better replacement planning. title: Algal-bacterial synergy in marimo granules enables low-carbon advanced nitrogen removal from wastewater
abstract: Abstract Marimo, a natural microalgal-bacterial consortium, represents a low-carbon solution for nitrate pollution control in low-nutrient waters. However, the adaptation of its nitrogen-cycling network to fluctuating nitrate levels remains poorly understood. This study reveals that elevated nitrate drives water matrix-dependent metabolic shifts, enhancing denitrification and assimilatory nitrate reduction performance in oligotrophic lake water, while strengthening dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium in carbon-richer wastewater treatment plant effluent. title: Evaluation of sub-daily precipitation variability and its diurnal characteristics in satellite and reanalysis datasets against ground-based observations
abstract: The diurnal cycle of precipitation serves as a fundamental diagnostic of the climate system's energy budget and hydrological cycle. Yet comprehensive evaluations of both its regular diurnal and irregular intermittent components across multiple satellite and reanalysis products against extensive ground-based observations remain limited. title: Adaptive Fuzzy Hybrid Optimal Event‐Triggered Output‐Feedback Control for an Unmanned Surface Vehicle System
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates an adaptive fuzzy hybrid optimal event‐triggered output‐feedback control strategy for an unmanned surface vehicle (USV) subject to external disturbances. To estimate the unmeasurable velocities of the USV system and reduce the number of actuator updates, a fuzzy state estimator is designed and two event‐triggered mechanisms are established. title: Geospatial multi-indicator assessment of flood risk in a wetland ecosystem, using a PCA-weighted risk framework
abstract: Flood risk in wetland ecosystems is increasing due to hydro-climatic variability, land-use changes, and socio-economic vulnerability, particularly in low-lying regions of South Asia. This study presents a geospatial multi-indicator framework to assess flood risk in the Chalan Beel, one of the largest freshwater wetland ecosystems in Bangladesh. title: Study of the operation of the tractor diesel fuel supply system on reverse fuel emulsions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The use of mixed fuel in diesel engines, including renewable ethanol-based fuels, contributes to the expansion of the fuel base. This factor is relevant in the context of the transition of the Russian Federation to a low-carbon model of development and reduction of emissions of harmful substances. Studies confirm the effect of ethanol supplementation on engine performance and emission parameters. title: Integrated hydrological-hydraulic modeling for the 2025 Jakarta flood and its implications for urban resilience
abstract: Despite numerous meetings and impressive initiatives, floods in Jakarta remain an unresolved challenge. The March 2025 Jakarta flood, particularly in the Ciliwung Watershed, caused by heavy rainfall and worsened by rapid suburban development, became one of the city's worst in recent years, killing nine people, displacing over 90,000 residents, and causing major damage. title: Recent extreme heatwaves are no match for future events
abstract: Abstract In recent years, record-breaking heatwaves have occurred over many regions of the Earth causing serious impacts to human and natural systems. Here we show that recently observed exceptional heatwaves are no match to potential future 21 st century events based on multiple metrics. For several observed heatwaves, this holds even under low- and medium-emissions scenarios. In a high- to very high-emissions future, many regions are projected to experience heatwaves that generate several times more cumulative heat and are many times longer (up to several months) than the observed heatwaves.

(garlic) are widely used as food or condiment, while they have also been used as a famous traditional medicine since ancient times for the treatment of diarrhea, dysentery, pertussis, tuberculosis and scabies, etc. However, most studies have focused on bulbs, and few studies have focused on the abundant aerial parts, which are usually discarded during the harvest season. title: MEASUREMENT OF MUNICIPAL NEW-QUALITY PRODUCTIVE FORCES AND REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
abstract: Guided by the policy of developing new-quality productive forces in light of local conditions, this paper takes panel data (2015-2024) of five core cities in Jiangxi including Nanchang, Ganzhou, Jiujiang, Shangrao and Yichun as research samples. An evaluation system for municipal new-quality productive forces is constructed covering scientific-technological, green and digital dimensions. title: Image Watermarking with Adversarial Attack on Secret Key Networks: from Zero-Bit to Semantic Vectors
abstract: Imperceptible watermarks are essential for ensuring authenticity and protecting image creators’ rights. While zero-bit watermarking offers strong imperceptibility and robustness, it remains vulnerable to security threats such as counterfeiting and watermark replacement, and its signatures contain no semantic information. To address these limitations, we propose a secure and semantic watermarking framework based on a Secret Key Network (SKN). title: Improved residential load forecasting using multi-feature, multi-layer LSTM exploiting trend and periodic patterns in historical data
abstract: Accurate day-ahead forecasting of individual residential electricity demand remains challenging because household consumption is highly variable, nonlinear, and influenced by recurrent behavioral and environmental patterns. This study proposes a multi-input, multi-feature Long Short-Term Memory (MIMF-LSTM) framework for direct 24 hour residential load forecasting at 15 minute resolution. The proposed architecture independently processes two lag-aligned temporal profiles: the immediately preceding 24 hour period and the corresponding 24 hour period one week earlier. title: Climate change-driven compound dust storm and heatwave extremes in Central Asia under future CMIP6 scenarios
abstract: Central Asia (CA) faces rising temperatures and shifting atmospheric conditions, increasing the urgency to address extreme events like heatwaves and dust storms. This study examines the co-evolution and regional co-variability of heatwaves and atmospheric dust loading, represented by dust extinction aerosol optical thickness (AOT). Using a multi-model ensemble of CMIP6 General Circulation Models (GCMs) and high-resolution reanalysis datasets, we analyzed heatwave indices alongside AOT across six clusters from 1992 to 2100. title: Performance of sustainable ultra-high-performance concrete with microplastics: comparative strategies of nano-coated microplastics and direct nanomaterial incorporation
abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants with increasing urgency for sustainable management strategies. Their incorporation into cementitious materials offers a promising pathway for waste valorization; however, the weak interfacial transition zone (ITZ) between MPs and the cement matrix severely limits mechanical performance and hinders structural applications. title: Prediksi Hasil Panen Tanaman Padi di Kabupaten Deli Serdang Menggunakan Metode Singular Spectrum Analysis
abstract: This study aims to forecast rice harvest yields in Deli Serdang Regency using the Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) method and evaluate the accuracy of the resulting model. The study employed a quantitative approach using secondary data on monthly rice harvest yields, measured in terms of dry milled grain (Gabah Kering Giling, GKG), from January 2020 to December 2024, comprising 60 observations. The data were divided into 48 in-sample observations for model development and 12 out-of-sample observations for testing. title: Wireless sensor network-based real-time monitoring system for large ship airbag launching: design and field validation
abstract: Traditional monitoring solutions for airbag launching of large ships rely on mechanical pressure gauges with limited spatial coverage, slow response times (from several hundred milliseconds to a few seconds), and an inability to monitor dynamically changing attitude parameters during the launching procedure. This paper introduces a WSN-based real-time monitoring solution that combines IMUs and pressure sensors installed at strategic positions on the ship hull and airbags. title: Toward a Methodology for Geopolitical Analysis
abstract: A geopolítica, historicamente disputada entre o determinismo clássico e a teoria crítica, exige uma abordagem analítica rigorosa e sistemática para que possa produzir resultados relevantes para a formulação de políticas públicas. Este texto propõe uma metodologia estruturada de análise geopolítica, fundamentada na literatura clássica e contemporânea, delineando as etapas essenciais, as ferramentas analíticas e as competências centrais que um analista geopolítico deve dominar. abstract: ABSTRACT Developing sustainable and biocompatible bio‐based foams for medical application presents a major challenge, particularly concerning structural integrity and cellular colonization. This study focuses on the development and characterization of macroporous cellulose foams as a promising material, specifically tailored for potential medical applications. title: Parameterization-dependent uncertainty quantification in adjoint-based history matching of channelized reservoirs
abstract: History matching channelized reservoirs is severely ill-posed: a single best-fitting model is of limited value without an estimate of its uncertainty. We present a verified Python framework for adjoint-based history matching of multiple-point-statistics (MPS) channelized fields, and quantify how the parameterization shapes the inferred posterior. title: Adaptive Iterative Learning Trajectory Tracking Control of 2‐DOF Picking Manipulator Considering Input Constraint
abstract: ABSTRACT The improvement of picking efficiency and fruit recognition ability in picking tasks has effectively promoted the development process of agricultural intelligence. However, manipulator trajectory‐tracking control, as a core technical link for achieving accurate picking, has not received sufficient attention to its importance. journal: International Journal of Adaptive Control and Signal Processing

title: SiamDUKF: RGBE Siamese tracking with a differentiable unscented Kalman filter
abstract: In practical UAV tracking, performance is often degraded by nonlinear maneuvers, abrupt illumination changes, and occlusion. Single-modality trackers therefore struggle to maintain robust performance in complex environments. To address this issue, we propose SiamDUKF, a Siamese-network-based tracking framework that integrates RGB and event information with a differentiable unscented Kalman filter (Diff-UKF). Built upon SiamFC, the framework adopts a dual-branch backbone with unshared weights to extract modality-specific features and employs CBAM for adaptive cross-modal refinement and fusion.

title: Research Progress on Carbon and Nitrogen Migration, Transformation, Monitoring, and Engineering Regulation in Soil–Water Environmental Systems
abstract: Carbon and nitrogen are two key elements driving biogeochemical cycles in soil-water environmental systems. Their transport and transformation along the soil-river-reservoir-estuary continuum directly affect water eutrophication, organic carbon burial fluxes and regional eco-environmental security. Based on two representative studies—the effect of water-sediment regulation (WSR) of the Xiaolangdi Reservoir on suspended sediment and organic carbon in the Yellow River, and a systematic comparison of factors affecting soil nitrate-N and ammonium-N extraction—this review summarizes: (1) the power-

title: Optimización de líneas de producción mediante análisis predictivo y mantenimiento basado en condición para mejorar la eficiencia operacional
abstract: El objetivo fue evaluar el efecto de una estrategia integrada de análisis predictivo y mantenimiento basado en condición sobre la eficiencia operacional de líneas de producción en empresas manufactureras ecuatorianas. Se desarrolló un estudio cuantitativo, aplicado, descriptivo-correlacional y cuasiexperimental, con mediciones antes y después y comparación entre un grupo experimental y otro de control. title: Review and comparison of hybridized ACO capabilities in locating warehouse benefits from KSA manufacturable raw materials
abstract: Multi-echelon supply chain problems involving sources, warehouses, and customers are categorized as NP-complete. This review highlights the hybridized Ant Colony Optimization (hACO) approach in meeting accurate coordinates of the Integrated Industrial Complex (IIC), which relies on manufacturable KSA raw material useful in many industries, such as feldspar, bauxite, phosphate, limestone, silica sand, copper, and its by-products (i.e., source). title: Cosmic neutrino background is within reach of future neutrino telescopes
abstract: The cosmic neutrino background (C$ν$B) can be boosted to high energies due to scatterings with energetic cosmic rays (CRs) across cosmological scales. Previous calculations focused on neutral current incoherent and coherent elastic scatterings of cosmic-ray protons off relic neutrinos. However, charged current interactions and deep inelastic scatterings are also expected to occur, which enhances the boosted relic neutrino fluxes on Earth. abstract: Introduction This study examined the temporal organization of ENSO variability in relation to two Earth–Sun orbital-state descriptors, ΔLP and Fi, over the period 1948–2025. Methods Annual series were analyzed using Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA), Information Theory, partial wavelet coherence (PWC), and multiple wavelet coherence (MWC) as complementary methods. title: Soil erosion response to future climate variability and best management practices in the Kesinga catchment, India
abstract: Abstract Soil erosion poses a growing threat to watershed sustainability under changing climatic conditions, particularly in monsoon-dominated regions. This study integrates the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) with bias-corrected CORDEX–South Asia climate projections to quantify present and future sediment yield and to evaluate the effectiveness of structural best management practices (BMPs) in the Kesinga catchment, eastern India. abstract: To evaluate the utilization of different dietary oils by juvenile murrel ( Channa striata ), five isonitrogenous (45%) and similar inclusion levels (8%) of selected oils, namely fish oil (FO), soybean oil (SO), mustard oil (MO), rice bran oil (RBO), and groundnut oil (GNO), were used. A total of two hundred twenty-five (225 ) Channa striata juveniles of average weight (6.35 ± 0.01g) were stocked in triplicates following a completely randomized design in a 150 L fiberglass-reinforced plastic (FRP) tank. title: Risk-Based Quality Assurance and Advanced Pipeline Integrity Management for Long-Distance Crude Oil and Gas Transmission Systems in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Long-distance crude oil and gas pipelines depend on a chain of assurance extending from material acceptance and girth-weld qualification to corrosion surveillance, defect assessment and intervention. These activities are frequently managed as separate programmes, although an undetected construction deviation can later appear as an integrity threat, while uncertain inspection data can distort repair priorities. title: Enhancing water security: a review of water quality and treatment technologies for remote Australian communities
abstract: Abstract Access to safe and reliable water is fundamental to human health and well-being and to achieving United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 6. Yet many remote Australian communities, including First Nations communities, face challenges in securing drinking water. Supplies do not consistently meet the Australian Drinking Water Guidelines, with adverse public-health and socio-economic consequences. title: ‘Location Matters’: Incorporating Spatial Autocorrelation Into Modelling the Drivers of Cyanobacterial Biomass in Reservoirs of Northeastern Brazil
abstract: ABSTRACT Spatial autocorrelation (SAC) is a critical yet often overlooked component of ecological analyses, which can significantly influence the accuracy and interpretation of statistical models. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the spatial distribution of cyanobacteria biomass among tropical reservoirs at the watershed scale and to identify the main environmental predictors associated with this distribution, explicitly incorporating SAC into regression models. title: Integrated Geological-Dynamic Analysis and Development Optimization of Interlayer Connectivity in an Offshore Calcareous-Barrier-Controlled Stacked Reservoir
abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous barriers influence pressure support and water entry in offshore stacked reservoirs, but their development implications are difficult to evaluate where well control in the upper zone is sparse. This study integrates drilled barrier interpretation, operation-screened production dynamics, geological monitoring priorities, and reservoir simulation for Zone B and the underlying Zone C of the LFA field. title: Recent Slowing Arctic‐Amplified Warming Drives an Unprecedented Water Recovery in the World's Most Voluminous Freshwater Lake
abstract: Abstract The Lake Baikal, containing one‐fifth of Earth's unfrozen surface freshwater, faces increasing hydrological uncertainty under climate change. Its water balance depends on Selenga River inflow and Angara River outflow. We present a 343‐year combined Selenga and Angara streamflow reconstruction using a tree‐ring network to provide a multi‐century hydroclimatic baseline. The reconstruction captures intermittent drying trends throughout the 20th century, including a ∼90% streamflow decline from high levels, consistent with long‐term regional aridification. title: Carbon Dots as Corrosion Inhibitors: Precursor Effects, Adsorption Mechanisms and Sustainability – Review
abstract: Carbon Dots have proven to be a highly important class of material thanks to their minute sizes, which fall in the range of 1-10 nm. The ability of such materials to bind onto various substrates can be significantly improved with the use of oxygen-, nitrogen-, and carbon-containing functional groups. The term corrosion refers to a natural, spontaneous process that leads to the degradation of a particular substance. title: Many-objective reservoir operation optimization using NSGA-III and decision-support analysis: a sustainable management framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India
abstract: Abstract Efficient reservoir operation requires simultaneous consideration of competing goals related to hydropower generation, water-supply reliability, flood management, and storage regulation. However, deriving balanced operating policies becomes increasingly complex when several conflicting objectives are considered concurrently. This study develops a many-objective optimization framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India, considering four objectives: maximization of hydropower generation and minimization of water deficit, spill losses, and storage deviation. title: TopoToolbox 3, a laboratory for quantitative geomorphology
abstract: TopoToolbox has been widely used to analyze and model landscapes across geomorphology and other geospatial disciplines for the past 15 years. Its documentation and accessible interfaces have made it a valuable resource for teaching and learning quantitative geomorphology while its customizability and efficiency have allowed researchers to use it as a platform for experimentation and implementation of their own analyses and models. title: WAVES PROPAGATION FOR THE CONFORMABLE TIME-FRACTIONAL BENJAMIN-BONA-MAHONY-BURGERS EQUATION ARISING ON THE SURFACE OF WATER
abstract: This study investigates solitary wave solutions of the conformable time-fractional Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers (TFBBMB) equation. This is a special type of Sobolev-type equation that can describe long waves on the surface of water in a channel with a minimal amplitude. Three techniques are employed: The generalized projective Riccati equation (GPRE) approach, the modified auxiliary equation (MAE) technique, and the generalized exponential rational function (GERF) approach. title: Geometry-Guided Optimization for Offshore Wind Farm Collection System Routing via Adaptive Circuit Partitioning
abstract: Abstract Offshore wind farm collection system routing requires cost-effective networks that satisfy coupled electrical and geometric constraints. Existing methods often improve topology search or path feasibility separately, relying on restricted candidates, predefined routes, or post-hoc repair to handle crossings, obstacles, irregular boundaries, and export-corridor conflicts. This paper proposes a geometry-guided optimization method based on adaptive circuit partitioning. title: GeoSlideFormer: an interpretable hybrid Transformer-CNN framework for landslide segmentation in high-resolution remote sensing imagery
abstract: Rapid and accurate landslide mapping from high-resolution remote sensing imagery is essential for post-disaster assessment, landslide inventory development, and geohazard risk management. However, pixel-level landslide segmentation remains challenging because landslides exhibit highly variable scales, irregular boundaries, partial occlusion, and strong spectral or textural similarity with surrounding terrain. title: Spatial Optimisation of Local Climate Zones in Kuala Lumpur for Surface Urban Heat Island Mitigation Using ResNet and Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Abstract Land Use & Land Cover (LULC) optimisation is critical for mitigation of Urban Heat Island (UHI) effects. We use the Local Climate Zones (LCZ) classification system to optimise LULC as it has achieved very strong results in Surface UHI intensity (SUHII) modelling. Two evolutionary algorithms are employed to minimise extreme SUHII in Greater Kuala Lumpur: Genetic Algorithm, and Particle Swarm Optimisation, with total population and GDP set as constraints that should not decrease. title: Dam-regulated flow fragmentation and sand-mining-driven threshold shifts shorten the Mekong–Tonle Sap reverse-flow season
abstract: Sand mining, dam construction, and climate change have profoundly altered the hydrological dynamics of the Mekong River-Tonle Sap Lake floodplain system, one of the world's most ecologically productive river-lake complexes. This study provides an integrated, multi-scale assessment of flow regime alteration across the Mekong mainstream and its coupling with the Tonle Sap Lake across three periods: pre-dam (1976–1991), transition (1992–2009), and post-dam (2010–2024). title: From Flood Susceptibility to Adaptation Priorities in an Arid City‐Region: Evidence From Sharjah, United Arab Emirates
abstract: ABSTRACT Flood susceptibility maps identify potentially affected land but provide limited guidance on the form of adaptation. We examined how susceptibility can inform urban retrofit, landscape retention and protection priorities in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates (UAE). Nine environmental predictors supported a Random Forest model trained on a synthetic mask derived from terrain, wetness and urban‐runoff rules. title: A Review on the Flow-Induced Excitation Mechanism of Centrifugal Pumps During Off-Design Conditions
abstract: In thermal power plants, both cooling water and boiler feedwater need to be delivered by centrifugal pumps. When centrifugal pumps operate under off-design conditions, significant flow-induced vibration problems often arise due to the complex unsteady flow inside, which in turn affects their operational reliability and service life. This paper presents a comprehensive review of flow-induced vibration issues in centrifugal pumps under off-design operating conditions and the corresponding mitigation methods. title: Predicting discrete traits in evolving systems
abstract: Discrete data are prevalent across biology, from nucleotide base pairs to mating systems or petal count on a flower. Predictions using discrete data are central to imputation, forecasting, and hypothesis testing in biology. How much accuracy and confidence they deliver together, and how this varies across scenarios and taxa, has not been quantified systematically. Here, using accuracy and log loss, we benchmark these models across scenarios varying in tree size, evolutionary rate, and trait coevolution. abstract: ABSTRACT Hermite–Gaussian (HG) and Laguerre–Gaussian (LG) modes are two fundamental modes in structured light, and astigmatic mode conversion between them has been extensively investigated. Conventional structured light manipulation generally treats complete HG eigenmodes as the fundamental degrees of freedom (DOFs), with beam control achieved through the superposition of multiple eigenmodes. title: Multi-trophic risk from human superpredators may alter predator–prey coexistence and population dynamics
abstract: Humans are efficient predators, yet they also interact with wildlife in non-lethal ways. Here, a lethal superpredator is defined as a predator with 100% per-encounter lethality whose abundance is not regulated by its prey, with humans who hunt or fish as the motivating example. Using an agent-based model that includes both the lethal and non-lethal (behavioral) effects of humans and predators on prey, this study explored how replacing natural apex predators with superpredators affects mesopredator–prey dynamics, focusing on trophic targeting and on lethal vs. non-lethal interactions. title: Integrated assessment of aerosol optical properties over West Africa: multivariate classification, seasonality, and long-term variability
abstract: Despite substantial advances in aerosol remote sensing, objective characterization of mixed aerosol regimes and their seasonal evolution over West Africa remains poorly constrained, limiting accurate assessments of aerosol–climate interactions and regional air quality. This study addresses this gap by developing a robust, data-driven framework that integrates Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) to objectively classify aerosol regimes using four complementary aerosol optical properties (AOD, SSA, AAOD, and AE) derived from integrated AERONET, MODIS, MISR and MER
institutions: National Space Research and Development Agency

title: Test-Time Adaptation and Domain Generalization in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis: From Laboratory to Real-World Deployment
abstract: The deployment of multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) systems in real-world environments is hindered by domain shift, where performance degrades significantly when test data diverges from the training distribution. This review paper provides a comprehensive survey of two pivotal strategies to address this challenge: domain generalization (DG) and test-time adaptation(TTA). We present a novel taxonomy of state-of-the-art methods, categorizing them into data manipulation, representation learning, meta-learning, and hybrid approaches. title: A global panel study on urbanization and energy consumption as drivers of black carbon emissions
abstract: Black carbon is a short-lived climate pollutant formed during the incomplete burning of fossil fuels. It has turned out to be a significant cause of global warming, climate change and air pollution. This paper examines the impact of urbanization and fossil fuel energy consumption on black carbon emissions across 125 countries from 2005 to 2022 with the help of both panel regression and multiple linear regression model estimated using OLS. title: LLM-Assisted Multimodal Graph Attention Network for Multilabel Tourist Profiling
abstract: Tourist profiling from digital traces is intrinsically multimodal, relational, and weakly supervised. Visitors interact with heterogeneous entities, generate textual content, visit visually characterized points of interest, and exhibit overlapping behaviors. Existing approaches typically address only subsets of these aspects, while the generation of reliable supervision for fine-grained tourist profiles remains costly and difficult. title: Enhancing Social and Environmental Sustainability in Tourism Through Smart Tourism Systems Integration
abstract: ABSTRACT This research is an explanatory sequential mixed‐methods study focused on the effect of Smart Tourism Systems (STS) on sustainable tourism. 543 participants were included, and 22 were interviewed in a semi‐structured manner. Structural equation modeling found significant positive associations across the model. Environmental sustainability tourism was associated with social sustainability tourism ( β = 0.508), and social sustainability tourism with sustainable development outcomes ( β = 0.426). title: Simulación de microrredes híbridas con integración de fuentes renovables y almacenamiento para resiliencia energética.
abstract: Integrating renewable energy sources into power grids presents challenges regarding energy variability, dynamic stability, and supply continuity during grid outages; this research addresses the coordination of photovoltaic generation, energy storage, and backup power generation to ensure the resilient operation of critical loads. The study aims to develop and analyze a hybrid microgrid through dynamic simulation using DIgSILENT PowerFactory 2024, integrating a 2.5 MWp photovoltaic plant, a 6 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS), and a 3.2 MW diesel backup generator. title: Inteligencia artificial en marketing: Logística y sostenibilidad en el comercio electrónico (2020-2026)
abstract: El comercio electrónico ha experimentado una transformación sin precedentes entre 2020 y 2026, impulsada por la pandemia y la consolidación de la inteligencia artificial (IA) como infraestructura del marketing digital. Sin embargo, la literatura sobre IA en marketing, logística del comercio electrónico y sostenibilidad ambiental ha crecido de forma fragmentada, sin integrar sus hallazgos. title: Temperature Field Optical Detection and Reconstruction: Methods, Principles and Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT The temperature field constitutes a core parameter for thermal‐process analysis and equipment optimization. Traditional contact‐based temperature‐field measurement techniques suffer from flow‐field interference and single‐point‐detection limitations and cannot satisfy high‐precision measurement requirements within complex high‐temperature environments. This paper systematically reviews the physical principles, detection methods, and reconstruction algorithms of non‐contact optical temperature measurement and temperature field reconstruction. title: NDFI-SC: a robust near-real-time flood-mapping workflow using an SDWI-derived stable reference
abstract: Flood mapping requires workflows that are automated and robust under cloud-prone conditions. Recent reference-guided adaptive thresholding studies have improved threshold selection in change-detection-based flood mapping, but they still depend on usable optical reference data and may become constrained when cloud-free observations are unavailable. To address this limitation, this study develops NDFI-SC, a robust flood-mapping workflow implemented on Google Earth Engine that combines normalised difference flood index (NDFI) change detection with a Sentinel-1 Dual-Polarisation Water Index (SDWI)

title: The limits of green incentives: a stochastic profitability analysis of sugar kelp farming in Europe
abstract: Seaweed cultivation can deliver carbon sequestration and nutrient removal, which have value beyond the market price of the biomass. If these ecosystem services were quantified, certified and compensated, they could provide additional income for farmers. This study evaluates whether such payments, together with other green incentives, can make sugar kelp ( Saccharina latissima ) farming in Europe profitable, and how much each incentive contributes. title: DINOSAR: large-scale Sar self-supervised pretraining with content-aware view construction
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) provides a scalable approach to learning transferable representations from unlabeled synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery. A common SSL strategy is label-free self-distillation, which derives supervision by aligning randomly cropped global and local views. However, in SAR imagery, informative scattering structures are sparsely and unevenly distributed, so random view construction may miss target content or repeatedly sample the same strong scatterers, weakening the consistency signal. abstract: Fire escalation in tank farms is a major process safety risk, but CFD simulation is too slow for emergency use and purely data driven models ignore the irregular layout and the physics of radiative escalation. This work proposes PI-GAT-CNN-GRU, a physics-informed graph attention enhanced CNN-GRU model that forecasts fire spread paths under a strictly causal protocol and decodes node probabilities into ordered cascade paths, with a stochastic decoding of concurrent escalation. title: Estimating groundwater levels and their associated uncertainty through spatiotemporal kriging of groundwater-level data
abstract: Abstract Sustainable groundwater management requires, among other factors, reliable monitoring of groundwater levels (GWLs) and their spatiotemporal evolution in an aquifer with meaningfully quantified uncertainty. Geostatistical methods can estimate GWL surfaces directly from available groundwater monitoring data. This contrasts with groundwater flow modeling, which requires much more detailed data. This study estimates spatiotemporal GWL maps and quantifies associated uncertainties by spatiotemporal kriging, which combines spatial interpolation with temporal gap filling and noise filtering.

abstract: Abstract Purpose Plastic pollution in water is a global issue. As polymeric materials degrade, micro- and nanoplastics are formed, and release substances used in their production, many of which exhibit estrogenic effects on organisms. The main aim of the study was to investigate the relationship between the concentrations of selected organic compounds, mainly used in plastic production, in the sediments of artificial reservoirs and the land use of their catchments, under varied anthropogenic pressure. title: Extreme glacier melt on the Central Tibetan Plateau during the summer of 2022: detection and mechanisms
abstract: Extreme glacier melt events accelerate mass loss, increase glacier instability, and temporarily increase downstream runoff, potentially alleviating drought conditions. title: Night Jasmine Blooming Optimization (NJBO): A Novel Nature-Inspired Algorithm for Electrical Engineering Applications
abstract: Optimization algorithms have become vital to the solution of complex optimization problems that are difficult to solve using conventional methods. In this paper, we introduce a novel nature-inspired metaheuristic algorithm called the Night Jasmine Blooming Optimization (NJBO) algorithm, which is inspired by the blooming of the night jasmine plant (Cestrum nocturnum). title: Technological path dependence in the water management systems in the late prehistoric Yangtze Delta
abstract: Water management system can stabilise access to water resources while simultaneously creates path dependence, in which material, ecological and organisational commitments shape the possibilities for subsequent development. title: VARS: value-aware robotic sorting of waste streams via orienteering with time windows
abstract: The transition toward a circular economy necessitates high-quality material recovery from increasingly complex and heterogeneous waste streams. However, state-of-the-art robotic sorting algorithms primarily optimize system throughput, a proxy metric that treats all objects as equally valuable and often results in lower revenue and higher output stream contamination. abstract: For over two decades, the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and its follow-on mission (GRACE-FO) have been monitoring Earth’s gravity field. Their measurement principle relies on precisely tracking distance variations between two satellites chasing each other in the same orbit, separated by approximately 200 km. abstract: Homotopy is a central concept of algebraic topology with broad theoretical and applied ramifications, whose educational dimension in higher education remains scarcely documented. This systematic bibliometric review, complemented by a thematic classification of content, examined the evolution, productivity, and thematic structure of research on homotopy and determined the place that its educational dimension occupies within this literature. title: Shale‐Oil Micromigration and Sweet Spot Evaluation of the Shahejie Formation in the Dongying Sag, Bohai Bay Basin
abstract: ABSTRACT Strong heterogeneity of lacustrine shales in China hinders high‐precision shale‐oil sweet spot delineation, whereas the conventional “hydrocarbon generation‐retention” paradigm fails to account for widespread hydrocarbon micromigration. title: Multi-centennial precipitation reconstructions for Dublin: comparing documentary-instrumental and circulation-based approaches
abstract: Long precipitation records are needed to place recent droughts and wet periods in their historical context. This study combines documentary weather accounts, early rain-gauge measurements, atmospheric-circulation and temperature indices, and tree-ring isotope evidence to reconstruct precipitation for contrasting lowland and upland water-resource domains for the Greater Dublin Area (GDA). abstract: This study investigated the temperature-dependent postmortem metabolism and structural dynamics of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) stored at 4 °C and 20 °C. abstract: The restructuring of industrial cities takes various forms depending on local conditions and strategic choices. One approach to addressing this challenge is to link industrial park development with the circular economy. Some of these initiatives are led by local governments, creating a governance dilemma as they are expected to enable both public value creation and business profitability. This article examines the role of city government and its relationships with key stakeholders in building a green growth coalition around a recycling-oriented industrial area. abstract: Air pollution is an acute environmental challenge to the sustainability and even human health, but traditional methods of visualization do not always succeed in clearly displaying the multidimensional relationship between the measured multidimensional pollutant and the resulting effects thereof. abstract: The scientific characterization and information fusion of complex electromagnetic spectral spaces remain fundamental challenges because existing models often rely on inconsistent electromagnetic representations and loosely organized data structures across dimensions. abstract: ABSTRACT In aerosol‐ and condensation‐dominated corrosive environments, ion transport through coatings and surface droplet retention jointly govern corrosion initiation and propagation. However, existing strategies emphasize spatial diffusion barriers while overlooking interfacial liquid regulation. title: Unreported mass movement cascades and future Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) hazard in Jammu and Kashmir, Western Himalaya
abstract: The Warwan sub-basin in Jammu and Kashmir is a remote glaciated region containing several glacial lakes and has recently experienced population growth and infrastructure development. Due to inaccessibility and geomorphic masking, multiple mass movement events, including avalanches and glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs), have remained largely unreported. title: CellScore: an open-source image-based pipeline for automated cell quantification in microalgae
abstract: Accurate quantification of microalgal cell density is essential for both basic research and industrial applications, as it directly reflects culture growth, productivity, and physiological status. There are existing methods routinely used to measure cell counts, although many are limited by high cost, labor-intensive workflows, or steep technical barriers. abstract: Satellite-derived observations of inland waters are widely used in environmental monitoring, often forming the basis of long-term analyses in the absence of continuous in situ measurements. abstract: Context Wildlife monitoring is a crucial component of conservation management, and drones are an increasingly important tool for wildlife surveys. This study evaluated antiparasitic effects of glutaraldehyde (GA) against C. irritans tomonts and its therapeutic potential during C. irritans infection in large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea). Therefore, the investigation of microbial life in diverse environments can reveal bacteria with unique physiological and biochemical traits, which may be useful for biotechnological applications. abstract: Parasitoid wasps are important biological control agents, but their small size and subtle morphological differences hinder rapid identification and require taxonomic expertise. This study developed a computer vision framework for recognizing parasitoid wasps from single-plane microscopy images. This study characterized metabolic changes associated with different levels of G. boninense infection in oil palm stem tissue using untargeted gas chromatography–mass spectrometry metabolomics. abstract: This study investigates the machinability of Monel 400 under four machining environments: dry cutting, Minimum Quantity Lubrication (MQL), cryogenic liquid nitrogen (LN₂) cooling, and hybrid cryogenic–minimum quantity lubrication (Cryo-MQL). abstract: This study tackles the persistent head–efficiency trade-off in centrifugal pump impeller design by developing a data-efficient, constraint-based optimization framework that integrates CFD with response surface methodology (RSM). abstract: Wall-bounded turbulent flows play a central role in engineering and geophysical applications. title: Two snapshots of fish diversity and body size in an Amazonian market
abstract: Tropical freshwater fisheries support both biodiversity and human livelihoods, yet long-term fishery characteristics data remain scarce across much of the Amazon Basin. abstract: Large-scale ecosystem restoration requires spatial planning tools that identify where limited resources are most likely to deliver durable ecological benefits. abstract: Image captioning models are vulnerable to adversarial examples that can induce descriptions inconsistent with visual evidence, commonsense knowledge, or physical rules. abstract: Coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) microscopy enables label-free chemical imaging of biological samples and materials. abstract: Landslide is a common geohazard that often occurs in mountainous areas. abstract: Spectral 3D computer vision combines wavelength-resolved measurements with geometric information to support material-aware reconstruction, perception, and scene analysis. However, the literature remains fragmented across hyperspectral and multispectral sensing, cross-spectral depth and pose estimation, spectral point clouds, LiDAR–hyperspectral fusion, and neural scene representations.
