title: Factores ambientales y constructivos que promueven el deterioro prematuro de viviendas costeras de Veracruz, México
abstract: El deterioro prematuro de estructuras de concreto reforzado en zonas costeras resulta de la acción combinada de la agresividad del ambiente marítimo y las deficiencias de la construcción informal. El presente trabajo identifica y cuantifica los factores determinantes del deterioro en viviendas de la costa central de Veracruz bajo la hipótesis de un modelo multicausal, a partir de un diagnóstico exploratorio en 65 estructuras ubicadas en ocho localidades costeras. title: Spatial differentiation and refined susceptibility mapping of flash floods in Chongqing, southwest China
abstract: Chongqing's environmental heterogeneity complicates flash-flood susceptibility assessment. Using 596 historical occurrence points and an equal number of pseudo-absence samples, this study combined K-means clustering, frequency ratio analysis, and random forest modelling to compare unified and partitioned approaches. Two locally interspersed environmental types were identified: a drainage-network convergence type in the western hills and valleys and a mountain-hillslope type in the northeastern and southeastern mountains. title: A Regional Screening Workflow for Urban Differential Land Subsidence Risk Using the European Ground Motion Service: The Emilia-Romagna Region Case Study (Italy)
abstract: In 2022, the Copernicus Program launched the European Ground Motion Service (EGMS), providing open-access ground displacement products across Europe. This development created the need for methodologies to evaluate these datasets and integrate them into risk assessment frameworks. This study proposes an operational screening workflow for differential land subsidence risk based on EGMS Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) displacement measurements. abstract: To examine the quality of synergy and potential mismatch risks between production and recreational functions during the multifunctional transformation of freshwater fisheries, this study constructs a composite index of recreational fisheries development using panel data from 29 Chinese provinces from 2008 to 2023. Freshwater aquaculture efficiency is measured using a benevolent cross-efficiency model incorporating both desirable and undesirable outputs. abstract: ABSTRACT Mango ( Mangifera indica L.) dry matter (DM) content is a critical quality indicator determining consumer acceptance and commercial value, yet conventional oven‐drying methods are destructive and time‐consuming. Visible and near‐infrared (Vis‐NIR) spectroscopy offers a rapid and non‐consumptive alternative, but existing models suffer from poor generalizability due to spectrally homogeneous training sets. abstract: Introduction The effects of historical industrialization on health are well documented and frequently acknowledged in bioarchaeology, particularly in studies focusing on the health of European or North American populations of the 17th-19th centuries. Specifically, the negative impacts of coal burning and factory pollution on air quality and UV exposure are commonly cited in bioarchaeological research as primary influences in vitamin D deficiencies in historical industrialized populations. title: Modeling afforestation suitability in the Cross-Niger transition forest through remote sensing and analytical hierarchy process to advance global goals
abstract: Afforestation is a crucial strategy for conserving biodiversity, mitigating climate change, and preventing land degradation to accomplish Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.2. It is the process of establishing forests in previously unforested areas. Accordingly, the study integrates remote sensing and the analytical hierarchy process (AHP) to identify optimal sites for afforestation suitability that support SDGs within the Cross Niger transition forest. abstract: Abstract Purpose The present study aims to investigate the dynamic behavior of a magnetorheological tuned liquid column damper (MR-TLCD) coupled to a single degree of freedom (1 DoF) mechanical system and to validate a reduced-order analytical model through parametric identification. Methods Forced vibration tests are performed using a discrete sine-sweep excitation technique to obtain accelerance frequency response functions of the coupled system, with and without magnetic field application. title: Mitigating cycle skipping in full waveform inversion using max-pooling-based approximate envelope and shot patching
abstract: Full waveform inversion (FWI) can produce accurate subsurface velocity models. However, the lack of sufficiently low-frequency content in field data often causes cycle skipping and traps the inversion in local minima. The Hilbert-transform envelope (HTE) provides a low-frequency representation that helps mitigate cycle skipping, but it may be insufficient when the initial velocity model is highly inaccurate. title: Assessing long-term and seasonal changes of post-mining lakes using multispectral remote sensing
abstract: Flooding and water reclamation of former underground and opencast workings of the former “Friendship of Nations–Babina Shaft” brown coal mine, has led to the formation of an anthropogenic lake district in Western Poland. The water reservoirs of this lake district are characterized by different origins, multicolored waters, low pH, and high concentration of iron compounds. This publication focuses on the spatiotemporal changes of 26 lakes located within the aforementioned post-mining area between 2016 and 2025. title: Field-Based Evaluation of Water Quality, Macroinvertebrates and Sediment in the Downstream Segment of the Upper Konto Sub-Watershed, Indonesia
abstract: As the last self-purification zone before inflow enters Selorejo Reservoir, the downstream reach of the Upper Konto Sub-watershed is critical for controlling pollutant and sediment transfer. An integrated ecohydraulic approach was used in this study to evaluate the water quality, sediment characteristics, and ecological condition under organic pollution pressure. Water quality was assessed at six sites and deposited sediments at four sites during the dry and rainy seasons. title: RGB Image - Based Characterization of Dolomite Weathering for Mining Applications
abstract: This study explores the potential of RGB image - based analysis as a predictive approach for characterizing weathering in dolomites and for guiding excavation tool optimization in mining engineering. The investigation was conducted at the Dolomite Quarry (G e bze, NW Türkiye), where two stratigraphic levels (A – B) of a representative dolomitic profile were systematically analyzed. title: Advances in Wire-Laser Metal Deposition: Bimetallic Fabrication, Defect Mitigation, and Future Directions
abstract: Abstract Wire-Laser Metal Deposition (W-LMD) is a transformative additive manufacturing technology that utilizes a laser heat source to melt metallic wire feedstock for the high-efficiency fabrication of large-scale, near-net-shape components. The technology is distinguished from other manufacturing processes due to its high material utilization efficiency and superior safety compared to metal powder-based systems. title: Vision-semantic alignment with hierarchical consistency constraints for multi-attribute museum artifact classification
abstract: The digitization of museum collections has produced vast multimodal data, yet existing automated classification methods treat classification attributes as independent flat categories and overlook the hierarchical taxonomic structures embedded in museum cataloging systems, frequently yielding predictions that are taxonomically illegitimate. We present a multimodal hierarchical learning framework for multi-attribute museum artifact classification that combines vision-semantic alignment with hierarchical consistency constraints. title: Balancing Innovation and Sustainability: Digital Technology-Driven Tourism Growth and the Overtourism Challenge
abstract: The study examined the dual role of digital technology adoption in tourism growth and the threat of overtourism, highlighting the need to balance digital innovation with sustainable destination management. The findings show that capacity score (-0.70) and visitor volume (+0.69) are the strongest predictors of overtourism risk, while deficient accommodation infrastructure increases risk. title: Behind the missing skull: A unique fin configuration redefines the Jurassic shark † Palaeoscyllium formosum Wagner, 1857 (Neoselachii, Galeomorphi)
abstract: The holotype of the type species † Palaeoscyllium formosum Wagner, 1857 from the Jurassic of Europe, lacking the cranial region, is herein carefully re-described and re-evaluated to clarify the taxonomic and nomenclatural status of this taxon. Post-cranial morphological characters identified through direct revision of the holotype are extensively compared with those of morphologically similar fossil and extant sharks, with particular emphasis on species-specific diagnostic traits. title: Megacity particulate matter airsheds redefine urban pollution exposure boundary
abstract: Urban air quality assessments typically focus on populations within municipal boundaries, despite atmospheric transport allowing pollution to affect large populations well beyond city limits. Here we develop a data-driven, reduced-complexity airshed framework to delineate the spatial domain relevant to fine particulate matter (particles no larger than 2.5 micrometers in diameter) exposure for 53 global megacities. title: Hierarchical Bayesian modeling of hotel availability using high-resolution panel data: Application to post-earthquake accommodation market dynamics following the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake
abstract: This study proposes a hierarchical Bayesian model to estimate regional accommodation availability using high-resolution booking data from an online travel agency. The model employs a binomial structure to separate facility scale from vacancy probability, capturing facility-level heterogeneity beyond aggregated data. It incorporates booking lead-time information up to one month before check-in. title: Reference-Based Exterior Orientation of Non-Metric Oblique Aerial Imagery with Reliability Screening and Multi-Frame Recovery

title: Essential oil extraction: critical appraisal of conventional and novel techniques
abstract: Essential oils have been valued for centuries by communities worldwide. These aromatic and volatile compounds possess antioxidant, antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties. These therapeutic properties are primarily attributed to the presence of monoterpenes and sesquiterpenes. Further, these oils are utilized as valuable ingredients in the industrial sector. title: Improving Cross-Regional Generalizability of Bridge Deck Deterioration Prediction through Transfer Learning and Explainable Discrete-Time Survival Models
abstract: Data-driven deterioration models for bridge decks are trained and validated on pooled national data but are used by individual agencies whose climate, materials and inspection practice differ. On the nationwide National Bridge Inventory panel of 150,144 concrete decks, the published discrete-time gradient-boosted hazard model (DT-GBH) reaches a C-index of 0.769 on a random split but only 0.647 on states withheld from training, no better than Cox regression, while its 5-year calibration error grows from 0.009 to 0.050. title: A forward genetics workflow for EMS mutagenesis, agar-based screening, and genomic analysis of Macrocystis pyrifera gametophytes
abstract: In this study we establish a proof-of-concept workflow for conducting a mutagenesis screen in Macrocystis pyrifera g ametophytes. We accomplish this by treating the gametophytes with chemical mutagen ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS), which is known to induce G > A and C > T transitions. We then culture the EMS-treated gametophytes on solid media to immobilize them for streamlined screening and strain isolation. title: Pose-guided cross-scale attentional transformer learning with spatial–contextual fusion for explainable frame-based tennis stroke recognition
abstract: Understanding sports actions from visual data has become increasingly important for intelligent coaching systems, athlete performance analysis, and automated video analytics. Tennis presents a particularly challenging problem because many stroke categories differ only in subtle body poses, racket positions, and spatial interactions. Existing convolutional and transformer models often struggle to capture both fine-grained local patterns and broader contextual information at the same time. abstract: As the core component of electrical equipment, the abnormal concentration of dissolved gases in the oil of transformers not only affects the stability of the power system, but also may bring serious safety hazards. To conduct fault analysis on transformers, the study first utilized improved sand dune cat swarm optimization to improve the parameters of long short-term memory networks, and built a gas concentration prediction model based on long short-term memory networks and parameter optimization. title: Port Electrification: Definitions, Pathways, and Grid Impact Assessment
abstract: Abstract Ports are increasingly central to decarbonization strategies, but port electrification is defined inconsistently across academic and policy literature. This ambiguity matters because different definitions imply different electricity-demand profiles, peak loads, connection requirements, and grid-upgrade needs. We examine how port-electrification pathways emerge under different combinations of contextual dynamics, policy signals and technological development, and how these differences matter for grid planning. title: State of Health Estimation for Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Physics-Informed Health Factors and Cascaded Optimized HKELM
abstract: Abstract Accurate state of health (SOH) estimation is essential for ensuring the safety, reliability, and economic operation of lithium-ion battery systems. However, the battery aging process is highly nonlinear and strongly affected by feature quality, parameter optimization efficiency, and model generalization under limited samples. title: Optimal Allocation of Distributed Generation Using an Improved Cloud Drift Optimization Algorithm with Brownian–Lévy Search Mechanism
abstract: Reliable optimization of distributed generation (DG) planning requires algorithms capable of handling nonlinear, high-dimensional, and constrained search spaces while avoiding premature convergence. This paper proposes an Improved Cloud Drift Optimization (ICDO) algorithm for engineering optimization and optimal DG allocation in radial distribution networks. title: The bovine milk microbiome as a One Health interface for antimicrobial resistance, food safety and nutrition
abstract: Bovine milk is both a nutrient-rich food matrix and a microbial ecosystem in which composition, food safety and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) intersect. However, these domains are often considered separately, limiting understanding of how milk composition, microbial ecology and resistance dynamics interact across the dairy chain. title: Microplásticos em ambientes aquáticos: uma revisão sobre a bioacumuação em peixes e suas consequências para a saúde animal e humana
abstract: A poluição por microplásticos em ambientes aquáticos representa uma ameaça crescente à vida dos ecossistemas e à saúde pública em todo o mundo. Devido à sua ampla distribuição e capacidade de se movimentarem entre compartimentos ecológicos, esses polímeros alcançam diversos níveis tróficos através da cadeia alimentar. Este trabalho teve como objetivo realizar uma revisão bibliográfica sobre os impactos da bioacumulação de microplásticos na saúde dos peixes e suas consequências para os seres humanos. abstract: Flood risk communication requires methods that translate technically robust flood information into spatial representations that can be interpreted in relation to buildings, roads, and other urban assets. Existing 3D visualisation approaches are often technically sophisticated but are not consistently demonstrated for routine GIS practice, while other approaches emphasise public engagement without documenting a GIS-based workflow. abstract: Nabire Port is the main logistics node of Central Papua Province, yet its service performance has rarely been examined from a queueing perspective using operational data recorded at the level of individual arrivals. This study analyses ship services and freight-forwarding truck services at Nabire Port as two separately observed subsystems and combines their subsystem-level results into a constructed logistics-time indicator, not a verified tandem queue. title: Out of Amazonia: Biogeography of a Neotropical fern radiation
abstract: The Neotropics are Earth’s most species-rich region, so understanding how this diversity has emerged is of great interest. Here we address this question by assessing how species richness, speciation and dispersal are connected to geological and climatic history using the Neotropical fern genus Danaea (Marattiaceae) as a model. title: Anthropogenic atmospheric heavy metal emission inventories in China: Theoretical frameworks, methodological evolution, and future perspectives
abstract: Heavy metals (HMs) pollution is a global environmental and public health concern due to its persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity. Reliable atmospheric HM emission inventories (AHMEI) are essential for identifying source characteristics and supporting air pollution mitigation policies. This study summarizes the historical evolution and methodological advances in AHMEI quantification, including both top-down and bottom-up approaches. abstract: Abstract AI-based ensemble weather prediction is emerging as a new paradigm for probabilistic forecasting, yet its ability to represent the key physical processes that govern high-impact extreme rainfall remains unclear. Here, we compare an AI-based ensemble system (AIFS-CRPS) with a conventional physics-based ensemble (IFS-ENS) in relation to the July 2024 extreme rainfall event in Hunan, China, associated with the remnants of Typhoon GAEMI. title: Politicized science communication and motivated reasoning: social media responses to the Fukushima radioactive water discharge in Japan, South Korea, and China
abstract: The Fukushima radioactive water discharge became a major international controversy in East Asia, where scientific risk, evaluations of government and institutional actors, and diplomatic conflict intersected. While the Japanese government promoted the discharge policy by emphasizing its scientific safety, the South Korean government adopted a relatively cooperative stance toward Japan, whereas the Chinese government strongly criticized the discharge. abstract: В данном исследовании прогнозируются будущие изменения метеорологических показателей (температуры воздуха, относительной влажности, атмосферного давления, скорости ветра и количества осадков) для города Ташкента на основе нейронной сети. title: Integrated Human–Equipment Reliability Assessment of Ammonia Loss of Containment During Shore-to-Ship Bunkering
abstract: Current studies on ammonia bunkering safety have largely focused on release scenarios, dispersion modelling and equipment-related hazards, while human error, equipment failure and emergency response are often assessed separately. This creates an important gap because the safety of ammonia bunkering depends on how operators and engineered systems work together during both routine and abnormal conditions. abstract: Study’s main aim was to shed the light on data democratization as one of business intelligence practices and examine its influence in increasing efficiency within multi-national organizations in terms of (accessibility, interpretability, collaboration, governance, empowerment, scalability and feedback loop). title: Hybrid Semi‐Quantitative Risk Assessment for Aging Offshore Platforms: A HAZOP–FMEA–Bow‐Tie Framework With Sensitivity Analysis and KRI‐Based Governance
abstract: Aging offshore installations increasingly operate beyond their original design life, yet conventional periodic risk assessments capture barrier degradation only intermittently. This study presents a barrier-conditioned semi-quantitative risk-assessment workflow that integrates Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP), Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and bow-tie barrier analysis. title: Evaluation and improvement of the cold pool parameterization in the LMDZ climate model against Large Eddy Simulations
abstract: Cold pools, formed under clouds by the evaporation of precipitation, play a central role in maintaining and organizing atmospheric convection. It is suspected that their absence in climate models may lead to significant errors in the representation of convection, such as the premature convection extinction after sunset. abstract: Pre-demolition and Pre-reconstruction audits can enable more circular deconstruction by identifying recoverable materials and planning End-of-Life (EoL) pathways. abstract: In nature, all microbial populations form biofilms. Aggregated microbial communities attached to surfaces form a biofilm, surrounded by biosynthesised polymeric substances. In polymicrobial biofilm formation, the interspecific interactions within microbial communities remain unclear. abstract: Global temperatures have averaged 1.2 °C above pre-industrial levels over the past decade, yet regional warming patterns and remaining warming budgets under Paris Agreement limits remain uncertain owing to insufficient historical observations. Here we quantify and attribute warming across all IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) regions since pre-industrial times using a Bayesian framework combining multi-model simulations with observations, enabling robust estimates in data-sparse regions. abstract: Panzhou City of Guizhou Province is a core coal-mining base in Southwest China. Long-term intensive underground coal exploitation has triggered widespread mining-induced ground subsidence, threatening regional ecological security and the stability of linear transportation infrastructures. title: Seaweed-Based Biostimulants in Sustainable Agriculture: Bioactive Compounds, Mechanisms, and Applications Across Plant, Livestock, and Aquaculture Systems
abstract: : Seaweeds (macroalgae) are being increasingly recognized as multifunctional agricultural inputs. This is due to the diverse set of compounds they provide, namely polysaccharides, phytohormones, phenolic antioxidants, and essential minerals. This review presents current knowledge on the bioactive compounds in seaweeds and the mechanisms through which they improve productivity across plant, livestock, and aquaculture systems. title: Dynamic electrochemical modelling and parameter estimation of PEM electrolyzers across broad thermal and pressure envelopes using BO-LSBoost
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates accurate electrochemical parameter identification in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer systems (PEMWES), which is essential for multiphysics digital twins and dynamic control. Conventional analytical and metaheuristic methods may suffer from numerical instability, parameter coupling, and high computational latency under coupled thermal and pressure variations. title: Groundwater Storage Trends in the Great Salt Lake Basin, 2002–2024
abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater storage change in the Great Salt Lake Basin (GSLB) is difficult to quantify because monitoring data are uneven. title: The Emerging Role of UAV for Heathland Monitoring and Conservation: State of the Art and Perspectives
abstract: ABSTRACT Heathland ecosystems have undergone substantial degradation over the past 150 years, mainly driven by land‐use changes, agricultural intensification and climate change. As they support significant biodiversity, their conservation is a major concern for both scientists, practitioners and public authorities. Heathland monitoring and conservation can be addressed through field‐based ecology and remote sensing, which rely on distinct but overlapping concepts, data and methodologies. abstract: Urban development boundaries require continuous monitoring as land use and available development space change with land approval, supply, development and boundary adjustments. Conventional assessments rely on static inventories and repeated polygon overlays, making parcel-level information difficult to maintain. This study presents a parcel-based Spatial Ledger framework for tracking land-use changes within urban development boundaries. title: Toward climate-resilient date palm agriculture in the United Arab Emirates: a strategic triangulated knowledge mapping
abstract: The date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) plays a vital role in food security, rural livelihoods, and cultural heritage in the hyper-arid United Arab Emirates (UAE). However, increasing climate stress, water scarcity, and persistent production constraints threaten the sector’s long-term resilience. Addressing these challenges requires a comprehensive understanding of existing research and its limitations. title: Evaluating health indicators on few run-to-failure units: Unit sensitivity and acquisition confounders in four public archives
abstract: Raw-signal health indicators are validated by a pooled cross-validated coefficient against a reference measurement, often on few physical units. We measure how such a coefficient depends on its units by deleting one unit at a time on four public run-to-failure archives: Li-ion batteries, bearings, milling tools and fatigued lap joints. title: Negotiating educational value in children’s media: A Design-Cycle Framework from a U.S. public media production
abstract: The development of children’s educational media is typically evaluated through analyses of final products, with limited attention to the processes through which educational value is constructed. This exploratory study examines how educational, narrative, and disciplinary priorities are negotiated during production. Using qualitative content analysis, we analyze 163 feedback comments generated across iterative development stages of three episodes of a preschool educational animated series. title: Global threat of Fusarium head blight to wheat production: Projecting host‐pathogen overlap under climate change
abstract: Societal Impact Statement Wheat is one of the world's most important staple crops, but its production is increasingly threatened by Fusarium head blight, a disease that reduces yield and grain quality. We mapped where wheat and its major disease‐causing fungi are likely to overlap now and under future climate change. Our results show that several major wheat‐producing regions may remain or become persistently vulnerable, including parts of North America, South America, Europe, East Asia, Australia, and New Zealand. title: Estimating the resilience of non-stationary systems
abstract: A wide body of work has applied the concept of critical slowing down to estimate the stability of different Earth system components. Most of them - such as global vegetation - are inherently non-stationary, for example due to strong seasonal forcing that complicates the estimation of their resilience to external perturbations. Here, we introduce a method to account for non-stationarity in estimating the resilience of diverse synthetic and real-world systems via a regression-based formulation of the Langevin equation. Our method does not require extensive data pre-processing, is robust to gaps

abstract: Plant-derived extracts are promising renewable corrosion inhibitors, yet their chemically heterogeneous composition complicates understanding of interfacial adsorption and concentration-dependent protection. This study investigates Matoa seed extract (MSE), recovered from seed biomass residue, as a multicomponent inhibitor for low-carbon steel (LCS) in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 . title: Weather-induced colour change in wood: material response in different European locations
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the colour evolution of Norway spruce wood during one year of natural weathering across multiple European locations as part of a Round Robin experiment. Colour measurements ( CIE Lab ) were performed on samples with monthly-resolved exposure duration to quantify discolouration and determine total colour change ( ΔE ). The results show that weathering induces rapid colour modification, with the most pronounced changes occurring within the first month of exposure. title: Multi-task learning for multi-goal path planning with path-cost estimation and heuristic-guided RRT sampling
abstract: Multi-goal path planning (MGPP) requires identifying a closed, collision-free trajectory that visits a set of goals in an optimal sequence. This is typically formulated as a Physical Traveling Salesman Problem, where the quality of the visiting order depends on an undirected complete graph with precise edge weights representing inter-vertex path lengths. title: Adaptive Integration of Wastewater and Digital Proxies for Infectious Disease Forecasting: A Flexible Pipeline Evaluated Across Multi-Country Datasets
abstract: Accurate infectious disease forecasting using wastewater surveillance data is often limited by small sample sizes and the inherent stochasticity of environmental signals. We developed a data-centric modeling framework that embeds feature selection and applied it to one-week-ahead prediction of reported COVID-19 cases at 11 sites in France, Spain and Japan during 2020-2021, before the emergence of the Omicron variant. abstract: The endonuclear symbiont Holospora obtusa invades the macronucleus of Paramecium caudatum using an infectious-form invasion tip containing a major 89-kDa periplasmic protein implicated in escape from the host digestive vacuole and macronuclear invasion. Sequence-based analyses placed this protein within a Holospora-specific family and predicted an N-terminal membrane-anchoring module and a long α-helical C-terminal region. abstract: The southwestern Yangtze Block hosts several Mesozoic low-temperature metallogenic systems, including the Youjiang Au-As-Sb-Hg province and the Sichuan-Yunnan-Guizhou Pb-Zn province. Near their transition, the Pingqiao fluorite-cookeite deposit represents a rare example of a cookeite-dominated hydrothermal Li mineralization, yet its relationship to the surrounding regional hydrothermal ore-forming systems remains poorly understood. title: Investigating production of TeV-scale muons in extensive air shower at 2400 m underground
abstract: Abstract Deep underground experiments present a new avenue to probe the first interactions in extensive air showers or hadronic interactions in the extreme forward phase space. The China Jinping Underground Laboratory, characterized by a vertical rock overburden of 2400 m, provides an exceptionally effective shield against cosmic muons with energies below 3 TeV. The surviving high-energy muons, produced in the first interactions of extensive air showers, open a unique observational window into primary cosmic rays from tens of TeV up to the PeV scale and beyond. title: Moderating Role of Global Financial Integration in the Climate Finance–Digitalisation–Renewable Energy Nexus: Empirical Evidence From Pacific Island Countries
abstract: ABSTRACT Pacific Island Countries contribute a negligible share of global greenhouse gas emissions yet face existential threats from climate change. This study examines how climate finance, digitalisation and renewable energy consumption affect carbon dioxide emissions per capita in 11 Pacific Island Countries over 2000–2024, and whether global financial integration moderates these effects. abstract: Abstract Species Distribution Modeling (SDM) is central to biodiversity assessment, yet its diagnostic outputs rarely translate into spatially explicit conservation strategies. We present an AI-driven Geodesign framework that embeds Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) modeling in an iterative refinement cycle to produce phased conservation priorities. abstract: Thin-bed and small-extent seismic facies are geologically consequential yet difficult to segment reliably, with characteristic errors such as smearing, fragmentation, and omission. title: Equity-aware multi-objective optimization of nature-based solutions for flood susceptibility reduction
abstract: Abstract Nature-based solutions (NBS) are increasingly promoted for flood mitigation, yet how to allocate limited resources while balancing aggregate effectiveness and social equity remains poorly understood. In particular, it is unclear whether directing greater mitigation benefits toward socially vulnerable communities necessarily requires substantial losses in overall flood-susceptibility reduction. abstract: This article examines the sustainability practices of four major Greek music cultural organizations: the Thessaloniki Concert Hall, the Athens Concert Hall, the State Orchestra of Thessaloniki, and the State Orchestra of Athens. Through a comparative analysis based on content analysis of official sources and semi-structured interviews with marketing directors, the study explores how these institutions engage with environmental, social, and economic sustainability, while treating digital innovation as a transversal enabling factor. abstract: Abstract The Madden‐Julian Oscillation (MJO), a crucial source of subseasonal predictability, experiences El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO) modulation whose impacts vary by event type. Using an analog‐based methodology that incorporates a history of dynamical system evolution and epsilon‐based neighborhoods, we quantify how Eastern‐Pacific (EP) and Central‐Pacific (CP) ENSO events distinctly regulate the predictability limit of the real‐time multivariate MJO (RMM) index. abstract: Water treatment infrastructure in Saudi Arabia is of course a vital public health function and is equally important in enabling industrial development, urban growth and the diversification of water supplies. You can't judge the reliability of that infrastructure on its capacity alone. An apparently continuous supply of water of poor quality could be a far more serious failure than a short-lived, isolated interruption. abstract: Pendataan dan pemantauan lahan sawah memerlukan integrasi informasi administratif, lokasi, dan riwayat kondisi untuk mendukung pengelolaan pertanian yang sistematis. International human rights law developed within a terrestrial matrix predicated on sovereign territorial jurisdiction, geographical borders, and the natural availability of an unmanaged biological biosphere. abstract: Integrating big data into hydrogen systems is essential for enhancing performance and sustainability by improving efficiency, reducing costs and boosting energy security. The primary objective of this research is to provide a comparative decision framework for evaluating and ranking the big data challenges in hydrogen systems. abstract: Surfactin, a lipopeptide biosurfactant, has drawn growing attention for agricultural use, but its large-scale production remains limited by substrate cost, low titers, and downstream recovery. This review compiles quantitative data on agro-industrial residues as feedstocks, comparing substrate classes, fermentation performance, optimization routes, recovery methods, and field-level applications reported to date, drawing mainly on Scopus-indexed literature published in 2016–2026 together with earlier key studies. abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a contribution to the development of evolutionary fuzzy optimization control for computational intelligence (CI)‐based robust visual simultaneous localization and mapping (VSLAM) in autonomous mobile robots. The proposed SLAM method integrates visual perception, image processing, model predictive control (MPC), and fuzzy logic to improve localization robustness and map consistency. title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of land surface temperature and vegetation cover in Thanjavur district Tamil Nadu India using remote sensing and GIS
abstract: Land Surface Temperature (LST) and vegetation dynamics are widely recognized as reliable indicators of environmental change, urbanization, and climate variability. Understanding their spatial and temporal interactions is essential for sustainable environmental planning, particularly in agriculturally intensive regions experiencing rapid land-use transformation. This study investigates the spatio-temporal variations of LST and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu, India, using multi-temporal Landsat imagery acquired during 2011 and 2021. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines patterns of socioeconomic inequality among Brazil's 26 state capitals and the Federal District, totaling 27 capitals, and assesses the discriminatory capacity of SDG‐related indicators within the country's five major regions. As crucial elements of the host's innate immune system, Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs) are viewed as a compelling alternative or synergistic adjunct to conventional antibiotics, owing to their broad‐spectrum antimicrobial activity, unique bactericidal mechanisms, and low propensity for inducing resistance. title: Heavy metal pollution in cement tile production: impact evaluation through grey water footprint, ecological risk and life cycle assessment
abstract: Cement tile manufacturing is a traditional industry in Iran, yet wastewater-related heavy metal pollution raises sustainability concerns. This study evaluates the environmental pollution using three distinct approaches. (1) The grey water footprint (GWF) quantifies the volume of freshwater required to assimilate pollution, based on net discharged loads and the receiving environment's limitations. abstract: Abstract Fallout radionuclide (FRN) archived in soils are key tracers of soil redistribution, sediment dynamics, and associated carbon fluxes, yet their global application is limited by poorly constrained baselines in the Southern Hemisphere. Here, we present the first hemisphere-scale baseline and uncertainty maps of 137 Cs and 239+240 Pu soil inventories. abstract: Abstract This paper presents a novel methodology for the strategic placement, control, and integration of a Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) within grid-connected and islanded microgrid (µG) systems that integrate Distributed Generation (DG). abstract: Abstract Power quality disturbances, particularly voltage sags and swells, pose significant challenges to modern distribution networks with increasing penetration of nonlinear loads and renewable energy resources. Dynamic voltage restorers (DVRs) are highly effective custom power devices for mitigating such disturbances; however, their performance depends strongly on the employed control strategy. title: Plant invasions in Natura 2000 habitats in Poland are driven primarily by macroclimatic factors
abstract: Invasive plants pose an ecological threat around the world. Their influence can also be observed in protected areas such as the European Ecological Network Natura 2000. Although invasions can endanger protected habitats, the specific impact of invasive species in such areas and the factors that determine their spread remain understudied. This study aimed to analyse the factors influencing the probability of plant invasion in five groups of habitat types protected under the EU Habitats Directive, based on Polish State Monitoring of Natura 2000 data. abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) fiber is widely used to develop Engineered Geopolymer Composites (EGC), but its relatively high environmental and economic burdens motivate the exploration of renewable alternatives. This study systematically investigated the effects of PVA fiber content and progressive substitution of PVA fiber by bamboo fiber on the mechanical performance, environmental impact, and material cost of EGC. abstract: The wedding industry in Bali is developing as a strategic opportunity for hotels to increase wedding package sales, but Six Senses Uluwatu, Bali experienced a decline in sales from 100 events in 2024 to 87 events in 2025. This study aims to analyze the 7P marketing mix strategy to increase wedding package sales. The study used a descriptive qualitative method. Indigenous Nations have long maintained relationships among salmon, people, and their environments through Indigenous knowledge systems, governance, stewardship, and reciprocal responsibility. abstract: This review synthesizes emerging literature on tourism crowding by organizing findings into five dimensions: perception, experience, destination, management, and response. Crowding perception highlights the subjective nature of tourists’ discomfort, shaped by cognitive and emotional evaluations. abstract: Digital twin irrigation districts rely on stable multiscale 3D representation of terrain and hydraulic objects, but multi-LOD terrain transitions often cause floating, misalignment, and discontinuous dynamic behavior. Existing methods focus on static geo-metric alignment and lack semantic-aware dynamic constraint mechanisms across scales. This work proposes a semantically driven dynamic integration framework for multi-LOD terrain and hydraulic objects. title: A lightweight dual-domain attention YOLO for small object detection in remote sensing images
abstract: Small object detection (SOD) in remote sensing images (RSIs) remains challenging due to limited pixel representation, complex background interference, and the requirement for computationally efficient lightweight models. To address these issues, this paper proposes LDA-YOLO, a lightweight detection framework built upon YOLOv8 that integrates adaptive refinement of multi-level features and dual-domain attention to enhance fine-grained perception while maintaining low computational cost. title: EVOLUTION OF INDUSTRIAL SYSTEMS: FROM THE HUMANIZATION OF INDUSTRY 5.0 TO THE BIO-DIGITAL SYMBIOTIC INDUSTRY 6.0
abstract: At the beginning of the 21st century, the world witnessed the Fourth Industrial Revolution (Industry 4.0), which laid the foundations for digitalization, cloud computing, and the Internet of Things (IoT). Despite undeniable technological successes, Industry 4.0 faced criticism for its "technocentricity" a model in which machine efficiency often took precedence over human well-being and ecological balance.

abstract: Abstract Heat-stress exposure in maritime regions reflects the combined influence of temperature and humidity, yet these relationships remain poorly characterized in small, cool-temperate regions such as Prince Edward Island (PEI), Canada. title: Addressing the acoustic signature of organic-rich mudstones for energy production and sub-surface storage
abstract: Organic-rich mudstones are commonly identified using borehole geochemical measurements and petrophysical proxies. Yet reproducible log-tied acoustic criteria for their discrimination remain limited. This study compares the acoustic character of organic-rich vs. organic-lean mudstones, and their distinct borehole petrophysical and lithological properties, based on data from four tectonically isolated basins and intervals. abstract: La inteligencia artificial puede mejorar la gestión pública, pero también dificultar la comprensión y revisión de decisiones que afectan derechos. abstract: Abstract Mesoscale moisture aggregation and cloud organization in shallow convection have gained much attention regarding their role in Earth's energy budget and cloud feedbacks on climate. abstract: Introduction Child labor remains a complex, multidimensional challenge in Indigenous and geographically isolated island communities in the Philippines. While much of the existing literature focuses on quantitative economic metrics or direct child self-reports, this study explores how parents and community leaders in Tawi-Tawi navigate, perceive, and make sense of the contextual barriers surrounding child labor and its multifaceted developmental impacts. abstract: Quinoa ( Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is a stress tolerant pseudocereal recognized for its nutritional value and adaptation to marginal environments. abstract: Waterlogging-induced hypoxia is becoming an increasingly important constraint to crop production under climate change. Although quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) is recognized for its tolerance to drought and salinity, its response to hypoxia remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of hypoxia on growth, root development, biomass accumulation, and individual seed yield in 28 quinoa genotypes. abstract: Ukraine has a unique ethnopharmacological heritage shaped by its exceptional floristic diversity, complex political history, and long-standing cross-cultural interactions with neighbouring regions. This narrative review provides a comprehensive and critical synthesis of the historical development of herbal medicine in the territory of modern Ukraine from the prehistoric and medieval periods to the early 21st century. abstract: Accurate site characterisation is essential in geotechnical engineering, but in practice, it is often constrained by the limited availability of field data such as cone penetration tests (CPTs). When combined with the complex three-dimensional variability of geological materials, this limitation makes the reconstruction of reliable ground models a persistent challenge. title: Fire Safety: Stage‐Dependent Fire Behavior, Performance Criteria, and Application‐Based Requirement
abstract: ABSTRACT Fire development is inherently stage‐dependent, with material responses and engineering concerns varying across fire scenarios and exposure conditions. Established fire safety engineering (FSE) and performance‐based design (PBD) approaches already connect fire development, test evidence, and mitigation strategies with defined safety objectives. Building on this foundation, this review examines the relationships among material fire behavior, testing methods, and application‐specific safety requirements across buildings, transportation, industrial processes, and energy storage systems.

abstract: The flight deck of a naval vessel is a high-risk operational environment in which a single initiating event can precipitate coupled hazard cascades encompassing concurrent fire propagation, progressive casualty deterioration, and damage-induced stability degradation. Conventional pre-plan-driven response approaches are architecturally ill-suited to such multi-hazard, temporally evolving scenarios, as they cannot adapt to stochastic hazard interactions in real time. abstract: Improper solid waste management (SWM) remains a critical environmental and public health challenge in peri-urban regions of developing countries, driven by weak infrastructure, socio-economic disparities and inadequate monitoring. abstract: Abstract Adaptive cruise control (ACC) relies on accurate range and relative-velocity measurements of the preceding vehicle, which frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar provides. This study presents a 77 GHz FMCW radar framework for ACC that integrates physically motivated models of rain, fog, and insect clutter with a two-dimensional cell-averaging constant false alarm rate (CA-CFAR) detector. abstract: Bicycle safety is essential for bikeability and transport efficiency, yet conventional surveys often fail to capture how people perceive cycling environments in real time because they depend on retrospective recall. This study proposes a video-based conversational AI chatbot survey, powered by large language models (LLMs), to collect perceptions of cycling safety and the reasons behind them. abstract: Abstract Socio-technical systems are becoming increasingly interconnected, heterogeneous, and dynamic while continuously evolving through new technologies, infrastructures, policies, resources, and operational practices. This revision leads to a re-interpretation of the Famennian succession, and the formal introduction of a new lithostratigraphic unit, the Santas Martas Formation. title: An improvement of global power tracking using skipping technique – based tunicate swarm algorithm for PV systems under partially shaded conditions
abstract: Irradiance on the PV modules is not distributed uniformly during partially shaded conditions (PSC). Bypass diodes employed to avoid the hot-spot phenomenon modify the power-voltage (P-V) curves such that several points corresponding to maximum power are generated. The metaheuristic algorithms track the global maximum power point (GMPP) by searching the whole space on the P-V characteristics. title: A Study on the Pathways for Transforming Practical Instruction in Digital and Intelligent Language Labs
abstract: The development of digital and intelligent information technologies has injected new momentum into language labs. This study thoroughly analyzes their profound impact on practical teaching, including their positive roles in language skill development and the innovation of teaching models—such as providing real-person-recorded foreign language materials for listening practice, creating innovative interactive platforms for oral training, and implementing blended online-offline teaching and flipped classroom practices. title: Advances in nanocellulose variants for sustainable food packaging and circular bioeconomy through network analysis
abstract: Nanocellulose is a promising renewable material for sustainable food packaging. This review examines cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs), cellulose nanofibers (CNFs), and bacterial cellulose (BC) by combining a network analysis of 689 Scopus-indexed documents (2010–2025) using VOSviewer, Tableau, and RStudio with a narrative review of their characteristics, applications, and role in the circular bioeconomy. title: A Study on the Geoeffective Event of 11 April 2022
abstract: Abstract Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) are the main drivers of geomagnetic storms. Studying their initial phases is important for understanding their propagation through the heliosphere and the effects they have on the Space Weather. In this work, as a case study, we investigate how SolO/Metis observations improve the accuracy in modeling a geoeffective CME that occurred on 11 April 2022. This event caused a geomagnetic storm of intensity of −81 nT in terms of Disturbance Storm Time (Dst) on 14 April 2022. This moderately geoeffective event serves as a challenging case to model and understand

title: Enhancing AI explainability and transparency through the integration of explainable AI and generative AI
abstract: This study examines how generative AI (GenAI)-mediated explanations of automated decision-making (ADM) shape users’ justice perceptions. It investigates how GenAI advances conversational XAI by enabling more open-ended and dynamically generated explanatory exchanges and examines their implications for the ethical evaluation of AI decisions beyond traditional usability and explainability outcomes. The study focuses on AI-driven loan evaluation contexts, where concerns about fairness, transparency, and accountability are especially salient. journal: Computers in Human Behavior Artificial Humans

title: Multi-objective optimization of hybrid semi-trailer powertrains based on data-driven matching and backward simulation
abstract: Heavy-duty commercial vehicles, despite accounting for less than 10% of the total vehicle parc, contribute nearly one-third of the total carbon emissions in the automotive industry. The electrification of heavy-duty vehicles represents a critical pathway to achieving sustainable and green transportation. Hybrid semi-trailer tractors combine the range of diesel vehicles with the advantages of electrification; their powertrain serves as the physical foundation of the entire vehicle, and its parameter matching plays a fundamental role in optimizing the vehicle’s overall energy consumption. title: Unveiling Dynamic Active‐Site Switching of NiFe Dual‐Atom Electrocatalysts With Axial Halogen Coordination for Enhanced Oxygen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT NiFe (hydr)oxides are among the most active oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts, yet their local structures, active sites, and synergistic effects remain under debate. Single‐atom catalysts (SACs), featuring atomically defined coordination environments, provide a model platform to address these questions, but their OER performance is limited. Here, we reveal for NiFe dual‐atom catalysts that dynamic active‐site switching from Fe to Fe‐Ni dual sites, coupled with axial halogen coordination, synergistically enhances OER. title: Physics-guided graph Transformer for composite pipeline damage detection
abstract: Composite pipelines are widely used in oil and gas transportation owing to their high specific strength and corrosion resistance. However, guided-wave-based damage localization remains challenging due to multimodal wave propagation, noise interference, complex propagation-path relationships, and limited labeled damage locations. To address these challenges, this study proposes a physics-guided graph Transformer (PGGT) framework for composite pipeline damage localization. title: Implementation of Legal Protection Against Environmental Activist
abstract: The numerous occurrences of environmental damage and other ecological crimes have led to legal problems and caused losses for affected communities. The objective of this study is to identify and analyze the legislative regulations concerning legal protection for environmental activists, the implementation of legal protection for environmental activists, and the challenges faced in its implementation. journal: Pena Justisia Media Komunikasi dan Kajian Hukum

title: Utilising Green Lean Six Sigma to Improve Sustainability in the Bakery Sector
abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to improve sustainability and environmentally friendly practices in an Irish bakery by reducing carbon emissions and reducing the use of single‐use plastics. Green lean six sigma (GLSS) methodology was utilised to improve sustainability performance. The use of single‐use plastics decreased by 33.9% through the adoption of intermediate bulk containers, the installation of solar panels and the purchase of green electricity, contributing to a 5% reduction in the carbon footprint. title: Frequency prototype-based source-free domain adaptation method and its application of wind turbine gearbox fault diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) for wind turbine gearbox fault diagnosis enables cross-domain generalization without accessing source data, effectively addressing privacy, security, and deployment challenges in real-world wind farm scenarios. However, existing approaches remain limited by the sensitivity of time-domain features to operating conditions and the unstable of pseudo-label supervision, which together hinder reliable domain alignment and robust cross-domain adaptation. title: Trap‐Mediated Photonic Synapses Based on Cs 2 AgBiBr 6 /ZnO x Heterojunctions for Audiovisual Physical Reservoir Computing
abstract: ABSTRACT Emulating biological sensory processing in hardware requires synaptic devices with tunable dynamics and multimodal integration capability. However, heterogeneous physical signals are difficult to encode uniformly in a single synaptic device. Herein, we construct an optically programmable photonic synapse (CZH‐PS) based on Cs 2 AgBiBr 6 /ZnO x (defect‐type) heterostructure, where abundant oxygen vacancy (Ov) deep traps in ZnO x dominate the synaptic plasticity. title: Oil Content and Mobility of Xiaganchaigou Formation in Yingxiongling Area, Qaidam Basin: Dominant Lithofacies and Controlling Factors
abstract: ABSTRACT Mixed shale represents an important target for shale‐oil exploration in lacustrine basins. However, its strong heterogeneity leads to pronounced variations in shale‐oil content and mobility. Therefore, identifying favorable lithofacies and clarifying their controlling factors are critical for shale‐oil sweet spot exploration. In this study, lithofacies of the Xiaganchaigou Formation in the Yingxiongling area, Qaidam Basin, were classified on the basis of mineral composition and subsequently evaluated using geochemical, pore structure, brittleness, and fracability characteristics. title: Four dimensions of high-quality economic development
abstract: Purpose Since 2012, China's economy has shifted from a stage of high-speed growth to one of high-quality development, yet a systematic theoretical generalisation of its economic connotations remains to be deepened. Taking Xi Jinping Thought on the Economy as the entry point, this paper aims to review China's practical experience of economic development in the new era, synthesise a series of landmark concepts into four theoretical dimensions of high-quality economic development, to clarify their core connotations and logical interrelations, and to indicate the significance of these insights for

title: Climate distress at a moral crossroads: how solastalgia conditions divergent consumer responses
abstract: Introduction Climate-related distress can support responsible consumption or coincide with affect-driven escape, yet the moral processes underlying these divergent responses remain unclear. This study develops and tests a dual-route framework in which moral disengagement (MD) and moral obligation (MO) link climate-change anxiety (CCA) and eco-grief (EG) with affective impulsive buying (AIB) and eco-conscious behavior (ECB), while solastalgia (BS) conditions key emotion-to-moral-processing associations. title: WasteGPS: A GPS-Based Mobile Application Connecting Households and Informal Collectors for Plastic Waste Collection in Airmadidi, Indonesia
abstract: Informal waste collectors recover a considerable share of the plastic produced by Indonesian households. Interviews in Airmadidi District, North Sulawesi, however, revealed that collectors spend much of their working day searching for households with plastic to sell, while residents have no way to tell collectors that their sorted plastic is ready. To address this problem, we designed and implemented WasteGPS, a two-role Android application that connects residents and collectors through GPS-tagged reports. journal: SAGA Journal of Technology and Information System

title: Modeling the distribution of bryophytes threatened according to the European Red List in Türkiye under climate change
abstract: Introduction Climate change is expected to become one of the greatest threats to bryophyte diversity; therefore, predicting the future distributions of species is vital for effective conservation planning. However, the absence of a national bryophyte Red List and threat assessments in Türkiye represents a major shortcoming in terms of biodiversity conservation. title: Groundwater quality dynamics and hydrochemical indicators of water insecurity in the semi-arid Sokoto Basin, Northwestern Nigeria
abstract: To determine groundwater quality at a basin level in climate-stressed, data-scarce basins, approaches need to be developed that go beyond traditional descriptive hydrochemistry and interpret the data to provide spatial indicators of water insecurity. Groundwater samples were collected from 54 boreholes and hand-dug wells from the Sokoto Basin across the contrasting basement and sedimentary aquifer systems with the aim of providing an integrated assessment of the quality dynamics of the groundwater. title: Engineering rice for enhanced abiotic stress tolerance using genome editing
abstract: Rice productivity is increasingly constrained by drought, salinity, heat, cold, submergence, heavy metal toxicity, and herbicide-related stresses. Although conventional breeding has improved stress tolerance, progress remains limited by the complex, polygenic, and environment-dependent nature of abiotic stress responses. Genome-editing technologies, including CRISPR/Cas systems, TALENs, ZFNs, base editors, prime editors, and CRISPR-Combo, provide precise approaches for modifying stress-responsive genes and regulatory pathways. institutions: Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences

title: Two Bayesian Approaches to Dynamic Gaussian Bayesian Networks with Intra- and Inter-Slice Edges
abstract: Gaussian Dynamic Bayesian Networks (GDBNs) are widely used for learning network structures from continuous time-series data. To capture both time-lagged and contemporaneous dependencies, GDBNs allow for dynamic inter-slice edges and static intra-slice edges. Two Bayesian approaches have been developed for such models, both extending the well-known Gaussian BGe score. We refer to them as the mean-adjusted BGe (mBGe) and the extended BGe (eBGe) models. title: Bayesian inference of expensive simulators: survey and comparison of design choices
abstract: Abstract We present a survey of approaches to Bayesian inference with simulator forward models, focusing on settings with prohibitively expensive simulators. In this domain, Bayesian optimization-based methods have emerged as the most promising approach. We unify existing methods into a general framework, enabling consistent reasoning about shared algorithmic structure across the fragmented literature. title: ANALISIS TEKNO-EKONOMI INVESTASI PEMBANGKIT LISTRIK TENAGA SURYA (PLTS) APUNG PADA WADUK WONOREJO SEBAGAI STRATEGI OPTIMALISASI ENERGI TERBARUKAN
abstract: The development of Floating Solar Power Plants (FSPP) in Indonesia has significant potential due to high solar radiation intensity and the availability of extensive water areas. This study aims to analyze the techno-economic feasibility of investing in a Floating Solar Power Plant at Wonorejo Reservoir, Tulungagung Regency, East Java, as a strategy for optimizing renewable energy utilization. The floating solar system was designed with a capacity of 10 MW using 18,182 JA Solar JAM72S30550 photovoltaic modules and 40 Sungrow SG250HX-20 inverters. title: A mosaic of bacterial communities and their functional potential across Antarctic moss, lichen and soil
abstract: Introduction Bacterial community composition differed markedly among substrates, whereas broad community-level differences between sampling localities were not statistically detected. The recovered U. aurantiacoatra bacterial community was dominated by Pseudomonadota, while A. regularis and soil communities exhibited greater taxonomic diversity, with Pseudomonadota, Actinomycetota, and Cyanobacteriota as dominant phyla. title: Entropy Generation Analysis of Unsteady Magnetohydrodynamic Buoyancy‐Driven Nanofluid Flow in a Porous Vertical Channel With Thermal Radiation and Chemical Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates entropy generation in an unsteady magneto‐hydrodynamic nanofluid flow with the influence of buoyancy forces embedded in a vertical porous channel. The simulation is carried out to assess the impact of thermal radiation and chemical reaction; the transport domain is bounded by a left‐cooled plate and a right‐heated plate. The schematic transport field reflects operating conditions commonly encountered in practical thermal and energy systems. title: From landlocked to linked: how the China–Europe Railway Express attracts foreign investment
abstract: Purpose International transportation networks are crucial to global capital allocation. This study aims to examine whether and how the China–Europe Railway Express (CR Express) attracts foreign direct investment (FDI) to connected Chinese cities. It identifies the causal effect of railway connectivity on FDI; investigates trade expansion, industrial upgrading and financial development as potential mechanisms; and explores variations across cities with different economic sizes, urban scales and industrial structures. title: Velocity-aided collaborative navigation for non-cooperative object localization in GNSS-denied environments
abstract: Abstract In collaborative multi-platform observation systems, radar-based localization of non-cooperative aerial objects is often limited by obstacles, sensing-range constraints, and measurement uncertainties. Moreover, in global navigation satellite system-denied environments caused by interference, spoofing, or other disruptions, the position and velocity estimates of aircraft can be affected by significant noise. First, a velocity-aided collaborative navigation filtering algorithm using inter-node range and radial-velocity measurements is developed for multiple cooperative platforms. Subseq
institutions: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

title: New records of Pseudoderma sinicarum and Lithophyllum nagaokaense (Lithophylloideae, Lithophyllaceae, Rhodophyta) from Korea
abstract: The subfamily Lithophylloideae includes non-geniculate coralline algal genera for which taxonomic uncertainty persists due to pronounced morphological plasticity and the limited availability of type-anchored molecular data. Here, we report Pseudoderma sinicarum and Lithophyllum nagaokaense as new records from Korea, identified based on plastid DNA markers (psbA and rbcL) and morpho-anatomical observations. title: Wild cereal harvesting ca. 14,000 years ago at Jeftelik (Western Syria)
abstract: The harvesting of wild cereals with sickle blades during the Late Epipalaeolithic Natufian period (ca. 14.6-11.5 ka cal BP) is widely documented; however, the scale and methods of sickle harvesting remain poorly understood. This study examines plant-harvesting activities through the functional analysis of glossed lithic tools from the Early Natufian site of Jeftelik (Western Syria), dated to ca. 14,000 years ago. title: Investigating urban development using remote sensing and GIS techniques (A case study: Sheberghan city (2005-2024)
abstract: The present study aimed to investigate the trend of spatial changes in land use in Sheberghan city during the period 2005 to 2024. This study, using remote sensing (RS) technology and geographic information system (GIS), analyzed the changes in land cover and different land uses in detail. For this purpose, Landsat satellite images from 2005, 2014, and 2024 were used, and after data preprocessing, supervised classification was performed using the Random Forest algorithm. title: Virion-associated nucleic acid metagenomics: Emerging approaches for plant virus discovery, molecular characterization, diversity and surveillance
abstract: Plant virus diagnostics has progressed from symptom-based observation and targeted serological or molecular assays toward untargeted high-throughput sequencing (HTS) approaches capable of detecting multiple known and previously uncharacterized viruses in a single sample. Among these approaches, virion-associated nucleic acid (VANA)-based metagenomics enriches nucleic acids protected within virus particles after removal of non-encapsidated host and microbial nucleic acids. title: Reinforcement learning‐enhanced adaptive sliding mode controller for underground articulated vehicles trajectory tracking
abstract: Abstract High‐precision trajectory tracking for underground articulated load‐haul‐dump (LHD) vehicles is significantly challenged by strong kinematic coupling and drastic payload variations. While sliding mode control (SMC) provides inherent robustness, its performance is often limited by fixed parameters that fail to adapt to varying path geometries. This paper proposes a reinforcement‐learning‐enhanced adaptive sliding mode control (RL‐SMC) framework, which utilizes a reinforcement learning agent for the online optimization of critical SMC parameters. title: Evaluating Multivariate Zero-Shot Chronos-2 for Probabilistic Forecasting of Selected Indonesian Banking Stock Return
abstract: Daily stock return forecasting is challenging because of low signal-to-noise ratios and changing market dynamics. Time-series foundation models such as Chronos-2 offer a zero-shot forecasting approach, but their effectiveness in emerging markets such as Indonesia remains insufficiently established. This study evaluates Chronos-2 for point and probabilistic forecasting of five LQ45 banking stocks (BBCA, BBNI, BBRI, BBTN, and BMRI). title: Métodos cuantitativos en la valoración de empresas: un estudio comparativo de literatura
abstract: Introducción: La valoración empresarial orienta decisiones de inversión, financiamiento y gestión estratégica en contextos económicos diversos, y la abundancia de procedimientos disponibles exige comprender sus fundamentos y condiciones de uso. Objetivo: Analizar de forma comparativa los métodos de valoración empresarial identificados en la literatura científica reciente. Método: El estudio adoptó un enfoque cualitativo de tipo documental. title: Combustion control strategies to achieve low temperature combustion in PCCI engines - A comprehensive review
abstract: Low-temperature combustion (LTC) has emerged as a pivotal solution for modern compression ignition engines, effectively breaking the traditional nitrogen oxide (NOx) and soot emission trade-off. Among LTC variants, Premixed Charge Compression Ignition (PCCI) stands out for its capacity to reduce in-cylinder emissions with minimal structural modifications. title: GENMAT: A multi-scale generative AI framework for material and structural design
abstract: Materials and structural design is an inverse problem posed at the crystal, microstructure and component scales, which existing tools treat separately. We present GENMAT , three generative architectures that share an explicitly specified property-conditioning interface , i.e. a normalised, masked, slot-based target with a routing rule and a four-part module contract. title: Vulnerabilities and agency of small technologically advanced states: Finland navigating Sino-US strategic technology competition
abstract: This article explores how a small technologically advanced state, exemplified by Finland, seeks to maintain agency and manage security risks in Sino-US strategic technology competition, and what future options experts envision for it. The US and China are presently the only ‘geoeconomic great powers’ with competences across four dimensions: investment leverage, supply chains, critical technologies, and technology standards. title: Optimization of Solar and Wind Systems Under Uncertainty: A Review of Recent Advances in Capacity, Configuration, and Storage Planning
abstract: The growing variability and uncertainty associated with renewable energy sources have made optimization under uncertainty an essential component of modern energy system planning. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of optimization approaches applied to solar photovoltaic (PV), wind, and hybrid PV–wind systems, with a focus on capacity planning, storage integration, and system configuration. title: Smallholder farmers' preferences for public expenditure priorities to support maize productivity: evidence from a best–worst scaling experiment in western Kenya
abstract: Understanding how smallholder farmers want public resources allocated is essential for designing effective agricultural policies, especially in the maize sub-sector, where public interventions often compete for limited fiscal resources. This paper determined smallholder farmers’ preferences for enhancing maize productivity in western Kenya. Using survey data from 1,531 smallholder farmers, the study applied a best–worst scaling experiment in which farmers evaluated seven policy options across seven choice sets. title: Diatomaceous Earth: A Sustainable Resource for Environmental Conservation and Agriculture
abstract: Diatomaceous earth (DE), or diatomite, is a natural sedimentary material derived from the fossilized remains of diatoms, microscopic algae that have accumulated over millions of years. This study explores the structural characteristics and multifunctional applications of DE, particularly in environmental protection and sustainable agriculture. DE’s high porosity and large surface area contribute to its exceptional adsorption capacity, enabling the removal of contaminants such as heavy metals and pollutants from water. journal: Journal of Food Health and Bioenvironmental Science

title: EvaluAI: Automatic scoring short-answer constructed-response questions with LLMs
abstract: Manual grading of short-answer questions in higher education is time-consuming and often relies on simplified methods that do not capture students’ conceptual understanding. We introduce EvaluAI , an automatic grading tool based on a large language model (GPT-4o mini) with a modular prompt that combines the human graders’ rubric with knowledge of the expected answer, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought analysis and feedback. title: The Influence of AI-Assisted Problem Solving on Decision Quality: Examining the Moderating Role of Cognitive Reflection
abstract: This study examined the influence of AI-assisted problem solving on decision quality and the moderating role of cognitive reflection among university students in Pakistan. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was employed, with a target sample of 335 undergraduate and postgraduate students from selected public and private universities, including the University of the Punjab, Bahauddin Zakariya University, Government College University Faisalabad, University of Karachi, University of Sindh, University of Peshawar, University of Malakand, and International Islamic University Islamabad

title: Electrode-associated growth reveals structure of OmcZ-type cytochrome nanowires in anaerobic methanotrophic archaea
abstract: Anaerobic methanotrophic (ANME) archaea are key regulators of methane emissions in anoxic environments, yet their physiology remains poorly understood due to the lack of axenic cultures. Here, we show that cultivation on poised electrodes yields near-axenic cultures (95.8% relative abundance) of a freshwater ANME, for which we propose the name 'Candidatus Methanoperedens vercellensis'. We identified key physiological properties of 'Ca. title: Developing the Desalination Resilience Dynamic Index ( DRDI ): A Multidimensional Framework for Assessing Adaptive Water Resilience
abstract: ABSTRACT Water scarcity has become a multidimensional sustainability challenge driven by climate change, demographic growth, governance quality and technological adaptation. Although desalination is increasingly recognised as a strategic response to water stress, existing assessment approaches remain fragmented and fail to evaluate its adaptive resilience comprehensively. This study develops the Desalination Resilience Dynamic Index (DRDI), a multidimensional framework integrating technological, economic, institutional and distributive dimensions to assess desalination resilience. title: Investigating the spatial patterns in the dependence of daily rainfall depth on wet spell duration over Europe
abstract: Daily rainfall amount and occurrence are often investigated separately, without accounting for the possible dependence of rainfall depth ( h ) on wet spell duration ( ws ). Here, we show that this dependence occurs across Europe and exhibits consistent spatial patterns. The approach adopted for modelling this dependence relies on a log-growth relationship between ws and normalized arithmetic (AM) and geometric (GM) means. title: La formación de la observación científica ante la IA: la atrofia perceptiva como concepto
abstract: El valor educativo de la inteligencia artificial depende, en parte, de cómo reorganiza las oportunidades de observar, intervenir y cuestionar las representaciones científicas. En este artículo desarrollamos un argumento conceptual sobre la atrofia perceptiva, entendida como el posible debilitamiento de capacidades adquiridas para discriminar rasgos y anomalías relevantes en una práctica científica. title: Breaking the Capacity‐Reversibility Linear Trade‐Off in Li–O 2 Batteries via Amorphous Non‐Precious High‐Entropy Alloy Catalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–oxygen (Li–O 2 ) batteries suffer from sluggish reaction kinetics and rely on precious metal‐based catalysts to facilitate the reaction process. Despite being effective, these costly catalysts would inevitably introduce a critical trade‐off between capacity and reversibility, compromising the high energy density advantage of Li–O 2 batteries. In this study, we have designed an amorphous non‐precious MnFeCoNiCu high‐entropy alloy (A‐HEA) catalyst via a mild liquid‐phase reduction strategy to break the above inherent linear trade‐off. title: Advances on triply periodic hyperbolic surface structures: from biological inspiration to artificial self-assembly
abstract: Triply periodic hyperbolic surfaces (TPHSs) are a class of complex structures that extend periodically throughout three-dimensional space and possess smooth surfaces with non-positive Gaussian curvature. They appear in a wide range of natural systems, from cellular membranes to butterfly wing scales and beetle exoskeletons. Owing to their unique geometries and extraordinary properties, TPHSs have attracted extensive attention and research interest. title: Development and In Vitro Evaluation of Kaempferol-Loaded Liposomes in LN-229 Glioblastoma Cells: Potency, Selectivity, and Modulation of ROS-Dependent Cytotoxicity
abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma multiforme has a median survival of 12–15 months despite multimodal treatment, due to blood-brain barrier impermeability limiting CNS drug bioavailability. Liposomal nanoformulations circumvent this barrier while offering tunable surface chemistry and amphiphilic drug-loading capacity. Here, we report encapsulation of kaempferol, a dietary flavonoid, within phosphatidylcholine-cholesterol liposomes (Lip-KPF) and evaluate cytotoxic activity against LN-229 glioblastoma cells relative to free kaempferol (KPF) and puromycin aminonucleoside (Puro-A). title: Noise-Induced Dynamics in a Multistable Erbium-Doped Fiber Laser: A Short Review From Extreme Events to Photonic Information Processing
abstract: Noise is often regarded as a source of instability and degraded performance in optical systems. In nonlinear dynamical systems, this view is incomplete: fluctuations can reveal critical susceptibility, activate transitions among coexisting attractors, generate rare extreme excursions, and enable probabilistic information processing. title: RNA and proteins joined up at the origins of life: Persistence is the point
abstract: What drove nucleic acids (NA) into functional associations with proteins (PR) at the origins of life? We reason from polymer physics and the Central Dogma that the fitness value of cooperating through a division of labor-NA for replication fidelity and PR for functional fitness-is much higher than for either polymer alone. Our model shows a Pareto Front, where NA and PR can bootstrap each other to achieve autocatalytic cooperativity toward biology.

abstract: Abstract Groundwater potential mapping in semi-arid karst regions is often compromised by spatially optimistic validation, limited assessment of predictive variability, and insufficient independent hydrogeological verification. This study introduces TriFusion-Karst, a stacked-ensemble model using RF and LightGBM as base learners and XGBoost as the meta-learner, embedded within a spatially robust and hydrogeologically validated workflow. abstract: The current study investigates the heat transfer characteristics of a chemically reactive Boger ternary nanofluid containing different-shaped nanoparticles over a stretching cylinder with torsional motion, considering homogeneous-heterogeneous reactions, thermal radiation, heat source/sink, magnetic field and nanoparticle shape effects.
