abstract: Innovative entrepreneurship is an important driver of regional economic development. According to the Knowledge Spillover Theory of Entrepreneurship (KSTE), universities contribute directly to innovative entrepreneurship by conducting state-of-the-art research and educating talent. abstract: The Executive Master in Smart Territories: Data and Decision Support Systems, recently proposed by ISMAT, emerges in a context where cities and regions face high complexity, data abundance, and increasing demands for transparency and efficiency in public decision making. In this scenario, it becomes crucial to explore how advanced training can position itself between the centrality of data and concerns with spatial justice in territorial governance. abstract: Silicon oxide memristive devices exhibit volatile current transients in addition to non-volatile resistive switching. Such transients are candidate temporary states for neuromorphic systems, but their form depends on coupled processes in the oxide and its electrode interfaces. abstract: Introducción: Esta investigación analiza la intersección literario-científica entre GenAI (IA generativa) e innovación educativa. abstract: With the rapid development of digital technology, digital governance has become an important path to modernizing national governance and a key issue in global economic cooperation. abstract: Benthic macroinvertebrates are widely used as indicators of freshwater ecosystem changes due to their sensitivity to environmental disturbance and important ecological functions. However, long-term variations in multiple biodiversity dimensions of benthic communities under eutrophication and seasonal environmental stress remain poorly understood. In this study, quarterly surveys were conducted at eight sites in Lake Chaohu from 2018 to 2024 to investigate temporal dynamics of benthic macroinvertebrate communities and their environmental drivers. abstract: Introduction Free-living amoebae (FLA) of the Vahlkampfiidae family are widely distributed in nature, occupying aquatic and terrestrial habitats. The group includes thermophilic amphizoic organisms such as Naegleria fowleri . This study aims to describe natural recreational freshwaters in terms of the presence of thermotolerant vahlkampfiids, sediment microbial communities and climatic/land use features. title: Research on the Double-edged Sword Effect of Employee Perception of AI in the Context of Digitalization and Intelligentization
abstract: As AI technology advances and digitalization accelerates, technological change brings both opportunities and challenges to employees. AI perception reflects employees’ awareness of AI’s impact on their work attitudes, behaviors, well-being and environment. While AI improves performance, it also introduces risks that significantly affect employees. Meanwhile, scattered and ambiguous concepts hinder research on AI’s psychological and behavioral impacts. abstract: Abstract The development of video camouflaged object detection (VCOD) is currently constrained by the scarcity of challenging benchmarks and the lack of robustness of models in the face of erratic motion dynamics. Existing methods frequently encounter challenges related to motion-induced appearance instability and temporal feature misalignment, particularly in complex motion scenarios. abstract: ABSTRACT River regulation has disrupted flow regimes that promote fish movement, contributing to population declines. Restoring hydrological cues through managed environmental flows can support recovery yet requires understanding how river flow drives movement. We analysed 10 years (2014–2024) of passive integrated transponder detections at 11 consecutive fishways spanning 600 km of the lower Murray River, south‐eastern Australia. abstract: Port digitalisation is widely promoted as a lever of port performance, yet empirical evidence remains dispersed and is drawn mostly from European and Asian ports. abstract: This case study examines whether early electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) adds forecasting information beyond an available linear-polarisation-resistance (LPR) measurement in reinforced fly-ash and fly-ash–metakaolin mortar. title: Advances and Challenges in Methane Emission Measurement in the Oil and Gas Sector: A Review
abstract: Methane emissions from the oil and gas sector are a major contributor to climate change. It is essential to monitor and mitigate these emissions. In this review, sources of methane emissions, available monitoring techniques, emission estimation models, associated uncertainty, and newly emerging technologies, including AI-based monitoring techniques, are critically evaluated. abstract: Laboratory extraction profiles from copper sulfide bioleaching are frequently treated as predictors of heap performance. However, the experimental regimes differ in wetting, gas access, thermal inertia, microbial attachment, and mineralogical heterogeneity. abstract: This manuscript examines the application of Visible Near-Infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy using the reflection method to predict banana ripeness. title: Assessing rural household food security in flood-prone areas: An integrated FAO–IPCC framework-based analysis in Iran
abstract: Floods are one of the most destructive natural phenomena affecting food security by reducing agricultural production, disrupting food access, and diminishing household income. Given the increasing severity of climate-associated hazards and the vulnerability of communities to their effects, understanding the impacts of floods on food security and identifying the factors associated with it are essential. abstract: Microbial communities often exhibit apparently complex dynamics driven by myriad interactions among community members and with their environments. Yet, practical modeling and control are often based on a limited number of observables, raising fundamental questions: are these observed dynamics low-dimensional? This study presents a reproducible LabVIEW virtual-instrument framework to characterise the intrinsic robustness of benchmark optimisation landscapes, rather than evaluate an optimisation algorithm. abstract: Abstract Energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectrometry is commonly used by archaeologists and museum staff to nondestructively characterize the elemental composition of artifacts or other materials of cultural relevance, ranging from obsidian and other lithics, to soils, pigments, metals, ceramics, and brick. abstract: Abstract Spatially compounding climate extremes are increasingly recognized as a source of climate-related risk, and their risk significance depends on how synchrony affects connected systems. The critical transition occurs when cross-regional synchrony reduces support from places that would otherwise buffer one another through substitution, reserve capacity, mutual assistance or recovery support—a condition we term spatial buffering loss. abstract: AbstractDiabetic nephropathy (DN), a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes, remains a principal cause of renal failure worldwide, yet its multifaceted molecular complexity continues to challenge effective therapeutic intervention. In this study, an integrative network pharmacology and computational modeling framework was employed to unravel the mechanistic basis of Terminalia chebula in mitigating DN pathology. abstract: This study aims to evaluate service quality and determine improvement priorities at the Savings and Loan Cooperative of PT Swabina Gatra by integrating Service Quality (SERVQUAL) and Importance Performance Analysis (IPA). abstract: The growing impact of anthropogenic activities, including urbanization, agriculture and industrial expansion, has intensified water and environmental pollution, and wastewater treatment has evolved beyond pollutant removal toward the recovery of nutrients, energy and high-value materials. abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) has transformed the business environment and redefined workforce skill requirements, compelling educational institutions to address these evolving needs. In accountancy, curricula prescribed by international and national governing bodies aim to align labour market expectations with graduate competencies to ensure employability and professional success. Frontal polymerization (FP) offers a promising path forward, enabling rapid, self-propagating curing during extrusion-based additive manufacturing (AM) without cementitious binders. abstract: Given the extended timelines of epidemics and pandemics, disasters are likely to arise concurrently with the potential to have compounding or cascading effects and feedback loops that could disrupt societal functioning and threaten societal resilience. This scoping review aimed to identify published literature related to the resiliency impacts of compound and cascading events occurring during or resulting in an epidemic/pandemic. Due to their ability to function at trace concentrations, AFPs are being explored for wide-ranging applications, from cryopreservation to food storage. abstract: Abstract Hainan Island is China’s largest tropical crop-production base, making its agricultural soil quality important for national food security. Despite these conditions, hypersaline lakes sustain stable microbial communities in which haloarchaea frequently dominate carbon turnover and energy fluxes. abstract: The main aim of the present paper is to examine the wind energy potential, as well as the performance and economic sustainability, based on mean monthly wind speed data collected from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET) and previous scientific studies. In this study, the Weibull distribution function is used to analyze the characteristics of the wind resources of 32 locations in Nigeria. abstract: ABSTRACT Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) pose an increasing threat to high mountain environments across the world, especially in the Himalayas where climate change is accelerating glacier retreat and permafrost degradation. This study presents a detailed GLOF susceptibility analysis of the western Himalayas covering five major river basins, ie Satluj, Chenab, Jhelum, Beas, and Ravi by integrating high‐resolution remote sensing data with a multi‐criteria decision‐making approach. abstract: Abstract Single-cell mapping methods convert raw, heterogeneous single-cell datasets into interpretable and comparable representations of biological identity. As reference cell-type taxonomies mature, mapping new datasets to shared references has become a central strategy for enabling cross-study integration, reproducible annotation, and cumulative biological knowledge. abstract: Human activities have fundamentally altered the functioning of most terrestrial ecosystems, particularly grazing ecosystems where vegetation-dependent processes underpin both human well-being and ecological resilience. Despite the importance of ground cover for sustaining these processes, the long-term dynamics of vegetation cover—and the degree to which temporal variability is explained by climatic drivers—remain poorly quantified at farm and paddock scales. abstract: Monitoring plant water stress and biomass is limited by labor intensive measurements techniques. Observing plant water conditions more broadly is now enabled by microwave remote sensing. abstract: The article confirms the relevance of the development and implementation of low-temperature technologies for road construction in swampy or flooded areas. Currently, the construction of temporary access roads in swampy and flooded areas is subject to seasonal restrictions. abstract: Miniaturization and high integration of 5G electronics, aerospace components, and intelligent devices have caused severe heat accumulation, shortening the service life and degrading the reliability of devices. abstract: Accurate precipitation estimation in data-scarce mountainous regions is essential for effective water resource management and hazard monitoring. title: Mapping food systems transformation in Horizon Europe (2021–2024): a co-word and network analysis of alignment with FOOD2030 pathways
abstract: The European Union promotes food-systems transformation through the research and innovation programme Horizon Europe and the FOOD2030 framework, which defines eleven pathways for action. abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater mussels play vital functional roles in aquatic ecosystems by mediating nutrient cycling, water clarity, and energy flow. abstract: Corrosion remains a major challenge that compromises the durability, safety, and service life of metallic structures, resulting in substantial economic losses and environmental concerns worldwide. title: Temperature effects on life history strategies for rapid growth potential of leaf epiphytic bacteria
abstract: Phyllosphere bacteria, occupying both epiphytic and endophytic habitats, constitute a critical plant-atmosphere interface. However, their community assembly and life-history strategies (LHSs) in response to temperature increase remain poorly understood. Here, we compared leaf phyllosphere bacterial communities with those in other plant compartments across four representative plant species from an alpine meadow on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. title: Development of a novel rule-based controlled strategy on a hybrid electric UAV
abstract: Abstract Hybrid electric propulsion has gained significant attention in reducing the fuel consumption and pollution emissions of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The problem of managing the energy within the powertrain of the aircraft is still a major concern within the aviation industry. This can be accomplished through an effective energy management strategy that ensures that the energy within the aircraft is properly distributed. title: Counter-Terrorism Financing and National Security in Nigeria: Assessing The Role of Financial Intelligence
abstract: Terrorism financing has emerged as a major national security challenge in Nigeria due to the ability of terrorist organisations to generate, conceal, and transfer financial resources that sustain violent activities. The persistence of groups such as Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) has highlighted the importance of financial intelligence as a strategic tool for detecting and disrupting terrorist funding networks. title: Antimicrobial Photodynamic Therapy Targeting Streptococcus mutans Biofilm for Caries Prevention in Pediatric Dentistry: A Scoping Review
abstract: Dental caries in children is largely associated with Streptococcus mutans biofilms, which may be controlled using minimally invasive antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT). This scoping review aimed to map the current evidence regarding the application of aPDT against Streptococcus mutans biofilms for pediatric caries prevention. The review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines using ScienceDirect, PubMed, ProQuest, and SpringerLink. title: THEOBROMA: an aggregated open database of 1.13 million natural products with per-compound license auditing, three-tier classification, and stereochemistry-aware deduplication
abstract: Abstract Natural products remain one of the most productive sources of pharmacologically active compounds for drug discovery. Open aggregators attribute licenses at database granularity, and the consequences of that choice have become tangible as the field grows. A recent relicensing event in one constituent source (the September 2024 transition of the Natural Products Atlas to CC BY-NC 4.0) demonstrates how database-level licensing propagates across an aggregate and motivates the per-compound audit framework presented here. title: Attack-Resilient Distributed Prescribed-Time Formation Control for Underactuated Unmanned Surface Vehicles Subject to Pose-Measurement False-Data Injection Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates an attack-resilient distributed prescribed-time formation control problem for underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) subject to pose-measurement false-data injection (FDI) attacks, input saturation, external disturbances, collision-avoidance constraints, and connectivity-maintenance requirements. title: How prenatal residential greenness links to congenital heart defects: The role of multi-pollutant mediating pathways and non-linear exposure-response
abstract: Background Rapid urbanization has intensified cardiovascular burdens, particularly congenital heart defects (CHDs), a leading cause of neonatal mortality globally. The first trimester is the critical exposure window, which results in the cardiac septation and outflow tract formation. The vegetation may affect air pollutants through processes such as purification, dust retention, and temperature regulation. These pollutants have been linked to disrupted embryonic cardiogenesis. title: Co-application of lime and Ca-Mg-B-Zn-Fe amendment reduces root rot incidence and enhances tobacco growth in a field trial
abstract: Introduction Soil acidification increases the incidence of soil-borne diseases, especially tobacco root rot. Lime and related amendments are widely applied to mitigate soil acidification and crop diseases, whereas their growth-promoting and disease-suppressive mechanisms remain elusive. Methods Using field experiments and high-throughput sequencing, this study investigated the effects of lime-based amendments on acidification alleviation, rhizosphere microbiota reshaping and tobacco root rot suppression. title: Advances and perspectives in organic inhibitor-based anti-corrosion coatings: Biodegradable polymers, natural extracts, and synthetic compounds
abstract: This review focuses on progress and advances in the preparation of anti-corrosion coatings using organic inhibitors. It looks at examples of biodegradable polymers, plant extracts, and synthetic organic compounds, revealing interesting results and offering new perspectives on their potential applications. The review provides both experimental and theoretical evidence of the high corrosion inhibitory properties of carbon steels and alloys in acidic and saline environments. title: 30th Anniversary Jubilee of Collaborative Research in Non-Destructive Testing
abstract: This paper reflects on thirty years of synergistic cooperation between the global NDT community— facilitated by NDT.net—and the theoretical and practical contributions of Edouard Nesvijski. Over three decades, this partnership has bridged the gap between complex wave physics and industrial application, particularly in the realms of structural health monitoring, ultrasonic transducer design, and the advancement of Non-Destructive Evaluation (NDE) methods. title: Yield determinants in rice under organic and conventional production systems: Implications for selection strategies
abstract: The persistent yield gap remains a major challenge in organic agriculture despite its increasing importance for sustainable food production. The present study compared the performance of 80 diverse rice genotypes (62 landraces and 18 modern varieties) under two contrasting production systems (organic and conventional). The experiment was conducted during the Kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024 using an alpha lattice design (8 × 10) with three replications. title: Human resource development through ESG-oriented agricultural training: Knowledge outcomes in IoT-assisted and conventional irrigation settings
abstract: Background: The social pillar of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) emphasizes human resource development, yet evidence on ESG-oriented agricultural training in non-farming urban communities remains limited. This study assesses changes in knowledge following an ESG-oriented agricultural training program and examines whether IoT-assisted infrastructure is associated with differential knowledge gains. title: Molecular and in-silico characterization of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus spp. isolated from clinical urine samples, Lahore, Pakistan
abstract: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci are a serious threat to public health because of their multidrug resistance and the limitations in the treatment options available. This study investigated clinical VRE isolates from Lahore, Pakistan, and characterized the vanA gene via in-silico approaches. In this study, urine specimens were collected and cultured on selective media. Morphological and biochemical observation, such as Gram staining and catalase, oxidase, and mannitol salt agar tests, were conducted. title: Effects of discharge flow and reservoir water level on intake water temperature with a front retaining wall
abstract: Following the construction and operation of hydropower stations in alpine and cold regions, the vertical thermal stratification structure of reservoirs is significantly altered. To mitigate the adverse ecological impacts of low-temperature water release and enhance the withdrawal of warm surface water, stratified intake measures are commonly adopted to satisfy downstream ecological protection requirements. title: Remote sensing reveals spatially uneven vegetation trends and seasonal rainfall associations in Somaliland from 2000 to 2022
abstract: Abstract Dryland vegetation in Somaliland is highly sensitive to rainfall variability, warming, and recurrent drought, yet Somaliland-wide evidence on MODIS-era vegetation–climate relationships remain limited. This study assessed vegetation dynamics and climatic variability across Somaliland during 2000–2022 using MODIS NDVI, CHIRPS rainfall, TerraClimate temperature, Mann–Kendall trend testing, Sen’s slope estimation, autocorrelation and modified Mann–Kendall sensitivity checks, correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, seasonal lag-response testing, pixel-wise NDVI trend mapping, and

title: Solid-State, Rapid Mechanochemical Pathway for Zinc Phthalocyanine-Embedded Schiff-Base Polymer-TiO2 Nanocomposite for LED Assisted Efficient Photochemical Remediation of Hexavalent Chromium
abstract: Abstract The processing and elimination of heavy metals and toxic components from water is indispensable due to its potentially hazardous and carcinogenic impacts on the well-being of people and the environment. Successful heavy metals and toxic components mitigation ensures adequate water quality for consumption, prevents ingestion in to living organisms, and limits the contamination of the environment. title: Alkali-activated cementitious materials for multifunctional structural capacitors: Multi-scale architectures, structure–property relationships and engineering applications
abstract: Smart infrastructure requires materials that simultaneously provide mechanical load-bearing capacity and active energy management functions. This article systematically analyzes alkali-activated cementitious materials as matrices for multifunctional structural capacitors, integrating strain sensing, Joule heating, electromagnetic shielding and absorption, and thermoelectric energy harvesting with in-situ storage. title: The quantum Black-Scholes Hamiltonian and tunneling risk: An application to option contract valuation in an emerging market
abstract: Este artículo presenta un marco pedagógico que transforma el modelo clásico de Black-Scholes en un paradigma de Black-Scholes cuántico (QBS) mediante la schrödingerización. title: Tutela jurídico-privada de los datos de salud en el Reglamento (UE) 2025/327: intimidad, autonomía y responsabilidad por daños
abstract: El Reglamento (UE) 2025/327, relativo al Espacio Europeo de Datos de Salud, ordena un nuevo marco europeo de acceso, circulación e interoperabilidad de los datos de salud electrónicos. Su finalidad es doble: mejorar la asistencia sanitaria mediante el uso primario de los datos y favorecer la investigación, la innovación y la formulación de políticas públicas mediante su uso secundario. journal: Indret: Revista para el Análisis del Derecho

title: Integrated statistical-analytical framework quantifying bond behaviour of FRP‑reinforced concrete structures
abstract: Air-entrained concrete (AEC) is widely used to enhance the durability of reinforced concrete (RC) structures, particularly under freeze-thaw exposure. This study investigates the combined effects of air entrainment and Fibre Reinforced Polymer (FRP) reinforcement on bond behaviour in concrete. An integrated analytical-statistical approach is proposed that combines analytical bond modelling with multifactor statistical evaluation. institutions: Budapest University of Technology and Economics

title: Uncertainty in geological mapping: a rock identification confusion matrix for a bedrock mapping project in Trøndelag, Norway
abstract: Geological mapping relies heavily on expert interpretation, guided by tacit conceptual models that are rarely formalised.As a result, rock-type classifications often carry significant yet unquantified subjective uncertainty.This study proposes a method to capture and structure such uncertainty in the form of a relational uncertainty matrix which represents a human perception-based rock identification confusion (RIC) matrix.As part of a regional geological mapping project in Trøndelag, Norway, 11 geologists independently assessed their perceived uncertainty in discriminating between rock pairs

title: A shipborne GNSS spoofing detection algorithm based on temporally constrained prior-association
abstract: Abstract Ship navigation relies on the global navigation satellite system (GNSS), but civil GNSS signals are vulnerable to spoofing attacks that can induce erroneous positioning results. Existing inertial- and sensor-based methods usually describe the consistency between GNSS information and measurements from non-GNSS sensors through direct motion comparison, filter innovations, or test statistics derived from acceleration constraints, but they do not fully characterize the temporal association changes in the motion inconsistency caused by spoofing attacks in maritime scenarios. title: Performative Minimalism in UAE mosques: from vernacular restraint to contemporary expressions
abstract: This paper examines how architectural restraint in mosque architecture and interiors in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has changed in cause and meaning, from historical vernacular buildings to contemporary religious spaces. The study distinguishes four overlapping modes: vernacular restraint, modernist and regional-modernist abstraction, historicist and neo-Islamic representation, and contemporary minimalism. title: The representation of SDG-related research in bibliometric databases: persisting imbalances and varying perspectives
abstract: Abstract The societal impact of research has become an explicit goal of research activities and argument for the funding of the science system. Providers of bibliometric databases algorithmically assign scientific publications to SDG goals to show how single research outputs contribute to society, but substantial disagreements among these classifications have been quantified. Moreover, large language models (LLMs) are being introduced as a technology that processes scholarly records. title: Synergistic Enhancement of Piezoelectric Performance in Wood‐Like Anisotropic Porous PVDF / BaTiO 3 /Graphene Parts via Dual‐Filler and Structural Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT The ongoing advancements in smart interactive systems have drawn tremendous interest toward piezoelectric energy conversion devices. However, conventional devices suffer from limited deformation modes and insufficient stress utilization. Herein, a novel wood‐like anisotropic porous polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)/barium titanate (BaTiO 3 )/graphene part was successfully fabricated. title: Modeling and Regression‐Based Study of Heat and Mass Transfer in Electrically Conducting Trihybrid Nanofluids
abstract: ABSTRACT Comparing ternary nanofluids is vital in science and engineering because it helps identify the most efficient combinations for heat and mass transfer while balancing cost and minimizing drawbacks like frictional losses. This study examines the magnetohydrodynamic flow of a trihybrid nanofluid through a diverging/converging channel, incorporating the influence of chemical reactions and a non‐uniform source of heat. title: Hybrid Markov Regime-Switching and Hurdle modeling of last-mile livestock logistics in Ukraine under systemic volatility
abstract: Abstract This study examines the transformation of last-mile logistics in Ukraine’s livestock supply chains under conditions of prolonged systemic volatility and infrastructure disruption. A hybrid analytical framework is proposed that integrates Random Forest Recursive Feature Elimination (RF-RFE) for preliminary predictor screening, a two-state Markov Regime-Switching (MRS) model for identifying latent logistics regimes, and a two-part Hurdle model for separately estimating disruption probability and conditional freight-cost intensity. title: Named entity recognition for climate change research
abstract: The rapid growth of scientific literature on anthropogenic climate change necessitates automated information extraction to manage and synthesise complex, multi-scalar climate phenomena. Although the research community increasingly relies on natural language processing (NLP), particularly named entity recognition (NER), existing resources in this domain lack broad thematic coverage and rigorous multi-expert validation. title: Natural Rubber Latex as a Sustainable Modifier in Cementitious Materials: Mechanisms, Performance, and Environmental Implications
abstract: ABSTRACT This review highlights the role of natural rubber latex (NRL) as a sustainable alternative to traditional synthetic material in cementitious applications. It discusses advancements in latex technologies and their implications for enhancing cement performance, particularly regarding fluidity and bonding properties. The review also emphasizes innovative bio‐based approaches that strengthen and increase the durability of cementitious materials. title: Equity-centered disaster risk assessment among formal and non-formal workers and willingness to pay for flood risk insurance in Bali, Indonesia
abstract: Disaster risk assessments have traditionally emphasized hazard exposure and physical infrastructure performance, often overlooking the heterogeneous distribution of flood risks and recovery capacities across diverse social and livelihood groups. This study redefines disaster risk through an equity-centered lens by integrating Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA) with a binary logistic model of willingness to pay (WTP) for flood risk insurance. title: Fluid‐Controlled Tidal Modulation of Aftershocks Following the 2022 M6.8 Luding Earthquake
abstract: Abstract Aftershock sequences record how fault zones recover and weaken after earthquakes, but the roles of fluid migration and stress heterogeneity remain difficult to isolate. Earth tides impose predictable stress perturbations and thus provide a natural probe of faults near failure, although their signals are often obscured by aftershock clustering. title: Impacts of synoptic circulation types on nocturnal ozone increase in the North China Plain: meteorological drivers and physical mechanisms
abstract: Nocturnal ozone (O 3 ) increase (NOI) has become common worldwide, raising the risk of O 3 pollution. While weather types serve as critical drivers of NOI, their specific dynamic influences remain poorly understood. Using ground observations and reanalysis datasets, this study identified the relationship between weather types and NOI days in a representative city in the North China Plain, and revealed the meteorological characteristics and physical mechanisms driving these events. title: Bacterial community structure and stable predicted functional profiles in the renal sac fluid of the cuttlefish Acanthosepion pharaonis
abstract: Cephalopods have high metabolic rates and rely heavily on amino acid catabolism, producing large amounts of ammonia that must be efficiently excreted to avoid physiological stress. The cephalopod renal organ, consisting of renal appendages enclosed within an acidic and ammonia-rich fluid-filled renal sac, plays a central role in nitrogen waste elimination. title: The Nexus Between Green Finance, Renewable Energy Consumption and Technological Innovation: Evidence From G20 Economies
abstract: ABSTRACT Green finance is intended to support decarbonisation, yet an average emissions relationship may conceal differences across financing instruments and the conditional emissions distribution. This study examines these differences in G20 economies during 2012–2018, alongside renewable energy consumption (RE) and research and development expenditure (RD). title: An evidence-prior collaborative image inpainting method based on counterfactual-inspired prototype contribution selection
abstract: The inpainting of complex damaged images relies not only on contextual inference from the visible regions of the current image, but also on the effective introduction of external reference priors when single-image evidence is insufficient. However, cross-image reference information and the image to be inpainted often suffer from structural, textural, and semantic mismatches, and direct prior injection may lead to erroneous reference propagation and unreliable content generation. abstract: La cuenca del río Manzanares ubicada al norte de Venezuela, atraviesa un proceso acelerado de sedimentación vinculado a erosión hídrica, deforestación y expansión agropecuaria, lo que compromete su estabilidad hidromorfológica. abstract: Este estudio investiga la influencia de la longitud focal en el rendimiento de un concentrador solar de disco parabólico (CDP) mediante el método de trazado de rayos. Se utilizaron el software SolTrace, Tonatiuh y un programa desarrollado en MATLAB para analizar cómo varía la energía concentrada en el receptor al modificar la longitud focal del paraboloide. title: EFM-GAN: enhanced feature modeling for multimodal MRI synthesis under missing-modality settings
abstract: Abstract Objective . Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) synthesis has been widely investigated for recovering unavailable imaging modalities under incomplete acquisition scenarios. However, existing approaches often rely on implicit feature fusion strategies, where modality-specific appearance information and cross-modal anatomical representations are entangled in a shared latent space. title: Simulation-based performance evaluation, techno-economic, and environmental assessment of a rooftop PV system for the garment industry in Chittagong, Bangladesh
abstract: Garment industries in Bangladesh are one of the key sectors that account for 83.9 percent of all exports, employing more than 4 million people. This vital sector often faces power shortages that reduce productivity and hinder economic activity. This crisis is largely driven by dependence on imported fossil fuels, highlighting the need for reliable and sustainable power sources. title: A multilingual mobile application for digital mental health support, emotional tracking, and therapist interaction
abstract: Introduction Depression and other mental health challenges can affect daily functioning and well-being, while social stigma and limited access to culturally appropriate digital resources may discourage individuals from seeking support. This study presents REWAA, a bilingual mobile application designed to support emotional self-tracking, access to mental health resources, and interaction with mental health professionals in Arabic and English. title: A text-mining analysis of climate risk disclosure and corporate energy efficiency in Chinese listed firms
abstract: This study examines the association between climate risk disclosure and corporate energy efficiency using Chinese A-share data from 2012 to 2024. A firm-level disclosure index is constructed via text mining based on the TCFD framework. Two-way fixed effects models show a positive association, with a one-standard-deviation increase in disclosure corresponding to approximately a 3.6% increase in energy efficiency, robust to endogeneity tests. title: Cultural Representation in English Culinary Menu Translations to Enhance Tourism in South Sulawesi
abstract: Culinary tourism has become a significant driver of destination attractiveness, particularly in culturally rich regions such as South Sulawesi, Indonesia. This study examines how cultural representation is conveyed in English culinary menu translations and how it contributes to enhancing tourism experiences. title: Optimal desynchronization of a noisy simplicial phase oscillator population based on backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs)
abstract: This paper studies optimal desynchronization in a noisy population of phase oscillators with pairwise and triadic interactions. The model combines stochastic phase dynamics, higher-order collective coupling, and a finite-horizon control objective that penalizes both coherence and control effort. title: Can nationally determined contributions anchor regional policy and strategic developments in the southern African development community? Lessons from a development-climate ambition dichotomy in the Inkomati-Usuthu catchment management area
abstract: The dichotomy between climate change, sustainable development, and critical resource demands sits at the crux of transboundary basin cooperation and climate action approaches. The Inkomati-Usuthu basin in South Africa reflects a national and supranational development-climate action dichotomy that shapes policy and climate-action configurations. title: Local environment shapes habitat suitability of the endangered mint Dicerandra cornutissima
abstract: Abstract Ecological niche models are shaped by the spatial and environmental scales at which they are built, making environmental grain especially important for range‐restricted species with specialized habitat requirements. We used fine‐scale environmental data at 250 m resolution to estimate the ecological niche characteristics of Dicerandra cornutissima , an endangered mint endemic to xeric scrub and sandhill habitats in central Florida. title: Forest restoration scenarios of Brazil’s Atlantic Forest with constrained multi-objective optimisation
abstract: Brazil’s Atlantic Forest has lost over 85% of its original cover and harbours one of the world’s densest concentrations of endemic species. Designing restoration plans that simultaneously maximise landscape connectivity, satisfy legal obligations, and stay within budget remains an open challenge. Existing decision-support tools require planners to pre-specify trade-off weights, returning a single solution that cannot reveal the full connectivity–cost exchange. title: Common targets, unfunded therapies: regulatory mapping and cost-utility of precision oncology for metastatic colorectal cancer in Brazil's public health system
abstract: BACKGROUND: Molecular targets are common in metastatic colorectal cancer, yet Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS) does not fund any biomarker-matched therapy. Where each pathway is interrupted-evidence, regulatory indication, incorporation, testing, or price-and what would overcome each barrier remain unclear. title: Molecular Thermodynamics of Lower Critical Solution Temperature Ionic Liquid/Water Mixtures: Tetrabutylphosphonium Trifluoroacetate
abstract: Lower critical solution temperature (LCST) ionic liquids (ILs) are thermoresponsive materials that undergo liquid-liquid demixing with water into water-rich (WR) and IL-rich (ILR) phases upon heating. Despite the vast combinatorial space of cation-anion pairings, LCST behavior is observed in only a handful of aqueous ILs. title: Measurement-informed fatigue-driven reliability analysis for century-old corroded steel rail-bridge integrating Bayesian inference and FORM
abstract: Abstract Fatigue damage is a predominant failure mechanism in historical riveted railway bridges, which is intensified by corrosion over time. This paper presents a fatigue-based reliability analysis of a century-old riveted steel railway bridge, decommissioned in 2010 due to significant corrosion-induced fatigue damage. As part of the German Thüringen railway system connecting Wolkramshausen and Erfurt, this bridge serves as a case study for observing a combined influence of fatigue and corrosion on the structural performance. journal: Journal of Civil Structural Health Monitoring

title: Plant‐ and Microbial‐Derived Soil Organic Carbon: Global Patterns and Divergent Climatic Associations
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) pools reflect the net balance of plant- and microbial-derived inputs, transformation, and loss, yet a global-scale assessment of distribution patterns, relative contributions, and hierarchical environmental correlates of microbial necromass carbon (MNC) and plant-derived carbon (PdC) remains incomplete. title: Comparison of Hydrochemical Characteristics of Groundwater in the Qihe River Alluvial Fan of North China over the Past 35 Years
abstract: Groundwater resources play a crucial role in socioeconomic development and domestic water use in piedmont alluvial plain areas. In this study, the Qihe River alluvial fan (QRAF) was selected as a representative area to investigate the evolutionary patterns of shallow groundwater chemistry in the North China Plain (NCP). Based on shallow groundwater monitoring data collected during the wet seasons of 1983 and 2017, the spatiotemporal trends in chemical characteristics and their influencing factors in shallow groundwater in the QRAF were studied using multi-hydrochemical and statistical methods.

abstract: Fiber-shaped batteries have moved beyond proof-of-concept demonstrations and are increasingly being treated as load-bearing, deformable power components for electronic textiles. Their practical performance, however, is governed by a coupled problem: electrochemical reactions must remain spatially uniform while slender multilayer structures are bent, twisted, stretched, woven, washed, and repeatedly loaded. title: A CRITIC-weighted composite meteorological indicator incorporating solar radiation and its assessment against residential natural-gas consumption: a case study of Sakarya, Türkiye
abstract: Composite indicators are used to summarize several meteorological variables for energy studies, but objective weighting schemes are rarely tested against measured energy use. title: Investigating Associations Between Media Sentiment Surrounding Climate Change Engagement (SDG 13) and Performance Measures: A Study of FTSE 100 Listed Firms
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether media coverage of climate change action (SDG 13) by FTSE 100 firms is associated with business performance in the following year. Drawing on 406,052 news articles published between 2013 and 2022, the study adopts a novel bibliometric keyword‐extraction approach to identify the valence of SDG 13‐related coverage of these firms. A dynamic panel model estimated by the generalized method of moments estimator shows that adverse SDG 13 media coverage of a firm is negatively associated with its sales, net profit, and Tobin's Q . title: Assessing Dothistroma needle blight severity in Pinus radiata using UAV multispectral imagery
abstract: Dothistroma needle blight (DNB) is a major foliar disease of Pinus radiata , an important plantation species in several Southern Hemisphere countries. DNB management and resistance breeding depend on subjective, labour-intensive visual severity scoring that is difficult to scale. Prior UAV studies have used broad severity categories and crown-mean reflectance, discarding both the ordinal structure of the field grade and the within-crown spatial pattern of infection. title: Investigating the Impact of Social Capital on Social Resilience and Mapping Informal Settlements
abstract: Marginalization and informal urbanization pose significant challenges in global south countries. This study aims to show the crucial role of social capital in enhancing social resilience in informal urban areas. The research utilizes an applied-developmental approach with a descriptive-correlation methodology. Data collection involves library research and fieldwork in five districts of Urmia, with a sample size of 384 determined using Cochran's formula and distributed randomly. The questionnaire's validity was confirmed by experts, and reliability was assessed using the Cronbach's alpha test.

title: Nusselt Number Correlation for Elliptical Helical Coils Based on Computational Fluid Dynamics and Experiments
abstract: A helical coil is an important component of wrapped helical-coil heat exchangers around an external tank, which helps reduce direct contact between the working fluid in the coil and the fluid inside the tank. Therefore, it is suitable for applications requiring contamination control. However, the design of this type of coil still has limitations, because the correlations used to predict the Nusselt number (𝑁𝑢), which is an indicator of heat transfer performance, have mostly been developed for circular-cross-section helical coils. title: 3D-Printed Triboelectric Nanogenerators: Materials, Challenges and Applications
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional printing (3DP) or additive manufacturing (AM) technology offers a systematic solution for revolutionizing triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) fabrication through multi-scale structural design and functional material integration. This review provides a systematic overview of the technological pathways, materials, challenges and core advancements in 3D-printed TENGs. title: Optimizing the Efficiency of Land Registration in Indonesia Through SAM-Geo: An Automated Farmland Detection and Segmentation Method
abstract: The application of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in the Complete Systematic Land Registration (CSLR) and Participatory Systematic Land Registration (PTSL) programs significantly accelerates land mapping through aerial photogrammetry. This method substantially enhances accuracy in land certification processes, boundary identification, disaster mitigation efforts, and spatial planning efficiency. However, despite its effectiveness, manual intervention remains necessary when ground objects are obstructed or parcel boundaries are visually indistinct. title: Analytical and experimental performance analysis of thermoelectric generators for low-grade water stream heat recovery
abstract: Thermoelectric generators (TEGs) present a promising technology for recovering thermal energy from waste heat in water streams; however, their performance under low-grade heat and continuous-flow conditions has not yet been fully characterized. This study presents a combined analytical and experimental investigation of a custom-designed thermoelectric energy recovery system integrated into a boiler–chiller water loop, representative of waste-heat recovery applications in water streams such as HVAC and industrial wastewater. title: Geological and climatic controls on landslide susceptibility and hazard along the Amarnath pilgrimage corridor, Kashmir Himalaya
abstract: Landslides are a recurrent and increasingly consequential hazard across the Himalaya, where steep terrain, tectonically weakened lithologies, climatic variability, and expanding anthropogenic activity interact to destabilize slopes. This study assesses landslide susceptibility along the Baltal-Amarnath-Panjtarni-Poshpathri pilgrimage corridor in the upper Sind catchment, Jhelum basin of the Kashmir Himalaya, India, using an integrated framework that combines high-resolution remote sensing, field-based geological mapping, geotechnical investigations, and climate-data analysis. abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) play a pivotal role in regulating RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), which are crucial in the progression of colorectal cancer (CRC). This study aims to explore the role of PTMs in modulating RBPs and their implications for CRC pathogenesis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We characterized phosphorylation, ubiquitination, and malonylation of RBPs in CRC using previously generated post-translational multi-omics datasets from paired CRC and adjacent non-tumor tissues in our previous studies. abstract: ABSTRACT The present work addresses the feasibility of friction stir lap welding (FSLW) for the joining of polycarbonate to nylon‐6 sheets in overlapped configuration. The effects of tool rotational speed, traverse speed, plunge depth using different tool pin profiles (swept ratios) were studied on quality characteristics of dissimilar welds using response surface methodology (RSM). title: Multi-stage near-field millimetre-wave phase processing for quantitative visualization of subsurface corrosion in 3LPE-coated metallic pipelines
abstract: Abstract Three-layer polyethylene (3LPE) coated metallic pipelines are widely used in oil and gas transportation, yet localized subsurface corrosion poses a major threat to pipeline safety. This study proposes a physics-guided multi-stage near-field millimetre-wave (NMMW) phase-processing framework for quantitative visualization of artificial corrosion beneath 3LPE coatings. title: Combinatorial Tuning of Multigene Biosynthetic Pathways based on RNA Interference
abstract: Fine-tuning the expression level of multigene pathways remains a major challenge in engineering eukaryotic microbial cell factories. Modifications to individual pathway genes and CRISPR-based approaches often require repeated genome reconstruction, large regulatory components, or complex guide-array assembly. Here, we developed a lightweight, post-transcriptional RNAi-based strategy that enables fine-tuning gene expression without iterative genome editing. title: Characterising the occurrence of monomodal and multimodal ice hydrometeor populations and their fall speeds in midlatitude frontal ice clouds using radar Doppler spectra
abstract: Multimodality in vertically pointing radar Doppler spectra is frequently observed in stratiform clouds, but understanding the microphysical processes causing these signatures, and indeed quantifying their occurrence, remains a challenge. In this study, we utilise Ka-band radar Doppler spectra from 23 deep stratiform clouds observed over Chilbolton, UK. We apply a peak finding algorithm to identify spectral reflectivity peaks in the Doppler spectra, which can be used to infer the presence of distinct coexisting ice particle populations, such as pristine crystals mixed with aggregate snowflakes.

title: AN INSIGHT INTO 'ILĀJ BI'L TADBĪR (REGIMENAL THERAPY) FROM PAST TO CONTEMPORARY INNOVATIONS
abstract: There are four methods of treatment employed in Unani system of medicine, namely ‘Ilāj bi’l Dawā (Pharmacotherapy), ‘Ilāj bi’l Ghidha’ (Dietotherapy), ‘Ilāj bi’l Tadbīr (Regimenal therapy), ‘Ilāj bi’l Yad (Surgery). Dietotherapy aims at treating certain ailments by the administration of specific diets or by regulating the quality and quantity of food. title: Genomic resilience of aquatic microbes in Sangam: insights from the Mahakumbh event
abstract: The Mahakumbh festival at Prayagraj represents an exceptionally intense and temporally concentrated anthropogenic perturbation superimposed on the dynamic riverine ecosystem at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers. The large gathering of people during the festival can alter organic loading, nutrient availability, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, microbial inputs, and exposure to pharmaceutical, fecal, and other anthropogenic contaminants, thereby providing a valuable natural observational framework for investigating microbial community responses to environmental disturbance. title: Development and characterization of TiB2 reinforced carbon fibre/PEEK composites for enhanced dynamic performance
abstract: Carbon-fibre-reinforced polyether ether ketone (CF/PEEK) offers a lightweight alternative to metallic fastening components, but its vibration response and mechanical performance can be further tailored through particulate reinforcement. This study investigates TiB 2 -reinforced CF/PEEK hybrid composites and their application in lightweight polymer bolts, with particular emphasis on the relationship between TiB 2 content, microstructural evolution, mechanical behaviour, thermal stability, and dynamic response. title: Socio-economic and Tribal Inequity in Healthcare Use and Out-of-Pocket Expenditure in Odisha
abstract: Odisha reports one of India's lowest out-of-pocket (OOP) expenditures per hospitalization and near-universal publicly funded insurance. Low spending may signal financial protection, but it may also reflect forgone care among poor and Scheduled Tribe (ST) households. Using NSS 75th Round (2017–18) and 80th Round (2025) unit-level data covering 19,078 and 22,315 persons in Odisha, with India as benchmark, this paper estimates Erreygers-corrected concentration indices, indirect need standardization, and Wagstaff decompositions to measure horizontal inequity (HI) in reported illness, outpatient tr

title: Enhanced IsiA accumulation under low light does not expand the functional antenna of photosystem I
abstract: Introduction Iron scarcity triggers specific acclimatory responses in cyanobacteria, among which is the synthesis of the IsiA protein that can associate with photosystem I (PSI) and increase its antenna size. However, cellular IsiA also occurs as PSI-free assemblies that do not contribute to PSI excitation, suggesting multiple physiological roles. In natural environments, limiting and stress factors often act simultaneously, causing co-limitation effects. title: Classifying type-specific green space using satellite imagery and LiDAR to assess associations with diabetes prevalence
abstract: Urban green space is often measured using greenness indices, such as the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index, but these indices do not distinguish among green space types. This study integrated 3-metre spatial resolution multispectral imagery and LiDAR-derived normalized Digital Surface Models (nDSM) to classify type-specific green spaces across Mississauga, Ontario, and examine their associations with diabetes prevalence. title: Sustainable co-production of electricity, hydrogen, oxygen, and cooling through waste heat recovery in seamless pipe production
abstract: Environmental pollution and concerns about the depletion of fossil fuel resources are driving the world towards energy sources that do not rely on fossil fuels. Hydrogen is a valuable and clean energy source that can help address these challenges. Utilizing waste energy in high-consumption industries to produce hydrogen could offer a solution for optimizing energy use and mitigating related issues. abstract: En este artículo se examina cómo las colisiones interpretativas del derecho procesal civil colombiano inciden en la materialización de los derechos sustanciales. title: Development of Markov model and an adaptive method for planning amphibious operations under dynamic stochastic threats
abstract: The object of this research is the process of planning and adjusting ship routes during amphibious operations under conditions of dynamic stochastic threats. The problem lies in the need to promptly adjust pre-planned ship routes in the event of changes in stochastic threats while simultaneously ensuring the necessary level of force survivability. title: Temporal Layering and Rule-Based Matching in Distributed Settlement Ledgers: A Multi-Horizon Reconciliation Architecture for Financial Break Detection
abstract: Financial settlement breaks remain a persistent operational risk. Batch-only reconciliation detects them only after end-of-day cutoff, while stream-based approaches often sacrifice coverage or lack shared rule semantics across horizons. This paper presents a multi-horizon reconciliation architecture coordinating three tiers over one transaction stream: daily batch, hourly incremental partitioning, and real-time listener-based interception. abstract: Characterizing multi-lithofacies aquifer architecture from sparse borehole data is essential for groundwater flow and solute transport modeling, yet remains challenging because categorical lithofacies fields must honor hard conditioning data while representing realistic proportions, anisotropic continuity, and connectivity. abstract: Impacts of invasions may be assumed to be spatially uniform, but few published studies have tested whether impacts from the initial location of an invasion are transferrable. We address this gap using the Asian swamp eel ( Monopterus albus/javanensis ), a predatory fish whose establishment in one smaller drainage (Taylor Slough) of southern Everglades National Park (Florida, USA) was linked to subsequent declines of native fishes and crayfishes. abstract: Chloride-containing fertilizers, especially those used as accompanying components in nitrogen fertilizers, are widely applied into the soil for agricultural production. However, the long-term impacts of this chloride input on nitrification and inorganic nitrogen supply remain poorly understood. title: Beyond Coverage: Recomposition, Mechanism, and Divergence in Health Equity in Odisha, India
abstract: This paper departs from the standard question of whether low out-of-pocket (OOP) spending in Odisha reflects financial protection or forgone care. It asks instead whether the architecture of inequity has been rebuilt as insurance expanded, whether tribal exclusion is produced by supply-side or demand-side failures, and whether the standard equity indicators used to monitor universal health coverage (UHC) are internally consistent. abstract: ABSTRACT Even as the legitimacy of states appears to derive ever more explicitly from nationalist claims, nation‐states and national economies remain deeply entangled. abstract: Abstract Objective Management efforts for Largemouth Bass Micropterus nigricans, Florida Bass M. salmoides, and resulting hybrid fisheries (hereafter, referred to as the Largemouth Bass complex [LBc]) include the production of robust individuals for commercial and recreational purposes. abstract: Background Small island cities grow on scarce, steep, and hazard-prone land. Negeri Batu Merah, a customary village in Ambon City, is classified as a heavy slum area with 66,424 people on 911 ha. abstract: The global geography, behaviour, and impact of fires are shifting, as spatially varying human influences interact with a visibly changing climate. abstract: Abstract Raman spectroscopy is a powerful technique for molecular identification and quantitative analysis, but inherently weak scattering limits its use at low analyte concentrations. abstract: Forests are major sinks for atmospheric mercury (Hg) due to the efficiency of stomatal uptake and litter deposition. Tropical forests, highly productive ecosystems, remain understudied despite their pronounced climatic and phenological variability. abstract: In this study, we develop and characterize an advanced holographic instrument – HOLODROPS (HOLOgraphic DROPlet Sensor). abstract: Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans ( A. ferrooxidans ) exhibits strong arsenic resistance and plays a pivotal role in biometallurgy and sulfur cycling in ecosystems. abstract: Trend-driven environments change rapidly, and consumers' decision responses may fluctuate. These fluctuations may be shaped by emotional directions underpinned by different motivational bases: social pressure, self-endorsed values, or both. abstract: This study examines the historical foundations and gradual evolution of Pakistan-China relations, highlighting the enduring friendship between the two countries over seven and a half decades. abstract: The use of operational data from industrial machines can support the identification of abnormalities and maintenance planning. abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the mechanical feasibility and locomotion stability of microalgae-driven biohybrid micromachines under mass-loading conditions, a question that remains unexplored despite growing interest in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii-powered microrobotics. Five voxel-based micromachine designs (M1–M5), structurally inspired by experimentally validated microtrap architectures, were modeled in PyBullet and subjected to 15 simulations each under unloaded and suspended-particle-loaded conditions. title: Evaluation of the plant glucoside monoterpene indole alkaloid brachycerine for potential protection of human skin against ultraviolet damage
abstract: Sunlight ultraviolet radiation A and B (UV-A and UV-B) affect human skin and may be a cause of cancer. Damage to skin nerve fibers and cell DNA is often observed following excessive unprotected exposure. Plants produce numerous specialized metabolites involved in stress mitigation. Brachycerine, a major leaf glucoside alkaloid from the tree Psychotria brachyceras, absorbs in the UV range and is a powerful antioxidant protecting the photosynthetic machinery against this radiation. title: Detection of poly (vinyl chloride) microplastics through an optical fiber sensor: Effects of hydrodynamics and water matrix
abstract: Aging of poly(vinyl) chloride (PVC) tap water pipes may release microplastics (MPs) into water. Optical fiber sensors that detect MPs by utilizing refractive index (RI) changes in the evanescent field offers potential for in situ detection. This study evaluates the effects of water matrix, MP sizes, and hydrodynamics on the response and sensitivity of optical fiber sensors for PVC-MP detection in water supply pipes. abstract: Abstract Acid-extractable concentrations of Cr, Mn, Cu, Zn, As, Cd and Pb were measured by ICP-MS in 80 composite topsoil samples collected from five agricultural sites in the West Bank, Palestine, near wastewater sources or a landfill. title: Environmental due diligence and the scoping problem in circular infrastructure
abstract: International courts and tribunals have converged, across 2024 and 2025, on a standard of due diligence that is ‘informed by the best available science’. Commentary reads this convergence as an epistemic ratchet: as the evidence base improves, the obligation tightens. This article argues that the ratchet operates principally on the content of an assessment and only marginally on its frame, and that the difference is decisive for circular water and waste infrastructure. abstract: Abstract Urban heat is often mapped at pixel or neighborhood scale, although adaptation decisions are implemented through bounded public assets. We test a facility-aligned screening framework using Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2 imagery, Local Climate Zone context, and five surface indicators for 158 public primary schools in Barcelona and 276 in Madrid during July-August 2014–2024 (21,438 complete pixel-year observations). title: Beyond canopy cover: UAV-LiDAR reveals three-dimensional structural divergence and parsimonious candidate diagnostic traits for mangrove monitoring
abstract: Canopy cover is widely used in mangrove monitoring, yet its ability to represent three-dimensional (3D) community structure has rarely been quantified. We used UAV-LiDAR to survey 38 10 × 10 m plots across embanked (BW), tidal-creek (TC), and tidal-flat (TF) habitats on Jinniu Island, China, with TC and TF further pooled as tidally connected habitats (TCH). Seventeen structural traits spanning five dimensions were derived to compare the habitat-response strength of 2D canopy coverage and 3D structure and to identify a parsimonious set of candidate diagnostic traits. title: The task utility gap in human mobility modeling: evidence from environmental exposure assessment
abstract: Human mobility data are essential for applications such as environmental exposure assessment, but privacy constraints limit access to large-scale trajectory datasets. Trajectory generative models offer a promising solution, yet whether statistical-fidelity-based evaluation guarantees task utility remains unclear. Task utility is defined as the agreement between downstream results derived from generated and observed trajectories. title: Wavelet denoising of inertial sensor input data for GNSS-INS integration: simulation approach
abstract: Integrated Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and Inertial Navigation System (INS) architectures are widely employed to achieve reliable and continuous navigation under conditions of signal blockage, interference, and degraded satellite visibility. Although GNSS provides long-term positioning accuracy, its performance deteriorates in challenging environments, whereas INS offers continuous navigation as a self-contained system but suffers from accumulated inertial sensor errors and drift over time. abstract: ABSTRACT Static magnetic field effects on dissolved CO 2 /carbonic acid (H 2 CO 3 ) equilibria and ethanol–water hydrogen‐bond network reorganization were investigated using Raman, FTIR, and UV–Vis spectroscopy combined with principal component analysis (PCA), partial least squares regression (PLS‐R), and variable importance in projection (VIP) scoring. title: Autonomous Collision Avoidance for eVTOL in Air-Ground Coordination Based on Rule-Constrained Dynamic Velocity Obstacle
abstract: Abstract Autonomous collision avoidance for electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft in structured urban low-altitude airspace must satisfy both physical collision-prevention requirements and operational rules. This study proposes a rule-constrained dynamic velocity vector optimization (RC-DVVO) framework. First, urban low-altitude operational rules, including no-fly zones, flight corridors, altitude layers, and speed limits, are decomposed and mapped into a time-varying rule-feasible domain in velocity space. title: Overview of the Current Development Status and Key Technologies of 6G Integrated Sensing and Communication Technology
abstract: Currently, the mobile communication system is steadily progressing from the 5G commercial stage to the 6G technology verification stage. The integrated sensing and communication technology, which deeply merges communication transmission with environmental perception, will redefine the service boundaries of the next-generation wireless network. title: Spillover effect between oil prices, climate risks, and carbon prices in China: dynamic effects and key drivers
abstract: Against the backdrop of escalating global climate change and volatile international oil markets, the interdependence among energy prices, climate-risk information, and carbon markets has become increasingly prominent. Clarifying their dynamic spillover patterns is important for climate governance, energy security, and carbon-market risk management. This study examines the dynamic interactions among decomposed oil price shocks, physical and transition climate-risk indices, and China’s regional carbon price represented by the Guangdong pilot market. A dual-channel optical sensor for real-time microplastic classification via ratiometric fluorescence analysis
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are widespread contaminants of water and food, yet available methods for polymer identification remain costly, time-consuming, and poorly suited to continuous monitoring. We describe SMILE, a compact, low-cost fluorescence platform developed as a proof of concept for the automated detection and classification of selected MPs in flowing water. title: Molecular origin of pressure-induced re-entrant phase separation of CO2–H2O mixtures
abstract: CO 2 and H 2 O are the predominant fluid components in the Earth’s interior, spanning from the crust to the mantle. Fluid–fluid immiscibility in binary CO 2 –H 2 O fluids is of particular interest owing to its implications for geochemical processes and industrial applications, including geological CO 2 sequestration. CO 2 –H 2 O fluids exhibit re-entrant phase separation upon compression, yet, the microscopic origin of this behaviour remains unclear, in contrast to well-studied temperature-induced re-entrant phenomena. title: Bioconvective prandtl hybrid nanofluid flow over a rotating stretching sheet with activation energy
abstract: Hybrid nanofluids have attracted considerable attention for advanced thermal-management applications because of their enhanced heat-transfer characteristics compared with conventional single-particle nanofluids. This study investigates magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flow and heat and mass transfer of a Prandtl hybrid nanofluid containing zinc (Zn) and aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃) nanoparticles suspended in water over a stretching surface embedded in a porous rotating medium. title: Mapping environmental and agricultural health within One Health research: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis
abstract: The position of environmental and agricultural health within One Health literature remains insufficiently characterized. The aim of this study was to examine publication patterns, collaboration networks, conceptual structures, thematic evolution, and research fronts connecting environmental and agricultural health within explicitly One Health-oriented literature. A total of 1,852 English-language articles were retrieved from Scopus. Bibliometric and science-mapping analyses were conducted using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. abstract: ABSTRACT Runoff in the upper Hanjiang River Basin (HRB), a major water source for China's South‐to‐North Water Transfer Project, has changed under combined climatic and anthropogenic influences, but their relative roles remain unclear. This study examined long‐term changes in precipitation, runoff, and runoff coefficient during 1961–2020 and quantified indirect pathways linking climatic and anthropogenic factors to runoff during 2000–2020 using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM). abstract: Abstract This study applies a large-scale unsupervised learning pipeline to Saber Pro microdata from 452,020 Colombian higher education students (2021 to 2023), integrating academic performance across five modules with socioeconomic, financing, labor, digital-asset, and educational-background variables. K-means, Gaussian Mixture Models, DBSCAN, and HDBSCAN were evaluated on UMAP-reduced representations across 128 configurations, using a two-phase design: hyperparameter search on a validated 200,000-record stratified sample, followed by retraining on the full dataset. title: Symbolism of space and ritual-healing practices in the traditional dwelling of the Dnipro Ukraine region in the second half of the 20th century
abstract: Background. The traditional hut of the Dnieper region of the second half of the 20th century is considered as a holistic symbolic space, within which spatial zoning and interior elements become carriers of spiritual, ritual and healing-magical practices. The main attention of the article is focused on the key elements of the dwelling (stove, penance, icons, textiles, home amulets) as symbolically loaded loci associated with folk beliefs and ideas about protection, treatment and harmonization of space. title: OUTAGE SITUATIONAL AWARENESS FOR TRANSMISSION STORM RESTORATION: A REVIEW OF DATA SOURCES, INTEROPERABILITY STANDARDS, AND OPEN GAPS
abstract: Restoring the transmission system after severe weather depends on an accurate and current picture of what is out of service, what has lost its source of supply, and how restoration is progressing. That picture is assembled from data built for other purposes: outage-management records, real-time telemetry and topology processing, asset records, network models, and a growing set of public datasets. title: Translational pharmacology of (+)-terrein: from biological activity to oral and periodontal therapeutic development
abstract: Previous terrein reviews have emphasized its isolation, synthesis, production, and broad biological activities. Among the prior reviews identified in the literature, no oral/dental indication-specific critical appraisal was found that integrated chemical comparability, evidence directness, exposure, target engagement, formulation, safety, and reproducibility. title: Millimeter‐Scale Single‐Layer RGB Achromatic Metalens via Time‐Simultaneity‐Free Design
abstract: ABSTRACT Compact and high‐performance optical components are essential for miniaturizing next‐generation imaging and display systems. While metalenses offer a promising ultrathin alternative to refractive optics, scaling up achromatic metalenses is fundamentally hindered by the trade‐off between aperture size and operational bandwidth. title: Latest Oligocene amphibians from Coderet (France)
abstract: The French locality of Coderet (latest Oligocene, MP30) yielded an astonishing number of amphibian fossil remains. The studied amphibian assemblage from Coderet consists of 8,639 skeletal remains referred to 10 taxa, making it a hot spot for diversity during the Palaeogene. Urodeles are the dominant group, almost 99% of the fossils, represented by the family Salamandridae, including both subfamilies Salamandrinae and Pleurodelinae. abstract: Abstract Under global warming, compound heatwave and drought events (CHDEs) have become increasingly frequent. title: Extreme Hurricanes and Forest-Sector Employment: Evidence from Hurricane Michael
abstract: Abstract Hurricanes of increasing intensity are major disturbances in the southeastern United States, affecting working forests and forest-dependent economies. This study examines employment impacts of Hurricane Michael across the forestry supply chain, including forestry, logging, and wood products industries. title: Sustainable Polysaccharide‐Based Triboelectric Nanogenerators for the Biomechanical Harvesting and Real‐Time Motion Monitoring System
abstract: Self‐powered sensors are becoming increasingly essential for creating sustainable, autonomous devices, as they eliminate the need for external power sources. In this study, we introduce the design and fabrication of environmentally friendly green triboelectric nanogenerators (G‐TENGs), offering a simple, low‐cost, and eco‐friendly method for converting mechanical stress into electrical energy for self‐powered sensing. abstract: In the Pacific Northwest region of the United States, forests within the range of the Northern Spotted Owl (Strix occidentalis caurina) have changed dramatically over the last two centuries. It began with the loss of frequent fires that indigenous communities set annually to manage their natural resources. This change was exacerbated a century later with the advent of effective fire suppression by the United States Forest Service. title: Integrating social vulnerability and landslide susceptibility for spatial risk assessment in the Langat basin, Malaysia
abstract: Landslides are among the most significant natural hazards in Malaysia, threatening human lives, infrastructure, and socioeconomic development. This study developed an integrated landslide risk assessment framework by combining landslide susceptibility modelling and social vulnerability analysis in the Langat Basin, Malaysia. Landslide susceptibility was modelled using the Frequency Ratio (FR) approach based on six conditioning factors: elevation, slope, aspect, geology, land use, and distance to river. abstract: Accurate and reliable detection of missing bolts remains challenging under exposure anomalies, low illumination, and cluttered backgrounds. Visible images are sensitive to illumination changes and may lose texture and detail, whereas infrared images are more illumination-robust but lack the detail and resolution required for accurate standalone detection. abstract: Las comunidades pesqueras del litoral venezolano afectadas por los terremotos de 2026 dependen de un trabajo femenino poco registrado, por cuanto los sistemas algorítmicos de ayuda pueden invisibilizar sus necesidades laborales y reproductivas. abstract: Accurate tomato instance segmentation in greenhouse scenes remains challenging because of fruit occlusion, instance contact, ambiguous boundaries, and the visual similarity between green fruits and leaves. This study presents a lightweight YOLO11n-seg framework that combines a morphology-based shape-boundary-driven (SBD) weighting strategy with the previously proposed CMPRD multi-scale context module. abstract: This study examines the metaphorical framework of “natural disaster” in health communication discourse on the COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnamese online newspapers. abstract: Objective To conduct a scoping review of non-material preparedness for household disaster readiness in the context of disasters, and to provide a reference for improving household emergency response and disaster preparedness capabilities. abstract: Global lithium demand has increased rapidly, driven largely by expanding battery production, with consumption estimated at 263, 263,000 t in 2025. Oilfield- produced water in North America has emerged as a potential additional lithium source, particularly because oil and gas production already generates large volumes of this waste stream.

abstract: Agriculture remains a fundamental pillar of the economy of Uzbekistan, providing employment for a significant portion of the population and contributing substantially to the gross domestic product (GDP). However, traditional agricultural practices in the region are increasingly challenged by critical water scarcity, land degradation, climate volatility, and fluctuating market demands. abstract: Waste accumulation presents an environmental challenge that cannot be understood solely through individual disposal behavior, particularly where waste disposal facilities are limited. This study aims to explore community environmental awareness amid limited waste disposal facilities in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia, focusing on how residents understand waste accumulation, perceive environmental responsibility, and respond to infrastructural constraints in their everyday lives. title: Pantoea agglomerans T6SS effectors reside in hotspots with combinatorial antibacterial and antiviral arsenals
abstract: ABSTRACT Gram-negative bacteria deploy type VI secretion systems (T6SSs) to mediate interbacterial competition. Although numerous T6SS effectors have been identified, their pan-genomic repertoires and evolutionary dynamics remain poorly understood. Here, we combine proteomics and comparative genomics to map the T6SS effector landscape across Pantoea agglomerans , a species that includes pathogenic and beneficial strains. title: CREATING AN INTERACTIVE WEB MAP FOR THE LOWER AMU DARYA STATE BIOSPHERE RESERVE BASED ON THE GOOGLE EARTH ENGINE PLATFORM
abstract: This article describes the methodology for monitoring the ecological state of the Lower Amu Darya State Biosphere Reserve and creating an interactive web map based on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform. The study analysed spatial-dynamic changes in land cover, vegetation status, and water bodies based on Sentinel-2 satellite images. Using the Google Earth Engine platform allows for rapid processing of large-scale remote sensing data, visualisation of ecological processes, and creation of web-cartographic resources that support decision-making.

abstract: This study examined the utilization of instructive strategies in teaching Grade 7 Mathematics and their association with students’ academic performance in selected public secondary schools in Santa Fe District, Bantayan 1 District, and Tabogon District, Cebu Province, during School Year 2026–2027. abstract: Despite extensive protein engineering efforts to significantly increase the catalytic efficiency of plastic-degrading enzymes, inefficient plastic-enzyme interactions during the interfacial biocatalytic process continue to impede their widespread applications.
