title: Impact of Reservoirs on Streamflow Extremes in India
abstract: Abstract India has an extensive network of reservoirs, yet their influence on streamflow extremes remains poorly quantified. To understand how reservoirs have altered the natural flow regime across India, we integrate 223 reservoirs into a national hydrologic modeling system integrating Noah‐MP land surface model and MizuRoute hydrodynamic model. title: Spatial variations in wet-bulb globe temperature during the Bank of America Chicago Marathon
abstract: Prior work has recommended the use of Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) to inform operational management of marathons. However, there is limited and potentially conflicting results on the spatial extent at which WBGT should be measured to sufficiently capture racecourse variability. abstract: The corrosion of buried natural-gas pipelines is jointly governed by soil ionic composition, pH, and interfacial mass transport. title: Water Vapor Buoyancy and the African Easterly Jet
abstract: Abstract The African easterly jet (AEJ) is a prominent circulation feature in the tropical atmosphere. It transports mineral dust and affects easterly waves that serve as seeds for hurricanes. Conventional wisdom holds that the AEJ is in thermal wind balance with the positive meridional temperature gradient over North Africa. title: A high-precision measurement method for ruby balls based on multi-scale adaptive edge detection
abstract: A high-precision, non-contact measurement method for ruby balls is proposed by integrating annular dark-field imaging with multi-scale adaptive edge detection. Multi-scale gradient-response fusion and entropy-guided local thresholding are used to improve outer-contour extraction under non-uniform contrast and noise. Cubic-spline interpolation provides sub-pixel edge localization, while RANSAC screening and geometric-distance circle fitting reduce the influence of outliers. title: Inter-simulator reactive-transport modelling of CO2 trapping mechanisms in the UK Bunter Sandstone Formation
abstract: Reliable prediction of subsurface CO 2 behavior is critical for the safe deployment of geological CO 2 storage. The Bunter Sandstone Formation is a prospective storage reservoir in the UK. However, uncertainties remain regarding geochemical reactions between rock-forming minerals and CO 2 -saturated brine and the consistency of storage predictions across reactive-transport simulators. This study investigates mineral trapping and associated geochemical evolution during 50 years of CO 2 injection into the Bunter Sandstone Formation. abstract: Contaminated sites of hazardous waste disposal are recognized as a global environmental and public health challenge. This study characterized organic contamination using 416 soil and 48 groundwater samples from a typical contaminated site of hazardous waste disposal in Jiangxi province, China, and assessed health risks under restricted use without redevelopment and industrial redevelopment. abstract: Drought is a significant hydrological hazard that leaves a serious footprint on the environment, society and human life. Water resources, agricultural productivity, ecosystems, livelihoods and socio-economic well-beings are negatively impacted by drought. title: Genome-wide association study of growth-related traits in mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi): identification of cross-trait associated loci and candidate genes using single-trait and multivariate linear mixed models
abstract: Mandarin fish ( S. chuatsi ) is China’s most economically important freshwater aquaculture species, yet selective breeding remains constrained by long generation intervals and limited genomic resources. We performed whole-genome resequencing of 98 Siniperca chuatsi individuals (minimum 10-fold coverage), retaining 1,310,398 quality-controlled bi-allelic SNPs across 24 chromosomes. abstract: Innovation is widely seen as a driver of sales growth, but little is known about how consumers in emerging markets respond to innovation in everyday products such as carbonated beverages. This study explores how product innovation influences consumer purchase behavior, satisfaction and brand loyalty in Wa Municipal, Ghana. abstract: En Los modelos extensos de lenguaje (MEL) como ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini y Claude han mostrado avances significativos en la traducción automática; no obstante, la traducción del habla coloquial sigue siendo un reto debido a la presencia de expresiones idiomáticas, jerga marcadores pragmáticos y referencias culturales. abstract: Phospholipid-bound omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PL-ω-PUFAs) represent a novel class of functional lipids with glycerophospholipids as carriers, which have garnered extensive attention in the intervention of chronic metabolic diseases. abstract: SWound healing is a dynamic process regulated by mechanical cues, inflammation, cellular senescence, extracellular matrix remodeling, and regenerative signaling. Dysregulated mechanotransduction can alter cell behavior, gene expression, and tissue architecture, contributing to persistent inflammation, senescence, infection, and chronic non-healing wounds. title: Rapid RPA ‐Cas12a Assay for Streptococcus agalactiae Serotype III in Fish Featuring Photocontrolled One‐Pot Detection
abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae is a primary pathogen responsible for significant mortality in tilapia, a critical and affordable source of animal protein. Among the various serotypes affecting aquaculture, serotype III is increasingly recognized for its high virulence and zoonotic potential, with multidrug resistance reported in some lineages. title: First records of Isonychia ignota (Walker, 1853) in Latvia and Estonia (Ephemeroptera, Isonychiidae)
abstract: We report the first records of Brush-legged Mayfly, Isonychia ignota (Walker, 1853), from Latvia and Estonia together with an overview of the species global distribution. Nymphs were found from two localities in the Gauja River. Our findings represent the northwestern limit of the known distribution of I. ignota in the Palaearctic.

abstract: ABSTRACT Polyethylene oxide (PEO) and chitosan (CS) are widely used polymeric building blocks in biodegradable materials, yet the molecular origin of their blend compatibility remains poorly defined. To clarify the noncovalent interactions that stabilize PEO–CS systems, we performed a comprehensive DFT study on representative oligomeric models in aqueous medium at the M06‑2X/cc‑pVDZ level. abstract: En este trabajo se utiliza un enfoque integrado para regular la trayectoria y posición de la plataforma móvil de un robot paralelo tipo delta (RPTD) de tres grados de libertad. abstract: The Federal Institutes of Education, Science and Technology (IFs) play a strategic role in promoting innovation and territorial development. The 2030 Agenda recognizes science, technology, and innovation as central instruments for achieving its goals. This article analyzes the titles of innovation projects approved by the Federal Institute of Sergipe (IFS) between 2014 and 2023, classifying them according to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through a large language model (LLM). title: BMAT: a footprint-level building facade material dataset for 73 major cities worldwide
abstract: Building facade materials are closely associated with urban microclimates, energy consumption, and carbon emissions, yet existing urban building datasets typically capture only building footprints and heights, leaving semantic material information unavailable at the individual-building level. Here we present BMAT, a footprint-level dataset of dominant visible street-facing facade materials covering 22.09 million buildings across 73 major cities worldwide. abstract: Beacon towers were warning and communication nodes in the Ming Great Wall defense system. We developed an interpretable graph learning framework combining a graph attention network (GAT) with random forest (RF) for Yansui Garrison. The GAT learned graph embeddings by integrating 11 node variables with spatial neighborhood relations, and RF used these embeddings to predict relative siting propensity. title: Immediate Marking and Feedback in Higher Education: A Transformational Assessment Strategy Using a Case Study Approach
abstract: Previous research highlights a persistent misalignment between tutor feedback intentions and student understanding, a challenge often intensified by delayed feedback practices in higher education assessment. This study aims to examine the impact of an immediate marking and feedback approach on student engagement, academic performance, and progression within a first-year undergraduate module. title: Synergizing mechanical alloying and friction stir processing for sustainable aluminium matrix composites: A review on microstructure, mechanical properties, circular economy
abstract: Interest in solid-state processing methods is increasing due to the demand for lightweight, high-performance materials with lower environmental impacts. This review examines mechanical alloying (MA) and friction stir processing (FSP) as complementary solid-state techniques for fabricating aluminium matrix composites (AMCs). It traces the transfer of MA principles into FSP-based composite fabrication and places both processes within a sustainability and circular economy framework. title: A geospatial decision-support framework for groundwater potential zonation and artificial recharge planning in the Bikkeru watershed, India
abstract: Abstract Groundwater, as a key natural resource held in aquifers, is important for the development of the economy, human health and ecological systems. With the increasing demand for water, it has become essential to extract groundwater. The development of geo-information technology has simplified the monitoring and management of these resources. abstract: Recent video diffusion models have achieved remarkable generation quality, but high-fidelity results still largely depend on closed-source systems or costly large-scale infrastructure. Test-time scaling (TTS) offers a training-free way to improve lightweight generators by spending additional inference compute, yet existing methods mostly remain within a noise-search paradigm: they sample, select, or perturb denoising trajectories and discard low-scoring candidates after expensive generation. title: Large-extent Classification of Wetland and Management Types Using Satellite Remote Sensing and Auxiliary Data
abstract: There have been few studies examining how effectively land use / land cover (LULC) classes of wetland types and their management can be detected with remote sensing and auxiliary data. We conduct wetland-specific present-day LULC classification and long-term change detection in seven European study areas. We assess how accurately LULC types and their changes can be detected with satellite remote sensing and to what extent auxiliary data improves classification accuracy. abstract: In this paper, I take stock of past field research and DNA sample collection conducted in different parts of the world to elucidate how this work was undertaken and the knowledge of human biological diversity it produced. Drawing upon firsthand experiences, I discuss some of the challenges involved in collecting and transporting biological samples from the field to the lab for genetic analysis. abstract: Abstract It is widely accepted that water markets can support adaptation to climate change. However, quantifying this adaptive capacity is difficult as it requires models that represent both stochastic water supplies and forward-looking behaviour by market participants. We develop a stochastic dynamic model of the Murray-Darling Basin water market in which irrigators form rational expectations over future water prices, and make monthly water use, annual crop planting, and long-run investment decisions. abstract: Background Pithecellobium clypearia (PC) is a traditional Chinese medicine with anti-inflammatory effects. However, the preventive efficacy and underlying mechanisms of PC in ulcerative colitis (UC) remain unclear. Objective This study applied an integrated microbiome-metabolomic approach to investigate PC’s pharmacological mechanisms against UC. abstract: Emerging contaminants in urban wastewater, including pharmaceuticals, poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), personal care products, surfactants, and disinfection byproducts, represent an increasing environmental and public health concern because conventional urban wastewater treatment plants (uWWTPs) are unable to remove them efficiently. abstract: In groundgen airborne wind energy systems that utilise conventional feedback control architecture, the pumping cycle power is largely influenced by four controller set points: reel-out radius, reel-out distance, reel-out winch speed, and reel-in winch speed. Whilst the best set-point combination that maximises power can be found through a 4D optimisation or a parameter sweep, the computation cost of both approaches is significant. abstract: A growing number of multistatic meteor radar networks are being established worldwide. The multistatic geometry with overlapping observation volumes of several meteor radars or passive receivers permits the inference of higher-order kinematic properties of the wind field or even the retrieval of arbitrary wind fields using tomographic algorithms. abstract: Sustainable natural resource management requires effective legal and institutional frameworks capable of addressing environmental challenges, competing stakeholder interests, and social conflicts over access to and use of natural resources. abstract: The extensive use of galvalume roofing in Darul Muttaqin Batu Islamic Boarding School offers practical advantages, including light weight, durability, and ease of installation. Nevertheless, this metallic roofing material can reduce thermal comfort because rooms beneath the roof become hotter during strong solar exposure. abstract: ABSTRACT The present study examined the phytochemical composition, antioxidant, antibacterial, and in silico properties of Elaeagnus angustifolia seed extracts. Methanol and ethanol extracts exhibited the highest yields (7.22% and 4.63%), reflecting the predominance of polar constituents. abstract: In low salinity water flooding (LSWF), oil–brine and rock–brine interactions are strongly influenced by potential determining ions (PDIs), which have been predominantly studied for divalent ions such as Mg 2+ , Ca 2+ , and SO 4 2− . abstract: Abstract Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) are bioelectrochemical systems that enable simultaneous wastewater treatment and bioenergy recovery through microbial oxidation of organic substrates. abstract: This study examines the pivotal role of Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) organizations in advancing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and proposes a structured framework to assess their contributions through Sustainable Performance Indicators (SPIs). STI organizations are key enablers of progress in areas such as clean energy, healthcare, education, and climate resilience; however, existing measurement systems often overlook their broader societal and environmental impacts. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the efficiency and air logistics‐based trade competitiveness of five major Asian hub airports: Incheon International Airport, Hong Kong International Airport, Narita International Airport, Singapore Changi Airport, and Beijing Capital International Airport. Robots, on the other hand, are not yet able to work similarly closely with humans and to effectively convey information when engaging in physical-social human-robot interaction (psHRI). title: Vegetation cover dynamics in the Modder River Basin, South Africa: evidence from climate drivers and land cover during the 2015–2024
abstract: Dynamic changes in vegetation cover within semi-arid inland river basins are crucial for understanding global climate change and regional ecological security. journal: AILIJ Anuario de Investigación en Literatura Infantil y Juvenil

title: Hydrological decoupling of groundwater from natural climatic forcing in a heavily managed megacity
abstract: Introduction Groundwater recharge is traditionally understood to be primarily controlled by precipitation and other climatic processes. However, intensive anthropogenic water management and urbanization may weaken this relationship in megacities. This study investigates hydrological decoupling at the municipal scale in Beijing, China, and quantifies the relative contributions of anthropogenic and climatic drivers to groundwater dynamics. title: Adaptive Perturbation-shaping Model Predictive Path Integral for Robotic Manipulator Pose Control
abstract: This study proposes a model predictive path integral (MPPI) control method that combines adaptive covariance adjustment with low-pass perturbation filtering for the pose control of a robotic manipulator. The proposed method updates the sampling covariance according to the position and orientation errors of the tool center point, which allows a large sampling range during the approach phase and reduces the perturbation magnitude near the target pose. title: Rotatiridoid, a rare iridoid from Phlomoides rotata (Benth. ex Hook.f.) Mathiesen and its anti-inflammatory activity
abstract: A rare iridoid featuring an unusual 3-O-8 bridged ether bond, named rotatiridoid (1), was obtained from Phlomoides rotata (Benth. ex Hook.f.) Mathiesen, along with five known analogues. Its structure was established by means of HRESIMS, 1D and 2D NMR experiments, and ECD calculations. When evaluated in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages, compound 1 displayed anti-inflammatory activity, suppressing the production of pro-inflammatory mediators such as NO and ROS at 7.5 μM.

title: Modeling branch diameter in Larix olgensis using living branches, knot profiles and stem scars: climate–soil associations
abstract: Branch diameter (BD) strongly influences crown architecture, knot formation and wood quality, yet BD development is commonly modeled using living branches alone, leaving the diameter attained by dead branches at growth cessation insufficiently represented. Here, we developed a BD model as a function of branch age for Larix olgensis by combining living first-order branch measurements with longitudinal knot profiles and external stem-scar diameters. title: Western screech‐owl occupancy is higher in warm, dry landscapes with diverse topography
abstract: Understanding how species distributions vary across environmental gradients is critical for conservation, particularly for species facing interacting threats. The western screech‐owl Megascops kennicottii is a widespread but understudied forest owl in the Pacific Northwest of North America, where populations may be influenced by habitat conditions and interactions with invasive barred owls Strix varia . title: Monitoring the spatiotemporal dynamics of summer-irrigated agriculture under conflict and drought: The Middle Orontes Basin, Syria (1995–2025)
abstract: Abstract In semi-arid regions like the Orontes River Basin in Syria, summer-irrigated agriculture is critical for food security but remains highly sensitive to environmental and sociopolitical fluctuations. This study monitors the spatiotemporal changes in the summer-irrigated agricultural extent across four distinct geographic sectors within the conflict-affected Middle Orontes Basin (1995–2025). title: Research and Practice on Developing Teaching Teams for AI General Education in Higher Vocational Colleges
abstract: This study examines how teaching teams can develop the complementary capabilities in technology application, industry understanding, and translation of expertise into teaching required for AI general education in higher vocational colleges. Taking Jiangsu Maritime Institute as a case, it explores pathways for team development and mechanisms for teaching delivery. title: Antibacterial effects of cinnamon, eucalyptus, and green tea extracts vs. chlorhexidine and their impact on efflux pump activity in Streptococcus
abstract: Dental caries is a common oral health challenge, and using antimicrobial agents like chlorhexidine gluconate is one approach to managing its progression, although its long-term application is limited by various side effects. Given that plant-based solutions such as cinnamon, eucalyptus, and green tea extracts offer promising antimicrobial effects, this study examines their potential as natural alternatives for preventing and managing dental caries. title: AHI LAI: a seamless 500 m, 4-day leaf area index dataset of the Asia-Pacific region (2015–2025) generated from geostationary Himawari-8/9 observations
abstract: Vegetation plays a critical role in Earth system processes, making the monitoring of vegetation dynamics a fundamental component of global change research. Leaf area index (LAI) acts as a primary indicator for assessing vegetation canopy structure. Optical observations from polar-orbiting satellites often experience data gaps because relatively infrequent observation opportunities can coincide with regional cloud cover. title: Overview of biological resources for the study of airborne pollutants
abstract: Airborne nanoparticles constitute a significant global health threat. To reduce animal testing and better replicate the exposure of humans to airborne pollutants, environmental toxicology relies on in vitro cell culture and advanced cell-supporting models and platforms. Traditional submerged cell cultures, using either primary cells or continuously-growing cell lines, have provided valuable insights into the toxicity of nanoparticles. title: Evaluating 210Po occurrence in Chinese bottled waters: Radiochemical determination, multielement profiling, and ingestion-dose implications
abstract: Polonium-210 ( 210 Po) is one of the most radiotoxic naturally occurring radionuclides, yet its occurrence in commercially bottled drinking waters remains insufficiently characterized, particularly in rapidly expanding markets such as China. Here, 210 Po activity and multielement composition were determined in bottled drinking waters from high-selling commercial brands in China. title: Overcoming resistance in MDR Klebsiella pneumoniae: a dual approach using thymol and carvacrol to enhance antibacterial activity and inhibit biofilm-mediated virulence
abstract: Background The escalating prevalence of resistant bacterial strains, including MDR, XDR, and PDR, poses a major threat to public health. Klebsiella pneumoniae is of primary concern, identified by WHO as a critical priority pathogen in hospital-acquired infections. Therapeutic options were relegated to last-resort antibiotics like colistin, limited by its nephrotoxicity, and tigecycline, which now faces emerging bacterial resistance, raising the need for different treatment options. title: Evaluating Groundwater Contribution to Streams in Moderate‐Relief Catchments Using Paired Air‐Stream Temperature Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater discharge to headwater streams plays a critical role in maintaining flow during dry periods and buffering stream temperatures, yet groundwater‐stream interactions remain poorly understood in low‐ to moderate‐relief headwater catchments. In this study, we used paired analysis of air, stream and groundwater temperature across 53 site‐years collected over 2 years to assess the relative importance and depth of groundwater contributions in four moderate‐relief headwater catchments in a cold, humid region (eastern Canada). title: Archetypes of resilience and adaptability in high Andean farming systems facing simultaneous disturbances
abstract: High-Andean farming systems face simultaneous socio-environmental disturbances that challenge their resilience. Yet assessments based on average structural typologies often overlook extreme adaptation cases. This study identified farm types according to their responses to dominant stressors in La Cruz, Nariño, Colombia, and examined how these strategies align with resilience and adaptability criteria. abstract: Low-flow centrifugal pumps have become widely used in modern rocket and space modules-ranging from low-thrust turbopump feed systems to electric pump units for spacecraft thermal control systems–delivering heads of up to 2.5 × 105 J/kg at specific speeds of ns < 40. title: Energy-efficient and QoS-aware clustering routing framework using improved sharpbelly fish optimization and adaptive regularized routing optimization for WSNs
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) face persistent challenges in maintaining energy efficiency, balanced resource utilization, and reliable data transmission as network density increases. Existing clustering and routing approaches generally address these requirements independently, resulting in inadequate coordination among cluster-head selection, node grouping, routing, and cooperative resource allocation. title: Chuyển đổi số trong doanh nghiệp du lịch vừa và nhỏ: tổng quan hệ thống và đề xuất khung lý thuyết tích hợp
abstract: Chuyển đổi số là xu hướng tất yếu đối với doanh nghiệp du lịch vừa và nhỏ trong bối cảnh cạnh tranh gia tăng sau đại dịch COVID-19. title: Modality matters to parents who support K-12 online learners: A literature synthesis
abstract: In this literature synthesis we investigated parent perspectives on how instructional modality affects the type and amount of support parents need to provide their primary/secondary online learners. Informed by the Academic Communities of Engagement framework (Borup et al., 2020), we analyzed parents' perceptions of their support roles for primary/secondary online learning and their students’ support needs given the context of their instructional modality. title: RISK-BASED HSE GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCING THE RESILIENCE OF CRITICAL INDUSTRIAL INFRASTRUCTURE IN SAUDI ARABIA
abstract: Saudi Arabias industrial growth is predicated on infrastructure and the disruption of that infrastructure can have a cascading effect on the safety of workers, the safety of the communities around it, the environment and the delivery of essential services. Traditional HSE (health, safety and environment) arrangements tend to look at these various aspects in isolation through separate compliance, occupational and process safety regimes. title: Assessment of hydrological response and water balance components using the Variable Infiltration Capacity model in the Cauvery River Basin, India
abstract: Accurate estimation of water balance components at the river basin scale is essential for sustainable water resources management, particularly in regions experiencing increasing climatic variability and growing anthropogenic pressures. The Cauvery River Basin, one among the major river basins of peninsular India is taken up in this study. This study presents a comprehensive water balance analysis of the Cauvery River Basin using the Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) model integrated with satellite based remote sensing datasets. title: Nitrogen metabolism, plant growth, leaf gas exchange and stomata density under inoculation of Pseudomonas fluorescens and Azospirillum brasilense into hydroponic arugula
abstract: Plant growth-promoting bacteria may improve nutrient acquisition and physiological performance in hydroponic crops, but the benefits of increasing inoculant concentration remain poorly understood. Two independent experiments were conducted to evaluate Pseudomonas fluorescens strain CCTB03 and Azospirillum brasilense strains AbV5 and AbV6 in hydroponically grown arugula. title: Biogenic Silver Nanoparticles from Penicillium chrysogenum Incorporated in Polymeric Micelles: Antimicrobial Activity and Cytotoxicity Evaluation
abstract: Abstract Biogenic silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) are investigated for their antimicrobial activity and reduced toxicity associated with metabolite-derived surface coatings. Their stability and biological activity are enhanced by metabolite-derived coatings produced by the synthesizing organism. This study develops hybrid nanocarriers by combining biogenic AgNPs synthesized from Penicillium chrysogenum with poloxamer micelles. abstract: Corrosion of copper in sulfuric acid environments poses persistent challenges across numerous industrial applications, necessitating the development of effective and mechanistically well-understood inhibitors. title: Fabrication of a Beeswax-Based Chest Phantom Incorporating Anadara antiquata Shell-Derived CaCO3 for Adult Lung Cancer Simulation
abstract: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer mortality, while chest CT requires careful radiation dose optimization. Commercial anthropomorphic phantoms are costly, and shell-derived bone substitutes for chest phantoms with simulated pulmonary nodules remain insufficiently evaluated. This study developed and assessed a low-cost adult chest phantom using locally available materials: polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) for soft tissue, polyurethane (PU) foam for lung tissue, calcium carbonate derived from Anadara antiquata shell waste for bone, and beeswax for a simulated pulmonary nodule. abstract: Thermal evolution modifies both shale pore systems and hydrocarbon properties, with implications for shale oil occurrence and mobility. title: Loss of bmp15 gene function does not abolish fertility in male Atlantic salmon
abstract: Introduction Bone morphogenetic protein 15 (BMP15), a transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) superfamily member, is well known for its crucial involvement in regulating female reproduction in mammals, and recently also in fishes. However, the biological function(s) of Bmp15 in male reproduction are largely unknown in vertebrates in general. title: Fútbol lúdico escolar como estratégica pedagógica para optimizar la coordinación motriz en preadolescentes
abstract: La práctica del fútbol lúdico escolar es una herramienta pedagógica que, a través del juego y de actividades lúdicas, contribuye a la formación integral de los preadolescentes. Su implementación ayuda a mejorar la coordinación motora, las destrezas básicas y el control corporal, facilitando un aprendizaje divertido y relevante. El objetivo se enfoca en evaluar un programa de fútbol como estrategia lúdica en el desarrollo de la coordinación motriz de los estudiantes de 10 a 12 años. abstract: Objective To evaluate the association between short-term ambient fine particulate matter (PM 2 . 5 ) exposure and sleep-disorder-related emergency admissions at a psychiatric hospital, characterize the short-term lag pattern, and explore potential differences by diagnostic category and sex. title: Enamel–dentin differentiation alters modeled stress transfer in a Maastrichtian crocodyliform tooth
abstract: Some finite element analyses of fossil teeth have assigned homogeneous, dentin-like material properties, although the consequences of this simplification for tissue-specific stress transfer remain poorly resolved. Here, an isolated crocodyliform tooth, SC000903, from the Maastrichtian Yuliangzi Formation was investigated using external morphology, high-resolution micro-computed tomography, three-dimensional reconstruction, and finite element analysis. title: Integrated Assessment of Pollution Hotspots and Decision Support for Rivers in a Rapidly Urbanizing Indian State: Moving Beyond Monitoring to Management
abstract: ABSTRACT Telangana's river systems are increasingly exposed to pressures associated with urbanization, industrial activity and wastewater generation, creating a need for integrated assessment of multiple dimensions of water‐quality degradation. This study presents a 6‐year (2020–2025) regional assessment of major rivers in Telangana using monitoring data from the Telangana State Pollution Control Board. title: Geo‐Setting Risk Assessment in Eurasia: A Multidimensional Framework and Strategies
abstract: Amid intensifying geopolitical tensions and climate-related pressures, geo-setting risk has become increasingly multidimensional. This analysis of geo-setting risk in 16 Eurasian countries from 2010 to 2023, using a composite framework integrating regional geopolitical, political, economic, social, and ecological indicators, revealed marked spatial and temporal heterogeneity. abstract: ABSTRACT Nitric oxide (NO), a major atmospheric pollutant emitted from fossil‐fuel combustion and industrial processes, poses serious risks to both ecosystems and human health. At the same time, ammonia (NH 3 ) is an essential chemical feedstock and energy carrier, although its conventional production relies on energy‐intensive Haber–Bosch synthesis. abstract: Representatives of the order Pyxidiophorales (Laboulbeniomycetes, Ascomycota) are reported for the first time in Ukraine based on intensive mycological surveys conducted in the grasslands in Mykolaiv, Odesa, and Zakarpattia (Transcarpathian) regions. abstract: Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by the degeneration and progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra of the midbrain, leading to motor symptoms that affect the functional gait of individuals with this diagnosis. Among non-pharmacological treatment strategies, Aquatic Physical Therapy demonstrates several benefits for gait rehabilitation. abstract: The study presents the moment–rotation (M–φ) characteristics of semi-rigid I-profile joints made using header plates and flush end-plates. title: Climate-Resilient Spatial Zoning for Temporary Cultural Infrastructures: A framework for Flood-Prone Contexts
abstract: Event spaces and cultural areas are often built temporarily. These temporary structures are built without considering the possibility of defending against extreme weather events like floods. Under unforeseen situations like extreme weather, the accessibility and services will collapse. abstract: The flight performance of a golf ball is governed by its surface geometry, which controls boundary-layer transition, separation and wake formation, yet the effects of convex surface topology and of ball mass remain underexplored. title: Divergent Responses of Bacterial and Microeukaryotic Diversity to Water‐Level Fluctuations in a Lake‐Floodplain System
abstract: Water-level fluctuations (WLF) are widely accepted as key drivers of aquatic species diversity in lake-floodplain systems, with diversity increasing as water levels rise. abstract: This study investigates the enhancement of the aerodynamic performance and efficiency of horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT) blades through passive trailing-edge morphing. The novelty of this work lies in the application of substantial trailing-edge deflection at 50% chord to a NACA 2412 airfoil for HAWT applications. title: Sustainability by Design in Big Science
abstract: Abstract Public investment in Big Science and large-scale research infrastructures increasingly depends on their demonstrated long-term sustainability and societal value. This article argues that sustainability should not be treated as an external constraint imposed on scientific missions, but as a property that can be embedded by design. Drawing on evidence from major international research infrastructures, the article conceptualises Big Science projects as long-term, open and collaborative endeavours that can transform public expenditure into durable societal assets. title: Heat accumulation dictates microstructural evolution, tensile anisotropy and wear behavior in cold metal transfer-wire arc additive manufacturing of high-strength low-alloy steel

However, this step inevitably leads to information loss by concealing intra‐cluster variability—an important component of functional biodiversity—and the extent of this loss depends on the clustering scheme. abstract: ABSTRACT In this paper, we derive the static equations for a poro‐elastic plate from Biot's equations. abstract: Australia has a distinctive pattern of urban settlements, comprising six states and two territories each dominated by their capital city, and the increasing population and economic activity within these capitals has long been a concern. abstract: Developing representative driving cycles is essential for vehicle testing, fuel consumption, and emission analysis, as standard cycles often fail to reflect regional driving behavior, particularly on highways. This study develops a representative driving cycle for the Isfahan-Damghan motorway using the K-means clustering algorithm. title: Transforming AI chatbots into metacognitive partners: Culturally grounded mathematics learning in LMS-based environments
abstract: The utilization of AI chatbots in mathematics education is on the rise, with these bots often serving as the primary providers of answers, potentially limiting learners’ engagement in reflective and metacognitive reasoning processes. The present study examines how AI chatbots can function as metacognitive partners within a culturally contextualized mathematics learning framework implemented through a learning management system (LMS). title: Career Attitudes, Employability Perceptions, and Industry Expectations among Tourism and Hospitality Undergraduates in South India
abstract: The tourism and hospitality sector plays a significant role in generating employment, fostering economic growth, facilitating cultural exchange, and promoting regional development throughout India. However, despite the increasing job opportunities within this industry, graduates in tourism and hospitality often do not exhibit a strong commitment to pursuing long-term careers in the field. abstract: Chemical toxicants, including organophosphorus pesticides, heavy metal ions, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, antibiotics, synthetic dyes, phenolic compounds, and PFAS, pose severe threats to ecosystems and human health because of their high toxicity, environmental persistence, and bioaccumulation. Hydrogels are functional polymeric materials with three-dimensional network structures. abstract: Abstract Video games reach billions of people worldwide and may offer a scalable opportunity to engage players in climate and environmental action. However, little empirical research has assessed whether video games can influence the pro-environmental behavioural determinants or actions they aim to promote. To address this gap, we evaluated a 21-day ‘green activation’ embedded in Love & Pies, a popular mobile game participating in the 2024 Green Game Jam. abstract: ABSTRACT This review article analyses decolonial and posthumanist thought within critical language studies, highlighting the convergences, divergences and implications of these critical paradigms. abstract: Schatten- p norm optimization has emerged as an effective non-convex relaxation for low-rank matrix completion. abstract: La creciente necesidad de incorporar la seguridad desde las primeras etapas del desarrollo de software ha impulsado la adopción de prácticas DevSecOps reforzadas con inteligencia artificial (IA). En este contexto, el presente estudio tuvo como objetivo evaluar el efecto de la implementación de estas prácticas sobre la seguridad y la eficiencia del desarrollo de software en una empresa de fábrica de software de Lima durante 2025. title: Cell-cycle inhibition preserves robust development but rebalances lineages in mouse gastruloids
abstract: Cell differentiation and proliferation are fundamental to multicellular development. While studies in various non-mammalian species show that development can proceed despite disrupted cell-cycle progression, the extent to which normal cell-cycle dynamics are required in mammals remains unclear. Using mouse gastruloids, we examined the effects of cell-cycle inhibition on development. abstract: Introduction White spot syndrome virus (WSSV) threatens shrimp aquaculture. PCR is sensitive but laboratory dependent. Isothermal amplification with CRISPR/Cas12a offers an alternative, but one-pot integration is limited by competition between double-stranded amplicons and crRNA for Cas12a. Methods A one-pot assay (OAERA-Cas12a) integrating asymmetric enzymatic recombinase amplification (aERA) with CRISPR/Cas12a was developed. Key parameters were optimized. abstract: The spatial (habitat-based) and seasonal (phenological) distribution patterns of wild shrub vegetation in Jhelum District, Punjab, Pakistan, are significantly influenced by various abiotic factors. This study aimed to investigate the taxonomic richness, distribution patterns of shrubs in relation to habitat characteristics and environmental gradients in the Jhelum district. abstract: Abstract Climate and land-use changes are major drivers of species extinction. However, whether threatened and non-threatened species differ in their responses to these pressures remains unclear. Moreover, the factors inducing the difference are poorly understood. title: Shape Memory Alloy Sealing Gaskets for High-Pressure Flange Connections
abstract: Abstract High-pressure flanges are essential components for joining pipes, ensuring sealing, and preventing liquid and gas leakage. Gaskets play a critical role when subjected to high stresses, situation where they can cause irreversible deformations that, combined with fluctuations in mechanical and thermal loads, can compromise their integrity. The present work aims to evaluate the use of shape memory alloy (SMA) sealing gaskets, specifically NiTi alloys. This work establishes a comparative performance analysis of NiTi and AISI 316 stainless steel gaskets under the same operating conditions.

abstract: Nonhuman primates (NHPs), the closest evolutionary relatives of humans, are pivotal models for biomedical and ecological research. Gut phage are recognized as critical modulators of gut microbial communities; however, comprehensive insight into gut phage of NHPs is lacking. We used gut metagenomes spanning 25 NHP species and constructed an integrated gut phage catalogue (IGPC) comprising 11 389 nonredundant phage genomes. title: Class-wide sequence, structural, and docking-profile diversity of insect odorant receptors and structural specialization of Orco
abstract: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor–odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. abstract: La inteligencia artificial está transformando la educación superior. However, fresh organs are difficult to digitize due to their deformability, moist reflective surfaces, and rapid post-mortem deterioration. abstract: A new species of Gonatopus Ljungh, 1810 is described from Québec, Canada: G. quebecensis sp. nov . abstract: During a study in 2025, our results indicated a large population of Lycaena helle ([Denis & Schiffermüller], 1775) in the study area, an alpine bog, characterized by a male-skewed sex ratio and high survival rates. title: Extraction and validation of flood disaster impacts from news reports with large language models
abstract: Reliable local impact data are essential for risk assessment but remain difficult to obtain from unstructured newspaper text. Here we introduce News2Impact (N2I), a pipeline that converts news articles about natural hazards into geo-referenced, event-level impact records. title: Beyond the Score: Mapping Local Human Development in Poland with Scalar and Vector-Based Indices
abstract: Abstract This study investigates local human development dynamics in Poland by applying a dual-method approach that combines the classic scalar-based Local Human Development Index (LHDI) with a novel vector-based formulation using complex numbers and visual typogram representation. abstract: ABSTRACT Coal‐fired power plants are a major anthropogenic source of elemental mercury (Hg 0 ) emissions. abstract: The impact of views on health is well established, yet the mechanisms linking residential urban view features, well-being, and preference remain underexplored. This systematic, large-scale empirical study investigates (1) how the quantity and composition of a broad set of view features influence preference and emotional well-being, and (2) whether well-being mediates view preference. abstract: ABSTRACT Household digital low‐carbon technologies can support sustainable consumption while expanding the collection and algorithmic use of domestic data, creating a tension between environmental benefits and the legitimacy of data‐intensive consumer systems. Drawing on privacy‐calculus, digital‐trust, institutional‐legitimacy, responsible‐innovation, and sustainable‐consumption perspectives, this study examines how governance cues and datafication risks relate to consumer adoption through responsible data trust and perceived green‐data legitimacy. title: Geography education and climate change awareness among secondary school teachers and learners in Tubah Subdivision, Cameroon
abstract: By integrating physical and human environmental processes, Geography education is increasingly recognised as an important vehicle for climate literacy. However, evidence on its contribution to climate change awareness and adaptation-oriented learning at school level remains limited. This study examines how Geography teachers and learners in secondary schools in Tubah Subdivision, Cameroon, perceive the contribution of Geography education to climate change awareness. abstract: INTRODUCTION: In Italy, many facilities have started adopting telemedicine services since their regulation in 2020. Rural areas mainly benefit from telemedicine implementation due to their geographic features. We investigated the interests, attitudes, and perceptions of healthcare providers operating in the Italian Dolomites regarding the adoption of telemedicine. abstract: The luxury hotel sector operates in a fluid and highly competitive environment where providing outstanding guest experiences is crucial for long-term success. In this context, employees are the key drivers of service quality, making effective Human Resource Management (HRM) practices essential for organizational performance. abstract: We highlight a hierarchical property that is found in many sequences, the property of subunit structure, in which sequence symbols are joined together in tightly knit groups to create new subunits at higher levels of organization. title: Assessing the attentional dynamics of Responding to Joint Attention in infancy via online webcam-based eye-tracking
abstract: Responding to Joint Attention (RJA) is a foundational social-cognitive skill that unfolds through a sequence of distinct attentional processes: engagement with a social partner, orienting toward a referent, and sustained attention to a shared point of interest. Traditional assessments of joint attention often rely on aggregate behavioral scores that may not capture this fine-grained temporal structure. title: Middle East war-driven energy supply disruptions could influence air pollution in India and China
abstract: Abstract Rapid economic growth has increased energy demand to ~ 11,000 TWh in India and ~ 50,000 TWh in China, where coal accounts for 57.5% and 54.79% of total energy consumption, respectively. Both countries also depend strongly on imported oil, with ~ 45% of India’s and ~ 54% of China’s crude-oil imports originating from the Middle East, creating vulnerability to geopolitical energy-supply disruptions. Here, we investigate whether such disruptions could influence regional air pollution by integrating energy data, sector-resolved emissions, GEOS-Chem simulations, and satellite observations.

abstract: Background: Nipah virus (NiV) poses a significant public health threat due to its high fatality, yet public readiness for medical countermeasures remains understudied. abstract: Abstract Catfishes (order Siluriformes) inhabit diverse aquatic environments worldwide, ranging from tropical lowlands to fast‐flowing mountain rivers. However, the contribution of genomic variation to ecological diversification in catfishes, particularly within high‐altitude lineages, remains poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Combined cycle power plants are among the most efficient technologies for large scale electricity generation. This study presents a comprehensive energy and exergy analysis of an F-class combined cycle power plant equipped with dual three-pressure heat recovery steam generators, supplementary firing, and an air-cooled condenser. abstract: Food limitation has long shaped understanding of animal behavior, physiology, reproduction, and population dynamics. Yet food abundance alone does not capture the energetic conditions experienced by wild animals. Resources may be inaccessible, nutritionally inadequate, unpredictable, or unreliable over time, causing individuals in the same habitat to experience very different energetic environments. abstract: Global climate change has evolved into a multidimensional crisis reshaping national and international policy priorities. abstract: Cassava (Manihot esculenta) is a key staple crop supporting global food security, yet its productivity is increasingly constrained by declining soil fertility and climate variability. In many cassava-producing regions, phosphorus (P) recommendations rely on static fertilization grids that do not adequately account for site-specific soil and crop response variability. title: APLICACIONES DE LA INGENIERÍA DE SISTEMAS DE PROCESOS EN EL NEXO AGUA-ENERGÍA-ALIMENTO: AVANCES, RETOS Y PERSPECTIVAS
abstract: La Ingeniería de Sistemas de Procesos (ISP) es una rama de la ingeniería que se enfoca en analizar, diseñar y optimizar sistemas complejos. Su aplicación en el nexo agua-energía-alimento resulta esencial para enfrentar los grandes desafíos de la sostenibilidad, ya que permite comprender cómo se interrelacionan estos tres recursos fundamentales. A través de modelos, simulaciones y herramientas de optimización, la ISP ha impulsado avances en áreas como la agricultura de precisión, el uso eficiente del agua, la integración de energías renovables y la mejora en la producción de alimentos. title: Anti‐Dissolution Tungsten Alloying Stabilizes Highly Active Platinum for Industrial‐Grade Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Platinum‐based alloys remain the most promising electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet suffer from activity‐stability trade‐offs, particularly in alkaline media where Pt‐Ni alloys undergo continuous dissolution. Herein, we report the rational design of intermetallic Pt 2 W alloy nanoparticles uniformly anchored on N‐doped carbon nanomeshes (N‐CM), leveraging tungsten's exceptional thermodynamic stability and corrosion resistance to address this dilemma. title: MORPH – Lessons learnt from the development and application of an individual-based model
abstract: This paper summarises some of the lessons learnt over approximately 25 years from the development and application of the individual-based model, MORPH. The overall purpose of the model is to predict how the survival, condition, and behaviour of populations of animals are influenced by the food resources available and other environmental factors. The model was originally developed for a single bird species at a single site but was designed to be very flexible, hence its name. title: Interpretable soil thickness mapping with nested and spatial validation in the Angulinao semi-arid lake basin
abstract: Soil thickness varies markedly across semi-arid basins, yet sparse profile observations make these spatial patterns and their environmental controls difficult to resolve. We mapped soil thickness in the Angulinao semi-arid lake basin using 92 profiles and 27 environmental covariates. Twelve feature-selection and regression pipelines were evaluated by repeated nested cross-validation. title: Ethical-efficiency balance of AI in international Chinese teacher development
abstract: This mixed-methods study investigates ethical tensions in AI-integrated Chinese language teacher training for international students. Analyzing 100 candidates from Thailand, Vietnam, Korea, and other Southeast Asian countries across three Chinese universities through linguistic assessments, pedagogical evaluations, and ethical inventories, four key findings emerge: 1) Cross-cultural divergence: Thai participants showed substantially greater concern for cultural authenticity than participants from other countries; 2) Efficacy-autonomy tension: AI meaningfully enhanced pronunciation accuracy and

title: Influence of biomass burning on suburban PM2.5 variability in Nakhon Pathom, Thailand: a multi-scale analysis of fire intensity and atmospheric transport
abstract: This study examined the influence of biomass burning on the variability of fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 , aerodynamic diameter ≤ 2.5 µm) at a suburban receptor site in Nakhon Pathom, Thailand, during the dry seasons of 2023 and 2024. Regional transport was characterized using backward trajectory clustering and concentration-weighted trajectory analysis, fire characteristics using satellite-derived fire radiative power, and local source–receptor relationships using time-lagged Spearman correlation stratified by wind direction. title: Design of a Shipboard Sewage Treatment Plant Control and Monitoring System Using Microcontroller
abstract: This study focuses on the design and simulation of a microcontroller-based control and monitoring system for a shipboard sewage treatment plant aimed at improving operational reliability and automation. The system employs a dual microcontroller configuration using PIC16F84A devices to manage the operation of essential components, including the inlet pump, aerator, discharge pump, and dosing pump under both automatic and manual modes. title: Room‐Temperature CO 2 Sorption of NH 2 ‐Appended UiO‐67(Zr) Metal‐Organic Framework
abstract: Fossil fuel combustion elevates atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) to critical levels, driving climate change and intensifying natural disasters. This reality underscores the urgent need for efficient CO 2 capture technologies. In this regard, UiO‐67(Zr) being a highly porous and thermally stable metal‐organic framework (MOF) could be used as a promising candidate for CO 2 sorption. Herein, we report the in situ synthesis of amine (–NH 2 ) functionalized UiO‐67(Zr)‐NH 2 using a prefunctionalized 3,3′‐diamino‐[1,1′‐biphenyl]‐4,4′‐dicarboxylic acid (dbda) linker. title: Optimizing open space capacity under heritage constraints in the ancient city of Suzhou: a multi-scale recursive approach
abstract: Abstract Optimizing open spaces in historic urban areas presents a unique challenge: balancing macro-level planning objectives with the preservation of irreplaceable heritage. This study introduces a multi-scale recursive optimization framework that integrates assessment, prediction, and configuration to address these conflicts. Using the ancient city of Suzhou, China (a UNESCO World Heritage site), as a case study, we applied the framework at city, community, and plot scales. title: A new gradient-free active subspace estimation method with application to rare event probability estimation
abstract: To reduce the cost of estimating the probability of a rare event involving a very large number of random parameters, we propose a new strategy for dimension reduction coupled with a surrogate model for the expensive part of the algorithm. To this end, we extend the Ordinary Kriging Active Subspace (OK-AS) method into a sequential version. title: Crystal-field modulation activates dormant tetrahedral Co sites for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution
abstract: Water activation in the Volmer step is a major kinetic bottleneck in alkaline hydrogen evolution, yet the catalytic potential of many lattice sites remains underutilized. Here, we develop an oxalic-acid-assisted treatment to modulate the surface coordination environment of spinel Co 3 O 4 while preserving its crystalline framework. title: Effects of Liquid Organic Fertilizer, Biochar and Their Interaction on Growth and Yield of Mung Bean (Vigna radiata L.)
abstract: This study investigates the effects of combined biochar and liquid organic fertilizer treatments on the growth and yield of mung bean (Vigna radiata L.). The experiment was conducted at the Hera Research Center, Faculty of Agriculture, UNITAL, Cristo Rei Administrative Post, Dili Municipality, from February to June 2025. Two treatment factors were evaluated: locally produced liquid organic fertilizer (Lof-nachi) and biochar application rates. title: HERC5-mediated co-translational ISGylation in innate immunity: molecular mechanisms, context-dependent regulation, and therapeutic potential
abstract: HERC5 is the predominant E3 ligase for interferon-stimulated gene 15 (ISG15) in human cells and is now considered a central component of interferon-driven innate immune regulation. Unlike conventional E3 ligases that primarily modify mature proteins, HERC5 has been reported to mediate co-translational ISGylation by associating with ribosomes and modifying nascent polypeptides during protein synthesis, providing a mechanistic link between interferon activation, protein modification, and rapid cellular adaptation during immune responses. title: China's Irrigation‐Induced Evapotranspiration Largely Returns to Land as Precipitation Through Atmospheric Recycling
abstract: Abstract Irrigation‐induced evapotranspiration (IrrET), the atmospheric flux of irrigation water consumption (IWC), is commonly treated as local freshwater depletion, yet where this water returns as precipitation through atmospheric recycling remains poorly quantified. Here, we develop a high‐resolution estimate of China's IrrET and combine it with Lagrangian moisture tracking to quantify its contribution to local and remote precipitation. title: Climate health action in Latin America and the Caribbean: Priorities identified through a multi-stakeholder engagement process
abstract: Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) is highly vulnerable to climate change despite contributing minimally to global greenhouse gas emissions. Climate-related hazards — including extreme heat, floods, droughts, and hurricanes — exacerbate health risks and disproportionately affect Indigenous peoples, Afro-descendant populations, rural communities, women, older adults, and individuals with chronic conditions. title: “We Just Can’t Prove Our Burden Under These Circumstances”: Judge Advocate Perspectives on Consent and Alcohol-Involved Sexual Assault Cases
abstract: Alcohol-involved sexual assault remains a persistent issue within the U.S. military despite significant institutional reform. To understand how alcohol-involved sexual assault cases are interpreted within the military justice system, this article draws on 23 qualitative interviews with 11 members of the Judge Advocate General’s Corps. Lawyers engaged in discursive strategies that highlighted the alleged victim’s intoxication as lowering inhibitions while simultaneously silencing the role alcohol has in diminishing capacity to consent and the accused’s responsibility to assess that capacity. title: Accelerating an ensemble of variational data assimilations with randomized preconditioning
abstract: Abstract Ensembles of variational data assimilations (EDAs) require solving systems of linear equations with iterative methods. The solution process can be accelerated using a limited‐memory preconditioner constructed with approximations of the leading eigenpairs of the Hessian matrix. Randomized methods for low‐rank matrix approximations provide a feasible approach for computing these eigenpairs. title: Grundlagen der zuverlässigkeitsbasierten Bemessung | Teil 1 – Methodik: 1. Empfehlung des Arbeitskreises 2.15 der DGGT „Zuverlässigkeitsbasierte Methoden in der Geotechnik“
abstract: Abstrakt Die erste Empfehlung des Arbeitskreises 2.15 der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Geotechnik führt in die Grundprinzipien einer zuverlässigkeitsbasierten Bemessung ein. Der hier vorliegende Teil 1 stellt das bekannte Teilsicherheitskonzept als semi‐probabilistischer Ansatz dem zuverlässigkeitsbasierten und dem risikoinformierten Ansatz vergleichend gegenüber. Alle drei Konzepte haben eine ausreichende Zuverlässigkeit des betrachteten Systems zum Ziel, welche hinsichtlich möglicher Grenzzustände der Tragfähigkeit und der Gebrauchstauglichkeit einschließlich der Dauerhaftigkeit bewertet werde

title: Recent Advances in Adsorptive Removal of Dyes from Wastewater: Mechanisms and Performance of Advanced Adsorbents
abstract: The increasing discharge of dye-containing wastewater from textile and related industries has become a major environmental concern because of the toxicity, persistence, and poor biodegradability of many synthetic dyes. This review presents an overview of dye classification, chemistry, environmental impacts, and wastewater treatment technologies, with particular emphasis on adsorption as an effective dye removal method. title: Enhancement of enzymatic biodiesel production: influence of reaction conditions, type of alcohol and lipase
abstract: Biodiesel is gaining importance as renewable fuel to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and dependence on fossil fuels. Enzymatic biodiesel production offers a more sustainable alternative to conventional chemical processes, operating under milder conditions and with lower energy requirements. This study evaluated the influence of temperature (30–50 °C), oil/alcohol molar ratio (1/3–1/30), alcohol type, reaction time and lipase formulation on enzymatic biodiesel production by transesterification. title: The Impact of the Digital Economy on the High-Quality Development of Foreign Trade: Evidence from City-Level Panel Data in Anhui Province
abstract: The digital economy is reshaping global trade and creating new opportunities for the high-quality development of foreign trade.Taking the prefecture-level cities of Anhui Province during 2010–2023 as the empirical sample,this paper constructs a composite index of digital economy development along four dimensions—digital infrastructure,digital industrialisation,the digitalisation of industry,and digital talent—and an index of the high-quality development of foreign trade covering foreign trade volume,foreign trade structure and foreign trade competitiveness, both measured using the entropy weig

title: Effect of Cryogenic Soaking Duration on the Crystallographic Structure and Corrosion Resistance of ASTM A36 Steel
abstract: This study investigates the influence of cryogenic soaking duration on the crystallographic characteristics and corrosion resistance of ASTM A36 structural steel. Specimens were immersed in liquid nitrogen at −196°C for 0, 12, 36, and 60 hours. Crystallographic analysis was conducted using X-ray diffraction (XRD), while electrochemical corrosion behavior was assessed through Tafel polarization in 3.5% NaCl solution using an Autolab PGstat. title: Molecular Interactions between Styrene Oligomers and Human Serum Albumin: A Multiscale Computational Study of a Plastic-Derived Environmental Contaminant
abstract: Abstract Micro- and nanoplastics are pervasive environmental pollutants known to accumulate in human organs. While the hazards of larger plastic particles are under intense investigation, the toxicological impact of molecular-level plastic oligomers with dimensions around 1 nm is a critical and underexplored area. This study provides a comprehensive molecular-level in silico characterization of the binding interactions between styrene oligomers (1–7 units) and HSA, characterizing their molecular basis and its potential relevance to HSA’s ligand transport function. title: Multimodal Liquid Biopsy for Prostate Cancer Stratification
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTC) and platelet-derived RNA are emerging liquid biopsy biomarkers in prostate cancer. While AR-V7 expression in CTC has been associated with resistance to androgen receptor-targeted therapies, their low abundance limits molecular characterization. We evaluated a multimodal liquid biopsy approach integrating CTC enumeration and platelet-derived androgen receptor (AR) profiling in localized and metastatic prostate cancer. title: Enhancing Urban Biocapacity Assessment through High- Resolution Tree Cover Density Data: A Carbon Sequestration Proxy Approach
abstract: Accelerating ecological overshoot increases the need for spatially explicit ecological accounting, particularly in urban landscapes. Conventional biocapacity assessments often rely on generalized land-cover data that may overlook fine-scale vegetation structures. This study evaluates whether integrating high-resolution Tree Cover Density (TCD) data with Corine Land Cover (CLC) and Urban Atlas (UA) improves the spatial representation of vegetated land-use types and their carbon dioxide (CO2) sequestration potential. title: Metaheuristic driven MPPT intelligence for unified PV battery EV energy convergence
abstract: This paper discusses the challenge of reliable maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in solar photovoltaic (PV) battery electric vehicle (EV) charging systems, which face rapidly changing irradiance and temperature. Unlike standard MPPT studies that focus only on standalone PV systems, this work examines MPPT performance within an integrated PV battery grid EV charging framework. title: Evaluating the impacts of low-carbon transitions on urban ecological resilience: quasi–natural experimental evidence from China
abstract: The enactment of the low-carbon city pilot policy (LCCP) plays a pivotal role in strengthening urban ecological resilience (UER) and achieving sustainable urban development. Herein, we used panel data from 282 cities from 2005 to 2022 and applied a multiperiod difference-in-difference model to evaluate the impact of the LCCP on UER. The LCCP significantly enhances UER, guiding cities toward substantially sustainable development. title: Knowledge security and its integration within the research governance infrastructure
abstract: International research collaboration is integral to the scientific endeavour. Recent geopolitical developments have, however, put such collaboration under scrutiny, highlighting concerns about foreign interference in research and education. As a result, the notion of 'knowledge security’ is gaining ground. Knowledge security requires researchers to make decisions about the kinds of research partners and collaborators they work with, along with the internalisation of a specific security rationality and adoption of self-regulatory practices. Beyond ecological protection: unravelling the Social Matrix and biocultural drivers of heritage tree conservation
abstract: The long-term persistence of heritage trees is shaped by ecological suitability, species traits, land-use pressure, and climate, and may also depend on social arrangements that sustain protection across generations. Yet existing conservation frameworks rarely specify how cultural meaning, governance, knowledge, livelihoods, and collective capacity combine to produce durable stewardship. abstract: ABSTRACT Montane watersheds in the Himalayan region are becoming increasingly vulnerable to hydroclimatic extremes that cause floods, landslides, droughts and seasonal water scarcity. These risks are compounded by ecohydrological transformation resulting from shifts in forest composition, notably the widespread establishment of pine plantations, as well as climate variability and intensified land‐use activities. abstract: BACKGROUND: Disaster events that overwhelm health system capacity often require the deployment of nurses from non-critical care clinical areas to supplement the specialist intensive care workforce. However, the role of deployed registered nurses in intensive care is poorly defined and without clear role boundaries, experienced intensive care nurses often bear disproportionate supervisory burdens, and deployed staff may assume clinical responsibilities for which they are inadequately prepared. title: Inteligencia artificial y aprendizaje financiero: Percepciones estudiantiles y contraste de resoluciones. Caso Sahagún, Córdoba
abstract: El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo describir las percepciones asociadas al uso de inteligencia artificial (IA) generativa en el aprendizaje financiero y analizar los patrones de coincidencia y divergencia reportados al contrastar una resolución propia con otra apoyada en IA. title: Provenance-aware multimodal resource organization for smart library wellbeing services: A data-driven study of bibliotherapy-informed recommendations
abstract: Abstract Purpose: This study examines how the openly shared tabular portion of a publicly archived corpus of bibliotherapy-informed recommendations can be independently re-annotated and reorganized into a provenance-aware and media-sensitive framework for smart library wellbeing services. Methods: The analytical corpus comprises 391 unique resources and 447 source-occurrence records, all traceable to the publicly archived data package of X. Wang et al. (2026b). title: Rethinking climate resilience: How digital transformation reconfigures tourism governance in Vietnam
abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly promoted as a pathway for strengthening climate resilience in tourism, yet little is known about how it reshapes governance and differentiated adaptive capacity within local communities. Drawing on a longitudinal qualitative case study conducted between 2018 and 2026 in a community-based tourism village in Vietnam, this study examines how digital transformation has reshaped information flows, visitor acquisition, and informal coordination among local tourism actors. abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of digitalization through internet access in strengthening the economy in North Sumatra Province using panel data for the period 2010–2024 with the Vector Autoregression (VAR) method. The variables used include the Human Development Index (HDI), Investment (INV), Internet Access Users (IAU), Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR), and Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP). title: Productive Struggles in Planning for Ambitious Science Teaching: Insights From Elementary Preservice Teachers
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated elementary preservice teachers' (PTs) experiences in planning to elicit students' ideas within ambitious science teaching (AST). The study involved 53 elementary PTs in the context of a science teaching methods course at the elementary education program at a public university in Türkiye. Data were collected through PTs' individual written reflections on their planning for eliciting students' ideas in AST and collaboratively developed group lesson plans and analyzed using thematic analysis. abstract: Determination of the encapsulation efficiency (EE) of liposomal drugs generally requires prior physical separation of free drug from liposomes, which is time-consuming and can perturb drug partitioning. Herein, an electrochemical sensor was fabricated using vertically ordered mesoporous silica film (VMSF) grown on the adhesive, conductivity-enhancing interlayer of electrochemically reduced graphene oxide-multiwalled carbon nanotube-N-doped graphene quantum dot (ErGO-MWCNTs-NGQDs) ternary carbon nanocomposite. title: Ground wars: Vegetality and the undoing of the plantation form
abstract: Abstract Above the banana plantations of northern Martinique, drones and satellites read the surface of the land for the stress it endures and the yield it promises. Beneath them, in soil that a synthetic pesticide has saturated for centuries to come, the ground is quietly undoing what was done to it. This lecture gives that undoing two names. title: Multi‐Analytical Characterization and Taxonomic Distinction of Australian Plant Exudates
abstract: Plant exudates have been used worldwide for millennia in broad applications due to their unique physicochemical properties. Indigenous Australians have used exudates in long-standing cultural and technical practices, including hafting adhesives and paint binders. Chemical characterization and botanical identification can provide important insight into the origin, properties, and usage of exudate materials from the archaeological past to the present. title: Edge-Constrained Food Retrieval System
abstract: Fine-grained food image and text retrieval requires models that can distinguish subtle differences in ingredients, preparation methods, and visual appearance. While vision language models provide strong multimodal reasoning capabilities, their computational requirements can make direct deployment on edge devices impractical. This paper proposes a training free retrieval framework that combines efficient candidate retrieval with selective vision language reasoning. title: Genetic diversity of bacterial endophytes associated with Crotalaria (Rattlepods)
abstract: Crotalaria is a diverse legume genus valued for its ecological and agronomic roles. However, its associated endophytic microbiome remains minimally characterized. This study examined the genetic diversity and community structure of bacterial endophytes inhabiting domesticated and wild Crotalaria species. Twenty-nine healthy Crotalaria plant samples were analyzed using the culture-independent 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing approach. title: Quantum-inspired differential evolution with Elite Perturbation for high-dimensional portfolio optimization
abstract: Abstract High-dimensional portfolio optimization is a challenging computational problem due to its large search space, nonlinear objective structure, and practical constraints on asset allocation. To improve the computational tractability of Sharpe ratio-based portfolio optimization, this paper reformulates the original constrained model as an unconstrained single-objective problem by embedding equality and inequality constraints into the objective function through penalty terms. title: Lightweight Zero-DCE-Driven YOLO for Nighttime Low-Light Object Detection
abstract: To address the issue of difficulty in balancing accuracy improvement and computational overhead in the joint deployment of low-light enhancement and target detection, this paper constructs a lightweight Zero-DCE-driven YOLO night low-light target detection framework. Depthwise separable convolution, spatial attention, and SE attention are all common components. This paper does not consider them as independent structural innovations. title: Natural hydrogen in the Middle East and North Africa: Geological prospectivity, global analogues, and a play-based exploration roadmap
abstract: Natural hydrogen, free molecular H 2 generated by water-rock reaction and radioactive decay, has moved from curiosity to exploration target since production began at Bourakébougou, Mali. The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) hosts several settings that generate H 2 elsewhere, yet has attracted little dedicated study. title: Plume emission rate estimation using Gaussian plumes in remote imaging spectroscopy with SPIIRE
abstract: The detection and quantification of methane and other trace gas emissions using remote sensing with imaging spectroscopy is an increasingly important tool for understanding local, regional, and global emissions. Traditional algorithms for quantifying the emission rate often rely on user-determined, instrument-dependent parameters and arbitrary plume boundaries. In this paper we present a new algorithm to estimate the emission rate based on a statistical inversion of a physical, Gaussian plume model that does not depend on such parameter choices or plume boundaries, termed SPIIRE. abstract: Ports are increasingly becoming urban cyber-physical systems in which maritime operations, terminal activities, buildings, electricity networks, renewable generation and environmental pressures interact. Energy Management Systems (EMS) can coordinate energy production and consumption, while Digital Twins (DTs) can connect real-time data, simulation and decision support. Yet port digitalisation and port decarbonisation are still frequently treated as separate domains. title: Towards a green China: energy policy, technological innovation, and green investment as drivers of environmental sustainability
abstract: China’s pursuit of environmental sustainability has become one of the defining policy experiments of the twenty-first century, combining an ambitious dual-carbon pledge with the world’s largest deployment of clean-energy technology and green capital. This review synthesizes recent scholarship to examine how three interlocking levers, energy and climate policy, technological innovation, and green investment, jointly shape China’s transition toward a lower-carbon and more resilient development path. abstract: Objectives This paper provides a three-dimensional nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) model to clearly understand the effects of flooding on agricultural farmlands. The model uses three interacting state variables: farmland productivity F(t), soil quality index S(t), and floodwater level W(t). title: Molecular docking and in-vivo study of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) of Cypriniformes, Siluriformes, and Anabantiformes for aquaculture applications
abstract: Aquaculture frequently employs hormonal induction to trigger spawning, with gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues recognized as among the most effective agents. This study identified potential GnRH-1, GnRH-2, and GnRH-3 peptides from the orders Cypriniformes, Siluriformes, and Anabantiformes through in silico analysis and evaluated the best candidate for inducing zebrafish spawning. title: Deep reinforcement learning control scheme for frequency control of microgrids
abstract: The growing integration of renewable energy sources into microgrids poses substantial challenges to traditional load-frequency control, primarily due to the intermittent nature of generation and continuously changing operating conditions. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an adaptive control strategy based on reinforcement learning, in which a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) agent is used to automatically tune a cascaded PIDF controller for frequency regulation. abstract: ABSTRACT Protein nanofibrils assemble hierarchically, yet directing the mesoscale topology that connects fibrillar growth to network mechanics remains challenging. Here, we show that crystalline seed identity redirects regenerated silk fibroin assembly while retaining a common silk II packing motif. title: Multi-timescale evaluation of satellite precipitation products using 15-minute gauge observations in complex terrain, Ethiopia
abstract: This study evaluated the performance of six widely used satellite precipitation products, including GPM-IMERG V06 ER, IMERG V07 FR, CMORPH, PERSIANN-CCS, GSMaP-MVK, and MSWEP against observed sub-daily, and daily timescale rainfall. title: Antibody–drug conjugates in colorectal cancer: target biology, resistance, and the clinical-trial landscape
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer morbidity and mortality, and outcomes in microsatellite-stable metastatic disease have improved only modestly despite optimised cytotoxic, anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR regimens. Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) link tumour-associated antigen targeting to intracellular delivery of potent payloads, but their place in CRC is still being defined.
