title: Multiscale modeling and industrial validation of the water-gas shift reactor in an ammonia unit using COMSOL multiphysics
abstract: The high temperature water-gas shift (HT-WGS) reaction is a central conversion step in ammonia production since it boosts the hydrogen yield and reduces the carbon monoxide content in the synthesis gas mixture before subsequent purification and ammonia synthesis. The industrial reactor was analyzed numerically with COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2. title: Exact wave structures, nonlinear dynamics, and stability of the conformable fractional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
abstract: Abstract The conformable fractional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation (CNLSE) serves as a robust mathematical model for understanding nonlinear wave propagation across various media, including optical fibers and plasma. This study introduces a cohesive analytical-computational framework to explore exact wave structures, nonlinear dynamics, and stability associated with the CNLSE. title: Evidence for Hunga-Tonga eruption influence on the anomalously strong Northern-Hemisphere stratospheric polar vortex in 2024/2025
abstract: The 2022 Hunga Tonga (HT) eruption injected an unprecedented amount of water vapour (WV) into the stratosphere and mesosphere, emerging as a potential multi-year driver of variability in those layers and associated climate feedbacks. Using satellite and reanalysis datasets, and ensemble simulations with the SOCOLv4 model, with and without the HT forcing, we diagnose the chain of processes linking the eruption to the exceptionally strong Northern Hemisphere stratospheric polar vortex (SPV) observed in winter 2024/2025. title: Weather regime adaptive multi-relation dependence modeling for joint scenario generation in wind farm clusters
abstract: Accurate probabilistic characterization of wind power variability is essential for the secure and efficient integration of large-scale wind generation. However, existing methods commonly rely on independent sampling or a single static spatial structure, thereby overlooking the weather regime dependence and functional heterogeneity of cross-farm interactions. To address this limitation, this study develops a weather regime adaptive multi-relation dependence framework for joint scenario generation. title: A multi-scale terrain mapping method using hillshade abstraction
abstract: Terrain generalization aims to selectively simplify terrain details across scales while preserving the overall terrain form and key geomorphic features. An effective representation of terrain structure provides an important basis for preserving terrain structure during generalization. To support this goal, this study introduces hillshading to represent terrain form and structural information through variations in illumination. title: Snake‐Scale‐Inspired Serrated Structures With Frictional Anisotropy for Tunable Bidirectional Shear‐Force Sensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible tactile sensors are essential components of intelligent robotics, wearable healthcare systems, and human‐machine interfaces. However, most existing tactile sensors have limited capability to discriminate the direction of tangential forces, restricting multidimensional tactile perception under complex loading conditions. Herein, inspired by the serrated unidirectional compliant architecture of snake ventral scales, we develop a bioinspired serrated anisotropic tactile sensor (BSATS) for normal‐pressure sensing and bidirectional shear‐force discrimination. title: Interfacial multilayer evolution and structure-property relationships in hot-extruded Cu/Ti composites
abstract: Cu/Ti composites combine the complementary mechanical and electrical characteristics of Ti and Cu, but interfacial reactions during thermomechanical processing complicate control of their overall response. In this study, Cu/Ti composites were fabricated by hot extrusion over an extrusion-temperature range of 600-800 °C and an extrusion-ratio range of 4:1-25:1. title: A distributed clustering and alignment method for cooperative localization from short-range measurements in dynamic irregular networks
abstract: Cooperative localization in dynamic irregular networks estimates node positions from incomplete, noisy, and time-varying short-range measurements. This paper presents a distributed clustering and alignment method that decomposes global stress minimization into cluster formation, relative localization within clusters, and coordinate registration between clusters. title: Vegetation greening and soil drying in Central Asia: Evidence for bidirectional vegetation-soil moisture feedback
abstract: In arid Central Asia (CA), variations in soil moisture (SM) strongly influence vegetation dynamics, while vegetation can affect SM through evapotranspiration. Although SM variation and its influence on vegetation dynamics have been widely documented, the bidirectional feedback between vegetation and SM remains inadequately explored. title: Grey epistemic-trust QUALIFLEX framework for software platform vendor selection under uncertainty
abstract: Virtual industry-education collaboration platform procurement requires combining judgments from stakeholders whose expertise varies by criterion while retaining bounded uncertainty in both criterion importance and vendor performance. This study develops a grey-epistemic-trust (GET) weighting rule and integrates it with the established permutation-based Grey–QUALIFLEX ranking procedure. title: Adaptive Energy‐Aware Routing for Wireless Sensor Networks Using Fuzzy Logic‐Driven Greylag Goose Optimization
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) commonly form part of smart monitoring and data collection systems, in which energy‐efficient communication is still a challenging issue caused by the insufficient battery capacity of sensor nodes. A hybrid fuzzy logic‐based clustering and Gray Wolf Optimization (GWO) based routing, ECFGWO, called ECFGGO, is proposed in this paper for sustainable and adaptive data transmission in WSNs. title: Aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial para el aprendizaje personalizado del cálculo: una revisión bibliográfica
abstract: La enseñanza del cálculo diferencial e integral presenta desafíos asociados con la abstracción, la diversidad de conocimientos previos y la dificultad de proporcionar retroalimentación individual en grupos numerosos. Este artículo analiza las aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial (IA) para personalizar el aprendizaje del cálculo mediante una revisión bibliográfica narrativa de publicaciones entre 2021 y 2026. abstract: El creciente papel de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en actividades públicas, administrativas y judiciales representa un desafío constitucional que solo puede abordarse a nivel técnico y ético. El diseño y operación de un sistema algorítmico en situaciones que involucren decisiones que puedan afectar derechos fundamentales se convierte así en una cuestión de legalidad, debido proceso, igualdad, privacidad y transparencia, protección judicial efectiva y responsabilidad pública. title: Colourful and blooming cities – spatio-temporal proxies of pollinators for citizen science
abstract: Biodiversity monitoring is essential for detecting spatio-temporal changes and conservation effectiveness. Citizen science is expanding and complementing expert-based monitoring, yet its widespread success depends on simple and reliable sampling protocols. Simplified proxies are required in pollinator research to overcome taxonomic limitations, but their reliability remains uncertain. title: Quantifying the contribution of climate change and human activities to NPP in a typical karst area
abstract: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is an important indicator of ecological sustainability. The karst ecosystem is extremely delicate, featuring limited environmental capacity, severe erosion, and poor self-recovery capabilities. Quantifying the relative contributions of climate change and human activities to NPP in karst areas remains challenging. This study chose a typical karst area, Wiling Mountain in Guizhou Province, China, as the study area. title: Virtual Flood Experience Enhances Preparedness Through Emotional and Neural Engagement
abstract: As climate change intensifies flood risks, strengthening individual preparedness is essential for sustainable societies. This study tested whether first-person three-dimensional computer graphics (3DCG) flood videos can complement official flood maps in motivating preparedness. We used these materials as operationalizations of experiential and descriptive information, respectively. abstract: ABSTRACT Recent advances in metamaterials and fabrication techniques have revived interest in mechanical computing. Contrary to techniques relying on static deformations of buckling beams or origami‐based lattices, the integration of wave scattering and mechanical memory presents a promising path toward efficient, low‐latency elastoacoustic computing. abstract: ABSTRACT Metatranscriptome mining has dramatically expanded the known diversity of ribovirians at all taxonomic levels. We explored the class Stelpaviricetes in the phylum Pisuviricota that currently includes three orders and six recognized virus families: order Stellavirales with family Astroviridae infecting vertebrates; Patatavirales with families Potyviridae, the largest known family of plant ribovirians, and Potyliviridae; and Hypofuvirales consisting of three families of viruses associated largely with phytopathogenic fungi. title: Cryptic diversity highlights the challenge of Linnean and Wallacean shortfalls and the integral role of taxonomy in biodiversity conservation
abstract: Abstract Reliable and current taxonomic data are essential to conservation planning and prioritization. The use of genetic and genomic tools has revealed significant cryptic diversity across taxa and ecosystems, suggesting we are underestimating threatened biodiversity and using outdated species distributions. title: The growth period and earliness of cotton (Gossypium spp.): phenological architecture, environmental and genetic regulation, and breeding perspectives
abstract: The growth period of cotton ( Gossypium spp.), spanning emergence to boll opening, is a highly complex quantitative trait governed by genetic potential, thermal accumulation, photoperiodic sensing, resource availability, and agronomic management. Optimizing developmental duration and enhancing earliness are essential for mitigating grain-cotton land competition, enabling mechanized harvesting, and strengthening climate resilience. title: Riparian Land-Use Change and Selected Water Quality Parameters in the Upper Brantas River: A 10-Year Buffer Zone Analysis
abstract: Land-use changes and human activities continue to pressure the upper Brantas River. This study investigated land-use change within a 200 m river buffer from 2014 to 2024 and checked its patterns to water quality along the Upper Brantas River. Selected indicators for domestic wastewater, organic pollution, and nutrient input were chosen. title: How Can a Circular Economy for Sustainable Tourism be Assessed? Evidence From an Ecological Resort in Taiwan
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate mandates pressure the tourism and hospitality industry to decarbonize rapidly, making circular economy implementation in fragile destinations an immediate priority. Hotels usually focus inward on building efficiencies. abstract: Catenulids are free-living flatworms, common in eutrophic freshwaters such as ponds, ditches, or peatbogs. Although the majority of the species have been described from warmer climates, most molecular studies have been done on animals from temperate zones in Europe. abstract: ABSTRACT Land use and land cover changes (LULC) are driven by anthropogenic activities and, in turn, affect the availability of products and ecosystem services for people and other living organisms. Hence, the aim of this study was to determine the Pre‐ and Post‐Conflict Land Use Detection Matrix and Ecosystem Service Value (ESV) analysis in Hirmi State Forest, Northwestern Ethiopia. title: Dataset Recommendation for Heterogeneous and Dynamic Scholarly Graphs via Multimodal Representation Learning
abstract: Researchers struggle to find relevant datasets amid the volume of data across repositories and the growth of scholarly publications. Manual dataset retrieval is time-consuming and often fails to surface valuable resources not easily discoverable through direct links or popularity metrics. Dataset recommendation — identifying datasets relevant to a paper, author, or query — has become essential for improving dataset discoverability and reuse. abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) can be implemented on deployable and large coverage regions that enable the data collection and aggregation by multiple routing protocols. The challenges for reliable data aggregation with low energy consumption arise from the dependence of network performance on energy consumption, routing efficiency and sensor mobility. title: Digital Transformation of Work-Integrated Learning in Vocational Education: Microcredential Technology, Collaboration, and Industry Engagement
abstract: Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) is a strategic approach bridging vocational education and industry requirements. This study investigates digitalized WIL implementation in Indonesian vocational schools, focusing on microcredential technology utilization, interdisciplinary collaboration, and industry engagement. abstract: Despite the growing push to bring mobile phones to smallholder farmers for access to crop information, there is limited evidence for productivity gains for high-value crops. This study aims to determine the constraints of informative mobile phone usage and its impact on tomato output from 200 tomato farmers of Noakhali Sadar in Bangladesh through a survey. title: Integrated Lime–Soda Ash Softening and Vacuum Distillation for Sustainable Zero-Liquid-Discharge Treatment of Flue Gas Desulfurization Wastewater
abstract: South Africa’s dependence on coal-fired power generation necessitates the implementation of flue gas desulphurization (FGD) systems to control sulphur dioxide emissions. However, wet FGD processes generate wastewater containing high concentrations of hardness ions, sulphates, chlorides, and dissolved solids that require effective treatment before discharge or reuse. abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated approach, coupling rockfall risk assessment with a vehicle-based surveying for the large-scale management of slope assets along transportation corridors. Rockfall risk was assessed qualitatively using relative rating scales. title: Segmented Iterative Trend–Seasonal Decomposition (SITS) for time series with structural disruptions
abstract: Time series decomposition is widely used to separate trend and seasonal components in environmental data. However, standard approaches assume a single continuous trend and often fail in the presence of structural disruptions, leading to biased estimates. abstract: La enseñanza del algoritmo de la división escrita constituye uno de los núcleos más complejos en la aritmética escolar de la educación básica. El presente ensayo analiza la articulación entre las fases procedimentales del algoritmo y las tecnologías emergentes para fundamentar un marco de mediación pedagógica. abstract: Objective To examine the associations of job performance, job satisfaction, and workload with occupational self-efficacy among educators in rural areas of Peru. abstract: Abstract The urgent need to decarbonize the chemical sector and reduce dependence on fossil-derived carbon has renewed interest in biomass as a sustainable feedstock for chemical production. In this context, biomass has emerged as a versatile feedstock for producing both liquid and gaseous fuels, such as syngas, biogas, and compressed biogas (CBG). title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of informal settlement thermal environments and their driving factors in Nairobi, Kenya
abstract: Rapid urbanization in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) has expanded informal settlements where residents face extreme heat, yet informal settlement thermal dynamics remain understudied. Nowhere is this more evident than in Nairobi, one of SSA’s most rapidly growing metropolises, which faces critical challenges from unregulated informal settlement expansion, characterized by high population density and threats to urban sustainability and resident well-being. abstract: This study aims to assess the spatio-temporal dynamics of urban expansion and its influence on urban green and blue spaces (UGBSs) during 1995–2025 in Jabalpur city using geospatial techniques and align UGBSs with sustainable development goals (SDGs) target 11.3. For this Landsat datasets have been utilized for land use and land cover (LU/LC) mapping and extraction of UGBSs using spectral angle mapper (SAM) technique. abstract: Abstract Facing the dual challenges of climate change and resource sustainability, efficient recovery of medium‐low temperature industrial waste heat is crucial for achieving the “dual carbon” goals. Stirling engines (SEs) have emerged as a preferred solution due to their unique advantages. However, traditional cycles suffer irreversible heat loss from non‐ideal isothermal heat transfer. abstract: Nature-based Solutions (NBS) have the potential to provide solutions to a range of societal challenges, such as climate adaptation, and simultaneously contribute toward biodiversity goals. NBS are increasingly implemented in urban sustainability practice, especially in residential districts and business sites. title: Post-fire assessment of soil physicochemical properties in Tamgout Forest, Northern Algeria
abstract: Understanding how fires affect forest ecosystem components is crucial for predicting vegetation recovery and guiding forest management. Yet information on wildfire consequences for soil properties remains limited in Algeria. This study investigated the impact of wildfire on the physicochemical and structural properties of forest soil in the Tamgout area, northern Algeria. abstract: Thinning can improve stand spatial structure but removes living biomass carbon, creating a trade-off that may vary among stand types and future climate pathways. abstract: El uso de herramientas basadas en inteligencia artificial se ha intensificado en la educación superior, generando debate sobre su valor de cara a la procrastinación, Estos instrumentos se pueden considerar parte de un andamiaje cognitivo que puede minimizar la postergación de actividades complejas, aunque también podría favorecer la dependencia tecnológica, minando la autorregulación. abstract: Metal–organic framework (MOF)–poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrenesulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) composites represent an emerging class of hybrid materials that integrate high porosity with electrical conductivity. title: Resilience Governance and Public Service Innovation in Local Government: A Study of Public Service Mall in Barru Regency, Indonesia
abstract: The growing emphasis on integrated and digitally enabled public services has not necessarily ensured resilient and equitable service delivery, particularly in local governments facing uneven infrastructure, geographic barriers, and variations in institutional capacity. This study examines how resilience governance shapes public service innovation through the implementation of the MPP in Barru Regency and identifies conditions required to transform institutional capacity into resilient service delivery. title: HORIZON and LocoMMotion: a descriptive cross-study comparison of outcomes in triple-class refractory multiple myeloma
abstract: Background Multiple myeloma (MM) is a relapsing plasma cell malignancy. Patients’ refractory to proteasome inhibitors, immunomodulatory drugs, and anti-CD38 antibodies (triple-class refractory) and, more recently, to T-cell-redirected (TCR) therapies have limited treatment options and a poor prognosis. Melphalan flufenamide (melflufen), a first-in-class peptide–drug conjugate, delivers intracellular alkylators independently of prior resistance mechanisms. title: The mediating effects of perceived quality and brand image between country-of-origin and purchase intention for refurbished iPhones
abstract: This study investigates how Country-of-Origin influences Students’ Purchase Intention toward Refurbished iPhones, with Brand Image and Perceived Quality as mediating variables. A quantitative explanatory design was applied, involving 136 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS). The empirical results revealed that Country-of-Origin positively and significantly affected Brand Image, Perceived Quality, and purchase intention, both directly and indirectly. title: Seasonal–hourly assessment of data center spatial flexibility under renewable variability: A case study of Jeju Island
abstract: Policy interest in data center deployment away from the Seoul metropolitan area has made renewable-rich Jeju Island a leading candidate, yet its island grid offers limited transfer capability, and the demand it can accommodate has not been quantified. Spatial flexibility has emerged as a promising alternative to network reinforcement, but transmission-level studies remain limited, and those available specify the data center capacity as an input rather than determining it. title: Preparing for the next drought: delineating safe groundwater reserves in post-subsidence cities
abstract: Abstract Cities recovering from land subsidence face a critical water-security dilemma: how to safely use groundwater in emergencies—such as prolonged droughts—without reactivating unrecoverable subsidence. Focusing on post-subsidence Tianjin, we develop a hydro-geomechanical framework that defines subsidence-safe pumping limits. By quantifying a regional-average intrinsic vertical hydraulic gradient (IVHG) in the confined aquifer system, we establish an IVHG-governed continuous aquifer model that replaces the traditional layered model. title: Protective effects of AKBA against hypoxia-induced cognitive dysfunction: potential involvement of SLC2A1, PTGS1, and BCL2L1
abstract: Introduction Hypoxia-induced cognitive impairment (HICI) is associated with neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota dysbiosis, highlighting the need for effective neuroprotective interventions. Acetyl-11-keto-β-boswellic acid (AKBA), a bioactive triterpenoid derived from frankincense, possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, but its protective effects against hypoxia-associated cognitive dysfunction remain insufficiently understood. title: Research on an improved RRT-APF path planning algorithm for tomato harvesting manipulators
abstract: To address the problems of low path planning efficiency and excessive redundant nodes in tomato harvesting manipulators, an improved RRT-APF path planning algorithm is proposed. First, a goal-biased strategy is introduced into the standard Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) framework to reduce search randomness and improve sampling efficiency. The Artificial Potential Field (APF) method is then integrated with a greedy strategy to perform obstacle avoidance and update nodes. title: Multi‐Scale Hydrodynamic Simulation Framework for Flood Risk Assessment of Urban Metro Stations
abstract: ABSTRACT Urban metro stations are highly vulnerable to pluvial flooding, yet accurately evaluating internal risks remains challenging due to the disconnected modeling approaches between surface inundation and internal intrusion processes. This study proposes a practical multi‐scale 2D hydrodynamic modeling framework that bridges overland flooding with multi‐level internal metro station inundation. title: Eco-anxiety as a public health imperative: from individual resilience to culturally informed holistic engagement
abstract: Eco-anxiety has increasingly drawn public health attention. Although often conceptualized as an individual psychological burden, eco-anxiety may also serve as a catalyst for collective action. However, prevailing coping strategies largely center on individual resilience, with insufficient focus on social connectedness and the human-nature bond. title: Immobilized Epiphytic Bacteria Enhance Macrophyte Suppression of a Bloom‐Forming Cyanobacterium
abstract: Harmful cyanobacterial blooms are an increasing threat to freshwater ecosystems and water security worldwide. Biological control using macrophytes or algicidal bacteria is often studied separately despite natural co-occurrence. Here we show that the epiphytic bacterium Priestia megaterium strain BW, isolated from submerged macrophytes, exhibits strong algicidal activity and forms an enhanced suppression system with its host plant Vallisneria natans. title: ‘I think it's a rebrand…’: Pre‐service teachers' conceptualisations of adaptive teaching and differentiated instruction
abstract: Abstract This paper explores how pre‐service teachers (PSTs) conceptualise adaptive teaching in relation to differentiation within the contemporary policy landscape in England. Drawing on qualitative focus group data and informed by Bourdieu's theory of practice, the study examines how pedagogical understandings are shaped by social justice concerns, institutional constraints and emerging professional identities. The findings introduce pedagogical cynicism as a significant lens through which PSTs interpret reform alongside nuanced forms of teacher agency. The study offers original insight into

title: Institutional Capture and Mining Governance Resilience: Evidence from Bangka Belitung and Jambi, Indonesia
abstract: Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (ASM) remains a governance dilemma in Indonesia, balancing livelihoods against environmental degradation. This article investigates how ASM governance functions in two contrasting provinces—Bangka Belitung (tin) and Jambi (gold)—assessing system resilience against policy adaptability, enforcement consistency, institutional autonomy, and implementation gaps. Using a qualitative comparative case study, data were collected through extensive in-depth interviews and focus group discussions with regulators, miners, financiers, and civil society. title: LA INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL Y LAS FUNCIONES EJECUTIVAS EN EL ESTUDIANTE UNIVERSITARIO
abstract: La aparición en la esfera pública de la inteligencia artificial ha generado un impacto significativo en la educación universitaria global. En este sentido, el propósito de este ensayo busca responder la siguiente pregunta: ¿en qué punto las inteligencias artificiales que utilizan nuestros estudiantes para apoyarse en actividades escolares se convierten en herramientas que promueven el sedentarismo intelectual y ralentizan el desarrollo de sus funciones ejecutivas? title: Spatial Variability in Soil Necrobiome Communities Appears to have a Negligible Effect on Post-mortem Interval Estimation
abstract: Microbial succession can be used to estimate the post-mortem interval (PMI); however, the impact of spatial variability within the cadaver decomposition island (CDI) is not well understood. This study examined spatial variation in necrobiome communities where soil samples were collected over time and across spatial locations from the CDIs of two human body donors. Microbial communities were characterized using 16S rRNA sequencing and statistical modelling of community variation and PMI relationships were conducted. title: The Influence of Tourism Attributes on Destination Image Post-Reclamation Mediated by Tourist Satisfaction at Tampomas Eco Park Sumedang
abstract: The transformation of former mining sites (mining brownfields) into sustainable tourism destinations presents complex challenges, particularly in reshaping public perceptions and overcoming the stigma associated with environmental degradation. This study aimed to examine the relationships between tourism attributes, destination image, and tourist satisfaction as a mediating variable at Tampomas Eco Park, Sumedang Regency, Indonesia. title: Georeferenced records of Zizula hylax hylax (Fabricius, 1775) (Lepidoptera, Lycaenidae) in Thailand, with observations on developmental stages and molecular confirmation
abstract: Zizula hylax hylax (Fabricius, 1775), commonly known as the Tiny Grass Blue, is widely distributed across several countries, including Thailand. We report georeferenced records of Z. h. hylax associated with the host plant Ruellia tuberosa L. (Acanthaceae) from Nakhon Pathom, Phetchaburi, and Bangkok, Thailand. In Nakhon Pathom Province, we documented all four developmental stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult. title: Multi-band localized surface plasmon enhanced terahertz biosensor chip with electrostatic and acousto-optic active tuning
abstract: Introduction Terahertz (THz) biosensing can read biomolecular vibrations without labels, yet two practical problems limit its sensitivity: sub-wavelength biological samples interact only weakly with the radiation, and 1/f noise dominates slow readouts. Methods We propose a multi-band localized surface plasmon (LSP)-enhanced THz biosensor chip in which a gold metasurface of nine spectrally isolated cross-resonator sub-arrays sustains LSP resonances at 0.1–0.9 THz, concentrating the field in deep-sub-wavelength hot spots at the resonator arm ends and gaps. title: Navigating multipolarity: India–China relations and the reconfiguration of global and regional order in South Asia
abstract: This paper examines how India and China are reconfiguring global and regional order through three interconnected objectives: the changing nature of global order and its influence on India and China as rising powers, the pragmatic cooperation between the two nations under balance-of-power politics, and their competing roles in reshaping the regional order in South Asia. title: A deep reinforcement learning-based algorithm for regional drone routing problem with nonlinear fuel consumption
abstract: With the boom of e-commerce and increasing policy support, regional logistics serving medium- and short-distance transportation have grown rapidly. Large fuel-powered drones are increasingly adopted in this field due to their flexibility and efficiency, yet their deployment has raised concerns regarding pollutant emissions and environmental sustainability. To balance logistics efficiency with environmental responsibility, this paper proposes a regional drone routing problem using large fuel-powered drones, accounting for nonlinear fuel consumption and multiple pollutant emissions. journal: Transportation Research Part E Logistics and Transportation Review

title: Human neocortical glutamatergic neurons revealed through multimodal profiling
abstract: The human neocortex underlies higher cognition and is the engine of complex thought. Yet our understanding of its neuronal diversity is limited by sparse access to tissue, inconsistent sampling across studies, and a lack of multiple modality data. Although single-cell transcriptomic taxonomies are an important framework for characterizing cell type diversity, transcriptomic information alone cannot reveal the cellular properties that define neuronal computations. title: From mineral weathering to alkalinity export: a soil-barrier diagnostic for enhanced rock weathering in tropical soils
abstract: Mineral dissolution is necessary for enhanced rock weathering (ERW), but it does not determine when weathering products become measurable beyond the soil profile. This study defines alkalinity breakthrough as the point at which weathering-derived base charge exceeds internal soil interception by proton demand, exchange storage, and other sinks sufficiently for export to emerge. This transition was evaluated using a daily charge-conserving model across four Ghanaian climates, four tropical soil archetypes, five feedstocks, three hydrologic structures, and 2,400 Latin hypercube simulations. title: Satellite assessment of ecological condition and associated recovery constraints in China's main ion adsorption rare earth mining landscape from 2000 to 2025
abstract: In Ganzhou, China, ion adsorption rare earth mining sites are registered only as points, which do not show where recovery lags. We assessed ecological condition with a Remote Sensing Ecological Index adapted to mining (M-RSEI), harmonized across Landsat sensors. Mean M-RSEI rose gradually from 0.598 in 2000–2005 to 0.670 in 2020–2025, and three quarters of the cells improved. title: Microplastics and microbiota: deciphering the concealed environmental threats to health
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) have emerged as ubiquitous environmental pollutants, infiltrating terrestrial, aquatic, and atmospheric ecosystems. Recent research highlights a critical, bidirectional relationship between these particles and microbiota, particularly within the gastrointestinal (GI) tract of humans and animals. The gut microbiota, a complex and diverse community of trillions of microbes residing in the human GI tract, plays a critical role in host digestion, metabolism, immune function, and overall health. title: Determinants of Entrepreneurial Intention among Fisheries Students in Kerala: Evidence from a Primary Quantitative Survey Using the Theory of Planned Behaviour
abstract: The objective of this research is to identify the determinants of entrepreneurial intention among students of fisheries and allied programmes in Kerala using the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) after extending it with entrepreneurship awareness and perceived government support. title: YOLOv8-CNR: a lightweight fire and smoke detection model for forest fire scenarios based on improved YOLOv8
abstract: Introduction To address irregular morphology and drastic scale variations of flame and smoke targets in forest fire detection, and the difficulty of lightweight models in balancing accuracy and real-time performance, this paper proposes YOLOv8-CNR based on improved YOLOv8n. Methods The model optimizes backbone, neck, and loss function: C3_ConvNeXtv2 enhances flame texture and smoke edge representation; RepNCSPELAN4 strengthens multi-scale flow and small-target smoke features; SIoU improves localization of irregular targets. title: Inteligencia artificial conversacional y psicología clínica como complemento o sustitución profesional: Revisión narrativa crítica de evidencia internacional e implicaciones para Ecuador
abstract: La inteligencia artificial (IA) conversacional se utiliza para apoyo emocional, psicoeducación e intervenciones autoguiadas. Esta revisión narrativa crítica examina beneficios clínicos, limitaciones, riesgos e implicaciones profesionales, y analiza su pertinencia para Ecuador. abstract: Perkembangan AI generatif menawarkan efisiensi produksi konten pemasaran bagi UMKM, namun memunculkan masalah berupa keseragaman linguistik, hilangnya identitas merek, dan berkurangnya kedekatan emosional. title: Determination of groundwater potential zone in an urban area using GIS-based multi-criteria analysis: Case of Bangui and its surroundings
abstract: ABSTRACT Access to safe drinking water remains a critical challenge in the Central African Republic (CAR), where basic water access rates stand at approximately 40%. In Bangui, the capital city, water supply depends primarily on the Oubangui River, whose discharge significantly decreases during the dry season, exacerbating water insecurity for an urban population of approximately 1.5 million inhabitants. title: DTReq4.0: a catalog of digital twin requirements for Industry 4.0
abstract: Abstract Digital twins (DT) have been applied across different product life cycle stages, such as design and operation, and have been crucial in advancing various application domains, including Industry 4.0. For DT development, identifying their requirements is essential to ensure that the projects meet expectations and mainly describe the digital model containing the characteristics and behavior of physical twins. title: Clinical task-driven design of gastrointestinal wet-adhesive hydrogels across the treatment course
abstract: Gastrointestinal tissues present a particularly challenging environment for wet adhesion because persistent fluid exposure, chemical degradation, tissue motion, and biological renewal can disrupt both material–tissue contact and therapeutic function. Adhesive hydrogels have consequently evolved from tissue-binding materials into therapeutic interfaces for local drug delivery, wound coverage, hemostasis, and defect sealing. title: Complete Genome Sequences of Mycobacterium smegmatis Phages SVoro and PrinceCharming
abstract: SVoro and PrinceCharming were isolated from moist soil on the campus of Winthrop University and isolated on the host bacterium Mycobacterium smegmatis mc 2 155.SVoro has a myovirus morphology and a genome of 155,109 bp, while PrinceCharming exhibits siphovirus morphology and a genome of 67,429 bp.Lysogens could not be raised for SVoro or PrinceCharming, suggesting these are virulent phages.SVoro is classified in the C1 subcluster, and PrinceCharming belongs to the B2 subcluster.

abstract: General Background: Equitable hospital distribution is essential for healthcare accessibility, yet aggregate health infrastructure statistics may conceal disparities across smaller administrative areas. Specific Background: Hospital availability in periurban regions may differ considerably between subdistricts despite seemingly sufficient regional healthcare resources. abstract: ABSTRACT Adhesively bonded aluminium joints are widely used in lightweight structures, but their durability is often limited by interfacial crack growth, fatigue damage, moisture ingress, and limited recovery of fracture resistance after damage. This study develops a sustainable, multifunctional jute/epoxy composite interlayer by combining graphene oxide‐coated jute fabric with a dual epoxy–mercaptan microcapsule self‐healing chemistry to achieve fatigue‐resistant aluminium adhesive joints. title: Hybrid diffusion–DE-based 3D UAV deployment for joint coverage enhancement and energy efficiency in IoT networks
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted communication has become a key enabler for next-generation wireless networks, particularly in post-disaster recovery and remote-area connectivity. A major challenge lies in jointly maximizing the coverage of Internet of Things devices (IoTDEs) while minimizing the energy consumption of UAV base stations (UAV-BSs). To address this issue, we propose a novel hybrid 3D deployment algorithm, termed D3E, which achieves an effective balance between communication coverage and energy efficiency. title: A GEOSPATIAL-BASED EDUCATION MANAGEMENT MODEL AS A WEIGHTED DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEM FOR SUSTAINABLE TOURISM VILLAGES
abstract: This study aims to develop and operationalize a geospatial-based education management model as a weighted Decision Support System (DSS) framework for sustainable tourism villages. A qualitative case study approach was employed in Panglipuran Village, Bali, Indonesia. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, field observations, and document analysis involving traditional leaders, village government officials, religious leaders, administrators, and community representatives. title: Numerical Modelling of 3D-Printed Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer Composites: Challenges, Limitations, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Three-dimensional printing of the carbon fiber-reinforced polymer composites has attracted considerable attention for lightweight structural applications due to their outstanding specific strength, design adaptability, tailorable fiber placement, and improved specific mechanical performance. abstract: ABSTRACT With tonnes of battery shredded globally, tracing down pathways in upcycling black mass (BM) as catalysts would be a game changer. Existing unwavering synergic combination of inherent metals and graphite in BM drives this novel objective. Herein, we report the critical role of spent graphite for electrocatalytic water splitting applications by systematic evaluation of diverse NMC, LFP, and LCO BM. title: From Severe Delamination to Enhanced Wear Resistance: Unraveling the Microstructural Evolution and Wear Performance of A390 During ECAP-Route BC at 400°C
abstract: The effects of equal-channel angular pressing (ECAP) via route BC at 400 °C on the microstructure and dry-sliding wear behavior of a hypereutectic A390 Al–Si–Cu alloy were investigated for up to four passes. Particular attention was given to the relationships between second-phase particle evolution, grain-boundary characteristics, and wear resistance. The results revealed a distinctly non-monotonic wear response with increasing pass number. abstract: Study region The Fourmile Branch Creek catchment at the Savannah River Site (SRS), USA, a watershed historically impacted by tritium ( 3 H) releases from nuclear production facilities. abstract: Wearable inertial measurement unit (IMU) networks are an affordable alternative to optical motion capture for lower-limb measurement in sport, physical activity, and rehabilitation outside the laboratory, but two problems limit their kinematic signal: the reference-frame dependence of joint angles formed by differencing Euler angles from separate sensors, and frame-level desynchronisation caused by unscheduled wireless transmission. abstract: Pembangunan bandara internasional berperan strategis dalam meningkatkan konektivitas wilayah dan pertumbuhan ekonomi, tetapi juga mendorong transformasi spasial yang berpotensi menimbulkan tekanan terhadap keberlanjutan lingkungan. abstract: Background Proteases from bacteria and their secondary metabolites have bioactivity which can be utilized in therapeutical industries to overcome the negative effects of existing conventional medicines. Methods This study focused on isolating bacteria from different kinds of soil and contaminated coconut samples. title: Burst-to-burst information resetting in sequential rhythmic neural activity
abstract: In multiple neural systems, networks of bursting neurons generate and coordinate robust sequential rhythms, such as those observed in central pattern generators (CPGs) that control motor activity. In this paper, we combine electrophysiological experiments and biophysical models of the pyloric CPG to investigate cycle-by-cycle coordination resetting in sequential rhythms. title: Bacillus fermented complete feed: a green alternative to improve disease resistance, growth performance and hepato-intestinal health of Nile tilapia
abstract: Due to the prominent antibacterial activity and favorable fermentation characteristics, Bacillus strains are widely utilized in the preparation of fermented complete feed in aquafeed industry. However, synthetic microbial consortia are preferentially applied in industrial-scale production than single Bacillus strains alone. To date, the evaluation and comparison of the probiotic effects of single strains or synthetic microbial consortia fermented complete feed for fish are still insufficient. title: Fungi-engineered metal nanoparticles for advanced therapeutics
abstract: Growing concern over the environmental toxicity and biomedical risks of conventional physical and chemical nanoparticle synthesis has intensified interest in sustainable routes to metal nanoparticle production. Myconanotechnology, which uses fungi as biological nanofactories, has emerged as a versatile green platform: fungi tolerate high metal concentrations and secrete abundant enzymes, proteins, and polysaccharides that act as reducing, stabilizing, and capping agents. title: From oligosaccharide evolution to functional food design: A critical review of Polygonati rhizome processing with evidence grading
abstract: Polygonati rhizomes are traditionally consumed after hydrothermal or wine-assisted processing, yet their transformation from a raw botanical into a reproducible food ingredient remains chemically under-resolved. This review evaluates, as an explicitly hypothesis-driven framework, the proposed sequence linking processing severity, carbohydrate depolymerization, oligosaccharide enrichment, biological responses and food functionality. abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), and photothermal effects are integrated into a single reaction system through Fe doping into HEOs. abstract: La integración de inteligencia artificial (IA) en la formación docente abre posibilidades para la enseñanza de la literatura y la preservación del patrimonio cultural, pero también plantea desafíos sobre representación, sesgos lingüísticos y control comunitario del conocimiento. abstract: Current military and civilian demands require more efficient and versatile aircraft configurations. Tiltrotor aircraft combine the vertical takeoff and landing capability of helicopters with the high cruise speed advantage of turboprop aircraft. Unlike traditional aircraft, tiltrotors exhibit unique aeroelastic behaviors that vary significantly across their multiple operating modes. title: Los ámbitos de aplicación del Reglamento de Inteligencia Artificial: extraterritorialidad y unilateralismo regulatorio en el Derecho internacional privado europeo
abstract: El presente trabajo ofrece un estudio sistemático y conjunto de los ámbitos de aplicación material, personal, territorial y temporal del Reglamento (UE) 2024/1689 de Inteligencia Artificial desde la perspectiva del Derecho internacional privado. El análisis sitúa el RIA en el marco del unilateralismo regulatorio europeo y sostiene su caracterización como norma de policía que autodelimita su ámbito de aplicación en el espacio a través del artículo 2, desplazando, aunque sin excluir, el método conflictual.Sobre esta base, el trabajo reconstruye los distintos ámbitos de aplicación del Reglamento.

title: Simulation of subtropical courtyard microclimate evolution and optimization algorithm for landscape design based on multi-source remote sensing data fusion
abstract: Abstract Subtropical courtyards temper heat and admit light, yet their thermal performance has been hard to quantify at a scale fine enough to guide design. abstract: Abstract Plasma-induced liquid flow is an emerging topic receiving accelerated interest in recent years within the larger inter-disciplinary field of plasma-liquid interactions. abstract: The term “Anthropocene” captures humanity’s profound impact on Earth’s geology and ecosystems, and it has become central to understanding the relationship between human societies and the Earth system. abstract: Nasal colonization by Staphylococcus aureus among healthcare professionals represents a potential risk for the spread of resistant strains in hospital settings. abstract: Abstract Catastrophe insurance economics has long recognized that disaster insurance markets fail on both sides of the market, with households under-insuring low-probability high-consequence risks and insurers unable to diversify or price correlated catastrophe exposure. abstract: Understanding the sequence determinants of antibody affinity within a clonal family is a central challenge in therapeutic antibody discovery. Here, we applied amino acid frequency analysis to a large phylogenetic clonal tree of anti-ST2 monoclonal antibodies, where V(D)J recombination is constant and only somatic hypermutations vary. title: Scenario-based screening of agricultural residues and perennial energy grasses for hydrothermal co-production of xylooligosaccharides and fermentable sugars
abstract: Agricultural residues and perennial energy grasses are promising lignocellulosic resources; however, their suitability for hydrothermal biorefineries depends on conversion performance, hydrolysate quality, biomass supply, and economic context. Here, 12 feedstocks, including five agricultural residues and seven perennial energy grasses, were evaluated under a unified hydrothermal pretreatment condition of 190℃ for 10 min (severity factor, log R 0 =3.65) for the co-production of xylooligosaccharides (XOS) and fermentable sugars. title: Environmental drivers of microbial community dynamics in a cool-water aquaponics system
abstract: Aquaponic systems represent an integrated water-efficient approach to food production by combining recirculating aquaculture with hydroponic plant cultivation. Performance and stability of these systems depend not only on fish and plant interactions but also on the structure and function of associated microbial communities, which regulate nutrient cycling and water quality. Microbial communities play a central role in the stability and performance of aquaponic systems, yet the relative importance of temporal dynamics, spatial heterogeneity, and environmental drivers remains poorly understood.

title: Beyond Micro‐/Nanostructures: Close‐Packed Nanostructure Enables Superior Superhydrophobic Anti‐Icing Coatings
abstract: Hierarchical micro-/nanostructures have long been regarded as the optimal architecture for superhydrophobic anti-icing surfaces. Here, by constructing superhydrophobic coatings with identical surface chemistry but distinct microscopic architectures, we directly compare the anti-icing performance of a close-packed nanostructure and a hierarchical micro-/nanostructure. title: Spatial assessment of soil fertility in high-Andean potato systems using a multivariate index in the Pasco region, Peru
abstract: Potato cultivation in the central Andes of Peru occurs under highly heterogeneous environmental conditions, where soil fertility is influenced by interactions among lithology, geomorphology, climate, and vegetation. This study evaluated the spatial variability of soil fertility in high-Andean potato systems across three river basins of the Pasco region, Peru, through the development of a multivariate Soil Fertility Index (SFI). title: Spatializing the Circular Economy: Firm-Level Evidence and Socio-Demographic Factors within a National Post-Consumer Sneaker Network
abstract: Post-consumer footwear constitutes a highly heterogeneous and minimally circular segment of the consumer goods economy. Although the sector has a substantial environmental footprint, empirical research on post-consumer footwear collection and reverse logistics remains limited. This study contributes to circular economy scholarship by showing that post-consumer sneaker collection depends largely on intermediary capacity, territorial coordination, and robust reverse-logistics infrastructure. title: Temperature-driven dormancy loss shapes subsequent germination thermal requirements in Centaurium somedanum
abstract: Abstract Seed dormancy is a key mechanism regulating germination timing by determining how seeds respond to environmental cues. However, the extent to which temperatures experienced during dormancy loss alter subsequent germination thermal requirements remains poorly understood. We investigated this process in Centaurium somedanum , a narrow endemic of calcareous mountain springs in northern Spain, with non-deep simple morphophysiological dormancy. title: Language Transformation and Subjectivity: A Lacanian Psychological Literary Criticism of Daniel Keyes’ Flowers for Algernon
abstract: This study examines subjectivity construction, stabilization, and disintegration in Daniel Keyes’ Flowers for Algernon, highlighting language as the main narrative mechanism for producing subjectivity. Using narratological, stylistic, and Lacanian psychoanalytic frameworks, the analysis views subjectivity not as a stable psychological essence but as a fragile, language-dependent formation via narrative discourse. title: Allometric scaling of adaxial–abaxial stomatal allocation in amphistomatous plants worldwide
abstract: Amphistomatous plants distribute stomata between the adaxial and abaxial leaf surfaces, but whether this dual-surface allocation follows a predictable scaling relationship, and why species deviate from it, remains poorly understood. Here, we compiled a global dataset of adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities for 559 species across 380 sites and 63 families. abstract: Sensorimotor deficits can profoundly affect the life quality of patients with neurological disorders, yet our understanding of central dysfunction at the cellular or circuit level is limited. Using a forward genetic approach to generate loss of auditory function in zebrafish larvae, we identified a recessive mutation in split ends ( spen ), which encodes a transcription factor implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders in humans. abstract: The current study intends to theoretically examine the behaviour of heat transfer in the water-ethylene glycol(EG)-based nanofluid flow containing copper nanoparticles through a rectangular channel. Considering a 50:50 and 70:30 volume ratio of water and EG, this study intends to further analyse the influence of an external magnetic field and viscous dissipation on the flow and heat transfer properties of the nanofluid. title: Municipal sludge disposal emerges as a major, hidden, and rapidly growing atmospheric mercury source
abstract: Wastewater treatment greatly reduces mercury pollution in aquatic ecosystems but does not eliminate it. title: Pathogen persistence, inflammation resolution, and bone repair in Staphylococcus aureus osteomyelitis
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus osteomyelitis commonly involves persistent infection, inflammatory bone destruction, and impaired repair. Coordinating infection control with recovery of bone function remains an important therapeutic challenge. This review examines the relationships among pathogen persistence, innate immune responses, and bone repair, with inflammation resolution as its central focus. abstract: In shipping agency and general supplier services, customers evaluate providers through operational dependability, pricing practices, and confidence in business commitments. abstract: Abstract The surface of fresh vegetable leaves harbors diverse microorganisms with the potential to influence human health through the microbiome-food-gut axis. abstract: Introduction The site index is the most commonly used indirect indicator of forest site productivity, based on the height-age relationship. title: Recent Changes in North and South America Monsoon Rainfall
abstract: The North American Monsoon (NAM) and South American Monsoon (SAM) are the two dominant seasonal precipitation systems of the Western Hemisphere, yet a systematic comparison of their recent changes over the satellite era remains limited. This study investigates recent changes in NAM and SAM rainfall over the period 2001–2024 using NASA's Integrated Multi-satellitE Retrievals for GPM (IMERG) daily precipitation product, interpolated to a 1x1deg grid. abstract: Introduction Maternal health during pregnancy is critical for favorable birth outcomes and long-term wellbeing of both mothers and infants. Women in rural, malaria-endemic regions face unique biological and socioeconomic challenges that may increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). This study investigated the proportions and determinants of APOs among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Webuye sub-County Hospital in Western Kenya, a rural malaria-endemic setting. abstract: Abstract Functional peptidomic studies produce data sets of thousands of peptides, which are assigned bioactivities through curated databases and prediction tools. Because peptides often have multiple bioactivities, grouping by function can double-count peptides and overstate total functional abundance within each sample. abstract: This research examines the effects of the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), Halal Awareness, and religiosity on Muslim consumers' intention to purchase halal cosmetic products in Indonesia. A quantitative research design was employed, and data were collected from 325 respondents selected through purposive sampling. abstract: Heritage buildings adapted for contemporary library use often face difficulties in providing adequate and uniform lighting while preserving their architectural character. This study evaluates the lighting quality of Montgomery Hall, a historic Neo-Classical reading space within the Quaid-e-Azam Library, Lahore, with particular emphasis on illuminance, visual comfort, and compliance with recommended lighting requirements. title: Comparative analysis of dye decolorization efficiency and growth kinetics of microalgae in the presence of Methyl orange and Rhodamine B dye
abstract: Textile industries are the major contributor to water pollution due to the usage of highly toxic synthetic dyes. Synthetic dyes are non-biodegradable and toxic in nature and, pose significant ecological and health risks. Therefore, this study explores the impact of two prevalent dyes, Rhodamine B (RB) and Methyl Orange (MO), on microalgal growth and their decolorization efficiency. abstract: Abstract Decarbonization policies aim to electrify the transportation sector by increasing the use of Electric Vehicles (EVs); consequently, Electric Vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) are widely integrated into distribution systems (DSs). title: Does the use of smart logistics platforms improve operational performance? Evidence from Chinese export firms
abstract: Smart logistics platforms now support routine export operations in many Chinese B2B firms. However, firms still differ in how intensively they use these platforms. Firms also differ in the process gains they obtain. We use survey data from 324 firms. We examine whether organizational capabilities and product characteristics explain differences in smart logistics platform utilization. title: Digital Bureaucracy and the Paradox of Participation in Indonesia: Challenges for Public Policy Governance
abstract: This study explores the relation between digital bureaucracy, public engagement, and challenges in Indonesian governance via an ILR consisting of 57 articles indexed in Scopus (2021-2024). Though Indonesia strongly advocates for digital transformation, the results of the study indicate a significant gap. Despite implementing Digital Bureaucracy, Indonesia has been unable to overcome its governance deficit. abstract: Abstract This study examines the impact of Data Analytics Capability on organisational performance within an emerging economy’s local government assembly, with particular focus on the mediating role of Data-Driven Decision Making and the influence of Top Management Support. Grounded in the Organisational Information Processing Theory and the Upper Echelons Theory, the study adopts a cross-sectional survey explanatory design. abstract: Bioactive natural products remain a premier source of lead scaffolds for drug discovery. This review integrates recent advances in the chemical synthesis, structural modification, pharmacological activities, and molecular mechanisms of natural products, with particular emphasis on linking structural optimization to pharmacological performance. abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) is a promising technology for converting wet biomass into biocrude. However, hydrothermal liquefaction wastewater (HTL-WW) presents sustainability challenges because of its high organic loading, nutrient content, and inhibitory compounds. abstract: Water Cherenkov Detectors (WCDs) are pivotal in various scientific fields, including neutrino physics, gamma-ray astronomy, and cosmic-ray research. abstract: ABSTRACT Designing biomaterials compatible with plants and specific payloads enables new technologies for precision agriculture, including targeted and dose‐controlled agrochemical delivery that overcomes the runoff, drift, and cuticular exclusion limiting conventional methods. However, broader implementation requires a systematic understanding of the complex interactions among payloads, biomaterial properties, and plant responses to establish design principles that support a sustained biotic–abiotic interface. title: The PADI Model: Community Service as Peace Infrastructure for Preventing Social Conflict
abstract: Indonesian law assigns the prevention of social conflict not only to the state but also to society, yet community engagement programmes run by universities rarely take up this mandate in a sustained way. This article asks how community service (pengabdian kepada masyarakat) can be designed to function as part of the local infrastructure for peace rather than as a one-off awareness activity. title: Improving flood-modeling accuracy with refined NRCS Curve Number and Lag Time estimation via remote sensing-based land cover classification correction
abstract: Land use/cover change (LULC) is a major driver of hydrological alteration and flood risk, yet reliable estimation of Curve Number (CN) and Lag Time (T lag ) remains challenging in data-scarce regions where conventional empirical formulas often fail to capture local watershed conditions. This study develops an integrated framework for enhancing the empirical Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) equations through the combined use of remote sensing, hydrological modeling, and parametric error correction. title: Low-Budget Topographic Mapping: Systematic 360° Camera Surveys with Ground Control Points for Drone-Restricted Archaeological Contexts
abstract: Abstract This article introduces a low-budget approach to archaeological land surveying using spherical cameras, developed for contexts where drone photography is unavailable or where UAV regulations impede its use. The technique combines a 360° camera with standard accessories, making it affordable, portable, and deployable on demand across varied logistical conditions. title: Integrating TPB and UTAUT to explain renewable energy adoption intentions in rural Terengganu, Malaysia: The role of facilitating conditions and policy awareness
abstract: The transition to renewable energy technologies (RETs) is essential for achieving Malaysia’s sustainable development and carbon-reduction goals. Despite various national initiatives, adoption rates in rural communities remain modest. This study develops and empirically tests an integrated behavioural framework that combines the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) to explain intentions to adopt renewable energy in rural Terengganu, Malaysia. A structured questionnaire survey was administered to 200 rural household decision-makers
institutions: Tun Hussein Onn University of Malaysia

title: Training interbrain synchrony through dyadic neurofeedback modulates empathy-for-pain
abstract: Dyadic neurofeedback offers a socially grounded approach for modulating neural processes that unfold between interacting individuals. While recent work demonstrates that dyadic neurofeedback can enhance inter-brain synchrony during interaction, whether its effects extend beyond the trained dyad remains unclear. Here, we examined whether dyadic neurofeedback targeting inter-brain synchrony in the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) is associated with changes in empathy-for-pain toward unfamiliar social targets. title: Potential assessment of rooftop photovoltaic in global cities considering economic feasibility
abstract: Rooftop Photovoltaics (RPV) serve as a promising distributed form of clean solar energy utilization, especially in highly dense urban areas. However, the global variation in the economic potential of RPV remains unknown. Here, we integrate the 3D building footprints and electricity demand to assess both the technical and economic potential of RPV at the global scale. The results show that the global technical potential of RPV in urban areas reaches 4048 TWh·yr − 1 , but the economic potential accounts for only 41.8% of the technical potential. title: The Time‐Varying Coding Length Scheme Consensus Control of Multi‐Agent Systems Based on an Adaptive Quantizer
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the consensus problem of multi‐agent systems (MASs) with parameter uncertainties under bandwidth‐limited communication networks. During information transmission, limited bandwidth resources may lead to increased encoding errors, packet losses, and reduced throughput performance. To enhance bandwidth resource utilization, an adaptive quantizer with a time‐varying coding and decoding length scheme is employed to improve coding accuracy. title: EDUCATIONAL EQUITY POLICIES INCLUDING ACCESS TO CURRICULUM AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY FOR UNDERPRIVILEGED GROUPS: COMPARATIVE CASES FROM CHINA, MALAYSIA & THAILAND
abstract: Achieving Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG4) requires bridging the long-standing gaps faced by ethnic minority and underprivileged students in enrollment opportunities, educational quality, recognition and access to the STEAM education curriculum integrating emerging Communication Technology (CT) aiming at developing framework in support of Sustainable Development Education for All (EFA). title: A Dempster-Shafer-Based Expert System for Personalized Higher Education Major Recommendation
abstract: Selecting a study program at a State University (Perguruan Tinggi Negeri/PTN) is a decision that many senior high school students approach without a systematic review of their interest, aptitude, achievement, and career goals, a gap made more pressing by the limited counseling capacity available at most schools. title: The Influence of Motivation, Workload, and Job Stress on the Performance of Employees at the Katibung Inpatient Community Health Center
abstract: Employee performance is crucial for maintaining the quality of healthcare services, particularly in addressing the challenges of work motivation, workload, and work stress. This study aims to analyze the partial and simultaneous influence of these three variables on employee performance at the Katibung Inpatient Community Health Center. The study employed a quantitative approach with a causal associative design. The population consisted of 56 employees, all of whom were sampled through a saturated sampling technique. title: Fast, Long-Range Synchronization Utilizing Emergents: Proof of Concept and Prospective Applications of Emergent Computing
abstract: So far, synchronization tasks designed in complex systems are working at the level of their constituting elements. The proposed pilot study explores synchronization at the level of emergents. The main objective of this research is threefold: (i) to demonstrate that synchronizing emergent structures rise from a continuous interaction of micro-processes that are operating above a constituting matrix (medium) using a simple microevolution rule and a special type of extended neighborhood; (ii) to provide a specific example of a long-range emergent coordination that is generated within a short-rang

title: Dietary polysaccharides as direct substrates for SCFA production: mechanisms and precision prebiotic intervention strategies
abstract: Conventional prebiotics lack the structural specificity to direct colonic fermentation toward defined outputs. Dietary polysaccharides (DPs) serve as direct fermentation substrates, and their architecture—monosaccharide composition, glycosidic linkages, molecular weight and branching—determines which short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing taxa can access them. This selectivity is governed by carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) repertoires and cross-feeding networks. title: Estudio paramétrico de un algoritmo genético con redes de Petri
abstract: El problema de programación de tareas tipo job-shop (JSSP) es NP-difícil y requiere métodos aproximados. Este trabajo evalúa un algoritmo genético acoplado a una red de Petri temporizada adaptativa, empleada como evaluador exacto del makespan. Mediante un estudio paramétrico factorial completo 3×3 se combinaron tres tamaños de población (50, 75 y 100) y tres umbrales de reinicio por estancamiento (10, 15 y 20), sobre 18 instancias estándar de dimensión 10×10, con diez corridas independientes por configuración (1620 corridas). abstract: Self-compacting concrete (SCC) containing Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag (GGBS) and reinforced with recycled polyethylene terephthalate (RPET) fibres is subjected to repeated flexural loading in this paper, and the experimental results are presented. The investigation is quantitative, decision and considers the effect of combined of concrete grade, fibre dosage and cyclic stress condition on fatigue performance. title: Modeling lowland‐adapted irrigated wheat profitability and economic feasibility in Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Improving wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) productivity in Ethiopia's lowland areas through efficient irrigation is critical for enhancing food security for smallholder farmers. This study aims to use the Farm Analysis Tool to evaluate the farm‐level economic viability of lowland‐adapted irrigated wheat in Ethiopia by integrating yield response and profitability across various irrigation levels and validating the results against midland/highland conditions over 2 years. title: Modern determination of pion and kaon fragmentation functions from single-inclusive electron-positron annihilation and high-precision COMPASS SIDIS multiplicities
abstract: We present a combined determination of charged-pion and charged-kaon fragmentation functions (FFs), denoted HAPS-PiFF1.0 and HAPS-KaFF1.0, at next-to-leading order (NLO) and within a next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) perturbative QCD setup. title: Molecular design of ion-selective polymer membranes for electrochemical water purification and resource recovery
abstract: Ion-selective membranes enable electrochemical water purification and resource recovery. Effective molecular design must balance preferential target-ion uptake, rapid transport, and limited water crossover under changing feed and electrical conditions. This review examines how fixed charge, hydration, pathway connectivity, and ion-specific interactions govern transport in charged polymers, microporous materials, recognition membranes, selective surface layers, and covalent organic frameworks. title: The MegaWave Radio Surveyor
abstract: Several Decadal-level questions in astrophysics, exoplanets, astrobiology, and cosmology can be addressed only at low radio frequencies inaccessible from Earth. The MegaWave Radio Surveyor would open this largely-unexplored region of the electromagnetic spectrum with a space-based interferometer to (1)~Track the space weather of other stars; (2)~Detect magnetically-generated emission from exoplanets to probe their interiors and assess magnetic shielding of their atmospheres; (3)~Probe the Universe's evolution during the Dark Ages via the highly-redshifted HI hyperfine line; and (4)~Assess the

title: Inteligencia Artificial, Cultura Visual y Memoria histórica: El caso del Palacio de Justicia (1985)
abstract: Este artículo analiza la reconfiguración de la memoria histórica de la Toma y Retoma del Palacio de Justicia a partir de la circulación de imágenes restauradas o generadas mediante inteligencia artificial. Desde la cultura visual, la investigación narrativa y la ética informativa, se examina cómo estas visualidades tensionan las nociones de verdad, autenticidad y documento histórico. journal: SOCIAL REVIEW International Social Sciences Review / Revista Internacional de Ciencias Sociales

title: Valorization of tea waste: Composition, extraction technologies, and sustainable applications across agriculture, industry, and biotechnology
abstract: Amid growing global interest in sustainable resource management, tea ( Camellia sinensis ), the second most consumed beverage after water, generates substantial biomass waste throughout cultivation, processing, distribution, and consumption. A significant portion of this waste is still managed through conventional practices such as composting, incineration, or landfilling, which limits its potential value recovery and may increase operational and environmental burdens across the supply chain. title: A 1 km gridded dataset of Northern Hemisphere permafrost active layer thickness (2000–2024)
abstract: Active layer thickness (ALT) is a key indicator of permafrost change, with important implications for soil hydrothermal conditions, carbon feedbacks, ecosystem processes, and cold-region infrastructure. However, hemispheric-scale ALT mapping remains challenging because field observations are sparse and unevenly distributed, while thaw depth is controlled by complex and nonlinear environmental interactions. title: Multiscale climate vulnerability assessment in São Paulo state for climate adaptation planning
abstract: Climate change poses significant challenges to densely populated and economically dynamic regions. This study presents an integrated assessment of climate vulnerability across municipalities in São Paulo State, Brazil, combining climatic indicators, socio-environmental conditions, public health data, and institutional capacity variables. Using multivariate statistical techniques and spatial analysis, a Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) was developed to identify patterns of exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. title: Participatory conceptual mapping with guardrailed large language models: An audit-ready DAPSI(W)R(M) workflow from workshop transcripts to scenario testing
abstract: Participatory conceptual mapping is widely used in sustainability research to represent stakeholders’ knowledge, concerns, and perceptions of causal relationships within complex social-ecological systems. Yet translating workshop dialogue into reliable, auditable causal maps is labor-intensive and prone to interpretive drift. We present a four-step workflow combining guardrailed large language model (LLM) assistance with human oversight to transform workshop transcripts into DAPSI(W)R(M)-consistent conceptual maps, feedback structures, and qualitative scenarios. title: Fault Interaction Analysis in Manufacturing Process With Extended FMEA Model by Using Cloud Model Theory and DEMATEL: A Novel Approach for Risk Assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT Failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA) is widely used in numerous manufacturing processes to identify and minimize various problems; nevertheless, its usefulness is dubious until it is more directly associated with the resolution of complex issues. In addition, the disruptions experienced in the production process are interrelated and cannot be considered independent of each other. title: On sampling methods for inverse biharmonic scattering problems in supported plates
abstract: Abstract We study the inverse problem of qualitatively recovering a supported cavity in a thin elastic plate governed by the flexural (biharmonic) wave equation, using far-field pattern measurements. We derive a reciprocity principle and a factorization of the farfield operator for the supported plate boundary conditions, and we analyze its range properties to justify both the linear sampling method (LSM) and the direct sampling method (DSM). title: A PCA-based composite drought index integrating meteorological and vegetation indicators in the North-Eastern Dry Zone of Karnataka, India
abstract: Abstract Drought is a recurring climatic hazard in the North-Eastern Dry Zone (NEDZ) of Karnataka, affecting agriculture and water-resource availability. This study analysed the spatio-temporal variability of drought and wet conditions during 2000–2024 using daily meteorological observations from KSNDMC and IMD and MODIS MOD13Q1 vegetation data. title: Farm practice typologies as a strategy for management-relevant land use and land cover mapping in the Great Lakes Region
abstract: Abstract The Great Lakes region (GLR) is dominated by agricultural land use, characterized by diverse land use and land cover (LULC), land management practices (LMPs), and, in turn, diverse land processes. Conventional LULC classification systems often rely on coarse categorizations, summarized into spatial units that are either unmeaningful to management or lack the fidelity to capture human-driven heterogeneity relevant to environmental outcomes. title: Distribution and Interactions of Soil Nutrients and Organic Carbon at University of Calabar Campus, Nigeria
abstract: Plant biodiversity depends fundamentally on soil nutrient availability. However, nutrient dynamics within university campuses remain poorly studied, and less attention has been given to soil health, plant biodiversity, and the ecosystem services supported by campus soils. This study evaluated the influence of soil depth on the distribution, relationships, and multivariate interactions of soil nutrients and organic carbon across the University of Calabar campus, Nigeria. title: Characteristics, Source Apportionment, and Ecological and Human Health Risk Assessment of Heavy Metals in Cultivated Soils from the Jiamusi Section of the Lower Songhua River
abstract: The Jiamusi section of the lower Songhua River is an important commodity grain production area in China, and the environmental quality of its cultivated soils is directly linked to regional food security and ecosystem stability. To clarify the status of heavy metal pollution in soils in this area, identify pollution sources, and assess potential risks, this study established sampling units in typical cultivated land in the Jiamusi section in 2023, collected 276 topsoil samples (0-20 cm), and determined the contents of eight heavy metals, namely As, Cd, Cr, Cu, Hg, Ni, Pb, and Zn, as well as ph

abstract: Foreland thrust belts commonly host vertically stacked gas accumulations in multiple stratigraphic intervals, yet the charging chronology, source relationships, and three-dimensional accumulation processes of deep and shallow gases remain difficult to constrain precisely. The Wuqia structural belt in the southwestern Tarim Basin contains deep Carboniferous–Permian carbonate gas reservoirs and shallow Cretaceous Kezilesu Group clastic gas reservoirs, providing a representative setting for investigating multistage gas charging and three-dimensional accumulation. title: Characterizing the post-marketing safety profile of duvelisib: a comprehensive pharmacovigilance analysis of the FDA adverse event reporting system
abstract: Introduction Duvelisib, a dual phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)-δ/γ inhibitor, is used for relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), but serious safety concerns warrant continued post-marketing surveillance. Methods We analyzed the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from the third quarter of 2018 through the second quarter of 2026. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines steady three‐dimensional rotational stagnation‐point flow of an incompressible micropolar fluid over a biaxially stretching or shrinking surface. The energy model combines Cattaneo–Christov heat conduction with thermal radiation and viscous and microrotational dissipation. title: Reimplante tardio de incisivos centrais superiores avulsionados em adolescentes: uma revisão de escopo e relato comparativo de dois casos
abstract: Background: Dental avulsion is an emergency; its prognosis depends on the dry extraoral time, the storage medium, and the condition of the periodontal tissues. Delayed reimplantation carries a risk of ankylosis and root resorption. Purpose: To describe the evidence regarding the management and outcomes of delayed reimplantation of permanent maxillary central incisors, and to present two clinical cases involving adolescents.
