title: Enhancement of plant photosynthesis by seaweed extracts under optimal and abiotic stress conditions: physiological and molecular mechanisms
abstract: Global climate change is intensifying abiotic stress in crops, posing a serious threat to agricultural productivity and global food security. In this context, seaweed extracts (SWEs) have emerged as key sustainable biostimulants to optimize plant performance. This review critically examines recent scientific evidence on the physiological, biochemical, and molecular mechanisms by which SWEs enhance photosynthesis under both optimal growth conditions and environmental stress scenarios (drought, salinity, and extreme temperatures). abstract: Structural and practical parameter non-identifiability issues are common when mathematical models are used to interpret data. Such issues motivate model reparameterisation and reduction methods. Here, we consider Invariant Image Reparameterisation (IIR), which asks when symbolic reparameterisation conditions can be replaced by numerical derivative calculations at a single reference point. abstract: Purpose – This study analyzes how ritual-based religious counseling operates within the Jama'ah Tabligh as a da'wah (Islamic propagation) management strategy, read through the Islamic Guidance and Counseling (IGC) approach, and identifies the forms of spiritual transformation that its members experience. title: Climate‐Driven Distribution Modeling of the Glacial Apollo Butterfly ( Parnassius glacialis ) for Biodiversity Conservation
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how climate change affects insect distribution is critical for biodiversity conservation, particularly in the case of range‐restricted and ecologically sensitive species. The glacial Apollo, Parnassius glacialis (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae), is a high‐altitude butterfly of notable scientific and esthetic value, yet its ecological response to climate change remains poorly understood. title: The Relationship between Local and Scientific Knowledge in the Management of Semurup Hot Spring Tourism: An Epistemological and Environmental Ethics Study
abstract: Although local and scientific knowledge have received considerable attention in environmental studies, their epistemological relationship and ethical implications for managing Semurup Hot Springs Tourism in Kerinci Regency, Jambi, remain insufficiently examined. This study analyzed the relationship between these forms of knowledge and its implications for environmental ethics and sustainable tourism management. title: Policy Integration in the Federal Governance of Food Security in Mexico
abstract: ABSTRACT This article analyzes the degree of public policy integration in the federal governance of food security in Mexico. Drawing on the policy integration framework proposed by Candel and Biesbroek, the study examines four key dimensions: (1) policy frame, (2) subsystem involvement, (3) policy goals, and (4) policy instruments. title: Upcycling: A conceptual process model and perspectives of undergraduate students pursuing fashion design in a Kenyan university
abstract: The global fashion industry generates substantial quantities of textile waste. Much of the Global North’s discarded clothing is exported to African countries, including Kenya, where it is often disposed of in landfills, water bodies, or incinerators, worsening pollution and climate change. Upcycling offers a sustainable solution, transforming this waste into higher-value products. abstract: El desarrollo de interfaces cerebro-computadora, sistemas de inteligencia artificial capaces de inferir estados mentales y técnicas de estimulación neural ha desplazado la tutela de la persona hacia un ámbito que el constitucionalismo clásico apenas pudo anticipar: la actividad cerebral como soporte de la identidad, la autonomía y la libertad. abstract: This study analysed the effect of Climate Change on Agricultural Output in Nigeria. title: Taxonomic revision of the genus Trachelophora Perroud, 1855 (Cerambycidae, Lamiinae, Homonoeini), with the description of a new species
abstract: A taxonomic revision of the genus Trachelophora Perroud, 1855 is presented. Trachelophora woroae sp. nov . is described from Sulawesi, Indonesia. A revised diagnosis of Trachelophora is provided, the previous misidentification of T. lineata Aurivillius, 1923 is clarified, and an updated identification key and distribution data for all known species are presented.

title: Detection of zoonotic Cryptosporidium parvum in invasive beavers from southern Tierra del Fuego, Chile
abstract: Since their introduction to Tierra del Fuego in 1946, invasive beavers ( Castor canadensis ) have expanded their population and caused extensive environmental degradation across the sub-Antarctic region. Beaver dams have profoundly impacted peatlands, mature sub-Antarctic forests, and watercourses. Here, we report a pathogen in invasive beavers in Patagonia and discuss their potential role as a reservoir of waterborne zoonotic pathogens. title: Integrating Principal Component Analysis With Discharge‐source Monitoring for Assessing Water Quality of Dong Nai River, Vietnam
abstract: ABSTRACT This study systematically evaluates how major pollution sources affect Dong Nai River water quality by integrating principal component analysis (PCA) with monitoring data from 128 discharge points representing industrial parks, healthcare facilities, livestock operations, residential‐urban areas, and other production sectors. abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal differentiation of hydrological connectivity and its driving factors is essential for the management and sustainable use of soil and water resources in basins. However, the interactive effects of multiple natural and anthropogenic drivers on hydrological connectivity and their spatial heterogeneity remain poorly understood. The Dongjiang River Basin, comprising 256 sub-basins categorized into four topographic types, was selected as the study area. abstract: Critical illness disrupts microbial communities through antimicrobial exposure, altered nutrient supply, tissue injury, and loss of anatomical barriers. title: Solid Waste Disposal and Urban Flooding in Swali, Yenagoa Local Government Area, Bayelsa State, Nigeria
abstract: Solid waste disposal and urban flooding are increasingly occurring simultaneously in many Nigerian cities. This study examined the relationship between solid waste disposal practices and urban flooding in Swali, Yenagoa Local Government Area, Bayelsa State. A descriptive survey design was used. A structured four-point Likert questionnaire was administered to 320 household heads, and 300 copies were correctly filled and returned. abstract: Malayness is often understood as an identity associated with ethnicity, language, Islam, adat, and cultural heritage. While MPPT and reverse current protection have been widely studied, they are often implemented separately, increasing circuit complexity and cost. abstract: Contemporary global crises increasingly intersect, creating complex and mutually reinforcing threats to socioeconomic stability, human security, and sustainable development. abstract: Environmental impact assessment (EIA) is an essential instrument for anticipating and mitigating the ecological effects of development projects before they are authorized. abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how policy regulation and external innovation environment jointly influence manufacturing firms' adoption of emerging technologies and subsequent operational performance. Drawing on institutional theory and the resource‐based view, we analyse survey data from 451 Chinese manufacturing firms using structural equation modelling. abstract: Subsurface drainage provides an outlet for excess water and leached salts in salt-affected cropland, but its benefits for crop production are not always straightforward. abstract: Flooding can disturb interconnected components and processes of urban social-ecological systems. This study maps and analyses the industrial landscape of the JS-SEZ, focusing on the spatial distribution of industrial parks, data centre infrastructure, and the development of Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) Sedenak. title: From Coop to Market: Transforming Poultry Enterprise Skills into Sustainable Microenterprises through Capability Development in Urban Poor Communities
abstract: This study uses the resource-based view and human capital theory to examine the effects of the “Poultry Enterprise Skills: From Coop to Market” training on the livelihood and business performance of the marginalized sector of Barangay 176-C, Bagong Silang, Caloocan City. This study reconstructs the Poultry Enterprise Skills Training (PEST), Enterprise Capability Development (ECD), and Livelihood and Business Performance (LBP) constructs, focusing on the role of enterprise capability as a mediating factor. title: Sample Pretreatment and Green Analysis of Organic Compounds in Sediments in Contact with Surface Water: A Review
abstract: Sediments that are exposed to surface water might take up organic contaminants from natural sources and humans, thus bringing about environmental pollution and creating a risk to human health. Hence, this gives enough reason to indicate the need for conducting proper analysis of pollutants. The literature on sediment pre-treatment, extraction of contaminants, cleaning, concentration, and instrumental analysis is covered in the review. title: Betel‐Quid Exposure and Site‐Specific Prognostic Patterns in Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Betel-quid chewing is a risk factor for oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC), but its associations with tumour subsite and depth-of-invasion (DOI) related prognosis remain unclear. We examined site-specific associations and exposure-stratified DOI thresholds for disease-specific survival (DSS). METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 454 patients from southern Thailand. title: Climate‐Driven UV‐B Variability Across the Indo‐Gangetic Plains Alters Grain Traits, Nutrient Sequestration, and Flour Functionality of Tropical Pearl Millet Cultivars
abstract: Summary statement This study unravels how enhanced UV‐B modulates cultivar‐specific adaptive and metabolic responses in pearl millet grain quality. By integrating these multifaceted responses, we propose a mechanistic model for understanding the role of this critical, potent stressor in affecting crop grain quality in view of climate‐changing environments.

abstract: Background Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) has reported anti-atherosclerotic effects and may alter the gut microbiota, but its relationship to the microbial choline–trimethylamine (TMA)–trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) axis remains unclear. Methods In this exploratory pilot, twelve male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to Control, 1% choline (Model), or 1% choline plus AS-IV (40 mg/kg/day) groups (n = 4 each) for 28 days. abstract: The study investigates the impact of Global Value Chain (GVC) participation on socio-economic development and environmental quality in African economies. Specifically, it examines how agricultural and industrial activities within these chains influence natural resource consumption and environmental pollution (carbon emissions). While GVC integration offers African nations pathways to technology transfer and export diversification, the environmental costs, such as resource depletion and increased carbon intensity, remain underexplored. title: Leaf spectroscopy detects site-associated functional differentiation in a dominant mangrove species near its northern range margin
abstract: Functional variation within species may be especially important at range margins, yet conventional trait measurements constrain population-level assessments. Leaf reflectance spectroscopy integrates signals associated with pigments, water, chemistry, and structure, potentially revealing functional differentiation. We analyzed leaf spectra from 48 Kandelia obovata trees across a southern reference population (SRP), a natural range-margin population (NRM), and a long-established planted population north of the historical range margin (PNR). title: Structural and functional tuning of carbon-supported NiMo hydrogen evolution reaction electrocatalysts for anion exchange membrane water electrolysis
abstract: s NiMo/C electrocatalyst (EC) can be a promising alternative to scarce and overpriced platinum group metals (PGMs) for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). However, resolving the optimal Ni-to-Mo ratio and understanding how the carbon support helps develop a suitable electrocatalytic architecture remain unclear. title: Zinc-doped carbon catalysts with peroxidase-like activity for Neutral-pH antibacterial applications via reactive oxygen species generation
abstract: Bacterial antibiotic resistance has evolved into a severe global public health threat, creating an urgent demand for non-antibiotic antibacterial strategies. Peroxidase (POD)-like nanozymes that generate bactericidal reactive oxygen species (ROS) from H 2 O 2 hold great promise for infection treatment; however, most carbon-based nanozymes suffer from intrinsically low catalytic activity and strict acidic pH preference, which severely restricts their antibacterial efficacy under physiological neutral microenvironments. title: Building Consensus on Satellite Imagery in Human Rights Investigations across Epistemic Communities: Insights from Journalism and Law
abstract: Abstract Satellite imagery has gained a paramount role in human rights investigations. Once the preserve of state intelligence agencies, the increase of commercially-available satellite imagery in recent years has enabled a broader range of actors to analyze earth observation data as part of their investigations. Investigative journalists were at the forefront of incorporating these techniques, with human rights organizations and international tribunals now utilizing satellite imagery as evidence of atrocity crimes. title: EXPERIMENTAL TEST BENCH FOR INVESTIGATING THE CHARACTERISTICS OF A HYDRAULIC DRIVE WITH AN ANTI-SLIP DEVICE
abstract: The article presents the development and methodological substantiation of a specialized experimental test bench for investigating the characteristics of a hydrostatic drive with an anti-slip control system. The study used hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) modeling methods, stall test (maximum-load test) and transient response test protocols. title: Thickness‐Confined Mo‐VO 2 /CNTs Heterogeneous Composite Films for Synergistic Dynamic Infrared Camouflage and Electromagnetic Protection
abstract: ABSTRACT As a typical phase‐change material for adaptive infrared (IR) camouflage, the development of VO 2 is constrained by its inherent “extreme‐emissivity trap”, with modulation limited to a narrow range of 0.9–0.65, and suffers from intrinsically low free‐electron density that precludes coinstantaneous electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding. title: Percepción de profesores de matemática de educación secundaria sobre juegos no digitales
abstract: One of the major challenges facing mathematics education in secondary education is the lack of student interest. This explains the fundamental role teachers play in classroom management and the implementation of different strategies. [Objective] The objective of this study was to analyze mathematics teachers’ perceptions of the use, effectiveness, and potential difficulties in the implementation of non-digital games in secondary school classrooms (K7-K12). title: Simulation of the impacts of a sensor’s PSF on mixed-pixel unmixing: adjacency and overall effect
abstract: The point spread function (PSF) of optical sensors is a critical source of error in mixed-pixel unmixing, and the statistical characteristics of PSF-induced unmixing errors remain poorly understood. Characterizing these statistical behaviours can clarify the underlying mechanisms through which the PSF affects unmixing procedures and provide a theoretical foundation for developing high-precision models for correcting PSF-induced errors. abstract: Abstract Intermittent aeration drives partial nitritation-anammox (PN-A) systems, yet how microbiomes regulate aerobic and anaerobic respiration during rapid, oxygen-limited redox shifts remains poorly understood. Here, we applied genome-resolved metatranscriptomics to evaluate transcriptional dynamics in a long-term PN-A bioreactor treating low concentrations of ammonium. title: The Synergistic Antibacterial Activity of Curcumin and Quercetin Against Nocardia seriolae and Evaluate Their Therapeutic Effects in the Infected Largemouth Bass
abstract: ABSTRACT Nocardia seriolae is an important bacterial pathogen causing chronic granulomatous disease in cultured fish, and effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. This study aimed to identify natural compounds with synergistic antibacterial activity against N. seriolae and evaluate their protective effects in largemouth bass ( Micropterus salmoides ). A structure‐guided screening strategy targeting N. seriolae isocitrate lyase (ICL) was performed using molecular docking, ADMET prediction, and in vitro antibacterial assays. title: Coordination-engineered layered double hydroxides for photocatalytic energy utilization and environmental remediation
abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are a versatile class of lamellar coordination materials, consisting of edge-sharing metal hydroxide layers and interlayer anions, whose tunable metal-ligand environments empower precise regulation of their structural, electronic, and surface properties. These characteristics render LDHs promising materials for contaminant mitigation and sustainable energy conversion. title: Container Throughput across Eastern Mediterranean Ports: National Renewable Integration, Carbon-Price-Weighted Trade Exposure, and Logistics Infrastructure, 2005-2023

title: Geochemical characteristics of granitoids suggest a subduction origin for the Singhbhum Craton
abstract: New geochemical results are integrated with existing Paleo- to Mesoarchean igneous and detrital datasets to develop a crust-mantle evolution model for the Singhbhum Craton, India. title: Historical trade-route connectivity predicts the flavour map of world cuisines
abstract: Did two thousand years of Silk Road exchange make the world’s cuisines more or less alike? We construct a cross-cultural flavour network with 104,770 recipes and 1507 ingredients, in which cuisine is treated as measurable intangible cultural heritage (ICH). Connectivity along 18 historical trade routes predicts flavour similarity among 20 modern, English-language national-cuisine corpora (partial Mantel r = 0.479 controlling for geography, p = 2.0 × 10⁻⁴), and the geographic gradient is better explained by historical connectivity than by distance. title: Cyber Sovereignty: National Security in the Digital Age
abstract: In an era of increasingly sophisticated cyber threats, cyber sovereignty has become the latest fad as states seek to assert control over their digital domains. This paper explores how each of these leading nations is navigating the complex landscape of cyber sovereignty to safeguard national security, including China, Russia, the United States, and the European Union. abstract: Introduction China’s policy framework calls for integrated protection of cultivated land quantity, quality, and ecological functions, but how this objective is reflected in subnational compensation rules remains unclear. Methods From 650 initial records, this study constructed a two-tier corpus of 155 legal and policy documents: 108 dedicated compensation documents and 47 containing embedded provisions. title: Dynamical analysis and optimal control of a novel fractional-order compartmental model for phone addiction
abstract: This paper formulates and compares a new fractional-order mathematical model of the transmission dynamics and behavioral development of mobile phone addiction across distinct user subpopulations. The model is developed in the context of fractional derivatives. The population is categorized into susceptible population, three classes with addiction-intensity levels, a treatment population, and a recovered population. title: Infestation Dynamics and Quantitative Impact of the Seed Borer, Trachylepidia fructicassiella (Lepidoptera: Pyralidae), on Cassia fistula Pods
abstract: The lepidopteron seed borer, Trachylepidia fructicassiella, is a pest that causes severe damage to the pods of the golden shower (Cassia fistula L.) and several other forest trees. The caterpillars burrow into the pods, devouring the seeds and pulp, which later impairs seed viability. Molecular characterization and phylogenetic studies of the caterpillars have confirmed that the specimens collected from infested C. fistula pods in this study were T. fructicassiella. title: Land use dynamics and hydro-climatic variability to hydrological responses in Tawa River Basin, central India
abstract: Quantifying hydrological responses of river basins to combined hydro-climatic variability and land use/land cover (LULC) change (1999–2019) is fundamental to sustainable water resource management in regions experiencing intensifying anthropogenic pressures. This study investigates how climatic variability and land-use dynamics drive hydrological change in the Tawa River Basin, a strategically important tributary of the Narmada River in central India, whose hydrological behaviour underpins regional agricultural productivity, ecosystem functioning, and water supply security. title: La liquidación del siniestro en el reaseguro a la luz de los Principles of Reinsurance Contract Law (PRICL): riesgo decisorio y gobernanza contractual
abstract: La liquidación del siniestro constituye uno de los ámbitos más relevantes y, al mismo tiempo, menos sistematizados del contrato de reaseguro desde el punto de vista jurídico. title: An Evaluation of Gaziantep Nature Park Based on a Content Analysis of TripAdvisor Visitor Reviews
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the visitor reviews of Gaziantep Wildlife Park, Turkey’s largest and the world’s fourth-largest wildlife park, posted on TripAdvisor, through content analysis. To this end, reviews regarding the wildlife park on TripAdvisor were examined and evaluated using the MAXQDA 2018 qualitative data analysis software. The study population consists of 164 visitors who visited Gaziantep Wildlife Park and posted reviews on TripAdvisor. The study examined Turkish online reviews. title: Dual-role catalyst: Influence of multi-nonmetal incorporation in Bi2WO6 for comparative photocatalytic water purification and electrocatalytic oxygen evolution
abstract: Sustainable energy generation and environmental remediation heavily depend on the development of highly efficient noble metal-free catalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and advanced photocatalysts for the degradation of contaminants. In this study, we synthesized sulfur-doped, boron-doped, and sulfur–boron co-doped Bi 2 WO 6 via a hydrothermal process to compare dual functional performance. title: Concurrent Strong Winds and Heavy Precipitation Contributed to the Early 2010s Mortality Pulse of Korean Fir (Abies koreana)
abstract: Abstract Although climate-induced physiological stress is often considered the primary driver of high-elevation conifer forest decline, mortality pulses implicate episodic physical disturbances. We investigated the early 2010s mortality pulse of Korean fir ( Abies koreana ) using 16 years of tagged-stem monitoring data (2005–2021) on Jirisan Mountain, alongside meteorological records. title: Divine and Human Matters of Ireland: Messianic Allegory in James Joyce's Ulysses
abstract: The present article examines James Joyce’s Ulysses through the entwined lenses of messianic allegory, Benjaminian historical theory, and postcolonial critique. Departing from the conventional understanding of allegory as a system of stable symbolic correspondences, the article proposes a model of ‘messianic allegorical disruption’: a mode of figuration in which the ruins of history accumulate without resolution, salvation is perpetually deferred and meaning is produced not through closure but through interruption. title: Transdisciplinary Ecosystem Thinking for World Water Security Amidst the Climate Crisis
The Hidden Cost of Forest Loss: Soil Mercury Stocks Across Contrasting Land Uses in the Amazon, Cerrado, and Their Transition Zone
abstract: The effects of land-use change on soil organic matter (SOM) and mercury (Hg) dynamics across tropical biomes and ecotonal transitions remain poorly understood. We evaluated how the conversion of native vegetation to cropland and pasture influences SOM quality, soil fertility, and Hg dynamics in the Amazon, Cerrado, and Cerrado-Amazon Ecotone. Soil samples were collected to a depth of 1 m under forest, cropland, and pasture systems. title: Bridging science and sustainability by empowering the next generation of African researchers under the African Planet Prize
abstract: The African Planet Prize (APP) was launched in 2025 as a collaboration between the African Academy of Sciences (AAS) and the Frontiers Research Foundation (FRF), conceived as an African-facing extension of the global Frontiers Planet Prize. The initiative recognises and supports early-career African researchers whose work addresses planetary boundary science, including climate instability, biodiversity loss, freshwater scarcity, and land degradation. title: Effect of Computer-Based Concept-Mapping on Interest in Genetics among Low-Achieving Students’ in Colleges of Education, North-West, Nigeria
abstract: Genetics is an important component of biology education; however, low-achieving students often exhibit low interest in learning genetic concepts. This study investigated the effect of computer-based concept-mapping on interest in genetics among low-achieving students in Colleges of Education in North-West Nigeria. The study adopted a pretest-posttest quasi-experimental control group design. title: Nonlinear backstepping control with GWO-based global MPPT for grid-connected photovoltaic systems under partial shading conditions
abstract: Under partial shading conditions (PSCs), grid-connected PV systems exhibit multiple LMPPs, which can cause conventional MPPT methods such as P&O to converge to a local optimum instead of the GMPP, resulting in power losses. To overcome this limitation, this work proposes a hybrid Grey Wolf Optimization–Backstepping Control (GWO-BSC) strategy for reliable and accurate GMPP tracking in a two-stage three-phase grid-connected PV system. title: Live imaging of largemouth bass virus dissemination in zebrafish
abstract: Introduction Understanding how viruses infect and spread within a living host is an attractive yet formidable goal. However, our understanding of these processes relies primarily on in vitro imaging studies conducted in cell culture models. Methods Here, we developed a zebrafish model of Largemouth bass virus (LMBV) infection, enabling for the first time real-time tracing of iridovirus spread in vivo . title: Robust Funnel Control for Vehicle Lateral Tracking Without Road Curvature Information
abstract: ABSTRACT This article addresses the challenge of autonomous vehicle control on curved roads by developing a funnel‐based control framework, in which vehicle motion is decomposed into longitudinal and lateral subsystems using the Frenet frame. A funnel‐based lateral controller is designed to constrain the lateral tracking error within prescribed time‐varying boundaries. abstract: Whether large-scale clean-energy infrastructure can alleviate the trade-off between economic growth and environmental degradation is central to environmental regulation under China's dual-carbon goals. This study examines the relationship between ultra-high voltage (UHV) transmission access and corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance using firm-year observations of Chinese A-share listed companies with valid Sino-Securities ESG ratings from 2009 to 2022. title: High-pyrolysis-temperature acidified straw biochar improves soil hydrological functioning and increases maize yield in saline soils
abstract: Biochar contributes to the restoration of soil fertility and crop productivity in saline-affected farmlands. Soil hydrological functioning is a key indicator for assessing the degradation and rehabilitation of saline soils. However, the mechanisms by which acid-modified maize straw biochar produced at different pyrolysis temperatures regulates the hydrological properties of saline soils remain unclear. abstract: Buchaa bandh and its 4 km buffer zone in Purulia has been selected as study area to show the impact of urban heat island included water scarcity and its impact. The study aims 1) To assess the changes in LULC between 2020 and 2025, and examine their relationship with UHI. 2) To identify and delineate heat exposed areas based on spatial distribution of UHI intensity. 3) To identify areas affected by water scarcity and examine its impact on livelihood. title: Evapotranspiration From a Mountain Peatland: Potential Impact of Diminishing Snow Cover on Water Yield
abstract: ABSTRACT Peatlands store large volumes of water, playing an important role in catchment hydrology, and thus regional water cycles. Water from peatlands is released both as streamflow and via evapotranspiration (ET) to the atmosphere. ET is linked to snow cover through recharge and water availability; however, the direct impact of snow cover on ET has received little research attention. We hypothesised that snow cover has the potential to influence rates of ET from a mountain peatland. abstract: The article examines the role of public administration as a key determinant of national resilience in the context of a rapidly changing geopolitical environment. The analysis focuses on contemporary security challenges such as armed conflicts, hybrid threats, cyber risks, energy insecurity, and disinformation campaigns. A conceptual framework is developed, linking public administration capacity with national resilience and security. title: Micro- and nanoplastics and fecal microbiota transplantation: a conceptual framework linking gut dysbiosis and intestinal barrier dysfunction
abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) is increasingly recognized as a promising therapeutic option for microbiota-related disorders. Its efficacy may be affected by factors related to both donor microbiota and the recipient’s intestinal barrier. Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs), emerging environmental contaminants, have been recognized for their detrimental impacts on intestinal health. abstract: Alpine-cold wetland ecosystems are highly sensitive to human disturbance, yet the responses and relationships of soil–plant systems to anthropogenic disturbance remain poorly understood. Taking the Napahai alpine-cold wetland in north-western Yunnan as the study area, this research assessed the responses of soil and plant systems to different disturbance types and explored the potential relationships among soil properties, microbial indicators, and vegetation characteristics. abstract: Building the bridge pier foundation for the Bratislava motorway bypass in Slovakia required the construction of a cofferdam in the Danube River. During construction, a local failure occurred, and its cause had to be investigated. In addition to significant cracks on the inner surface of the cofferdam, one of the struts tore away from the sheet pile wall. abstract: Abstract Alarm calls enable animals to warn conspecifics of imminent threats and coordinate collective responses. abstract: La incorporación de los resultados de aprendizaje en la educación superior colombiana ha hecho más exigente la coherencia entre el currículo, la evaluación y el aseguramiento de la calidad. abstract: China is one of the countries most severely affected by flood disasters. Long-term and systematic flood impact data are essential for flood risk assessment, flood impact model calibration, disaster prevention and reduction. However, an open, long-term, China-focused event-scale database with detailed flood disaster impact indicators remains lacking. abstract: The collapse of the Assad regime has opened both opportunities and profound challenges for peacebuilding in Syria. abstract: The modernization of school education in Central Asia has placed innovative learning technologies at the center of national education policy, yet evidence on how such technologies perform in ordinary classrooms remains scarce. abstract: Background Hypospadias is one of the most common congenital malformations in boys, with rising incidence worldwide. Environmental factors, including endocrine disruptors, are suspected to play a role. abstract: It is important for developing safe and effective materials for wastewater disinfection to reduce the hazard posed by waterborne pathogens. title: Improving nitrogen and phosphorus use efficiency in agriculture: a critical review of management practices
abstract: Introduction Nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) are major nutrients in agricultural production worldwide, but only about half of applied nutrients are recovered, contributing to financial losses, soil degradation, and nutrient pollution. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified the effects of management practices on nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and phosphorus use efficiency (PUE), with particular attention to smallholder farming systems in Zimbabwe, especially granitic sandveld soils and fertility gradients between homefields and outfields. abstract: Background: Between 2021 and 2022, China's health system reforms deployed two overlapping cost-containment instruments in quick succession: diagnosis-related group (DRG) bundled payment and a nationalized volume-based procurement (VBP) programme that cut orthopedic implant prices by 70%−90%. abstract: Introduction Volatile organic compounds (VOC), especially isoprene oxidation products such as methacrolein (MACR), contribute significantly to tropospheric ozone and secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation. abstract: Background and Aim: In many education systems, science classrooms have traditionally followed a transmission model in which teachers explain content and students listen, copy notes, and memorise facts for tests. abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and intensified human activities, grassland soil wind erosion has emerged as a prominent issue threatening ecological security. abstract: ABSTRACT Unsaturated hydrofluorocarbons (HFOs) have become a potential environmentally friendly replacement for chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) due to their shorter lifespans, zero ozone‐depletion potentials (ODPs), and low global warming potentials (GWPs). abstract: Abstract Background Bacterial L-asparaginases are key therapeutics for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but their clinical efficacy is limited by off-target L-glutaminase co-activity, which contributes to severe side effects. abstract: Palaeoseismological databases are important for reconstructing long-term seismic activity in regions where historical and instrumental records of large earthquakes are limited. We present SwissPaleodatabase 2.0, an updated compilation of published geological, geomorphological, archaeological and historical observations with potential paleoseismological relevance from Switzerland and surrounding Alpine regions. abstract: La satisfacción académica se usa con frecuencia como indicador de calidad en la educación superior, pero en México su estudio generalmente se limita al uso de la estadística descriptiva. Ese enfoque oculta la heterogeneidad real entre estudiantes. abstract: Postharvest loss of perishable fruits and vegetables is a significant challenge which can be mitigated by processing them into shelf stable products. This study investigated the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) on consumption as well as drivers for consumer demand of selected raw and processed fruits and vegetables among low-income consumers and retailers in Kenya. abstract: Freshwater ecosystem degradation creates an urgent need for entrepreneurial solutions that combine ecological restoration with economically viable business models. abstract: ABSTRACT This study develops a context‐sensitive analytical framework for understanding tensions encountered when hotels implement green practices in a developing‐economy destination. abstract: ABSTRACT Cork oak forests are of significant environmental and socioeconomic importance in the Mediterranean basin. Among these, Phytophthora species, particularly P. cinnamomi , remain among the primary drivers of decline. abstract: Introduction Seasonal variation in plant activity and soil processes can influence soil silicon (Si) cycling, but the season-dependent warming responses of operationally defined reactive soil silicon fractions remain poorly understood. abstract: ABSTRACT Effective management of severe hemorrhages and chronic diabetic wounds requires navigating a contradictory fluidic challenge: efficiently clearing hazardous exudates and pathogens without depleting critical regenerative factors. title: Lo extraño frente a la normatividad algorítmica. Estéticas de lo liminal y xenoimágenes
abstract: In just two years of democratization of generative tools, the same volume of images has been produced as in the one hundred and fifty years of photography. The aesthetic and content-based agency of these images consolidates the normal: each one ratifies the dominant patterns of its training archive, thereby homogenizing the collective imaginary. title: National benchmarking of operational energy and carbon performance in England's NHS estate: determinants and net zero trajectories
abstract: England's National Health Service (NHS) has committed to net zero by 2040 for the emissions it controls directly, but its national totals cannot show whether reductions come from the estate, a cleaner electricity grid, changes in reporting coverage or milder weather. This study uses the mandatory Estates Returns Information Collection (ERIC) to separate these drivers and test whether trusts are on track for 2040. abstract: The CRISPR-Cas systems have been traditionally viewed as adaptive immune mechanisms; however, increasing evidence indicates that they also perform broader regulatory functions. abstract: BACKGROUND: Human echinococcosis remains a major zoonosis in Xizang, China, where marked climatic, topographic and landscape gradients may be associated with spatial variation in disease prevalence. abstract: Scholars have proposed the adoption of a contemporary global taboo against bats to prevent the outbreak of diseases to which humans are susceptible (zoonotic diseases). abstract: Precision fermentation (PF) offers a flexible method for producing high-value food ingredients, but it generates large volumes of spent media and microbial biomass, which pose environmental and economic challenges. abstract: To effectively mitigate the free-riding phenomenon prevailing in inter-enterprise collaborative carbon emission reduction behavior, this paper establishes an evolutionary game model for cooperative carbon emission reduction based on the spatial public goods game. title: Role of Geospatial Surveying in Enhancing Crop Quality Through Land Assessment and Resource Optimization: A Case Study of Smallholder Farmers in Guduru District
abstract: Agriculture is the cornerstone of Ethiopia’s economy, yet its productivity is constrained by soil degradation, inefficient land management, and uniform application of inputs. These challenges are acute in Guduru District of the Horro Guduru Wallaga Zone, where smallholder farmers depend on traditional methods that do not account for spatial variability in soils, topography, and vegetation. abstract: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone mass, microarchitectural deterioration, and increased fracture risk. However, long-term use of current pharmacological therapies is often associated with adverse effects, underscoring the urgent need for safer and more sustainable intervention strategies. abstract: The shoot and fruit borer, Earias vittella (Fabricius), is an important pest of okra, and its occurrence may vary considerably across contrasting agro-climatic environments. abstract: Abstract Shape memory polymers are a distinct category of intelligent materials that can change their configuration in response to external stimuli, such as moisture, light, or temperature. 4-dimensional (4D) printing offers the advantages of 3-dimensional printing and shape-memory capability. abstract: The objective of this study was to develop and evaluate a hybrid smart-bin system integrating solar power, ozone disinfection, and Internet of Things (IoT)-based monitoring to improve urban waste management at the source. abstract: The desert mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus crooki) is distributed throughout the southern United States and northern Mexico. As a large herbivore, this subspecies plays a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance. While its distribution is closely linked to water availability and vegetation type, climate change is increasingly altering these factors and shifting potential habitats. abstract: Egg production is a critical economic indicator in the Australian poultry industry, particularly for Ross breeder broilers. abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exposed a fundamental weakness in global diagnostic preparedness. Although BDBV had been recognized for nearly two decades and diagnostic tools existed, gaps across the diagnostic ecosystem delayed outbreak recognition and response. abstract: Introduction The inefficient and spatially uneven allocation of healthcare resources remains a major public health governance challenge in China. title: "Bats Are There, But Who Will Protect Them?": Community and Institutional Perspectives on Cave-Dwelling Bat Conservation
abstract: Cave-dwelling bats face escalating anthropogenic pressures globally, yet their conservation is frequently compromised by limited community ecological literacy, persistent cultural myths, and inadequate integration of community and institutional perspectives into management. This study investigated community perceptions, staff knowledge, and short-term observations of bat activity at Sudwala Caves, Mpumalanga Province, South Africa, to inform evidence-based conservation strategies. title: Individual elephants, not populations: a practical approach to managing human–elephant interactions in a plantation landscape in southern India
abstract: India holds nearly 60% of the world’s wild Asian elephants, and much of their range is shared with people; negative human–elephant interactions (HEIs) cause approximately 500 human deaths in India each year. Forest department staff and local residents have knowledge of specific individual elephants that are tolerant of people, but this knowledge is rarely used systematically in management. abstract: Abstract The emission of pollutants from human activities in industrial zones poses significant challenges to air quality and soil health, particularly in semi-arid environments. Utilizing 56 sampling stations and geostatistical modeling, this study conducted a comprehensive, multi-pathway assessment of lead (Pb) dynamics in the ambient air and surface soil of the Salafchegan Special Economic Zone (SSEZ) in Iran. title: Value Orientations, Product-Specific Considerations, and Conditional Consumer Acceptance of Refrigerators Containing Recycled Materials in Poland
abstract: Abstract The transition toward a circular economy requires not only technological and regulatory changes but also consumer acceptance of products incorporating recycled materials. While previous research has extensively examined pro-environmental consumption, comparatively less attention has been paid to high-involvement durable goods, where purchase decisions are infrequent and involve substantial financial and functional considerations. abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the protective efficacy of castor ( Ricinus communis L.), neem ( Azadirachta indica A. Juss.), and physic nut ( Jatropha curcas L.) oils at concentrations of 0, 10, 20, 30, and 40% against the phytopathogen Lasiodiplodia laeliocattleyae (Sibilia) A. Alves. title: Disruption of the programmed cell death nexus: potential roles of microplastics and nanoplastics in tumorigenesis
abstract: As global plastic pollution continues to intensify, microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) have become widely distributed in air, water, the food chain, and even the human body, constituting a novel environmental exposure that is difficult to avoid. Although there is still insufficient evidence to classify MPs/NPs as established human carcinogens, a growing body of research suggests that they may participate in tumor initiation and progression through multiple pathways, including the intrinsic toxicity of the particles themselves, pollutant carrier effects, and microenvironmental remodeling.

abstract: ABSTRACT Many biosensor-based and automated bioaerosol monitoring systems report relative signal changes, making it difficult to relate their outputs to standardized concentration units. To address this limitation, we developed an automated, IoT-integrated fungal bioaerosol monitoring system (FABMS) that estimates airborne fungal burden as a culture-referenced CFU/m 3 -equivalent value in near-real time. abstract: Abstract This study explored the oat cultivar PD 2 LV 65 as a native source of dietary fiber (DF) and optimized its extraction using response surface methodology. A three‐factor three‐level design assessed the impact of time (10, 20, and 30 min), temperature (20°C, 30°C, and 40°C), and amplitude (60%, 70%, and 80%) on the extraction efficacy. abstract: Abstract This study employed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to systematically investigate the microscopic friction mechanisms of a sealing pair consisting of diamond-like carbon (DLC) coated plungers and nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) under oil-lubricated conditions. abstract: Kinematic rigs provide a structured interface for articulating 3D meshes but lack any associated pose space , i.e., an explicit representation of the plausible manifold of joint configurations for a given mesh. Without such a pose space, stochastic sampling or manual manipulation of raw rig parameters easily results in semantic and/or geometric violations, such as anatomical hyperextension and non-physical self-intersections. title: Late Triassic Dipnoi from south Gondwana, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
abstract: Mesozoic lungfishes are often represented in the fossil record by isolated tooth plates, which impose limitations on their taxonomic identification and on the interpretation of their diversity. In the Triassic of South America, these organisms remain poorly documented. The present study describes eight isolated tooth plates from the Candelária Sequence of the Santa Maria Supersequence (Carnian, Late Triassic), southern Brazil, being attributed to three taxa: Ptychoceratodus phillipsi , P. eliseui sp. nov., and Ferganoceratodus cabreirai sp. nov. title: Factoring gendered risks of military operations into revisions of the AP Commentary
abstract: Abstract The International Committee of the Red Cross’s upcoming revisions to its 1987 Commentary on the Additional Protocols to the 1949 Geneva Conventions provide an opportunity to reconsider the scope, meaning and application of Article 76 of Additional Protocol I (AP I), on “Protection of Women”, in military operations. Article 76 could provide a sound basis for factoring the gendered risks of international armed conflicts into differentiated protections for women consistent with the formal equality with men that is secured for them in international humanitarian law. title: Gastruloids reveal alternative morphogenetic routes for body-axis elongation with distinct cytoskeletal dependencies
abstract: Morphogenesis requires cells to integrate genetic and environmental information to pattern and shape tissues. Recent studies in vivo and in vitro have shown how alterations in environmental cues can induce alternative morphogenetic programs. However, what determines which morphogenetic strategy cells deploy in different environments remains unknown. title: Phenological characterization and thermal requirements of prominent cultivars of litchi in the Indo-Gangetic Plain
abstract: Aim: Litchi (Litchi chinensis Sonn.) exhibits marked phenological variability among cultivars, which influences productivity and climate adaptability. This study aimed to characterize and compare the phenological behavior of ‘Shahi’ and ‘China’ using the extended BBCH (Biologische Bundesanstalt, Bundessortenamt and Chemische Industrie) scale and to examine the influence of thermal indices on phenophase progression. title: Bridging data gaps in risk assessments of endangered plants: The role of reproductive strategies and pollinator traits
abstract: Abstract Risk assessments for pesticides (or plant protection products) for species listed under the United States Endangered Species Act (ESA) are often hindered by limited data on the biology of many species, particularly for plant species. We investigate the integration of publicly available plant and pollinator trait data to enhance ESA risk assessments, with an emphasis on the potential indirect effects to plants that may result from insecticide use affecting pollination. abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Resolution of the topological branching patterns, the timing of demographic events and the effective population size changes associated with major demographic events. abstract: Introducción: El edentulismo es la pérdida total o parcial de los dientes naturales. abstract: Phylogenetic analysis of the nucleotide sequences of the cytochrome oxidase I gene of specimens of Albanycada Villet, 1989 supported the hypothesis that the genus includes more than one species-level lineage. title: Urban greenspace exposure and inequality are associated with mortality in cities across multiple countries
abstract: Abstract Background Urban greenspace is recognized as a key component of healthy cities, yet evidence linking greenspace to mortality remains geographically fragmented, while the association between unequal greenspace distribution and mortality remains poorly understood. We aim to examine associations of greenspace exposure and inequality with all-cause, cardiovascular, and respiratory mortality across cities in multiple countries. abstract: El objetivo del artículo fue analizar los fundamentos y las condiciones de pertinencia para crear un centro universitario tecnológico en Asunción, orientado al desarrollo económico y social regional, con referencia temporal en octubre de 2026. title: Resource Productivity in the European Union: An Empirical Assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT The objective of this study is to analyze the factors influencing resource productivity in the European Union region from a sustainable development perspective using spatial analysis methods. In this way, the feasibility of implementing circular economy principles to enhance resource productivity among European Union countries was assessed. title: The association between dietary protein intake and mental disorders in older adults: a scoping review
abstract: Background Mental disorders are increasingly prevalent among older adults, significantly affecting their quality of life and overall wellbeing. Recent evidence suggests that dietary factors, particularly protein intake, may play a role in mental health outcomes. However, the association between dietary protein intake and mental disorders in older adults remains underexplored. This scoping review aims to examine the relationship between dietary protein intake and mental disorders among older adults. abstract: Greenwashing has become a critical issue in corporate sustainability implementation; however, research on the impact of financial distress on greenwashing remains limited and yields inconsistent results. abstract: Deteriorating food quality and stress-ridden professional commitments have severely affected the health quality and physical efficacy, making it mandatory to monitor the food quality for cautiously limiting the intake of processed eatables. With exposure to debilitating environmental toxins remaining unabated, regular checkups have emerged as essential for adopting timely cautions. abstract: Ammonia is a promising carbon-free fuel for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), since nickel-based anodes can crack it internally without a separate reformer. Direct-ammonia operation, however, compromises durability through nickel nitriding and coarsening. abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) can convert captured CO2 and renewable electricity into fuels and chemical feedstocks, but selective C-C coupling to C 2+ products remains a central challenge. abstract: ABSTRACT Gold (Au) nanocatalysts are promising for visible‐light‐driven environmental remediation, yet constructing highly active, stable Au catalysts for liquid‐phase pollutant degradation remains challenging. abstract: Studying day-to-day corruption raises hurdles for qualitative teams that cut across methodological, emotional, and ethical domains. title: An Analytical Investigation of the Energy Performance of Double-Skin Façade Systems in a Mild-Humid Climate: The Trabzon Case
abstract: This study quantifies the effect of Double-Skin Façade (DSF) systems on building energy performance and indoor thermal comfort under temperate-humid, diffuse-radiation climatic conditions, using Trabzon, Turkey, as a case study. title: MARKETING CAPABILITIES AND TOURIST SATISFACTION IN MALAYSIA’S HALAL TOURISM SMES: SERVICE QUALITY AS MEDIATOR
abstract: The halal tourism industry has emerged as one of the fastest-growing segments of the global tourism economy, driven by the rising number and expanding purchasing power of Muslim travellers worldwide. Malaysia, consistently ranked among the leading halal tourism destinations, positions small and medium enterprises (SMEs) as the operational backbone of this sector, delivering the food, accommodation, transportation, and retail services that shape the Muslim tourist experience. abstract: Background: Continuing professional development (CPD) is expected to maintain competence as technology, regulation, service models and patient expectations change. abstract: ABSTRACT Jane Knight's definition of knowledge diplomacy is deliberately generic, designed to apply across diverse geopolitical contexts and sectors. Knight's framework identifies reciprocity and mutuality as core values, and her subsequent reflection highlights an important risk: ‘Social washing,’ in which partnerships adopt the language of shared commitment while falling short in practice. abstract: Rock masses inherently contain numerous fractures ranging from micro- to macro-scale. When excavating caverns within rock masses, these fractures become active. title: Comparative Case Study of Production Efficiency, Financial Performance, and Business Risk in Laying Hen Farms with Different Housing Systems and Management Conditions
abstract: The laying hen sector continues to expand in response to increasing demand for animal protein; however, productivity remains sensitive to environmental conditions, particularly temperature fluctuations that affect production stability. The housing system represents a key management factor influencing farm performance. This study aims to compare production efficiency, financial performance, and business risk between closed-house and open-house laying hen systems. abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome is a critical innate immune sensor detecting diverse pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs/DAMPs). Its activation triggers the maturation and release of the proinflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18, as well as pyroptotic cell death. abstract: Las tecnologías digitales transforman la economía, pero no existe una respuesta uniforme sobre cómo patentarlas. Las oficinas de patentes siguen criterios distintos para evaluar las invenciones implementadas por computador (IIC), lo que incide directamente en la seguridad jurídica, la estrategia empresarial y la protección transnacional de la innovación. abstract: Background Sepsis-induced Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) represents a catastrophic breakdown of systemic homeostasis, where uncontrolled pulmonary inflammation is inextricably linked to gastrointestinal (GI) dysfunction via the “gut-lung axis.” Current management lacks interventions capable of simultaneously modulating systemic inflammation and restoring GI function. title: Sustainable biosorptive recovery of Mn2+ from low grade manganese ore leachate using NaOH activated Artocarpus heterophyllus seed derived biosorbent
abstract: Sustainable recovery of manganese from low-grade ores requires efficient and environmentally compatible approaches for treating ore-derived leachates. This study investigates Mn 2+ recovery from an actual manganese-rich pregnant leach solution (PLS) using NaOH-activated Artocarpus heterophyllus Lam. seed biomass (NaOH – Ah SB), an agro-waste-derived biosorbent. title: Controversy: Anticoagulants need to be maintained after catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation in patients at risk of stroke—Pro and Contra
abstract: The pillars of atrial fibrillation (AF) management include stroke prevention, patient-centred symptom directed decisions on rhythm or rate control, and the proactive management of comorbidities and lifestyle changes. These pillars are not in isolation; they are complementary to each other. While oral anticoagulants (OACs) are highly effective for reducing stroke and all-cause mortality in patients with AF, these drugs confer a risk of major bleeding, including intracranial bleeding. title: Assessment of trace metals in irrigation water, soil, and vegetables along the US-Mexico border and their health risks
abstract: The Rio Grande, an important river that borders the USA and Mexico is recharged with untreated and treated wastewaters from binational sources and therefore is known to contain potentially toxic elements (PTEs) like As, Cd, Co, Cr, Pb, and Sb. These elements are nonbiodegradable and can accumulate in soil and crops when contaminated surface water is used for irrigation. abstract: The industrial application of Polymer Inclusion Membranes (PIMs) for pharmaceutical wastewater remediation is often limited by the extraction–stripping trade-off and carrier-mediated transport kinetics. abstract: ABSTRACT Tensegrity structures, which combine rigidity and flexibility, can overcome the limitations of rigid robots in challenging terrains and the slow locomotion speed of soft robots. abstract: Objetivo: Se analizó el diseño de un sistema de control industrial basado en un controlador lógico programable (PLC) para automatizar el arranque y fortalecer la protección de motores eléctricos trifásicos, considerando su importancia para mejorar la seguridad y la continuidad operativa en entornos industriales. abstract: The genus Tanacetum L., is one of the cosmopolitan members of the tribe Anthemideae (Asteraceae), encompassing approximately 160 species. abstract: Abstract Approximately half of veterans with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) experience suicidal ideation (SI), and many report intimate relationship problems. Historically, there has been hesitation to engage veterans with SI in PTSD treatment for fear that trauma‐focused interventions could potentially exacerbate SI. abstract: Abstract Nanoparticle-cell interactions often determine the safety and efficacy of nanomedicines. title: Tumor location in the pancreatic body/tail as an independent risk factor for early recurrence after curative resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Background Early recurrence after radical resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a primary cause of poor prognosis. Published definitions of early recurrence use postoperative cutoff points ranging from 6 to 12 months. This study aimed to analyze perioperative clinicopathological features associated with early recurrence after PDAC surgery, with particular focus on the impact of tumor location, to facilitate individualized treatment decisions. title: Traditional Medicine Use and Pharmacist Involvement Among Patients with Diabetes and Hypertension in Semarang, Indonesia: A Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Patients with diabetes or hypertension often take traditional medicine alongside prescribed drugs, yet little is known about how they involve pharmacists in that use. This descriptive cross-sectional study enrolled 110 adult users of traditional medicine, recruited by purposive sampling at a community health centre and a private clinic in Semarang, Indonesia, and surveyed them with a structured questionnaire. Their mean age was 59.5 ± 10.3 years, 77.3% were women and 73.6% had diabetes. Ginger (40.9%), turmeric (39.1%) and Indonesian bay leaf (34.5%) were the remedies named most often. Pharmac

title: Global-scale meteorological-to-groundwater drought propagation and the drivers and patterns of multi-year groundwater drought
abstract: Groundwater stores a third of all global freshwater and supports water supply, irrigation and ecosystems across the world. As such, groundwater drought can have wide-reaching financial, social and environmental impacts, particularly when drought events are prolonged or multi-year. Although recent work has made significant progress in understanding the drivers and patterns of multi-year meteorological droughts, we do not know how this signal translates into multi-year groundwater drought, where subsurface processes, anthropogenic influences and abstractions can alter the meteorological signal.

title: Sustained Higher Education Expansion and Firms' Productivity: Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the relationship between China's sustained higher education expansion and the productivity of A‐share listed firms from 2004 to 2020. We find that a larger supply of university graduates is associated with significantly higher firm total factor productivity (TFP) on average, a result robust to extensive testing. Mechanism analysis points to three plausible channels: an increased share of skilled labor, strengthened innovation, and accelerated digital transformation. However, the relationship is asymmetric. title: Metal-based nanoparticles against drug-resistant bacteria: mechanisms, applications, and safety
abstract: The accelerating emergence of drug-resistant bacteria demands novel therapeutics beyond conventional antibiotics. Metal-based nanoparticles (NPs) have gained attention as promising alternatives, providing potent and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity owing to their distinctive nanoscale characteristics. title: Drivers of basal respiration rate in intact samples from carbon-rich lowland soils across Denmark
abstract: Soil basal respiration rate (BRR) measured under controlled laboratory conditions is an important indicator of a soil's microbial CO 2 production potential. Although temperature and drainage status are known to control BRR, the relative importance of physical, chemical, and microbial controls remains poorly understood, particularly in organic soils. BRR was measured on intact topsoil samples from 112 carbon-rich lowland soils in Denmark at 15°C at a soil-water matric potential corresponding to field capacity (pF = 2), alongside a range of soil physical, chemical and biological properties. title: Engineering Delivery across Plant Barriers: Nano- and Microtechnologies for Plant Bioengineering
abstract: Abstract Plant bioengineering is moving from proof-of-concept genetic modification toward programmable, spatially controlled, and environmentally responsive intervention in living plants. Yet delivery remains the central bottleneck. Plant tissues impose a nested series of barriers, including the cuticle, stomata, trichomes, cell wall, plasma membrane, apoplast, vascular network, organelle membranes, and rhizosphere microbiome, that restrict the transport and functional deployment of nucleic acids, proteins, sensors, agrochemicals, and living microbes. title: Effects of structure and conduct on the performance of small-scale dairy farmer groups in Kericho and Nakuru counties, Kenya: a panel data study
abstract: Milk productivity among small-scale dairy farmers in Kenya remains below potential despite widespread participation in farmer groups designed to enhance agricultural practices and managerial skills. Persistent output disparities across similarly trained groups suggest that internal organizational dynamics may be influencing performance. This study used a group-level panel dataset covering 2018–2021 to examine how group structure and leadership conduct affect the performance of small-scale dairy farmer groups in Kericho and Nakuru counties. title: Adaptive Compound Fault Diagnosis of Rolling Bearings Under Strong Background Noise: A Hybrid Framework Integrating Improved CEEMDAN With VMD Guided‐MCKD
abstract: ABSTRACT In practical mechanical systems, the measured fault signals of rolling bearings are often submerged by strong background noise, making it difficult to extract compound fault features. To address this issue, this paper proposes a fault signal processing framework that integrates Improved Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (ICEEMDAN), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) guided‐Maximum Correlated Kurtosis Deconvolution (MCKD). title: Recent Development and Applications of Peridynamics to Fatigue Failure Analysis: A Critical Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Peridynamics (PD) provides a nonlocal framework for modeling fatigue damage and evolving cracks without prescribing their final paths. This review examines how mechanical formulations, cyclic constitutive models, and fatigue laws determine PD predictions across crack initiation, propagation, and total life. Applications to variable‐amplitude loading, interacting cracks, heterogeneous materials, and environmental coupling are assessed. title: Prospective assessment of emerging circular economy technologies: A case study for sewage sludge-to-biofuel via hydrothermal liquefaction
abstract: This study evaluates the prospective techno-economic and environmental performance of four hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL)-based technological pathways for converting sewage sludge into biofuels at facilities co-located with wastewater treatment plants. Two sewage sludge carbon-accounting cases based on IPCC guidelines are considered: a 100 wt% biogenic carbon case and a case containing 7 wt% fossil carbon in the sewage sludge stream. title: The ESPA model as a strategic framework for sustainable human resource management in seasonal hospitality
abstract: This study aims to conceptualize and empirically examine the ESPA Model (Environment–Support–Performance–Appreciation) as a strategic framework for sustainable human resource management (SHRM) in seasonal luxury hospitality. Employing a positivist epistemological stance and a quantitative, cross-sectional explanatory design, data were collected via structured surveys from 312 employees across five-star seasonal hotels in Crete, Greece. title: Capítulo 9. Adobe Premiere Pro
abstract: Este capítulo presenta un flujo de edición no lineal con Adobe Premiere Pro que conecta la organización de los materiales con la construcción del relato audiovisual. Explica la configuración de proyectos y secuencias, la función de los principales paneles y la clasificación de recursos mediante contenedores. La selección de tomas y el montaje inicial se plantean como decisiones narrativas que preceden al ajuste del ritmo, la continuidad y las transiciones. title: β-glucosidase-mediated hydrolysis of Ophiocordyceps polysaccharides enhances antioxidant and immunomodulatory activities and ameliorates intestinal barrier function to maintain gut homeostasis
abstract: Polysaccharides derived from Ophiocordyceps (Chinese Cordyceps) exhibit notable bioactivities, yet their high molecular weight may limit their fermentability by the gut microbiota, thereby modulating the production of bioactive metabolites. This study aimed to prepare low-molecular-weight Ophiocordyceps polysaccharides (OPs) through enzymatic modification and to elucidate the associated structural alterations and mechanisms underlying intestinal barrier regulation. title: Successional dynamics and driving factors of soil multitrophic communities along coal mine reclamation chronosequences in Shanxi, China
abstract: Introduction The recovery of multi-trophic soil communities is pivotal to ecological restoration of reclaimed coal mining areas, yet their succession and the driving mechanisms of soil multifunctionality (SMF) across regional gradients remain poorly understood. Methods We investigated three reclaimed coal mining areas in Shanxi Province, China-Pingshuo (north), Gujiao (central), and Qinshui (south)-using a 25-year chronosequence of Pinus tabuliformis plantations ( n = 75). title: In vitro anticancer activity against HCT-116 cells and in vivo anti-inflammatory efficacy of mannose-laden exopolysaccharide from probiotic Pediococcus pentosaceus 4412
abstract: Introduction Exopolysaccharides (EPSs) are complex carbohydrate structures that play an incredible role in immunomodulation and mitigating inflammatory factors. This study examines the anticancer and anti-inflammatory activities of EPS produced by Pediococcus pentosaceus 4412. Methods We performed probiotic assays on isolated P. pentosaceus 4412 and assessed the in vitro antioxidant potential of the extracted EPS-4412. title: Green hydrogen from curtailment: Real data analysis
abstract: As renewable energy capacity has expanded worldwide, curtailment has emerged as a critical issue owing to transmission constraints and mismatches between generation and demand, resulting in significant energy losses. This study assesses the techno-economic potential of green hydrogen production by utilizing real data of curtailed electricity from wind and photovoltaic sources distributed over more than 2000 km and belonging to a single electrical system. title: The impact of population growth on land-use: a system dynamics model for sustainable land-use planning in the Elgon Region of Uganda
abstract: Land-use and land-cover change poses major environmental challenge in regions where population growth increasingly drives encroachment into ecologically sensitive landscapes. This challenge arises from the dynamics of interacting feedbacks among; demographic change, declining household land size, ecosystem degradation, and delayed institutional responses. Previous studies in the context of Uganda, have investigated these factors, either independently or in pairs, but not holistically. title: La integración de la inteligencia artificial en el Espacio de Libertad, Seguridad y Justicia: avances en el ámbito de la cooperación judicial civil
abstract: Este estudio analiza la transformación de la cooperación judicial civil en la Unión Europea a través de la digitalización y la inteligencia artificial. El Reglamento (UE) 2023/2844 instaura el principio de digital por defecto para las comunicaciones transfronterizas, apoyado en la infraestructura e-CODEX y el marco de confianza digital eIDAS 2.0. Pese a estos avances, la lex fori conserva un papel estructural en la articulación del proceso civil digital europeo. title: Treeline ecotones as habitat archipelagos for spiders: A case study from the Alps
abstract: Trees surrounded by low–stature alpine vegetation may function as habitat islands for canopy fauna. We examined whether diversity patterns of canopy–dwelling specialist spiders in an alpine treeline ecotone in the French Alps aligned with predictions of island biogeography. We focused on the lower canopy of pine (evergreen) and larch (deciduous) trees, collecting data in Spring, Summer and Autumn. title: Dual Hydrogen Donor‐Mediated Reduction of Nitroarenes Over a Magnetically Recoverable CoFe 2 O 4 @GO Nanocomposite: Mechanistic and Kinetic Insights
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing high‐performance and sustainable catalytic systems for reduction of nitroaromatics remains an important objective in both environmental remediation and synthetic chemistry. We report herein a CoFe 2 O 4 @GO catalytic system synthesized using co‐precipitation method as a magnetically recoverable heterogeneous catalytic system for the selective reduction of nitroarenes into corresponding amines using sodium borohydride and hydrazine hydrate as reducing agents. title: Morocco’s Energy Mix in the Context of Global Climate Change: A Socioeconomic Perspective
abstract: As global climate challenges intensify, the transition toward low-carbon energy systems has become a central pillar of national sustainability strategies. Morocco, with limited fossil fuel resources and growing energy demand, has embarked on an ambitious energy transition aimed at enhancing energy security, promoting renewable energy, and contributing to global climate mitigation efforts. title: Development and validation of an optimized spiking strategy for cross‐layer transfer of near‐infrared soil organic matter models
abstract: Abstract Soil organic matter (SOM) is crucial for soil fertility and is strongly linked to soil productivity. The heterogeneity of soil at different depths leads to variations in spectral characteristics. This study addresses the challenge of using near‐infrared (NIR) spectroscopy to estimate SOM across heterogeneous soil profiles. Analyzing spectral data from soil cores (≈150 cm), samples were categorized into surface (0–30 cm), subsurface (>30 cm), and complete profile datasets. title: Identification of patterns of intra-varietal variation and selection of promising clonal forms of local and introduced grape varieties
abstract: The object of research is the variability and clonal forms within populations of local and introduced grape varieties, analyzing their morphometric and biometric traits. The research material consisted of local and introduced grape varieties cultivated in the Absheron collection vineyard of the Research Institute of Viticulture and Winemaking (Baku, Azerbaijan). A significant challenge lies in the insufficient understanding of the intra-varietal genetic and phenotypic diversity of local and introduced grape varieties, as well as the clonal variations that have emerged within their populations.

title: Beyond electricity generation: Nuclear power plants as circular chemical manufacturing hubs for plastic waste valorization
abstract: Abstract Large nuclear power plants have traditionally been regarded as facilities dedicated to electricity generation. This study proposes a systems‐level concept in which they function as circular chemical manufacturing hubs integrating plastic waste valorization, hydrogen production, carbon utilization, and downstream polymer synthesis within a unified industrial complex. title: Windthrow of Forest Trees and Its Effect on Tree Regeneration and Diversity of Understory in the Hyrcanian Temperate Upland Forests of Iran
abstract: Windthrow is a major natural disturbance shaping canopy dynamics in temperate forests, yet high-elevation (upland) Hyrcanian forests remain poorly studied, particularly with respect to regeneration responses and topographic controls. This study examined windfall effects in Dashte Daman forests, northern Iran (1027–1629 m elevation). abstract: Background The biomedical industry is one of three priority industries for development in Shanghai. However, the contradiction of ‘conducting research and development (R&D) in Shanghai, while technology transfer flows elsewhere’ is increasingly apparent. Although Shanghai has a high concentration of R&D institutions, innovative talent, and capital, much of its R&D is industrialized in the surrounding Yangtze River Delta and beyond. abstract: Abstract Soil-related properties associated with potato yield and quality are implicitly linked to soil water storage (SWS) determined by soil texture (ST). title: Virulence and antimicrobial resistance in hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae: molecular mechanisms and emerging therapeutic strategies
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is a ubiquitous opportunistic pathogen distributed across diverse environments, ranging from natural ecosystems to clinical settings. It has emerged as a major global health threat due to the rapid spread of multidrug-resistant lineages through horizontal gene transfer. MDR K. pneumoniae is associated with both community and hospital-acquired infections with substantial morbidity and mortality. abstract: This study presents a unified mathematical model for the triple-stratified Darcy-Forchheimer flow of a micropolar nanofluid containing gyrotactic microorganisms over a porous vertical stretching sheet by simultaneously incorporating thermal radiation, viscous dissipation, activation energy, Brownian motion, thermophoresis, mixed convection, and porous medium effects. title: Mutual scaffolding: The convergence of smart city and blue-green-grey infrastructure discourses
abstract: Smart-city and blue-green-grey infrastructure (BGGI) scholarship emerged from distinct intellectual traditions—one centered on digital technologies and urban management, the other on ecological planning and nature-based infrastructure—yet a growing body of work now operates at their intersection. This paper presents a qualitative content analysis of the literature operating within the smart-city–BGGI overlap, using a systematic mapping approach, with documented searches of Web of Science, Scopus, EBSCOhost and Google Scholar, reported according to PRISMA 2020. title: Business Intelligence: Material básico: Maestría tecnológica en desarrollo e innovación digital en inteligencia de negocios
abstract: En un contexto empresarial caracterizado por la creciente generación de información, la aceleración tecnológica y la necesidad de responder oportunamente a las exigencias de los mercados, la inteligencia de negocios (Business Intelligence, BI) se ha consolidado como un componente estratégico para la gestión organizacional. abstract: El objetivo fue analizar críticamente la contribución de las tecnologías digitales a la calidad educativa escolar. Se realizó una revisión narrativa estructurada en Scopus, delimitada a artículos en español del área de Ciencias Sociales publicados entre 2022 y 2026. abstract: The Late Miocene fossil record of large viverrids is sparse, limiting understanding of their origin, early evolution, and dispersal. title: Antidiabetic potential of cocoa bean shell extract (Theobroma Cacao L.): phytochemical profile, Α-glucosidase inhibition and ex vivo GLP-1 secretion
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) affects approximately 537 million adults worldwide, demanding therapeutic strategies that mitigate postprandial hyperglycemia. This study investigated the antidiabetic potential of the aqueous extract of cocoa bean shell (AECB), an agro-industrial by-product, through phytochemical characterization and biological assays of enzymatic and incretin modulation. abstract: In practical applications, compressible particle-laden flows in moving geometries involve complex, non-linear, and multi-scale interactions with turbulent structures.
