title: Can integrated legal and administrative governance reduce corporate carbon emissions?
abstract: Traditional environmental governance often relies on a single regulatory form, necessitating the exploration of more comprehensive integrated governance models. Utilizing the pilot program of procuratorial public interest litigation in China as a quasi-natural experiment, this study investigates the impact of integrated legal and administrative governance on corporate carbon emissions and the underlying mechanisms. abstract: To investigate the potential use of Ginsenoside Rg1 as an adjuvant for the H9N2 avian influenza vaccine, the study examined Rg1’s immunomodulatory effects on an inactivated H9N2 vaccine. A total of 150 one-day-old non-immunized Arbor Acres (AA) chickens were randomly assigned to three groups ( n = 50 each): one receiving the H9N2 inactivated vaccine, another receiving Rg1 alongside the vaccine, and a control group treated with PBS. title: Immune microenvironmental regulation of odontogenic differentiation in dental pulp stem cells: mechanisms, signaling networks, and regenerative strategies
abstract: Dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) are a promising cell source for dentin regeneration, but their regenerative behavior is strongly shaped by the local immune microenvironment. This review integrates evidence on immune mediators, immune cell–DPSC interactions, intracellular signaling, and immunomodulatory biomaterials. Particular attention is given to how mediator concentration and exposure duration influence the balance between inflammatory injury and differentiation-associated responses. title: Selection for Targeted Therapy Resistance Indirectly Selects for Cancer Cells with Enhanced Phenotypic Plasticity and Evolvability to Orthogonal Stressors
abstract: Resistance to targeted therapies is frequently associated with stem-like features and partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Understanding whether these programs directly drive resistance or instead reflect increased phenotypic plasticity is needed to guide strategies for overcoming resistance. Here, we found that resistance to ALK inhibitors (ALKi) in non-small cell lung cancer was associated with increased phenotypic plasticity, reflected in enhanced adaptability to orthogonal stressors and increased metastatic potential, without intrinsic cross-resistance in short-term assays.

title: The northernmost blind beauty rediscovered: The identity and cryptic diversity of the troglobiotic millipede Typhloiulus polypodus (Loksa, 1960) (Diplopoda, Julidae) from caves of the Western Carpathians
abstract: European blind forms of millipedes in the family Julidae constitute a taxonomically diverse ecological group of mostly cavernicolous species inhabiting primarily the Balkan Peninsula. Their northernmost endemic populations are confined to a few caves in two neighbouring karst areas in the Western Carpathians of Central Europe. title: Mindfulness‐Based Intervention Improves Cognitive Function in Patients With Schizophrenia in Remitted: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with schizophrenia exhibit deficits in facial emotion recognition (FER), attention, P300, and quality of life (QoL), which severely hinder functional recovery. abstract: Female fitness depends on reproductive pace and offspring survival, both of which are determined by the ability to balance resource allocation between current and future reproduction. abstract: Lipids have garnered attention for their importance in pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals. Famously, oleaginous filamentous fungi produce essential fatty acids. abstract: Third-party libraries are essential in software development as they prevent the need for developers to recreate existing functionalities. However, vulnerabilities within these libraries pose significant risks to dependent projects. Upgrading dependencies is infeasible when no patched version is available or when downstream projects have strict version constraints. abstract: Understanding regional warming dynamics is critical for assessing climate-related risks in agriculturally intensive regions. This study evaluated historical and future temperature variability, temperature transitions and warming trajectories across five agroclimatic zones of Punjab, India, using India Meteorological Department (IMD) temperature data (1951–2024) and bias-corrected CMIP6 EC-Earth3 projections (2025–2100) under SSP1: 2.6, SSP2: 4.5, SSP3: 7.0, and SSP5: 8.5 scenarios. title: Building an inclusive scientific enterprise: institutional pathways for innovation and equity in Canadian science
abstract: Inclusion and diversity in science are essential to fostering innovation, particularly as the scientific community is increasingly called upon to address global challenges such as climate change, an equitable energy transition, and rising wealth and income inequality. However, the scientific community has come under heightened scrutiny, as shown by declining public trust and persistent gaps in representation and diversity across scientific fields. abstract: ABSTRACT The sustainable life cycle of electronics is one of the major challenges of modern society. Moreover, the manufacturing of conventional electronics significantly impacts the environment due to the extensive consumption of raw materials, energy, and the release of harmful byproducts. In this regard, manufacturing of electronics using eco‐friendly materials through digital printing routes represents a promising and sustainable solution. title: The full spectrum of thyroid late effects following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in pediatrics: insights from a large multicenter cohort
abstract: Introduction Thyroid disorders are among the most prevalent late sequelae of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). While total body irradiation (TBI) is an established risk factor, the toxicity of alkylating agent-based conditioning regimens remains poorly characterized. title: Characterization of flavor profiles and screening of candidate aroma contributors in Gardeniae Fructus oil during processing with GC-IMS coupled with E-nose and multivariate analysis
abstract: Introduction Gardeniae Fructus oil is a natural and healthy oil widely used in various fields, including food, daily chemicals, and medicine. Methods This study combined electronic nose (E-nose) and gas chromatography–ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS) technology to comprehensively analyze dynamic changes in the volatile organic components (VOCs) of Gardeniae Fructus oil at different processing levels. title: Minimum Wage Policy and Innovation Strategy: Evidence from Chinese Industrial Firms
abstract: We examine the impact of the minimum wage policy on firms’ innovation strategies. Using a sample of Chinese industrial firms consisting predominantly of manufacturing firms, we find that upon an increase in the local minimum wage, firms adjust their innovation strategies to focus more on process innovation. title: A fracability evaluation method for low-permeability sandstone-hosted uranium deposits and its application
abstract: Poor injectability and limited recoverability remain key technical challenges restricting the efficient exploitation of low-permeability sandstone-hosted uranium deposits. Hydraulic micro-fracturing is an effective approach for improving permeability, and fracability evaluation provides a critical basis for selecting favorable ore-bearing intervals for fracturing. abstract: ABSTRACT Europium‐based scintillators are attractive for X‐ray imaging because of their high color purity, large Stokes shift, and tunable coordination chemistry. However, the fabrication of large‐area, mechanically compliant scintillation films typically relies on polymer matrices or high‐temperature processing, which inherently dilute the scintillator phase, increase optical scattering, and complicate direct integration with detector backplanes. title: Chemical composition characteristics and potential source areas of PM₂.₅ across different pollution levels in a typical industrial basin city of northern China
abstract: Background PM2.5 pollution persists in industrial basin cities of northern China, yet the evolution of its chemical composition across pollution levels remains unclear. Methods Based on one year (2025) of PM₂.₅ monitoring and chemical composition data for Linfen City in the Fenwei Plain of northern China, this study characterized water-soluble ions and carbonaceous components across five pollution levels and examined a representative heavy-pollution episode, with the aim of clarifying the evolution of PM₂.₅ composition and its exposure relevance in an industrial basin city. title: Climate Risk Exposure and European Banking Sector: A Forward‐Looking Transition Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether banks' financial vulnerability and characteristics predict their future climate‐transition risk exposure. Using the Climate Risk (CRISK) methodology of Jung et al. (2025) for 126 listed European banks over 2007–2024, it shows that financial vulnerability captured by Systemic Risk has weak power to predict climate vulnerability, while significant predictive relationships emerge among smaller, Less Significant Institutions and during financial distress. title: Soil potassium fractions and crop yield as influenced by inorganic fertilisers, crop residues and green manuring under rice-wheat cropping system in calcareous soil
abstract: Soil potassium (K) occurs in multiple fractions, but the effects of integrated nutrient management (INM) on K dynamics remain poorly characterised in calcareous alluvial soils of the middle Indo-Gangetic Plains (IGP). A field experiment was conducted in an ongoing rice–wheat cropping system (RWCS) at Dr Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University (RPCAU), Pusa, Bihar, to evaluate eight nutrient management treatments involving nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (NPK) fertilisation, cereal residue recycling, green manuring and Pusa Decomposer (PD) application on soil K fractions and crop pro

title: Proximity-based accessibility and socio-economic inequality: rethinking redistributive urbanism
abstract: Proximity-based urban planning is often presented as a means of promoting urban equity, yet concerns persist that accessibility improvements may reinforce socio-spatial inequalities and gentrification. Empirical findings on the socio-economic distribution of accessibility are mixed: while some studies associate higher accessibility with socio-economic advantage, others find that disadvantaged populations also reside in highly accessible areas. title: Integrated genomic and transcriptomic analysis reveals the biocontrol and plant growth-promoting mechanisms of Burkholderia gladioli PNB20-1 against peanut southern blight
abstract: Introduction Peanut southern blight, caused by Sclerotium rolfsii , is a devastating soilborne disease that threatens peanut production worldwide. Members of Burkholderia have attracted attention as biocontrol agents owing to their diverse secondary metabolites and plant growth-promoting (PGP) capacity. Methods We isolated B. gladioli PNB20-1 from the disease-healthy junction of peanut plants. title: Morphological variation in five edible Capsicum species from Ecuador
abstract: Morphological characterization provides a fundamental phenotypic basis for documenting, managing, and prioritizing plant genetic resources for subsequent breeding-oriented evaluation. This study characterized 74 edible Capsicum accessions conserved by the Ecuadorian National Institute for Agricultural Research (INIAP), representing C. annuum (n = 4), C. baccatum (n = 23), C. chinense (n = 26), C. frutescens (n = 17), and C. pubescens (n = 4). title: Multi-layered immune regulatory networks in cotton against Verticillium wilt
abstract: Cotton ( Gossypium spp.), a globally important economic crop, is severely threatened by Verticillium wilt caused by Verticillium dahliae ( V. dahliae ). This disease affects more than 40% of cotton fields in China and causes annual economic losses of 2.5-3.1 billion US dollars. Therefore, disease resistance breeding must take into account the inherent fitness trade-offs between disease resistance and fibre yield-quality performance. title: Study design and rationale for the Dog Aging Project Pack: a prospective, long-term, longitudinal, observational study of biological and environmental determinants of healthy aging in US companion dogs
abstract: Companion dogs are a valuable source of translational discovery about the basic biology of aging because of their well-characterized genome, phenotypic variation in lifespan, aging, and disease profiles, and diverse environmental exposures shared with their human owners. The Dog Aging Project (DAP)'s prospective, longitudinal open cohort study was begun in 2019 to investigate the biological and environmental determinants of healthy aging in companion dogs. title: Surface modification of soft materials (polymers and hydrogels) using plasma: Mechanisms, strategies, and emerging applications
abstract: Soft materials such as hydrogels (natural and synthetic), elastomers, and silicone-based polymers commonly suffer from low surface energy, weak interfacial adhesion, and hydrophobic recovery due to surface aging, which restricts their performance in biomedical and functional applications. Plasma-assisted surface modification has emerged as a controllable and solvent-free technique for modifying surface chemistry and topography without changing the bulk properties. title: Vertical treatment efficiency of constructed wetlands: vegetation influence and caffeine removal
abstract: Constructed wetlands are widely implemented as a nature based solution for treating stormwater runoff, relying on the functions of vegetation, substrate and microbiome to remove pollutants. Horizontal subsurface flow constructed wetlands (HSCW) are often planted with macrophytes such as Phragmites australis and Arundo donax, which enhance stormwater treatment through root-zone interactions. However, treatment efficiency within a single wetland unit can vary vertically between the surface and bottom layers. title: Variations and influential factors of the seed oxygen isotope ratios across 42 forest plant species
abstract: Abstract Oxygen isotope ratios ( 18 O/ 16 O, hereafter δ 18 O) of plant tissues are widely used for various purposes, including paleoclimatic reconstruction, identification of the geographical origin of plant-based products, and understanding plant water use. On the other hand, δ 18 O values of seeds have been rarely measured. We measured the δ 18 O values of whole seed testas of 42 forest plant species at a single location to clarify the variation in δ 18 O values of seeds among species and its influential factors for exploring how they can be used. title: Assessing fire intensity and burned area in Portugal: the influence of meteorological variables using copula functions
abstract: Fire activity is intrinsically linked to severe meteorological conditions, which explain most of the interannual variability of burned area (BA). Nonetheless, the effect of weather conditions on fire intensity is less understood. Using copula functions, the relationship between fire intensity and burned area with meteorological conditions in northern and central Portugal was studied. The occurrence of high weekly Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and BA under extreme wind speed and temperature was assessed at four time periods from March to October. journal: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change

title: A bibliometric analysis of climate change and food security research
abstract: Abstract Background Climate change has become a global concern, influencing water resources, food security, public health, and societal progress worldwide. Floods, droughts, and irregular monsoons, as manifestations of climate change, adversely affect crops, farmers' livelihoods, and food security. A bibliometric analysis of climate change and food security (CCFS) research can indicate progress and emerging research directions on adaptation and risk-management practices, supporting farmers, policymakers, and investors in decision-making. title: Male ornaments predict contact and parasite transmission between pairs of guppies, Poecilia reticulata
abstract: Males with higher quality ornaments are often more parasite resistant and should therefore present less transmission risk to conspecifics, but this prediction has never been directly tested. Transmission risk is a product of both behaviour, dictating contact between hosts, and parasite transmissibility, dictating which contacts result in transmission. We tested how male ornament quality shapes both, using pairs of Trinidadian guppies (Poecilia reticulata) in which one was infected with a directly transmitted ectoparasite (Gyrodactylus turnbulli). title: Downregulation of PRDX3 promotes the progression of bradyarrhythmia via inducing ferroptosis and inflammatory macrophage infiltration in cardiac ganglion plexus
abstract: Aim Bradyarrhythmia is a prevalent cardiac disorder often necessitating lifelong pacemaker implantation, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. This study investigated the role of Peroxiredoxin 3 (PRDX3), a mitochondrial antioxidant enzyme, in the pathogenesis of bradyarrhythmia. Methods A rat model of bradyarrhythmia was constructed. title: Mcf-7 Cell Line: A Comprehensive Review on Breast Cancer Research, Mechanisms and Therapeutic Screening
abstract: The MCF-7 cell line is one of the most widely used in vitro models for investigating estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer. Since its establishment, MCF-7 cells have contributed substantially to understanding breast cancer biology, endocrine responsiveness, molecular signaling, cell-cycle regulation, apoptosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, metabolic adaptation, and therapeutic resistance. title: Mitigating Photoinduced Reactive Oxygen Species From TiO 2 and ZnO UV Filters: Materials Design and Evaluation
abstract: ABSTRACT Titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) and zinc oxide (ZnO) are widely used ultraviolet (UV) attenuating materials, but photoexcitation of these semiconductors can generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) through interfacial redox reactions. Their oxidative activity is not an intrinsic constant, but depends on crystal structure, particle size and morphology, surface defects, coatings, aggregation, surrounding matrix, and irradiation conditions. title: Development of a climate-sensitive disease forecasting tool in the Horn of Africa: A multi-stakeholder exploration of priorities in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda
abstract: Extreme climate events impose significant impacts across the Horn of Africa. One way to monitor these is by using novel digital tools to forecast extreme events and climate-sensitive disease outbreaks. However, limited information exists on stakeholder use of such tools. This qualitative study identified key multidisciplinary stakeholders in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda, and conducted a needs assessment and gap analysis. title: The Relationship of Maqasid Al-Syari’ah in Building Sakinah Families in Generation Z
abstract: Social changes driven by digital technology, globalization, and shifting life values have shaped Generation Z into a more open, adaptive, and dynamic group. However, these conditions also challenge the formation of a harmonious family, including low readiness for marriage, rising household conflicts, and weaker commitment to Islamic values. This article analyzes the relevance of maqāṣid al-syarī’ah as a conceptual basis for realizing a sakinah family in Generation Z. title: From Mitochondrial Targeting to Microbial Killing: Twinkle-Derived Peptides as an Emerging Class of Potent AMPs
abstract: Abstract Mitochondrial targeting sequences are short N-terminal peptides that direct proteins to mitochondria. Notably, their amphipathic α-helical architecture closely resembles that of many potent antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This structural convergence reflects the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria and suggests that contemporary mitochondrial targeting sequences may retain latent antimicrobial properties. title: Unravelling the Chemolithoautotrophic Metabolism of the Carboxydotrophic Knallgas Bacterium Hydrogenophaga pseudoflava
abstract: ABSTRACT The sustainable production of chemicals is critical to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and environmental pollution. Gaseous feedstocks from industrial waste streams and waste gasification, including CO, CO 2 and H 2 , represent abundant and underutilized resources for biotechnology. Syngas fermentation has been predominantly studied under anaerobic conditions, whereas aerobic processes may offer advantages for the biosynthesis of energy‐intensive products. title: Influence of Gliricidia sepium living support on rhizosphere bacterial recruitment and fruit metabolomics in black pepper (Piper nigrum)
abstract: The ability of the rhizosphere to recruit beneficial microorganisms is central to the sustainable management of crops. Here, we investigated, through shotgun metagenomic sequencing and mass spectrometry techniques, the microbial composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMRs), and metabolomic profiles of Piper nigrum cultivated under two support systems: living Gliricidia sepium support (SL/RL) and dead wooden support (SD/RD). title: Diet pattern and human grey wolf conflict in Orakzai District, Pakistan
abstract: Introduction The grey wolf ( Canis lupus ) is an important apex predator whose persistence in human-dominated landscapes is increasingly influenced by livestock depredation and negative human perceptions. This study investigated grey wolf diet composition, reported livestock depredation patterns, and community perceptions in Orakzai District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. title: Inteligencia artificial y mediación docente en educación inicial: criterios pedagógicos para el diseño y la valoración de cuentos contextualizados
abstract: La disponibilidad limitada de materiales didácticos en instituciones públicas de educación inicial de Durán y Guayaquil, Zona 8 de Ecuador, plantea la necesidad de diversificar los recursos narrativos mediante alternativas contextualizadas. abstract: There is increasing global interest in developing gluten-free functional foods using composite flours from locally available crops to enhance the agro-economic value of underutilized botanicals in non-wheat-producing countries and to provide gluten-free alternatives for individuals who require or choose gluten-free diets. This study evaluated and genotypically profiled the microbial community associated with three ready-to-eat baked products (bread, biscuits, and cake) prepared from pre-fermented and post-fermented gluten-free composite flours of sweet potato, maize, and pigeon pea. title: When politics meet wheels: How consumer sentiment transmits geopolitical risks to household transport expenditure
abstract: How do geopolitical risk shocks affect household transport consumption, and does consumer sentiment mediate this effect? We examine this question using a SVAR model and Australian data from 2013 to 2025. We identify the direct and indirect effects of geopolitical risk using hypothetical impulse responses that shut down the sentiment channel. title: Temperature as a Key Factor in Cone Initiation of Pinus sibirica: Evidence from a 28-Year Study in Western Siberia
abstract: Siberian stone pine (Pinus sibirica Du Tour) is a long-lived gymnosperm species that dominates the taiga forests, where its successful seeding ensures a balance between forest ecosystems and the sustenance in them of diverse wildlife. Seed cone production is erratic, with exceptionally large cone crops (or mast seeding) occurring once every 3–4 years. As such, it is important to study the factors that cause this periodicity at all successive stages of crop formation, including cone initiation. title: Soft spatial imaginaries as a regional dynamic capability
abstract: Soft spatial imaginaries offer a novel conceptualisation of a regional dynamic capability to adapt to and shape collective action on regional development challenges towards desirable futures. This capability encompasses six dimensions embedded within a time- and region-specific opportunity space: sensing change, seizing opportunities, transforming organisations, boundary organisations, place leadership and continuous activity. abstract: La iluminación audiovisual se aborda como un recurso técnico y expresivo que permite modelar volúmenes, organizar el espacio y construir atmósferas narrativas. title: The power of play in language development: an educational proposal in a case of Landau–Kleffner syndrome
abstract: Landau–Kleffner syndrome (LKS) is a rare epileptic disorder characterized by the loss of receptive and expressive language skills following normotypical development. This study aims to design an educational proposal based on playful strategies to promote language development in a 9-year and 5-month-old child diagnosed with LKS. The research adopts a mixed-methods approach using a single-case study design. title: Taxonomía de la investigación en Salud Pública basada en la complejidad del análisis de datos
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Public health requires operational classifications that organize studies according to the complexity of data analysis, not just by design or purpose. The objective of this paper was to construct a classification of levels of public health research based on the analytical treatment of data using Grounded Theory. title: Economic performance and associated characteristics of gross margin in peri-urban dairy camel farms around Nouakchott, Mauritania
abstract: Camel farming occupies a growing place in the Mauritanian pastoral economy. The profitability of camel milk production, particularly in peri-urban systems around major cities, remains poorly documented, despite the country’s persistent dependence on dairy imports. This study aimed to assess the economic performance of peri-urban dairy camel farms and to identify the technical and socio-economic characteristics associated with their gross margin. title: A predictive multi-agent learning framework for energy-constrained ultra-reliable edge systems under stochastic environments
abstract: Ultra-reliable low-latency systems operating at the network edge are increasingly constrained by stochastic environmental factors, including energy variability, dynamic workloads, and time-varying communication conditions. Existing learning-based resource management approaches predominantly rely on reactive decision-making and assume stable energy availability, limiting their applicability in energy-harvesting edge systems where uncertainty is intrinsic and future conditions critically influence system reliability. title: Bioimaging and comparative genomics for characterization of surface-bacteria isolated from a blood bank facility
abstract: Blood banks represent highly controlled healthcare environments where microbiological surveillance has traditionally focused on Blood products rather than environmental microbial reservoirs. Despite their crucial role in transfusion safety, the ecology of surface-associated microorganisms remains poorly understood. This cross-sectional study characterized culturable bacteria recovered from Blood-bank surfaces. title: An exploratory study of academic experiences of rescued trafficked children in school
abstract: In order to provide access to formal education for all children in the economy, successive governments, non-governmental organisations (NGOs), and public-spirited individuals have contributed in rescuing trafficked children and reintegrate them into the school system. The attempts have been beneficial although, how these children fare academically in school has not received much research attention. title: Could local climate, forest site and stand conditions mitigate the defoliation in European beech stands? – The case of southern Belgium
abstract: Although climate change has been a major factor in the declining health of European beech ( Fagus sylvatica L.) stands since the end of the 20th century, it seems that local site and stand conditions may play a key role within the beech’s climax region by exacerbating or mitigating this phenomenon. In this study, we assessed crown defoliation in 1515 dominant trees distributed across 101 mature beech stands, located along bioclimatic and ecological gradients in the Ardenne region (southern Belgium) during July and August 2022. title: Tracing millennial climate imprints and emergent adaptation in ancient Chinese roof morphology through jiehua paintings
abstract: Whether long-term climate adaptation leaves a measurable imprint on architectural form remains difficult to test because historical proxies are scarce. Chinese jiehua paintings offer a unique archive for this question. Geometric analysis of 111 roof profiles from 48 artworks spanning a millennium provides a quantitative basis for interpreting roof–paleoclimate relationships. title: Migrant Network Opportunities and the Pathways to Social Integration: Evidence From Urban China
abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of migrants into urban society has become a critical challenge in China's transition from land‐based to people‐oriented urbanization. Although migrant networks have been widely discussed as a source of migration‐related social capital, less is known about how the local concentration of co‐origin migrants creates opportunities for network formation and shapes migrants' social integration. title: Sensing Bone-Conducted Speech With Earbuds
abstract: Clear capture of the wearer’s own voice (OV) is essential when using earbuds for mobile communication. However, OV capture remains challenging in noisy environments. Bone-conducted speech, which can be sensed as vibrations of the earbud housing, can be used to improve OV capture. title: Recent advances in chiral organic room‐temperature phosphorescence with circularly polarized luminescence
abstract: Abstract Circularly polarized room‐temperature phosphorescence (CPRTP) materials combine the dual advantages of long‐lived triplet emission and chiral optical response, demonstrating broad application prospects in information security, bioimaging, and flexible optoelectronics. This review outlines recent progress in organic CPRTP materials from molecular chiral design, aggregation modulation, performance tuning and application scenarios. title: Combating Urban Air Pollution in Indonesia: Recent Advances in Electrospun Nanofiber Membranes for High-Efficiency Particulate Matter Capture
abstract: Indonesia faces a severe air pollution crisis, with average PM2.5 concentrations exceeding WHO guidelines by more than sevenfold and contributing to an estimated 13% of annual deaths nationwide. Emerging evidence further links PM2.5 exposure to increased vulnerability to viral infections, including COVID-19 and influenza, compounding the country's public health burden. abstract: Beneficial ownership transparency shapes the quality of the financial intelligence on which anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) measures rely. South Africa's 2022 reforms secured a largely compliant re-rating of Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations 24 and 25 and preceded its removal from the grey list in October 2025, but the effectiveness of the reformed regime remains to be re-tested. title: Conceptualizing carbon accounting disclosure and firm performance under sustainability committee oversight in Malaysian oil and gas industry
abstract: In the era of global warming crisis, companies in high-carbon emission industries like Oil and Gas (O&G) are under growing pressure to improve the transparency of their carbon emissions. In emerging economies such as Malaysia though, Carbon Accounting Disclosure (CAD) is still largely voluntary and non-standardized, and the relationship between CAD and firm performance is still unclear. abstract: We analyze whether the European Union’s Cohesion Policy and its broader regional funds have accelerated the economic convergence of EU regions, using eight funding instruments across 239 NUTS-2 regions of the EU27 over 2014–2024. title: Private lands, public water: distribution and environmental associations of Veredas wetlands in the Cerrado
abstract: Abstract The water crisis demands urgent protection of water-provisioning ecosystems like the Cerrado, the world’s most biodiverse savanna and major agricultural region. Situated on a plateau, it acts as a rainwater collector, feeding rivers and sustaining Brazil’s river systems. Veredas are key Cerrado wetlands formed in flatlands where the water table emerges. abstract: El calcio es un ion fundamental en múltiples procesos fisiológicos, incluyendo la contracción muscular, la transmisión sináptica y la coagulación, siendo su homeostasis esencial en pacientes críticos. La hipocalcemia es frecuente en la unidad de cuidado intensivo (UCI), aunque suele ser asintomática y autolimitada en la mayoría de los casos. abstract: PREMISE: Due to greater cell and nucleic acid nutrient requirements, polyploids have been hypothesized to be more constrained than related diploids in terms of cell synthesis and biomass accumulation when soil nutrients are limited. abstract: The synthesis of high-purity lepidocrocite-type titanate nanotubes from natural ilmenite minerals remains challenging due to the presence of iron impurities and the limited understanding of their structural stability during thermal treatment. abstract: Background Sleep disturbances are well documented following large-scale disasters; however, less is known about insomnia severity among individuals living with anticipated seismic threat before a major earthquake occurs. abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Polyploids are widely expected to be more frequent at high latitudes, where polyploid vigour may confer advantages under stressful or highly seasonal climates. abstract: Background Out-of-pocket payments remain the primary source of healthcare financing in many low- and middle-income countries, frequently resulting in catastrophic and impoverishing expenditures. Neurosurgical care is particularly costly due to substantial direct and indirect expenses borne by patients and caregivers, typically with little or no financial protection. This study quantifies these OOP costs, estimates the prevalence of catastrophic and impoverishing health expenditures, and examines their socioeconomic impact to inform equitable surgical financing policies. title: Wild Edible Plants as Underutilized Agro-Biodiversity in Albania: Traditional Knowledge, Use, Among the Adolescents
abstract: Wild edible plants (WEPs) are an important but underutilized component of agro-biodiversity, providing nutrient-dense food, raw materials, and cultural value, yet across the Mediterranean and the Balkans the traditional knowledge that underpins their use is eroding as rural lifeways change. abstract: Background The homeodomain transcription factor Engrailed-1 (EN1) is best known for its roles in developmental patterning and the maintenance of neuronal integrity. Recent studies indicate that EN1 can be reactivated under pathological stress, where it contributes to fibroblast state transitions, fibrotic remodeling, and selected cancer phenotypes. title: Physical activity as a psychosocial strategy for promoting mental health in vulnerable youth
abstract: Adolescence is a critical developmental window during which mental health disorders often emerge, yet a substantial proportion of young people-particularly those from socially and economically marginalized backgrounds-face significant barriers to accessing traditional mental health services. Structured physical activity and sport-based interventions have been proposed as a low-cost, non-stigmatizing, and accessible adjunctive strategy for promoting psychological well-being in this population. abstract: Abstract Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) in the cytoplasm and nucleus serve as direct molecular readouts of cell signaling pathways that govern cell differentiation, cancer, and other diseases. However, interpreting raw PTM data into pathways requires complex computational steps that may not be accessible to all researchers. title: Polysaccharides in the treatment of brain injury-related diseases: blood–brain barrier limitations and peripheral action pathways
abstract: Natural polysaccharides possess outstanding advantages including low toxicity, favorable biocompatibility, and multi-target regulatory capabilities. They hold broad application prospects in neuroprotective research on Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and depression. Owing to their high molecular weight and strong hydrophilicity, intact polysaccharides cannot readily cross the blood–brain barrier (BBB). abstract: Enhancing soil water availability is critical for improving crop drought resilience in highly weathered tropical soils. title: Experimental and numerical analysis of a CF-PAEK beam under low and ultrasonic cyclic bending frequencies
abstract: This work investigates the fatigue damage behavior of a carbon fiber-reinforced Poly-Aryl-Ether-Ketone (CF-PAEK) laminate under monotonic, low frequency, and ultrasonic frequency three-point bending conditions. abstract: Background In Angola, schistosomiasis remains a critical public health challenge, where traditional medicine serves as a pillar for primary healthcare. Methods Ethnobotanical data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 23 TMPs. title: Population trends and habitat preferences of ground‐nesting bees in arable landscapes from public‐based records
abstract: Abstract Bees play a crucial role in maintaining ecosystem services that support a healthy environment and agricultural productivity. Understanding of bee distribution and population changes, particularly in arable landscapes, remains limited, let alone how this varies among different bee groups, including solitary bees and social bees such as bumblebees. This study investigated the distribution and change of ground‐nesting bees in eastern Scotland, an agriculturally extensive region of the UK. abstract: This study examines the transformation of sovereignty within historical and systemic contexts, with particular attention to the rise of sovereignty claims in Europe during the transitional phase from globalization to deglobalization under the influence of multiple crises. abstract: Background This study aims to evaluate the restorative effects of ticagrelor (TIC), a well-known antiplatelet drug, on wound-healing capacity using cationic hyalurosomes loaded into an aerogel. abstract: Abstract The present paper advocates for incorporating Big Team Science practices into the language sciences. Big Team Science is a promising mode of collaborative research in which top-down coordination directs efforts by a large number of researchers from different institutions towards a common scientific goal. abstract: Synthetic pesticides remain the dominant curative technology of global crop protection, yet the terms on which they are justified, chiefly private profitability at the farm gate, increasingly diverge from the terms on which society evaluates them: ecosystem integrity, water quality, pollinator persistence, soil function and rural health. abstract: Las asignaturas teóricas de los programas de gastronomía suelen percibirse como menos atractivas que las prácticas de cocina, aun cuando sostienen buena parte del perfil profesional. abstract: El presente estudio analiza el marco jurídico europeo aplicable a la violencia digital contra las mujeres y evalúa si los instrumentos vigentes ofrecen garantías suficientes para una protección efectiva de las víctimas en entornos digitales transfronterizos. title: When circular economy barriers stir emotions: how SME leaders respond
abstract: Emotions shape how small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) leaders respond to barriers in the transition to a circular economy (CE); however, the emotional dimension of CE leadership remains under-explored. To understand how SME leaders engaged in CE appraise and cope with barriers that hinder the adoption of circular business models, this study explores emotions in organisational behaviour. title: Atherogenic lipoprotein particles and premature coronary artery disease: from molecular mechanisms to precision prevention
abstract: Premature coronary artery disease (PCAD), commonly defined as coronary disease before age 55 in men and 65 in women, reflects interactions among inherited susceptibility, metabolic dysfunction, environmental exposures, and vascular inflammation. This narrative review examines cumulative exposure to atherogenic apolipoprotein B (apoB)-containing particles as one major, modifiable pathway in atherosclerotic PCAD. abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐blind ultraviolet photodetection is important for low‐background ultraviolet communication, flame and corona warning, environmental monitoring, and space optoelectronics. abstract: Coffea arabica L. is an economically important crop grown in diverse geographical regions of Yemen. title: Canopy conductance regulation and water use strategies in poplar plantations in North China under dry versus wet years
abstract: Canopy conductance ( g c ) is a key physiological and ecohydrological parameter controlling canopy transpiration, stomatal regulation and vegetation–atmosphere carbon–water exchange. However, the extent to which the environmental regulation of g c pathways shifts between contrasting hydroclimatic conditions remains poorly understood. abstract: Introduction Presently, domestic geese remain genetically less studied farm animals. Goose breeding is a traditional branch of animal husbandry in Russia. abstract: This study investigates biodegradable cushioning materials for delivery packaging based on sago starch combined with hydrogel-based biopolymers. The research aims to address damage, environmental pollution, and packaging waste associated with conventional petroleum-based cushioning materials. abstract: The development of a universal H9N2 avian influenza vaccine is essential to reduce the occurrence of disease and economic losses in the poultry industry. abstract: ABSTRACT Meat quality is a critical economic trait in ruminant production because it directly influences consumer acceptability, market value, and the long‐term sustainability of the livestock industry. Amino acids (AAs) have traditionally been regarded primarily as substrates for protein synthesis. However, growing evidence indicates that they also regulate multiple aspects of meat quality. abstract: The heterotrimeric kinesin-2 motor (KIF3A/KIF3B/KAP3) drives anterograde intraflagellar transport and is essential for mammalian ciliogenesis. abstract: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae ( Xoo ) and X. oryzae pv. oryzicola ( Xoc ) are major bacterial pathogens of rice that cause bacterial blight and bacterial leaf streak, respectively. Successful infection by these pathogens depends largely on a functional type III secretion system (T3SS), which delivers diverse type III secretion effectors (T3SEs) into rice cells to manipulate host transcription, immunity, metabolism, and cellular processes. abstract: Introduction The education curriculum in any milieu is dynamic and a continuous, evolving process. However, the influence of Western philosophy on educational curricula raises concerns about the harmful impact of crime and food insecurity on Nigeria's food sustainability. abstract: Motor creativity is widely recognized as a component of physical literacy, encompassing the ability to adapt movement by generating original and functional solutions to motor challenges in dynamic environments. abstract: The main aim of this research was to investigate site selection for two types of Eurasian badger (Meles meles) setts (main and secondary) in relation to environmental factors (soil type and vegetation structure) and distances to meadows, rivers, human settlements, and public roads in the Stobrawa Landscape Park (SLP, southwestern Poland). abstract: North Bihar, situated in the eastern Indo-Gangetic floodplain, is characterized by fertile alluvial soils deposited by major Himalayan rivers such as the Kosi, Gandak, Bagmati and Mahananda. abstract: Abstract While many determinants of higher education (HE) class skipping have been documented, its relationship with high school academic performance remains underexplored. This study explores the relationship between high school academic performance and HE class skipping. abstract: This study investigates the relationship between implicit cultural knowledge and acquired musical knowledge—developed through diverse forms of learning—in the performance and interpretation of Sephardic music. abstract: Intergenerational relationships are central to later-life wellbeing and the transmission of cultural identity, yet older adults’ own accounts of these processes remain underrepresented in Gulf societies. This qualitative interview study explored how older Emirati adults understand intergenerational cohesion, cultural continuity, and the role of family and community institutions in sustaining these ties. abstract: Species are shifting their geographical ranges, yet the consequences of these spatial redistributions for species interactions have not been examined at broad spatial and temporal scales. Here, we characterize shifts in the potential for predator-prey interactions among North American birds over the past 50 years. abstract: Biochar is a promising low-carbon cement additive that combines carbon sequestration with biomass-waste utilization. abstract: Climate change is predicted to have severe impacts on mammal diversity in southeastern Amazonia. abstract: ABSTRACT As tourism enters the phygital era, digital preview media have become key pre‐purchase touchpoints. Drawing on cognitive fit theory, this study challenges the assumption that immersive virtual reality (VR) always outperforms static images by examining how media form (VR panoramic video vs. static images) and information framing (hedonic vs. utilitarian) jointly shape tourism booking intentions. abstract: Rural tourism is often promoted as a means of advancing gender equality, yet little is known about how women’s empowerment translates into lasting behavioral support for tourism, particularly outside a few well-studied regions. abstract: This paper furthers understanding of the capabilities and skills required to manage complex organisations and processes in a place leadership setting by examining the experiences of local authority chief executives during local government reorganisation in England. abstract: Rural governance in Bangladesh is very much linked with the lived experience of citizens in relation to public institutions and public services in everyday life. This study analyses the perception of citizens on rural governance, looking at the three service areas of health, education and agriculture, and a comparison of perceptions by different socio-economic groups. abstract: Abstract Background Urban trees provide essential ecosystem services, including carbon storage. In addition, most existing equations rely solely on diameter at breast height (DBH), which is hard to obtain from remote-sensing data, thus limiting scaling to city level. title: Capítulo 7. Producción audiovisual
abstract: La producción audiovisual se presenta como el proceso de planificación y coordinación que convierte una propuesta creativa en un proyecto realizable. El capítulo recorre la preproducción, el rodaje, la postproducción y la distribución, explicando sus relaciones y las responsabilidades del productor y de los distintos departamentos. title: Exploratory Comparative Ovarian Transcriptomic Profiling in Dekalb White Hens Identified Candidate Signatures Associated with Egg-Laying Plateau Persistence
abstract: The peak egg-laying plateau in poultry is regulated by complex genetic factors. title: From welfare to the environment: social policy, natural resources, and ecological sustainability in G20 economies
abstract: Ecological degradation has emerged as a critical challenge to achieving sustainable development, particularly in G20 economies where economic growth, social welfare objectives, and environmental constraints frequently interact. Using annual data for 17 G20 countries over 2000–2021, this study examines the effects of social welfare (SCWF), economic policy uncertainty (ECPX), trade openness (TROP), life expectancy (LIEX), natural resource rents (NARN), and tourism (TRSM) on ecological footprints (ECFP). title: Biostimulant potential of Limnospira platensis biomass fermented with lactic acid bacteria in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris): strain characterization, biochemical shifts, and growth promotion
abstract: The excessive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides in conventional agriculture poses significant risks to soil health, environmental quality, and food security. Plant biostimulants derived from microorganisms, microalgae and cyanobacteria offer a sustainable alternative. Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and cyanobacteria such as Limnospira platensis are recognized for their plant growth-promoting characteristics. title: Inhabiting a wounded world: a qualitative phenomenology of ecological anxiety
abstract: Introduction Ecological anxiety is defined as distress caused by awareness of the ongoing climate crisis. This qualitative phenomenological study aimed to describe how lived experience is altered in ecological anxiety. Methods We conducted 58 interviews with 30 participants who identified themselves as experiencing ecological anxiety. Interviews combined lifeworld analysis with a micro-phenomenological approach to explore specific experiential episodes. title: Beyond self, time, and space: exceptional experiences and altered states of consciousness
abstract: Exceptional experiences commonly described as parapsychological or as extra-sensory—including precognition, telepathic impressions, meaningful coincidences, and other forms of anomalous cognition—remain among the most controversial topics in consciousness research. Population studies consistently demonstrate that such experiences are widespread across cultures and appear to transcend ordinary spatial and temporal constraints. This critical review focuses on methodological challenges and theoretical implications of investigating phenomena that may suggest forms of non-local consciousness. Exper

title: Earnings Call Tone and Investors' Reliance on Mandatory Disclosures
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether the tone of earnings conference calls is associated with investors' subsequent use of firms' mandatory disclosure filings. Using conference call transcripts and EDGAR web traffic data from 2007 to 2016, I find that more positive conference call tone is followed by lower subsequent requests for firms' periodic filings. This relation persists after controlling for firm characteristics, earnings news, analyst following, institutional ownership and leverage, and remains robust in matched sample and weather‐based analyses. abstract: For acute mountain sickness prevention and the treatment of respiratory, cardiovascular, and nervous system diseases, pharmacological (prolyl hydroxylase domain inhibitors, plant extracts, erythrocyte pyruvate kinase activators, and hemoglobin oxygen affinity allosteric activators) and non-pharmacological approaches (hypoxic training and hypoxic therapy) are used. title: Stochastic assembly outweighs deterministic filtering: crop phenological stages drive bacterial-fungal divergence between bulk and rhizosphere soils in saline-alkali fields
abstract: Soil salinization threatens crop productivity partly by disrupting rhizosphere microbiomes that support plant stress tolerance. However, most studies have focused on single growth stages or bulk soil, limiting a deeper insight into the temporal dynamics and assembly mechanisms of rhizosphere communities across the crop life cycle. We investigated bacterial and fungal communities in a long-term maize field with saline-alkali soil. Bulk and rhizosphere soils were sampled at seedling, heading, and maturity. title: Sustainable and multifunctional biocomposite materials for energy storage applications: A comprehensive review
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable, high-performance energy storage technologies has driven interest in biocomposite materials derived from renewable resources. Combining bio-based polymers with bio-fillers and functional bionanomaterials, these materials offer environmentally friendly alternatives for applications in supercapacitors and lithium-ion batteries, as well as energy-conversion technologies such as fuel cells and solar cells. title: Microclimatic regulation effects of landscape elements on university campus in a temperate monsoon climate zone: A case study during extreme summer heat
abstract: Although temperate monsoon climate regions are traditionally known for their harsh winter climates, the combined effects of rapid urbanization and global climate change have significantly intensified summer urban heat island effects in these areas, making them a neglected yet increasingly severe challenge in high-latitude urban climate adaptation planning. This study takes a typical campus in Shenyang, a temperate monsoon climate region in Northeast China, as the experimental subject. title: Capítulo 10. Adobe Audition
abstract: El capítulo desarrolla los fundamentos de la postproducción sonora con Adobe Audition, desde la grabación y organización del material hasta la mezcla, la masterización y la exportación. Distingue el trabajo sobre archivos individuales en el editor de forma de onda y la construcción de proyectos en el entorno multipista. La configuración técnica, el control de los niveles de entrada y la conservación de los originales se relacionan con la calidad y la seguridad del proceso. Se explican procedimientos de restauración, captura de perfiles de ruido, diagnóstico, procesamiento dinámico y ecualizaci
journal: Espejo de Monografías de Comunicación Social

title: Capítulo 11. Corrección de color y etalonaje
abstract: Este capítulo diferencia la corrección técnica del color y el etalonaje como procesos complementarios de la postproducción audiovisual. La primera equilibra la imagen y mantiene la continuidad entre planos; el segundo desarrolla su tratamiento expresivo y su identidad visual. A partir del matiz, la saturación, la luminosidad y la temperatura de color, se examina cómo las decisiones cromáticas participan en la caracterización de personajes, la organización temporal y la construcción de atmósferas. Las asociaciones emocionales del color se presentan atendiendo a su contexto narrativo y cultural.
journal: Espejo de Monografías de Comunicación Social

title: Perspectives of Biomaterial‐Based Sustainable Integrated Micro‐ and Nanophotonics
abstract: ABSTRACT Biomolecular photonics is emerging as a pathway toward sustainable alternatives to fully semiconductor‐based devices, leveraging the unique optical properties and solution processability of proteins, nucleic acids, and other biogenic molecules. This review covers recent advances in nano‐ and microscale biophotonic devices, spanning biopolymer waveguides (with optical losses down to 0.24 dB cm −1 ), bio‐organic LEDs and lasers (luminous efficiencies up to 130 lm W −1 ; lifetimes >3600 h), biohybrid photovoltaics (PCE up to ∼20%), photodetectors, and optoelectronic memristors. title: Study on Gas Drainage Mechanisms and Techniques in Low-Permeability Coal Seam
abstract: This study investigates gas drainage mechanisms and techniques for low-permeability coal seams. It examines coal structure, gas-flow behaviour, permeability controls, and internationally applied drainage methods. Permeabilityenhancement approaches, including hydraulic fracturing, hydraulic slotting, and controlled blasting, are evaluated alongside borehole design and operating factors. title: Extracellular vesicle surface proteins in tissue recognition, organotropism, biomarkers, and therapeutic engineering
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), including exosomes, carry donor-cell-derived molecular features that influence their interactions with recipient cells. This review links EV biogenesis and the assembly of surface recognition cues to cellular interactions, tissue distribution, and translational applications, with an emphasis on the evidence required to interpret surface localization, biomarker value, and therapeutic outcomes. title: A Comprehensive Review on Advancements in Photocatalytic Applications of Nanostructured Metal Oxides Toward Environmental Remediation
abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing energy crisis and environmental contamination have become one of the most pressing global challenges, prompting the advancement of eco‐friendly and effective advanced treatment technologies. Although photocatalysis enabled by semiconducting materials has garnered intense research interest for pollution remediation, large‐scale application of widely studied semiconductor photocatalysts remains constrained by inefficient utilization of the visible‐light, fast recombination of charge carriers, and limited operational stability. title: Targeting convergent pathogenic pathways: precision nutrition and lifestyle strategies in ulcerative colitis
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) exhibits rising global incidence and substantial disease burden. Limited therapeutic response and side effects of standard medications create demand for safe adjunctive management approaches. It appraises existing evidence for targeted nutritional supplementation and structured lifestyle adjustments in UC care, covering vitamin D, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) particularly butyrate, probiotics including Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) and multi-strain blends, prebiotics, synbiotics, phytochemicals, and trace elements, together with physical activity, stress managem

title: From ‘yuck’ to ‘ahhh’: a focused review on the bacteriophage-based strategy for malodour mitigation to improve the aspirational quotient of toilets
abstract: Most of the user-interface of toilets is associated with in-situ , decentralised wastewater treatment systems. Specifically, on-site sanitation systems (OSS) and decentralised wastewater treatment systems (DEWATS) are mainly used to treat toilet blackwater (faeces, urine, and flush water). Though ideal, malodour generated within these systems can hinder their adoption, especially where sanitation infrastructure is limited. title: Chikungunya virus: from global emergence to immunopathology and therapeutic frontiers
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, has transitioned from an endemic pathogen to a global public health threat. In May 2026, the World Health Organization’s second rapid risk assessment classified the global public health risk of CHIKV transmission as moderate. Although two vaccines (IXCHIQ ® and VIMKUNYA ® ) have been authorized in selected countries, no antiviral therapy has been approved, and supportive care remains the mainstay of clinical management. title: User-Centered Design of Interactive Recommender Systems for Cancer Patients and Caregivers
abstract: User-centered design is a commonly accepted approach in designing interactive systems; however, its application to the design of interactive recommender systems is still limited. This paper reviews the design of H ELPeR, a patient-focused interactive recommender system for ovarian cancer ( O vCa) patients and caregivers. It has a dual goal: to present an example of an interactive recommender system in a health domain and to demonstrate a case of user-centered design of a recommender system in this challenging domain. title: From chronic airway injury to lung cancer: epithelial memory, field cancerization, and premalignant evolution
abstract: Chronic airway injury induced by tobacco smoke, environmental pollutants, and persistent inflammatory lung diseases provides a biological foundation for lung carcinogenesis, yet the cellular and molecular trajectory from repeated epithelial damage to invasive malignancy has only recently come into focus. abstract: Introduction Microbiome multi-omics studies frequently identify microbial, metabolic, and host transcriptional associations, but their reproducibility and support for connected biological mechanisms remain uncertain. We evaluated these relationships in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and colorectal cancer (CRC) using an eight-dimensional, non-compensatory evidence-gating framework. abstract: Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) are next-generation class of zero-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterials exhibit variable bandgap energies and quantum dimensional effect suitable for advanced electrochemical energy conversion and storage applications. Their intrinsic properties such as high specific surface area, chemical versatility, and electrochemical stability increase their performance characteristics in electrocatalytic systems, batteries, and supercapacitors. title: Long-term sex-specific consequences of prenatal hypoxia on systemic hemodynamics and baroreflex sensitivity in rats
abstract: Background Intrauterine hypoxia is a common pregnancy complication that programs long-term cardiovascular dysfunction. However, stage-specific effects on cardiac vs. vascular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Aim We investigated baroreflex coefficient (BRC) and cardiac reactivity in peripubertal and adult rats exposed to acute hypobaric hypoxia at different gestational stages, examined autonomic mechanisms, and differentiated between cardiac and vascular components of the programed phenotype. title: Physiological functions of fructooligosaccharides and its application progress in food
abstract: Abstract Fructooligosaccharides (FOS) are naturally sourced, low-calorie carbohydrates that resist human digestive enzymes in the gastrointestinal tract. They are selectively fermented by certain Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium species in the colon, thereby producing short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). title: Revisiting a 50-year-old ecological study of Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera species in Estaragne River (French Pyrenees): why taxonomy matters?
abstract: Long-term ecological surveys (LTES) and historical species inventories are essential for assessing changes in biodiversity. However, comparisons over time may be heavily biased if they disregard the evolution of taxonomic knowledge. To investigate, at a later date, changes in the distribution of aquatic species over the last 50 years, we revisited the Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera (EPT) species inventory conducted by Pierre Lavandier in the 70’s in the Estaragne, a subalpine and alpine catchment area in the French Central Pyrenees. title: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi enhance growth, mineral nutrition, metabolic traits and essential oil bioactivity in Thymus satureioides Coss.
abstract: Thymus satureioides is a native plant of the Moroccan Atlas Mountains and is valued for its culinary, medicinal, and cosmetic uses. The increasing pressure on its populations and its vegetation calls for sustainable farming. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) are among the beneficial microbes that promote growth, phytochemicals, and bioactive properties. title: Emerging anti-infective strategies based on host regulation and host–pathogen interactions
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance continues to worsen, posing a major challenge to the prevention and management of infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria. Although conventional antibiotics, antimicrobial nanomaterials, and phage therapy have expanded the available antimicrobial options, their application remains constrained by selective pressure for resistance, biosafety concerns, narrow host range, and incomplete clinical translation. title: Acid-sensing ion channels in pain and psychiatric disorders: from basic properties to comorbidity mechanisms
abstract: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that mediate Na + and Ca 2+ influx upon activation by extracellular acidification. Beyond protons, endogenous ligands, toxins, and small molecules modulate ASIC gating through direct or synergistic mechanisms. ASICs have emerged as key players in pain and psychiatric disorders. Tissue acidosis drives hyperalgesia via sustained ASIC activation, synaptic plasticity disruption, and central sensitization, thereby promoting chronic pain. title: OmniFaceRig: Fully Automatic Inner-Mouth-Aware Face Rigging Across Diverse 3D Character Topologies
abstract: Facial rigging—creating FACS-based blendshapes together with inner-mouth geometry (teeth, gums, and tongue)—remains a major bottleneck in 3D character production. abstract: This study represents the first systematic survey of far-right female influencers in the German-speaking TikTok community since the rise of a new neo-Nazi youth cultural movement in 2024, thereby filling a key research gap in the fields of digital far-right studies and political geography. The methodological focus is on multimodal discourse analysis, which examines TikTok videos as complex compositions of text, image, and sound. abstract: Este artigo discute a noção de exclusão escolhida como uma categoria analítica para compreender as persistentes desigualdades digitais na contemporaneidade. Parte-se da hipótese de que a exclusão digital não decorre apenas de limitações tecnológicas ou infraestruturais, mas também de decisões políticas, econômicas e institucionais que definem quais territórios, grupos sociais e populações serão incorporados aos ecossistemas digitais e quais permanecerão à margem. title: Heterogeneity of Farmer Preferences Towards Collective Agri‐Environmental Schemes: A Latent Class Analysis for Biodiversity Conservation in Switzerland
abstract: ABSTRACT Collective agri‐environmental schemes offer a promising approach to improve biodiversity promotion in agriculture by providing landscape connectivity. However, how to design these schemes to foster participation in the presence of farmers' heterogeneous preferences and perceived transaction costs remains an open question. title: Engineering functional perfusion in vascularized cardiac grafts through bioactive biomaterials and biofabrication
abstract: Vascularized cardiac grafts are being developed to overcome the limited survival and incomplete integration of engineered myocardial tissues after implantation. Although many platforms can now generate endothelial networks, the central challenge is no longer the presence of vascular-like structures alone, but the establishment of networks that remain perfusable, mechanically stable, and functionally coupled to the host circulation. abstract: This study examines explosive price dynamics consistent with bubble-like behavior in clean and renewable energy ETFs, index, and equities compared to traditional energy counterparts, using the Generalized Supremum Augmented Dickey-Fuller (GSADF) test across four subperiods: Pre-Paris Agreement, Paris Agreement, COVID-19, and Russia-Ukraine War. title: Developing an outcomes framework for greenspace programmes supporting individuals experiencing problem substance use: a scoping review and analytical synthesis
abstract: Background Greenspace programmes are known to support health and wellbeing, yet limited research exists on their impact for individuals experiencing problem substance use. Early findings are promising, but systematic exploration of appropriate outcome measures and evaluation methods remains sparse. This paper addresses that gap by developing an outcomes framework tailored to this population. Methods A mixed methods approach was used. title: The Cross-Border Care Model, a middle-range nursing theory for mobile populations in Latin America and beyond: Discussion paper
abstract: Background Research on migrant and refugee health in Latin America and the Caribbean points to a finding with direct clinical consequences. The conditions that borders create appear to shape the health of people on the move more consistently than cultural difference does. Administrative status, racialised exclusion and the physical conditions of crossing affect presentation, access and outcomes, often long after the crossing. title: Medicinal plant agrobiodiversity, biocultural management, and conservation in a Mixtec indigenous community in Oaxaca, Mexico
abstract: Medicinal plants constitute an important component of agrobiodiversity in Indigenous landscapes, where wild, cultivated, and locally managed resources contribute to household health care, biocultural continuity, and biodiversity conservation. This study characterized medicinal plant agrobiodiversity, therapeutic uses, management practices, and intracultural variation in ethnobotanical knowledge in Santiago Ixtaltepec, a Mixtec Indigenous community in Oaxaca, Mexico. title: cGAS–STING signalling in triple-negative breast cancer: a functional-state framework for biomarker-guided intervention
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) combines genomic instability with heterogeneous immune responses. Cyclic GMP–AMP synthase (cGAS) detects mislocalised DNA and produces cyclic guanosine monophosphate–adenosine monophosphate (cGAMP), which activates stimulator of interferon genes (STING). title: Contextualizing a process information approach in material passports: a case on modelling circular façade product requirements
abstract: Information gaps are a key challenge in transitioning to a circular economy, particularly beyond the first use of building products. Material passports could bridge these information gaps by acting as shared information repositories across actors and product stages. However, current material passport research primarily defines product-centric information requirements addressing the here and now, while process-related information to enable future reuse remains less examined. abstract: The development of stable, sunlight-mediated photocatalysts capable of simultaneously removing chemically diverse organic pollutants remains a critical challenge for sustainable wastewater remediation. This study report is an interfacial engineered and eco-friendly biogenic Ag/Cu-Zn trimetallic heterostructure stabilized by tannic acid for efficient degradation of a mixed cationic-anionic dye system (methylene blue and methyl orange). title: CD8 + T cells induce RIPK1-regulated brain endothelial cell death in cerebral malaria
abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a potentially lethal complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and brain hemorrhage. Although immune-mediated endothelial damage is central to CM pathology, the mechanisms linking cytotoxic immune responses to endothelial injury remain unclear. title: Epidemiological patterns of black pod (Phytophthora spp.) and frosty pod rot (Moniliophthora roreri) in cocoa plantations of Tequendama, Colombia
abstract: Cocoa is an important crop in Colombia and a key productive alternative in post-conflict rural areas. Similar to other tropical production systems, yields are constrained by diseases such as black pod disease and frosty pod rot. This study evaluated the temporal and spatial epidemiological patterns of both diseases on three cocoa farms located in the Tequendama region of Colombia through analyses of disease incidence, severity, disease progress, and spatial distribution. abstract: As a test of the uniformity of competence assumption—the notion that there is an ideal state of native speaker competence—and to establish how variability in native speakers compares to variability in non-native speakers, this study examined individual differences in morphosyntactic attainment in adult monolingual native speakers of Brazilian Portuguese. title: Current advances on the phytochemical composition, pharmacological applications, and toxicology of Micromeria graeca
abstract: Background Micromeria graeca ( M. graeca ) is a species belonging to the Lamiaceae family, regarded as a shrub that is widespread throughout the world and widely cultivated in many countries. It is used traditionally in food, cosmetics, and medicines. Objective The objective of this review is to examine the pharmacological, phytochemical, and toxicological activities of M. graeca . abstract: Based on morphological characteristics and phylogenetic analyses using ITS, nrLSU, rpb 2, and tef 1-α sequence data, six new species belonging to subg. title: Improved COPD Epidemiological Awareness Following Standardized Education Independently Associated with Better Inhaled Medication Adherence: A Multicenter Prospective Pre-Post Study
abstract: Background: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) contributes substantially to global morbidity and mortality, while suboptimal inhaled medication adherence worsens clinical outcomes. title: Climate change risk and corporate pension funding
abstract: This paper investigates how climate change risk influences corporate pension funding decisions. Based on the precautionary motive, we hypothesize that firms facing greater climate-related uncertainty will increase pension funding to protect against potential financial disruptions. Using 13,871 firm-year observations of U.S. publicly traded firms from 2001 to 2023, we find a positive correlation between climate risk exposure and pension funding. This finding remains consistent when using alternative variable definitions, restricted samples, and various methods to address endogeneity concerns. F
journal: Journal of International Money and Finance

title: Illusionism as a theory of mental content
abstract: Analytic philosophers of mind seemingly take the hard problem of consciousness to be the only aspect of the mind-body problem that has not been in principle solved. But phenomenal consciousness is not the only puzzling and mysterious mental phenomena. The capacity of our minds to have contents — to “be about” or “of” objects, and to represent them — is also puzzling and mysterious. And whilst, from the ‘80s on, it was largely assumed that mental contents could have been easily naturalized, the repeated and systematic failures of naturalistic theories of content invite us to search for an alter
journal: THEORIA An International Journal for Theory History and Foundations of Science

title: From Sea Surface Height to Velocity - A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Inferring upper-ocean velocity from altimetric sea surface height (SSH) remains challenging below 50~km, scales now resolved by the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission. Conventional methods rely on geostrophic or cyclogeostrophic balance. Here, we demonstrate that deep learning can predict the full velocity vector from SSH and environmental data and recover derivative-based diagnostics, including spectral energy flux. We trained a U-Net encoder--decoder on hourly fields from the pre-SWOT Cape Basin extraction of the LLC4320 ocean simulation, with 1.5-km grid spacing ($11.8$--$15.

title: A Deep-Learning Framework for the Generalized Emulation of Atmospheric Radiative Transfer at Microwave Frequencies
abstract: This paper presents an application of machine learning to the problem of the computational expense of atmospheric radiative transfer calculations from physics-based models. While in recent studies individual emulators have been created that emulate certain radiative transfer schemes for different sensors, we show that a general framework can be applied to emulate the radiative transfer method itself. title: Uncertainty-Aware Sea-Ice Type Mapping with Multiple Ice Charts
abstract: Sea-ice stage of development (SoD) describes the age and associated thickness of sea ice and provides important information for navigation, operational ice monitoring, and assessment of ice conditions. SoD labels are obtained from operational ice charts, where trained analysts interpret satellite observations and assign standardized stage codes to regions with similar ice conditions. These codes often represent ranges of compatible ice thicknesses rather than exact physical values. Deep-learning methods can automate SoD mapping from satellite imagery and commonly adopt operational ice charts a
institutions: Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences
National Snow and Ice Data Center

title: SHAPE: Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions A machine learning approach to solar flare forecasting
abstract: Solar flares are the most energetic impulsive events in the solar system, and reliable operational forecasting of the rarest and most destructive M- and X-class events remains an open problem. We present Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions (SHAPE), a two-phase deep-learning pipeline that bypasses sunspot proxies in favour of direct soft X-ray observations from the GOES X-ray Sensor (XRS).
