title: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment
abstract: Fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) on harmful data in a narrow domain, such as bad medical advice, can make it broadly misaligned. How realistic this risk is remains unclear, since models are very rarely fine-tuned on explicitly harmful data in practice. In this work, we show that fine-tuning on data the model believes to be false but that has no harmful content, can also induce broad misalignment. title: Assignment-Free Swarm Navigation via Adaptive Target-Field Planning and Mean-Shift Exploration
abstract: Mean-shift exploration enables assignment-free swarm shape assembly, but obstacle-constrained navigation additionally requires coordinated adaptation of the desired morphology and its physical execution. This paper presents an environment-adaptive navigation framework that integrates target-field planning, execution regulation, and morphology-preserving mean-shift exploration. title: Rules, Choice, and Chance: A Welfare Evaluation Framework for Student-School Matching
abstract: Centralized student-school matching systems, adopted in the United States, Chile, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom, assign students to schools based on their submitted preference rankings and schools' priority policies. Yet welfare in these systems is typically measured through a narrow lens: a few aggregate statistics published by education authorities, such as the share of students unmatched or assigned to a top-ranked choice. title: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together?
abstract: Dantzig--Wolfe reformulation strengthens the linear relaxation of a mixed-integer program by convexifying constraint families, and each candidate costs a column generation run. title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Bubble-Induced Performance Losses in Microstructured Copper Electrodes for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
abstract: Water electrolysis is a promising technology for sustainable hydrogen (H$_2$) production. Existing theoretical models fail to connect computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and electrochemistry to analyze how bubble dynamics affect the performance of gas-evolving microstructured electrodes. title: LAION-Audio-XL: A Web-Scale Corpus and Scaling Studies for Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining
abstract: Recent progress on contrastive audio-language models can be attributed mainly to the scale and quality of their training data. Larger training datasets expose models to a broader range of sounds and corresponding audio captions. To exploit this, we collect 1.48 billion audio samples from academic datasets, internet datasets, web collections, Common Crawl, and YouTube, and process them with a multi-stage curation pipeline. Furthermore, we generate short and long captions for samples in our corpus that lack them. We use our dataset to study the scaling behavior of contrastive audio-language mode

title: Limits to research in astrophysics
abstract: Fundamental physics faces several intrinsic limitations, such as the finite speed of light in vacuum, the absolute zero temperature, Heisenberg's uncertainty principle and so on. At the same time, the material resources necessary to conduct research in astrophysics, such as energy, fresh water, and rareearth elements, are also limited in both quantity and extraction capabilities, a concept often referred to as planetary boundaries. In the context of scientific research growing at a frenetic pace, following the greedy quenchless extractivist model of our era, and which is giving rise to an ever

title: Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents
abstract: Frontier language models are increasingly deployed as agents, and how well an agent performs depends not only on its model but also on its harness: the prompts, tools, memory, and control loop through which the model acts. When an agent is applied to a new problem, a natural question is whether it can use the feedback of the task to improve the way it works, and not merely its answer. Most existing benchmarks keep the agent's harness fixed and score the solution it produces, or target large-scale model training. We introduce Flex-RSI, a benchmark for the recursive self-improvement of agents on

title: Do agents need to sleep?
abstract: LLM-based agents, which increasingly operate persistently across sessions and accumulate memory through interaction, already exhibit the familiar symptoms of unchecked plasticity: semantic drift, degraded retrieval precision, propagation of stored errors, and saturation of memory capacity. Drawing on the selectionist "ringing, resonance and renormalization" (RRR) account of sleep, we propose that each of its three phases maps onto an operation feasible in digital memory architectures. Engineers building stateful agents, meanwhile, are independently rediscovering the problems sleep evolved to s

title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
abstract: Modern video models possess strong visual priors, yet do not natively represent human action in metric 3D space. We present EgoGeneralist, which adapts pretrained video generators to unify action-conditioned video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation for egocentric manipulation. Our role-adaptive action renderer provides video-native representations for multidirectional action-video learning, making metric motion usable as both a spatial control signal and a recoverable generation target. Cross-stream action-video coupling establishes close correspondence between metr

title: Free energy of the Hopfield model
abstract: We identify the limit of the free energy of the Hopfield model with independent symmetric Bernoulli patterns, for every temperature and loading ratio. A Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation reduces the problem to that of identifying the limit free energy of a bipartite spin glass with $\pm 1$ and spherical spins. One key difficulty is that the patterns, which become the coupling coefficients in the bipartite model, are Bernoulli instead of Gaussian, and the limit free energy is sensitive to the law of these coefficients. We show that the model is in fact equivalent to one involving Gaussian pat

title: Not All Frames Deserve Full Computation: Accelerating Autoregressive Video Generation via Selective Computation and Predictive Extrapolation
abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models enable long-form video generation but remain expensive due to repeated multi-step denoising. Existing training-free acceleration methods rely on binary cache-or-recompute decisions, overlooking intermediate cases where direct reuse is too coarse yet full recomputation is unnecessary. Moreover, asynchronous AR schedules assign different noise levels to co-generated frames, yet existing methods process the entire valid interval uniformly. To address these AR-specific inefficiencies, we present SCOPE, a training-free framework for efficient AR video diff

title: Clock-Shift-Aided Blind Doppler Matching in Passive SDR Monitoring Data for LEO Doppler Positioning
abstract: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite signals have recently attracted increasing attention as opportunistic signals for positioning, navigation, and timing. Most Doppler-based LEO positioning studies rely on tracked satellite signals or raw in-phase/quadrature (IQ) samples that preserve signal-level structures for acquisition, Doppler tracking, or satellite association. In contrast, passive software-defined radio (SDR) monitoring systems often retain only time-frequency power scans, in which LEO Doppler traces appear as unlabeled ridges without raw IQ samples or identifiable signal structures. This

title: Distinguishing among reasoning levels of GPT 5.5 Pro via a grammar lens benchmark
abstract: Does the level of test-time processing effort affect a language model's computational capability? A formal grammar-lens benchmark method, derived from the theory of computation, generates novel data at specified levels, each successively more computationally powerful than the levels below. Using this data, we tested GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.5-Pro-Medium, -High, and -XHigh, showing incrementally increased acceptance of test data: 16, 40, 43, and 52\%, respectively, illustrating the benchmark's ability to discern fine-grained differences among models' added test-time reasoning levels. Additionally, as

title: Improving Precision in Cluster-Level Pricing Experiments with Temporal Switchbacks
abstract: Online pricing systems often cannot randomize treatments at the user level because prices are deployed over operational units such as routes, regions, or markets. This creates low-powered A/B tests due to persistent cluster heterogeneity, seasonality, and autocorrelated demand. We study temporal switchback designs for cluster-level pricing experiments, where each cluster alternates between treatment and control over time. Using LATAM Airlines ancillary-pricing data and calibrated simulations, we show that switchbacks can substantially reduce standard errors relative to parallel cluster designs

title: You don't need long context
abstract: Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens. On frontier open weight models, the disparity in cost may rise to as much as 7x. Through frequent compaction, we show across a broad range of long-horizon and long-input tasks that frontier language models sacrifice little to no task accuracy when maintaining short contexts. We further demonstrate that LLM performance does not collapse on long-horizon software engineering tasks even when taking at most one action per context, and based on that we outline the concept of semantic state space models (SSSMs). Our findings question the need

title: PolyUQuest: Verifiable Structure-Aware Web RAG over Heterogeneous Graphs
abstract: Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems treat web pages as flat text, losing the structural and semantic signals encoded in HTML. We present PolyUQuest, a verifiable, structure-aware web RAG framework built on a heterogeneous graph that unifies hyperlink topology between pages, DOM hierarchy within pages, and entity–relation knowledge across pages. A two-tier router dispatches each query to one of three retrieval modes matched to its structural need, including direct block retrieval, cross-page graph traversal, and multi-hop entity reasoning. Each answer carries traceable provena

title: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems
abstract: Foundation models in changing environments can encounter unfamiliar domain knowledge that their original training did not cover. However, new domains rarely provide large amounts of expert-created training data or reliable supervisory signals for further training. We introduce Recursa, a foundation model system that adapts to new domains by learning from its own experience without human experts or a stronger teacher model. Recursa uses a knowledge repository to store what it learns: domain-specific skills and instructions on when to apply them, along with memories of past task experiences and

title: Less Is More: Balancing Positive and Negative Space in Visual Concept Blending
abstract: Graphic designers often blend visual concepts to communicate multiple ideas within a single image, leveraging positive and negative space to create balance, emphasis, and aesthetic appeal. While computational methods have begun to support automatic concept blending, they largely overlook the role of spatial composition in the design. To address this gap, we present an automatic pipeline that explicitly applies positive and negative space throughout the blending process. Our approach first identifies plausible regions for concept integration by combining semantic reasoning from vision–language

title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: While Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG) has shown promising results, it still struggles with complex multi-hop reasoning tasks. Existing methods primarily focus on independent instance-level matching, which often fails to capture explicit relationships across modalities and documents. Although Graph-enhanced methods introduce structural modeling, they face a fundamental challenge in multimodal scenarios: incorporating fine-grained visual features leads to rapid graph expansion and retrieval noise, whereas coarse-grained representations cause the discarding of critical local ev

title: One Leak Away: How Pretrained Model Exposure Amplifies Jailbreak Risks in Finetuned LLMs
abstract: Finetuning pretrained large language models (LLMs) has become the standard paradigm for developing downstream applications. However, its security implications remain unclear, particularly regarding whether finetuned LLMs inherit jailbreak vulnerabilities from their pretrained sources. We investigate this question in a realistic pretrain-to-finetune threat model, where an attacker has full access to a released pretrained LLM but no access to its proprietary finetuned derivatives. Empirical analysis shows that adversarial prompts optimized on the pretrained model transfer most effectively to its
institutions: RIKEN Center for Advanced Intelligence Project

title: MAIC-UI: Making Interactive Courseware with Generative UI
abstract: Creating interactive STEM courseware traditionally requires HTML/CSS/JavaScript expertise, leaving barriers for educators. While generative AI can produce HTML codes, existing tools generate static presentations rather than interactive simulations, struggle with long documents, and lack pedagogical accuracy mechanisms. Furthermore, full regeneration for modifications requires 200–600 seconds, disrupting creative flow. We present MAIC-UI, a zero-code authoring system that enables educators to create and rapidly edit interactive courseware from textbooks, PPTs, and PDFs. MAIC-UI employs: (1) str

title: Kernelized Stable Fluids for simulating physically accurate solutions
abstract: The Stable Fluids algorithm is a fractional step method for solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in an unconditionally stable way. It was initially developed for visual effects and allows real-time simulations because of its low computational complexity. The method solves the advection step by using the method of characteristics which is implemented via linear interpolation. This results in excessive diffusion of vorticity and is one of the main reasons for the physical inaccuracy of the algorithm. We propose Kernelized Stable Fluids with Sparse Cholesky Preconditioning (KSF

title: Learning-to-Memorize: Dynamic Context Management for Long-Horizon Autoregressive Video Generation
abstract: Autoregressive video generation has achieved impressive results on short clips, yet generating long videos remains challenging due to error accumulation over extended horizons, where each predicted frame depends on potentially imperfect previous frames. Existing approaches typically rely on static context management strategies, such as sliding-window caches that discard early frames or fixed sink frames that permanently preserve initial content. These designs either lose critical long-range context or anchor generation to outdated information, which can lead to degraded fidelity, motion stagna

title: Exascale-ready HemeLB for large-eddy simulation of full-human arterial blood flow
abstract: Direct numerical simulation (DNS) of blood flow through the whole human arterial tree is limited by the number of lattice sites that must be advanced on a high-performance computer. We address this limit by combining the lattice Boltzmann solver HemeLB with Smagorinsky large-eddy simulation (LES). HemeLB runs with the same scaling behaviour on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA graphics processing units (GPUs) and sustains about 10 trillion lattice-site updates per second (TLUPS) on both the Frontier and Aurora exascale supercomputers. In stenotic aortic flow, LES on lattices five and ten times coarser tha

title: Quantum Pointwise Dimension (QUPID): An algorithm for identifying classical chaos in quantum dynamics
abstract: The Pointwise Dimension is a diagnostic that reveals the effective dimensionality of classical trajectories in a $2N$-dimensional phase space. The essence of this diagnostic is to find a scaling according to which density changes with radius $r$ around a point of interest in phase space. Particularly, regular trajectories are confined to an $N$-dimensional invariant torus, while chaotic trajectories explore a $(2N-1)$-dimensional energy surface. In classical mechanics, this trajectory density can be found by counting recurrences to within the sphere of radius $r$. In quantum mechanics, probabi

title: PageLLM: A Multi-Grained Reward Framework for Whole-Page Optimization with Large Language Models
abstract: Whole-page optimization (WPO) decides how search and recommendation results are surfaced to users, and large language models (LLMs) open a new route to it by treating page generation as sequence generation. Adapting LLMs to web-scale WPO, however, remains bottlenecked by the need for costly human annotations and by the mismatched granularity between page-level coherence and item-level placement. In this work we show that these two challenges are coupled: implicit user feedback alone suffices for alignment, provided the reward signal is decoupled into two complementary granularities. We propose

title: Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment
abstract: Self-evolving agents write interaction experience into artifacts and reuse them in later tasks. Most work supports such methods with three proxy signals: artifacts accumulate, behavior changes once they are loaded, and metrics rise. We call this signal-based evaluation. What these signals are meant to indicate, however, has not been defined. To fill this gap, we define capability formation from artifacts as five sequentially dependent properties, two of which form a checkpoint for capability formation, and introduce three-scale diagnosis, which judges these properties at the state, game, and l

title: A wider state, not wider arithmetic, for single-precision time integration
abstract: Single precision (FP32) halves the memory and data movement of double precision (FP64), and on accelerators is often several times faster. Its rounding errors are harmless except in the stored state. A modified equation for Runge-Kutta methods in Shu-Osher form and linear multistep methods separates the rounding of the stored state, a forcing proportional to $1/Δt$, from truncation and from right-hand-side rounding, which sets a $Δt$-independent floor. We bound this forcing for strong-stability-preserving schemes and identify two mechanisms that keep its sign fixed, so it accumulates as a bias

title: Scalable Full-Horizon SFC Deployment over Predictable SAGIN Topologies via Configurable Column Generation Framework
abstract: Space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs) integrate heterogeneous communication and computing resources to support ubiquitous services. Service function chains (SFCs) enable complex services to be composed of ordered functions and executed collaboratively across these resources. Mobility continuously reshapes connectivity throughout service execution, yet much of the resulting topology evolution is predictable. Decisions based only on isolated topology snapshots may therefore overlook valuable future connectivity. We formulate an admission-first, cost-aware model on a time-expanded graph f

title: TestHallVQA: Exploring LVLMs' Document-Level Reasoning under Redundant Contexts from Scientific Exams
abstract: Large Vision–Language Models (LVLMs) are increasingly expected to perform visual question answering (VQA) over planar media. However, existing planar VQA benchmarks typically emphasize isolated challenges: some emphasize long-document understanding with limited reasoning depth, while others require complex visual reasoning but remain restricted to single-page, noise-free settings. Moreover, through theoretical analysis, we identify the impact of irrelevant visual tokens, which leads to measurable performance degradation but has received little attention with respect to systematic quantificatio

title: TRIAD: Multimodal Retrieval across Abstraction, Constraints, and State
abstract: Multimodal retrieval increasingly supports agentic systems, where user requests can involve cross-level relations, combine multiple constraints, and evolve across dialogue turns. In these settings, a highly similar result may still violate the user's requirements, while retrieved content may directly inform downstream actions without human screening. We introduce TRIAD, a multimodal retrieval benchmark for evaluating how well retrieval systems satisfy these complex, evolving requests. TRIAD comprises three tracks: abstraction, testing bidirectional retrieval between visual instances and concep

title: PosIR: A Multilingual Benchmark for Diagnosing Position Bias in Information Retrieval
abstract: Position bias—the systematic effect of where key information is located on retrieval effectiveness—is a critical concern in information retrieval. Although recent studies have identified such bias in dense retrievers, existing analyses focus predominantly on monolingual English, fail to disentangle document length from information position, and lack a standardized framework for controlled evaluation. institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

title: Results from a Stellar Occultation by (623) Chimaera
abstract: We present results from a stellar occultation by the asteroid (623) Chimaera on October 21st, 2025, when it passed in front of V magnitude 13.86 star UCAC4 626-004193. Chimaera is the largest asteroid in the Chimaerid asteroid family and will be subject to a spacecraft flyby in the 2030s. Eighteen telescopes were deployed, spanning the United States from Arizona to North Carolina, incrementally spaced by $\sim4.4$\,km with respect to the cross-track of the shadow. title: Multi-Granularity Communication-Computing Resource Mapping for User Association in MEO-Assisted LEO Satellite Networks
abstract: Low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite networks are evolving into spaceborne communication-computing infrastructures. Their user association must jointly account for the radio link and the CPU, GPU, NPU, memory, cache, storage, energy, queue, and thermal states that determine executable service capacity. This paper studies a MEO-assisted LEO architecture in which medium-Earth-orbit (MEO) regional state aggregators collect and relay time-stamped telemetry, the network operation control center (NOCC) maintains the global logical resource view and makes the final association decisions, and LEO satellite

title: Short-term associations between wild-bird and mammalian high pathogenic avian influenza detection in the United States
abstract: High pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) detections in mammals have raised concern about repeated wildlife spillover and the targeting of mammalian surveillance. We evaluated whether wild-bird detection records contained short-term explanatory and predictive information about mammalian detections in the United States. Public surveillance records from April 2022 to July 2026 comprised 18,523 wild-bird and 815 mammalian detections. title: ProGram: A Grammar for Progressive Computation Pipelines
abstract: Progressive Visual Analytics (PVA) systems have demonstrated the effectiveness of time-bounded, incremental computation for exploring large-scale data. However, our survey reveals that existing PVA implementations are often difficult to reuse and extend, as their progressive behaviors are typically realized through ad hoc, hard-coded mechanisms distributed across servers and clients. To address this limitation, we present ProGram, a grammar for progressive computation pipelines. Informed by a comprehensive analysis of prior concepts and design practices in existing PVA systems, ProGram is desi

title: PACEE: Parent-Centered AI Scaffolding for Emotion Education in Early Childhood Conversations
abstract: Emotion education is critical for children aged 3 to 6. However, existing technologies depend substantially on direct child-AI interaction, overlooking the central role of parents in guiding early emotional development at home. To address this gap, we conducted co-design sessions with five kindergarten teachers and five parents to identify key parental challenges and opportunities for AI support in family emotion education. title: AutoCSF: A Provably Safe Indexing Framework for Filter-Augmented Compressed Static Functions
abstract: We consider the problem of building space-efficient indexes for static key-value datasets with highly skewed value distributions. A standard technique for this task is to augment a compressed static function (CSF) with an approximate set membership prefilter to handle a dominating value and break the one-bit-per-key barrier. However, we observe that prior approaches decide when to apply such a prefilter using idealized cost models or data-driven heuristics, and, as a result, can recommend using a prefilter in regimes where it actively increases space usage. institutions: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

title: WAVES: Wearable Active Vibroacoustic Elasticity Sensing for Low-Cost and Non-Invasive Muscle Stiffness Monitoring
abstract: Muscle stiffness is a physiologically meaningful biomarker associated with a wide range of musculoskeletal and neurological conditions. However, existing muscle stiffness assessment methods, such as shear wave elastography (SWE), manual palpation, and handheld mechanical probes, remain impractical for continuous, everyday monitoring due to bulky hardware, operator dependence, and limited self-use. Meanwhile, wearable muscle-sensing modalities such as Electromyography (EMG) and Mechanomyography (MMG) primarily capture muscle activation rather than passive mechanical properties of tissue at rest

title: A Proximal Newton Framework with Local Superlinear Convergence for Simple Bilevel Optimization
abstract: In this paper, we study a penalty method for simple bilevel optimization in which the lower-level objective has a convex composite structure. Our approach is based on a vanishing-penalty reformulation, which gives rise to a sequence of penalized problems as the penalty parameter decreases. A key difficulty is that metric subregularity of the lower-level optimality mapping does not, in general, yield a uniform error bound for the penalized problems as the penalty parameter vanishes, preventing a direct application of standard proximal Newton theory. institutions: Southern University of Science and Technology

title: DRAFT-Bench: Evaluating Frontier Agents Across the Professional Design Lifecycle
abstract: Can frontier general-purpose agents understand client intent, explore creative directions, execute revisions, and prepare production deliverables? We introduce DRAFT-Bench (Design Reliability Across Feedback and Tasks), a lifecycle-oriented evaluation of requirement elicitation, creative exploration, constrained editing, iterative revision, and production handoff. Its Requirement-to-Artifact framework links evolving requirements, protected properties, artifact versions, and delivery obligations. We compare native Codex/Astra and Claude Code across 35 design briefs under 43 conditions, alongsid

title: Setting the Stage: Enhancing Music Recommendations with Spoken Introductions to Stimulate Serendipity
abstract: People like to keep their music listening fresh and interesting, but recommender systems often struggle to support this need. Even when a recommended song is potentially refreshing and enriching, listeners may not perceive it as such. Building on Silvia's appraisal theory of interest, this paper studies whether enhancing recommendations with spoken introductions, immersive or informative, can stimulate two distinct flavors of experienced serendipity: taste-broadening (sparking interest in music outside one's typical preferences) and taste-deepening (deepening interest in music within one's typ

title: Integrating Domain Adaptation and Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Saline-Alkali Land Reclamation Planning
abstract: Reclamation of saline-alkali land requires management plans that account for soil and water conditions, treatment evidence, and financial constraints. This study develops Wenyao, an agricultural decision-support system integrating domain adaptation with retrieval-augmented generation. A bilingual corpus of 8,664 research papers was processed using a 110-indicator schema to construct SA-Bench, comprising 4,860 paper-level planning instances. A QwQ-32B model was adapted through low-rank supervised fine-tuning and combined with case retrieval for budget-conditioned planning. Evidence extraction a

title: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery
abstract: Hardware designs may be available only as gate-level netlists or input-output descriptions when the original register-transfer-level (RTL) design and documentation are not accessible. Low-level representations obscure word-level computation and its finite-width behavior. Recovering high-level RTL from such representations therefore helps engineers understand a circuit's functionality and enables RTL rewriting and resynthesis. A plausible function model is also insufficient unless the generated RTL is equivalent to the original circuit for all input combinations. In this paper, we present RTLRE

title: Mirage: Provable Defense Against LLM KV Cache Timing Side Channels with Topology-Aware Isolation
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as shared multi-tenant services, relying on advanced optimizations like KV cache and prefix sharing to improve throughput and reduce latency. However, these optimizations introduce a critical vulnerability: attackers can exploit time-to-first-token (TTFT) variations between KV cache hits and misses to infer sensitive prompt tokens via prefix-matching side-channel attacks. title: After the Higgs: Looking for the Universe Behind the Particle
abstract: Fourteen years after its discovery, the Higgs boson has changed roles. It was once the object of the search, but today it is an instrument with which we interrogate Nature's vacuum, test quantum field theory and look for new principles. This shift comes at a time when, unlike before the Higgs discovery, we have no theoretical argument guaranteeing new physics within experimental reach. At the same time, securing long-term support for fundamental science is becoming increasingly challenging. title: Can Large Language Models Review the Scientific Literature? A Test Against a 102-Article Benchmark
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support scientific literature reviews, yet evaluations often examine individual tasks rather than the review process as a whole. We assess six AI tools across four stages: finding relevant articles, interpreting them, synthesizing across them, and proposing future research. The benchmark is a published review of the Spanish plume weather pattern and its 102-article corpus. In the initial searches, five tools collectively identified 57 articles, with the best individual tool finding 42. Institutional library access increased discovery from 4

title: One number per hour is not enough: directional carbon intensity of data-center ramps on the PJM fleet
abstract: A data-center campus can change its load by hundreds of megawatts within an hour, yet every carbon signal in use gives one value per hour for a load change, whatever its size or direction. We compute the directional carbon intensity, the emission caused or avoided per megawatt-hour of a finite upward or downward ramp, for every hour of 2025 on the PJM Interconnection's fossil fleet, and compare it with the locational marginal emission rate (LME) and the regional average. The LME misstates a 1 GW ramp by more than 10% in 60% to 83% of hours in eleven months. Upward and downward ramps differ in

title: CascadeFilter: Cost-Efficient Semantic Filtering with Joint Threshold Selection
abstract: Semantic filtering selects records that satisfy a natural-language predicate and is an important operation in data analytics based on large language models (LLMs). Executing an expensive model on every document incurs substantial inference cost. Existing approaches reduce this cost by accepting predictions from cheaper models and forwarding uncertain records to an oracle. Task Cascades further varies document portions and operations, and provides an accuracy-guaranteed extension. institutions: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

title: Sweep Less, Steer More: Using Activation Steering Geometry for Reduced Hyperparameter Search
abstract: Representation steering methods like difference-in-means (DIM) offer a lightweight approach to controlling LLM behavior, but their effectiveness varies widely across concepts, datasets, and layers, making principled deployment costly without exhaustive hyperparameter sweeps. We build on the discriminability index $d'$, a compute-cheap geometric measure of how well contrastive training activations separate along the steering direction. Across five behaviors on 3 models, we demonstrate uses beyond its established role as a dataset-level steerability predictor. First, in the multiple-choice quest

title: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Recipe for Image Quality Enhancement
abstract: A real photograph is often blurry, grainy, compressed, scratched, and low-resolution at the same time. Each defect has its own severity and its own place in the image. The corrections for these defects conflict with each other. Exist- ing models describe the whole image with one description, so they cannot say where each correction belongs. To solve this problem, we present Wonder 4, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model for image quality enhancement. It corrects several defects of a real photograph at the same time, each in the region where it occurs. Every block of the model holds a mixture of N

title: Definability and Interpolation in Philosophy
abstract: This paper offers a light tour of occurrences of Craig’s interpolation theorem and Beth’s definability theorem in philosophy. There is no coherent research program with a central agenda around this theme in the literature, but extending the discussion in [9], we trace some lines and identify some issues in establishing contacts at this interface between the realms of logic and the philosophy of logic, of science, of language and information, epistemology, and metaphysics. Our presentation can also be viewed as a case study for more general aspects of the logic–philosophy interface.

title: Improving the performance of regularized Stokeslet simulations using Rosenbrock time integration methods
abstract: The method of regularized Stokeslets (MRS) is widely used to model fluid-structure interactions of microscopic bodies in viscous environments. Specifically, MRS computes the fluid velocity generated by regularized forces distributed on an immersed body, which in turn defines a system of ordinary differential equations with which to evolve the body so that the no-slip condition is enforced. title: Temporary gas turbines powering a US AI data center created a cross-state air pollution hotspot
abstract: Data centers increasingly use on-site gas turbines that regulators can treat as temporary. Two satellites show the fleet powering SpaceXAI's Colossus 2 raised local nitrogen dioxide columns by about half as it expanded, the most anomalous increase among 656 urban locations nationwide since 2020. Mississippi authorized the fleet, but two-thirds of the hotspot's 116,000 mostly Black residents live in Tennessee, and the hotspot contains no regulatory nitrogen dioxide monitor. title: Fueling Inflation Risks: An Oil Shortage Scenario
abstract: Central banks routinely use alternative scenarios to assess risks to the economic outlook, but these are usually generated from linear models that are unable to speak to the likelihood of extreme outcomes. We develop a nonlinear modeling framework that turns a narrative oil market scenario into a fully probabilistic assessment of the dynamics of oil and gasoline prices, aggregate inflation, and household inflation expectations. institutions: Center for Economic and Policy Research

title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
abstract: We construct a divergence-free velocity field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x},t)$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ that is a genuine function of position and carries both defining properties of turbulent transport: Richardson pair dispersion and a dissipative anomaly. No synthetic field has carried both, because the frame that gives the first destroys the field the second requires. institutions: Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats

title: Reliable Bistatic Ranging With Unreliable Communication Payloads
abstract: This paper addresses a key challenge in bistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC): \textit{How to achieve reliable ranging using communication data signals that cannot be reliably recovered?} In modern communication systems, data payloads typically occupy far more time-frequency resources than pilots, offering substantially more observations to improve sensing accuracy. Exploiting them requires recovering the transmitted symbols to form sensing references. However, propagation and reflection losses can severely weaken target echoes. title: PRISM-Bench: An Audio-Centric Diagnostic Benchmark for Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
abstract: Text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation has advanced rapidly, but its evaluation still underestimates the audio modality. Existing benchmarks either treat audio as an auxiliary component of video quality or assess it in isolation from audiovisual grounding, making it difficult to diagnose where current systems truly succeed or fail in audio generation. We present PRISM-Bench, the first audio-centric diagnostic benchmark for T2AV generation. title: Analyzing Simultaneous Charging Factors of Electric Vehicles Using Monte Carlo Simulation: A Case Study in Phu Quoc City, Vietnam
abstract: This study estimates the simultaneous charging factor (SCF) of electric vehicles (EVs) in Phu Quoc City, Vietnam, using a Monte Carlo simulation. Three planning scenarios (2030, 2035, and 2040) are developed from population-based EV uptake assumptions and vehicle-specific charging probability profiles over 24 hours, reflecting distinct operating patterns of motorbikes, cars, taxis, and buses. For each vehicle class and scenario, 1,000 simulation runs are performed to compute SCF and its uncertainty, reported via 95% confidence intervals. Results indicate that SCF decreases as EV penetration in
institutions: Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology and Engineering

title: Time-Aware Urban Flood Routing with Sticky Edge Closure on Forecast Depth: A Hanoi Case Study
abstract: During urban flash floods, commuters and guiding agencies require awareness towards which roads remain passable when a vehicle actually arrives, rather than relying solely on which links appear open at initial departure. Most existing flood-routing tools apply a single static snapshot to each route; meaning that corridors that appear clear initially can become flooded before arrival. This paper presents a routing engine that ingests a two-hour water forecast, renewed every 15 minutes, and plans each journey around roads that the forecast closes for that specific vehicle class. title: LongVidSearch: An Agentic Benchmark for Multi-hop Evidence Retrieval Planning in Long Videos
abstract: Long video question answering (Long-Video QA) increasingly relies on agentic tool use to retrieve evidence from long videos. In realistic settings, this process often requires multi-hop retrieval, where agents must iteratively gather multiple discontinuous evidence clips. However, existing long-video benchmarks are largely static: they rarely enforce strict multi-hop retrieval and typically lack a standardized evidence-access interface, making it difficult to separate failures in retrieval planning from those in answer generation. title: A Jump-Diffusion Model of Home Price Dynamics and Neighborhood Change
abstract: We develop a dynamical model that links the fluctuations of individual home prices to changes in the full distribution of home prices in an urban area. We model the price of an individual home as a jump-diffusion stochastic differential equation. To capture the dynamic and hyper-local economic conditions that drive the residential real estate market, we allow all parameters to depend on both time and neighborhood. In the mean-field limit, we derive the associated Fokker-Planck partial integro-differential equation (PIDE) governing the evolution of the home price distribution in a neighborhood.

title: Language Defaults Before Content: A Causal Layer Map of Multilingual Generation
abstract: Multilingual generation requires large language models (LLMs) to determine both what to say and in what language to say it, yet these two commitments are difficult to disentangle from model outputs alone. We use translation as a controlled probe: for multi-parallel segments that a model translates well in one language direction but poorly in another, content is held fixed while language varies. title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based main sample of 160 papers spanning four temporal periods and a separate purposive style-contrast sample of 40 papers. title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
abstract: Real-time long-video generation requires continuous output with consistent appearance and natural motion. Existing chunk-wise autoregressive methods face challenges in both generation efficiency and long-video quality: serialized denoising and history-cache refresh require two forward passes even with one-step denoising, and longer rollouts can degrade quality and cause camera drift. We propose Wave Forcing (WF), which co-designs generation, training, and execution for continuous video output with multi-step denoising. title: Optimizing Geo-replicated Deterministic Databases
abstract: In transactional databases, achieving active-active replication among geo-distributed replicas is challenging due to the high coordination cost in ensuring the serializability of concurrent cross-node transactions. Deterministic concurrency control (DCC) has emerged as a promising alternative: it establishes a global order for a batch of transactions before execution and thereby amortizes this coordination cost across the batch. title: From LLM Hallucinations to Inspiration in Creative Work
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can introduce unexpected ideas through hallucinations, yet little is known about when creative practitioners find these errors inspiring or how these judgments shape interactions. We conducted a retrospective qualitative study with 20 experienced practitioners in research, design, and social media content creation, thematically analyzing 41 hallucination cases and 20 semi-structured interviews. title: A Geometric Theory for Nonequilibrium Transformer Dynamics
abstract: We develop a variational and geometric theory based on statistical physics for the joint evolution of Transformer attention and token representations at fixed model parameters. To this end, we introduce a free energy for the attention and model the evolution of the attention weights by its Fisher--Rao gradient flow. title: LLM-Generated Investment Research Memos Need Validation
abstract: LLMs are increasingly adopted to draft long-form investment research memos, but their reliability is judged claim by claim, while readers read each memo as a whole. In this paper, we show that a low claim-level error rate does not necessarily mean that a memo is reliable: even with a refutation rate of just 1-2%, roughly four in ten memos contain at least one claim contradicted by official filings. title: From Geometry to Function: A Multi-Task LiDAR Benchmark Dataset for Semantic and Functional Parsing of Urban Facades
abstract: Understanding building facades is central to urban digital twins, heritage modelling, and sustainable city analysis, yet existing LiDAR benchmarks stop at geometry and semantic segmentation and offer little support for reasoning about the functional role of each architectural element. We introduce HFX3D, a large-scale urban facade benchmark of approximately 492 million LiDAR points from 26 buildings in Halifax, Canada, captured across four seasons, day and night, and varied weather. title: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments
abstract: Current mobile GUI agent benchmarks systematically fail to assess memory capabilities, with only 5.2-11.8% memory-related tasks and no cross-session learning evaluation. We introduce MemGUI-Bench, a comprehensive memory-centric benchmark with pass@k and staged LLM-as-judge evaluation. Our contributions include: (1) a systematic memory taxonomy analyzing 11 agents across 5 architectures; (2) 128 tasks across 26 applications where 89.8% challenge memory through cross-temporal and cross-spatial retention; (3) MemGUI-Eval, an automated pipeline with Progressive Scrutiny and 7 hierarchical metrics;

title: BECON: Belief-Conditioned Constrained Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Drifting Preferences and Budgets
abstract: Constrained preference-conditioned MORL typically assumes full task observability, treating preferences and safety budgets as stationary task signals. In real-world deployment, however, these signals are often unreliable proxies: intent may drift, safety tolerances may shift with context, and exposed descriptors may be noisy, delayed, or incomplete. We therefore formulate constrained preference-conditioned MORL as a partially observed task-specification problem, where the agent must navigate a fundamental conflict between unreliable external signals and latent interaction dynamics. title: SemanticSlider3D: Training-Free Continuous Semantic Editing for 3D Objects
abstract: Fine-grained control over continuous semantic attributes of 3D objects is essential for 3D content creation, but is not well supported by conventional 3D modeling workflows or prompt-based interaction with existing generative AI tools. While slider-based methods have proven effective for fine-grained semantic control in 2D image generation, no equivalent approach exists for 3D. Extending these 2D methods to 3D is non-trivial due to challenges unique to 3D, including geometric integrity and cross-view coherence. title: Measuring Public Institutions and their Agents: Disparities and Agreement, with Application to Asylum Decisions in the U.S. Immigration Courts
abstract: Public institutions derive their legitimacy from the professionalism and impartiality of their agents. In order to maintain standards of conduct, the performance of an agent is often compared to the performance of her peers. But public institutions typically assign agents to different tasks, and as a result, naive comparisons may reflect the difficulty of the assignment and not an agent's performance. title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used for information access, content production, and agent-based task execution, but their outputs remain vulnerable to subtle, high-risk hallucinations. To systematically evaluate and advance post-generation hallucination detection, we introduce HaluCheck, a large-scale, bilingual benchmark comprising over 42k instances spanning both factual hallucinations in text and faithfulness hallucinations in agent trajectories. abstract: We study how to compute valid dual bounds for mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) with finite variable bounds under data perturbations. In an offline-online setting, a nominal instance is solved once and its information is reused to evaluate perturbations. abstract: This paper develops Bayesian wombling, or boundary analysis for tracking invasive species. We focus on three invasive species of concern in North America: Lycorma delicatula, Adelges tsugae, and Microstegium vimineum. We aim to demonstrate the applicability of wombling for supporting invasive pest management activities. abstract: We compute the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-$N_c$ limit using the Twisted Eguchi-Kawai (TEK) reduced model. abstract: Both the heart and the brain are built from electrically excitable cells, yet the emergent dynamics of these organs could not differ more. In the myocardium, a coherent traveling wave of action potentials ensures coordinated contraction; in the cerebral cortex, distributed, irregular spiking underlies efficient information processing and the generation of behavior. abstract: In the parity doublet model the nucleon mass includes a chiral invariant part $m_0$, which is conventionally assumed to be medium independent. abstract: Abstract Glycosylation is widespread in biology and shapes molecular recognition, yet the diversity and biosynthetic organization of viral glycosyltransferases (GTs) remain poorly understood. Here we integrate structural-alphabet-guided searches and structure similarity networks with genomic-neighbourhood and biosynthetic gene cluster embedding analyses to examine viral GT-A proteins. title: A liquid vapor phase transition in quantum statistical mechanics
abstract: We prove a liquid vapor phase transition for a quantum system of particles in the continuum. The system is the quantum version with Boltzmann statistics of the point particles model introduced in by Lebowitz, Mazel and Presutti.

abstract: There are exceedingly few chemical abundance measurements available in the literature for K dwarf stars, especially for those with T$_{eff} <$ 4700 K due to an incompatibility of traditional analyses with their molecular-line-ridden optical spectra. abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people seek and consume information, including accounts that differ across languages and regions, especially on contested topics. abstract: Heavy-quark spin correlations in small-$x$ deep-inelastic scattering receive corrections beyond the back-to-back limit. abstract: Accurate forecasting of Earth's dynamic systems is vital in geophysics, where neural operators offer a powerful data-driven paradigm. Standard operators often treat the Earth as a flat Euclidean plane, introducing geometric artifacts. abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly used to support freight transportation decisions, but their predictions are rarely accompanied by evidence that the associated explanations can be trusted. abstract: We introduce a graph attention network for reconstructing near-surface air temperature fields from incomplete observations. abstract: Mesoscale eddies carry most of the ocean's kinetic energy and move heat, salt and nutrients across basins, yet where an eddy will be two weeks ahead is still read off ocean models with post-hoc tracking heuristics. We introduce HaiRuo, which forecasts eddies as fields and as objects at once: from 30 days of satellite sea-level maps, one forward pass returns 15 days of sea level and geostrophic velocity, daily eddy masks and the trajectory of every eddy alive today. abstract: Species distribution modelling is a widely used approach for studying species’ environmental niches and identifying the main drivers of species distribution. title: Tropical Cyclones Increasingly Reach Peak Intensity Near Continental Landfall
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclones (TCs) typically weaken before landfall after reaching peak intensity over the open ocean. Here we show that this behavior has changed markedly in recent decades. Using global best‐track and reanalysis data sets from 1980 to 2023, we find a significant increase in TCs that intensify within 24 hr of landfall and attain peak intensity at or near the continental coast. abstract: Abstract Land‐derived nitrate degrades coastal groundwater quality, with denitrification in intertidal aquifers serving as a critical barrier to its seaward flux. While geologic heterogeneity has been recognized as a key factor affecting nitrate transport, denitrification, and discharge in coastal aquifers, few studies have investigated how fractures regulate nitrate fate, particularly the main fractures dominating water flow. abstract: Extreme precipitation over South China is commonly attributed to tropical sea surface temperature forcing, yet the role of extratropical circulation remains unclear. Using observational and reanalysis data, Rossby wave propagation diagnostics and numerical experiments, we investigate record-breaking April–May 2024 rainfall. title: Regional Contrasts in the Mechanisms and Thermal Impacts of Surface Strong‐Wind Events Along the Ross Sea Coast, Antarctica
abstract: Abstract Surface strong wind events (SWEs) along the Ross Sea coast are often treated as a common phenomenon, but our results show that the three main hotspots represent distinct regional regimes. Using a 2014–2023 database from coastal automatic weather stations, ERA5, we compare SWEs in Terra Nova Bay (TNB), Ross Island (RI), and Siple Coast (SC). TNB shows the most persistent events and is dominated by East Antarctic outflow, RI exhibits mixed pathways, and SC is controlled by West Antarctic air. abstract: Abstract The Early Eocene Climatic Optimum (53 to 49 million years ago) was an interval in Earth’s history when reconstructed temperatures and atmospheric CO 2 concentrations were among the highest of the Cenozoic Era (that is, the last 66 million years). The causes of the high CO 2 levels remain unclear. CO 2 changes over recent ice age cycles appear to be largely controlled by the biologically mediated build-up and release of carbon from the Southern Ocean, a process that might have also played a role earlier in the Cenozoic. abstract: Abstract Heterotrophic bacterial metabolism is a globally critical component of the marine carbon cycle, but its progression within a complex network of compounds and organisms challenges our ability to quantify carbon fate. Currently unresolved are the genomic underpinnings that control the path of carbon through microbial food webs and the role of metabolic exchange in these dynamics. abstract: In the summer of 2025, the first thorough archaeological research of a potentially polluting wreck HMS Cassandra was carried out in Estonia. HMS Cassandra , which sank in 1918 was a British light cruiser with a maximum capacity of about 1100 cubic meters of fuel oil. The research included a high-resolution multibeam survey combined with the creation of a photogrammetric model of the wreck. title: Detecting the Oceanic Moho Using Teleseismic P‐Wave Coda Autocorrelations of Ocean Bottom Seismograph Records
abstract: Abstract Although active‐source seismic methods can image the oceanic Mohorovičić discontinuity (Moho) at high resolution, their high cost motivates passive approaches using OBS, for which receiver functions (RF) are often complicated by instrument tilt, azimuthal misalignment, sedimentary layers, and water‐column reverberations. title: Hydrodynamic controls on harmful algal bloom connectivity in an estuarine system: insights for monitoring
abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose a significant threat to aquatic ecosystems and public health. In the Chowan River-Albemarle Sound system of North Carolina, recurrent HABs pose persistent ecological and management challenges. abstract: The ocean plays a critical role in sequestering carbon, yet how the air–sea carbon sink will respond to rapid reductions in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations remains a key uncertainty for climate mitigation and carbon accounting. In this study, we utilize the ECCO-Darwin ocean biogeochemistry model to simulate the ocean's response to a range of near-term CO 2 mitigation scenarios which are simulated with reduced atmospheric carbon concentrations. title: Dynamical precursors to summer temperature extremes on the Antarctic Peninsula
abstract: Extreme warm summer near-surface temperatures over the Antarctic Peninsula (AP) can lead to surface melting and the disintegration of ice shelves. While individual case studies have linked such events to anomalous large-scale circulation, a systematic assessment of the dynamical pathways leading to AP-wide extreme austral summer warm events remains limited. This study uses ERA5 reanalysis data to investigate the large-scale dynamical precursors associated with extreme warm days over the Antarctic Peninsula. abstract: Abstract The Ocean Induced Magnetic Field (OIMF) is produced by the motion of the electrically conducting ocean through Earth's ambient magnetic field, and its time‐dependence carries information concerning ocean dynamics and electrical conductivity changes. Here, we present an algorithm to estimate, from satellite magnetic field observations, the band‐limited OIMF, focusing on annual variations (periods 300–430 days) and spherical harmonic degrees 19 to 28. title: Iceberg‐Generated Waves From SWOT: Disintegration of Iceberg A‐76A in the Southern Ocean
abstract: Abstract Amid rising global temperatures, icebergs are calving more often and drifting into open waters. Their disintegration processes can trigger energetic surface gravity waves that propagate away from the iceberg remain poorly documented. This study presents an analysis of 12 iceberg‐generated wave fields associated with the disintegration of iceberg A‐76A, utilizing sea surface height anomaly data from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission. We analyzed wave height, wavelength, depth regime, and Time Since Impact (TSI) using wavelet scalograms matched to dispersion curves.

title: Fractal attractor of the deep convection cycle in the northwest Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Deep convection in the Gulf of Lion is an important ocean mixing process in the western Mediterranean Sea caused by large cooling fluxes at the sea surface. It aids the Mediterranean thermohaline circulation, and promotes phytoplankton blooming. This work investigates the three different periods of the process: preconditioning, deep convecting, and restratification, through the lens of fractal attractor analysis with the local correlation dimension. abstract: The hydrodynamic characterization of Marajó Bay was conducted through computational modeling using SisBaHiA®, aiming to identify tidal types and amplitudes, flood and ebb slack waters, high and low tides, the relationship between flow velocity and water level elevation, and phase differences. abstract: Abstract In September 2024, record-breaking rainfall caused severe flooding and landslides in the Noto region, Japan, where recovery from the devastating Noto Peninsula earthquake was still ongoing. During this event, the Sea of Japan experienced record warmth, with monthly-mean sea surface temperature anomaly of + 2.9 °C. title: Non-local numerical modelling of riverbank stability during rainfall events
abstract: This study examines the stability of a near-vertical riverbank composed of homogeneous, highly over-consolidated, weakly cemented clayey silt in the event of prolonged rainfall. In the numerical study, a non-local modelling approach was employed to accurately reproduce the formation and propagation of the shear band that caused the bank to collapse. abstract: Abstract A harsh marine environment causes severe surface damage to underwater infrastructure, jeopardizing its long-term reliability and necessitating in-situ underwater repair. Underwater laser additive manufacturing (ULAM) is a promising technique that enables direct deposition of metallic materials on water-exposed components. abstract: This work presents a thorough experimental and numerical investigation into the mechanical behavior of sandwich panels subjected to three/four-point bending, as well as flatwise and edgewise compression. The studied structure is designed for aerospace and marine applications, aiming to optimize the trade-off between weight and stiffness. The core consists of a 10 mm thick, grooved, closed-cell Airex C70.55 PVC foam. title: Wave and slope thresholds for mangrove restoration and nature-based solution design
abstract: Abstract Globally, shorelines are experiencing widespread recession, promoting greater interest in nature-based solutions (NbSs) for coastal protection. Along tropical and sub-tropical coastlines, mangroves are among the habitat-forming species increasingly targeted for nature-based coastal protection. title: Future projections of compound events around the Main Hawaiian Islands
abstract: The consequences of overlapping environmental stressors – referred to as compound events – may be more harmful to marine ecosystems than as individual stressors. Using recently conducted submesoscale-permitting future projections for the Main Hawaiian Islands, we present the first assessment of future compound events for Hawaiian waters. abstract: The Indian Ocean plays a critical role in the global climate system by regulating heat and moisture transport, influencing major fluxes that drive atmospheric circulation. abstract: Antarctic surface mass balance (SMB) projections are a major source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise estimates, and regional climate models (RCMs), thanks to their finer resolution and polar-tailored physics, are increasingly used to refine and complement Earth System Model (ESM) projections. abstract: Abstract The global transition to low‐carbon energy systems is driving demand for lithium, a critical raw material for battery storage technologies. abstract: Aerosol vertical distributions are a major source of uncertainty in quantifying aerosol–cloud–climate interactions. Using observations collected during the 2022 TRACER campaign in Houston, Texas, we investigate how atmospheric boundary layer dynamics shape the vertical structure of aerosol populations in a coastal urban environment. abstract: Ice-rich Arctic permafrost coasts are eroding rapidly, threatening ecosystems, infrastructure and cultural heritage. Herschel Island Qikiqtaruk (HIQ), Yukon, Canada, combines ice-rich permafrost with heritage buildings and park infrastructure at the shoreline, but the most recent island-wide records of shoreline change end in 2011. abstract: Abstract Wind‐generated near‐inertial waves (NIWs) are important pathways for transferring wind energy into the ocean interior, yet their propagation is strongly modulated by mesoscale eddies. The wave‐train index (WI) and blocking index (BI) have been used to classify cold surge events that were first identified using surface temperature and Siberian High criteria, but their utility for detecting cold surge candidates directly from index time series has not been fully evaluated. abstract: Prevailing models of neurodegeneration center on amyloid-β and tau, yet metabolic dysfunction precedes proteinopathy by decades. title: Increased Hydrological Connectivity Does Not Always Lead to Increased Nutrient Removal Potential in a Coastal River Delta
abstract: Abstract Coastal river deltas can act as important nitrate sinks, reducing nutrient loads that contribute to coastal hypoxia. Their removal capacity depends not only on local biogeochemical conditions but also on the transport pathways of nutrients through the delta. Nutrient transport to key processing areas, the deltaic islands, is governed by hydrological connectivity, which varies with discharge and seasonal vegetation. However, this species is particularly vulnerable due to overfishing, high genetic fragmentation, late first reproduction, and the restriction of spawning to limited, heavily impacted coastal areas. abstract: Abstract Central Pacific (CP) El Niño‐Southern Oscillation (ENSO) variability has intensified since the late 1990s. Existing literature has emphasized the role of upper‐ocean stratification in modulating ENSO, primarily focusing on decadal thermal changes. This study further demonstrates that the regime shift of ENSO is modulated by the increasing salinity in the CP region. abstract: Abstract Mixed transitional layer instability (MTI) was proposed as a mechanism to generate deep‐penetrating submesoscale processes (submesoscales) in the upper ocean. abstract: Tidal hydrokinetic turbines offer promising opportunities for energy generation, but turbine-induced turbulence may alter fish movement, passage and habitat use. title: Increasing trends in the severity of Australian fire weather conditions over the past century
abstract: Understanding how weather and climate influence fire risk is important for many purposes, including climate adaptation planning and decision-making in sectors such as emergency management, finance, health and infrastructure (e.g. for energy and water availability). In this study, bias-corrected 20CRv2c (Twentieth Century Reanalysis ver. 2c) reanalysis data are used to investigate the climatology and long-term trends of weather conditions associated with landscape fires in Australia. abstract: Abstract The magnetic perturbations generated by Europa's plasma interaction undergo oscillatory variations since Jupiter's magnetospheric current sheet periodically sweeps across the moon. abstract: Abstract Passive microwave observations have been actively assimilated into numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems due to their ability to provide atmospheric thermodynamic information even under cloudy conditions. However, the presence of ice crystals and large hydrometeors causes significant scattering of microwave radiances, leading to signals that differ substantially from clear-sky conditions. abstract: This study investigates the hydrodynamics of the inner shelf in the lee of the jetties at the Patos Lagoon mouth, Brazil. The jetties extend approximately 4 km offshore, nearly perpendicular to the coastline, and represent the only rigid structure along an otherwise uninterrupted sandy coast. abstract: Abstract The Great Green Wall (GGW) initiative aims to restore 100 million hectares of degraded land across 22 African countries by 2030, as a flagship initiative under the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification. title: New Kinematic Constraints on Tectonic Extrusion in Southwestern Taiwan From a Mud Volcano Offset by a Creeping Fault
abstract: Abstract Southwestern Taiwan consists of a fold‐and‐thrust belt undergoing southwestward tectonic extrusion. abstract: This study investigates the seasonal hydrogeochemical evolution and persistent hydrogeological controls in a salinized shallow aquifer-aquitard system located in a reclaimed coastal lowland. The study focuses on two adjacent agricultural field plots with contrasting hydrostratigraphic settings. abstract: Arid and semi-arid environments are highly sensitive to climate variability and water scarcity, yet theecohydrological dynamics of many coastal deserts in southern Peru remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Chlorophyll regulates solar radiation absorption in the upper ocean, influencing the ocean's mean state and climate. abstract: Abstract Wave energy (WE) flux aligns with the direction of group velocity, in contrast to the conventional Eliassen‐Palm (EP) flux, which describes wave activity transfers. abstract: Coastal lagoons are heterogeneous and highly dynamic ecosystems that are particularly sensitive to anthropogenic pressures. However, across South Asia, an anomalous trend of moistening, indicated by an increase in surface relative humidity (RH), has been observed in recent decades despite continued land-surface warming. abstract: Abstract It is well-known that fronts, atmospheric rivers (ARs), and mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) are important weather phenomena linked to hydrological events. abstract: Abstract Extreme precipitation has intensified over North China during the early twenty‐first century, yet the interplay among thermodynamic moistening, atmospheric circulation, and decadal ocean variability remains insufficiently understood. Here we investigate summer precipitation extremes over the Beijing‐Tianjin‐Hebei (BTH) region using daily observations. title: Spring Westerly Winds Shape Early Precursors of El Niño Diversity Across the Spring Predictability Barrier
abstract: Abstract Predicting El Niño diversity, specifically the distinction between Eastern Pacific (EP) and Central Pacific (CP) events, remains challenging due to the boreal spring predictability barrier (SPB) and the inconsistent detection inherent in discrete wind‐burst metrics. abstract: We identify materially defined regions in unsteady two-dimensional flows that combine finite-time contraction with elevated accumulated intrinsic rotation along trajectories, which we term Lagrangian rotating contracting structures. These regions are detected using existing objective diagnostics-the Lagrangian-averaged vorticity deviation (LAVD) together with direct tests of material contraction-without relying on the geometry of LAVD level sets. title: Changes in Regional Extreme Cold Events over Northern China and Their Circulation Associations Under Arctic Amplification
abstract: In recent decades, rapid Arctic warming has intensified Arctic amplification (AA), and its potential impacts on mid-latitude extreme weather events have received increasing attention. Using meteorological station observations and reanalysis datasets from 1979 to 2024, this study investigates the variations of regional extreme cold events (RECEs) over Northern China and their associated circulation characteristics under different Arctic amplification periods. In this study, a novel round gyroid triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) metamaterial is designed, fabricated 3D printing, and systematically investigated under quasi-static compression loading. abstract: Renewable energy assets are certified against hazard functions that classical reliability theory treats as fixed in time, yet the climate driving heat stress, humidity, wind extremes, and flooding is shifting in ways that make stationarity untenable for long‑lived infrastructure. abstract: Abstract Saharan dust outbreaks are a major source of atmospheric variability over Southern Europe and are known to reduce photovoltaic (PV) power generation through aerosol‐induced attenuation of solar radiation. However, the relative importance of direct dust radiative effects and indirect aerosol–cloud interactions remains poorly constrained. abstract: Abstract An extensive body of literature has documented declines in western U.S. snow, including increases in snow drought (extreme low snow), but the spatial extent of snow extremes may also substantially impact the consequences of snow losses and has been relatively underexamined. abstract: Abstract Precipitation-phase transitions in winter storms remain difficult to predict because they depend sensitively on the depth and evolution of near-0 °C stratification in the lower troposphere. title: Multi-scale dynamics and mesoscale drivers of the catastrophic September 2022 Marche (central Italy) flood
abstract: The catastrophic flood that hit the Marche region (central Italy) on 15 September 2022 has been analyzed using high-resolution Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model simulations. The convective rainfall event responsible for the flood was favored by the passage of warm, moist air masses that interacted with the central Apennines. title: Major volcanic eruptions episodically disrupted the continuity of polar warming through aerosol forcing
abstract: Abstract The polar regions are warming rapidly, exceeding the global average due to greenhouse gas emissions from human activities. Using CMIP6 simulations, HadCRUT5 data, and MERRA-2 aerosol records, this study shows that major 20th-century volcanic eruptions, Agung (1963), El Chichón (1982), and Pinatubo (1991) temporarily offset polar warming through sulfate-induced cooling. title: Hydroelastic optimization of submerged composite foils with flutter and ventilation constraints
abstract: Abstract Hydrofoils impact the speed and efficiency of high-performance marine vessels, and their hydrodynamic loads scale with the square of speed. Designers can exploit the material anisotropy of composite materials to tailor the deformed shape under hydrodynamic loading. Composite hydrofoils face design challenges, two of which are flutter instability and ventilation inception. abstract: Piled port structures experience repeated operational loading that may degrade soil–pile interaction and reduce foundation capacity over time. abstract: Characterizing compound drought–heat extremes remains challenging because inferred event characteristics are sensitive to event definition and dataset representation, including climate-variable dependence. abstract: Abstract The pattern of sea surface temperature (SST) warming in the tropics modulates global climate variability. However, the key physical processes that govern this pattern remain poorly understood. This study investigates the influence of high- and low-cloud radiative effects on the tropical SST warming pattern from 1985 to 2014. abstract: ABSTRACT We analyzed the environmental fields of moderate non‐mountain wave turbulence around the Baiu front in Japan from 2010 to 2017. Using reanalysis data, we extracted the Baiu front and calculated 14 turbulence diagnostics. A higher number of turbulence encounters was recorded on the north of the Baiu front. abstract: As a key component for perception of the environment and structural response, the normal operation of sensors is crucial for the safety assessment of pipe-rack offshore platforms. However, in long-term service, sensors on the jacket platform are susceptible to high salt-spray corrosion and strong vibration in marine environments, which can lead to bias, drift, accuracy degradation, gain anomaly, and stuck-at faults. abstract: Abstract The United States (US) summer warming hole, marked by muted warming or cooling in maximum dry‐bulb temperature ( T max ) across parts of the central and southeastern US, is a regional exception to broader warming. abstract: In this paper, a new set of depth-integrated double-averaged Navier–Stokes equations (DIDANS equations), which describe 1D unsteady vegetated flow, is derived. title: A Paired Lake–Land Observation Dataset of Mesoscale Lakes over the Tibetan Plateau for Analyzing Lake-induced Thermal and Moisture Modulation
abstract: Abstract Lakes on the Tibetan Plateau are sensitive indicators of climate change and important regulators of local land–atmosphere exchanges. However, continuous in situ observations remain limited, especially for mesoscale lakes with lake areas of 100–500 km 2 . abstract: The JUpiter ICy moons Explorer spacecraft (JUICE) successfully performed a Lunar and Earth gravity assist maneuver on 19 and 20 August 2024, which provided an excellent opportunity to test its instruments before its arrival at Jupiter in 2031. title: Modeling Mud as Flocculated and Suspended Bed‐Material Load in Rivers and Deltas
abstract: Abstract Mud transport in coastal rivers and deltas is important for understanding land loss, carbon cycling, and landscape evolution. Mud is often treated differently than sand due to the effects of cohesion on bed entrainment and because of vanishingly small settling rates that can result in washload behavior. abstract: Air entrainment often plays a crucial role in determining impact loads exerted by free-surface wave flows interacting with structures, yet its modeling is often oversimplified in numerical approaches. In this study, a two-phase numerical model, based on the Lattice Boltzmann Method coupled to a conservative Allen–Cahn interface-capturing equation, is employed to perform three-dimensional simulations of dam-break waves propagating over a dry bed and impacting vertical walls. abstract: ABSTRACT In this paper, open‐hole compression (OHC) tests were conducted on quasi‐isotropic (QI) laminates to compare the performance of drilled and molded holes. abstract: Extreme precipitation estimation commonly assumes stationarity, although climate variability can modify its temporal distribution. abstract: Abstract Precipitation is a critical driver of the hydrological cycle in the mountainous Colombian Andes (mCA), yet its diurnal organization remains complex due to significant orographic modulation. abstract: The nighttime ozone chemical equilibrium (NOCE) is a key assumption widely employed in various applications within the mesopause region, such as retrieving difficult-to-measure characteristics from observational data. abstract: The installed capacity of floating photovoltaics (FPV) is growing, and deployment at more exposed locations, such as larger lakes and nearshore or offshore environments, is increasingly being considered. abstract: Grabens and arrays of sub-parallel synthetic normal faults are typical geologic structures that develop in extensional systems. abstract: To better identify emission sources of airborne plastics, we employed nine plastic-associated chemicals (PlsACs) in 240 daily PM2.5 samples collected in Singapore during 2018-2020. abstract: Wave energy remains pre-commercial despite European targets of 1 GW ocean energy capacity by 2030 and 40 GW by 2050. title: Mining Fossil Water: A Review of Groundwater Depletion, Recharge and Sustainable Management of the Nubian Sandstone Aquifer System
abstract: The Nubian Sandstone Aquifer System (NSAS), shared by Egypt, Libya, Sudan and Chad, is the largest fossil groundwater system on Earth, underlying about two million square kilometres of the eastern Sahara. Most of its water was recharged during humid periods of the Pleistocene and early Holocene and is effectively non-renewable on human timescales. abstract: The South Asian High (SAH) is an important component of the Asian monsoon system. Studies have indicated that meridional movement of the SAH can exert substantial influences on the weather and climate over surrounding and remote regions. This study shows that the meridional movement of the SAH can be divided into three types. The first type represents the meridional movement of the whole SAH (WBSM). title: Sediment properties regulate pioneer plant performance in salt marshes: a mesocosm study of Salicornia spp.
abstract: Salt marshes dynamically adapt to a range of environmental boundary conditions and their long-term resilience depends on feedbacks between vegetation, sediment, and hydrodynamics. The vegetation of the pioneer zone, a transitional area located between the tidal flats to the vegetated salt marshes, contains very few species.
