title: Statistics of moisture sources for extreme precipitation events over the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei-Shanxi region of 1983–2022
abstract: ABSTRACT This study employs a Lagrangian model (FLEXPART) to identify the major moisture sources and quantify their contributions to representative extreme precipitation events (REPEs) over the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei-Shanxi region from May to September of 1983–2022. The role of circulation anomalies on modulating moisture transport and source contributions is also examined. title: The Combined Effects of Temperature and Grain Size on Nitrate and Colloid Transport in Saturated Porous Media
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the combined effects of temperature and media grain size on nitrate and colloid transport in saturated porous media using laboratory column experiments and numerical modelling. Experimental treatments consisted of three temperatures (15°C, 30°C, and 45°C) and three granular media with different grain size ranges: fine (0.6–1.2 mm), medium (1.2–2.4 mm), and coarse (2.4–4.8 mm). title: Convectively‐Induced Turbulence: High‐Resolution Aircraft Measurements Over Central Argentina
abstract: Abstract We investigate a convectively‐induced turbulence (CIT) event encountered by the German High‐Altitude Long‐Range research aircraft (HALO) over central Argentina during the Southern Hemisphere Transport, Dynamics, and Chemistry campaign. Convectively‐induced turbulence is analyzed using in situ 1, 10‐, and 100‐Hz flight‐level data, complemented by radar data, satellite imagery, and high‐resolution numerical model outputs. title: What Controls the Seasonality of Poleward Energy Transport by Intense Extratropical Cyclones?
abstract: Abstract Intense extratropical cyclones shape midlatitude weather extremes, but their role in the seasonal cycle of poleward energy transport remains poorly constrained. Here we develop a localized, Lagrangian‐mean moist static energy (MSE) framework that combines objective feature tracking with the Eulerian‐mean MSE budget. The framework attributes stormtrack intensity to individual cyclones, anticyclones, and the sources and sinks of their associated heat transport. abstract: Abstract Context Jack pine budworm (JPBW), Choristoneura pinus pinus, is a major defoliator in Canada, yet remains absent from theoretical discourse on outbreak synchrony, despite sharing key life history traits with the archetypal “cross-scale” pest, spruce budworm (C. fumiferana). JPBW has primarily been studied in host-rich landscapes, raising questions about its behavior in host-sparse regions. title: Investigating the transition in ice dynamics from a land- to lake-terminating glacier using a simple glacier dynamics model
abstract: Glaciers interact with adjacent proglacial lakes through a range of thermomechanical processes. These interactions occur in addition to climate-driven ablation and are capable of amplifying or modifying climatic effects through various feedback mechanisms. title: Contrasting dynamical and thermodynamical pathways shaped the 2024 North-Central Indian heatwave
abstract: Abstract An unprecedented heatwave affected North-Central India (NCI) during the 2024 pre-monsoon season, with two connected episodes, against the backdrop of the warmest year on record and Pacific sea-surface temperature conditions favorable for extreme heat. This superposition makes it difficult to determine whether the event was driven by natural climate variability or background influence of global warming. title: Performance Investigation of a Solar-Driven Air Gap Membrane Distillation System Coupled with PEM Electrolysis for Sustainable Water and Hydrogen Production
abstract: Freshwater scarcity and the rising demand for clean energy standout as two ofthe most pressing global challenges, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. To tackle these interconnected issues, this study explores an innovative approach utilizing a solar-powered Air Gap Membrane Distillation (AGMD) system integrated with a Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolyzer.This hybrid system is designed for the simultaneousproduction of freshwater and green hydrogen. abstract: Abstract In steelmaking, inert gas injection is widely employed during ladle refining to enhance mixing and promote chemical reactions. Argon is injected through the bottom of the ladle, inducing a turbulent recirculating flow that improves heat and mass transfer. This agitation promotes molten metal homogenization, inclusion removal via the slag layer, alloy mixing, and slag-metal reactions. title: Power Coefficient Variation of an H-Darrieus Turbine with S1046 Airfoils at Different Tip Speed Ratios
abstract: Vertical Axis Wind Turbine (VAWT) efficiency is influenced by the airfoils´ geometry and its rotational speed. Previous research has been conducted to increase the Power Coefficient (Cp) using mainly NACA airfoils and reporting cycle-averaged performance parameters. However, the effect of the Tip Speed Ratio (TSR) on the instantaneous evolution of Cp and the Torque Coefficient (Ct) per cycle, as well as its relationship with the flow field in contact with the blades, has not been fully characterized. title: Two distinct modes of North American spring temperature evolution shaped by tropical SST regimes and midlatitude circulation
abstract: Abnormal temperature fluctuations during spring can substantially impact vegetation growth, agricultural productivity, and ecosystem stability. However, the physical processes underlying year-to-year variations in the evolution of North American spring temperature anomalies remain poorly understood. Here, we apply Season-reliant Empirical Orthogonal Function (S-EOF) analysis to identify the leading modes of spring temperature evolution over North America. title: Quantifying capillary trapping in coal matrices and its impact on coal seam gas recovery
abstract: Coal is a dual-porosity system comprising matrices and cleats; more than 90% of coal seam gas (CSG) is stored in an adsorbed state within the microporous matrices, while formation water occupies larger pores and cleats. Gas production is therefore controlled by the coupled processes of gas-water and matrix-cleat interactions. title: Numerical simulation of water-sediment two-phase erosion in a split-frame aqueduct and comparison of pier geometry schemes
abstract: To investigate local erosion in split-frame aqueducts under sediment-laden flow, a three-dimensional water–sediment two-phase numerical model was developed using the RNG k–ε turbulence model, the Discrete Phase Model (DPM), and the Neilson–Gilchrist erosion model. title: The last builders of megaliths in the South of the Iberian peninsula? The Bronze Age necropolis of Trafalgar (Barbate, Cádiz, Spain)
abstract: The archaeological excavations undertaken at the Trafalgar tombolo during 2021-2022 led to the identification of a Bronze Age megalithic necropolis. This paper presents an interdisciplinary study, considering chronological, structural, bioarchaeological, and archaeometrical evidence of two megalithic tombs. The main aim of this work is to date both tombs through the use of Bayesian statistical models that confirms the use of the necropolis during the first quarter of the 2nd millennium BC. title: When Laboratory Studies of Plumes Shed the Veil of the Enceladus' Interior
abstract: Abstract Since the discovery by Cassini of plumes of water vapor and icy particles erupting from the South Polar Terrain (SPT) of Enceladus, numerous numerical models have been proposed to explain the mechanism driving these plumes, and how they relate to the thermodynamic conditions inside the underlying crevasses. title: Multi-class plastic additives in outdoor particulate matter at schools across the Pearl River Delta: descriptive geographic contrasts, mixture profiles, and modeled external particle-bound inhalation intake
abstract: Airborne plastic additives (PAs) occur as complex mixtures, yet their regional distribution and exposure relevance remain poorly characterized in school-associated outdoor air. We characterized 168 PAs in particulate matter from 98 schools across six cities in the Pearl River Delta (PRD), China, using summer PM 2.5 , winter PM 2.5 , and winter PM 1 datasets. abstract: Geomagnetic storms disturb the ionosphere through interacting electric fields, particle precipitation, thermospheric heating, and changes in atmospheric composition. Their consequences for satellite services depend on the structure of the disturbed plasma and the design of the receiving system, rather than on magnetic storm intensity alone. abstract: Abstract High-resolution and long-term Doppler wind LiDAR observations obtained over various land cover types in the city of Hong Kong were analyzed in this study. abstract: The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) influences vegetation far beyond the tropical Pacific, but its imprint on temperate maritime vegetation, where the teleconnection acts indirectly through winter circulation, temperature and precipitation, has rarely been quantified at the site scale. title: Past and future projected radiative effects from irrigation
abstract: Irrigation is the most dominant freshwater use practice on Earth, yet its effect on the top-of-atmosphere (TOA) radiative budget remains uncertain because past estimates have relied on idealised experiments or single-model frameworks. Here, we use historical simulations (1902–2014) from the Irrigation Model Intercomparison Project (IRRMIP) to provide the first multi-model quantification of irrigation-induced effective radiative forcing (ERF), defined as the change in net TOA radiative flux including rapid atmospheric adjustments. title: A Modified Clod Card Design for Measuring Mass Transfer as a Proxy for Water Motion Inside Oyster Cages
abstract: ABSTRACT Physical conditions within shellfish cages are often not well characterized in situ, largely due to difficulties finding inexpensive tools that can withstand turbulent environments with a small footprint. A novel clod card design was developed and tested for use in oyster cages for 4–12 h deployments. This clod card is smaller than previous designs and is fitted inside an aluminum bait cage for protection. abstract: Malaria remains a major public health challenge in Ghana despite recent reductions in cases attributable to various interventions, with disease endemicity varying across regions due to diverse seasonal and temporal factors that support mosquito proliferation. abstract: Abstract Past work suggests a possible connection between spring soil moisture conditions in the southwestern United States and the onset of the North American Monsoon (NAM). We test the NAM's response to both moist and dry spring soil moisture perturbations under different synoptic circulation regimes using high-resolution numerical simulations. abstract: Abstract Validation results for mass estimates measured by GRACE (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment) and GRACE‐FO (GRACE Follow‐On) currently hold uncertainties exceeding 10 gigatons (Gt), due to errors in auxiliary models and leakage noise from surrounding hydrological signals. abstract: Glacier cryoconite hosts metabolically active microbial communities despite exposure to solar radiation, which both provides energy and imposes stress. However, how radiation regimes are associated with microbial energy acquisition strategies and ecosystem organization remains unclear. abstract: Cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) are key components of aerosol-cloud interactions (ACI). Thus, a precise knowledge about their number concentrations (Nccn) is crucial for climate models and ACI studies. This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of the recently published CAMS-derived total Nccn using direct observations from 25 ground-based sites. abstract: Rain-gardens are widely promoted as nature-based solutions (NbSs) within blue-green infrastructure (BGI), yet their contribution to broader resilience objectives raises questions about how localized projects are governed, maintained, and connected to watershed planning. abstract: Curvilinear steel bar structures are increasingly applied in the design of various roof coverings. abstract: Accurate air quality modelling is crucial for assessing public health risks, particularly in regions with complex terrain. This study investigates the influence of meteorological drivers on the performance of the LOTOS-EUROS chemical transport model by comparing two setups: the standard configuration using operational data from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), and a dynamically downscaled setup using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model. title: Enhancement Pathways for Urban Water Ecological Resilience
abstract: Enhancing urban water ecological resilience (UWER) is increasingly essential as climate change, rapid urbanization, and ecological degradation intensify pressures on urban aquatic systems. However, knowledge of the mechanisms required to systematically enhance UWER remains fragmented across the ecological, technological, and governance domains. abstract: Abstract The North Pacific Meridional Mode (NPMM) is a key extratropical trigger of El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events, and its influence on ENSO has increased markedly in recent decades, offering a pathway to improve ENSO predictability. abstract: Abstract The Nordic countries of Norway, Sweden, and Finland have traditionally been characterised by less intense heatwaves than continental Europe. abstract: River crossing pipelines are the best and economical ways for the transit of any kind of liquids or gases from one side to another side of a river. abstract: The rapid growth of offshore wind energy has increased the size and complexity of Offshore Wind Turbines (OWTs), making fabrication, transportation, and installation critical to project cost and schedule. abstract: Esta investigación tiene como objetivo analizar las barreras, oportunidades y prioridades para avanzar hacia una gobernanza costera integrada y adaptativa en la Comunidad Valenciana, un territorio con elevada fragmentación institucional, presiones urbanísticas y vulnerabilidad climática. abstract: Atmospheric rivers (ARs) are major drivers of hydroclimatic extremes in mid-latitude regions, with important implications for water resource management and climate services. This study evaluates the hydroclimatic and hydrological response of Lake Villarrica in south-central Chile to AR landfalls during 2000–2024. title: Subducted Seamounts Promote Slow and Fast Slip Throughout the Seismic Cycle
abstract: Abstract The role of subducted seamounts on slip behavior is debated: they have been proposed to act as seismic asperities, or to favor aseismic slip and rupture arrest. We use numerical simulations and fracture mechanics to investigate how seamounts affect the seismic cycle. Motivated by long‐term subduction models, we assume that seamounts cause a down‐dip region of enhanced compression, and an up‐dip region of reduced compression (“weak patch”). journal: Journal of Geophysical Research Solid Earth

title: Attributing compound flood impact from tropical cyclone Idai in Mozambique to climate and population change
abstract: Abstract Impacts of extreme weather events are a complex interplay of compounding climatic and socio-economic drivers. In this paper, we attribute the effect of climate and population change on the number of people exposed to flooding from tropical cyclone (TC) Idai, making landfall in Mozambique in 2019. We apply an extended storyline attribution framework based on a globally-applicable model chain to simulate compound flooding and exposed population as a proxy for impact under factual and counterfactual climate and population conditions. title: Applicability of a modified weather research and forecasting (WRF) model to heavy rainfall information
abstract: Abstract The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) issues “Forecast Information on Linear Rainbands” (FILR; translated by the authors) approximately half a day before the expected formation of linear rainbands. A linear rainband is identified according to a set of operational criteria. A modified Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model was applied to sixteen heavy rainfall events associated with erroneous FILR decisions. title: Forcing dataset updates impact regional but not global Earth radiation budget trends in the GFDL AM4 climate model
abstract: The availability of up-to-date forcing datasets is critical for reconciling Earth system model simulations with contemporary observations. With the newly released CMIP7 forcing dataset, which extends the historical record through 2021, this study provides a systematic evaluation of how using updated forcings over the "middle-of-the-road" SSP2-4.5 scenario forcings influences the simulated radiation budget in the GFDL AM4 climate model. title: Physical Constraints on Future Tropical Cyclone Genesis Over the Western North Pacific: A CMIP6 Multi–Model Assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable projections of tropical cyclone genesis frequency (TCGF) under global warming remain challenging. We evaluate three genesis potential indices (χGPI, DGPI, and χMqGPI) over the western North Pacific (WNP) using 22 CMIP6 models under four SSP scenarios, supplemented by HighResMIP simulations under SSP5–8.5. All three indices broadly reproduce the observed spatial distribution and seasonal cycle of TC genesis, with χMqGPI showing the smallest bias and root‐mean‐square error in the seasonal cycle. title: Combining different views on internal climate variability of temperature over Europe
abstract: Internal climate variability (ICV) represents the intrinsic fluctuations within the climate system. Understanding how ICV varies across regions, seasons, and climatic conditions is crucial for detecting externally forced climate change and assessing future climate risks. It can also provide a useful benchmark for assessing climate model performance and the emergence of anthropogenically forced climate change. title: Sistema osservativo per le lagune dell'Alto Adriatico
abstract: The lagoons of the Northern Adriatic are highly productive transitional ecosystems, sensitive to climate change and human pressures. Within the PNRR MER project, ISPRA upgraded the observing system: the historical Venice lagoon tide-gauge network was expanded with new stations and inlagoon wave sensors. Furthermore, fixed stations andbuoys now measure water quality in real time. In parallel, stateof-the-art morphodynamic and biogeochemical models developed by research institutes are being moved towards operational use operational. title: A coupled Terzaghi – Biot model for blast-induced liquefaction
abstract: We investigate the impact of short-wave impulses on soil liquefaction and fluid pressure dynamics. Using a Biot poroelastic model with an elasto - plastic representation of the sand matrix, numerical simulations are conducted to evaluate soil displacement, pore pressure, and wave velocities. Comparisons between coupled (Biot) and decoupled (Terzaghi) models reveal critical differences in displacement and pore pressure predictions. title: Hydrokinetic energy recovery using a controllable-pitch propeller on a kite-assisted ship: Propeller performance mapping and a notional route case study
abstract: To enhance the efficiency of wind-assisted ships, the propeller may operate as a turbine. Because harvesting efficiency is strongly dependent on blade pitch, this study maps the propulsive and generative performance of a controllable pitch propeller (CPP) by simulating the Potsdam Propeller Test Case (PPTC) across a wide range of blade and advance angles. The power coefficient ( C P ) reaches 0.22 at design pitch, but achieves a global maximum of 0.44 at a 215° reversed pitch. title: Selective Waiting-Time Reduction in Indonesian Fiberglass Shipbuilding: A Digital Lean Simulation Framework
abstract: Background: Uniform waiting-time reduction in fiberglass shipbuilding may compromise essential technical processes, including curing, inspection, and safety checks. Therefore, waiting time must be classified according to its technical function and potential for reduction. Objective: This study develops a simulation-based Digital Lean Manufacturing framework for selectively reducing waiting time in Indonesian engineer-to-order fiberglass shipbuilding. title: The moisture mode-to-gravity wave spectrum as a framework to define tropical weather systems
abstract: While mid-latitude weather is commonly described in terms of discrete “weather systems”, such as cyclones and fronts, an equivalent framework is less established in the tropics due to the wide range of relevant scales. Instead, tropical weather is often analysed either in Lagrangian terms, through the tracking of mesoscale convective systems, or via spectral decomposition into planetary-scale wave-like disturbances. title: Non-land-use forcing significantly drives projected trends of atmospheric black carbon over Africa: Implications for mitigation strategies
abstract: Black carbon (BC) plays a critical role in climate forcing and poses significant health risks, yet its trends and drivers remain poorly constrained across Africa. Here, we quantify the relative contributions of land-use and non-land-use forcing to the projected trends of BC using the Meteorological Research Institute Earth System Model version 2.0 (MRI-ESM2-0) under the Aerosol Chemistry Model Intercomparison Project (AerChemMIP). title: Synoptic analysis and WRF sensitivity experiments of SACZ-driven extreme rainfall over Petropolis, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Extreme rainfall in the mountainous region of Petrópolis (Brazil) is frequently associated with South Atlantic Convergence Zone (SACZ) episodes, low-level moisture, and complex terrain. Despite its operational relevance, the sensitivity of numerical forecasts to physical parameterizations under these high-impact environments remains poorly understood. title: Numerical investigation of partially submerged H-type porous barrier in front of a seawall
abstract: This study examines the hydrodynamic response of an H-type porous breakwater positioned at a specified distance from a partially reflecting seawall using linear wave theory. The boundary value problem is solved using the dual boundary element method (DBEM) to acquire numerical results for various values of barrier porosity, relative submergence depth, wave steepness, and seawall porosity. title: Global Rossby wave rivers connecting remote wave activity to the East Asian summer monsoon
abstract: We introduce a sink-oriented Rossby wave river (WR) framework that traces remote wave activity along continuous propagation pathways converging toward specific sinks, and use the Li-Yang wave ray flux to diagnose the global WRs converging into the East Asian summer monsoon (EASM) region. At 850 hPa, Southern Hemisphere and pan-tropical pathways dominate and converge near the Philippines; at 500 hPa, low-latitude easterly and midlatitude westerly WRs become comparable in strength; at 200 hPa, WR propagation becomes concentrated along the jet waveguide. title: Impacts of Convective Microphysics Parameterization on MJO Simulation in E3SM
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the impact of convective microphysics parameterization on the simulation of the Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO) in the Energy Exascale Earth System Model (E3SM). Specifically, the two‐moment, five‐class convective microphysics parameterization (CMP) scheme from Song et al. (2025, https://doi.org/10.1029/2024ms004656 ) was implemented into Zhang and McFarlane (1995, https://doi.org/10.1080/07055900.1995.9649539 ) convection scheme in E3SM. title: Evolution of the Fiastrone Gorge from Jurassic Rifting to Apennine Orogeny. Insights from new detailed geological mapping
abstract: A new 1:10,000-scale geological mapping of the Fiastrone Gorge (Northern Apennines), provides a revised interpretation of its Jurassic palaeogeographic and tectonic evolution. The Meso-Cenozoic evolution of the Umbria–Marche succession, exposed in the area, was controlled by the complex palaeogeography inherited from Early Jurassic rifting of the Western Tethys. title: Validation of PREFIRE mid- and far-infrared radiances during the WHAFFFERS campaign
abstract: Despite containing up to half of the Earth's thermal emission to space, the far-infrared spectral region (FIR, defined here as 100–667 cm −1 or 15–100 µm) has seldom been observed from satellites. This has contributed to substantial uncertainties in the spectroscopy of water vapour, radiative properties of clouds, and surface spectral emissivity; these in turn limit confidence in modelled FIR energy flows. Objective: To assess the documentation readiness of a Pasacao, Camarines Sur fish-landing study and specify a prospective microplastic surveillance protocol. title: Relative dispersion and eddy diffusivity in laboratory experiments of β-plane turbulence
abstract: We present the first experimental measures of relative dispersion and turbulent diffusion in rapidly rotating turbulence in the zonostrophic regime, i.e. in the presence of instantaneous and dominant zonal jets. Synthetic Lagrangian trajectories are computed from time-resolved experimental velocity fields, from which we measure relative (two-particle) dispersion. title: A synoptic overview of the EUREC 4 A field campaign
abstract: Abstract We present an overview of the important synoptic features that occurred during the EUREC 4 A field campaign. These results are based on workshops bringing together forecasters and researchers to look in detail at cloud patterns in the region of interest (Barbados and the upstream trade winds) and how they were influenced by synoptic features. Consistent with previous studies, we found that the influence of, or lack of, midlatitude and subtropical features was important for cloud patterns. abstract: ABSTRACT Cuttlefish and squid attach to various substrates in their environment remarkably well using arms and extensible tentacles lined with arrays of suckers. Each sucker has a stiff internal ring with terminal teeth and microstructured rim. Previous studies have measured attachment forces of amputated suckers; however, in vivo investigations are lacking given the short time scales of attachment (milliseconds) and complex array geometries. abstract: While high-fidelity methods, such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)- Finite Element Analysis (FEA) coupling, can accurately capture structural collapse under severe slamming when the modeling and analysis conditions are appropriately specified, their high computational cost makes them impractical for repeated use in early-stage design or risk screening. title: How Can Local Knowledge and Infrastructure Engineering be Bridged for Tsunami Resilience? A Systematic Scoping Review of Socio-Technical Mitigation Framework
abstract: Tsunami resilience research has advanced significantly in both indigenous knowledge and engineering-based mitigation. However, these domains are often treated in isolation, which limits the development of integrated socio-technical catastrophe risk reduction solutions. This review examines how recent literature conceptualizes the relationship between local knowledge and tsunami mitigation engineering and operational planning, identifies mitigation functions that bridge these domains, and highlights existing knowledge gaps in socio-technical tsunami resilience. title: Green infrastructure for urban heat risk reduction: case Saudi Arabia
abstract: Rapid urbanisation in arid megacities produces severe urban heat islands (UHI) that increase building energy demand, degrade outdoor thermal comfort, and amplify carbon dioxide emissions. Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, three of the largest cities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, house a combined population exceeding 12 million inhabitants in climates characterised by extreme summer temperatures that routinely surpass 45 °C. title: Secondary ice production affects tropical convective clouds under different aerosol conditions
abstract: Secondary ice production (SIP) modulates tropical convection, but its interactions with aerosol loading remain uncertain. Using the UK Met Office Unified Model with detailed SIP parameterizations, this study investigates how multiple SIP mechanisms affect a Hector storm under weak instability and varying cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) concentrations. title: Non-eruptive debris flows at Mount Shasta: historical record, drivers, and implications for future hazards
abstract: Assessments of water-driven mass flows at snow and ice-covered volcanoes are often based on the assumption that the most impactful flows will happen during eruptions (lahars). However, as eruptions are a relatively low-probability event, non-eruptive debris flows tied to precipitation or glacial outburst floods may be more common. This is especially relevant at Mount Shasta, one of the southernmost glaciated stratovolcanoes in the Cascade volcanic arc, where past hazards assessments focused on the possibility of larger flows triggered by eruptive activity. title: Wave Energy Conversion Systems Dynamic Performance Enhancement Using Pied Kingfisher Optimization–Based Control Approach
abstract: This paper presents a model of a wave energy conversion system (WECS) consisting of an oscillating water column (OWC) and a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) connected to a grid. It introduces a control strategy for a generator-side converter (GSC), the purpose of which is to optimize the PMSG’s active power generation and reduce PMSG losses. title: Linking Deep Carbon to Surface Emission in the Carpathian–Pannonian Region: Isotope Systematics of Fluid Inclusions and Groundwater
abstract: Abstract CO 2 degassing from the deep Earth provides important insights into the global carbon cycle. CO 2 ‐rich fluid inclusions in mantle xenoliths record fluid sources and migrations in the deep lithosphere, while the contribution of mantle components in groundwater can be traced via dissolved gas geochemistry. Here, we integrate basin‐scale geochemical observations with thermo‐kinematic modeling to reconstruct CO 2 release in the Neogene Carpathian–Pannonian continental back‐arc system. title: Evaluating the representativeness of aircraft sampling strategies for cloud water content in LASSO simulations over the ARM Southern Great Plains (SGP) Site
abstract: Aircraft observations are widely used to evaluate cloud simulations; however, their inherently localized sampling may not fully represent the domain-scale cloud properties resolved by large-eddy simulations (LES). This study quantifies how aircraft-like sampling strategies influence the representativeness of in-cloud cloud water content (CWC) derived from LES output. title: The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
abstract: Compound dry-hot extremes (CDHEs) are among the most damaging climate hazards. Most metrics used to diagnose them are estimated at monthly or seasonal resolution or rely on precipitation-based drought proxies that can miss fast soil moisture-driven land–atmosphere feedbacks. This paper delivers two tightly linked products for global CDHE monitoring over land (excluding Antarctica) at 0.1° resolution for 1961–2023: (i) a continuous, daily severity index, i.e. the Standardized Soil Moisture–Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI), and (ii) a companion, event-based CDHE catalogue derived from SSTCI. title: Enhanced rock weathering for sustainable carbon capture: advances, challenges, and future prospects in terrestrial ecosystems
abstract: Abstract Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) is a carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy that accelerates mineral dissolution in terrestrial systems to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), with the potential for co-benefits across managed and natural ecosystems. This review evaluates ERW’s real-world effectiveness through the lens of measurable carbon fluxes and storage permanence. title: Urbanization Enhances Inner‐Core Rainfall During Tropical Cyclone Landfall
abstract: Abstract How urbanization modulates precipitation in landfalling tropical cyclones (LTCs) remains poorly understood. Previous studies disagree on whether the mechanism is primarily dynamical or thermodynamic, particularly within the inner core under intense wind–rain conditions. Using high‐resolution simulations and storm‐relative framework, we quantified the effects of urban land‐cover change (ULCC) and anthropogenic heat (AH) on peak inner‐core precipitation during Typhoon Bebinca's 2024 landfall in Shanghai. title: Experimental and numerical study of a scaled Airfish 8 wing-in-ground vehicle
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of a stationary ground plane on the performance of a scaled-down Airfish 8 wing-in-ground vehicle at Reynolds numbers Re of 200 000, 250 000, and 300 000 in cruise. Experimental results show that reducing the spacing between the vehicle and the stationary ground plane leads to a substantial lift augmentation of up to ∼50% at the smallest spacing h investigated: h/c̄=0.25, where c̄ is the mean aerodynamic chord. title: Conservation of migratory species at risk: environmental conditions experienced from pre‐gestation to parturition affect fall recruitment in migratory caribou
abstract: Annual variations in environmental conditions can strongly affect demographic rates of wild populations, such as survival and recruitment. These effects are likely to be exacerbated in highly seasonal environments and in species facing substantial energetic needs during specific seasons. In migratory mammals, for instance, females must contend with the energy expenditures required for long‐distance travel as well as those needed to complete gestation. title: The Heterodyne Wind Lidar Gadget HEDWIG for the German research aircraft HALO: instrument design, wind retrieval and first airborne observations
abstract: The HEterodyne Detection Wind lIdar Gadget (HEDWIG) is a new airborne Doppler wind lidar developed at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) for high-resolution observations of atmospheric wind profiles. The instrument operates at an eye-safe wavelength of 1617 nm. A newly developed double-wedge scanner provides rapid and flexible beam steering, enabling both conical scanning for horizontal wind retrieval and parallel nadir-pointing observations for direct measurements of the vertical wind component. title: More than meets the eye: artificial eyelashes as an unrecognized source of microplastics and heavy metals
abstract: Despite growing concern over microplastic pollution, leave-on cosmetic products such as artificial eyelashes remain largely unexplored as sources of microplastics and associated contaminants. Here, nine artificial eyelash products were characterized for polymer composition, heavy metal content, and fiber release under simulated environmental conditions. Three polymers were identified: PBT (55.56%), PET (33.33%), and PVC (11.11%). Metal profiles varied widely across samples, with several metals of toxicological concern (Al, Ba, Co, Cr, Cu, Pb, Sb, Zn) detected but not declared on product labels

title: Regional infrastructure repurposing: Pathways from assessment to geothermal energy production and storage
abstract: Addressing the growing demand for sustainable energy, we explore the innovative potential of repurposing existing subsurface infrastructure for geothermal energy production and energy storage. We present an integrated technical, economic, and legal framework for repurposing regional-scale infrastructure to systematically evaluate and optimize geothermal resource utilization. title: Creating forecasts of cattle heat stress for Australia: challenges and prototypes
abstract: In Australia, a heatwave is defined as a run of unusually high daytime and night-time temperatures persisting for three or more days and is routinely forecast by the Bureau of Meteorology through its heatwave service, primarily to support human health and community safety. No equivalent spatial heat stress forecasts currently exist for Australian cattle or other grazing livestock, creating an important information gap. Climate Change Forces Hydrological Regime Shifts in Australian Wetlands
abstract: Abstract Wetlands provide crucial biodiversity benefits and ecosystem services but are at risk from changing hydrological regimes under climate change. Understanding likely future changes in wetland hydrology will help mitigate impacts and guide adaptation strategies for high‐value sites. We used satellite‐based observations of wetland inundation to calibrate conceptual runoff models modified to represent wetland storage dynamics across 34,890 wetlands in the state of Victoria, Australia. title: Local wind profile anomalies during spring successive warming in Altay—based on GPS sounding
abstract: Abstract To explore the triggering conditions of snowmelt floods in the Irtysh River basin of northern Xinjiang, China, we analyzed the anomalous features and the formation mechanism of wind profiles in three successive warming processes (‘SWPs’) observed during the high-frequency radiosonde campaign at Altay Station in the spring of 2021. title: Poorly Constrained Planetary Boundary Layer Height and Emissions Factors Drive High Uncertainty in Atmospheric Chemical Modeling of Emissions from Forests
abstract: Abstract The impact of emissions on atmospheric chemistry requires a detailed chemical understanding of their transformation and fate. However, there are many sources of potential uncertainty in modeling the life cycle and transformation of biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOC). This study investigates the sensitivity of a 0-D box model to several sources of potential uncertainty at a southeastern U.S. forest site over the summer season, including mixing ratios of critical trace oxidants (O3 and NO2), planetary boundary layer height (PBLH), and the factors that control emission rates. title: Analysis of turning maneuverability performance of a tanker in shallow water under wind disturbances
abstract: Increasing ship dimensions and maritime traffic have intensified maneuvering challenges in harbors and channels, particularly in shallow water under external wind disturbances. This study investigates the effects of steady wind on ship turning performance using a Maneuvering Modeling Group (MMG) model incorporating regression-based aerodynamic coefficients. Simulations are conducted across different ship speeds, depth-to-draft ratios (h/T), wind speeds, and wind directions. abstract: Os sistemas de água doce na Amazônia brasileira oriental estão cada vez mais vulneráveis à expansão do uso da terra, à mineração, à intensificação agrícola e ao enfraquecimento da governança ambiental. abstract: A compact transport vehicle with a crane boom is assessed using signed moments about support edges. abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrological restoration re-establishes tidal exchange in degraded mangroves, but its influence may weaken with distance from reopened channels. abstract: Abstract Friction stir additive manufacturing (FSAM) is an emerging additive manufacturing process for fabricating large aerospace components made from aluminum alloys (e.g., EN AW-7075-T6). In the studies presented in this article, the hardness losses typical for this process were addressed. title: Experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy
abstract: We present a proof-of-concept experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy converter array with a shared closed-loop hydraulic power take-off system, where energy is extracted through the collective motion of the buoy array. Pressurised flow generated by individual buoys drives a turbine within the hydraulic circuit. A downscaled model was tested in the wave tank at the University of Oslo. title: A representative subarray method for radiation hydrodynamic modelling of large floating arrays with modularized configuration
abstract: Radiation hydrodynamic modelling of large floating arrays requires constructing immense influence coefficient matrices, with computational costs increasing rapidly with array size. Because these arrays typically feature modularized configurations, the surrounding-module arrangements of different modules exhibit repeated spatial patterns. To reduce computational cost, a representative subarray method is proposed based on arrangement repetition and the distance-dependent decay of radiation interactions. In this approach, a representative subarray is selected to encompass all required surrounding

title: Active wave absorption method for force-controlled wavemakers based on amplitude–phase fitting
abstract: Reflected waves at flume boundaries adversely affect the accuracy of wave simulation experiments, motivating the development of active absorption techniques. The absorption methods of force-controlled wavemakers, however, remain limited due to the complexity of their transfer functions. This study first derives the absorption transfer functions of piston-type and flap-type wavemakers in the frequency domain based on force control, and then uses them to design an active absorption system based on infinite impulse response (IIR) filters. A filter with the appropriate design is derived by fitting
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Coastal and Offshore Engineering

title: Microclimate persistence in island montane cloud forests
abstract: Abstract Montane cloud forests (MCFs), ecosystems critically dependent on persistent cloud immersion and high moisture availability, have been presumed vulnerable to regional warming and atmospheric drying. Yet their microclimatic resilience under regional climate variability remains poorly understood. Here we show that MCFs maintain remarkably stable near-surface relative humidity (RH), despite sustained regional warming, using a 42-year (1980–2021) high-resolution (2-km, hourly) climate dataset from Taiwan. institutions: National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction

title: A multi-indicator framework for assessing the likelihood of ENSO impacts across southern Africa
abstract: The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the dominant source of seasonal predictability for southern Africa, yet operational guidance rarely conveys which agriculturally relevant variables it can skillfully predict, or where ENSO impacts are most likely. We present an operational analysis framework that converts an ENSO state, classified by phase and strength, into gridded, analogue-composite outlooks for 15 indicators spanning rainfall, evaporative demand, related standardized indices (SPI, SPEI), crop water balance, dry-spells, rainfall-season timing, and heat extremes. title: Magma fragmentation processes during a large-scale explosive phreatomagmatic eruption constrained from volatile contents of volcanic glass
abstract: Phreatomagmatic eruptions are one of the most common and hazardous eruption styles on Earth. To understand the explosive phreatomagmatic eruptions, it is essential to constrain the mechanisms of magma–water interaction and the environments in which they occur. We investigated the quenching depths of ascending magma during the large-scale and explosive phreatoplinian eruption that occurred at Kutcharo volcano, Japan, based on the water content measurements for volcanic glass shards using scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) and Fourier transform infrared spectro

title: Breaking the Ice: Contributions and Challenges for Andean Glaciological Research Led by Women
abstract: Abstract This study examines the participation of women in Andean glaciology over the past four decades, combining a bibliometric analysis of 204 peer-reviewed articles (1983–2022) and a survey of female first authors (2018–2022). Results show a steady increase in women-led publications, rising from 8 percent in the 1980s–1990s to 30 percent in the past decade. However, structural barriers, including unequal access to funding, resistance to female leadership, and the disproportionate burden of caregiving, continue to limit gender equity in the field. title: Оцінка метеорологічних умов суднових аварій у Північній Атлантиці за даними реаналізу ERA5
abstract: У статті представлено методологічний підхід до кількісної оцінки взаємозв’язку між метеорологічними умовами та ава- рійністю морських суден в Північній Атлантиці на основі поєднання даних реаналізу ERA5 та архівних записів про реальні морські інциденти. title: Nationwide assessment of land subsidence related to groundwater depletion in Spain using InSAR and GRACE-assimilated groundwater-storage data
abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater overexploitation can lead to land subsidence, posing risks for infrastructure, ecosystems, and long-term aquifer sustainability. However, detecting and prioritizing groundwater-related subsidence at the national scale remains challenging due to limited pumping data and heterogeneous monitoring networks. This study presents the first nationwide assessment of potential groundwater-related subsidence across Spain by integrating satellite observations and hydrogeological information at the groundwater body (GWB) scale. title: Otters appear to have declined throughout Ireland amid increased pressures on water quality, but remain ubiquitous
abstract: Abstract Governments must report on the conservation status of species designated as protected. We assessed changes in the Near Threatened Eurasian otter Lutra lutra population throughout Ireland (the whole island) from the 1980s to the 2020s using four National Otter Surveys (6,060 sites surveyed) and citizen science data (10,980 records). In 2023–2024, otters were recorded at 65% (95% CI 62–68%) of sites in the Republic of Ireland and 66% (95% CI 58–74%) of sites in Northern Ireland. title: Mountain-to-plain mesoscale convective systems in North China: propagation patterns and precipitation characteristics under varied synoptic-scale environments
abstract: Mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) frequently propagate from China’s second-step terrain to North China Plain (NCP), yet the regime dependence of their spatiotemporal characteristics and the controlling environments remains insufficiently understood. Using Himawari-8/9 brightness temperature data and an iterative tracking approach, this study identified warm-season mountain-to-plain MCSs (MP-MCSs) over North China during 2016–2023. abstract: Precipitation is one of the primary indicators of climate change and plays a critical role in environmental processes. Changes in the amount, distribution, and frequency of precipitation are directly influenced by climatic variations, while precipitation characteristics significantly affect ecosystems, water resources, and regional climate conditions. title: The Effects of Intra‐Day Temperature Variability on Cause‐Specific Mortality: A Time‐Stratified Case‐Crossover Study in Chongqing, China
abstract: Abstract Although temperature variability (TV) has been linked to an increased mortality risk, the independent effect of intra‐day TV remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the association between intra‐day TV exposure and cause‐specific mortality in a Chinese population. We collected daily mortality data and meteorological variables from 2016 to 2022 in Jiulongpo District, Chongqing, China. title: Effects of carbonization temperature on the performance of bamboo fiber-reinforced cementitious composites and their potential applications in deicing pavement
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the effects of carbonization temperature and fiber dosage on the mechanical properties, thermal conductivity, and rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT) response of bamboo fiber-reinforced C40 concrete. Bamboo fibers were incorporated at dosages of 1.5%–4.5% and used in three states: uncarbonized, carbonized at 300 °C, and carbonized at 800 °C. title: Development of a point-of-care field test for Tasmanian devil facial tumour disease
abstract: Abstract The Tasmanian devil (Sarcophilus harrisii) population has undergone a major decline in the wild owing to the epidemics of two transmissible cancers known as devil facial tumour 1 (DFT1) and devil facial tumour 2 (DFT2). Understanding the distribution and prevalence of DFT1 and DFT2 is challenging as they can only be detected in field conditions when tumours are large enough to be visually observed. abstract: Abstract Seismic velocity provides key insights into the structure and thermodynamic state of the Earth's mantle. title: Continuous Reduction of Black Carbon Emissions From China During 2009–2022: Estimates From Observations at Remote Sites in Japan
abstract: Abstract To assess the climate impact of black carbon (BC), accurate emission inventories are crucial for climate model simulations. However, bottom‐up emissions inventories have substantial uncertainties regarding anthropogenic BC emissions from China and struggle to capture rapid changes in emissions. Top‐down analysis using atmospheric observations is an useful method to evaluate inventories and to immediately estimate BC emissions. abstract: Snow drought, characterized by anomalously low snow water equivalent (SWE) relative to climatological conditions, has become an increasingly important cryospheric hazard with substantial environmental and socio-economic impacts. Although numerous snow drought identification methods have been developed, existing implementations are typically fragmented into independent scripts and region-specific workflows, hindering methodological consistency, reproducibility, and systematic intercomparison. title: Performance of Earth System Models in Representing Vegetation Functional Response to Heat and Water Stresses
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the performance of four CMIP6 Earth system models (ESMs) in capturing the apparent optimal temperature (T opt ) and the response of light use efficiency (LUE) to heat and drought across forests and grasslands. ESMs effectively reproduce T opt for C4 plants, but show large discrepancies for C3 plants, with NorESM2‐MM slightly underestimating T opt , CMCC‐ESM2 underestimating it at mid‐latitudes, and CNRM‐CM6‐1 substantially overestimating it. title: THERMO-MECHANICAL FINITE ELEMENT ANALYSIS OF COMPRESSIVE AXIAL PRESTRESS IN FRICTION STIR WELDING OF DISSIMILAR AA6061-T6 AND AA5083-H111 ALLOYS
abstract: Friction stir welding (FSW) of dissimilar aluminium alloys is accompanied by non-uniform thermal expansion and contraction that can generate significant residual stresses and influence joint response. This study numerically investigates the effect of externally applied compressive axial prestress on the thermo-mechanical behaviour of dissimilar AA6061-T6 and AA5083-H111 friction stir welded joints. title: Regional covariation between climate-normalized storm rarity and landslide magnitude in Taiwan is sensitive to rainfall timing
abstract: Abstract Climate-normalized rainfall rarity may facilitate comparisons across climates, but pooled rainfall–landslide associations can obscure regional structure and rainfall timing. We examined 994 reported rainfall-induced landslides in Taiwan (1987–2018) using 2-km hourly precipitation and generalized extreme-value climatologies for 1980–2019. Rainfall rarity ( T max ) was defined as the maximum of 1–72-h duration-specific return periods, not the recurrence interval of an entire storm. title: A regional climate modeling investigation of wetland-related coupled hydrologic–atmospheric processes in central South America
abstract: Abstract This study investigates how the Pantanal, one of the world’s largest tropical floodplains, modulates local and regional climate in central South America through coupled land–atmosphere processes. Using the RegIPSL regional climate modeling framework, two simulations covering the 1998–2019 period were conducted: one including an explicit floodplain scheme and one without it. title: Sustained crustal helium enrichment associated with postseismic viscoelastic relaxation following the 2025 Myanmar earthquake
abstract: Earthquakes can alter fluid flow far from a rupture, but the processes that sustain such changes for months remain uncertain. Here we report a sustained increase in gas-phase helium concentration at a thermal spring on the Red River Fault, about 600 kilometres from the 2025 magnitude 7.7 Myanmar earthquake. Minute-scale monitoring recorded intermittent fluctuations before the earthquake and a progressive concentration increase afterwards. title: Increasing the critical shear stress in sandy beds to control bed scour using alkali-activated cement
abstract: Scouring during flood events is a critical problem in hydraulic and geotechnical engineering, threatening the stability and service life of bridge piers and abutments, foundations, and embankments. This study evaluates the use of alkali-activated cement (AAC) derived from ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) for the prevention of streambed scour and to enhance the erosion resistance of sandy soils. title: Accelerating anthropogenic influence on annual peak wood density and associated carbon accumulation across northern conifers
abstract: Northern coniferous forests hold significant climatic and ecological importance, yet the optimal air temperature (OAT) governing their annual peak wood density remains unknown. Here, using tree-ring maximum latewood density (MXD) from 14,000 samples at 551 sites, we reveal an OAT range of 15–21 °C governing annual MXD variability, a more sensitive thermal metric than seasonal temperature. title: Global health impacts of the 2018–2019 heatwaves and air pollution events under warmer climates
abstract: Extreme temperatures and ambient air pollution are closely linked and impose substantial global health burdens, yet their regional responses to additional warming remain poorly understood across the world. Using a storyline approach based on the exceptionally warm years 2018 and 2019, we examine how heatwaves (HWs), fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), ozone (O 3 ), and their separately estimated mortality burdens respond to two counterfactual climates at +2 K and +2.75 K warming levels. title: Who will import hydrogen in 2050? Global assessment with China and U.S. case studies
abstract: This study assesses the global hydrogen import potential in 2050 by looking at the renewable hydrogen production potential in prospective import-oriented countries. Renewable energy potentials calculated with a GIS based model and 2050 primary energy consumption projections are used to identify candidate importers by comparing it with expected demand. title: Harvest shifts carbon–water dynamics and environmental controls in a managed loblolly pine plantation in the southeast United States
abstract: How carbon–water coupling reorganizes across stand development and harvest in managed plantations remains poorly quantified. We used 20 years (2005–2024) of eddy covariance measurements at a loblolly pine ( Pinus taeda L.) plantation (US-NC2, North Carolina, United States) to quantify carbon and water flux dynamics across three stand development stages spanning pre- and post-harvest periods. title: Comparing surface albedo and land surface temperature of reflective roofs across five United States Cities
abstract: Abstract Rapid urban expansion and increasingly intense summer heat have heightened interest in reflective roofing as an urban heat-mitigation strategy. This study evaluates associations among roof type, surface albedo, and land surface temperature (LST) across five climatically distinct U.S. urban regions: Chicago, New York City (NYC), Las Vegas Valley (LVV), Los Angeles (LA), and Houston. abstract: In the Friuli Venezia Giulia (FVG) region of northeastern Italy, declining groundwater levels and changing precipitation patterns have raised concerns about the long-term sustainability of groundwater resources. This study evaluates the potential of Managed Aquifer Recharge (MAR) in the upper Friuli Plain, with a focus on the Sammardenchia site. This study investigates three different double-cylindrical re-entrant cores (REC-R, REC-N, and REC-W) in sandwich structures, with the reference REC-R topology tested only in the rectangular configuration, fabricated by additive manufacturing. title: When GRACE Measures More Than Water: Geomorphic Mass Redistribution in Terrestrial Water Storage Trends
abstract: Abstract The Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment and its Follow‐On missions (GRACE/GRACE‐FO) provide indirect estimates of regional‐scale water storage changes, albeit at a coarse resolution (∼300 km). Interpreting GRACE‐derived trends in geomorphically complex settings presents additional challenges. abstract: ABSTRACT In the manufacturing of fiber‐reinforced composites, different stacking configurations are commonly adopted in dry fabric preforming, while the resulting inter‐ply angle difference ratio can affect the through‐thickness deformation of the preform. Dry fabrics also exhibit time‐dependent and irreversible deformation during compaction, which should be considered for accurate prediction of preform thickness evolution. title: Multivariate Gaussian process emulation for multifidelity computer models with high-dimensional spatial outputs
abstract: Risk assessment of hurricane-driven storm surge relies on deterministic computer models that produce outputs over a large spatial domain. The surge models can often be run at a range of fidelity levels, with greater precision yielding more accurate simulations. title: Decoupled vegetation structure and composition in a mangrove–apicum ecotone in Northeastern Brazil
abstract: Abstract Mangrove–apicum ecotones are heterogeneous transition zones in which woody colonization need not follow a single age-ordered trajectory. We reanalysed an author-validated area-level matrix from ten successional mangrove patches in the Barra de Gramame estuary, northeastern Brazil. Five patches belonged to a 6–10-year and five to an 11–15-year site-history category inherited from the original survey. abstract: ABSTRACT Calcium leaching degrades concrete durability through progressive dissolution and decalcification of cement hydrate phases, yet it is commonly modelled by assuming local equilibrium between the pore solution and solid hydrates. While useful for estimating how much calcium is eventually depleted, such approaches do not fully resolve the kinetic coupling among hydrate dissolution, ionic transport within the bulk concrete and across the concrete-solution interface, and ultimately porosity evolution. title: Spatially Explicit Assessment of Rainwater Harvesting Performance under Climate Change Scenarios: A Municipal-Scale Analysis for Portugal
abstract: Rainwater harvesting (RWH) systems are increasingly recognized as decentralized solutions capable of improving urban water resilience under climate change, particularly in Mediterranean regions characterized by strong hydrological seasonality and recurrent water stress. abstract: Assessing regional economic recovery after major earthquakes is critical for disaster risk reduction. This study aims to evaluate the disaster resilience of the Wenchuan earthquake-stricken area and explore its spatially varying influencing factors. abstract: Industrial infrastructure in Saudi Arabia is undergoing expansion and renewal with the environment being as much a factor as the infrastructure itself with exposure to extreme heat, flash flooding, complex supply chains and highly interdependent utility services. abstract: The transition to low-carbon energy systems requires technologies that provide renewable electricity, flexible energy storage, and pathways for decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors. This review critically compares solar photovoltaic (PV) and hydrogen-energy technologies within an integrated system-level framework, considering technological maturity, efficiency, economics, environmental impacts, infrastructure, applications, and future prospects. title: Evolution of Precipitation in Zhengzhou over the Past 42 Years and the Multi-scale Mechanisms of the "720" Extreme
abstract: Based on NASA MERRA-2 and Zhengzhou Meteorological Bureau precipitation data from 1982 to 2024, this study analyzes the evolution of annual precipitation in Zhengzhou and the mechanisms associated with the "7·20" extreme rainstorm. abstract: Adaptive phenotypic plasticity can bolster fitness in changing environments, but the extent to which plasticity evolves rapidly, and which forces shape its evolutionary trajectory, are largely unknown. abstract: ABSTRACT Meteorological dry–wet abrupt alternation (M‐DWAA) is an important compound climate extreme that can impose complex stresses on agricultural and ecological systems through rapid shifts between water deficit and excess moisture. Its impacts on land‐surface and ecosystem processes depend partly on whether and how meteorological signals are transmitted into soil moisture. abstract: Individuals selected for the Inca capacocha ritual, sacrificed at high-altitude sites to act as messengers to the mountain deities, are occasionally found preserved as frozen mummies, providing key insights into Inca life and religious practices. abstract: Deep geological repositories for high-level radioactive waste (HLW) rely to a large extent on the long-term sealing integrity of host rocks to limit fluid flow and radionuclide migration. Low hydraulic conductivity (K<10-10 m s −1 ; StandAG, 2017) is a key factor for effective long-term barrier performance. Among other properties, argillaceous formations are promising candidates due to their effective aquitard characteristics. title: CLASSIFICATION OF FACTORS INFLUENCING THE ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY OF TRANSPORT AND LOGISTICS FLOWS UNDER WARTIME CONDITIONS
abstract: The article examines the factors influencing the economic efficiency of transport and logistics flows under wartime conditions. It is substantiated that transport efficiency is determined not only by the relationship between results and costs but also by delivery time, route capacity, capacity utilisation and the ability of the logistics system to maintain operational continuity. Here, we use a tracer‐aided, fully distributed ecohydrological modeling framework to investigate how future climate conditions may influence water fluxes and nitrate dynamics in such systems, using the Demnitzer Mill Creek catchment in Germany as an exemplar. abstract: While there is growing evidence about how African farmers are adapting to climate change, there remains a lack of research highlighting direct linkages between future climate scenarios, impacts on agriculture, and viable adaptation strategies. To address this gap, our research objectives are to understand how farmers in Tanzania perceive (1) climate change-impacts, (2) current adaptation strategies and future adaptation options given climate scenarios. abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and methodological provisions for developing a mechanism aimed at enhancing the transfer potential of agricultural holdings’ logistics centers. Transfer potential is interpreted as the ability of a logistics center to ensure the transmission, adoption, integration, and scaling of technologies, information, resources, managerial decisions, and logistics practices. abstract: The filling of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam remains highly contentious despite reaching 95% of storage capacity by the end of hydrological year 2024–2025, without major downstream impacts. This study assesses the first filling (2020–2024) by comparing the planned and actual filling trajectories. In the absence of data exchange, river inflows were estimated using a hydrological model, reservoir filling was reconstructed from satellite observations, and impacts were evaluated using a River Basin Simulation model. abstract: ABSTRACT Assessing the spatiotemporal dynamics of large wood is critical for understanding the dynamic processes influencing river channels, floodplains and organisms using the riverscape. We quantified large wood in the lower White River, Colorado and Utah, which has an unregulated flow regime and has been invaded by woody vegetation, primarily Russian olive ( Elaeagnus angustifolia ). title: Thermal acclimation as an emergent property of economically optimal photosynthesis
abstract: Summary Leaf‐level photosynthesis acclimates to growth conditions over days to weeks, with the instantaneous optimal temperature for photosynthesis ( T opt ) increasing with growth temperature ( T growth ). We investigated how this behaviour emerges in the P model, a primary production model based on eco‐evolutionary optimality hypotheses. title: A Municipal Flood Early-Warning Framework for Community-Centred Development in Urban Uganda
abstract: Urban flood early-warning services in Uganda face interconnected challenges involving incomplete rainfall records, limited monitoring infrastructure, intermittent power and communications, and fragmented arrangements for warning and response. Guided by the World Meteorological Organization’s (WMO) people-centred early-warning framework and the Sendai Framework for Disaster-Risk Reduction, this paper develops a structured pre-deployment municipal framework linking risk knowledge, monitoring, communication, preparedness and accountable governance. title: Limit-equilibrium analysis of shield tunnel face stability under seepage flow considering partial soil arching
abstract: Construction risk in shield tunnelling is closely related to the tunnel face stability. This study investigates the shield tunnel face stability under seepage flow conditions by developing a novel prism-circular-arc slice model that combines limit equilibrium theory with numerical simulation to determine the limit support pressure at the tunnel face. abstract: Purpose This study explores the multipolar network spatial organization of the regional economy, clarifies its connotation, characteristics and value and provides theoretical and practical support for solving regional economic strategic issues, building a new development pattern and promoting Chinese modernization. abstract: Integrating dihydrogen (H 2 ) into energy mixes requires assessing its viability in underground gas storages (UGS) like deep aquifers. The primary challenge is H 2 consumption by autochthonous microorganisms, leading to site-dependent issues like souring and petrophysical changes. We performed an innovative approach combining an experimental simulation of a deep aquifer in a high-pressure reactor using native rock and formation water, which was then modeled using a biogeochemical model. abstract: A three-dimensional conjugate heat transfer model of a 400 W high-power LED fishing lamp (Scheme A) was established in COMSOL Multiphysics by coupling Heat Transfer in Solids, Heat Transfer in Fluids, laminar flow, and non-isothermal flow. The effects of input power, heat sink fin thickness, inlet air velocity, and heat sink structure on junction temperature and thermal behavior were analyzed and validated using infrared thermal imaging. title: Physiological, plasma biochemical, and heat-shock responses of starry flounder ( Platichthys stellatus ) to acute and chronic high-temperature exposure
abstract: High water temperature is a major environmental stressor affecting the survival and physiological condition of cultured fish. This study evaluated survival, plasma biochemical responses, stress-related indicators, and heat-shock protein expression in starry flounder ( Platichthys stellatus ) exposed to gradual or acute high-temperature conditions. A total of 140 fish were used: 20 were sampled to determine the initial physiological status, and the remaining 120 were assigned to control, gradual-exposure, and acute-exposure groups, with two replicate tanks containing 20 fish each per treatment.

title: Spatial Distribution of Mudclast-Conglomerate and Mudstone Bodies in Braided Fluvial Sandstones and their Influence on Effective Permeability
abstract: Thin mudstone and mudclast-conglomerate lenses in braided fluvial sandstones can exert a disproportionately large control on fluid flow, relative to their volumetric proportion, by reducing effective vertical permeability. This study presents the first quantitative outcrop dataset in the Sherwood Sandstone Group, UK that characterizes the dimensions and spatial distribution of such mudstones, using high-resolution photomosaics, architectural analysis, and point-pattern spatial statistical analysis of two perpendicular quarry faces. title: Thermal fatigue, water-weakening spalling, and structural instability of Nabataean rock-cut façades
abstract: Rock-cut monumental façades of the Nabataean civilisation at Hegra (Al-’Ula, Saudi Arabia) exhibit progressive surface-perpendicular fracturing and surface-parallel spalling in a hyper-arid environment. The Case 2 lateral crack geometry, in which stress intensity increases monotonically with crack height with no arrest mechanism, and its probabilistic failure timeline have not previously been quantified for rock-cut heritage façades. title: Optimizing the California low carbon grid to include Social Cost of Carbon, and modeling grid expansion to 2050
abstract: Carbon emissions from the electrical energy and transportation sectors are two of the largest contributors to global greenhouse gas emissions. Reducing these emissions will be key to mitigating the worst impacts of global climate change. This study models the economic and lifecycle carbon impacts of transitioning California toward a deeply decarbonized electric power grid and light-duty electric vehicle fleet. title: Mapping Climate and Air Quality Risks for Acute Respiratory Infections in Eastern Priangan, Indonesia
abstract: Climate change has become a significant public health concern, particularly through its influence on air quality and the incidence of respiratory diseases. Variations in temperature, precipitation, humidity, and wind speed have been shown to exacerbate health vulnerabilities, especially in climate-sensitive regions. This study examines the relationship between climatic parameters, air quality, and respiratory disease admissions in East Priangan, Indonesia, using observational data from 2022 to 2023. abstract: Energy consumption of the word increasing year by year, however, the world cannot afford the generation of energy through conventional means of fossil fuel. To meet the growing demand of energy, various sources of renewable energy is utilized across the globe. Tidal Current is one such renewable energy source and grab the attention of large no of researcher both on industrial and academic level, due to its high predictable and stable nature. abstract: Honeycombs have garnered significant research interest owing to their multifunctional attributes and exceptional mechanical performance. This study develops an improved variant of the multi‐arc enhanced reentrant honeycomb (MAERH) inspired by the multi‐arc reentrant auxetic honeycomb (MARAH). A combined experimental‐numerical methodology is employed to investigate the compression behavior of additively manufactured specimens under quasi‐static loading. title: Continuous measurement of oxygen consumption rate in hypoxic conditions with adherent cells using an oxygen-sensitive optode
abstract: Cellular oxygen consumption rate (OCR) is a widely used readout of mitochondrial respiration and oxidative metabolism. However, many OCR assay workflows are limited by short assay durations, expensive specialized instrumentation, and reduced flexibility under controlled low-oxygen conditions. Here, we describe an in-incubator method for continuous, non-disruptive OCR measurement in adherent cell cultures using the PreSens OxoDish optical oxygen-sensing system. title: Role of hydrometeorological variables and catchment area to flood generation over the monsoonal climate region of India
abstract: Indian River basins experience frequent flooding during the Indian summer monsoon and pose several challenges for the region's large population, yet the hydrometeorological and catchment-scale drivers that control flood processes remain poorly explored across India. title: Heat, Water Control and the Limits of Fertilizer: Fixed-Effects Quantile Evidence on Cereal Yields in South Asia
abstract: Cereal production in South Asia faces rising temperatures, erratic monsoon rainfall, and diminishing returns to input intensification. This study examines how weather and farm inputs shape cereal yields across the conditional yield distribution in Bangladesh, India, Nepal, and Pakistan, which account for about 99% of the cereal area of South Asia outside Afghanistan, over 2000–2023. title: Event-specific Dust-to-Power screening of aerosol dimming and potential soiling-monitoring priorities for northern China photovoltaics
abstract: Abstract Dust events motivate separate monitoring of atmospheric dimming and potential photovoltaic (PV) surface soiling. We developed Dust-to-Power as an event-specific monitoring framework across eight northern Chinese provinces. abstract: Abstract The Cretaceous High Arctic Large Igneous Province (HALIP) is dominated by evolved continental tholeiitic basalts. title: Weak morphological constraints on species roles and partner identity in a facultative ant–plant mutualism
abstract: Abstract Mutualisms contribute substantially to biodiversity and ecosystem functioning, yet the factors structuring facultative mutualisms remain poorly understood. Trait-based approaches suggest that functional traits may shape species roles and interaction patterns by influencing resource access, exploitation efficiency, and competitive ability, but whether they constrain partner identity remains unclear. title: Wave breaking in Newtonian and viscoplastic vertical falling liquid films
abstract: We examine the onset of wave breaking in highly viscous gravity-driven vertical falling liquid films in a quiescent atmosphere via multiphase direct numerical simulations. Both Newtonian and Herschel–Bulkley liquids are considered. Analysis of the force balance acting on wave humps shows that the transition from travelling waves to breaking states is governed primarily by the competition between gravitational and capillary forces. title: Hydrodynamic characteristics of double heave plates: A combined experimental and numerical investigation
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the hydrodynamic characteristics of double heave plates, combining forced oscillation experiments with numerical simulations. title: Heat pump integration in 3rd generation district heating: Effects of refrigerant, flowsheet, design, and modeling on efficiency predictions
abstract: Large-scale heat pumps are a key technology for decarbonizing district heating systems. But, their economic viability strongly depends on estimated operational costs derived from performance models in early design stages. These estimates are highly sensitive to modeling assumptions. This study quantifies the impact of model choice on the predicted coefficient of performance ( C O P ) and heating capacity using thermodynamic cycle models of vapor-compression heat pumps. abstract: This study presents a novel hybrid implicit–explicit time-integration strategy for simulating injection-induced fault reactivation within a fully coupled poroelastodynamic extended finite element (XFEM) framework. Modeling these systems is inherently challenging due to the extreme separation of temporal scales – ranging from hours to days for fluid diffusion to milliseconds for dynamic rupture. title: Beyond the Carbon Footprint: Bridging Climate Services and Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment
abstract: Life cycle sustainability assessment (LCSA) evaluates the environmental, economic, and social impacts of products and systems, yet the systematic integration of future-oriented climate information remains poorly documented. Climate services, such as climate projections, early warning systems, and risk maps, offer a largely untapped source of such information. abstract: ABSTRACT The liquefaction susceptibility of saturated sands is commonly evaluated using macroscopic indices such as relative density and confining pressure, whereas the role of particle morphology remains less well understood. In this study, a coupled computational fluid dynamics‐discrete element method (CFD‐DEM) framework is used to investigate particle‐shape effects on liquefaction under a unified deposition and cyclic loading protocol. title: Characterizing variability and vertical structure of water vapor in the extratropical lower stratosphere
abstract: Stratospheric water vapor strongly affects Earth’s radiative balance, especially in the extratropical lower stratosphere, yet large uncertainties remain regarding its variability, long-term trends and relationships to tropopause behavior. Here we characterize the seasonality, vertical structure, and variability of water vapor near the extratropical tropopause and the extratropical transition layer (ExTL). title: Viewing extreme precipitation intensification through an absolute-change lens
abstract: Abstract While relative fractional changes are widely used to characterize extreme precipitation intensification under climate warming, absolute changes provide a complementary perspective that more directly quantifies the magnitude of extreme precipitation intensification, with direct implications for assessing potential impacts. title: Legionella Risk Management in Building Water Systems: Current Perspectives from Industry Practitioners
abstract: Building water systems are internationally recognised reservoirs for opportunistic premise plumbing pathogens, including Legionella , the causative agent of Legionnaires’ disease. Inadequate design, operation and maintenance can promote Legionella proliferation and expose building occupants to potentially fatal infection. Effective management is therefore critical; however, there is limited international evidence regarding how guidelines for controlling Legionella risk are implemented in practice. abstract: Abstract Rapid Arctic warming intensifies wildfire activity across high‐latitude ecosystems, yet post‐fire surface responses of boreal forests and tundra remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate land surface temperature (LST) and energy partitioning responses during the first post‐fire summer across the pan‐Arctic using satellite observations and surface energy‐balance diagnostics. title: Auxetic meta-biomaterial with low cell adhesion and stiffness matching for human intervertebral disc repair
abstract: Lumbar disc herniation is a common cause of disabling back pain and requires effective treatment strategies; however, conventional fusion devices are highly rigid and can severely restrict vertebral motion. To address this limitation, a novel auxetic intervertebral disc implant was designed and fabricated by 3D printing followed by oil-coating post-processing. abstract: Abstract 2D finite deformation analysis commonly relies on simplified assumptions such as plane strain and isovolume, which are insufficient to fully characterize 3D geological structures, leading to incomplete tectonic interpretations. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the Mohr‐cyclide for finite deformation as a new kinematic tool to fully visualize and quantify 3D deformation.
