abstract: Hydroclimate variability across the East European Plain plays a critical role in regional ecosystems and climate dynamics, yet moisture-sensitive tree-ring proxies remain scarce in this region, particularly at high latitudes where tree-ring width (TRW) and density are primarily controlled by temperature. Tree-ring cellulose oxygen isotopes ( δ 18 O TRC ) have the potential to serve as a useful hydroclimate proxy, but their climatic signal in this region remains poorly understood. title: Coordination between respiratory flexibility, photosynthetic carbon gain, and primary carbon metabolism allows thermal acclimation in different quinoa ecotypes
abstract: Temperature strongly influences plant carbon balance by altering the coordination between photosynthesis, mitochondrial respiration, and carbon allocation. However, how these processes are integrated during thermal acclimation remains poorly understood in quinoa ( Chenopodium quinoa Willd.). We hypothesized that Altiplano and lowland quinoa ecotypes exhibit distinct thermal acclimation strategies, characterized by differences in the coordination of photosynthetic carbon gain, respiratory flexibility, and carbon allocation between growth and stress-related metabolism. title: Violencia digital y normalización de conductas agresivas en bachillerato: implicaciones neurobiológicas
abstract: Exposure to aggressive content in digital environments poses challenges for school coexistence and adolescents’ perceptions of harm. This study aimed to describe reported exposure to digital violence, attitudes towards its normalization, emotional sensitivity, empathy, and behavioural responses among high-school students in Durán, Ecuador. A non-experimental, cross-sectional, descriptive quantitative study was conducted using aggregated tabulations from 92 questionnaires. title: Droplet dynamics in upward and downward Full-Cone sprays under atmospheric and Sub-Atmospheric conditions
abstract: This study compares droplet size, velocity, and sampled computational-parcel distributions in upward and downward full-cone water sprays under atmospheric and sub-atmospheric pressures. Spray orientation, angle (65° and 75°), flow rate (1.75 and 3.50 L min –1 ), and chamber pressure were investigated using Particle Image Velocimetry, Shadowgraph imaging, and Large Eddy Simulation coupled with the Discrete Phase Model. abstract: ABSTRACT Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has demonstrated its usefulness for population-level monitoring of many biomarkers in near-real time. As a source of data, it has continued potential across many applications, but with resources finite and uncertainties potentially large, methodological advancements are required for this potential to be achieved. abstract: This paper investigates the grammaticalization of the numeral ‘one’ in Slavic languages at the syntax-semantics interface. abstract: ABSTRACT There is a growing interest in the use of nature-based solutions (NbS) to mitigate natural hazards. However, limited parameterization exists for runoff, erosion, and mudflow models, preventing upscaling of NbS effects to the catchment scale for management purposes. In this study, a parameterization of NbS such as fascines, hedgerows, grass strips, and ponds is proposed and implemented in a catchment-scale runoff and erosion model applicable by non-experts (WaterSed). abstract: Abstract Wetland water quality plays a vital role in controlling emissions of methane, a strong greenhouse gas, and it is regulated by the sequestration of nutrients and toxic metals on iron‐rich soils. abstract: Wind turbine wakes significantly reduce downstream performance, yet accurately modeling their sensitivity to atmospheric stability and terrain remains a challenge. abstract: Absorption muography infers path-averaged density from the attenuation of atmospheric muons. Transient flux variations driven by weather, solar activity, and geomagnetism bias sequential measurements that rely on a non-simultaneous background. title: Cropland and population exposure to extreme precipitation events in Central Asia under future climate change
abstract: Central Asia (CA) is experiencing rapid warming and an intensifying hydrological cycle, with important implications for extreme precipitation events (EPEs). However, future changes in cropland and population exposure to EPEs remain insufficiently quantified in this climate-sensitive dryland region. Here, we projected changes in EPE characteristics and associated cropland and population exposure across CA using daily precipitation simulations from five bias-adjusted ISIMIP3b global climate models under SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5. The historical period 1995–2014 was used as the reference,

title: Tectonics on Early Earth Driven by Earth's Changing Shape During Tidal Recession of the Moon
abstract: Abstract Few fragments of Earth's earliest crust have survived, and so this formative period of our planet's history is shrouded in mystery. To leverage the limited data available, it is important to understand all the processes that could have shaped our young planet. Here, I explore a previously neglected aspect of early‐Earth dynamics: rotation. Earth after the Moon‐forming impact was rapidly rotating with its rotation rate slowing significantly during the first tens of millions of years after the impact as the Moon tidally receded. title: Rising temperatures, shifting population: Changes in children’s ambient heat exposure in China
abstract: The frequency and intensity of heat waves are increasing, but how these trends translate to changes in the ambient heat to which children are potentially exposed (hereafter, exposures) is not well established. One complicating factor is that it is not only extreme temperatures that change over time, but also the geospatial distribution of children. title: Understanding convection in sputnik Planitia, Pluto, requires additional rheological measurements of volatile ices
abstract: The volatile ices N 2 , CO, and CH 4 are central to the geology of the distant Kuiper belt, but data on the rheological behavior of these ices are limited. This is especially true for N 2 ice, for which there is only one published study. Although theoretical models of diffusion creep are undoubtedly applicable to these ices, the dominant creep mechanisms under geological conditions are likely non-Newtonian, or power-law. title: VECTORS OF PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP DEVELOPMENT BASED ON AN ECOSYSTEM APPROACH IN UKRAINE
abstract: The study investigates the principles of public-private partnership (PPP) development as a key instrument for the post-war reconstruction of Ukraine. It is substantiated that traditional approaches ignore systemic interconnections and disrupt the integrity of the economic environment. Based on the analysis of the regulatory and legislative framework, a comprehensive mechanism for evaluating and initiating investment projects has been developed. title: From Temporary Projects to Project Lineages: Explaining Continuity Across Projects
abstract: This research examines how continuity is constituted across formally separate projects. Drawing on a 10-year longitudinal case study of repeated owner-contractor interaction in the expansion of Shanghai Pudong International Airport, it investigates how temporary project organising can generate inter-organisational project lineages that sustain continuity over time. The study adopts a process perspective and shows that project termination need not mark the end of organising. title: Correlation of conventional histopathology and GeneXpert MTB/RIF in the diagnosis of spinal tuberculosis.
abstract: Introduction: Spinal tuberculosis (STB) remains a significant health burden in tuberculosis-endemic regions, including India. Diagnosis is challenging because conventional microbiological methods, including acid-fast staining and mycobacterial culture, have limited sensitivity in paucibacillary disease. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of GeneXpert MTB/RIF in comparison with conventional histopathological examination (HPE) for the diagnosis of STB. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included 64 patients with clinical and radiological suspicion of spinal tuberculosis

title: The single Cryptosporidium rhoptry sequentially drives invasion and host-parasite interface formation
abstract: The apicomplexan parasite Cryptosporidium is a leading cause of diarrheal disease in young children. Within the intestinal epithelium, Cryptosporidium establishes a unique intracellular niche in the apical brush border of enterocytes. A structurally complex interface between host and parasite acts as a holdfast and enables protein and metabolite transport. How the parasite invades its host cell and builds the interface is poorly understood. Here, we reveal parasite invasion with high temporal and spatial resolution using rigorous molecular markers. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: An integrated analytical framework linking green and blue infrastructure spatial patterns with human thermal stress using UTCI
abstract: Urban heat stress poses a critical challenge under climate change and rapid urbanization, prompting the adoption of Green-Blue Infrastructure (GBI) as a key mitigation strategy. Despite its potential, previous studies have reported inconsistent relationships between GBI spatial configuration and urban thermal environments due to methodological variations and urban structural diversity. title: Longitudinal profiling of putative SCFA-associated gut taxa and sodium butyrate epithelial assays in acute myeloid leukemia
abstract: Introduction Intensive therapy for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) disrupts intestinal homeostasis, but the relationship between microbial composition and epithelial injury remains uncertain. Methods We analyzed 508 longitudinal stool samples from 67 patients using patient-clustered models, conducted an exploratory microbiome Mendelian randomization (MR) screen and host-gene annotation, and evaluated sodium butyrate (NaB) in chemotherapy-injured epithelial and inflammatory cell assays. title: Constraining Ganymede’s interior structure and bulk composition from its present-day magnetic field strength
abstract: Ganymede is the only Solar System satellite with a global magnetic field driven by a core dynamo. Although its small moment-of-inertia (MoI) factor indicates a differentiated structure of a metallic core, rocky mantle, and outer hydrosphere, its exact bulk composition and layer thicknesses remain highly uncertain. We developed a comprehensive, long-term thermochemical evolution model that couples thermal history with magnetic field generation. title: Current Evidence Does Not Support Substantial DNA Cytosine Methylation in Myxosporean Genomes
abstract: Some invertebrate lineages are known to have lost their ability to methylate DNA cytosines. These lineages have often lost the enzymes responsible for cytosine methylation (DNMT1 and 3), as well as other enzymes that interact with methylated cytosines. Previous studies showed that myxosporeans, a group of parasitic cnidarians, lack recognisable DNMTs and other canonical methylation enzymes, and observed a lack of cytosine methylation in two myxosporeans using whole genome bisulfite sequencing. title: Agent‐Based Modelling of Microbialite Formation Through Sedimentation and Precipitation Dynamics
abstract: Fossil microbialites resulting from the interplay of sedimentation and precipitation are among the oldest evidence of life on Earth and help geobiologists to interpret many sedimentary environments. However, the factors governing their internal structure and external morphology are still poorly understood. Additionally, abiotic processes can mimic the morphology of some microbialites, complicating their use as 'biosignatures'. title: Mountains Modulate the Response of Precipitation Flashiness to Warming in High‐Resolution Simulations Over the Western US
abstract: Abstract Global climate models (GCMs) robustly predict that precipitation will become flashier (i.e., more concentrated in time) as the climate warms, with extremely wet events accounting for a larger share of total precipitation at a given location. Here we test this prediction across the western United States, where precipitation is modulated by orographic mechanisms that GCMs do not resolve. Using the daily Gini index, we analyze the change in precipitation flashiness within an ensemble of high‐resolution regional climate model (RCM) simulations. Mechanical equivalence of circumferential and spherical-cap debonding morphologies in CFST columns
abstract: Steel–concrete debonding in concrete-filled steel tube (CFST) members reduces composite action by delaying or suppressing the mobilization of confinement. Debonding is commonly described through scalar geometric parameters, such as debonded area ratio or arc-length ratio, although different gap morphologies may induce different confinement mechanisms. This paper investigates the mechanical equivalence between two representative debonding morphologies in circular CFST short columns: circumferential debonding gaps (CDG) and spherical-cap debonding gaps (SDG). title: Eurocodes evolution: basis of design
abstract: Mungo Stacy and Steve Denton explain the key technical changes and practical implications of the updates to basis of design in the second-generation suite of Eurocodes.

title: Pine straw raking increases evaporative flux from forest floor
abstract: Litter layer removal by commercial pine straw raking has potential to increase forest floor evaporation (E s ) by strengthening soil surface-atmosphere coupling; however, its effects on E s and soil water availability remain poorly quantified. We investigated the influence of pine straw raking on E s within a closed-canopy loblolly pine ( Pinus taeda L.) plantation using non-weighing box lysimeters with both intact and removed litter layers (litter and rake treatments, respectively) over a one-year period, hypothesizing that raking would increase annual E s . title: Perceived benefits and socio-environmental pressures of urban service tourism in Hat Yai, Thailand
abstract: Border cities often pursue service-led tourism because visitor spending supports accommodation, transport, food, retail and leisure. The same demand may also intensify pollution, living costs and pressure on urban land. This study provides a 2025 post-pandemic descriptive update on perceived socioeconomic and environmental impacts of service tourism in Hat Yai, Thailand. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey covered 300 respondents recruited through purposive and snowball procedures, with equal quotas of residents, tourism operators and domestic/international tourists (n = 100 each). title: iHeatApp: A climate data visualization and delivery technology for mitigating heat exposure and risks in agriculture
abstract: Agricultural workers are routinely exposed to extreme heat, posing serious health risks. Effective communication of information about heat risk requires fast, easy-to-use, real-time tools for the relevant stakeholders. For this purpose, we have developed the iHeatApp web-based application, accessible via smartphones, tablets, or computers, to visualize forecasted Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) and to quantify the risks at given WBGT levels. The app was developed using free and open-source technologies, with a Python-based backend for data retrieval and transformation and a React-based front
journal: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction

title: Nature-based ecologies of cooling: place-based pathways to advancing heat resilience in an informal settlement of Chennai (India)
abstract: Urban heat is transforming as a major disaster and challenge to urban planners and policy makers. The impacts of urban heat are disproportionate and much severe amongst marginalized communities. Nature-based traditional ecological knowledge has become a vital heat adaptive mechanism for such communities. This study offers distinctive contribution, by reframing nature-based traditional ecological solutions for advancing urban heat resilience through the lens of informal settlements, a context that is largely overlooked in mainstream climate adaptation research and policy. title: From element tests to field-scale creep: Back-analysis of the Prackovice landslide with viscohypoplasticity
abstract: Slow-moving landslides impose cumulative damage on roads, bridges, and retaining structures over years to decades, yet predicting displacement rates – their magnitude, spatial distribution, and seasonal modulation - remains beyond the reach of standard stability analyses. Existing approaches to creeping-slope simulations rely either on empirical correlations, on viscoplastic models whose rate parameters are back-fitted to field displacements rather than derived from laboratory tests, or on analytical solutions restricted to uniform geometries. title: Transformational Faulting: The Case of Quartz‐Coesite
abstract: Abstract Transformational faulting in olivine has been widely invoked as a possible triggering mechanism for deep‐focus earthquakes, yet its dynamics remain debated. It is unclear whether it requires the combined effects of heat release, volume change and mechanical strength contrast, or whether it can be triggered by any one of these alone. Here, we tested if transformational faulting can be caused solely by a large volume change, through deformation experiments on novaculite during the quartz‐coesite transition. title: Plant hydraulic traits regulating productivity and drought resistance in boreal crops
abstract: Plant hydraulics play a critical role in coordinating photosynthesis, water use, and hydraulic safety when facing water scarcity. The hydraulic traits of boreal crops and their relevance to productivity and drought resistance, however, remain poorly researched. In this study, we combined multi-year carbon and water flux measurements from two Finnish fields representing contrasting boreal cropping systems – a perennial forage grass mixture and an annual cereal crop (oats) – with a novel modelling framework coupling plant photosynthesis, hydraulics, and soil moisture dynamics to decipher the fie

title: Microfluidic synthesis of core/shell structured nanoplatelet-encapsulated microcapsule materials with high monodispersity for carbon capture
abstract: An off-shelf needle-based microfluidic emulsification system was developed for fabricating the core/shell structured microcapsules in a multiphase system using the water-in-oil-in-water (W/O/W) double emulsion template. The interfacial flow dynamics in the multiphase microsystem were modulated, and potassium carbonate, monoethanolamine (MEA), and MEA with graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) were successfully encapsulated, respectively, in silicone-based polymer TEGO RAD 2650. title: Experimental study of the impact dynamics of polymeric hollow droplets
abstract: The impact dynamics of hollow droplets, while influential in applications such as coating and spraying, remain less explored than their dense counterparts. This knowledge gap is particularly pronounced for viscoelastic hollow droplets. This study presents an experimental investigation into the impact of hollow Newtonian (water) and viscoelastic (polymeric solution) droplets on a solid surface at different impact velocities and polymer concentrations. title: Impulse flushing of the Inhulets River taking into account sedimentation in the Karachunivske Reservoir
abstract: The study investigates the potential effect of changing the release regime from the Karachunivske Reservoir when applying the impulse flushing method to the Inhulets River on the transport, settling, and export of suspended material. The relevance of the study is determined by the fact that previously proposed impulse flushing regimes were assessed mainly in terms of water quality and water-use efficiency, whereas the possible sedimentation consequences of changing the temporal structure of releases were not considered separately. title: Quantifying Ion‐Specific Effects on the Size‐Exclusion Transport of Multi‐Sized Colloids in Porous Media Using a Novel Synthetic DNA Labeling Approach
abstract: Abstract Colloids strongly adsorb pollutants and promote their co‐transport in aquatic environments, posing substantial ecological contamination risks. However, quantifying the size exclusion effect (SEE), a critical mechanism that enhances colloid transport, remains challenging in multi‐sized colloid systems, owing to limited high‐resolution labeling methods and ion‐induced dynamic aggregation. title: Experimental and Numerical Analysis of Vinyl Ester Composites Reinforced with Coconut and Glass
abstract: Vinyl ester composites reinforced with treated coconut (shells and fibers) and glass (powder and fibers) have been investigated using numerical, experimental, and statistical methods. Tensile and bending tests were applied. Numerical simulation was conducted using the Finite Element Method (FEM) with the ABAQUS CAE 2019 program for tensile and flexural samples. title: Experiments and numerical simulations on the characteristics and protection of water hammer in long-distance liquid ammonia pipelines
abstract: With the expansion of ammonia energy applications, long-distance liquid ammonia pipelines are expected to support large-scale cross-regional ammonia transport. However, rapid valve closure during pipeline operation can generate severe water hammer pressures, posing significant threats to system safety. title: Chrono-grounding of the Micoquian and Aurignacian occupations at Piekary III open-air site (Krakow, Poland)
abstract: Abstract Human occupation of Central Europe during the Late Pleistocene was strongly influenced by climatic fluctuations, resulting in discontinuous settlement patterns and repeated phases of regional abandonment and recolonization. Southern Poland represents a key frontier zone within these dynamics, yet the chronological resolution of many sites remains limited, particularly for assemblages excavated during the early twentieth century. title: Assessing Strategies to Optimize Participatory Science Data in Species Distribution Models
abstract: ABSTRACT Aims Data from participatory science projects are widely used to understand species distributions. However, participatory science data often contain biases that can obscure real patterns. We address two sources of sampling bias: location uncertainty of individual records and spatially heterogeneous sampling effort. A variety of data processing and modelling strategies have been used to address these biases, without consensus on their relative effectiveness. title: Experimental and Numerical Hydrodynamic Analysis of a Waterfall Humidifier
abstract: This study experimentally and numerically investigates the hydrodynamic performance of a waterfall-type direct humidification system under crossflow air conditions. A transient, three-dimensional, multiphase Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model based on the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method was developed to simulate the interaction between the horizontal air stream and a vertical water column. title: Short fire-return intervals modify fuel structure, changing flammability and fire behavior in dry forests of southeastern Australia
abstract: Abstract Shortening fire-return intervals are pushing fire-tolerant ecosystems in temperate Australia beyond their ecological limits, producing alternative vegetation states with markedly different composition and structure. While the structural effects of these regime shifts on fire-tolerant eucalypt forests have been documented, their consequences for flammability and fire behavior remain largely untested. title: Lead-free soft hybrid materials for piezoelectric sensors: A paradigm shift from toxic lead-based ceramics to sustainable electronics
abstract: The development of piezoelectric materials has significantly transformed modern electronic and sensing technologies, and their use has extended from extremely precise actuators to wearable self-powering devices. But the problem is that these materials are commonly made out of lead-based ceramics, and for example, lead zirconate titanate (PZT) contains 60% of lead. title: Combustion performance and low NO emissions of hydrogen-enriched gas industrial boilers based on flue gas recirculation technology
abstract: To reduce the NO emissions of hydrogen-enriched industrial gas boilers caused by temperature enhancement, the flue gas recirculation technology was implemented in hydrogen-enriched industrial gas boilers to achieve low-nitrogen combustion. A Diffusion Flamelet model with the reaction mechanism of GRI-Mech 3.0 and an iterative method for calculating boundary conditions was built to numerically investigate the effects of hydrogen blending ratio and flue gas recirculation ratio on the combustion performance and NO emissions. title: Do protected-area enclaves constrain NPP gains in forest landscapes? Counterfactual evidence from Hainan tropical rainforest national park, China
abstract: Protected-area enclaves are areas geographically surrounded by protected areas (PAs) but outside the jurisdiction of their management authorities, yet their implications for conservation effectiveness remain understudied from a counterfactual perspective. Using estimated net primary productivity (NPP) data from 2014 to 2024, we examined five large enclaves in Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park within a propensity score matching–difference-in-differences (PSM-DID) framework. title: INTEGRATED HYDRO-ECONOMIC ASSESSMENT OF GROUNDWATER WELLFIELD DEVELOPMENT USING COUPLED MODFLOW-WEAP MODELING: CASE STUDY OF KIGALI, RWANDA
abstract: Rapid urbanization and population growth have substantially increased municipal water demand in Kigali, Rwanda, creating an urgent need for sustainable and economically efficient groundwater development strategies. This study presents an integrated hydro-economic framework for optimizing groundwater wellfield development in the shallow alluvial and weathered rock aquifers of the Nyabarongo River basin. abstract: Abstract Early pressurized flowback following large-scale hydraulic fracturing may substantially increase well-control risks under high-temperature, high-pressure, and sand-laden downhole conditions. In this study, an integrated analytical, finite-element, and experimental framework is established to investigate the mechanical behavior of a controllable downhole blowout-prevention workstring during run-in, shut-in pressure holding, and unsetting and retrieval. abstract: To characterize the regional differences, spectral composition, and temporal stability of pressure pulsations throughout the entire flow passage of a large prototype Francis turbine under different loads, three-dimensional unsteady simulations were performed at three representative operating conditions-OP65, OP80, and OP100-corresponding to approximately 65%, 80%, and 100% of the rated power output, respectively, under fixed head and rotational speed. title: Comparative mitogenomics of Hippophae reveals conserved gene content, repeat-mediated structural variation, and limited phylogenetic resolution
abstract: Plant mitochondrial genomes retain conserved coding content but evolve rapidly in structure. We assembled mitogenomes of four Hippophae taxa from long reads and compared them with four published mitogenomes. abstract: This paper describes a physically-based algorithm for estimating the mass-weighted raindrop diameter ( D m ) and the corresponding Doppler velocities ( V D ) which are the radar reflectivity-weighted terminal velocities of the raindrops. The algorithm exploits the attenuation-corrected radar reflectivity ( Z e ) and the specific attenuation ( k ) observed by Ku- and W-band space-borne Doppler radars and estimate D m assuming a specified drop size distribution DSD. title: Coupled Geophysical and Technoeconomic Industrial Growth Constraints on Geological Carbon Storage Scale-Up: Application to UK Offshore Resources
abstract: Geological carbon dioxide storage is central to meeting many national climate change commitments, but large-scale deployment may be limited by both techno-economic rates of growth and physics-based processes imposed by subsurface geology. We develop a modeling framework for the assessment of feasible CO2 storage scale-up trajectories that unifies constraints arising from industrial rates of growth, dynamic injection rate limits from reservoir pressurization, and static maximum cumulative storage resource. title: Aspects of mesh sensitivity for phenomenological damage models using small solid and large shell elements
abstract: Application-oriented simulations, such as automotive crash simulations, often utilize large shell elements to optimize computational efficiency. This study applies the crack band approach typically used for concrete materials to steel sheets. The aim was to examine this regularization method for different stress states with plane stress shell elements to reduce mesh sensitivity, in respect to element size as well as to element shape. title: Spatiotemporal variability of atmospheric drought during the growing season in Poland: a multi-index analysis based on SPEI, VPD, and HTC (1980–2024)
abstract: Atmospheric drought constitutes one of the most significant manifestations of contemporary climate change in Central Europe, including Poland, where rising air temperatures and changes in precipitation patterns lead to increasing water deficits. The aim of this study was to analyze the temporal and spatial variability of atmospheric drought in Poland during the growing season over the period 1980–2024, with particular emphasis on the calendar periods of plant development. title: Design-oriented comparison and load adaptability of deep cement mixing columns with different cross-sectional geometries for soft-soil bridge foundations
abstract: This study develops a capacity-equivalent framework for selecting circular, square, and rectangular deep cement mixing (DCM) columns for a soft-soil bridge foundation when pier load varies in service. Unlike equal-length shape comparisons, the required column length was determined separately for each geometry and area replacement ratio under the same 240 kN bearing-capacity criterion. title: Exploring Magnetic Reconnection in a Sub-A-class Microflare Using Data-constrained Numerical Simulation and Multi-instrument Observations
abstract: Abstract Solar flares are intermittent events that convert free magnetic energy into heat and kinetic energy of charged particles, along with a rearrangement of magnetic field lines (MFLs) through magnetic reconnection. This work investigates an active-region sub-A-class microflare detected by the Solar X-ray Monitor on board Chandrayaan-2. title: Multiple genetic routes to pelvic spine loss in brook stickleback
abstract: Pelvic spine loss has evolved repeatedly in stickleback species and represents an intri-guing opportunity to study genetically parallel adaptation. While previous work has identified key loci associated with this trait, the extent to which different populations rely on the same genetic mechanisms remains unclear. The genetic basis of pelvic spine loss in Culaea incon-stans (Kirtland 1840) has only been investigated in three populations. title: Degradation-front evolution and micromechanical heterogeneity in cement pastes incorporating expansive agents under sodium sulfate attack
abstract: Expansive agents (EAs) are widely used in concrete but have the potential to reshape the physicochemical pathways under external sulfate attack (ESA) due to the internal introduction of calcium-aluminum-sulfur. ESA induces a depth-dependent degradation front that drives progressive microstructural and chemical degradation; however, the evolution of this reaction front in EA-modified systems remains poorly understood. title: Code-Based Design and ANSYS-Ready Nonlinear Finite Element Modeling of Isolated and Raft Reinforced Concrete Foundations under ECP 203, ACI 318, and Eurocode 2
abstract: This study presents a systematic computational framework for the code-based design and ANSYS-ready nonlinear finite element modeling of isolated and raft reinforced concrete foundations. Thirty base scenarios, comprising 18 isolated footings and 12 raft foundations, were designed according to ECP 203 (2018), ACI 318-19, and Eurocode 2 (EN 1992-1-1), yielding 90 code-specific design alternatives. title: Nitrogen fertilization and plant density effects on sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L.) productivity, chlorophyll status, and grain yield under semi-arid Mediterranean conditions
abstract: Nitrogen (N) fertilization and plant density determine sorghum ( Sorghum bicolor L. Moench) productivity and govern the fertilizer energy and irrigation water used per unit of grain. title: The effect of tuned liquid damper placement on the seismic response of a high-rise building: A reduced-order modelling study
abstract: High-fidelity fluid–structure interaction (FSI) analysis is widely recognized as one of the most accurate approaches for evaluating the seismic performance of tuned liquid dampers (TLDs). However, coupling a three-dimensional FSI model with a detailed finite-element model of a high-rise building requires substantial computational resources, limiting its application in routine engineering analysis and preliminary design. abstract: Human activities and climate variability jointly threaten biosphere functional integrity and ecosystem functioning. abstract: Naturally occurring magnetotactic bacteria have an inherent ability to sense and align to earth's geomagnetic field due to the presence of magnetosomes-membranous microstructures containing iron oxide nanoparticles. These functionalities can be exploited for tuning movements and guided spatial patterning in controlled magnetic field. While being arduous to culture in laboratories, these organisms have complex genetic make-up with tight regulation on their magnetosome synthesis. title: Surface and Subsurface Water Interactions and Recycling in an Alpine Watershed on Tibetan Plateau: Multi‐Scale Evidence From Reach to Basin
abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater–river water interactions govern water redistribution within alpine watersheds, yet the linkage between reach‐scale water exchange and basin‐scale water budgets remains poorly constrained. This research takes the Buha River watershed on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau as an example to explore these connections with the aid of hydrogeochemical and hydrological analyses. Results indicate that pronounced upstream‐to‐downstream geological variability can lead to considerable differences between reach‐scale and basin‐scale water budgets in cryosphere‐influenced alpine watershed

title: Streamwise measurements of a hypersonic shock layer radiation
abstract: Abstract A simultaneous spectroscopic and visualization system was developed to study hypersonic shock layer radiation along a streamwise line-of-sight. The system was implemented to observe emissions ahead of projectile travelling at approximately 7 km/s in a controlled argon environment at the JAXA/ISAS two-stage light gas ballistic range facility. Experimental conditions were designed to establish equilibrium flow within the shock layer, enabling comparison of the measured emission spectra with equilibrium radiation models. abstract: Abstract The dominant Earth–Moon tide is accurately described by Newtonian theory, but interpreting a possible off-diagonal residual requires separating its signature from errors in the standard tidal model. In a local lunar principal frame, the Newtonian plus channel varies as cos ( 2 β ) , whereas a symmetric off-diagonal residual enters the sin ( 2 β ) quadrature. We extend this separation to a globally defined three-dimensional symmetric trace-free tensor with two transverse coefficients projected onto each station vertical. title: Examining the spatial effect ranges of new classes of long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) on malaria infection and vector abundance: an anisotropic semivariance analysis in the context of a phase-III cluster-randomised malaria vector control trial of dual active-ingredient LLINs
abstract: At high levels of population coverage with long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs), reductions in malaria vector populations can create a community effect, protecting individuals in an area who do not sleep under a net themselves. In cluster-randomised trials evaluating new LLINs, spatially localised reductions in malaria transmission may impact nearby clusters unless carefully designed, leading to attenuated treatment effect estimates. title: Spatiotemporal hydroclimatic signals in native Andean forests of Argentina inferred from carbon and oxygen stable isotopes
abstract: Understanding past hydroclimatic variability is important for sustainable water resource management in semi-arid mountainous regions. This study characterizes the contrasting hydro-thermal signals recorded by stable isotopes from two strategically selected tree-ring chronologies at two contrasting sites in the Argentine and Central Andes. We analyze a 212-year δ¹³C record from Fitzroya cupressoides in the humid forests of northern Patagonia (950–1060 m a.s.l.) and a 122-year δ18O record from Polylepis tarapacana in the arid Altiplano (3500 m a.s.l.). title: Impact of aerosol absorption and scattering on winter fog lifecycle: insights from NWP simulations over Indo-Gangetic Plains
abstract: The Indo-Gangetic Plains (IGP) of India frequently experience widespread and dense winter fog with substantial health and economic consequences. This season also coincides with elevated aerosol loading. This study investigates the influence of aerosols on the development and evolution of dense fog over the IGP using high-resolution numerical experiments. We focus especially on the relative contributions of absorption and scattering to aerosol-radiation interactions (ARI). title: Process sequencing in torrefied pellet production: Evidence gaps, performance trade-offs and a decision framework for industrial deployment
abstract: Torrefaction and pelletisation are reviewed as complementary biomass-upgrading operations, yet plant design lacks a defensible basis for deciding which operation should precede the other. This synthesis evaluates torrefy-then-densify (T → P) and densify-then-torrefy (P → T) by separating direct comparisons from single-route experiments and system evidence. title: Guided-wave transmission of ultrasonic signals using compressive sensing and time-domain encoding
abstract: The increasing deployment of intelligent structures and embedded sensor networks creates a growing demand for reliable transmission of measurement data in environments where conventional wired and wireless communication methods are ineffective. In metallic and enclosed structures, electromagnetic waves are strongly attenuated, while wired solutions increase system complexity and weight. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel guided-wave-based framework for the transmission of full ultrasonic measurement signals within structural elements. title: Temperature-dependent tribological performance of HVOF-thermal sprayed FeCoCrNiAl HEA coating deposited on TC4 alloy
abstract: Abstract A FeCoCrNiAl high-entropy alloy (HEA) coating was deposited on a Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) alloy substrate by high-velocity oxygen fuel (HVOF) thermal spraying to enhance its sliding wear performance. Reciprocating sliding tests were conducted from 25 to 300 °C, and the temperature-dependent friction behavior, wear morphology, and damage evolution were examined. Meanwhile, an Archard-based finite element model incorporating the arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian adaptive mesh technique was established to reproduce the progressive wear process. title: Transient VOF analysis of geometry-controlled water ingress in residential sliding-window sills
abstract: Wind-driven rain (WDR) can cause water ingress through residential window-frame assemblies during tropical-cyclone events, even when structural failure does not occur. While external WDR exposure has been widely studied, the transient hydraulic response within sliding-window sill cavities remains less well quantified. This study presents a three-dimensional transient two-phase CFD investigation of water ingress through a residential sliding-window sill, focusing on the influence of internal drainage geometry. title: Energy stability and performance of hybrid turbine systems in hydropower plants
abstract: Hydropower plants designed around a single turbine lose a considerable share of their conversion efficiency when river discharge falls below the design range, a situation that is becoming more frequent as drought periods lengthen. This study uses computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to evaluate whether a sequentially operated Francis–Pelton configuration can keep energy conversion stable over a wide discharge range at a common net head of 200 m. title: Dependent autonomy: developing and refining a theoretical construct of managerial autonomy in healthcare
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Value-based healthcare (VBHC) and High-Value Health System (HVHS) frameworks identify components intended to support healthcare transformation. Their practical use may depend partly on organisational conditions affecting managerial authority. This study aimed to develop and refine dependent autonomy as a proposed theoretical construct concerning the practical exercise of delegated authority. title: Coordinated physical and chemical defenses underlie selenium nanodots-primed rice resistance to a stem borer
abstract: Seed priming is a promising strategy for boosting plant insect resistance, and selenium nanodots (Se NDs) stand out for their superior biocompatibility and bioactivity. Here, we report that seed priming with 50 mg/L Se NDs (ND50) strongly enhances rice resistance against the striped stem borer, Chilo suppressalis (Walker) (Lepidoptera: Pyralidae), across three rice cultivars (Minghui 63, Xiushui 11 and Nipponbare). title: Characterization of physical and chemical properties controlling the transport of 129I and 99Tc in ultra-high-performance grout
abstract: Ultra-high-performance grout (UHPG) was evaluated as an engineered barrier for encapsulating solid waste generated during nuclear waste processing. The objective of this study was to measure geochemical, hydrological, and physical properties related to 129 I and 99 Tc transport through UHPG. 99 Tc and 129 I are key health-risk drivers associated with near-subsurface nuclear disposal facilities. title: Individualized Homoeopathy Added to Standard Pharmacological Care for Migraine: A Pragmatic Randomized Open-Label Blinded-Endpoint Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background: Migraine is the second leading cause of years lived with disability worldwide and the leading cause among young women; daily functioning, rather than attack frequency alone, is now a priority outcome. Individualized homoeopathy is widely used as an adjunct, yet adjunctive pragmatic evidence in tertiary public-sector Indian care is scarce. title: The Effect of Field Line Tracing Height on Wang‐Sheeley‐Arge Solar Wind Predictions at Earth
abstract: Abstract A key component of the widely used Wang‐Sheeley‐Arge model is the tracing of magnetic field lines in the solar corona, as that largely determines the modeled open/closed field regions and in turn the predicted large‐scale solar wind structure. However, small closed field regions interspersed among the open field lines inside coronal holes (CHs) often hinder determination of the large‐scale open–closed boundary. title: General Solution Scaling Relations in Linear Elastic Dynamic Rupture Models
abstract: Abstract Dynamic rupture models have been widely used to enhance our understanding of earthquake processes and associated hazards. A commonly held insight among modelers is that if the initial stress, rheological parameters, and space and time coordinates are scaled by certain factors in a specific manner, the solution will scale accordingly and remain similar. title: How Coffee Farmers Respond to Climate Stress in East Java’s Mountain Regions: A Social-Ecological Resilience Perspective
abstract: Tropical mountain coffee farms integrate crop production with tree cover, soil functions, water use, and rural livelihoods. In East Java, farmers reported irregular rainfall and interacting pressures affecting coffee production and household decisions. This study examines farmers’ response breadth and interprets these patterns through a social-ecological resilience perspective without treating response counts as direct measures of resilience. institutions: National Pingtung University of Science and Technology

title: Potential Operational, Economic and Carbon Consequences of Geopolitical Airspace Restrictions for Philippine Long-Haul Aviation: A Scenario Analysis
abstract: Geopolitical airspace restrictions can alter long-haul routing, fuel use, costs and emissions. This study evaluates the conditional consequences of assumed path extensions for eight Manila airport pairs. Published Fuel Estimation in Air Transportation coefficients for the Airbus A350-900, Boeing 787-9 and Boeing 777-300ER were combined with five assumed path increments, yielding 120 deterministic cases. title: Microstructural properties of ordinary concrete mixed with rubber and plastic waste under aggressive environmental conditions: A full‐factorial design study
abstract: Abstract The aim of this study was to incorporate the waste plastic and rubber into concrete in order to manufacture concrete that is resistant to aggressive environments, using the factorial approach to assess the effect of different factors (rubber and plastic) on the selected responses. In this research, ordinary Portland cement and fine aggregate were partially replaced with rubber and plastic as a mass substitute in the proportions of 2% and 4% and the fine aggregate 2%, 4%, and 6%, respectively. title: Retrieval of bimodal aerosol size distributions for stratospheric sulfate and smoke aerosols using multi–wavelength satellite measurements
abstract: Pyrocumulonimbus events (pyroCb) are a natural driver of stratospheric aerosol variability by injecting smoke plumes containing aerosols and trace gases into the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere. Smoke aerosols are distinct in their chemical, optical, and microphysical properties from stratospheric sulfate aerosols. A new approach in retrieving the bimodal lognormal aerosol size distribution from stratospheric aerosol observations is developed. title: Experimental Validation of Skull Acoustic Modelling Strategies for Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Simulation: A Cross-Comparison Study
abstract: Objective Accurate acoustic modelling of the skull is important for simulation-guided transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) applications. However, existing skull parameterization strategies vary widely in complexity and reported accuracy. This study systematically evaluates commonly used modelling approaches to determine their predictive performance across multiple frequencies and skull types. title: The evolution of hourly strombolian cycles towards paroxysmal activity at Etna volcano
abstract: Abstract Lava fountains are typical of basaltic volcanic eruptions, especially during paroxysms when activity shifts from intermittent Strombolian explosions to sustained high lava discharge often accompanied by ash emission. Cyclic eruptive behaviour –marked by regular variations in explosive intensity and lava fountaining over periods of minutes to hours– has been observed before but rarely captured in the geophysical record. title: An analytical framework for atmospheric tides on rocky planets. II. Semidiurnal thermotidal torque
abstract: The thermodynamic acceleration induced by atmospheric thermal tides has a major impact on the rotation of temperate rocky planets, where gravitational and radiative tidal forcings are of comparable strength. This acceleration drives planets away from synchronous rotation, thereby affecting their climate, large-scale circulation, and surface conditions. These implications underline the need to better constrain the dependence of thermotidal torque on tidal frequency and on the physical parameters characterising a star-planet system, as this relationship remains insufficiently understood. title: A Physically Based Storage‐Runoff Relationship for Steep Hillslopes and Its Application to Distributed Flood Modeling
abstract: Abstract Kinematic wave models are widely used to represent hillslope runoff in distributed hydrological models. However, their simplified descriptions often prevent the effective use of observed soil hydraulic parameters during calibration. To address this limitation, we derived a new analytical storage–runoff relationship that explicitly incorporates percolation under wet‐soil conditions and rapid drainage through subsurface pipes. title: Environmental disruptions and malaria dynamics: causal evidence from climate extremes and fires in the Amazon
abstract: Abstract This study examines the causal effects of droughts, unusually high annual precipitation, and fire exposure on malaria incidence in the Brazilian Amazon using a staggered difference-in-differences approach. Combining municipal-level data from 2007 to 2021, we exploit variation in the timing of exposure to climatic and environmental shocks to estimate their dynamic impacts on malaria outcomes. title: Stationary Resistive MHD Solutions near an Isolated Three-dimensional Magnetic Null
abstract: Abstract Magnetic null points define the topology of magnetic fields in stellar coronae, planetary magnetospheres, and astrospheres and are commonly associated with magnetic reconnection. We investigate the local structure of stationary 3D resistive, incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows in the vicinity of an isolated magnetic null and an isolated velocity stagnation point, assuming that the two nulls are colocated. title: Performance Assessment of Solar Thermal Systems with Heat Storage in Multifamily Buildings Under Real Climatic Conditions
abstract: This study evaluates the long - term performance of a solar thermal system coupled with thermal energy storage (TES) for a reference multifamily building in northeastern Poland using 14 consecutive years (2010 – 2023) of hourly PVGIS - SARAH3 meteorological data . The reference building comprises 16 dwellings and 48 occupants. Domestic hot - water (DHW) consumption was assumed at 50 L per person per day, with cold - and hot - water temperatures of 10 and 55 °C, respectively, and a lumped DHW distribution and storage ef ficiency of 70%. title: A preliminary sustainability assessment framework for traditional medicinal knowledge built from an existing ethnographic record: the Gayo ethnomedicine system, Lut Tawar, Central Aceh, Indonesia
abstract: Traditional medicinal knowledge (TMK) links human health, biodiversity and cultural continuity, yet sustainability-indicator frameworks rarely assess it directly. Our contribution is methodological: we show how an existing ethnographic record can be turned into a transparent, traceable sustainability assessment framework. We worked only from a 2024 ethnographic technical report on the Gayo community of Lut Tawar, Central Aceh, Indonesia, with no new fieldwork and no informant-level data. title: Unsteady early-stage behaviour of horizontal cryogenic hydrogen releases in crosswind
abstract: The impact of crosswind on the early stages of transient horizontal hydrogen release under low pressure-ratio (PR) conditions is investigated using Unsteady Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (URANS) simulations, validated with existing literature data. Our results show that flow separation occurs at the head of the plume during the release event, generating detached parcels of potentially flammable gas that can travel considerable distances. title: A Wall-Modeled Large Eddy Simulation Framework for Sheared Convective Atmospheric Boundary Layers
abstract: Abstract This study presents a wall-modeled large-eddy simulation (WMLES) framework to simulate high-Reynolds-number daytime unstable sheared convective boundary layers (CBL). The framework is implemented using the open-source computational fluid dynamics code OpenFOAM, which employs finite-volume discretization on both uniform and non-uniform grids, and incorporates Hargreaves–Wright-based wall functions to model surface momentum and heat transfer. title: Exploring wake interactions in a counter-rotating dual-rotor system for different yaw configurations: an experimental study
abstract: As an opportunity to increase turbine and wind park efficiencies, multi- and dual-rotor turbines have received great attention among research and industry. The goal of this experimental study is to validate and add findings to numerical simulations on dual rotors. It will be shown that the rotational sense greatly influences the lateral interaction and therefore the downstream evolution of a dual wake. title: Superconducting hydrogen-powered propulsion: Enabling technologies, coupling mechanisms, and system optimization
abstract: Superconducting hydrogen-powered propulsion, synergizing the high specific energy of Liquid Hydrogen (LH 2 ) with the superior power density and efficiency of superconducting technologies, represents a transformative pathway toward zero-carbon aviation. This paper provides a critical review and a dedicated optimization framework for this emerging domain. Fundamental principles of hydrogen and superconductivity are elucidated, with the Hydrogen-Electric-Thermal (HET) coupling mechanism highlighted as the governing nexus of thermodynamic and electromagnetic synergy. title: Slip effects in gravity currents of power-law fluids
abstract: We investigate the propagation of gravity currents of power-law fluids spreading over a slippery substrate. We develop a one-dimensional lubrication model that incorporates a Navier slip condition at the substrate and accounts for shear-dependent viscosity. The resulting formulation shows that the current dynamics is governed by three independent parameters: the injection exponent, the rheological index, and a slip number quantifying the relative importance of substrate slip with respect to bulk viscous transport. title: Análisis de radiación solar y validación experimental en un sistema fotovoltaico aislado.
abstract: The problem of poor energy management and rapid degradation of components in single-source electric vehicles is addressed in this article. To solve this problem, a hybrid energy system combining a lithium-ion battery, supercapacitors, and hydrogen fuel cells is proposed. The vehicle's performance during acceleration and regenerative braking is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. title: Constraining Subsurface Connectivity by Water‐Trace Experiment in Deep, Semi‐Arid Karst Terrain
abstract: Abstract This pilot water‐trace experiment evaluates subsurface hydraulic connectivity between an ephemeral channel and a deep fractured‐carbonate aquifer (vadose zone thickness >300 m) to assess managed aquifer recharge (MAR) feasibility in semi‐arid settings. The study site comprises an ephemeral channel incised into fractured limestone, selected for its documented infiltration capacity and proximity to structural lineaments expected to enhance vertical permeability through the deep unsaturated zone. abstract: Coseismic rupture length is a key parameter for predicting earthquake magnitude and strong ground motion. In contrast to the conventional assumption of fault segmentation, multi-segment earthquakes and partially ruptured earthquakes occur. Therefore, a probabilistic approach to evaluating rupture propagation plays a crucial role in hazard assessment. Turbulent Rayleigh--Bénard convection offers a paradigmatic example, for which Charney conjectured that temperature measurements alone should suffice to determine the velocity field. title: A coupled lattice Boltzmann model for pore-scale mushy-layer dynamics with application to sea ice
abstract: A pore-scale lattice Boltzmann model is developed for reactive transport in phase-changing porous media, coupling solute transport in the liquid with conjugate heat transfer across the solid and liquid phases. Two methodological developments are introduced: a novel link-based Volume-of-Pixel formulation for direction-dependent interface motion, and a generalized Robin boundary treatment for solute redistribution at moving interfaces. title: FESOM2.8 in single precision: climate fidelity over six decades and performance on CPUs and GPUs
abstract: Halving the floating-point precision of an ocean model can make it substantially faster, but whether the rounding errors stay negligible over climate time scales has rarely been tested. We implement single precision in the global ocean-sea-ice model FESOM2 and compare 60-year hindcasts with double-precision controls. abstract: Near-nadir radars, from altimeters and rain radars to wave scatterometers, need a geophysical model function (GMF) relating backscatter to wind, yet most operational models are empirical and specific to one band. This paper delivers KuKa-Mod, an operational near-nadir GMF for wind retrieval at Ku and Ka band, built on one physical description of the sea surface, and evaluates it. abstract: The presence of extreme ocean waves poses substantial threats to the safety of marine engineering applications and navigational activities. Accurate prediction of the nonlinear wave loads on offshore structures in large-diameter cylindrical configuration, such as monopile wind turbines and platform columns, requires a robust solution to the high-order wave diffraction problem. abstract: This work describes a computational approach for rapidly estimating and characterizing the covariance structure of a Gaussian random field from a modest number of i.i.d. replicates by formulating the problem in terms of a sparse inverse Cholesky factor of the data's covariance matrix. title: Shifts in Rossby wave regimes via the change of group velocity with zonal jets
abstract: Evidences show it is questionable to use the trends in Rossby wave phase speed (Cpx) to interpret the relation between the changes of extreme events and westerly jets. title: Sensitivity of the IceCube atmospheric muon rate to decadal trends in the effective atmospheric temperature
abstract: Decadal changes in the Antarctic stratosphere, generally associated with ozone recovery and shifts in polar circulation, are of broad geophysical interest. However, independent long-term measurements of the atmosphere above the Antarctic interior are scarce. We assess whether the atmospheric muon rate recorded by IceCube could constrain decadal changes in the effective atmospheric temperature, $T_\mathrm{eff}$, a weighted average of temperature through the atmosphere that is most sensitive to the stratosphere. abstract: Recent experiments on a wide GaAs quantum well report a fractional quantum Hall state at filling factor ν=1/2 with an unusually large activation gap, a sharp maximum of the gap as a function of density, and a possible transition from the non-Abelian Moore-Read Pfaffian to the Abelian Halperin 331 state. title: Mathematical and Numerical Analysis of Tsunami Generation and Propagation: The Initial Tsunami Condition
abstract: This work investigates the appropriate initial condition for tsunami propagation that allows replacing a kinematic system with its corresponding static formulation, where the bottom is fixed at its final earthquake-induced deformation. Using the two-dimensional (2D) nonlinear shallow-water equations (NSW) and a 2D dispersive $abcd$-Boussinesq system, we prove that for the NSW system, the appropriate initial free-surface condition is exactly the final bottom deformation. title: Is AMOC collapse too unstable in climate models?
abstract: It has been a long-held paradigm that the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation in coupled climate models is too stable, underestimating the possibility of a collapse. A recent analysis of extended simulations to year 2300 in the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project, CMIP6, demonstrated a partial AMOC collapse where the deep circulation completely vanishes. This collapse was simulated by at least one model in all emission scenarios, and it occurred in every model forced by the highest emission scenario when extended to year 2300. title: Spatially varying quantile downscaling of summer temperature from atmospheric circulation and long-term trends over peninsular Spain
abstract: Over recent decades, high temperatures have intensified worldwide, with impacts on human health, ecosystems, and the economy. Understanding their spatial evolution requires accounting for long-term temperature changes and the role of atmospheric circulation. Quantile regression provides a flexible framework for characterizing changes across the temperature distribution, with relevance to extremes. title: Constraining tau-sterile neutrino mixing with high-energy astrophysical neutrinos
abstract: Whether a sterile neutrino mixes with the three active ones remains an open question. Its mixing with the tau neutrino, $|U_{τ4}|^2$, is the least constrained, since terrestrial experiments probe it only indirectly and over limited ranges of sterile-neutrino mass. We show that TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos probe it differently. Their sources make almost no $ν_τ$, but oscillations over cosmological distances turn about one third of them into $ν_τ$ before they reach Earth. title: Haptic Shared Control for Multi-Robot Systems
abstract: Multi-agent systems offer significant advantages in terms of flexibility and redundancy, enabling the efficient distribution of complex tasks among multiple robots. However, their deployment requires advanced control strategies to ensure optimal cooperation between autonomous agents and human operators. We propose a modification of the global connectivity maintenance algorithm to incorporate measurements taken in agent's local frame, using sensors with limited fields of view. title: A unifying view of averaging for wave-mean flow decomposition
abstract: Geophysical flows are routinely decomposed into mean flow and waves, and the procedure used determines how the motion is divided between the two. Ideally, the wave and mean motions of interest evolve on distinct timescales, in which case they can be separated by taking an infinite-time average over all wave periods. Individual waves average away, while exactly resonant interactions contribute to the averaged dynamics because they are steady on the fast timescale. title: Adaptive Kalman Filtering for Streamflow Models with Application to the Camastra Basin
abstract: Accurate streamflow estimation requires a consistent representation of model and observation uncertainty. Such consistency is difficult to obtain when rainfall information is unavailable, or not temporally aligned with the discharge observations. We develop an adaptive Kalman filter for Generalized Shot Noise streamflow models, with recursive estimation of the measurement and process-noise covariances. title: A Second-Order Semi-Implicit Projection Time-Stepping Scheme for the Shallow-Water Equations on the Sphere Using Compatible Finite Elements
abstract: We propose a second-order, semi-implicit time-stepping scheme for the shallow-water equations on the sphere discretised with compatible finite elements. The scheme splits the advection operator from the wave operator, applying a DG-upwind SSPRK3 method to the advection part and an $H(\text{div})$-conforming implicit discretisation to the wave part, solved efficiently via hybridisation. title: Coupled Effects of Biofilm Dynamics and Flow on Hydrogen Transport in a Hydrogen-Generating Fracture
abstract: Biofilm growth in hydrogen-generating fractures modifies fluid flow and hydrogen transport, while microbial activity consumes hydrogen. These coupled processes influence hydrogen recovery in stimulated geologic hydrogen systems. We use high-fidelity simulations to investigate flow, biofilm dynamics, and hydrogen transport in a rough fracture with reactive walls. Flow rate and biofilm permeability were varied to quantify changes in fracture permeability, biomass accumulation, and outlet hydrogen concentration. title: Reflective Nature Experiences in Virtual Reality
abstract: This paper presents the design and evaluation of an accessible virtual reality (VR) nature experience developed to promote mindfulness, reduce stress, and support emotional well-being. The system immerses users in a calming natural environment through realistic landscapes, ambient soundscapes, guided breathing exercises, and interactive checkpoints that encourage reflection. Accessibility was a central design consideration, particularly for users with diverse physical and sensory abilities or limited access to natural environments and traditional mindfulness resources. title: A model-based adaptive sampling framework for infectious disease surveillance
abstract: Longitudinal surveillance must choose each round's sampling design before the next observations arrive. Fixed sample-size rules treat each round as an isolated cross-sectional survey and ignore the evolving uncertainty in the epidemic process, which changes as transmission, vaccination, interventions, variants, and behavior change. We present a model-based adaptive sampling framework for choosing the next-round design. A state-space model represents the epidemic process and maps latent states to surveillance estimands. title: Ejecta fate and deposition in the Didymos-Dimorphos system after the DART impact
abstract: Kinetic impact is a promising technique for asteroid deflection in planetary defense. The NASA Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) spacecraft collided with Dimorphos, the satellite of the binary asteroid (65803) Didymos, at 6.1449 km s^{-1} in 2022. Observations revealed changes in both the orbit of Dimorphos around Didymos and the heliocentric orbit of the Didymos-Dimorphos system. The ESA Hera spacecraft will arrive at the system at the end of 2026 to investigate the post-impact surfaces. title: Two teams that cancel: a didactic analysis of a teaching progression for signed numbers from Grade 5 to Grade 7
abstract: Signed numbers make learners revise what addition, subtraction and the minus sign meant for whole numbers. This paper presents the design rationale and a critical analysis of a three-level source progression for signed numbers (Grades 5-7, nominal ages 10-13), from which French-curriculum and International Baccalaureate chapters published at https://commeunjeu.org are assembled. title: Pollutant Concentration Reconstruction in Porous Media from Localized Measurements
abstract: Reliable environmental monitoring and groundwater protection heavily rely on the ability to reconstruct full pollutant concentration fields from sparse, partial field measurements. In porous media, dissolved contaminants are transported by groundwater flow while undergoing hydrodynamic dispersion and complex chemical or biological reactions. To address practical contamination challenges, this work investigates the reconstruction of pollutant distributions using water samples collected at discrete locations in unsaturated or saturated soils via sampling tubes equipped with ceramic tips. title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
abstract: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.

title: Replication Certification at Publication: Checkable by Anyone, Anywhere, in Seconds, Forever
abstract: Authors increasingly deposit replication datasets---the data and code behind publications---in archives, and journals increasingly require them to, under progressively onerous rules. But a deposit alone proves little, so authors keep paying: months for the journal's reanalyses, years answering readers' questions, and rancor as failed replications become accusations because no record establishes what actually ran. Local Climate Change Reporting: Do Locality Framing and Interactive Maps Impact Risk Perception and Memory?
abstract: Considering the impact of local journalism in the context of climate change, this research investigates how locality framing and interactive features as important elements of digital local journalism affect news audiences. We used an article on heavy rainfall with a map visualizing data to test how local versus national framing and interactive versus static maps influence risk perception, responsibility attribution, article memory, and enjoyment in a 2 × 2 between-subjects online experiment with 632 German participants. title: Google Earth y mapas interactivos para el desarrollo de la orientación espacial y la cartografía básica: una revisión bibliográfica
abstract: La orientación espacial y la cartografía básica son aprendizajes esenciales para comprender la ubicación de personas, objetos y fenómenos en el territorio. En la educación, estas competencias permiten interpretar planos y mapas, utilizar referencias cardinales, reconocer escalas, identificar símbolos y describir relaciones entre lugares. Google Earth y los mapas interactivos ofrecen entornos digitales en los que el alumnado puede explorar el espacio desde diferentes escalas, observar imágenes satelitales, recorrer rutas, medir distancias y relacionar representaciones cartográficas con paisajes

title: Isotopic Insight Into Nitrate Sources and Cycling in Polar Sea Ice
abstract: Abstract Sea ice alters nitrate (NO 3 − ) availability in polar oceans, yet the influence of sea‐ice type on NO 3 − sources and cycling remains poorly constrained. We analyzed NO 3 − concentrations and isotopic compositions ( δ 15 N, δ 18 O, Δ 17 O) in Antarctic one‐year and Arctic multi‐year sea ice to investigate NO 3 − sources and transformation processes. title: Temporal and spatial variation in microbial extracellular enzyme activity in a nearshore Gulf coast system
abstract: Microbial extracellular enzymes are critical for the degradation of organic matter and mineralization of nutrients in marine systems, yet few studies have examined how enzyme activity varies over short-and long-term timescales in nearshore coastal environments. This study assessed the day-to-day, week-to-week, and month-to-month variation in the activity of three hydrolases (phosphatase, β-glucosidase, N-acetylglucosaminidase) in seawater and sand at five beaches along the Mississippi coast, as well as the activity of two oxidases (phenol oxidase, peroxidase) in sand. title: Dissolved oxygen gradients regulate microbial community assembly, metabolic function, and biogeochemical cycling in the southern Indian Ocean
abstract: Dissolved oxygen (DO) is a fundamental determinant in assessing the integrity and resilience of marine ecosystems. However, the influence of DO fluctuations on microbial community assembly, metabolic potentials, and interactions remain unresolved from the open ocean surface to the seafloor, especially in the Ninety East Ridge (NER) region of the southern Indian Ocean. title: Projected Climate Change Impacts on Deep‐Sea Corals of the Red Sea
abstract: Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation, among other co-occurring factors, are shifting species ranges throughout the marine environment. Mesophotic and deep corals are understudied in their response to climate changes, particularly in the Red Sea, which has relatively high temperatures and salinities and is projected to undergo major changes in the future, with little assessment of the impacts to date. abstract: The low spatial resolution (300–400 km) of Gravity Recovery and Climate Experience (GRACE) and the 11-month data gap between GRACE and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) complicate the evaluation of long-term ice mass loss at sub-region scale. Although several studies have downscaled GRACE data for water storage evaluation, efforts to downscale ice mass change are limited. title: No evidence of elevated mercury in sessile coastal biota exposed to Greenland glacial runoff
abstract: Abstract Melting glaciers have been claimed to be a significant and unaccounted-for source of mercury (Hg) in Greenland, raising concerns for communities, ecosystem health, and economics. Here we demonstrate, however, consistently low Hg concentrations in sessile organisms across >100 km spatial gradients and decadal time scales in three Southwest Greenland fjords exposed to glacial melt. abstract: This study focuses on optimizing the energy-absorbing characteristics of bio-inspired thin-walled structures (BTS) based on naturally inspired structural features. Three design parameters are investigated: wall thickness t, inner diameter d, and number of diaphragms n. title: Marine Heatwave and Extreme Hypoxia Coincide With Rapid Coral Bleaching and Mortality on a Central Red Sea Coral Reef
abstract: ABSTRACT Coral bleaching and mortality are commonly associated with heat stress during marine heatwaves (MHWs), yet attributing these responses solely to heat stress may overlook the complexity of contemporary MHWs. Here, we document a severe MHW affecting a central Red Sea reef in mid‐2024 that coincided with repeated nighttime low‐oxygen events. title: Holocene and last interglacial relative sea level changes in Sri Lanka based on geological indicators
abstract: Earth’s climate oscillations between interglacial and glacial periods have driven significant sea level changes. Sri Lanka, located in the Indian Ocean, provides an ideal natural setting for studying paleo sea level changes. This study compiles 92 Holocene sea level records and identifies last interglacial stratigraphic evidence from Point Kudrimalai to reconstruct paleo sea level fluctuations in Sri Lanka. abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) forms the largest reservoir of reduced carbon in the ocean, yet its bioavailability and the microbial processes governing its transformation remain poorly constrained. Traditional seawater batch cultures have been indispensable for measuring bioavailable DOC (BDOC), but their long incubation times and limited throughput constrain comparisons across environmental gradients and treatments. title: Stony coral symbioses show variable responses to future ocean conditions
abstract: Coral reefs support over a quarter of marine species and nearly a billion people worldwide but are also among the ecosystems most threatened by anthropogenic impacts. There is long-standing debate about whether coral symbioses will be disrupted or respond adaptively under future ocean conditions. Using a factorial 2.5-year future-ocean mesocosm experiment across eight coral species representing the major coral lineages, we tracked symbiont community shifts within replicate fragments from the same individual coral. title: Using Environmental DNA to Track Latitudinal Biodiversity Patterns and Ecological Changes of Eukaryotes Along Japan's Kuroshio Current
abstract: ABSTRACT Japan is an island nation whose economy, culture, and well‐being are deeply tied to the ocean, yet scientific understanding of its marine biodiversity remains uneven across taxa. abstract: Accurate acquisition of topographic data at the land - water interface is a fundamental step in bridging the gap between terrestrial and hydrographic datasets. In the complex fluvial environment of the Danube Delta, achieving a unitary representation of the riverine relief is hindered by dynamic morphological features and significant water - level fluctuations. abstract: Abstract Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices offer strong potential for lightweight structural and energy-absorbing applications, however, the coupled influence of lattice topology, relative density, and post-processing-induced microstructural changes on their mechanical response remains insufficiently understood. In this study, Gyroid, Diamond, Primitive, and IWP AlSi10Mg TPMS lattices were fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) at three relative densities and investigated in both as-built and EOS T6 heat-treated conditions. title: Low‐Velocity Impact Response and Damage Characterization of Bio‐Sandwich Composites With Montmorillonite Nanoclay
abstract: ABSTRACT The bio‐sandwich composites have higher specific stiffness and lower weight than conventional composites under transverse loads. abstract: Coastal lakes in the Mediterranean are highly sensitive ecosystems facing increasing pressure from the combined effects of anthropogenic activities and climate change. This study examined environmental changes in five Egyptian Mediterranean coastal lakes: Mariout, Edku, Burullus, Manzala, and Bardawil from 2020 to 2025, including an intermediate dataset for 2022. abstract: This study investigated chemistry students’ misconceptions about common salt in seawater and their implications for the chemistry education curriculum. Using a phenomenological design within the Model of Educational Reconstruction framework, the research engaged forty-five (45) first-year chemistry students at the University of Education, Winneba (UEW), Ghana. title: Fate of legacy ammonium in the coastal Baltic Sea
abstract: Eutrophication has enriched coastal sediments globally with organic matter (OM), fuelling internal nutrient loading once benthic hypoxia occurs. Internal ammonium (NH4+) loading may be particularly prominent in the coastal Baltic Sea due to the existence of a substantial NH4+ pool in its sediments, accumulated via OM deposition and mineralization over long-term eutrophication. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neurosurgical advancements in Parkinson's disease (PD) treatment can significantly improve symptoms. However, the use of these modalities in Southeast Asia (SEA) faces barriers. METHODS: We conducted an online cross-sectional survey among movement disorder specialists in SEA. Respondents provided country-level estimates of utilization, targets, financial coverage, and limitations in the utilization of four neurosurgical modalities. title: Regional seawater-chemistry controls on ocean alkalinity enhancement efficiency: Carbonate precipitation risk under pH-equilibrated OAE
abstract: Ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is a marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) strategy that increases seawater alkalinity and promotes atmospheric CO 2 uptake. However, the stability of stored carbon remains uncertain, particularly when carbonate saturation favors secondary calcium carbonate precipitation. In this study, we evaluate how regional seawater chemistry controls aragonite saturation state (Ω Ar ) under pH-equilibrated OAE conditions, in which seawater is enriched in dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) while pH remains close to the natural seawater value.
