abstract: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) is an increasingly popular tool for marine mammal monitoring. Until recently, most monitoring efforts targeted lower frequency sounds made by large baleen whales and were not optimized for the mid-frequency signals made by many other marine mammals. This is partially due to the directivity of the DAS system and the spatial averaging effect of the gauge length, which acts as a low-pass filter, markedly decreasing signal amplitude above 300-500 Hz, depending on the angle of incidence. title: Siting concentrating solar power for green hydrogen in Morocco: An integrated geospatial multi-criteria decision-making framework
abstract: The deployment of Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) systems in Morocco requires a systematic approach to identify optimal locations that balance technical, environmental, and socioeconomic factors. Addressing the limitations of prior regional assessments, this study presents a novel, integrated two-phase Geographic Information System (GIS) and Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) framework designed to identify optimal CSP sites and quantify green H 2 production potential. abstract: Background Coastal mega-developments require robust environmental baselines to distinguish natural biogeochemical variability from emerging anthropogenic pressures. Establishing pre-development reference conditions is essential for detecting future impacts on marine ecosystems, yet comprehensive baseline datasets remain scarce in rapidly developing coastal regions. abstract: This paper articulates the conceptual and formal architecture of Oceanic Narratology within contemporary Indian English fiction, challenging the entrenched land-centric paradigms of postcolonial literary criticism. abstract: ABSTRACT Large‐scale biodiversity patterns are increasingly reshaped by climate change, yet long‐term empirical comparisons across aquatic systems remain scarce. abstract: Abstract The global flux of terrestrial organic matter increases annually, while the fate of terrigenous dissolved organic matter (tDOM) in marine environments is not well understood. title: A compact set of sea star footprint proteins mediates the adhesion of Asterina gibbosa
abstract: Sea stars achieve strong yet reversible underwater adhesion using a duo-gland system in their tube feet. While adhesive sea star footprint proteins (Sfps) are well characterized in Asterias rubens, comparable molecular data for other asteroids are limited. abstract: Abstract The Deep Scattering Layer (DSL), formed as an antipredator refuge, shapes the ecology of the mesopelagic system. title: Transferable Data-Driven Hydrodynamic Variability-Based Stability Assessment for Marine Renewable Energy Site Selection: A Case Study in Spanish Waters
abstract: Early-stage planning of floating marine renewable energy infrastructures can benefit from identifying areas with favorable hydrodynamic conditions. Hydrodynamic stability assessment can support the planning of floating photovoltaic systems, offshore wind turbines, and renewable hydrogen production facilities. abstract: Accelerating ocean deoxygenation driven by ocean warming, eutrophication, and water column stratification poses a global threat to coral reef ecosystems. abstract: Abstract The Triassic Songpan‐Ganzi basin, located in northeastern Tibet, is one of the world's largest preserved ancient deep‐marine siliciclastic basins, yet its tectonic origin remains contentious. While often regarded as a remnant‐ocean basin, it has also been interpreted as a stretched and thinned continental margin. title: A biofilm-derived peptide as an underwater adhesive
abstract: Wet adhesives that perform under water have broad applications in industrial and biomedical settings. To date, molecular designs for underwater adhesives have largely been inspired by marine animals including mussels and barnacles. Here, we propose bacterial biofilms as an alternative source of inspiration for underwater adhesives. Specifically, we demonstrate the application potential of a peptide derived from biofilms formed by the notorious pathogen Vibrio cholerae . title: The Influence of the Antarctic Circumpolar Deep Water on Deep‐Sea Eukaryotic Biodiversity and Distribution in the Western Pacific Ocean
abstract: The Antarctic region, a centre of biodiversity origin, influences deep-sea ecosystems by supplying species to distant regions. Understanding the influence of Antarctic Upper Circumpolar Deep Water (UCDW) on deep-sea eukaryotic diversity is therefore essential for outlining global biodiversity patterns. Our results showed the UCDW community exhibited ~1.5-fold higher taxonomic and phylogenetic diversity than the Caroline Basin control community and contained a substantial proportion of unique taxa across multiple eukaryotic lineages. title: Geopetal occurrence and spatial organization of framboidal pyrite in shallowly buried deep-sea sediments
abstract: Framboidal pyrite is widespread in anoxic marine sediments, but the processes that control the redistribution and preservation of pyrite aggregates after their formation remain poorly constrained. Here, I examine the microfabric and spatial organization of framboidal pyrite in shallowly buried deep-sea sediments from the Sagami Trough and the Sea of Japan using complementary freeze-dried and resin-embedded specimens. title: Local hydrology and seasonality outweigh the influence of Phragmites australis on coastal bacterial communities across two Baltic Sea bays
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aquatic macrophytes shape microbial habitats in shallow coastal systems, yet the relative influence of plant-driven effects versus local hydrology and seasonal environmental variation remains poorly resolved. We investigated how Phragmites australis influences sediment, water, and phyllosphere bacterial communities in two shallow Baltic Sea bays, Haapsalu and Pärnu, that are approximately 83 km from each other. title: Circular Economy Practices and Firm Financial Performance: Empirical Evidence from FMCG Companies in Southeast Asia
abstract: This article examines how circular economy practices influence financial performance and market valuation among fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies in Southeast Asia. It focuses on two operationally consequential dimensions: waste-management practices and compliance with green regulation. These dimensions are considered alongside resource efficiency, circular product and packaging design, reverse logistics, and the quality of environmental disclosure. title: Long COVID: A Modified Delphi Consensus on Definition, Burden, Diagnosis and Management in Southeast Asia
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long COVID is a heterogeneous post-infectious condition following acute severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. Ongoing uncertainty around its definition, burden, diagnosis and management complicates clinical recognition and care in Southeast Asia. METHODS: A modified Delphi consensus study was conducted with twelve experts from six Southeast Asian countries to develop regional guidance on long COVID. title: Seasonal timing separates algal bloom records from marine heatwave exposure
abstract: Abstract Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly invoked in explanations of coastal algal blooms, yet shared seasonality can confound apparent MHW–bloom coincidence. We assembled a source‐resolved catalogue of 48 algal bloom records and a satellite‐derived regional daily sea surface temperature series for Sansha Bay, China, to evaluate bloom‐record timing against MHW exposure during 2005–2020. title: Assessing River Flood Vulnerability in Niger Delta Coastal Communities: A Hydro-Meteorological Analysis
abstract: Flooding is one of the major hazards in the coastal areas of Niger Delta State, Nigeria, due to the topography and climatic status. This paper examines flood vulnerability in the riverine communities of Rivers, Delta, and Bayelsa States using seven hydro-meteorological parameters: rainfall, sea level rise, river discharge, river flow velocity, temperature, wind speed, and elevation. title: Pathways of positive youth development, hope, and life satisfaction: A multi‐country study among Southeast Asian youth
abstract: Positive Youth Development (PYD) has gained prominence through models such as the 7Cs-competence, confidence, connection, character, caring, contribution, and creativity-yet relatively little is known about how these dimensions function in Southeast Asian contexts, where young people navigate diverse cultural values, socio-economic structures, and access to resources. title: "I wanted a PhD, not a label": Capital constraints, symbolic stigma, and Chinese international doctoral mobility to Southeast Asia
abstract: This study examines Chinese international doctoral mobility to Southeast Asia as a process shaped by unequal distributions of economic, cultural, social, and symbolic capital. Moving beyond push–pull and rational-choice explanations, it explores how doctoral pathways form, are sustained, and are evaluated under conditions of structural constraint. Based on semi-structured interviews with 18 Chinese doctoral students enrolled in public universities in Malaysia and Thailand, the findings identify three interconnected stages of mobility: pathway formation, maintenance, and conversion. abstract: The implementation of artificial habitats made from recycled materials can significantly enhance marine habitats for seahorses and other species, especially in areas where the natural habitat has been altered by anthropogenic factors such as pollution, trawling, beach enlargement, eutrophication, invasive species, and climate change. title: Dissolution and Heterotrophy at a Florida Coral Reef One Year After Severe Bleaching
abstract: Abstract Net ecosystem calcification (NEC) and net ecosystem production (NEP) are key metabolic indicators of reef functioning that underpin habitat formation and biomass assimilation, providing insight into ecosystem responses to environmental stressors. We employed a gradient‐flux approach at a shallow inshore reef in the Florida Keys to measure hourly NEC and NEP one year after the 2023 coral bleaching event. title: Fine‐Scale Variability of Cold‐Water Coral and Sponge Communities on Protected Northeast Pacific Seamounts
abstract: ABSTRACT Cold‐water corals and sponges (CWCS) on Northeast Pacific seamounts form important biogenic habitat that is intersected by a broad oxygen minimum zone (OMZ) and exposed to ongoing deoxygenation. Many seamounts in this region lie within marine protected areas (MPAs), making an understanding of fine‐scale community structure particularly relevant for conservation and management. title: Spatial and Seasonal Structuring of Bacterial Communities and Putative Pathogen‐Associated Bacterial Taxa at Four Korean Coastal Locations
abstract: Coastal marine environments are dynamic transition zones where offshore water masses and terrestrial inputs shape microbial community structure. However, standardized comparisons of bacterial communities across geographically distinct Korean coastal waters remain limited, constraining the development of microbial baselines for long-term monitoring. Surface seawater bacterial communities from four Korean coastal locations were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. From co‐occurrence to temporal coupling in a coral defender guild
abstract: Coral‐dwelling decapods can improve host fitness by defending corals against corallivores and sediment accumulation, yet the temporal dynamics linking co‐resident defenders remain poorly understood. Guard crabs Trapezia and snapping shrimp Alpheus provide complementary benefits to pocilloporid corals, and previous, largely cross‐sectional work has reported behavioral accommodation, non‐random co‐occurrence, and effects on host‐associated community assembly, patterns that suggest their association reflects facilitation instead of independent use of shared habitat. title: Assessing the spatio-temporal variability and environmental drivers of European anchovy Engraulis encrasicolus eggs distribution in the gulf of Cadiz (SW Spain)
abstract: Quantifying the spawning area of marine species is essential for developing management strategies that ensure the sustainability of natural populations. The European anchovy ( Engraulis encrasicolus ), one of the most abundant pelagic fish species in the Gulf of Cadiz (GoC), spawns in this region due to favorable environmental conditions. However, understanding the spatiotemporal variability of its spawning area remains a key gap in improving management strategies. title: Estuarine Biofilm Communities Adapt to Changing Conditions While Retaining Crucial Pollutant‐Combatting Functions
abstract: Industrialization has increased the influx of toxicants into intertidal and estuarine ecosystems. Intertidal sediments are exposed to heavy metals, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, pesticides, and other xenobiotics through effluents, shipping, spillages, battery disposal, and agricultural run-off. Pollutants accumulate in sediments, disrupting nutrient cycling and impairing primary productivity, thereby threatening coastal food webs. title: Multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to extended Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
abstract: Despite their profound consequences for the global carbon cycle, multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing remain poorly constrained. Here we investigate long-term oceanic responses to atmospheric CO 2 forcing using the Model for Interdisciplinary Research on Climate, Earth System version 2 for Long-term simulations (MIROC-ES2L) Earth system model driven by extended Shared Socio-economic Pathway (SSP) scenarios through to the year 2500. title: Eddy‐Induced Forcing Reshapes Taxon‐Specific Copepod Gut Contents and Feeding Preference in the South China Sea
abstract: Abstract Mesoscale eddies reshape pelagic habitats by modifying water‐column structure, primary production, and plankton distributions, yet how these changes affect zooplankton feeding across taxa and depths remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we tracked a cyclonic‐anticyclonic eddy pair and sampled zooplankton across cyclonic, frontal, anticyclonic, and outside‐eddy regions in the northwestern South China Sea. title: Critical Thermal Tolerance and Physiological Stress in the Estuarine Catfish, Mystus gulio
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding critical thermal tolerance and physiological stress responses is crucial to evaluating fish resilience to environmental changes. This study evaluated the critical thermal maximum (CTmax) and minimum (CTmin) under normoxic (sufficient oxygen supply; dissolved oxygen (DO) > 6.0 mg/L) and hypoxic (deficient oxygen supply; DO < 2.0 mg/L) conditions in long‐whiskered catfish ( Mystus gulio ), a commercially important, climate‐sensitive estuarine species from the Bay of Bengal. title: A coastal beach seed bank shows high diversity, but low similarity to the adjacent forest vegetation in an Amazonia Marine Extractive Reserve
abstract: Abstract Marine Extractive Reserves (RESEX-Mar) play a fundamental role in conserving Amazoniana coastal biodiversity, maintaining ecosystem services, and supporting the livelihoods of traditional communities. However, the relationship between seed taxonomy and adjacent vegetation remains poorly understood. This study evaluated whether the taxonomic composition of seeds deposited on the beaches of the RESEX-Mar in the municipality of Soure, Brazilian Amazon, reflects the composition and diversity of the adjacent vegetation. abstract: Theory and meta-analyses suggest changes from feeding to non-feeding larvae in marine animals may be an adaptation to conditions such as ocean productivity or circulation, but testing such predictions is difficult because intraspecific dimorphism in larval type (poecilogony) is rare. In gastropods, known examples are three caenogastropods and six heterobranch sea slugs, including five of ∼400 species in clade Sacoglossa. title: From community profiling to functional insights: bacterial populations in marine sediments from an Antarctic Specially Protected Area (Terra Nova Bay, Ross Sea, Antarctica)
abstract: Marine sediments remain among the least characterised components of the Antarctic microbial landscape. Here, bacterial communities were investigated in sediments from three sites within the Antarctic Specially Protected Area No. 161, in Terra Nova Bay (Ross Sea, Antarctica). Samples were collected during the XXXIII Italian Antarctic Expedition. The sites differed in their local environmental context, including proximity to the Adélie penguin colony and Mario Zucchelli Station. title: Seagrasses and macroalgae incorporate land-derived metal pollution while limiting its transfer through estuarine food webs
abstract: Estuarine areas provide critical ecosystem services by supporting biodiversity, maintaining water quality, and supplying seafood resources. Anthropogenic activities can introduce harmful metals into estuarine systems, potentially threatening these services. title: Cascading impacts of Atlantic meridional overturning circulation weakening and collapse on marine biogeochemistry
abstract: As Earth’s surface temperature continues to warm, the Atlantic meridional overturning circulation risks crossing a tipping point. Then, multiple Earth system components may be irreversibly altered. Here, we use the NASA-GISS Earth System Model to investigate the responses of ocean carbon uptake, net primary productivity, oxygen concentration, and carbon storage to a collapse of the overturning circulation under a moderate forcing scenario. abstract: Introduction: Coral reefs are essential ecosystems for the functioning of the planet and human well-being, providing three-dimensional habitats for a great diversity of marine life and multiple ecological, economic, and cultural services. Coral reefs are constructed by hermatypic corals, which maintain a symbiotic relationship with dinoflagellates of the Symbiodiniaceae family, which provide them with up to 90-95% of their energy in exchange for shelter and nutrients. title: Calibration of refractive housings for underwater vision
abstract: Abstract Many underwater applications rely on vision sensors and therefore require accurate camera calibration, i.e., precise knowledge of the incoming light ray associated with each image pixel. While in the ideal pinhole camera model all viewing rays intersect at a single point in 3D space, underwater imaging systems are affected by potentially multiple refractions at the interfaces between water, glass, and air. title: Riverine biogeochemistry from the Andes to the ocean: longitudinal patterns along a Mediterranean Andean catchment in central Chile
abstract: Rivers act as dynamic connectors between terrestrial and marine ecosystems, transporting and transforming materials along the aquatic continuum. We investigated longitudinal biogeochemical patterns across the Rapel catchment (central Chile) by integrating dissolved organic matter (DOM) characterization, dissolved metals and nutrients, and microbial community profiling from the Andean headwaters to the Pacific Ocean. title: Hydrogeochemistry and suitability assessment of surface and groundwater for drinking, irrigation, and corrosive potential in the Coastal District Porbandar of Gujarat, India
abstract: Abstract Surface and groundwater resources in semi-arid coastal regions are highly susceptible to salinity buildup, hydrochemical changes, and human activities, which compromise their usability for drinking, irrigation, and industry. This study assesses the hydrogeochemistry, spatial variation, and suitability of surface and groundwater in Gujarat's Coastal District Porbandar (CDP). title: Impacts of ocean warming, acidification and food quality on European abalone growth and reproduction: A Dynamic Energy Budget model approach across climate scenarios
abstract: Ocean warming and acidification can alter physiology, growth and reproduction of marine ectotherms, yet their combined effects remain unresolved under future food conditions. We use a Dynamic Energy Budget (DEB) model to investigate how temperature, pCO 2 , seasonal food availability, and food quality may shape growth and reproductive phenology of the European abalone Haliotis tuberculata across four coastal environments from 2019 to 2100. title: Preferences of Australian and Chinese tourists for behavioural restrictions during snorkelling in Fiji: implications for marine environmental conservation
abstract: This study explores the preferences of Australian and Chinese tourists for restrictions on marine-based tourism activities in Fiji. Given the importance of marine ecosystems in the Pacific, for both ecological and economic outcomes, and potential consequences of tourists on these systems, restrictions on tourist behaviour during recreational activities could be important policy mechanisms. title: Observations of Mammalian Predation on Pacific Sleeper Sharks in Southeast Alaska
abstract: The predator-prey relationship between marine mammals and sharks may not be as well defined as originally believed. Both groups can be either predator or prey. In the case of the Pacific sleeper shark, previous studies have documented the sharks predating upon juvenile Steller sea lions and scavenging whale falls, while other studies have reported offshore killer whales predating upon Pacific sleeper shark. abstract: Early life history traits strongly influence survival and recruitment in small pelagic fishes, yet regional variation in these traits remains poorly understood for young-of-the-year (age-0) mackerels in Kuroshio-influenced coastal systems. title: Governing seawater desalination: Connecting technical fixes and socio-political realities
abstract: As the global water stress intensifies, seawater desalination (SWD) is increasingly deployed as a supply-side strategy for enhancing freshwater availability. Critical scholarship has questioned whether technically oriented approaches to desalination adequately address the socio-political drivers of water scarcity and the governance conditions shaping desalination policy. title: Metabarcoding as a Tool in Characterizing Nordic Deep‐Sea and Arctic Benthic Ecosystems
abstract: ABSTRACT Deep‐sea and Arctic soft‐bottom organism communities remain severely underexplored. Sediment environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding can complement existing survey methods, but its ability to discriminate among habitats and to reliably assign taxa must be critically evaluated. Here, we analyzed sediment samples from 10 areas in the Nordic Seas and adjacent Arctic, including the Arctic Mid‐Ocean Ridge (AMOR), continental slope habitats, and abyssal environments. title: Improved light conditions sustain pelagic primary production in western Wadden Sea despite biomass declines under major nutrient reductions
abstract: Abstract Pelagic microalgae supply the major part of labile and readily accessible organic carbon in coastal systems, making long‐term monitoring of phytoplankton blooms and primary production (PP) essential for assessing the Wadden Sea's carrying capacity. Over the past three decades (1990–2023), our phenology analysis indicates that both the spring and summer‐autumn phytoplankton blooms declined in peak magnitude, and secondary blooms shifted later in the season (≈ 40 d over 34 years). title: First record and biological data of juvenile Dosidicus gigas in the Gulf of Tehuantepec, eastern Central Pacific Ocean
abstract: The Humboldt squid, Dosidicus gigas D'Orbigny, 1835, is endemic to the eastern Pacific. Knowledge of its biology is largely limited to commercial-sized adults, leaving juveniles scarcely documented. This study provides the first reference on the distribution, sex ratio, and feeding of juvenile D. gigas in the Gulf of Tehuantepec (GT). The study was based on 403 juveniles collected in April 2022 aboard the RV Dr. Jorge Carranza Fraser (IMIPAS). abstract: Abstract Mangroves can adapt to sea-level rise (SLR) and help mitigate climate change through sedimentation processes, particularly by trapping and accumulating sediment inputs from upstream catchments, which drive surface elevation change (SEC), sediment accretion rates (SAR), and ultimately carbon burial. title: Cutaway Single-Cylinder Marine Diesel Engine
abstract: This study aimed to design, fabricate, and utilize a cut-away single-cylinder marine diesel engine as an instructional device to enhance the theoretical and laboratory learning experiences of Bachelor of Industrial Technology Management (BITM) students. Specifically, it sought to improve the instructional materials of the Engineering and Technology Department and supplement the existing equipment in the BITM laboratory. title: Development and application of cryomilled heterogeneous micro- and nanoplastics labeled with upconverting nanoparticles for tracking interactions with freshwater plankton
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics ( MNPs ) pose environmental and health risks, yet their detection and tracking in biological matrices remain challenging. To facilitate the study of their fate, model luminescent MNPs are frequently used; however, they often lack environmental relevance and are limited by the drawbacks of conventional fluorescence labeling. title: Public perceptions and knowledge of nationwide shellfish reef restoration
abstract: Large-scale restoration of coastal and marine ecosystems is increasingly used to address biodiversity loss, yet its long-term success depends on public awareness, understanding, and support. Despite rapid expansion in shellfish reef restoration worldwide, little is known about how the public perceive these ecosystems or the value of restoring them. abstract: The geometry and ventilation of upper deep-water masses in the Pacific sector of the Southern Ocean are critical to glacial carbon storage, yet their evolution since the Last Glacial Maximum remains poorly constrained. Here, we present the foraminiferal neodymium isotope composition (ε Nd ) from core MD97-2115 (eastern Chatham Rise, 2160 m water depth), which is located at the present-day boundary between Upper Circumpolar Deep Water (UCDW) and modified North Pacific Deep Water (mNPDW) in the Southwest Pacific, to reconstruct the upper deep-water mass changes since 30 ka. title: Dynamics of diffusive-convective staircases in the ocean
abstract: Diffusive-convective (DC) staircases in the ocean are observed across a wide range of settings, but their formation, structure and persistence are not fully understood. Theories for DC staircases are reviewed to identify mechanisms governing their development and evolution. Staircase evolution through layer merging and possibly interface splitting, including the relationship to background turbulence, is assessed. title: Heavy metal contamination in Saudi Arabian soil and water: Regional distribution
abstract: Arid and semi-arid environments are highly vulnerable to potentially toxic element accumulation because low rainfall, high evaporation, dust transport, episodic runoff, irrigation return flow and groundwater salinity can concentrate metals in soil and water. Saudi Arabia provides a distinctive national case because rapid urbanization, agriculture, cement production, wastewater reuse, coastal development and petroleum-related activities occur across contrasting geological provinces. title: When marine turtles and vessels overlap: Mapping encounter risk along Florida's Atlantic coast
abstract: Abstract Marine turtle encounters with vessels can alter their behavior and habitat use and may lead to collisions causing injury and/or mortality. Despite existing protective measures, recreational vessel activity in coastal areas remains a significant threat due to limited understanding of the spatiotemporal dynamics of turtle–vessel interactions at regional scales. abstract: This study examines the spatial relationships among three religious landmarks in Nha Trang, Vietnam: the Ponagar Cham temple complex, Long Son Pagoda and its hilltop Buddha statue, and the Catholic Stone Church. title: Insights Into the Respiratory Microbiome of Free‐Ranging Tamanend's Bottlenose Dolphins ( Tursiops erebennus ) from Drone‐Collected Blow
abstract: ABSTRACT Although understanding of respiratory health in free‐ranging cetaceans has historically been limited, recent advances in drone technology have enabled noninvasive collection of cetaceans exhaled respiratory vapor (i.e., “blow”), offering new opportunities to study cetaceans' respiratory microbiome. This study aimed to collect blow from Tamanend's bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops erebennus ) in the Charleston Estuarine System (CES) to investigate their blow microbiome. title: Free-living autotrophs drive a carbon fixation peak within the Orca Basin chemocline while heterotrophs dominate total activity from seawater to brine
abstract: Deep hypersaline anoxic basins (DHABs) are stratified, polyextreme environments found within enclosed and semi-enclosed seas worldwide. Here, we quantified microbial activity in Orca Basin, the largest known DHAB, to investigate carbon cycling across its steep chemical and salinity gradients. We measured total anabolic activity and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) fixation as a function of metabolic lifestyle (autotroph or heterotroph) and spatial niche (free-living or particle-associated) using dual-isotope labeling experiments and single-cell analysis by nanoscale secondary ion mass spectrom

title: Lightweight Instance Segmentation for Underwater Grout Overflow Monitoring in Offshore Wind Turbine Jacket Installation
abstract: The installation of grouted connections in deep-water offshore wind turbine jackets faces severe visibility constraints and limited diver operation time, necessitating an unmanned, real-time monitoring solution using remotely operated vehicles (ROVs). However, the lack of dedicated datasets and the challenge of balancing segmentation accuracy with edge-deployment efficiency remain major obstacles. This paper addresses these gaps by constructing, to the best of our knowledge, the first underwater grout overflow instance segmentation dataset reported in the published literature, comprising 2088
institutions: Suzhou University of Science and Technology

title: Sensitivities of a simulated Arctic stratocumulus to aerosol and microphysical parameters
abstract: Low-level, mixed-phase clouds are a key component of the Arctic energy budget and can impact the extent and thickness of sea ice. These clouds are influenced by aerosols and microphysical processes that can determine the phase partitioning and thereby cloud lifetime and radiative impacts. Atmospheric models often struggle to represent phase partitioning in Arctic mixed-phase clouds correctly. title: Phylogenetic, Ecological, and Physiological Factors as Modulators of the Intestinal Microbiota in Stranded Marine Mammals in Uruguay
abstract: ABSTRACT Gut microbiota plays a key role in host physiology and may reflect ecological and health‐related processes, yet it remains poorly studied in marine mammals. We characterized and compared the gut bacterial communities of seven marine mammal species stranded along the Uruguayan coast between 2022 and 2024, including pinnipeds and cetaceans with different trophic habits. Tissue samples from 21 individuals were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding targeting the V3–V4 regions, with amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) inferred using DADA2 and taxonomic assignment based on SILVA 138.1. title: Temperature Carryover Effect Revealed for Marine Fishes Using Spatio‐Temporal Distributed Lag Models
abstract: Understanding the impact of changing temperature on population densities is necessary to predict the likely impact of climate anomalies (e.g., marine heatwaves) or forecast distribution shifts under future climate scenarios. Population densities are often analyzed using spatio-temporal models (STMs), which typically predict densities based on local habitat conditions while also estimating latent spatial and spatio-temporal variation. institutions: NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service Alaska Fisheries Science Center

title: Influence of soft coral density and depth on benthic communities on Fiji's Rainbow Reef
abstract: Some soft corals have the potential to increase in prevalence on tropical coral reefs as the severity of anthropogenic climate change increases. While soft corals are therefore an increasingly important component of reef ecosystems, little is known about their ecological role on coral reefs and their influence on community dynamics and diversity. We used Bayesian network inference (BNI) to identify the associations among benthic taxa across sites with varying degrees of soft coral dominance on Fiji's Rainbow Reef, and then employed spatial point process analysis (SPPA) to reveal the ecological

title: Technological Transitions and Material Culture in the Ancla Macuca Shipwreck (Late 18th to Early Nineteenth Century): An Archaeometric Study from Alacranes Reef, Gulf of Mexico
abstract: The Ancla Macuca shipwreck, located within the Alacranes Reef National Park in the Gulf of Mexico, represents a palimpsest context resulting from the superposition of material remains from at least two distinct wrecks, the late eighteenth to early nineteenth-century Ancla Macuca site and the R.M.S. Forth (1849). This study presents the results of an interdisciplinary project integrating underwater archaeological survey, documentary research, archeometallurgical characterization, and conservation science. title: Taxonomic efforts in deep sea hydrothermal vents are approaching total coverage
abstract: Despite centuries of taxonomic research, an estimated approximately 90% of marine invertebrate species remain undescribed. Taxonomy must become more efficient for policy and conservation decisions; however, we know little about how taxonomic practices have changed over recent decades. We used ChatGPT 4.0 to extract metadata from the original descriptions of all 588 species endemic to deep sea hydrothermal vents, and examined temporal trends in species discovery, authorship, institutional and national representation, and description length. title: Hollow Glass Microsphere/Polymer Composites for Thermal Insulation: Mechanisms, Fabrication, and Performance‐Driven Multifunctional Expansion
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal insulation materials play an important role in industrial thermal insulation and high‐end equipment. Traditional polymers often suffer from relatively high thermal conductivity, while highly porous polymers demonstrate insufficient mechanical properties. Hollow glass microspheres (HGMs) offer a solution with low thermal conductivity, high strength, low density, and robustness. This paper thoroughly reviews the factors and mechanisms influencing the intrinsic thermal conductivity of polymers, and details the fabrication methods of HGM/polymer composites. title: Wildland Fire Retardants and Foams in the Megafire Era: Ecotoxicological Risks and a GIS-Based Decision Framework
abstract: Increasingly extreme fire weather is expanding the aerial use of fire retardants and firefighting foams, yet their environmental effects rarely inform operational decisions. This review assesses their ecotoxicological risks to forest soils, freshwaters and coastal waters. We synthesized 150 sources from four bibliographic databases (Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed and Google Scholar) and official EFFIS/GWIS datasets, calculated un-ionized ammonia fractions across pH 6.5–9.0 and 10–30 °C, and overlaid Greek burned-area and protected-area data. title: A feasibility demonstration of integrated deionization and electrolysis for portable hydrogen production from seawater
abstract: Reducing the water purification footprint for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) can enable portable hydrogen production from impure water sources. Here, we report a critical first step in the design of a thermally integrated deionization and electrolysis (TIDE) device for portable hydrogen production from seawater. The TIDE concept intends to leverage vapor-fed PEMWE operation, utilizing the waste heat from electrolysis to vaporize water through pervaporation to supply reactant water for electrolysis. title: Resilience Communication Model for Coastal Communities Facing Slow-Onset Disasters: A Netnographic Study of Jakarta
abstract: Climate change has shifted the global disaster paradigm from the dominance of rapid-onset disasters toward slow-onset disasters that develop gradually, such as sea-level rise, coastal abrasion, saltwater intrusion, and land subsidence. Coastal communities in Muara Angke and Marunda, North Jakarta, represent urban coastal areas that face the simultaneous accumulation of these ecological pressures. This study aims to develop a Coastal Community Resilience Communication Model (CCRCM) that is participatory, adaptive, and sustainable in facing slow-onset disasters. Using a qualitative approach with
journal: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Social Sciences Study

title: Steps Toward Vitrification and Banking of Coral Larvae Using Field‐Friendly Cryomesh Technology
abstract: Coral reefs are declining globally, and novel solutions, such as cryopreservation, can help secure coral biodiversity and genetic diversity. Factors that affect successful cryopreservation of coral larvae include cryoprotectant type and concentration, membrane permeability, larval developmental stage, lipid content, volume, and freezing and warming rates. This study examined conduction-dominated "cryomesh" technology across a range of coral species, distinguishing vitrification on cryomesh, 24 h swimming survival, and settlement competence as separate measures of success. Using a previously su

title: Development of an interdisciplinary coastal erosion vulnerability index for urban communities in the eastern sector of the Togolese coast
abstract: Abstract The coasts of West Africa are particularly vulnerable to coastal erosion due to the interaction of physical, climatic, and anthropogenic factors. This study assesses the composite vulnerability of urban communities to coastal erosion along the eastern sector of the Togolese coastline, which spans 39 km and is subdivided into three coastal sections. The methodology combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), vulnerability scoring, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). A coastal erosion vulnerability index (CVI) was calculated based on two complementary sub-indice
institutions: Institut de Recherche pour le Développement

title: Methodology for Source Identification of Plastic Pellets Spilled at Sea – Application to Real Spill Scenarios
abstract: Unintentional spills of plastic pellets represent the second largest source of primary microplastic emissions to the marine environment. Polyolefins (polyethylene, polypropylene), representing ~50% of annual thermoplastic production, are the most common pellets found on beaches. Being buoyant, they may be transported over large distances. Beached pellets can be visually or compositionally similar despite different origins. Here, we demonstrate an analytical toolbox for source identification of plastic pellets spilled at sea. The protocol combines physical characterization with pyrolysis and th
institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

title: Optimal design and techno-economic analysis of wave-integrated hybrid energy systems for coastal communities
abstract: Wave energy has the potential to improve renewable complementarity in coastal microgrids; however, its technoeconomic competitiveness under moderate resource conditions remains uncertain. This study develops a two-stage stochastic mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework to evaluate the integration of wave energy converters (WECs) into hybrid offshore microgrids under joint resource and demand uncertainty. Renewable generation and demand are modeled using ARIMA-based forecasting, with interdependencies captured via a Student-t copula and reduced through k-mediods clustering. The frame

title: Influence of Sea Surface Temperature and Chlorophyll-a on Biomass Availability and Body Size of the Black Skipjack (Euthynnus lineatus) in the Mexican South Pacific
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the relationship between oceanographic variability, specifically sea surface temperature ( SST ) and chlorophyll- a (Chl- a ) concentration, and the abundance and size structure of Euthynnus lineatus (black skipjack) along the southern Pacific coast of Mexico from October 2022 to October 2024. The region experiences two distinct seasons: a dry season with strong “Tehuano” winds causing upwelling, and a rainy season influenced by the Costa Rica Coastal Current. High-resolution satellite data were integrated with biometric and catch data from local artisanal fish
journal: Thalassas An International Journal of Marine Sciences

title: Applying CITES for sea cucumber conservation: A structured review across the Indo-Pacific
abstract: International trade regulation under CITES is increasingly used as a market-based mechanism to conserve marine invertebrates, yet implementation of trade provisions remains heterogeneous across regions and taxa. This review evaluates the implementation of CITES Appendix II listings for sea cucumbers with a focus on the Indo-Pacific region. Using a structured review of published and grey literature, contextualised with export data, we examined the preparation of Non‑Detriment Findings (NDFs) and reported trade of sea cucumbers. We assessed the types of data, analytical depth, and technical guid
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Response of phytoplankton biomass to sea surface temperature fluctuations in the Bay of La Paz, Southern Gulf of California: a 17-year satellite study
abstract: Phytoplankton biomass is a vital indicator of ecosystem health, yet its dynamics are increasingly sensitive to thermal variability and large-scale climatic events. Utilizing a 17-year satellite-derived dataset (2002 to 2018) from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), this study investigates the relationship between chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) concentration and sea surface temperature (SST) in the Bay of La Paz, Gulf of California, with a focus on the influence of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Our findings reveal a pronounced seasonal cycle. Chl-a peaked at 1.5 mg m-3

title: Global review of bull shark Carcharhinus leucas (Valenciennes, 1839) museum specimens: summary of records, geographic analysis, and assessment of their scientific value
abstract: Background Museum specimens provide critical data for taxonomy, systematics, biogeography, and conservation. Well-preserved vouchers are essential for documenting both historical and contemporary distributional records, supporting a better understanding on species distribution in a world undergoing constant environmental changes. Regarding the euryhaline bull shark, Carcharhinus leucas , voucher specimens reliably confirm occurrences in areas where the species' status was previously unclear and clarify the identity of morphologically similar shark species found in freshwater environments. title: ASSESSMENT OF FALL-RISK IDENTIFICATION COMPLIANCE AND DEVELOPMENT OF A PATIENT MONITORING DASHBOARD AT MUHAMMADIYAH LAMONGAN HOSPITAL
abstract: Background: Fall prevention is a core component of hospital patient safety. Visual identification of patients at risk of falling supports staff awareness, but compliance with identification procedures may be inconsistent. Objective: To describe compliance with fall-risk identification among hospitalized patients at Muhammadiyah Lamongan Hospital and the development of a monitoring dashboard as a quality-improvement support tool. title: Harnessing GIS to map trawl fishing grounds and reduce carbon footprint along India’s west coast
abstract: Aim: This study examines the spatial and temporal dynamics of key commercial fish species along the west coast of India through GIS-based mapping, aiming to reduce the environmental footprint of trawl fisheries by optimizing fishing effort, minimizing scouting time, and lowering carbon emissions. Methodology: Data from customised logbooks for each fishing operation were geo-referenced using recorded latitude–longitude coordinates to delineate the spatial extent of fishing grounds. title: Diversity, stability and ecosystem functioning relationships across marine fish communities facing contrasting environmental and anthropogenic pressures
abstract: Abstract Understanding the mechanisms that underpin ecological stability has traditionally focused on the role of diversity, and particularly through biodiversity and ecosystem functioning (BEF) relationships. Yet, BEF relationships and the drivers of stability remain poorly explored across contrasting systems exposed to multiple pressures, such as exploited marine fish communities. title: Initial Fisheries Bycatch Estimates for Threatened Marine Mammals in Cambodia
abstract: ABSTRACT Bycatch is the biggest threat to marine mammals globally. To estimate bycatch and investigate bycatch drivers for Irrawaddy dolphin ( Orcaella brevirostris ), Indo‐Pacific humpback dolphin ( Sousa chinensis ), Indo‐Pacific finless porpoise ( Neophocaena phocaenoides ) and dugong ( Dugong dugon ) in Cambodia, questionnaires were conducted with 449 vessels (gillnet, trap, longline, trawl and surrounding net) across Cambodia's coastline between September and October 2023. journal: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems

title: What drives the winter behaviour and ecology of the temperate coral Astrangia poculata? An examination of thermal and nutritional cues
abstract: Abstract In temperate ecosystems, accessing subtidal environments in the winter is challenging, and therefore, winter ecology and seasonal variation are understudied. For the temperate coral Astrangia poculata, winter is thought to be a period of biological ‘reset’, in which many cellular processes slow or stop, and the microbiome and symbiont community shift dramatically. The period of quiescence, when corals enter a dormant state with limited feeding or metabolic activity, is primarily driven by cold temperatures. title: Spatio-temporal variation of the pocilloporid coral-associated symbiotic crustaceans (Decapoda) of the central Mexican Pacific
abstract: Introduction: Coral symbiotic crustaceans maintain close associations with their hosts, which may be obligate or facultative. In addition to their dependence on corals for survival, these organisms play an important role in the health and persistence of their hosts. However, there is still limited information regarding the spatio-temporal variation in their biomass and the factors regulating it. Objective: This study analyzed the spatio-temporal variation in the taxonomic diversity and biomass of symbionts associated with pocilloporid corals in the Mexican Central Pacific, as well as their rel

title: Revealing the Widespread Bias of Extinction Risk in the Antarctic and the Southern Ocean
abstract: Accelerating environmental change in the Antarctic and Southern Ocean (ASO) necessitates robust extinction risk assessments to inform conservation priorities. Nevertheless, no systematic, region-wide baseline of extinction risk currently exists for tracking ASO biodiversity responses to ongoing change, a significant barrier to global biodiversity monitoring. Here, we conducted the first ASO-wide synthesis of current extinction risk knowledge for plants, animals and Fungi. This included examining biases in current assessments, the distribution of Threatened species and their associated threats.

title: Energy Harvesting From Aquatic Animals and Device Attachment Strategies Toward Long‐Term Tracking and Sensing Underwater
abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement and miniaturization of tracking devices have deepened our understanding of aquatic ecosystems, including how human activities affect underwater animals and their habitats. However, long‐term or life‐cycle monitoring remains a major challenge because conventional animal‐borne devices rely on batteries with limited lifespans. As a sustainable alternative, researchers have introduced self‐powered tags and sensors that harvest electrical energy directly from the aquatic animal to power device operation. title: Formal Description of Cladocopium proximale sp. nov., a Coral Photosymbiont From the C1 Radiation
abstract: ABSTRACT Coral reefs are among the most biodiverse ecosystems on Earth and rely on endosymbiosis with Symbiodiniaceae, a diverse family of dinoflagellates essential for coral nutrition and which also play an important role in thermal tolerance. Despite their ecological importance, resolving species boundaries within Symbiodiniaceae remains challenging, partly due to limited phylogenetic signal in commonly used genetic markers and the absence of broadly accepted criteria for species delimitation. Refining taxonomic resolution is therefore critical for understanding symbiont diversity, distribut

title: Ecosystem services in shellfish reef restoration and coastal policy: A global scoping review
abstract: Shellfish reefs can contribute to nature-based solutions (NbS) that can support coastal protection, water quality, and biodiversity, yet the extent to which their ecosystem services (ES) are reflected in coastal policy remains unclear. This global scoping review maps the scientific evidence on ES associated with shellfish reefs and examines their relationships with restoration approaches, policy instruments, and governance frameworks. institutions: Forest Science and Technology Centre of Catalonia

title: Comparative population genetic structure of two antlion species, Neleon bore and N. solers , inhabiting sandy beaches along the sea of Japan
abstract: Abstract Sandy beaches are important habitats for a wide variety of organisms. However, extensive human activities in these areas have led to marked decreases in the populations of many coastal species. Although antlions are integral components of these ecosystems, their population genetic structures remain poorly understood. In this study, we collected samples of two antlion species from sandy beaches along the sea of Japan: Neleon bore , which is widely distributed, and N. solers , which has a restricted distribution. title: Pole-to-pole LOV-domain receptor diversity points to an early stramenopile origin and global dominance of aureochromes
abstract: Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. Yet molecular adaptations of photoreceptors to the extreme seasonality of polar regions remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that the diversity of candidate blue-light-sensing LOV-domain proteins increases at higher latitudes. We identify aureochromes, blue-light-sensitive transcription factors unique to stramenopiles, as the most frequent LOV-domain receptors across ocean latitudes. title: PROSPECTS FOR THE APPLICATION OF REMOTE SENSING AND GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEM TECHNOLOGIES IN MONITORING PASTURE LANDS
abstract: This study explores the prospects of applying remote sensing and Geographic Information System (GIS) technologies for monitoring pasture lands and evaluating their ecological condition and productivity. Remote sensing provides timely and objective spatial information about land surface characteristics, while GIS enables the integration, processing, analysis, and visualization of large volumes of geospatial data obtained from multiple sources. The research focuses on the use of Landsat 8 satellite imagery and ArcGIS software to assess vegetation cover, land degradation processes, and spatial ch

title: A quantitative framework for identifying umbrella taxa in the supralittoral zone of wave-exposed sandy beaches
abstract: Sandy beach biodiversity is under increasing pressure from anthropogenic stressors across the ocean-land interface, creating an urgent need for cost-effective conservation tools. Umbrella taxa can serve as proxies for co-occurring biodiversity in spatial conservation planning and guide habitat-based conservation actions that benefit broader communities. However, quantitative frameworks for identifying and validating umbrella approaches remain limited. title: Latitudinal Heterogeneity in South Asian Monsoon Changes Since the Last Glacial Maximum Revealed by Ganga–Brahmaputra Vegetation Record
abstract: Abstract Future changes in South Asian climate are expected to amplify flooding and drought, yet the spatial and temporal variability of the South Asian monsoon (SAM) under different climate regimes remains poorly constrained. Here, we present a new marine pollen record from the Bay of Bengal (BoB), informing on the vegetation of the Ganges‐Brahmaputra (G‐B) River basin whose outlet via the lower Meghna lies near 21.3°–21.8°N, and compare it with bulk and leaf‐wax δ 13 C and δD, and planktonic foraminiferal δ 18 O records, all from the same site. title: Modelling low-trophic aquaculture in the North Sea: From parameter estimation to ecosystem dynamics
abstract: The North Sea represents a promising but complex system for expanding sustainable food production through low-trophic aquaculture, particularly using bivalves and seaweed. However, assessing production potential and ecological carrying capacity in such systems requires mechanistic approaches that account for strong environmental variability and ecosystem interactions. Here, we present the parametrisation, sensitivity analysis, and application of a one-dimensional pelagic ecosystem model for the Dutch North Sea called Aqua-DEB. title: Biological status and coastal resource management of Anadara tuberculosa in the Eastern Tropical Pacific
abstract: Anadara tuberculosa is a mangrove-associated bivalve of high ecological, economic, and sociocultural importance in the Eastern Tropical Pacific, where it supports coastal livelihoods and contributes to ecosystem functioning. However, widespread population declines driven by overexploitation, habitat degradation, and coastal pollution threaten its long-term persistence and pose growing challenges for integrated coastal resource management. This review synthesizes and critically evaluates the available scientific and technical literature on the biology, ecology, population structure and genetics

title: Gendered social norms in coastal farming systems in Bangladesh
abstract: Women play a fundamental role in agriculture, yet gendered social norms significantly shape their participation and access to benefits within farming systems. While these norms influence agricultural structures and practices, their impact on women’s agency and economic contributions remains insufficiently examined. Our study addresses this gap by critically examining the influence of gendered social norms in coastal farming in Bangladesh. title: Submersion method for neuroanatomical photography: visualizing arachnoid membranes and cisterns
abstract: IntroductionThe subarachnoid space expands into cisterns, limited by arachnoid membranes. Dissection within these compartments is the hallmark of microneurosurgeons, working in-vivo, within the head, with the brain bathed in cerebrospinal fluid, under magnification, and extra-illumination. title: Climate change vulnerability, adaptive strategies, and food security of small-scale fishers in marine protected areas (MPAs) of the Island Garden City of Samal
abstract: Abstract Currently, there are no updated assessments on the climate vulnerability and food security status of the communities located near or hosting marine protected areas in Samal. To address this question, we assessed the vulnerability and food security status of small-scale fishing communities located near or at the community-managed marine protected areas (MPAs) in the Island Garden City of Samal, Philippines. title: Visualizing Heritage: Culturally Accurate Storytelling in Pakistani Mythology and Folklore
abstract: The research recognizes the power of visuals and imagery in storytelling and acknowledges the importance of cultural accuracy in portraying mythological and folkloric elements. By employing culturally appropriate visuals, this research seeks to foster a stronger connection and familiarity between artists, storytellers, and their audience, ultimately reinforcing cultural identity and shared values in Pakistan. title: Shoreline armouring on the north shore of mainland Nova Scotia
abstract: Using Google Earth (GE) and ground proofing of selected shorelines, we mapped coastal defense measures (CDMs), along the coast of the Northumberland Strait of Nova Scotia from the New Brunswick border to the Canso Causeway. An initial method used 256 point samples from Tidnish to Cape George at 0.5’ of longitude and revealed a 22.8% occurrence of armouring. A second method used GE images and the ‘path’ tool to trace the lengths of each individual wall along 15 shoreline segments facing the Northumberland Strait and selected bays and estuaries. title: Antileishmanial and antimalarial activities of synthetic marine endoperoxides
abstract: Synthetic samples and analogs of marine endoperoxides derived from mycaperoxides and plakortides were screened for their antileishmanial and antimalarial activities. It was found that these compounds exhibited significant activity against both parasites in the micromolar range. However, mycaperoxide analogs also exhibited high cytotoxicity against both cancer and healthy mammalian cell lines in the micromolar range. title: Blue carbon development and ecosystem services in oligotrophic environments: the case for a shallow coastal installation on the shelf off Tenerife (Canary Islands)
abstract: This study assessed the unplanned ecosystem services provided by a submarine monitoring station over 18 months, including an environmental characterisation of a shallow coastal shelf area off SW Tenerife (Canary Islands), a calculation of the benthic biomass developed (the generated blue carbon) and the identification of the species pool related to the installation, representing the associated biodiversity. title: Dual Stress of Ocean Acidification and Sulfide: Physiological Adaptation Mechanisms of the Tropical Seagrass Thalassia hemprichii
abstract: ABSTRACT Ocean acidification and sulfide intrusion are key environmental stressors affecting seagrass bed ecosystems. Although sulfide stress drives large‐scale seagrass mortality, the physiological response of seagrasses under ocean acidification remains unclear. Therefore, this study selected Thalassia hemprichii , a dominant species of seagrass beds, to investigate the effects of ocean acidification (pH 7.7), sulfide stress, and their interaction on its physiological responses and growth. title: Organized Polycentricity: Structural Characteristics and Operational Mechanisms of the Adaptive Governance Network in the Yancheng Yellow Sea Wetlands
abstract: ABSTRACT Adaptive governance has been largely developed and applied in the Global North, and there is a significant tension between its theoretical assumptions and the relatively concentrated governance structures and government‐led governance realities in the Global South. Therefore, whether adaptive governance can be effectively applied to the Global South largely depends on contextual conditions such as the role of government and social structure. Evaluating spatiotemporal variation in PFAS contamination and gene expression in oysters in a large wind-driven estuary
abstract: Oyster reefs provide critical ecosystem services, including habitat provision, water filtration, and coastal protection; however, they are susceptible to anthropogenic contaminants such as per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), which can impact organismal health and immunity. Despite these concerns, the impacts of PFAS exposure on wild oyster immunity remain poorly understood. title: Seasonal trends in the zooplankton community in the NW Arabian Gulf
abstract: Seasonal trends in zooplankton community composition and abundance were investigated in the Northwestern Arabian Gulf from 2013 to 2016. A total of 72 zooplankton taxa were found: 29 copepod taxa, 18 types of meroplanktonic larvae, 16 non-crustacean taxa, and 9 other crustacean taxa. Copepods dominated the community throughout the year (>65% of total zooplankton abundance), with small copepods such as Paracalanus spp, Acartia pacifica, Oithona spp, and Euterpina acutifrons contributing most of the abundance. title: Anemonefish prioritize mutualistic partner over social group during a marine heatwave
abstract: Abstract Changing their behaviour is animals' first line of defence in response to environmental disturbance. However, changes in behaviour towards social group members and mutualistic partners can also lead to reduced fitness and resilience. Here, we use clown anemonefish, Amphiprion percula, to understand how disturbances alter social and mutualistic behaviours directly and indirectly via degraded mutualistic partners. abstract: Epidemics of beneficial microorganisms (beneficial to the host) generally go unobserved; a few recent advantageous epidemics have been reported, including an epidemic of corals by a Vibrio species that made them resistant to bleaching and epidemics of stinkbugs by Burkholderia spp. that conferred resistance of the insect to the insecticide fenitrothion. There are similarities and differences between epidemics caused by pathogenic and by beneficial microbes. Both contain genomic islands (GIs) involved in epidemics. title: Ultra-low-temperature seawater zinc–air batteries enabled by carbon nanochannel-confined high-entropy alloy catalysts
abstract: Abstract Seawater-based solid-state zinc–air batteries are attractive for extreme-environment applications because of their high energy density, intrinsic safety, low-temperature operability, and in situ resource utilization. However, sluggish cathodic oxygen redox kinetics at low temperatures and catalyst degradation in strongly alkaline seawater severely compromise their energy efficiency and cycling stability. title: Long Term Analysis of the Diet of South American Sea Lions and the South American Fur Seals on the Base of Instantaneous Supply Over Time in a Context of Ecosystem Change
abstract: ABSTRACT The instantaneous diet of South American sea lions ( Otaria byronia ) and South American fur seals ( Arctocephalus australis ) was analyzed using scats collected from shared haul‐out islands in the northern region of San Jorge Gulf, Patagonia, Argentina. Prey species were identified using otoliths, squid beaks, and crustacean exoskeletons during a long‐term project from 1999 to 2024. abstract: The Kodaiyar River is an important water source of Kanyakumari and Tirunelveli Districts in Tamil Nadu. The aim of the present research is to use the hydrogeochemistry and water quality of groundwater along the Kodaiyar River to assess the suitability of drinking and agricultural purposes through integrated approach. Totally twenty-five groundwater samples were collected from bore wells and open wells along the river course and near the confluence point of the river. abstract: ABSTRACT Novel species interactions between resident and range shifting species in response to warming are posing challenges for conservation and management. This is especially the case when major predatory species are involved, as seen in the appearance of a mixed species outbreak of coral‐eating crown‐of‐thorns sea stars Acanthaster cf. solaris (As) and the lesser‐known Acanthaster brevispinus (Ab) in the tropical to subtropical transition zone in eastern Australia. title: Heavy Metals in Rice Fields at a Typical Southeast Coastal Industrial Site: Spatial Distribution and Toxicity Centroids with Health Risk Assessment
abstract: This study investigated heavy metals (Cd, Pb, Cr, Cu, Zn) in the soil-rice system of Sanming, a typical industrial and rice-growing region in China, to analyze their spatial patterns, sources, and ecological and health risks. Standard deviation ellipses based on the geoaccumulation index (Igeo), single ecological risk index (Er) and comprehensive ecological risk index (RI) were used to visualize spatial disparities of pollution and risk. Cd was the primary pollutant with the widest distribution; its average (Igeo) reached 2.29, and roughly 80% of samples presented moderate to heavy pollution.

title: A transient occurrence of Ipomoea fimbriosepala (Convolvulaceae) on Gapado Island, Korea
abstract: Ipomoea fimbriosepala Choisy (Convolvulaceae) is reported here for the first time from Korea, based on specimens collected on Gapado Island, Jeju-do, in 2021. The species is readily distinguished from related Korean taxa by its unequal sepals, with ovate, abaxially 3-winged outer sepals and smaller, unwinged inner sepals, as well as by its glabrous, sagittate or deltoid leaves. title: Conserved molecular properties of dissolved organic matter during Weddell Sea Deep Water formation
abstract: Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) is decreasing in volume due to climate change with potential consequences for abyssal carbon storage, where carbon is locked away from the atmosphere for centuries. Understanding the formation and export of dissolved organic matter (DOM) on the Antarctic shelf is therefore essential to determine how organic carbon enters this deep-sea reservoir. Here, we investigate solid-phase extractable DOM (SPE-DOM) transformations in the Weddell Sea, where half of AABW forms. title: Feedback between land cover changes and socio-environmental drivers on the Eastern Shore of Virginia, United States
abstract: Coastal communities face interacting land-cover, agricultural, and socio-economic pressures as climate change, sea-level rise, and development reshape low-lying landscapes. Satellite land-cover products are essential for monitoring these changes, but they may not fully capture local interpretation, management context, and community-level relevance. title: Offshore wind farms in German waters: Seabird responses across multiple sites range from attraction to strong avoidance
abstract: Offshore wind farms (OWF) play a major role in addressing the climate change crisis. Large-scale OWF are currently planned in many parts of the global oceans, and thorough investigations of their effects on the marine environment are therefore needed. The aim of this work was to identify the OWF effects on the density of five abundant seabird species across 21 OWF in the German North Sea through a large-scale before-after-control-impact analysis using ship-based and aerial surveys. title: Dynamics of algal overgrowth and predation related tissue loss in corals from the Southern Gulf of California, México (2019–2025)
abstract: Introduction: Coral reef ecosystems are undergoing increasing degradation associated with oceanographic changes, higher predation, bioerosion, and anthropogenic pressures, all of which affect their structural complexity, resilience, and functioning. Visible lesions, such as algal overgrowth and tissue loss, serve as practical indicators of colony health. title: Pulse disturbances from hurricanes differentially structure temporal α‐ and β‐diversity in coastal benthic communities
abstract: Coastal benthic community structure is shaped by a dynamic interplay between pulse disturbances, such as hurricanes, and press stressors, such as coastal land loss and climate change. We examined a five‑year time series of a benthic community and environmental data from Terrebonne Bay, Louisiana, spanning five major hurricanes. Repeated, high‑intensity hurricanes produced abrupt, short‑term declines in macrofaunal α‑diversity (species richness and Hill numbers), particularly within the first one to three months post‑disturbance. title: Elephant Presence Shapes Butterfly Communities in an East African Coastal Forest
abstract: Habitat disturbances shape the diversity and composition of plant and animal species. It is important to distinguish between natural disturbances caused by megaherbivores and anthropogenic disturbances caused by human activity, as different disturbance regimes differently affect biodiversity. In this study, we analyse butterfly diversity and community structure in three forest areas with different habitat disturbances in the Arabuko Sokoke dry coastal forest of south-eastern Kenya. abstract: Purpose: This study aims to analyze the measures taken by the local government to address tidal flooding in Bontang Kuala Village, as well as to recommend strategies that can be developed by the government and the community to enhance the resilience of the coastal area against tidal flooding in Bontang Kuala Village. abstract: ABSTRACT The development of multifunctional antibacterial nanomaterials is of considerable interest in combating antibiotic resistance and marine biofouling. abstract: Flooding and temporary waterlogging are recurring environmental concerns on the campus of Universitas 17 Agustus 1945 Samarinda, East Kalimantan, Indonesia, particularly in low-lying and highly impervious areas. This study aimed to map flood susceptibility within the 12.01 ha campus by integrating rainfall, slope, elevation, distance to drainage, and land use using a Geographic Information System (GIS)-based weighted overlay approach. title: Anomalous terrigenous input to the continental margin of tropical western South Atlantic at the Pleistocene-Holocene transition
abstract: Continental slopes off southeastern Brazil preserve key records of terrigenous sediment transfer during the last deglaciation, yet the processes controlling these deposits remain poorly constrained. Here, we analyse four sediment cores to investigate the origin of a distinct terrigenous-rich layer (TM facies) identified across all records. Sedimentological, inorganic geochemical, and geochronological data were integrated to reconstruct the depositional history of this interval. abstract: This study presents a comprehensive quantitative morphometric analysis of the five drainage basins of Hor Al-Shuwaicha in eastern Iraq, which cover a total area of 22,245.54 km². Previous morphometric studies have primarily focused on three basins (Torsaq, Shosharin, and Galal Badra), the morphometric characteristics of the entire drainage system insufficiently characterized. title: Tourism Potential Index Mapping for Underdeveloped Historical Sites in South West Nigeria: A GIS-Based Suitability Model
abstract: Historical and cultural heritage sites in Southwest Nigeria have immense potential for tourism development but remain underdeveloped due to poor infrastructure, accessibility, and investment prioritization. While previous studies have documented the preservation problems and the state of sites, a systematized approach to site identification with the highest potential for tourism development has been lacking. This study develops a Tourism Potential Index (TPI), a GIS-based suitability model that ranks historic sites by their readiness for tourism investment. The model was built using ArcGIS Pro

title: Genetic Diversity and Putative Origin of the Bait Polychaete, Diopatra aciculata Knox and Cameron 1971 (Annelida: Onuphidae), Occurring in South Africa
abstract: ABSTRACT The bait polychaete Diopatra aciculata is commercially farmed in Australia and is collected as bait in several South African estuaries. Despite its widespread use, the species' geographic origin remains uncertain, hindering management efforts within sensitive estuarine ecosystems. Mitochondrial Cytochrome Oxidase subunit I (mt COI ) data and ddRAD‐generated single‐nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were used to gain insight into the origin and genetic diversity of D. aciculata . title: Metabarcoding of Mediterranean monk seal (Monachus monachus) scats from the isolated population of Madeira reveals a diverse piscivorous diet
abstract: The Mediterranean monk seal ( Monachus monachus ) is one of the world’s most endangered marine mammals, and information on its feeding ecology is needed to support conservation planning. Here, high-throughput DNA metabarcoding of scat samples from Madeira was used to characterise fish prey in the diet of this geographically isolated population. Fourteen samples were analysed using universal fish primers targeting the mitochondrial 12S rRNA gene, enabling detection of both bony and cartilaginous fishes. title: Integrative assessment of “smart” Zn–Al and Mg–Al layered double hydroxides: marine ecotoxicity, hazard and environmental behavior
abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are increasingly used as functional (sometimes also called “smart”) nanocarriers in maritime coatings, and other advanced applications, as their layered structure enables the retention of active compounds and modulates their release in response to specific environmental stimuli. Yet, their behavior and hazard in marine environments remain poorly understood. title: Predator-Specific Deployment of Defensive Behaviors in the Marine Isopod Cleantiella isopus (Isopoda, Idoteidae): Arched Posture Against Fish and Escape Against Crabs
abstract: Many prey species are exposed to multiple predators that use contrasting hunting modes. To enhance survival under such conditions, the prey may discriminate among predator types and deploy predator-specific defenses. Secondary defenses expressed following contact with predators are likely to require an accurate assessment of predation risk, as inappropriate responses can prove fatal. abstract: Abstract Marine sponges of the order Verongida constitute a rich source of bioactive secondary metabolites, mainly bromotyrosine-derived compounds. title: Microbiological quality of inland and coastal springs: Escherichia coli, other coliforms, and implications for public health
abstract: Untreated springs remain important domestic water sources in rural communities, yet their microbial safety and spatial and seasonal variability are insufficiently characterised. This study evaluated concentrations of Escherichia coli and other coliforms in inland and coastal springs within the King Sabata Dalindyebo Local Municipality, South Africa. Ten springs, five inland and five coastal, were sampled on five occasions during both wet and dry seasons, producing 100 water samples. abstract: Abstract Ocean worlds such as Enceladus, Europa, and Ceres exhibit erupted surface materials, including salts, likely derived from potentially habitable subsurface liquid‐water environments. Linking surface salt compositions to their potential chloride‐, carbonate‐, ammonia‐, and/or sulfate‐bearing ocean sources is essential for constraining key habitability parameters such as pH and salinity. title: The Impact of Nutrition Social Marketing on Awareness, Behaviour Change, and Food Expenditures: A Cluster Matched Study from Coastal Kenya
abstract: Malnutrition continues to be a persistent global challenge, frequently affecting small-scale producers. Nutrition-focused social marketing has been shown to increase nutrition awareness and improve diets and nutrition outcomes, but less is known about the pathways to these positive outcomes as well as impacts on other nutrition-related behaviors like household food expenditure. We present findings from Samaki Salama, a community-based nutrition and fisheries sustainability trial conducted in coastal Kenya. abstract: Salinity intrusion in coastal Bangladesh has reduced the reliability of conventional drinking-water sources and encouraged the expansion of reverse osmosis (RO) systems. We examine RO here not simply as a desalination infrastructure but as a socio-technical water service whose outcomes depend on access, governance, energy, infrastructure, and environmental management. abstract: A study on assessment of diversity in banana and plantain cultivars available in coastal salt ecosystem of Bangladesh and performance of selected plantain genotypes was accomplished during July 2022 to May 2023 in in situ and ex situ conservation sites. A survey was done according to a questionnaire to assess the plant diversity and crop husbandry of banana and plantain. title: Epidemiological surveillance of bacterial pathogens in cultured European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye
abstract: Intensive aquaculture of European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) along the Aegean coast of Türkiye faces continuous production challenges from infectious diseases, yet comprehensive multi-year baseline data remain limited. This study presents a multi-year retrospective surveillance program (2020-2025) monitoring bacterial pathogens associated with 748 distinct cage-level disease outbreaks in fish across 19 discrete offshore commercial sea farms. title: Microplastic ingestion is ubiquitous in threatened stingrays from the Amazon estuary
abstract: Microplastic pollution has become pervasive across freshwater ecosystems worldwide, including the Amazon Basin, where increasing levels of plastic contamination have been reported. Despite growing evidence of microplastic (MP) ingestion in aquatic organisms, studies focusing on threatened species remain extremely scarce, particularly for estuarine elasmobranchs. Rays present high extinction risk among vertebrates and in majority are apex predators, which enhance direct interaction with MPs. title: Designing a Cost-Informed, burden-based Prioritization Index for SDG transformations
abstract: This study develops a Cost-Informed SDG Transformation Priority Index (CI-STPI) using the selected-target dashboard of the Global Sustainable Development Report 2023 (GSDR 2023). The index operationalises relative ex ante transformation burden through three directly observable dimensions: distance from target, trend of SDG progress in 2023, and directional change between 2020 and 2023. title: Integrated proteomics and transcriptomics provide insights into molecular basis of ascidian metamorphosis
abstract: Shallow-water ascidians are invasive, fouling marine organisms that rapidly metamorphose from planktonic larvae to sessile forms. To gain insights into their environmental adaptability and develop methods for biofouling control, it is crucial to explore the molecular and cellular orchestration of metamorphosis. Here, we employed 4D label-free quantitative proteomics combined with transcriptomics to monitor protein and gene expression during ascidian Ciona metamorphosis across five post-embryonic stages. title: Impact of climate change on long-term corrosion of offshore wind turbine monopiles
abstract: Offshore steel structures are subjected to deteriorating environmental actions affecting their performance and structural reliability. Marine corrosion is recognized as a leading factor reducing service life and reliability of offshore wind turbine (OWT) monopiles. This paper evaluates the influence of corrosion on the structural performance and reliability of OWTs’ monopile using a bi-modal corrosion model. abstract: ABSTRACT The invasive macroalga, Nitellopsis obtusa (‘ N. obtusa ’), commonly known as starry stonewort, is rapidly expanding across North American freshwater systems. This study assessed the spatial distribution and abundance of N. obtusa over time in coastal wetlands of the Laurentian Great Lakes (hereafter ‘Great Lakes’) using data collected from the Great Lakes Coastal Wetland Monitoring Program.
