title: Non‐native ants that coexist in abundance with many native ant species are the most widespread on an oceanic island
abstract: Abstract Non‐native ant establishment is one of the greatest threats to native biodiversity on oceanic islands. Interactions with native ant species may provide beneficial ecological resistance that prevents non‐native ants from spreading across island landscapes. We linked the fine‐scale co‐occurrence of non‐native and native ants with the island‐scale establishment of non‐native ant species across the Caribbean island of Montserrat. title: Plastisphere Assembly and Surface Transformation of Common Plastics across Environments
abstract: Abstract Plastic waste in the environment has a significant adverse effect on ecosystems and human health. Plastic biodegradation has been observed in certain environments as a potential strategy for end-of-life plastics management. Recent research has focused on plastispheres, a microbial biofilm that forms on plastic surfaces. title: Local Wisdom and Religious Beliefs in Tsunami Preparedness in the Digital Era: A Case Study of Coastal Communities in Pacitan, Indonesia
abstract: Coastal communities in Pacitan, East Java, Indonesia, face tsunami hazards that require disaster preparedness approaches responsive to local social and cultural contexts. Local wisdom and religious beliefs may shape how communities understand disaster risks and preparedness. This study compares community-reported knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to local wisdom and religious beliefs in the context of tsunami preparedness. abstract: Livability in coastal settlements is a critical issue, particularly vulnerable to environmental degradation, climate change, and land constraints that directly compromise housing quality, necessitating an integrated approach that bridges technical standards and community perspectives. This study aims to determine the priority of physical livability criteria, analyze the suitability level between importance and performance, and formulate development alternatives in the coastal settlement of Karangsari, Tuban, Indonesia. abstract: ABSTRACT Vibrio species adapt to different niches by sensing and responding to environmental signals such as nutrients, host cues, and quorum sensing autoinducers. Vibrio campbellii uses the master quorum sensing transcription factor LuxR to control the expression of hundreds of genes at high cell density. title: Shared transport system, different liveability realities: residents’ and tourists’ perspectives from seasonal coastal destinations
abstract: Transport systems in seasonal tourism destinations are shared by residents and tourists, yet little is known about how these groups experience transport-related liveability while using the same infrastructure. This study examines how transport conditions shape transport-related liveability from the perspectives of residents and tourists in two seasonal coastal destinations on the southern Baltic coast of Poland: the Hel Peninsula and the Vistula Spit. title: Late Holocene Occupation and Resource Use in the Sub‐Coastal Moreton Region: The Open‐Air Howard Creek Site, Southeast Queensland
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper reports archaeological investigations at the Howard Creek site, a Late Holocene open‐air site in the sub‐coastal Moreton region of southeast Queensland. The site adds to a regional record based largely on rockshelter excavations. Development‐led salvage investigations included excavation, radiocarbon dating, lithic analysis, and use‐wear and residue studies. Six radiocarbon determinations provide a broad chronological framework for site use during the last approximately 2000 years. title: FROM THE LECTURE HALL TO THE DECK: PSYCHOLOGICAL CHALLENGES OF FEMALE CADETS ON THEIR FIRST VOYAGE
abstract: Maritime universities today proudly showcase a growing number of female students training to become officers. However, the real test does not happen in the simulator room. Academies do a great job teaching ship stability and navigation, but female cadets often step on board feeling unprepared for the emotional toll. title: Integrating psychosocial factors with geospatial analytics to assess community climate resilience
abstract: Abstract Conventional climate adaptation strategies emphasize infrastructure, hazard modelling, and ecosystem management while underestimating psychological processes that shape how communities perceive and respond to climatic risks. Cognitive appraisal, emotional attachment, and behavioural engagement fundamentally influence preparedness, adaptation, and recovery. This study introduces GeoPsyche Futures , an interdisciplinary framework that integrates psychological indicators with geospatial analytics to map community resilience in a holistic, human-centered way. title: Plant invasion alters rhizosphere microbial communities across temperate ecosystems
abstract: Invasive plants threaten ecosystems, and their management remains a challenge in ecological restoration. Control and replanting outcomes can vary considerably, with restoration sites often experiencing re-invasion, secondary invasion, or failed native plant establishment. While impacts are often focused above ground, plant invasion can also alter rhizosphere microbial communities in ways that may inhibit recovery. title: Vascular plant diversity and spatial heterogeneity on the dried bed of the Aral Sea (Uzbekistan): a grid-based floristic assessment
abstract: The desiccation of the Aral Sea has resulted in the formation of the Aralkum, one of the largest anthropogenic deserts in the world. Despite profound environmental transformation, spatially comprehensive assessments of vascular plant diversity across the Uzbek sector of the dried seabed remain limited. This study presents a grid-based floristic analysis of vascular plants on the dried bed of the Aral Sea (DBAS) based on field surveys conducted between 2020 and 2023. title: Saltwater Intrusion Threatens Old-Growth Bald Cypress Trees Adjacent to Ghost Forests in Smith Creek, North Carolina
abstract: ABSTRACT Ghost forests of standing dead trees are emerging in coastal areas of the eastern US as brackish water is driven inland and upstream by relative sea-level rise (RSLR). In the Northeast Cape Fear River (CFR) watershed of North Carolina, RSLR from both anthropogenic global warming and dredging of the CFR contribute to saltwater intrusion. Saltwater intrusion leads to tree-growth suppression and widespread tree mortality as the dominant freshwater wetland tree, bald cypress ( Taxodium distichum (L.) title: Acute Toxicity Assessment of Heavy Metals Arising from Deep-Sea Polymetallic Nodule Mining in Mytilus Coruscus: Bioconcentration, Oxidative Stress, Tissue Damage, and Gene Expression
abstract: Deep-sea polymetallic nodules are rich in multiple critical metals and abundant reserves essential for green energy, infrastructure, and military applications. However, during their mining process, widely dispersed sediment plumes are generated, which pose potential risks to deep-sea ecosystems. In this context, the toxic impacts of heavy metal release from these plumes on benthic filter-feeding organisms in and around the mining areas remain underexplored. title: Biofilm-Mediated Carbonate Mineralization for Enhanced Bio-Based Building Materials
abstract: : Microbially induced calcite precipitation (MICP) is an ambient-temperature route for binding granular materials into bio-based construction products. However, conventional biocementation workflows commonly rely on planktonic cells that are weakly retained on aggregate surfaces and are therefore vulnerable to washout during cementation-solution flow. title: Propylene Glycol Alginate Sodium Sulfate (PSS): The First Oral Heparinoid Marine Drug—A Pharmacological and Clinical Review
abstract: Propylene glycol alginate sodium sulfate (PSS) is the first oral heparinoid marine drug, derived from brown algal alginic acid and marketed in 1986. Its core pharmacology, including anticoagulation, lipid-lowering, microcirculation improvement, and neuroprotection, makes it an affordable oral option for chronic ischemic cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. title: Linking Morphological and Genetic Differentiation Among Populations in Seagrass Species With Contrasting Dispersal Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐distance dispersal sustains genetic diversity across populations and facilitates recovery from disturbance, and dispersal also may shape how ecologically important morphological traits shift in response to environmental change. We examined links among morphology, genetic differentiation, and dispersal through surveys of traits and genetics for Thalassia testudinum and Halodule wrightii distributed across a naturally occurring gradient in concentrations of total phosphorus in the water column along Florida's Gulf Coast (USA). title: Reflection Seismic Insights Into the Pleistocene An-Nafud Sand Sea and the Underlying Paleozoic to Ediacaran Geology North of the Arabian Shield
abstract: The An-Nafud sand sea formed during the Pleistocene and occupies approximately 60,200 km 2 of northern Saudi Arabia. The erg has regional significance within the North African – Arabian Pleistocene desert trend, recording aeolian system development and early hominin migrations, while the underlying geology represents the poorly-documented Ediacaran and Paleozoic history of the northern sector of the Arabian plate. Reflection seismic data and deep wells have been used to establish the first description of the 3D geometry of this erg and the tectonostratigraphy of the underlying bedrock geology.

title: Succession of Microbial Communities and Identification of Indigenous PAH‐Tolerant Bacteria Under Multiple PAH Stresses in Mangrove Sediments From Maowei Sea, Guangxi, China
abstract: Elucidating microbial community shifts under polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) stress and screening indigenous PAH-tolerant microbial resources are valuable for exploring potential bioremediation strategies for PAH-contaminated mangrove ecosystems. In this study, surface sediments were collected from mangrove wetlands of the Maowei Sea, Guangxi, China. title: Heritage Resilience in Tropical Contexts: Recovery, Adaptation and Transformation in Vernacular Architecture—The Cases of Fiji, Bangladesh, Zanzibar and Mozambique
abstract: Cultural heritage in tropical coastal settlements faces recurrent climatic pressures, yet its resilience depends on more than the survival of built fabric. This article examines how vernacular practices, adaptation strategies, and institutional action shape heritage conservation and resilience in Navala (Fiji), Sandwip (Bangladesh), Stone Town (Zanzibar, Tanzania), and the Island of Mozambique (Mozambique). abstract: The green macroalga Bryopsis nana M.J.Wynne, 2005 (Bryopsidaceae, Bryopsidales, Chlorophyta) was collected during a winter survey of hard-substrate macrobenthic communities at Plage l’Ilot, Ain Benian, west of Algiers, Algeria. The specimen occurred as an epiphyte on a geniculate coralline alga on a wave-exposed rocky/vermetid platform. Identification was based on stereomicroscopic and light-microscopic examination of diagnostic morphological characters and comparison with the protologue. title: Comprehensive characterization and human health risk assessment of microplastics in ten shellfish species from the South Yellow Sea Mudflat: Implications for safe seafood consumption
abstract: Microplastics (MP) intake through shellfish consumption could result in potential health risks to humans. This study comprehensively investigated MP characteristics and potential risks in shellfish from South Yellow Sea mudflat. MP were detected in all ten species of shellfish, wherein the maximum MP abundance was detected in Perna viridis (11.73 items/individual) and Mercenaria mercenaria (3.5 items/g). title: Role of Biofilm-Associated Virulence Genes in Chronic Wound Infections Caused By Pseudomonas Aeruginosa
abstract: Chronic wound infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa are difficult to manage because biofilm formation can support bacterial persistence and reduce antimicrobial effectiveness. This study framework examined relationships between biofilm-associated virulence genes, biofilm formation, antimicrobial resistance, and clinical characteristics using a dataset of 120 patient–isolate records. Biofilm categories were derived from triplicate synthetic optical density measurements, while gene carriage and antimicrobial susceptibility classifications were generated for illustrative analysis. title: Aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA) toxicity under salinity stress scenario in Mytilus galloprovincialis: population-associated differences in cellular response patterns
abstract: Climate change is expected to intensify extreme rainfall events, the frequency of coastal hyposalinity episodes and the mobilisation of land-based contaminants such as glyphosate and its main degradation product, aminomethylphosphonic acid (AMPA), a major metabolite whose ecotoxicological impact remains poorly understood especially under interactive climate stressors. title: Resilience of cities to climate change: a tool to assess resilience of urban open spaces against flood risks
abstract: Urban flooding is an increasing challenge in coastal cities, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region, where rapid urbanization and limited adaptive infrastructure exacerbate vulnerability. This study develops an integrated Geographic Information System (GIS-based) framework to assess the effectiveness of nature-based solutions (NBS), specifically sponge city systems, in enhancing the resilience of urban open spaces against flood risks in Alexandria, Egypt. title: Climate‐Related Disaster Adversity and PTSD‐Related Outcomes Among Adolescents in Coastal Bangladesh: A Propensity Score Overlap‐Weighted Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Climate-related disasters are important environmental stressors for adolescent mental health, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. However, evidence regarding post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and complex PTSD (CPTSD) among adolescents experiencing cumulative disaster adversity remains limited. This study examined associations between disaster adversity and PTSD-related outcomes among adolescents in coastal Bangladesh. title: The high-quality genome of the sea cucumber Holothuria glaberrima reveals new and extended gene families in Holothuroidea
abstract: The sea cucumber Holothuria glaberrima is a premier model for regenerative research that has allowed the discovery of key cellular and molecular characteristics of intestinal and neuronal regeneration. However, the lack of a high-quality reference genome has limited molecular studies of regenerative processes in this species. We generated a chromosome-level genome assembly using PacBio long-read sequencing and Omni-C chromatin conformation capture data. abstract: This study aimed to design, fabricate, and utilize a cut-away single-cylinder marine diesel engine as an instructional device to enhance the theoretical and laboratory learning experiences of Bachelor of Industrial Technology Management (BITM) students. Specifically, it sought to improve the instructional materials of the Engineering and Technology Department and supplement the existing equipment in the BITM laboratory. title: Large-amplitude internal waves near a wharf: Observations and implications for navigation
abstract: Large-amplitude, nonlinear internal waves are rarely considered in operational navigation, yet they can generate strong and rapidly varying currents in stratified coastal environments. This study investigates their potential impact on ship manoeuvrability near the Grande-Anse Terminal in the Saguenay Fjord (QC, Canada), motivated by a 2019 docking incident involving a cargo vessel under otherwise calm conditions. abstract: The resource utilization of food industry wastes is of great significance. This study aimed to prepare a novel polysaccharide from sea buckthorn pomace, and investigate its structural features and lipid-lowering potential. The homogeneous polysaccharide, designated as D2N1, consisted of arabinose, galacturonic acid, galactose, glucose, mannose, rhamnose, glucuronic acid and fucose in a molar ratio of 70.12%: 11.74%: 6.60%: 4.40%: 2.93%: 2.93%: 0.79%: 0.49%, with the average molecular weight of 8.839 kDa. title: Plenty of fish in the farm: Analysing the effect of aquaculture-based tourism on public perceptions of aquaculture
abstract: This study explores aquaculture-based tourism as a tool to improve public perceptions of aquaculture, promote sustainable development of marine industries, and advance Blue Growth. Global aquaculture production is rapidly increasing due to increased food security demands, protein needs, and declining wild fish stocks. However, the sustainable growth of the aquaculture industry is challenged in policymaking due to public scepticism and environmental concerns. abstract: Tablasupa Village in Depapre District, Jayapura Regency, covers an indicative area of 1,662.34 ha and is home to 1,281 people. The village is exposed to slope instability, rockfall, surface erosion, land fires, coastal abrasion, tidal flooding, and local flooding along the Amai River, yet this hazard information had not been compiled in an integrated spatial database that the village government and residents could use. title: Transforming a complex ecosystem model to a MICE and optimizing between complexity and performance
abstract: Ecosystem modelling constitutes a fundamental approach to gain insights into the structure, function and dynamic processes of complex marine ecosystems. In this context, species aggregation introduces a way to reduce model complexity and evaluate the effects on model output. Increasing model complexity does not necessarily improve model performance. Regarding model structure and complexity, Models of Intermediate Complexity for Ecosystem assessments (MICE) are positioned between whole-of-ecosystem models, such as Ecopath with Ecosim (EwE), and single-species models. title: Late Iron Age Graves With Sewn and Hybrid Lapstrake Boats in Northern Norway: Burials and Boat Technology From Multiethnic Contexts
abstract: Lapstrake-built boats in graves are a valuable source of insights into nautical technology and how it was used and developed during the Late Iron Age in Scandinavia. In this study, boat grave evidence documents the importance of sewing and the addition of rivets to sewn vessels to produce a hybridized lapstrake boat construction technology that is unique to northern Norway. It is argued that sewn and hybrid boats reflect a shared boat building tradition between coastal Sámi and Norse communities. title: New Insight to Morphogenetic Movements Underlying Gastrulation in the Freshwater Gastropod Lymnaea stagnalis (Mollusca: Heterobranchia)
abstract: Gastropod molluscs, inhabiting marine, freshwater, and terrestrial environments, are a unique group to uncover the evolution of developmental pathways shaped by adaptation to novel environments. However, the detailed comparative data are available for a few marine gastropods only. We present here the first comprehensive, stage-by-stage description of early embryogenesis in a representative of freshwater gastropod molluscs. title: Objectscapes on the Frontier: Diachronic Transformations of Fish Iconography in the Mosaics of the Middle Euphrates
abstract: This article investigates the diachronic transformation of fish and marine iconography across the mosaic pavements of the Middle Euphrates basin, spanning the Hellenistic, Roman, and Late Antique periods. Employing the conceptual framework of ‘objectscapes,’ the study examines how circulating visual repertoires actively constituted regional identity and localized artistic agency along the provincial frontier. title: Host species identity drives temporally stable octocoral microbiomes in Florida
abstract: Octocorals are foundational components of Caribbean reef ecosystems, yet their bacterial microbiomes remain poorly characterized compared to scleractinian corals. We present an extensive 16S rRNA gene survey of western Atlantic octocoral microbiomes, characterizing 180 samples from four co-occurring South Florida species over three years: the encrusting species Briareum asbestinum and Erythropodium caribaeorum, and the branching species Eunicea flexuosa and Muricea muricata. title: Cyclone-induced economic and non-economic loss and damage in coastal Bangladesh: A geospatial comparison of Kalapara and Dumki using an Integrated Loss and Damage Index
abstract: Tropical cyclones continue to cause extensive economic and non-economic losses across coastal Bangladesh. Empirical assessments often focus narrowly on monetary damage while ignoring spatial disparities and non-economic impacts. This study provides a comparative evaluation of cyclone-induced loss and damage (L&D) in two distinct upazilas of Patuakhali District: the highly exposed coastal zone of Kalapara and the inland Dumki. title: Noble gas and CO2 systematics of petit-spot magma reveal low-degree melting of the upper mantle
abstract: Petit-spot volcanoes erupt on old oceanic plates far from mid-ocean ridges. Their magmas are characterised by exceptionally high initial CO 2 concentrations of up to ∼10 wt%. Although petit-spot magmas have been inferred to originate from CO 2 -rich melts at the lithosphere–asthenosphere boundary, their mantle source and melting mechanism remain debated. abstract: In this paper, we study the dynamical behaviour and exact travelling wave solutions of a non-standard nonlinear Schrödinger equation. title: Multi-omics analyses unveil the molecular mechanism involving significant bioactive substances of sea buckthorn at various growth years
abstract: Sea buckthorn fruit quality varies with tree age, but the molecular relationships between branches and fruits remain unclear. This study characterized age-dependent changes in fruit quality and branch–fruit associations in 4-year-old, 5-year-old, and 6-year-old sea buckthorn ( Hippophae rhamnoides L.) using phenotypic analysis, targeted and untargeted metabolomics, transcriptomics, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. abstract: Seabirds are critical ecosystem members providing connectivity between marine and terrestrial ecosystems. Seabird foraging is often facilitated by other marine predators (e.g. tuna) that aggregate prey at the surface. Some seabirds have been anecdotally reported to 'hawk' (catch mid-air/in-flight) flyingfish and flying squid forced into flight by subsurface predators. title: Effects of Tiger Tail Sea Cucumber Bohadschia argus on Wound Healing In Vitro and In Vivo Using an Acute Rat Model Infected with Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Abstract Infectious wounds caused by Staphylococcus aureus remain a significant clinical challenge due to delayed healing and increasing antimicrobial resistance, necessitating alternative therapeutic strategies. This study aimed to evaluate the wound-healing potential of the ethanol extract of the tiger tail sea cucumber Bohadschia argus (EEBA) through integrated in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. title: Risk criticality model for bushfire threatened water distribution networks
abstract: Background Water authorities commonly use vulnerability assessments to evaluate asset bushfire risk for large or key facilities; however, this traditional approach ignores the vast array of distributed component assets (e.g. pipes, air valves, etc.). Aims To address this, a new risk criticality model was developed to correlate geographic information system (GIS)-referenced bushfire intensity data with water distribution asset data to determine risk criticality for each component asset. title: THE EFFECTS OF SAND ENCROACHMENT ON ROAD TRANSPORT IN MAKKAH REGION
abstract: This research aims to evaluate the impact of sand dune movement on land transport routes in the Makkah region. The study analyzes the mechanisms of sand dune formation and their role in the development of dust storms, ultimately modeling the risks posed by sand dunes to roads and classifying these routes based on their level of exposure to such hazards. title: Bycatch and mortality of three prohibited shark species in northeast U.S. commercial gill-net and trawl fisheries
abstract: Abstract Objective Incidental capture in nontarget fisheries can contribute to mortality of prohibited shark species with low productivity and slow population growth. In the U.S. northwest Atlantic Ocean, the Dusky Shark Carcharhinus obscurus, Sand Tiger Carcharias taurus, and White Shark Carcharodon carcharias have been prohibited from retention for more than two decades, yet incidental captures persist. abstract: ABSTRACT Effective conservation of marine mammals depends on reliable demographic information, yet acquiring such data for highly mobile cetaceans is challenging. Harbour porpoises ( Phocoena phocoena ) are widely used as sentinel species, but much of what is known about their demography comes from stranding and bycatch records. abstract: Thraustochytrids can be a promising raw source of nutritionally valuable compounds, particularly protein and fatty acids. The high cost of carbon and nitrogen sources remains a major bottleneck for the industrial-scale heterotrophic cultivation of thraustochytrids. The current study investigates the potential of Aurantiochytrium limacinum SR21 (ATCC MYA-1381) as a rich source of protein and fatty acids, using sea salt, glucose, and different protein extracts as nitrogen sources (peptone vs. yeast extract). title: Plastic bag deposition alters the macrofaunal structure and function in mangrove mudflats: temporary refuge or ecological trap?
abstract: Plastic debris is recognised as a persistent anthropogenic stressor in coastal ecosystems; yet few experimental studies have examined its ecological impacts in situ over biologically relevant time scales. abstract: Kimberlite-borne eclogite xenoliths ultimately derive from ancient subducted oceanic crust. Some specimens still record the chemical and redox conditions of their igneous protoliths, allowing a view into contemporaneous convecting mantle sources. title: Geochronology, Geochemistry, and Sr–Nd–Pb–Hf Isotopes of Late Triassic Granitoids in the Qiongdongnan Basin, Northern South China Sea: Insights into Petrogenesis and Tectonic Implications
abstract: Abstract The South China Sea (SCS) has experienced a complex tectono-magmatic evolution since the Paleozoic, making its Late Paleozoic–Early Mesozoic tectonic evolution poorly constrained and widely debated. abstract: Cephalopods originated in the Cambrian approximately 500 million years ago, evolving from externally shelled ancestors to forms with diverse morphologies. Despite their morphological diversity, the macroevolutionary patterns and drivers of their diversification remain incompletely understood. Here, we construct a time-calibrated phylogenetic framework for fossil and extant neocoleoid cephalopods and quantify evolutionary rates and morphological disparity over ~490 million years. title: Pax Lambayeque? Trauma, interpersonal violence, and environment over 3,000 years in the Lambayeque Valley Complex, Peru
abstract: Previous research at archaeological sites in the coastal desert of northern Peru suggests strong human behavioral responses to environmental shifts. title: African penguins' behaviour is affected by motor boat airborne noise: an experimental study on wild penguins
abstract: Maritime traffic has expanded exponentially in recent decades, leading to a significant increase in marine noise pollution, a recognized threat to biodiversity. The African penguin ( Spheniscus demersus ), now classified as Critically Endangered, has experienced a dramatic population decline, with fewer than 8000 breeding pairs remaining as of 2025. abstract: The Global Historical Climatology Network Daily (GHCNd), maintained by NOAA’s National Centers for Environmental Information, provides archived daily climate observations from over 25,000 stations worldwide. During extreme precipitation events, accurate weather-station observations are crucial for forecasting, climate analysis, and hazard response. However, hurricanes and other severe storms can disrupt stations through power outages, communication failures, sensor malfunction, or physical damage. title: Value chain analysis of Nature-based Solutions in Europe: Understanding demand, supply, and mainstreaming potential
abstract: This paper investigates the mainstreaming of Nature-based Solutions (NbS) into economic value chains, identifying key sectors driving demand and supply, as well as the barriers and enablers for their uptake. Employing a multi-method approach, combining a systematic literature review (SLR) with eight empirical case studies and input-output modelling, we map NbS value chains across six landscape types (urban, inland waters, coastal and marine, agriculture, forestry, mountains). title: THE ANALYSIS OF THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY IN A NAVAL SHIP’S ENGINE POWERED BY VLSFO AND MGO
abstract: Presentation of the current state of regulations on energy efficiency on board of sea-going ships and the issue of air pollution in the maritime domain, where the nominative energy efficiency index (EEDI), the vessel's energy efficiency management plan (SEEMP) and the operational efficiency indicator (EEOI) were scored. Analysis of thermodynamic parameters and energy efficiency in a marine engine powered dual by MGO and VLSFO. title: Synergy in viral–bacterial co-infection expedites algal bloom demise
abstract: Algal bloom demise, often caused by viruses, is a major driver of carbon cycling in the surface ocean1,2. However, although blooms collapse synchronously, fewer than 30% of algal cells are actively infected by viruses3, indicating the involvement of additional mortality agents. Here we quantified tripartite interactions within a synthetic community composed of the abundant coccolithophore Gephyrocapsa huxleyi, bacteria and viruses isolated during a bloom. title: Community-based exploitation of fishery resources in a salinity-stressed environment: A case study of artisanal fisheries in the commune of Loul Sessène (Sine-Saloum estuary, Senegal)
abstract: Seasonal salinity fluctuations strongly influence fishery resource availability and exploitation strategies in estuarine systems. While the main branches of the Sine-Saloum estuary are well studied, its smaller secondary hydrographic branches remain poorly documented. This study characterized small-scale fisheries in the commune of Loul Sessène (Sine-Saloum Estuary, Senegal), combining a literature review, field observations, fisher and trader surveys, and biological monitoring conducted from September to October 2024. Bound by Containment: Egypt’s Policy Toward Gaza Under Hamas
abstract: Egypt’s policy toward Gaza has been characterized by a persistent tension between its asserted role as a regional mediator and the imperatives of national security and regime stability. This article analyzes the institutionalization of a security-centered approach from the Second Intifada onward and argues that this approach evolved through a path-dependent process, with the General Intelligence Service (GIS) gaining greater authority over the Palestinian file after 2000. title: Organic matter composition and origin differ between restored and natural UK saltmarshes up to 100 years after the breach
abstract: Restoring saltmarshes to enhance atmospheric carbon dioxide uptake is thought to represent a means of climate change mitigation. While carbon stocks in restored marshes were found to reach equivalence with natural sites, the shares of autochthonous and allochthonous carbon sources entering these marshes are less well known. This issue is important because allochthonous carbon is usually excluded from stock calculations. title: Combination of high throughput sequencing and morphological identification assess the diversity and distribution of key benthic taxa in anthropogenic environments
abstract: Abstract Port environments are both heavily impacted by human activities and of high societal importance, making their ecological monitoring essential. The assessment of marine macro invertebrate communities is an important part of such monitoring programs. In an era where molecular methods, such as metabarcoding of bulk DNA or environmental DNA (e-DNA), become increasingly integrated into benthic monitoring, it is crucial to evaluate their performance against morphology-based assessments and to develop robust protocols supported by comprehensive reference databases. title: Phototrophic Fe(II)‐Oxidizers Can Use Multiple (In)Organic Substrates Simultaneously
abstract: ABSTRACT Anoxygenic phototrophs are metabolically flexible bacteria. However, it is unclear how Fe(II) oxidation is affected by the simultaneous availability of organic or inorganic substrates. We therefore cultivated six green‐ and purple non‐sulfur photoferrotrophs from freshwater and marine environments with 2 mM Fe(II), amended with 0.6 mM organic co‐substrate or H 2 . We found that photoferrotrophs generally utilized organics and Fe(II) simultaneously, and that two marine strains preferred Fe(II) over H 2 . title: GEOGRAPHICAL INDICATIONS AND INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES: COLLECTIVE RIGHTS, CULTURAL IDENTITY AND EQUITABLE BENEFIT-SHARING IN INDIA AND NEW ZEALAND
abstract: Geographical indications (GIs) identify goods whose quality, reputation or other characteristic is essentially attributable to their geographical origin. GI protection can sustain rural livelihoods, preserve traditional production practices and promote regional identity, but it does not by itself secure the collective rights of Indigenous communities, whose products often embody customary knowledge, cultural values and intergenerational relationships with land. title: Age and growth of the spiny butterfly ray G ymnura altavela ( E lasmobranchii, G ymnuridae) in the S outhwest A tlantic (in situ) and under human care in a public aquarium (ex situ): Plasticity and population patterns
abstract: Abstract This study provides the first age and growth assessment of the endangered spiny butterfly ray, Gymnura altavela (Linnaeus, 1758), in the Southwest Atlantic, while also updating the growth parameters (asymptotic disc width—DW ∞ and growth coefficient— k ) estimated in an ex situ a marine aquarium setting. In situ growth was assessed by analyzing the vertebrae of 95 individuals captured off the southeastern coast of Brazil. title: Beyond Commodities: Centering Communities in Fisheries Improvement Efforts
abstract: ABSTRACT Small‐scale fisheries (SSFs) support local economies, contribute to food security, and provide livelihoods to millions of people worldwide. However, the SSF sector faces significant challenges, despite years of diverse interventions, including market‐based certifications and fisheries improvement projects. Many interventions have largely focused on narrow conceptions of environmental sustainability and overlooked SSF communities that target nonexport‐oriented resources, crucial for local food security and nutrition. title: Evaluation of social assistance services for people experiencing homelessness in Brazil: strengths and barriers from an implementation evaluation
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the implementation of Specialized Care for Vulnerable Populations (SEAS) and the Specialized Reference Centers for People Experiencing Homelessness (Centros POP) in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, identifying potential strengths and barriers. This evaluative study adopted the Type 1b implementation analysis framework proposed by Champagne et al. Previously validated questionnaires were administered to management and care professionals to assess the structure and process dimensions of the services. title: High-impulse and reactant-regenerative combustion-based micro actuators
abstract: The use of combustibles in micro-actuator technologies enables powerful impulsive actuation capabilities comparable to those of natural organisms. However, the exogenous dependence of fuel limits the development of combustion-based actuators. We present a closed-cycle reactant regeneration strategy wherein the bidirectional interconversion between hydrogen and water achieves real-time fuel replenishment for reactant-regenerative electrolysis and combustion reactions. title: Coverage of tourism and climate change issues in the French news media: An exploratory lexico-semantic approach
abstract: This article examines how the French news media addressed the relationship between tourism and climate change between 2020 and 2025, a period marked by the COVID-19 crisis and intensified climate debates. Drawing on environmental communication and tourism studies, it explores how the media frame these issues, and the extent to which they mobilize scientific knowledge about tourism, climate change, and sustainability transitions. title: Review and Outlook for Aquaculture of Ornate Spiny Lobster (Panulirus ornatus)
abstract: Panulirus ornatus is a high-value seafood species of the Indo-West Pacific. Anthropogenic pressures since the mid-20th century have led to noticeable declines in wild populations, prompting China to enact protective legislation, while other countries focus on aquaculture and germplasm research to sustain supply and preserve wild populations. Current practices rely on rearing wild-caught post-pueruli in sea net cages, as full-life-cycle commercial breeding faces challenges, high mortality of phyllosoma, poorly understood nutritional needs, and uncertain environmental factors. title: Sedimentary controls on pyrite sulfur isotopes in euxinic settings
abstract: Abstract Pyrite is widely used to reconstruct ancient euxinic (anoxic and sulfidic) conditions, yet whether its sulfur isotope composition ( δ 34 S) preserves primary water-column signals remains debated. Here, we show combined bulk and microscale δ 34 S data from pyrite grains collected across the Black Sea water-column and deep-basin sediments. Water-column-derived pyrite consists exclusively of framboidal grains with narrow size and δ 34 S ranges, consistent with formation from local aqueous sulfide and minimal alteration during nucleation and settling. title: Gems wrought by blizzards: Denaturalizing the image in Susan Schuppli’s Not Planet Earth
abstract: The article examines the feedback between the melting Svalbard Archipelago and the sensory and technological apparatuses through which it is perceived, considered through the lens of Susan Schuppli’s short conceptual film Not Planet Earth from 2021. Consisting of eleven shots made during a circumnavigation of Spitsbergen the previous year, Not Planet Earth offers a series of didactic reflections on how to visualize the process of Arctic warming, which primarily transpires on wavelengths below the small sliver of light accessible to human eyesight. title: RiverScan and the third mission: Community engagement and challenge-based learning for urban water governance in Metropolitan Cebu
abstract: As universities strive to make a meaningful societal impact through their third mission activities, they need innovative strategies to connect education, research, and community engagement to address the climate change challenges faced by vulnerable communities. This study evaluates the RiverScan initiative in Cebu City, Philippines, as a practice-based approach to knowledge co-creation and community engagement. title: Petroleum systems and hydrocarbon prospectivity of the offshore Garad Basin, north-central Somalia
abstract: The petroleum potential of the offshore Garad Basin in north-central Somalia remains poorly constrained. This study provides an integrated reassessment of the basin’s structural framework and petroleum system using 2D seismic reflection and well data, and 1D/2D basin modeling. Seismic interpretation reveals coast-parallel culminations, tilted fault blocks, and rollover structures at shelf-to-upper slope depths, with several closures identified within the Upper Cretaceous interval. title: Contactless River Discharge From Unoccupied Aerial Systems Hydrometry: A Multi‐River Evaluation Across a Wide Range of Near‐Natural Cross‐Sectional Conditions
abstract: Abstract Discharge is a fundamental hydrological variable, yet often unavailable under hard‐to‐access or critical conditions, hindering understanding of ungauged catchment hydrology. Unoccupied Aerial Systems (UAS) offer promising contactless approaches for monitoring inland waters under such conditions. Numerous studies have assessed UAS discharge estimation, but few have focused on evaluating fully contactless approaches across diverse river conditions. title: Temporal Changes in the Climatic Predictors of Hatching Success in Leach's Storm‐Petrels
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change is rapidly altering ecosystems worldwide and can modify the demographic rates of long‐lived vertebrates. For seabirds, which rely on ocean productivity, reproductive success is particularly sensitive to climatic variability. Identifying the scale and stability of climate drivers is therefore critical for predicting population dynamics. title: Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
abstract: Protists, defined as eukaryotes distinct from plants, animals and fungi, comprise much of eukaryotic phylogenetic diversity and perform key ecological functions, yet most lineages remain uncultivated and poorly represented in reference databases. Amplicon-based 18S rRNA gene surveys have transformed protist ecology, but primer bias, PCR bias and marker length can limit recovery of divergent lineages. title: Mapping educational infrastructure for rapid urban growth through analysis of spatial inequality and school siting priorities in Adama city, Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Rapid peri-urban growth in Global South secondary cities consistently outpaces municipal public service delivery, generating severe spatial inequalities. This paper examines the spatial and institutional production of primary school infrastructure deficits in Adama City, Ethiopia. title: DNA metabarcoding reveals that Galapagos pinnipeds might not be competing as thought
abstract: Interspecific competition is a key process shaping species distributions and biodiversity. In the western bioregion of the Galapagos archipelago, two endemic and endangered pinniped species coexist: the Galapagos sea lion (GSL) and the Galapagos fur seal (GFS). Previous studies reported marked dietary differences between these species and proposed niche partitioning as the mechanism allowing their coexistence. title: Biodistribution and residue depletion monitoring of 65Zn-labeled sulfadiazine in rainbow trout using PET imaging and HPGe gamma spectroscopy
abstract: Monitoring veterinary drug residues in aquaculture is essential for food safety, regulatory compliance, and the determination of reliable withdrawal periods. Sulfadiazine remains one of the therapeutically relevant antibiotics in fish farming, yet characterization of its long-term depletion kinetics in edible tissues is often limited by the sensitivity of conventional analytical methods and by the high cost and synthetic complexity of classical radiotracers such as carbon-14. title: Crossing the Atlantic: geography, power and the transformation of global oil price formation
abstract: How do commodity price benchmarks adapt when their material foundations erode? We answer through the 2023 reconstitution of Brent, the world's most widely used oil price benchmark. The inclusion of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Midland, delivering US crude into a North Sea benchmark, was debated in the dry register of price-reporting methodology. title: Physicochemical characterization of traditionally fried Moroccan fish bones: A preliminary assessment based on iodine number determination
abstract: With its geographical location between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean a stretch of approximately 3500 km, Morocco has significant fishery resources. It is one of the leading fish producers on the African continent and plays a leading role in the marine fisheries sector in Africa. As a result, it has one of the highest rates of seafood consumption among Mediterranean countries, consisting mainly of small pelagic species such as sardines, horse mackerel, hake, and anchovies. title: TYPES OF SPECIALIZED MAPS AND REGISTERS IN INVESTMENT PROJECT DESIGN
abstract: Specialized maps and registers are an important source of spatial and thematic information in spatial planning and investment project design. The aim of this study is to systematize the main types of specialized maps and registers used in the surveying, design, construction, and operation of investment projects. The study examines specialized maps and registers related to real properties, technical infrastructure, perennial crops, surface waters, subsurface natural resources, terrain, and sites and territories subject to special legal regimes. abstract: The thyroglobulin (TG) gene is a cornerstone of vertebrate endocrinology, serving as the macromolecular precursor for thyroid hormone biosynthesis. Here, we reconstructed the full-length TG sequence of the sea lamprey (Petromyzon marinus), a basal vertebrate of key evolutionary significance, and performed comparative analyses across 50 representative species. title: Developing a Desalination Site Prioritization Index Utilizing the Nexus Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Evaluating water scarcity alone is not enough to determine the priority of desalination projects in the face of limited financial and natural resources. It asks to bear in mind the national development plans, the availability of land, food production, energy supply, environmental conditions, and socio‐economic needs. This study develops the Desalination Site Prioritization Index (DSPI‐SLWF3ESNI) based on the Strategies, Land, Water, Food, Energy, Environment, and Socio‐Economic Nexus. title: Crystallinity‐Governed Liquid Wettability and Mobility on Solid Surface
abstract: ABSTRACT Control over liquid wettability and droplet mobility is essential for several emerging applications including open microfluidics, anti‐icing, self‐cleaning, and heat transfer. Existing strategies generally rely on permanent chemical modification or continuous external stimuli to regulate droplet spreading, pinning, and sliding. Here, we report a unified approach for reconfiguring wettability states and droplet mobility by regulating crystalline packing of a semicrystalline polymer. title: Spatial assessment of land suitability for aquaculture in the Tena River basin, Napo‐Ecuador
abstract: Abstract Aquaculture in the Tena River Basin (Ecuador) is a key contributor to the local economy and food security; however, it also poses environmental risks, including water pollution and the decline of native species. This highlights the need for land‐use planning to identify suitable areas for its development, considering environmental, socioeconomic, and legal criteria. abstract: Research subject . Massive sulfide complexes of the Early Devonian Magnitogorsk Megazone (MMZ) and volcanogenic massive sulfide complexes of Cretaceous and Eocene age on the island of Cyprus and in Turkey. Aim . abstract: This work provides first experimental results of the use of ternary fuel blend consisting of ammonia (NH3), water (H2O) and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) being used as carbonless diesel fuel blends in a conventional small-bore diesel engine. The work is aimed at identifying safe mixtures of fuels that contain zero carbon and that could replace current fossil fuels without requiring major engine replacements. abstract: The management of laboratory assets at the Faculty of Marine and Fisheries Science (FIKP) is still carried out manually using physical documents and Microsoft Excel, which is prone to recording errors, data duplication, and reporting delays. This study aims to develop an integrated web-based laboratory equipment inventory and rental information system. title: Hunters in Danger: Evolutionary Diversity and Conservation Priorities in Carnivore Species of the American Continent
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Many mammals of the order Carnivora are key ecosystem predators. In the American continent, they have a complex biogeographical history, shaped by processes of colonization and adaptive radiation that have generated a high diversity of lineages. However, under the global biodiversity crisis, this group faces increasing extinction risk, and conservation efforts have focused mainly on species richness while neglecting evolutionary relationships. abstract: Animal communities at shallow and upper-slope hydrothermal vents are shaped by vent-fluid conditions, geological setting, substrate composition, and the surrounding shelf ecosystems. Here, we compare two contrasting vent fields north of Iceland: the Kolbeinsey vent field, a shallow shelf system at approximately 100 m water depth dominated by pillow lava and cobble with localized high-temperature venting on top of the ridge, and the Grimsey vent field, an upper-slope, sediment-hosted system at approximately 400 m water depth characterized by active anhydrite chimneys and hot sediments. title: BUT telepresence: a fully open-source VR framework for low-latency stereoscopic video streaming with end-to-end latency instrumentation
abstract: Abstract Advances in immersive telepresence have enabled compelling virtual reality (VR)-based teleoperation, yet existing systems remain difficult to reproduce, inflexible in their streaming configuration, and largely devoid of end-to-end latency instrumentation. Current research prototypes typically rely on fixed encoding parameters, do not expose a unified interface for real-time reconfiguration, and rarely support hardware-accelerated decoding on standalone VR headsets. abstract: Elasmobranchs are exposed to coastal pollution, yet molecular biomarkers are scarce, and their bile proteins have so far been described only for a single shark individual. Bile from two endangered batoids caught by artisanal fisheries off Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, namely the spiny butterfly ray Gymnura altavela ( n = 20) and the groovebelly stingray Dasyatis hypostigma ( n = 21), was characterized. abstract: Abstract This study assesses landscape services (LSs) in Strunjan Landscape Park, Slovenia, comparing the applicability of elementary (landscape features and land cover) versus complex (landscape patterns) spatial units for evaluation. The assessment of two types of service-providing units (SPUs) is performed through a two-tiered process combining qualitative and descriptive evaluation with quantitative/numerical LS evaluation. abstract: Abstract Crimson snapper scales are an underutilized marine by-product rich in bioactive peptides and therefore represent a promising resource for functional food development. In this study, the anti-inflammatory effects of crimson snapper scale peptides (CSSPs) were evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages and dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis mice. abstract: Marine mammals in the St. Lawrence (Canada) face cumulative anthropogenic stressors, including contaminant exposure. abstract: ABSTRACT A sustainable healthcare waste (HCW) management strategy for Dhaka integrating material flow analysis and comparative life cycle assessment is proposed. The current scenario (SC1), heavily reliant on landfilling, low recycling, and incineration without energy integration, is compared with the proposed alternative scenario (SC2), with higher material recycling, waste‐to‐energy conversion, and heat integration. abstract: Abstract The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource 1 . abstract: The existence of highly soluble evaporites in the form of Zagros Fold-Thrust Belt, especially in the case of the Gachsaran Formation, creates a favorable environment for sinkhole formation in gypsum rocks in the southwestern region of Iran. The aim of the current paper is to study the controls on the formation of sinkholes in five selected areas (Changleva, Tang Sarakh, Dishmook, Maroon, and Jaber) using a combination of field investigation, morphometric analysis, and spatial analysis in GIS environment. abstract: Maritime port infrastructure represents one of the most critical and increasingly targeted categories of critical infrastructure in Europe. Ports such as Constanta — Romania’s largest seaport and the busiest on the Black Sea — concentrate extensive digital systems managing cargo operations, customs processing, navigation, and supply chain logistics, creating a complex attack surface that adversarial actors have increasingly exploited through ransomware, operational technology attacks, and data breaches. The authors attempt to reconstruct the key physical and geographic features and patterns of anthropogenic impact associated with land use in a microregion of present-day Tambov Oblast, located at the southern margin of the Great East European Forest and the threshold of the Great Steppe. abstract: ABSTRACT Acoustic geophysical surveying often precedes sediment coring in studies of extant lakes and reservoirs. Compressed high-intensity radiated pulse (CHIRP) acoustic reflection data acquired in lakes are generally recorded as an amplitude envelope for each trace. This format allows real-time imaging and optimizes on-site planning for sediment coring. abstract: Bangladesh’s coastal salt industry depends largely on solar evaporation and is therefore sensitive to rainfall, temperature, sunshine duration and other weather conditions. This study examines national salt production and demand trends, explores associations between salt output and selected meteorological variables, and identifies production constraints reported by salt farmers. abstract: The development of Hainan International Design Island requires local universities to strengthen the links between design education and regional industries, cultural communication, and public services. title: Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
abstract: Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. title: Objetos afectivos: vínculos entre hermanas en tres novelas mexicanas
abstract: This paper offers a materialist reading of novels that showcase bonds between sisters through objects: El libro de Aisha (2018) by Sylvia Aguilar Zéleny, Entre los rotos (2019) by Alaíde Ventura Medina, and El invencible verano de Liliana (2021) by Cristina Rivera Garza. We visualize assemblages and read proxemics between subjects and objects. In these books, the appearance of objects produces a material record of the lives of loved ones and disorients the affections of those who interact with them. title: Heavy metal contamination and health risk assessment in surface water of the Karnaphuli estuary, Bangladesh
abstract: Abstract The Karnaphuli estuary (KE) is a highly dynamic coastal system in southeastern Bangladesh, functioning as a critical trade gateway and supporting rich biodiversity. It is an ecologically and commercially vital location with distinct tidal dynamics; however, intense shipping, land reclamation, industrial effluents, urban sewage, and agricultural runoff have negatively impacted water quality, endangering both aquatic ecosystems and human health. title: Integrated stage-specific management across the production cycle of Macrobrachium rosenbergii: effects of broodstock nutrition, larval salinity and biofloc carbon management
abstract: This study evaluated stage-specific management strategies across three successive phases of the Macrobrachium rosenbergii production cycle: broodstock conditioning, larval rearing, and juvenile grow-out. Each phase was evaluated through an independent experiment testing specific nutritional, environmental, or microbial management factors, while together the three experiments provided a coordinated production framework. title: MULTI-OBJECTIVE OPTIMIZATION OF RESIDENTIAL INDUCEMENT PARAMETERS IN A METROPOLITAN AREA USING A GENETIC ALGORITHM
abstract: This study conducted multi-objective optimization using a genetic algorithm (GA) to identify optimal residential inducement parameters for future population distribution in the Nagoya metropolitan area, Japan. The design variables consisted of three parameters defining spatial zoning patterns and five parameters representing population change rates across different zones. Three objective functions were formulated to evaluate residential–railway station distance, flood exposure, and the scale of population redistribution across the entire area. title: Classification of Flood-Prone Areas in Padang City Using Landsat-9 Satellite Imagery
abstract: Flood-susceptibility mapping requires spatial information that captures the combined influence of hydrological conditions, topography, soils, and land cover. This study classified and mapped flood-prone areas in Padang City by integrating six parameters: rainfall, elevation, slope, distance from rivers, soil type, and land use/land cover. A quantitative spatial approach using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) was employed. title: The overlooked health risks of pluvial flooding and emerging research directions
abstract: Urban flooding is the most frequent and costly natural disaster globally. It not only causes significant damage to property and infrastructure but also has significant impacts on human health, both physical and mental. While the impacts of coastal and riverine flooding on health have been widely studied, the literature on the impacts of pluvial (rainfall-induced) flooding on health remains scant. Unlike large-scale flood events, pluvial flooding is often hyper localized, occurring in small pockets within densely populated areas. title: Benchmarking genome recovery and ecological representation across aquatic communities of contrasting complexity
abstract: Abstract Genome-resolved metagenomics links microbial taxa to metabolic potential, but the ecological interpretation of reconstructed genomes depends on which taxa and genomic features are recovered. How sequencing inputs and reconstruction workflows influence this representation across communities of contrasting complexity remains insufficiently resolved. We generated 252 metagenomic assemblies spanning short- and long-read input volumes, assemblers, and polishing modes in coastal water and mangrove sediment communities, and paired each assembly with five binners. title: Application of Magnetometric Methods for Detecting Submerged Metallic Pollution: Case Study of Radacinosu, Trei Iezere and La Amiaza Lakes (Danube Delta)
abstract: One of the most effective non - invasive geophysical techniques for detecting and characterizing buried or submerged ferromagnetic objects is the magnetometric method, widely used in marine, environmental, and archaeological applications. Identifying sources of metallic pollution in sensitive ecosystems such as the Danube Delta is essential for assessing ecological risks and implementing remediation measures. title: Dynamic, Wet‐Adhesive Hydrogels for Enhanced Interface Healing in Cartilage Repair
abstract: Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self-repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial-based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. title: Transcriptomic analysis implicates microtubule-dependent motor proteins and mitochondria in spermatid development and seasonal reproduction of Phascolosoma esculenta
abstract: This study investigated the molecular mechanisms governing seasonal reproduction in the commercially important marine invertebrate, Phascolosoma esculenta, via transcriptomic analysis of male coelomic fluid, complemented by immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy validation. Sequencing identified 30,897 differentially expressed genes. title: Ecological crisis and extractive capitalism in Sangihe: A Garrardian reading of Perempuan yang Menunggu di Lorong Menuju Laut
abstract: Ecological crisis has become a prominent theme in contemporary Indonesian literature, particularly in narratives portraying the environmental consequences of extractive industries. This study examines how ecological crisis is represented in Dian Purnomo’s Perempuan yang Menunggu di Lorong Menuju Laut (2nd ed.), set in the mining-affected Sangihe Islands. journal: Notion Journal of Linguistics Literature and Culture

title: Mapping Urban Land Transformation in Dehradun City, Uttarakhand, India (2001-2025): A Remote Sensing and Land Transformation Analysis
abstract: The modern world is the absolute example of an urbanized world. The pace of urbanization keeps on constantly varying the physical dimension of an urban area, changing the spatial distribution of its built-up area, green cover and various other land use classes. The present research examines the transformation in the urban land use pattern in Dehradun city, Uttarakhand, from 2001 to 2025, using multi-temporal satellite data and remote sensing as well as GIS technology. title: Optimalisasi Potensi Ekowisata Berbasis Perikanan di Kelurahan Tingkir Tengah, Kota Salatiga, Jawa Tengah
abstract: This community service activity aimed to identify fish farming activities and analyze and map the water quality of the Payaman River as supporting information for introducing fisheries-based ecotourism potential. The activity was conducted from July to August 2026 through field observation, identification of aquaculture potential, water sampling, water quality analysis, and GIS-based mapping. title: A pH-responsive cascade oxygen-generating sodium alginate hydrogel with self-moisturizing and adhesive properties for infected diabetic wound healing
abstract: Hypoxia impairs infected diabetic wound healing by suppressing angiogenesis, sustaining inflammation, and delaying tissue repair. We developed CSZM, a self-moisturizing, adhesive, and injectable calcium-crosslinked sodium alginate hydrogel containing ZnO 2 and MnO 2 nanoparticles. In acidic wound microenvironments, ZnO 2 releases antibacterial Zn 2+ and H 2 O 2 , whereas MnO 2 converts H 2 O 2 into O 2 and limits peroxide accumulation. title: Transitional calcite-aragonite stacking as a signature of hexagonal aragonite in biogenic and inorganic deposits
abstract: Aragonite abundantly crystallizes in marine and continental environments and occurs ubiquitously in biominerals, despite being metastable under ambient conditions. To resolve this apparent contradiction, we studied the crystal structure of aragonite that grew on calcite of biogenic (Berger Károly cave; Hungary) and inorganic (Sonnenberg; Italy and Erzberg; Austria) origin, in a range of natural settings and temperatures. title: Targeting P23 by PM534 suppresses glioblastoma via disruption of SFPQ-mediated phase separation
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is one of the most lethal human malignancies, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 5% and limited effective therapeutic options beyond standard-of-care regimens, underscoring an urgent need for novel therapeutic agents and druggable targets. Here, we report that PM534, a marine sponge-derived synthetic compound, potently suppresses GBM malignancy in orthotopic patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models and in vitro , with IC 50 value of 1.86 nM in patient-derived GBM#P3 cells. title: Fast and cleanup-free determination of trace elements in highly saline matrices using transient inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (t-ICP-MS)
abstract: Standard ICP-MS (inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry) for trace element analysis in highly saline samples (>1% dissolved salts) suffers from salt deposits, reduced sensitivity, and a shortened service life of components. Conventional remedies such as extensive dilution or matrix separation are time-consuming and prone to contamination. title: Integrating Digital Tools into Agricultural Science Instruction in Secondary Schools: Opportunities and Challenges for Curriculum Developers in Delta State
abstract: This study explored the opportunities and challenges for curriculum developers and educators in integrating digital resources into agricultural science instruction in public secondary schools in Delta State, Nigeria.The present study adopted a convergent parallel mixed-methods design (QUAN + QUAL).The quantitative strand sampled 280 agricultural science instructors using a stratified proportionate sample across nine Local Government Areas in the Delta North, Delta Central and Delta South senatorial districts, with 268 verified questionnaire returns (95.71% response rate).The qualitative arm in

title: Consumer preference and willingness to pay for low-commercial-value small pelagic fish in Sri Lanka: Evidence from a choice experiment
abstract: Small pelagic fish play a key role in the livelihoods of coastal fishers; however, most species face persistent marketing challenges that affect fishers’ incomes. This study examined consumer preferences and willingness to pay (WTP) for products derived from low-commercial-value species, with Sardinella gibbosa as the focal species, using a discrete choice experiment (DCE) with urban supermarket buyers (n = 199) in the Gampaha District of Sri Lanka. title: Using Photography as a Tool for Critical Urban Diagnosis: An Undomestication Strategy
abstract: This research describes a teaching experience of urbanism using photography as a critical pedagogical strategy of educating the look to raise awareness among undergraduate students about the problems of their context, employing the objective worldview of each participant regarding their perception of the city and understanding their role as knowledge builders.This was a descriptive field research, based on participant observation methodology, structured in four stages, through a process of categorizing photographs taken by the attendees, shaping positive and negative aspects of the experience.

abstract: Methods for inferring extinction are well established for events that either occurred on millennial time scales (e.g. the late Quaternary) or are unfolding in the present. However, these methods employ distinct data types inherent to palaeontological or neontological settings, yielding a potentially disjointed view of the extinction process. abstract: Kelurahan Kawal, Kecamatan Gunung Kijang, Kabupaten Bintan memiliki beragam potensi ekonomi pesisir, seperti usaha pengolahan hasil laut, kuliner, perdagangan, pariwisata, serta fasilitas pendukung aktivitas pesisir. Namun, informasi mengenai persebaran potensi tersebut belum tersedia dalam bentuk peta khusus yang terintegrasi dan mudah diakses oleh masyarakat. title: Cooper’s Ferry/Nipéhe, stratigraphic integrity, and confirming early inland dispersal: Evaluating peopling of the Americas modeling
abstract: Statistical models shape debates over the timing and geography of the initial peopling of the Americas, but their value depends on testing their assumptions against archaeological evidence. We examine the Apparent Stratigraphic Integrity Index (ASI), used to infer postdepositional mixing at Late Pleistocene sites and support a relatively late occupation of temperate North America. abstract: ABSTRACT Objectives Reconstructing dietary practices in prehistoric hunter‐gatherer populations requires disentangling complex ecological, cultural, and chronological variables. In the Cis‐Baikal region of Siberia, subsistence systems relied on combinations of freshwater and terrestrial resources, including fish, Baikal seals, and terrestrial game. title: First juvenile production of Florida Pompano (Trachinotus carolinus) through captive reproduction and larval rearing in southeastern Mexico
abstract: The Florida Pompano (Trachinotus carolinus) is an emerging species for marine aquaculture due to its rapid growth, high market value, and adaptability to captive conditions. However, the reliable production of hatchery juveniles remains a major bottleneck limiting commercial expansion. The present study evaluated the technical feasibility of captive reproduction, larval rearing, nursery rearing, and juvenile production of T. carolinus under tropical hatchery conditions. title: Relationships between birds, macro-litter, and vegetation in artificial urban wetlands in Greater Melbourne, Australia
abstract: Artificial urban wetlands provide valuable habitat to birds in extensive urban areas. However, these wetlands are often designed primarily for ecosystem services such as stormwater and wastewater remediation and tend to accumulate pollution. The potential impact of macro-litter pollution on birds in these ecosystems is poorly understood. We explored this relationship by surveying birds, macro-litter, and vegetation at 27 artificial urban wetlands across Greater Melbourne, Australia, during the austral summer of 2024/2025. abstract: Since the mid-Miocene, climatic cooling and Quaternary climatic oscillations have significantly reduced plant diversity. abstract: This study examined flood risk zones within the Usuma Watershed in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nigeria, with the aim of identifying spatial patterns of flood vulnerability and informing sustainable flood risk management. The objectives were to map flood-prone areas, analyze flood frequency, and evaluate the biophysical and anthropogenic factors contributing to flood risks. title: Capturing the midnight sun: Ernst Herrmann’s film and photography of Svalbard in the 1930s
abstract: The German geographer Ernst Herrmann was the first explorer to make a colour film of the Arctic while on an expedition to Svalbard in the summer of 1937. The following year, he returned to conduct a series of flights above the archipelago and to further explore the Arctic Ocean. Returning home to Germany, Herrmann brought his film and thousands of photographic images back to present to audiences. This paper explores the impact of Herrmann’s visual work on the development of polar imaginaries. abstract: Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) has been proposed as a scalable carbon dioxide removal strategy, yet long-term field-based constraints on weathering rates and associated carbon sequestration remain limited. Here, we present a 5-year field assessment of Greenlandic glacial rock flour (GRF) applied at 50 t ha −1 to a sandy agricultural soil in Denmark. title: Northward shifts and range contractions: future distribution of Plicosepalus acaciae in Vachellia woodlands of AlUla, Saudi Arabia
abstract: Parasitic plants such as Plicosepalus acaciae act as keystone species but can exacerbate host stress under warming and drying conditions. To inform adaptive woodland management, this study models the current and future potential distribution of P. acaciae under climate change scenarios in AlUla, Saudi Arabia. abstract: Identifying and preserving groundwater recharge potential zones (GWRPZs) is essential for integrating water security into territorial planning. While maintaining high recharge potential theoretically supports subsurface water storage and landscape resilience against extreme weather events, long-term spatial evaluations of how land-use policies preserve these functions remain limited. abstract: The lower Shullcas River basin has a medium-high to low level of risk from landslides. This risk is made worse by geological, climatic, and topographic factors. Climate change, especially through intense rainfall and higher temperatures, increases this risk and makes it necessary to use proper mitigation strategies and more efficient urban development plans. abstract: Abstract Meretrix lusoria is a nutritionally rich bivalve, but thermal extraction degrades bioactives and impairs sensory quality. abstract: This study aims to analyze factors influencing wildfire occurrence and generate a wildfire risk map for Thung Salaeng Luang National Park. Hotspot data were acquired using the satellite sensor of Suomi NPP and the VIIRS system over the study period ranging from 2021 to 2025, having a total of 420 hotspot records. abstract: BACKGROUND: Saline industrial effluents are difficult to treat because elevated ionic strength can inhibit biological treatment and alter metal speciation. This study evaluated two moderately halotolerant microorganisms recovered from seawater and shark-associated samples and examined whether gamma selection altered the performance of the more radioresistant isolate. abstract: The evolution of flow structure is fundamental to establishing an accurate framework for predicting turbulent energy dissipation, momentum transfer, and sediment and nutrient transport within and above flexible stem arrays. The dynamics of flexible stems plays a crucial role in shaping these physical features. abstract: Abstract Acquiring a critical understanding of how organisms respond to environmental changes requires integrating molecular and whole‐organism perspectives while investigating how latitudinal gradients shape thermal responses. abstract: Macrocyclic natural products possess conformationally defined structures that enable recognition of complex biomolecular surfaces, making them attractive scaffolds for modulating protein-protein interactions (PPIs). title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Urban Expansion and Vegetation Cover Using Remote Sensing and NDVI in Mwanza City, Tanzania (2015–2025)
abstract: Rapid urban expansion can alter vegetation cover and the spatial distribution of urban green spaces. This study examined the spatiotemporal dynamics of urban expansion and vegetation cover in Mwanza City, Tanzania, between 2015 and 2025 using Landsat 8 imagery and a geographic information system (GIS)-based Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) analysis. abstract: Simulating large-scale free-surface flow by coupling a localized 3D fluid solver to a cheaper 2D surface model has long faced a mismatch in wave dynamics: efficient 2D wave models used in graphics are typically either linear or non-dispersive. title: Characterization of transcriptomic profiles underlying gross morphological changes observed in semelparous pink salmon ( Oncorhynchus gorbuscha )
abstract: Pacific salmon undergo dramatic physiological remodeling during their terminal spawning migration, culminating in reproductive maturation, senescence, and death. title: Analysis of Spatial-Temporal Changes in Rainfall and Temperature of Baringo County from 1994-2024
abstract: Climate change is reshaping the ecological foundations of pastoralism in the drylands of Africa, where livelihoods depend heavily on seasonal rainfall. In Baringo County in Kenya, changing climatic conditions are increasingly altering rangeland systems that sustain pastoral livelihoods. abstract: Biosphere reserves represent important laboratories for testing innovative approaches to sustainable regional development. In recent years, increasing attention has been paid to the role of smart innovations, particularly those that combine digital technologies, open data infrastructures and participatory governance. abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an educational stand intended for programming and control of an industrial process using a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and a Human-Machine Interface (HMI). title: Advancing multi‐objective optimization in spatial planning
abstract: Abstract Growing demands for food, energy, minerals and other natural resources are intensifying pressure on ecosystems. Meeting these demands while reducing biodiversity loss requires making decisions about which areas can simultaneously support sustainable development, conserve biodiversity and maintain or restore ecosystem services. title: Cedar Tree in Assyrian Reliefs
abstract: This study examines the representation of cedar and timber acquisition in Assyrian royal discourse and visual culture, with particular attention to the Neo-Assyrian period. It considers how a valuable building material could become a sign of royal provision, access to distant landscapes, and participation in imperial networks. The method is an interpretive comparison of published royal inscriptions, museum catalogue records, and scholarship on Assyrian narrative art. title: Skin-Protective and Anti-Photoaging Potential of a Collagen-Based Bioactive Complex in Hs68 Dermal Fibroblasts
abstract: As we age, combined intrinsic and extrinsic aging processes lead to functional and structural alterations in the skin. Supplementation with nutraceuticals combining collagen peptides and plant-derived bioactive compounds represents a potential strategy to maintain skin health. In the present study, we aimed to investigate the skin-protective effects of collagen-based bioactive complex (CBC), which contains marine-derived bioactive peptides and plant-derived bioactive compounds, such as Amla, lingonberry, and other bioactive ingredients. title: An integrated assessment framework for comparing and enhancing flood resilience in heterogeneous floodplains
abstract: Climate change is intensifying flood hazards in deltas, challenging agricultural communities dependent on hydrological conditions. Flood resilience has therefore emerged as an alternative to traditional risk management. Yet, comparative resilience studies often overlook how resilience measures vary across floodplain hydrological regimes (FHRs) within a delta. title: Structural insights into light harvesting and photosystem II evolution in the basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride
abstract: The basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride represents a critical evolutionary transition toward land plants, yet the molecular basis of its ancestral light-harvesting strategy remains elusive. Here, we present a 2.25-angstrom resolution cryo-EM structure of the M. viride PSII-LHCII-LHCP supercomplex, revealing a unique C 2 S 2 M p2 L p2 -type architecture. title: Linking soil erosion to phytoplankton communities: roles of suspended sediment and water quality in a sediment-laden river on the Loess Plateau
abstract: Soil erosion has a substantial impact on riverine ecosystems in the Loess Plateau. However, how these effects propagate through suspended sediment (SS) and water quality to influence phytoplankton communities and how these pathways vary across terrains remain inadequately quantified. In this study, we used models and in situ monitoring to analyze the cascading effects of the soil erosion modulus, SS concentrations, water quality parameters, and phytoplankton community structure in the Beiluo River Basin on the Loess Plateau.
