title: Tourism, gentrification and loss of habitability in Teacapán and Chametla
abstract: Tourism and real estate development are advancing on the coastal localities of southern Sinaloa, Mexico, yet the perceptions of their residents are rarely measured. Using the preliminary data cut from the pilot survey of project FZ-HAB-0021 on the Factoriza UAS platform, this study described the initial behaviour of a fifteen-item scale with three dimensions, Presence of tourism, Living conditions and Rootedness, in Teacapán (Escuinapa) and Chametla (El Rosario). title: Bauhinia chicoi sp. nov. (Leguminosae: Cercidoideae): a new species from the Brazilian Cerrado domain
abstract: Bauhinia is the most diverse genus of Cercidoideae (Leguminosae), with important representation in open and seasonally dry environments in Brazil, especially in the Brazilian Cerrado, which is the domain with the highest number of species in the country. During the preparation of taxonomic treatment for the genus from the Brazilian Cerrado, specimens from western Bahia and southeastern Tocantins that had previously been identified as Bauhinia dubia or considered morphologically related to Bauhinia acuruana were recognized as belonging to a distinct and previously undescribed species. title: Digital Transformation of Cross-Border Logistics in Landlocked Countries: Drivers, Barriers, and Pathways
abstract: Landlocked developing countries (LLDCs) face structural disadvantages in cross-border logistics, with trade costs up to 74% higher than the global average and border crossing times twice as long as those of coastal countries. Digital transformation offers a pathway to overcome these geographic constraints, yet the drivers, barriers, and implementation pathways specific to LLDC contexts remain poorly understood. abstract: ABSTRACT Graphical abstract shows how continuity of catchment objectives across scales and governance functions supports nature-based solutions. Nature-based solutions (NBS) can support urban flood mitigation, water-quality improvement and climate adaptation, yet their effectiveness at catchment scale depends on coordination across multiple actors, governance functions and spatial scales. abstract: ABSTRACT The animal symbiont Vibrio fischeri has served as a model organism for molecular processes underlying bacterial group behaviors, including quorum sensing, and biofilm development. Here, using a genetic approach to identify negative regulators of biofilm formation in V. fischeri , we identified a membrane-bound RNA-binding protein, RtmR (VF_2432), that acts as an inhibitor of the symbiosis polysaccharide (SYP) biofilm. abstract: Alginic acid is a marine-derived polysaccharide with potential applications as an aquaculture feed additive, although its integrated effects in crustaceans remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated its effects on growth, feed utilization, physiological and immune responses, antioxidant status, digestive enzymes, intestinal bacteria and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), muscle quality and composition, ovarian development, and energy status in Macrobrachium nipponense . abstract: Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here, we analyze intermittent Lévy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the Lévy spectrum. title: Trait evolution and nomenclatural adjustments in the Hawaiian lobeliads (Campanulaceae: Lobelioideae)
abstract: Abstract The 143 species of Hawaiian lobeliads constitute the largest adaptive radiation on any oceanic archipelago and comprise six recognized genera distributed across eight well‐supported clades. While molecular studies, including a recent study based on 633 nuclear loci, have supported a single colonization of the Hawaiian‐Emperor seamount chain, the Hawaiian species of Lobelia and the endemic genera Clermontia and Cyanea are not monophyletic. title: Comparative Phylogeography and Genetic Diversity Between Mainland and Island Populations of Common Ground Doves ( Columbina passerina ) and Their Parasitic Lice
abstract: Island archipelagos are ideal natural laboratories for studying genetic variation in populations of organisms. However, relatively little attention has been given to parasites associated with hosts from oceanic islands. Here, we focus on Common Ground Doves (Columbina passerina) and two ecomorphs of parasitic lice, Physconelloides eurysema body lice and Columbicola passerinae wing lice. Both louse species parasitize C. passerina doves and their close relatives but differ in their dispersal abilities. title: Place attachment and perceived insecurity on the Mazatlán malecón
abstract: The Mazatlán malecón is a coastal public space valued by local residents and, at the same time, a setting for experiences of insecurity. This study examined, using a preliminary data cut from the pilot survey of project FZ-HAB-0003 on the Factoriza UAS platform, the initial psychometric properties of a ten-item scale with two dimensions, Bond with the malecón and Fear on the malecón, and the association between them. title: Thermal baselines and climate‐space geometry mediate systematic terrestrial biodiversity responses to warming
abstract: Global warming is rapidly restructuring biological communities, yet terrestrial ecosystems often appear to lack the systematic climate‐driven signatures observed in marine realms. We hypothesise that this apparent idiosyncrasy arises from neglecting the geographic structure of climate. abstract: Although microplastics and nanoplastics (MPs/NPs) are pervasive environmental contaminants, our understanding of cellular toxicity remains incomplete, as adverse effects are often attributed to long-term intracellular accumulation, while the spatiotemporal onset of cellular damage remains poorly defined. title: Storage, Connectivity, and Stream Drying in Headwater Systems: Modeling Across Hydrogeomorphic Features
abstract: Abstract Headwater streams play a critical role in the physical, chemical, and biological functions of downstream waters. However, predicting their specific impact on a landscape scale remains a grand challenge, prompting the development of the river corridor framework to integrate the study of stream channels and hyporheic zones with that of adjacent hillslopes and riparian zones. title: From plant blindness to plant awareness: a narrative and visual framework for botanical literacy
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Plants underpin terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems, yet they often remain unnoticed in public consciousness, reflecting what is increasingly described as plant awareness disparity. This perceptual and emotional bias limits botanical understanding, weakens conservation engagement, and contributes to broader ecological disconnection. In this Perspective, I argue that narrative and visual storytelling can help shift attention from plant invisibility to plant awareness. title: Journeys Toward Impact: A Critical Reflection on Participatory Evaluation in Five European Citizen Science Initiatives
abstract: Evaluating the impacts of citizen science is challenging, and existing approaches often fail to capture the complexity of outcomes across domains. The MICS project (European Union Horizon 2020 Measuring the Impact of Citizen Science, 2019–2022) addressed this by developing a framework to measure the impacts of citizen science across five domains: society, science and technology, environment, economy, and governance. title: A multi-indicator framework for environmental scoring of food products
abstract: This article proposes a framework for assessing the environmental sustainability of food products, with potential applications in product assessment and decision support. The framework applies to both domestically produced and imported food products and aggregates multiple environmental indicators into a weighted score on a defined scale. It is based on the Environmental Footprint (EF 3.1) impact assessment method and was further developed through stakeholder input and evaluation of additional environmental aspects relevant to food systems. abstract: Ophichthus remiger, commonly known as the common eel, is commercially important in Ecuador because Asian markets have high demand. Since industrial fishing began in 2004, no systematic population monitoring has been conducted, limiting understanding of the species' population dynamics and challenging sustainable management efforts. This study provides essential biological parameters of O. remiger in the Gulf of Guayaquil, Ecuador, including size structure, sex ratio, length-weight relationship, and size at first sexual maturity (SFSM), estimated as the median length at sexual maturity (L50). abstract: Abstract This study investigates the main environmental factors causing deterioration in Al-Fustat archaeological area in Historic Cairo. A multidisciplinary approach was applied, combining field observations, hydrochemical analysis, remote sensing, and GIS techniques. Water samples were collected and analyzed to evaluate groundwater quality, while land use/land cover (LULC) and land surface temperature (LST) changes between 1996 and 2022 were assessed using Landsat data. abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Major declines in native biodiversity are occurring globally. Although these patterns are well‐documented in marine and terrestrial ecosystems, large river studies are uncommon, regularly focus on a few freshwater species and often rely on inconsistent methods. By sampling the full fish assemblage in a large river, we evaluated whether (1) downriver reaches are more susceptible to invasion than upriver reaches; (2) habitat specialists differ in their longitudinal river position; and (3) decadal changes are present and, if so, which potential drivers explain them. abstract: Constanta Maritime University (CMU) has educated officers and specialists for the maritime industry for many years, since the establishment of the Civil Marine Institute. abstract: Eudocimus ruber (Linnaeus, 1758), commonly known as the scarlet ibis, is a wading bird widely distributed throughout northern South America and along the Brazilian coast. abstract: ABSTRACT Crossed‐lamellar mollusk shells are among the toughest natural ceramic composites. This is achieved through their hierarchical architecture consisting of multiple orthogonally oriented macro‐layers, each composed of sheet‐like lamellae assembled from progressively finer mineral building blocks. abstract: Urban pluvial flooding poses critical challenges to the operational continuity of transport infrastructure, yet city - scale assessments of flood - induced road disruption remain limited. title: Biogeography of Argentine Stem Weevil Invasion of Southern New Zealand and Two Offshore Islands
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the biogeography and genetics of the invasion of oceanic islands by pest species can provide insights into how to limit such incursions. The invasive pasture pest weevil, Listronotus bonariensis (Kuschel), has established in both New Zealand and some of its offshore islands, causing significant economic damage. abstract: To halt and reverse rapid biodiversity loss, countries are pursuing the ambitious goals and targets in the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) to restore and protect biodiversity in representative networks of protected areas. However, the associated monitoring framework lacks indicators of ecosystem representativeness for Target 3. title: Wild edible fruits of Mozambique: Biodiversity hotspots and priority species for food security and sustainable development
abstract: Societal Impact Statement Wild edible fruits (WEFs) are an important but underutilised resource for improving food security in sub‐Saharan Africa. abstract: BACKGROUND: Timely access to emergency medical services (EMS) is essential for improving survival outcomes and public health. abstract: Background: The increasing frequency and intensity of physical climate hazards—including floods, extreme temperatures, storms, and rising sea levels—pose significant challenges to the transportation sector, which relies heavily on long-lived, capital-intensive assets. abstract: ABSTRACT The inner ears of teleosts are structurally diverse, reflecting the crucial role of audition in sound detection, balance, and social communication within each species’ ecological niche. However, very little is known about the inner ear morphology of large pelagic teleosts. abstract: Abstract Wildfires are increasingly affecting aquatic systems in forested landscapes in many areas around the world. However, in many forested regions aquatic systems are influenced by a legacy of previous forest disturbance in the form of timber management. As we explore wildfire impacts to aquatic biota in forested streams, it is valuable to contextualize post‐fire fish responses relative to past disturbance to understand relative impacts and to acknowledge potential legacy effects. abstract: The goal of this paper is to analyse geocentric spatial concepts in Mandarin, i.e. spatial relations defined via reference to salient locations (“anchors”) in the geographic environment. abstract: Over the past 2.6 million years there have been ~52 glacial-interglacial cycles, which have had profound implications for species’ distributional changes through time. abstract: This study assesses the economic viability of commercial-scale floating offshore wind farms in Portugal under a range of contract for difference (CfD) mechanisms. abstract: Co-ordinated circular swimming by tiger sharks (Galeocerdo cuvier) was documented by divers in the Fernando de Noronha Archipelago, Brazil, on 1 October 2023 under non-provisioned conditions. abstract: Abstract Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. abstract: Abstract In heterogeneous landscapes, mobile organisms can track habitat conditions across multiple spatial and temporal scales, but selecting one condition often comes at the expense of another. In aquatic ecosystems, trade‐offs between temperature and dissolved oxygen (DO) are ubiquitous, and diel cycles of solar heating and photosynthesis can make them dynamic. title: Krill swarm structure drives trophic partitioning in sympatric baleen whale species on the Northern California Current foraging grounds
abstract: For sympatric species, niche differentiation may manifest through resource selection or spatiotemporal partitioning of shared resources. Traits including body size, physiology, and morphology influence the tactics that predators, such as baleen whales, use to meet their energetic needs. Blue, fin, and humpback whales require rich prey patches, like the extensive swarms the zooplankton krill form, to offset the energetic burden incurred by their large body sizes. Krill swarm characteristics (e.g., length, height, biomass) may influence whale foraging efficiency and therefore habitat selection.

abstract: Mangroves offer a wide range of ecosystem services, yet have historically attracted negative perceptions, often tied to real or perceived disservices. title: Salinity filtering and hydrological stage transitions drive the community reassembly of eukaryotes and particle-attached bacteria in Yuncheng Salt Lake
abstract: Extreme salt lakes represent natural model systems for investigating microbial community assembly under strong environmental filtering. However, cross-kingdom associations between eukaryotes and particle-attached bacteria, as well as the combined effects of salinity and hydrological phase transitions on community structure, remain poorly unresolved. We conducted a field survey in Yuncheng Salt Lake, comparing eukaryotic and particle-attached bacterial communities across high-salinity and low-salinity habitats during crystallization and stabilization phases. abstract: Anaerobic methanotrophic archaea are key members of the methane cycle, preventing emissions of the potent greenhouse gas into the atmosphere. Previous studies of freshwater anaerobic methanotrophs targeted their activity at circumneutral pH whereas molecular ecology studies detected anaerobic methane oxidizers in acidic environments such as peatlands. title: Strong Spatial Gradients in Habitat Suitability for Salmonids in a Proglacial River
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change is causing the rapid retreat of glaciers, leading to the formation of new lakes and rivers as well as the evolution of downstream floodplains that could provide new habitat for species such as Pacific salmon ( Oncorhynchus spp.). However, these habitats downstream of glaciers may initially have hyper‐cold temperatures, elevated turbidity and high rates of sediment movement that could preclude successful spawning and rearing by salmonids. title: Hydrogeochemical Indicators of Water Quality Degradation and Inferred Biological Stress in Razzaza Lake, Central Iraq
abstract: Razzaza Lake is considered one of the largest lakes in central Iraq. It extends across the governorates of Karbala and Anbar. The lake's surface area has markedly decreased, and its water level has dropped due to severe climatic changes in recent years, which have caused a significant decrease in freshwater recharge coupled with high evaporation rates. This study aims to evaluate the evaluation of the lake's hydrochemical and environmental characteristics, as well as its pollution levels, in order to determine water quality and its suitability for aquatic life and human investment. abstract: Los murciélagos insectívoros se encuentran entre los mamíferos nativos menos estudiados en Galápagos, los cuales pueden ser vulnerables a presiones antropogénicas emergentes. Este estudio evaluó los patrones espaciales y estacionales de la actividad acústica de Lasiurus borealis brachyotis y L. villosissimus en tres sitios contrastantes de las Islas Galápagos: dos áreas húmedas de tierras altas en la isla Santa Cruz (Santa Rosa y El Camote) y un sitio árido de tierras bajas en la isla Baltra. title: Deciphering morphometric and terrain-driven controls on groundwater recharge and agricultural suitability using geospatial and multivariate modeling
abstract: This study presents an integrated assessment of basin morphometry, groundwater recharge potential, and agricultural suitability in the Lower Thamirabarani River Basin, Tamil Nadu, using geospatial datasets and statistical analyses. The morphometric results indicate an elongated basin (Rf = 0.268; Re = 0.584) with a moderate drainage density (1.4 km/km 2 ), reflecting a balanced runoff response and a reduced tendency toward flash flooding. title: In silico analysis of arginine and creatine kinases, exploring the coexistence of phosphagens in the cannonball jellyfish Stomolophus sp.2
abstract: The cannonball jellyfish Stomolophus sp.2 is distributed in the southern region of the Gulf of California. At high temperatures, it shows metabolic responses that produce large amounts of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to cope with thermal stress. In addition to mitochondria, phosphagens are suggested as one mechanism for rapid ATP production in this species. abstract: Fish is a critical component of global food security and human nutrition, providing high-quality protein, essential fatty acids, vitamins, and minerals. Despite its importance, comprehensive nutritional data for locally consumed fish species in many Nigerian freshwater reservoirs remain limited. This study assessed and compared the proximate and mineral composition of two commonly consumed fish species, Lates niloticus (Nile Perch, family Latidae) and Barbodes binotatus (Spotted Barb, family Cyprinidae), from Tungan Kawo Reservoir, Kontagora, Niger State, Nigeria. title: Sex‐dependent carry‐over effects of non‐breeding habitat use on breeding performance in the Eurasian curlew
abstract: In migratory birds, the effects of habitat use during the non‐breeding period can carry over to body condition in subsequent stages of the annual cycle and affect the breeding performance of individuals. We investigated whether the habitat types used on the non‐breeding grounds and at spring stopover sites influenced nest success through carry‐over effects in the Eurasian curlew, a migratory species with declining populations. title: Geometry Optimization of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Hyperspectral Surveys for Water Quality Retrieval and Comparison with Satellite Data in Mining-Impacted Waters
abstract: Rapid spectral surveying of water quality at high spatio-temporal resolution remains challenging. Advances in UAV-based spectral imaging offer new opportunities. This study evaluates the optimal configuration and acquisition strategy of a lightweight UAV-based visible and near-infrared (VNIR) hyperspectral system for monitoring water quality and hydrogeochemical anomalies in mining-impacted areas. title: Analysis of Fishing Household Income in Leato Selatan Urban Village, Dumbo Raya Subdistrict, Gorontalo City
abstract: Fishers' income from fishing is seasonal and uncertain, so fishing households often seek other sources of income. This study aims to analyze fishing household income from the fisheries sector and to determine its contribution to total household income in Leato Selatan Urban Village, Dumbo Raya Subdistrict, Gorontalo City. The study employed a survey method with descriptive statistical analysis of 35 fishing households selected from a population of 70 households. title: From global solution space to local strategies: integrating adaptation pathways and global scenarios for water scarcity
abstract: Abstract Adaptation to climate-change-induced water scarcity requires structured approaches to develop strategies that are plausible under uncertain climate and socioeconomic futures. We test a framework for integrating adaptation pathways into the scenario framework across three case studies: Caribbean SIDS, Rural Ethiopian Communities, and the Rhine-Meuse Delta. title: Predator loss amplifies the disruptive impacts of heatwaves
abstract: Heatwaves are intensifying under climate change, often triggering the catastrophic loss of predators. Still, it remains unclear whether their ecological impacts on ecosystems arise from direct thermal stress or from altered food web dynamics following predator loss. Using experimental tri-trophic fresh water food webs, we independently manipulated heatwave intensity (none, moderate or severe) and predator persistence (fish removed during the onset of heatwaves versus fish persisted during heatwaves) to disentangle these pathways. title: A High‐Resolution Stable Isotope Database Revealing Within‐City Tap Water Variability and Source‐Water Connectivity in Trinidad
abstract: ABSTRACT This Data Note presents a georeferenced stable isotope dataset from the island of Trinidad, comprising 309 water samples collected between 2018 and 2026. title: Assessing Toxic Metal Bioaccessibility and Health Risks in Fish from Rasul Barrage, Pakistan through a Simulated Gastrointestinal Model
abstract: Elevated levels of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in aquatic environments pose risks to ecosystem integrity and human health through fish consumption. This study assessed PTE concentrations in water and edible muscle tissues of six fish species ( Labeo rohita, Sperata seenghala, Rita rita, Cirrhinus mrigala, Cyprinus carpio, and Gudusia chapra ) from Rasul Barrage, Punjab, Pakistan, and evaluated human health risks using total and bioaccessible PTE concentrations following simulated gastrointestinal digestion. title: Modelling the Source of 2017 Casamicciola Earthquake (Ischia Island, Italy): A Critical Review and New Insights into the Interaction Between Volcanic and Tectonic Processes
abstract: Abstract We investigate the source of the 21st August 2017, Md 4.0 Casamicciola volcano-tectonic earthquake (Ischia Island, Italy), which caused heavy damage on the northern flank of the Mt. Epomeo resurgent block of the Ischia caldera. We adopt a multidisciplinary approach that combines geophysical, geological and coseismic ground deformation data mapped since after the earthquake occurred. title: Spatiotemporal Analysis of Temperature Extremes Under Future Climate Scenarios in the Borana Zone, Ethiopia
abstract: Climate change has intensified temperature extremes worldwide, with particularly severe implications for semi-arid regions such as southern Ethiopia. This study assessed historical and future temperature extremes across the Borana Zone using ENACTS observational datasets (1985–2014) and bias-corrected outputs from nine CMIP6 global climate models under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Extreme temperature indices recommended by the Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices (ETCCDI) were computed using the Climate Data Tool. title: Experimental diagenetic transformation of biogenic aragonite to calcite in sulfate and/or phosphate-bearing fluids
abstract: The transformation of biogenic aragonite to calcite in phosphate or phosphate-sulfate bearing fluids was investigated through hydrothermal experiments at 60–80 °C up to 90 days. A phosphate-only system (BF) and a phosphate-sulfate system (BFS) were characterized by XRD, FTIR, and aqueous geochemical analyses supported by PHREEQC modelling. title: Attribution science and climate change litigation in India
abstract: Abstract In climate change litigation, attribution science is increasingly being used as an evidentiary tool to ascertain responsibility, accountability, liability, and provide redress the impact on human life and the environment. The Indian judiciary implicitly uses scientific evidence in an unstructured or fragmented manner without it being clearly labelled as attribution science. title: Drought characteristics of European river basins derived from GRACE and GRACE Follow-On total water storage (2002–2026)
abstract: Hydrological drought, i.e. a persistent deficit of water stored on and below the land surface, is poorly represented by traditional climate indices based on individual meteorological data. Now, well-established geodetic techniques provide a reliable insight into total water storage (TWS) anomalies. We analyze drought characteristics of 24 major river basins of Europe and its south-eastern margins using TWS from the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) missions, computed from the recent JPL mascon solution for April 2002 to February 2026. title: Recent advances in transcriptome research in fishes: A review
abstract: Transcriptomic studies have allowed researchers to examine gene activity across the genome and gain insight into many areas of fish biology. This review, following PRISMA guidelines, synthesizes recent studies on fish development, aquaculture, physiology, immunity, nutrition, toxicology, and evolution. abstract: Legacy contaminants (DDX and PCBs) persist in fishes of the Southern California Bight, yet most consumption advisories rely on species- and region-level averages that ignore within-species variation among harvested individuals. We evaluated whether individual traits improve prediction of contaminant burden in a "fish in hand," and whether any gains can be achieved using information available to anglers at capture (e.g., size, region) versus traits requiring post-hoc laboratory analysis (e.g., age, stable-isotope-inferred trophic ecology). title: Interspecific Interactions Constrain Individual Niche Divergence and Reveal Energetic Cost of Niche Expansion
abstract: ABSTRACT Individuals vary in resource use, generating trophic niche variation that shapes a population's niche width (PNW). Interspecific interactions are predicted to constrain PNW, though individual responses are often heterogeneous. The keystone niche individual (KNI) framework identifies individuals that disproportionately expand PNW by exploiting resources beyond the population's realized niche, but whether interspecific interactions limit their emergence is unknown. title: A Geophysical Crustal Model of Central Italy for Geoneutrino Predictions in Borexino
abstract: Abstract Predicting the geoneutrino signal at underground detectors requires a local crustal reference whose precision matches the experimental uncertainty. The current Borexino reference is 15 years old and deterministic. title: Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO2 by the stick-to-culture strategy
abstract: The accelerating global energy demand, coupled with diminishing fossil fuel reserves and growing carbon emissions, underscores the urgent need for sustainable energy solutions. Autotrophic microalgae are promising cell factories for converting CO2 into renewable biofuels. However, conventional microalgal biofuels typically depend on energy-intensive or nutrient-deficient regimes that suppress microalgal proliferation, resulting in a critical trade-off between biomass growth and lipid biosynthesis. title: DIA-based proteomic insights into quality deterioration and spoilage biomarkers of chilled anchovies (Stolephorus commersonii)
abstract: Anchovy ( Stolephorus commersonii ) rapidly undergoes postmortem autolysis. This study investigated chilled anchovy degradation over 7 days at 4 °C using physicochemical, histological, and enzymatic analyses, coupled with DIA-based comparative proteomics between day 1 and day 7 samples. title: Turnover and ecological release drove biogeographic shifts during the Ordovician/Silurian transition
abstract: Abstract Whether mass extinctions consistently drive global homogenization or instead produce phase-dependent restructuring remains debated. Here, we evaluate the impact of the Late Ordovician mass extinction on global biogeographic structure and its relationship to biodiversity dynamics across the Ordovician/Silurian transition. title: STATISTICAL METHOD FOR CALCULATING LATERAL DEFORMATIONS OF RIVER CHANNELS
abstract: The paper focuses on improving the methodology for calculating horizontal deformations of river channels, taking into account the statistical heterogeneity of bank erosion. The conventional regulatory approach, which relies on direct extrapolation of the actual erosion rate based on past periods, fails to account for the probabilistic nature of channel processes: depending on the selected retrospective interval, it yields a significant spread in the predicted values. title: An emerged salt diapir in a low-purity salt formation (Pinoso Diapir, SE Spain). Geomorphology, long- and short-term kinematics, and impact of salt mining
abstract: This work analyses the geomorphology, evolution and current kinematics of the emerged Pinoso Diapir (Eastern Betics, Spain), expressed as a salt fountain 333 m in local relief, covering 7.9 km 2 , and with an estimated volume of 791 Mm 3 . abstract: ABSTRACT Shallow lakes provide many vital ecosystem services, particularly when dominated by submerged macrophytes. However, they face increasing ecological degradation due to multiple stressors, such as eutrophication and climate change, which lead to enhanced frequency of short-term heatwaves and storms. title: Green hydrogen pipeline network planning for West African export corridors
abstract: West African countries have extensive renewable energy generation potential, making the region promising for green hydrogen production. However, most Africa–Europe hydrogen pipeline analyses focus on hydrogen supply from North Africa. Existing and planned pipeline infrastructure links West Africa with Europe, providing potential routes for hydrogen transport. abstract: SUMMARY Spring algal blooms are characterized by the rapid expansion of phytoplankton populations under favorable environmental conditions, yet the intracellular mechanisms that enable this rapid proliferation remain poorly understood. In this study, using the colonial green alga Pediastrum duplex , we found that mother cells enlarged with starch accumulation under cold conditions in the light promote an increase in the number of cells per daughter colony under subsequent warm conditions. title: Assessment of the accumulation of selected trace elements in agricultural and non-agricultural soils using contamination indices: a case study from Kahramanmaraş (Türkiye)
abstract: Soil serves as the foundation of our food system. Therefore, consistent and reliable information about soil is essential for understanding, managing, and protecting it. This study examines the concentrations of trace elements of environmental importance, including vanadium (V), antimony (Sb), tungsten (W), thallium (Tl), and bismuth (Bi), in agricultural and non-agricultural areas in Kahramanmaraş (Türkiye) and evaluates their accumulation levels using contamination indices (i.e., enrichment factor (EF) and contamination factor (CF)). title: Adapting the SWOT matrix as a territorial planning tool for urban flood management
abstract: Abstract Urbanization significantly alters watershed runoff, increasing peak flows, reducing base flows, and degrading river ecosystems. Without adequate control measures, urbanization increases flood vulnerability, heightening flood risks and damaging urban infrastructure. Recent academic and technical perspectives emphasize the importance of efficient stormwater management, advocating for a systemic approach to address urban flooding risks. title: ADMINISTRATIVE CAPACITY AND DISASTER RISK GOVERNANCE IN SMALL ISLAND PROVINCES: LESSONS FROM NORTH MALUKU, INDONESIA
abstract: Small island provinces face acute disaster risks due to their geographic isolation, ecological vulnerability, and exposure to natural hazards. Effective disaster risk governance in these regions fundamentally hinges on public administrative capacity. This study examines how administrative capacity shapes disaster risk governance in North Maluku, an archipelago province in eastern Indonesia. title: Too threatened to try: how extinction risk drives research neglect in rays and skates
abstract: Global biodiversity loss demands that research effort be directed towards species most at risk. Yet conservation science is biased by species' accessibility and perceived charisma, raising concerns that threatened species may be overlooked. We apply a structured causal modelling framework to 651 species of rays (superorder Batoidea), a highly threatened yet understudied lineage of cartilaginous fishes, to disentangle the drivers of research effort. title: Development of an Engineering Geological Zoning Map of Iraq Based on the Reclassification of an Existing Geological Map
abstract: This study presents the development of a nationwide engineering geological zoning map of Iraq through the reclassification of an existing geological map. The aim is to extend the available engineering geological information for Iraq and provide a regional - scale framework applicable to land - use planning, foundation engineering, infrastructure development, and other engineering activities. title: Whale swimming evolution recorded in vertebral microanatomy from the Eocene to present
abstract: Among modern aquatic amniote clades that evolved pelagic locomotion, whales are a prime example, but timing and mode of evolutionary changes in their swimming are poorly understood. Here, we use 3D vertebral microanatomy derived from CT scanning to investigate swimming patterns in extinct whales. All vertebral centra from a single specimen of the extant common dolphin Delphinus delphis were used to provide a baseline for the correlation of microanatomical parameters and spinal movements in our dataset of fossil whales. title: Web-based Direct-to-Consumer Marketplace for Small-Scale Fisheries Products: Rapid Application Development and Functional Evaluation in Jaring Halus Village, Langkat, Indonesia
abstract: Fishery and micro-enterprise products in Jaring Halus Village, Langkat Regency, Indonesia, are sold primarily within the village through face-to-face transactions and manual record keeping. This condition limits producers’ market reach to physically present consumers and provides no persistent transaction data for monitoring or business development. title: A Museum‐Curated, Voucher‐Backed 12S Barcode Reference Library for Fishes of the Ecuadorian Amazon
abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding is an emerging method that promises to expedite and improve biodiversity surveys by identifying species from the genetic material they shed into the environment. eDNA methods offer many advantages over conventional specimen-based surveys, but their effectiveness hinges on reference libraries, which for highly biodiverse regions such as the Ecuadorian Amazon are too often incomplete, inconsistently curated and disconnected from morphological voucher specimens needed to reliably identify and revise taxa. title: Distance Sampling for Aerial Waterbird Surveys—Application to an Ephemeral Wetland of International Significance
abstract: ABSTRACT Ephemeral wetlands can radically change the ecology of arid landscapes but are difficult to robustly survey when flooded, challenging conservation management. The Fortescue Marsh ( Martuyitha ) is one of the largest water features of northwest Australia, with significant cultural and ecological value. title: Isolation and Screening for Prodigiosin Producing Serratia marcences from Different Sources
abstract: Prodigiosin is a red bioactive pigment produced by several bacterial species, particularly Serratia marcescens. It has potential applications as a natural colorant and has been reported to exhibit antimicrobial, anticancer, and immunosuppressive properties. This study aimed to isolate and screen Serratia isolates from Kano State, Nigeria, for prodigiosin production. Samples were collected from multiple locations across the state. title: Differential effects of moisture on surface versus mineral soil microbial communities in the High-Arctic
abstract: Microorganisms play key roles in nutrient/carbon cycling and greenhouse gas fluxes in High-Arctic soils. However, the influence of soil conditions on tundra microbiomes remains poorly understood. Using high-throughput sequencing, we studied bacterial, fungal and micro-eukaryotic communities in surface soil-biocrust matrices and the underlying mineral soil along two environmental gradients in Svalbard. title: Simulated In‐Stream CO 2 Production Under Changing Organic Carbon Quantity, Quality, and Stream Geochemistry
abstract: Abstract Increasing urbanization and changing precipitation confound our understanding of carbon (C) cycling in streams. Precipitation drives organic C into waterways, while watershed urbanization can increase the lability of dissolved organic carbon (DOC). Uncertainty in how C quantity and quality interact to influence in‐stream CO 2 production limits predictions of stream responses to urbanization and extreme precipitation. title: Ecology and morphology as drivers of passerine song differentiation across an island archipelago
abstract: We conducted an integrative analysis to explore possible explanations for the song differentiation in bird populations from the mainland and the Tres Marías Archipelago (TMA) on the central‐western Pacific coast of Mexico. abstract: This qualitative literature review reexamines the corporate turnaround of PT Pembangunan Jaya Ancol Tbk (PJAA) by integrating contemporary scholarship with its newly available unaudited consolidated statements for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The study extends an earlier second-stage turnaround framework by examining earnings quality, debt-maturity concentration, cash-flow provenance, operating productivity, and destination competitiveness. title: How concentration, temperature, and pH affect soapberry’s cleaning power compared to commercially available detergents
abstract: The widespread use of synthetic cleaning products significantly contributes to environmental pollution, creating the need for natural alternatives. In this study, the capillary tube method was used to investigate the effect of concentration, temperature and pH on the effectiveness of soapberry as a plant-based detergent and compare its effectiveness to commercially available detergent and bio-detergent. abstract: Wetlands remove nitrogen, phosphorus and organic pollutants, yet the same biogeochemical processes also release carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O); improving water quality and affecting the climate are therefore two sides of one system. The comparison between constructed and natural wetlands in this review covers pollutant fate and greenhouse-gas effects together, and it also asks whether their evidence bases are comparable at all. title: Runtime Bias Correction of Parameterized Lakes in Climate Models
abstract: Abstract A novel approach is presented for improving atmosphere‐lake heat and evaporative fluxes in global and regional climate models. The method involves deriving and applying runtime corrections to lake surface water temperature (LSWT) and lake ice, to reduce biases in the climatological annual cycle of these quantities. The bias correction procedure is developed for a particular single‐column thermodynamic lake model but could, in principle, be applied to other lake schemes, including fully prognostic models with hydrodynamics. journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems

title: Gas permeation in flexible multilayer pipes: Multiphysics modelling and experimental validation
abstract: Flexible pipes used in oil and gas and emerging energy applications are subject to gas permeation through polymeric layers, leading to the accumulation of species such as CO 2 , CH 4 , H 2 O, and H 2 S in the annulus and potentially driving corrosion-related failures. Accurate prediction of annulus conditions is therefore critical for design and life assessment. title: Spatiotemporal Structure of the Invasion of Hypolimnas misippus (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae) in Brazil Suggests Multiple Colonization Events
abstract: ABSTRACT The Danaid Eggfly Hypolimnas misippus (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae) is a species of butterfly native to the Afro‐Asian region and is recognized for its colonization of tropical areas around the globe, including the Americas. However, its presence in Brazil has been recorded sporadically over 100 years, without certainty as to whether its status is established or not in the country. This research aimed to compile and analyse records of the species in Brazil to understand spatial and temporal patterns of its occurrence. Searches were conducted in entomological collections, biodiversity dat

title: Effect of predation on the performance and microbial ecology of a membrane-based biofilm photobioreactor
abstract: Eukaryotic predation can have a significant effect on the performance of bacterial biofilm processes, yet little is known about the effect of predation on photosynthetic biofilms. This study evaluated the effects of predation on a membrane-based biofilm photobioreactor (MB-PBR) by introducing enriched mixed protozoa in the system. The effects of predation on performance were compared to a control in which predation was inhibited by the addition of cycloheximide, a eukaryotic growth inhibitor. The effects of predation on a suspended photoautotrophic system were also studied. Lastly, 16S and 18S

title: Digital Marketing Acceleration of Shopee for Lapeo Marlin Shredded Fish Products as a Catalyst for Economic Resilience and Independence of Local Communities
abstract: Lapeo Village, Campalagian District, Polewali Mandar Regency holds significant fishery potential, notably the processing of marlin fish into shredded fish (abon) by the Rezky Kuliner Lapeo Business Group. However, this potential is hindered by conventional marketing, simple packaging, and the absence of a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). This partnership-based community service program aims to accelerate digital marketing via the Shopee platform, redesign product packaging, create a QRIS account for non-cash transactions, and compile operational SOPs to build resilience and economic indepen
journal: MOVE Journal of Community Service and Engagement

title: The evolutionary history of transporters of the plastid outer envelope of Chloroplastida– a structure-sequence comparison
abstract: Plant metabolism heavily relies on plastids, derived from once free-living organisms. However, how two distinct organisms merged into one remains currently only partially understood. Protein-mediated metabolite exchange across the double-membrane plastid envelope is essential for plant cell function. Here, we investigate the evolutionary origins of plastid outer envelope proteins (OEPs) involved in these transport processes. institutions: Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences

title: Can omnivores be considered keystone species? Bears as a study case
abstract: Abstract The functional roles of herbivores and carnivores in ecosystems have been relatively well studied: both can shape ecosystems through strong direct and indirect top‐down controls on other guilds. By contrast, the role omnivores play has been rarely explored, even though their diet spans several trophic levels and potentially has numerous effects on ecosystems through trophic and non‐trophic interactions. To gain a better understanding of the potential ecosystemic role of omnivore trophic and non‐trophic interactions, we performed a literature review on bears (Ursidae): a specific group
institutions: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

title: Environmental Trade-Offs in port energy Systems: Global evidence and transition challenges for West African ports
abstract: The global push for sustainability has increased pressure on ports to decarbonize. This review critically examines the environmental trade-offs of port energy systems and assesses how global experience can inform the energy transition of West African ports. It considers biofuels, hydrogen, onshore power supply, renewable energy and hybrid systems alongside the infrastructure, economic and institutional conditions affecting implementation. title: IgE-binding proteins of myofibrillar proteins in Miyakea nepa (Stomatopod)
abstract: Shellfish allergens exhibit significant molecular diversity across crustacean taxa, yet the allergen repertoire of stomatopods remains largely unexplored. We hypothesized that the extensive evolutionary divergence between Stomatopoda and Decapoda has resulted in distinct allergen profiles, comprising both conserved pan-allergens and stomatopod-specific IgE-reactive proteins. To test this hypothesis, we characterized the immunoproteomic profile of Miyakea nepa (mantis shrimp) and compared it with those of three decapod species ( Thenus orientalis , Portunus pelagicus , and Penaeus vannamei ). title: Assessment of Arsenic and Mercury Contamination in Water and Sediments Around the Jaboi Sabang Geothermal Area Using ICP-OES
abstract: The Jaboi Sabang Geothermal Area in Aceh, Indonesia, comprises four active craters that release geothermal fluids and gases into surrounding water sources used by local communities for daily activities. Despite the known toxicity of arsenic (As) and mercury (Hg) in geothermal environments, baseline data on their occurrence and distribution in local water and sediment remain limited. This study assessed As and Hg contamination in water and sediment samples using Inductively Coupled Plasma–Optical Emission Spectrometry (ICP-OES). Water samples were collected from hot springs, bathing pools, rive

title: Horizontal Gene Transfer from Fungi to Myxozoa: Genomic Evidence and Evolutionary Implications
abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is increasingly recognized as an important mechanism driving evolutionary innovation in eukaryotes, yet its functional significance in parasitic lineages remains poorly understood. Myxozoans are obligate cnidarian parasites characterized by extreme genome reduction and complex two-host life cycles, making them an intriguing system for investigating the evolutionary role of HGT. We conducted a comparative genomic and transcriptomic analysis to identify and characterize candidate genes putatively transferred from fungi to myxozoans. Phylogenetic reconstruction, seq
institutions: Instituto de Ciências Ambientais, Químicas e Farmacêuticas

title: Occurrence and characteristics of microplastics in dug-eell groundwater of the Kandy District, Sri Lanka
abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution is an emerging environmental concern, yet groundwater systems remain inadequately studied, particularly in Sri Lanka. Groundwater, which remains under-researched, is the primary drinking water source for some rural and semi-urban areas in the country. This study aimed to evaluate the occurrence, abundance, and characteristics of MPs in groundwater across Kandy District. Thirty wells representing urban, semi-urban, and agricultural settings were sampled. title: Polysaccharide-based superwetting and hydrated antibacterial interfaces: evidence gaps, mechanisms, and translational criteria
abstract: Polysaccharide materials are often called superwetting antibacterial systems because they swell or have a low initial water contact angle. But these measurements do not show that the materials kill bacteria or control biofilms. This review looks at polysaccharide-based superwetting and hydrated interfaces, including coatings, polymer brushes, porous membranes, fibrous layers, hybrid interfaces, and selected hydrogels. Distinct Cyanobacterial Taxa are Associated with Microcystin and 2-Methylisoborneol Production (MIB) in a Mixed Bloom
abstract: Cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms (cHABs) threaten drinking water supplies through the production of cyanotoxins and taste-and-odor (T&O) compounds, yet identifying the organisms responsible remains challenging in mixed cyanobacterial communities. We characterized a July 2025 bloom in Lake Kickapoo (Texas, USA), a primary drinking water source for the City of Wichita Falls, using microscopy, quantitative PCR, and Nanopore sequencing for targeted amplicon and 16S rRNA community analyses. title: Metagenomic and Mineral Characterisation of Biofloc Cultured With Anaerobically Treated Distillery Spent Wash
abstract: ABSTRACT This study characterised the microbial community and mineral composition of biofloc cultured in three independently managed 50 t indoor raceway tanks (R1, R2 and R3) using anaerobically treated distillery spent wash as the exogenous carbon source. The mineral profile of the biofloc was determined for each tank by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, whereas the microbial community was characterised by whole metagenome shotgun sequencing of a single composite library pooled across all nine biofloc samples. title: How lake sediment records inform archaeology: examples from the Americas and potential future applications in Colombia
abstract: Paleolimnology, the study of lake and wetland sediments, provides a powerful means of reconstructing long-term interactions among climate, environment, and human societies. Drawing on examples from across the Americas, where sediment records have clarified the environmental contexts and ecological consequences of agriculture, deforestation, hydraulic engineering, and demographic change, this paper examines how such archives can strengthen archaeological interpretation. title: Systematic Evaluation of Cyanidioschyzon merolae Across Photobioreactor Systems: Linking Reactor Design to Biomass Production and Biochemical Composition
abstract: ABSTRACT Extremophilic red microalgae are promising platforms for sustainable biotechnology, combining robust growth under selective thermoacidophilic conditions with production of thermostable phycobiliproteins and carbon‐rich biomass. However, reactor‐dependent effects on growth, product formation, and biomass composition remain insufficiently resolved. Here, we systematically evaluated the extremophilic red microalga Cyanidioschyzon merolae across cultivation scales and reactor formats and benchmarked its performance against the well‐established Galdieria javensis and Limnospira platensis .

title: Hovering in turbulent rock‐array microhabitats: Multidimensional kinematic responses of S chizothorax grahami
abstract: Abstract The interaction between flow and riverbed structures creates spatially heterogeneous turbulent microhabitats that influence fish station‐holding strategies and energy allocation. This study investigated the hovering behaviour of Schizothorax grahami in complex turbulent microhabitats formed by rock arrays of different scales using flume experiments. title: Fault‐Related Structure Revealed From Surface‐Wave Attenuation Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing on Dark Fiber
abstract: Abstract Blind fault mapping requires dense observations over large areas, and distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) provides a viable solution using dark fibers. Seismic attenuation is sensitive to fault‐related structure but relies on reliable amplitude measurements. In DAS data, amplitudes are distorted by non‐attenuation effects, including non‐uniform coupling and small‐scale heterogeneity, limiting their direct use for attenuation imaging. title: Complex evolutionary history and possible unrecognized diversity in Philippine waterside skinks (Squamata: Scincidae: Tropidophorus) inferred from molecular and morphological evidence
abstract: We present the first robust geographical characterization of variation and phylogeographic population structure in Philippine Tropidophorus (spiny waterside skinks), based on extensive sampling from throughout the archipelago and a combined focus on genetic and morphometric variation. Last revised more than 40 years ago, the Philippine Tropidophorus have never been the subject of an integrative study to evaluate their evolutionary relationships, genetic diversity, population structure, and species boundaries. title: Terrestrial Analog Constraints on Radar Detection of Cross-stratified Martian Aeolian Deposits
abstract: Abstract Active desert dunes constitute field-scale terrestrial analogs for Martian aeolian deposits, as their migration-driven stratigraphy and dry, low-loss sandy materials provide a natural counterpart to radar-detected wind-blown units on planetary surfaces. However, their subsurface architecture and electromagnetic properties remain poorly constrained, owing to the difficulty of characterizing unconsolidated dune interiors without disturbing primary sedimentary structures. title: Weathered microplastics reshape gastrointestinal responses to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances during co-exposure
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet the biological consequences of their co-exposure remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the individual and combined effects of weathered polyethylene MPs and three representative PFAS (PFOA, PFOS, and PFBA) using Caco-2 cells and a mouse oral-exposure model, complemented by tissue distribution analysis and multi-omics profiling. title: How an endemic became widespread: the peculiar situation of the groundwater amphipod Niphargus boulangei Wichers, 1964 (Amphipoda, Niphargidae)
abstract: Abstract Niphargus boulangei (Amphipoda, Niphargidae), a rare groundwater amphipod from the northern continental range of the genus, was long known only from Pas-de-Calais (French Channel coast). Recent phylogenetic studies added records from Moselle (France) and Wallonia (Belgium). We molecularly screened available but undetermined Niphargus of North-Western Europe and collated all available information on the ecology, genetic diversity and distribution of the species. title: Genomic diversity and inferred dispersal routes of Ostreid herpesvirus type 1 infecting Magallana gigas across Europe and the Pacific region
abstract: Abstract The order Herpesvirales comprises double-stranded DNA viruses characterized by substantial genomic plasticity, including recombination, structural variation, gene gain and loss, and lineage turnover. These processes can obscure phylogenetic relationships and complicate the reconstruction of viral evolutionary histories. Within this order, Ostreid herpesvirus 1 (OsHV-1) is a major pathogen of the Pacific oyster Magallana gigas and is responsible for recurrent mortality events affecting global aquaculture. title: Changes in subfossil chironomid and cladoceran assemblages along water depth in Swiss lowland lakes
abstract: Abstract Aquatic invertebrate remains in lake sediments can potentially be used to provide information on past changes in water depth based on sediment records. However, only limited data are available on the distribution of invertebrate remains across varying water depths in stratified Central European lowland lakes. We analysed fossil chironomid and cladoceran assemblages from surface sediments sampled along ten transects of six Swiss lowland lakes with the aim of exploring the relationship between the distribution of species assemblages of these indicator groups and water depth. title: The cyanobacterium Anabaena uses pleomorphism as an acclimation strategy to high‐light stress
abstract: Phytoplankton species display characteristic morphologies that are generally assumed to confer adaptive advantages, yet the functional significance of cell shape remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether pleomorphism contributes to acclimation to changing light environments. Using the cyanobacterium Anabaena sp. title: 3D Solar‐Driven Interfacial Evaporator Based on Tailored TiO 2 Nanotube Arrays by Wireless Anodizing for Efficient Desalination
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is an energy‐efficient desalination strategy. However, the existing solar‐driven interfacial evaporators mostly rely on a surface‐localized photothermal layer for heat confinement, which limits evaporation exclusively to the top surface. title: DEVELOPING AN INTEGRATIVE STRATEGY AND STRUCTURE FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND PRACTICE IN OKE- OSUN FARM SETTLEMENT IN OSOGBO
abstract: This study presents a conceptual and three-dimensional (Autodesk 3Ds Max) model of an integrated mixed farming system designed for the wetland ecosystem at Agric Farm Settlement, Oke - Osun, Osogbo, Osun State, Nigeria. The system integrates (i) stilt-elevated poultry housing (6 units, 2.5m high concrete stilts), (ii) lowland rice (Oryza sativa) cultivation on raised paddies, and (iii) fish farming (Clarias gariepinus and Oreochromis niloticus) within an interlinked water maze channel system between rice plantings. title: Validity of SPT–CPT Correlation for Bearing Capacity Prediction of Reclaimed Soils in Lagos Island, Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: Background: Engineers often apply published, generic SPT–CPT correlation ratios to estimate one test from the other when only one is available. These ratios were developed for natural soils, and their validity for reclaimed soils in Lagos Island, Nigeria, has not been tested. Methods: Secondary SPT, CPT and borehole data from six reclaimed sites in Ikoyi, Victoria Island, Lekki and Sangotedo were analysed. Waterbird assemblage spatial organization as an ecological response indicator of water-level management in a saltpan wetland
abstract: Waterbird monitoring usually counts birds and species, but these measures do not show how different species are arranged in space. We tested whether the spatial organization of individually mapped waterbirds could provide an additional indicator of biological response to water-level management at Yongan Wetland, Taiwan. Bird locations from 44 weekly surveys were compared with a null model that kept the locations and habitat conditions fixed while rearranging species labels within the same survey day, zone, and habitat class. title: GREEN FINANCE AND THE EVOLVING ROLE OF INSURANCE IN MARITIME SUSTAINABILITY
abstract: The maritime industry is a vital component of global trade and economic development, yet it faces growing pressure to adopt sustainable practices in response to environmental challenges and climate change. This paper examines the growing role of green finance in supporting maritime sustainability initiatives, focusing on innovative financial instruments and investment strategies designed to mitigate environmental impacts. Additionally, it examines the evolving function of insurance in promoting sustainable practices, including coverage for eco-friendly vessels, emissions reduction technologies

title: Extracellular polymeric substances drive Curvibacter host adaptation and cospeciation with Hydra
abstract: The interactions between hosts and their microbial symbionts play a crucial role to host physiology. Bacteria can adapt to specific host environments over evolutionary timescales, leading to cospeciation and the formation of specialized host–microbe relationships. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying these adaptations provides key insights into the evolution of symbiosis and the stability of microbial communities. title: Spatiotemporal Patterns and Projected Changes in Rainfall and Temperature Over the Harari Region, Ethiopia
abstract: Climate variability and climate change pose major challenges to sustainable development in Ethiopia, particularly in regions that depend heavily on rain-fed agriculture. This study investigated the historical (1985-2025) and projected (2041-2100) spatiotemporal variability of rainfall and temperature across the Harari Region using high-resolution observational datasets (Ethiopian Meteorological Institute (EMI), obtained through the Enhancing National Climate Services (ENACTS) dataset rainfall and temperature) together with statistically downscaled CMIP6 multi-model ensembles under the SSP2-4.5

title: Forested peatland margins as biogeochemical control points of dissolved organic carbon export
abstract: Peatlands store large carbon reservoirs, but the landscape controls on their lateral carbon losses remain insufficiently resolved. We investigated dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentrations and export along a bog–swamp forest–Klyuch River continuum within the Great Vasyugan Mire, Western Siberia. Peat-profile characterization, pore-water chemistry and hydrometeorological monitoring were combined to assess spatial and seasonal DOC patterns. title: Enigmatic HCl detections as a potential signature of igneous activity on Mars
abstract: Mars is reputed to lack ongoing volcanic activity. However, marsquakes were revealed recently, and clues to volcanism younger than tens of million years have accumulated. While sulfur dioxide, so far undetected, could testify to ongoing eruptive activity, evidence of active magma chambers may be better identified by seepage of halogen gases, such as hydrogen chloride (HCl). title: Forest or tundra? How different vegetation reconstructions of Last Glacial landscapes in Europe may shape our perception of early human dispersal processes
abstract: ABSTRACT Regional variability and long‐term changes of past ecosystems likely had a strong impact on hunter–gatherer population dynamics, including the expansion of anatomically modern humans and the disappearance of Neanderthals. However, our understanding of these ecosystems remains limited, even when looking at large‐scale patterns, such as the extent and distribution of forested areas. title: A high-order, structure preserving scheme for the stochastic Galerkin shallow water equations - unification and two-dimensional extension
abstract: Recently, two independent research efforts have been made to study the stochastic Galerkin formulation of the shallow water equations. title: A low-coercion, open-loop design provides preliminary evidence of visually guided discrimination and individual differences in two Neotropical otters (Lontra longicaudis)

title: Effects of formalin residues in marketed fish in Haryana on physicochemical and textural properties and their mitigation strategies
abstract: Formalin, a solution of formaldehyde, is widely misused in the fish trade due to its antimicrobial and tissue-firming properties. This study investigates the prevalence and impact of formalin adulteration in fish marketed across four major cities of Haryana, India-Faridabad (FDB), Yamuna Nagar (YNR), Panipat (PNP), and Bahadurgarh (BHG). title: Coolitude Culinary Memory as Cultural Expression Among Indentures a Gastrocolonial Approach in Khal Torabully's Selected Poems
abstract: The present research study focuses on how food can be interpreted as a sort of indentured resistance in Khal Torabully's selected poems. The idea of Gastrocolonial is used as analysis of the various manifestations of food memories, spices, and markets as symbols of cultural continuity for Indian indentured laborers. The poems suggest the historical interrelationship between slavery, indenture and colonial trading networks. It highlights the subjective lives of migrants that transcended the Kala Pani. title: Rock damage mechanisms and reservoir protective drilling fluid optimisation for a sandstone block in Dagang Oilfield
abstract: Abstract The tight sandstone reservoir in a certain block of the Dagang Oilfield exhibits a dual-porosity structure, comprising nanoscale matrix pores (average diameter: 11.99 nm) and natural fractures (50–100 μm). A key challenge facing this formation is severe water sensitivity caused by a mixture of sodium feldspar and montmorillonite clays, which account for 56% of the total clay content. title: Temporal Trends in Extreme Precipitation Events in Eight Flood‐Prone US Inland Cities (1981–2023)
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme precipitation is one of the leading drivers of hydrometeorological hazards and urban flood risk across the United States. However, most previous analyses focus on broad geographic scales, often obscuring the local variability and urban microclimate effects critical for understanding risk in metropolitan areas. This study investigates temporal trends in the frequency and magnitude of extreme precipitation events at the HUC12 watershed scale in eight flood‐prone inland US cities for 1981–2023. title: Seasonal and spatial dynamics of in-channel water bodies on a river sandbar and associated macroinvertebrate communities
abstract: In-channel water bodies (ICWBs) on river sandbars, including backwaters and riverine ponds shaped by hydrological disturbance, remain poorly understood with respect to their seasonal and fine-scale spatial dynamics. We investigated the environmental conditions and benthic macroinvertebrate assemblages in ICWBs formed around traditional wood-based river training structures ("Seigyu") within a single sandbar in a regulated river in central Japan. title: The spatiotemporal evolution mechanism of enterprise-led organic agriculture: Evidence from Shandong Province
abstract: This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of enterprise-led organic agriculture in Shandong Province, China. Using panel data on certified organic enterprise production bases across 16 prefecture-level cities from 2014 to 2023, we combine spatial statistical analysis, Local Moran's I, two-way fixed-effects regression, and robustness checks. title: Non-target and target screening for pollution profiling and ecological risk assessment in the danjiangkou reservoir and its tributaries
abstract: As the source water hub of the South-to-North Water Diversion Middle Route Project, the characteristics of pollutants in the Danjiangkou Reservoir and their ecological risks are crucial for regional water environment security. This study integrated non-target screening and target analyse to systematically characterize the composition of organic pollutants and the occurrence and preliminary spatial patterns of 19 per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the Danjiangkou Reservoir and its tributaries, as well as to assess their potential ecological risks. title: Influence of the Nature of the Cationic Residues on the Activity of the Antimicrobial Peptides of the Lynronne Family
abstract: Most antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are cationic, with positively charged amino acid residues (i.e., arginine, lysine, and/or histidine) being responsible for their selective interaction with bacteria. In the present study, we investigated the influence of the nature of cationic residues taking the Lynronnes peptides as models. title: Performance Evaluation of Historical CESM2 Rainfall Before and After Linear Scaling Bias Correction in the Sadar Watershed, Indonesia
abstract: Accurate rainfall data is fundamental for hydrological analysis, yet Global Climate Models (GCMs) such as CESM2 exhibit systematic biases compared to ground observations. This study evaluates historical CESM2 monthly rainfall before and after Linear Scaling (LS) bias correction in the Sadar Watershed, East Java, Indonesia (2000–2014). abstract: Chronic hyperglycaemia in type 2 diabetes drives a self-perpetuating cycle of glucotoxicity. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of extracts from the green seaweed Chaetomorpha linum (O.F.Müller) Kützing, 1845 to mitigate glucotoxicity in rats adipocytes. title: Geochemical and petrophysical characterisation of igneous rocks in the southern Sydney Basin: implications for radiogenic heat production and geothermal potential
abstract: Anomalously high bottom-hole temperatures were recorded in a historical petroleum exploration well (‘Lake Nepean 1’) in the southern Sydney Basin. abstract: Indwelling medical devices remain susceptible to biofouling, which can lead to infection, device failure, and patient complications. title: Species-specific shrub strategies shape carbon balance and soil processes in high-arctic tundra
abstract: The expansion of shrub communities in the High Arctic significantly alters carbon (C) and nutrient cycling, yet distinct species are often treated as functionally equivalent in ecosystem models. In this study, we investigated the physiological strategies, plot-scale CO₂ fluxes, and plant-soil-microbe interactions in two dominant high-arctic dwarf shrubs ( Salix polaris and Dryas octopetala ) with bare soil included as a reference. title: Managerial Factors Influencing Inland Container Depot Operational Performance in Tanzania: A Case of Dar es Salaam Inland Container Depot (DICD), Kurasini, Tanzania
abstract: This study examined the associations of leadership quality, staff competency and strategic decision-making with operational performance at Dar es Salaam Inland Container Depot (DICD), Kurasini, Tanzania. Using a pragmatic mixed-methods design, the study analysed 119 questionnaire responses through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression, complemented by thematic interpretation of managerial interviews. title: Agroirrigational Sedimentation and Pedogeochemical Transformation of Irrigated Oasis Soils in Uzbekistan
abstract: Introduction Long-term irrigation is a major driver of morphogenetic, agrophysical, and pedogeochemical transformation in oasis soils of arid and semi-arid regions. This study evaluated the regional variability and anthropogenic transformation of irrigated oasis soils formed under contrasting depositional, geomorphological, and hydrological conditions in Uzbekistan. title: Population genomics of heterosporous lycophytes: allopatric speciation and historical persistence through paleoclimatic fluctuations
abstract: Speciation is the fundamental process driving the origin of earth biodiversity. While speciation mechanisms have been revealed in many plant taxa, the evolutionary dynamics of heterosporous lycophytes remain largely unexplored. Here, we used the Selaginella sanguinolenta group, comprising seven montane species in eastern Asia, as a model system. We generated a high-quality, chromosome-level reference genome for S. aitchisonii, conducted whole-genome resequencing of 191 individuals across 49 populations, and integrated population genomic, phylogenomic, morphological, and ecological analyses. However, the asset recording process at PT Astra Daihatsu Ngurah Rai Tuban was previously conducted using a semi-manual approach, resulting in data redundancy, delays in report generation, and difficulties in obtaining real-time inventory information. abstract: Dinamika ekologis sungai perkotaan, seperti yang melintasi Kota Yogyakarta, rentan terhadap tekanan antropogenik, namun pemahaman komprehensif mengenai interaksi antara kondisi abiotik, tingkat pencemaran, dan respons keanekaragaman hayati pada tiga sungai utamanya (Winongo, Code, dan Gajah Wong) masih terbatas. abstract: This study evaluated the implementation of the local government dike project in Barangay Lawis, Inabanga, Bohol, the level of community satisfaction with its delivery, and its perceived effectiveness in mitigating the risk of high tide. Anchored on Expectation-Confirmation Theory, the SERVQUAL Model, and Good Governance Theory, the study employed a descriptive survey design involving 100 respondents: 10 local government representatives selected through purposive sampling and 90 community residents selected through simple random sampling. title: AUREOCHROME 1b is a candidate transcriptional regulator of pigment biosynthesis in Phaeodactylum tricornutum
abstract: Diatoms have attracted attention for their potential to produce high-value metabolites, such as terpenoids. However, the regulatory mechanisms governing their isoprenoid metabolism remain poorly understood, which poses a major bottleneck in engineering them for greater production efficiency. title: EroMapper – a QField plugin for soil erosion mapping
abstract: Soil erosion is one of the main threats to agricultural productivity and environmental sustainability worldwide. Detailed and consistent field data on erosion features are essential for a better understanding of erosion processes, identifying driving factors and supporting the development and evaluation of suitable soil erosion mitigation strategies and soil erosion prediction tools. Existing digital mapping solutions are often limited in terms of standardisation, flexibility and ease of use. title: Eggshell-derived CaO₂@MgO–Al₂O₃ composite for phosphate removal through adsorption and precipitation
abstract: The increasing discharge of phosphate-containing wastewater and the accumulation of calcium-rich household waste are two significant environmental challenges that require sustainable remediation strategies. This study demonstrates the feasibility of converting eggshell waste into a value-added phosphate-removal material, with potential application as a low-cost adsorbent for phosphate reduction in wastewater treatment systems. title: Globally Unregulated UV-329 Dominates Serum Body Burden and Is Associated with Lower Platelet Counts in Elderly Adults: Evidence from Mixture Epidemiology and Computational Toxicology
abstract: Benzotriazole ultraviolet stabilizers (BUVs) are ubiquitous contaminants, yet their internal exposure profiles and hematotoxic potential in elderly populations remain uncharacterized. Here, we report the first cross-sectional biomonitoring study of five BUVs in serum from 57 elderly participants (≥64 years) of Han and Mongolian ethnicity in a remote agro-pastoral region of China. title: Evaluating Thermal Resistance in Cryogenic LNG Cargo Containment Systems: A Case Study of The Tangguh–FSRU Jawa Satu Transport Route
abstract: This study evaluated the thermal resistance performance of spherical cryogenic storage tanks on liquefied natural gas carriers operating between the Tangguh refinery and the Jawa Satu Floating Storage Regasification Unit to address the operational challenge of cargo shrinkage. The natural evaporation of cryogenic fluids during maritime transportation represented a physical loss of energy supply and caused a significant financial burden on the national energy supply chain. title: Mechano-electrochemical energy harvesting and self-powered sensing via dynamic liquid metal–electrolyte interfaces
abstract: Wearable devices, stretchable sensors, and soft electronics benefit from harvesting ambient energy using compliant materials, yet existing approaches often face limitations in power density, scalability, and electrode adaptability. Here, we report a liquid metal mechano-electrochemical energy harvester (LMMEEH) that converts mechanical stimuli into electricity through dynamically regulated electrode-electrolyte interfaces. title: Effects of dietary taurine supplementation on growth performance, serum biochemical responses, and intestinal health of juvenile American eel ( Anguilla rostrata )

title: Evolutionary shifts in condition-transfer effects but not anticipatory maternal effects in Trinidadian killifish ( Anablepsoides hartii )
abstract: Transgenerational plasticity (TGP) shapes offspring phenotypes independent of changes in DNA sequence. However, it remains unclear whether transgenerational plasticity primarily reflects adaptive anticipatory adjustments to predicted future environments or condition-dependent carryover from the parental energetic state. Because traits differ in their functional roles within life-history architecture, selection may favour distinct cross-generational mechanisms depending on the ecological context. title: Structures of methanogenic schizorhodopsins reveal divergent strategies for proton transport and thermal adaptation
abstract: Schizorhodopsins (SzRs) are light-driven inward proton pumps found in Asgard archaea (Promethearchaeota), contrasting with most microbial rhodopsins that export protons. Some SzRs, including Methanoculleus taiwanensis SzR (MtSzR) and Methanoculleus sp. SzR (MsSzR), exhibit high heat tolerance, suggesting structural adaptations to extreme environments. title: Prioritizing Sustainable Development Goals Indicators for the Automobile Sector
abstract: ABSTRACT Ten years after adopting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a consistent prioritization approach for business sectors is still lacking. This study develops a prioritization method for SDG indicators for industry sectors based on the criteria of “footprint” and “urgency.” Urgency is defined as the distance between indicator performance and the target level. To determine the target level, a decision‐making process is developed. This method is used to prioritize 23 environmental SDG indicators for the automobile sector in the European Union. title: Local food production could link food security and invasive plant control in Galapagos
abstract: Context Balancing food security and biodiversity conservation is a major challenge in the Galapagos Islands, where agriculture overlaps with vulnerable native ecosystems. Objective We evaluated the potential of local agricultural production in Santa Cruz, Galapagos, to increase food self-sufficiency while conserving native vegetation under future population growth, and assessed the effects of land use change on invasive plant cover.
