title: Lipid emulsions and catheter material regulate the formation of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms on intravascular devices
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a commensal bacterium involved in many healthcare-associated infections, sometimes through the formation of biofilm on invasive vascular devices in intensive care units. Yet, little is known about the main factors driving the development of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms on intravascular devices, especially in critical care settings. This study introduces a new in vitro Staphylococcus aureus biofilm model on both central venous and arterial catheters. title: Six new species in the Colostethus latinasus group (Anura: Dendrobatidae) highlight hidden biodiversity in Panama
abstract: For decades, there has been taxonomic confusion regarding the identity of Colostethus pratti -like frogs occurring in Panama. By including a sample from the close vicinity of the type locality of C. pratti (Valdivia, Colombia), we revealed that these Panamanian frogs instead form a monophyletic clade sister to C. latinasus . title: MICROPLASTICS: HEALTH HAZARDS AND THE WAY FORWRAD
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are tiny pieces of plastics, less than 5 mm in size. They cause a type of pollution that has become a public health concern worldwide.. Current studies have increasingly focused on understanding the possible health hazards of MPs exposure on the human body. This review seeks to highlight the exposure pathways, pathophysiology and toxicity of MPs as well as proffer possible solutions.. title: Valley-bottom wetland agricultural conversion and recovery shape greenhouse gas dynamics and soil organic carbon stocks in an African tropical highland system
abstract: Tropical wetlands significantly impact global greenhouse gas (GHG) budgets and carbon storage; however, data from sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) remain limited. Highland valley-bottom wetland (HVBW) agriculture supports millions, yet its effects on GHG emissions and carbon storage remain undocumented. This study quantified soil emissions of nitrous oxide (N 2 O), carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), and methane (CH 4 ) in the Taita Hills, Kenya, from 12 converted, 10 recovering, and one reference (intact) HVBW. title: Do local communities or large museums better serve Scotland's fossil heritage? The case of dinosaurs on the Isle of Skye
abstract: In common with many museums around the UK, The Hunterian in Glasgow is managing its collections in a new light. Historically, specimens and artefacts were collected by museums with little thought to the needs of local communities. Scientists would arrive at a location, focused only on the items they needed to collect for their research; or museums would swap and buy artefacts, without ever informing the communities from which those specimens were collected. title: The impact of a hypothetical nuclear explosion’s source region electromagnetic pulses (SREMP) on urban communications infrastructure
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the effects of nuclear electromagnetic pulses, with a particular focus on source region electromagnetic pulses (SREMP), on essential urban infrastructure, notably telecommunications systems. Through systematic analysis, the investigation seeks to clarify the extent of disruption and the vulnerabilities SREMPs pose to urban communication networks, contributing to a deeper understanding of critical infrastructure resilience in the face of such electromagnetic threats. title: Determining the heights and horizontal positions of Tatra Mountain peaks using GNSS measurements, mapping services, and LiDAR data
abstract: Accurate heights and horizontal positions of mountain peaks and passes are important for tourism, research, and public use, yet map-based information often lacks documented accuracy. This study provides precise Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) measurements of 140 peaks and passes in the Tatra Mountains and uses them to validate heights and horizontal positions derived from Polish (PL) and Slovak (SK) LiDAR data, geographic registry (PRNG), OpenStreetMap (OSM), OpenTopoMap (OTM), and Google Maps (GM). title: Cold Plasma Modulates Microbial Community Structure, Enhances Quality Attributes and Extends Shelf Life of Chilled Mutton
abstract: Chilled mutton is highly nutritious; however, oxidation and microbial contamination during refrigerated storage can lead to quality deterioration, safety risks, and economic losses. Cold plasma (CP), an emerging nonthermal preservation technology, has considerable potential for controlling microbial contamination in food. This study evaluated the effects of CP treatment on the quality of chilled mutton stored at 4 °C for 30 days. title: “Compete, Cooperate... Why not both?” Player orientation and hybrid vs. competitive mechanics in gamified crowdsourcing with JellyfishGO!
abstract: Sustaining participant engagement while maintaining data quality is a central challenge for games with a purpose (GWAPs). In this article we examine whether player orientation (according to Bartle’s taxonomy) shapes contribution volume under competitive and hybrid (intra-team cooperation + light inter-team rivalry) GWAP mechanics. Although the design provisioned a purely cooperative arm, too few cooperative-only sessions materialised for session-level analysis, so the empirical comparison is Competitive versus Hybrid. abstract: The use of sewage sludge in agricultural lands is one of the sludge management options that must be ensured to avoid environmental and health consequences. Considering the content of heavy metals in sewage sludge, the aim of this study was to measure the concentration of these elements in sewage sludge and assess the ecological and health risks resulting from its use in agricultural lands in southwestern Iran using Monte Carlo simulation. abstract: Sedimentation in the Lake Tondano watershed was assessed by comparing estimates from the Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE), Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE), and Modified Universal Soil Loss Equation (MUSLE) with direct field observations from ten major inlet rivers. title: A comprehensive framework for mesh sensitivity analysis: Advancing Savonius wind turbine CFD simulations
abstract: Numerical errors in convective flows are often diffusive and can make computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations depart markedly from physical reality. Savonius wind turbine (SWT) simulations are especially affected by transient flow separation and inconsistent numerical methodologies. title: Connecting conservation communities: From social network analysis to practical application
abstract: Abstract This study explores how social network mapping and analysis can be applied to support community‐based conservation practice, and what benefits and challenges emerge in doing so, enlisting the Northern Rivers, New South Wales, Australia as a case study. We identified 273 local conservation groups, conducted 51 semi‐structured interviews and 50 meetings and open interviews, and created a publicly accessible, interactive network map using the Kumu platform based on desktop analysis and group members' contributions. abstract: ABSTRACT Acid mine drainage (AMD) represents a major environmental challenge associated with sulfide-rich mining activities. Metagenomic approaches and microbial diversity analyses were used to characterize AMD from a gold-polymetallic mine in the Lori Region (Armenia). To evaluate variations in community composition between AR1 and AR2 zones, statistical analyses of α- and β-diversity of microbial communities were conducted. title: Thermal asymmetry and density-dependent behavioural shifts drive competitive displacement between two globally invasive ants
abstract: While co-occurring invasive species are often assumed to accelerate degradation via 'invasional meltdown,' the temporal dynamics of their interactions and cascading effects on native communities remain poorly resolved. Here, we investigate the spatiotemporal interactions between two devastating invasive ants, Solenopsis invicta and Wasmannia auropunctata. title: Quantifying the Association Between Inbreeding and Mortality in Endangered St. Lawrence Estuary Beluga Whales
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding factors that limit the growth of endangered populations is crucial for conservation. Depleted populations are vulnerable to losses of genetic variation and inbreeding depression. Genetic factors have been cited as one of the potential contributors to the lack of recovery of the isolated St. Lawrence Estuary (SLE) beluga ( Delphinapterus leucas ) population, which remains endangered despite decades of protection from hunting. title: Ecological and productive variation across a silvopastoral chronosequence under retained tree cover in high-Andean grazing systems
abstract: Abstract Livestock systems in high-Andean environments can modify vegetation structure and soil conditions through changes associated with grazing management and land use. Silvopastoral systems established under retained tree cover represent an alternative management strategy in these landscapes; however, ecological responses associated with different stages of farmer-managed silvopastoral establishment under high-Andean conditions have received comparatively less attention. title: Performance Evaluation of PPP-AR Using WUM Final Products for Coordinate Accuracy and Crustal Velocity Estimation: Comparison with GAMIT/GLOBK Solutions in Northern Central Java, Indonesia
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of Precise Point Positioning with Ambiguity Resolution (PPP-AR) using Wuhan University (WUM) final precise products for coordinate consistency and deformation velocity estimation at five InaCORS stations in northern Central Java. title: Green Synthesis of Gold Nanoparticles Using Citrus aurantiifolia Extract and Their Potential for Polystyrene Microplastic Detection
abstract: Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) were successfully synthesized through a simple and green route using dried Citrus aurantiifolia extract as a bioreductant. The synthesis was carried out at a bioreductant concentration of 10%, a gold precursor concentration of 0.60 mM, pH 7, and a reaction time of 5 min. title: Chronic Exposure to Chlorpyrifos Induces Blood Biomarkers, Somatic Indices and Organ Histopathology of Banded Gourami ( Trichogaster fasciata )
abstract: ABSTRACT Pesticides have become an integral part of agricultural crop production for growing more food. However, the excessive use of pesticides ultimately reaches the aquatic ecosystems and demonstrates pernicious impacts on non‐target aquatic organisms, including fish. Hence, the current study aimed at unravelling the chronic toxicity of an organophosphate insecticide, chlorpyrifos (CPF), on a battery of blood biomarkers, somatic indices and histopathological aberrations of liver and kidney in banded gourami ( Trichogaster fasciata ). title: DIGESTION, AMINO ACID COMPOSITION, AND ANTIOXIDANT ACTIVITY OF BUK-SIAM MAEJO HYBRID CATFISH HYDROLYSATE ESSENCE SOUP
abstract: Protein hydrolysate essence soup from Buk-Siam Maejo hybrid catfish was studied before and after retort treatment using simulated gastric and intestinal digestion. title: Listening to energy: How electricity markets become audible through hydropower
abstract: Sound is present in many ways in and around hydropower infrastructure, from environmental impacts and equipment monitoring to structural safety and the management of aquatic species. Yet these uses of sound are often separated by disciplinary and institutional boundaries, limiting what we can learn about the relationships between energy infrastructures, markets, and environments. title: Box modelling the transfer of sulfur on Mars using Earth as a geochemical analogue
abstract: Volcanism was once the primary source of sulfur transport on Mars, and its present-day surface preserves a geological record of these mineralogical processes. Sulfur plays a key part in the eruption process, forming sulfides, and less commonly sulfates in the magma chamber, and being expelled as sulfur dioxide-rich gas. title: Integrating indigenous knowledge and ecological modeling to understand anthrax transmission risk
abstract: Anthrax, caused by Bacillus anthracis, remains a persistent zoonotic threat across African savannas, yet its transmission dynamics are poorly understood in regions with limited surveillance systems. Northern Limpopo National Park (Mozambique) combines ecological conditions favorable for spore persistence with Indigenous communities that depend on unfenced grazing and frequent wildlife contact. title: Adapting Citizen Science for Environmental Research in Post-War South Lebanon: Civilian Science in Action
abstract: War severely affects ecosystems, yet assessing environmental damage during conflict is constrained by restricted access, safety risks, and institutional disruption. This article examines whether citizen-led soil sampling can produce fit-for-purpose environmental evidence under wartime conditions. abstract: Abstract Resistance to fluoroquinolone antibiotics is rising across bacterial pathogens, including the important pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( Mtb ), posing a major threat to global health. Novel bacterial topoisomerase inhibitors (NBTIs) can overcome fluoroquinolone resistance. However, the only FDA-approved NBTI, the triazaacenaphthylene compound gepotidacin, is not indicated for mycobacterial infections. abstract: ABSTRACT Profiling microbiomes is an important way to understand the function and composition of communities in the wild, but natural microbiomes are often highly complex and often unamenable to experimentation to reveal cause-and-effect relationships. By using a small group of cultivable strains to represent those found in the wild, synthetic communities are one solution to this problem. title: Hypoxic preconditioning promotes recipient monocyte adaptation to improve heart transplant outcomes
abstract: Acute heart allograft rejection remains a major barrier to long-term transplant survival, yet the mechanisms by which environmental factors influence recipient alloimmunity remain poorly understood. abstract: Animals and robots encounter mud at the water-land interface. Like sand, mud can stay solid or flow like a fluid. title: Water, power and progress: development of large dams in Chile
abstract: Large dams have resurged in recent decades both to meet growing energy demand and to mitigate climate change effects. Historically, they have been associated with the exercise of State power, nation-building, and territorial control. In Chile, where water access and control are shaped by market mechanisms, the study of large dams requires an approach that accounts for their inherently political nature. abstract: How early life exploration shapes the adult annual routines of migratory animals remains challenging to study, especially in long-lived species. abstract: The distribution pattern and agglomeration characteristics of traditional villages play a crucial role as historical and cultural assets in rural development, emphasizing the significance of regional cultural preservation and rural revitalization. This study examines 362 national traditional villages in the Qiantang River Basin (QRB) in Zhejiang to uncover their spatial settlement patterns and analyze the influencing factors. abstract: Abstract Variations in solar radius (hereafter R ⊙ ) is a key reference for solar magnetic activity over time. abstract: Montane elevational gradients provide natural laboratories for investigating how environmental heterogeneity, geographic isolation, and historical climatic dynamics shape demographic history, population divergence, and diversification. Topographic complexity and historical climatic oscillations are major drivers of biodiversity patterns in mountain regions worldwide. abstract: Abstract The composition and evolution of Earth's earliest crust provide critical constraints on how continents grew and when modern geodynamics emerged. Lead isotopes provide a time-resolved record of planetary differentiation and unlike commonly used systems such as Lu–Hf, are particularly sensitive to fractionation within the crust, offering a powerful complementary perspective on early Earth crustal evolution. title: Securing Nigeria’s oil pipelines: delegation and hybrid security governance
abstract: How does delegating oil infrastructure security to politically embedded non-state actors (re)shape the political relations through which oil is governed? This article addresses this question by examining the case of pipeline surveillance contracts awarded by the Nigerian government to former militant leaders in the Niger Delta. title: Elevation-associated variation in bumble bee venom composition is not retained under common-garden conditions
abstract: Bumble bees (Bombus) are vital pollinators across diverse habitats. Female bumble bees have a defensive, venomous sting used against predators. Little is known about the factors associated with intraspecific variation in bumble bee venom. We studied the venom composition of wild-caught Bombus vosnesenskii and tested for elevation-associated differences along an elevation gradient in Oregon, USA. abstract: ABSTRACT Slippery liquid‐infused porous surfaces (SLIPS) have gained great attention as antifouling materials due to their outstanding properties, such as self‐repairing, self‐cleaning, and broad liquid‐ and microbe repellency. This material class relies on a nano‐ or microporous scaffold infused with an interlocked lubricating liquid. title: Assessing a population of stocked muskellunge (Esox masquinongy) using photo-identification and online angler-submitted data
abstract: The current methods used to assess recreational fish stocks require substantial time and monetary investment. Constraints become more prevalent in large management zones with numerous waterbodies. The popularity of online angling platforms presents an opportunity for fisheries managers to enhance monitoring effort beyond the scope of what can be achieved in a costly, limited field season. abstract: ABSTRACT Air is receiving increasing recognition as a biologically rich source of taxonomically diverse environmental DNA (eDNA). Multiple proof‐of‐concept studies have explored air as a medium for the detection of single terrestrial species and even entire terrestrial communities, including mammals, non‐anemophilous plants, and arthropods. title: Plant species' distribution patterns, functional traits, and range shifts along an elevation gradient
abstract: Knowledge about species' distributions is essential for understanding biodiversity patterns and predicting responses to climate change. The shapes of species' density distributions reflect how their performance varies across their range – shaped by environment, biotic interactions, and dispersal. Because these distributions reflect emergent properties of populations, they may reveal deterministic processes underlying species' past and future ranges and range shifts. title: Beyond biomass yield: A conversion-aware framework for climate-resilient feedstocks and sustainable biofuel production
abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens biofuel feedstocks through drought, salinity, temperature extremes, flooding and interacting stressors. However, feedstock resilience is commonly assessed from biomass survival or yield, with limited consideration of how stress-induced changes in biomass quality affect downstream conversion and sustainability. title: Reclassifying the rural: A critical review of European rural typologies through a socio-relational and justice lens
abstract: Rural territories have moved to the centre of European policy agendas, tasked with supporting ecological, digital, demographic, and energy transitions. Yet the classificatory frameworks used to define and differentiate rural areas remain largely anchored in structural-functional logics centred on density, settlement morphology, and relations with urban systems. This paper critically reinterprets European rural typologies through a relational and spatial justice lens. title: The missing piece to nutrient management in lakes: Animal‐mediated nutrient cycling
abstract: Abstract Nutrient cycling in freshwater ecosystems is an essential ecosystem service, partly facilitated by animals through transport and release of bioavailable nutrients needed for sustaining primary production. To date, the importance of animal‐mediated nutrient cycling remains poorly understood in lakes. Additionally, the contribution of animals to a lake's nutrient pools is rarely explicitly accounted for in nutrient budgets. abstract: Landslides are among the most significant natural hazards worldwide, causing extensive financial and human losses and destroying natural resources annually. abstract: Despite its high protein content, hempseed cake remains an underutilized byproduct of the oil industry due to the limited bioaccessibility of its bioactive components. This study examined whether solid-state fermentation (SSF) could enhance the generation of bioaccessible peptides and related bioactivities from hempseed cake after gastrointestinal digestion. abstract: Veii was an emerging urban center in Tyrrhenian Central Italy, playing a crucial role in the development of the Etruscan society at the beginning of the first millennium BCE. Strategically situated close to the Tiber River, Veii controlled extensive trade networks and prospered through economic and cultural exchanges with Italic and Mediterranean groups. abstract: In this study, we determined the complete mitochondrial genome of Rhopalaea crassa (Herdman Citation1880), a solitary ascidian belonging to the family Diazonidae. The mitochondrial genome of R. crassa is 15,413 bp in length, containing 13 protein-coding genes, 24 transfer RNA genes, and two ribosomal RNA genes. abstract: ABSTRACT Dielectric elastomers (DEs) are promising candidates for soft robots to achieve efficient electromechanical conversion and lightweight integration. abstract: Energy devolution in Kenya has progressed unevenly, with many counties yet to complete their County Energy Plans (CEPs), posing challenges for integration into the forthcoming Integrated National Energy Plan (INEP). A key gap lies in translating qualitative, needs-based insights from county planning documents into quantitative inputs for energy demand modelling. abstract: Winter snowpack loss exposes fine roots to freeze-thaw cycles at high latitudes and elevations, but the mechanisms of injury and reasons for species differences in vulnerability are not well understood. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper reports elemental analysis results of 51 glass beads from Peki, an inland transatlantic trade node in southeastern Ghana. abstract: Fertilisers are essential for increasing agricultural output and ensuring food security. In India, fertiliser consumption has increased substantially to 32.93 million tonnes by 2025 and the imbalanced and excessive use of fertilisers has led to declining soil fertility and reduced fertiliser use efficiency (FUE). abstract: El estudio aborda la discrepancia entre superficies planimétricas y topográficas en San Andrés Tuxtla, Veracruz, subrayando sus implicaciones fiscales, jurídicas y ambientales. abstract: Ancestral adaptive variation is thought to play an important role in facilitating adaptation to insular environments. However, to properly evaluate its role, we need to determine the age of genetic variation. In this study, we investigate the Iago sparrow (Passer iagoensis), a generalist endemic to the Cabo Verde archipelago, to understand how genetic diversity is maintained in an island lineage where populations are likely ephemeral and adaptation to environmental extremes is ongoing. abstract: Abstract Archaeologists investigating large, stratified sites face a persistent problem of scale: research questions that demand diachronic, site-wide understanding are constrained by the cost, logistics, and ethics of extensive excavation. title: Investigating the impact of slash and burn (jhum) cultivation on sediment-discharge-nutrient dynamics in high-rainfall tropical hilly catchments
abstract: Slash and burn, also known as jhum cultivation, is the oldest agricultural practice in South and Southeast Asia. This study investigated the impact of jhum cultivation on catchment-scale processes, such as streamflow, sediment, and nutrient dynamics. Three experimental catchments, out of which two are under jhum cultivation (JH01 and JH02) and one forested (KF) catchment, in the Mizoram district, India, were identified. abstract: ABSTRACT For wintering and migrating birds, contamination from oil and other substances may delay arrival on the breeding grounds and lead to lower body mass upon arrival. These delays and losses of body mass could lead to smaller clutch sizes and lower propensity to renest. abstract: Polynomial transformation is a classic mathematical tool in geodesy, used to convert coordinates between different reference systems. It is mainly used in cases where the exact geometric or physical model of the relationship between the systems is unknown, as well as in the presence of significant local deformations in the source data. abstract: Retaining wall sheet pile is a vertical structure used to support soil and prevent erosion or collapse, renowned for its lightweight design, ease of installation, and effectiveness in providing excavation support for applications like water barriers and cofferdams. abstract: Free ammonia poses a threat to aquatic systems already in very low concentrations (<25 µg·L-1) but is currently challenging to continuously monitor at these levels using effortless and compact analytical tools. We evaluated total concentrations and environmental associations of Fe, Mn, Cr, Cu, Ni, Zn, Pb, and As in surface soils from three rice-growing areas of the Yuna River basin, Dominican Republic, with primary emphasis on Arenoso. abstract: Aim: Food is a fundamental human necessity and integral to cultural identity. This study investigates the intention of urban citizens to consume local dairy products in Rasht, Iran. Drawing upon improved planned behavior theory, the study examines the influence of factors such as attitudes towards local dairy products, food heritage, perceptions of food health (good food), willingness to pay, and socio-demographic characteristics on consumer intention. abstract: Introduction: Healthcare systems aim for continuous improvement to ensure excellent clinical outcomes, including optimized quality of life. This relies on accurate data and evaluation patient-centered as well as biomedical outcomes. This data increasingly arises from real-world data (RWD). abstract: ABSTRACT Pangolins are among the world's most trafficked and endangered mammals, yet their exposure to emerging organic contaminants (EOCs) remains largely uncharacterized. abstract: Specialised professional skills are required for sustainable facilities management to achieve operational effectiveness in commercial green buildings. The interest in the development of green buildings in Nigeria is on the increase, but empirical evidence on the competencies required to manage these facilities after occupation is still limited. abstract: Upper Lake, Bhopal, a Ramsar designated wetland and one of the largest natural freshwater lakes in central India, supports rich fish diversity and provides important ecological, economic, and fisheries resources. Accurate identification is expected to make proper conservation of any animal species, yet traditional morphometric methods are challenging and time consuming. title: Emissions Poised to Rocket: Modeling the Environmental Impacts of Low Earth Orbit Satellite Constellations
abstract: Abstract The proliferation of satellite megaconstellations in low Earth orbit represents a significant advancement in global broadband connectivity. However, we urgently need to understand the potential environmental impacts, particularly greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with these constellations. This study addresses a critical gap in modeling current and future GHG emissions by developing an open‐source life cycle assessment methodology, applied to 12 launch vehicles and 24 megaconstellations. title: Hagen-Poiseuille distributed-pressure model of osmotically-driven cytoplasmic flow in severed axons
abstract: Repair (sealing) of traumatic plasmalemmal lesions involves the formation, movement, and accumulation of vesicles at the injury site by active transport and by passive bulk flow of cytoplasm. title: Biases and gaps in freshwater mollusks research in Latin America and the Caribbean: a multi-decadal bibliometric analysis (1976–2024)
abstract: Abstract Freshwater molluscs play key ecological roles in aquatic ecosystems, yet they are among the most threatened and least studied invertebrate groups worldwide. This study evaluates how scientific knowledge on freshwater molluscs is structured across Latin America and the Caribbean, testing the hypothesis that research effort is uneven and shaped by multiple knowledge shortfalls that constrain ecological understanding and conservation planning. abstract: Background: Chronic circadian disruption, such as that experienced during jet lag, is associated with various physiological disturbances, yet its molecular consequences in peripheral tissues like the cochlea remain poorly understood. Methods: We established a chronic jet lag (CJL) mouse model by subjecting C57BL/6J mice to recurrent 8-hour phase advances of the light schedule over four weeks, while control mice were maintained under a regular 12-hour light/dark cycle. abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are bio-based plastics produced by bacterial fermentation from renewable resources. PHAs with unsaturated bonds can undergo post-biosynthetic chemical modification or crosslinking to improve material properties. Previous studies have demonstrated that sulfur-vulcanized PHAs exhibited rubber-like properties and increased toughness. On the other hand, it is also important to add inexpensive fillers, such as calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ), to reduce the amount of expensive resins required. title: More stopovers facilitate migratory waterfowl tracking shifting vegetation green‐up
abstract: Climate change is altering the phenology of food resources, and migratory birds may respond by adjusting migration timing to track shifting food availability (i.e. their phenological sensitivity). The ability to adjust migration timing can vary among species according to traits such as ecological guild, body size and migration distance. Stopover sites are critical components of migration, allowing birds to refuel and acquire updated environmental information. title: Business Resilience as a Mediator between Financial Management Practices and Business Performance among Mompreneurs in Makassar City
abstract: Mompreneurs contribute significantly to local economic development through their participation in micro and small enterprises. Despite their growing economic role, many mompreneurs continue to face challenges in sustaining business performance amid financial limitations and business uncertainties. This study examines the relationship between financial management practices and business performance and investigates the mediating role of business resilience among mompreneurs in Makassar City. title: A single-residue deletion in H9N2 hemagglutinin uncouples viral burden from disease severity
abstract: H9N2 avian influenza viruses are characterized by significant genetic diversity. Deletions within the hemagglutinin (HA) receptor-binding domain represent a notable, albeit rare, evolutionary trajectory. Here, we systematically characterized the multifaceted impact of a single-amino-acid deletion at residue 227 of HA (designated HAΔ227), a naturally occurring deletion within the 220-loop that overlaps a key antigenic epitope, using isogenic reverse genetics H9N2 viruses. title: Foodways of “The Wall People”: unraveling medieval subsistence at the long-wall system in Mongolia through pottery residue analysis
abstract: Abstract This research presents the first comprehensive analysis of medieval pottery (10th–13th centuries CE) from Mongolia, focusing on ceramics unearthed from the Medieval Border Systems. Lipid residue and archaeobotanical analyses revealed the presence of domesticated plants, particularly various types of millets, suggesting that millet was an important dietary component alongside domesticated animals and wild resources through collection, hunting, and fishing. title: Perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands among Chinese enterprise respondents: an exploratory network analysis
abstract: Workforce-needs surveys can conflate broad endorsement, uniform answering and specific relations among knowledge domains. We applied a measurement-aware diagnostic analysis to perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands. In a non-probability online survey, 93 Chinese enterprise respondents rated seven study-specific knowledge domains and selected six generic competencies; no invitation denominator was retained. abstract: Abstract Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport (ESCRT)-III proteins are crucial for membrane remodeling and repair across all domains of life. Eukaryotic ESCRT-III and cyanobacterial homologs such as Phage shock protein A (PspA) and Vipp1/Imm30 remodel membranes into diverse structures, including vesicles, rings, filaments, tubular rods, and multivesicular bodies (MVBs). abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as soil contaminants, yet their time‐dependent associations with dissolved organic matter characteristics, redox behavior, biochemical constituents, and biofilm‐associated responses are often investigated separately. title: Isolation of High‐Purity Rutin and Quercetin From Tartary Buckwheat By‐Products Using HPLC Separation and MS Quality Control
abstract: Tartary buckwheat (Fagopyrum tataricum) is a nutrient-rich cereal abundant in flavonoids, including rutin, with excellent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and other health-promoting properties. Cultivated for its grain-like seed, the vegetative tissues of buckwheat are considered feedstock or agricultural waste. abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Whether different organism groups show similar β‐diversity across space has major implications for biotic interactions. We compared β‐diversity patterns of three kingdoms across the same set of 40 sites, while explicitly accounting for sampling effects. title: Beyond Fragmentation: A Conceptual Taxonomy of Existing Methodologies for a Layered Analysis of Historic Urban Landscape
abstract: Urban analysis of historic cities faces a persistent methodological fragmentation. Existing approaches tend to operate within disciplinary fields, addressing either historical evolution, present spatial configuration, or cultural meaning, but rarely in an integrated manner. abstract: The Japanese spined loach, Cobitis sp. 'yamato' species complex (hereafter Yamato spined loach), is an allotetraploid group originating from two diploid Cobitis species hybridization. abstract: The study examined the relationship between household vulnerability, community adaptation capacities and flood-induced displacement in Asaba, Delta State, Nigeria. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, involving a cross-sectional survey of 400 households selected from high-, moderate-, and low-risk flood-prone neighbourhoods. abstract: The date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) produces enormous quantities of lignocellulosic waste (DPW) - including leaves, stems, fibers, and seeds - which remain largely underutilized in the MENA region. This systematic review provides a comprehensive analysis of scientific literature (296 articles evaluated) on the biochemical conversion of DPW into second-generation bioethanol. abstract: Critical thinking is a fundamental competency that requires systematic cultivation from the elementary school level, including through social studies instruction, which is closely related to students' social lives. This study aims to describe teachers' perceptions of elementary school students' critical thinking skills in social studies instruction. abstract: ABSTRACT China's complex river basins constitute a critical biogeographic setting for investigating genetic differentiation and lineage divergence in freshwater fishes. abstract: Abstract Crops grown on over 40% of arable land are limited by low levels of bioavailable phosphorus (P). abstract: In this paper, we have assessed how climate change might impact hydrology and electricity production in the Drammen River basin. title: Algae as Bio-Cell with Zero Emission Next Generation Energy Source
abstract: Traditional batteries demand a lot of energy to maintain and constantly need recharging. abstract: Abstract Alternaria toxins are naturally occurring food contaminants with limited and often inconsistent genotoxicity and mutagenicity data. abstract: In current low-pressure turbine cascades, around a third of the losses are determined by the complex interaction between endwall boundary layers and blade profiles. abstract: The climate feedback from soil microbial respiration is a critical yet uncertain determinant of global soil carbon cycle and its vulnerability to climate change. Current assessments predominantly rely on responses to mean temperature shifts, largely neglecting the ecological importance of climate variability, particularly short-term temperature fluctuations. title: PEONY: a global reference database of DNA viral (vOTU) sequences from viral size-fractionated metagenomes (viromes)
abstract: We present an update to the Phages and Integrated Genomes Encapsidated or Not reference database of DNA viral sequences (viral operational taxonomic units [vOTUs], mostly dsDNA bacteriophages) from global ecosystems. abstract: Endowing synthetic materials with adaptability and responsiveness to dynamically optimize their states represents a premier frontier in biomimetic science. However, achieving life-like, rapid yet reversible adaptation under benign triggers remains hindered by high reconfiguration energy or delayed structural recovery. abstract: Abstract Io's surface hosts numerous mountains and volcanic paterae generated by processes that occur at depth, including tidal heating and the resultant crustal recycling and subsidence stresses. Global trends in the shape and orientation of surface features could provide insight into these subsurface processes. abstract: ABSTRACT Cobalt (Co) is a required component of cofactors and coenzymes in all life and has a pronounced role in the one carbon metabolism of methanogens. title: Carbon Sequestration Capacity of Sudlon Watershed in Barangay Central, Mati City, Davao Oriental
abstract: The study was conducted to quantify the biomass and carbon storage of the vegetative cover of Sudlon Watershed in Barangay Central, Mati, Davao Oriental. The specific objectives of this study were to determine the total area of the vegetative cover, to determine the vegetative structures, to identify the status of the vegetation, and to provide recommendations in relation to the management of the watershed. abstract: Objectives Multidrug-resistant ( MDR ) Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a significant global health concern due to its high prevalence in nosocomial infections and limited treatment options. Lytic bacteriophages offer a targeted, antibiotic-free strategy to combat these resistant pathogens. This study aimed to isolate and characterize lytic bacteriophages from municipal sewage and evaluate their antibacterial efficacy against MDR P. aeruginosa strains collected from clinical samples. title: Geomorphological mapping of the municipality of Chía, Colombia: methodological contributions and proposed classification
abstract: This article presents the application of a geomorphological mapping methodology developed in Brazil to the municipality of Chía, located in the Colombian Andes. The research relies on the interpretation of geological maps, topographic charts, satellite images, geotechnologies, and fieldwork, enabling geomorphological characterization across various scales of analysis. title: Distributed bioretention under tropical rainfall and tidal backwater: a SWMM-LID assessment for a catchment in Ho Chi Minh City
abstract: Green infrastructure (GI) is widely promoted for urban flood control, yet the performance figures most often quoted come from temperate cities and are a poor guide for tropical, tide-affected deltas. abstract: This study developed a novel grass carp variety, designated improved grass carp (IGC), by crossing gynogenetic grass carp (GGC, 2n = 48) females with gold grass carp ( Ctenopharyngodon idella red var., RGC, 2n = 48) males, aiming to integrate desirable parental traits and generate new hybrid germplasm. abstract: Materials, at their essence, are networks defined by homogeneity: uniform bonds, fixed thicknesses and discrete length scales. abstract: Background: Auguste Comte's thought has fundamentally transformed human perspectives, shifting them from mythos to logos. title: Cell size asymmetry regulates neural stem cell proliferation and lineage expansion in the Drosophila brain
abstract: Asymmetrically dividing invertebrate and vertebrate stem cells can produce unequal sibling cell sizes but the function of cell size asymmetry (CSA) remains underexplored. Here, we use Drosophila neural stem cells (NSCs) to investigate how changes in CSA affect cell fate decisions and neurogenesis. Using live-cell imaging, NSC lineage analysis, and gene expression profiling, we find that altering CSA expands the NSC pool but restricts lineage expansion. title: Predator Becomes Prey: Records of Intraguild Predation Between Velvet Worms (Onychophora) and Arthropods (Arthropoda) With an Expanded Review of Predation on Velvet Worms
abstract: From 3954 citizen-science observations screened, we report novel cases of predation by omnivorous arthropods on velvet worms, including the first confirmed records for harvestmen and a cave wētā. Using photographic evidence derived from citizen-science observations, we document multiple predation events involving harvestmen (Opiliones: Cranaidae and Triaenonychidae) and a cave wētā (Orthoptera: Rhaphidophoridae), encompassing both intraguild predation and higher-order opportunistic predation within cryptic terrestrial habitats. title: Interfacial Electronic Coupling and Surface Reconstruction in Co(OH) 2 @NiFe‐btz for Durable Alkaline Oxygen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Coupling metal hydroxides with coordination frameworks offers a route to active and durable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrodes. abstract: Abstract Fat, oil, and grease (FOG) accumulation in sewer systems is a major environmental and operational challenge, leading to sewer blockages, reduced hydraulic capacity, increased maintenance costs, and the formation of persistent deposits known as fatbergs. These deposits arise from complex physicochemical processes involving the hydrolysis of triglycerides into free fatty acids, followed by their reaction with divalent metal ions, particularly calcium (Ca2+) and magnesium (Mg2+), resulting in insoluble metallic soaps. title: DNA Metabarcoding Reveals Flying Arthropod Diversity and Community Turnover Across Ancient Tea Agroforestry Landscapes in Southwest China
abstract: Ancient tea agroforestry landscapes in Southwest China are structurally complex systems that may support high arthropod diversity, yet their biodiversity value remains poorly documented. We used COI metabarcoding of Malaise-trap bulk samples to assess flying arthropod assemblages at four tea-associated sites in the Mengku Ancient Tea and Cultural System, Yunnan, China: a wild ancient tea tree community, a village-adjacent cultivated ancient tea garden, a forest-adjacent cultivated ancient tea garden, and a young-shrub tea plantation. title: Discovery and characterization of microbial GH18 chitinases exhibiting activity at low temperature from raw chilled prawns
abstract: Endo-chitinases (chitinases, EC 3.2.1.14) catalyze the hydrolytic cleavage of chitin ((1→4)-2-acetamido-2-deoxy-β-D-glucan) and are categorized in glucoside hydrolase (GH) families GH18 and GH19. title: Perceptions of Opisthorchis viverrini infection and raw fish consumption among villagers in Champasak Province, Lao PDR: a qualitative study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Opisthorchis viverrini (O. viverrini) infection is a major public health concern in the Greater Mekong Subregion. Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) has been reported to have a remarkably higher prevalence. This study aimed to explore local perceptions and practices related to O. viverrini infection and raw fish consumption. We conducted a qualitative study on O. viverrini infection in villages in Champasak Province, Lao PDR. title: Co-culture of Acetobacter pasteurianus and Lactobacillus plantarum enhances biofilm formation and improves vinegar characteristics
abstract: Abstract Acetic acid bacteria and lactic acid bacteria are core microbial components in traditional Chinese vinegar brewing, where biofilm-associated microflora form unique and stress-resilient consortia. This study explored bacterial adaptive responses and biofilm development in bicultures of Acetobacter pasteurianus with individual Lactobacillus strains. Across all bi-cultures, A. pasteurianus exhibited a competitive dominance over Lactobacillus strains. abstract: Pengelolaan pengadaan dan persediaan barang yang efektif menjadi faktor penting dalam menunjang kelancaran operasional usaha. abstract: Aim: The study aimed to identifying optimal stocking densities and transport durations of Pearlspot (Etroplus suratensis) of varying sizes (1–3 inches) in closed, oxygenated systems. Methodology: Pearlspot fry and fingerlings were transported for 6, 12, 18, and 24 hr in 30 l polythene bags containing 5 l of oxygenated 15 ppt brackishwater. abstract: Abstract The massive accumulation of debris following the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes necessitates sustainable resource recovery strategies for resilient infrastructure reconstruction. This study establishes a multi-criteria decision-making framework to evaluate the Overall Material Sustainability (OMS) of pavement base layers incorporating earthquake-induced Recycled Concrete Aggregates (RCA) at varying replacement ratios (0% to 100%). title: Influence of extender type, freezing temperature, and sperm concentration on the cryosurvival of Santa Inês ram spermatozoa
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of three extenders (Tris, HEPES, and skim milk), three freezing temperatures (-79, -90, and − 120 °C), and three final sperm concentrations (600, 800, and 1000 × 10⁶ spermatozoa/mL) on the post-thaw quality of Santa Inês ram semen. title: Digital Reforms in The Public Distribution System and Policy Outcomes: An Assessment of Cooperative-Run Fair Price Shops in Tamil Nadu
abstract: The Public Distribution System (PDS) has progressively moved from a predominantly manual welfare-distribution arrangement towards a digitally enabled governance system. In Tamil Nadu, this transformation has been supported by electronic Point of Sale (e-POS) devices, Smart Family Cards, Aadhaar-linked authentication, online transaction recording, digital stock monitoring and other technology-enabled administrative mechanisms. title: Interfacial Electronic Regulation in N-Doped Carbon-Encapsulated NiCo Alloy Enables High-Current Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO 3 − RR) offers a route to couple wastewater remediation with green ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis, but remains kinetically and mechanistically challenging under high-current-density operation. title: Marketplace Diplomacy: The Political Economy of US–Soviet Sister‐City Relations, 1971–1991
abstract: Abstract This article situates US–USSR sister‐city initiatives within the history of Cold War trade and exchange, arguing that municipal twinning functioned not only as citizen diplomacy but also as a semi‐official mechanism for facilitating economic cooperation across ideological boundaries. Drawing on Soviet and American archival sources and periodicals, it demonstrates that Soviet cultural and diplomatic institutions actively courted US corporations, private donors, and municipal actors, challenging assumptions that exchange initiatives were primarily American‐driven. title: Whole Wheat Biscuits Fortified With Softened Whole Harpiosquillid Mantis Shrimp Powder: Characteristics, Nutritional Enhancement, and Acceptability
abstract: ABSTRACT Fortification of whole wheat biscuits with softened whole Harpiosquillid mantis shrimp (HMS) powder at different levels (5%, 10%, 15%, and 20%) was carried out. Physiochemical, amino acid, elemental composition, textural property, and consumer acceptance were determined. Rheology of dough and microstructure of biscuits were also examined. HMS powder fortification increased total protein, fats, ash, calcium, and magnesium contents, while reducing carbohydrate in comparison with the control biscuits. title: Direct high‐temperature intervention restructures fermented freshwater surimi gels: time‐dependent remodeling and aggregation in an acidified myofibrillar protein model
abstract: BACKGROUND: The mode of heat treatment can either promote protein gel network formation or cause network destabilization in acidified fermented surimi, but the underlying process-structure-function relationship remains unclear. We hypothesized that direct high-temperature intervention (DHTI) at 90 °C would favor gel restructuring by coupling suppression of cathepsin L (CTSL) activity with protein crosslinking, whereas prolonged high-temperature exposure would eventually cause excessive aggregation and functional decline. title: Reading a low-visibility record in the central Apennines: first results from the Archaeological Landscape Survey at Rascino Plateau, Italy
abstract: Mediterranean uplands often appear archaeologically poor, yet their surface record is shaped by geomorphic and post-depositional processes that vary over short distances. The 2025 Archaeological Landscape Survey at Rascino Plateau (ALSRaP) in Italy combines non-site survey and geoarchaeology to reconstruct the formation, preservation and visibility of the archaeological record in mountain landscapes.

title: Assessment of APTI and dust accumulation potential of urban trees for sustainable cities and societies
abstract: Abstract Air pollution is a serious global threat that adversely affects both human and plant health. Once pollutants enter the environment, plants serve as natural filters, capable of absorbing, accumulating, and detoxifying them in various forms. The urban trees play a significant role in mitigating air pollution by capturing and dispersing dust. A present study was conducted to assess the dust accumulation potential on the foliar surfaces of plants and its effects on their tolerance towards pollution ( i.e. , APTI). title: ASSESSING THE IMPACTS OF LAND USE/ LAND COVER CHANGES ON LAND SURFACE TEMPERATURE IN JOS NORTH AND SOUTH LGAS, PLATEAU STATE, NIGERIA.

title: Logistics and product quality in perishable food trade
abstract: Growth in trade of perishable foods has significantly increased global access to fresh foods, but important trade-offs arising from perishability are not captured in standard trade models. In this paper, we develop a model of age-related product freshness that places importer logistics choices at the center of the analysis. The model highlights order size and order frequency as key trade margins, alongside the nonlinear pricing that arises from scale economies in trade. title: Driver-specific temporal shifts in post-fire vegetation recovery: a multi-year Landsat-based analysis of the 2022 Uljin forest fire, South Korea
abstract: How the relative importance of environmental factors shifts during post-fire vegetation recovery remains underexplored in temperate forests with complex terrain and mixed-species canopies. title: Transmission epidemiology and spatial characteristics of 1305 Chikungunya cases in Guangzhou, China from July to November 2025
abstract: From July to November 2025, Guangzhou, the capital city of Guangdong Province of China, went through a large-scale Chikungunya outbreak that 1305 cases were reported to Guangzhou Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Guangzhou Health Supervision Institute) by November 11. The epidemic presented two waves and was influenced by the public health control measures, population mobility and climate change. abstract: The article takes 267 traditional villages in the Tibetan-Yi Corridor region as the research object, the spatio-temporal differentiation and influencing factors of the traditional villages in the Tibetan-Yi Corridor were analysed with the help of ArcGIS software. title: Intensification of intraguild interactions between top predators in a climate change impacted environment: a new potential evolutionary pathway
abstract: Adaptations of coexisting species to climate‐driven environmental changes might not necessarily lead to extinctions, but rather to trait variations that generate new competitive hierarchies in ecosystems. Top predators have a pivotal role in ecosystems, but long‐term effects in changing environments have not been sufficiently explored. We used long‐term data on the territory (n = 65 survey points) and breeding (n = 69 nest‐boxes) dynamics of two coexisting, ecologically similar and closely related forest raptors, the warm‐tolerant tawny owl Strix aluco and the cold‐tolerant Ural owl S. uralens

title: PROCUREMENT AND SUPPLY CHAIN OPTIMIZATION IN SAUDI OIL & GAS MEGAPROJECTS
abstract: Saudi oil and gas megaprojects depend on globally distributed engineering,fabrication, transport and construction networks. Their performance is often constrained less by isolated purchasing decisions than by misalignment among design maturity, contracting schedules, supplier capacity, shipping, site readiness and project controls. This review examines procurement and supply chain optimization through an integrated project-delivery perspective relevant to Saudi Arabia under Vision 2030. title: Design of the “SI AKA” Domestic Wastewater Treatment System Based on Wastewater Characteristics and Flow Rate
abstract: This research sets out to profile the domestic wastewater produced at the study site, quantify the discharge generated by the surrounding community, and develop an appropriate Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP), named Si Aka, that fits actual field conditions while meeting the applicable regulatory standards. The assessment covers physical, chemical, and biological parameters that together define the pollution level and the resulting treatment burden. abstract: Abstract Long-term monitoring of actual evapotranspiration (ETa) is critical for assessing land–atmosphere water dynamics, yet optimizing monitoring networks requires a deeper understanding of spatial synchronization and predictive dependencies in water-limited environments. Utilizing GLEAM v4 satellite-derived data (1980–2023), we propose an integrated trend–topology–directionality framework to assess ETa variability across Iran. title: Emulate the Leader? Explaining Crisis Policy Change in the Canadian Federal System
abstract: ABSTRACT In times of crises, do governments coordinate or do they make their own choices independent of what others do? Convergence of COVID‐19 policy at the beginning of the pandemic has been widely studied in federal countries. Yet, there is limited literature looking at the mechanisms that made policy between jurisdictions so similar. title: Electrochemical Capture and Accumulation of Uranium Using a Layered Uvanite Electrode
abstract: Abstract Extracting uranyl ions (UO22+) from uranium mining leachates can enhance national uranium security and mitigate the environmental impact of nuclear energy. Conventional techniques such as ion exchange and iron-based reductive precipitation have notable limitations. This study reports that the uvanite (U2V6O21) electrode, a layered uranium-vanadium oxide, enables potentiodynamic decoupling of UO22+ and proton intercalation/deintercalation, as well as proton-induced UO22+/UO3 precipitation and dissolution reactions. title: Exceptional preservation reveals the deep-time reproductive ecology and trophic breadth of Early Cretaceous viviparid gastropods
abstract: Direct empirical evidence regarding the reproductive biology and trophic strategies of ancient freshwater invertebrates remains scarce due to the typical loss of internal anatomical and dietary records. Here, we report an exceptionally preserved assemblage of the freshwater snail 'Viviparus' sp. from the Lower Cretaceous (c. 120 Ma) Kitadani Formation, central Japan. title: Generalizing the LoD transition space for continuous multi-scale representation using straight skeletons
abstract: Continuous multi-scale representation enables geographic features to evolve smoothly across Levels of Detail, avoiding abrupt transitions between independently generalized datasets. However, existing approaches provide limited support for complex transformations involving different geometric and topological configurations. abstract: Shore power replaces onboard auxiliary-engine generation with grid electricity at berth. Most assessments report its full-deployment potential, in which every port and vessel is equipped and every call uses the connection, rather than the reduction realizable with the vessels, ports, and grids now in place. This study aims to quantify the realizable carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) reduction from shore power in global container shipping and identify the constraints and interactions that limit its realization. title: Optimizing chlorine management in garlic to improve nitrogen use efficiency and agronomic performance
abstract: Chloride (Cl − ) depletion has emerged as a potential constraint in intensive garlic production, where chlorine (Cl)-containing fertilizers are rarely applied. We evaluated the agronomic, nutritional, economic, and environmental effects of Cl fertilization using a two-year field experiment with six Cl application rates (0–300 kg ha −1 ) in a major garlic-producing region of China. Chloride accumulated predominantly in stems and leaves and promoted nutrient accumulation, photosynthetic performance, bulb development, and nutritional quality. abstract: Daerah Aliran Sungai (DAS) Air Dingin, khususnya di Kelurahan Lubuk Minturun, Kota Padang, mengalami tekanan lingkungan akibat perubahan tutupan lahan, pertumbuhan permukiman, dan aktivitas masyarakat yang tidak sepenuhnya memperhatikan daya dukung lingkungan. title: Criminalizing ecocide beyond the Rome Statute: Comparative domestic approaches and lessons for environmental accountability in Bangladesh
abstract: Ecocide is an emerging concept in contemporary international environmental law and international criminal law jurisprudence. It has not yet been recognized as an independent international crime under the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. However, the increasing scholarly discourse and domestic legislative initiatives have intensified discussions regarding criminal responsibility for severe environmental harm. title: Gadolinium as an Emerging Contaminant: Environmental Cycling, Human and Plant Interactions, and Mitigation Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT Gadolinium (Gd) is a rare earth element whose anthropogenic cycle has expanded rapidly, driven primarily by the widespread medical use of gadolinium‐based contrast agents (GBCAs) in magnetic resonance imaging, alongside its use in selected electronic and energy‐related technologies. title: Comparative analysis of barriers and opportunities for implementation of blue-green infrastructure for enhancing urban flood resilience in Uganda, Rwanda, and Sweden
abstract: Recent studies have identified a combination of socio-economic, institutional, governance and financing barriers that constrain the adoption of Blue-Green Infrastructure (BGI) for enhancing urban flood resilience and provision of multiple benefits in cities. However, most barrier analysis studies have used literature reviews, semi-structured interviews, or questionnaire surveys in case studies in the Global North; in contrast, there is limited research and uptake of BGI in flood prone cities in Sub-Saharan Africa. title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002
abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. title: Maternal genetic diversity and population structure of four mandarin fish ( Siniperca chuatsi ) populations inferred from mitochondrial D-loop sequences
abstract: Mandarin fish ( Siniperca chuatsi ) is an economically important freshwater aquaculture species in China, yet the maternal genetic composition of cultured stocks from different regions remains insufficiently characterized. To assess maternal genetic diversity and population structure, 120 individuals were sampled from one wild-origin population from Huzhou, Zhejiang Province (ZJHZ), and three cultured populations from Chizhou, Anhui Province (AHCZ), Wuhan, Hubei Province (HBWH), and Jiangmen, Guangdong Province (GDJM). title: Occupational Risk and Students’ Perceptions of Solid Waste Handling at the South Campus of the University of Education, Winneba
abstract: Solid-waste handling in university settings may expose sanitation workers to occupational hazards while leaving the nature of their work largely outside students’ awareness. This study explored sanitation workers’ accounts of occupational hazards and students’ perceptions of waste handling at the South Campus of the University of Education, Winneba, Ghana. abstract: Similarity of body-plan features across distant phyla provides striking testimony to the Darwinian concept of common descent throughout Metazoa. In both the cnidarian Nematostella and chordates, gastrula organizers direct the initial establishment of embryonic axes. abstract: Gamta village is predominately populated by Muslims, while Magei village is predominately populated by Protestant Christians. The strong sense of brotherhood that existed between the two villages, however, led to a number of joint activities. The fact that the crops grown by the Magei villagers must first be tasted by their relatives in Gamta village is one of the brotherhood’s peculiar customs. abstract: The fate of organic carbon at convergent margins depends in part on its transformation into relatively inert graphite, yet the influence of precursor composition remains poorly constrained. Here we show that two organic precursors, vitrinite and liptinite, follow distinct graphitization pathways under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. title: Dormancy stabilizes structured food webs
abstract: Theory predicts that strong species interactions drive instability in large ecosystems, but strong interactions are common in nature while strong instability appears rare. This discrepancy motivates enduring interest in ecological mechanisms that limit or counteract instability. Dormancy-reversible metabolic suppression-may be one. Dormancy is a ubiquitous life history trait found in organisms ranging from bacteria to trees. abstract: Abstract Raising groundwater levels in drained peatlands used for dairy farming aims to reduce peat decomposition, land subsidence and associated carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. title: Spatial and Seasonal Assessment of Physicochemical Water Quality in the Lower Tapi River
abstract: Deteriorating of river water quality has become an important environmental challenge in India, particularly where river system is relied upon for drinking water supply. The Tapi river serves as major water resources for Surat. The study evaluates the seasonal variation and quality of water status of Tapi river in Gujarat, India, using the Weighted Arithmetic Water Quality Index (WAWQI) method. This study presents a yearlong assessment (Dec. 2024 to Nov. 2025) of seasonal and spatial variations in water quality at five selected sites: Galteshwar, Kamrej, Utran, Causeway and ONGC Bridge. title: A distinct class of conjugative megaplasmids is associated with prophages in distantly related bacterial lineages
abstract: Closely related prophages have been found in phylogenetically distant bacteria in the human gut, despite limited evidence of productive phage infections across broad host ranges. It remains enigmatic how the wide distribution of prophages could emerge. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized association between a distinct group of conjugative megaplasmids and prophage genomes. title: Incidence of and household responses to paediatric diarrhoeal disease and acute respiratory infection in Chitwan, Nepal: protocol for a prospective cohort study
abstract: Introduction Diarrhoeal diseases and acute respiratory infections (ARIs) disproportionately affect young children and families facing disadvantages at the individual, household and neighbourhood level. This unequal burden especially impacts children in low- and middle-income countries, such as Nepal. Data limitations impede the ability to understand children’s illness episodes and treatment trajectories across the course of early childhood and their relationship to household-level and neighbourhood-level social determinants of health. title: Who Really Buys? DMU Discovery and Market Entry Strategy in B2B Geospatial Services
abstract: This study examines how a geospatial survey startup in Indonesia discovered and corrected a pre-entry buyer assumption. In-depth interviews with eight participants, two internal company representatives and six from three candidate markets, were analyzed through the Gioia methodology. The research finds that architects are structurally excluded from geospatial survey purchasing decisions in design-and-build construction projects. title: Redirecting gypsum scaling in pervaporation desalination via activated alumina granules
abstract: Membrane scaling, particularly CaSO4 (gypsum) crystallisation, severely limits the practical application of pervaporation (PV) desalination for high-salinity wastewater treatment. Herein, an online interception strategy using nitric acid-activated alumina granules (AAG) is proposed to redirect gypsum scaling from the membrane surface to a sacrificial medium. By tuning nitric acid activation, the physicochemical properties of AAG were optimised. title: Is Indigenous Knowledge meaningfully represented in the IPCC AR6? A bibliometric meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract In recent global climatic and environmental reports, Indigenous Knowledges (IK) are recognised as essential to comprehending social-ecological systems and multi-scalar climate-society relationships. However, IK and Indigenous Peoples (IP) continue to be mostly excluded from important and powerful processes such as the UNFCCC and the IPCC reports. In the current (AR7) cycle of the IPCC, it is important to understand whether the last cycle (AR6) meaningfully engaged with IK and IP. title: Effects of Place Attachment on Flood Risk Management in Kogi Local Government Area, Kogi State, Nigeria
abstract: Place attachment is the emotional, cultural, and socio-economic bond between people and their environment is a critical but underexplored factor in flood risk management. This study examined its effects on flood risk management in Kogi Local Government Area, Nigeria, focusing on six communities. A descriptive survey with 400 respondents (Yamane formula, population 287,450) was employed. Findings revealed that place attachment significantly influences flood risk perception (M=3.25, SD=0.72), with ancestral ties being the strongest dimension (M=3.40, SD=0.68). title: Hematological profile, morphology, and morphometry of blood cells from healthy free-ranging neotropical Paraguayan hairy dwarf porcupines (Coendou spinosus) from the State of São Paulo, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Hematologic analysis is a fundamental tool for screening, diagnosing, treating, and monitoring animal diseases, and it requires constant multidisciplinary collaboration to expand knowledge for exotic and free-ranging animals worldwide. The study aimed to determine the hematological parameters, morphology, and morphometry of blood cells from the wild Paraguayan hairy dwarf porcupine ( Coendou spinosus ), a medium-sized rodent relatively common in Southeastern Brazil, extending to Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay. title: What shapes urban planning trade-offs of NBS in compact city agendas: A case study of the Catharijnesingel restoration in Utrecht, the Netherlands
abstract: The current research examines the intersection of urban nature-based solutions (NBS) and the compact city model, interrogating how processes of the compact city influence the manifestation of NBS-related trade-offs across the urban planning cycle. We conceptualise and operationalise a synthesis between the types of urban NBS trade-offs, processes of compact urbanism and environmental justice dimensions. title: USP22 Facilitates Cervical Cancer Progression via Deubiquitinating and Stabilizing IRAK1 to Activate NF ‐ κB Signaling
abstract: Cervical cancer remains one of the most commonly diagnosed malignancies among women worldwide. Although USP22 is known to be involved in tumor progression, its specific function in cervical cancer remains unclear. This study explored the biological significance of USP22 and the mechanism by which it regulates cervical cancer progression. Through bioinformatic analysis, we identified that USP22 expression was significantly upregulated in cervical cancer tissues and was associated with proliferative potential. title: Biofilm selection activates c-di-GMP synthesis by the bifunctional enzyme MbaA
abstract: Abstract Biofilms, in which microbes are encased within a self-produced matrix, represent the primary mode of microbial life. Yet, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing biofilm formation remains incomplete, limiting the development of targeted interventions against biofilm-associated infections. By selecting for Vibrio cholerae biofilms, we identified mutations in the polyamine-regulated, bifunctional enzyme MbaA that alter its enzymatic activity in metabolizing the conserved second messenger cyclic diguanylate (c-di-GMP). title: Genetic variability within Triatoma sanguisuga complex in North America and the re-description of Triatoma ambigua Neiva, 1911, with specimens from Florida, USA
abstract: Triatoma sanguisuga is the most widely distributed triatomine vector in North America, occurring in at least 23 U.S. states and capable of transmitting Trypanosoma cruzi to humans. Historical morphological variability led to the description of several subspecies, but their taxonomic validity has remained unresolved. We integrated molecular (cytochrome b, n = 58; ITS-2, n = 23) and morphometric (18 characters, n = 82 specimens) data to reassess species boundaries within T. sanguisuga sensu lato. title: Simulating an imaging atmospheric radio telescope to observe cosmic gamma rays and cosmic neutrinos
abstract: Observations of cosmic gamma rays with energies above the 10 12 electronvolts (TeV) regime are often a direct probe of events where our theoretical predictions are challenged by extreme conditions. Because high energetic cosmic gamma rays are rare, one needs collection areas with the size of roughly a dozen football fields (10 5 m 2 ) or more to gather significant counting statistics in a short time. abstract: Background The Secondary Care Medicines Data (SCMD) makes detailed data on medicines issued by National Health Service (NHS) hospital trusts in England openly available for the first time. These data provide an opportunity to understand medicine use patterns, highlight variation, and drive improvements in evidence-based practice, prescribing safety, and cost-effectiveness. However, this dataset requires extensive domain and technical knowledge to access, clean, transform, and link to other external sources before it can be used effectively. title: Limited effect of basalt amendment and mycorrhizal inoculation on soil chemical properties and maize growth on a nutrient-rich soil
abstract: Enhanced weathering (EW) of silicate minerals has emerged as a promising carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategy, with potential benefits for soil fertility and crop performance. However, the soil processes that determine these co-benefits remain poorly explained. In particular, interactions between basalt amendments and soil biota such as arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) may influence nutrient mobilization and plant uptake, but these effects have rarely been quantified. title: Reindeer habitat selection and movement change with cumulative impacts from mining and wind power development
abstract: Industrial expansion often occurs in landscapes already affected by multiple disturbances, resulting in cumulative impacts on biodiversity and local communities. Although societal pressure for a rapid ‘green transition’ accelerates land-use change, most impact assessments remain local and project-based and are therefore unable to adequately address cumulative impacts. We conceptualized and disentangled key dimensions of cumulative impacts and integrated them within habitat selection, calving site selection, and movement analyses in a case study of reindeer and Sámi reindeer husbandry in Scandi

title: Metabolomic and transcriptomic characterization of Actinokineospora bangkokensis 44EHWT: enhancing anti-anthracnose production through N-acetylglucosamine supplementation
abstract: N -acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) serves as a key carbon source and regulatory signal for secondary metabolism in actinomycetes, yet its role in Actinokineospora remains poorly understood. Here, genome mining, transcriptomics, and untargeted metabolomics were integrated to investigate GlcNAc-supplemented Actinokineospora bangkokensis 44EHWT. title: Assessing Urban Growth Patterns of Agroha Town of Hisar, Haryana Using Directional and Geostatistical Approaches
abstract: This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics, direction and intensity of urban expansion in Agroha Town, a historically significant and rapidly urbanizing peri-urban center in the Hisar district of Western Haryana, India. Employing multi-temporal high-resolution satellite imagery from Google Earth (2015 and 2024), administrative boundary data from the Bhuvan platform and spatial benchmarks from the Town and Country Planning (TCP) Haryana Agroha Draft Development Plan 2031, land use and land cover (LULC) transformations across a 15.10 sq. km municipal boundary were systematically quantif

title: Isoprenoid quinone profiling using a novel semi-quantitative HPLC-MS/MS method: application to wastewater sludges
abstract: Isoprenoid quinones are ubiquitous redox lipids that mediate electron transfer in various cellular processes across all domains of life. These molecules also serve as taxonomic and metabolic markers, facilitating the characterisation of microbial communities. However, their structural diversity and extreme hydrophobicity are challenging for comprehensive detection and quantification in complex biological matrices. title: Climate‐driven compositional shifts across a temperate–subtropical island ecotone
abstract: Climate change is expected to drive substantial shifts in species distributions, yet ecological responses are often delayed under disequilibrium dynamics, limiting the effectiveness of range‐based indicators for detecting ongoing change. Compositional approaches have been proposed as an alternative; however, conventional comparisons based on gradient shape or pointwise differences may fail to detect change when the overall gradient structure is conserved, because small and spatially heterogeneous differences cancel out across the gradient. title: Freeze-drying-induced structural enhancement of graphene quantum dot–modified carboxymethyl cellulose beads for highly efficient cypermethrin removal
abstract: The influence of drying procedures on the pore structure and adsorption performance of graphene quantum dot-modified carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC/GQD) beads for cypermethrin removal has not been sufficiently elucidated. Therefore, hydrogel and cryogel forms of CMC/GQD beads were comparatively evaluated to clarify the effect of oven-drying and freeze-drying on cypermethrin adsorption from aqueous media. title: Statistical and Perceived Ethnic Diversity in Urban Activity Spaces: Evidence from Auckland, New Zealand
abstract: The study of segregation in activity spaces has received renewed attention, fueled by the increasing availability of mobility data from mobile phones and social media. These new data sources enable high-resolution analysis of how people move through cities and interact across diverse neighborhoods. A key goal of this work is to inform the design of inclusive spaces that foster intergroup contact, which is presumed to enhance social cohesion. title: Evaluation of soil fertility status of Shivpur village in Pathalgaon block of Jashpur district, Chhattisgarh
abstract: The present study entitled “Evaluation of soil fertility status of Shivpur village in Pathalgaon block of Jashpur district, Chhattisgarh” was conducted during 2025–26 at the Department of Soil Science, College of Agriculture, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur. The study aimed to assess soil fertility status, nutrient variability, nutrient index values and soil-test-based fertilizer recommendations. title: Performance of AC systems under future climates and heatwaves: From degradation to temperature regime optimization and dehumidification control
abstract: Rising outdoor temperatures and the increasing frequency of heatwaves raise pressing challenges to the resilience of building cooling systems, particularly in tropical regions where cooling demand is continuous, and dehumidification is essential. This study investigates the impact of future climate scenarios, including typical meteorological years and heatwave years provided by the International Energy Agency’s Annex 80, on the seasonal performance of conventional vapor-compression cooling systems: unitary systems, represented by split units. title: Genetic structure, inbreeding and effective population size in an endangered island cockatoo, following management-led recovery
abstract: Abstract Island populations are particularly vulnerable to genetic risk. The glossy black-cockatoo Calyptorhynchus lathami halmaturinus has been restricted to Kangaroo Island, South Australia, since the mid-20th century and had declined to a few hundred individuals before management-led recovery. To understand how this population bottleneck might have affected population structure, genetic diversity and inbreeding, we analyzed single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), principally generated from feather samples collected from nestlings during two breeding seasons.
