title: A Multi‐Stage Framework for Diagnosing Structural Redundancy Between Selected Functional Diversity Metrics: Empirical Applications Under an A Priori Expectation of Overlap
abstract: Functional diversity (FD) is widely used to study ecosystem processes, leading to the continuous development of FD metrics. However, the proliferation of these descriptors raises concerns regarding structural redundancy, particularly in ecological modelling, where the simultaneous use of highly concordant FD metrics may compromise model parsimony.We propose a multi-stage approach to diagnose structural redundancy among selected FD metrics when theoretical, mathematical, or empirical considerations suggest overlap, using complementary analyses across continuous and categorised representations.

title: Development of CeO2 coated functional CNT-reinforced thin film for enhanced bonding and electrochemical nitrite sensing
abstract: Nitrite (NO₂⁻) contamination in water poses serious environmental and health risks, necessitating sensitive and reliable detection platforms. However, achieving strong film adhesion alongside high electrocatalytic performance remains a key challenge in electrochemical sensor design. title: ENVIRONMENTAL SATISFACTION AS A MODERATOR IN THE HARNESSING OF COMMUNITY-BASED TOURISM FOR SUSTAINABLE GROWTH
abstract: Community-based tourism (CBT) has come up as a viable solution towards development of sustainable tourism. Against the conventional tourism models, CBT focuses on the active participation and empowerment of the local communities in the planning, management, and decision-making processes in tourism. Through prioritization of local ownership, cultural preservation and environmental conservation, the CBT seeks to achieve more equitable distribution of tourism benefits and minimizing negative impacts. abstract: Brown rot, caused by Monilinia spp., is a destructive postharvest disease of cherry. title: Natural grass cover enhances microbial network stability via soil metal elements in deep black soil
abstract: Microbial network stability is a critical indicator for assessing the resilience of soil ecosystems under long term agricultural disturbance. However, how different land use types affect microbial co-occurrence network stability across deep black soil profiles remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Abstract In the eastern sector of the Sistema de Famatina, both natural processes and anthropogenic activities pose considerable risks to the landscape and its inhabitants. This study investigates the geohazards and environmental agents that have historically affected the region, with a focus on their implications for local communities and territories. The analysis integrates case studies of documented natural events, identification of mitigation strategies, satellite imagery interpretation, landform recognition, and direct field observations. title: Organic matter source and thermal maturity of coals from Muara Teweh Mine, Barunang area, Warukin formation, Barito Basin, Central Kalimantan: A preliminary study using polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons approach
abstract: This study presents a preliminary assessment of organic matter source and thermal maturity of coal samples from the Muara Teweh Mine, Barunang Area, Warukin Formation, Barito Basin, Central Kalimantan, using GC–MS based on Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) biomarker proxies. title: Status and ontogenetic structure of rare wild populations of Vitis vinifera (Vitaceae) in Uzbekistan
abstract: Vitis vinifera is an ancient fruit crop whose wild populations constitute a valuable genetic resource for grape breeding. In Uzbekistan, these populations are rare and fragmented, and the species is listed under Category 3 in the national Red Data Book (2019). This study assessed the ontogenetic structure, demographic characteristics, and conservation status of six wild cenopopulations of V. vinifera in Uzbekistan. abstract: The theory of island biogeography (TIB) explains species richness patterns, yet its extension to compositional dissimilarity (β diversity), particularly from multidimensional perspectives, remains limited. Using butterfly assemblages across 44 land‐bridge islands in the Zhoushan Archipelago, China, we applied an integrative framework to unravel how island geography and species traits shape multi‐faceted β diversity. title: People and bats in Fiji: perceptions and interactions
abstract: Abstract The management of wild bat populations often presents challenges in balancing the needs of biodiversity conservation and public health risks from zoonotic diseases. In Fiji, the most important recognized zoonotic infection is Leptospira, which was recently detected in wild bat populations. Five out of six species of Fijian bats are considered threatened to critically endangered on the IUCN Red List. abstract: Tourism can play a significant role in revitalizing low-density territories, yet transforming dispersed territorial assets into a coherent and competitive tourism offer remains a complex challenge. This study examines Portugal’s Estrada Nacional 2 (EN2) as a case of route-based tourism and explores how territorial resources, collaborative governance, and digital/gamified visitor engagement can contribute to sustainable territorial development. title: Aflatoxins contamination of aquafeed: Toxicological impacts and mitigation strategies in finfish and crustacean aquaculture
abstract: Mycotoxins are toxic secondary metabolites produced by fungi that pose a significant challenge to the safety, productivity, and sustainability of global aquaculture. Aquafeed ingredients, particularly cereals, oilseed meals, and other plant-derived protein sources, are frequently contaminated with mycotoxins, including aflatoxins (AFB1, AFB2, AFG1, and AFG2), ochratoxin A (OTA), fumonisins (FB1), trichothecenes (T-2 toxin), and zearalenone (ZEA). title: The Quaternary paleo-lacustrine deposits of Bamako and their significance for the development of the Niger River course
abstract: Sills play a crucial role in shaping river courses. They are typically natural dams that obstruct water flow and create lakes along the river. This study examines the case of the Sotuba sill in the Niger River's development in West Africa. It discusses four Quaternary outcrops in Bamako, the Niger Valley, composed of lacustrine deposits covered by fluviatile sediments, indicating a change in depositional environment. abstract: A central challenge in microbial ecology, particularly in engineered systems, is understanding how competing guilds coexist and why communities deviate from expected stability. Whereas polyphosphate accumulation provides energy and redox buffering in many heterotrophs, how lineages lacking polyphosphate synthesis manage equivalent redox imbalances remains an overlooked question. title: A practical guide to using Q‐methodology in conservation science
abstract: Abstract Conservation scientists and practitioners are increasingly incorporating social research methods into their work. Q‐methodology is an established social research tool with multiple potential applications in conservation, but its uptake remains comparatively limited. Q‐methodology integrates qualitative and quantitative approaches, providing an accessible, effective technique for identifying subjective perspectives on conservation topics. abstract: This article focuses on discussing and comparing the most critical aspects of metrology in testing gaseous emissions from aircraft engines during ground tests, such as choice of measuring equipment, its layout on site and its technical parameters. By referencing actual measurement campaigns and research projects, the study characterizes the objects of investigation – turbojet (specifically turbofan) engines used in commercial aviation – as well as global policies regarding emission analysis, the objectives and scope of engine trials, and the environmental conditions accompanying these tests. abstract: Mapping of soils and depicting spatial variability across agro-ecological regions remains underexplored, especially in Nepal's hilly areas. The current study aimed to assess spatial variability and map key soil properties such as pH, soil organic matter, total nitrogen, available phosphorus, and available potassium across the Kaski district, Nepal. A total of 263 composite, geo-referenced samples from 0-20 cm depth were collected using a proportional random sampling design across different land- use types. abstract: This study systematically investigated the extraction and identification of umami peptides, as well as their mechanism for masking bitterness. The hydrolysate of Antarctic krill was isolated and purified, and umami components were identified through sensory evaluation and instrumental analysis. 12 potential umami peptides were obtained via virtual screening using databases. title: Matricentric feminism is not a dirty word: Fieldwork and equity
abstract: Abstract Gendered and intersectional inequities shape access, safety, and participation for mothers and pregnant women within field‐based research in archaeology and biological anthropology. Mothers routinely confront discrimination and structural barriers associated with pregnancy, breastfeeding, childcare, and gendered norms embedded in fieldwork culture. abstract: Abstract Harnessing solar energy with semiconductors offers a feasible path toward sustainable hydrogen production via photocatalytic water splitting. abstract: Abstract Fungal infections, such as those caused byCandida albicans (C. albicans), represent a growing global health threat due to rising antifungal resistance and limited antifungal therapy options. abstract: Abstract Listeria monocytogenes is a major foodborne pathogen whose persistence in food-processing environments is strongly associated with its ability to survive under a wide range of environmental conditions and form biofilms on different surfaces. Metabolites produced by beneficial lactic acid bacteria may represent a natural source of antimicrobial and antibiofilm compounds capable of affecting bacterial behavior even at subinhibitory concentrations. abstract: Abstract Nitrogen (N) pollution from livestock production significantly threatens China’s air and water quality, necessitating innovative solutions to balance food security and environmental sustainability. Studies have mostly overlooked the spatial heterogeneity of N-related environmental impacts and the trade-offs between reducing ammonia (NH3) emissions and N concentrations in water. abstract: Geothermal energy is increasingly considered a promising and sustainable supplement to conventional fossil-fuel–based power systems, but many regions, including southeastern Nigeria, remain insufficiently investigated for geothermal potential. This study applies residual Bouguer gravity data to evaluate the geothermal characteristics of the Okigwe area within the Lower Benue Trough. title: Antiviral Activity of Morus nigra L. Molasses and an Anthocyanin‐Rich Extract Against Herpes Simplex Virus and Development of a Film Formulation
abstract: This study evaluated the in vitro antiviral efficacy of Morus nigra L. (black mulberry) molasses (BMM) and an anthocyanin-rich extract (BME) incorporated into mucoadhesive films for potential topical treatment against herpes simplex virus (HSV). Recurrent orolabial herpes requires effective localized therapy. Morus nigra is rich in bioactive polyphenols, flavonoids, and anthocyanins known for potent antioxidant and antiviral properties. title: Heavy Metal Contamination and Screening-Level Risks in Soils Affected by Persistent Coal Fires in Northwestern China
abstract: Persistent coal fires can mobilize potentially toxic elements and create long-lasting soil contamination. This preliminary screening study evaluated Cr, Mn, Ni, Cu, Zn, As, Cd, and Pb in nine composite surface-soil samples from coal-fire, non-combustion reference, and residential zones at the Rujigou mine in northwestern China. Concentrations were measured by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry. title: High-strength, UV-blocking, antioxidant, recyclable shape memory, EMI shielding biobased composites based on Eucommia ulmoides gum and lignin
abstract: Eucommia ulmoides gum (EUG) is a natural polymer with superior film-forming properties, wear resistance, and biocompatibility that has attracted increasing attention. However, its susceptibility to oxidation and poor UV resistance severely limit its application in high-performance materials, and the high-value utilization of different components of Eucommia biomass remains challenging. In this study, EUG was efficiently separated via ball milling, and esterified lignin with different chain lengths (C8-C18) was prepared and combined with EUG to form EUG-bio-based composites. title: Living on the edge: A qualitative exploration of informal life under flyovers in Dhaka
abstract: Homeless populations face multiple and intersecting vulnerabilities in rapidly urbanizing cities; however, the lived experiences of individuals residing beneath flyovers in Dhaka remain underexplored. This study explores their lived experiences, with particular attention to shelter, food security, safety, and personal identity, and challenges related to food, income, housing, safety risks, extreme weather, and sexual violence. abstract: Reducing bat mortality at wind turbines has become an urgent conservation priority. However, operators often fail to identify and avoid areas of high bat activity when planning wind facilities, despite recommendations from environmental authorities, and existing curtailment strategies still require optimization. Although acoustic monitoring has been suggested as a practical way of assessing collision risk, the relationship between bat activity and fatalities remains poorly understood and lacks scientific consensus. title: Climate-Induced Migration in the African Sahel: Legal Invisibility and International Protection Gaps
abstract: In the African Sahel, an increase in temperature, heatwaves, desertification, drought, floods, loss of ecosystems, and collapse of livelihoods are forcing vulnerable populations to migrate from their habitat. These climate-related stressors interact with poverty, insecurity, armed conflict, and weak institutions, creating complex displacement dynamics. But despite the scale and intensity of climate-induced migration in the Sahel region, existing international refugee, human rights, and climate change governance systems do not provide adequate protection for climate-displaced persons. title: Molecular basis of quorum-sensing signal transduction by CqsS and its inhibition by CqsA, the autoinducer synthase
abstract: Vibrio bacteria possess multiple quorum-sensing systems, each of which conveys information into the cell concerning the cell density and species composition of the vicinal community. Germane to the present work is the CqsA-CqsS quorum-sensing pathway that vibrios use for intragenus communication. CqsA is the synthase for the autoinducer ( S )-3-hydroxytridecan-4-one (CAI-1), and CqsS, a bifunctional two-component kinase-phosphatase, is the CAI-1 receptor. title: Analysis of Cost and Returns in Rice Production among Contract and Non-Contract Smallholder Producers in Benue and Niger States, Nigeria
abstract: This study analyzed the costs and returns of rice production among contract and non-contract smallholder producers in Benue and Niger States, Nigeria. A multi-stage sampling design was used to select 400 contract and non-contract rice producers. Primary data were collected using a well- designed questionnaire. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, farm budgetary technique, and ordinary least squares (OLS) regression model. title: The bacterial swarming factor SwrD belongs to a diverse family of proteins that form hexameric rings
abstract: Prokaryotic swarming is a collective surface-associated behavior that supports rapid colonization, biofilm formation, and host interactions. Swarming requires enhanced flagellar motor (FM) torque generation under high-load conditions. In many bacteria, this adaptation is achieved through increased stator unit recruitment and coordinated transcriptional regulation of motility genes. Genetic studies have implicated several relatively poorly characterized proteins in swarming, including SwrD, a component of the fla-che operon whose loss impairs torque generation in Bacillus subtilis. title: Effects of Pre‐Existing Crack Location and Orientation on the Aero‐Structural Response and High‐Stress Influence Zones of a Carbon/Glass Hybrid Composite Wind Turbine Blade
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the effects of crack location and orientation on the structural response and high‐stress influence zone (HSIZ) of a 1.5 MW carbon/glass hybrid composite wind turbine blade using laminate tensile tests, digital image correlation (DIC), computed tomography (CT), and one‐way aerodynamic–structural coupling analysis. Laminate tests revealed orientation‐dependent strain localization and damage paths. title: Driving Organizational Transformation Through P.A.T.R.O.L. Plan 2030: A Comprehensive Blueprint Towards Sustainable Enhancement
abstract: This research ascertained the implementation of “Driving Organizational Transformation through P.A.T.R.O.L. PLAN 2030 particularly on the component “T” (Transformation) in the select cities of Cebu. Specifically, it determined the extent of implementation in terms of crime management, resource optimization, stakeholder’s collaboration, monitoring and evaluation. It also evaluated the level of perception regarding the core processes, namely: strategy formulation, mapping and cascading. title: Detrital Zircon Double Dating Reconstructs the Missing Grenville Foreland and Great Unconformity Exhumation
abstract: Abstract The c. 1090–980 Ma Grenville Orogeny that resulted in final amalgamation of the supercontinent Rodinia is not associated with extensive preserved foreland basins common in other convergent margins, which has generated controversy about why these basins are absent and the nature of Meso‐Neoproterozoic orogenesis. The c. 993 Ma Jacobsville Sandstone and correlative units preserved in the North America Midcontinent region are the only known syntectonic units associated with the final stage of Grenville orogenesis. title: Traceable Privacy and Cybersecurity Compliance Control Baseline for Indonesian Academic Information Systems
abstract: Academic information systems process student identities, academic records, library transactions, authentication logs, learning analytics, and third-party service integrations. In Indonesia, privacy and cybersecurity compliance is difficult to operationalize because legal obligations are often separated from system risks, IT governance controls, ownership, and audit evidence. This study develops a traceable privacy and cybersecurity compliance control baseline for Indonesian academic information systems. The method applies structured literature-based conceptual synthesis and design science-insp

title: Temporal fluctuations in retinal artery occlusions: an 11-year German cohort study
abstract: PURPOSE: Cardiovascular events have been shown to follow seasonal and monthly distributions. It is unclear whether this applies to retinal vascular diseases. This study aims to determine the existence of seasonal variations in the onset of retinal artery occlusions (RAO) in a European population. METHODS: This retrospective, monocentric study included 646 eyes of 646 patients who were treated for RAO at the University Hospital Münster, Germany, between 2014 and 2024. title: Occurrence and distribution of plant-parasitic nematodes in flooded rice-producing regions of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Rice ( Oryza sativa L.) is a crop of great economic and social importance for many countries around the world. Brazil is among the countries with the highest rice production in the world, and the state of Rio Grande do Sul accounts for more than 70% of national production. However, biotic threats, including plant-parasitic nematodes, may limit rice production across the state’s producing regions. title: Hot deformation behavior and phase-dependent deformation mechanisms of 00Cr27Ni7Mo5N hyper duplex stainless steel
abstract: Hyper duplex stainless steels (HDSSs) with high nitrogen and alloying element contents exhibit excellent mechanical properties and corrosion resistance, making them promising for extreme service environments. However, their high nitrogen and alloying element contents can exacerbate deformation incompatibility between ferrite and austenite, resulting in heterogeneous strain partitioning, distinct phase-dependent softening behavior, and deteriorated hot workability. title: Geochemical suitability of recycled clay materials for use in impermeable barriers: laboratory and field-scale leaching assessment
abstract: Recycling polluted and remediated excavated soils can enhance resource efficiency and replace the use of finite virgin materials. However, reuse of the fine silt/clay fraction remains limited. This study evaluates the geochemical suitability of two alternative clay materials: soil washing filter cake (SWFC) and excavated cement-stabilized clay (ECSC) for use in constructed impermeable barriers, alongside conventionally used dry crust clay (DCC) for comparison. title: Stakeholder Engagement: Sustainable Tourism Development Strategy in Pati Regency
abstract: Tourism is a leading sector that makes a significant contribution to the national economy. Therefore, tourism management is directed towards sustainability with stakeholder synergy. The main problem in the tourism sector is the lack of synergistic, comprehensive, integrated, and sustainable integration or collaboration between stakeholders. Structural egos between parties are still high, and overlapping duties and functions often become obstacles faced, especially in the development of Indonesian tourism. title: Contrasting Spatial Genomic Structure in Two Widespread Grassland Species Across Norway Supports Species‐Specific Seed Sourcing
abstract: ABSTRACT Ecological restoration typically relies on locally sourced seed material, yet seed sourcing in many countries is based on broad administrative regions rather than empirical genetic data. Whether these generalized zones reflect biologically meaningful population genomic structure, particularly among co‐occurring species used together in restoration, remains poorly understood, thus limiting genetically informed restoration practices. abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, a novel triple‐mode biosensor based on a Cu‐N 4 single‐atom nanozyme (Cu‐N 4 SAzyme) and an In 2 O 3 /Bi 24 O 31 Br 10 Z ‐Scheme heterojunction was constructed for the highly sensitive detection and photocatalytic inactivation of Vibrio alginolyticus ( V. alginolyticus ). title: Fluorite solubility in Na-K-Cl-SO4 aqueous solutions at elevated temperatures and pressures: Experimental constraints and thermodynamic modeling
abstract: Fluorite solubility in hydrothermal fluids plays an important role in fluorite mineralization and fluoride transport, yet reliable thermodynamic models at elevated temperatures and pressures remain limited. Here, we developed a Pitzer-based thermodynamic model for fluorite solubility in Na-K-Cl-SO 4 -bearing aqueous solutions at temperatures up to 260 °C and pressures up to 500 bar. title: UAV-based method for measuring CO 2 emissions in forest ecosystems
abstract: This study addresses the difficulty of accurately quantifying CO 2 emissions in forest ecosystems due to spatial heterogeneity, complex terrain, and the combined effects of horizontal and vertical transport. A methodology for quantifying 3-D CO 2 emissions using an unmanned aerial vehicle was developed, evaluated, and applied to a forest ecosystem. title: Occupational Safety and Disaster Risk Convergence in Upstream Oil and Gas Operations in Nigeria: A Conceptual Framework and Comparative Case Analysis
abstract: Upstream oil and gas facilities in Nigeria are workplaces and, at the same time, hazard sources for the communities and ecosystems around them. Occupational safety and health (OSH) and disaster risk reduction (DRR) have nonetheless developed as separate fields with separate laws, metrics and institutions. This article argues that this separation contributes to recurring blind spots: events that begin as process-safety failures end as community disasters. abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders (NMOSD) are autoimmune neuroinflammatory conditions characterized by widespread brain alterations. However, how cortical hierarchical organization is altered across these disorders and how such alterations relate to underlying molecular architecture remain unclear. title: Swimming motility and type IV pili modulate phagocytosis by shaping physical interactions between Pseudomonas aeruginosa and macrophages
abstract: During chronic lung infections, Pseudomonas aeruginosa diversifies under selection from antibiotics, metabolic constraints, and host defenses. Macrophages are key sentinels of the innate immune system and play a central role in clearing airway pathogens. Yet, how they process heterogeneous bacterial populations remains poorly understood. abstract: Herein we report on preliminary data for the Trichoptera assemblage for the Piedra Jabón Geosite, a proposed UNESCO defined geological site located in Coclé Province, near Penonomé. abstract: This study was designed to prepare bio-assisted Fe-based nanocomplexes (Fe-based NCs) using two different biological precursors, namely green tea extract (Fe-T NCs) and Kilka fish extract (Fe-F NCs), and to evaluate their physicochemical properties and effects on the foliar characteristics of Zataria multiflora Boiss. abstract: High-risk logistics systems face a timing problem: intensive intervention is costly, yet withdrawal before collaboration is durable or operational risk has subsided may be premature. We develop a reciprocal nonlinear dynamical framework with three strategy variables and four persistent system states—governance capability, data credibility, collaboration capability, and logistics risk. abstract: ABSTRACT The diversity of small non‐volant mammals is shaped by multiple environmental factors, with habitat structure as a key driver. abstract: Abstract The 18S rRNA gene has emerged as the primary molecular marker for amplicon-based characterization of microalgal communities, including in wastewater treatment systems, yet trade-offs between short- and long-read approaches remain poorly defined. We systematically compared V8–V9 short-read sequencing (SR; Illumina MiSeq), near-full-length long-read sequencing with ss5ss3 primers (LR; PacBio Sequel II), and computationally extracted V8–V9 regions from LR data (LS). title: Differentiation in ant-eating spiders based on offensive and defensive exploitation of ants
abstract: Abstract Ecological speciation via host-race has been documented in several herbivores and parasitoids. Analogous prey-race has recently been suggested to explain the diversity of specialised ant-eating spiders. title: Upcycling waste polyester into cobalt-molybdenum sulfide-decorated carbon foam for photothermal desalination and parametric optimization using Taguchi design of experiments
abstract: Photothermal desalination is an emerging solar-powered technique for water desalination. One of the primary open issues in the field is the development of new materials that guarantee high photothermal efficiency and evaporation rates. In this study, waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles are upcycled into carbon foam, which is then decorated with Co-Mo2S3 via hydrothermal synthesis to prepare a photothermal evaporator. title: Pluvial flood impacts on ambulance travel and spatial disparities in emergency healthcare accessibility in Thessaloniki, Greece
abstract: Urban pluvial flooding can disrupt road networks, delay emergency medical services and produce spatially uneven losses of access to urgent healthcare. This study evaluates how flood-induced road disruption affects ambulance travel performance and identifies buildings, neighbourhoods and populations that experience reduced emergency healthcare accessibility under rainfall events with return periods of 10, 20 and 100 years in Thessaloniki, Greece. abstract: ABSTRACT Greenhushing has emerged as a strategic corporate response to political and regulatory uncertainty, yet less is known about how firms recalibrate previously established sustainability signals when external conditions change. Drawing on signaling theory, this study examines changes in corporate climate and ESG commitments during the political transition to the second Trump administration. title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
abstract: Abstract Celtic languages are today restricted to Europe’s Atlantic fringes but were widely spoken across the continent during the Iron Age 1–3 . How Celtic achieved this early distribution remains contested 4 , with alternative archaeological and linguistic models proposing different homelands and dispersal routes. abstract: Increasing temperatures can impair ecosystem services and the reproduction of dung beetles. We investigated the effects of increased nest temperatures on reproduction, dung burial, and the development of 2 dung beetle species (Onthophagus binodis and Digitonthophagus gazella). Three pairs of sexually mature F1-beetles at 15 days of age were housed in temperature-controlled chambers for 2 weeks. abstract: Microalgal systems are receiving significant attention for wastewater treatment because of their effective treatment performance while simultaneously generating valuable biomass for energy recovery. This study compares the performance of three biological systems - green microalgae, diatoms, and aerobic bacteria for the treatment of real domestic wastewater. title: Polycrisis, spatial inequality and places of ‘left-behindness’: An analytical integration
abstract: The relationship between polycrisis and regional and urban inequalities remains under-examined. This conceptual paper addresses this gap by analyzing how intersecting crises shape spatial disparity, with particular emphasis on the European Union context, where territorial cohesion has long been a central policy objective. The paper argues that crises are not isolated phenomena but interacting events that significantly reshape spatial inequalities. abstract: In tunnel smoke extraction systems, the multi-point lateral vent configuration is critical for fire emergencies. However, variations in the fire heat release rate and the vent layout often cause non-uniform plug-holing at individual vents, which reduces the smoke extraction efficiency. To address this challenge, a theoretical method was developed to identify and quantify plug-holing. title: Tunable porosity and dye removal performance of kaolin-based geopolymer membranes via H2O2-assisted foaming
abstract: Indonesia’s abundant Bangka-Belitung kaolin provides a locally available raw material for developing geopolymer membranes for dye-contaminated water treatment. abstract: To assess the feasibility of using proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) to target G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), we constructed a degron-tagged GPCR library in which a HaloTag7 protein fusion tag was engineered into the cytoplasmic carboxyl terminal tail. abstract: This research presents a robust and effective approach for enhancing the active corrosion protection of UiO-66 through in-situ and physical hybridizations with nanodiamond (ND) in epoxy coatings under neutral, acidic, and alkaline conditions. title: Shock-Driven Price Dynamics in the Dutch TTF Natural Gas Market: An Econometric Analysis of the 2022–2023 Crisis
abstract: The European natural gas market has experienced extreme volatility due to major exogenous shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine conflict. This study analyzes short-term price dynamics and volatility in the Dutch TTF market from January 2022 to June 2023 (78 weekly observations), treating this interval as a distinct crisis regime. A multiple linear regression is first employed to assess the contribution of key fundamentals, followed by ARIMAX models and conditional volatility specifications (GARCH and EWMA). title: SPATIAL VARIATION OF TUBERCULOSIS OCCURRENCES IN ILORIN, KWARA STATE NIGERIA
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is one of the deadliest infectious diseases globally. It was responsible for 1.6 million deaths in 2019 and the leading cause of mortality from a single infectious agent, especially in developing countries. In Africa, the incidence of TB was estimated to be rising, with 1500 deaths daily. Despite current global efforts to reduce TB, Nigeria’s TB prevalence is increasing in many communities. This study therefore focused on the assessment of the spatial variation in the occurrence of tuberculosis in Ilorin, Kwara State, through the analysis of notified TB cases across local gov
journal: International Journal of African Development and Sustainable Research

title: A century of soybean breeding increased photosynthetic capacity but not NPQ relaxation
abstract: Accelerating photoprotective regulation to improve carbon assimilation is a promising strategy to increase crop productivity. Although rapid non-photochemical quenching (NPQ) relaxation has been validated as a target through metabolic engineering, it remains unclear whether conventional breeding has improved this trait. Here, we investigated whether more than a century of soybean breeding enhanced NPQ relaxation alongside light-saturated carbon assimilation and seed traits. title: Impact of VOSO4 on the physicochemical properties of coprecipitated NH4MgPO4(H2O)6 struvite: a new heterogeneous Fenton-type catalyst for methylene blue degradation
abstract: The impact of vanadyl sulfate (VOSO 4 ) on the physicochemical properties of coprecipitated NH 4 MgPO 4 (H 2 O) 6 struvite was investigated. A series of NH 4 Mg 1–x V x PO 4 (H 2 O) 6 samples (x = 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75) were obtained by controlled coprecipitation with synthesis yields above 86%. Powder X-ray diffraction with Rietveld refinement confirmed that all samples crystallize in orthorhombic system ( Pmn 2 1 -space group, Z = 2). title: Structural vulnerability regimes of water supply systems under climate change: A robustness-based analysis using multi-dimensional sustainability indicators
abstract: Climate change is expected to intensify hydrological variability and extreme events, increasing the vulnerability of basin-scale multi-sector water supply systems. Conventional assessments commonly summarize vulnerability using failure probability, providing limited insight into how failure-prone conditions are organized across system states. This study develops a multi-dimensional sustainability framework to characterize structural vulnerability regimes in the Seomjin River Basin, Korea. institutions: Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology

title: Dynamic redox reactivation of platinum sites for long-term glycolate electrosynthesis from polyethylene terephthalate wastes
abstract: Glycolates are indispensable in the health, chemical and pharmaceutical industries, whereas their mainstream production involve toxic chemicals and harsh operating condition. An alternative route for glycolate production is electrifying ethylene glycol (EG) that originates from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) but suffers from poor durability of active platinum site that tend to deactivate. title: OPERATIONAL RESILIENCE IN U.S. AND INTERNATIONAL CARGO LOGISTICS (2026): RISK-ADJUSTED ROUTING, DIGITAL INTEROPERABILITY, AND MULTIMODAL CAPACITY UNDER VOLATILE DEMAND
abstract: Freight operators face a persistent decision problem: a route that appears economical at dispatch may become expensive after congestion, a missed connection, additional handling, or cargo damage. The problem is particularly visible when a domestic road movement must be compared with a cross-border movement involving several carriers and transport modes. This article develops a decision-oriented framework for evaluating these alternatives without equating low nominal freight rates with operational efficiency. Drawing on the practical context of specialist forwarding and a comparison with the U.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: The Language of Vegan Beauty: Lexical Choices in Rare Beauty’s Advertisements
abstract: Beauty advertising increasingly associates products with natural ingredients, presenting nature as an essential source of beauty and personal care. However, such representations may primarily serve promotional purposes rather than communicate genuine environmental responsibility. This study explores the representation of nature through lexical choices in Rare Beauty cosmetic advertisements, focusing on how advertising language constructs associations between natural ingredients, beauty, and personal well-being. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, the study analyzes ten selected excer
journal: Austronesian Journal of Language Science & Literature

title: Nanoparticle-Based Antibacterials: Microbial Techniques, Bacterial Defence Responses and Antimicrobial Resistance Detection
abstract: Objectives The escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has necessitated the development of alternative therapeutic strategies. Among the many approaches, nanoparticle-based antimicrobial agents have shown significant promise. These nanoscale systems offer targeted drug delivery, enhanced penetration and potential to overcome resistance mechanisms. However, there is a need for rigorous and diverse microbial techniques to evaluate their efficacy and the risk of inducing resistance/persister cells. title: Comparative assessment of floristic composition and diversity following anthropogenic disturbance in Nigerian lowland rainforest
abstract: Nigerian lowland rainforest, a biodiverse ecoregion with widespread vegetation, has experienced selective anthropogenic disturbances. Understanding the current species composition and forest recovery following a decrease in disturbances is critical for forest biodiversity and conservation. This study assessed the species composition and diversity of a once disturbed forest site in comparison with two (2) neighboring undisturbed forest sites within Nigerian lowland rainforest along Warri River. title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils
abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified ph
institutions: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology

title: Understanding range-wide immune gene variation in an endangered big cat ( Panthera tigris )
abstract: Abstract Assessing genetic diversity at loci putatively involved in fitness, such as immune genes, could provide important insights into the survival and vulnerability of endangered species. Research on immune genes in wild species has traditionally focused on the Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) genes, which represent only a small proportion of the immune gene repertoire, thereby limiting our understanding of immunity in non-model species. title: Regulatory mechanism of LuxS/AI-2 quorum sensing system on biofilm formation of Listeria monocytogenes on the surface of fresh-cut iceberg lettuce
abstract: ABSTRACT Listeria monocytogenes ( L. monocytogenes ) readily forms biofilms on the surfaces of leafy vegetables, but the regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the role and mechanism of the LuxS/AI-2-mediated quorum sensing (QS) system in biofilm formation by L . monocytogenes during its colonization of fresh-cut iceberg lettuce (FCIL). The study found that inoculation of L . monocytogenes on FCIL increased the production and accumulation of autoinducer-2 (AI-2), which was closely associated with the acceleration of the activated methyl cycle (AMC). title: The Short-Term Fertility Impact of Abortion Law Restrictions: A Research Note
abstract: Poland's 2020 abortion ruling led to a sharp 6% drop in births 37 weeks later. The decline exceeded the number of legal abortions previously performed. The decline was strongest among younger and childless women. Abortion bans may reduce fertility when they heighten risks of childbearing.

title: Expedited Structure Elucidation of Novel Cyclic Peptides Using 15 N Stable Isotopic Labeling
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural products have historically been a rich and diverse source of biologically active compounds. Some of the most interesting members of this category are cyclic and acyclic peptides. Although this structural class has a high potential for development into medicines and application to numerous therapeutic indications, the elucidation of their structures is not always trivial. title: Decoupling environmental suitability from realized recruitment through ontogenetic environmental filtering in a long‐lived Mediterranean palm species
abstract: Long‐lived plants facing anthropogenic disturbance often exhibit recruitment failure despite persistent reproductive adults, generating extinction debt masked by longevity. However, whether adult presence reliably reflects environmental suitability for recruitment remains unclear. Here, we examine ontogenetic niche differentiation and its consequences for recruitment in Jubaea chilensis , an endangered long‐lived Mediterranean palm with an aging population. title: Shifting Dietary Ecologies of Early Ungulates Across the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum in the Bighorn Basin, Wyoming
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the interplay between climate change and ecology is crucial when attempting to reconstruct the evolutionary history of species, as well as predicting how modern species may fare in light of current anthropogenic climate change and habitat destruction. Here we use dental microwear texture analysis (DMTA) to infer the foraging ecologies of three lineages of early ungulates (the phenacodontids Copecion and Ectocion and the early perissodactyl Sifrhippus ) across the Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM) in the Bighorn Basin of western North America. title: From Climate Futures to Future Migration: The Groundswell Reports and Their Reception in German Media Discourse
abstract: Over the past decade, international organizations have sought to raise awareness about climate migration and secure its place on national political agendas. Scholars have critically examined how these organizations frame climate migration and what assumptions inform their efforts to set the agenda. Yet, little attention has been paid to the temporal logic and futurity underpinning this discourse: It treats climate migration as an anticipated threat, rather than an observable phenomenon. institutions: Max Planck Institute for the Study of Societies

title: The Impact of South Sudan Petroleum Fiscal Regime on the Generation of Government Revenue
abstract: The petroleum fiscal system is a key component of economic dynamics because it controls how investors and host governments divide risks and rewards. South Sudan’s petroleum fiscal system remains the central determinant of the state’s economic viability. petroleum accounts for approximately 70% of government revenue and 95% of exports. Under the existing Exploration and Production Sharing Agreements (EPSAs), the Joint Operating Companies (JOCs) recover costs and profit oil at rates that leave the government with a diminished share of its own resource wealth. title: Cross‐Cultural Adaptation of Children's Assessment of Participation and Enjoyment (CAPE) and Preferences for Activities of Children (PAC) in a Danish Context
abstract: BACKGROUND: Participation in leisure and everyday activities is central to children's development, health and social inclusion. Although participation is increasingly used as an outcome in clinical practice and research, no cross-culturally adapted Danish-language instrument is currently available for systematically assessing children's participation and activity preferences. The Children's Assessment of Participation and Enjoyment and Preferences for Activities of Children (CAPE/PAC) is widely used internationally but requires cross-cultural adaptation prior to use in Denmark. title: Broad‐Scale Landscape Structure and Fine‐Scale Microhabitat Jointly Shape the Distribution of the Jeju Salamander, Hynobius quelpaertensis
abstract: ABSTRACT Species distribution models often assume that species occupy all environmentally suitable space, but low‐dispersal amphibians may track landscape structure that has persisted over long periods as well as current local conditions. We examined how broad‐scale landscape structure and fine‐scale microhabitat jointly shape the distribution of the Jeju salamander, Hynobius quelpaertensis , on Jeju Island, Republic of Korea. title: Upcycling Post‐Harvest Soybean Straw Into FeCo Alloy‐Embedded N, S Co‐Doped Carbon as Electrocatalysts for Rechargeable Zinc–Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The sluggish kinetics of oxygen reduction and evolution reactions (ORR/OER) at air cathodes restrict the practical performance of rechargeable zinc–air batteries (ZABs), driving the urgent demand for low‐cost, robust non‐noble metal bifunctional electrocatalysts. Abundant agricultural soybean straw, featuring native porous frameworks and abundant oxygenated functional groups, represents a promising carbon substrate that facilitates electrolyte penetration and homogeneous immobilization of catalytic active sites. title: Comparative Assessment of Population Structure and Genetic Diversity With SNPs and Microsatellites: A Case of Endangered Black‐and‐White Snub‐Nosed Monkeys
abstract: ABSTRACT Detecting fine‐scale population structure and gene flow barriers is crucial for the conservation and management of endangered species. Many such species have traditionally been studied using microsatellite genotyping; however, genome‐wide single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) may challenge conclusions made on limited numbers of loci. title: Improving The Financing of The Tourism Sector
abstract: The article aims to analyse existing financing mechanisms in the tourism sector and identify ways to improve them. The significance of the topic stems from the need to develop tourism infrastructure, enhance service quality, and attract investment. The article examines opportunities to finance tourism projects through bank loans, public funding, private investment, and public-private partnerships. title: Integrating Sentinel-2 Remotely Sensed Data into Center-Pivot Irrigation Management for Sustainable Water Resource Use: Evidence from the Nasho Irrigation Scheme, Rwanda
abstract: The Nasho Irrigation Scheme, one of Rwanda's largest centre-pivot irrigation schemes, faces challenges in aligning irrigation management with spatial and temporal variations in crop conditions. This study evaluated how Sentinel-2 remotely sensed data can support sustainable water resource management and crop productivity by assessing spatial and temporal variation in crop health using the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalised Difference Moisture Index (NDMI), examining the relationship between NDVI and crop yield, and identifying barriers to the adoption of geospatial to
journal: East African Journal of Environment and Natural Resources

title: Organic amendments and antibiotic resistance gene diversity in tropical agroecosystems of Réunion Island: an exploratory study
abstract: Environmental reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) are increasingly recognized as important components of One Health surveillance. We explored antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) across agricultural environments on Réunion Island using high-throughput qPCR targeting 349 ARGs in 16 samples comprising manure, soils, water and vegetables. ARGs were widespread, with the highest richness and relative abundance in manure-amended soils and manure. title: Geochemical and petrological characteristics of meta-conglomerate and wacke of the Jaban Formation, Champaner Group, western India: Provenance, origin and evolution
abstract: The Jaban meta-conglomerate with wacke (JMW) of the Champaner Group represents a polymictic clastic unit important for understanding sediment provenance, basin evolution and post-depositional processes within Proterozoic supracrustal sequences. This study integrates field observations, petrography, bulk rock major and trace element geochemistry, and in situ mineral chemical analyses to constrain provenance characteristics, depositional conditions and post-depositional element redistribution within this unit. title: Nutrition in abrupt sunlight reduction scenarios: a scenario-based modeling study of malnutrition prevention in low-income regions
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Abrupt sunlight reduction scenarios (ASRSs), triggered by nuclear war, volcanic eruption, or asteroid strike, risk global agricultural collapse. Despite resilient food interventions, economic inequality may leave low-income countries (LICs) at severe risk of malnutrition even where global food production is partially maintained. Objectives To assess the nutritional adequacy of low-cost ASRS-resilient food baskets (~$1/person/d) for LIC populations across 2 postdisaster periods, and to identify micronutrient gaps requiring targeted intervention. title: Enhancing Resolution in Local Passive Seismic Tomography: Adaptive Grid Implementation at Agung Volcano, Indonesia
abstract: Passive seismic tomography is a widely used method for imaging subsurface structures, relying on natural seismicity sources without the need for artificial sources. Grid‑node parameterisation is a key aspect of subsurface reconstruction in passive seismic tomography. Although many data distribution‑based adaptive grid‑node methodologies and schemes have been developed, their implementation in local‑scale passive seismic tomography is still very limited. title: Natural history and ecological variation in dwarf Phrynosoma hernandesi of the San Luis Valley, Colorado
abstract: Abstract Body size strongly influences natural history and ecological traits. Although many squamates exhibit reduced body size with increasing latitude and elevation, cases of localized mainland dwarfism are rare. We investigated the ecology of a dwarf population of Phrynosoma hernandesi (greater short‐horned lizard) of the San Luis Valley, Colorado. Here, adults are >30% smaller than surrounding non‐dwarf populations and 10%–22% smaller than those at the northernmost extent of the species' range, where body size reaches its minimum. title: Effect of Filler Metals on Microstructure, Mechanical Properties, and Corrosion Resistance of Gas Tungsten Arc Welded 316UG Stainless Steel
abstract: The welding of 316UG stainless steel, widely used in oil and gas industries, plays a critical role in ensuring structural integrity and corrosion resistance under harsh service conditions. This study investigates the effects of different filler metals (ER316L, ER310, and ER347) on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and corrosion behavior of Gas Tungsten Arc Welded (GTAW) joints of 316UG stainless steel. title: Conical Roofs in Vernacular Architecture: Transformation and Integration into the Cultural Landscape
abstract: Vernacular architectures with conical roofs constitute distinctive morphological elements within rural landscapes associated with productive activities such as agriculture, livestock farming, and water management. This study examines how these architectural typologies contribute to the transformation and integration of the cultural landscape across different territorial contexts, through a qualitative comparative approach applied to case studies in Portugal, Spain, and Peru. title: Differential methanogenic archaea-induced TLR8-dependent signaling engages gene classes regulated by NF-κB p65 and STAT1/2
abstract: Abstract Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program but with distinct kinetics: M. stadtmanae triggered an earlier and stronger response, whereas M. smithii acted more gradually. title: Dye-ligand functionalized collagen fibers as an affinity chromatography stationary phase for efficient protein separation
abstract: Dye molecules serve as promising affinity ligands with significant potential in bioseparation applications. In this study, a series of dye-affinity collagen fibers (CFs-Dye) stationary phases was fabricated by immobilizing reactive dyes (reactive red 118, reactive blue 171, reactive blue 19, reactive blue 114, reactive blue 21, and reactive blue 116) onto CFs for the selective separation and purification of lysozyme (LyZ). title: Remote sensing-based analysis of land use in spring protection zones in Southern Brazil
abstract: Springs are important ecosystems that help maintain water quality and quantity and are legally protected in Brazil as Permanent Preservation Areas (PPAs). They play a key role in aquatic ecosystems and help maintain biodiversity. The study aimed to characterize land cover in PPAs surrounding springs in the micro-watersheds of Jacarezinho, Paraná, Brazil. We mapped the springs of four micro-basins in the municipality and assessed vegetation cover in their PPAs using MapBiomas remote sensing data and geoprocessing tools. title: MONITORING AND ASSESSMENT OF SURFACE WATER QUALITY IN THE THA THONG RIVER INFLUENCED BY DOLOMITE MINING ACTIVITIES, SURATTHANI PROVINCE, THAILAND
abstract: Maintaining surface water quality within regulatory standards is important local communities and ecosystems. The present study aims to monitor and assess the surface water quality in the Thathong River, Surat Thani Province, specifically within the dolomite mining zone throughout the rainy season (May - July 2025). Water samples were taken from 9 monitoring stations to determine physicochemical parameters and amounts of heavy metal. title: Absence of males is associated with delayed progression of vitellogenesis in yellowtail Seriola quinqueradiata
abstract: Abstract Stable hatchery production of yellowtail requires effective brood stock management, particularly control of vitellogenic progression. Although the absence of males impairs oocyte maturation and ovulation in several fish species, its influence on yellowtail reproduction remains unclear. This study compared female-only and mixed-sex groups over two reproductive seasons, referred to as year 1 and year 2, respectively. title: DESIGN AND REALIZATION OF A PROFILE NOTCHING DEVICE FOR AUTOMOTIVE ELASTOMER COMPONENTS
abstract: This paper presents the engineering design and constructive realization route of a profile notching device intended for automotive elastomer components manufactured in small and medium batches. Secondary profiling operations on rubber-based parts are difficult because elastomers combine low stiffness, large recoverable deformation, and sensitivity to local compression, which can generate dimensional scatter, tearing, or edge defects when conventional manual trimming is used. title: Anchoring Pd Single Atoms on N‐Doped MOF‐Derived TiO 2 for Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution With an Ultra‐High Rate up to 185.8 mmol g −1 h −1
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic hydrogen (H 2 ) evolution provides a sustainable pathway for clean energy production. However, conventional photocatalysts suffer from wide bandgaps and rapid charge recombination, leading to low photocatalytic efficiency. Herein, we construct an asymmetric N─Pd─O coordination environment by anchoring Pd single atoms (SAs) onto N‑doped MIL‑125‑derived TiO 2 . title: Two Ume6 target gene classes in the biofilm regulatory network of Candida albicans
abstract: ABSTRACT Biofilm formation by the fungal pathogen Candida albicans is a major source of infection. The biofilm regulator Ume6 forms complexes with partner transcription factors Efg1, Ndt80, and Upc2 to drive expression of biofilm-related genes. Here, we present chromatin immunoprecipitation with sequencing data for Ume6-chromatin association in both wild-type and efg1 Δ/Δ ndt80 Δ/Δ upc2 Δ/Δ backgrounds. title: Precipitation frequency analysis informed by atmospheric physics: understanding and using the SMEV approach
abstract: Precipitation frequency analysis is fundamental for hydrological risk assessment, infrastructure design, and insurance/reinsurance. The Simplified Metastatistical Extreme Value (SMEV) is an approach to precipitation frequency analysis derived from the Metastatistical Extreme Value distribution. It relies on ordinary events, rather than extremes only, providing estimates of extreme precipitation values with reduced uncertainties with respect to traditional methods based on asymptotic statistics. title: Spatiotemporal NDVI Analysis of Kipengere Forest Reserve Dynamics in Tanzania: Evidence from 1995 to 2026
abstract: Forest ecosystems are of great importance for biodiversity conservation and water resource regulation but are increasingly subject to environmental and land-use changes. The study analysed the spatiotemporal dynamics of vegetation condition in the Kipengere Forest Reserve, Southwest Tanzania from 1995 to 2026 using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) generated from Landsat satellite images. title: Biodiversity and ecosystem multifunctionality show contrasting recovery patterns across tropical forests with different logging histories
abstract: Globally, a growing proportion of logging‐disturbed tropical forest is recovering, holding great potential for biodiversity conservation and ecosystem functioning. However, how ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) and its trait‐based predictors in these secondary forests differ from those in old‐growth forests remains unknown. title: Interface engineering of crystalline–amorphous hollow c-Co₃S₄/a-CoxP nanocages for all-pH hydrogen evolution
abstract: Exploring highly active and stable non-noble-metal electrocatalysts is critical for the widespread adoption of hydrogen energy technologies. In this work, we report the synthesis of hollow crystalline–amorphous nanocages composed of crystalline cobalt sulfide (c-Co 3 S 4 ) and amorphous cobalt phosphide (a-Co x P), derived from ZIF-67, through precise morphology and structural modulation. title: Shallow Cumulus Cloud Statistics in Real‐Case Large‐Eddy Simulations and Their Dependence on Soil Moisture
abstract: Abstract The ability of weather and climate models to reproduce the statistical properties of shallow cumulus clouds (SCCs) is critical for representing boundary‐layer transport, cloud cover, and cloud‐radiative effects. This study investigates statistical properties of SCC ensembles using the Icosahedral Nonhydrostatic model in large‐eddy simulation mode for three cases during the Field Experiment on Submesoscale Spatio‐Temporal Variability in Lindenberg campaign. title: A query language for aggregating object-centric event data
abstract: Object-centric process mining focuses on analyzing event data in the context of many interacting objects. Process mining analysis in general relies on summarization of event data through aggregation. Existing techniques mainly aggregate events based on activities, without considering related objects, or require event log manipulation prior to aggregation. To overcome this, we propose a high-level query language designed for aggregating object-centric event data. title: Characterization and multi-response optimization of epoxy–castor oil composites reinforced with coconut shell and marsh barbel powders
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable polymer composites has led to the use of agricultural waste and natural materials as alternative reinforcements. The present work deals with the characterization and multi response optimization of epoxy castor oil composites reinforced with coconut shell powder (CSP) and marsh barbel powder (MBP). Hand lay-up casting technique was used to prepare six formulations with different loadings of natural powder and with 20 wt% castor oil, cured at room temperature. title: Constructed a stable coordination polymer for highly efficient and selective capture of thorium

abstract: As forest landscape restoration advances, balancing ecological protection and local development has become a key challenge in natural forest governance. abstract: Arc andesites are hybrids generated by mixing of mafic and silicic magmas. abstract: ABSTRACT Alpine meadows (AM) and desert steppes (DS) are major grassland types in northern Qiangtang that support ecosystem functioning, livestock production and pastoral livelihoods. abstract: The cytoplasm is a crowded, active medium whose mechanical properties underpin essential cellular functions, yet how intracellular rheology adapts during tissue maturation remains unclear. Here, we examine the evolution of cytoplasmic viscoelasticity in Madin-Darby canine kidney epithelial monolayers as cell density increases. abstract: Karst spring systems with thermal anomalies commonly involve complex groundwater circulation, water–rock interaction, and cold–hot water mixing. However, hydrochemical evidence alone is often insufficient to fully characterize groundwater circulation and geothermal processes in highly heterogeneous karst systems. abstract: ABSTRACT As energy demand grows, sustainable solutions are required to mitigate climate consequences and improve energy security. This study includes the comparative life cycle assessment and life cycle costing of electricity production from rice husk gasification and traditional coal power electricity, based on a cradle‐to‐gate system boundary and a functional unit of 1 kWh. abstract: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are widely explored as potential probiotics because of their beneficial physiological properties. abstract: Bacterial contamination of drinking water remains a major public health concern in rural sub-Saharan Africa, where unprotected sources such as ponds, wells, and rivers often harbor pathogenic microorganisms. This study assessed the microbial load, pathogenicity, and antibiotic resistance profiles of waterborne bacteria in the cotton basin of Banikoara. abstract: Understanding local climate processes is a key challenge in undergraduate Earth science education. Concepts such as surface energy balance and heat transfer are often taught through abstract models, making it difficult for students to connect thermodynamic theory to the environments they inhabit. abstract: Flow-electrode capacitive deionization (FCDI) has emerged as an intriguing desalination technology. However, the performance of FCDI is fundamentally limited by the transport properties of the flow-electrode materials. abstract: This practice review reflects on two connected planning processes in northern Lazio, Italy, where an external project manager became central to coordination. abstract: Abstract HFO-1336mzz(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). abstract: Herbal interventions are increasingly investigated for wound infection due to their potential for antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, tissue-repair and angiogenic activities. abstract: Culture, traditions, and social expectations play an important role in determining beauty and makeup standards. Thus, the purpose of this research project is to examine and compare the difference between Emirati and Chinese women in terms of makeup styles, colour preferences, and beauty perceptions. abstract: The intensifying effects of global climate change have made extreme weather events a critical design input for the built environment. This study focuses on Antalya, the province in Türkiye most frequently exposed to extreme weather events in recent years, and proposes a data-driven model for climate-adaptive building design. abstract: The aquaculture industry helps meet the seafood demands of a rapidly growing human population. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in chronic cystic fibrosis infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa is shaped by pathogen-specific adaptation, yet the mechanisms driving cephalosporin resistance in epidemic clinical lineages remain incompletely defined. abstract: ABSTRACT Following a tick bite, Borrelia burgdorferi spirochetes replicate in human skin and disseminate through tissues, including subcutaneous adipose tissue. abstract: Background High-quality healthcare resources remain unevenly distributed across China, while cross-provincial care seeking, teleconsultation, and regional medical collaboration are increasingly common. Existing studies have mainly explained regional disparities in terms of resource endowments, geographic proximity, and spatial accessibility, with less attention to network structure, tie formation and persistence, and changes during public health crises. title: CO 2 fertilization to climate limitation: shifting drivers in a dryland forest
abstract: Dryland forests represent a significant but uncertain component of the terrestrial carbon sink, where rising CO 2 and intensifying drought and heat stress exert opposing controls on carbon and water fluxes. Using ED2.2-hydraulics calibrated against 21 years of flux tower and inventory data from Yatir Forest, an arid pine plantation in Israel, we simulated carbon fluxes, biomass dynamics, and water-use efficiency under current climate and high-emission scenarios (SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5) through 2100 using five general circulation models. title: Mantle metasomatism drives oxidation of arc peridotite revealed by significant Fe3+/FeT variations in spinels from Kamchatka Peninsula
abstract: Redox conditions strongly influence mantle phase equilibria and arc magmatism, yet the processes driving elevated oxygen fugacity ( f O 2 ) in subarc mantle remain unresolved. We investigate six harzburgitic peridotite xenoliths from Shiveluch volcano, Kamchatka, to estimate f O 2 shifts induced by metasomatic reactions. title: Perceptions of perennial crops among urban agriculture growers in England
abstract: Given increasing evidence of the unsustainable nature of conventional intensive agriculture, alternative methods of food production must be considered. Urban agriculture (UA) is one proposed mechanism for increasing food system sustainability, given the potential to provide social and ecological benefits while increasing access to nutritious food. In conventional farming, the incorporation of more perennial crops has been proposed to increase sustainability through reduced soil disturbance, increased water retention and supporting higher biodiversity than annual cropping. title: Synergistic fractionation of sugarcane bagasse using a [BMIM]Cl–levulinic acid system for enhanced enzymatic saccharification and multi-pathway valorization
abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass recalcitrance limits its efficient conversion into value-added products, highlighting the need for effective and sustainable pretreatment strategies. In this work, a green fractionation system based on 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride ([BMIM]Cl) and levulinic acid (LA) was developed for sugarcane bagasse, enabling coordinated utilization of its three main components. Under selected pretreatment conditions, efficient delignification was achieved with a lignin removal of 85.27%. title: A Case Study on Household Waste Management in an Urban Commune
abstract: This case study assessed household waste generation and management practices in the Urban Commune of Faranah, Guinea, with the aim of proposing measures to improve the current system. Data were collected between 15 January and 25 February 2020 through a literature review, socio-economic surveys (85 household and authority questionnaires), and field investigations in two neighbourhoods, Abattoir II and Faranah-Koura. title: Thermoresponsive Self‐Healing Carbon Nanotube‐Reinforced Dual‐Network Hydrogels for Wearable Sensors and Information Concealment
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of multifunctional hydrogels combining mechanical robustness, autonomous self‐healing, electrical conductivity, and stimuli responsiveness remains challenging. Here, we report a thermoresponsive, self‐healing dual‐network hydrogel reinforced with carbon nanotubes (CNTs), integrating reversible dynamic crosslinking, ionic liquid‐mediated phase transitions, and electrical conductivity. abstract: The ecological and environmental management department require the treatment of oilfield produced water to comply with the "Technical Requirements and Analytical Methods for Water Quality Indicators of Clastic Rock Reservoir Water Injection" SY/T 5329–2022. This standard imposes strict limits on injected water quality indicators, including suspended solids concentration, median particle size, and oil content, which are generally determined according to reservoir permeability. title: Development of an E-Module on Geometric Transformations Based on the Ethnomathematics of North Kalimantan Batik, Focused on High School Students’ Problem-Solving Skills and Interest in Learning
abstract: This study aimed to develop an ethnomathematics-based geometry transformation e-module integrating North Kalimantan batik motifs to improve senior high school students’ mathematical problem-solving ability and learning interest. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model, involving Grade XI students of SMA Negeri 1 Nunukan and a One-Group Pretest–Posttest Design. title: Curing-state-dependent rheology governs electrospinning of silicone elastomers for hydrophobic surface coatings
abstract: Fibrosis around cochlear implant electrode arrays increases impedance and disrupts predictable stimulus propagation. Electrospun hydrophobic silicone coatings represent a promising strategy to mitigate fibrosis. However, electrospinning silicone elastomers remains challenging because their low glass transition temperature causes deposited fibers to collapse before curing is complete. Previous approaches have focused on developing in situ curing systems, such as heated collectors. Although fiber-like structures have been generated, nonwovens with interconnected pores have not yet been achieved.
journal: Journal of Materials Science Materials in Medicine

title: Friction surfacing of Al2O3 reinforced aluminium coatings on low carbon steel with microstructural and tribological characterization
abstract: Friction surfacing (FS) was employed to create Al–7.5 wt% Al 2 O 3 metal matrix composite coatings on low carbon steel (AISI 1018), enhancing surface performance by solid-state processing. Two parameter sets were examined to identify their effects on coating microstructure and tribology. SEM–EDS showed dense, defect-free coatings with uniform reinforcement particle distribution, good metallurgical bonding, and a narrow compositional transition across the coating–substrate interface. title: Social Sustainability in Ecovillages: A Systematic Scoping Review of Collective Processes and Contextual Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Ecovillages merge ecological practices with alternative modes of collective living, but their sustainability cannot be solely attributed to environmental commitments. This systematic scoping review synthesizes findings from 96 publications identified through Scopus and Web of Science. It examines five social process domains—governance and power, conflict and relational dynamics, collective identity, membership and justice, and everyday practices—alongside economic, institutional, and spatial conditions, as well as various formation pathways. title: Synergistically Modulating Electronic Structure and Interfacial Wettability of MnF 2 /NF−CNF Toward Enhanced Oxygen Reduction in Zinc−Air Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Modulating the electronic structure and interfacial wettability of cathode catalysts is crucial for enhancing intrinsic activity and broadening triple‐phase interfaces for oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) in zinc−air batteries (ZABs), yet achieving their synergistic regulation faces a big challenge. Herein, an N/F source modulation strategy is proposed to synthesize porous carbon nanofibers anchored with MnF 2 nanocrystals and N/F heteroatoms (MnF 2 /NF−CNF). title: An Ablation Study of Constraint-Handling Mechanisms in Differential Evolution for Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing with Time Windows
abstract: Classical Differential Evolution (DE) solves the Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (MDVRPTW) efficiently but struggles to maintain time-window feasibility. This study investigates whether DE can be systematically hybridized with three constraint-handling mechanisms: adaptive penalty control, Large Neighborhood Search (LNS), and Tabu memory, implemented as independently toggleable components in a Java/JavaFX solver, enabling a controlled ablation across four MDVRPTW instances from Vidal et al. title: Post-fire trajectories of forest habitat structure depend on fire regime and environmental context
abstract: Fire is a key disturbance in forests around the globe. Fire shapes the structure in forests that provide essential habitat for wildlife. The post fire recovery of forests have often been characterised as a function of time since fire, overlooking the influence of additional fire characteristics, and post-fire environmental conditions. This knowledge is vital to support wildlife conservation under rapidly changing fire regimes arising from climatic extremes. title: S-layer expansion is mediated by hoop-like cracks in the paracrystalline lattice during Bacillus anthracis growth
abstract: Surface layers (S-layers) are paracrystalline protein monolayers that envelop archaea and some bacteria, including Bacillus anthracis. S-layer subunits in B. anthracis are tethered to the underlying cell wall through glycopolymers that are covalently attached to the peptidoglycan (PG) meshwork. Cell growth in this rod-shaped organism occurs by dispersed PG synthesis throughout the cell cylinder. How the crystalline lattice expands in lockstep with the cell wall has remained unclear. title: Biostimulation Sustains a Carbonic Anhydrase‐Producing Bacterial Consortium for CO 2 Hydration and Residual Oil Utilization Under Simulated Reservoir Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Depleted oil reservoirs are potential targets for geological CO 2 storage; however, temperature, salinity, pressure, and nutrient scarcity can suppress microbial activity. In this study, a consortium comprising the carbonic‐anhydrase‐producing bacterium Bacillus licheniformis S5 and the petroleum‐degrading bacterium Bacillus cereus S0 was evaluated in a stirred high‐pressure liquid system containing simulated brine and residual crude oil. title: Curcuma amada Roxb. (Mango ginger): Ethnobotany and Ethnomedicinal Uses, Phytochemical Constituents and Therapeutic Potential: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: The genus Curcuma (family Zingiberaceae) contains more than 100 species which are mostly found in tropical and subtropical regions. Curcuma amada Roxb., is one of the most important species of Curcuma genus and it is commonly known as mango ginger due to its mango like fragrance and it has significant therapeutic potential. It has traditionally been used in Ayurveda, Unani and folk medicine system for its anti-inflammatory, wound healing and respiratory ailment potential. title: Efficacy of polymyxin B against different pathogens in carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacterial pneumonia and its relationship with alveolar epithelial lining fluid concentration: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Background The relationship between polymyxin B (PMB) concentrations in alveolar epithelial lining fluid (ELF) and pathogen clearance in carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (CRGNB) pneumonia remains unclear. This study evaluated the efficacy of combined nebulized and intravenous PMB and its association with ELF exposure.Methods This prospective cohort study included 104 patients with CRGNB pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA, n=34), Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB, n=38), and Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP, n=32) receiving nebulized PMB (25 mg every 12 h) plus intravenous PMB (1

title: The origin of Group B Streptococcus in Australian dogs, cats and cows
abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae, known in human medicine as Group B Streptococcus (GBS), affects numerous animal species, including dairy cattle and companion animals such as dogs and cats. In cattle, where GBS is a common cause of mastitis, host-specialist and host-generalist clades have been detected, whereas data on the origin of companion animal GBS is limited and somewhat contradictory. Here, we analyse a collection of 39 animal GBS isolates from Australia. title: Molecular Identification and Phylogenetic Characterization of Actinomycetes from Libyan Soils via 16S rRNA Gene Sequencing
abstract: Molecular and genetic analysis of actinomycetes is crucial because these soil bacteria produce the majority of natural antibiotics. This investigation sought to identify actinomycetes using the 16S rRNA gene sequencing technique. Actinomycetes were isolated from soil samples collected near Derna, northeastern Libya. Starch casein medium supplemented with tetracycline and nystatin was employed to isolate actinomycete colonies. Eight isolates were obtained from twenty soil samples collected. title: Expression of a chimeric OXR protein remodels rice architecture for enhanced grain yield by modulating redox and hormonal pathways
abstract: SUMMARY The growth–defence trade‐off limits crop biotechnology because stress adaptation typically reduces productivity. We engineered and characterised OXR‐Q12 (Q12), a mitochondrial chimeric protein combining the regulatory N‐terminus of AtOXR1 with the catalytic TLDc domain of AtOXR2. In silico analysis predicted higher stability for Q12 than for native orthologues. title: “It’s Like Life is Frozen”: Navigating Uncertainty and Adolescence Among Unaccompanied Refugee Boys in Transit in Greece
abstract: Unaccompanied refugee adolescents in Europe experience high levels of distress, yet little is known about how adolescent boys navigate this already challenging life stage during migration transit, which involve long periods of uncertainty and family separation. This qualitative study examines how unaccompanied refugee boys (ages 13-17) in Greece cope with stress and prolonged uncertainty. The analysis draws on two rounds of interviews and a participatory drawing exercise with 12 boys in a residential shelter in Athens, conducted between January 2019 and February 2020.
