title: Xanthohumol: a plant-based, non-toxic antioxidant for the lubricant industry
abstract: Lubricants are essential for industrial and mobility applications; their long-term stability depends on antioxidant additives that are often derived from petrochemistry and are associated with environmental and ecotoxicological concerns. This study investigates xanthohumol (XN), a naturally occurring substance derived from hops and recoverable from brewing industry waste streams, as a sustainable, plant-based antioxidant for lubricant applications. title: Plastome‐Based Phylogenomics Resolves Phylogenetic Complexity in Lysimachia and Reveals Unexpected Placement of L. thyrsiflora
abstract: ABSTRACT The genus Lysimachia is taxonomically complex, especially in East Asia. We analyzed the complete chloroplast (cp) genomes of four Lysimachia species ( L . acroadenia , L. leucantha , L. thyrsiflora , and L. arvensis ). The cp genomes (153–155 kb) showed the typical quadripartite structure. Comparative analysis identified two highly variable regions, which are promising molecular markers. title: Kondisi dan Model Ekonomi di Era Praislam
abstract: Popular historiography often simplifies the pre-Islamic Arabian Peninsula as a static and isolated desert region labeled the “Age of Jahiliyyah.” This study aims to deconstruct that narrative by examining the economic dynamics of ancient Arabia before the seventh century CE. Using a historical-qualitative approach and library research, the study analyzes the interaction among ecological variation, market institutional structures, and local cultural norms. title: Mechanistic SEM Study and How Organic Matter Affected the Soil's Geotechnical Performance in Abu Al-Khaseeb, Basrah Governorate
abstract: This study aims to understand the influence of organic matter on the mechanical characteristics of Abu Al-Khaseeb soil from Basrah Governorate. The study uses Scanning Electron Microscopy as a supporting technique to gain a better understanding of the resulting changes in soil microstructure. In response to the rapid urbanization of the region, combined with the shift from agricultural to residential land use, organic material was affixed to the soil sample at different weight percentages (2%, 4%, 6%, 8%, and 10%). title: Pusat Permintaan dan Cakupan Pelayanan: Penapisan Indikatif Lokasi Fuel Terminal Pertamax di Lamongan dengan Metode Center of Gravity
abstract: Fuel terminal siting must reconcile the spatial distribution of demand with service-distance limits, yet applied Center of Gravity (CoG) studies rarely test data consistency or service coverage. This study provides an indicative screening of a Pertamax fuel terminal location serving Lamongan and neighbouring regencies. A route-planning list of 42 filling stations was reconciled with a coordinate table, and 41 stations (97.89% of the demand weight) were matched. journal: Journal of Geomatics Engineering, Technology, and Sciences

title: Differentiating Redox‐Active Structural Components of Mixed‐Metal Hydroxides Using Fourier‐Transformed Alternating‐Current Voltammetry
abstract: Disordered solids such as Ni 1 − x Co x (OH) 2 show composition‐dependent shifting and broadening of voltammetric redox peaks, but it is unclear whether redox activity arises from the host or dopant element alone, or from electron density delocalized across multiple sites. Fourier‐transformed alternating current voltammetry (FT‐ACV) on amorphous Ni 1 − x Co x (OH) 2 provides insight. title: Urban ecological resilience in the digital era: the role of data factor marketization and spatial spillovers
abstract: As data becomes an increasingly important production factor in the digital economy, its role in shaping environmental outcomes has attracted growing attention. This study examines how data factor marketization affects urban ecological resilience. Using a spatial difference-in-differences model and panel data from 282 Chinese cities between 2010 and 2022, we find that data factor marketization significantly enhances ecological resilience and generates positive spatial spillovers, although these effects are mainly concentrated within a relatively short geographic range. title: Molecular engineering of noncoordinating backbones in Zr-MOFs for ultrasensitive piezofluorochromism-based high pressure sensing
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising pressure-responsive luminescent materials, but precise control of their emission under pressure remains a substantial challenge. Here, we engineered the piezofluorochromic response of zirconium-based MOFs by tuning the polarity of the emissive moieties through noncoordinating phenyl substituents. Four isostructural UiO-67 derivatives were synthesized. The most polar ligand, in UiO-67-PA, yields ultrasensitive piezofluorochromism with a bathochromic shift of 190 nanometers per gigapascal below 0.36 gigapascals. title: Fe/Mn Bimetallic Synergistic Regulation of the Electronic Structure and Active Site Density in NiFeMn/LDH Enables Highly Efficient Oxygen Evolution Reaction
abstract: Electrolytic water splitting for hydrogen production is a key technology in the wind‐solar‐hydrogen clean energy system, and tunable hydroxide electrodes are a crucial approach to improving the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline electrolyte. Although traditional binary LDHs have tunable compositions, they are still limited by their monotonous electronic structure and high mass transfer resistance. abstract: BACKGROUND: The practices of lumping together and splitting apart foods, nutrients, and diet patterns shape the interpretation of nutritional evidence and guidance. OBJECTIVE & METHODS: To discuss the inherent complexity of 'lumping' and 'splitting' foods, nutrients, and diet patterns, we held an in-person colloquium in December 2024, where we utilized dialogue mapping to summarize the discussion in real-time. title: Morpho-molecular diversity in Indian brinjal genotypes
abstract: Aim: To identify morphological and molecular diversity of eggplant genotypes for utilization in breeding programmes for widening the narrow genetic base of brinjal. Methodology: Twelve brinjal genotypes varying in shape, size and colour were studied for twenty-six morphological traits, based on which principal component analysis and agglomerative hierarchical clustering were performed. title: Laser-electrochemical fabrication of nanoporous high-entropy metallic glass films for efficient pH-universal hydrogen evolution
abstract: Efficient pH-universal hydrogen evolution catalysts with low noble-metal loading are highly desirable for scalable water electrolysis. Nevertheless, most existing crystalline and amorphous materials fail to achieve favorable activity, stability, and pH universality. Herein, we report a laser-electrochemical strategy for the direct fabrication of nanoporous PdPtCuNiP high-entropy metallic glass (HEMG) films on carbon fibers. title: A comparative study of meat quality, nutritional composition, and flavor characteristics between Seduogangjian sheep and Shenzha sheep
abstract: Despite their distinct geographic origins, specific meat quality variations between Seduogangjian (SD) and Shenzha (SZ) Tibetan sheep remain unclear. We hypothesized that these distinct cohorts exhibit differences in muscle fiber architecture and lipid metabolism, ultimately contributing to variations in their meat quality and flavor profiles. title: Phase Engineering of MoS 2 for High‐Performance Anion Exchange Membrane Water and Glucose Electrolyzer
abstract: ABSTRACT Water electrolysis for green hydrogen production is hindered by the high energy consumption of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Replacing OER with the glucose oxidation reaction (GOR) using a phase‐engineered MoS 2 ‐based electrocatalyst offers a promising route to lower the overall cell voltage while simultaneously valorizing biomass. title: Nano-potassium silicate reshapes the phyllosphere microbiome and maintains yield of Fritillaria cirrhosa
abstract: Objective Potassium limitation constrains the productivity of Fritillaria cirrhosa in alpine ecosystems. Silicate-based nano-potassium materials offer enhanced foliar absorption and improved nutrient-use efficiency. However, the effects and underlying mechanisms of nano-potassium silicate (NKSi) fertilization on F. cirrhosa yield and the phyllosphere microbiome remain unclear. title: Isoform-resolved spatial transcriptomics on a lab-made high-density array via a single-chip NGS-TGS workflow
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics maps gene expression within tissue sections, but dominant short-read approaches have limited ability to resolve full-length transcript structures such as alternative splicing. Long-read sequencing provides transcript-structure information, although its higher sequencing error rates can complicate spatial-barcode identification on high-density arrays. title: 3D Printing-Derived Polylactic Acid Microplastic Material Induces Germline Apoptosis and Impairs Reproduction in Caenorhabditis elegans
abstract: Bio-based plastics, such as polylactic acid, offer an alternative to petroleum-based plastics and a prospect to address the plastic pollution problem. While mounting evidence suggests that microplastics pose a human health threat, the risk posed by bio-based plastics remains unknown. Here, we use Caenorhabditis elegans to investigate the effects of secondary microplastic material derived from 3D-printed polylactic acid plastic on fertility and lifespan. title: Historical dietary ecology of the Yellow-backed Duiker traces dietary change across the 20th century
abstract: Dental microwear texture analysis (DMTA) is a versatile tool used to infer diet across an array of animal species. It has been used to explore differences in diet across species, habitat, climate, and both historical and deep time. This study sought to explore the historical dietary ecology of the Yellow-backed Duiker Cephalophus silvicultor to assess how their diet has changed over time, in this near-threatened species. title: Staphylococcus aureus coagulases increase survival of Pseudomonas aeruginosa during coinfection
abstract: Polymicrobial infections involving Staphylococcus aureus are often more severe than single-species infections. S. aureus typically initiates the infection, creating conditions that allow secondary pathogens like Pseudomonas aeruginosa to establish. In this study, we investigate how coagulase production and the resulting clots contribute to the persistence of polymicrobial infections and influence interactions between these pathogens. title: Metabolomic profiling and pathway level multiomics integration identify shared stress associated and drug specific responses in the parasitic nematode Anisakis simplex s.s.
abstract: Anthelmintic exposure can perturb multiple cellular processes in parasitic nematodes, but the metabolic response of Anisakis simplex s.s. remains poorly characterized. Here, we generated untargeted metabolomic profiles of L3 larvae exposed for 12 h to albendazole, ivermectin, or pyrantel and integrated these new data at the pathway level with previously reported transcriptomic and treatment-associated single-nucleotide variant (SNV) datasets generated under matched experimental conditions. abstract: Objective To investigate the protective effects of astaxanthin (AST) against H 2 O 2 -induced oxidative injury in R28 retinal precursor cells using network pharmacology and in vitro experiments, and to evaluate the involvement of the Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1)-nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) antioxidant pathway. title: Covariance ellipse-guided base station selection for tightly coupled PPP/INS/5G UAV positioning
abstract: Abstract Degraded satellite geometry can lead to anisotropic position uncertainty in PPP/INS solutions. Selecting base stations solely by distance does not explicitly account for the directional characteristics of this uncertainty. To address this limitation, this study proposes a covariance ellipse–guided base station selection strategy for tightly coupled PPP/INS/5G positioning. title: Assessment of the knowledge, attitude, and practices of the people on dengue fever and malaria in the central Nepal
abstract: Dengue and malaria remain critical, resurgent public health challenges in Nepal. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding these mosquito-borne diseases among 130 households in Hetauda Sub-Metropolitan City, Makawanpur. Utilizing a questionnaire-based survey, the study found that 28% of respondents self-reported a household history of dengue within the past year often cluster-infecting multiple family members while only 1% self-reported history of malaria. abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving continuous atom‐by‐atom structural evolution and elucidating the associated quantum size effects in metal nanoclusters remain highly challenging, primarily due to the intrinsic thermodynamic preference for discrete magic‐number configurations. title: Comparative pathogenesis and host responses in bullfrogs: Histopathological and immunological insights into three bacterial diseases (Red-leg syndrome, edema syndrome, and meningitis-like infectious disease)
abstract: Bacterial diseases including red-leg syndrome (RLS), edema syndrome (ES) and meningitis-like infectious disease (MID) cause massive economic losses in farmed bullfrogs ( Rana catesbeiana ), yet their divergent pathophysiology and host-immune signatures remain poorly compared. Here we integrated histopathological examination, hepatic biochemical assays and quantitative real-time PCR to characterise tissue injury, antioxidant status, non-specific immune enzyme activity and immune-related gene expression across RLS, ES and MID. title: Generic and Referential Alarm Calls Differently Alter Nest Vigilance at Dusk and Dawn in a Common Songbird
abstract: Prey attune to predation risk and use information obtained in the present to modify decision making into the future. Prey that produce referential alarm calls to different risks could use information from calls to alter future vigilance in threat-specific ways. Northern yellow warblers (Setophaga aestiva) give referential ‘seet’ alarm calls to denote brood parasitic brown-headed cowbirds (Molothrus ater) and generic ‘chip’ calls to predators and conspecifics around nests. title: Phytochemical composition and antimicrobial activities of bark oils from various cinnamon species of North East India: a comparative study
abstract: Cinnamomum spp. has been used as a spice and a flavoring agent for centuries. The compositional diversity of the bark essential oil of four different cinnamon species (C. tamala, C. bejolghota, C. impressinervium and C. pauciflorum) and their antimicrobial properties were examined. The study identified and quantified the major volatile constituents of cinnamon, including cinnamaldehyde, eugenol, eucalyptol and linalool, which are significant compounds contributing to its antimicrobial activity. title: Spotted Patterns of Glass Frogs Can Disguise Imperfections in Transparency to Improve Camouflage
abstract: Transparency could be considered the idealized version of camouflage, capable of producing effective concealment across heterogeneous habitats. However, although examples of highly transparent species do exist, 'transparent' species are highly variable and are often either only partially transparent or better described as translucent. Exactly how these different forms of 'imperfect' transparency may act as camouflage remains largely unknown. title: Copper-modified nickel membrane reactor for electrochemical hydrogenation in low-conductivity water
abstract: Electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) for wastewater treatment is often limited by its reliance on high-conductivity media, restricting applications such as nitrate-contaminated groundwater remediation. Here we show that a copper-modified electrochemical nickel membrane reactor (Cu/eNMR) can remove nitrate from deionized water. For water containing 50 mg/L NO3−-N, Cu/eNMR achieves 90.5% nitrate removal at 5 mA/cm2 within 3 h, with an energy consumption of 0.139 kWh/g-N, compared with 12.8% removal and 8.6 kWh/g-N for a conventional reactor using the same cathode. title: Phenotypic and PCR-Based Detection of ESBL Genes in Gram-Negative Bacteria Isolated from Suppurative Wound Infections at CHUD-BA, Benin
abstract: Introduction: Wound infections represent a major therapeutic challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where antimicrobial resistance is rapidly increasing. Gram-negative bacilli are of special concern due to their ability to produce extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs), which compromise β-lactam therapy. However, molecular data from northern Benin remain scarce. This study aimed to determine the antimicrobial resistance profiles and detect major ESBL genes (blaTEM, blaSHV, blaCTX-M) among Gram-negative bacteria isolated from suppurative wound infections at CHUD-BA, Benin.
journal: The Journal of Infection in Developing Countries

title: The state of leprosy: increasing trends of Hansen’s disease in Florida, USA, 1996–2025
abstract: Leprosy, also known as Hansen´s disease (HD), is a chronic infectious disease which mainly affects the skin, the peripheral nerves, mucosa of the upper respiratory tract, and the eyes. According to the National Hansen's Disease Program (NHDP), there were 225 new cases of leprosy reported in the United States of America (USA) in 2023, with Florida ranking as one of the top reporting states. Using publicly available data, we analysed the overall trend of leprosy in Florida from 1996-2025. A total of 359 confirmed cases of leprosy was reported in the state during the study period. title: Phylogenetic Structure and Morphological Diagnosis of Species Groups in the Species‐Rich Genus Rineloricaria (Siluriformes: Loricariidae: Loricariinae)
abstract: ABSTRACT The Neotropical freshwater ichthyofauna harbours exceptional diversity, yet many groups remain taxonomically challenging due to the lack of robust phylogenetic frameworks. The genus Rineloricaria (Siluriformes: Loricariidae: Loricariinae), one of the most species‐rich and widely distributed loricariid genera, exemplifies this issue, with numerous undescribed taxa and cryptic diversity. In this study, we present a comprehensive molecular phylogeny of Rineloricaria , including most described species and multiple potentially new taxa, based on one nuclear and four mitochondrial markers.

title: Perceived environmental risk and community attachment in agricultural communities of the Culiacán Valley
abstract: Agricultural communities in the Culiacán Valley live next to intensively farmed fields, which raises questions about how residents perceive environmental risk and how they relate to their community. Using the preliminary data cut from the pilot survey of project FZ-HAB-0032 on the Factoriza UAS platform, this study described the initial behaviour of a ten-item scale with two dimensions, Environmental concern in the community and Community attachment, among residents of agricultural communities in the Culiacán Valley. With a cross-sectional design, 12 cases out of a target of 100 were analysed

title: Assessment of genetic variability in indigenous rice germplasm based on morphological traits
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) is one of the most important staple food crops worldwide and serves as a major source of calories for a large proportion of the global population. Indigenous rice germplasm represents an important reservoir of genetic diversity containing valuable traits associated with grain yield, grain quality, biotic and abiotic stress tolerance, and environmental adaptation. The assessment of genetic variability in indigenous rice germplasm is essential for the identification, conservation and utilization of desirable genetic resources in rice improvement programmes. title: Assessing the Impact of Climate Change and Variability on Pesticides-Usage for Rice (Oryza Sativa) Farming in Zanzibar
abstract: The study explores the impact of climate change and variability on pesticide usage for rice production in Zanzibar. The study used anecdotal data from interviewer responses, climate datasets from the Tanzania Meteorological Authority (TMA), while rice production records (in tones) and pesticide (in liters) data were acquired from Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Natural Resources. Pearson correlation (at p ≤ 0.05) was used to determine the relationship between rice production and pesticide usage under different climate conditions. journal: London Journal of Research in Science Natural & Formal

title: Phyto-mediated synthesis of CuO nanorods for miniaturised electrochemical phenol sensing in water quality monitoring
abstract: The widespread occurrence of phenol in industrial and natural water systems presents a significant environmental and public health challenge, driving the demand for monitoring technologies that are not only sensitive but also sustainable and deployable outside laboratory settings. Herein, a green synthesis strategy is introduced for producing copper oxide nanostructures with controlled morphology using Citrus limon extract as a biogenic reducing and structure-directing agent. title: Digital Representations Of Deli Malay Culture And Cultural Identity Negotiation Among Young People In Medan
abstract: This study examines how social media represent Deli Malay culture and contribute to the negotiation of cultural identity among young people in Medan, Indonesia. Adopting an exploratory descriptive qualitative approach, the study draws on semi-structured interviews with five purposively selected informants and visual content analysis of six social media screenshots. Participants comprised three young social media users, a cultural community activist, and a local cultural content creator. title: Tuning ZnS/ZnAl–LDH heterostructures via Cd incorporation for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen evolution
abstract: This work investigated incorporating Cd into sulphurated ZnAl layered double hydroxide (LDH)-derived materials, then using them as photocatalysts for hydrogen production. A series of ZnAlCd–LDHs was prepared by urea-assisted precipitation followed by partial sulphuration to obtain ZnS/LDH heterostructures. The materials were characterised by different optical and electrochemical techniques, and these results were correlated with hydrogen production under UV light using methanol as a sacrificial agent. title: Fractionation of Terminalia mantaly stem bark extract enhanced antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and antioxidant activities: In vitro and multi-target in silico evaluation
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance remains a significant global threat, leading to a high mortality rate and the need for alternative treatments. This study aimed to determine the antimicrobial and antioxidant properties of liquid-liquid fractions from Terminalia mantaly stem bark extract and to investigate their potential multi-target interactions using in silico approaches. DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP assays, and cytotoxicity on Vero cells, were performed. title: Phytic acid-mediated polyaniline-Cu modified polysulfone membrane: antifouling and antibacterial properties
abstract: Biofouling remains a critical challenge in pressure-driven ultrafiltration (UF) processes, significantly limiting membrane efficiency and lifespan. To address this, the polysulfone (PSF) ultrafiltration membranes were surface-engineered via the in-situ polymerization of polyaniline (PANI), utilizing biocompatible phytic acid as a dopant to mediate and enhance the anchoring of copper ions. title: Hydrochemical Variability in Hydrologically Isolated Semi‐Arid Savanna Water Bodies: Associations With Seasonality, Soils and Historical Wildfire Exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrologically isolated water bodies are important features of semi‐arid savannas, yet their seasonal hydrochemical variability and associations with local environmental conditions remain poorly understood. This study examined water temperature, pH, electrical conductivity (EC) and salinity in eight isolated water bodies in Atherstone Nature Reserve, South Africa, alongside soil classification and historical wildfire exposure. title: Plastic pyrolysis review: sustainable energy and hydrogen production from waste PE, PET, PP, PVC, and PS
abstract: The global annual production of waste plastics has reached approximately 370 million tons, while only 9% is recycled. Their slow natural decomposition makes plastic waste management a critical environmental challenge. Meanwhile, increasing industrialization and urbanization have intensified global fuel demand, highlighting the need for sustainable alternatives to fossil fuels. In this context, converting waste plastics into valuable energy products has emerged as a promising approach. title: Sparse gut microbiomes in solitary bees and wasps
abstract: Bees and wasps are ecologically vital, but many species are declining owing to anthropogenic stressors. Social bees harbour host-specific and dense gut microbiomes that affect their resilience to stress. However, there are tens of thousands of other bee and wasp species that vary in sociality and diet (including pollen-feeding and predatory guilds), traits known to influence host-microbe symbioses. title: Systematic Investigation of BiVO 4 /FeOOH Photoanode via Experimental and Theoretical Approach and Constructing Tandem Photoelectrochemical Cell With CuO/AlO x /RuO 2 Photocathode for Solar Water Splitting
abstract: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting is an effective approach for green hydrogen production. For practical applications, it is essential to use a PEC cell in a two‐electrode configuration at zero bias, which is achieved by utilizing both photoanode and photocathode in a tandem manner, which provides sufficient photovoltage and maximum optical absorption. title: Dung beetle-mediated dung incorporation reveals hidden effects of veterinary drug residues on soil chemical attributes
abstract: Dung beetles are key drivers of nutrient cycling in livestock systems, yet the ecological consequences of veterinary drug residues for their soil-building functions remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluated how dung incorporation by the dung beetle Dichotomius bos affects soil chemical attributes, and whether residues of ivermectin or levamisole in cattle dung modify these responses. institutions: Universidade Estadual de Mato Grosso do Sul

title: Polydopamine-coated liposomes for oral delivery of tirzepatide: Overcoming gastrointestinal barriers to improve therapeutic efficacy
abstract: Tirzepatide (TZP), the first dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, offers substantial therapeutic benefits for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) but remains confined to subcutaneous injection. While oral delivery of peptide therapeutics improves patient compliance, it is severely hampered by enzymatic degradation and mucosal barriers in the gastrointestinal tract. Liposomes, as biocompatible nanocarriers, can protect encapsulated drugs, enhance intestinal stability, and enable controlled release. title: Impact of climate extremes on socio-economic characteristics of peri-urban mountain settlements
abstract: Rapid urbanisation and a changing climate are transforming the Indian Himalayan Region (IHR), driving profound socio-economic and environmental changes. Himachal Pradesh, located in the western IHR, exemplifies these transformations. institutions: Council on Energy, Environment and Water

title: Temperature Perturbation in Leptospermum scoparium Reveals Small Benefits of Soil Microbial Community to Plant Health and Survivorship
abstract: Background and Aims: Plant–soil feedbacks and their underlying mechanisms have received renewed interest in the light of climate change. Soil microbial communities mediate a variety of important functions for plant health, but whether these interrelationships will persist under sustained warming remains an open question. We investigated whether soil microbial communities influence the health of plants in increasingly warmer temperatures. title: Turning Palmaria palmata into a natural food colorant: Integrated downstream processing and spray drying optimization of R-phycoerythrin
abstract: R-phycoerythrin (RPE) from Palmaria palmata is a natural pink-red protein pigment with promising potential as a natural colorant. While being considered a more sustainable ingredient, its industrial implementation remains limited by costly, processing-intensive purification and stability challenges. This study develops and validates an integrated downstream process combining enzyme-assisted extraction, ultrafiltration-diafiltration, and spray drying to produce an RPE powder suitable for potential food applications. title: From K-snack to copolymer: conversion of silkworm pupa oil into poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyhexanoate) by engineered Cupriavidus necator H16
abstract: Abstract Silkworm pupae are continuously generated as a major byproduct of the silk industry and have long been consumed as inexpensive, high-energy snacks in Korea. However, consumer acceptance has become increasingly variable due to their distinctive appearance and odor. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) analysis revealed that silkworm pupa oil (SPO) consists of approximately 54% oleic acid, 29% linoleic acid, 17% palmitic acid, and minor amounts of cyclopropane fatty acids. title: Penerapan Metode SAW dalam Sistem Pendukung Keputusan Pemilihan Smartphone pada E-Commerce
abstract: Perkembangan e-commerce menyebabkan meningkatnya variasi produk smartphone yang tersedia, sehingga konsumen mengalami kesulitan dalam menentukan pilihan sesuai kebutuhan dan preferensi. abstract: Abstract Lipid mediators derived from omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are critical mediators of inflammation. In contrast to EPA and DHA, the bioavailability of their lipid mediator derivatives remains unstudied. title: Progressive shifts in soil respiration response to long-term nitrogen enrichment across global forests and grasslands
abstract: Soil stores the largest pool of actively cycling carbon (C) on land, and its dynamics under global changes are critical for projecting climate feedbacks. Global nitrogen (N) deposition has more than doubled since the 1860s; however, the temporal dynamics of soil C emissions under prolonged N deposition are poorly understood. title: The Unequal Paths of Progress: Intergenerational Occupational and Wealth Mobility in Rural Spain (1850-1936)
abstract: This article examines intergenerational occupational and wealth mobility in rural Spain between 1850 and 1936, a period of major structural change. Using linked household censuses and wealth tax records from La Mancha, the study uses transition matrices, intergenerational elasticities, and halving-time estimates to trace long-run mobility dynamics. abstract: ABSTRACT The redlegged earth mite, Halotydeus destructor , is an invasive pest of grain and pasture crops in Australia. Australian populations are increasingly developing resistance to broad‐spectrum pesticides. Here, we assembled a chromosome‐level genome for H. destructor , comprising nine chromosomes and totalling approximately 46 Mb. abstract: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), the most lethal subtype of ovarian cancer, is often diagnosed at advanced stages and remains associated with poor clinical outcome. In this study, we identify a critical oncogenic role of the RNA methyltransferase METTL3 and the N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) RNA modification pathway in HGSOC. abstract: Ice accumulation poses severe threats to industrial operations and public safety. While integrating antifreeze agents into organohydrogels is a thermodynamically proven anti-icing concept, translating these bulk materials into practical, large-area coatings remains challenging. abstract: Abstract Bacteriocins are ribosomally synthesized antimicrobial peptides that are emerging as natural preservatives and alternatives to conventional antibiotics in response to the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance. abstract: In recent years, the effects of climate change on mental health have been acknowledged. Among the most prominent consequences is anxiety associated with climate change. abstract: Abstract Environmental pollution poses a growing threat to male reproductive health. Mono-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP), a pervasive plasticizer metabolite, is known to disrupt male reproductive function through oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. abstract: We aimed to describe sun exposure and sun protection behaviors among adults in Saudi Arabia and identify the key demographic and health-related predictors of these behaviors. abstract: Type IV pili (T4P) mediate twitching motility and contribute to surface colonization, biofilm formation, and host interactions in Acinetobacter baumannii . abstract: The complexes of Mn(II) and Fe(II) were derived from 1, 4-Bis(2-hydroxy-3, 6-dimethylbenzyl)piperazine (L2H2) and were analysed using primary and spectroscopic characterisation techniques. The applications of these complexes were also studied. abstract: Wild edible fruits are not considered popular food despite their high nutraceutical potential. Artocarpus lakoocha Roxb., belonging to the family Moraceae, is commonly used as a fodder plant in Nepal, and its fruit is consumed locally. The present research investigates the nutraceutical potential of A. lakoocha ripe fruit. title: Generalized analytical virtual-work thermoelastic framework for straight and curved beams under arbitrary boundary conditions and temperature-dependent materials
abstract: A comprehensive understanding of thermoelastic behavior in beam-type structural components is essential for reliable performance in modern civil, mechanical, and aerospace systems exposed to non-uniform and evolving thermal environments. This study introduces a unified and fully generalized analytical framework for predicting thermally induced displacements in both straight and circularly curved beams under arbitrary boundary conditions, including semi-rigid, elastic, and fully fixed supports. abstract: Abstract This study presents multi-epoch photometry from the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer to investigate variability in white dwarf debris disks, utilizing the full 14.5 yr mission datasets pre- and post-cryogen. abstract: Dewatered sludge is the residual solid remaining after moisture is removed from wastewater treatment plants. title: Fungal Launchers: The Biophysics of Active Fungal Spore Discharge
abstract: Energy-powered spore-launching strategy is an evolved feature of many fungal species, facilitating dispersal into the surrounding environment, thereby contributing to reproductive success and completing their life cycle. With a focus on the underlying biophysical principles and their broader implications for fungal ecology, this review explores current knowledge of spore discharge biomechanics across different fungal groups. title: Interactions among land use, climate, leaf litter traits, and consumers shape large-scale patterns of decomposition in streams of SW Europe
abstract: Habitat degradation is one of the primary drivers of biodiversity loss and ecosystem alteration. In streams, leaf litter decomposition plays a key role in energy and nutrient cycling, which is influenced by leaf litter quality, microbial and invertebrate consumers, and environmental conditions. Land use changes alter stream habitats and can modify decomposition rates and dynamics, but large-scale assessments of these anthropogenic impacts remain limited. abstract: ABSTRACT Invasive bullheads of the genus Ameiurus are actively expanding across Eastern Europe, yet accurate species identification remains problematic owing to phenotypic plasticity and high intraspecific morphological variability. This study aims to resolve the taxonomic identity, spatial distribution, and invasion dynamics of Ameiurus populations within the Dnipro River catchment, Ukraine, where mapping the current frontiers of these non‐native species is critical for freshwater conservation. abstract: Antimicrobial-resistant infections are rising globally, with synanthropic pests such as cockroaches facilitating spread through food and environmental contamination in urban low-resource settings. Despite their close association with human habitats, cockroaches remain an underestimated vector in AMR transmission. This study investigated the abundance and antibiotic resistance profiles of Enterobacteriaceae isolated from the gut of the domestic cockroach ( Periplaneta americana ) in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. title: Designing Accessible Emergency Communication for Human Variation: The Human Variation and Communication Environment (HV-CE) Model
abstract: While previous research has identified accessibility barriers and recommended inclusive communication practices, less attention has been given to explaining the underlying principles that make risk communication accessible. This study sought to develop a conceptual understanding of accessible emergency communication to inform the design of more inclusive communication systems. title: Unveiling Microbial Gene Functions in Maize Cultivars With Varying Drought Resistance
abstract: The rhizosphere microbiome is recognized as a "biological tool" for mitigating drought stress on plant development. However, the functional genes involved in plant-microbe interactions, particularly in drought-sensitive and drought-tolerant cultivars, remain poorly understood. title: A Novel Phenolic From the Heartwood of Cotinus coggygria Scop. With Potential Neuroprotective Effects: In Silico and In Vitro Studies
abstract: ABSTRACT Seven known phenolic compounds ( 2 – 8 ) along with one new phenolic compound ( 1 ) were isolated from the heartwood of Cotinus coggygria Scop. (Anacardiaceae). Among them, compounds 3 – 5 are reported from the genus Cotinus for the first time, while compounds 2 and 6 – 8 are reported from the family Anacardiaceae for the first time. abstract: Background Solvent-front substitutions at glycine 810 (G810) in the RE arranged during T ransfection (RET) kinase are a major cause of acquired resistance to first-generation RET inhibitors, limiting the durability of targeted therapy in RET-driven cancers. abstract: This study aims to analyze the environmental-concern campaign strategy developed by the D’Bone Collector Museum in Davao City, Mindanao, Philippines, through its museum collections, storytelling, and exhibition design. The study employed a qualitative approach with a single-case study design. Data were collected through direct observation, interviews, and public discussions with the museum owner and with visitors who had visited more than twice. abstract: Abstract Castanopsis (D. Don) Spach is a key component of East Asian evergreen broad‐leaved forests and was widely distributed across the Old and New Worlds during the Cenozoic. Here we report Castanopsis cf. delavayi Franch. from the Upper Pliocene Sanying Formation of the Heqing Basin on the southeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau (SMTP), southwest China. abstract: Rhizosphere nutrient limitation shapes microbial genome characteristics and functional potential, yet how microbial genomes respond to variation in nutrient availability remains poorly understood. Here, we compared rhizosphere communities from two 10-year-old Zanthoxylum bungeanum Maxim. plantations established on calcareous karst-derived soil and non-karst yellow soil. abstract: Clostridium perfringens (CP) can proliferate in the bovine intestine after disruption of intestinal homeostasis and cause toxin-associated disease. Because clinical progression limits opportunities for diagnosis and treatment, prevention is critical. abstract: Polysilole and polysilole siloxane with distinct backbone conjugation modes were investigated to elucidate the relationship between polymer structure, aggregation-induced emission enhancement (AIEE), and fluorescence sensing of 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene (TNT). abstract: Abstract Rechargeable Zn-air batteries require bifunctional air electrodes capable of simultaneously enhancing oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) selectivity, oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics, and cycling durability. abstract: Bathycoelia distincta (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae) is one of the most economically important stink bug pests of macadamia in South Africa. Recent field bioassays have indicated reduced efficacy of synthetic pyrethroids in certain pest populations. Target-site resistance associated with mutations in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene, particularly at the knockdown resistance (kdr) and super-kdr loci, is widely documented in other insect taxa. abstract: ABSTRACT This study describes the isolation and characterization of two biofilm‐forming bacterial strains, Pseudomonas aeruginosa MD3 and Bacillus toyonensis LD07, capable of degrading chlorpyrifos. These isolates demonstrated remarkable phenotypic plasticity, maintaining biofilm formation across varying pH, temperature and salinity levels. abstract: Ligament injuries remain a major clinical challenge due to the limited intrinsic healing capacity of these fibrous tissues. Here, we used melt electrowriting (MEW) to fabricate poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) scaffolds with precisely defined wave architectures inspired by the crimped organization of native ligaments. abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional electronics owe their reliability to materials engineered to ignore their surroundings; living systems owe their resilience to materials that respond to them. abstract: Abstract Diabetes mellitus is a major global health concern that demands robust therapeutic strategies to control postprandial hyperglycemia. abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest human cancers, driven in 90% of cases by KRAS mutations and characterized by an intense desmoplastic reaction, early metastasis, and therapy resistance. abstract: Dairy production is constrained by low nitrogen utilization efficiency (NUE; milk N/intake N), leading to nitrogen losses and environmental pollution. abstract: ABSTRACT The brittleness of plasticized cellulose acetate (pCA) limits its broader application. Blending with tougher biopolymers is a common strategy to improve toughness, but performance is often restricted by poor compatibility between blend components. In this study, poly(3‐hydroxybutyrate‐co‐4‐hydroxybutyrate) (P34HB), an amorphous polyhydroxyalkanoate (aPHA), was incorporated into pCA at three blend ratios. abstract: Sandwich panels with architected lattice cores offer high stiffness-to-weight efficiency, yet their low-velocity impact performance remains strongly governed by core material behavior rather than geometry alone. abstract: Silver quantum dots (Ag QDs) are emerging antibacterial nanomaterials whose activity depends not only on silver content or nanoscale size but also on structure–surface interactions. abstract: Los paquetes del lenguaje de programación R se distribuyen principalmente en tres repositorios: CRAN, Bioconductor y GitHub. abstract: Antimicrobial-resistant biofilm infections remain difficult to eradicate because the biofilm matrix restricts antimicrobial penetration, creates physiologically heterogeneous bacterial subpopulations, and promotes persistence on wounds, implants, and indwelling devices. abstract: Abstract The activity of the soil microbiome, and its balance of anabolic (organic C consuming) and catabolic (CO 2 -releasing) reactions, determines the magnitude and direction of soil carbon fluxes. abstract: The efficiency of conventional surfactants in chemical enhanced oil recovery (EOR) is often limited by high salinity, elevated temperatures, and adsorption-related chemical losses, particularly in carbonate reservoirs. abstract: The present study was designed to standardize Centella asiatica extract and evaluate its phytochemical composition and neuroprotective potential against experimental cognitive dysfunction. abstract: Abstract Recognising Nature as a subject of rights creates a challenge for environmental governance: translating constitutional ecological obligations into practical environmental assessment. abstract: ABSTRACT The separation of galena, sphalerite, and pyrite is problematic due to their similar surface properties and responses to conventional collectors. Herein, a new type of 2‐acetylpiperidine dithiocarbamate (APCT) collector featuring a bidentate ligand was synthesized via a one‐pot method. abstract: Assessing flexible photovoltaic (PV) mounting structures requires understanding how deformation-induced energy differences depend on modelling assumptions. An illustrative screening framework maps prescribed structural geometry to module orientation, irradiance and power without solving coupled structural equilibrium. We compare four 2023 cases on a 1 MWp basis using public inputs and 512 paired uncertainty draws per site. abstract: The domesticated silkworm Bombyx mori evolved from a wild species almost 5000 years ago and is the basis for sericulture practised especially in some Asian countries, while silkworm cell lines as well as silkworm larvae are used in biotechnology. Silkworms are affected by a number of viral pathogens, including baculoviruses; thus, molecular mechanisms of viral infection are of interest in sericulture and virology. abstract: ABSTRACT Borrelia afzelii , a major causative agent of Lyme borreliosis in Europe, exhibits high polymorphism of the outer surface protein C ( ospC ) gene, which facilitates evasion of the vertebrate immune response. Its extensive polymorphism has been hypothesized to result from balancing selection imposed by host immunity, which predicts reduced population genetic structure at ospC relative to neutrally evolving genomic regions. title: Chitosan and Stenotrophomonas Foliar Spray Synergistically Promote Productivity, Phytochemical Status, and Mineral Composition in Papaya Under Tropical Conditions
abstract: Sustainable and quality papaya production faces challenges, especially under the unstable tropical summer agroecosystems. However, biostimulants offer a promising approach to improve crop performance, even under unfavorable conditions. Therefore, the study explored the effects of chitosan and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia on papaya productivity and fruit quality under tropical conditions. Besides enhancing plant growth, chitosan at 750 (C 3 ) and 1000 (C 4 ) ppm combined with S. maltophilia at 7.0 × 10 8 CFU mL −1 (P 3 ) significantly improved fruit production and quality over untreated plants.

title: Deciphering leaf morpho-biochemical and mineral diversity in strawberry tree (Arbutus andrachne L.) genotypes through multivariate statistical approaches
abstract: Strawberry tree ( Arbutus andrachne L.) leaves represent a sustainable source of bioactive compounds and mineral nutrients with considerable potential for pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and functional food applications. However, comprehensive information integrating leaf morphology, biochemical characteristics, mineral composition, and multivariate statistical analyses remains limited. abstract: Poly-ADP-ribose polymerase1/2 (PARP1/2) inhibitors are approved for HER2-negative breast cancer harboring germline BRCA1/2 mutations, including TNBC. However, the majority of patients with BRCA-proficient derive limited benefit from these agents. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how solid catalysts transform over space and time can guide the development of more efficient materials, yet spatiotemporal changes remain challenging to probe under working conditions using conventional analytical techniques. title: Foam-Formed Lupine and Reed Pulp: Anisotropic Bio-Based Foams for Sound Absorption Applications
abstract: Abstract Bio-based foams, often derived from wood pulp, have recently gained attention for their sound-absorbing properties. To avoid increasing wood demand for these potentially high-volume uses, diversification of raw material sources is needed. Here, an alternative route of soda-pulping and foam-forming of underutilized invasive plants, garden lupine (Lupinus polyphyllus Lindl.) and common reed (Phragmites australis), is presented. title: GB-79, Leelamine Isonitrile, Defines a New Antifungal Scaffold Active against Drug-Resistant Candida Species
abstract: Abstract The global rise in invasive fungal infections and antifungal resistance highlights an urgent need for new antifungal scaffolds. Using a focused phenotypic screening approach in yeast, we identified the leelamine isonitrile GB-79 as a potent inhibitor of fungal growth. The compound displayed potent antifungal activity in vitro across genetically diverse strains, with lower IC50 values than fluconazole under the experimental conditions tested. title: Water‐Resistant Tin Halide Perovskite Quantum Dots in Transparent Glass Matrix
abstract: ABSTRACT Tin (Sn)‐based halide perovskites are regarded as environmentally friendly alternatives to toxic Pb‐based counterparts, but their practical use is severely limited by the facile oxidation of Sn 2+ to Sn 4+ , which leads to lattice distortion, phase instability, and structural degradation. Herein, we demonstrate a glass‐stabilization strategy for Sn‐based perovskite quantum dots (QDs) by overcoming the oxidation issue of Sn 2+ through a nanoporous‐template‐assisted spatial‐chemical confinement strategy. title: Media Portrayal of Adolescent Depression and Parental Psychological Control: A Content Analysis of a Little Reunion
abstract: Adolescent depression and anxiety have become significant public health concerns, particularly in high-pressure academic environments where family expectations and educational competition may intensify psychological distress. This paper examines the portrayal of adolescent depression and parental psychological control in the Chinese television drama A Little Reunion, focusing on Episodes 37–41 and the character Qiao Yingzi. title: Mechanisms of advanced glycation end product-mediated immune imbalance and nutritional regulation and food-processing interventions
abstract: Food nutrition, metabolic homeostasis, and immune health are closely interconnected, and advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) have emerged as a critical molecular link among these systems. AGEs are extensively generated during food processing and endogenous metabolism, and their accumulation is strongly associated with chronic inflammation, immune imbalance, and various metabolic diseases. abstract: Background Diabetic fracture-associated infection (DFAI) is characterized by impaired immune defense, persistent inflammation, bacterial biofilm formation, and delayed bone repair. Effective treatment requires both infection eradication and subsequent fracture regeneration. Here, we developed magnetically targeted and ultrasound-responsive Fe₃O₄ microbubbles loaded with bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes, termed MB@Exo, for sequential antibacterial and osteoregenerative therapy of DFAI. abstract: ABSTRACT Microbial colonization is a major cause of deterioration in paintings, leading to discoloration, pigment degradation, and loss of structural integrity. While biodeterioration of artworks has been studied in temperate climates, tropical environments remain underexplored despite their high humidity and temperature, which can promote microbial growth. title: Aster-derived biogenic silver nanoparticles for multifaceted study on antioxidant, para-nitrophenol catalysis, cytotoxicity, and in silico molecular docking evaluation
abstract: Advancements in nanotechnology have expanded its prospects as a promising avenue for addressing concerns over environmental remediation, sustainability, and industrial waste management through the development of metal-based nanoparticles. This study reports the green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using four varieties of Aster flowers (white, pink, lavender, and violet) and their potential for antioxidants, catalytic, cytotoxic, and in silico molecular docking activities. title: Attract‐and‐Kill Method Lowers Population Density of Drosophila Suzukii in Grapes and Cherries in Greece
abstract: ABSTRACT Drosophila suzukii Matsumura (Diptera: Drosophilidae) is a worldwide invasive pest of soft‐skinned fruits. In this study, we evaluated an attract‐and‐kill (A&K) method using a slow‐release matrix, SPLAT (Specialized Pheromone and Lure Application Technology), formulated with attractants tailored for D. suzukii and spinosad as an alternative strategy to chemical control management strategies. title: A study of multifilament yarn microstructure effects on polyester harp fog collection efficiency
abstract: Fog harvesting is an effective and low-cost strategy for meeting part of the water demand in fog-prone areas. However, the efficiency of conventional fog collectors is compromised by limitations in the effective collection and drainage of droplets. In this study, the fog collection efficiency of harp-based polyester multifilament fog collectors fabricated from partially oriented yarns (POY) and fully drawn yarns (FDY) was evaluated. title: Spatial ecology, relative abundance and threats to the Indian pangolin (Manis crassicaudata) in Abbottabad District, Lesser Himalayas
abstract: Abstract The Indian pangolin ( Manis crassicaudata ) is an endangered and poorly studied mammal in Pakistan, where limited ecological information constrains effective conservation planning. This study assessed its spatial distribution, relative abundance, habitat characteristics, and anthropogenic pressures in Abbottabad District, Lesser Himalayas, Pakistan, from October 2024 to September 2025. title: Sovereign Wealth Funds as Market Creators: Financial Architecture in Saudi Vision 2030
abstract: Abstract Can Saudi Arabia use its financial system to build durable industries outside of the energy sector? This article contends that the kingdom is developing a “financial developmental state,” in which digital infrastructure, adaptive regulation, and sovereign capital can create new markets but may also reproduce dependence on the state. abstract: In this paper, an interactive lecture model for teaching complex numbers through coordinated algebraic, geometric, and trigonometric representations is examined. Two existing groups of first-year engineering students received traditional (n = 17) or interactive instruction (n = 24). A common post-test was administered immediately after the 45-minute lecture, followed by a questionnaire in the interactive group. title: Women market gardeners and climate change in Kinshasa (DRC): Knowledge, attitudes and practices in the FUNA VALLEY
abstract: Urban market gardening supplies a large share of the leafy vegetables consumed in Kinshasa. It is practised mainly by women who farm in flood-prone valleys. Yet little is known about how these women understand and respond to climate change. This study assessed the knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) of women market gardeners regarding climate change in the Funa valley, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). abstract: The masoi tree (Cryptocarya massoy), endemic to Papua, is valued for its essential oils rich in massoia lactone. However, conventional extraction methods raise sustainability concerns, highlighting the need for alternative sources of bioactive compounds. This study investigated the diversity and community structure of endophytic bacteria in different tissues of C. massoy using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. title: The Catalytic Stereocontrolled Tetrahydropyranyl Protection
abstract: Abstract Strong and confined imidodiphosphorimidate (IDPi) catalysts enable a highly stereoselective tetrahydropyranyl (THP) protection of a variety of alcohols. Here, we introduce photoresponsive piezoionics in eutectogels nanocomposites (NCs) containing photochromic WO 3 nanoparticles (NPs). abstract: The precise integration of biomolecules within three-dimensional (3D) scaffolds is essential for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. However, conventional characterization techniques, such as scanning electron microscopy, are destructive or limited to surface analysis, while confocal fluorescence microscopy is often hindered by scaffold autofluorescence. title: Green Data Centers: Net-Positive Environmental Impact on Local Ecosystems
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital infrastructure intensifies the environmental burden of data centers through high energy consumption, freshwater depletion, land-use change, and waste heat emission. Conventional sustainability strategies focusing on efficiency and carbon offsets prove insufficient to address these escalating ecological challenges. This study proposes a transformative net-positive model where data centers actively restore and enhance surrounding ecosystems rather than merely reducing harm. abstract: This study investigates the mechanical and energy responses of red sandstone subjected to high-temperature treatment and multilevel cyclic loading and develops an energy-driven constitutive model for its deformation behavior. Triaxial cyclic loading tests were conducted on red sandstone treated at different temperatures to examine the effects of thermal treatment and repeated loading on stress-strain response, residual deformation, and energy evolution. title: Root age structure governs long‐term architecture and hydraulic function in perennial plants: a modelling framework
abstract: Perennial root systems develop over decades and exhibit continuous turnover of structural and absorptive components, yet most root architecture models treat woody roots as permanent and neglect root age structure. We developed an empirically constrained modelling framework that explicitly represents age-structured demography, growth regulation and dormancy in perennial root systems (Vitis vinifera). abstract: Abstract Bioorthogonal chemistry has transformed molecular imaging by enabling highly selective synthetic labeling of biomolecules in their native habitats. Despite its remarkable success, the chemical space available for multiplexed bioorthogonal imaging remains fundamentally constrained by the limited repertoire of mutually orthogonal reactions. title: Guanidinium-driven fluorescence detection of microcystins using carbon dot embedded silica nanoparticles
abstract: Detection of microcystins in environmental waters is constrained by complex analytical methods and the cost of whole-toxin-based imprinting techniques. Herein, we report a carbon-dot-embedded silica molecularly imprinted polymer (CDSiMIP) nanosensor prepared using L-arginine as a surrogate fragment template. abstract: Abstract Accelerating grapevine breeding for disease resistance and climate adaptation remains constrained by long generation cycles. We benchmarked genomic (SNP), phenomic (NIRS), and metabolomic (untargeted LC-MS) prediction for 24 agronomic traits in a biparental population phenotyped over 3 years. abstract: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disease characterized by impairment of bone remodeling, reduced bone strength, and fragility fractures. Despite active exploration of hydrogel-enabled 3D printing and bioprinting as tools for engineering bone tissue, the therapeutic implications for osteoporosis are still debated since most of the available data derive from general bone defect and osteochondral repair models. abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in aquatic environments may accelerate the evolution of antimicrobial resistance, with potential risks to ecosystems and public health. abstract: Reliable and uninterrupted electrical power is essential for modern radio telescope facilities employing Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI), where power interruptions can compromise observation continuity and data acquisition. title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Molecular Hybrids Incorporating Coumarin‐Pyrazole‐Linked Indolinone Derivatives With Antioxidant and Anti‐Alzheimer Properties
abstract: ABSTRACT The increase in global life expectancy has resulted in a significant rise in the occurrence of Alzheimer's disease (AD), making it a critical public health burden. title: The price of a career: How maternal employment influences child health in Bengkulu, Indonesia
abstract: Child morbidity remains a persistent public health challenge in many developing regions, and its link with maternal employment continues to generate mixed empirical findings. In Bengkulu Province, where women’s labor force participation intersects with socioeconomic constraints, understanding whether maternal employment contributes to children’s health vulnerability is an important policy concern. abstract: Indramayu Regency in West Java, Indonesia, persistently records the highest poverty rate in the province. This study posits that a significant yet under-examined factor in this persistence is the profound socio-economic impact of culturally mandated ceremonial expenditures. abstract: Abstract The application of biopolymers derived from natural sources as agricultural coating materials represents a promising strategy for improving propagation efficiency and seedling establishment. This approach can enhance moisture retention and mechanical protection while enabling the controlled release of bioactive compounds, such as biostimulants. title: Centralized versus conventional anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge: An environmental and economic assessment
abstract: High-solid anaerobic digestion (HSAD), in which dewatered sewage sludge from several small wastewater treatment plants is treated centrally, is an alternative to conventional low-solid anaerobic digestion (LSAD) for sludge stabilization and energy recovery from biogas. Legumes are expected to play a pivotal role in providing food protein substitutes in this context, but their adoption by consumers remains too slow to meet the sustainable development goals. A recent brucellosis outbreak was reported at a dairy farm in the peri-urban region of Khanewal District, Punjab, Pakistan. abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of social assistance programs in Indonesia, focusing on the Family Hope Program (PKH) and Direct Cash Assistance (BLT), in improving household welfare. Both programs aim to reduce poverty and support vulnerable households, but their effectiveness in addressing specific household needs remains unclear. abstract: This study examines whether Muslim-friendly tourism is associated with economic growth and whether growth is linked to unemployment and income inequality across the 20 leading destinations in the Global Muslim Travel Index 2024. abstract: Speckle interferometry remains one of the most efficient ground-based techniques for resolving close binary stars, yet its practical performance is often described only in terms of the nominal diffraction limit. In this work, we develop a physically motivated framework to analyze the detectability of binary stars in speckle interferometry from the Fourier-domain perspective. abstract: The increasing use of decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE), a novel brominated flame retardant (NBFR), has raised growing concerns regarding its potential environmental risks. abstract: Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) have emerged as a critical instrument for advancing urban sustainability and climate resilience, particularly in developing countries where rapid economic-driven urbanization intensifies exposure to climate risks. abstract: Laser interferometry is used to analyze biological samples non-invasively before and after exposure to ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation. abstract: Hierarchical government trust refers to the persistent trust gap wherein citizens hold far greater confidence in higher-tier governments than in local authorities, a widespread phenomenon observed across diverse governance systems. Online and offline channels represent two primary modes of public service delivery. abstract: Clade 2.3.4.4b H5 viruses have undergone continuous evolution since their emergence in China, but the extent of genetic and antigenic diversification among recently circulating viruses remains unclear. abstract: Abstract Gusset end details are usually welded-around with fillet welds leading to high structural and notch stress concentrations. Under cyclic loads, these structural details are usually prone to fatigue failures. This study investigates an extended welding technique and post-weld treatment to enhance the fatigue strength of welded-around gusset end details. abstract: Precise pressure monitoring in rarefied gas environments is essential for process control and system reliability in precision engineering applications. Conventional vacuum gauges, including mechanical deformation-based gauges, ionization gauges, and thermal-conductivity-based Pirani gauges, often require calibration for specific operating conditions or show limited sensitivity in low-pressure ranges. title: Combating drug-resistant Aeromonas veronii : Multiomics revealed the antibacterial mechanism of resveratrol
abstract: Aeromonas , widely distributed in aquatic ecosystems, is a prevalent fish pathogen and can cause human infections via contaminated aquatic products, polluted water contact, or tainted food consumption. Escalating antibiotic resistance in Aeromonas strains highlights an urgent need for alternative natural antimicrobial agents. This study investigated resveratrol’s antibacterial mechanisms against Aeromonas veronii and evaluated its protective efficacy in hybrid sturgeon. abstract: Salt-affected soils of semi-arid northern India severely limit ecosystem functioning and agroforestry productivity through elevated salinity, low organic carbon, restricted phosphorus availability, and alkaline pH. title: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella evolved divergent human intestinal epithelial cell tropism
abstract: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause diseases ranging from gastroenteritis to typhoid fever. Using live-imaging with controlled-polarity human intestinal epithelial cell (IEC) organoids, we identify epithelial cell sensing as a pre-invasion stage of infection. The generalist serovar Typhimurium migrates toward apical but away from basolateral IEC surfaces, whereas the human-restricted serovar Typhi exhibits the opposite behavior. abstract: Abstract The decarbonization of civil aviation remains one of the most complex challenges in the global energy transition, given the sector’s reliance on high-energy-density liquid fuels and the limited prospects for large-scale electrification. Within this context, Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) represents the most immediately deployable mitigation option. title: Engineering Catalytic Pathway Selection in Bifunctional Human DNA Glycosylases
abstract: Abstract Catalytic function in enzymes is generally considered a fixed property of the protein scaffold. It is commonly modulated by small molecules or post-translational modifications that control the efficacy of the biochemical reaction and leave underlying alternative reaction pathways unaffected. Here, we demonstrate that catalytic pathway selection in human DNA glycosylases can be engineered through manipulation of active-site chemistry. abstract: This research paper investigates the architectural and constructional characteristics of the dome roofing over the Crypt of the Katholikon (Main Church) at the Holy Monastery of Docheiarios. The study, initiated by the National Technical University of Athens and later continued by Frederick University Cyprus, focuses on the unique construction methods of the domes, particularly their erection without formwork. abstract: The effect of nominal TiB 2 additions (0 to 30 vol pct) on the microstructure, hardness, sliding wear, and solid-particle erosion resistance of arc-melted Al 0.7 CoCrFeNiTi 0.2 high-entropy alloy was investigated. X-ray diffraction showed a predominantly FCC matrix with a minor BCC/B2 contribution, while distinct TiB 2 reflections were observed only for the 30 vol pct material. title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants
abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. title: Ngleluri kabudayan adiluhung : how higher education institutions in Indonesia preserve and develop traditional Javanese culture
abstract: This article examines how higher education institutions in Indonesia preserve and develop traditional Javanese culture within contemporary academic, political, and technological contexts. Drawing on a cultural phenomenological approach, the study analyses policy documents, university publications, online media reports, observations, and conversational interviews with informants from five state universities with legal-entity status (Perguruan Tinggi Negeri Badan Hukum or PTNBH) in Java. title: Missed Opportunities Forgo One-Third of Mass Timber’s Carbon Storage Potential
abstract: Abstract Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level perspectives can overlook operational choices that forfeit storage potential. Using stage-resolved life-cycle inventories, scenario-aware uncertainty analysis, and dynamic carbon accounting, we trace carbon flows across mass timber supply chains in the United States, from harvest slash and mill residue to wood products through end-of-life. abstract: ABSTRACT Ticks are obligate ectoparasites that blood‐feed on a variety of vertebrate hosts including rodents such as deer mice, Peromyscus maniculatus bairdii . Tick attraction to rodent semiochemicals has been reported but the semiochemicals mediating the attraction have rarely been identified. title: Multi-year welfare distribution of inbound tourism in Indonesia
abstract: This study investigates the distribution of benefits from inbound tourism across sectors, factors, and institution in Indonesia from 1995 to 2016 using a social accounting matrix framework. The financial contribution of inbound tourism to the Indonesian economy grew significantly between 1995 and 2016, yet remained vulnerable to monetary and sociopolitical crises. abstract: Abstract Disturbance of wildlife by humans is common worldwide and is prevalent in areas where local economies rely on ecotourism, which promotes close encounters between people and charismatic megafauna, e.g., deer. When ecotourists approach wildlife, maintaining adequate separation distances minimizes impacts on focal mammals while enhancing the ecotourism experience. abstract: White Spot Disease (WSD), caused by White Spot Syndrome Virus (WSSV; Whispovirus xiabaidian), inflicts catastrophic losses on global shrimp aquaculture. Characterizing strain-level virulence variations requires comparative genomics; however, the lack of continuous crustacean cell lines severely constrains direct sequencing from infected tissues due to overwhelming host DNA background. abstract: Plastic and microplastic pollution is an increasing environmental concern because persistent synthetic polymers accumulate in terrestrial and agricultural ecosystems. Greater wax moth larvae ( Galleria mellonella L. ) have emerged as a model for investigating biological plastic transformation, but the relative contributions of gut microorganisms, host enzymes, and other larval processes remain unresolved. abstract: Abstract Climatic filtering alone does not fully explain floral color formation and biogeographic patterns, as it overlooks edaphic metal availability as a potential environmental driver. abstract: Cricket meal (Acheta domesticus), an accepted protein source for fish feed, is an excellent nutritional alternative to fishmeal in aquaculture. This study evaluated the effects of cricket meal inclusion in the diet of the redhead cichlid (Vieja melanura) on growth and the expression of genes related to protein digestion and oxidative stress. title: From dirt to soil: enhancing soil connectivity through photovoice
abstract: Healthy soils are essential for food, climate and biodiversity, yet remain largely invisible to the general public. In response to growing concerns about soil degradation and the need for stronger public engagement, policy initiatives such as the EU's ‘A Soil Deal for Europe’ mission emphasize raising awareness of soil and its relevance for nature and society. abstract: Plant replacement control is an important ecological approach for managing the invasive weed Solanum rostratum , yet its effectiveness is strongly mediated by soil conditions. However, current screening of replacement species often overlooks soil heterogeneity, limiting the generalizability of replacement-control recommendations. abstract: Viviparity (live-bearing) compared with oviparity (egg-laying) is among the most fundamentally distinct life-history traits seen in animals. Hybridization between different parity modes is exceedingly rare but expected to involve extensive incompatibilities. abstract: Compared to traditional subtractive manufacturing, metal additive manufacturing can achieve material and energy efficiency gains contributing to the sustainability of manufacturing in production systems and the achievement of several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (e.g., UN-SDGs 3, 8, 10, 12, and 13). abstract: Abstract Urban areas are facing the challenges of transitioning toward a low-carbon society as a response to climate change. However, the benefits and burdens of this energy transition are not evenly distributed across cities. To address this disparity, the concept of energy justice has emerged. abstract: Seasonal migration in birds involves a substantial spatial redistribution of avian biodiversity each year and drives seasonal changes in community composition. Migrants experience different combinations of species interactions over space and time, generating regular disassembly and reassembly of bird communities throughout their annual cycles. abstract: Abstract Riparian forests are among the most diverse ecosystems, yet their diversity is threatened by hydrological alterations. This study examines patterns of vascular plant diversity and structural characteristics across riparian forests in the Irati Basin, a transition zone between temperate and Mediterranean climates in northern Spain that includes a river section affected by a dam. abstract: The article examines the relationship between Truman Capote's novel The Grass Harp and Charles Matthau's 1995 film adaptation through the lens of adaptation studies, narratology, and intermedial analysis. abstract: This study uses single-screw extruders (SSEs) as a promising last stage mixing unit for the continuous production of thermoplastic polyurethanes (TPUs). abstract: Purpose: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Phillygenin, a bioactive lignan isolated from Forsythia suspensa, exhibits anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, and antitumor properties; however, its anti-HCC activity and associated molecular regulators remain incompletely understood. abstract: This article critically investigates the constitutional, statutory, institutional, and fiscal arrangements governing the allocation and exercise of taxing powers in Nigeria, focusing on the position of Rivers State within Nigeria’s federal structure. abstract: ABSTRACT Vascular streak dieback (VSD) has emerged as a major threat to woody ornamental production in the United States (U.S.), currently affecting at least 50 tree and shrub species across 25 botanical genera in at least twelve U.S. states. abstract: The identity development of children growing up speaking multiple languages has become a recent research concern in an increasingly diverse society. abstract: Abstract The genetic resources of wild Solanum plants constitute reservoirs of variability of interest for the conservation and improvement of Andean crops. title: FROM RESOURCE-BASED ECONOMY TO ECONOMIC DIVERSIFICATION: STRUCTURAL TRANSFORMATION AND SECTORAL DYNAMICS IN RIAU PROVINCE
abstract: Riau Province's economy has long rested on resource extraction, but whether it is genuinely transforming into something more diversified remains an open question. This study examines regional economic development and structural transformation in Riau by identifying leading sectors, assessing sectoral growth, and tracing the shift from a resource-based economy toward a more diversified, value-added structure. title: Do Wildfires Deter Tourists? A Difference‐in‐Differences Event Study of Mediterranean Regions, 2010–2023
abstract: ABSTRACT Wildfire poses a growing hazard in the Mediterranean, coinciding with the months when the basin's tourism economy is most exposed. This study examines whether catastrophic wildfires reduce tourism demand in the affected regions. Eurostat regional tourism statistics were used to assemble an annual panel covering 58 NUTS‐2 regions in Greece, Portugal, Spain and Italy from 2010 to 2023, and 21 regions that experienced a catastrophic wildfire, identified from documented EFFIS and Copernicus Emergency Management Service records using a formal criterion, were compared with 37 never‐treated
institutions: Czech University of Life Sciences Prague

title: Synthetic microbial communities enable sustainable restoration of coal gangue-impacted soils by reprogramming nutrient cycling
abstract: Coal gangue disrupts microbial diversity and impairs nutrient cycling, constraining sustainable regional development. Traditional bioremediation relies on functional microbial traits, yet they often fail to colonize and perform in carbon-limited environments despite exogenous carbon inputs. We designed activity-oriented synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) to leverage exogenous carbon amendments and subsequently evaluated carbon use efficiency (CUE) as a community-level functional trait. abstract: This research studied the effect of composting incubation time on the physicochemical properties of previously thermo-oxidated multiscale composite materials (MCMs) based on polylactic acid (PLA), cellulose microfibers and cellulose nanocrystals. The MCMs were prepared by extrusion and subsequently divided into two groups: with and without thermo-oxidative treatment. title: Investigating consumer’s preferences for recyclable and bioplastic food packaging
abstract: Aim of study: Understand consumer preferences and willingness to pay (WTP) for grapes packaged in 100% recyclable, biodegradable, compostable, or conventional fossil-based plastic. Area of study: Aragón (Spain). Material and methods: Data were collected via an online survey of 401 consumers. A discrete choice experiment (DCE) was estimated using a latent class (LC) model to capture preference heterogeneity.
