title: Insights into the Drosophila Serotonin Transporter: An Ionic Switch as a Regulator of Transporter Conformation
abstract: Abstract Monoamine concentrations in the synaptic cleft are primarily regulated by reuptake through monoamine transporters (MATs) located in presynaptic terminals and axonal membranes. In the serotonin transporter (SERT), the canonical alternating-access cycle is mediated by Na+, Cl−, and the substrate in a 1:1:1 stoichiometry. However, structural studies of human SERT have revealed a second Na+ binding site, whose precise role in the transport cycle remains unresolved. title: Exploratory screening of faba bean germplasm for winter adaptation and seed quality in Northwestern Europe
abstract: Abstract Faba bean ( Vicia faba L.) is a high-protein legume suited to Northwestern Europe, yet adoption is hindered by limited winter survival, acute cold events, and seed anti-nutritional factors notably vicine and convicine (VC) that constrain food use despite high protein content. We conducted a two-year, two-season study in Belgium (2022–2024) directly comparing winter versus spring accessions via field phenotyping, intact-seed NIRS (n=343), and standardized breadmaking (10% wheat-flour substitution). Winter accessions experienced pronounced cold stress, exhibited slower photothermal grow
institutions: Institute of Biological, Environmental and Rural Sciences

title: Actors, technology and geography: arenas of political economy for industrial decarbonisation policy in the United Kingdom
abstract: Industrial decarbonization (ID) involves significant uncertainty about technical and economic pathways, and it interacts with industrial and trade policy. The UK has been an early leader in ID efforts, developing a specific strategy and a set of deployment policies in the early 2020 s, with a strong focus on carbon capture and storage (CCS) and hydrogen, and a regional 'cluster' approach. In this article, we assess the policy choices the UK has made, through the application of a novel framework for analyzing their 'arenas of political economy'. institutions: Libera Università Internazionale degli Studi Sociali Guido Carli

title: Root Microbiota Reprogram Aboveground Metabolite Allocation Across Tea Plant Tissues
abstract: Tea quality is determined by the composition and spatial distribution of specialized metabolites, such as amino acids, catechins, and caffeine, which vary across tissues and developmental stages. However, the mechanisms underlying metabolite allocation among tissues remain unclear. Plant-associated microbiota, particularly root communities, play important roles in regulating plant metabolism, yet their coordinated effects across plant compartments are poorly understood. title: STUDY OF MICROSTRUCTURE AND CORROSION OF FRICTION-SURFACED AA5083
abstract: Friction surfacing (FS) is a solid-state additive manufacturing technique that produces fine-grained coatings, but the microstructural gradients generated across the deposit can affect its corrosion resistance. This study correlates the FS characteristic local microstructure of the advancing side (AS), retreating side (RS) and center of a multi-layer AA5083 deposit with its corrosion after immersion in 0.2 mol L−1 AlCl3 (pH 2.83) for 24 hours. title: Isolation and characterization of calcite-solubilizing plant growth-promoting bacteria and their effects on maize in calcareous soil under controlled conditions
abstract: Calcite-solubilizing bacteria (CSB) are emerging as novel agents for agricultural applications. Twenty-four CSB strains were isolated from marble slurry dump yard soil and characterized morphologically and biochemically. Plant growth-promoting traits included IAA production (23 strains), phosphorus solubilization (20), ammonia production (23), HCN production (21), siderophore production (17) and potassium solubilization (22). title: Nephroprotective and Gastroprotective potential of Aerva javanica (L.) green synthesized nanoparticles, supported by Molecular Networking
abstract: NSAIDs pose a significant risk to the stomach and kidneys, with oxidative stress being a key driver in the development of indomethacin-induced gastric ulcers and acute kidney injury by disrupting the balance between oxidation and antioxidation. Effective management of oxidative stress and bolstering antioxidant defenses are crucial strategies for preventing and treating these conditions. This study explored the potential of Aerva javanica, a plant abundant in Saudi Arabia and used in traditional medicine, to mitigate these adverse effects. institutions: Modern University for Information and Technology

title: Notch-mediated thyroid hormone regulation of skin development in the zebrafish caudal fin
abstract: Thyroid hormone (TH) is a systemic regulator of vertebrate development. Although TH is known to be involved in the maturation of stratified skin, this role has remained incompletely understood. Using the skin at the peripheral-most edge of the zebrafish caudal fin, we characterized the trajectory of epidermal maturation during the transition from juvenile to adult. We found that TH regulates the allometric expansion of the peripheral edge (PE) by stimulating both cell proliferation and hypertrophy of the epidermis. title: Atomic structure of selenium incorporated into mackinawite unveiled by density functional theory
abstract: Selenium-79 is an important contributor to the long-term radiological hazards in deep geological repositories for high‑level radioactive waste. Investigating the environmental behavior of selenium (Se) is crucial for its safety assessment. In this study, the stable structures of Se incorporated in mackinawite, an iron sulfide mineral, were elucidated using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The results indicate that it is important for Se atoms to be separated by a sufficient distance from one another. Furthermore, over the full concentration range, a symmetric structure at a Se ato
journal: Journal of Nuclear Science and Technology

title: Evolutionary dynamics of adaptive introgression and balancing selection in domestic and wild Capra species
abstract: Abstract Introgression is increasingly documented, yet its detection remains challenging because patterns used to infer gene flow may reflect multiple processes, including the persistence of ancestral polymorphism under balancing selection. Domestic species, like goats, and their wild relatives provide informative models for testing the biological feasibility and genomic consequences of interspecific gene flow. We analyze whole-genome sequences from 164 individuals of the genus Capra , including 36 newly generated, to investigate hybridization and signatures of introgression within the genus.

title: Pollination syndromes poorly predict main flower visitors in a disturbed Atlantic forest fragment
abstract: Abstract Pollination syndromes are often used to guide pollinator conservation and ecosystem restoration, but their effectiveness in predicting main pollinators is contested. This study characterized floral traits and pollination syndromes of 69 plant species in a Mixed Ombrophilous Forest fragment and assessed whether observed floral visitors matched the expected syndromes. Floral attributes (anthesis, color, odor, size, shape, symmetry, orientation, stamen position, nectar guides, resources) and plant characteristic (habit, sexual system, plant status, and occurrence) were recorded. title: Development and Validation of Serological Tests for Avian Influenza Antibodies in Meat Juice From Wild Birds
abstract: BACKGROUND: The global increase and fluctuations in high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) cases and its impact on wild birds and poultry highlight the importance of serological surveillance. Serum is the standard sample material for antibody detection but obtaining serum from wild birds can be challenging. This study evaluated meat exudate (meat juice) as an alternative sample matrix for post-mortem detection of avian influenza virus (AIV) antibodies using commercial ELISA kits. title: Three-dimensional seed morphology and evolutionary diversification in the grape family (Vitaceae)

title: Mutational and phenotypic landscape of circulating vaccine‐derived Poliovirus 2 in sewage in a high vaccine coverage area
abstract: The final phases of the Global Polio Eradication Initiative are challenged by the circulation of vaccine-derived polioviruses, particularly serotype 2, occurring even in certified polio-free countries. Integrated environmental surveillance and long-read deep sequencing enable resolution of the viral haplotype network. Structural modelling of this network reveals the poliovirus phenotypic landscape. Together, these approaches uncover the complete poliovirus quasispecies in a population of approximately 1.8 million inhabitants.

title: Design, Synthesis, in silico Studies, and Biological Evaluation of N4-Acetyl/Benzoyl Piperazinyl Ciprofloxacin–Amino Acid Conjugates as Broad-Spectrum Antimicrobial Agents
abstract: This study reports a second-stage optimization of our previously reported ciprofloxacin derivatives through molecular hybridization, with structural modifications aimed at improving antimicrobial potency and activity against resistant strains. Their structures and identities were confirmed by spectroscopic techniques, elemental analysis, and HPLC. In vitro antimicrobial activity showed enhanced potency across a panel of bacterial strains. title: Silence to story: Mapping water stewardship and relational literacies of early childhood teachers
abstract: Early childhood education is increasingly recognized as a critical site for climate learning, yet there is a need for further exploration around how educators introduce ecological responsibility in developmentally meaningful and emotionally attuned ways. This qualitative multi-case study examines how three preschool teachers engaged young children in water-centered storytelling and inquiry as an entry point into climate literacy. Drawing on narrative cartography and a justice-oriented climate storytelling framework, the study traces how teachers described and navigated pedagogical decisions re

title: A novel method for the preparation of haemoglobin-based oxygen carriers via near-complete polymerization under static conditions
abstract: The clinical development of haemoglobin-based oxygen carriers (HBOCs) is hindered by residual haemoglobin (Hb) from incomplete polymerization, which causes vasoconstriction and hypertension, while its removal requires complex and costly purification. To overcome this, we developed a static polymerization strategy for synthesizing near-completely polymerized haemoglobin (PolyHb) using Hb purified from porcine blood. title: Organic Amendments for Simultaneous Soil Carbon Sequestration and Soil-Borne Pathogen Suppression: Mechanisms and Perspectives
abstract: The depletion of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the escalating prevalence of soil-borne plant pathogens represent critical challenges to terrestrial biogeochemical stability and global food security. With approximately 24% of terrestrial carbon reserves lost and over US$220 billion in annual crop losses attributed to soil-borne diseases, understanding biotic and geochemical controls on soil health is essential. This review evaluates the dual functionality of organic amendments (agricultural residues, animal manures, and urban biosolids) as drivers of simultaneous carbon restoration and pathogen
journal: Journal of soil science and plant nutrition

title: Heat treatment optimization and Chromium Nitride precipitation control in heavy-section Superduplex Stainless Steel forgings
abstract: The optimization of mechanical properties in superduplex stainless steel forgings requires precise control of phase balance and precipitation kinetics. This study investigates the effect of different heat treatment routes, including single- and double-step solution annealing and varying cooling rates, on Cr nitride precipitation and secondary austenite formation in S32760 superduplex stainless steel. Mechanical and corrosion properties were assessed through Charpy impact, tensile, Vickers hardness, and pitting corrosion tests, complemented by optical and SEM microstructural characterization. U

title: Evaluation of an NS1-Based ZIKV/DENV IgG ELISA approach for serological differentiation in a dengue-endemic setting
abstract: Accurate serological differentiation of Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus (DENV) infections remains challenging in dengue-endemic regions due to extensive flavivirus cross-reactivity, particularly in populations with pre-existing DENV immunity. Although plaque reduction neutralization testing (PRNT) is considered the reference confirmatory assay, its labor-intensive and time-consuming nature, together with its interpretive challenges in flavivirus-endemic settings where cross-reactive neutralizing antibodies from prior DENV exposure complicate ZIKV-specific interpretation, limits its large-sc

title: Ex situ population dynamics of Brazilian parrots based on zoo, trade and conservation data
abstract: Abstract Zoos contribute to ex situ conservation of taxa affected by habitat loss and wildlife trade, including parrots, but their success in maintaining viable populations remains unclear. This study assessed the role of zoos in the ex situ maintenance and reproduction of Brazilian parrot species over 2004–2024 using Zoological Information Management System demographic records, Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) trade data and International Union for Conservation of Nature Red List categories. title: Making Medicine Buddha local: text, sound, image, and healing practice in Thailand’s Buddhist ecology
abstract: The current research focuses on how the Bhaiṣajyaguru tradition is localized in the Theravāda influenced Buddhist environment of Thailand through text, sound, image, space, and performance of rituals. Data was collected in Bangkok and Nakhon Pathom between February and July 2025 using ethnographic field observation, study of ritual texts, visual data collection, and information provided by six key informants who belonged to Thai-Chinese, Annam Nikāya, Jin Nikāya, university, and women’s Buddhist communities. title: Different from bone: Tooth formation and enameloid mineralization are not affected by reduced dietary phosphorus intake
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vertebrates rely on phosphorus intake for skeletal mineralization. In humans, hypomineralized teeth associated with rickets, hypophosphatemia, hypophosphatasia, or idiopathic molar-incisor-hypomineralization pose significant problems. Here tooth development in wild-type zebrafish and in osteocalcin GFP reporter-line zebrafish is examined under conditions of low, regular, and high dietary phosphorus (P) intake. title: L-Carnitine and α-Tocopherol as Potential Modulators of Oxidative Stress in Cyclophosphamide-Treated Erythrocytes: An Ex Vivo Study
abstract: Introduction: Oxidative stress (OS) compromises erythrocyte structural and functional properties and alters membrane permeability, ultimately resulting in hemolysis. Cyclophosphamide (CYP) is a widely used chemotherapeutic agent frequently implicated in OS due to the generation of cytotoxic reactive metabolites. Although CYP therapy is clinically associated with anemia, its direct effects on erythrocyte redox homeostasis remain underreported. title: Small‐Pore Chitosan Microcarriers Support Surface‐Adherent Growth of Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell–Derived Neural Stem Cells and Improve Intranasal Therapy of Murine Anosmia
abstract: Intranasal delivery of neural stem cells offers a non-invasive strategy for central nervous system repair, yet its efficacy is limited by rapid mucociliary clearance and poor cellular retention. Although chitosan-based carriers have been explored, the architectural principles governing neural stem cell behavior in the intranasal microenvironment remain poorly defined. title: Legal and Institutional Barriers to the Circular Economy in Ghana’s Industrial Supply Chains: Constraints and Reform Pathways
abstract: Ghana’s transition to a circular economy (CE) depends on legal rules that decide when waste becomes a resource, who is responsible for products at end of life, and which institutions may authorise material recovery. This study examines these conditions in three industrial supply chains (electronic waste, construction and packaging) using a qualitative multiple-case design informed by the multi-level perspective on sociotechnical transitions. title: Effects of Curing Time and Initial Suction on the Erodibility of Lime-Treated Lateritic Soils
abstract: Abstract Soil stabilization is considered a feasible approach to controlling water erosion; however, limited research has been conducted on this topic in the context of tropical soils and reservoir shorelines. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of curing time and initial suction on the mass loss of lateritic soils treated with a lime solution and subjected to surface runoff under variable initial hydraulic conditions. title: Untangle air connectivity and tourism development in China’s domestic market
abstract: This paper examines how domestic air connectivity shapes spatial patterns of tourism development in China. We construct a Domestic Airport Connectivity Index (DACI) at the city level for 2000–2024 and employ an instrumental variable strategy to address potential endogeneity, using the interaction between high-speed rail (HSR) expansion and proximity to hub airports as an instrument. title: Coplanar Capacitive Sensor Film from Nata de Coco-Reduced Graphene Oxide- Gelatin for Eco-Friendly Intelligent Food Packaging
abstract: Abstract The escalating global challenges of food waste and environmental pollution from conventional plastic packaging necessitate the development of sustainable and intelligent food packaging solutions. This study presents a novel bio-composite material fabricated from Nata de Coco (NDC), reduced Graphene Oxide (rGO), and food-grade gelatin, designed for smart and sustainable packaging applications. title: COMPUTER SIMULATION OF THE CONTINUOUS EXTRUSION PROCESS OF WIRE FROM HIGH-STRENGTH ALUMINUM ALLOY 7075 ACCORDING TO THE CONFORM SCHEME
abstract: This article presents the results of a finite element numerical simulation study of the 7075 alloy wire production process using the Conform method. A 12 mm diameter rod cast in an electromagnetic mold used as the starting material. A 3D assembly model of the tool and workpiece was developed and presented. During the simulation, the workpiece temperature, tool temperature, and wheel and roller speeds were varied, which made it possible to determine optimal Conform extruding conditions on the presented unit. title: Greek views of Russia after the invasion of Ukraine: a far left-right ‘axis of ressentiment’ against the West
abstract: How did Greeks view Russia after the invasion of Ukraine, and why? Based on a 2022 nationally representative survey of 1,578 Greek adults, this paper argues that pre-existing and interconnected left-right ideologies and East-West identities substantially divided the Greek public in their views of Russia. Specifically, there was a positive quadratic relationship between ideology and views of Russia, with supporters of the Greek far left (KKE) and far right (Greek Solution) the most pro-Russian, and centre right (New Democracy) supporters the most anti-Russian. title: A Sustainable, Robust, Soft‐Gated Janus Bio‐Membrane for High‐Flux Aromatic Recovery From Saline Industrial Wastewaters
abstract: ABSTRACT The selective recovery of aromatic pollutants from saline wastewater remains a central challenge in sustainable chemical engineering. We present a bio‐derived Janus membrane that couples a sorption‐active, mechanically robust wood scaffold with an ultrathin polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layer for soft‐gated aromatic transport. Spectroscopic, molecular, and free‐volume analyses support transient hydroxyl‐mediated phenol capture, favorable interfacial association, and onward diffusion through PDMS. title: Limits to adaptation: Agroforestry buffers but does not offset climate change impacts on maize yields in Dodoma, Tanzania
abstract: Abstract Agricultural productivity in the semi-arid region of central Tanzania is low and projected to further decrease due to climate change, exacerbating the already high levels of food insecurity among the rural population. Agroforestry is actively promoted in the region as an adaptation strategy due to its multiple biophysical and socio-economic benefits, but whether it can buffer future climate change impacts on maize yields has not yet been quantified. title: Deciphering the contributions of hybridization and genome dosage to vegetative vigor in perennial forage maize
abstract: SUMMARY Heterosis and genomic dosage each enhance plant vigor, yet their manifestation and underlying mechanisms in vegetative growth, particularly within polyploid systems, remain unclear. We synthesized and analyzed a series of Zea – Tripsacum allopolyploid trihybrids (MTPs) with varying genomic compositions to dissect the synergistic contributions of hybridization and polyploidy/aneuploidy effects to vegetative vigor. title: Engagement-Zone-Aware Input-Constrained Guidance for Safe Target Interception
abstract: This paper addresses target interception in contested, GPS-denied environments with multiple finite-range, moving defenders. Conventional methods impose conservative stand-off constraints based on maximum engagement distance and neglect actuator limitations, while safety-critical designs typically rely on online optimization. Instead, we formulate safety constraints using defender-induced engagement zones (regions of the attacker’s state space from which capture becomes inevitable under the defenders’ current capability). title: Mitochondrial diversity and population structure of Matsucoccus matsumurae across South Korea
abstract: Matsucoccus matsumurae is an important pine pest in East Asia, but its mitochondrial diversity and population structure across South Korea have not been assessed nationwide. We analyzed mitochondrial ND5 (603 bp; n = 356) and CytB (550 bp; n = 329) sequences from 24 populations to evaluate haplotype diversity, population structure, and isolation by distance. We identified 27 ND5 and 24 CytB haplotypes; concatenated sequences (1,153 bp) from 320 individuals yielded 55 composite mitochondrial haplotypes. title: Dynamical plausibility of triple-assisted interaction in Be-star multiple systems
abstract: Classical Be stars are rapidly rotating B-type stars surrounded by gaseous circumstellar disks. The origin of the angular momentum required to sustain their near-critical rotation remains uncertain. Binary interaction is a promising spin-up channel, and in hierarchical multiple systems a tertiary companion may drive the secular evolution of an unresolved inner binary. title: In Situ Dynamic Compatibilization Enables High-Performance Compatibilizer-Free Bio-Based Thermoplastic Elastomer
abstract: : The thermoplastic vulcanized rubber (TPVs) is undergoing a rapid transition toward bio-based TPV, driven by the urgent need to replace non-recyclable rubbers with environmentally sustainable and recyclable alternatives. A novel bio-based degradable and compatibilizer-free TPV is developed by dynamically vulcanizing bio-based polyester rubber (BPR) within a poly(hydroxybutyrate-co-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) matrix through an in-situ dynamic compatibilization strategy. title: Marked thermal heterogeneity within a small mountain stream network and its response to climate warming
abstract: Water temperature is a key driver of aquatic ecosystems, yet thermal heterogeneity across river networks at fine spatiotemporal scales remains poorly understood. This study investigates the thermal regime of five mid-altitude streams (500–1400 m a.s.l.) in the Serio River catchment (Orobic Alps, Northern Italy), influenced by contrasting water sources (snowmelt/stormwater vs. groundwater) and hydrological modifications (reservoirs), and evaluates how thermal patterns may change under future climate warming scenarios. title: Siblings in Flight: Unravelling Reproductive Barriers Between Two Butterfly Sister Species
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how reproductive isolation is maintained between closely related taxa is a central question in evolutionary biology. Here, we investigate the mechanisms underlying divergence and isolation between two sister butterflies, Erebia palarica and Erebia meolans , which occur in sympatry in the Cantabrian Mountains (N Spain) and in allopatry elsewhere. title: Phytofabrication of Polyvinyl Alcohol Stabilized Bioactive Nano Copper for Microbial Disinfection
abstract: ABSTRACT The designing of bioactive polyvinyl alcohol stabilized nano copper (P n Cu) has been carried out by the herbal reduction of copper acetate precursor. Ficus benjamina (FB) leaf extract facilitated the bioreduction of copper ions, which was further accompanied by the stabilization with polyvinyl alcohol polymer chain. The influence of reaction temperature and PVA concentration on the growth of copper nanoparticles was monitored. title: Exploring winter barley phosphorus and nitrogen needs in western Nebraska
abstract: Abstract Cropping systems in the U.S. High Plains are primarily limited by water availability and a shortened growing season due to the region's high elevations. Winter barley ( Hordeum vulgare L.) shares similar agronomic requirements and equipment needs with winter wheat, and Nebraska's large cattle industry provides an established market for barley as feed or grazing, supporting its adoption with minimal infrastructure changes. title: Taxon‐Specific Selection Drives Contrasting Fast–Slow Strategies of Montane Small Mammal Communities
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Understanding how life history strategies vary among sympatric taxa along environmental gradients is fundamental to predicting biodiversity responses to climate change. We evaluated how mechanistic linkages between life‐history strategies and environmental change operate in montane small mammals (specifically glires and insectivores). We then assessed how these linkages can inform monitoring and management decisions. Location A 2200‐m elevational gradient in the Minshan Mountains, Southwestern China. title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
abstract: Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. title: Effects of fig and kiwifruit extract injection combined with ultrasound treatment on proteolysis and tenderness of low-grade Holstein beef
abstract: Objective: Comparative evidence for fig and kiwifruit extracts standardized to equivalent protease activity and combined with ultrasound treatment remains limited. Therefore, this study evaluated their effects on proteolysis, tenderness, and purge and cooking loss of low-grade (Quality Grade 3) Korean Holstein beef M. longissimus thoracis during refrigerated storage. title: Criterios para seleccionar una ubicación óptima para micro y pequeños negocios restauranteros: Implementación cualitativa del Modelo BESST como herramienta de selección de ubicación en Cancún, México

abstract: Promoting circularity in schools for climate adaptation requires detailed assessments of their resource metabolism, which is typically challenging due to lack of data. This paper proposes a bottom-up methodology for mapping and quantifying water and food flows in schools that combines the principles of Material Flow Analysis (MFA) and citizen science. title: Where There Was Fire… Changes in the Community of Nest Predator in Burned Grasslands of the Southern Pampas, Argentina
abstract: ABSTRACT Fire plays a key role in grassland ecosystems by modifying vegetation structure and, consequently, influencing predator–prey interactions that can affect the reproductive success of grassland birds. The reduction in vegetation density and height resulting from fire affects the reproductive success of birds by increasing the likelihood of nest predation and may modify the relative importance of different predator types to nest fate. Streams grasslands are preferred breeding sites for grassland birds in the Southern Pampas of Argentina, in a context of intensive agriculture and grazing.

abstract: Abstract The growth of asynchronous delivery in higher education has made it increasingly important to examine the conditions that support meaningful student engagement. abstract: The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) has been widely applied to predict human behavior across diverse domains; however, its application in disaster contexts remains limited. abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) have emerged as a central framework for advancing sustainable development within Higher Education Institutions. abstract: Background: Salmonellosis remains a major challenge in poultry production due to economic impact and zoonotic significance. abstract: Malathion (MAL), a widely used organophosphate pesticide effecting environment and causes serious health hazards. Herewith, this work introduces a highly sensitive electrochemical sensor for the sensitive detection of MAL in various environmental samples by utilizing NiO/borophene nanomaterial. title: ROS‐Responsive Micellar Delivery of Bergapten for Coordinated Attenuation of Oxidative Stress and Neuroinflammation in Neonatal Hypoxic‐Ischemic Brain Damage
abstract: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain damage (HIBD) represents a leading contributor to neonatal death and persistent neurological impairments, yet effective therapeutic options beyond hypothermia remain limited. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and Toll-like receptor (TLR)-mediated neuroinflammation contribute to neuronal loss during hypoxic-ischemic injury. title: Sexual Dimorphism in the Facial Morphology and Skin Color in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: In human faces, sexual dimorphism manifests itself in both morphological traits and skin color differences between males and females. Existing research has focused mainly on facial shape, but less is known about the interplay between dimorphism in facial structure and skin color, particularly in African populations. title: Scientific Understanding Across Disciplines: In Varietate Concordia?
abstract: Abstract Understanding is a generally acknowledged aim of science, but the way in which understanding is pursued and criteria for when it is achieved differ widely across scientific disciplines. This paper offers a comparative analysis of this disciplinary variation, aimed at revealing differences as well as commonalities in methods and criteria for achieving understanding. abstract: Urban plant communities assemble from a regional species pool shaped by both ecological processes and horticultural trade, yet how these two forces jointly structure its functional composition remains poorly understood. We characterized the potential regional species pool of Switzerland by compiling 5295 vascular plant species spanning herbs, shrubs, and trees and comparing established species (wild-established only), commercial species (horticulturally available only), and overlapping species (both). abstract: ABSTRACT Black soil (Mollisol), characterized by high soil organic matter (SOM), is becoming more vulnerable to extreme heat events, yet the effects of heat on decomposition of SOM, thus N 2 O emission remain unclear. title: Bibliometric mapping of research hotspots among highly cited papers and hot papers in the web of science organic chemistry category from 2014 to 2025

Therefore, the rapid diversification of this literature has made the systematic identification of influential research themes increasingly important. This study presents a cross-sectional bibliometric analysis of 568 Highly Cited Papers and Hot Papers published from 2014 to 2025. Derwent Data Analyzer, VOSviewer, and Pajek were employed to examine the intellectual and thematic structure of the selected literature through keyword co-occurrence, cited-reference co-citation, and bi

University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Biogeographic Barriers and Gut Microbiome Turnover Across the Peromyscus maniculatus Species Complex
abstract: Biogeographic barriers are fundamental in shaping the distribution of animals and plants, yet the role of discrete landscape features in constraining microbial dispersal remains poorly understood. Identifying the barriers that partition gut microbial communities is essential for modelling the distribution of hosts and their symbionts across physical space and evolutionary time. title: Influence Of Vertical Soil Moisture To Root Growth And Biomass Allocation In Acacia Senegal Linn Seedlings From Two Provenances
abstract: Acacia senegal is an important drought-tolerant species, but limited information exists on how vertical soil moisture affects its early growth from different provenances. Uneven moisture distribution in drylands may influence root development and biomass allocation, affecting seedling establishment. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the influence of vertical soil moisture gradients on root growth and biomass allocation in Acacia senegal seedlings from two provenances, to determine best provenance and moisture condition for survival. Study was conducted in the greenhouse at Federal Univ
journal: Journal of Science Research and Reviews

title: Comparative Effects of Sponge Gourd and Kidney Bean on Olfactory Preference and Fitness of the Leafminer Liriomyza trifolii
abstract: ABSTRACT Liriomyza trifolii is an invasive pest causing severe damage to crops worldwide. This study examined its olfactory responses and life history traits on sponge gourd and kidney bean to evaluate their potential for ecological pest management. Y‐tube olfactometer assays showed that L. trifolii adults preferred damaged sponge gourd leaves over damaged kidney bean leaves but showed no preference between intact leaves. title: Combined toxicity of copper–nickel co-exposure on growth, digestive function, antioxidant status, and transporter- and inflammation-related gene expression responses in Oreochromis niloticus , with potential mitigation by watermelon rind ( Citrullus lanatus )
abstract: Abstract Although copper (Cu) is an essential trace element for fish, excessive concentrations can induce toxic effects. In contrast, nickel (Ni) is generally regarded as a non-essential heavy metal with potential toxicity. Collectively, exposure to concentrations exceeding safe thresholds for either metal poses a significant risk to fish health. Therefore, the combined toxicity of Cu–Ni co-exposure in Oreochromis niloticus was assessed with or without supplementation with watermelon rind (WMR). abstract: Reliable site‐specific seismic hazard assessment for critical structures requires accurate bedrock ground‐motion estimates. Today, such motions are rare (few surface stations are located on hard‐rock sites free of site effects). A common approach is then to apply either generic or site‐specific corrections (e.g., 1D site response modeling) to surface recordings to remove the influence of site effects and to estimate the corresponding bedrock motion. title: Mediator kinase inhibition exposes a transcriptional vulnerability and synergizes with venetoclax in AML
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous and aggressive hematologic malignancy associated with poor survival despite recent therapeutic advances. To identify novel anti-leukemic agents, we performed a high-throughput viability screen of 10,000 small molecules across 56 genetically diverse primary AML samples. Compounds with similar activity profiles were grouped into Compound Correlation Clusters (CCCs), leading to the identification of CCC163, which includes AML874, as a potent and selective hit. title: Modulation of Fe3+ homeostasis by African Swine Fever virus facilitates its efficient replication in Ornithodoros lahorensis and pigs
abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) can be transmitted through direct contact and, in specific ecological settings, by Ornithodoros spp. soft ticks. However, the cellular mechanisms that support ASFV replication in both porcine host and tick vector remain poorly understood. Iron is essential for cellular metabolism and viral replication, but excessive labile iron can induce oxidative stress and ferroptosis-like morphological changes in mitochondria. Whether and how ASFV exploits intracellular Fe3+ homeostasis to sustain its replication has not been fully defined. In this study, proteomic analysis

title: ZhiXie capsule mitigates ionizing radiation-induced intestinal injury by inhibiting PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of Zhixie Capsule (ZXC) on ionizing radiation (IR)-induced intestinal injury (radiation enteritis, RE) and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, focusing on the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. A rat model of RE was established by 12 Gy abdominal IR. institutions: Yunnan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

title: Peptide Bioconjugates: an Emerging Strategy in the Pharmacotherapy of Dermatological Diseases (2015-2025). A Review
abstract: Peptide-based bioconjugates are emerging as a highly versatile and powerful class of therapeutics in modern dermatology, offering precise molecular targeting combined with the flexibility of advanced chemical design. These systems demonstrate broad applicability — from antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory interventions to photodynamic and antineoplastic therapies — while addressing key limitations of conventional treatments through controlled delivery, sustained release, and enhanced cellular selectivity. title: Ionic Transport in LPSCl/PIB Composite Electrolytes: Effects of Particle Size, Binder Molecular Weight, and Stack Pressure
abstract: Slurry‐processed composite solid electrolyte membranes for all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) are governed by particle size and binder molecular weight. Here, we vary Li 6 PS 5 Cl (LPSCl) average particle size ( d p = ~5.6, ~7.5, and ~9.0 µm) and polyisobutylene (PIB) binder molecular weight (M w = ~1050, ~1550, and ~3050 kg mol −1 ) across a factorial design to resolve their effect on ionic conductivity ( σ ion ), ionic tortuosity factor ( τ ), and activation volume ( V * ) under controlled stack pressure ( P s ). title: Mutant Human Erythropoietin from Insect Cells as Novel Low Molecular‐Weight Internal Standards for ERAs Analysis
abstract: Doping analysis of erythropoietin receptor agonists (ERAs) is frequently hindered by the "no band" phenomenon, in which endogenous erythropoietin (EPO) becomes undetectable owing to a variety of pre-analytical factors. The absence of an internal standard (ISTD) poses the risk of an undetected sample preparation failure. Furthermore, the EPO gene variant c.577del presents a substantial analytical challenge. title: Dual-niche profiling identifies maternal gut microbiome differences associated with intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, with no detectable association in vaginal communities
abstract: Abstract Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP) remains central to malaria control, yet its associations with the maternal microbiome are incompletely characterized. We conducted a cross-sectional study using 16 S rRNA gene sequencing to profile the gut and vaginal microbiota of term-pregnant Ghanaian women. IPTp-SP uptake was assessed using two contrasts: no versus any exposure and suboptimal (< 3 doses) versus optimal (≥ 3 doses) uptake. title: Amplified Spontaneous Emission and Carrier Dynamics in Ruddlesden–Popper and Dion–Jacobson Quasi‐2D Perovskite
abstract: ABSTRACT Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) quasi‐2D perovskites exhibit disparate chemical bonds and structures due to distinct organic spacer cations, endowing them with distinctive physical properties. A more far‐reaching investigation of the fundamental structure–physical relation, including the carrier dynamics, is expected in these layered perovskites. title: Transient species can increase resident metapopulation size by modifying local conditions and regional connectivity
abstract: Abstract Populations are regulated by processes operating at both local and regional scales. As a result, species can interact not only within local communities but also through regional-scale processes. However, the feedback between local and regional processes of species interactions in shaping metapopulation dynamics have rarely been tested experimentally. title: From Past to Present: Rediscovering the Legacy of Chemical Analyses of Metals and Glass in the South Caucasus, Georgia
abstract: ABSTRACT Soviet and post‐Soviet scholars (ca. 1921–2000s) produced a substantial body of archaeological science data on the South Caucasus, much of it published in Georgian and Russian and largely inaccessible to the international research community. These legacy datasets, detailing the volumetric and spectroscopic properties of metals and glass, offer valuable insight into material composition, production techniques, and metallurgical practices from Early to Late Bronze Age (ca. 3500–1500 bce ), and glass production from Late Bronze Age to Medieval period. title: Air transport networks and urban economic activity: Dynamic relationships across major global airports
abstract: This study examines the dynamic relationships between air transport network structure and urban economic activity across the world’s top 50 airports by passenger volume in 2024, using monthly data from 2014 to 2024. As the aviation indicator, we adopt the Global Airport Connectivity Index (GACI), a composite measure of network measurements; as the economic indicator, we use Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) Nighttime Lights (NTL), providing a globally consistent, high-frequency proxy for urban economic activity. title: Tracing the origin of non-brittle rachis TtBTR1 alleles in wheat
abstract: The evolution of non-brittle rachises, controlled by the TtBTR1 genes, was a key step during wheat domestication. Here, using k -mer-based approaches applied to a large diversity panel, we refine previous estimates of the geographical and temporal origins of the three known Ttbtr1 loss-of-function alleles and show that they emerged in distinct wild emmer subpopulations. For this, we generated a chromosome-scale dika wheat assembly carrying the recently discovered Ttbtr1-Ab allele. title: Evaluating the Impact of Attachments on the Dynamic Stability of Agricultural All-Terrain Vehicles
abstract: All-Terrain Vehicles (ATVs) are widely used in agriculture but are susceptible to rollover, particularly when carrying attachments. This study evaluated the effects of attachment type (solid and liquid), amount, and location on the dynamic stability of five agricultural ATV models. Standardized steady-state circular driving (ANSI/ROHVA) and lateral transient response (ISO 7401) tests were performed under multiple loading configurations. A preliminary integrated experimental and in Silico assessment of insulating oil leakage effects on soil microbiota and plant germination
abstract: Abstract Leakage of high-voltage insulating oils into soil represents an underexplored source of environmental contamination with potential biological consequences. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of insulating oil (ISOLEC KL 2-3) on soil microbial communities and plant germination under realistic field conditions. Soil samples were collected from an actual leakage site, including both contaminated and uncontaminated soils. title: The Ecology of Beech Bark Beetle Mycobiomes: Similar Fungal Composition Despite Host, Elevation and Site Gradients
abstract: Bark beetles form varying associations with fungi, yet the mycobiomes of many deciduous phloem-feeding species are poorly studied and their ecological significance remains underexplored. Here, we used ITS2 metabarcoding to characterize the fungal communities of the beech bark beetles Ernoporicus fagi and Taphrorychus bicolor collected from 61 forest patches across six regions in Germany. title: Two Decades of Molecular Surveillance in Kenya Reveal Shifting Plasmodium falciparum Drug Resistance Mutations Linked to Frontline Drug Changes
abstract: Malaria control has faced repeated challenges due to the emergence and spread of antimalarial resistance. In the present study, temporal trends in Plasmodium falciparum resistance mutations were analyzed using molecular inversion probe sequencing of 625 samples from 11 Kenyan sites (1998-2021), spanning multiple frontline treatments. title: Market chain analysis of myrrh in southeastern Ethiopia
abstract: Aim of the study: To investigate myrrh production and marketing channels in the El-Weyni district of Ethiopia’s Somali Region, identify the roles and relationships of market participants, analyze market structure and practices, and determine factors influencing household-level myrrh supply. Area of the study: The research was conducted in El-Weyni district, an area with substantial but underutilized potential for non-timber forest products (NTFP), particularly gums and resins. title: Coupled Variable-Order Conformable Dynamics for Hydrogen Gas Turbine Efficiency and Exergy Analysis
abstract: Hydrogen-fueled gas turbines motivate theoretical approaches for describing coupled thermodynamic evolution beyond constant-parameter models. We develop a generalized variable-order conformable formulation coupling reaction enthalpy, phenomenological reaction exergy, the evolving order α ( T ), and a formal thermal-efficiency indicator. The order evolves through an auxiliary local conformable equation of fixed order γ , with β 1 governing self-relaxation and β 2 controlling exergy feedback. title: Dynamics, Challenges, and Prospects of CRVS Systems in Southern Ethiopia: A Qualitative Study of Dilla City and Wonago Woreda
abstract: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) systems are fundamental to governance, rights protection, and evidence-based development planning. Despite legal and structural reforms in Ethiopia, registration completeness remains significantly low. This qualitative study examined the status, operational challenges, community perceptions, and opportunities surrounding vital events registration (births, deaths, marriages, and divorces) in the Gedeo Zone, specifically contrasting the urban context of Dilla City Administration with the predominantly rural setting of Wonago Woreda. title: Critical raw material intensity of electricity generation technologies: A probabilistic and multicriteria approach applied to the European Union
abstract: The global energy transition is expected to substantially increase the deployment of renewable electricity technologies in the European Union (EU), intensifying both consumption and dependency on critical raw materials. Existing studies do not support robust comparisons between electricity generation technologies for decision-making in energy planning and policy. In this context, the present study proposes a probabilistic multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) framework to assess and rank electricity generation technologies according to their material requirements in t/MWh. title: Human Tolerance in Romanian Brown Bears ( Ursus arctos ): Access to Human Food Sources Can Lead to Changes in Bear Behaviour
abstract: ABSTRACT Tolerance to humans in wild animals can lead to several conflict situations and contribute to a generally negative perception of these animals among people. When a wild animal becomes reliant on human‐derived food, dangerous situations can arise, posing risks to both animals and humans. The brown bear ( Ursus arctos ) is a controversial species in Romania, as it is protected but also responsible for incidents with livestock, crops, or even humans. title: Single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy revealed by gastric cancer Perturb-seq
abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. To study how gastric cancer molecular phenotypes are regulated by cell-intrinsic genetic alterations interacting with cell-extrinsic therapeutic pressures, we performed direct capture Perturb-seq to interrogate >200 gastric cancer-related genes against 4 distinct epigenetic therapies in normal gastric and gastric cancer lines. title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies molecular signatures associated with high-risk of systemic reactions to honeybee venom and olive pollen
abstract: Abstract Background Disease manifestation in IgE-mediated allergies is highly heterogeneous, partly due to the distinct exposure patterns of different allergens. High-risk of systemic reactions to immunotherapy is characterized by molecular patterns that are still not well defined. Methods Two patient cohorts, one of bee venom and one of olive pollen allergic patients, were recruited and stratified into two groups, according to the risk of developing systemic reactions (low-risk or high-risk). title: Inflammatory biomarker profiles and their associations with Nordic dietary habits and metabolic outcomes in adults affected by MAFLD
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is commonly accompanied by chronic low-grade inflammation. The Aggregate Index of Systemic Inflammation (AISI) is an accessible inflammatory marker, while the Healthy Nordic diet may have favorable metabolic effects. This study investigated relationships among AISI, healthy Nordic Food Index (HNDI), and metabolic health in adults with MAFLD. In this cross-sectional study, 253 adults with MAFLD were evaluated. title: Healthy diets and heart rate variability in a cross-sectional analysis of over 7000 adults attending the Maastricht study
abstract: A limited and conflicting body of evidence exists on the association between adherence to healthy diets and HRV. The current study aimed to investigate the association between the Mediterranean Diet, Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH), Dutch Healthy Diet (DHD), and the Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) diet and HRV in adults. The baseline data from the Maastricht study were used for this cross-sectional research. Dietary adherence was assessed via a validated Food Frequency Questionnaire. title: On the Advantage of Combining Radon and Chloride to Estimate River Corridor Exchange
abstract: ABSTRACT The transient storage model (TSM) is commonly used to simulate solute transport and exchange in the river corridor, processes that are central to the biogeochemical functioning of streams. Despite the widespread use of the TSM, establishing relationships between TSM parameter values and metrics of stream morphology has proven elusive. One possible explanation is poor parameter constraints obtained in previous modelling approaches, potentially because the slug tracers traditionally used for TSM calibration do not capture temporally longer flow paths. title: Agronomic Value of Carnallite-Derived Potassium and Magnesium Fertilizers: Nutrient Availability, Soil Interactions, and Crop Performance
abstract: Carnallite is a hydrated potassium–magnesium chloride mineral that can supply K and Mg, but its agronomic value cannot be inferred from stoichiometry or dissolution alone. This critical narrative review examines processing-dependent nutrient inventories, product quality, soil exchanges, K–Mg nutrition, chloride exposure, and crop-response evidence. We evaluated the supplied 2010–2026 candidate bibliography thematically; we cannot reconstruct its retrieval and screening history. title: Fire risk to U.S. structures nearly triples by mid-century
abstract: Fire is a nationwide crisis, driven by climate change, land use, and continued development into fire-prone landscapes. As these processes blur the boundary between wildland fuels and the built environment, living with fire is becoming a reality for a growing number of communities. We reconstruct fire risk to structures from 1945-2023 and project its evolution through 2060 across the U.S. using high-resolution historical data on area burned, settlement patterns, and fire impacts. title: Controlled-temperature microwave drying of whole silver rasbora (Rasbora argyrotaenia): Drying kinetics and apparent moisture diffusivity
abstract: Silver rasbora ( Rasbora argyrotaenia ) is commonly consumed whole and presents a heterogeneous anatomical matrix for drying. This study characterized moisture removal during controlled-setpoint microwave drying at 55, 60, 65, and 70°C using dry-basis moisture histories, five thin-layer models, and a simplified Fickian slab analysis. title: Engineering MgFe layered double hydroxide-nanographite interfaces via facile assembly for enhanced solar-driven hydrogen production
abstract: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs), despite being abundant and low-cost photocatalysts for H₂ production, typically exhibit rapid charge-carrier recombination, which limits their efficiency in solar-driven photocatalytic water splitting. Herein, a MgFe LDH–nanographite (NG) composite was fabricated through a simple ultrasonication-assisted physical mixing strategy without additional chemical modification or thermal treatment. title: Regulated but not chromatically codified: a comparative study of cross-regional color grammar in Ming-Qing Paifang
abstract: Paifang in the Ming-Qing ritual architectural system were closely regulated in form and function, but not governed by a unified chromatic code. This paper examines how local color practices emerged within this regulatory gap. Drawing on representative cases from five sites, it combines field records, standardized image-based color sampling, CIELAB metrics, statistical tests, and comparative case analysis to assess three mechanisms: material properties, functional classification, and period-related material change. title: Integrated Biorefinery-Inspired Strategies and Multistage Valorization Pathways of Baijiu Distillers’ Grains
abstract: ABSTRACT Baijiu distillers’ grains are abundant by-products of baijiu production containing valuable bioactive compounds and offering great potential for integrated biorefinery development. This review summarizes recent advances in the conventional and high-value utilization of baijiu distillers’ grains within a cascading biorefinery framework. Traditional applications including feed, fertilizer, microbial fermentation, and silage improve nutrient availability and promote agricultural resource recycling. title: Envenomation Leads to Venom Protein Reduction and a Recovery Period in Bumblebee Workers
abstract: ABSTRACT The evolution and deployment of venom systems in animals have been central to their ecological success, though not without costs. For social bees, venom plays a key role in nest defence; yet for species such as honeybees, the act of stinging generally leads to death. However, for other social bee species such as bumblebees, where stinging is not apparently fatal, it raises the question of what, if any, are the consequences associated with venom usage (envenomation). title: Embedding research in Living Labs: insights from a case comparison of knowledge co-production processes
abstract: Abstract Increased focus on collaborative change-making in Living Labs creates a need to better understand how knowledge co-production enables experimental investigation of and engagement with sustainability challenges. Tracing how knowledge co-production in Living Labs supports learning processes beyond local contexts is equally important. This study uses a multiple-step reflection process to compare four workshop series about improving water and landscape governance within Living Labs in Sweden, Germany, Finland, and Latvia. title: Negative Role of the Receptor‐Like Kinase GbMIK2 in Regulating Cotton Verticillium Wilt Resistance
abstract: The leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinases (LRR-RLKs) function in multifaceted processes in plant growth, reproduction, cell differentiation and immunity. title: Light-responsive transcription factor SsWRKY8 is positively associated with sclareol biosynthesis in Salvia sclarea L
abstract: Sclareol is a naturally occurring diterpene that is primarily synthesised in Salvia sclarea L. The biosynthesis of terpenes and the underlying regulatory mechanism remain largely unclear. Here, we provide the genome-wide characterisation of WRKY transcription factors in S. sclarea , identifying 37 members classified into three major groups (Group II subdivided into five subgroups). title: Techno-economic optimization of an off-grid solar-wind-battery energy storage system for sustainable rural electrification in Dibo, Ethiopia
abstract: Existing microgrid modeling often ignores the electrical mismatch in the modules and obstructions in the vicinity, creating unrealistic estimates of energy production. To fill this gap, this study combines weather data from Meteonorm 8.1 with PVsyst for accurate 3D spatial shading analysis and Hybrid Optimization Model for Electric Renewables Pro for life-cycle cost optimization of an off-grid solar-wind-battery system in Dibo, Ethiopia. title: La historia en la formación del profesorado: un estudio empírico del cálculo de Leibniz
abstract: La necesidad de una sólida formación del profesorado de matemáticas que trascienda el dominio algorítmico e incorpore una comprensión conceptual del cálculo integral ha motivado la revisión de episodios históricos. title: Global assessment of flood-related environmental hazards and dengue risks: the roles of population exposure, duration, and societal resilience
abstract: Population flood exposure and flood duration may have distinct associations with dengue transmission. We analysed a country-month ecological panel using negative binomial models with a log link, population offset and country, year and month fixed effects. The main analysis included 4,840 country-months from 125 countries during April 2010–August 2025. title: SELLER RELIGIOUS IDENTITY AS A HALAL SIGNAL IN INFORMAL FOOD MARKETS: A SIGNALING-THEORY PERSPECTIVE FROM INDONESIA
abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether sellers' religious identity functions as an observable halal signal in informal food markets when Muslim consumers have limited access to formal, verifiable halal information. Drawing on Signaling Theory, the study conceptually investigates how seller religious identity shapes consumers' perceived halalness and consumer trust in the informal food market of Tembilahan, Indonesia. title: Multispectral and Computational Modeling Analysis of the Kinetic Inhibition and Binding Properties of Inonotus obliquus Extract on Xanthine Oxidase
abstract: Xanthine oxidase (XO) is a key enzyme in uric acid (UA) metabolism. The extracts of Inonotus obliquus (I. obliquus) have the potential to inhibit the activity of XO. In this study, the contents of protocatechuic aldehyde (PAH) and protocatechuic acid (PA) from I. obliquus were quantitatively analyzed using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). title: Participatory assessment of potato landrace diversity and conservation vulnerability in northern Peru
abstract: Crop genetic diversity is fundamental to the resilience and adaptive capacity of agricultural systems. However, the conservation of native potato varieties is increasingly under threat. This study assessed the diversity currently maintained, varietal vulnerability, locally lost varieties, and farmer-perceived factors associated with varietal loss in 12 high-Andean communities of Cajamarca, Peru. title: Particulate Matter Induces Apoptotic Death of Brain Vascular Endothelial Cells in Association with Oxidative Damage, DNA Damage Response, and MAPK/NF-κB Signaling
abstract: Particulate matter (PM) is associated with cerebrovascular and neurological disorders, but the responses of brain vascular endothelial cell (BVEC) to PM remain incompletely understood. PM10 reduced BVEC viability and increased cell death, TUNEL labeling, and cleaved caspase-3 and PARP, accompanied by increased intrinsic and death receptor-associated apoptotic proteins, DNA damage response markers, MAPK/NF-κB signaling components, and lipid and protein oxidation markers. title: Navigating Circular Economy Challenges in the Internationalization of Food Companies: MCDM‐Based Investigation
abstract: ABSTRACT In today's rapidly changing and highly competitive environment, internationalization has become a strategic necessity. It is no longer merely a source of competitive advantage, but a fundamental requirement for organizational survival. This need is particularly pronounced in the food industry, which faces stringent quality requirements and growing pressure to comply with international regulations. title: The Staphylococcus aureus Superantigen TSST-1 Directly Impairs Endothelial Migration and Vascular Regeneration
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus causes invasive infections characterized by extensive tissue injury and impaired healing. Although staphylococcal superantigens are best known for immune activation, emerging evidence suggests that they also directly disrupt vascular repair. This study investigated how toxic shock syndrome toxin-1 (TSST-1) affects endothelial migration and angiogenic remodeling. Immortalized human aortic endothelial cells were evaluated using viability and proliferation assays, cell-exclusion assays and live-cell imaging, actin staining, and proteomic profiling. title: Sequencing-based quantification of Erwinia amylovora strains identifies contribution of strain × strain × host interactions underlying apple fire blight severity
abstract: Multiple pathogen strains coexist in the field, and their interactions with host genotypes can strongly affect disease severity and management. Fire blight, caused by the bacterium Erwinia amylovora , is one of the most devastating bacterial diseases of apple and pear worldwide. The interaction between the genetics and phenological stage of the host, the genetics of pathogen strains, and environmental conditions results in outbreaks and changes the severity of the fire blight infection. title: Regional distribution and soil extractability of cadmium in cacao systems across the Cordillera subregion of Nariño in Colombia
abstract: Abstract The primary objective of this observational study was to characterize the regional distribution of cadmium (Cd) in cacao-growing soils and beans and to identify soil properties associated with extractable Cd and plant accumulation. A secondary exploratory objective was to describe clone-related patterns at intentionally selected high-risk farms. Sampling was conducted in two phases during 2020–2021. title: A Review of Starch‐Based Bioplastics From Plant and Agro‐Based Sources: Extraction, Characterization, and Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT The persistence of nonbiodegradable petrochemical plastics, which can endure for centuries, poses ecological challenges. Their accumulation and toxic emissions during disposal contribute to plastic pollution, an escalating environmental and public health concern. Starch‐based bioplastics are promising because they are low‐cost, recyclable, and available from plant sources and agricultural waste, including potato, corn, rice, wheat, cassava, banana peel, jackfruit seed, mango seed, avocado seed, and lucuma seed. title: Habitat type shapes the restructuring of peatland dragonfly communities over two decades
abstract: Abstract Climate warming is restructuring insect communities, and its effects are uneven among species. Understanding which species gain, which decline and why requires long‐term data on community composition, interpreted through the traits of the species involved. Peatlands hold isolated populations of cold‐adapted odonates at the southern margin of their ranges, yet long‐term data on how their assemblages are changing remain scarce. title: Effects of IRM 902 aging on the mechanical thermal and chemical properties of injection molded and extruded thermoplastics
abstract: This study investigates the aging behavior of injection- and extrusion-processed polypropylene impact copolymer (PP), polyethylene of raised temperature (PERT), and an impact-modified polyphenylene sulfide (PPS) grade formulated for pipe fabrication. Specimens were immersed in IRM 902 reference oil at both room temperature (RT) and 95 °C. title: Barbed microneedle patch with programmable CO release for long-term and stage-specific therapy of chronic infected wounds
abstract: ABSTRACT Chronic infected wounds are difficult to heal because bacterial colonization drives persistent inflammation, which further impairs tissue regeneration. This dynamic pathology requires stage-specific intervention, with rapid bacterial suppression followed by sustained inflammatory regulation. Carbon monoxide (CO) has concentration-dependent antibacterial and immunomodulatory activities, but on-demand and temporally programmed local CO release remains challenging. abstract: ABSTRACT BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) and chronic latent DNA virus infections frequently reactivate after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), where they contribute to major complications in humans with limited options for prevention or treatment. Mauritian cynomolgus macaques (MCMs; Macaca fascicularis ) serve as an important animal model for transplantation research due to their limited major histocompatibility complex diversity. title: Mechanisms by Which Lipid-Lowering Agents Modulate the Lipid-Inflammation Circuit and Their Stratified Clinical Use in Rheumatic Immune-Mediated Diseases
abstract: Rheumatic immune-mediated diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and spondyloarthritis, combine persistent inflammation with increased cardiovascular risk. Inflammation alters lipoprotein production, remodeling, function, and clearance, explaining why low or apparently normal cholesterol concentrations may coexist with accelerated atherosclerosis. title: Growth Performance, Haematobiochemical Profile and Enteric Methane Emission of Goats Supplemented With Terminalia brownii Dried Leaves
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Goats are vital for livelihoods and food security in tropical regions such as Ethiopia. However, poor‐quality feed, especially during dry seasons, limits their growth, health and overall productivity. Objective To evaluate the effect of supplementing Terminalia brownii tree leaves on growth performance, hematobiochemical profile and methane (CH 4 ) emission of goats. title: Fish welfare: MS-222 sedation in juvenile Xenocypris davidi transport, dose screening, and exploratory gill transcriptomic profiling
abstract: Transport stress remains a significant challenge in aquaculture. To optimize sedation protocols, we evaluated MS-222 (tricaine methanesulfonate) for juvenile Xenocypris davidi by combining behavioral dose screening (32–50 mg L⁻¹) with gill transcriptomics and histology analysis. title: Diet-induced chromatin states influence intestinal stem cell behavior
abstract: SUMMARY Intestinal stem cells (ISCs) integrate dietary cues through a metabolic–transcriptional axis, but whether these mechanisms create a lasting epigenetic memory remains unclear. Here, we investigate diet-induced chromatin adaptations in ISCs using a high-fat Western diet (HFD) mouse model. HFD broadly remodels chromatin accessibility, altering pre-existing open regulatory regions. title: The taxonomic status and phylogenetic relationships of Toxorhynchites (Diptera: Culicidae) species from Panama
abstract: Mosquitoes of the genus Toxorhynchites are specialized predators of container-breeding Aedes mosquito larvae. Despite their biocontrol potential, species boundaries and phylogenetic relationships remain poorly understood. Utilizing country-wide sampling across Panama, we evaluated the taxonomic status and diversity of local Toxorhynchites species. We collected 147 specimens from artificial and natural containers, yielding 97 cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) barcodes from 101 sequenced individuals. title: Common transcriptional changes in the brain during hibernation and Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Hibernation demands rapid brain adaptations, involving cycles of reduced metabolic rate during torpor, followed by brief periods of arousal. Previous studies show hibernation induces a drastic increase in Tau hyperphosphorylation, but a mechanistic connection to disease remains unclear. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing on hippocampi of golden hamsters, we unveil large transcriptional shifts across the hibernation cycle in all cell types, especially glia. title: DESIGNING DESTINATIONS, COMMUNICATING EXPERIENCES: THE CASE OF PORTUGUESE REGIONAL TOURISM ORGANISATIONS ON INSTAGRAM
abstract: The image of a tourist destination is one of the central elements of contemporary tourism communication and promotion. In this context, Instagram has established itself as a strategic tool for tourism promotion and for building the image of destinations. The aim of this study is to analyse the image projected by the Regional Tourism Organisations (RTO) of Mainland Portugal through the communication of tourist experiences on Instagram. title: Dual-scaffold imageable embolic system with microenvironment normalization enhances hypoxia-activated chemoembolization for HCC
abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by the post-embolization tumor microenvironment (pE-TME), which drives revascularization and fibrosis, thereby narrowing the hypoxic window and restricting drug penetration for hypoxia-activated prodrugs like tirapazamine (TPZ). To overcome this challenge, we developed a dual-scaffold theranostic platform integrating an iodinated thermosensitive PNIPAM hydrogel with genipin-crosslinked albumin microspheres for the coordinated co-delivery of nintedanib (NIB) and TPZ. title: Genomic Diversity and Population Structure of Tibetan Antelopes Sampled From the Selincuo Region
abstract: Based on genome-wide SNP data, this study assessed genomic diversity and population structure in Tibetan antelopes sampled from the Selincuo National Nature Reserve. The analyses included runs of homozygosity (ROH), genomic inbreeding coefficients, genetic diversity, linkage disequilibrium (LD), effective population size, genomic relatedness, principal component analysis (PCA), and sNMF. title: Predicting Vital Pulp Therapy Outcomes Using Pulpal Biomarkers and Clinical Indicators: A Prospective Clinical Study
abstract: AIM: The aim of this prospective clinical study was to investigate whether patient history, preoperative clinical findings and intraoperative parameters, including pulpal biomarker profiles, are associated with the outcome of vital pulp therapy (VPT) in mature permanent teeth and to evaluate their potential prognostic value. METHODOLOGY: Fifty mature permanent teeth diagnosed with reversible or irreversible pulpitis underwent partial or full pulpotomy and were followed for 6 months and 1 year. title: Polydopamine-modified hyaluronic acid hydrogel incorporating Bi2S3 for photothermal antibacterial therapy and wound healing
abstract: The development of smart wound dressings that combat bacterial infection and promote tissue regeneration remains a clinical challenge. Here, we report a chemically modified hyaluronic acid-based hydrogel (Bi 2 S 3 /PDA-HA) with injectability, self-healing, and tissue adhesion, enabled by dopamine functionalization of the hyaluronic acid backbone. abstract: RATIONALE: Comprehensive characterization of plant metabolomes is essential for understanding phytochemical diversity and identifying location-specific metabolic signatures. However, the high complexity of untargeted metabolomics datasets requires robust analytical workflows that integrate high-resolution mass spectrometry with chemometric and pathway-based analyses. This study aimed to characterize the metabolomic landscape of Neolitsea pallens leaves collected from diverse Himalayan locations using an untargeted UHPLC-QTOF-MS/MS metabolomics approach. abstract: Abstract Protein bioconjugates possess widespread utility as potential therapeutics necessitating an expansion of the chemical toolbox used for their production. One particularly promising methodology is the application of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) as a route to produce homogeneous and rationally engineered conjugates. Consequently, the development of new ncAAs and bioorthogonal reactions represents a means to further advance the field. abstract: The performance of sole and intercropping systems in sugarcane cultivation determined productivity and physciochemical properties in Pakistan. abstract: Abstract Control of magnetic order through optical manipulation of orbital states can be realized in a wide range of materials, including insulators. In the latter case, electrons are excited into different electronic states, whose character may be a complex result of spin-orbit-lattice coupling. title: Transferring Culture on Screen: Subtitling Constraints and Strategies in Netflix's KPop Demon Hunters
abstract: This study examines cultural specific items and subtitling strategies using Newmark's (1988) theory for categorizing culturally specific items and Gottlieb's (1992) theory for subtitling strategies in the subtitles of the film KPop Demon Hunters. This study uses descriptive analysis to examine the cultural specific items that emerge from data classification and to describe the patterns of subtitling strategies frequently used in movie subtitles. title: Interactive effects of litter availability and temperature on lipid decomposition in subalpine forest and pasture soils
abstract: Warming and changing litter inputs jointly influence soil organic carbon dynamics in subalpine and alpine ecosystems, yet the molecular-scale interactions in these soils remain poorly understood. We incubated subalpine pasture and forest mineral soils for 360 days at three temperatures (12.5, 16.5, 20.5 °C), representing the current growing-season temperature and projected end-of-century warming under RCP8.5 in the European Alps, with and without addition of Lolium perenne grass litter, and analysed free extractable lipids as molecular tracers of decomposition. abstract: PREMISE: Recent advances in genomic technologies now enable the reconstruction of evolutionary histories at fine spatial scales, illuminating the complex dynamics that shape biodiversity patterns in naturally discontinuous, archipelago-like ecosystems such as cloud forests. METHODS: We investigated the evolutionary history and phylogeography of Ocotea psychotrioides (Lauraceae), a narrowly endemic tree of eastern Mexico, using genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) data comprising 8579 single nucleotide polymorphsims (SNPs) from 101 individuals sampled across 10 populations. abstract: ABSTRACT Executive functions (EFs), conceptualized as conscious, goal‐directed control processes of thought, action, and emotion, develop rapidly during early childhood and predict various developmental outcomes. Previous research has linked socialization practices to early EFs and EFs to mathematics achievement, yet has largely focused on WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) contexts. title: Effects of replacing cottonseed cake with mung bean straw on feed intake, nutrient digestibility, growth performance, and economic returns of simien sheep fed natural pasture hay
abstract: Abstract Background Sheep production plays an important role in the livelihoods of rural households and contributes substantially to food security, income generation, and the national economy in Ethiopia. However, the productivity of indigenous sheep breeds remains constrained by inadequate nutrition and seasonal shortages of quality feed resources. title: CH2Cl2 emissions from China inferred from atmospheric observations
abstract: The importance of dichloromethane (CH2Cl2) on stratospheric ozone has intensified in recent years, with China suspected to be a contributor to global emissions. However, China’s post-2019 emissions remain poorly constrained. Here we show that CH2Cl2 emissions in China were 931 ± 107 gigagram per year (Gg yr−1) in 2024, an increase of 303 ± 111 Gg yr−1 relative to 2019. title: Evaluating operational reliability of smartphone-based measurement systems for forest volume estimation under measurement uncertainty
abstract: Abstract Smartphone applications offer considerable potential for rapid forest inventory, but their reliability for plot-level volume estimation remains uncertain. Therefore, this study evaluated how smartphone-derived diameter at breast height (DBH) and tree height measurements influence model-derived plot-level volume estimates in a peri-urban forest in central Nepal. title: Hierarchical porous silica nanoparticles for interfacial engineering and thermomechanical enhancement of basalt fiber composites
abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer composites (FRPCs) are pivotal in aerospace and automotive sectors; however, their limited thermal stability under extreme conditions remains a challenge. In this study, the thermomechanical behaviour of unidirectional basalt fabric-reinforced unsaturated polyester (BFPC) composites was enhanced through the incorporation of silica nanoparticles with varying morphologies, namely nonporous, semiporous, and porous structures, as secondary reinforcements. abstract: Maintaining end-to-end connectivity under disruption is a central problem in systems resilience. This study examines how limited protection resources can increase the minimum node-removal cost required to disconnect a specified service. Mission-Path Cut Fortification (MPCF) models a directed service as a functional graph and treats protection as a finite increase in node-removal cost. abstract: Abstract Understanding how precipitation responds to temperature change is critical for interpreting hydroclimate risk over the Tibetan Plateau, a high-elevation water tower supplying major Asian river systems. While global-mean precipitation increases more slowly than Clausius–Clapeyron moisture scaling, regional responses can vary strongly with circulation and topography. title: Effect of water curing, interval spraying, and raffia-frond covering on compressive strength development of normal-strength concrete
abstract: Concrete curing is essential for maintaining moisture conditions required for cement hydration and compressive-strength development. This study evaluated the effects of continuous water curing, interval spraying, and raffia-frond covering on the compressive-strength development of concrete at 7, 14, 21, and 28 days.
