abstract: This study investigates the environmental, economic, and technological determinants of sustainability in ASEAN and SAARC using panel data techniques, including FGLS, PCSE, Fixed-Effect OLS, and two-step System-GMM, alongside quantile regression. Sustainability is assessed through two complementary indicators: renewable energy consumption (REC), capturing energy transition, and adjusted net savings excluding emission damage (ANS), reflecting long-run resource-based sustainability. title: Consultant and trainee perspectives on endoscopic spine surgery training in Australia: A cross-sectional survey
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endoscopic spine surgery (ESS) is expanding, but training access and educational preferences in Australia remain underexplored. We surveyed consultants and trainees/fellows to identify priorities for ESS education. METHODS: A 17-item cross-sectional online survey was circulated through an Endoscopic Spine Society of Australia (ESSA) professional group and an informal neurosurgical trainee network. title: Global Potential Distribution and Climatic Niche Dynamics of the Invasive Alien Weed Solanum rostratum Dunal
abstract: ABSTRACT Whether invasive species conserve their ancestral climatic niches or undergo realized niche changes during global spread fundamentally affects the reliability of invasion risk projections. We integrated ensemble species distribution models (SDMs), the extended COUE framework, and Multivariate Environmental Similarity Surfaces (MESS) to quantify the global climatic niche dynamics and invasion risk of Solanum rostratum Dunal (Solanaceae) across its native North America and four invaded regions. title: A place-based perspective on local wind energy acceptance: the role of place attachment, motivations, and social norms
abstract: Wind energy is widely supported, yet specific projects encounter local contestation. Moving beyond NIMBY-based interpretations, this research examined social acceptance of wind energy as a place-based and socially situated judgment. Across two Italian experimental studies, we tested whether making place attachment salient reduces acceptance of a proposed wind farm and whether environmental, economic, and social motivations relate to acceptance under different place and normative conditions. title: Surface Glare Suppression in Retinal Imaging With a Cross‐Polarized Line‐Scanning Color Fundus Camera
abstract: Fundus imaging is critical for the early detection and management of retinal diseases, yet cost and technical limitations remain barriers to broad implementation, especially in resource-limited settings. Conventional fundus photography and scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO) involve trade-offs in cost, field of view (FOV), color fidelity, and image contrast, and are often affected by corneal surface glare. title: Leaving X: How scale insects repeatedly evolved alternatives to chromosomal sex determination
abstract: Abstract Reproduction is a core feature of life, yet it is still unclear why sex determination systems are conserved for hundreds of millions of years in some taxa but repeatedly turn over in others. A prime example is the true bugs; the vast majority of families employ a conserved X sex chromosomal system, but in scale insects (Coccomorpha), sex determination systems are more varied. Scale insects may retain X chromosomes, employ a form of haplodiploidy known as paternal genome elimination (PGE), or reproduce via selfing as simultaneous hermaphrodites. abstract: With the accelerated growth of e-commerce following the Covid-19 pandemic, driven by globalization and society's new consumption habits, the demand for sustainable packaging has increased significantly. title: Field Evaluation of Bio-Pesticides and Selected Insecticides Against Spodoptera frugiperda (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) in Maize with Receptor-Ligand Modelling of Spinetoram
abstract: The fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda (J.E. Smith) is a destructive pest that causes negative impacts on maize production. abstract: [Objective] This study aims to analyze the perceptions of in-service teachers in primary education (ages 6-12) regarding the role of the affective domain in mathematics teaching. [Methodology] Based on a descriptive and exploratory study, a previously validated questionnaire designed to explore different dimensions of the affective domain in mathematics teaching was administered to 28 primary education teachers from the Araucanía region (Chile), working in both publicly funded private schools and municipal schools. title: Tannin Phenology is Associated with the Timing of Asiatic Black Bear Foraging among Persimmon Fruit Types
abstract: This study examined whether variation in tannin concentrations and tannin insolubilization timing among persimmon fruit types influences foraging frequency and seasonal timing in Asiatic black bears (Ursus thibetanus). abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the effects of geopolitical risk (GPR), economic policy uncertainty (EPU), and trade policy uncertainty (TPU) on corporate CTR in China from January 2010 to December 2022. title: Local segregation effects in nominally premixed turbulent lean syngas–air flames
abstract: The effects of preferential diffusion and chemical kinetics on reaction zone structure and combustion characteristics in turbulent premixed syngas–air flames are investigated using direct numerical simulation. Freely propagating statistically planar flames with varying H2/CO composition, equivalence ratio, and turbulence intensity are analyzed within the thin reaction zones regime. title: Effectiveness of Rotating Versus Fixed Three‐Section Watchkeeping Schedules on Crews' Well‐Being, Cognitive Performance, Sleep and Salivary Cortisol in the Navy
abstract: When 24 h-work needs to be distributed among crew members on ships, on-watch duty times can be either stable over time or can vary on a regular basis. abstract: ABSTRACT To improve the filtration‐control performance and stability of cellulose ether‐based additives under high‐temperature and high‐salinity conditions, a cellulose‐based composite filtrate reducer (HASF) was developed for water‐based drilling fluids. HASF was synthesized by free‐radical graft polymerization of hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) with acrylamide, 4‐acryloylmorpholine, and sodium p ‐styrene sulfonate, followed by incorporation of carboxylated cellulose nanofibers (CNF). title: Microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid regulates glucose homeostasis via remodeling of hepatic mitochondrial metabolism
abstract: The gut microbiota produces metabolites that circulate to host tissues and are increasingly linked to metabolic health, yet the mechanisms by which individual microbial products regulate liver glucose metabolism remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the tryptophan-derived microbial metabolite indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) as a direct modulator of hepatic glucose production. In primary hepatocytes, a focused screen of indole metabolites revealed that several indole-containing compounds suppress glucagon-stimulated glucose output, with IPA selected for further characterization. title: Co-Designing English Teaching Materials through Dialogue: Lessons from a Research–Practice Partnership
abstract: English language teaching (ELT) materials are not neutral pedagogical tools but cultural and ideological artifacts that shape which forms of knowledge, values, identities, and cultural practices are legitimized in language education. ELT materials research is broadly categorized into studies of content, consumption, and production and argues that more research is needed on researcher–practitioner collaboration in materials writing. journal: Studies of Applied Linguistics in Asia

title: Saccadic suppression enhances saliency of ecologically relevant stimuli in the zebrafish optic tectum
abstract: Saccadic suppression, a reduction in visual sensitivity around the time of rapid eye movements, is well-documented in primate psychophysics, but its mechanisms and functions remain debated. Here, we use zebrafish to trace the origins of saccadic suppression, and we demonstrate how saccadic suppression selectively enhances the visual salience of ecologically relevant stimuli. Saccadic suppression thus contributes to more than just compensation for rapid saccade-induced image shifts. title: Nocardia seriolae Infection Causes Granulomatous Pathology, High Mortality and Growth Impairment in Cultured Rice Field Eel ( Monopterus albus )
abstract: ABSTRACT During a recent epidemiological survey of rice field eel ( Monopterus albus ) aquaculture farms in Jiangxi Province, China, we observed a characteristic presentation of multifocal granulomatous nodules suggestive of nocardial infection. Bacterial isolation yielded light‐yellow, pigmented colonies with a granular texture and dry, wrinkled surface. Microscopy revealed branching filamentous rods characteristic of Nocardia , while histopathology demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with severe necrosis. title: CHARACTER ANONYMITY IN THE DIALOGI OF SULPICIUS SEVERUS
abstract: Abstract In approximately 403 c.e. Sulpicius Severus, a Gallo-Roman litterateur, composed his Dialogi , following on from his hagiographic tour de force, the Vita sancti Martini. Anonymous characters feature throughout the three books. This article argues that the dialogue genre is ideally positioned to interrogate the dynamics of character anonymity. Using Sulpicius’ Dialogi as its focus, the article explores three case studies: Gallus ‘The Gaul’, the Empress Arriana/Justina and Rufinus of Aquileia. title: Family Firms’ Productivity in Complex Regions
abstract: Abstract Prior studies suggest that regional contexts shape family firm performance, yet evidence remains mixed, often attributed to heterogeneity among family firms and regional characteristics. Less attention has been paid to how regional economic complexity influences family firm outcome. Using a panel of more than 90,000 Swedish firms over 25 years, we examine the relationship between regional economic complexity and family firm labour productivity. The results show that family firms benefit more from economically complex regions, exhibiting significantly higher labour productivity. This a

title: Spatio-temporal clustering of dengue in Valle del Cauca, Colombia
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dengue is endemic in Colombia's Valle del Cauca region. The precise timing and spatial scale of seasonal dengue transmission necessary for effective reactive interventions at the sub-municipal level across the 42 municipalities of Valle del Cauca remain unclear. This study aimed to identify spatio-temporal dengue clusters in Valle del Cauca. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: A retrospective observational study was conducted using individual laboratory-confirmed dengue cases, including residential geolocation and consultation dates, reported by healthcare providers to the Sistema Naci
institutions: Centro Internacional de Entrenamiento e Investigaciones Medicas

title: When carbon counts differ: the complexities of biogenic carbon accounting in BECCUS and why accounting choices matter
abstract: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (BECCUS) is an important pathway towards net-zero and net-negative emissions. Its mitigation potential depends on net atmospheric CO2 removal into durable storage after accounting for system-wide emissions and removals. However, lifecycle assessment, national greenhouse gas inventories and carbon-market frameworks apply differing accounting approaches, producing divergent mitigation estimates. title: Microbiome structure, function, and drivers across different soil groups in an agricultural region of Serbia
abstract: Soil is the largest reservoir of biodiversity, with distinct physical, chemical, and biological properties. Microorganisms play essential roles in soil formation and fertility. This study aimed to analyse the microbiomes of three selected soil groups (Chernozem, Solonchak, and Vertisol) in an important agricultural region of Vojvodina (Serbia) by 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding and explore their association with soil properties, including soil pH, texture, organic matter, nutrient status, cation exchange capacity, and selected macro- and micronutrients. title: Linking climate change to self-harm: A global study of over 200 countries from 1990 to 2020
abstract: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a major threat to both environmental and human health; however, a comprehensive global assessment of its impact on mental health and self-harming behaviours remains lacking, particularly with respect to demographic and socioeconomic modifiers and their potential interactions. title: Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) affects a substantial proportion of individuals with major depressive disorder, posing a significant clinical and societal burden. Among emerging interventions, tractography-guided Subcallosal Cingulate Deep Brain Stimulation (SCC-DBS) shows promise as a treatment for TRD. However, despite the use of connectome-based targeting methods, clinical outcomes remain variable across individuals. Here, we examined individual white matter (WM) properties underlying the variability of SCC-DBS response for depression by analyzing a patient-specific diffusion MRI datas
institutions: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

title: Organ and Carcass Condemnations and Associated Financial Losses in Cattle Slaughtered at Woldia Municipal Abattoir, North Wollo Zone, Ethiopia
abstract: Background Abattoirs serve as crucial surveillance points for animal diseases and food safety. Organ and carcass condemnations resulting from pathological conditions represent significant economic losses to the livestock industry and pose potential public health risks. Objective This study aimed to identify the major causes of organ and carcass condemnation in cattle slaughtered at Woldia Municipal Abattoir and estimates the associated direct annual financial losses. title: Comparison of gravimetric and spectrophotometric lignin quantification methods across sugarcane cultivars and harvest ages
abstract: The objective was to evaluate which method for determining lignin is most suitable for characterizing the quality of sugarcane as forage for ruminants. The treatments were lignin quantification using the acid detergent fiber method, lignin quantification using the acetyl bromide cell wall method, and lignin quantification using the acetyl bromide neutral detergent fiber method. The lignin concentration was quantified in samples from four sugarcane cultivars, IAC86-2480, IACSP93-3046, IACSP04-704, and IACSP04-656, at three vegetative growth stages, 365, 420, and 480 days. title: The mediating role of individual entrepreneurial orientation in the relationship between perceived organizational support and employee performance in the manufacturing sector
abstract: This study examines the influence of perceived organizational support on employee performance by incorporating individual entrepreneurial orientation (IEO) as a mediating variable in the manufacturing sector. The study addresses how employees’ perceptions of organizational support can stimulate entrepreneurial-oriented behavior that contributes to improved performance. A quantitative approach with a correlational survey design was applied to test the proposed relationships. Data were collected from 86 employees of PT Feng Tay Indonesia Enterprises using structured questionnaires and a probabil
journal: Jurnal Ilmiah Bisnis dan Ekonomi Asia

title: pH-Universal Electrocatalytic Nitrate-to-Ammonia Reduction on Ruthenium-Decorated Copper Foam
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic reduction reaction of nitrate to ammonia (NO3RR) has emerged as a promising strategy that couples nitrate pollutant remediation with sustainable NH3 production. Practical nitrate-containing industrial wastewater usually presents a wide pH distribution range, which puts forward an urgent requirement for pH-adaptive NO₃RR catalysts with high ammonia selectivity. Conventional NO3RR catalysts fail to deliver high NH3 Faradaic efficiency under extreme acidic or alkaline conditions, mainly due to uncontrollable competitive adsorption of hydrogen intermediates on active site
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

title: Primary Cavity Excavators in Community‐Managed Lowland Forest of Nepal: Woodpecker Assemblage, Nest‐Tree Preference, and Its Implications for Forest Management
abstract: ABSTRACT Woodpeckers are keystone species playing a crucial role as ecosystem engineers, with their highest species richness and diversity in the tropical and subtropical regions. Although most research on the species' ecology originates from the temperate regions, it leaves a substantial gap in woodpecker assemblage and nesting ecology in tropical and subtropical areas. Our study fills this gap in the subtropical region of South Asia, exploring woodpecker diversity, abundance, and factors influencing cavity nest occurrence in the lowland sal Shorea robusta forests of Nepal. title: The Ancient Language of the Great Pyramid
abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical and interpretive framework, termed the Prime Language, which reads the Great Pyramid of Giza as a geometric model for organising and preserving information. The framework rests on a five-stage hierarchy, the five logos: Food (Sustenance), Water (Life), Medicine (Knowledge), Architecture (Structure) and Education (Wisdom). The aim is not to claim an ancient law, but to examine whether the Pyramid’s documented geometry can support an internally consistent model of hierarchical order. title: Overview of Oleochemicals in Metal–Organic Frameworks Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are crystalline materials formed by linking organic linkers with metal ions or clusters. MOFs are highly porous materials with tunable structures that have numerous applications from environmental remediation to energy storage. Oleochemicals have gained attention as biodegradable building blocks for MOF synthesis, reflecting a growing interest in sustainable feedstocks for advanced materials. title: Spring phenological timing modulates intra-annual growth: evidence of a seasonal advantage for early-flushing trees
abstract: Abstract The timing of budburst is a key determinant of a tree’s fitness within its environment. While numerous studies have investigated the environmental drivers of phenology, less attention has been paid to how phenological traits influence individual tree performance within the forest. Here, we assessed at the individual-tree scale whether earlier budburst is associated with enhanced growth and how intra-annual growth dynamics differ between early- and late-flushing trees. We analyzed annual and intra-annual growth together with budburst phenology across the Spanish plots of the ICP Forest
institutions: Instituto Nacional de Investigación y Tecnología Agraria y Alimentaria

title: Oxygen Vacancy Mediated Plasmonic Bi 2 S 3 /W 18 O 49 S‐Scheme Heterojunction for Efficient Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven hydrogen production requires photocatalysts with broad‐spectrum light harvesting and efficient charge separation. Herein, a plasmonic Bi 2 S 3 /W 18 O 49 S‐scheme heterojunction was constructed via a one‐pot solvothermal strategy, with W 18 O 49 nanowires grown in situ on Bi 2 S 3 nanorods. title: Fermentation of Lini S Arabica coffee using coffee-fermentation-derived microbial isolates to improve coffee quality and flavor
abstract: This study examined the effects of anaerobic fermentation using coffee-derived lactic acid bacteria and yeasts on Lini S Arabica coffee quality and chemical characteristics. Lactobacillus plantarum strain UL4 (LP), Pichia kudriavzevii strain W10 (PC), and Pichia kudriavzevii strain D1Y-13 (PK) were used for 24 and 48 hours. Samples underwent cupping tests, GC–MS analysis of aroma compounds, and measurements of pH, total titratable acidity (TTA), caffeine, chlorogenic acid (CGA), and reducing sugar content. title: Beyond linear outage costs: Estimating duration-dependent economic impacts in Puerto Rico
abstract: Electric power disruptions impose substantial economic and societal costs, particularly in islanded power systems exposed to extreme weather, geographic isolation, and limited opportunities for grid support. Existing outage cost estimates are largely derived from mainland U.S. data and short-duration interruptions, limiting their applicability to prolonged outages in islanded systems. title: Bacteroides fragilis toxin (BFT) detection and neutralization using phage display-derived synthetic hagfish VLRBs
abstract: Enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis (ETBF) weakens the intestinal epithelial barrier and promotes inflammatory signaling through secretion of B. fragilis toxin (BFT), a metalloprotease associated with chronic intestinal inflammation. By triggering the breakdown of the E-cadherin glycoprotein in cellular junctions, BFT compromises tissue integrity and affects pathways involved in tumor suppression and signal transduction. institutions: University of the Philippines Los Baños

title: Silent battles: intra-gender power struggles and the scorpion loop in women’s academic leadership
abstract: This study investigates the existence, manifestations, and organisational mediation of intra-gender power struggles among women leaders in Arab higher education, alongside the forms of allyship that facilitate their advancement and retention in senior roles. Guided by gendered organisations theory, intersectionality, and social capital, the research employed vignette-based semi-structured interviews with eighteen senior and mid-level female academics from diverse faculties. title: An active Lorentz gas: walking droplets in periodic media
abstract: Abstract The Lorentz gas is a paradigmatic model in dynamical systems theory for understanding the origin of nonequilibrium transport in terms of microscopic deterministic chaos. In the periodic setting, a point particle scatters elastically off disks arranged on a two-dimensional lattice. Here we replace the disks by smooth potentials and the particle by the widely studied walking droplet, which propels itself on a vertically vibrating fluid. title: Critical Success Factors for Waste Management Startup Development in Indonesia: A DEMATEL-Based ANP (DANP) Analysis
abstract: Indonesia faces growing waste management challenges, while existing management efforts remain insufficient to address increasing waste generation. In response, waste management startups have emerged as innovative solutions. Despite their potential, many struggle due to weak regulation, technological barriers, and low public awareness. This study identifies Critical Success Factors (CSFs) influencing their development using the DEMATEL-based ANP (DANP) method, which captures interrelationships among 37 validated CSFs through expert judgment and modeling. title: Integrating hydrogen into Ontario’s energy hub: A robust, carbon-aware framework for power–heat–transport
abstract: Decarbonizing electricity generation, heating, and transportation simultaneously requires integrated planning tools that coordinate multiple energy carriers while remaining reliable under uncertainty. This paper develops a carbon-aware and uncertainty-resilient optimization framework for a grid-connected multi-energy hub that co-optimizes electricity, heating, cooling, and transportation services with an explicit hydrogen sub-hub. title: Re-description of Durinemella elongata Andrássy 2009, andUniqaxonchium megaspiculatum Dhanam & Jairajpuri 1998 (Nematoda: Belondiroidea) with emended generic diagnosis
abstract: The population of Durinemella elongata and Uniqaxonchium megaspiculatum were isolated from the soil samples collected from Western Ghats of India. We compared our isolated specimens with the original description of both the species. The inconsistences in morphology, morphometrics, and some errors in the original description of these species encouraged us to re-describe them. The newly recorded specimen of Durinemella elongata showed a thin sheath surrounding the expanded part of the pharynx without spiral bands, which was not mentioned in original description. title: Mitochondrial DNA control region of the endangered Busok cat (Felis catus) from Ra’as Island, Indonesia
abstract: Abstract The domestic cat originated in the Near East and dispersed along human trade routes, and its mitochondrial control region is used to trace this spread. Island populations are informative as each founding event samples only a portion of the source gene pool. However, relatively few island populations have had genetic evaluations. The Busok cat, a blue-gray, short-tailed landrace from Ra’as Island, Indonesia, was recognized in 2022 with a defined phenotypic breed standard. title: Effects of Substrate Composition on Kombucha Quality: A Study of Liang Tea and Siam Orange (Citrus nobilis var. microcarpa) Blends
abstract: Background and Aim: The development of functional kombucha beverages from herbal and fruit substrates needs optimization of formulation to achieve a favorable balance between physicochemical and microbiological characteristics. This study aimed to assess the effects of different Liang tea-Siam orange (Citrus nobilis var. microcarpa) ratios on the physicochemical and microbiological characteristics of kombucha. title: Bioactivity and Fatty Acids of Wild Myrtus communis L. in Kadirli, Turkey
abstract: Myrtus communis L. (myrtle), largely distributing in the Mediterranean Basin, has been used in folk medicine for treating some ailments. This study presents a detailed investigation of myrtle leaves from Kadirli (Osmaniye), including its chemical composition, and biological activities. Between May and August 2022, plant samples were collected from the northern region of Osmaniye, Turkey. Leaves of M. communis L. were used to prepare different extracts. title: Human-cattle Relations in Selected Chinese News Discourse: A Corpus-assisted Ecolinguistic Analysis
abstract: In the context of modernity, profit-driven and unethical practices, such as artificially increasing beef weight and enhancing its visual freshness to meet consumer expectations, have led some traders to inject water into live cattle. Such practices not only violate animal ethics, undermine animal welfare, and disrupt species ecology but also prompt people to reconsider human–cattle relations in China. title: SPATIAL DISPARITIES IN CULTURAL TOURISM: A MULTIDIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS OF MUSEUM ATTENDANCE DYNAMICS IN BULGARIA
abstract: This study aims to identify and analyse spatial disparities and structural stratification of regional museum activity in Bulgaria over a 13-year period (2012-2024). The primary objective is to evaluate the stability, growth trajectory, and resilience of regional cultural supply models in response to external and macroeconomic shifts, specifically the COVID-19 pandemic. title: Effects of Different Game Mechanics on 2D Location Learning in a Serious Game
abstract: Serious games teach players skills or knowledge applicable outside the game, but the choice of game mechanics may influence the underlying perceptual, memory, and cognitive processes involved, potentially affecting quality of learning. We developed two serious games that both have the goal of teaching the locations of important commands in a simple 2D grid UI, but that have different game mechanics (a sequence-based mechanic that could interfere with location memory for individual items, and a restricted visual search mechanic that could promote intentional learning). title: Tunable production strategy for lignin-containing cellulose nanofibers from aspen biochemical mechanical pulp
abstract: Lignin retention during nanocellulose production critically influences the ultraviolet (UV) barrier, antioxidant, mechanical, and hydrophobic properties of bio-based films, but conventional single-step treatments offer limited compositional tunability. Here, we integrate beating pretreatment with tartaric acid (TA) hydrolysis to produce lignin-containing cellulose nanofibers (LCNFs) from aspen biochemical mechanical pulp. title: Lipid nanoparticle-based mRNA delivery system for cancer management
abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA)-based therapeutics have transformed cancer treatment strategies, especially after the success of lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-enabled mRNA vaccines. LNPs are effective non-viral delivery vehicles that protect mRNA, enhance intracellular delivery, and improve therapeutic safety. This review discusses recent advancements in LNP-mediated mRNA therapies, including mRNA vaccines, cytokine delivery, immune modulation, and CAR-based strategies. title: Beyond tolerance: Distinct pathways shape human attitudes toward wildlife conflict
abstract: Abstract Human–wildlife conflict is driven by socio‐economic factors that are often overlooked or unaccounted for by most conservation plans and policies. These include social attitudes like tolerance of and opposition to wildlife which act and operate through distinct pathways rather than along a single continuum. Here, we distinguish these as two related but distinct attitudinal dimensions of human responses to wildlife conflict. title: Spatial pattern of soil properties and earthworm communities in oak- based traditional wood pastures of Romania
abstract: Abstract Solitary trees such as oak ( Quercus spp.) play a central ecological role in wood pastures. They alter the surrounding soil and abiotic conditions, with largely unclear consequences for the soil fauna such as earthworms. We investigated how solitary oak trees alter soil properties and whether those alterations impact earthworm communities. Soils and earthworms were sampled across 30 oak-based traditional wood pastures in Transylvania, Romania. title: MXenes-based heterostructures versus carbon-based anodes for metal-ion batteries: performance benchmarks, commercial viability, and translation challenges
abstract: MXenes and MXenes-based heterostructures have emerged as promising anodes for metal-ion batteries because of their high electrical conductivity, tunable surface chemistry, and layered structures. However, their practical competitiveness must be evaluated against commercially established carbon-based anodes rather than theoretical capacity alone. title: Root lipid–associated uptake and species responses decouple accumulation and toxicity of liquid crystal monomers in leafy vegetables
abstract: Liquid crystal monomers (LCMs), released from electronic products and e-waste, can enter agroecosystems and accumulate in edible crops, raising concerns about crop health and food safety. However, how plant species and contaminant properties jointly regulate LCMs accumulation and subsequent phytotoxic responses remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the accumulation and physiological responses of four leafy vegetables exposed hydroponically to eight representative LCMs. Total LCM concentration (ΣLCMs) reached 0.73–1.67 μg/g dry weight (dw) in roots and 0.56–1.26 μg/g dw in shoots. title: Valorisation of blueberry pomace as a valuable ingredient: Potential and utilisation in food and non-food applications
abstract: Blueberry is one of the most commercially important fruits in the world and it has been widely processed in various food products, such as juice and wine. During the processing chain, blueberry pomace is a major by-product that is generally discarded as food waste; however, it retains high nutritional value, such as dietary fibre and bioactive compounds, which can be recycled as a valuable ingredient and re-utilised across sectors. The complete utilisation of blueberry pomace is a promising approach to enhance the value of the blueberry processing chain and promote food system sustainability.

title: Low-temperature and partial closed-loop chemical recycling of glass fibre-reinforced recyclamine epoxy composites with fabric-scale recovery
abstract: This study presents a low-temperature chemical recycling process for glass fibre-reinforced recyclamine epoxy composites, in which the epoxy matrix was solubilised, allowing the reinforcement materials to be retrieved and recovered at full fabric scale. The recycled glass fabrics largely retained their fabric architecture, and following washing with deionized water, the texture of the recycled glass fabrics closely resembles that of the virgin glass fabrics. title: Life-history trade-offs explain local adaptation in Arabidopsis thaliana
abstract: Local adaptation has been demonstrated in many organisms, but the traits involved and the temporal and spatial scales at which selection acts are generally unknown. We carried out a multi-year study of 200 accessions (natural inbred lines) of Swedish Arabidopsis thaliana using local field sites and a combination of common-garden experiments that measured adult survival and fecundity, and selection experiments that measured fitness over the full life cycle. title: Racial segregation and urban space in Salvador, Brazil: comparative evidence from the 2010–2022 Demographic Censuses
abstract: Abstract Racial residential segregation constitutes a central dimension of urban inequalities, as it shapes how population groups are distributed across the territory and how they access infrastructure, public services, and opportunities. This article analyzes racial segregation in Salvador’s neighborhoods, comparing the 2010 and 2022 Demographic Censuses of the Brazilian Bureau of Statistics. title: Evaluating tree susceptibility to bark stripping by Asiatic black bears through multi-scale analysis and field surveys addressing time-varying environmental factors
abstract: In previous research on determinants of bark stripping by bears, the hierarchical structure of bear habitat selection has often been overlooked. Additionally, the temporal disparity between damage occurrence and field observation, potentially leading to spurious associations and underestimation of risk factors, is overlooked. For example, we could misinterpret the association between tree size and the probability of bark stripping, because bark stripping negatively affects the growth of damaged trees while the surrounding undamaged trees continue to develop. title: Factors influencing the timeliness of reporting highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks in Europe
abstract: Timely reporting of zoonotic infectious diseases allows for rapid response and mitigation by health authorities. However, little is known about the factors influencing the timeliness of disease outbreak reports. The World Animal Health Information System provides extensive data on delays that arise between first suspecting and subsequently reporting outbreaks of notifiable animal diseases. title: Recovery Boiler or Fuel Route? Consequential Break-Even Conditions for the Use of Kraft Prehydrolysis Liquor
abstract: Abstract Kraft mills that produce dissolving-grade pulp burn their prehydrolysis liquor in the recovery boiler. We quantify when converting this liquor to hydrocarbon fuels, at constant pulp output, lowers the climate impact of the mill. A consequential ex-ante life cycle assessment compares combustion with two routes scaled from the laboratory to industrial operation: one-step hydrodeoxygenation of furfural to hydrocarbons (HC route) and five-step synthesis of aviation-range hydrocarbons (AF route). title: Valence-driven structural transformation and phase coexistence in chemically substituted EuPd 2 Si 2
abstract: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. title: SIMPLE-C: Multi-LiDAR Extrinsic Calibration using a Simple Moving Reflective Target in Feature-Sparse Maritime Environments
abstract: Abstract Multi-LiDAR sensor configurations enhance perception for autonomous tasks in robotics compared to single sensors, but they require precise extrinsic calibration. Existing methods often depend on moving the platform or feature-rich environments, making them impractical in extremely sparse maritime settings where water surfaces yield unreliable LiDAR returns and vessels are expensive to move. title: Associations among interleukin-6, superior frontal gyrus thickness, and executive control in long-term high-altitude migrants
abstract: This study examined how systemic inflammation, prefrontal cortical structure, and executive control performance are related in long-term high-altitude residents. A total of 129 healthy Han Chinese adults who had relocated from low-altitude regions and were living and working in Lhasa, Xizang (3650 m) underwent hematological testing, structural MRI, and an Attention Network Test (ANT). title: Salmonella Serovars Distribution in Poultry Meat and Genetic Characterization of Antimicrobial-Resistant Isolates: A Five-Year Monitoring in Sicily
abstract: Salmonellosis is one of the most frequently reported zoonoses, and broiler meat/meat products are among its main vehicles of transmission. Continuous monitoring on Salmonella serovars and the spread of antimicrobial resistance is essential for epidemiological surveillance. From 2021 to 2025, a total of 350 poultry samples were collected in Sicily and analyzed for Salmonella spp. detection, serotyping and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) phenotyping. title: Recent environmental change shapes biotic homogenisation of Orthoptera and Mantodea communities in semi-dry grasslands
abstract: Semi-dry grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems in Europe. However, many grassland remnants are undergoing gradual habitat degradation due to climate change, atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and the relaxation or abandonment of traditional management. While declines of specialised insects have repeatedly been reported, the extent to which these drivers promote long-term community reorganisation and biotic homogenisation remains poorly understood. title: RcbHLH79 negatively regulates 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene biosynthesis and flower scent in roses
abstract: Roses hold significant ornamental, economic, and cultural value, particularly for their diverse fragrances. Among the volatiles, 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene (TMB), unique to ancient Chinese roses, contributes to their tea-like scent. Despite its significance, the molecular mechanisms regulating TMB synthesis remain poorly understood. This study integrates multi-omics approaches and molecular biology techniques to uncover the regulatory network of TMB biosynthesis in Rosa chinensis 'Old Blush'. title: Fitness and flexibility of metabolic phenotypes in a temperate resident bird
abstract: Abstract Resident songbirds in seasonal environments are adapted to fluctuating conditions and show marked phenotypic flexibility of metabolic rates. However, the potential strength and direction of selection for metabolic phenotypes may depend on the context of the seasonal and environmental conditions, which standardized metabolic rate is measured, and which life‐history traits (i.e., survival and reproduction) are considered. title: Targeting hepatocyte-derived LRG1 with dothiortone alleviates hepatic ischemia–reperfusion injury and remote renal damage via suppressing NETosis
abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI), a major complication following liver surgery, involves neutrophil infiltration and hepatocyte apoptosis that contribute to graft failure and multiorgan injury; however, the role of neutrophil-hepatocyte crosstalk remains unclear. Through proteomic profiling, leucine-rich α-2 glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) was identified as a markedly upregulated protein in mouse HIRI models, a finding corroborated by elevated plasma LRG1 levels in patients who underwent hepatectomy. title: Governance preferences for urban sustainability transformations in two European neighbourhoods
abstract: Abstract Urban sustainability transformations (UST) are claimed as necessary solutions to intertwined ecological, social and economic challenges related to the ”business-as-usual” urban development – including increased greenhouse gas emissions, decreased biodiversity and deepened social inequality. However, it is unclear how different types of governance modes bring the UST forward and whether understandings between stakeholders differ in what this should and could entail. We study how stakeholders perceive ideal governance and frame the envisioned process of UST in game-assisted negotiations

title: Valorization of banana plant corm: Optimization of starch extraction using response surface methodology and development of biodegradable packaging film
abstract: Banana plant corm, a starch-rich residue left in the field after fruit harvest, has received little attention as a feedstock for bio-based materials. This study is the first to use response surface methodology (RSM) to optimize starch extraction from banana corm and link the optimized starch directly to biodegradable packaging film production. Using a face-centered central composite design, sodium metabisulfite concentration (1–3%) and soaking time (60–180 min) were varied to maximize starch yield and lightness. title: Controlling Radical Reactivity for Visible‐Light Bioorthogonal Chemistry
abstract: Bioorthogonal chemistry enables selective reactions within complex biological environments. Visible‐light photocatalysis expands this toolbox by generating carbon‐centered radicals through single‐electron transfer under mild conditions, enabling selective bond‐forming transformations with spatiotemporal control. title: Influence of Sustainable Agricultural Practices on Microbial Aspects of Soil
abstract: Abstract Soil is a non-renewable natural resource essential for supporting plants, animals, and microorganisms. The intensification of conventional agriculture has substantially affected soil health, including its microbial component. This review evaluates how sustainable agricultural practices, including crop rotation, intercropping, cover cropping, organic amendments, and agroforestry, influence microbial aspects of soil health, with particular emphasis on microbial biomass, diversity, community composition, and functions related to nutrient cycling. title: Do legumes fulfill their promise of nitrogen release? Analyzing forage nutrient dynamics in crop–livestock systems
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the impact of nitrogen (N) and potassium (K) fertilization strategies in an integrated crop–livestock system (ICLS) involving common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) followed by winter pasture, focusing on nutrient cycling and forage production. Although legumes are commonly assumed to supply nitrogen to subsequent crops, this capacity is highly variable in common bean, for which biological nitrogen fixation may be limited and substantial nitrogen can be exported through harvested grain. title: Roles of Interstitial Albumin in the Subcutaneous Delivery of Therapeutic Peptides
abstract: Subcutaneous administration of biotherapeutics is increasingly favored for better safety profile, improved stability, and patient compliance compared with intravenous administration. Despite these advantages, the roles of extracellular matrix (ECM) components and interstitial proteins, particularly albumin, in the mechanisms governing therapeutic pharmacokinetics and bioavailability remain poorly understood. title: Sensitivity Kernels for Earthquake Coda-Correlation Wavefield Features and Applications to Global Seismology
abstract: Summary Seismic coda-correlation methods have revealed numerous body-wave-like features in globally stacked correlograms, offering new opportunities to constrain the structure of Earth’s deep interior. Unlike the common assumptions about the diffuse ambient noise field that enable reconstruction of surface waves, earthquake coda-correlation features arise from cross-terms in reverberating body waves of common slowness that share a subset of propagation legs. title: Navigating external conflicts, technological innovations, and financial risks for sustainable development: evidence from the EKC and ecological footprints in the next eleven
abstract: Abstract To achieve sustainable development, ongoing research needs further investigations in detail for stronger environmental protection. For this purpose, several studies have investigated the factors of ecological footprints (EF), but very few of them have taken external and internal conflicts with technological innovations in the context of EKC. Against this backdrop, this study applies some advanced techniques like wavelet plots and augmented mean group (AMG) methods over the panel data of 1984-2022 for the Next Eleven nations. title: Assessing sectoral output impacts of climate change in Iran using a dynamic input-output model
abstract: Iran is expected to experience increasingly severe economic consequences from climate change, given that its annual precipitation is less than one-third of the global average. This study investigates the potential impacts of climate change on economic output across different sectors of the Iranian economy using a dynamic input-output (IO) modeling framework. The results indicate that climate change could reduce annual aggregate economic output growth from approximately 2.7% under a no climate change baseline to 1.6–2.0% across the simulated climate scenarios. title: The Effect of News‐Based Measures of Biodiversity Exposure on Corporate Green Revenue Disclosure
abstract: ABSTRACT Biodiversity loss has emerged as a significant challenge for firms. As firms face increasing pressure from stakeholders to address nature‐related risks, green revenue disclosure has become a potentially important strategic means of communicating environmentally oriented business activities. Using 12,055 firm‐year observations from S&P 1500 firms from 2005 to 2023, this study examines whether and when a firm with biodiversity exposure (defined as a news‐based measure of biodiversity exposure risk based on textual analyses of 10‐K statements) is associated with green revenue disclosure.

title: Climate extremes, soil moisture, and agricultural production in Somalia: evidence from national annual data
abstract: Using 50 national annual observations for 1974–2023, this study examines short-run associations between agricultural production, drought severity, excess-rainfall intensity, soil moisture, agricultural land, and rural-population growth in Somalia. Production is measured by the FAOSTAT Agriculture Gross Production Index; climate and soil-water indicators are derived from monthly TerraClimate data. The analysis combines ARDL bounds testing, a mixed-order dynamic regression, robustness checks, bootstrap cointegration testing, and stability diagnostics. title: Mathematics Persistence as Influenced by Mathematics Higher-Order Thinking Skills and School Classroom Engagement in Math
abstract: This study examined the influence of mathematical higher-order thinking skills and school classroom engagement in math on the mathematics persistence of Grade 10 students in selected private schools in Davao City. A quantitative descriptive-correlational research design was employed. Data were gathered using adapted research instruments which were validated by experts and subjected to reliability test. title: Comparative in vitro Antifungal Efficacy of Botanical Seed Oils Against Geotrichum candidum Associated with Tomato Fruit Rot in Gombe State, Nigeria
abstract: In Nigeria, tomato production plays a major role in food security and income generation for farmers and traders Northern Nigeria. In Gombe State, as elsewhere in the north, field and postharvest losses resulting from microbial infections remain a major setback to sustainable tomato production and marketing. This study evaluated the antifungal efficacy of four botanical seed oils: neem, moringa, mahogany and castor, against Geotrichum candidum causing sour rot of tomato fruit. title: Determinants of agroforestry-based smallholder farmers’ choices of adaptation to climate change and variability in southern Rift Valley Escarpments of Ethiopia
abstract: Climate change poses substantial risks to agriculture and food security in Ethiopia, particularly among smallholder farmers in the southern Rift Valley. This study investigates the key determinants influencing adaptation choices among farmers in the Gedeo Zone. Employing an explanatory research design, the study integrates both quantitative and qualitative methodologies. A structured questionnaire was administered to a sample of 384 households across three districts, complemented by focus group discussions and key informant interviews to enrich qualitative insights. title: Oculomotor Behavior During Visually Guided Responses in Inline Speed Skaters
abstract: Inline speed skating requires efficient visual processing and oculomotor coordination, particularly during physically demanding exercise. This study investigated whether an acute training session alters oculomotor behavior during visually guided responses to spectrally narrow-band chromatic stimuli. Fifteen federated speed skaters (16.90 ± 6.54 years) were assessed before (PRE) and after (POST) a complete training session. title: Gene tree discordance characterizes shallow evolutionary scales of Tillandsia subgenus Tillandsia (Bromeliaceae, Poales)
abstract: Phylogenetic discordance poses significant challenges for reconstructing evolutionary relationships, particularly in recently diversified lineages where incomplete lineage sorting, hybridization, and gene flow may obscure evolutionary history. We employed a Hyb-Seq approach to generate complete plastomes and nuclear data from 295 loci to investigate phylogenetic relationships and discordance in the Tillandsia erubescens species group, a recently radiated lineage endemic to Mexico. title: From barriers to breakthroughs: Navigating success drivers of women entrepreneurs in China
abstract: Despite the adolescence stage, the past 30 years have evidenced the proliferation of mainstream academic research for the most interesting and emerging phenomenon, ‘Women Entrepreneurship’. To further shed light on the above-stated phenomenon, this study aims to explore the success drivers and challenges of women entrepreneurs in the specific context of China. title: A molecular characterization of Eastern Canada winter wheats for agronomic, quality, and disease resistance traits using KASP and STS markers
abstract: Abstract Winter wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) in Eastern Canada is under increasing pressure from stresses associated with climate change. Breeding programs must increase efficiency to keep pace with these changes, and marker‐assisted selection (MAS) remains an efficient tool to retain or introgress favorable alleles of key traits and improve their genetic gains. The present study characterized the Eastern Canadian Winter Wheat Genomic Selection (EWGS) panel of 352 varieties and breeding lines from four public winter wheat breeding programs in Ontario and Québec. title: FROM FOLLICLE TO FORMULATION: EXPLORING SAW PALMETTO AND CAFFEINE SHAMPOOS FOR ALOPECIA MANAGEMENT
abstract: Alopecia is a common hair disorder characterized by excessive hair loss and reduced hair density, with androgenetic alopecia (AGA) being strongly associated with genetic factors and dihydrotestosterone (DHT). Limitations of conventional treatments have encouraged the exploration of alternative topical formulations. Saw palmetto (Serenoa repens), rich in fatty acids and phytosterols, may influence 5α-reductase activity, while caffeine may promote hair follicle activity and regulate hair growth. title: A review of the biogenic fabrication of metal oxide nanoparticles using phytochemical reducing and stabilizing agents across diverse systems
abstract: Abstract The transition from laboratory-scale nanofabrication to sustainable industrial manufacturing is currently hindered by the “precision-toxicity trade-off,” where high-quality metal oxide nanoparticles (MONPs) traditionally require hazardous precursors or energy-intensive physical methods. This comprehensive review (covering literature from 2019 to 2026) proposes a biogenic surface engineering framework that uses plant-derived metabolites (phenols and flavonoids) as sophisticated dual-function capping ligands for specific metal oxides, including TiO₂, NiO, CuO, and CeO₂. title: Broad vaccine protection against globally diverse influenza A/H5Nx viruses
abstract: Influenza A/H5Nx viruses continue to diversify and undergo gene reassortment as they infect avian and mammalian hosts worldwide. The severity of human infections varies substantially between different H5 clades and neuraminidase (NA) reassortants, creating unpredictable pandemic risk. Existing H5 vaccines, typically based on a single hemagglutinin (HA) strain, cannot keep pace with this natural variation. title: Panax notoginseng residue fertilizer drives tobacco quality enhancement via rhizosphere multi-omics cascades
abstract: The potential of using traditional Chinese medicine residues as organic fertilizers to improve crop quality has attracted increasing attention, yet the underlying soil microecological mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of Panax notoginseng residue composite organic fertilizer on tobacco quality formation. A field experiment was conducted with three treatments: no organic fertilizer (CK), traditional farmyard manure (CL_1), and P. notoginseng residue fertilizer (CL_2). title: Water Footprint and Scarcity Risks of Low-Carbon Fuels
abstract: Abstract Production of ammonia, methanol, and hydrogen is key to decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors but is also water-intensive. However, the water implications of scaling these energy carriers under low-carbon pathways remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate direct water consumption with facility-level geospatial analysis and hydrological modeling to quantify water-scarcity exposure across each production facility in North America. title: Independent effects of sowing date and seeding rate on grain yield, seed quality, and quinolizidine alkaloid content in white lupin ( Lupinus albus L.) under rainfed subhumid conditions
abstract: Abstract White lupin ( Lupinus albus L.) is a high‐protein and nitrogen‐fixing leguminous plant with potential in rainfed systems, although approaches to maximize its yield, seed quality, and safety of quinolizidine alkaloids (QAs) remain inadequate in subhumid South Asian regions. title: Towards integrated fire management in the Peruvian Andes: Moving beyond disaster risk management to address wildfires
abstract: Wildfires pose an escalating environmental, economic, and social threat in the Peruvian Andes. This study examines wildfire disaster risk management (DRM) across seven Andean regions, assessing legal frameworks, institutional actions, and the integration of Integrated Fire Management (IFM). Combining documentary analysis and semi-structured interviews with public officials, it reveals fragmented, hierarchical governance and weak intergovernmental coordination. title: Performance of hermetic and conventional storage bags for controlling insect and rodent pests and preserving wheat quality in smallholder systems
abstract: Postharvest losses caused by insect and rodent pests remain a major constraint to food security in smallholder farming systems, necessitating effective storage technologies that preserve grain quantity and quality. This study evaluated the performance of ZeroFly® hermetic (ZFH), ZFH with polyethylene liner (ZFH + liner), conventional polypropylene (PP), and PP with polyethylene liner (PP + liner) bags during 12 months of household wheat storage in Ethiopia under homogeneous (single bag type per household) and heterogeneous (multiple bag types per household) storage configurations. abstract: Alkaline polymer electrolytes need a host combining low crystallinity for hydroxide transport with a cohesive network, but the contributions of blending and crosslinking remain unresolved in KOH-doped PVA/chitosan systems. title: A comparative TEA–LCA study of biomethane production through anaerobic digestion and five upgrading technologies: Amine scrubbing, water scrubbing, membrane separation, PSA, and cryogenic separation
abstract: Producing grid-quality biomethane from sewage-sludge biogas is promising, yet selecting an upgrading route remains uncertain because mature technologies differ in energy use, cost, methane losses in off-gas or vent streams, and the fate of biogenic CO 2 . This study evaluates anaerobic digestion integrated with five commercial upgrading technologies: amine scrubbing, water scrubbing (WS), membrane separation (MEM), pressure swing adsorption (PSA), and cryogenic separation (CRYO), modelled for a municipal wastewater treatment plant. title: Insight into the dynamics of intrinsic thermoacoustic instability-driven swirl flames
abstract: This study investigates the flame, flow, and acoustic coupling of intrinsic thermoacoustic (ITA)-driven combustion instability using a high-shear swirl injector in partially premixed mode in a model combustor. The combustor is operated with pure methane and a methane–hydrogen mixture as fuels, with the airflow rate varied while keeping the fuel flow rates constant, corresponding to a Reynolds number range of 8000–19 000 and a fixed thermal power of 16 kW. title: Deciphering salinity tolerance during germination in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L) through systematic phenotypic screening
abstract: Wheat is the major staple crop contributing about 20% of global calorie intake and ranks second to maize in worldwide production. It is vital to increase the production of wheat by about 70% by 2050 to feed world population. However, soil salinity is a critical constraint that impairs plant growth and development during germination stage. Therefore, identifying salt-tolerant bread wheat genotypes at germination stages is critical for mitigating yield losses. title: Metabolic ecology and habitat stability explain the disproportionately high species richness in standing waters
abstract: Abstract The metabolic theory of ecology (MTE) conceptualizes that temperature is the primary driver of species richness, a pattern well supported in terrestrial taxa but less certain for freshwater organisms. Limited global‐scale evidence and frequent violations of MTE's assumptions, particularly regarding the stationarity of body size and abundance, further undermine its applicability. abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater sustains streamflow in humid catchments, yet the interactions among hydraulic properties, groundwater storage, and isotope‐derived indicators remain poorly understood in tropical environments. This study investigated how topographic position and saturated hydraulic conductivity ( K sat ) influence groundwater storage and subsurface flow along a plateau–hillslope–valley toposequence in a tropical forest headwater catchment in Central Amazonia, Brazil. abstract: Abstract: Background: Nanoparticles have gained considerable attention as versatile platforms for the diagnosis and treatment of different diseases, particularly cancer. Lipid-coated hybrid nanoparticles (LCHNPs), comprising a polymeric core enveloped by a lipid shell, offer improved targeting and potential solutions for multidrug-resistant cancers. abstract: Abstract Despite the great diversity of tree species in the Neotropics, most commercial reforestation efforts in this region continue to rely on exotic species. Over the past few decades, with the aim of promoting the use of native species such as Retrophyllum rospigliosii , experimental plantations have been established in the tropical Andes to assess their viability for commercial reforestation projects. title: Development and validation of a measurement-based fatigue load model for railway bridges
abstract: Accurate fatigue assessment of existing railway bridges requires traffic load models that are both conservative and representative of actual operating conditions. This study develops and validates a measurement-based fatigue load model using four years of railway traffic data recorded by a Track Performance Detection System on a major mixed-traffic corridor in Hungary. abstract: Abstract Introduction Malaria remains one of the leading public health challenges globally, with over 95% of the disease burden occurring in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). In 2023, approximately 263 million malaria cases and 597,000 deaths were reported worldwide, most of them in Africa. Uganda continues to experience a high burden of malaria, particularly in transmission hotspots such as the Busoga sub-region in Eastern Uganda, where children under five years and pregnant women are disproportionately affected. title: Assessing the range expansion of a generalist carnivore by a novel approach combining questionnaires to experts and dynamic occupancy models
abstract: Abstract Despite the ongoing global biodiversity crisis, the geographic ranges of many mesopredators are expanding, largely driven by their generalist life histories and the decline of apex predators. Quantifying these expansions and identifying their underlying drivers remain challenging and require innovative methodological approaches. We aimed at quantifying the factors driving the recent spatial expansion of the Egyptian mongoose ( Herpestes ichneumon ) at the European edge of its range. title: Topographic gradient as a determinant of phylogenetic diversity patterns in the understory of a neotropical forest
abstract: Abstract Topography is a well-known driver of changes in plant community organization in the tropics. However, we have a limited understanding of how the evolutionary history of component species shapes the organization of these plant communities along topographic gradients. We investigated how the phylogenetic structure of an understory plant community changes along a topographic gradient. abstract: Abstract Four sets of dual-responsive statistical copolymers are synthesized from N,N-dimethylacrylamide and acrylamide comonomers bearing photoresponsive 4-aminoazobenzene (AzBn) side groups linked by various amino acid spacers. abstract: Karst systems sustain a substantial share of global freshwater supply, yet their internal discharge dynamics are difficult to characterize because conduit networks are often inaccessible to direct observation. Fluorescent tracer tests can quantify recharge-area-to-spring connections and travel times, but only under the conditions at the time of testing. title: Future of rare and endangered medicinal material substitutions: key strategies, challenges, and prospects
abstract: Owing to the combined impacts of anthropogenic and natural factors, rare and endangered traditional medicinal materials are experiencing progressive depletion, thereby necessitating urgent acceleration of research into viable substitutes. This article comprehensively reviews policies and strategies governing the development of substitutes for rare and endangered traditional medicinal materials, with particular emphasis on critically evaluating the respective advantages and limitations of natural versus artificial replacement strategies. title: Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Brain Network Dynamics Reveal Cognitive Function Variability During Acute High-Altitude Exposure
abstract: Abstract After acute exposure to high altitude (HA), the mechanism underlying hemodynamics-related cerebral function remains unclear and comprehensive and systematic studies are lacking. In this paper, functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was used to characterize cerebral activation and brain network dynamics during acute exposure to HA. title: MR imaging and spectroscopy reveals metabolic changes in glioblastoma driven by treatment with temozolomide and lonidamine
abstract: Abstract Resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) limits the efficacy of treatment in glioblastoma (GBM) which is fuelled by a metabolic reprogramming of the cancer cells and alterations in the tumour microenvironment. Lonidamine (LND), a glycolytic and mitochondrial inhibitor, modulates tumour metabolism and can alter tumour response to treatment. title: Climate Events and Life Satisfaction: The Role of Migration in Rural Bangladesh
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate change is increasingly displacing rural populations, and migration may reduce economic losses from environmental stress. However, climate events and migration can also entail social and psychological costs overlooked by economic measures. This paper examines the relationship between climate events and life satisfaction in Bangladesh and whether migration mediates this relationship. title: Hydrogen Production and Fuel-Cell Technologies: A Review of Operating Principles, Applications and Sustainability Challenges
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cell technology is a possible avenue for sustainable energy production and greenhouse gas reduction. This paper provides a detailed overview of hydrogen fuel cell such as their principle of operation, key types, hydrogen generation processes, technological advancement, application, problems and future possibilities. title: A framework for spatially quantifying household-level water-energy-food security: Application to South Africa
abstract: To be secure of Water-Energy-Food (WEF) resources is crucial for individual and public health and well-being, livelihoods and, ultimately, achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). While national level WEF security can be achieved, spatial inequalities exist due to the variations in local socio-economic and biophysical environments that determine WEF security. abstract: ABSTRACT As sustainability claims proliferate on food packaging, understanding their implicit market value is important for effective policy design and competitive firm strategy. This study quantifies the price premiums of sustainability attributes in the U.S. market using product‐level data. We analyze 210,515 food and beverage product launches from the Mintel Global New Products Database (2012–2024) and document a near‐doubling in the prevalence of sustainability claims, rising from 18% of new products in 2012 to 37% in 2024. title: Ant dominance may mask effects of tree diversity on carcass decomposition
abstract: Abstract Tree diversity promotes the diversity of organisms at higher trophic levels and associated ecosystem functions. Tree diversity may thus also influence communities of insect decomposers and thereby accelerate the decomposition of animal carcasses. To test this, we placed 864 dead mice and measured their decomposition over two days across 96 plots in a forest biodiversity experiment (BEF-China) during the monsoon season in subtropical China in 2024. title: Effects of emissions labels on consumer choice of lower-emission flights
abstract: Air travel generates disproportionate greenhouse gas emissions, without viable supply-side mitigation options. Demand-side measures, such as emissions information at the point-of-sale, are thus gaining interest. In a pre-registered experiment with a nationally representative sample ( N = 1,000), we tested whether current emissions labelling systems shift consumers towards lower-emission flights. Participants were randomised to see either (i) no emissions information, (ii) absolute emissions values, (iii) absolute values with a relative emissions label or (iv) absolute values with a relative la

title: Proton conducting Cicer arietinum L starch electrolyte doped with NH4SCN for electrochemical double layer capacitors
abstract: Abstract A chickpea starch–agar biopolymer electrolyte plasticized with glycerol and doped with NH 4 SCN was successfully developed for symmetric electrochemical double-layer capacitor (EDLC) applications. FTIR confirmed the interaction between NH 4 SCN and the biopolymer matrix, while XRD revealed increasing amorphous character with salt addition. The optimized CSA5 electrolyte exhibited a maximum ionic conductivity of 1.1 × 10 − 3 S cm −1 , a low bulk resistance of 43.60 Ω, an ionic transference number of 0.89, an electrochemical stability window of 1.8 V, and good thermal stability. title: Biosynthesis of selenium nanoparticles with orange peel waste in microwave: characterization, and spectral properties
abstract: Abstract The objective of this study was to reuse agroindustrial waste from orange peels to obtain an orange peel aqueous extract (OPEa), used in the biosynthesis and characterization of selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs). The OPEa acted as a reducing and stabilizing agent in the synthesis of SeNPs, due to its polyphenolic compounds, such as flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, and coumarins, identified by UHPLC-HRMS/MS. title: Performance of a solar box cooker with positive temperature coefficient heaters and thermal energy storage
abstract: Solar box cookers provide an environmentally friendly cooking option that can reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with conventional fuels. However, their principal limitations are slow cooking rates and dependence on favourable solar conditions. Even when thermal energy storage (TES) is incorporated, prolonged cloud cover can prevent effective cooking. This study experimentally investigates the thermal performance of a small solar box cooker equipped with six TES containers and two direct-current positive-temperature-coefficient (PTC) heaters connected in parallel. title: European robin cryptochrome 4a does not bind 8-HDF or MTHF as second antenna chromophores
abstract: Cryptochromes and photolyases are blue-light-sensitive flavoproteins that generally bind flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) and have distinct functions. Cryptochrome 4a (CRY4a) expressed in the double-cone photoreceptors of migratory songbirds such as the European robin ( Erithacus rubecula ) is the hypothesized primary sensor for avian magnetoreception. In addition to FAD, many photolyases and some cryptochromes bind antenna chromophores such as 8-hydroxy-5-deazaflavin (8-HDF) or 5,10-methenyltetrahydrofolate (MTHF). title: Dual Histone Deacetylase/PD-1/PD-L1 Inhibitors Reprogram Tumor−Immune Interactions and Are Effective in Therapy-Resistant Melanoma
abstract: Abstract Epigenetic modulators and immune checkpoint inhibitors represent two major therapeutic avenues in oncology, yet resistance and recurrence limit their efficacy. To address this, we designed and synthesized a series of dual histone deacetylase (HDAC)/PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors (compounds 1−6). Among them, compounds 4 (HDAC6-selective) and 5 (HDAC1−3-selective) emerged as the most promising, both disrupting the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction in the nanomolar range and reducing tumor cell viability in vitro. title: “Absolutely Pure, Therefore Best”? Manufacturing “Purity” in the British Cocoa and Chocolate Industry, c.1850–1939
abstract: Beginning with the famous advertising slogan for Cadbury’s Cocoa, “Absolutely Pure, Therefore Best,” this article examines how British cocoa and chocolate manufacturers shaped evolving meanings of food purity to their advantage across legislative and commercial domains, from the 1850s until the eve of the Second World War. The article applies a cultural history lens to discourses of food adulteration produced by government-appointed select committees, contemporary publications in newspapers, journals and magazines, advertising materials, and extant corporate archives. title: Domestic science vs. international science? The myth of the entanglement between science and politics in China on transboundary air pollution in East Asia
abstract: Introduction Since the 1990s, East Asia has prioritized the production of scientific knowledge based on monitoring and modeling data, devoting significant effort to understanding the source-receptor relationships of transboundary air pollution among countries in the region. However, the lack of a common understanding of the causal mechanisms underlying air pollution in the region has persisted for decades. Despite persistent disagreements regarding the causal understanding of transboundary air pollution, there has been little research assessing whether air pollution studies in the region are s

title: Critical mineral removal from mining‐impacted waters using microalgal biomass
abstract: Abstract Rising demand for critical minerals has led to increased mining and mineral processing activities, resulting in the release of metal‐contaminated waters requiring treatment. Conventional treatment methods, such as lime neutralization, effectively precipitate metals; however, they are less effective at low metal concentrations and produce large volumes of sludge. Microalgae offer a promising alternative approach for the remediation of mining‐impacted waters through extracellular biosorption and intracellular bioaccumulation mechanisms. title: Gravitational form factors of the proton in the improved holographic QCD model
abstract: A bstract We compute the gluonic contribution to the gravitational form factors of the proton using the improved holographic QCD model, in which the proton is described in terms of bulk Dirac fermions. Model parameters are constrained using lattice and phenomenological input, allowing us to obtain estimates for the gravitational form factors and to compare them with results from other approaches. Using the extracted form factors, we analyze mechanical properties of the proton, including pressure and shear distributions. title: Aging modifies the immunological signature of pesticide exposure: increased circulating sTREM-1 and sTREM-2 in rural workers
abstract: Pesticides pose significant risks to human health through both environmental and occupational exposure. In agricultural contexts, occupational exposure is particularly prevalent and has been linked to the activation of inflammatory pathways and dysregulation of the immune response. Nevertheless, the acute and chronic impacts of pesticide exposure on biomarkers of innate immunity remain poorly characterized. In this context, the soluble forms of TREM-1 and TREM-2 have emerged as sensitive indicators of inflammation and/or been associated with neurodegenerative disorders, respectively, however,
journal: International Archives of Occupational and Environmental Health

title: Over 20 years of GIAHS. A perspective on the impact and future development of the FAO Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems Programme
abstract: The Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS) Programme is a flagship initiative of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), aimed at identifying and preserving Agricultural Heritage Systems for future generations. GIAHS represent a rural development model based on dynamic conservation principles, provisioning of ecosystem services, and sustainability. This perspective paper aims to assess the evolution, impacts, and future development of the GIAHS Programme after more than 20 years since its establishment. To ensure the long-term effectiveness of the GIAHS Programme, we sug

title: Redox Orchestration of organ regeneration
abstract: Abstract The evolutionary transition from anaerobic to aerobic life imposed significant oxidative challenges, while also enabling the emergence of reactive oxygen species (ROS) as key regulators of cellular signaling. This review synthesizes current knowledge on how ROS, once considered merely toxic byproducts, have been co-opted as essential signaling molecules that orchestrate organ regeneration across phylogenetically diverse species. institutions: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

title: Beyond experience: Rating quality and rater behaviors in integrated writing
abstract: Assessing source-based writing is challenging for raters due to the complexity of language usage and source integration (Plakans & Ohta, 2021). During the rating process, raters draw upon their prior experience, but despite a substantial body of research (Barkaoui, 2010a; Lim, 2011), no consensus has been reached regarding the impact of experience on assessment quality. This explanatory mixed-methods study compares rating performance of six novice and four experienced raters, who rated text products from integrated writing tasks using an analytic rating scale. title: Spatial and seasonal variation in soil organic matter responses to landfill disturbance in the Hyrcanian Forests
abstract: Forest ecosystems are increasingly exposed to anthropogenic pressures that threaten soil functioning and long-term ecosystem stability. Among these pressures, landfill-based waste disposal has emerged as a growing concern in developing regions, particularly where forest soils play a central role in organic matter turnover and nutrient retention. However, the responses of these systems to waste-derived inputs under contrasting climatic settings remain insufficiently constrained. In this study, we examine how municipal solid waste disposal alters soil organic matter characteristics, with emphasi
institutions: Sari Agricultural Sciences and Natural Resources University

title: A Layered View of LLM Support in Underwater Robotics
abstract: This extended abstract discusses a specific and, in our experience, practically relevant role for large language models (LLMs) in underwater robotics. Our main premise is that, in underwater fielding missions, the immediate difficulty is often not the synthesis of new low-level control laws, but the operation of complex robotic systems under limited communications, partial observability, and expensive field time. In particular, a significant fraction of the effort during sea trials is devoted to fault diagnosis, telemetry interpretation, mission adjustment, and coordination across heterogeneou
institutions: NATO Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation

title: Bottom-boundary identification using asymptotic observers in dispersive shallow-water models
abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of identifying the bottom-boundary of an ocean basin, particularly in the coastal region where shallow-water theory applies. Our main contribution is the development of an easy-to-implement observer-based approach of identifying the bottom-boundary profile from measurements of the free-surface. Furthermore, we prove that the true profile can be obtained by minimising the long-time observation-error as computed from the observer equations associated with a class of linear dispersive shallow water-wave models. title: Projecting the Public: Reflections and Recommendations for Empirical Visualization Studies of General Audiences
abstract: Calls for shifting visualization research to general audiences outside of professional contexts have been put forward since the early 2000s, but expanding outwards means contending with a diversity in visualization's communicative purpose beyond transmitting insights from data. After our own experiences studying public-facing visualizations, we sought a set of considerations to help early-career visualization researchers reason through designing empirical visualization studies for the general public that confronts the various ways visualizations are interpreted.
