title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
abstract: Personal AI agents face social engineering attacks supported by forged multimodal content, but existing evaluations mainly focus on text-based dialogue, leaving their intrinsic security under such attacks insufficiently studied. We introduce Multimodal-SEA, an interactive benchmark comprising 608 expert-designed tasks grounded in real-world fraud cases, covering 14 domains and 152 attack scenarios with prepared multimodal content. The tasks span four difficulty levels and reflect the distinct social and cultural contexts of Chinese and English environments. Agents inspect content, verify reque
institutions: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

title: H-SPAR: Hydrodynamic-aware Simulation for Particle Transport and Autonomous Robots
abstract: Abstract Environmental robotic sampling requires considering the dual influence of water currents on robotic motion and particle transport. Existing marine robotics simulators generally model flow, autonomy, and sampling targets separately, limiting joint evaluation of mission cost and sampling performance. H-SPAR integrates spatially and temporally varying velocity fields, Lagrangian particle transport, probabilistic sampling, and ROS 2/Gazebo-based uncrewed surface vehicle (USV) autonomy. title: Experimental Realization of Higher-order Topological Water Wave Crystal
abstract: Free-surface water waves provide a macroscopic platform in which topological localization can be measured through surface-elevation fields. Higher-order topological phases offer a route to localizing wave modes at structural corners, yet their experimental realization in water-wave systems remains largely unexplored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a water-wave higher-order topological crystal, where surface waves are confined to structural corners and spectrally identified through measured free-surface responses. title: Grid Trouble in Paradise: Uncovering Vulnerable Distributed Energy Resources and Their Grid-Level Risks
abstract: Grid-connected solar distributed energy resources (DERs), such as solar inverters and monitoring platforms, have been deployed at unprecedented scale over the past few years, with global solar capacity more than doubling since 2022. To support monitoring and control, many of these systems are Internet-connected and configured by installers or end users, yet the real-world scale of their Internet exposure and the implications for power grid operation remain poorly understood. In this paper, we present an Internet-scale evaluation of exposed and vulnerable solar DER infrastructure, and assess th

title: Can You Say This for Me? Speaking Up by Proxy in Co-Located Discussion
abstract: Equal participation in co-located discussion is important for effective collaboration, yet people often hold back when they anticipate negative interpersonal or professional consequences, especially when raising a point requires voicing it themselves. We present SecondVoice, a mixed-reality system that enables people to speak up through an embodied virtual proxy. By separating what is said from who says it, SecondVoice brings hesitant points into the live spoken discussion without putting the speaker on the spot. Using a private overlay, users specify their intent through a structured specific

title: h-NESDF: An Infinitely Differentiable Signed Distance Between Two Sets with Robotic Applications
abstract: Computing distances between sets is important in many robotic applications, such as motion planning and control. In many applications, derivatives of the distance are needed as well. It is well known that the Euclidean distance is not always differentiable, which create issues to algorithms that need a derivative. In this paper, we introduce NESDF, the Normal Euclidean Signed Distance Function between two general (with mild regularity assumptions but possibly non-convex) sets. title: Riemannian Optimization-based Whole-body Obstacle Avoidance for Mobile Continuum Robots in Cluttered Environments
abstract: Inspired by the coordination of global motion and local shape adaptation in snakes, elephant trunks, and octopus arms, we propose a unified planning and control framework for mobile continuum robots in cluttered and confined environments. Existing approaches often address high-level path planning and local motion control separately, limiting coordinated base-arm motion, kinematic consistency, and collision avoidance. title: Lensless single-pixel imaging through dynamic coded-aperture illumination
abstract: We demonstrate a lensless single-pixel imaging (SPI) system combining dynamic coded-aperture illumination with single-pixel detection. Binary digital micromirror device (DMD) masks generate tailored grayscale intensity fields through coherent propagation, without relay projection optics or temporal grayscale synthesis. Six target-field configurations---uniform, Rayleigh speckle, squared-Rayleigh speckle, and sparse binary fields with $p=10\%$, $5\%$, and $1\%$---are evaluated using binary and grayscale objects. title: Meme Coin Factories: Uncovering Large-Scale Manipulations on pump.fun
abstract: Once complex, creating and deploying a new cryptocurrency has become trivial. Coin launchpads now allow users to generate a new coin with merely a few clicks, at a minimal cost. Launchpad popularity has grown in tandem with the rise of "meme coins," which usually do not offer any novel technological properties and are purely created for fun. The most prominent coin launchpad, pump.fun, has gained significant traction, grossing over 100 million USD in daily trading volume. The mass adoption of coin launchpads, however, also enables strategic actors to easily manipulate trading signals, unbeknow

title: K-subareas partitioning subject to coinciding boundary segments of neighboring subareas
abstract: A method for the problem of partitioning an area into K subareas subject to coinciding boundary segments of neighboring subareas is presented. The given area may be non-convex and may additionally include obstacle areas. The proposed hierarchical method involves three steps: repeated bisection splitting, merging and the solution of traveling salesman problems. Geographic real-world outdoors areas data is used for the evaluation of the method. The benefit of computational simplicity at the cost of imbalanced subarea sizes is highlighted.

title: Atomic Transition Rates on a Quantum Annealer
abstract: Electric-dipole (E1) transition rates underlie applications across many areas of physics and demand more accurate wavefunctions than ground-state energies do. We report the first calculation of E1 transition rates on a D-Wave quantum annealer, for neutral Li, Li-like Be, neutral Na, and Na-like Mg. We use a zooming-and-sigma-annealing scheme with floating-point encoding within the Quantum Annealer Eigensolver (QAE) algorithm, which yields ground-state eigenvectors accurate to the chosen three decimal places. title: SeCo-SBIR: Semantically Consistent Prompt Learning for Zero-Shot Sketch-Based Image Retrieval
abstract: Adapting CLIP for zero-shot sketch-based image retrieval (ZS-SBIR) via prompt learning faces a fundamental tension: the model must bridge the sketch-photo domain gap through task-specific adaptation, yet the added flexibility risks overfitting to seen training categories and eroding CLIP's zero-shot generalization. We present SeCo-SBIR, a semantically consistent prompt learning framework that resolves this tension from both sides. title: GINsim 3.1: Qualitative modelling and dynamical analysis of logical regulatory networks
abstract: GINsim is a software for the definition and dynamical analysis of qualitative (Boolean and multi-valued) models of biological regulatory networks. Building on its modular architecture, based on the MDDlib decision-diagram and bioLQM model-manipulation libraries, GINsim version 3.1 introduces new functionalities aimed at the analysis of large logical models: the symbolic computation of trap-spaces, the Booleanisation of multilevel models and the reversal of model dynamics. institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: Restoring Semantic Fidelity for Training-Free High-Resolution Image Generation in Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based text-to-image models have recently achieved remarkable success in image synthesis. However, when directly applied beyond their training resolution, these models often suffer from severe semantic degradation, where meaningful semantic content disappears. Although existing training-free high-resolution generation methods can mitigate this issue, the inherent semantic degradation at high resolutions remains largely unresolved, leading to degraded fine-grained details. institutions: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

title: AirForesight: Current-to-Future Spatial Map Imagination with Cross-Space Planning Consistency for UAV-VLN
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Vision-Language Navigation (UAV-VLN) requires agents to follow language instructions, infer spatial structure from sparse multi-view observations, and execute feasible 3D motion in complex outdoor environments. Despite recent progress with large language models, most existing methods still map vision-language inputs directly to actions, providing limited explicit scene grounding and future-aware spatial reasoning. title: Language Scent: Exploring Cross-Language Information Navigation
abstract: While multilingual users often switch between languages when seeking information, this process remains undersupported by current systems where information is typically siloed by language. Our formative study reveals that users select their search language based on its perceived value for their current information need, a concept we formalize as language scent. title: Schwinger Effect with a Transversal Boundary
abstract: We study the effect of a boundary on pair production by an electric field. In particular, we are interested in the case in which the electric field has a normal component with respect to the boundary. This is essentially more complex than pure tangential fields due to the reflection of created particles against the boundary. In this article we provide the explicit solution for the case of an instantaneous electric pulse which is spatially uniform and normal to a flat surface. title: Singular Perturbations for Control Systems Safety
abstract: Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) offer a powerful theory for enforcing safety in dynamical systems. Yet, applying this framework to complex systems is challenging when subsystems are feedback-interconnected and operate at different timescales. Such structures arise naturally in multiphysics systems and in control architectures where physical plants interact with optimization, estimation, and control algorithms. title: Nanobubbles, pristine emulsions, high ionic strength electrokinetics – Paradoxes of Colloid and Interface Science
abstract: There are three paradoxes in the modern Colloid and Interface Science supported by large bulk of experimental evidence and contradicting classical theoretical models: We overview many dozens of experimental papers by broad spectrum of scientific groups from many countries. We consider this vast experimental data as evidence that these phenomena exist. On other hand, classical theoretical models discussed here deny such possibility. title: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects
abstract: Training data can have unexpected side effects on language model behavior outside the training domain: insecure code data can induce broad misalignment, and outdated bird names can induce a 19th-century persona. Understanding such generalization is hard because only dozens of isolated examples exist, each constructed by hand or discovered by accident. We propose automatically discovering such datasets with surprising side effects (DSSEs). title: Dramarrator: Object-Based Audio Editing for Audio Drama Production from Books
abstract: Audio dramas weave dialogue, sound effects, and music into immersive stories. Creators often adapt books into audio dramas, but this process remains labor-intensive, requiring them to interpret source material, author scripts, generate audio assets, and assemble them on a timeline. Because story elements like characters and scenes manifest across many interdependent assets, a single change can ripple into manual updates across the entire project. We present Dramarrator, an audio drama authoring tool built around object-based audio editing, where these story elements are represented as editable

title: Brillouin comb line amplifiers for optical atomic clocks
abstract: Optical atomic clocks outperform the microwave clocks at the heart of current timing and navigation infrastructure by orders-of-magnitude, and recent progress in on-chip integration provides the opportunity to widely deploy them. Conventionally, a narrow linewidth laser interrogates the atomic transition, and an optical frequency comb divides its stabilised frequency (hundreds of terahertz) down to a microwave that is electronically countable. The laser(s) impose a significant size, weight, power and cost penalty, which is a current barrier to low-cost, scalable, fully on-chip optical clocks.

title: Empirical rather than simulated spectral band adjustment of MODIS to Sentinel-3 OLCI for European vegetation monitoring
abstract: Spectral band adjustment derived from convolved spectra describes sensor differences under controlled conditions, but its applicability to operational products requires assessment. We compare this approach with adjustment estimated directly from MODIS and Sentinel-3 OLCI observations for European vegetation monitoring. Both streams undergo atmospheric correction and Ross-Thick/Li-Sparse Reciprocal BRDF normalization to nadir viewing and local solar noon. title: NitroFusion2: Bringing Adversarial Loss to the Text Stream of Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Adversarial diffusion distillation has conventionally relied on image features for discrimination. We revisit this choice for multimodal diffusion transformers (MMDiTs), whose text stream becomes image-dependent through joint attention. We introduce Text-Stream Adversarial Distillation (TSAD), which exploits intermediate text-token states as a new adversarial representation. Because the text stream has already read the image while remaining tied to the text condition, changing that condition changes what information it extracts from the image. title: Annular webs and Guralnick's conjecture
abstract: Using annular webs and Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients, we disprove Guralnick's absolute boundedness conjecture for first cohomology.

title: Estimating cosmogenic backgrounds in nEXO at SNOLAB using Geant4 and FLUKA
abstract: The nEXO experiment was designed to search for neutrinoless double beta decay in the isotope $^{136}$Xe, using a five-tonne, isotopically-enriched liquid xenon time projection chamber (TPC). To meet nEXO's sensitivity goal, significant effort is placed on background mitigation strategies. Here, we evaluate the expected cosmogenic background rate for nEXO if placed at its preferred underground host site, SNOLAB. title: Bistatic UAV-Based 3D SAR Imaging Using Integrated Sensing and Communications Transceivers
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks enable autonomous systems to jointly perform radar sensing and wireless communication using common spectral and hardware resources. Prior art on ISAC-enabled UAV for SAR focused on monostatic configurations for two-dimensional target imaging. In this work, we propose a bistatic UAV tomographic SAR framework in which the IEEE~802.11ad waveform, RF hardware, and spectral resources are jointly utilized for communication and radar sensing for three-dimensional (3D) localization of complex targets. title: Vanishing sea ice threatens Southern Ocean isopod species diversity
abstract: Sea-ice retreat is rapidly transforming the Southern Ocean (SO), yet consequences for benthic biodiversity remain poorly resolved. Here, we show that declining sea ice is directly linked to reduced species diversity in benthic isopods, a dominant SO fauna (Pearson's r = 0.56). We analysed 214 isopod species from 78 genera in the Atlantic sector using a 14-year dataset integrating satellite and in situ observations across 60-77° S and 403-4976 m depths. title: Graph-theoretic multi-view feature engineering for interpretable BGP Anomaly detection
abstract: Graph-based and flat, statistical feature spaces are both used for operational anomaly detection, yet how complementary they are---and how well detectors built on them transfer across deployments---remains largely untested. We study both questions for Internet interdomain routing (BGP). We combine a graph-topological view and a statistical view in a multi-view detector and evaluate cross-domain transfer with a 2 x 2 factorial design (two autonomous systems, two route collectors) and CORAL domain adaptation over 12 directed transfer pairs. abstract: Abstract Accurate, high‐resolution measurements of Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) are essential for radiative forcing assessment and air quality management. However, a critical observational gap exists between ground in situ monitoring networks (e.g., AErosol RObotic NETwork) and satellite products compromised by low revisit frequency, and sparse resolution. title: A Comprehensive Review on Biostimulants for Sustainable Agriculture: Global Market Trends and Experimental Challenges
abstract: Biostimulants are substances, either natural or synthetic, that enhance plant growth without functioning as fertilizers or pesticides. According to the European Biostimulants Industry Council and EU regulations, biostimulants improve the efficiency of nutrient use, help plants withstand challenging conditions, and increase crop yields by activating specific plant functions. Unlike biofertilizers, which supply nutrients through living microbes, biostimulants influence plant development and interactions with beneficial microbes. title: From Stream to State: Engaging Communities in Approved Water Monitoring Frameworks
abstract: Abstract More than 50% of Oklahoma's surface water systems are classified as impaired by the US EPA, with limited funds designated toward surface water monitoring. Community science data can contribute to increasing the amount of quality‐controlled government water quality reporting. A framework is presented for implementing a community‐based approach to generating quality‐controlled water field data to support water quality monitoring by local and regional governments. title: Marine Gravity Field Refinement Using Iterative Frequency-Domain Combination
abstract: Summary High-accuracy marine gravity fields are essential for resolving fine-scale seafloor structures and supporting marine geophysical studies. However, the recovery of short-wavelength gravity signals from conventional satellite altimetry is limited by track spacing, measurement noise and filtering. The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides dense wide-swath observations and improves the recovery of shorter-wavelength sea-surface slopes. title: A review of the cost-effectiveness of using near-patient G6PD tests before treatment with radical cure of vivax malaria
abstract: Abstract Background Currently, primaquine and tafenoquine are the only available drugs to kill the dormant liver-stage parasites of Plasmodium vivax and P. ovale spp. Since both drugs can cause life-threatening hemolytic events in individuals with glucose−6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, G6PD screening is recommended before their prescription. title: Development Status and Future Directions of Unmanned Surface Vehicles in Marine Geological Surveying
abstract: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) have emerged as a new type of marine carrier platform and are attracting increasing attention in marine geological surveying owing to their flexibility, low observability and unmanned operation. This review systematically traces the development history and current status of USVs worldwide and in China and summarizes the state of the art of USV-based marine geological survey technology from three perspectives: autonomous control, sensor integration, and data transmission and processing. title: Nanotechnology-enabled construction of bispecific and multispecific antibody platforms for enhanced antitumor therapy
abstract: Refractory solid tumors are characterized by pronounced antigen heterogeneity, dense tissue barriers, and immunosuppressive microenvironments, which limit the tumor coverage and durable immune clearance achieved with conventional monospecific antibodies. Bispecific and multispecific antibodies (BsAbs and MsAbs) can recognize two or more antigens or epitopes, thereby integrating tumor targeting, immune-cell recruitment, and regulation of multiple signaling pathways within a single therapeutic system. title: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
abstract: Abstract Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m −2 yr −1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m −2 yr −1 . title: Consistency of HY-2B/C/D Altimeter Sea State Products in Chinese Coastal Seas: Wave Height, Wind Speed, and Parameter-Dependent Inter-Satellite Bias
abstract: The HY-2B/C/D constellation delivers routine altimeter significant wave height (SWH) and sea-surface wind speed over the Chinese coastal seas through four product streams (GDR, IDR, ODR, and SDR), yet whether the three satellites are mutually consistent, and whether that consistency is the same for both parameters, has not been established. title: Microplastics and environment-weighted ecological risk: synergistic response of marine sedimentary microorganisms in the East China Sea
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as a critical environmental threat to the East China Sea. Nevertheless, existing studies highlight a notable data gap regarding the distribution patterns of MPs in marine sediment, not to mention the associated ecological risks. This study revealed the distribution patterns of MPs in offshore and open sea sediments of the East China Sea by combining laser direct infrared spectroscopy and pyrolysis-gas chromatography–mass spectrometry. title: Combinatorial Selection of Multi-Pass ICESat-2 ATL24 Calibration Tracks for Sentinel-2 Satellite-Derived Bathymetry
abstract: ICESat-2 ATL24 data provide along-track shallow-water depths that can serve as spaceborne calibration information for satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB). A study area is usually crossed by multiple passes, but the tracks differ in quality, depth coverage, and spatial coverage. Existing studies still mainly pool all tracks, use a single pass, or refine the data point by point, and no systematic method yet exists for selecting among large numbers of candidate-track combinations. title: Screen-printed inorganic perovskite thick-film sensor for clinical electron beam quality assurance
abstract: Abstract In the field of radiation therapy, inorganic perovskites, which exhibit excellent radiation responsiveness, are attracting attention as solid-state sensor materials for precise quality assurance (QA). However, conventional nano-scale perovskite thin-films have limitations due to insufficient active volume in measuring high-energy (high-E) radiation characterized by high penetrating power. To overcome these limitations, we fabricated a micro-scale CsPbI 2 Br thick-film sensor and irradiated it with high-E electron beams of 6, 9, and 12 MeV using a clinical linear accelerator under expe

title: ASSESSMENT OF THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE MARINE INSURANCE MARKET IN THE BLACK SEA UNDER HEIGHTENED OPERATIONAL AND FINANCIAL RISK
abstract: This paper analyzes the sustainability of the marine insurance market in the Black Sea region amid ongoing geopolitical instability and an escalating risk environment. It examines the impacts of operational risks (military actions, sea mine hazards, rerouting) and financial risks (surging war risk premiums, sanctions regimes, elevated freight rates) on vessel insurance coverage. The adaptation mechanisms of insurers and Protection & Indemnity (P&I) Clubs are evaluated alongside the broader implications for maritime supply chain security and transport economics in the Black Sea basin.
journal: EPRA International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research (IJMR)

title: Impact of Winter Convection on Carbon Variability in the South Adriatic Gyre: A 1D Argo‐Driven Modeling Approach
abstract: Abstract Understanding the variability of air–sea carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) fluxes is fundamental for quantifying the ocean's role in the global carbon cycle. While large‐scale and long‐term flux patterns are relatively well constrained, the processes driving variability at regional and shorter temporal scales remain poorly understood. Addressing this gap is crucial for improving our understanding of how physical and biogeochemical processes modulate ocean‐atmospheric carbon exchange. This study examines two research questions: whether the use of pair trawl by Vietnamese fishing vessels complies with Law No. 45 of 2009 on Fisheries (Fisheries Law) and the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS 1982); and how the applicable legal framework has been enforced. title: Measurement report: Size-resolved seasonal study of inorganic ions and isotopic carbon signatures of aerosol particles at the Wadden Sea
abstract: Measurements of aerosol size-resolved chemical composition and source contribution of carbonaceous aerosols provide a unique opportunity to characterize continental outflow over the sea. Studies at coastal sites usually show an interesting mix of continental and marine aerosol sources. However, few data exist on the size dependence of the aerosol chemical composition and isotopic source apportionment of organic carbon (OC). title: Vertical Ozone Structures and Sea-Breeze Transport in Southern Taiwan Revealed by UAS Observations during the KPEx 2024 campaign
abstract: Ground-level ozone is a persistent air quality problem in southern Taiwan, particularly in the Kao-Ping region. However, the roles of coastal emissions, sea-breeze circulation, and photochemistry in inland ozone enhancement remain poorly resolved due to limited vertical observations. This study combined surface measurements at the coastal Linyuan site and the inland Wanluan site with 191 unmanned aircraft system (UAS) profiles collected during the Kao–Ping Experiment (KPEx) from February to March 2024. title: Eocene Environmental Evolution and Organic Matter Enrichment in a Marine–Continental Transitional Rift Basin: Insights from the Northern and Central Sectors of the Western Slope Belt, Xihu Sag, East China Sea Shelf Basin
abstract: The Eocene Baoshi Formation (BAF) and Pinghu Formation (PIF) are the main source-rock intervals in the western slope belt of the Xihu Sag, East China Sea Shelf Basin. This study integrates TOC and Rock-Eval pyrolysis, major and trace element geochemistry, and biomarker data from five wells to reconstruct the Eocene paleoenvironmental evolution and evaluate the controls on organic matter (OM) enrichment. title: High-Resolution Nearshore Wave Direction Retrievals from X-Band Radar Using an Adapted Slope-Array Method
abstract: Abstract Coastal observing platforms typically lack the spatial resolution needed to monitor the transformation of surface gravity waves, which impact nearshore circulation patterns, wave-driven runup, and sediment transport. Previous studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of deriving surface wave information from X-band radar by applying three-dimensional Fast Fourier Transforms (3D FFTs) to backscatter images in the open ocean. Near the coast, however, X-band retrievals are more challenging to interpret since wave fields are spatially inhomogeneous due to bathymetrically driven shoaling

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Analyses Reveal Metabolic Reprogramming and Stress Responses in Spotted Sea Bass Lateolabrax maculatus Under Cold Stress
abstract: Low temperature is a major environmental stressor that severely affects the physiology and survival of marine fish. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying cold stress responses in spotted sea bass Lateolabrax maculatus remain poorly understood, particularly from a multi-omics perspective. Here, integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses were performed to systematically investigate hepatic responses to acute cold stress (8 °C). title: SUSTAINABLE COASTAL TOURISM IN THE MTHUNZINI AREA, SOUTH AFRICA: CHALLENGES, LESSONS, AND STRATEGIC INTERVENTIONS
abstract: Sustainable coastal tourism in the Mthunzini area of South Africa holds immense potential to stimulate local economic growth, preserve marine biodiversity, and strengthen community livelihoods. However, several interlinked challenges have constrained this potential. Key barriers include inadequate infrastructure development. The overreliance on seasonal tourism, the lack of inclusive participation by local communities, and the insufficient marketing of Mthunzini’s unique ecological and cultural assets further intensify the problem. title: Marine bioindicators of volcanism: Trace metal patterns in Anemonia viridis across two eruptive events
abstract: Volcanic eruptions release trace metals that can accumulate in marine biota, yet few studies have compared bioaccumulation patterns between submarine and subaerial events using the same sentinel species. We measured eight metals (Al, Cd, Cu, Fe, Li, Ni, Pb, and Zn) in the sea anemone Anemonia viridis at one volcanic and one control site on each of two Canary Islands: El Hierro, affected by the submarine Tagoro eruption of 2011 and 2012, and La Palma, affected by the subaerial Tajogaite eruption of 2021. title: Microplastic contamination in sediments and bivalves from a litter-retaining Scottish sea loch: body-size scaling and growth-related traits
abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastic pollution is widespread in coastal environments, yet its relationship with organism-level variation under natural field conditions remains poorly understood. This study quantified microplastic contamination in intertidal sediments and two bivalve species, cockles ( Cerastoderma edule ) and mussels ( Mytilus edulis ), from Arrochar, a semi-enclosed sea loch on the west coast of Scotland. title: Mission-Oriented Payloads and Platform Support for Unmanned Surface Vehicles: From Aquatic Observation to Operational Applications
abstract: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) are increasingly used for hydrographic surveying, environmental monitoring, ecological observation, infrastructure inspection, and underwater search. Previous studies often focus on autonomous navigation, vehicle design, platform types, or individual applications, leaving relationships among mission objectives, payloads, platform support, and data products unclear. This paper examines these relationships for USV tasks beyond routine navigation-related surface perception. title: Microplastic Contamination in Riverbank Sediment and Commercial Marine Fish in Eastern Sabah, Malaysia
abstract: ABSTRACT The occurrence of Microplastic (MP) pollution has been receiving more attention worldwide. However, to date, no comprehensive study has examined the occurrence and spatial distribution of microplastic pollution in Tawau, Eastern Sabah, Malaysia. Therefore, the objective of this study is to investigate the occurrence and distribution of MPs in the riverbank sediment from Tawau River and commercial marine fish presence in Tawau area. title: How decision‐makers perceive and assess risk is key to scaling up coastal restoration
abstract: Abstract Understanding how government decision‐makers perceive and assess risk is essential to scaling up coastal restoration. We examined risk perceptions associated with oyster reef restoration and reintroduction of tidal flow by interviewing 17 permitting officials across Queensland, New South Wales, and Commonwealth agencies. Participants identified a wide range of risks, often shaped by uncertainty, novelty, and regulatory frameworks designed primarily to prevent harm rather than enable restoration. abstract: The use of Earth Observation data for monitoring of aquatic and coastal ecosystems has expanded significantly, yet gaps remain in the spectral and thermal capabilities needed to detect and characterize liquid discharges. This study evaluates the potential of simulated pre-launch CHIME and LSTM observations, integrated with operational Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 data, for water-quality anomaly detection across diverse aquatic environments, demonstrating that the simulated datasets are sufficiently realistic to reproduce key water-quality and thermal indicators and support pre-operational applic

title: Richness and composition of Coleoptera (Curculionidae, Scarabaeidae and Passalidae) in a tropical coastal mountain range in Colombia
abstract: Current conservation challenges have made it imperative to document insect fauna, which faces many threats, especially in megadiverse countries like Colombia. However, exploring large taxonomic groups at a regional scale imposes technical and budgetary limitations that are difficult to overcome. In this project, academics and members of the Arhuaca indigenous community of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (SNSM), in Colombia, joined forces to study three groups of beetles (Coleoptera): weevils (family Curculionidae), bess beetles (family Passalidae) and dung beetles (Scarabaeidae, Scarabaeinae)

title: Salicylic acid offsets productivity-infrastructure trade-off in marine microalga cultivation without carbon dioxide dosing
abstract: Salicylic acid supplementation recovered part of the productivity lost when a marine microalga was grown at elevated salinity without carbon dioxide dosing or pH control. Chrysochromulina rotalis was grown in a six-stage sequential-batch cascade in 10 L bubble-column photobioreactors, with pH control switched off, restored and switched off again at 35 and 50 practical salinity units and paired supplemented and control reactors at every stage. abstract: Abstract The continuous advancement of magnetic shielding technology has posed greater challenges for underwater magnetic target detection. Given that installation position errors are inevitable during the installation of underwater fluxgate sensor, and that significant errors can cause the detection system to fail, a localization method based on event-triggered particle swarm optimization (ET-PSO) is proposed for underwater fluxgate sensors. title: State Obligations and the Fragmentation of Regional Legal Regimes in Governing Illegal Fishing Marketing Networks in the Strait of Hormuz: Implications for Coastal Food Security
abstract: The Strait of Hormuz is widely recognised as a critical chokepoint for global energy transportation, yet its fisheries governance has received limited attention in legal scholarship. This article examines how fragmentation within the regional legal regime creates gaps in state obligations that may enable illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing and associated marketing activities to persist. title: Response of sunflower varieties to silicon in the coastal region of Bangladesh
abstract: Silicon is known as a beneficial plant nutrient element; however, its beneficial role in sunflower grown at coastal ecosystem of Bangladesh is yet not documented. This experiment was conducted in a coastal region to examine the effect of Si supplementation on the growth, yield and Si uptake of different varieties of sunflower. The experiment was set at Kartikpasha village of Dumki upazila, Patuakhali district during Rabi (dry) season of 2024. title: Biological insights and methodological challenges learned from working with a diverse heterotrophic marine bacterial library
abstract: Abstract Organized collections of bacterial strains can help bridge the gap between studying model organisms and communities, through comparative experiments between genetically and phenotypically diverse strains. Yet, to date, few studies discuss in a detailed and systematic manner the processes of collecting and maintaining bacterial strain libraries. title: Unlocking the Seaweed Value Chain: Constraints and Possible Solutions in the Understudied Coastal Areas of Mainland Tanzania
abstract: ABSTRACT Seaweed is a vital food and livelihood resource in Tanzania, with potential to strengthen and diversify food systems. It enables the production of high‐value products while delivering environmental benefits. Tanzania has witnessed promising research and advances in the seaweed value chain (VC), particularly in Zanzibar. abstract: Coastal ecosystems harbor diverse Vibrio populations that facilitate the decomposition of organic matter while simultaneously encompassing species with significant implications for aquatic animal and human health. This investigation examined the prevalence of culturable Vibrio spp. and evaluated extracellular enzyme activities in isolates recovered from the Ponnani coastal region, Kerala, India. title: Plastic and Microplastic Pollution in the Nile River and the Eastern Mediterranean: Sources, Occurrence, Ecological and Human-Health Risks
abstract: Plastic pollution has become one of the most pervasive forms of environmental contamination, and the semi-enclosed Mediterranean Sea is among the most plastic-polluted water bodies in the world. Rivers are major conduits of land-based plastic to the sea, yet the Nile, the longest river on Earth and the lifeline of Egypt and Sudan, was not studied for microplastics until 2020. title: The crabeater seal reference genome reveals hallmarks of persistently large effective population size and sustained population expansion in the World’s most abundant pinniped
abstract: Population genetic theory predicts that a species' demographic history shapes patterns of genome-wide variation. However, conservation genomic studies have disproportionately focused on small or declining species, where low genetic diversity and inbreeding are major concerns, while highly abundant species have attracted comparatively less attention. Here, we investigate the crabeater seal (Lobodon carcinophaga) which, despite being one of the most numerous large mammals on Earth, remains largely uncharacterised in terms of its genomic diversity and demographic history. title: Prompt engineering for synthetic deep-sea mining video: A controlled evaluation of four text-to-video systems
abstract: Abstract Deep-sea mining video is scarce, and low illumination, sediment plumes, and moving equipment challenge visual monitoring. We evaluated four text-to-video systems on six VBench dimensions, first in an archived 300-video system-level comparison and then in a 240-video extension crossing four prompt conditions, five scenarios, and three requested seeds. title: Anchors as weapons: Chinese maritime grey-zone operations and the limits of Chinese influence typologies
abstract: Existing typologies of Chinese influence in Europe organise activities into four categories: economic leverage, elite capture, information manipulation, and critical infrastructure positioning. This paper argues that Baltic Sea cable incidents since 2023 require a fifth – physical grey-zone operations – that the existing typology cannot capture. title: Marine-derived chitosan as an antimicrobial biopolymer: properties, mechanisms, applications, and perspectives from Vietnam
abstract: Marine-derived chitosan, primarily obtained from crustacean shell by-products, is a biodegradable and biocompatible biopolymer with antimicrobial activity reported against a range of bacteria, yeasts, and filamentous fungi. Growing concerns about food safety, antimicrobial resistance, and sustainable use of seafood-processing waste have increased interest in chitosan-based antimicrobial systems for seafood preservation, packaging, and aquaculture. title: A framework for assessing producer empowerment in wild-capture marine fisheries: insights from MSC-certified fisheries in developing economies
abstract: Abstract Empowerment is increasingly recognised as a critical dimension of sustainability in marine fisheries, particularly in promoting equity. Recognising and reporting empowerment dynamics could enhance sustainability outcomes and build resilience in fishing communities. However, little is known about how management interventions, such as eco-certification schemes, render producer empowerment visible or not. This paper makes two contributions. title: Beyond the tip of the iceberg: widespread plastic and cellulosic contamination in fish consumed by island populations of French Polynesia
abstract: Marine organisms across Pacific Islands are increasingly exposed to a complex mixture of anthropogenic particles, yet regional patterns of contamination and the relative contribution of plastic particles versus cellulosic fibers remain poorly understood. Here, by examining 180 fish from two reef species across six islands and 12 tuna specimens from the open ocean, we provide the first multi-species, multi-island assessment of debris (> 100 µm) ingested by fish in French Polynesia. abstract: ABSTRACT Pradofloxacin is approved orally for dogs and cats and parenterally for cattle and pigs in the U.S. The objective was to determine the pharmacokinetics of pradofloxacin in loggerhead turtles ( Caretta caretta ) and whether the plasma concentration is sufficient to treat susceptible bacteria. Pradofloxacin (200 mg/mL, diluted to 20 mg/mL in sterile saline) 10 mg/kg was administered SC and IV to 16 yearling loggerhead turtles with sparse sampling blood collection. title: Exploring Environmental Influences on Mono(2‐Ethylhexyl) Phthalate (MEHP) Exposure in Common Bottlenose Dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) in Sarasota Bay, FL, USA
abstract: Abstract Phthalates, endocrine‐disrupting, persistent organic pollutants widely used in plastic manufacturing, can readily enter aquatic environments and contaminate estuaries. As apex predators, resident bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) provide critical insights into ecosystem health. title: THE EVOLUTION OF DOMESTIC OLIGOPOLISTIC SHIPPING MARKETS IN INDONESIA THROUGH THE LENS OF THE CABOTAGE PRINCIPLE
abstract: Indonesia has confined domestic sea transport to national-flag vessels since Presidential Instruction No. 5/2005 and Law No. 17/2008, and the national fleet has expanded markedly since. Whether protection of this kind also entrenches market power in container liner shipping, a segment with high sunk costs and strong scale economies, remains an open empirical question. abstract: Dredged Marine Soil (DMS) is considered improper for use as a subgrade in roads due to high moisture content, low strength, and inability to withstand load. Additionally, there are concerns about the environmental aspects of disposing of DMS, thus necessitating the search for appropriate methods for sustainable use. abstract: Silicon (Si) has emerged as a beneficial nutrient element for increasing crop resilience under various stresses; however, limited information is available regarding the comparative performance of different application methods and sources for wheat production in coastal areas of the Ganges delta. A field experiment was conducted during two consecutive winter seasons of 2024–25 and 2025–26 in Patuakhali district of Bangladesh, to examine the effects of different Si sources and application methods on growth, yield, Si uptake and economic performance of wheat in coastal soil. title: Ultrawide‐Temperature Stable Superelasticity in a Nanoprecipitation‐Strengthened NiTi Strain Glass Alloy
abstract: ABSTRACT Superelastic materials exhibiting flag‐shaped hysteresis are valued for their high elasticity and damping capacity, which arise from stress‐induced martensitic transformation and related phase‐transition hysteresis, enabling effective energy absorption and vibration mitigation. abstract: Small urban mangrove remnants may undergo substantial spatial reorganization that regional land-cover products or endpoint area change alone poorly represent. abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated potassium (K) adsorption characteristics of soils derived from five contrasting parent materials (alluvium, basement complex, coastal plain sand, sandstone, and shale) at three soil depths (0-20, 20-40, and 40-60 cm) in Southeastern Nigeria. DOA chickens, defined as birds died between catching and unloading at the slaughterhouse, pose food safety risks and are prohibited (haram) for Muslims. title: A fractional–order MRSA transmission model: theoretical analysis and screening strategy comparison
abstract: Hospital outbreaks of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) remain difficult to contain because both patients and healthcare workers can carry and transmit the bacterium, often without symptoms. A Caputo fractional-order model is developed to capture this transmission process at hospital admission and discharge, partitioning the hospital population into uncolonized, colonized, and infected patients, uncontaminated and contaminated healthcare workers, and screened community members classified as flagged or unflagged. abstract: Early Permian magmatism records a major phase of tectonomagmatic reorganization in eastern Tianshan. Small felsic plutons provide age constraints on this transition and preserve evidence of crustal melting and magma differentiation, but their source relationships and temporal links to regional deformation remain incompletely resolved. abstract: ABSTRACT The Lower Cretaceous reservoirs off the coast of the Mandawa Basin, in the East Pande Block of southern coastal and offshore Tanzania, have been poorly studied, and their detailed petrophysical properties remain insufficiently documented. This study integrates the interpretation of velocity deviation logs and conventional well logs, including sonic, neutron, density, gamma ray, and resistivity logs, to characterize these reservoirs. abstract: Advanced aerosol measurements at high-altitude observatories are scientifically valuable but operationally demanding, and the established standard procedures, such as those of WMO/GAW and ACTRIS, were developed largely for near sea level stations. This technical note sets out operating procedures for advanced aerosol instruments at high-altitude sites, with an emphasis on tropical observatories, and is intended to complement rather than restate those guidelines. abstract: Change-oriented behavior (CB), that is, self-directed actions that question and seek to improve how work gets done, is one way employees drive constructive change at work. abstract: Background: Bupropion and sertraline, together with their major metabolites hydroxybupropion and desmethylsertraline, require reliable simultaneous determination for pharmaceutical quality control, stability assessment, and analytical characterization. abstract: The albacore (Thunnus albacares) is one of the large migratory fish species regularly landed by the small-scale coastal fishery at the Abobo-Doumé canoe wharf in Côte d’Ivoire. This study focuses on determining several reproductive parameters of this species. This was achieved by monitoring the gonadosomatic ratio (GSR), the hepatosomatic ratio (HSR), the condition factor (K), and the macroscopic appearance of the gonads in females and males, as well as by determining the sex ratio within the studied population. title: Diversity of Cladocera and Cyclestherida (Crustacea, Branchiopoda, Diplostraca) in continental waterbodies of southern Vietnam
abstract: Microscopic crustaceans, particularly Branchiopoda, often dominate the zooplankton and microzoobenthos of continental waterbodies and are widely utilised in aquaculture as a vital food source for fish and invertebrates. Despite their ecological and economic importance, the knowledge of their diversity and distribution remains highly uneven across the globe. title: Towards an Integrated Maritime Court System in Indonesia: Realizing Fair, Efficient, and Low-Cost Justice in Maritime Disputes
abstract: Abstract: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelagic nation and has significant economic opportunities in its ocean-based industries. However, the legal framework governing maritime activities is fragmented across multiple disconnected areas. At present, maritime disputes fall under the jurisdiction of different institutions: the Maritime Court, District Court, Fisheries Court, and National Transportation Safety Commission. This divided arrangement creates problems with overlapping powers, procedural bottlenecks, and uncertainty for businesses and individuals working in the maritime sector.

abstract: International maritime transport plays a central role in the global economy while significantly contributing to greenhouse gas emissions, thus positioning itself within the contemporary debate on climate change. abstract: Rasa Śāstra is an important branch of Ayurveda concerned with the identification, processing, pharmaceutical transformation, and therapeutic use of metals, minerals, and other Rasa Dravyas. Rasa Dravya Vargikarana provides a systematic framework for understanding these substances based on their properties, pharmaceutical applications, therapeutic importance, and role in Parada Karma. abstract: Coccoloba uvifera (L.) L. is widely cultivated in coastal regions of Vietnam, but phytochemical data on Vietnamese-grown material remain limited. This study investigated the flavonoid constituents and antioxidant activity of C. uvifera leaves using a bioactivity-guided approach. The leaves were extracted with 80% ethanol and successively partitioned with n-hexane, chloroform, ethyl acetate, and water. abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium relies on biofilm formation to withstand environmental stressors, resist antimicrobials, and establish persistent host infections. title: Beyond Aggregate Import Dependency: Commodity-Specific Food Price Transmission in Developing Asia
abstract: Global food-price shocks pose a challenge for developing Asian economies, but aggregate import-dependency measures can obscure differences in exposure across commodities. Whether commodity-specific import dependence predicts differential transmission to national food inflation remains insufficiently understood. abstract: Urban growth and expansion have aggravated the volume of fine particulate matter pollution, especially in the high-rise cities. abstract: Abstract Monofloral honeys, particularly Iranian Sidr honey, are highly valued for their unique sensory and medicinal properties; however, they are also prone to fraud. To address this issue, it is essential to create reference databases documenting the physicochemical and pollinological profiles of these honeys. abstract: The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) is one of the world's climate-change hotspots. abstract: Abstract Hypoxic events (i.e. reduction of dissolved oxygen in water) are natural events, which intensity and frequency have been amplified by human activities. abstract: Radionuclide accumulation in glacial environments is of increasing concern due to its potential ecological implications associated with retreat of glaciers worldwide. title: Influence of additives on the adsorption of contaminants by microplastics: role of surface properties
abstract: Plastic additives can change the surface properties of plastics and, as a result, influence the environmental interactions of microplastics (MPs) generated by their degradation. However, the role of additives in environmental interactions is rarely considered. In this study, MPs were manufactured from virgin high-density polyethylene (HDPE) or HDPE containing carbon black (CB, 2% w/w) or glass fibers (GF, 20% w/w), two additives commonly used in commercial formulations. abstract: Mineral nutrition is a key determinant of dairy cow productivity and health in Ethiopia’s Rift Valley, where seasonal fluctuations and location-specific feeding systems influence mineral availability. Despite its importance, evidence on seasonal and spatial variations in the mineral status of lactating dairy cows in Ethiopia’s major dairy-producing areas remains limited. abstract: The Qaidam Basin is endowed with abundant Paleogene–Neogene hydrocarbon resources and possesses major exploration potential. Lacking an overall understanding on sequence stratigraphy and sedimentary facies of the basin is not favorable for making new progress in hydrocarbon exploration. abstract: Abstract Atmospheric stilling, defined as long‐term decline in wind speed, has emerged as a widespread climate signal, yet its role as an independent driver of eutrophication in shallow lakes remains poorly understood. abstract: This study assessed water supply conditions and their relationship with tourist experience in Del Carmen, Surigao del Norte, Philippines, and identified existing water scarcity mitigation strategies. abstract: ABSTRACT Infectious disease in aquaculture is shaped by interactions among pathogens, hosts and the surrounding environment. Temperature, salinity and other physicochemical conditions are established modifiers of several aquatic diseases, whereas environmental contaminants have been studied predominantly for their direct toxic effects. abstract: Persistent organic pollutants can accumulate in urban soils, yet data on polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) and dioxin-like polychlorinated biphenyls (dl-PCBs) in Portuguese urban park soils remain limited. title: Russian Journalists on Svalbard in the 1930s
abstract: The article aims to reconstruct aspects of community life in mining settlements on Svalbard in the mid-1930s, with Barentsburg as a centrepiece. Little known multilingual press and archive material has been used to do so, with microhistorical research as a guiding principle, formulated by Carlo Ginzburg (1993: 33): “Any social structure is the result of interaction and of numerous individual strategies, a fabric that can only be reconstituted from close observation”. abstract: Residues of organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) and their diester transformation products in rice have raised concerns due to their widespread occurrence and potential for human exposure. abstract: Surface water quality degradation from increasing pollution is a major worldwide threat, particularly in Morocco, a country with limited water resources, where preserving available clean water is therefore of the utmost importance. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA methodology, using scientific databases and Moroccan official reports. abstract: Retail food prices in Ghana are usually read as an echo of what happens on farms and in wholesale yards. Drawing on Price Transmission Theory, Transaction Cost Economics and bounded rationality, this study examined how supply chain and macroeconomic conditions shape retail adjustment in the Kasoa, Kotokuraba and Mankessim markets of Ghana's Central Region. abstract: In the post-war period, Mediterranean Europe became the world’s pre-eminent tourist destination. abstract: Abstract Background Competency frameworks guiding engineering education often separate technical and social dimensions, obscuring the inherently context‐dependent and sociotechnical nature of engineering practice. This fragmented framing can lead to challenging transitions and identity tensions for graduates entering the profession. title: Beyond the Gangway: Seafarers' Shore Leave Experiences and Mental Well-Being
abstract: Shore leave has long been regarded as a key recovery mechanism for seafarers, yet access to it has become increasingly rare and brief. Existing studies tend to treat shore leave as a minor component of seafarer welfare or to measure it through access and frequency, so little is known about how seafarers' lived experiences of both access to and restriction from shore leave shape their mental health and emotional well-being. abstract: Building on earlier research (Silva, 2025), this paper argues that caste in Sinhala society is not merely a human affair, but a multispecies entanglement in a tropical setting involving humans, animals, plants and spirits. abstract: Retail micro and small enterprises (MSEs) are vital to Dagupan City’s commercial economy, yet many owner-managed firms lack formal systems for managing business risks. abstract: The commercial trade in exotic pets has raised concerns about population-level impacts from collection in the wild; however, proponents of the trade claim that such concerns are unfounded. abstract: Los Tuxtlas Biosphere Reserve is one of the last remaining areas of primary tropical rainforest in Mexico. This fragile ecosystem heavily reduced by human perturbations is part of the Mesoamerican hotspot. The reserve harbors many endemic species. abstract: Prison-based entrepreneurship and financial education is increasingly promoted as a pathway to reintegration, yet evidence from Southeast Asian correctional settings is thin, and short community-engagement programs rarely disclose what their evaluations can and cannot show. This paper reports a lecturer–student program delivered to 31 inmates of the Class II A Salemba Correctional Institution in Jakarta on 15 July 2026. abstract: Abstract The contamination of water by heavy metals is a great concern for many countries worldwide because of their potential to harm human health and biota. However, data on metal concentrations and related risks remain scarce. abstract: Abstract Chytridiomycosis caused by the amphibian chytrid fungus ( Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis , Bd) is one of the most devastating wildlife diseases of our time 1,2 . abstract: This article interrogates the conceptual terrains of hope, temporality, and wonder in the context of the Anthropocene, arguing that dominant framings of hope – anchored in ontological loss and critique – risk reproducing modernist binaries they seek to dismantle. While hope has been widely deployed as a tool for imagining alternatives to modernity, its reliance on affirmation or negation often tethers imaginaries to reactive postures vis-à-vis the modernist project. abstract: This article explores the entanglements of nation, nature, spirituality, and childhood through the practice of collective biography. title: The Construction of Religious Education Ideology and the Representation of Power in Wisran Hadi’s Play Perguruan: A Deconstructive Study
abstract: Background. Narratives of the Padri War in Minangkabau have generally framed the conflict as a binary struggle between religious reformists and adherents of customary law (adat). Wisran Hadi’s play Perguruan places a religious school at the heart of this conflict, yet it has not been examined in terms of ideological construction and power. Purpose. This study aims (1) to explain how the ideology of religious education is constructed in Perguruan, (2) to identify the forms of power it represents, and (3) to show how the text destabilizes the binary oppositions between adat, religion, and power.

abstract: OBJECTIVE: This paper examines how the National Best Practice Unit Tackling Indigenous Smoking (NBPU TIS) supports program-funded organisations through collaboration, knowledge exchange and culturally responsive practice, and how these processes strengthen community-driven approaches to reducing smoking and vaping prevalence among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. title: Percepción de educadores sobre la calidad y eficacia de la formación en Guatemala
abstract: La calidad del sistema educativo de un país está estrechamente relacionada con la calidad de sus docentes. El propósito de esta investigación consistió en determinar la percepción de calidad de la formación en profesores de enseñanza primaria guatemaltecos. title: Exploring Soil Bacterial Taxonomy and Functional Diversity through Metagenomics in Veerakkal forest area, Western Ghats
abstract: Soil is a dynamic, living system and a vital reservoir of microbial diversity. Investigating soil microbial communities is essential, as these organisms play a key role in sustaining soil health by recycling nutrients, forming humus and enhancing soil structure. title: Bridging the gap: A qualitative study on veterans’ experiences with systemic barriers and support during transition
abstract: Many veterans face complex challenges during the transition from military to civilian life, particularly when navigating healthcare and benefits systems. This qualitative study examines how recently separated veterans with service‑connected musculoskeletal disorders perceive and navigate systemic barriers within Department of Defense and Veterans Affairs transition and healthcare systems. title: From Primary Production to Value-Added Fish Products: International Technology Transfer in A Rural Rice-Fish Farming Community
abstract: Small-scale rice–fish farmers commonly market harvested fish as fresh products, limiting opportunities for product differentiation and downstream value creation. This community engagement program aimed to strengthen the initial capacity of a rice–fish farming community in Lubuk Bayas Village, North Sumatra, Indonesia, in value-added fish processing, food hygiene, product diversification, and market preparation through international academic collaboration. title: Bio-inspired nanotechnology for dengue vector control: Progress and prospects
abstract: The global resurgence of dengue fever due to Aedes aegypti has necessitated the development of innovative and potentially sustainable vector control strategies. Conventional methods that were initially effective now pose significant challenges, causing nuisance to the environment and public health with the resurgence of the vector. To overcome these challenges, the combination of natural products with nanotechnology offers a promising green alternative. title: Advanced Biopolymer-Based Active and Intelligent Packaging Systems for Food Preservation: A Critical Review
abstract: Balancing reliable food protection against the ecological damage caused by synthetic plastics is a major priority in food processing. Polysaccharide systems, chiefly chitosan, starch, and functionalized celluloses, serve as practical substitutes to prolong food shelf life using active and intelligent mechanisms. This review covers developments in biopolymer preservation technologies from 2010 to 2026. title: Are We Ready for the Next Crisis? Threat Versus Coping: The Role of Knowledge Valence and Government Trust in Travel Intentions Across Regulatory Contexts
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how crisis‐related knowledge, perceived risk, and government trust jointly shape travel intentions across distinct regulatory regimes. Drawing on Protection Motivation Theory and the Cognitive Mediation Model, the study distinguishes between threat‐oriented pandemic knowledge and coping‐oriented travel health knowledge to explain divergent behavioral responses during prolonged crisis conditions. title: Balancing nutrients and metal contaminants: sustainable land application rates for livestock manures in Ireland
abstract: Livestock manures are valuable nutrient sources for crop production, but variable composition and inappropriate application rates can cause nutrient imbalance, phosphorus accumulation and trace-metal loading, increasing the risks to water quality and the wider environment. This study evaluated manure-specific application rates by considering nutrient and trace-metal composition, crop requirements and soil phosphorus status. abstract: The increased use of skincare products has raised growing global concerns as regards exposure to heavy metal contaminants andmicrobes. The aim of this research study was to assess microbial contamination, heavy metals and associated health risks in skincareproducts from different market sources. A total of forty skincare products were randomly sourced and analyzed. Microbial contamination was assessed using standard microbiological methods. title: Optimising electrocoagulation for oilfield produced water treatment
abstract: Petroleum produced water constitutes the largest aqueous by-product of onshore hydrocarbon extraction in Saudi Arabia, and its saline, oil-bearing matrix restricts the options available for on-site reclamation. This study examined electrocoagulation (EC) as a treatment stage for produced water drawn from an onshore facility in the Eastern Province. abstract: ABSTRACT Soil salinization severely restricts soybean growth and productivity. Therefore, uncovering salt‐tolerance genes and their regulatory mechanisms is critical for breeding salt‐tolerant soybean varieties. In this study, a genome‐wide association study (GWAS) was conducted across four environments, and 7 quantitative trait locus (QTLs) associated with salt‐tolerance traits were identified. title: Improvement and Equitable Economic Distribution Based on Village Potential and Green Industry in Central Java
abstract: Pursuing equitable economic growth in Central Java requires a shift from urban-centric industrialization to a decentralized, village-based green economy. In line with the vision of Governor Ahmad Luthfi and Deputy Governor Taj Yasin for 2025–2030, this paper explores the strategic integration of village potential with green industry policies. title: Protective Cultures in Meat Products and Plant-Based Meat Alternatives: Prospects and Challenges
abstract: In view of the considerable levels of food loss on a global scale, the attendant greenhouse gas emissions, and the expanding demand for foods that are as natural as possible, bioconservation strategies—protective cultures in particular—are becoming increasingly important in food production. The objective of this review was to present the current state of research on the use of protective cultures and bacteriocins in plant-based meat alternatives as well as in cooked meat products. title: Sentinel‐2 in PRODES : Enhancing Cerrado Vegetation Suppression Mapping
abstract: ABSTRACT The PRODES Cerrado system provides annual mapping of native vegetation suppression for Brazil's tropical savanna but has historically relied on 30 m Landsat imagery without systematically assessing higher‐resolution alternatives. This reliance may limit the detection of small or early‐stage clearings, particularly in heterogeneous and cloud‐prone regions. abstract: Abstract Motivation The EU's geopolitical turn has reshaped its development cooperation. The Global Gateway, launched in 2021 with a pledge of EUR 300 billion by 2027, is its flagship vehicle and has been widely read as a transactional repurposing of aid towards European self‐interest. How geopolitical it is at the operational level has, however, been answered through inference rather than measurement. abstract: The growth of streaming platforms and social media has transformed consumption patterns toward more flexible, multiplatform, and participatory models. Audiences not only consume content but also comment, share, and interact in digital communities centered around television series. abstract: Oxygenated volatile organic compounds (OVOCs) including ethanol, methanol, acetone, and acetaldehyde are important components of urban VOC emissions, yet their sources and emissions magnitudes remain highly uncertain. In this study, we leveraged data from a Vocus proton-transfer reaction mass spectrometer deployed during a long-term tower-based eddy covariance flux study and a mobile monitoring campaign to characterize the emissions and sources of urban OVOCs. abstract: Tea is one of the most widely consumed beverages worldwide, making contamination by potentially toxic metals a public health concern. This study determined the concentrations of arsenic (As), cadmium (CD), chromium (Cr), nickel (Ni), and lead (Pb) in five commercially available tea brands sold around Bayero University Kano (BUK) Old Campus, Nigeria, and assessed their transfer into tea infusions and associated health risks. abstract: Abstract Background The genus Peperomia (family Piperaceae) is the only known lineage with Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM) in the Magnoliids.. Previous studies have demonstrated C 3 +CAM in multiple Peperomia species, yet there are ~ 1,600 species in the genus and very few have been assessed for CAM. Further, no studies have used genomics to understand CAM evolution in the Magnoliids. abstract: OBJECTIVE: Research on moral injury (MI) continues to grow despite a lack of consensus definition, and qualitative, exploratory studies can enable further construct clarification. This study sought to understand how post-9/11 veterans perceive MI and how these perceptions impact their responses to existing measures of MI. title: Cultivating ISI: Shaping the Future of Idiomatics in Language Education and Research
abstract: This article advances the evolving field of Idiomatics, devoted to the rigorous study of idiomatic and figurative language. It is organized into five main sections, framed by a preamble and a prologue that establish the conceptual stage, and concluded by an epilogue and a coda that reflect on the work’s implications and future directions. abstract: The aim of this research was to evaluate the physico-chemical parameters of milk of Gir cow (N = 200) and Jafarabadi Buffalo (N = 40). Samples were collected from the Kathiyawadi native residents settled in Raver, Bhusawal, Chopda, and Yawal tehsils in Jalgaon district of Maharashtra. abstract: This legal mapping paper aims to aggregate state-specific policies on the impact of criminal legal system contact—more specifically, the impact of criminal convictions—on social work licensure. abstract: Background Intestinal helminthic infections during pregnancy are still a major public health problem in low-resource settings, posing risks to both mothers and fetuses. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors associated with intestinal helminthiasis among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Andabet Health Center, Ethiopia. abstract: Driven by the imbalance between nutrient discharge and availability of natural resources, there is a growing need for sustainable strategies for managing wastewater. Nutrient recovery from domestic wastewater through struvite crystallization presents one such efficient and circular technology for recovering nutrients and producing fertilizer. abstract: Building on the theory and methods developed by proponents of the practice turn in the study of international relations, this article provides an innovative examination of Russian power politics using the concept of power repertoire. The empirical focus is on the actual Russian power practices in the MENA region, in Ukraine, and in the strategically important energy domain. abstract: Hemoglobin H (Hb H) disease, caused by the functional loss in three of the four α-globin genes, exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity that is not fully explained by primary α-globin genotypes. abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of the work environment and job placement on job satisfaction, with motivation as a mediating variable, among employees of the Regional Secretariat of Temanggung Regency. abstract: Abstract The understanding of the user engagement, selection and adoption of Improved Cooking Stoves (ICS) in developing countries is important to deploy measures to sustain their use. abstract: Environmental enrichment is widely used to improve the welfare of captive animals, yet its effects on reptilian gut microbiota remain poorly understood. abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 pandemic emphasized the critical role of face masks in preventing the transmission of respiratory viruses, especially in medical settings. Respiratory viruses, including SARS, influenza, and adenoviruses are primarily transmitted through the respiratory pathways, making face masks the primary barrier for protection. abstract: Abstract Plants can regulate soil biogeochemical processes via root exudates, yet how exudate quantity and composition influence soil nitrogen (N) transformations remains unclear. abstract: Since the 20th century, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has been widely explored by researchers and practitioners across different contexts. Over time, the concept has evolved into a complex and multidimensional framework, characterized by diverse interpretations and the absence of a unified theoretical consensus. abstract: Stress arising from academic, professional and financial demands is common among students and young professionals, and the coping methods within easiest reach, such as listening to music, do not always suffice. This paper presents a survey-driven design for a virtual reality (VR) gadget that combines selectable immersive natural environments, environment-matched sound therapy and heart-rate biofeedback for short relaxation sessions. abstract: This article examines how India’s transnational cultural influence is produced through everyday practice and mediated by diaspora networks, and it offers a sociological reading of soft power that complements state-centred accounts. Studies of soft power usually concentrate on states: their cultural resources, their public-diplomacy programmes and their positions in perception indices. abstract: Abstract Ireland has largely avoided the escalation of far-right populism seen across Europe. There has, however, been an upsurge in far-right politics and activism, underpinned by anti-immigration sentiment. Within this context, this paper aims to determine how two Irish political parties commonly identified by media outlets as far-right present their websites, which issues they seek to own and whether these issues align with far-right ideology. abstract: Generative AI is rapidly reshaping educational practice, yet in preservice teacher education it remains unclear how pedagogical reasoning can be evaluated when AI-assisted outputs become increasingly polished and accessible. This study utilized diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) and diffuse correlation spectroscopy (DCS) to longitudinally monitor tumor physiology in a preclinical rat model of breast cancer. abstract: Optimizing the business environment is a pivotal aspect of China’s governance modernization. abstract: Ionospheric total electron content provides an integrated measure of the plasma through which satellite radio signals propagate. Its variability reflects solar radiation, magnetospheric energy input, neutral atmospheric dynamics, and redistribution of charged particles. title: New particle formation contribution to aerosol mass: regimes and implications for future urban environments
abstract: New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of global aerosol number concentration yet its contribution to aerosol mass remains unclear. Here we propose a regime framework for NPF mass contributions using aerosol dynamic simulations constrained by atmospheric measurements. abstract: The strength of the Australian studies community in China has long been cited as a standout achievement of the field. Some recent scholarship is more critical, arguing, for example, that Australian studies in China has failed to appropriately diversify away from its origins in literature studies, which limits its engagement with contemporary Australia. abstract: Population administration services, particularly the issuance and correction of Family Card (Kartu Keluarga/KK) documents, play a strategic role in guaranteeing legal identity for Indonesian citizens. This study analyzes the quality of population administration service in handling name discrepancies on Family Card documents at the Purworejo Village Office, Sanankulon District, Blitar Regency, and identifies the factors that hinder that service quality. abstract: As climate change intensifies, sugar beet ( Beta vulgaris L.) crops face unprecedented threats from severe drought, soil salinity, and extreme temperatures. Safeguarding this vital source of global sugar production and bioethanol feedstocks requires an urgent shift toward climate-smart agriculture. This review highlights an integrated "signal-to-selection" strategy designed to accelerate the development of resilient, stress-resisting cultivars. abstract: Understanding the role of social relationships in shaping livelihood outcomes is critical to addressing persistent food insecurity among smallholder farmers in Nigeria. abstract: BACKGROUND: The start of a gold rush on the lands of the Awiakay (Papua New Guinea) in 2020 set in motion a range of adverse changes in social relations, community life, and everyday practices. Accompanied by a shift towards the lingua franca Tok Pisin, these changes may be disrupting the transmission of traditional ecological knowledge (TEK) to the younger generation. abstract: Although higher education institutions (HEIs) in Uganda are supposed to be the heartbeat of national transformation by serving as nursery beds for innovations, testbeds for policies, hubs for technology development and training grounds for both prospective public servants and in-service civil servants, they are challenged for being unresponsive. abstract: Advances in ancient DNA research have expanded the range of materials from which genetic information can be recovered, enabling the analysis of atypical materials. These often preserve both host and exogenous DNA, for example due to handling or native microbes, offering a window into past diversity. abstract: Agricultural trade is a key sector in Indonesia’s trade. One of the agricultural export subsectors is horticulture. The increase in Indonesia’s banana exports is part of the promotion of fresh fruits. Banana exports face a number of challenges, primarily related to meeting food safety standards in export destination countries. title: From Local Resources to Safe Water: Circular Approaches for Decentralized Water Treatment
abstract: Access to safe water remains a challenge in low-income and rural regions, where conventional purification can be unaffordable or unsustainable. Cocoa production waste, particularly cocoa pod husk, can be valorized as a precursor of activated carbon, while natural zeolites provide a complementary adsorptive and ion-exchange medium. abstract: Guava (Psidium guajava L.) is an important tropical and subtropical fruit crop, valued for its nutritional quality and economic importance. abstract: This paper aims to elaborate on a philosophical split between two explanatory strategies in Cognitive Semantics: Semantic Gestalt Theories (SGT) and Usage Statistical Models (USM). abstract: Type I interferon (IFN-I) and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) are central regulators of antiviral immunity, yet how they cooperatively govern CD8 T cell exhaustion remains unresolved. abstract: This study evaluated tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L.) seedling responses to three white-light-emitting diodes (LEDs) spectra and assessed post-transplant performance in a commercial greenhouse.
