abstract: BACKGROUND: It is unclear whether time to antibiotics changes outcomes for hospitalized children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and whether observation is safe. OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to compare outcomes among children with CAP admitted to the hospital who did and who did not receive antibiotics within 4 h of presentation to the Emergency Department. abstract: Cactus species is increasingly recognized as a nature-based solution for restoring degraded drylands, yet quantitative evidence of its influence on soil quality across contrasting arid environments remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of three cactus canopy covers (bare, scattered, and dense) on soil physicochemical properties in two zones (EST=Eastern zone and SE=Southeastern zone) of Tigray, Ethiopia. abstract: Portland Limestone Cement (PLC), designated as Type IL under ASTM C595/C595M and Type GUL under CSA A3001, is now a mainstream clinker-reduction strategy for concrete infrastructure. abstract: Early-life conditions can shape molecular ageing processes, yet to what extent developmental variation in telomere length (TL) influences ageing trajectories remains unclear, particularly in long-lived mammals. We investigated how early-life environmental conditions and maternal age relate to juvenile TL and short-term survival in two long-lived bat species, Myotis myotis and Rhinolophus ferrumequinum. abstract: Abstract Town criers were ubiquitous civic officials in early modern Europe. Their voices contributed to a continuous cycle of noise that informed, regulated and shaped urban life. Formally representing political authorities via the proclamation of the law, criers also served as agents of the public by announcing commercial or personal news. abstract: Abstract Height is an anthropometric measure of nutritional levels and health status during childhood and adolescence and can strongly predict health and developmental outcomes across the lifespan. abstract: Bread wheat is an important cereal crop worldwide, but its productivity in acidic soils is constrained by low soil fertility and limited use of effective soil amendments. This study evaluated the agronomic and economic performance of combined coffee husk biochar (CHB) and NPSB blended fertilizer for bread wheat production under limed and unlimed conditions during the 2023 main cropping season. title: comfort-db: A Python toolkit to access, preprocess and explore the oceanographic COMFORT dataset
abstract: comfort-db is a Python library that facilitates working with the COMFORT SQLite dataset, version 2. The dataset assembles global oceanographic measurements from ten datasets and contains a total of 458,724,734 in situ measurements from the years 1772 to 2020. comfort-db enables easy access to the database and provides preprocessing and exploratory analysis utilities. abstract: LiDAR-based localization and mapping systems produce registered point clouds that serve as geometric measurements for downstream estimation and navigation. Registration errors introduce duplicated surfaces and structural deformation into these measurements. abstract: This paper considers online intrusion-risk assessment and graded warning for unmanned aerial vehicles under bounded measurement attacks. To address this problem, we develop a monitoring framework that combines trusted state estimation, attack-aware risk assessment, and probabilistic signal temporal logic (PrSTL). title: Precision determination of $B_c$ and $B_c^*$ meson decay constants from lattice QCD
abstract: We present a lattice QCD study of heavy-heavy meson decay constants using the HISQ gauge ensemble generated by the MILC Collaboration. Employing the HISQ action for both charm and bottom valence quarks tuned to their physical masses, we determine pseudoscalar, vector, and tensor decay constants for heavy quarkonium and $B_c$ systems. abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) achieve strong performance on complex tasks by generating explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, but the safety implications of this intermediate reasoning surface remain underexplored. abstract: Comprehensive visibility into Internet Background Radiation (IBR) requires diverse measurement infrastructure. abstract: South Korean families spend heavily on hagwons, private cram schools that prepare students for the university entrance exam. abstract: Background-field lattice calculations extract weak-field response coefficients from correlators computed at several field strengths. abstract: Detection and characterization of Earth-like worlds is a primary science goal for the upcoming NASA flagship Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). The HWO mission will be the first of its kind to specifically search for Earth-like worlds around Sun-like stars and characterize their atmospheres to identify potential biosignatures. title: Recursive Self-Improvement of Exoskeleton Assistance Policies through Human-in-the-Loop Feedback
abstract: To reduce reliance on manual design and extensive parameter tuning, a framework for the autonomous evolution of exoskeleton assistance policies through human feedback is proposed. Assistance policies are autonomously generated as executable control code by an intelligent agent and evaluated in experiments with human participants. abstract: We propose and study a first-order hyperbolic approximation of the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation in $N$ spatial dimensions. abstract: The vertical motion in tropical anvil clouds is crucial for understanding their maintenance and evolution but is notoriously difficult to observe. This work explores the potential utility of EarthCARE in revealing previously unobserved aspects of anvil clouds using the radar-only (2A.CPR_CLP) and radar-lidar synergy (2B.AC_CLP) products. Composite vertical profiles of cloud fraction sorted by ice water path (IWP) are constructed as a statistical representation of anvil clouds and deep convection. title: Extreme cold–dry events in East Asia during glacials reflect insolation thresholds
abstract: Abstract Whether extreme climate events reflect intrinsic threshold behaviour of the climate system remains uncertain, in part because most terrestrial archives integrate multiple climatic signals and lack simultaneous constraints on temperature and hydroclimate. Here we present high-resolution ( ~ 900 years) quantitative reconstructions of land temperature and monsoon precipitation from the Chinese Loess Plateau spanning the past ~250,000 years, based on molecular fossil proxies. title: Regional reorganization of fire carbon emissions linked to vegetation productivity and drying demand in interglacial simulations
abstract: Fire regulates terrestrial carbon storage and land–atmosphere carbon exchange, yet its response to past warm climates is strongly region dependent. Here we use EC-Earth3-Veg simulations to investigate changes in fire carbon emissions during the Mid-Holocene (MH, 6 ka) and Last Interglacial (LIG, 127 ka) relative to the pre-industrial (PI) state. Fire carbon emissions reorganized regionally rather than uniformly: small positive global land-mean anomalies masked increases over the Sahel and decreases over parts of the Americas. title: Climate Variability Drives Increasing Gross Primary Production in Europe Since 1772
abstract: ABSTRACT Satellite‐based datasets of terrestrial gross primary production (GPP) are available only since the early 1980s, leaving pre‐industrial ecosystem dynamics largely unconstrained. Here, we fill this gap by reconstructing European GPP from 1772 to 2020 using Multivariate nonlinear regression with multiple interactions (MNLRMI). The model was trained with a homogenized GPP dataset derived from eddy‐covariance and FLUXCOM data (1981–2018). The various stakeholders within the offshore wind-to-hydrogen production chain (wind power companies, hydrogen producers, and government policymakers) form a highly complex multi-stakeholder collaborative system. abstract: The article examines how Japan’s energy engagement with Central Asia has changed from resource-oriented diplomacy towards cooperation in power-sector modernization, energy efficiency and supply-chain resilience. It asks through which mechanisms a distant, land-locked region can contribute to Japan’s energy security when direct fuel deliveries remain limited. abstract: The Earth Cloud, Aerosol and Radiation Explorer (EarthCARE) provides the first spaceborne Doppler radar measurements. We construct a tropical cyclone (TC) dataset by collocating 16 months of EarthCARE observations with the International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship, comprising 96 intercepts of 27 TCs. title: State-dependent influence of ENSO and NAO on spring hydroclimatic variability at the watershed scale in the South-central United States (1950–2025)
abstract: Large-scale climate oscillations modulate spring precipitation across the south-central United States, but their hydroclimatic response at the watershed scale remains poorly quantified. We evaluate how the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) are associated with spring (March–May) precipitation across three watersheds in Northwest Arkansas and Northeast Oklahoma from 1950 to 2025, accounting for antecedent winter (December–February) precipitation. title: Mantle Migmatites
abstract: Textbooks on igneous petrology explain a range of primitive basalts and more alkaline volcanic rocks such as basanites, nephelinites and melilitites as products of various degrees of partial melting of mantle peridotite – a supposedly uniform rock consisting of four minerals olivine, ortho- and clinopyroxene and either spinel or garnet, depending on depth. We provide a critical, georeferenced synthesis of continental diatoms from Paraná State, southern Brazil, integrating bibliographic records, herbarium collections, nomenclatural revision, and spatial analyses. The compiled dataset comprises 86,775 occurrence records from 3649 samples collected between 1951 and 2025 at 712 georeferenced sites. abstract: Changes in mineral surfaces and gas dispersion can improve a flotation stage without increasing overall copper recovery. This critical review examines these interactions in copper-bearing carbonaceous shales, saline process waters and concentrator tailings. We compare published studies by feed material, operating conditions, measurements and position in the circuit. title: Aligning Facility Mix with User Demographics in Former Industrial Waterfront Piers: An Exploratory Comparison of Four North American Cases with Implications for Busan North Port
abstract: As maritime industries decline, many waterfront piers have become underutilized. Existing scholarship addresses spatial configuration, governance, and sustainability but says little about how the demographic characteristics of surrounding populations should inform facility programming in revitalized piers. This paper examines that relationship through an exploratory comparison of four former industrial piers: Pier 17 and Pier 57 (New York), Pier 57 (Seattle), and Pier 39 (San Francisco). abstract: Abstract Tectonic movements and related depositional responses are always complicated in a typical foreland basin. title: Using high-frequency data to quantify how urban nature affects air temperature and energy consumption
abstract: Globally, cities account for 78% of energy consumption and 70~75% of greenhouse gas emissions. Using spatially explicit data on urban vegetation, water bodies, and buildings, combined with extensive daily observations of air temperature and electricity consumption for the subtropical megacity of Shenzhen, China, this study shows that urban nature contributes to urban cooling, reducing energy consumption and associated greenhouse gas emissions. title: Age of smoke sampled by aircraft during FIREX-AQ: methods and critical evaluation
abstract: The age of smoke, meaning the time elapsed since it was produced in a fire, is an important parameter for interpreting measurements of evolving smoke composition. This study describes the smoke age estimates developed for large plumes sampled in the 2019 NASA-NOAA FIREX-AQ field experiment. Smoke ages are computed using two methods and applied to observations from two aircraft: the NASA DC-8 and NOAA Chemistry Twin Otter. abstract: Abstract Climate change creates new challenges for conservation, yet capacity limitations often hinder practitioners' ability to consider climate change in restoration activities. Place‐based climate adaptation workshops can help practitioners develop tractable restoration strategies. In Hawaii, restoration needs are large, and climate change amplifies ecosystem vulnerability, calling attention to the potential benefit of more disturbance‐resilient restoration practices across the archipelago. abstract: Abstract Mesoscale convective systems, such as squall lines, produce large amounts of rainfall but remain challenging to forecast. abstract: Accurate cryogenic calibration from -196 °C to +50 °C is a critical requirement for environmental monitoring, medical diagnostics, aerospace, superconductivity, materials science and the development of cryogenic instruments. The most accurate method is fixed-point calibration according to the International Temperature Scale of 1990 (ITS-90), but it requires skilled personnel, expensive fixed-point cells and time-consuming procedures, limiting it to some national metrology institutes. abstract: Luminescence is a powerful method for detecting trace analytes and monitoring biological processes. However, most bioluminescence reagents, including luciferase and its substrates, are sensitive to temperature, limiting their usable shelf lives, and resulting in inconsistent performance. Enhancing the stability of these reagents could reduce signal variability between experiments, simplify workflows, and address cold chain storage issues. abstract: Large-scale copper-gold mining in Mimika generates tailings that interact with the Ajkwa River system and may influence aquatic geochemistry. This study integrated paired water-sediment sampling, laboratory metal(loid) analysis, censor-aware interpretation of non-detect water data, and spatial modeling to characterize environmental patterns along the Ajkwa River corridor. Twenty paired surface-water and sediment samples were collected at identical coordinates. abstract: The dissolution mechanisms of UO 2 and α-U 3 O 8-x in 4 mol L -1 nitric acid at 40°C were investigated using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). title: Responses of surface radiative balance to wildfires differ across ecosystems
abstract: Wildfires alter land surface albedo and temperature, modulating the radiative budget and climate. Previous studies have predominantly reported enhanced shortwave absorption induced by post-fire surface darkening over forests. Here, using two-decade (2001–2020) satellite observations of wildfires, we show that post-fire summer surface albedo and radiative balance shifts vary significantly across ecosystems. abstract: Abstract Connecting soil nutrient stocks with nutrient transport generates a meaningful indicator for evaluating sustainability in agricultural systems. Soil erosion remains a critical challenge for sustainable agriculture, affecting soil quality, nutrients, and crop productivity globally. abstract: Abstract This study evaluates classical and contemporary wind tunnel blockage correction methods for propeller testing, with a focus on slipstream effects in closed section tunnels. abstract: Research into collocation learning in second and foreign language environments has gained significant scholarly attention. Yet, cross-linguistic influence (CLI) on the use of collocations has received little attention from researchers, especially in the Tunisian context. Therefore, this study investigates how L1 Arabic influences the production of English lexical collocations among 50 third-year Tunisian EFL undergraduates at the Higher Institute of Human Sciences of Medenine. abstract: This study developed an efficient and environmentally friendly extraction method for obtaining multifunctional carbohydrate extracts from Palmaria palmata . Ethanol was applied for pigment removal, while citric acid (0.03 M) was selected as a safe, food-grade, and efficient extraction solvent. abstract: This paper presents an optimal control framework for nonlinear systems with noise using Hamiltonian-based discretisation to enhance the approximation of stochastic differential equations. abstract: ABSTRACT Urban pluvial flooding (UPF) poses a growing threat in highly urbanized areas, where rainfall intensity, topography, and human activities interact, amplifying flood risk. title: Oh Muse, Tell Me About a Complicated Man: The Odyssey by Christopher Nolan, Followed by the Ulysses of James Joyce and Teolinda Gersao
abstract: This paper examines the film Odyssey (2026) by British filmmaker Christopher Nolan, analyzing the role of adapting a classic literary work for high-resolution, technically complex cinema. It discusses the filmmaker's creative freedom to interpret the original work, adapting it to the social context of his time and his own unique vision of the classic text. title: Field monitoring of wind erosion of organic soils in southwestern Quebec, Canada
abstract: Estimated regional soil losses of 1 to 4 cm per year have been reported for organic soils used for agricultural production in the Montérégie region of southwestern Quebec, Canada. However, little research in this region or elsewhere has focused on estimating the contribution of wind erosion to such losses. In this study, wind erosion was monitored from July 2019 to October 2022 at two sites in the region. One site was left bare, while the other was cultivated. title: Nonlinear Dynamics and Wear Characteristics of a High-Frequency Flapping-Wing Mechanism with Multiple Revolute-Joint Clearances
abstract: Micro flapping-wing air vehicles are increasingly used in low-altitude and aerospace applications, creating a growing need for accurate motion and stable dynamic performance. This trend motivates a detailed investigation of the dynamic behavior of their actuation mechanisms. Manufacturing and assembly tolerances inevitably introduce small clearances into the kinematic joints, which reduce the motion accuracy of the mechanism, induce high-frequency vibration, and accelerate interfacial wear. abstract: The 2003 Bawean Incident, where two Indonesian Air Force (TNI AU) F-16 aircraft intercepted a US Navy F/A-18 Hornet jet on an air cover mission, demands an in-depth analysis of the alignment between Indonesia’s national airspace regulations and international air security practices. abstract: Photoexcitation of chemical compounds, together with the light transmittance of the biological window, enables targeted phototherapy. title: Root‐associated fungi modulate plant recruitment in Mediterranean forests
abstract: Abstract Established plants affect directly and indirectly the success of juvenile plants recruiting in their close vicinity, what is defined as a canopy–recruit interaction. Such interactions affect plant species demography and community dynamics. Root‐associated fungi (RAF) can influence plant performance and survival, thus contributing to the sign and intensity of canopy–recruit interactions. title: Household affordability of sanitary landfilling is governed by cost allocation rather than metropolitan economic capacity
abstract: Abstract Open dumping remains a dominant municipal solid waste disposal practice globally, including in megacities whose populations and economic output rival that of small countries. Sanitary landfilling is a common transition away from open dumping, yet system-level feasibility does not translate into household affordability. abstract: We present speckle-interferometric observations obtained with the 1.3 m TAOS-II Site~1 telescope at the Observatorio Astronómico Nacional at San Pedro Mártir, aimed at evaluating its performance for high-angular-resolution studies of visual binaries. The observations were acquired in the r -Gunn band with an EMCCD-based speckle module and include calibration binaries together with systems having published visual orbits over a broad range of separations, magnitude differences, and orbit grades. abstract: Este trabajo presenta una metodología innovadora para la estimación del volumen de residuos mineros en instalaciones cerradas o abandonadas en España, así como para depósitos de residuos en general donde no existe información de otro tipo. abstract: Satellite-based monitoring provides spatial information on surface changes in active volcanic regions, yet displacement patterns around Mount Marapi, West Sumatra, spanning the December 2023 eruption require further examination. This study mapped and analyzed surface displacement using differential interferometric synthetic aperture radar (DInSAR). title: Spatial distribution and pollution assessment of potentially toxic elements in stream sediments of the Luis Moya region, Central Mexico: Evidence from mining-affected areas
abstract: The main activities in the Luis Moya region of central Mexico are agriculture and tourism; however, a long history of mining may have enriched the surroundings with potentially toxic elements (PTEs), including As, Cd, Cr, Sn, and Pb. Areas of PTE enrichment were identified using stream sediments as the sampling medium. Stream sediments (top 5 cm) were collected from 20 sites throughout this region, and their metal concentrations were determined using X-ray Fluorescence (XRF). abstract: This study presents an exact analytical solution for the two-dimensional (2D) thermoelastic state of a long, two-layer hollow cylinder composed of inhomogeneous materials under mixed boundary conditions. By accounting for distinct thermoelastic properties and internal heat generation within layered structures, this research addresses a significant gap in the existing literature. Productivity and economic benefits of intercropping buckwheat and green gram with chilli under the Northern transition zone of Karnataka
abstract: Intercropping systems improve agricultural resource efficiency and crop productivity, especially for spice crops like chilli. This research assessed the productivity and economic advantages of intercropping buckwheat and green gram with chilli. The study was conducted during the kharif seasons of 2022 and 2023 at the Main Agricultural Research Station, Dharwad, Karnataka. abstract: Charging probability is the greatest source of uncertainty in electrical mobility-based measurements of aerosol size distributions, but its influence on the results is rarely quantified and reported. In bipolar charging, the charge distribution is almost universally modeled using the Wiedensohler approximation, although it has been shown to deviate significantly from the true charge distribution under many measurement conditions. title: The reception of Cartagena's thought in the late fifteenth century and its fate in the golden age
abstract: Alfonso de Cartagena was a prominent figure in the cultural revolution of the early Renaissance, widely read and praised both in Spain and abroad, and in correspondence with humanist scholars and political leaders in both Latin and the vernacular. The high esteem in which he was held was expressed in numerous texts up to his death in 1456; and yet by the end of the century only a limited proportion of his works were still in circulation, and his name was systematically silenced even by those who knew it. abstract: This article introduces the concept of the ‘Coniferocene’ as a heuristic for examining the long-term co-evolution of European forests, forestry, and industrial wood utilization. It highlights a series of developments that emerged unevenly from the eighteenth century onward, became more clearly defined during the nineteenth century, and continue to shape forest environments today, though under increasingly unstable conditions. This research investigates a sand-free alternative aggregate matrix for wall-coating mortars by fully substituting natural quartz sand with waste expanded polystyrene (EPS) and crushed sururu seashells ( Mytella falcata ) on an absolute volume basis. abstract: We study the construction of invariant measures associated with higher order conservation laws of the intermediate long wave equation (ILW) and their convergence properties in the deep-water and shallow-water limits. title: Remembering the Unexpected: Prediction Errors Gate Stress-induced Memory Enhancements
abstract: Stress influences memory not only for the stressful event itself but also for neutral events encoded nearby in time, with important implications for eyewitness testimony and clinical contexts. Previous research has generally assumed that stress uniformly affects temporally adjacent information. In contrast, we propose that stress modulates memory selectively, depending on the prediction error evoked by each event. title: Affirming Spaces: A Critical Race Theoretic Analysis of Experiential Knowledge at a Hispanic-Serving Institution
abstract: Racism in the United States permeates institutions, including universities. Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) initiatives were created to support and empower racially marginalized students, but political backlash ended DEI initiatives across the U.S. Amid this abandonment, students of color are increasingly seeking institutions that affirm their racial and cultural identities. abstract: Hybrid photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) systems suffer from thermal accumulation, which limits their widespread adoption in high-irradiance regions. This work proposes a novel PVT system that employs zig-zag fins, a perforated surface, and a four-inlet chimney to cool the PV panel with airflow while low-flow water circulates inside the panel. abstract: Abstract Research on innovation beyond metropolitan cores has paid less attention to whether peripheral participation is matched by formal ownership of patents on key technological paths. We distinguish spatial and network participation from the headquarters geography of patent applicants, and apply kernel density, core–periphery network, and main-path analyses to sixty-two Japanese Green Transformation technologies. abstract: Abstract Free fatty acids (FFAs), specifically the ω-3 forms α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are important modulators of lipid membrane structure and dynamics, yet how these three species compare within a single, consistent framework remains unclear. abstract: The perihelion of comet 1P/Halley in 2061 is an excellent chance to revisit this object of outstanding scientific and cultural relevance. During its 1986 approach to the Sun, it was targeted by several flyby missions. Due to its retrograde, highly-inclined orbit, the relative velocities during the encounter were large, restricting the scientific return due to the short time spent inside the coma. abstract: The county high school policies (CHSPs) is crucial for improving the quality of basic education in China's counties and promoting rural social development. As policy documents are the foundational elements of policy systems, it is crucial to evaluate current policy texts, identify their shortcomings, and provide empirical evidence for future policy development. abstract: Abstract Pigments in open-air rock art are often in heavily deteriorated superimposition sequences, limiting visualisation using standard photographic approaches. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is emerging as a portable, non-invasive approach for in situ pigment analysis, but collection of spectral-spatial information typically relies on controlled illumination, which is challenging in remote settings. abstract: Ray tracing in X-ray science has typically been limited to descriptions where refraction occurs only at interfaces, ignoring the refraction occurring due to the continuous variations in index of refraction in the bulk of a material, as are common in biological samples like bone. We propose a method to simulate X-ray images directly on voxel grids using curved rays. title: A covariance density for a point process and a random field
abstract: The spatial point process literature offers a well-developed theory for characterizing covariances within a point process or between different point processes using joint intensity functions or cross joint intensity functions. However, similar summary statistics are missing for characterizing the covariance between a point process and a random field. abstract: The most important features that distinguish fluid flow in the atmosphere and ocean are the effects of rotation and stratification, which are described by the Boussinesq equations with rotation. This paper examines the stability threshold at high Reynolds number $\mathbf{Re}$ for the 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near Couette flow and a vertical stratified temperature. abstract: This paper extends our prior work on interface conditions between two poroelastic domains to the case when a poroelastic domain interacts with a pure fluid. The porous medium is assumed to be deformable and modeled following mixture theory. When not in a mixture, each constituent of the porous domain is assumed to be incompressible. title: Well-posedness and large deviations for 3D primitive equations with jumps
abstract: We establish the global pathwise well-posedness and a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for the three-dimensional viscous primitive equations driven by multiplicative Lévy noise represented by a compensated Poisson random measure. Under local Lipschitz and moment growth assumptions on the noise coefficient, we construct local martingale solutions and obtain a unique maximal pathwise solution with càdlàg trajectories in the $H^1$ energy space. Additional sixth-moment growth in $H^1$ and $L^6$ growth bounds on the baroclinic component of the noise yield global pathwise well-posedness.

title: ColNav: Uncertainty-Aware Spacetime Collision Checking with Bounding Volume Hierarchies
abstract: Safe navigation for mobile robots in dynamic and uncertain environments requires planning paths that avoid collisions with other moving targets. Typically this involves forward propagating the robot motion and checking for collisions at sampled points in space and time. Such methods can miss collisions between sampled points and are not robust to uncertainty in the state estimates. We propose ColNav, a robust collision check formulation with geometric volumes. abstract: We study the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation, a model describing the motion of a fluid with variable density through a porous medium under the action of gravity. abstract: In the present paper, our primary focus is on the Boussinesq equations with fractional velocity dissipation $Λ^αu$ and temperature diffusion $Λ^βθ$. abstract: We present the dependence of the depth of maximum of extensive air showers (EAS), $X_{\max}$, on the energy of the primary particle, as determined from data recorded with the wide-angle Cherenkov array TAIGA-HiSCORE during the 2021--2025 observation seasons. title: Detecting space objects with Earth-observation radar satellites
abstract: Millimetre-to-centimetre orbital debris poses a hazard to spacecraft, but its abundance remains difficult to measure. abstract: We analyze a delay differential model for phage therapy in which a cocktail of $n$ different types of bacteriophages, each with its own latency period, is administered and coinfection is allowed. abstract: This study examines the relationship between economic growth, measured through gross value added (GVA), and CO₂ emissions in the European Union’s marine primary sector (fisheries and aquaculture) over the period 2008–2024. Using the Tapio elasticity framework and a multi-level clustering approach, we assess the extent and nature of decoupling across EU member states and institutional contexts. abstract: Hotel tax is one of the main sources of Local Own-Source Revenue (PAD) in Pandeglang Regency, due to its high coastal tourism potential. title: The Role of Environmental Education in Supporting the Blue Economy: A Literature Review
abstract: Environmental education serves as a cornerstone for optimizing the blue economy—a sustainable development concept that prioritizes environmental justice and economic advancement for coastal and maritime communities. This study examines the extent to which environmental education can support the blue economy, employing a qualitative research method based on a literature review. The research highlights that integrating environmental education values ​​into blue economy programs is crucial for balancing economic growth with environmental conservation. abstract: With a focus on the social equity issues in the construction of urban climate resilience, this paper employs the analytical system of environmental justice and climate equity, draws upon domestic and foreign experiences in urban climate adaptation, and identifies the main problems in social equity at the core of resilience construction. abstract: Since 2016, under regulations issued by the Ministry of Science, Research, and Technology, metadata for theses, dissertations, and their proposals (TDPs) in Iran’s National Thesis, Dissertation and Proposal Registration System (NTDPRS) have been immediately open access, with full texts released after designated embargo periods. abstract: Blue and green waqf are emerging instruments that reposition the classical Islamic endowment as a vehicle of sustainable Islamic financing, directing perpetually dedicated assets and their returns toward environmental conservation, renewable energy, and coastal and marine resource management. This study maps the intellectual structure of the field through a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed, English-language journal articles retrieved using the keywords “sustainable waqf”, “blue waqf”, and “green waqf”. title: Polymetallic nodules provide a distinct habitat for abyssal meiofauna
abstract: Abstract Deep-sea abyssal plains harbour extensive biodiversity, much of which remains undocumented. Polymetallic nodules in the abyssal plains of the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ), Central Pacific, harbour diverse meiofaunal communities within their crevices, representing an understudied habitat. Given their high concentrations of nickel, copper, and cobalt, nodules are currently one of the primary targets for the extraction of deep-sea mineral resources. title: A Integrated Waste Management in Supporting The Achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
abstract: The problem of waste in densely populated coastal areas such as Kalibaru Village, Cilincing District, North Jakarta is still a serious challenge for urban environmental governance, with uneven service coverage and high daily waste generation. This study aims to analyze the contribution of integrated waste management in supporting the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially the 11th, 12th, and 13th goals. abstract: As public sector governance adapts to administrative modernization and digital transformation, effective property inventory management is vital for ensuring local government asset accountability and operational efficiency. This study evaluated the property inventory management practices in the Provincial General Services Office (PGSO) of Eastern Samar, focusing on property acquisition and receipt, warehousing and storage control, inventory tracking and record-keeping, and asset reconciliation and disposal. abstract: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) is a key backstop technology for achieving carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, and a monitoring system that is safe, effective and cost-rational is a prerequisite for the approval, continued operation, and public acceptance of CO2 geological storage projects. title: Prospects for mitigating IUU fishing in Africa through Africa-US strategic development cooperation
abstract: Although Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing is recognized as a threat to sustainable fisheries, prospects for reshaping win-win cooperation agendas in Africa remain underexplored. This study reviews 75 peer-reviewed articles and policy documents to explore prospects for stimulating strategic development cooperation with key actors, such as the United States (US), to mitigate and control IUU fishing in Africa. title: A floating electronic tag and LoRa-based infrastructure for jellyfish tracking and recapture
abstract: Jellyfish biologging remains challenging due to the animals' fragile morphology, weak buoyancy, and the absence of dedicated tracking devices. This work presents the Jellyfish float tracker, an open-source floating electronic tag and associated data infrastructure designed for jellyfish tracking and recovery. The system combines a lightweight 3D-printed waterproof float, a low-power GNSS receiver, a LoRaWAN communication transceiver, and an end-to-end data processing pipeline based on The Things Network, MQTT, Node-RED, and InfluxDB. abstract: Maritime transportation remains central to Nigeria’s economic development, international trade and the exploitation of marine and offshore resources. The effectiveness of this sector, however, depends substantially on the availability of an efficient, specialised and responsive maritime justice system capable of resolving disputes arising from shipping, carriage of goods, marine insurance, charterparties, ship financing, salvage, collision, limitation of liability and other admiralty-related transactions. title: Preventive Detention and the Right to Personal Liberty: A Constitutional and International Law Analysis of Article 10 of the Constitution of Pakistan
abstract: This paper examines the legal framework of preventive detention law in Pakistan and its constitutional implications. It also traces the law of preventive detention from its colonial origin to its contemporary application in counter-terrorism and national security contexts. It examines the law of preventive detention and its effect on liberty and fair trial, which are guaranteed by the Constitution of Pakistan, Articles 9 and 10A. abstract: This research analyses Ethiopia’s diplomatic challenges with the Gulf States in the context of the Red Sea’s rising strategic importance. Using qualitative methods—including expert interviews and the review and analysis of policy documents—the study examines the underlying causes of diplomatic hurdle in these relations. abstract: The health of coastal ecosystems is important for recreational values. title: Hooks of the ancient mariners: The oldest specialized maritime technology in the Americas dating to the Pleistocene-Holocene transition
abstract: Isla Cedros, Baja California, México is a remarkable place; it is a high, mountainous and tectonically active island located on the extreme west coast of the North American continent. It is home to some of the oldest evidence for human occupation of the coast along the Pacific Coast of the American continents, as well as the oldest fishhooks between the Bering Strait and the Atlantic Ocean. abstract: Prolonged and non-ergonomic sitting habits among adolescents have become an increasingly important public health concern, particularly in Islamic boarding school (pesantren) settings where santri spend long hours sitting while reading religious texts, memorizing the Qur'an, and attending lessons. abstract: This study aimed to design and conduct an initial market validation of an experiential tourism proposal named “Entre Mar y Óleos” for La Entrada, a coastal community in Santa Elena Province, Ecuador. abstract: The development of nuclear power in Indonesia raises questions about how regulatory oversight and public acceptance are addressed within energy policy. abstract: The main result of this study is a comprehensive examination of the current normative legal regulation of topical issues related to limiting greenhouse gas emissions into the environment. The paper attempts to formulate carbon law as a complex legal institution representing a set of mandatory rules of decarbonization. abstract: The presence of linguistic expressions of gender-fair language has experienced a steady increase in recent decades. abstract: Abstract We examine the relation between CEO military experience and insider trading in U.S. public firms. Military CEOs earn significantly lower insider trading profits than non‐military CEOs, particularly those who attained commissioned ranks or served in the Air Force, Army, or Marine Corps. abstract: Regenerative tourism and hospitality, aimed at restoring socio-ecological systems, have gained increasing relevance in both academic and professional spheres. This study presents a descriptive bibliometric analysis of the literature published between 2020 and 2024. abstract: This paper examines the legal framework governing the pre-contractual duty to disclose risk in life insurance under Spanish law, based on the principle of utmost good faith. abstract: Over the past thirty years, what Indigenous Peoples and local communities know about their environments has moved from the margins to the centre of global environmental assessment. Yet this knowledge is still treated, for the most part, as a store of information to be recorded, extracted and fitted into scientific and policy instruments. abstract: Traditional fishermen on Blimbingsari Beach have experienced a decline in income since 2022. This is due to extreme sea weather and the high cost of fuel per voyage. Although participants in FIH trials may personally benefit, the primary goal is to obtain participant baseline human safety knowledge or knowledge of intervention efficacy. abstract: This paper explores responses of host communities to offshore wind energy infrastructure through a case study of the Aberdeen Offshore Wind Farm (OWF), situated 2.4 km off the coast of northeast Scotland. abstract: Biodiversity refers to the structural, functional and evolutionary variability among living organisms across genetic, species and ecosystem hierarchical tiers. abstract: Abstract In this work, we present the results of an investigation into low-frequency seismic noise in an underground laboratory infrastructure, serving as a case study for the future Einstein Telescope. abstract: The accelerating challenges of climate change, resource depletion, urbanization, and social inequality have placed humanity and the planet at a critical juncture, where sustainability is no longer a choice but a necessity. abstract: Abstract Physical climate risks are a source of vulnerability in financial systems, yet existing risk measurement approaches struggle to translate them into decision-relevant metrics, reflecting a mismatch between how climate risk evolves and how financial risk is assessed. abstract: ABSTRACT In this wide‐ranging interview conducted for the Journal of Sociolinguistics, Emi Otsuji speaks with Alastair Pennycook about the trajectory of his scholarship across more than four decades in applied linguistics and sociolinguistics. abstract: Environmental problems often take a long time to deal with, but a turn in a board game is short. When real problems are put into a game, some details have to be left out. abstract: In 1953, a remarkable memoir appeared recounting the experiences of Englishwoman Helen Astrup during the German occupation of Norway (1940–1945), including her participation in resistance networks. abstract: Entrepreneurship education is an emerging approach that aims to develop transversal skills such as creativity, initiative, autonomy, and problem-solving. However, its integration into preschool education remains underexplored, and entrepreneurial competencies adapted to young children are still insufficiently structured. abstract: Abstract Rights of Nature (RoN) is increasingly used to challenge conventional legal frameworks, restructure governance over ecosystems and living beings, and rethink human–nature relations; however, its role in addressing human–wildlife conflict remains undertheorized and insufficiently defined. abstract: Based on a socio-technical literature review and comparative case studies, this paper analyses the place-based processes of industrial decarbonisation in the United Kingdom (UK). abstract: The Mesolithic of eastern Central Sweden is strongly associated with knapped quartz, pecked axes and a lack of preserved organic materials like bone, antler and wood. abstract: This paper examines whether the Cholas, Pandyas, Keralaputras and Satiyaputras stood under Mauryan authority during the reign of Aśoka (r. 268/272–232/235 BCE), and if so, in what sense. It assembles five bodies of evidence — Aśokan epigraphy, the Pali chronicle tradition, Tamil-Brāhmī inscriptions, Sangam poetry, and the later tradition of Aśokan presence in the Tamil country — and tests eleven propositions advanced in support of the hypothesis of Mauryan overlordship. title: Analysis of job performance in the administrative area of a high specialty hospital in the city of Villahermosa, Tabasco.
abstract: The objective of this project is to analyze the job performance of administrative staff at a high-specialty hospital in Villahermosa, Tabasco. The methodology will utilize the Likert scale technique, considering a population of 751 administrative staff members. A sample of 260 individuals will be surveyed, with a 95% confidence level. The research is of a mixed-methods, cross-sectional type, employing both qualitative and quantitative methodologies, and is situated within the current timeframe.

title: Regulation of transboundary impacts arising from the development of hydropower resources on international rivers
abstract: Situated against the backdrop of intensifying climate change and the ongoing “greening” of international water law, this paper examines the current patterns of hydropower development on international rivers and the resulting transboundary ecological and socio-economic impacts. Drawing on doctrinal analysis and selected cases, it analyzes the legal and environmental challenges associated with such projects, with particular emphasis on the principles of equitable and reasonable utilization and the obligation not to cause significant harm. abstract: Despite growing attention to global agendas in education systems, limited empirical research has examined how these agendas are translated into community-based adult education. This study investigates how Taiwanese community colleges reinterpret global educational agendas through locally situated educational practice. It conceptualizes community colleges as institutional mediators through which global educational priorities are recontextualized within local communities. abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of local finance laws in the management of the Tidore Kepulauan City Regional Budget in efforts to alleviate poverty, as well as to identify the normative and empirical barriers that affect its effectiveness. This study employs a socio-legal approach, using data collection techniques such as literature review, interviews, observation, and documentation. abstract: Global commitments to conserve 30% of land by 2030 place renewed emphasis on protected areas (PAs), yet governance shortcomings and distributional conflicts often undermine both conservation and socio-economic development outcomes. This paper examines PA governance in Central Karakoram National Park (CKNP), Pakistan’s largest national park in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), a region marked by constitutional ambiguity, contested land tenure, and infrastructure-driven market integration. title: Musicking the Revolution: Paul Revere, Phillis Wheatley, and the Boston Massacre
abstract: Abstract When Paul Revere published a broadside memorializing the 1770 Boston Massacre, he borrowed artwork that had been loaned to him by Henry Pelham, the young half-brother to the American painter John Singleton Copley. In spite of the fame of that broadside image in the history of the American Revolution, virtually no attention has been paid to the poem Revere printed on the broadside. title: SOMER: an assessment tool for social acceptance in wetland conservation contexts
abstract: Abstract Social acceptance plays an important role in wetland conservation, yet existing studies often rely on context-specific approaches that limit systematic assessment across wetland contexts. To fill this gap, this paper introduces the Social Monitor for Ecosystem Relations (SOMER), an assessment tool designed to examine social acceptance in wetland conservation contexts. In this study, social acceptance is operationalized through individuals’ perceptions of the costs and benefits of wetlands. abstract: Abstract Purpose: This study assessed the functionality of existing disaster preparedness strategies, namely early warning systems and resource preparedness, for maintaining service continuity at Julius Nyerere International Airport (JNIA), Tanzania’s busiest aviation hub. Design/methodology/approach: A mixed-methods, cross-sectional descriptive design guided by High Reliability Theory, the Resource-Based View and Crisis Management Theory was used. title: The Locust Motif as Political Commentary in Joe Ushie's A Reign Of Locusts
abstract: This study examines Joe Ushie's deployment of the locust motif as political commentary in A Reign of Locusts, analyzing how the poet transforms this biblical symbol into contemporary criticism of Nigeria's governance failures. Using archetypal criticism grounded in Carl Jung's analytical psychology and Northrop Frye's literary theory, the research investigates how Ushie uses the locust's collective and destructive nature to represent corrupt Nigerian political leadership. title: Climate change and facilities management in commercial real estate: Stakeholder understanding, operational impacts, and decision-making in Ghana
abstract: Climate change has gained global attention due to its effects on every aspect of society. This has led sectors worldwide to take action to address it. Effective sustainable facilities management practices are crucial in addressing climate change. Using institutional theory, the study examines understanding, perceptions, and support for climate change mitigation and adaptation in the commercial real estate sector, focusing on facilities management practices. The research employs a qualitative method consisting of a literature review and normative legal analysis of journal articles with verified DOIs or publisher webpages, as well as relevant legislation. title: Participatory foresight and regional place attractiveness: evidence from Halland, Sweden
abstract: Abstract Regional development is increasingly challenged by climate and demographic change, technological transformation, and growing uncertainty, requiring planning approaches that extend beyond short-term decision-making. While participatory foresight is widely used to explore alternative futures in regional planning, its contribution to understanding future place attractiveness remains underexplored. title: Karampuang Ecopedagogy Model: Local Wisdom and Ecological Education in Indigenous Communities in Sinjai, South Sulawesi
abstract: This study aims to describe the Karampuang Ecopedagogy model as a form of ecological education grounded in local wisdom within the indigenous community of Tompobulu Village, Sinjai Regency, South Sulawesi. The model is rooted in the ecological-spiritual philosophy of Sulapa Eppa, which emphasizes balance among fire, earth, water, and wind as the foundation of harmony between humans and nature. abstract: The article provides an in-depth examination of the complexities involved in contemporary English language usage when it comes to expressing comparisons, particularly through the lens of examples drawn from English-language fiction. abstract: The treatment of agricultural wastewater is a challenging process as pollution is comprised of a mixture of excess nutrients, pesticides, heavy metals, organic material, pathogens, pharmaceutical substances and salts. Treatment of such an extensive form of pollution necessitates techniques which can deal with various types of pollutants, chemically and physically, without causing pollution in any other compartment of the environment. abstract: Abstract The climate at high altitudes is changing more rapidly than in many other areas, with a variety of consequences for montane flora and fauna. We analyzed long‐term precipitation records from Crested Butte (2703 m, 1910–2025) and Gothic (2921 m, 1974–2026), Colorado, USA, in the West Elk Mountains. In Crested Butte, mean monthly precipitation during the growing season (May–September) can vary by over twofold and peak weekly precipitation occurs in late July and early August with the beginning of the summer monsoon. title: Actionable guidelines for promoting equity, diversity and inclusion in infectious disease modelling
abstract: Infectious disease modelling plays a critical role in understanding and addressing global health challenges. However, the field faces persistent barriers related to Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI), including language and cultural biases, underrepresentation of certain groups and systemic inequities in access to resources and opportunities. This paper identifies key challenges and proposes actionable guidelines to foster inclusivity, collaboration and innovation in the field. abstract: ABSTRACT This research examines nature‐based sustainable tourism destination development (NBSTDD) in Phuket, Thailand via the lens of Bottom‐Up Spillover Effect Theory, sustainable development goals (SDGs), and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) elements. A theoretical model is proposed, integrating these concepts, to understand their influence on locals' perceived quality of life (QoL) and their support for sustainable tourism development. abstract: This paper addresses the wake width variability downstream of bluff bodies with variable shape factors. abstract: Every US President has had a personal physician; in 1898 this doctor became a government employee. Later known as the White House Physician, many have provided inadequate medical care, and deliberately hidden evidence of incapacitating illnesses. Presidents Woodrow Wilson and Franklin Roosevelt are two of the most glaring examples: Wilson barely survived an incapacitating stroke, which his physician never disclosed, and Roosevelt’s physician repeatedly denied any serious illness. abstract: Background and objectives: Antimicrobial stewardship initiatives are designed to improve the appropriateness of antimicrobial use and thereby maximize benefits and minimize risks. Currently, there is no shared understanding of appropriate use. Qualitative research with key stakeholders in human and animal health is critical to inform a One Health definition and to support global stewardship efforts. title: Gender Equity and Decent Work in the Health Workforce in Nepal: Insights From Community Health Volunteers, Nurses, and Doctors
abstract: Gender equity in the health workforce is crucial for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. However, persistent inequities undermine workers' well-being, service delivery, and health system sustainability. This study examines how gender norms and hierarchical structures shape working conditions across Nepal's healthcare workforce. abstract: This article analyses six handbooks of water management written by publicly employed hydraulic officials in Augsburg, Barcelona, Bologna, Florence, Naples, and Rouen in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. title: Khep : Embodied commerce between Dubai and Karachi in the age of surveillance
abstract: Abstract This article explores khep , an embodied cross-border trade network that links Karachi and Dubai through trust, kinship, and risk. Based on ethnographic fieldwork with currency and commodity dealers who move money and goods between the two cities, I argue that khep is not merely a means of evading state regulation but a distinctive system of embodied commerce that has endured from the pre-colonial era to the present day. abstract: Stunting is a chronic growth disorder in children characterized by a height or length below the standards established by the World Health Organization (WHO). Maternal nutrition during pregnancy plays an essential role in preventing stunting, particularly through adequate vitamin D intake, which supports calcium metabolism, bone development, and fetal growth. abstract: This study critically reinterprets human rights values embedded in the Qur’an and Hadith through the philosophical hermeneutics of Hans-Georg Gadamer and Paul Ricoeur in contemporary Muslim societies. abstract: AIM: The prescription of antipsychotic medication during pregnancy, particularly second-generation antipsychotics, has increased in several countries in recent decades. This population-based study investigated trends and patterns in antipsychotic medication use during pregnancy between 2011 and 2023 in Northern Ireland (NI), UK. abstract: In the Lubuk Larangan tradition, communities temporarily close sections of a river to fishing before reopening them for communal harvesting. Reopening brings decisions about who can fish and how the proceeds should be used. Previous studies have examined customary rules and community welfare, while Islamic environmental ethics emphasizes stewardship and accountability. title: The effects of early years services (Sure Start) in Northern Ireland on social services interventions
abstract: Abstract Sure Start is an area-based intervention which offers support for families with children under four living in some of the most deprived areas in Northern Ireland. This study uses administrative data on almost every child born in Northern Ireland between 2006 and 2013 (n = 108,000). We use a quasi-experiment (Regression Discontinuity design) to measure the impact of Sure Start on interactions with social services in the first five years of life. Our results suggest that Sure Start substantially reduces rates of children who are referred to social services and become a ‘child in need’.

abstract: Air pollution remains a major environmental and global health concern, particularly in industrial areas where emissions from factories impact air quality and human well-being. This study examines the perception of air pollution and its associated health risks among residents living near a steel factory in Ifelodun Local Government, Kwara State, Nigeria. abstract: Abstract Grounded in the idea that vocality is linked to narrativity, this article argues that pagpangalimug (intoning) functions as a proto-narrative that sonically structures and mediates narrative experience among the Panay Bukidnon community in Panay Island, Western Visayas, Philippines. abstract: This study examined trichloroethylene (TCE) and tetrachloroethylene (PCE) groundwater contamination at the Hanam and Bonchon Industrial Complexes in Gwangju, South Korea. abstract: Traditionally, Ghanaian weddings functioned as modest, communal rites of passage that reinforced kinship solidarity, spirituality, and collective responsibility. In the past two decades, however, they have been reconfigured into elaborate, highly commercialisesed spectacles. This study critically examines this transformation through a Marxist theory of ideology, with particular attention to commodity fetishism, the culture industry, and Althusser’s concept of Ideological State Apparatuses (ISAs). The study's primary objective is to explore how dominant capitalist ideologies are constructed, pe
journal: African Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities Research

title: WHOSE CARBON, WHOSE BENEFIT? PANCASILA SOCIAL JUSTICE AND COMMUNITY BENEFIT-SHARING IN INDONESIA'S FOREST CARBON GOVERNANCE
abstract: Indonesia is rebuilding its forest carbon market at the same time as it accelerates the recognition of customary forests, yet the rules that decide who receives carbon revenue have received little legal scrutiny. This article asks whether Indonesia's emerging benefit-sharing arrangements meet the standard of social justice that the state's foundational philosophy, Pancasila, and the 1945 Constitution impose on the use of natural resources. journal: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável

title: Framework for Change: Progressing Planning for Disability Equity and Inclusion in Australia
abstract: Inclusive cities discourse is gaining prominence through global urban agendas, including the UN’s Sustainable Development Goal 11 and the New Urban Agenda, which link ideas of equity, inclusion and sustainability. Despite this global policy context, there remains little tangible progress towards equity and inclusion for diverse people with disabilities, including in Australia, where this research is grounded. This article addresses this gap by presenting a framework of change to progress planning for disability equity and inclusion. The framework was generated from participatory community-base

title: Loopholes in Australian wildlife, cultural heritage, human tissue and biosecurity laws: four case studies
abstract: Abstract We provide a novel investigation into where Australian legislation, meant to mitigate commerce in material cultural heritage, wildlife products and human tissue, clash in both their scope and practical application. Through an exploratory analysis of the legal context surrounding three recent Australian auction house sales and a social media post (demonstrating an example of successful import into Australia of human remains posing clear biosecurity risk), we identify legal loopholes through which these categories of trafficking can converge. title: Expert insight on the design, implementation, and monitoring of future community benefit funds within the energy transition
abstract: Increasingly, citizen and public participation are considered central to achieving the energy transition to a low carbon future. Such participation has different dimensions in new energy infrastructure, in terms of both renewable energy installations and additional electricity grid developments. Participation includes active involvement in decision making, the ability to invest in developer-led projects, and capacity for community owned renewable energy projects. title: A GREEN KHALIFAH: AKTUALISASI EKOTEOLOGI DALAM MEWUJUDKAN SUSTAINABLE CAMPUS DI UIN SUNAN GUNUNG DJATI BANDUNG
abstract: Krisis lingkungan hidup dewasa ini bukan sekadar persoalan ekologis, melainkan cerminan dari krisis moral dan teologis. Universitas Islam Negeri (UIN) Sunan Gunung Djati Bandung sebagai institusi pendidikan Islam memikul tanggung jawab profetik untuk mengembangkan wacana ekoteologi yang aplikatif. title: Unrequited: Zero‐sum asymmetry in the political domain fuels affective polarization
abstract: Abstract Zero‐sum beliefs about political relationships—the conviction that one party's gains are inevitably offset by another party's losses—have often been cited as drivers of partisan conflicts. However, across five studies with diverse samples of U.S. residents ( n = 1383), four of which were preregistered, we find that overall zero‐sum endorsement shows weak and inconsistent associations with affective polarization. title: La preuve par la Chine ? Jesuit networks, academic politics, and the shape of the Earth in 1730s Paris
abstract: This article argues that the Maupertuis-Cassini controversy over the shape of the Earth in the 1730s was intricately connected to Eurasian intellectual networks and academic politics. It focuses on the alliance of two Parisian pro-Cassini savants, Dortous de Mairan and Nicolas Fréret, and on their private correspondence with French Jesuits Antoine Gaubil and Dominique Parrenin in Beijing. journal: The British Journal for the History of Science

title: ACUPUNCTURE CARE FOR A PATIENT WITH SUBACUTE COUGH PRESENTING WITH WIND-COLD PATHOGEN INVASION SYNDROME: A CASE STUDY AT CAHAYA CLINIC, TANJUNGPINANG
abstract: Background: Cough is a vital protective respiratory reflex; however, when persistent, it severely disrupts physical comfort, nocturnal sleep architecture, and daily functional performance. While pharmacological antitussives and expectorants are commonplace, acupuncture represents an increasingly explored non-pharmacological modality in respiratory healthcare. Objective: To describe the clinical implementation, syndromic differentiation, and therapeutic outcomes of acupuncture care in a patient presenting with subacute cough at Cahaya Clinic, Tanjungpinang. Methods: A qualitative clinical case
institutions: Institut Teknologi, Sains, dan Kesehatan RS.DR. Soepraoen Kesdam V/BRW

title: Stoichiometric Optimisation of Vat Dyeing for Sustainable Colour Fastness in Cotton Fabrics
abstract: Purpose: Vat dyes are widely recognised for their superior colour fastness on cotton substrates; however, the efficiency of their reduction–oxidation cycle is highly dependent on the stoichiometric balance among the dye, sodium hydroxide (NaOH), and sodium hydrosulphite (Na₂S₂O₄). This study investigates how controlled variations in reagent ratios influence colour fastness, to develop a stoichiometrically grounded optimisation framework applicable to artisanal and semi-industrial dyeing systems in Ghana. Methodology/Design: An experimental factorial design was employed using mercerised cotton
institutions: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology

title: KETIKA ALGORITMA MENGENAL KITA: PENGARUH ALGORITHMIC PERSONALIZATION TERHADAP PURCHASE INTENTION MELALUI PERCEIVED INTRUSIVENESS
abstract: Personalisasi berbasis algoritma (algorithmic personalization) telah menjadi strategi utama platform e-commerce di Indonesia dalam meningkatkan relevansi produk yang ditawarkan kepada konsumen. Di sisi lain, personalisasi yang terlalu mendalam berpotensi menimbulkan persepsi gangguan (perceived intrusiveness) yang dapat menekan minat beli (purchase intention). Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh algorithmic personalization terhadap purchase intention secara langsung maupun melalui mediasi perceived intrusiveness. journal: Journal of Information System Applied Management Accounting and Research

title: Castigar la contradicción. Exclusión social y coherencia del reproche penal
abstract: Este artículo presenta la incoherencia normativa como un problema de justificación del reproche penal en la medida en que pone en cuestión los fundamentos que lo sostienen. La preocupación central es la posible arbitrariedad del sistema: el riesgo de que la aplicación de categorías formales a un contexto concreto desborde el sentido de sus presupuestos normativos. La coherencia serviría como un posible control de esta justificación. journal: Indret: Revista para el Análisis del Derecho

title: Directed evolution and characterisation of light harvesting complexes with altered spectral properties in purple non-sulfur bacteria
abstract: Abstract Purple non-sulfur bacteria (PNSB) are metabolically versatile microorganisms that inhabit diverse environments taking advantage of a remarkably efficient photosynthetic machinery. In this work, we describe the creation of a workflow for experimental studies aiming to compare the light absorption properties of structural variants of the light-harvesting complex 2 (LH2) of PNSB. title: Khalifah Fil Ardh sebagai Landasan Pengelolaan Pariwisata Berkelanjutan di Indonesia
abstract: The growing environmental crisis threatening the sustainability of tourist destinations in Indonesia calls for a management framework that is not only ecological and economic, but also ethical-theological. This study examines the concept of Khalifah Fil Ardh (vicegerency on earth) in Islam as a philosophical and operational foundation for sustainable tourism management in Indonesia. title: Turkish Mediation Diplomacy: Institutional Mechanisms, Track Records and the Ankara Process
abstract: Türkiye has become a prominent player in mediation diplomacy since 2003, as the Justice and Development Party (AKP) have prioritized mediation engagements across the world, leveraging it as a strategic instrument of Turkish foreign policy. In this regard, the present paper examines the implications of Turkish mediation diplomacy, with a particular focus on the Ankara process that deescalated tension between Ethiopia and Somaliland over the Ethiopia-Somaliland 2024 Memorandum of Understanding. The paper relied on an explanatory qualitative research design, employing a combination of primary and
journal: Ethiopian Journal of Strategic and International Affairs (EJSIA)

title: Carbon capture potential of recycled concrete aggregates from a full-scale recycling plant in the Brazilian federal district: A laboratory carbonation study
abstract: Accelerated carbonation of recycled concrete aggregates (RCA) can fix CO₂ while modifying aggregate properties, but most reported uptake values come from laboratory-produced aggregates that do not reproduce the heterogeneity of material leaving a real recycling line. This study assesses the carbon uptake of recycled sand and two coarse RCA fractions from a single industrial recycling plant in the Federal District, Brazil, sampled in two production campaigns. title: The critical role of political trust in the energy transition
abstract: Abstract Achieving net‐zero CO 2 emissions requires sustained collaboration between civil society and the private and public sectors across time and geographies, but low trust in and among these actors impedes coordinated action. This multidisciplinary review examines how different forms of trust, in particular political trust (i.e., trust between actors with differential power), shape the energy transition, addressing four core questions: How does trust impact energy project development and outcomes? How do the processes of building, maintaining, eroding, and repairing trust differ? What are

title: ‘Anchoring’ and ‘Staying’ as Ideal Types – War Refugees from Ukraine, Based on the Findings of a Study Conducted in Poznan in 2025
abstract: The article analyses the “anchoring” and “staying” of contemporary war migrants, with particular emphasis on the experiences of refugees from Ukraine in Poland. The aim of the study was to reconceptualise and re-operationalise the process of refugee integration. The study covered, among other things, the issue of deciding to stay, understood not as a single rationalised act, but as a social process. title: Federal impact assessment in Canada: from full retreat to total abdication?
abstract: Canada’s federal impact assessment regime is undergoing significant weakening through shortened timelines, reduced application and narrow scope. These changes represent an acceleration of rollbacks that were introduced in 2012. Driven by geopolitical risks and domestic economic pressures, the recent policy shifts prioritize fast-tracking major project approvals at the federal level of government and in some provinces. This article examines recent law and policy changes, including the new Building Canada Act, a law aimed at fast-tracking projects deemed to be in the ‘national interest.’ It also

title: Food security and wealth vs. environmental impact of agriculture as seen from a perspective of poor countries
abstract: Aim: The purpose of this article was to identify the determinants of low GDP per capita levels accompanied, and driven by, extreme food insecurity in the 25 countries with the lowest GFSI (Global Food Security Index). Methodology: The countries were divided into five groups for descriptive purposes, while the determinants of GDP per capita were examined using a fixed effects panel regression model. title: Good Manners and Right Conduct: Teaching Practices, Learners' Moral Development and Classroom Behavior
abstract: This study examined the influence of Good Manners and Right Conduct (GMRC) teaching practices aligned with the Philippine Professional Standards for Teachers (PPST) on learners’ moral development and classroom behavior in public elementary schools in Loay District, Bohol, during School Year 2025–2026. Anchored in the Theory of Planned Behavior, Character Education Framework, and Kohlberg’s Moral Development Theory, the study employed a descriptive-inferential research design involving 282 purposively selected respondents comprising 11 Grade 4 teachers, 11 school heads, and 260 learners from 11
journal: International Journal of Global Goals and Sustainable Development

title: The Island Equity Paradox: Capability, Governance, and Educational Reform in Peripheral Contexts
abstract: This study examines how China’s common prosperity reforms reshaped educational equity in two island counties of Zhejiang Province between 2020 and 2025. Addressing the dominance of cross-sectional approaches, it draws on a six-wave longitudinal qualitative study conducted from 2020 to 2025 with a 54-member core cohort of teachers and parents. Using the Island Capability–Equity Paradox Framework (ICEPF), the study traces how reform intentions were interpreted and enacted over time. title: Hidden biodiversity threats from fixed capital depreciation and regional inequality in China: Implications for conservation solutions
abstract: The continuous resource consumption and ecological externalities associated with the depreciation of China’s fixed assets pose systematic, yet often invisible, threats to biodiversity. This study constructs China’s yearly consecutive multi-regional input-output tables and a refined fixed capital investment database from 2000 to 2020, to support the spatial mismatch analysis between biodiversity responsibility and economic returns driven by capital depreciation. title: Food affordability and moral impartiality in Ghana, A Singerian analysis of households in the Central Region
abstract: Ghana's national Cost of a Healthy Diet bulletins exclude the Central Region for want of price data. Three things are therefore unknown: what an adequate diet costs there, how that cost falls across households, and whether the resulting distribution can be defended. Anchored in Singer's principle of equal consideration of interests and his preventable harm argument, and tested against the partiality and institutional critiques, this study addressed all three. title: The Impact of Cross-Border Data Regulation on the Resilience of China’s Industrial and Supply Chains
abstract: Digital transformation has created huge economic benefits for cross-border data flow around the world, but it has also caused real problems such as violating privacy and leaking business secrets. For China, how to manage data well and maintain the stability of the industrial supply chain is a difficult policy problem in the negotiation of international rules. This article analyzes two opposite effects of cross-border data regulation. On the one hand, strict regulatory review and uncertain policy results will increase the compliance burden of enterprises. journal: Academic journal of management and social sciences

title: Life cycle assessment of cement-bonded composite boards with municipal waste wood
abstract: Abstract The utilisation of waste wood in cement-bonded composites addresses pressing ecological challenges by diverting municipal waste wood from incineration. In this study, a life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted on a pilot-sized wood-cement composite board (1 × 1 m²; 18 mm thick) incorporating 25 wt% waste wood converted into wood chips. Environmental impacts were quantified for standard categories, including global warming, acidification, eutrophication, etc., in accordance with ISO 14044 guidelines. title: AGROFORESTRY MANAGEMENT INSTITUTIONS IN ENGKANGIN VILLAGE, AIR BESAR DISTRICT, LANDAK REGENCY
abstract: Agroforestry is an effective system for sustainable land use and provides significant benefits to community life. The success of agroforestry is highly dependent on strong institutional support. This study aims to explain the institutional management of agroforestry in Engkangin Village, focusing on organizational aspects and applicable rules. The approach used is descriptive qualitative, with data collected through observation, interviews, and documentation of agroforestry managers in Engkangin Village. The respondent sampling technique was purposive sampling. The results of the study indicat

title: Spatial and environmental influences on the assembly of silk microbiomes in a social spider
abstract: Abstract In nesting animals, the nest structure can play an important role in host‐associated microbiome assembly; however, the processes structuring the resulting microbiome remain underexplored. In the social spider Stegodyphus dumicola , philopatric sisters collectively build and maintain a silken nest, capture prey, and exhibit alloparental care. We used S. dumicola as a test system to assess the spatial and environmental processes structuring the nest microbial communities and address the role of extrinsic sources of nest‐associated microbiota. title: Beyond exposure: Pathways between urban greening, nature connection and wellbeing in Australian policy frameworks
abstract: Urban greening initiatives are increasingly positioned as strategies to improve health and wellbeing in cities. While academic research has long acknowledged the role of psychological connections to nature in shaping wellbeing, it is unclear whether and how this relationship is recognised in urban greening policy. This study examines how Australian urban greening and biodiversity strategies conceptualise and evaluate wellbeing and nature connection. title: Challenges and Opportunities Encountered by the Teachers in the Implementation of Science Investigatory Projects
abstract: This study examined the challenges and opportunities experienced by Grade 6 public elementary school teachers in implementing Science Investigatory Projects (SIPs) in five municipalities of Bohol, Philippines, to inform an evidence-based action plan. Using a convergent parallel mixed-methods design, the study surveyed 50 teachers selected through stratified random sampling and obtained qualitative accounts from 11 purposively selected teachers. journal: International Journal of Global Goals and Sustainable Development

title: Governing trade, governing carbon: How environmental provisions in RTAs affect carbon inequality within global value chains?
abstract: Environmental provisions in regional trade agreements (RTAs) play an important role in aligning trade with environmental objectives and mitigating carbon inequality. Using data covering 80 economies and 50 industries, we apply a multi-regional input–output model to construct a bilateral measure of carbon inequality from a value-capture perspective and examine whether deeper environmental provisions mitigate it. title: Extreme Climate Events, Governance Deficits, and Adaptation Failure in Africa: A Policy and Framework Review
abstract: Africa accounts for less than four per cent of cumulative global greenhouse gas emissions, yet it absorbs some of the most severe consequences of anthropogenic climate change. The literature documenting this disparity has grown substantially over the past decade, but most reviews stop at cataloguing impacts and listing recommendations. This paper goes further.
