title: La “paradoja maldita”: estereotipos de género, confianza política y percepción ciudadana española en el liderazgo femenino en la política
abstract: Esta investigación ex post facto, transversal, descriptiva y relacional analiza cómo se configuran los estereotipos de género en la percepción ciudadana española en relación con los atributos asignados a mujeres y hombres dedicados a la política. Para ello, considera la figura ideal de liderazgo, los niveles de confianza diferencial y las preferencias de liderazgo por género, aplicando como técnica cuantitativa una encuesta panel online profesional a 403 personas residentes en España. title: Palabras malsonantes y parodias: los retos que la libertad de expresión plantea en el derecho de marcas de la UE
abstract: Las empresas de moda y belleza se encuentran en mercados competitivos, globales y en los que captar la atención del consumidor es cada vez es más difícil. El uso de un nombre soez o la parodia de una marca muy conocida pueden ser vías para sobresalir en una industria donde la oferta es abrumadora.El presente trabajo tiene un hilo conductor que es la libertad de expresión. Este derecho fundamental se va a poner de manifiesto en relación a dos problemas actuales relacionados con el derecho de marcas europeo pero que se encuentran en dos planos o “momentos” diferentes. title: Countering populist radical-right parties: the institutional foundations of strategic voting, forced mobility, and party coordination in France and Germany
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates how institutional configurations shape strategic voting, forced mobility, and party coordination against populist radical right parties (PRRPs). As PRRPs expand their electoral support across Europe, voters and parties increasingly coordinate to prevent them from gaining power, but the forms and feasibility of such coordination vary across political systems. We argue that electoral systems, party-system structure, and type of democracy jointly shape the incentives and opportunities for electoral coordination and strategic voting. title: Business and human rights as a compensation to asymmetric investment treaty rights and obligations
abstract: This paper aims to analyze the correlation between business and human rights (BHR) regulations and investment treaties. With the economic investment dependency of host States, the imposition of rules to protect stakeholders against BHR infringements is a necessity and thus will correct inequalities caused by older investment treaties, that in some cases would forbid the host State to change their legislation to improve the welfare and human rights protections of their population. title: Foundational economy, geography and ‘left behind places’
abstract: Foundational economy (FE) is part of the proliferation of alternative approaches following the Global Financial Crisis in 2008. FE is an influential agenda in urban and regional studies, but its geographical dimensions are under-developed. This paper explains and demonstrates the value and challenges of a more geographically grounded and sensitive approach to FE. title: Indonesia’s Capital Relocation to Nusantara: Strategic Implications for Malaysia’s Bilateral Relations, Security and Economic Interests
abstract: Indonesia’s relocation of its national capital to Nusantara in East Kalimantan changes the spatial context of Malaysia–Indonesia relations on Borneo. This qualitative study combines documentary analysis with eight elite semi-structured interviews conducted in Malaysia and Indonesia. Three findings emerge. First, Nusantara does not create an immediate conventional military threat to Malaysia, but it increases the strategic salience of land-border management, maritime boundary diplomacy and non-traditional security coordination. title: Acquihires y control de concentraciones
abstract: El término acquihires describe un conjunto de operaciones empresariales dirigidas principalmente a la adquisición de talento humano que pueden plantear ciertos riesgos para la competencia, tanto en los mercados de productos como en los laborales, y paralelamente importantes retos para los sistemas de control de concentraciones. title: Methodology of Working with Facts in the Modern Information Space and Its Role in Shaping a Journalist's Professional Competence
abstract: This article examines the theoretical and practical significance of facts in journalistic practice, highlights their primary functions, and underscores the vital importance of fact-based journalism for contemporary society. As part of the empirical research, an open-ended survey comprising 20 specialized questions on "The Role of Facts in Journalistic Activity and Skills in Their Application" was conducted to analyze the perspectives and practical insights of media professionals.
journal: American journal of social and humanitarian research.

title: Bridging Outlooks: A Scoping Review on Commonly shared Indigenous, African, Asian and Non-Western Worldviews of Wellbeing
abstract: ABSTRACT Although wellbeing has been widely examined across disciplines and cultural contexts, its broader conceptualizations remain fragmented and largely rooted in Western paradigms. In contrast, non-Western frameworks (Indigenous, African, Asian, and among other collectivist traditions) offer alternatively rich and critical understandings of wellbeing that remain insufficiently integrated into mainstream interventions, research and policy frameworks. title: Enhancing Aquatic Persistence Assessments: Effects of Photosensitizers and Surfactants on Photochemical Degradation in the Environment
abstract: Photochemical processes substantially influence the environmental fate of chemicals, yet current persistence assessments rarely account for indirect photochemistry or interfacial effects. Here, we systematically investigated the photodegradation of the fungicide carbendazim, which is classified as persistent in aquatic environments according to current regulations. title: Empowering Women Farmers in Nueva Ecija through Entrepreneurship: The Role of Corporate Social Responsibility in Sustainable Economic Development
abstract: This study examined the role of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in empowering women farmers in Llanera, Nueva Ecija, through entrepreneurship and sustainable economic development. Specifically, it assessed the level of awareness of women farmers regarding CSR, the types and scope of CSR programs implemented by local businesses, their participation and engagement in entrepreneurship initiatives, the socio-economic impacts of CSR-driven activities, and the challenges that hinder program effectiveness. title: Working towards new means for reconciling wind power and reindeer husbandry through collaboration in Northern Finland
abstract: As formal governance and planning processes struggle to address energy transition related conflicts, there is a growing need for approaches that help parties understand emerging tensions and identify mutually acceptable solutions. In this paper, we present a case study from Finland where wind power developers and reindeer herders have established a collaborative arrangement to address conflicts and develop shared practices for communication and negotiation. journal: Journal of Environmental Planning and Management

title: Meditation Breathing Training and Short-Term Recovery in Patients Undergoing Thoracoscopic Lung Cancer Resection: A Non-Randomized Historical-Control Study
abstract: Objective: To investigate the association of meditation breathing training with short-term physical and mental recovery in lung cancer patients after thoracoscopic lobectomy. Materials and Methods: A non-randomized historical control study design was adopted. A total of 62 patients (31 per group) diagnosed with lung cancer and receiving thoracoscopic surgery at our hospital between January 2023 and June 2024 were enrolled. title: Integrating sustainability into higher education curricula to strengthen the sustainability-employability nexus via sustainable value chains (SEN-SVCs) in Ghana
abstract: While some Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) have started integrating sustainable practices into their training and development strategies to create sustainable value chains, many still find it difficult to justify adopting this emerging approach.This exploratory study asks to what extent sustainability practices are integrated in Ghanaian HEIs and how such integration can support sustainable value chains.Using descriptive analysis of secondary data from the QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2025 for the four Ghanaian HEIs listed (University of Ghana, Kwame Nkrumah University of

title: Can we justify the environmental and human health costs of reducing PFAS-4 in drinking water? A life cycle assessment in Sweden
abstract: PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) contamination of drinking water is a critical environmental and public health concern. As regulations become more stringent, water utilities are increasingly evaluating treatment technologies to ensure safe drinking water supplies. This study applies life cycle assessment to compare five treatment trains for PFAS-contaminated groundwater, each including pre-treatment, PFAS removal, post-treatment and PFAS destruction steps. title: Satellite Tracking and Citizen Science Provide Complementary Insights Into Spatial and Temporal Migration Patterns of Eastern Buzzards
abstract: ABSTRACT Individual bird tracking can resolve continuous migration processes but is limited by small sample sizes, whereas citizen‐science records provide broad spatial and multi‐year coverage but are affected by observation effort and spatial accessibility. However, few studies have evaluated how citizen‐science records and individual tracking correspond across both spatial and temporal components of the same migratory system, including migration routes, stopover sites, migration timing, and broad‐scale spatial coverage. title: First direct measurement of food transit time through the gastrointestinal tracts of plant-eating primates using isotopic tagging
abstract: Abstract The time it takes for food to transit animal gastrointestinal tracts is essential information to fields from organismal evolution to ecosystem ecology. Nevertheless, current estimation methods do not measure food directly, are impractical for many species and often require unnatural conditions to administer. We overcome these limitations by adopting techniques from organic geochemistry. title: Drilling in ‘paradise’: environmental governance, local communities and oil exploration in the Okavango Delta, Botswana
abstract: Abstract Oil exploration in ecologically sensitive landscapes presents significant environmental governance challenges, particularly where extractive development intersects with wetland conservation and community livelihoods. This study examines how international, regional, and national policy and legislative frameworks regulate oil exploration in the Okavango Delta, Botswana, using a qualitative desk-based review of legal, policy, and documentary sources. abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of service quality on customer satisfaction through service outcomes and customer trust as mediating variables among AEON Jakarta Garden City customers. This research uses a quantitative approach with purposive sampling. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 151 respondents who met the research criteria. Data analysis was performed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. title: dueños de la Patagonia: enriquecimiento injusto y restitución tras el despojo indígena
abstract: Tras el conflicto político entre Buenos Aires y las provincias que culminó con la Constitución de la Nación Argentina de 1860, la “cuestión del indio” ocupó un lugar central en la política de ese país. En este contexto, el Estado argentino lanzó campañas militares en los territorios indígenas entre 1878 y 1885, conocidas como la Conquista del Desierto. Sin embargo, la expansión hacia las zonas más australes del país siguió un camino diferente: con el apoyo del Estado, empresas privadas y colonos ocuparon esas tierras. institutions: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

title: Delegating Digital Policing: The Evolution of China’s Security-Industrial Complex
abstract: Abstract How did China build its formidable digital policing apparatus so rapidly? While prevailing narratives emphasize top-down state direction, this statist perspective obscures critical local dynamics. This article argues that China’s security-industrial complex actually emerged from decentralized administrative pressures. Burdened by unfunded, time-sensitive central security mandates, resource-strapped local security agencies abandoned state-led technological development and outsourced to the private sector. title: Plant Life and Plant-Worship in Tripuri Folktales: A Reading of Ethnobotany in Select Tripuri Folktales
abstract: This paper examines the representation of plant lifeforms and the significance of such narratives in select Tripuri folktales through the lens of Ethnobotany.The study argues that plants in Tripuri folk narratives should not be regarded merely as passive elements of nature.Rather, it explores how they frequently function as active participants that shape events, sustain human life, mediate relationships between human and nonhuman beings, and contribute to a critical interpretation of the landscape.The methodological framework of this study is grounded in the theoretical insights on "plant life

title: Personal Narratives of Homesickness: Tracing Concepts of Nostalgia, Memory and Form in Recollection (2015) and The Writing On The Wall (1991-1992)
abstract: This study subjects Palestinian filmmaker Kamal Aljafari's personal film Recollection (2015) and American contemporary artist Shimon Attie's installation project The Writing On The Wall (1991-1992) to a comparative narratological analysis along the axes of nostalgia, memory and form. The main aim of this research is to put forward how the transformative strategies that Alexis Lothian conceptualizes as the practices of "culture thieves" - sampling, erasing, ripping, remixing and burning - might have been operationalized in two different historical catastrophes, namely the Nakba and the Holocaus

title: Secondary school student and teacher perspectives about citizen science-based environmental education and youth agency
abstract: Education is thought to play a key role in driving positive environmental action. This study explores Hong Kong student (ages 11–19 years) and teacher perceptions about experiential environmental education and citizenship action, after engaging in environmental citizen science. We conducted semi-structured interviews with 46 students and 18 teachers across eight local and international schools, informed by behavioural psychology constructs such as motivation, self-efficacy and agency. title: Structured coupling beam control of six-wave mixing: from Helical Ince-Gaussian to Laguerre-Gaussian modes
abstract: Abstract We theoretically investigate six-wave mixing (SWM) in a coherently driven six-level atomic system using a structured coupling field. The probe and generated-field responses are obtained using the density-matrix formalism combined with the Maxwell Bloch equations. A Helical Ince–Gaussian (HIG) beam is introduced as the coupling field, and its ellipticity is varied to study the influence of its transverse structure on the nonlinear mixing process. title: Buy One Get One Free: Recognition, State-Building, and the Dual Peace Dividend in the Horn of Africa
abstract: Somalia and Somaliland are usually presented as competitors in a zero-sum sovereignty dispute. This article develops a different proposition: internationally recognized Somaliland statehood could also advance Somalia's stabilization and state-building. The "buy one get one free" formulation describes a potential dual peace dividend rather than an automatic result. The study combines qualitative, theory-guided historical and policy analysis with in-depth expert interviews and focus group discussions. Five theoretical mechanisms are proposed. title: THE EVOLUTIONARY STAGES OF THE FORMATION OF UZBEK DEMONONYMS
abstract: This article provides a linguistic and cultural analysis of the formation and evolutionary development stages of Uzbek demononyms. The corpus of demononyms does not originate from a single root; rather, it is a complex system born from the synthesis of ancient Turkic and Iranian mythology, Islamic theology, and fiction. The study categorizes the development of demononyms into four major strata in correlation with the evolution of human thought. title: The Rationale for the Merger of IGAD and EAC: Its Potential Benefits and Challenges for the Greater Horn
abstract: One of the ubiquitous problems of the African economic integration process is multiple and overlapping memberships in different regional economic communities (RECs). One solution for this is the merger of these RECs into a single, larger entity. This study examined the rationale for the merger of IGAD and EAC as one larger new regional economic community in the greater Horn of Africa and assessed its potential benefits and challenges for the region. title: A Novel Fe3O4-Coated Activated Carbon Catalyst for Drinking Water Disinfection and Toxic Disinfection Byproduct Control
abstract: Abstract Traditional drinking water disinfectants such as chlorine not only deactivate pathogenic microorganisms in source water but also react with dissolved organic matter (DOM) from natural and anthropogenic sources, leading to the formation of numerous toxic halogenated disinfection byproducts (DBPs). The strong oxidants generated through catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) by iron oxide (Fe3O4) are proposed to reduce dissolved organic carbon (DOC), a DBP precursor, as well as to disinfect pathogens in drinking water treatment. title: Putin’s Bestowals and ‘Care for the People’
abstract: This article examines a little-studied technique of governance in contemporary Russia: the public bestowal of grants, prizes, payments and honours associated with Vladimir Putin and other powerful figures. Drawing on online research and accounts from Russian interlocutors, particularly cases from Siberia, it explores how competitions and exceptional rewards are framed as personal acts of care while addressing needs inadequately met through regular state provision. title: Why Are Slurs Wrong? Slurs, Power, and Reclamation
abstract: ABSTRACT Everyone agrees that slurs are bad, but not about why they are bad. Philosophers often focus on the meaning of these terms and the linguistic puzzles they reveal—trying to identify the nasty content slurs convey and the mechanism through which they convey it. But this approach can only explain some of what makes slurs bad. This paper surveys recent work that goes beyond the communicative content of slurs to explain their (oppressive) social function. title: The migration trajectory is no longer linear: Insights from Kosovar Albanians immigrants
abstract: Migration trajectories are often conceptualized as linear flows — a one-directional movement from an origin to a destination, followed by settlement. However, this traditional view has been increasingly questioned, as contemporary migration processes frequently involve fragmented, multidirectional, and non-linear pathways. The current study draws on a social determinant and health perspective to explore how migration trajectories are shaped, experienced, and redefined over time. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with Kosovar Albanian immigrants currently living in the United Kingdom. R

title: Detection of evolutionary shifts in variance under an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model
abstract: Sudden changes in environmental conditions can lead to evolutionary shifts not only in the optimal trait value (θ), but also in the diffusion variance (σ2) under the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) model. While several methods have been developed to detect shifts in optimal values, few explicitly account for concurrent shifts in both evolutionary variance and diffusion variance. title: Implementation of Discipline in Improving the Performance of Employees at the Tourism Office of Buton Regency
abstract: This study aims to describe how discipline is implemented at the Tourism Office of Buton Regency and how this implementation supports employee performance. A descriptive qualitative approach was used. Informants were selected through purposive sampling from five sources: the Head of the Office, the Marketing and Promotion Division, the General Section, the Planning and Evaluation of Tourism Reporting Division, and the Head of the Destinations Division. title: Microstoria : Reducing the pro‐elite bias in management research
abstract: Abstract Much management research, more than perhaps any other neighbouring social science, and especially in recent times, has been organised around elites—founders, CEOs, top management teams and board members—as the privileged locus and production site of meaningful knowledge. title: Reconceptualizing Teacher Professional Competence through Medical Biochemistry: A Biopsychological Framework Linking Biochemical Health, Cognitive Function, and Educational Effectiveness
abstract: Teacher professional competence has traditionally been theorized through pedagogical, cognitive, and motivational lenses, treating biological health as a peripheral concern rather than a core determinant of instructional capacity. This paper proposes a biopsychological reconceptualization of teacher competence that positions medical biochemistry-specifically micronutrient status, hormonal regulation, gut-brain signaling, sleep architecture, and stress-biomarker profiles-as a foundational layer underlying cognitive function and, by extension, classroom effectiveness. title: Airway microbial-inflammatory endotypes are associated with disease severity and predicted survival in cystic fibrosis
abstract: BACKGROUND: The airway microbiome and host inflammatory response synergistically drive cystic fibrosis (CF) lung disease. We hypothesized that integrating airway microbial community structures with inflammatory biomarker profiles would reveal distinct ecological-inflammatory endotypes associated with clinical outcome measures. title: Housing Price Pressure and Employee Lawsuits: Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT This study explores how rising housing prices affect employee–employer conflict through the lens of employee lawsuits. Using a sample of Chinese listed firms from 2013 to 2019, we find that the likelihood of employee lawsuits against a firm increases with housing prices in the city where the firm is located. To establish causality, we employ a staggered difference‐in‐differences approach based on the implementation of home purchase restriction policies designed to curb housing price growth, and we also use land supply as an instrument for housing prices. title: “I live in an environment where I don’t feel very happy”: voices, representations, and needs in the education of Bangladeshi families living in Venice
abstract: Bangladeshi immigration to Italy is a relatively recent phenomenon. While the first Bangladeshis arrived in the 1980s, this increased rapidly in the 1990s and 2000s, when some ethnic enclaves or ‘Bangla-towns’ started to emerge, especially near the large industrial districts of north-eastern Italy, such as Marghera and Mestre in the province of Venice, the industrial areas in the province of Vicenza, and Monfalcone in the province of Gorizia. title: Who Pays the 20 Percent Deduction? Vacancy in Concession Funding Arrangements in Government Regulation Number 31 of 2026
abstract: Government Regulation No. 31 of 2026 establishes disability-related concessions across nine sectors but leaves unresolved the question of how service providers should finance the mandatory minimum tariff reduction of 20%. This study aims to identify sector-specific financing vulnerabilities, assess existing compensation mechanisms, and formulate feasible funding recommendations. A qualitative documentary research approach integrates legal analysis with a synthesis of published policy reports, subsidy practices, and budgetary frameworks. title: The anatomy of competitiveness
abstract: Abstract A large empirical literature in behavioral economics investigates heterogeneity across individuals and groups in preferences for competition. In this study, we provide a more detailed view on competitiveness by differentiating between three motivations for entering competitions: enjoyment of competition, desire to win, and competition for personal development. title: Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates Economic Diplomacy: Trajectory and Trends
abstract: This article examines the trajectory and trends of economic diplomacy between Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) from 2014 to 2023. The study employed concurrent mixed research approach, relying on both qualitative and quantitative data. The findings revealed that Introduction Ethiopia’s economic diplomacy with the UAE transformed from closed treaty-based to flexible strategic partnership. title: Building Operational Excellence: Evaluating Training System and Skills Development Program for Rmfb7
abstract: This study systematically evaluated the current training system and skills development program of the Regional Mobile Force Battalion 7 (RMFB7) at its Headquarters in Sibonga, Cebu. Grounded in the Kirkpatrick Model of Training Evaluation, Human Capital Theory, Knowles’ Andragogy, and Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory, the study utilized a descriptive-evaluative research design. title: Handloom to Mill: The Evolution of Indian Textile Industry in Colonial Times
abstract: The discovered textile fragment at Mohenjo-daro provides age-old evidence of textile production in India. Since ancient times, various regions of India had developed distinct techniques for producing different types of textiles. The quality and diversity of Indian textiles earned widespread recognition and acceptance among foreign traders and consumers. title: Reclaiming the commons of the sky: drones and the limits of property law
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the concept of the commons in the context of the emergence of convenience-based delivery drone networks around the world. It contends that the drone-facilitated commodification of our skies constitutes a modern form of enclosure, facilitated by a legal architecture that centres around questions of ownership. Additionally, and consistent with more traditional land-grabs, expropriation of the sky is supported by its characterisation as a vacant and unused resource. title: A large scale crisis: The Hopen accident and the struggle against the Soviet autonomy on Svalbard
abstract: This article examines the handling of the Hopen crisis of 1978 in light of the overall effort by the Norwegian authorities to curtail the self-rule, or autonomy, of the Soviet mining towns on Svalbard. By supplementing and defragmenting the existing accounts of the event, it investigates its causes, management and consequences in relation to this effort, and asks how the Soviets responded to it, which factors led to its successful resolution and whether it strengthened Norwegian sovereignty. title: Memory, Grief and Multimodal Mourning: Michael Rosen’s Sad Book from Page to Stage
abstract: Abstract While picturebooks about death have been extensively studied, few analyses trace how such texts are adapted into embodied, performative forms. This article addresses that gap by examining Michael Rosen’s Sad Book (2004) and its 2024—2025 stage adaptation by 201 Dance Company. The picturebook conveys mourning through first-person narration, tonal illustration and fragmented structure, presenting sadness as persistent rather than resolved. The dance adaptation reimagines this grief as an embodied, collective experience through choreography, gesture, projected imagery, sound and silence.

title: Información y posicionamientos en los debates presidenciales de Argentina en 2023
abstract: Este artículo analiza de forma cualitativa la información y los mensajes disponibles en los debates presidenciales de Argentina en 2023 por medio de técnicas de la sociosemiótica, del marketing político y de la teoría funcional. Al condensar no sólo las posiciones ideológicas y programáticas de los candidatos, sino también su carácter y sus aptitudes personales, los debates constituyen un espacio de exposición y contraste público de distintas posiciones. title: La protección del consumidor frente a la tutela de la propiedad intelectual en la Directiva (UE) 2019/770 sobre contratos de suministro de contenidos y servicios digitales
abstract: Este artículo analiza la protección del consumidor en los contratos de suministro de contenidos digitales frente a las restricciones de los titulares de la propiedad intelectual, en el marco del régimen de conformidad de la Directiva 2019/770. abstract: Abstract This article uses Critical Discourse Analysis to examine the racialised implications of the 2026 Schools White Paper: Every child achieving and thriving and the associated open consultation, SEND reform: putting children and young people first. Drawing on scholarship in critical race theory, disability studies, and intersectionality, the paper argues that policy frameworks often obscure the structural inequalities experienced by pupils who occupy multiple marginalised identities, particularly those at the intersection of special educational needs and different racial backgrounds. title: CHALLENGES OF RENEWABLE ENERGY INDUSTRY IN MALAYSIA
abstract: The purpose of this study is to highlight the challenges faced by the Renewable Energy (RE) industry in Malaysia. This conceptual review examines previous research and articles on renewable energy in Malaysia and internationally, including current statistics, developments, and the status of renewable energy worldwide. The review covers key areas related to renewable energy, including its definitions, purposes, barriers, problems, challenges, principles, policies, strategies, and recommendations. abstract: This study examines the impact of institutional quality and income inequality on environmental degradation for the selected South Asian and ASEAN countries for the time span 1985-2022. title: Pengaruh Kemitraan, Persaingan dan Pendapatan Ojek Online Terhadap Kesejahteraan Driver Gojek di Jakarta Selatan
abstract: This study is motivated by the rapid growth of the online motorcycle taxi (ojek online) industry in South Jakarta, which has triggered intense competition and affected drivers' welfare. Drivers face challenges such as fluctuating income, job insecurity, and policy changes by the application platforms. This study aims to analyze how partnership, competition, and income affect Gojek drivers' welfare in South Jakarta. title: Translating Cultural Context: A Pragmatic and Functional Evaluation of Moroccan Arabic Proverbs and Literary Texts
abstract: Cultural translation research attracts scholarly attention due to the need for appropriate translation approaches. Cultural context is a tangled issue in translation studies, being both pervasive and decisive in cross-cultural translation. Evaluating cultural translation demands robust semantic and pragmatic frameworks to bridge the gap between source and target language contexts. This paper investigates the impact of cultural context on translation by evaluating selected Moroccan Arabic proverbs and culture‑specific literary expressions translated into English. title: Quantifying stump-exclusion effects on aboveground biomass comparability in allometric equations for Nepal
abstract: Nepal’s Forest Research and Training Centre (FRTC) recently developed national allometric equations in which modelled aboveground biomass (AGB) excludes the basal 30-cm stump. However, the contribution of this excluded section to ground-level AGB, and how that contribution varies with tree size and species, has not been evaluated. title: Climate justice, fossil fuel lock-ins and opportunities
abstract: Abstract More than thirty years after the adoption of the UN Convention on Climate Change, fossil fuel still provides 80% of the world’s total energy consumption. The escalation in renewables makes a dent in fossil fuel use, but cannot, in itself, address the climate problem. Hence, this paper asks: What blocks the transition away from fossil fuel and what opportunities are there to phase out fossil fuel? abstract: Neutron absorbance efficiency is crucial for radiation shielding and nuclear reactors, with mushrooms like Pleurotus Ostreatus (PO) and Pleurotus Citrinopleatus (PC) enhancing this property due to their nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, cadmium, and carbon content. abstract: The purpose of the following study is to conduct a critical and in-depth investigation of the coal-based electricity projects and investment under CPEC (China-Pakistan Economic Corridor), discussing their environmental impacts, legal issues, and recommendations. This research uncovers various aspects of these projects, phases them out, and presents solutions to achieve sustainability. abstract: This study focuses on the methodological gap in the integration of nature-based concepts in basic design education and examines the phenomenon of crown shyness within the context of the conceptual–formal transformation process, addressing it as a structured teaching model supported by criteria-based evaluation parameters. abstract: Intangible cultural heritage represents the collective memory, cultural identity, and traditional knowledge of local communities, while its sustainable inheritance increasingly faces challenges arising from modernization, migration, and lifestyle transformation. title: An adhyātma reading of the Trimūrti through the Liṅgodbhava and Anantaśayana narratives
abstract: The Trimūrti of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva is usually read as a division of cosmic labour among creation, preservation and dissolution. title: Platformed Atmospheres: How Digital Platforms Reshape the Felt Experience of Family Life
abstract: This article develops the concept of platformed atmospheres to address how digital platforms reshape domestic life. Platformed atmospheres are defined as the multisensory and affective environments that emerge when platforms become infrastructural to family life, shaping not only what families communicate but the felt, sensory, and temporal conditions through which homes are inhabited. abstract: Este artículo propone una lectura textual del star system en el Hollywood clásico (1930-1945), centrándose en la representación de la vulnerabilidad emocional masculina en la pantalla. abstract: Abstract This article examines the sources for reconstructing Jesuit finances in China. While there are a multitude of anecdotal references in Jesuit letters and reports, only four in-depth accounting documents have survived. abstract: Abstract The Povos e Comunidades Tradicionais de Terreiro e de Matriz Africana in Brazil (Traditional Peoples and Communities of Afro-Brazilian Terreiro and African Matrix religions, henceforth Povos de Terreiro ) are Afro-Brazilian religious communities in which plants play important ritual, therapeutic, and cultural roles. abstract: This research investigates the contribution of Pencak Silat to the formation of social values within a community, focusing on its impact on character, solidarity, and social responsibility. The research aims to delve deeply into how the practice of Pencak Silat shapes social structures and cultural values within a society. title: Hydrogel-encapsulated microalgal biomass residues for vegetable cultivation in soil and hydroponics
abstract: The growing global dependence on inorganic fertilizers has raised sustainability concerns, while bio-based alternatives face challenges associated with rapid nutrient release and leaching losses. Herein, this study presents a novel strategy for the development of slow-release biofertilizers by encapsulating residual microalgal biomass in alginate hydrogels crosslinked with CaCl₂. abstract: This article discusses cross-language communication in one of the few contact zones of the Cold War: the Norwegian archipelago of Svalbard (Spitsbergen), where the Soviet Union maintained a permanent presence. Communication between the office of the governor of Svalbard and the administration of the Soviet mining villages occasionally involved ad hoc interpreters, who were either Norwegian bilinguals or Soviet citizens with some knowledge of English or German. title: The Dangers of Recognition for Energy Justice
abstract: In energy justice, it is generally assumed that recognition is just and that misrecognition should be battled. However, recently, critical theorists have articulated multiple dangers intrinsic to recognition that remain largely unthematized in energy justice scholarship. abstract: Germline data from African populations remain sparse, limiting characterization of population-specific BRCA1/2 pathogenic variants (PV). In a study of 175 Rwandan women with breast cancer, 7 unrelated carriers (4% of cases; 22% of PV carriers) harbored the same BRCA1 frameshift PVs, c.4065_4068del (p.Asn1355Lysfs*10), which is extremely rare in gnomAD yet recurrent in European, Asian, and Middle Eastern cohorts. title: Agroforestry ambitions fifty years after launch of a governance-people-science boundary concept
abstract: A novel word connecting agriculture and forestry, agroforestry, originated in 1976 with ambitions for radically better land use. At its 50'th anniversary, we reflect on its use in boundary work interfacing governance, people and science. Agroforestry as applied science started with describing the worlds' farmed lands with trees' in their eco-geographical and socio-historical context as plot/farm-level agroforestry ('AF1'). title: Elite Capture and Control in Participatory Budgeting: Evidence from a Sri Lankan Municipality
abstract: This study aims to examine how elite capture and elite control shape PB practices in a Sri Lankan local government, with a focus on how accounting mediates these practices. In particular, this explores how political and administrative elites utilise the PB process to dominate in the field during their respective leadership periods. To achieve the study’s aims, a qualitative case study was conducted in a Sri Lankan municipality, one of the earliest adopters of PB in the country. Data were collected through 24 semi-structured interviews with elected and administrative officials, complemented by
journal: International Journal of Accounting and Business Finance

title: CS3D and private enforcement: the journey from international jurisdiction obstacles to the omnibus structural enforcement gap
abstract: This contribution traces the evolution of the CS3D’s private enforcement mechanism from the 2024 Directive to Omnibus I, focusing on how private international law rules have shaped its effectiveness. Under the 2024 framework, the Directive provided for overriding mandatory civil liability rules, but it did not ensure access to Member State courts. The paper argues that the EU principle of effectiveness supported an implicit forum legis—a lesson relevant for future EU instruments with lois de police. title: Filling the gaps in Australian angiosperm genomes
abstract: The Genomics for Australian Plants Initiative (GAP) reference genome project aimed to provide high quality angiosperm genomes for previously underrepresented taxonomic groups with evolutionary significance, cultural value, biogeographic importance, and concerning conservation status in Australia. Here we present the results of long-read genomic sequencing and assembly for 29 selected angiosperm species, including analyses of genome completeness, contiguity, ploidy, gene annotations, and repeat content. title: Understanding the Basic Concepts of International Law
abstract: International law is often described as a system lacking a legislature, a compulsory judiciary and a central enforcement authority. These institutional limitations have long prompted questions about its status as law. This article reviews the fundamental concepts that give the discipline its structure and coherence. Adopting a doctrinal and conceptual approach, it draws on principal treaties, the jurisprudence of the International Court of Justice and leading scholarship, while setting aside historical narrative and detailed institutional analysis. It examines the nature of international law,
journal: International Scholar Journal of Arts and Social Science Research

title: Canid’s cradle: multigrain den site selection by wolves on the Scandinavian Peninsula
abstract: Carnivores can have different habitat requirements and vary in their sensitivity to disturbance across stages of their life cycle, particularly during reproduction. Despite being highly adaptable and able to tolerate substantial human disturbance, wolves ( Canis lupus ), may rely on specific habitat characteristics when selecting den sites to reduce human-related risks and enhance pup survival. Using multi-grain resource selection functions (MRSFs), we evaluated resource selection at wolf den sites. title: Development of a Ready-to-Eat Puffed Snack from Salmon Skin Using a Multi-Stage Hot-Air and Microwave Drying Process
abstract: Creating puffed snacks from protein-rich byproducts like salmon skin poses challenges in balancing drying efficiency, energy consumption, and product quality. This research focused on developing a ready-to-eat puffed snack using salmon skin through a multi-stage drying technique. The process involved initially drying the skins with hot air at 90 °C, followed by microwave puffing, and then returning them to hot-air drying until the moisture content fell below 4% (d.b.). The study examined how varying microwave power and puffing duration influenced drying rates, product quality, and energy use.

Using a normative juridical approach, the study examines Law No. 1 of 2024, the second amendment to the ITE Law, and the Constitutional Court's decision. The findings show that the Court narrowed the interpretation of crimina

title: Los retos de los seguros paramétricos frente al cambio climático y el medio ambiente
abstract: What are the challenges facing parametric insurance in the context of climate change and the environment? From the perspective of insurance law and insurance technique, the article applies an analytical method and a review of Colombian agricultural policy wordings to examine the concept and legal regime of this modality, index design, climate uncertainty, accessibility, regulatory and litigation challenges, financial sustainability and the parametric claim. It finds that Law 2294 of 2023 integrated the modality into indemnity insurance, subject to the requirement of correlation between the ind

title: Stanislavsky and the Question of Truth
abstract: Konstantin Stanislavsky’s pursuit of truth in acting remains central to contemporary actor training, and this paper examines how his evolving understanding of truth can be read alongside wider philosophical and cultural debates of his time, particularly those concerning belief, authenticity, and the performer’s experience of the self as transformative. It explores Stanislavsky’s notion of truth in performance in relation to late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century discussions on embodied expression and the ethical dimensions of artistic practice. title: La criminalización de la pobreza: un enfoque desde la Criminología y el Derecho Penal
abstract: The criminalization of poverty raises questions about how socioeconomic conditions shape exposure to institutional control and the consequences of criminal justice involvement. This study aimed to analyze the normative, procedural, and sanctioning mechanisms associated with this relationship and their criminological and legal implications. A critical synthesis of recent empirical research was organized around three dimensions: coercive regulation of subsistence activities, inequalities during criminal proceedings, and the economic effects of sanctions. Findings identified interventions targeti
journal: Journal of Economic and Social Science Research

title: The Closure Problem in Discourse Ethics: Ecological Truth and the Limits of the Tripartite Model
abstract: ABSTRACT Discourse ethics rests on the assumption that validity claims fall into a closed triad: facts about the objective world, norms about the intersubjective world, and self‐expressions disclosing the subjective world. This paper challenges that assumption. I argue that the tripartite framework is not exhaustive, and that treating it as such generates a previously unrecognized form of exclusion: not at the level of access, power, or expression, but at the level of intelligibility itself. To make this case, I introduce “ecological truth” as a candidate for a distinct kind of validity claim.

title: Effect of a solar-powered spatial emanator on malaria prevalence in Uganda (Mossie-GO trial): A double-blinded, cluster-randomised, and placebo-controlled trial
abstract: The continued threat of malaria has driven investigations into the efficacy of a range of new tools, including spatial emanators which release active ingredients that can affect mosquito host-seeking vector behaviour and reduce human contact. This study aimed to estimate the effect of a novel solar-powered spatial emanator in reducing the prevalence of malaria in rural and peri-urban settings. The Mossie-GO trial was a prospective, cluster-randomised, controlled trial conducted in Jinja and Buikwe in Eastern Uganda. Fifty-six clusters were randomised at a 1:1 ratio to receive either the spatia
institutions: London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine

title: Sustainable Green Marketing as a Business Model
abstract: This paper seeks to investigate sustainable green marketing as a business model in the African context. Promoting products or services that are eco-friendly is called green marketing. It involves incorporating sustainable principles into various aspects of marketing. Broadly, the sustainable business principles include investing profits in renewable energy, responsible waste disposal practices and avoiding printed materials. journal: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)

title: Floristic Composition, Structure, and Regeneration Status of Wakani Forest in Guagusa Shikudad District, Awi Zone, Northwestern Ethiopia
abstract: Understanding the floristic status of remnant forests is essential for future forest management interventions. This study aimed to investigate the floristic composition, vegetation structure, and regeneration status of Wakani Forest in the Guagusa Shikudad District of Ethiopia. A systematic sampling method was employed to collect vegetation data along three transect lines across altitudinal gradients. In total, 63 main sample plots (20 x 20 m) were established. title: Una Reflexión Autoetnográfica desde el Análisis Político del Discurso
abstract: Este artículo presenta una reflexión docente autoetnográfica sobre la experiencia de enseñar español como lengua extranjera (ELE) en una Universidad Históricamente Afroamericana (HBCU) en los Estados Unidos, desde el Análisis Político del Discurso (APD). Se examinan cuatro incidentes críticos (clases cortas, ausencia de libro de texto, barreras lingüísticas e irrupción de la IA) que generaron una dislocación en las prácticas pedagógicas sedimentadas del facilitador. A través de un enfoque cualitativo basado en la autoetnografía, busco abrir un espacio de diálogo entre mi introspección docente
publisher: Universidad Autónoma del Estado de Hidalgo

title: The Political Economy Of Uneven Economic Development In South Asia: Structural Inequalities, Institutional Constraints, And Pathways To Inclusive Economic Growth
abstract: Despite being one the world’s fastest-growing economic regions, the South Asian region continues to experience substantial disparities in economic development. The developmental benefits are fragmented and unequally distributed across regions and social groups. The gap exists on four different levels: regional, social, political and opportunity. The region remains one of the least economically integrated regions. title: Supporting health system resilience capacities in fragile and shock-prone settings: A qualitative synthesis of six years of learning from the ReBUILD consortium
abstract: Conflicts, crises and chronic stressors such as climate change are growing threats to health systems, which has led to increased focus on the concept of resilience. However, while there is an expanding literature on resilience, it has largely focused on conceptualization and measurement, rather than on understanding how to support the development of resilience capacities. ReBUILD, a research consortium which operated in 2020-2026, focused on building empirical evidence on this topic in relation to fragile and shock-prone (FASP) settings, where this is most urgent, challenging and neglected. title: Problems of Developing the Securities Market in the Region
abstract: The article identifies and systematizes the obstacles that slow the development of the securities market in Uzbekistan and, in particular, in its peripheral regions, using the Republic of Karakalpakstan as the regional case. The study uses a mixed desk-based design: (i) a theory-grounded review of the finance–growth and law-and-finance literature; (ii) an indicator analysis of the four dimensions of financial-market development (depth, access, efficiency, stability) based on official and institutional data from the National Agency of Prospective Projects (NAPP), the National Statistics Committ
journal: American Journal of Economics and Business Management

title: UNBALANCED GOVERNANCE OF CLIMATE FUNDING INSTRUMENTS: A GLOBAL SOUTH PERSPECTIVE
abstract: This article examines how international climate finance governance reproduces structural inequalities between the Global North and South. It adopts a qualitative, critical and comparative approach, combining documentary analysis of major multilateral climate funds from 2015 to 2025 with multilevel governance theory, dependency theory and postcolonial perspectives. The analysis identifies restrictive accreditation requirements, unequal institutional capacities, the predominance of loans, geographical and sectoral concentration of resources, and the marginalization of local knowledge. title: Aprendizaje mediado como principio pedagógico en la enseñanza en Reclutamiento y Selección en Psicología
abstract: INTRODUCCIÓN. El artículo presenta una experiencia de aprendizaje mediado en la asignatura de Reclutamiento y Selección de la carrera de Psicología de una universidad del norte de Chile. La propuesta, basada en las dimensiones del perfil del profesorado mediador y en la teoría de la modificabilidad cognitiva estructural, busca favorecer aprendizajes significativos, reflexión ética y transferencia a contextos profesionales en una asignatura centrada en procesos técnicos. abstract: Since vocabulary plays a significant role in second language acquisition, expansive vocabulary targets should be set and pursued. This paper explores the results of introducing affixes to develop vocabulary and increase motivation for beginner to intermediate-level English language learners (ELLs) pursuing academic disciplines in law, science, and technology at a New York City community college. title: Becoming Edible: Lessons from a Jungle Cat in Luis Sepúlveda’s Un viejo que leía novelas de amor
abstract: The relationship between humans and animals in Western thought is defined by opposition. In an attempt to rethink this division, I read Luis Sepúlveda’s 1989 novella Un viejo que leía novelas de amor and find its undoing in the relational ontology of Amerindian perspectivism. The starring performance in the story belongs to an ocelot, and through her relentless hunt for men, she achieves the unlikely feat of simultaneously inviting her prey into something like a relationship. title: SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL AND MANAGEMENT IN THE LECTURE AREAS OF FEDERAL POLYTECHNIC BIDA, NIGERIA
abstract: Solid waste, a type of land pollution comprises of any discarded solid or semi-solid material resulting from anthropogenic and animal activities in households, industry, institutions, commercial establishments, and public spaces. The research aims to study solid wastes disposal and management in the lecture areas of the Federal Polytechnic, Bida. title: Adoption and Impact of Climate-Smart Technologies on Agrifood Systems in Vihiga County, Kenya
abstract: Agrifood systems in sub-Saharan Africa face significant challenges from climate change, threatening food security and rural livelihoods. Climate-smart technologies (CSTs) offer a viable way to strengthen resilience, productivity, and sustainability in smallholder farming systems. This study examines the adoption and impact of CSTs in Vihiga County, a high-potential agricultural region in western Kenya with small landholdings and high vulnerability to climate variability. title: Sustainability of Chandragiri Hills: An Application of the GSTC Attraction Standard
abstract: Nepal is rapidly growing its commercial tourism industry that apples continuous sustainability assessment to determine whether the large-scale tourism project potentially benefit the local communities economically along with protecting the environment. This research paper examines the sustainability of Chandragiri Hills, one of the best tourism destination with the infrastructure in Kathmandu Valley, applying the Global Sustainable Tourism Council (GSTC) attraction standard framework. abstract: This paper offers a comparative conceptual analysis of the expression bənê hā’ĕlōhîm (בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים, “Sons of God”) within Jewish theology and the Qur’ānic reference to ʿUzayr in verse Q 9:30. abstract: El trabajo analiza el tratamiento de los acuerdos de estandarización de la sostenibilidad entre empresas competidoras en las Directrices europeas sobre la aplicabilidad del artículo 101 del TFUE a los acuerdos de cooperación horizontal, de 21 de julio de 2023. title: Older adults’ intention to use extended reality in China’s Yellow River Basin: an extended Technology Acceptance Model with intergenerational support
abstract: As older adults become an important segment of China’s tourism market and family-based multigenerational travel becomes more prevalent, extended reality (XR)-enabled cultural heritage tourism raises a broader question about older adults’ access to technology-mediated cultural participation. Although XR may enrich cultural heritage tourism, older adults’ engagement with XR may be shaped by digital barriers and varying levels of family-based support. title: حقوق المرأة في جزر القمر بين التشريعات الدستورية والواقع الاجتماعي 2005 - 2018

abstract: Este artículo analiza la transformación del derecho probatorio en entornos digitales a partir de un fenómeno estructural aún insuficientemente atendido: la utilización jurídica de evidencias que no fueron producidas con finalidad probatoria. title: Elevating Indigenous Voices for a Just Energy Transition
abstract: In the face of an accelerating climate crisis and shifting geopolitical power balances, the world is pursuing a “green transition” in which electrification is central. Electrification demands critical raw materials, including rare earth elements, a large share of which lie beneath Indigenous lands. Although the UN affirms Indigenous peoples’ right to own, use, develop, and control their traditional lands, these rights are routinely overruled, including on “national security” grounds. title: The right to belong-childhood statelessness in Australia: international and domestic legal measures to reduce statelessness at birth
abstract: To be stateless—that is, without any legally recognised nationality—is a multi-faceted phenomenon impacting millions of children—including those born in Australia—worldwide. There has been little academic analysis of childhood statelessness, however, in Australia. Little is understood about statelessness within the Australian legal and policy sectors, and indeed, more broadly. Without nationality, stateless children can face difficulty in accessing essential human rights. abstract: Introduction: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease damaging the supportive structure of teeth. It has systemic impacts including cardiac autonomic dysfunction. Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures an objective analysis of the extent of autonomic regulation and where decreased parasympathetic activity coupled with increased sympathetic predominance was determined to correlate well with risk in cardiovascular events. title: From Pesticide Pollution to Healthy Soils: Policy Assessment and Reform Options in Germany
abstract: Soil pollution in the EU and Germany is a pressing environmental issue. Multiple stressors contribute to soil pollution, including the use of plant protection products (here: pesticides). Policy goals, however, demand that the EU and Germany protect biodiversity and soils. Against this background, the present article adopts a qualitative governance analysis to investigate the extent to which German pesticide policies contribute to reduced pesticide pollution risks as well as biodiversity and soil health goals. abstract: A prominent study of the founding journals of Chinese folkloristics after 1949 argued that Zhong Jingwen’s definition of folk literature as the “oral creation of the laboring people” served both to establish political legitimacy and to exclude traditional Chinese opera (xiqu 戏曲) and professional storytelling (shuochang 说唱) from the discipline. abstract: Structure models of sub-Neptunes commonly assume purely adiabatic interiors with distinct layers of homogeneous composition. We assess how allowing for more complex interiors with composition gradients affects the inferred internal structure and bulk compositions of the sub-Neptunes K2-18,b and TOI-270,d. abstract: Background: Black and Hispanic individuals may experience a disproportionate burden of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]-associated atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk, and ASCVD-related mortality, yet remain underrepresented in cardiovascular (CV) clinical trials. abstract: This article addresses the role of mechanics in facilitating time travel for players of strategy games, with a particular focus on games that address the Fall of Rome and a central case study around Total War: Attila. title: Stress Levels and Teaching Performance of Secondary English Teachers in Bantayan, Cebu Province
abstract: This study examined occupational stress and teaching performance among 100 secondary English teachers from 14 schools on Bantayan Island, Cebu Province, during the 2024-2025 academic year. title: Modernisation of the public management system in Ukraine
abstract: The existence of Ukraine as an independent subject in the international arena provides for a modern legal and democratic system of public management, which serves as the basis for the evolutionary transformation of socio-political relations in the period of post-war development of the state. abstract: The Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu is home to all six of the State's Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs): the Todas, Kotas, Kurumbas, Irulas, Paniyans and Kattunayakans. This paper examines these groups with special reference to the Kattunayakans, a forest-dwelling community concentrated in the Gudalur and Pandalur taluks along the Mudumalai forests. abstract: This paper offers a culturally oriented comparative reading of Nathaniel Hawthorne’s The Scarlet Letter (1850) and Lu Xun’s The New Year’s Sacrifice (1924) through Michel Foucault’s theory of heterotopia. abstract: The CGHAZ is the fundamental mechanical weak link of A514 high-strength steel welded joints. abstract: The present paper examines whether human rights due diligence (HRDD) litigation improves access to remedy for victims of cross-border corporate human rights violations by addressing the legal barriers traditionally associated with more general corporate human rights litigation. title: The Care-ful Work of Climate Litigation: A Study of Women Climate Defenders
abstract: Climate litigation, often led by women, requires demanding work with little acknowledgement or support. The article argues that this work is a form of caring labour aimed at reproducing human society as well as the environment within which we are enmeshed. Rethinking care as including the environment draws from Indigenous ideas of ‘care for Country’, ecofeminist conceptions of our relationality with the rest of nature, and some versions of social reproduction theory. abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for lithium-ion batteries has intensified the need for sustainable and resilient supply chains for battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM). This study presents a cradle-to-gate Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of three hard-rock spodumene-based LHM supply routes: the conventional Australian–Chinese route (BASE), integrated Australian production (I-AUS), and integrated European production in Finland (I-FIN). The Romanians steadily began a policy of assimilating the native population and colonization. abstract: El presente trabajo aborda las múltiples, poliédricas y caleidoscópicas vicisitudes de la aplicación de la regla lex rei sitae a la propiedad de los meteoritos. abstract: This article examines two phenomena that are usually treated separately, the leaking of internal deliberations and threats against the physical safety of judges, as symptoms of a single institutional transformation: the shift of the Supreme Court of the United States from the least visible branch of the federal government to a permanent object of political conflict. title: The impact of geographical and technological proximity on knowledge spillovers from formal standards
abstract: Abstract Proximity is traditionally viewed as crucial for overcoming the search and transfer costs associated with imperfectly codified knowledge. But does proximity still matter when formal standard publication jointly enhances the codification, certainty, and accessibility of technical knowledge? Evidence from the U.S. Information and Communication Technology industry shows that technological proximity drives substantial spillover gains, largely irrespective of location. abstract: La biometría se ha incorporado al transporte aéreo para acelerar la identificación de pasajeros y reforzar el control fronterizo. Cuando el rostro, la huella dactilar o el iris se convierten en credenciales de acceso, la seguridad entra en tensión con la vida privada y derechos fundamentales. Este artículo examina, con perspectiva jurídica transnacional, el marco normativo aplicable, OACI, RGPD y Convenio 108+, los riesgos del tratamiento masivo de datos biométricos y de la vigilancia indiscriminada, y los principios de proporcionalidad y minimización junto al Privacy by Design como parámetro

Specifically, it assessed internal strategic processes, external environmental influences, digital readiness, and the acceptability of a proposed user-friendly digital platform. abstract: Abstract Enforcement is crucial for ensuring compliance by regulated entities in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions trading systems (ETSs). abstract: En Argentina, el Lechuzón Negruzco (Asio stygius) ha sido considerado una especie muy rara y poco conocida. A partir de la recopilación de registros y de trabajo de campo, encontramos que su distribución en el noreste argentino es más amplia de lo que se suponía. abstract: Background: Health and disease are socially constructed phenomena, shaped by the interplay of knowledge and power that determines the distribution of social determinants of health. The underdevelopment of public health in Africa is rooted in both historical and contemporary injustices. Racist policies, founded on beliefs in racial and cultural superiority, established frameworks of moral inclusion and exclusion that designated African people as “outsiders” and subjected them to exploitation. abstract: Abstract Religious freedom is protected in both international human rights law (IHRL) and international humanitarian law (IHL), yet the interference with that freedom caused by the mishandling, concealment and improper disposal of human remains in armed conflict has remained largely under-examined in the jurisprudence of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights (IACtHR). abstract: Underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSNs) face critical challenges in energy imbalance, connectivity, and data collection due to harsh environments. To address these issues, this paper focuses on the problem is how to achieve energy-balanced data collection in IoT-enabled UWSNs with a mobility-aware mobile edge computing (MEC), named MECEBDC. abstract: Lévy walks are recognized by the histogram of their flight lengths, while the renewal hypothesis on which the textbook model rests, that every flight is drawn afresh, is seldom tested. abstract: Quantile-based summaries, such as prediction intervals and medians, are commonly used in economic forecasting, climate science, and public health. abstract: Minimum shipment quota regulations ensure that socially critical commodities are not excluded from capacity-constrained freight markets by profit-driven allocation. abstract: Advanced attitude determination and control (ADCS) techniques can be difficult for small satellite teams to adopt: tightly coupled implementations require substantial code changes to evaluate different actuators, sensors, orbits, mission goals, and control laws. Existing tools often emphasize orbit mechanics or flight software rather than closed-loop ADCS. abstract: Online path planning is a core capability of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). abstract: Up until the first decades of the twentieth century, settler Australians were predominantly an outward-looking people, physically and culturally orientated toward the coastal fringes of the continent. Meanwhile, the ‘unsettled’ arid interior remained problematic within the settler geographical imaginary. abstract: When and how the southeastern Tibetan Plateau attained high elevation remains debated, yet resolving this question is fundamental to understanding the Cenozoic growth of the Tibetan Plateau. abstract: Most decapod crustaceans undergo a brief prezoeal stage immediately after hatching, during which the body remains enclosed within a thin embryonic cuticle. title: L'Absolutisme du Pouvoir Sultanesque d'Anjouan (Comores) : Fondements, Structures, Manifestations et Crises d'un Modèle Monarchique (XVIIe - XIXe Siècles)
abstract: Cet article analyse la construction, le fonctionnement et la crise du sultanat d’Anjouan (Nzwani), dans l’archipel précolonial des Comores, du XVIIe au début du XXe siècle. Il montre qu’Anjouan se distingue de la Grande Comore, marquée par la fragmentation politique et les rivalités entre « sultans batailleurs », par la mise en place précoce d’un pouvoir monarchique relativement centralisé et d’un territoire politiquement unifié. title: PLASTIC POLLUTION: A GROWING THREAT TO ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY
abstract: Plastic pollution has become a major environmental challenge globally, posing significant threats to human health, wildlife, aquatic ecosystems, and the general environment. The widespread use of plastic products, particularly single-use plastics, coupled with inadequate waste management systems and poor enforcement of environmental laws, has contributed to the increasing accumulation of plastic waste in Nigeria. title: Tektite wear during transport in air or water after initial fallout: a contribution to resolving the “age paradox” of the Australasian strewn field
abstract: It is argued sometimes that tektites composing the Australasian strewn field, recovered from sedimentary associations at the surface of the Earth, are not found in their original position of deposition, but have been reworked and transported by geophysical flows away from the location on the Earth's surface where they were first deposited. title: Reidentification of Volutopsius hirasei and its implications for the taxonomy of the genera Fusivolutopsius and Habevolutopsius (Gastropoda: Buccinidae: Volutopsiinae)
abstract: The identity of Volutopsius hirasei Pilsbry, 1907, the type species of Fusivolutopsius Habe & Sato, 1973 and Habevolutopsius Kantor, 1983, has long been confused because of conflicting interpretations based on material from geographically disparate localities. In this study, the taxonomic identity of V. hirasei is clarified through examination of the holotype and newly obtained specimens from off northeastern Honshu (Sanriku), Japan, including waters in the vicinity of the type locality. title: Arctic guide’s mindset: enhancing safety competence development from the perspective of instructors
abstract: This study examined the importance of safety knowledge and competencies for adventure guides leading Arctic trips. Given the challenging environment, remoteness, and limited resources, guides must have skills to prevent and respond to accidents. The research critically assessed Arctic adventure guide training programs in Svalbard, Iceland, and Greenland by interviewing six instructors to explore how curricula develop safety competency. title: Tacit knowledge management of fisherfolk in developing countries: designing a framework from the sustainability perspective
abstract: Fisherfolk communities possess tacit knowledge that supports ecological decision-making, livelihoods, cultural continuity, and adaptation, yet this knowledge is increasingly vulnerable as intergenerational learning is disrupted by youth migration, changing livelihood aspirations, environmental change, and unequal access to technology. This study examines how fisherfolk in Bangladesh and Indonesia preserve, share, and adapt tacit knowledge and develops a sustainability-oriented Tacit Knowledge Management Framework grounded in their experiences. abstract: Scyphozoan jellyfish exhibit the highest locomotive efficiency in the animal kingdom, making them of particular interest in fluid dynamics and bioinspired robotics. Despite this, prevalent analytical models of jellyfish swimming have been based on the swimming traits of hydrozoan jellyfish, which utilize jet propulsion, rather than scyphozoan jellyfish, which utilize paddling propulsive methods. title: Microwear analysis on Pinctada margaritifera tattooing combs from Central East Polynesia
abstract: Pearl shell tattooing combs form a small corpus in the material culture in Central East Polynesia, providing evidence for traditional methods of tattooing and body modification, and represent a significant form of cultural practice in ancient island communities. Three combs were analysed with microwear analysis, shedding light on manufacturing techniques and use, with an additional four combs analysed macroscopically. abstract: Introduction: Over 200 million people live at altitudes exceeding 2500 m above sea level and commercial aircraft cabins are routinely pressurized to equivalent altitudes of 1800-2500 m (Debenham et al., 2021). It is important to understand how reduced blood oxygenation impairs standing balance control for everyday functional safety. title: Maritime masculinity as the ‘common sense’
abstract: Abstract This article advances a new conceptualisation of maritime masculinity by arguing that it constitutes a distinct configuration of hegemonic masculinity operating through sexual hegemony. While the maritime industry has long been recognised as one of the world’s most masculinised sectors, existing scholarship has largely understood masculinity as an occupational identity or cultural characteristic. title: Scaling and trade-offs in multi-agent autonomous systems
abstract: Designing autonomous drone swarms is hampered by a vast design space spanning platform, algorithmic, and numerical-strength choices. We perform large-scale agent-based simulations in three canonical scenarios: swarm-on-swarm battle, cooperative area search with attrition, and pursuit of scattering targets. title: Technology Choice in Warrau Canoe Culture: An Ethnographic Case Study
abstract: Abstract Technology is selected at the societal level based on both functionally adaptive and socially meaningful considerations. Although the semiotic component of technology choice is frequently recognised in anthropological discourse, it tends to be ignored in ethnographic accounts of technology change in a maritime context, where change in nautical technology is usually interpreted in purely adaptive terms. This article uses a case study approach to explore both adaptive and nonadaptive factors influencing technology choices in the largely traditional maritime society of Imbotero, Guyana.

abstract: The Greater Male Region, (consist of Male, Hulhule, Hulhumale, Villingili, Gulhifalhu and Thilafushi) is the most densely populated urban cluster in the Maldives. Capital City Male' is one of the most densely populated City in the world. abstract: Water-based recreational activities, particularly paddlesports, have experienced significant growth since the COVID-19 pandemic due to their physical health benefits and alignment with social distancing practices. This study focuses on flatwater paddling in the southeastern United States and seeks to inform destination development strategies by examining how paddlers' needs, motivations, and spending behaviors differ across skill levels. abstract: To address navigation accuracy degradation caused by error accumulation in traditional Strapdown Inertial Navigation Systems (SINS), this paper systematically investigates error state representation and analysis methods for SINS in the earth-centered earth-fixed (ECEF) frame based on Lie group theory. title: Floristic composition and diversity of bryophytes along an elevation gradient in Kailali, Far West Nepal
abstract: Bryophytes were the first plants to colonize land. They are the most diverse group after angiosperms, but are a neglected group due to their small size. In Nepal, bryophyte-related studies have largely been confined to eastern and Central regions. Moreover, research focusing on species richness patterns and associated ecological parameters remains limited. To address these gaps, the present study employed a systematic random sampling method. abstract: The stratigraphy of a 91 m cored borehole through the White Chalk Subgroup, drilled at Cosham, Hampshire, on the Portsdown Anticline, is described in detail. title: A historical review of translocations of native bird species in Australia: the good, the bad and the perverse
abstract: The Australian bird fauna has undergone many changes since European colonisation in 1788. This review focuses on the role of translocations in these changes. Translocations began in the 1830s and have been undertaken for reasons that have varied over time. Many early translocations were done for utilitarian reasons, as foibles, or were the result of aviary escapes or release of captive birds. abstract: Insurance policy denotes a document containing details and terms of an insurance contract between the insurer and insured. It is an instrument in writing, by which one party (insurer) in consideration of premium paid, engages to indemnify another party (insured) against a contingent loss, by making payment in compensation whenever the event insured against happens. abstract: This paper examines Camus’s 1942 novel The Outsider through Sartre’s theory of existence. Although Camus resisted the existentialist label and took care to separate his philosophy of the Absurd from Sartre’s thought, The Outsider works as a compelling illustration of Sartrean ideas in practice. abstract: Global trade and migration have facilitated the arrival of alien species within new ecosystems. Alien species that become invasive constitute a major driver of biodiversity loss. abstract: In this study, 740 samples collected from the provinces of Ağrı, Ardahan, Iğdır, and Kars during the periods 2016–2017 and 2021–2023 were examined, and a total of 29 species belonging to the subfamilies Chrysomelinae, Cassidinae, and Eumolpinae (Chrysomelidae) were identified. abstract: In this article, we examine teaching and learning with underrepresented international students in a postgraduate outdoor environmental education (OEE) programme in England. abstract: Purpose: This study examines the decline of matriarchal governance in precolonial kingdoms of the Gambia Valley region within Greater Senegambia. abstract: Abstract Tropical forests contain approximately 60% of the biosphere’s carbon stocks, making their biomass a crucial buffer against anthropogenic carbon emissions. This study assessed biomass and carbon stocks in two vegetation types within the Amanã Sustainable Development Reserve, Central Amazon. Four permanent 1-ha plots were established, with two plots in each environment: Igapó and Paleovárzea. abstract: This essay examines Mario Cruz’s playwriting from the 1960s to the 1990s, situated at the intersection of theater, journalism, and mass culture. Through works such as Un cesante honorable, El extraño (1975), and Pablo y Alicia son novios (1994), along with his novel El Príncipe (1972), the study explores how his theater engages with popular culture, melodrama, and an aesthetics of excess. abstract: This paper focuses on how the American comics anthology Gay Comix, which ran for 26 issues from 1980 to 1998, addressed the AIDS crisis. Gay male comics had historically focused on casual sexual relationships; however, the epidemic complicated gay men’s relationship with sex, rendering these strips “bad taste.” At the same time, because gay cartooning was associated with humor, it was also considered “bad taste” to depict the crisis in this medium. abstract: Abstract: Developing a decolonized Greenlandic identity entails challenging colonial categories and fostering complex, inclusive national identities. While Greenlandic is not in immediate danger of extinction, its marginalization in professional, technical, and high-level administrative, or educational contexts poses a long-term threat to its status as a fully functional, modern language. abstract: Religion is known to be one of the common factors of conflicts in contemporary world. The introduction of religious sects and denominations in many parts of Nigeria compounded the causes of conflicts that trickled down to Goemailand and become one of the major problems that is bedeviling the area. title: Disasters and interstate conflict: Greek–Turkish relations after the 2023 earthquakes
abstract: How do disasters affect interstate conflict? Existing perspectives on this question propose conflict-reducing or conflict-inducing effects, attribute these effects to different theoretical mechanisms and implicitly study either short- or medium- to long-term post-disaster periods. We focus on the Greek-Turkish rivalry dyad, and the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes, to collect, develop observable implications for and test these competing perspectives.
