title: The Articulation Loop: State Signaling, Platform Infrastructures, and User Weaponization in China's Qinglang Era
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines how Qinglang (Clear and Bright), China's campaign‐based discourse of internet content governance, sustains regulatory force as its meaning shifts across state, platform, and user domains. It develops the articulation loop as a mechanism for explaining how a state‐authored yet semantically open signifier acquires practical force through its connections to institutional authority, platform governance infrastructures, organized user practices, and selective regulatory recalibration. title: India-Pakistan Nuclear race and its Impacts on Regional Security (1998-2022)
abstract: India-Pakistan nuclear competition has been a defining element of South Asian geopolitics, influencing regional security dynamics. Using the conceptual frameworks of the balance of power, deterrence, mutual assure destruction and security dilemma, this study focuses on the India-Pakistan nuclear race and its impacts for regional security. The research attempts to give a comprehensive explanation of how the security dilemma and deterrence theory contribute to shaping the region's stability and instability by examining the relationships between these two nuclear powers. title: Tracing the Evolution of Anti-Kremlin Communication and Audience Engagement on Telegram During the Russia–Ukraine Conflict
abstract: During Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Telegram became an important platform for both state-aligned communication and opposition-oriented discourse. Over time, anti-Kremlin Telegram channels emerged as prominent venues for dissent amid increasing restrictions on independent political expression. This study examines how anti-Kremlin communication and audience engagement evolved across seven phases of the conflict. abstract: This article explains Equatorial Guinea’s movement from late colonial institutional shallowness to resource authoritarianism, understood as rents enlarging executive fiscal, infrastructural and diplomatic capacity while limiting accountability. It advances a pre-rent state fragility thesis: oil did not create the state-formation problem, but reorganized weaknesses produced by Spanish colonial underdevelopment, compressed decolonization and the Macías-era collapse. title: Studies on the Balkan Lepidoptera III
abstract: New and interesting records of Balkan Lepidoptera are detailed. Aphelia stigmatana (Eversmann, 1844) is new for the Balkan fauna; for Holoterpna pruinosata (Staudinger, 1897) the third contemporary locality in Europe and the Balkan Peninsula is reported. title: Ecology of large cavities in trees: a review
abstract: Abstract Large tree-cavities (LTC) are conspicuous structures with specific ecological functions in large trees. We summarize the distribution, dynamics, ecological roles and conservation issues of LTC based on nearly 370 sources where these could be distinguished (based on entrances ca. 9 cm wide or larger). Large live broadleaved trees provide most LTC; live conifers and snags have importance in certain ecosystems. abstract: This paper examines the reception of the campaign of Alexander Ypsilantis and the Greek Revolution (1821–1829) in Serbia based on Serbian archival material, primarily unpublished and published documents preserved in the Archives of Serbia and the Archives of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts in Belgrade. title: Modelling symbols among the first-sedentary communities: Emergence of clay figurines in Epipaleolithic Southwest Asia
abstract: The emergence of clay technologies and their use in symbolic practices marks a momentous techno-symbolic innovation for human societies. While in North Africa, Europe and East Asia, this innovation was sporadically attested during the Upper Palaeolithic, in Southwest Asia, it has been commonly believed to emerge in full much later, as one of the innovations associated with Neolithic agricultural societies. title: Mithras, Magic and Appropriations in Roman Religion. An Interview with Richard L. Gordon
abstract: Richard L. Gordon (b. 1943) is a distinguished scholar of ancient religion and magic, with a particular focus on the Roman world. Over the course of a scholarly career spanning more than half a century, his work has left a lasting mark on the study of the Roman cult of Mithras, the sociology of Roman religion, and, especially, the historiography and study of magic in the ancient Greek and Roman worlds. abstract: Abstract The claim that Europe is strategically weak and incapable of defending itself, as most recently articulated by US President Donald Trump, has become a recurring feature of transatlantic political discourse in recent years. This article argues that Europe’s perceived weakness is not primarily the result of political complacency or strategic irresponsibility but rather the cumulative outcome of deliberate legal, institutional, and normative constraints embedded in the post–WWII security order. abstract: Coordinating autonomous underwater vehicles requires translating operator intent into feasible assignments while preserving autonomous execution when communication is limited. We present a hierarchical framework that couples Large Language Model (LLM) interpretation of natural-language mission instructions with Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and distributed Behaviour Tree (BT) execution. title: Reliability-Adaptive Multimodal Relative Pose Tracking for Underwater Leader-Follower Robots
abstract: Underwater leader-follower formation control requires continuous relative-pose estimation despite degraded sensing conditions and limited onboard computation. This paper presents a reliability-adaptive multimodal perception framework for six-degree-of-freedom relative-pose tracking between two moving underwater robots. title: TriMedium: A Cross-Medium Simulator for Embodied Networking Across Air-Ground-Sea
abstract: Embodied intelligent applications have expanded from air and ground into maritime environments, where missions such as coastal reporting require coordination among underwater sensing, surface gateways, and aerial relays. Yet field trials remain costly, and existing simulation tools make it difficult to study how cross-medium communication affects cooperation among these platforms. abstract: Small, holonomic Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) enable close-range inspection of underwater structures from arbitrary viewpoints, requiring accurate position and attitude tracking under state and input constraints. Model Predictive Contouring Control (MPCC) naturally handles these requirements, but relies on an accurate dynamics model, which is difficult to obtain underwater. abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite networks are reshaping maritime connectivity, offering much lower latency and higher capacity than traditional geostationary (GEO) links. As a single user terminal (UT) cannot serve hundreds to thousands of passengers, a cruise ship often deploys several UTs behind an onboard multi-WAN router for aggregated capacity and load balancing. abstract: Fish stock assessments need fish lengths paired with species from far more places than trained surveyors can reach. Recreationaldivers already visit many of those places, but measuring a fish underwater has required trained observers or specialist equipment.We present FishSense Lite, which recovers fish length from a single photograph taken with a recreational dive camera, a dive laserpointer, and a 3D-printed mount. title: Fractional Orbital Bombardment Systems
abstract: We analyze Fractional Orbital Bombardment Systems (FOBS) as a means of delivering nuclear weapons by placing warheads into partial orbits around the Earth, and show that they do not represent a game-changing advance in technology or capability. We consider potential uses of such a weapon, including evading missile defenses and delivering attacks with short warning time. FOBS could underfly current exoatmospheric defenses, but the required payload reduction may not justify its use if other countermeasures are deemed effective. abstract: Circumnavigating a stationary target with a team of robots requires each robot to hold its own standoff distance, to stay evenly spaced from its neighbours, and to avoid collisions with the target and with each other at every instant. The task becomes arduous when the robots are assigned different orbital radii, as their sensors or roles may demand. This paper presents a safety-critical control framework for this problem. abstract: This paper studies the problem of guiding an agent to localize and circumnavigate a stationary target at a prescribed radius using bearing measurements. Direct implementation of a classical scalar signed-distance estimator requires explicit evaluation of bearing rate signals that can be difficult to obtain in practice. title: Uncovering the seasonal trends of VOC production from ozonolysis of seawater
abstract: Large uncertainty exists in the role that the ocean plays as a net source for atmospheric volatile organic carbon (VOC) compounds, in part because of poorly quantified processes near the air–sea interface. Laboratory studies imply that heterogeneous reactions of ozone at the ocean surface may be a key source of VOCs to the marine atmosphere, but the representativeness of such experiments for the chemically complex surface ocean waters is unclear due to limited field evidence. title: Pharmaceutical Industry Pay‐Per‐Click Advertising Strategies to Influence Public Opinions on Drug Pricing
abstract: This analysis characterizes the magnitude, timing, and keyword targeting strategies of the Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America's (PhRMA) pay-per-click advertising expenditures and their relation to major drug pricing policy developments (2019-2025). Pay-per-click advertising allows advertisers to purchase prominent placement in search engine results, allowing their content to appear above organic results when users search for specific terms. title: Seawater Desalination in the Middle East and North Africa: Environmental Impacts of Brine Discharge, Energy Use and Pathways to Sustainable Expansion in Egypt
abstract: Desalination has become indispensable to water security in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), which produces almost half of the world's desalinated water. Egypt, facing a widening gap between Nile supply and demand, plans to expand seawater desalination from about 1.2–1.4 million m³ per day today to several million m³ per day within a decade. This review synthesises evidence on the environmental impacts of desalination, with emphasis on brine discharge, chemical additives, intake effects and energy use, and on management options relevant to Egypt's Mediterranean and Red Sea coasts. abstract: In this article, the author endeavors to explain the role of Antarctica in stabilizing sea ice & current, environmental protection and biodiversity in the polar region as well as in the global climate scenario. Due to global warming Antarctica’s ice sheets are melting at higher rate which has alarmed the planet. The paper studied the causes of melting of Antarctica and its successive impacts on sustainable development goals, environmental damages, and existence of coastal regions of Antarctica and its habitats. title: Mosaics with Marine Representations from the Archives of Rome: Revisions and Updates
abstract: Numerous documents, sketches, drawings, and photographs are preserved in the Archives of Rome, depicting archaeological discoveries made during excavations carried out between the late 1800s and the early decades of the 1900s, as part of the urban development of Rome, the capital of Italy. title: Coordinated Scheduling of Hydrogen Production and Flexible Loads in Offshore Wind-Powered Underwater Data Centers
abstract: Offshore wind-powered hydrogen production is increasingly recognized as an effective pathway for improving renewable energy utilization and facilitating the decarbonization of energy systems. abstract: This study examines people-place relationships in shallow bays on the Swedish Baltic Sea coast prior to ecological restoration. title: Estimation of body-mass distributions of Carboniferous tetrapod communities and comparison with modern coastal tropical wetlands
abstract: Abstract Coastal tropical wetlands have seen substantial change over the course of Earth’s history. Examining what commonalities lie between ancient tropical wetlands and their modern counterparts allows us to better understand the ecological building blocks foundational to their functioning. We evaluate the similarity of modern and Pennsylvanian tetrapod community structures from coastal tropical wetlands through the lens of body-mass distributions. title: ROCK ART ON THE ATACAMA DESERT COAST (NORTHERN CHILE): ITINERANCIES AND PRE-HISTORY
abstract: The rock art of the Atacama Desert coast (northern Chile) has not been thoroughly investigated. Only a few reports have illustrated the presence of this archaeological evidence on the coast. Because of this, very little progress has been made regarding its spatial distribution, formal variability, and chronology. In this article, we offer a summary of our research, which contributes to a first general picture of coastal rock art. title: Oceanographic Variability Constrains Recovery of Overexploited Cod and Haddock on the Faroe Bank: Evidence for Environmental Recovery Windows at Low Stock Size
abstract: ABSTRACT In a changing global ocean certain fish populations are approaching the upper limits of their thermal tolerance. Understanding how a warming climate and plankton dynamics affect stock recovery is thus a central challenge for fisheries management. This research investigates the preparedness of Village Red and White Cooperatives (Koperasi Desa/Kelurahan Merah Putih—KDMP) in Indonesia's coastal regions by assessing the disparity between their legal establishment and functional capacity. abstract: Understanding genetic diversity and structure in natural populations is important for conservation and developing resilience into restored populations for the future. Populations at the lower latitude (or northern) range edges tend to have lower levels of genetic diversity and are poorly connected, although they may be locally adapted to warmer environments. abstract: Abstract The long-term utilisation of marine sediment microbial fuel cells (MSMFCs) faces the challenges of diminished power output and the ambiguous diffusion mechanism of dissolved organic carbon (DOC). Here, a regulation strategy for enhancing MSMFCs performance by adding humic acid (HA) is proposed. abstract: This literature review provides an integrated analysis of the environmental, social, economic, and political impacts of sand extraction in the Wouri Estuary, Cameroon. Its objective is to understand how this activity transforms estuarine territories and to what extent current local governance mechanisms can sustainably regulate this resource. abstract: The Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor (GLP-1R) is a validated diabetes and obesity target, yet challenges with current peptide agonists necessitate orally bioavailable small-molecule alternatives. Marine natural products (MNPs) offer a structurally diverse reservoir for discovering such compounds for nutraceutical use. abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an emerging global health concern that demands the identification of novel drug targets and bioactive molecules to combat resistant bacterial pathogens. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are now among the most pervasive contaminants of global water bodies, driven by large-scale plastic mismanagement and industrial discharge. In Africa, MPs have been repeatedly detected in fish tissue, sediment, and surface water, most extensively in Nigeria and South Africa, yet the biochemical and molecular consequences of this contamination remain far less studied than its occurrence. title: Reactivating Turkey’s Erotica Archives on Netflix: Feminist Reparative Fabulation and Its Ambivalences in Erşan Kuneri
abstract: Streaming platforms offer cultural producers in right-wing populist regimes a paradoxical space that enables aesthetic experimentation and political critique within commercial and ideological limits. Combining archival research and close reading, this essay examines these dynamics through the Turkish Netflix original Erşan Kuneri (2022–2024). abstract: Mangrove restoration is essential for recovering the ecological functionality of degraded estuaries and reestablishing processes associated with coastal dynamics. Although these ecosystems are naturally adapted to salinity variations, changes in hydrological connectivity, such as water retention and reduced circulation, can compromise vegetation regeneration and the structure of aquatic communities. abstract: Tamarix chinensis , renowned for its extreme salt tolerance, is widely planted in the Yellow River Delta for ecological restoration, yet its salt reduction pathway and synergistic carbon sequestration mechanism remain poorly understood. Based on 7-year in-situ positioning experiments across lightly and heavily saline soils, we found that planting T. chinensis increased soil macroaggregate content by 140% and alkaline hydrolyzable nitrogen by 108%, while electrical conductivity decreased by 70% and Na + concentration by 77%. The development of cataracts is attributed to nutritional deficiencies, trauma, age, inadequate access to shade, and/or genetic risk factors. abstract: Coastal beach sports serve as an efficient method to rejuvenate fishing villages and develop local cultural tourism. By taking the case of beach sports activities organized by teenagers in Tanmen Town, Hainan as an example, this paper explores the process of organizing the activity in a period of seven days. abstract: This article examines the species composition, spatial distribution, habitat characteristics, and conservation of mammals found within the Aralkum National Nature Park. The study is based on monitoring surveys conducted in 2025 and data from the State Cadastre of Wildlife. We examined soils at five sites along the brackish‐to‐freshwater Elbe estuary, spanning salinity, inundation, and vertical redox gradients, to assess how operationally defined reactive Fe pools covary with soil organic carbon (SOC). abstract: This study aims to comprehensively analyze the multifaceted impact of PT Huady Nickel-Alloy's operations on the socio-economic conditions of the local community in Papan Loe Village, Bantaeng Regency. As industrialization increasingly penetrates rural territories, understanding its localized effects becomes crucial. abstract: Background: Sofifi Port is an important logistics distribution hub for the capital of North Maluku Province, but its service performance has not fully kept pace with increasing vessel traffic and cargo volumes. Objective: This study evaluates the optimization of cargo-handling services at Sofifi Port and formulates a phased development strategy through 2030. abstract: Coastal areas in Benin are facing increasing environmental pressure due to intensified human activities and the effects of climate change. The degradation of mangroves, coastal erosion, uncontrolled sand extraction, and water pollution are severely undermining biodiversity and essential ecosystem services. These disruptions directly impact the livelihoods of local communities who depend on fishing, agriculture, and aquaculture, while also exacerbating conflicts over resource use and food insecurity. title: Reflections, perceptions and practices of spearfishing among Ulithian communities
abstract: Abstract Spearfishing is a common and effective subsistence fishing method in coral reef‐dependent communities. Although its ecological impacts have been widely studied, spearfishing's sociocultural dimensions have received less attention despite its direct impacts on both reef and reef‐dependent communities. title: Maritime Chokepoints and the Fragility of Global Economic Security
abstract: Maritime chokepoints stand in a paradoxical position in the international legal order. On one hand they constitute indispensable arteries of global trade, and on the other hand their security depends upon a fragmented arrangement of coastal sovereignty along with war-laden navigational freedoms, disconnected collective security mechanisms and patchy private commercial decisions. The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) protects transit passage through the international straits. abstract: This study examines the development of cinchona cultivation and the monopoly of cinchona trade in Kediri, East Java, from 1830 to 1942, focusing on colonial economic policies, private investment, and plantation labour. abstract: Abstract Seafood is increasingly important for healthy dietary transitions in modern urban lifestyles. Yet, the patterns of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions remain poorly understood, which hinders the low-carbon pathways for city-specific seafood supply chains. Here, we constructed a disaggregated supply chain dataset to quantify the GHG footprint of consumption of five major seafood categories across 313 Chinese cities. abstract: The West African bloody cockle, Senilia senilis , is a saline-wetland bivalve of high ecological and socio-economic importance, distributed along the West African coastline from Rio de Oro (Western Sahara) to Angola. For centuries, the species has supported coastal livelihoods by providing food and income, particularly for women and young people. abstract: We present a georeferenced dataset of freshwater Malacostraca occurrences across continental Chile, compiled from published literature, technical reports and field studies. The dataset includes 625 occurrence records from 38 species across five families, covering a wide latitudinal gradient (~ 18°S to ~ 56°S). Community-based conservation (CBC) acts as a valuable complementary area-based conservation measure; yet few integrated domestic case studies combine ecological field monitoring with quantitative social–ecological assessment. abstract: How the life of prehistoric people was influenced by climate change and extreme events often remains elusive. abstract: Amidst the Cold War in the world and the national liberation movement in Vietnam, the 1954 Geneva Accords resulted in the temporary division of Vietnam and imposed an urgent mandate for troop regroupment. abstract: Abstract The main threat to New Zealand dolphins is entanglement in fishing nets. We developed an agent‐based model (ABM) to assess how area‐based controls on fishing methods can reduce fishing mortality and population declines. The model incorporates the behavior and distributions of dolphins and fishing vessels, and realistic displacement of fishing effort when protection is extended. title: Choosing the Right LCA Methodology for Sustainable Beverage Production
abstract: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is widely used to evaluate and reduce the environmental impact of products and industrial systems. In the beverage industry, which relies heavily on packaging materials, energy, and water resources, selecting an appropriate LCA methodology is essential for achieving sustainability goals in the industry. This review analyzes the major LCA approaches used in beverage production, including cradle‑to‑grave, cradle‑to‑gate, gate‑to‑gate, cradle‑to‑use, and end‑of‑life assessments. abstract: Declining soil fertility remains a major cause of reduced crop production among smallholder farmers in sub-Saharan Africa. abstract: Abstract The Great Unconformity marks a globally extensive erosive surface linked to climatic shifts 1 and environmental transitions 2 that preceded the Cambrian explosion of life. abstract: Abstract Although the characteristics of a region or site can have a large effect on the implications of climate change on wildfire risk, the associated causal relationships are poorly understood. abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are contaminants associated with anthropogenic activities. Objective: To map primary field studies of effluent-affected rivers by region, sampled compartment and pollutant group, with particular attention to the Barnoi River near Rajshahi. abstract: Abstract Wetlands are among the most threatened ecosystems worldwide, facing pressure from land-use change, hydrological alterations, and biological invasions. Historical vegetation records provide a valuable resource for assessing long-term changes in these environments. abstract: Light is a fundamental environmental cue influencing movement, habitat selection, and aggregation in aquatic organisms. abstract: In stratified turbulent flows such as the ocean, layered features (in which well-mixed regions of fluid are separated by sharp interfaces where the density varies rapidly) are a common occurrence. abstract: This paper explores climate change-driven housing insecurity by focusing on unstable foundations. abstract: Behrouz Boochani’s No Friend but the Mountains creates a musical and ecological relationship between death, detention, and nature. Written from inside Australia’s Manus Island prison for migrants seeking asylum, Boochani’s poetic prose renders nature not as backdrop but as witness, accomplice, and mourner. Birds, trees, insects, and the ocean form a chorus of protest, echoing the screams, scars, and rhythms of imprisoned life. Using motifs like the Chauka bird and the musical cadence of the dhol, Boochani’s place-based narrative is attuned to ecological temporality and trans-species mourning.

abstract: ABSTRACT Behavioural plasticity is considered highly relevant for biological invasions. As daily behavioural rhythmicity is plastic in response to environmental factors, we suggest that it may also be worth considering in the context of invasion success. abstract: Lactogenic insufficiency is a multifactorial condition of inadequate breast milk production that challenges successful breastfeeding and infant nutrition. Galactogogues include pharmaceutical agents, herbal medicines, nutritional supplements, and other natural bioactives, which are widely used to enhance lactation; however, their clinical utility varies. title: Threads of Evidence: The 1928 Hurricane Victims and Ways of Knowing Them
abstract: ABSTRACT In this article, the authors consider how two poorly preserved sets of skeletal remains can help us reflect on our molecular methods in bioarchaeology. These two skeletons are labeled as having come from the 1928 hurricane that hit Lake Okeechobee in Palm Beach County, Florida, drowning 2000–3000 people overnight in floodwaters from the lake. abstract: Introduction. Lipid complexes (LCs) from Barents Sea brown algae are a valuable source of biologically active compounds for the pharmaceutical industry. abstract: Abstract Multi‐ethnic party systems, which are mainly composed of multi‐ethnic parties, face a distinctive form of the “exclusion‐amid‐inclusion” problem. abstract: This article analyzes the activity of Major General A. B. Buturlin in administering the Derbent garrison in 1732–1733. abstract: Abstract In the interwar period, many industrializing states raised labor standards, introduced worker protections, and established deliberative labor institutions. Iran stands out as a remarkable outlier in this early wave of labor policy. Despite founding membership in the International Labour Organization (ILO), Iran kept labor protections at a bare minimum and workers excluded from decision-making processes altogether. abstract: This article theorizes how distinct world-making projects intersect and come into tension with each other through extended urbanization. It draws on archival and field research on the remnants of the Port Hedland immigration detention center in the Pilbara region of Western Australia. Port Hedland is geopolitically significant as the site of one of the first detention centers opened when mandatory immigration detention was introduced for irregular boat arrivals in the 1990s. abstract: Traditional linguistic landscape research largely concentrates on the semiotic analysis of physical signage, while dynamic digital linguistic symbols generated by large language models remain understudied. abstract: This article examines two distinct, and often intertwined, ways in which education produces hate. abstract: Abstract Synthetic dyes represent a category of organic compounds that are highly stable, durable, and often resistant to degradation through natural processes. abstract: The emergence of the blue humanities has encouraged a shift from predominantly terrestrial approaches to the study of human and nonhuman relations by foregrounding the cultural, material, and ecological significance of water. abstract: Two cornulitid species are described herein from the Late Ordovician of Spain. abstract: Abstract When anthropogenic CO 2 emissions cease, global temperature does not stabilize immediately. abstract: Vibrio harveyi is one of the major bacterial pathogens causing vibriosis in shrimp aquaculture, leading to significant reductions in production and economic losses. This study aimed to molecularly identify a mangrove sediment-associated fungal isolate and evaluate its antibacterial activity against V. harveyi. The research was conducted experimentally through molecular identification using ITS1 and ITS4 primers, phylogenetic analysis, and antibacterial activity assessment using the agar plug method. title: Mechanistic Characterization of a Bacterial Terpene Synthase That Bifurcates to Produce Both 6/10- and 5/11-Bicyclic Diterpenes
abstract: Abstract The mechanism of the bacterial diterpene synthase ChtS from Chitinophaga japonensis was investigated. ChtS was found to produce two major diterpenes, 5/11-bicyclic chitino-2,5,9-triene (11), and the previously uncharacterized 6/10-bicyclic chitinoeunicellene (12). Deuterium labeling experiments, site-directed mutagenesis, and isolation of minor products cembrene C (13), cembrene A (14), and chitinol (15) support initial 1,14-cyclization, two sequential 1,2-hydride shifts, prior to bifurcation to 11 or 12, ultimately retaining the E-configured C-2/C-3 alkene.

title: Assessment of the impact of handling time on blood parameters in healthy Grand Cayman blue iguanas (Cyclura lewisi)
abstract: Intensive captive breeding, head starting, reintroduction, individual and population health monitoring, and habitat protection for the past 20 years are credited for the ongoing recovery of the endangered Grand Cayman blue iguana (Cyclura lewisi). Comprehensive health assessments ensure only healthy animals are released, minimize the risk of inadvertent introduction of pathogens into free-ranging populations, and establish baseline health parameters for future reference and disease surveillance. title: Indigenous Diplomacy and Colonial Entanglement Through the Native Institution of New South Wales
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines the Native Institution, the first residential school for Aboriginal children in the British colony of New South Wales. It is well known and recognised as an early example of institutional child removal and assimilationist ideas that would later be known in Australia as the Stolen Generations. Yet, the Native Institution was also short‐lived. In colonial terms, it ‘failed’, as it could neither attract enough voluntary submission of children—nor retain them. This article looks again at the Native Institution to consider it through Indigenous practices of diplomacy

title: Emplacement of volcaniclastic mass flows during the 2023 eruption of Shishaldin Volcano, Alaska
abstract: Abstract Eruption-caused volcaniclastic mass flows were a significant feature of the four-month-long 2023 eruption of Shishaldin Volcano in Alaska. The volcano supports a nearly continuous cover of glacier ice and snow on the flanks of its upper edifice, and the emplacement of pyroclastic density currents over this snow and ice cover led to the generation of meltwater and lahars. Pyroclastic density currents that formed during the eruption were long and narrow in map view and did not develop marginal levees. title: Acid rock drainage caused by hydronium-bearing and Fe-deficient jarosite: An example from Lillesand, southern Norway
abstract: Acid rock drainage (ARD) represents a serious environmental concern due to potentially extreme lowering of pH and mobilisation of toxic metals. The present paper focusses on S-bearing gneisses in the Lillesand district in Norway based on 20 years of experience and research in the area. These Precambrian gneisses were affected by later extensive alterations involving hydrous sulphates. title: Relationships between landscape and the incidence of microplastics in fish: the case of a highly urbanized basin
abstract: The intensification of human activities has increased microplastic contamination in freshwater ecosystems, particularly affecting fish. This study evaluated the presence of microplastics in the stomachs and gills of 217 individuals belonging to 18 species, sampled across 16 sites in the Sorocaba River Basin. The overall mean was 0.05 microplastics per gram of fish, with a predominance of larger particles, fibers, and black coloration. title: Allometric growth of swimming-associated elements in Short-finnedpilot whales Globicephala macrorhynchus Gray 1846 (Cetacea: Delphinidae)
abstract: Ongoing research on cetaceans is revealing species-specific traits that reflect adaptations to different environmental conditions. Short-finned pilot whales are no exception to this trend. This species exhibits a specific diving behaviour, characterized by short bursts of acceleration at great depths, which likely necessitates special hydrodynamic adaptations in their body structure. Examining the growth rate of the structures involved in swimming could offer valuable insights. title: Analysing Opportunities and Risks in Utilizing Reverse Osmosis Reject Water for Tomato Cultivation
abstract: ABSTRACT Rising global soil salinity has increased freshwater scarcity, driving widespread use of reverse osmosis (RO) systems that generate high total dissolved solids (TDS) wastewater. This study investigated impact of RO reject water (ROR) at 100 mM of NaCl (ROR100) and 150 mM of NaCl (ROR150) treatments on tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L) growth and yield. ROR treatments significantly reduced shoot (34.83 g) and root (1.65 g) fresh weights, plant moisture (55.85%) and leaf number (9.28) compared to control. title: Seismic Attenuation Tomography of El Hierro: Insights Into Magmatic Processes in the Canary Islands
abstract: Abstract Recent eruptions in the Canary Islands highlight an increase in volcanic activity and provide an exceptional data set to investigate subsurface processes. We present the first 3D seismic attenuation model for the 2011–2012 eruption on El Hierro, using the coda normalization method and a large seismic data set. Our results complement previous 3D velocity models, improving constraints on crustal structure, magma pathways, and intermediate storage zones. title: Sm-Nd-Sr isotopic and geochemical signatures of mafic intrusive rocks in the Nigadoo River Syncline, northeastern New Brunswick: Implications for regional tectonics
abstract: Mafic dykes and sills occur throughout the Silurian–Devonian Nigadoo River Syncline of northern New Brunswick. These intrusive rocks are characterized by transitional to calc-alkaline compositions consistent with volcanic-arc and within-plate environments and have trends suggestive of fractional crystallization of a melt derived from a mantle source. title: The effects of wear on the morphology and puncture force of shark teeth
abstract: Sharks continuously replace their teeth throughout their lives, replacing an entire row of teeth every one to 5 weeks. It has been hypothesized that this is due to tooth wear, rather than tooth breakage. However, little is known about how quickly teeth wear and what affect this wear has on tooth puncture performance. Unworn teeth from five shark species, bull shark Carcharhinus leucas, blacktip shark C. limbatus, sandbar shark C. plumbeus, shortfin mako Isurus oxyrinchus and great hammerhead Sphyrna mokarran, were subjected to 400 puncture tests each on teleost prey. title: Reclaiming the Tap, Curbing Single-Use Bottled Water: An Agenda for Research and Policy
abstract: The dramatic global growth of bottled water over the past five decades, particularly in nations with nearly universal access to high-quality, low-cost public tap water, has generated a host of harmful environmental impacts, including a substantial contribution to the crisis of single-use plastic pollution, as well as negative social and economic impacts due to its far higher cost and unequal patterns of distrust in tap water. title: Revision of the fish parasitic branchial cymothoid genus Agarna Schioedte & Meinert, 1884 (Crustacea: Isopoda: Cymothoidae), with description of Gibbothoa gen. nov.
abstract: Abstract The genus Agarna Schioedte & Meinert, 1884, is reviewed and rediagnosed. The female, male and transitional stages of Agarna cumulus (Haller, 1880), the senior synonym of the type species, are redescribed based on the newly designated lectotype and additional material collected from the Caribbean parasitising doctorfish, Acanthurus chirurgus (Bloch, 1787), blue tang surgeonfish Acanthurus coeruleus Bloch & Schneider, 1801, and barber surgeonfish Acanthurus bahianus Castelnau, 1855. title: Nonlinear Responses of Chemodiversity to Total Organic Carbon Content in Lake Sediments
abstract: Abstract Lake littoral sediments are critical carbon cycle hotspots that bridge terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. The chemodiversity of dissolved organic matter (DOM) in these sediments reflects ecosystem multifunctionality, particularly regarding carbon storage. However, the relationship between DOM chemodiversity and sediment total organic carbon (TOC) content, a critical quality‐quantity nexus, remains poorly understood. title: The Arrival of Arabic in India and the Spread of Islam Through Trade, Scholarship, and Education
abstract: The Arabic language played a significant role in the spread of Islam in India through trade, religious education, and scholarly activities. Arab traders established commercial and cultural relations with Indian communities, especially along the Malabar Coast, which later became important areas for Islamic interaction. Through peaceful communication, honesty in trade, and religious teachings, Arabic gradually became associated with Islamic scholarship and worship in India. title: Oviposition Inside Land Snail Shells (Caracolus carocolla) by the Salamanquita Común (Sphaerodactylus grandisquamis guarionex) in a Subtropical Moist Forest of the Puerto Rican Karst
abstract: Los cambios en el tamaño corporal afectan el comportamiento de los organismos y pueden facilitar nuevas interacciones ecológicas. En la herpetofauna, la miniaturización ha evolucionado de manera independiente en múltiples ocasiones; sin embargo, la historia natural de las especies miniaturizadas ha sido poco estudiada. Reportamos evidencia de oviposición por la salamanquita común (Sphaerodactylus grandisquamis guarionex) en las conchas vacías del caracol arbóreo puertorriqueño (Caracolus carocolla). title: Little effect of further aging on soil-weathered plastics
abstract: Abstract Plastic waste accumulates in soils, impacting structure, biota, and ecosystem functioning. Understanding the persistence and aging of plastics in soil is therefore important. However, aging occurs over timescales which cannot be covered in conventional experiments. Many studies therefore focus on simulated weathering of pristine polymers over short timescales, but these experiments do not consider potentially different aging behaviour after extended environmental exposure. title: Age and growth of Alestes dentex (Linnaeus, 1758) in Lake Nasser, Egypt
abstract: The age and growth of Alestes dentex from Lake Nasser, Egypt, were studied based on scales readings. A total of 909 specimens of A. dentex, with total lengths (TL) ranging from 18.5 to 40.9 cm and weights from 58 to 500 g, were sampled twice monthly at two landing sites on Lake Nasser (Garf Hussein and Khor Kalabsha). The sampling covered the period from June 2023 to July 2024, except for April and May 2024, due to the seasonal closure of the lake (biological rest period). title: Fish Oil Mitigates Ozone-Induced Lung Inflammation by Restoring Oxylipin Homeostasis
abstract: Abstract Background and Aim: Ground-level ozone threatens respiratory health by inducing pulmonary inflammation. Although fish oil has demonstrated anti-inflammatory properties, its protective mechanisms against ozone-induced lung injury remain unclear. This study investigated fish oil efficacy in modulating oxylipin homeostasis and mitigating pulmonary toxicity induced by ozone exposure in a mouse model. title: Household Container Characteristics Associated with Mosquito Larval Presence in a Highland Community of Tana Toraja, Indonesia
abstract: Introduction: Dengue continues to pose a major mosquito-borne public health problem in tropical countries, including Indonesia, where household water containers frequently serve as habitats for mosquito larvae. However, studies examining household container characteristics associated with mosquito larval presence in highland communities remain limited. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted in Bombongan Urban Village, Makale District, Tana Toraja Regency, South Sulawesi, Indonesia. title: Multiplex PCR for Screening PKS-I and NRPS Biosynthetic Genes in Streptomyces: A Methodological Review
abstract: Streptomyces is an important source of microbial natural products, and many of its biosynthetic pathways are associated with polyketide synthase (PKS) and nonribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) gene clusters. PCR-based screening can be used to prioritize isolates for subsequent antimicrobial and chemical investigation, but the evidence for true multiplex detection of these targets has often been mixed with studies that used separate PCR reactions. title: Hydration Product Evolution and Thermodynamic Modeling of Aluminosilicate Glasses in Supersulfated Cementitious Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Supersulfated cement (SSC) is considered a promising low‐carbon cementitious material. However, the intrinsic characteristics of aluminosilicate glasses and their hydration behavior remain insufficiently understood. This study systematically investigates the hydration reactivity, phase evolution, and thermodynamic properties of synthesized aluminosilicate glasses with representative compositions in SSC systems. title: Transcriptomic insights into dichlorvos removal by Luteovulum azotoformans EBL0706 and its potential application for reducing pesticide residues on vegetables
abstract: Dichlorvos (DDVP), a widely used organophosphorus pesticide, poses considerable risks to environmental and food safety, making its effective removal an important objective. Microbial remediation offers a sustainable alternative to physicochemical treatments; however, the molecular responses associated with DDVP removal in phototrophic bacteria remain poorly understood. title: Fish gut microbiota mediate pollutant-induced lipid toxicity via bidirectional biotransformation and dysbiosis
abstract: Abstract The gut microbiota acts simultaneously as a target of environmental pollutants and as a driver of their biotransformation, but how these two roles jointly determine host toxicity remains insufficiently defined. Using zebrafish as a One Health model, we show that dietary exposure to environmentally relevant levels of triphenyl phosphate (TPHP), an organophosphate flame retardant, causes intestinal lipid accumulation, barrier disruption, and PPAR pathway dysregulation. title: Ammonia excretion dynamics of the silverside (Basilichthys microlepidotus) during the juvenile-to-adult grow-out phase, under different body sizes and stocking densities in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS)
abstract: The Chilean silverside (Basilichthys microlepidotus) is an endemic freshwater species with emerging potential for aquaculture and conservation-oriented production. However, key bioengineering parameters required for system design and biomass management remain poorly defined. This study evaluated how body size and stocking density affect total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) excretion rates in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) under controlled conditions. abstract: Abstract The public excavation and preparation of sixteen sediment blocks of a Late Cretaceous Lance Formation bonebed (Eastern Wyoming, USA) yielded a well-preserved mammalian lower jaw. title: Atmospheric Water Generation Technologies: Comprehensive Analysis, Economic Payback And Climate Suitability For Applications In Malaysia
abstract: Global water shortage has been one of the issues that has remained prevalent over the decades, with no viable solutions. Despite efforts and mitigation measures proposed by multiple international institutions and researchers, progress remains inadequate at present. Atmospheric water generation (AWG) emerges as one of the alternatives to the water shortage problem, offering sustainable water production from the ambient air while preserving natural water sources such as groundwater. title: The rapid spread of invasive smallmouth bass and chain pickerel and a changing Nova Scotia fishery
abstract: In the 1940s, Smallmouth Bass (Micropterus dolomieu) and Chain Pickerel (Esox niger) were confirmed in 14 lakes collectively in southwest Nova Scotia. By 2025, Smallmouth Bass had been documented in 340 lakes, while Chain Pickerel had been reported in 180 lakes, representing approximately 34% of the province’s lentic habitats. title: The Technical Competence and Navigation Systems as Drivers of River Pilotage Performance
abstract: Purpose – This study investigates the effects of work experience, technical competence, and navigation information systems on the safety and traffic-flow performance of ship pilotage operations in the Barito River, Indonesia, with job satisfaction examined as a mediating variable.Methodology – A quantitative explanatory research design was employed using a cross-sectional survey of 42 active ship pilots. title: Drivers of bird species turnover in the largest archipelago of China: Insights from zeta (ζ) diversity and multi‐site generalized dissimilarity modelling ( MS ‐ GDM )
abstract: Species turnover, the spatial dissimilarity in species composition, is a central concept in island biogeography and community ecology. Traditional pairwise beta diversity metrics are limited to two-site comparisons and cannot fully resolve the mechanisms driving turnover across multiple communities. Zeta (ζ) diversity overcomes this limitation by quantifying multi-site species sharing and capturing how both rare and widespread species contribute to species turnover along a continuum. title: Stress-resilient dryland cereals: A review on mechanisms of drought and salinity tolerance
abstract: Millets and sorghum, considered as dryland cereals are particularly known for their capability to grow in adverse environments. The tolerance mechanisms to major abiotic stressors remain fragmented across physiological, biochemical and molecular studies. This review aims to scrutinise and synthesise the major tolerance mechanisms that millets perform under drought and saline stress. Published evidence on stress perception, physiological adjustment, biochemical defence and molecular regulation was reviewed and integrated. title: Characterising the longer-term impacts of highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks prior to 2020 on wild bird populations
abstract: Since 2020, there has been a global escalation of the impacts of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) on wild bird species. However, the population-level consequences of this disease remain poorly understood, despite repeated outbreaks affecting wild birds over the past two decades. To address this, we collated population counts and mortality data from 40 historical cases where HPAI mass-mortality occurred in wild bird populations prior to 2020. title: Morphological abnormalities in erythrocytes as a preliminary indicator of genotoxicity of nano-tire rubber in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
abstract: Despite recent research interest in the toxic effects of tires, there is a lack of data on the genotoxicity of tire rubber particles in aquatic organisms. This study aimed to detect the cellular and genetic abnormalities affecting erythrocytes in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) exposed to tire rubber nanoparticles (TRNPs ≤1 μm) using a micronucleus assay. title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA
abstract: N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. title: Trait co‐occurrence networks reveal changes in community functional structure from local to landscape scales
abstract: Abstract The functional composition of communities reflects species performance and its interplay with local and regional drivers. Yet trait‐based analyses often overlook regional heterogeneity (geographic and environmental differences among communities), despite its central role for community assembly. This limits our ability to assess functional change across broad spatial extents or long time periods, which is essential to understand the functional consequences of global change. title: Effects of frying, grilling, and sous vide cooking on the nutritional composition and quality characteristics of fish balls
abstract: Comparative information on the effects of conventional and sous vide cooking methods on fish-ball quality remains limited. This study evaluated the effects of frying, grilling, and sous vide cooking on the proximate composition, fatty acid and free amino acid profiles, color, texture, and cooking characteristics of fish balls. title: Laboratory-based assessment of quantitative PCR to describe Arctic fish assemblages in surface water affected by acid rock drainage
abstract: Permafrost thaw has been identified as a cause of metal mobilization from acid rock drainage and transport to Arctic rivers. Elevated metal concentrations and precipitation of Fe(III) minerals (i.e., rusting) in surface waters deteriorates water quality and raises questions about ecosystem effects, especially to the health of fish species. title: The History of The Arrival and Development of Islam in the Malay World and its Influence on Society
abstract: This article focuses on studying the history of the arrival and development of Islam in the Malay region and its impact on people's lives. This research applies a qualitative descriptive approach as well as a literature study method. Data was collected by reviewing scientific journal articles and historical literature that explain the process of Islam entering the region, trade networks, the role of scholars, Malay kingdoms, and socio-cultural changes. title: Living the American Dream: Aasta Hansteen’s Transnational Feminist Experience
abstract: This article discusses the Norwegian feminist pioneer and emigrant to the United States, Aasta Hansteen. Hansteen has been studied by many, but her encounters with American feminism and progressive circles have so far received little attention. I argue that her experience as an immigrant made it possible for her to meet American feminists and live out her feminist dream as a free individual. abstract: Abstract Validating the controversial hypothesis that precursory gravity changes arise from sudden acceleration of subducting plates potentially triggering great earthquakes is of paramount importance. To rigorously evaluate proposed precursors for the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku and 2010 Mw 8.8 Maule earthquakes, we develop a statistical framework that enables (a) robust assessment of their statistical significance, (b) characterization of temporal evolution, and (c) integrative analysis across multiple GRACE gravity solutions with differing error characteristics. title: Mammals under pressure: presence data for assessing extinction of endemic, threatened and mammals subject to use in Colombia
abstract: Colombia is the sixth country in mammal richness worldwide (553 species) and the fourth in the Americas. This high diversity presents significant conservation and management challenges. Although knowledge of mammalian biology has advanced, the 2006 “Libro Rojo de los Mamíferos de Colombia” was the last major effort to assess the risk category for the country's mammals. New risk assessments require updated species records, especially for little-documented taxa. title: The alignment of sacred forests with the concept of other effective area-based conservation measures
abstract: Abstract Sacred natural sites, while not always formally recognised as protected areas, can protect biodiversity via the customs and practices that prohibit exploitation for spiritual reasons. As such, these sites may align with the concept of other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs), which recognise places that protect biodiversity outside formal protected areas. title: Freshwater Ornamental Fish Trade in Tanzania: Species Composition, Trade Practices and Conservation Risks
abstract: ABSTRACT The ornamental fish trade is one of the fastest‐growing sectors of the global aquatic animal industry, involving more than 7900 fish species. Global demand for ornamental fish has increased substantially over the past few decades, with millions of fish traded annually to supply the expanding aquarium industry. The industry in Tanzania is also expanding rapidly, yet information on traded species, trade practices and associated conservation risks remains limited. title: Sensitivity of climate analogues to problem-specific adjustments: a case study
abstract: Abstract Climate analogues, which identify present-day locations resembling projected future climates are widely considered to offer a powerful tool to support adaptation in climate-sensitive sectors. However, many existing applications rely on coarse climate model outputs and raw variables, often overlooking microclimatic variation and sector-specific climate metrics. abstract: DNA barcoding is widely accepted for the species level identification and their genetic characterization especially in fisheries and biodiversity evaluation. title: Mantle COH‐Rich Magmatic Lineage Tree Traces Thermochemical Change and REE Refertilisation in Continental Roots
abstract: ABSTRACT Continental roots are the ultimate sources for many giant metal deposits including rare‐earth elements (REEs). The ore‐fertile magmatic rocks inherently have undergone complex evolution, making metal pre‐enrichment processes in the mantle sources poorly understood. Co‐existing carbonatites and other COH‐rich magmatic rocks like kimberlites and lamproites in many polymetallic mineralisation areas likely represent different branches of similar COH‐rich mantle melt precursors. title: Methodological Concerns and Interpretation of Archaeometric Data in Recent Provenance Claims Concerning the Riace Bronzes
abstract: ABSTRACT Recent claims proposing a Syracusan provenance for the Riace Bronzes rely on selective petrographic, geochemical, and taphonomic evidence that raises crucial methodological questions. This paper critically reassesses the analytical premises and inferential logic underlying these claims, showing that they bypass established protocols in ceramic and sediment provenance studies, lack statistically meaningful reference groups, and raise concerns on the interpretation of archaeometric, radiocarbon, and lead isotope data. Additional arguments based on casting technology and taphonomy appear

title: Diet and digestive traits associated with crab digestion in the crab-eating frog (Fejervarya cancrivora)
abstract: Abstract Despite the mechanical resistance of chitin-rich exoskeletons, how anurans with limited chewing capacity utilize crustacean prey remains poorly understood. The crab-eating frog ( Fejervarya cancrivora ), which inhabits mangrove and brackish-water environments and feeds on crustaceans, provides a suitable model system for addressing this question. However, whether its natural diet is associated with host digestive traits and gut microbial functional potential remains unclear. title: Debasement and the production of copper-alloy coins in ninth-century Northumbria
abstract: The production of copper-alloy coins in the kingdom of Northumbria during the ninth century AD represents a unique move away from silver coinage in early medieval western Europe. While differing explanations for this debasement have been proposed, few consider non-numismatic evidence. The compilation and analysis of available ninth-century gold and silver objects found in Northumbria, presented here, sheds new light on the change in coinage. title: Studying invasive species by non-invasive methods: Real-time qPCR successfully detects protected vertebrate species in raccoon scats
abstract: Abstract Invasive alien species pose a major threat to biodiversity, particularly through predation on rare and endangered species. In Europe, studies on the impacts of invasive mammalian predators such as raccoons remain scarce, and existing diet analysis methods often fail to detect such predation events. This study therefore evaluates the suitability of real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) as a sensitive method for detecting predation on rare species. title: Hurricane disturbance leads to elevated wildfire activity in the Gulf Coast region U.S.A.
abstract: Abstract Building on long-standing hypotheses of a hurricane-fire interaction, this study assesses empirical evidence for hurricane-driven increases in wildfire activity along the Gulf Coast of the United States. It has been proposed that wildfire risk is elevated post-hurricane due to increased fuel accumulation and alterations to forest microclimates associated with treefall (e.g., increased radiation, temperature, aridity). title: Modern pollen, fungal non-pollen palynomorphs and vegetation associations in southern California: Insights into past and present-day landscape dynamics
abstract: This study analyses pollen and fungal assemblages from 64 samples- including moss, soil surface, root, and dung- collected along an elevational gradient extending from the Santa Barbara and Ventura coasts to the Transverse Mountains near Mount Pinos (up to ~2600 m asl) in Kern County, southern California, USA. title: Airborne Microplastic Generation and Transport from 3D Printing Activities in a University Setting
abstract: Plastics are everywhere in modern environments, and smaller plastic particles, known as microplastics (MPs, 1 µm-5 mm), have raised increasing concerns regarding indoor air quality and potential human exposure. Given that people spend more than 80% of their time indoors, understanding potential indoor sources and the distribution of MPs is important. Three-dimensional (3D) printing activities have become increasingly common in educational settings and may contribute to indoor MP pollution. title: Effect of treated sewage water irrigation on growth, yield and quality of China aster (Callistephus chinensis)
abstract: Freshwater scarcity makes treated sewage water a possible supplementary irrigation source for floriculture, yet the appropriate share for China aster is unknown. A field experiment was carried out in 2025–26 at the College of Horticulture, Kolar, Karnataka, India, in a randomized complete block design with four replications and five irrigation treatments: borewell water (control), 100% treated sewage water, 50% borewell water + 50% treated sewage water, 25% borewell water + 75% treated sewage water, and 75% borewell water + 25% treated sewage water. title: Mopane Worm ( Gonimbrasia belina ) as an Alternative Protein Source in Aquaculture: A Review of Nutritional Value, Digestibility and Physiological Responses
abstract: ABSTRACT The expansion of aquaculture has intensified the search for sustainable alternatives to fishmeal. The mopane worm, Gonimbrasia belina (syn. Imbrasia belina ), is a traditionally consumed southern African insect whose protein, lipid and micronutrient contents have prompted interest in its use as an aquafeed ingredient. This semi‐systematic review evaluates the nutritional value and digestibility of mopane worm meal and its effects on growth, feed utilisation and physiological responses in fish. title: Development of CaO/Al2O3 bifunctional catalyst for biodiesel production from jatropha oil: optimization and kinetic study
abstract: Biodiesel production from non-edible Jatropha curcas oil, which have high free fatty acid (FFA) content, presents technical challenges due to soap formation during conventional base-catalyzed transesterification. This often necessitates a costly and time-consuming acid pretreatment. To address this, the study developed a bifunctional heterogeneous calcium-/aluminum oxide (CaO/Al 2 O 3 ) catalyst synthesized from calcined snail shells (SS) and impregnated with alumina. The catalyst enables direct transesterification of high-FFA jatropha oil, thereby simplifying the process and reducing wastage.

title: New species of Eucystis (Blastozoa: Echinodermata) from Laurentia: implications for morphological and biogeographical patterns in the Paleozoic
abstract: Abstract A number of echinoderm groups lack representation in the Silurian fossil record, which becomes especially clear when considering the echinoderm fossil record of the Ordovician and Devonian. This paucity constrains our ability to resolve echinoderm evolutionary dynamics and biogeographic pathways during the Silurian, thereby underscoring the significance of newly discovered species. title: Crusader towns of the military orders: from the Levant to the Baltic
abstract: This paper examines the archaeology, urban plans, and history of towns founded by military orders in the Levant and the Baltic regions. First, the analysis compares the 13thcentury development of Templar Atlit (Israel) and Teutonic Elbląg (Poland). These two towns are shown to have developed in an almost identical way. They were similar in size, function, and origin, and both held important relics. title: Ontogenetic development of digestive enzymes in the crayfish Procambarus acanthophorus
abstract: Mexico boasts a great diversity of decapod crustaceans, including crayfish known locally as acociles. Within this group, Procambarus acanthophorus stands out as an important species for regional fisheries and has high aquaculture potential because it adapts quickly to captive conditions and develops directly without larval stages, giving it a significant advantage in growth and survival over other crayfish species. However, its digestive and physiological capabilities, which could inform the development of aquaculture technologies and enhance its aquaculture potential, remain largely unknown.

title: Periphyton-associated combined restoration promotes microbial restructuring and phosphorus cycling in gleyed paddy soil
abstract: Abstract Persistent reductive stress and soil acidification impose strong environmental filtering in gleyed paddy soils, suppressing microbial activity and limiting phosphorus (P) bioavailability. Inspired by natural soil-water interface dynamics, we developed a restoration strategy combining slow-release CaO2, periphyton development, and phosphate-solubilizing bacteria (PSB) to alleviate habitat constraints and reactivate endogenous P cycling under field conditions. title: Acclimatization of Candidatus Brocadia to high nitrogen and salinity loads in a sequencing batch reactor: performance and operational insights
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the acclimatization of Candidatus Brocadia, a freshwater anaerobic ammonium oxidation (Anammox) species, to high nitrogen (up to 1.39 gN/L) and salinity (up to 14.3 gNaCl/L) loads in a semicontinuous sequencing batch reactor. Over one year of operation, the reactor achieved stable nitrogen removal performance, with nitrite removal efficiency exceeding 99% at nitrogen loading rates and salinity concentrations up to 0.72 gN/L/d and 14.29 gNaCl/L, respectively. title: A dispersal-recolonisation 3D biofilm in vitro model based on co-assembled peptide amphiphiles and clinical wound fluid
abstract: Chronic wound infections are sustained by dynamic three-dimensional (3D) biofilm cycles involving maturation, dispersal, and recolonisation, yet existing in vitro models fail to reproduce these temporal and structural complexities. Here, we report a strategy that co-assembles a designed protease-inhibitory peptide amphiphile (PA) with patient-derived wound fluid (WF) to reconstruct the complete biofilm life cycle in vitro. title: A TaqMan assay that knows its mite: specific detection of Tropilaelaps mercedesae Clade I
abstract: Tropilaelaps mercedesae (Mesostigmata: Laelapidae), an invasive mite species native to South East Asia, is rapidly expanding its range, facilitated by global trade in bees and climate change. Recent detections in Eastern Europe raise concerns about its imminent spread into the European Union. As a notifiable parasite under the European Union Animal Health Law, member states are required to implement surveillance and prevent the spread to other member states. title: Terrestrial arthropod community responses to livestock grazing
abstract: Abstract Livestock grazing is a major land‐use globally with a wide range of documented effects on biodiversity. Arthropods are a dominant component of biodiversity in grazed landscapes, but their responses to grazing vary among taxa and ecosystem type. Here, we review and synthesise the global literature on terrestrial arthropod responses to livestock grazing, with the aim to identify trends and knowledge gaps in the literature and recommend research priorities to increase knowledge of how grazing activity by managed livestock influences community‐level processes and ecosystem function. title: Wahid Hasyim And The Transformation of Hajj Travel Accessibility in Post-Independence Indonesia By Ministry of Religion Affairs: A Leadership Analysis
abstract: The Hajj journey is a spiritual journey for Muslims as the fifth pillar of Islam, therefore performing the Hajj pilgrimage must have sufficient knowledge, physical, and material provisions. Hajj travel from Indonesia since the colonial era has become a complex problem because Hajj travel is often used as a business field without paying attention to the scientific aspects of performing it. title: Beyond Microbeads: The Overlooked Occurrence and Co-occurrence of Synthetic Polymers in Leave-On Cosmetics
abstract: Abstract Synthetic polymers are widely used in leave-on cosmetic products, yet systematic product analyses of their occurrence across leave-on cosmetic categories remain limited. This study evaluated the occurrence and distribution of 17 targeted polymers across cosmetic products using ingredient-level analysis of large cosmetic datasets. Approximately 31% of products contained at least one targeted polymer; some contained multiple targeted polymers, with up to six identified in a single product. abstract: Gentrification results in higher tax revenues, but also the displacement of longstanding residents. Housing insecurity has been associated with medication nonadherence among people with HIV; however, the existing literature does not assess neighborhood level variables (e.g., indicators of gentrification) in tandem with individual level variables to adequately assess the risk of displacement and its association with health outcomes. title: Haunted Environments: Political Violence and Ecologies of Memory in Ayu Utami’s Larung and Seno Gumira Ajidarma’s Kalatidha
abstract: Political violence damages bodies, historical records, and environments mediating the past. This article examines Ayu Utami’s Larung and Seno Gumira Ajidarma’s Kalatidha through comparative close reading informed by haunting studies, material ecocriticism, and environmental approaches to cultural memory. abstract: Groundwater quality and soil characteristics are important considerations in evaluating drinking-water resources and agricultural suitability. This study assessed water from existing wells and boreholes and examined soil properties in the Bajoga community. A well inventory was conducted, and water samples were collected following American Public Health Association (APHA) procedures. abstract: This study aims to investigate the projections of air temperature and precipitation climate extremes in the Brazilian Legal Amazon (BLA) through the end of the century. title: Assistência de enfermagem às mulheres com alterações do trato uriná-rio feminino
abstract: As alterações do trato urinário feminino constituem um conjunto de condições frequentes que podem comprometer a saúde física, emocional, social e sexual das mulheres. Entre as manifestações mais relevantes estão as infecções do trato urinário, a incontinência urinária, os sintomas de armazenamento e esvaziamento vesical e as condições associadas ao uso de cateteres urinários. title: Turbulence Anisotropy and the Roughness Sublayer in Diverse Canopy Flows: A Pathway for Generalization
abstract: Abstract Turbulent exchanges within the atmospheric surface layer (ASL) are influenced by the presence of canopies and terrain heterogeneity. Because the roughness sublayer (RSL) connects the canopy‐terrain system to the ASL, the flow properties within the RSL are receiving significant attention. However, basic questions about the RSL, including its thickness, remain unresolved beyond order‐of‐magnitude arguments. title: Work Conditions and Seafarer Performance: The Role of Occupational Safety
abstract: This study investigates the effects of contract duration, internet connectivity, and workload on Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) and employee performance among Indonesian seafarers employed by foreign shipping companies operating on international routes. In addition, it examines the direct effect of OSH on seafarer performance and evaluates the mediating role of OSH in the relationships between contract duration, internet connectivity, workload, and employee performance. title: Assessing biodiverse plant foods richness through dietary survey tools: availability of food consumption data at the inter- and intraspecific levels in an Italian case study
abstract: Dietary biodiversity is increasingly recognized as key to both diet quality and environmental sustainability. However, national food consumption surveys rarely record foods below the species level. The objectives of this paper were to assess the inter- and intraspecific biodiversity richness of plant foods in the food list used in the most recent Italian Food Consumption Survey (IV SCAI) and to evaluate the biodiversity richness of plant foods consumption as assessed during the survey. title: AHP-Based Prioritisation of Development Strategies for Semi-Intensive Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) Farming in a Mining-Affected Area, Central Halmahera Regency
abstract: Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) farming is a growing livelihood in Central Halmahera Regency, where nickel mining raises fish demand but may also threaten shared water resources. abstract: Sustainable development has emerged as a central paradigm of public policy, aiming to integrate environmental, economic, and social goals. Global waste-management reforms increasingly combine climate objectives, circular-economy strategies, and public-private implementation, but the enforceability of these commitments remains uneven, particularly in developing countries such as Cameroon. abstract: Egypt is the clearest case in the Middle East of a country whose food security depends on a single imported staple. Between 1975 and 2025 its population roughly tripled, from about 37 million to more than 107 million, while the cultivable area confined to the Nile Valley and Delta grew far more slowly. abstract: A non-integrating reprogramming approach was utilised to establish a human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) line (INNDSUi012-A) from the skin fibroblasts of a 14-year-old male patient with spinocerebellar ataxia type 2 (SCA2) caused by a pathogenic CAG repeat expansions in exon 1 of the ataxin-2 (ATXN2) gene. abstract: In this paper, we propose a reflection on transnational climate governance as a mechanism for implementing sustainable development. However, the paper discusses the current international system’s inability to articulate concrete public policies capable of dealing with the climate change scenario. title: Effects of dietary olive pomace (Olea europaea) on zootechnical performance and physiological responses of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) juveniles
abstract: The effects of increasing dietary inclusion levels of olive pomace (OP) on growth performance, zootechnical indices, body composition, energy metabolism, and lipid peroxidation were evaluated in juvenile Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ). Five experimental diets, formulated to be isoproteic (37% crude protein) and isolipidic (9% lipids), included 0% (OP 0 ), 5% (OP 5 ), 10% (OP 10 ), 15% (OP 15 ), and 20% (OP 20 ) OP. title: Stream-Dwelling Brown Trout Movements in a Mountain Headwater Stream
abstract: In Europe, the stream-dwelling brown trout (Salmo trutta) is very common in headwater streams, which also support most hydroelectric water intakes. These water intakes can contribute to the fragmentation of these ecosystems. Effective continuity restoration measures that would benefit this species are closely linked to whether individual trout need to move or not. However, trout movement patterns are not completely defined and can vary between populations and individuals. Therefore, we conducted a study in the Neste d'Oueil river, using PIT-tagging to improve our understanding of the movements
institutions: Institut de Mécanique des Fluides de Toulouse

title: Development Potential and Energy–Water–Land Nexus of Floating Photovoltaics in China Under the Carbon Neutrality Framework
abstract: With the intensification of climate change, achieving carbon neutrality and decarbonizing the global energy system have become pressing priorities worldwide. Floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems show a distinct synergy among clean energy production, decreasing water evaporation, and improving land use efficiency, which makes them of great value for realizing the transformation of new energy power systems. title: Assessment of cabin filtration efficiency: contribution to an on-road methodology
abstract: The use of cabin filters provides protection for passengers against outdoor pollution caused by particles (aerosols) when travelling by car. Their filtration efficiency is assessed through rigorous laboratory studies in accordance with standards. However, there are few or no comparable studies conducted under real road conditions using reference particle measurements to complement the laboratory results. In this context, our study aims to contribute to the improvement of on-road aerosol measurement by evaluating cabin filters with gravimetric measurements. To this end, a sampling line upstream
institutions: Institut national de l'environnement industriel et des risques

title: El discurso escondido de las Galápagos: Una relectura de The Encantadas, or Enchanted Isles de Herman Melville
abstract: This article examines the source of a counternarrative on Latin American and Ecuadorian historiography, by reinterpreting the seventh story of Herman Melville's The Encantadas (1856). If one of Melville's interests is his inability to accept or reject the Emersonianism, it is useful to identify the specificity of his criticism of transcendental philosophy by looking at his short stories. His stories allowed the author of Moby Dick to recreate a model of resistance based on the representation of the Galapagos, a crucial space for modernity in Western thought.

title: Tổng quan nghiên cứu về kỹ năng tư vấn tâm lý của Chính trị viên đại đội ở đơn vị cơ sở
abstract: Nghiên cứu tổng quan về các công trình liên quan đến kỹ năng tư vấn tâm lý trong quân đội, nhằm xác định cơ sở lý luận, các nhóm kỹ năng cốt lõi, yếu tố ảnh hưởng, biện pháp phát triển kỹ năng tư vấn tâm lý cho Chính trị viên đại đội ở đơn vị cơ sở. Kết quả cho thấy, các nghiên cứu tập trung vào bốn nhóm nội dung bản chất và tiến trình tư vấn tâm lý; cấu trúc và biểu hiện kỹ năng; các yếu tố ảnh hưởng và biện pháp phát triển kỹ năng. Tuy nhiên, phần lớn nghiên cứu được thực hiện trong lĩnh vực tư vấn chuyên nghiệp hoặc học đường; nghiên cứu trực tiếp về kỹ năng của Chính trị viên đại đội còn í
journal: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology

title: Recent Decline in Global Atmospheric COS Driven by Reduced Anthropogenic CS 2 Emissions
abstract: Abstract Carbonyl sulfide (COS) is an atmospheric tracer for carbon cycle processes. Global observations reveal a rapid decline in COS concentrations beginning in 2016, but the cause of this decline is unknown. Here we show that this decrease is unexpected. Previous COS trends followed rayon production which emits CS 2 , a COS precursor. However, the recent COS decline coincides with increasing rayon output. Multiple independent observing systems, including NOAA's global flask network and NDACC FTIR retrievals, show a consistent tropospheric COS trend of −1.2 ± 0.1% yr −1 from 2016 to 2022, ev
institutions: NSF National Center for Atmospheric Research

title: Self-organization through layering of β-plane-like turbulence in plasmas and geophysical fluids
abstract: Staircase formation and layering is studied in simplified, potential vorticity (PV) conserving models of plasmas and geophysical fluids, by investigating turbulent self-organization and nonlinear saturation with different mechanisms of free energy production-forcing or linear instability-and with standard or modified zonal flow (ZF) responses.
