title: When the Leviathan Devours: Law, Legitimacy, and the Experience of Sovereign Power
abstract: This paper examines Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Leviathan (2014) through Thomas Hobbes’s theory of sovereignty, asking what film can reveal about political power that political theory alone cannot fully capture. Hobbes conceptualizes the sovereign as an overwhelming but necessary authority capable of transforming insecurity and conflict into order. Zvyagintsev’s film complicates this account by depicting a political system in which order and functioning institutions persist while protection, accountability, and justice collapse. Through its portrayal of bureaucratic legality, coercive state power, re

title: Asymmetric Warfare in the Iran–USA Conflict: Strategies and Security Implications
abstract: The clash between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the United States is one of the most obvious contemporary examples of asymmetric warfare: a regional power (IR) vs. a global military power opponent (USA) that the IR cannot match on an even footing. This article will explore how Iran has turned its structural disadvantage into strategic advantage and how the United States has responded in terms of its posture to the war between Israel and Iran, which began in June 2025 and culminated in the US–Israeli campaign of 28 February 2026. Based on the qualitative and interpretive synthesis of recent

title: Structural Resilience and Institutional Response: An Empirical Study of Economic Recovery Pathways in UK Cities Following the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: The study empirically examines city-level data in the UK for 2019-2023, systematically accounting for the spatial divergence and the drivers of it along three main lines of inquiry: the recovery of incomes, the recovery of welfare spending, and the recovery of regional inequality following the COVID-19 pandemic, using a fixed-effects panel model approach. The results show a strong “Matthew Effect” in the recovery after the pandemic. Higher-skilled, industrial and institutional cities like metros and tech cities like Cambridge had a stronger performance regarding income and welfare security, ev
journal: Asia Pacific Economic and Management Review

title: Biomimicry-informed deconstruction of the cognitive system for Sino–Western hybrid architecture: A case study of Lushan UNESCO Global Geopark
abstract: Sino–Western hybrid architecture serves as a medium for cross-cultural exchange; however, its preservation faces two major challenges: unclear conservation standards and differing perceptions of cultural value. The hybrid architectural forms at Lushan developed in response to local terrain and climate, but the difficulty in defining authenticity for such buildings complicates conservation efforts. This study examines the villa cluster in Guling town, Lushan, employing biomimicry not as a design methodology but as an analytical framework to evaluate hybrid heritage through characteristics of en
journal: Journal of Chinese Architecture and Urbanism
institutions: Nanchang Business College of Jiangxi Agricultural University

title: Thermoregulatory strategy shapes physiological responses to dormancy in animals: A meta‐analysis
abstract: Abstract Dormancy allows animals to persist through prolonged periods of unfavourable environmental conditions by entering states of extreme metabolic depression. However, physiological responses to dormancy vary substantially across taxa and can involve changes in redox balance, immune function and endocrine adjustments. A key unresolved question is whether this variation reflects fundamental differences in how endotherms and ectotherms regulate metabolic depression and subsequent reactivation, with implications for understanding animal life histories and responses to climate change. title: Isolation and Screening of Endophytic Fungi from Nyctanthes arbor-tristis and Eucalyptus sp. for Lipolytic Activity and Lipid Accumulation Potential
abstract: Medicinal plants host a diverse range of endophytic fungi. These fungi are a great source of valuable lipids and hydrolytic enzymes. The objective of this investigation was to isolate endophytic fungi from the bark of Nyctanthes arbor-tristis and Eucalyptus sp. from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, India and to screen them for lipolytic activity and to assess their lipid accumulation potential. In total, 13 fungal isolates were recovered on PDA supplemented with chloramphenicol and were examined for their lipase activity through tributyrin and tween 80 agar media. title: Extreme light rare earth element enrichment in carbonatite-related rare earth element deposits driven by coupled immiscibility, fractional crystallization, and melt–wall rock metasomatism
abstract: Carbonatite-related rare earth elements (REE) deposits are the primary global source of light rare earth elements (LREE) resources. All known giant to supergiant carbonatite-related REE deposits show extreme LREE enrichment and relative heavy rare earth elements (HREE) depletion; however, the mechanism of LREE/HREE fractionation during the formation, evolution, and mineralization of carbonatitic magmas remains unclear. title: Reclamation Period and Straw Type Alter Soil Organic Carbon Composition via CAZyme Families in Coal Mine Agroecosystems
abstract: ABSTRACT Soil organic carbon (SOC) stabilization is crucial for effective ecological restoration in coal‐mining areas, yet the mechanisms underlying straw‐mediated carbon sequestration remain poorly understood. This study investigated how equal‐carbon but different‐mass incorporation of maize (S + M) and wheat (S + W) straw incorporation, across reclamation chronosequences (1, 10, 30 years; R1, R10, R30), associates with SOC composition, microbial communities, and carbohydrate‐active enzymes (CAZymes). title: IBD is associated with species-specific changes in gut microbial gene diversity
abstract: ABSTRACT Intra-species genomic variation provides the raw material for natural selection and can reflect the recent diversification history of microbial populations. Environmental stress may be regarded as the ultimate accelerator of the evolutionary process, especially for microorganisms, which can alter their DNA if presented with nutrient limitation, toxins, or pathogen attack. Chronic intestinal inflammation, as in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), represents prolonged environmental stress for gut commensal bacteria, bringing many enteric species down to undetectable levels. title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol C(OH)4
abstract: Abstract Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures <1200(200) K. The crystal structure of C(OH)4 was determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and corroborated by density-functional theory calculations together with Raman spectros
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A mid‐Cretaceous monocot flower from the Dakota Sandstone of Kansas and its potential implications for the fossil record of palms
abstract: PREMISE: Although the megafossil flora of the upper Albian-lower Cenomanian Dakota Formation in Kansas is well known for angiosperms, monocots have not been reported previously. METHODS: A mesofossil flower was discovered by X-ray analysis of a specimen collected more than a century ago from the Dakota Sandstone of central Kansas. A mid-Cretaceous (ca. 100 Ma) age is inferred from its stratigraphic provenance close to the Albian-Cenomanian boundary. title: Stability of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi-protist interaction networks strengthens vegetation-soil quality in plantations
abstract: Abstract Improving plantation quality is a key strategy for mitigating climate change. However, the mechanisms by which microbial diversity and interactions jointly affect ecosystem quality remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluated how arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) and protistan consumer diversity and interactions were related to soil (SQI) and vegetation (VQI) quality across 108 Pinus tabuliformis and Ulmus pumila plantation plots during spring and autumn. title: Retrieval of ultraviolet aerosol absorption from radiation measurements in young wildfire plumes
abstract: Aerosols play an important role for atmospheric radiative transfer in biomass burning (BB) plumes, where they control photochemistry, direct radiative forcing, and radiation-induced atmospheric dynamics. The optical properties of BB aerosol, however, remain poorly constrained with respect to their absorptive properties at ultraviolet and visible wavelengths. Aircraft-based observations show considerable variability due to heterogeneity in BB plumes, and different measurement methods do not agree with each other. title: Riqueza y distribución de Asteraceae en la Península de Yucatán, México
abstract: Antecedentes: La diversidad alfa cuantifica la biodiversidad a escala local e incluye los componentes taxonómicos y filogenéticos. En la Península de Yucatán se han realizado numerosos estudios botánicos; una de las familias con mayor riqueza de especies es Asteraceae. title: Kofumicins A−D, Antibacterial Glycosylated Linear Polyene Polyketides from Kutzneria kofuensis , Identified via Bacterial Activity Metabolomics
abstract: Abstract Four previously unreported glycosylated linear polyene polyketides, kofumicins A−D (1−4), were isolated from Kutzneria kofuensisNRRL 24061 and were found to inhibit Staphylococcus aureus growth. The kofumicins were identified from the crude extract using a bacterial activity metabolomics-guided approach, which employs split-flow HPLC-UV/MS to generate microtiter plate arrays enabling dereplication and bioactivity assessment prior to isolation. title: Framing Peninsular Crypto‐Jews as Part of the Sephardic Diaspora
abstract: ABSTRACT When we talk about the Sephardic diaspora, we often talk about Iberian conversos who leave the Peninsula, supposedly to live openly as Jews in places like Algiers, Venice, Amsterdam or the Ottoman Empire. But what about those conversos who continued to identify in some way as Jews but who remained in Spain and Portugal? To what extent can we talk about them as part of the Sephardic diaspora as we understand it today? title: Development of an Instrument to Assess Service Quality and Resource Adequacy in Midwifery Laboratories
abstract: Background: Midwifery laboratories are essential for developing clinical competencies, yet service quality and resource adequacy are frequently assessed separately. Objectives: This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an integrated instrument for assessing midwifery laboratory quality. Methods: Five experts validated the instrument, and 446 midwifery students with laboratory experience completed a 44 item questionnaire. title: On Taking Fate Into Your Own Hands: A Tentative Study of Hayao Miyazaki's Lateness
abstract: Hayao Miyazaki’s films have been a pillar of animation for over four decades, with a reputation that extends far beyond Japan's borders. Over those four decades, his work at Studio Ghibli has been recognized for its colorful aesthetics, fantastical twists on popular folklore, and orchestral soundtracks. The aim of this paper is to identify a potential break or trend in the late stage of Miyazaki’s career, as he is now 85 years old, by analyzing his last feature film to date: The Boy and the Heron. title: Adaptive Thermal Comfort Assessment in Mixed-Mode Office Buildings Under Current and Future Sub-Saharan Tropical Hot and Dry Climate Scenarios
abstract: Mixed-mode offices in sub-Saharan hot semi-arid climates face growing thermal stress, yet long-term evidence remains scarce. This study addresses this gap via a stress-test framework (RCP8.5) applied to a compressed earth bricks office in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. A calibrated DesignBuilder/EnergyPlus model evaluated four strategies—free-running (FR), natural ventilation (NV), mixed-mode (MM), and fully air-conditioned (AC)—under current (2023) and future horizons (2030, 2060, 2090). “What Roles for Women?”: Gendering the New International Economic Order at the UN Regional Economic Commission for Africa
abstract: ABSTRACT The 1974 declaration of the New International Economic Order (NIEO), which came just ahead of the UN's International Women's Year (IWY) in 1975, attempted a major renegotiation of global inequality without reference to gender. Through the rest of the 1970s, women at the African Training and Research Centre for Women (ATRCW) in Addis Ababa, itself an initiative of the IWY, leveraged the power of the NIEO to support their undervalued work on African women's economic lives. title: Helminth Fauna of the Caucasian Toad, Bufo verrucosissimus (Pallas, 1814) (Amphibia: Bufonidae), Collected from Türkiye
abstract: This study presents a helminthological investigation of 35 individuals (13♀♀ and 22♂♂) of the Caucasian toad, Bufo verrucosissimus (Pallas, 1814), collected from Artvin and Mersin provinces in Türkiye during 2024–2025. title: AMMONOIDS FROM THE NEW STENOPOPANOCERAS TRANSIENS SUBZONE AT THE DEŞLI CAIRA SECTION (MIDDLE TRIASSIC, NORTHERN DOBROGEA, ROMANIA), PROPOSED AS THE CANDIDATE GSSP FOR THE ANISIAN STAGE
abstract: We document several ammonoid taxa from the lowermost Aegean (lower Anisian) of the Deşli Caira B section, Dobrogea (Romania), candidate section for the GSSP of the Anisian stage. The specimens were collected from beds 2827 and 822A2, and include the new genus Simionescuites, with three new species, i.e., S. dobrogeanus n. gen. n. sp, S. laevicostatus n. gen. n. sp, and S. nodiumbilicatus n. gen. n. sp; Longobarditoides caucasius Shevyrev, 1961; Pseudosageceras sp. ind.; and Sageceras sp. ind. title: Dimming the fire of life: Cocooned aestivating frogs as a model of intrinsic metabolic depression
abstract: Abstract Metabolic depression occurs across a diverse array of invertebrate and vertebrate animals during aestivation (summer dormancy). Some aestivating vertebrates form a protective cocoon of shed epidermal layers (amphibians) or dried mucus (lungfishes) which precludes activity, and their metabolic rates (0.14–0.44 of standard) are typically lower and more stable than for non-cocooning aestivators. title: HAEMATOLOGICAL AND BIOCHEMICAL PROPERTIES OF Jatropha tanjorensis LEAVES EXTRACTS
abstract: Jatropha tanjorensis, commonly known as hospital too far is a plant with edible leaves that have both traditional, medicinal and culinary uses, particularly in Nigeria. The study determined haematological and biochemical properties of leaves of Jatropha tanjorensis. Packed Cell Volume (PCV), Alanine aminotransferase activity, Aspartate aminotransferase activity, Alkaline phosphate activity, Serum Creatinine Concentration, Serum Urea Concentration, Vitamin Quantification and Anti-oxidant assays (TAC and FRAP) were conducted using standardized methods. title: Market and Labour Opportunities as a Driving Factor? Explaining the Gendered Literacy Disparities in the Eighteenth-Century Antwerp Countryside
abstract: Abstract This article investigates regional and gender disparities in literacy in the eighteenth-century countryside of the Southern Low Countries, comparing the Campine area and the Scheldt Polder region. We explore the socioeconomic drivers behind divergent literacy rates by drawing on a rich combination of quantitative and qualitative sources – including marriage certificates, probate inventories, and school enrolment data. title: One field, two seasons: will goose hunting arrangements in autumn have implications for crop loss in spring?
abstract: Svalbard-breeding pink-footed geese ( Anser brachyrhynchus ) at stopover sites in Trøndelag, Mid-Norway, in spring and autumn, with challenges for agriculture in spring but providing local hunting opportunities in autumn. As a management recommendation to control the population increase, thereby reducing crop loss, farmers and hunters are encouraged to organise hunting optimally with fewer hunting days. title: A boundary-inertia-aware relaxed micromorphic model for finite-sized metamaterials under loss of scale separation
abstract: Homogenized continuum models are widely used to describe wave propagation and band-gap behavior in mechanical metamaterials without explicitly resolving their microstructure. Their validity, however, typically relies on the classical separation of scales assumption, according to which the wavelength of the propagating disturbance is much larger than the characteristic size of the unit cell. title: THE DEVELOPMENT OF COTTON PRODUCTION IN NAVOI REGION DURING THE SOVIET PERIOD AND ITS SOCIO-ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES (1982–1991)
abstract: The article analyses the development of cotton production in Navoi Region of the Uzbek SSR between its establishment in 1982 and the collapse of the USSR in 1991, and assesses its socio-economic, demographic and environmental consequences. Methods. Historical, systemic, comparative and source-critical approaches were applied to the scholarly literature and official statistical yearbooks, which were cross-checked against one another. abstract: Во фокусот на трудот е меланхолијата во избрани раскази од полскиот писател Стефан Жеромски (1864 – 1926) од збирката Ќе нè исколваат гаврани, врани (1895) и од македонскиот писател Симон Дракул (1930 – 1999) од збирката Одбрани раскази (1966). title: Shifting boundaries, ambivalent stakes: towards a critical research agenda on Intangible Cultural Heritage and Justice
abstract: As an introduction to the Special Issue on Frontiers and Boundaries of Intangible Cultural Heritage and Justice, this article explores the ambiguities of mobilising intangible cultural heritage (ICH) for social, environmental, and more-than-human justice. The Special Issue emerges from an observation that, increasingly, ICH is deployed as part of a broader repertoire of resistance, refusal, adaptation, and resurgence in struggles against various forms of violence, dispossession, erasure, top-down development, or environmental harm. title: Microclimate, Vegetation, and Soil Response to Micro‐Zonal Solar Photovoltaic Patterning in a Humid Sub‐Tropical Agrivoltaic Grazing System
abstract: Abstract Agrivoltaic grazing systems, or the integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) energy generation with livestock grazing, are the most common form of multi‐use solar energy in the United States and much of the world. However, there is a substantial gap in our understanding of the ecological impacts of combining PV and grazing in these novel ecosystems. Addressing this gap, we present data from the first 2 years of a study characterizing the interacting effects of PV infrastructure with land management (sheep grazing and mowing) in the Southeastern US. title: Migrant frugivorous birds assist plants in tracking climate change: A first spatially explicit approach
abstract: Abstract Climate change is causing biodiversity redistributions towards cooler areas at an unprecedented velocity. Plants are an essential component of terrestrial ecosystems that primarily rely on seed dispersal to redistribute. Yet, most seed dispersal occurs over short distances (i.e. less than 1 km), which is insufficient to track ongoing climate change. Bird migration can support seed dispersal at longer distances. title: Climate Change and Drinking Water Safety in Amassoma, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, Bayelsa State, Nigeria
abstract: Climate change is altering the way water behaves in the Niger Delta, and drinking-water safety is increasingly vulnerable. This study examined climate change and drinking water safety in Amassoma, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, Bayelsa State. The objectives were to examine the indicators of climate change as perceived by residents, to assess the level of drinking water safety, and to determine the effect of climate change on drinking water safety. title: Johan Willem Beyen and the creation of the internal market: Lessons from history and the social sciences for the micro-foundations of EU law
abstract: Abstract This article formalises and develops an individual-centred framework to explain what I call the micro-foundations of EU law, and applies it to Johan Willem Beyen’s role in the creation of the Common Market. It argues that standard structural accounts in European integration overlook the micro-foundations: the ways in which the desires, beliefs and choices of specific actors shape integration outcomes. title: Asymmetrical compositional gap between muscovite and NH 4 -bearing micas – structural constraints: a combined experimental–theoretical study
abstract: The usual coexistence in nature and in synthesised samples of NH 4 -bearing micas with NH 4 -free muscovite or illite has brought us to study their structural stability and characteristics. We used a combination of density functional theory methods and updated absorption-corrected nanoscale analyses of previously studied Germunde (Portugal) and Iberian Range (Spain) samples. abstract: Algal biomass is being investigated as a renewable feedstock for liquid fuels because microalgae can grow rapidly, can be cultivated on non-arable land, and can use a range of water sources and carbon dioxide streams. abstract: The research focuses on the impact of domestic politics on India’s China policy from 1991 to 2004. Due to the end of the Cold War and Indian economic liberalization, India’s foreign policy encountered both opportunities and difficulties. abstract: Faulting at Earth's surface often creates abrupt changes in elevation, which may lead to the formation of cliffs, escarpments and waterfalls. abstract: Groundwater resources are essential for crop production, enabling irrigation in many arid regions of the world. abstract: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss is an otologic emergency, and hypertension is often proposed as a vascular contributor to its onset and poor recovery. abstract: This article presents the development of and first experiences in teaching practice with ‘Memory of Textile Crafts’, a memory game-like learning game to facilitate discussion around textile techniques in (textile) design education. abstract: Recent clinical trials have reported an increased risk for atrial fibrillation (AF) in individuals treated with omega-3 fatty acids (FA). title: False reports of physical dormancy in seeds of gymnosperms and angiosperms
abstract: Abstract Eighteen families of angiosperms but no families of gymnosperms have been documented anatomically (palisade layer of macrosclereids with a light line and a water gap in the seed coat or endocarp – physical dormancy [PY] syndrome) and/or physiologically (imbibition tests of scarified versus nonscarified seeds) to contain species with PY. However, a literature review revealed that 76 families of angiosperms and 5 families of gymnosperms have been reported to have PY. Also, PY was wrongly reported in some genera of Anacardiaceae and Cucurbitaceae, which do have some genera with true PY.

abstract: Ego-dissolution is a phenomenon of central interest across interdisciplinary research on psychedelics. abstract: Contemporary arguments in feminist literary criticism have increasingly challenged the belief that agency must be expressed in terms of resistance, emancipation, or secular autonomy. title: Some Remarks on the Most Glaciotectonically Deformed Lignite Deposits in the World – Sieniawa, Western Poland
abstract: In the area around the village of Sieniawa in western Poland, lignite has been exploited on an industrial scale for over 150 years. The deposits where mining is carried out, initially underground and now opencast, were strongly deformed glaciotectonically during the Pleistocene. The lignite seam in the exploited deposits creates numerous folds and thrusts/nappes, giving them complex geology. As a result, the lignite deposits in the vicinity of Sieniawa are considered the most disturbed of all the world’s deposits still being mined.

title: Adoption Drivers of Blood-based Multi-cancer Early Detection Testing: a Seven-country Population Survey
abstract: Introduction: Blood-based multi-cancer early detection (MCED) tests have the potential to complement existing cancer screening programs and expand screening opportunities for cancers lacking established population-based screening pathways. Successful implementation will depend not only on test performance, but also on public acceptance and engagement. title: Minimum-time anti-sloshing motion planning for an open axisymmetric container transported by a 3-DOF planar motor
abstract: We consider the problem of transporting an open liquid-filled container along a straight line in minimum time while preventing liquid spilling. abstract: Abstract This review essay examines Ahmed Alnaouq and Pam Bailey’s We Are Not Numbers: The Voices of Gaza’s Youth and Nasser Rabah’s Gaza: The Poem Said Its Piece. Together, these works illuminate how Palestinians in Gaza narrate ordinary life, loss, survival, and imagination through memoir, testimony, and poetry.

abstract: Emissions from aging diesel vehicles represent a major environmental and public health concern, particularly in view of the widespread use of biodiesel blends in existing fleets. abstract: African indigenous communities have long used measures to protect springs, vital for domestic and consumption needs. However, amid modern development, springs are increasingly exposed to risks, prompting interest in indigenous safeguarding practices. Natural springs are threatened by deforestation, waste dumps, household litter, drought, mismanagement, and development initiatives. abstract: INTRODUCTION: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the most challenging complications of total joint arthroplasty, often complicated by limitations in diagnostic sensitivity. Standard clinical culture methods fail to identify pathogens in 20%-50% of cases, leading to potential under- or overtreatment. abstract: Historical analogies can inform policy debate and justify action, but public references alone cannot establish learning. abstract: RESUMEN La desaparición forzada en México ha producido una crisis humanitaria marcada por ausencias, duelos suspendidos y violencia persistente. Ante la ineficacia institucional, las madres buscadoras se han constituido en agentes activos de investigación, memoria y resistencia. abstract: This article analyzes the development of cinema art in Karakalpakstan during the years of independence and the achievements of the “Karakalpakfilm” studio. abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) is an important cereal crop with high nutrient requirements, particularly nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K). title: ACUPUNCTURE CARE FOR A PATIENT WITH POST-DISLOCATION SHOULDER INJURY PRESENTING WITH BLOOD STASIS SYNDROME: A CASE STUDY AT SINSHE HAN CLINIC, WEST JAKARTA
abstract: Background: Shoulder joint dislocation is an acute orthopedic trauma that frequently compromises periarticular capsuloligamentous structures, inducing severe localized pain, joint instability, functional immobility, and systemic emotional distress. While closed reduction and conservative analgesia represent standard clinical protocols, acupuncture is increasingly employed as a restorative complementary modality to resolve traumatic blood stasis and accelerate functional recovery. title: A Reflection on Trans-Generational Harms in International Human Rights Law
abstract: This article examines how international human rights law addresses transgenerational harms: present or continuing violations whose effects impair the rights of subsequent generations. Drawing on the ICCPR, ICESCR other UN treaties, and regional jurisprudence, it focuses on two areas in which such harms are especially visible: Indigenous peoples’ rights and environmental degradation and climate change. title: Além Paraíba Mylonite as a Heritage Stone of the Paraiba Do Sul Valley, Rio De Janeiro, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Além Paraíba Mylonite (APM), occurring within the NE–SW-trending Além Paraíba Shear Zone in southeastern Brazil, represents a unique geodiversity element and cultural heritage of the Paraíba do Sul Valley, spanning municipalities in the states of Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais. This ductilely deformed rock, associated with Neoproterozoic tectonic processes of the Brasiliano–Pan-African orogeny, has been widely used in historic constructions in the region during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. abstract: El sector de la aviación ha sido pionero en el establecimiento de metas y estrategias para alcanzar su desarrollo sustentable. abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the apparent prevalence and evaluate the effectiveness of post-mortem tuberculosis diagnosis at the Korhogo slaughterhouse. To this end, 600 bovine carcasses underwent post-mortem inspection. A prescapular lymph node was removed from each carcass, and any lesions suspected of being tuberculous were examined. These samples were then subjected to the Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) staining test. title: Shifts in rumen prokaryotic communities of grazing beef cows with divergent feed efficiency in response to seasonal grazing
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cow-calf operations represent a major component of beef production, typically relying on seasonal grazing of perennial forages. While understanding the role of the rumen microbiome in improving feed efficiency in grazing systems is essential for sustainable beef production, most studies have focused on cattle in confined systems such as feedlots. There is limited understanding of how rumen microbial communities change across feeding regimens in cow-calf operations with seasonal grazing. This study characterized rumen prokaryotic communities of beef cows across four feeding regimens

title: True metabolizable energy of moist‐soil seeds among dabbling duck species
abstract: Abstract True metabolizable energy (TME) assays were first developed to refine poultry diets but have since been adapted by wildlife biologists and conservation planners to determine the assimilable energy within natural wetland foods (i.e., seeds, invertebrates, vegetation) for waterfowl. Bioenergetic models incorporate TME values to quantify the energetic carrying capacity of wetlands. title: Hallazgo casual de un caso avanzado de hyperostosis frontalis interna en un frontal infantil
abstract: Exponemos un caso avanzado de hyperostosis frontalis interna en un hueso frontal aislado hallado casualmente en la localidad de Siles (Jaén). La hyperostosis frontalis interna consiste en un crecimiento anómalo de la tabla interna del frontal que afecta mayoritariamente a mujeres posmenopáusicas y que en la actualidad tiene una prevalencia significativamente superior a la de poblaciones del pasado. title: Calcium carboxylate-modified cementless fly ash binders via mechanochemical co-milling for reduced water uptake
abstract: Saturated fatty acids can reduce water uptake in cementitious materials but may retard early reactions and compromise strength. title: Exploring the effects of emerald ash borer-induced ash tree decline and invasive shrub treatment on understory plant communities in an Illinois forest ecosystem
abstract: Abstract The emerald ash borer ( Agrilus planipennis ) is an invasive insect in the United States that preferentially feeds on ash ( Fraxinus spp.) trees, causing widespread ash decline. Resulting canopy gaps may facilitate understory invasion by non-native plants, such as Amur honeysuckle ( Lonicera maackii ). We investigated whether ash decline and invasive shrub management, which opens the shrub layer, interact to influence understory plant communities. title: Effect of Si Content on Microstructure and Tensile Properties of Fe–Mn–Al–C Lightweight Steel
abstract: Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steels are promising candidates for weight‐sensitive structural components. However, the role of compositional tailoring in governing strength–ductility synergy remains to be fully clarified. In this study, Fe–Mn–Al–C steels with varying Si contents were designed and subjected to solution treatment to systematically investigate the effects of Si on microstructural evolution and tensile deformation behavior. title: Fibrilación ventricular autolimitada: un caso clínico inusual que resalta el rol estratégico de la enfermería en monitorización Holter
abstract: La monitorización electrocardiográfica ambulatoria mediante Holter de 24 horas constituye una herramienta fundamental para correlacionar síntomas como síncope o mareos con arritmias transitorias. El objetivo del presente trabajo fue desarrollar un plan de cuidados de enfermería estructurado en dos fases —previa a la implantación del dispositivo y durante la monitorización—, basado en los patrones funcionales de Marjory Gordon y las taxonomías NANDA-I, NOC y NIC, así como destacar el papel estratégico de la enfermería en la detección precoz de arritmias y eventos cardíacos.

title: Structural Assessment of Church of the Body of Christ in Jankovce, Slovakia
abstract: This article focuses on the structural assessment of the Church of the Body of Christ in Jankovce, in eastern Slovakia, built in the 18th century, which was severely damaged by an earthquake in October 2023. The main objective of the structural survey was to identify and assess the severity of defects, primarily to determine whether the church should be preserved or demolished, and to propose appropriate restoration strategies for selected areas of the church based on the extent of their damage. abstract: The Impact of Solid Waste Management on Community Livelihood in Rwanda: Case of Gahanga Sector, Kicukiro District (2020–2025). title: Experiencias con los modelos pedagógicos aplicados por docentes de una institución de carácter privado en la ciudad de Popayán, Colombia
abstract: Colombian schools are required to state a pedagogical model in their Institutional Educational Project (PEI); however, the way teachers understand and enact it does not always match what is declared. This article interprets the experiences of teachers at a private school in Popayán, Colombia, with the pedagogical models they apply, and analyzes their relationship with the socio-constructivist model stated in the institutional educational project (PEI, for its Spanish acronym). title: The Climate Impasse: Disavowal, Exhaustion and Everyday Life in the Climate Crisis
abstract: ABSTRACT The consequences of climate‐related disasters and emergencies are becoming increasingly stark. And yet in many places, consensus on climate action appears unattainable. I call this problem the climate impasse. In this paper, I draw on emerging theory on affect and negativity to characterise this impasse in three ways. I argue first that, rather than solely addressing governments' failure to act, this impasse develops through people's different lived experiences of the climate crisis. title: Eventos adversos asociados a la seroterapia y estrategias de atención segura en el accidente ofídico pediátrico: revisión exploratoria.
abstract: El accidente ofídico en pacientes pediátricos representa una emergencia que puede generar complicaciones importantes debido al efecto del veneno y a las posibles reacciones adversas derivadas del uso del antiveneno. El propósito de la revisión fue analizar la evidencia disponible sobre estos eventos adversos y las medidas utilizadas para garantizar una atención segura. Para ello, se efectuó una revisión exploratoria basada en los criterios del Joanna Briggs Institute y PRISMA-ScR, consultando bases de datos como PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, LILACS y WHO IRIS, con estudios publicados

title: Impacts of post-fire straw mulching on plant diversity dynamics and mid-term persistence of introduced weed species in a Mediterranean chronosequence
abstract: Post-fire straw mulching is widely used to reduce soil erosion and facilitate vegetation recovery in fire-affected ecosystems. However, straw mulch may introduce agricultural weedy species, raising concerns about their persistence and potential effects on post-fire plant community assembly. This study evaluated the medium-term ecological implications of straw mulch application using a post-fire chronosequence in semi-arid Mediterranean ecosystems of southeastern Spain. title: Impact of temperature variability on mortality during extreme heat and cold conditions over 20 years: A time-space-stratified case-crossover study
abstract: Background Climate change-induced temperature variability poses growing health risks. The effects of this variability on mortality are well established; however, its specific impact during extreme heat and cold conditions remains understudied. This represents a knowledge gap, as the human body’s physiological capacity to adapt to sudden temperature shifts is compromised when ambient temperatures are extreme. title: Cultural Insights from Arabic Poetry in the Cairo Genizah
abstract: Abstract Unlike other Genizah writings, such as letters or legal documents, poetry offers a flexible medium for expressing emotions and relationships. Rooted in ancient Arabic oral traditions, colloquial Arabic poetry exemplifies oral recitation remaining central to cultural transmission and identity formation even after poetry began to be preserved in written forms. abstract: La enseñanza de las ciencias naturales constituye un proceso formativo que requiere establecer vínculos permanentes entre los fundamentos teóricos del conocimiento científico y las experiencias prácticas que permiten comprender los fenómenos presentes en la realidad. title: Sustainable synthesis of highly porous carbons from lignocellulosic residues via oxalic acid-assisted hydrothermal carbonization for electrochemical capacitor applications
abstract: The development of sustainable synthesis strategies for high-performance porous carbons is increasingly important to reduce the environmental impact associated with conventional activation methods. In this study, highly porous carbon materials were synthesized from lignocellulosic biomass waste via hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) in the presence of oxalic acid (OA), followed by thermal treatment under an inert atmosphere. abstract: El objetivo de este trabajo es exponer un nuevo caso de atresia del conducto auditivo externo y poner al día el escaso registro paleopatológico. El temporal derecho CA-P5-195, procedente de la Sima del Ángel (Lucena, Córdoba), se caracteriza por carecer del conducto auditivo externo debido a la ausencia de la porción timpánica. title: Change, Transformation, Preservation and Continuity of Local Identity in the Roman Province of Arabia: A Conspectus
abstract: In the aftermath of the Roman annexation of Nabataea in AD 106, the newly established Province underwent a series of changes that profoundly affected the local society. In this paper, we will shed more light on these changes, analyze Roman-native interactions from different perspectives and examine how and to what extent the inhabitants of the Roman province of Arabia were integrated and assimilated into the Roman Empire. title: Assessment of Environmental Noise Pollution Across Urban Land-use Types and Self-reported Health Impacts in Ayobo Community, Lagos State, Nigeria
abstract: Noise pollution has become a major environmental health concern in rapidly urbanizing cities of developing countries as a result of increasing traffic, commercial activities, and widespread dependence on electricity generators. This study assessed environmental noise levels and evaluated residents’ perceptions of noise sources, associated health effects, and mitigation measures in Ayobo community, Lagos State, Nigeria. title: Depressive symptoms among people living with HIV in Northern Tanzania: The role of family history, social support, and maladaptive coping
abstract: BACKGROUND: Depression is a common mental disorder among people living with HIV (PLWH) and is driven by both neuroimmunological and psychosocial pathways. In turn, depressive symptoms worsen HIV outcomes through reduced adherence, risk behaviors, and impaired immune function. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of depressive symptoms and identify associated factors among PLWH attending health facilities in northern Tanzania. abstract: La generalización del uso de las redes sociales no ha alterado la configuración clásica de las intromisiones ilegítimas en el derecho al honor, pero sí ha transformado la intensidad y alcance de sus efectos. title: Algunos desafíos del Pacto de derechos civiles y políticos en el 60 aniversario
abstract: Este trabajo realiza algunas reflexiones en el 60 aniversario del Pacto de derechos civiles y políticos sobre algunos desafíos. De un lado los relativos a la interpretación de la noción de dignidad humana y su relevancia para acotar los titulares de los derechos. title: Intersectional gender inequities in access to malaria information, knowledge, and attitudes toward malaria services in Oromia, Ethiopia: a mixed-methods study
abstract: Malaria remains a significant public health challenge in Ethiopia. Access to malaria information and prevention is shaped by gender together with other social factors such as poverty, education, residence, and cultural norms. This study applied an intersectional gender lens to examine how these factors influence malaria information access, knowledge, and attitudes in Jimma Zone, Oromia Region. An exploratory sequential mixed-methods study was conducted in 2023. title: Negotiating Identity and Hybrid Spirituality: The Dynamics of the Congregation of the Asy-Syahadatain Order in the Urban-Digital Landscape
abstract: This study examines the dynamics of religiosity of the Asy-Syahadatain congregation in an urban landscape, focusing on the adaptation and negotiation of identity amidst modernity and digitalization. The congregation, originally rural-based in Panguragan, Cirebon, has now expanded to urban areas such as Bandung and Jakarta due to social mobility and economic migration. abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is prevalent in obesity and can progress to steatohepatitis (MASH), fibrosis, cirrhosis and liver failure. The intestinal microbiome (IM) and metabolites may play a role in MASLD severity but their potential relationships with the hepatic transcriptome are not clear. abstract: This study is based on the cultural heritage documentation of District Charsadda, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Pakistan by the roles of Melmastia as cultural hospitality roles. Charsadda is hub of Pakhtune cultural display in habited by different Pakhtune tribes. The study adopts a qualitative research design to explore the nature of hospitality in everyday life and communal life and its effect on the construction of social identity, cultural continuity and sense of community. title: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF MONGOLIAN AND CHINESE BLESSING EXPRESSIONS
abstract: This paper conducts an in-depth exploration of the linguistic features, cultural connotations, historical changes and social functions of Mongolian and Chinese blessing expressions, as well as their inheritance and innovation in modern society. It analyzes the similarities and differences between Mongolian and Chinese blessings mainly from the perspectives of linguistics, cultural communication, historical evolution and their functions in social communication, festival celebrations and ethnic unity. abstract: Abstract This paper presents evidence for the demand‐driven propagation of job losses in the context of the United States during the Great Recession. title: ECONOMÍA POPULAR Y SOLIDARIA: IMPACTOS SOCIOECONÓMICOS Y SU CONTRIBUCIÓN AL DESARROLLO SOSTENIBL
abstract: La economía popular y solidaria (EPS) se ha consolidado como un enfoque que articula la producción, el intercambio, el financiamiento y el consumo sobre principios de cooperación, reciprocidad y primacía del trabajo sobre el capital. Este artículo tiene como objetivo analizar, a partir de la literatura científica y de documentos institucionales, los impactos socioeconómicos de la EPS y su contribución al desarrollo sostenible en el marco de la Agenda 2030. abstract: En las últimas décadas, las reformas educativas neoliberales han transformado profundamente el trabajo docente, especialmente en contextos donde estas políticas han sido implementadas con fuerza y persistencia. Chile constituye un caso paradigmático de neoliberalismo avanzado, lo que lo convierte en terreno privilegiado para examinar los efectos más profundos y menos visibles de estas reformas sobre la subjetividad docente. abstract: Solitary-phase Oedaleus asiaticus (Bei-Bienko) can switch to the far more destructive gregarious phase as population density rises, posing a serious threat to agriculture, animal husbandry and local economies. title: Clinicopathologic characteristics and survival outcomes of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms in Peru: A 15-year retrospective cohort study

abstract: En este ensayo recorro algunos de los hitos que se produjeron en materia de educación y tecnologías en los últimos 25 años e invito a seguir pensando en clave de derecho las cuestiones vinculadas con la inclusión digital. abstract: Despite its economic potential, the pineapple value chain in South Kivu generates substantial organic waste, creating environmental and socio-economic challenges. title: Diet of caecilians (Amphibia: Gymnophiona): a review of prey records and knowledge gaps
abstract: Caecilians (Gymnophiona) are the least studied of the three extant amphibian orders, yet their predominantly fossorial or aquatic habits position them as potentially important predators within soil and freshwater food webs. Although over a century of scattered dietary observations exists, no synthesis of caecilian diet had previously been undertaken. abstract: Increasing global use of Electric Vehicles necessitates high-efficiency, and durable charging infrastructure. The spotted lanternfly ( Lycorma delicatula White; Hemiptera: Fulgoridae) is an invasive, polyphagous plant pest that has rapidly spread across eastern USA over the past decade. abstract: In the context of intensifying climate crises, early childhood education is increasingly positioned as a site for cultivating the capacities, sensitivities, and solidarities needed for more sustainable futures (Spiteri & Pace, 2023; UNESCO & MECCE, 2024). abstract: The article looks at the defensive policy that the Nguyen Dynasty carried out on the Southwest border of Cochinchina (Nam Bo) from 1802-1867. The Southwest border was a strategic location that connected the Mekong Delta to the countries of Cambodia (Chan Lap) and Siam (Siam La). abstract: Abstract Using paired Thermosphere–Ionosphere–Electrodynamics General Circulation Model (TIEGCM) simulations, we investigated the response of the equatorial thermospheric zonal wind jet to the X2.2 solar flare that peaked at 09:10 UT on 6 September 2017. abstract: Abstract This exploratory study describes the eco-emotions reported by young people aged 18 to 28 in the Área Metropolitana del Valle de Aburrá, Colombia, and their perceptions of how local government, companies and the education system respond to climate change and ecological degradation. abstract: Reducing enteric methane (CH 4 ) emissions can increase the sustainability of pasture-based dairy production systems. abstract: Vermicompost (VC) is an effective organic amendment of soil that is produced through the non-thermophilic biodegradation of organic waste by earthworms and microbes. This study focuses on identifying influence of VC on soil physical properties and biological functions such as soil structure, bulk density, and water-holding capacity, as well as its contribution to nutrient availability and microbial activity. This research takes Chinese A-share listed companies, from 2009 to 2023, as the research sample and, empirically analyzes the impact of executives’ overseas background on corporate ESG performance, based on upper echelons theory. abstract: ABSTRACT This article revisits Agamben's state of exception. Homo Sacer and State of Exception frame camps as spaces where law is suspended and life reduced to “bare life.” This decisionist paradigm underestimates the institutional and economic complexity of refugee management. This article proposes the concept of sovereignty by omission: Exclusion produced not by a decisive suspension of law but by legal ambiguity, bureaucratic deferral, and systemic inaction. abstract: Family offices are increasingly recognised as a potentially important source of capital for sustainability-related investment. abstract: This article explores how contemporary intangible cultural heritage (ICH) is produced and negotiated through lived engagements with megalithic sites in Portugal and Scotland. abstract: Abstract Carryover effects—where early‐life experiences influence performance at later stages—have become an important concept in ecological research. These effects can occur across life history stages and are particularly intriguing in organisms with complex life cycles, especially when different stages occupy distinct ecological niches. abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient capital allocation is central to balanced regional development, yet actual capital flows often contradict classical economic predictions, a discrepancy known as the “Lucas Paradox.” This paradox is also evident in China: despite a centralized political system and unified market, persistent regional disparities and distorted capital flows remain salient. abstract: In this study, we synthesized plutonium dioxide ( 239 PuO₂) pellets intended for use in Radioisotope Power Systems (RPS) for space missions, achieving high purity, structural integrity, and thermal properties essential for long-duration missions. title: QUESNAY AND TURGOT ON THE CONDITIONS OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT
abstract: This essay examines the physiocrats’ vision of economic development in eighteenth-century France, emphasizing their belief in agriculture as the foundation of prosperity. abstract: The motivation for this study was Jenkins’ (2000, 2007) call for a fine-tuning of the Lingua Franca Core (LFC), a set of pronunciation features that allegedly safeguard intelligibility in lingua franca contexts, where non-native speakers (NNSs) communicate mainly with other NNSs. abstract: La transición hacia fuentes de energía sostenibles constituye uno de los principales desafíos del siglo XXI. abstract: Iraqw is a Southern Cushitic language spoken in northern Tanzania. Previous studies have described some aspects of Iraqw phonology, but more information is needed about the consonantal changes that occur in the language and the conditions under which they take place. abstract: Abstract The large grove-forming ectomycorrhizal tropical tree Microberlinia bisulcata displays strong mast fruiting on poor soils. abstract: Food production is a major cause of biodiversity loss, but this loss can be mitigated by biodiversity-friendly food products. Using a quasi-experimental design, we investigated this in chimpanzee unvoiced calls (UCs), such as acoustic raspberries, known to show usage variation. We collected audio and contextual data in 91 chimpanzees (0 to 55 y), across eight wild and captive groups that differed in the presence or absence of adult role models. Aiming to eliminate them from Myanmar, the government undertook several repressive measures that led to deadly repercussions for this community. In their desperation to flee the country, the Rohingyas fell prey to traffickers posing as employment agents and smugglers. abstract: This study examines whether Japanese Boys’ Love (BL) manga reconfigures the conditions through which the symbolic order organizes desire. The analysis focuses on the centrality of the male body in the visual economy of the genre. Drawing on a framework that brings together theories of the gaze, Lacanian psychoanalysis, and the distinction between phallus and penis, it conducts a close reading of Yatamomo and Me wo Tojite Yume wo Miru, attending to the organization of the gaze, phallic logic, and the inscription of voice. From the perspective of transaction cost theory, this study interprets such markets as government-led institutional platforms that convert institutional supply into market functions by reducing information search, bargaining and contracting, supervision and enforcement, dispute governance, and financing conversion costs. abstract: This study employed an ultrasound-assisted surfactant extraction method to optimize the extraction conditions for flavonoids from Zanthoxylum bungeanum leaves (FZBL) using the response surface methodology. title: Synthetic seed production of Polygonatum verticillatum All. a threatened medicinal herb growing in Kashmir Himalaya
abstract: Polygonatum verticillatum , is an IUCN Red List-assessed Vulnerable medicinal plant exploited for its bioactive compounds. The species is declining rapidly in its natural habitat because of unregulated and intensive collection, highlighting the urgent need for its conservation. Encapsulation is an alternative approach for conservation and germplasm storage. During the present study, an encapsulation protocol was established to obtain artificial seeds of P. verticillatum. abstract: Abstract Community arts can transform lives, fostering connection, self-discovery, and a sense of purpose. While there is burgeoning evidence exploring wellbeing benefits of community arts for individuals, less is known about the implications over the longer-term. This study draws on experiences of past participants of a community arts program in Australia to understand perceived lasting wellbeing implications of community arts engagement decades later. title: Liquid perception in Chinese ink-wash animation: Duan Xiaoxuan’s cinematography in The Herd Boy’s Flute (1963)
abstract: This article recuperates the cinematographer and camerawoman Duan Xiaoxuan (1934–), the head of the Technology Department at the Shanghai Animation Film Studio (SAFS) and a dominant force behind socialist-era animation cinematography from the 1950s to the 1980s. Positioned within recent feminist and historiographic recoveries of women’s labour in PRC animation, the study reframes Duan as a hidden luminary whose technical mastery of SAFS’s hybridised multiplane camera enabled some of the Studio’s most celebrated ink-wash films. abstract: Abstract The genus Legionella comprises opportunistic pathogenic bacteria commonly found in natural and engineered water systems, where they interact with environmental microbes and protozoa, primarily in biofilms. Legionella pneumophila is the main causative agent of Legionnaires’ disease and is transmitted through inhalation of contaminated aerosols. abstract: Objective: Examines the structure and evolution of agricultural diversification in Western Mexico (Aguascalientes, Colima, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Michoacan, and Nayarit) between 2020 and 2024, focusing on monocultures and their implications for agri-food governance. abstract: The geochemical and mineralogical processes underlying the mechanical weakening of rock and soil in subtropical South China remain insufficiently quantified. We evaluated lithology-dependent chemical weathering as an intrinsic background for collapses and landslides in northern and eastern Guangdong, China, coupling 6,841 mapped hazard sites with X-ray fluorescence and whole-rock X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses of 40 samples from 11 sites. title: Queering the Form of the Judgment: On Misgendering, Deadnaming and Cisnormative Fact Construction in the Decisions of the European Court of Human Rights
abstract: In TH v Czech Republic (2025), the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) found in favour of a non-binary applicant for the first time. However, throughout its judgment, the ECtHR also misgendered the applicant by using masculine pronouns. In this article, we explore the effects of such seemingly small aspects of the judgment’s form through a queer lens. abstract: Context Rare plant species in arid regions may be vulnerable to genetic erosion, potentially influenced by constrained dispersal mechanisms. Aims To assess spatial patterns and underlying drivers of genetic variation in Synostemon hamersleyensis, a narrow endemic species in the ironstone ranges of the Pilbara region, north-western Australia. title: Ancestral Distance and the Cultural Foundations of State Capacity
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the role of long‐term population relatedness in shaping global variation in state capacity. It argues that longer periods of ancestral separation are associated with greater divergence in intergenerationally transmitted civic norms governing voluntary compliance with state institutions. abstract: ABSTRACT In line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (UNSDG) 13, which emphasizes the urgent need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate climate change, this study investigates the role of managerial ability and corporate governance in shaping firms' climate change commitments. title: Sperm phospholipase C signaling via PLCζ1 and PLCδ4 is essential for Ca2+ oscillations and fertility in mice
abstract: Fertilization-induced calcium (Ca2+) oscillations are essential for egg activation and embryonic development in mammals. The sperm-specific phospholipase C isoform, PLCζ1, is the primary trigger of these oscillations. Functional and clinical studies have linked mutations or reduced expression of PLCζ1 to male infertility. title: Plant–soil compartments predominantly shape microbiome structure and function across juvenile and mature moso bamboo
abstract: Plant-associated microbes are essential for host resistance and productivity, but their host age-related dynamics remain poorly explored in long-lived species such as bamboo. In this study, we investigated the microbiomes of various bamboo compartments (i.e., bulk and rhizosphere soils, roots, stems, branches, and leaves) in juvenile and mature moso bamboo ( Phyllostachys edulis ), to explore age-dependent microbial patterns in various compartments. The aim was to identify soil mixtures with high pollutant retention. In this study, silver dissolution was investigated using a system consisting of thiourea (TU), pyrite (FeS2), and H2O, with separate tests using cyanide conducted for comparison. abstract: The expansion of digital technologies has reshaped intimidation, sexual coercion, and violations of privacy, challenging traditional categories of criminal law. This study examines contemporary criminal law responses to digital harassment, sextortion, and image-based sexual abuse, identifying regulatory, evidentiary, jurisdictional, and victimological limitations documented between 2021 and 2026. [Methodology] To measure the dimensions associated with adjustment to university life, a questionnaire with the AjusteU scale was applied to a sample of 327 freshmen at the National University of Costa Rica. abstract: Abstract Rising global conflict increasingly destabilizes food systems and labor markets that underpin livelihoods and food security. Conflict-driven shocks—such as male outmigration or shifts toward manual, gendered tasks—can fundamentally reshape the structural inequalities that determine how men and women are compensated. However, quantitative research on gendered agricultural labor markets remains rare, particularly in conflict settings. abstract: ABSTRACT Urban vegetation combines invasive and introduced species with native relics, whose litter is the primary source of organic matter inputs in urban soils. Plant litter quality regulates both organic carbon (C) storage and microbial activity in urban soils. Here we examined the microbial respiration and organic C stocks in the subtropical urban soils depending on plant litter decomposability. abstract: Rapeseed-mustard (Brassica juncea (L.) Czern.) is a major oilseed crop that contributes significantly to edible oil production and farm income. abstract: In Latin America, there remains a limited understanding of the factors influencing residential satisfaction among people resettled after leaving informal habitats to move into social housing, as well as of the potential variations in the relative importance of these factors across different countries in the region. abstract: This study clarifies the meaning and role of the concept of “ruins” within Arata Isozaki's apocalyptic view of cities. abstract: Salinization is a major constraint to agricultural sustainability in arid and semi-arid regions worldwide. The ameliorative effects of grass clipping mulching on alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.) growth and forage quality in soda saline–alkali land in Northeast China and its regulatory mechanisms were studied. abstract: Background: Hepatic ailments, notably cirrhosis and chronic liver disease, impose a significant and growing global burden. The intent of this review is to methodically gather and carefully analyze the evidence that is currently available about the hepatoprotective properties of Rhus chinensis Mill. and its probable applications in HCC risk prevention by targeting hepatic precursor pathways. abstract: This article examines El Mundo Naval Ilustrado (1897–1901) through its tables of contents to characterize its subject matter, contributors, editorial structure, and thematic evolution. Documentary research and descriptive analysis were conducted on a chronological sample of 23 of the 135 published issues, yielding 321 entries classified by subject, type, authorship, and geographical scope. title: Cul4b sustains cell cycle in germinal center B cells and enables protective humoral immunity against influenza A virus
abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) are a major public health burden, infecting millions of people worldwide. Seasonal vaccines mitigate disease, in part, by triggering the production of IAV-specific antibodies by B cells. Viral evasion and limited vaccine-induced immunity pose barriers to vaccine effectiveness, warranting further investigation of factors influencing protective immune responses. title: Human-made structures as nesting sites for hummingbirds across the Americas: insights from citizen science
abstract: Abstract Urbanization can negatively affect nesting and reproductive behaviors of birds. Even so, certain species can survive in abundance despite its negative impacts, due to their ability to use alternative human-made structures as nesting sites. There are several studies focusing on hummingbirds’ floral resource use in urban environments, however, little is known about their reproduction and nesting in these areas. abstract: Abstract Sage‐grouse ( Centrocercus spp.) are considered an indicator species for sagebrush ecosystems but are declining range‐wide, resulting from a suite of anthropogenic threats that are reducing habitat availability and quality throughout the sagebrush biome. Climate change is widely expected to exacerbate existing stressors and impose additional negative effects on wildlife populations. title: Directional asymmetry of atmospheric pole-to-pole teleconnection
abstract: Paleoclimate proxies show that abrupt Greenland changes were followed by Antarctic responses within decades, suggesting a fast atmospheric pole-to-pole teleconnection involving shifts in the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) and reorganization of extratropical jets. Here, we examine how the mean ITCZ position modulates this interhemispheric teleconnection. abstract: LEO satellite networks such as Starlink provide Internet connectivity across continents, oceans, and airspace. IP geolocation providers map Starlink's IPv6 prefixes to locations mainly through its self-published GeoFeed. However, users may be far away from their assigned Points of Presence (PoPs), one label covers an entire prefix, and labels and PoP mappings can change while addresses stay the same. title: The Re-Foundation of Radar Meteorology
abstract: Since the early development of radar meteorology in the 1940s, rainfall retrieval has traditionally relied on empirical scaling relationships between radar variables and rainfall rate. Here, we revisit the premise that horizontal and differential reflectivity sufficiently constrain the rainfall rate despite the variability of the underlying drop size distribution. title: A Rule That's Made to be Broken? Reframing the Arrhenius Law for Ionic Transport
abstract: The Arrhenius law is ubiquitous in the physical sciences. It describes how an observable property scales with temperature, $T$, as $\exp(\pm E_A/k_BT)$ for a constant $E_A$, the 'activation energy'. Fitting to the Arrhenius law is a common procedure for both experimental and computational data. However, the physical significance of any 'activation energy' calculated is unclear. Here we focus on self-diffusion coefficients for potential solid electrolytes, and by identifying the individual 'diffusive steps' within the system, show how a physically significant activation energy can be extracted.

abstract: In clonal organisms, the genetic individual (genet) may consist of several physiological individuals (ramets). abstract: The detection of organics and potential biomolecules is an important goal of planetary science and astrobiology spacecraft missions, and many types of analytical chemistry for studying organics depend upon liquid solvents as working fluids. abstract: What distinguishes how humans navigate an information network like Wikipedia from what the underlying graph structure and language statistics alone predict? title: Earthquake Forecast via Neutrino Tomography at the DUNE Baseline
abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of accelerator-based neutrino oscillations to localized electron-density enhancements associated with seismic fault zones along the Fermilab SURF baseline of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE). Motivated by the reactor antineutrino proposal of Wang, Chen, and Li, we model the anomaly as a uniform-density slab embedded in the surrounding crust and calculate exact three flavour oscillation probabilities using layer by layer evolution. title: Preference-Based Constraint Handling for Multi-Objective Design-Decision Optimisation: Acceptability Relaxation and Feasibility Guidance
abstract: Multi-objective design-decision optimisation (MODO) problems contain negotiable acceptability limits and non-negotiable feasibility constraints. Hard constraints define the feasible design space, whereas actors may reconsider acceptability limits through deliberation and compromise. Relaxing such limits is a preference judgement: penalties or violation measures do not necessarily represent how actors value departures from initial requirements. title: Saidzoda-CA-EmbeddingGemma-300M: One Small Embedder for Tajik, Kazakh, Uzbek and Kyrgyz
abstract: The small open embedder EmbeddingGemma-300M, used as released, finds the right passage first for only 51.7% to 60.8% of Belebele questions in Tajik, Kazakh, Uzbek and Kyrgyz. We present Saidzoda-CA-EmbeddingGemma-300M, one model for all four languages. It is our Tajik fine-tune of EmbeddingGemma-300M, trained for one more epoch on 279,904 pairs: questions in Kazakh, Uzbek and Kyrgyz that our own language model wrote about source passages, a Tajik refresher, and English and Russian replay. title: Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment of Fossil- and Bio-Based Membrane Manufacturing
abstract: The transition towards sustainable membrane manufacturing is challenged by its reliance on fossil-based polymers, organic solvents, and generation of large volumes of contaminated water. We combined process simulation, life cycle assessment, and Monte Carlo simulation to identify hotspots in the manufacturing of ultrafiltration hollow-fiber membranes for pharmaceutical applications and evaluate strategies to mitigate impact and reduce waste generation. title: ROD-Dataset: A Pedestrian-Perspective Benchmark of Urban Obstacle Classes for YOLO-Based Detection
abstract: Two groups of pedestrians face avoidable risk on the city sidewalk: people living with visual impairment, who reach an obstacle before anything warns them, and people walking with divided attention, who register a hazard late or not at all. A vision system can warn them only about obstacles it has learned to recognize, so its training data limits the protection it offers. title: Self-Healing by design: Immune-system inspired autonomous cyber resilience
abstract: Digital innovations have strongly improved ship capabilities, including command, control & communication, navigation and combat management. In the wake of digitisation and geopolitical stress, resilience against cyber-attacks has become a key challenge. Autonomous Cyber Resilience (ACR) methods, inspired by features of the human immune system, provide a promising perspective. Proofs of concept of autonomous self-healing and self-protecting software have been realised in cloud environments using containerisation, monitoring and deployment technology. title: Infinitely Many Almost-Uniform 3-Qualitative Independence Hypergraphs are Cores
abstract: Qualitative independence is a property associated with the column vectors of well-known combinatorial designs known as covering arrays and qualitative independence hypergraphs characterize the existence of covering arrays on hypergraphs. The core of a hypergraph $H$ is an interesting structural characteristic to study, as it is the unique (up to isomorphism), minimal subhypergraph $H^\bullet \subseteq H$ which is homomorphically equivalent to $H$. title: X-ray magnetic circular dichroism in altermagnets: insights from symmetry
abstract: Altermagnets are a unique subset of antiferromagnets possessing ferromagnet-like responses that are odd in the Néel vector, making X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) a natural probe of ground state altermagnetic order. Because the relativistic ingredient of XMCD at the $L$-edge is supplied predominantly by core-level spin--orbit coupling (SOC), the dichroic signal can reflect the non-relativistic order of the valence electrons. title: Extracting and Characterizing Near-Fault Effects from Strong Motion Observations of the 2022 Chishang Earthquake Sequence
abstract: Accurately characterizing near-fault ground motions, particularly permanent tectonic displacements and velocity pulses associated with rupture directivity, is essential for seismic hazard assessment and infrastructure design. However, conventional ground-motion processing can distort or remove these characteristics. This study extends existing baseline correction methods by synchronously processing all three components of strong-motion recordings to preserve near-fault effects. The proposed methodology is applied to 59 recordings from the 2022 M 6.5 Guanshan foreshock and M 6.9 Chishang mainsh

title: Brueckner Orbitals in Local Pair Natural Orbital Coupled-Cluster Theory: DLPNO-BCCD(T) and DLPNO-BCCD(T)_Lambda2
abstract: In this work, we implement closed-shell Brueckner orbitals for the efficient domain-based local pair natural orbital DLPNO-CCSD(T) and DLPNO-CCSD(T)$_Λ$ methods of the free and open-source \textsc{Psi4} package. We introduce a new algorithm that allows Brueckner orbitals to be computed within the DLPNO framework, resulting in the novel DLPNO-BCCD(T) and DLPNO-BCCD(T)$_{Λ_2}$ methods. We show that DLPNO-BCCD(T) approximates its canonical BCCD(T) counterpart with significantly lower errors relative to the errors incurred by DLPNO-CCSD(T) over CCSD(T). title: A Sojourn Through $c=1$ String Theory
abstract: We revisit the $S$-matrix, the thermal $S$-matrix and the thermal free energy of $c=1$ string theory from the worldsheet perspective. By numerically integrating Virasoro conformal blocks with DOZZ structure constants, we compute the scattering amplitudes and thermal amplitudes up to 6-point at tree level and up to 3-point at one loop, in addition to the genus two thermal free energy. All results are in agreement with the predicted answers from the $c=1$ matrix model.

title: How light interacts with matter, revisited
abstract: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. title: Evaluating Shoreline Prediction Models Using Satellite Imagery and Open-Source Tools
abstract: This study integrates open-source satellite-based shoreline extraction and statistical shoreline-change analysis to evaluate tidal correction and prediction ability in two contrasting coastal settings. Shoreline change is assessed using CoastSat-derived shorelines and AMBUR (Analyzing Moving Boundary Using R)-based rate modeling at Texas, United States of America and Ishikawa, Japan. title: HYDROCARBON COMPOSITION IN COASTAL WATERS OF SOUTHWESTERN CRIMEA, EXPOSED TO FUEL OIL EMISSIONS FOLLOWING THE TANKER ACCIDENT IN THE KERCH STRAIT IN DECEMBER 2024
abstract: The Russian sector of the Black Sea is influenced by chronic hydrocarbon pollution. Black Sea ports handle significant volumes of petroleum products annually (over 100 million tons in total), creating a risk of oil spills both during routine (accident-free) operations and accidental spills characterized by the sudden release of big quantities of pollutants. On December 15, 2024, the Volgoneft-212 and Volgoneft-239 tankers sank in the Kerch Strait, released 2,500–3,000 tons of petroleum products into the marine environment. title: Diurnal cycle of the marine atmospheric boundary layer: Implications for rotor wakes
abstract: To elucidate the interaction mechanisms between the wake of large floating offshore wind turbines and the diurnal cycle of the marine atmospheric boundary layer, a fully coupled aero-hydro-mooring-elastic large-eddy simulation model is developed by extending an open-source platform. This strategy reconstructs the atmospheric and oceanic conditions over a typical diurnal cycle and investigates their impacts on the wake evolution of a 15-MW semi-submersible floating offshore wind turbine. title: Educational Design for Scaffolded, Interactive Simulation-Based Learning: SeaVarinv, an Open-Source GUI for Paleo-Sea-Level Reconstruction in Geoscience Education
abstract: Sequence stratigraphy asks students to reason in both directions along the model chain: forward, from sea level to strata, and backward, from strata to sea level. The backward direction is an inverse problem—ill-posed, non-unique, and dependent on regularization choices that textbooks describe but rarely let students feel. Research codes that close this loop assume command line fluency and stochastic sampler expertise beyond classroom reach, while existing educational tools are passive or forward only. title: Communication Strategies of the Malabero Coastal Fishermen’s Group in Responding to the Decline in Fish Catch
abstract: This study aims to identify and explain the communication strategies employed by the Malabero Beach Fishermen’s Group in Bengkulu City in dealing with the decline in fish catches. This study employed a qualitative method with a case study approach. The research informants were selected using purposive sampling and consisted of the group leader, senior members, and active fishermen. title: Evaluación y seguimiento del blanqueamiento coralino 2023 en el Parque Nacional Sistema Arrecifal Veracruzano, suroeste del golfo de México
abstract: Introduction: In 2023, the fourth mass bleaching event caused by a heatwave was recorded. This event affected virtually all of Mexico’s coral reefs. The bleaching began in August in the Veracruz Reef System National Park (PNSAV). For the first time, a bleaching event of this magnitude was recorded and monitored in the southwestern Gulf of Mexico. Objective: To estimate the extent and prevalence of bleaching in the corals of the PNSAV, as well as to monitor its progression. Methods: Two-minute videos were recorded at a constant depth and speed, with the camera positioned 1 m above the seafloor.

title: Occupational sun exposure and dry maculopathy and/or cataract in two Italian coastal populations with high solar irradiance: a 2026 comparative observational study between Ischia and the coastal areas south of Livorno.
abstract: Background: Occupational solar radiation exposure represents a recognized risk factor for several ocular disorders, particularly cataract formation, while its relationship with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains incompletely understood. Objective: To compare the prevalence of lens abnormalities and dry age-related macular degeneration in two populations of outdoor coastal workers chronically exposed to solar radiation and to explore the possible association between long-term occupational sun exposure and ocular alterations. Methods: A cross-sectional comparative observational study

title: Judicial review of bottom‐trawling restrictions in EU marine protected areas: Case T‐265/23 VDK v Commission
abstract: Abstract This case note analyses the EU General Court's judgment in VDK v Commission (Judgment of 21 May 2025, Case T‐265/23), which concerns the legality of spatial fisheries restrictions adopted to protect marine Natura 2000 sites in the German Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). As the applicant did not appeal the judgment, it has become final. title: Switching of residual exchange flows in a thermal low-inflow estuary
abstract: Abstract A low-inflow estuary showed a regime shift: from a ‘typical’ regime in spring to a ‘thermal’ regime in summer, with water density decreasing landward in both seasons. In spring, low salinity at the head relative to the mouth dominated the density gradient, favoring a positive estuarine circulation. In summer, residual circulation varied between the two sampling campaigns. title: Bi-stable Nonlinear Energy Sinks (BNESs) for Response Mitigation and Drag Reduction of Subsea Cables Undergoing Vortex-induced Vibrations
abstract: A methodology for passive vortex-induced vibration (VIV) mitigation of subsea dynamic power cables by means of a set of optimized strongly nonlinear bi-stable mass-spring-damper attachments, referred as bi-stable nonlinear energy sinks (BNESs) is studied within the open-source MoorDyn library. A fully 3D computational framework is formulated, capturing realistic cable dynamics, hydrodynamic forcing via Morison-type models, and nonlinear passive vibration-mitigation mechanisms under spatially and temporally varying dynamic currents. abstract: Killer whale societies have been investigated worldwide using association patterns and social network analysis. From residents living in enclosed matrilineal groups to the more flexible, fission-fusion-like groups, more details about killer whale societies continue to emerge. Despite these efforts, systematic investigation of inter-individual killer whale social exchanges remains sparse. Using frameworks established with in situ populations, we explored association and interactions networks of ex situ killer whales.
