title: Análise socioambiental de lagoas urbanas e periurbanas de Feira de Santana, Bahia
abstract: Located in the semi-arid region, the city of Feira de Santana is characterized by the richness of its hydrological system, composed of three river basins (Pojuca, Subaé and Jacuípe), whose bodies of water are predominantly located within the urban area, in addition to numerous lagoons, springs, and streams. This study aimed to map and update the registry of urban and peri-urban lagoons in Feira de Santana, as well as to analyze their socio-environmental conditions in the context of urban expansion. title: Large deformations of Oldroyd-B drops in a steady electric field
abstract: The deformation of viscoelastic drops under electric fields is central to applications in microfluidics, inkjet printing, and electrohydrodynamic manipulation of complex fluids. This study investigates the dynamics of an Oldroyd-B drop subjected to a uniform electric field using numerical simulations performed with the open-source solver Basilisk. Representative pairs of conductivity ratio ($σ_r$) and permittivity ratio ($ε_r$) are selected from six regions ($PR_A^+$, $PR_B^+$, $PR_A^-$, $PR_B^-$, $OB^+$, and $OB^-$) of the $(σ_r, ε_r)$ phase space. title: Acoustic detection probability of harbour porpoises depends on behaviour, detection unit, and click-train classification
abstract: Harbour porpoise (Phocoena phocoena) densities are estimated routinely from acoustic detections. Previous acoustic studies show the probability of detecting porpoises (or conversely false negative rate) depends strongly on porpoise behaviour, changing density estimates several-fold if unaccounted for. We quantify this in widely used automated click detectors (e.g., C-PODs), where post-processing is used to identify sequences of consecutive clicks ("click trains") and summarise results as detection-positive time units (e.g., click-positive seconds or minutes). title: Environmental Cues Driving Germination of Zostera muelleri : Critical Steps Towards Seed‐Based Seagrass Restoration in Aotearoa New Zealand
abstract: Seagrasses are globally important ecosystems that provide critical services, yet are rapidly declining, driving a need for restoration. While seed‐based restoration offers potential for large‐scale recovery, success is often limited at early recruitment stages. Germination cues are environmental signals that influence dormancy release and subsequent germination. They present a key bottleneck in seagrass restoration, where labour‐intensive, seed‐limited efforts make improving germination rates essential for restoration efficiency. title: Alteration in functional-structural connectivities of insula is associated with hypoxic ventilation
abstract: Background Hypoxia elicits ventilatory adaptation, and the anterior insula, a hub for interoceptive and exteroceptive integration, is highly vulnerable to hypoxic stress. We hypothesised that it mediates hypoxia-related ventilatory regulation.Methods Thirty-one college students completed 30 days of high altitude exposure. title: Maternal malaria and early-life infections shape humoral immunity to P. falciparum in infants
abstract: Abstract Maternally derived antibodies transferred across the placenta are hypothesized to protect infants against Plasmodium falciparum malaria in early life, but placental malaria may impair this transfer and alter the subsequent development of infant immunity. To test whether maternally derived and infant antibody responses are associated with protection from infection and clinical malaria, and how malaria exposure during pregnancy and infancy shapes these responses, we enrolled a birth cohort of infants in a birth cohort nested within a randomized trial of chemoprevention in Tororo, Uganda

title: Cold priming of Saccharina latissima gametophytes promotes sporophyte growth
abstract: Abstract Seaweed cultivation represents an emerging industry in Europe, where most biomass is still derived from wild harvesting. A potential approach to establishing a sustainable seaweed production industry involves improving seaweed strains. Temperature priming, introducing moderate stress to enhance subsequent performance, offers a rapid approach for improving growth. We examined the effect of three weeks temperature priming (0, 10, 20 °C) of gametophytes of Saccharina latissima on the early life stages (gametophyte growth, sporophyte recruitment, juvenile sporophyte growth). title: Inter-Individual Social Exchanges in a Group of Ex Situ Killer Whales
abstract: Although knowledge about killer whale (Orcinus orca) distribution, population structure, and foraging habits is quite extensive, data regarding their social behaviors, inter-individual exchanges, or relationship building and maintenance are critically lacking. This shortage can be partially explained by the challenges of observing such behaviors in the wild, thus managed care (ex situ) facilities offer a unique vantage to see inter-individual exchanges in greater detail. title: Extreme cranial asymmetry in extinct benthic feeding sperm whales
abstract: The fossil record provides critical insights into morphological changes beyond those observable in extant species, revealing evolutionary novelties. Among mammals, toothed cetaceans are notable for pronounced cranial asymmetry associated with sound-emitting forehead structures. Pygmy sperm whales (Kogiidae),display some of the most extreme cranial asymmetries known. Here, we describe Scaphokogia huachafo sp. nov., a new pygmy sperm whale species from the Late Miocene Pisco Formation, Peru. title: Chamber Pressure as a Decision-Making Design Metric in Bi-propellant Rocket Systems (and Overview of an Omani-Argentinian Collaborative Program in Space Applications)
abstract: In liquid propellant rocket propulsion, the absolute chamber pressure is one of the parameters for preliminary design. In the current study, we quantify the impact of this rocket design parameter (the chamber pressure) on various combustion and nozzle characteristics for three common liquid fuels, which are (1) liquid hydrogen (LH2), (2) liquid methane (CH4), and (3) Rocket Propellant-1 (RP-1), when used with liquid oxy-gen (LOX) as an oxidizer. title: Layering in double-diffusive convection
abstract: The formation of layered profiles (or 'staircases') in temperature, salinity and density, resulting from double-diffusive convection (DDC), is a widely observed oceanographic phenomenon. In the past two decades, new developments, both in numerical simulations and theory, have significantly advanced our under-standing of this fascinating process. Nonetheless, obtaining a complete description of layering-precisely when and why it occurs-still presents a sizeable theoretical challenge to fluid dynamicists. title: Seasonal icings reveal subsurface water drainage of a Greenland Ice Sheet outlet glacier
abstract: In many glacial settings, winter outflows of proglacial water create stratified domed ice structures on glacial forefields. These structures, called naledi, provide an opportunity to characterise solute concentrations in hydrological systems during winter, which are poorly constrained compared with summer outflows dominated by supraglacial meltwater. title: Persistence of scour at bridges using stochastic simulations
abstract: The stochastic and deterministic properties of the scouring process at bridges are analysed by coupling synthetic streamflow generations with a scour and fill model considering the upstream sediment supply. Streamflow was generated using the asymmetric moving-average (AMA) scheme that preserves the Hurst-Kolmogorov (HK) dynamics, the second-order dependence structure, time asymmetry, and the first four statistical moments of the marginal distribution. title: Filtering the mobile resistome: how evolutionary trade-offs in bacterial immunity shapes antimicrobial resistance
abstract: Although antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is traditionally viewed as a consequence of antibiotic selection, growing evidence indicates that bacterial immune systems regulate which mobile genetic elements (MGEs) successfully enter, establish, and persist within bacterial populations. Here, we argue that bacterial immunity helps determine access to the mobile resistome and, consequently, shapes the evolutionary opportunities upon which antibiotic selection acts. title: Synthesis and herbicidal activity of spiro 3‐Acyltetramic acid derivatives as endogenous abscisic acid synthesis regulator and HPPD inhibitors
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Potent herbicidal activity of tetramic acid containing compounds call for studying the structure–activity relationship of its derivatives. RESULTS A series of novel 3‐acyl‐5‐spiro tetramic acid derivatives ( C1–C12 , L1–L18 ) were synthesized and evaluated for their herbicidal activities. title: Test-track and on-road studies: Methodological insights on the assessment of carsickness and its modulating factors
abstract: The research on motion sickness and effective countermeasures has gained additional attention due to the ongoing development of highly automated driving vehicles. In order to understand the phenomenon of motion sickness better and support effective testing, this work sheds lights on motion sickness considering essential modulating factors: The relation between the development of carsickness and testing environment is explored in relation to psychological factors. title: Local and Indigenous knowledge and scientific evidence: The importance of navigating between assimilation, squeezing out, and isolation
abstract: How can the relationship between science, local knowledge, and Indigenous knowledge be understood in ways that support well-informed decision-making, both now and in the future? This paper addresses this question by comparing contemporary and historical discussions of knowledge exchange between science, local knowledge, and Indigenous knowledge with evolving conceptions of local and Indigenous knowledge systems. abstract: We present two new U–Pb zircon ages from andesitic sills exposed in the Sierra del Mayal, within the internal sector of the Chos Malal Fold-and-Thrust Belt (FTB), Neuquén Province, Argentina, integrated with petrographic, geochemical, and structural data. title: Mechanistic Insights into CO2 Photoreduction to HCOOH on BH- and NH-Modified g-C3N4-Based Photocatalysts
abstract: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is an attractive metal-free platform for the photocatalytic conversion of CO2 into value-added products, but its activity is limited by poor visible-light absorption, fast electron–hole recombination, and the intrinsic inertness of the CO2 molecule. title: Cataxia on the edge: range contraction of endemic montane mygalomorph spiders in a biodiversity hotspot
abstract: Context Large shifts in species distributions are projected under future climate scenarios, yet long-term empirical evidence remains scarce, particularly for invertebrates. Aims We quantified changes in occupancy, abundance, and population structure over 22 years for four short-range endemic trapdoor spider species (Cataxia sandsorum, C. stirlingi, C. colesi, C. barrettae) and tested associations with microhabitat, environmental, and disturbance conditions. abstract: Research subject . Pre-ore diorite porphyrite dikes of the Panovskaya Lyaga gold deposit in the Middle Urals. Aim . To determine the age of pre-ore dikes, clarify their geological position, and establish the lower age limit of deposit formation. Materials and methods . title: How climate change already impacts people who use alcohol and other drugs: Australian service staff perspectives
abstract: Increased prevalence and intensity of extreme weather events, as well as more gradual climatic shifts, have disproportionate impacts for people who experience poverty and stigmatisation. This includes many who engage with alcohol and other drug (AoD) services. The aim of this paper is to identify a broad range of already-occurring climate change impacts on Australian AoD service users, as observed by service staff. abstract: Amid accelerating environmental crises, economic geography has increasingly turned to green path development. Yet existing research underplays how actors strategically shape the coevolution of fossil and green paths, particularly in Global South resource peripheries where industrial trajectories emerge simultaneously. This article advances the interpath linkages framework by examining how actors govern interpath relations during the critical phase of resource mobilization. abstract: The emergence of biomolecular homochirality requires both an initial symmetry-breaking event and a mechanism to amplify and preserve a chiral imbalance. Magnetic minerals have been shown to function as chiral agents through the chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect and may have enabled homochirality on early Earth, yet the magnetic properties of magnetite formed under realistic prebiotic conditions remain unexplored. abstract: The geomorphic history of Grand Canyon, and especially Western Grand Canyon, remains unsettled. abstract: Abstract Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) offer exceptional colour purity and efficiency for next-generation display applications. abstract: Abstract Background Migration is a complex behaviour, requiring individuals to integrate genetic, environmental and social information to reach distant goals, with important consequences for individuals, populations and communities. abstract: AIMS: Bacterial infections of the cornea, also known as bacterial keratitis, are a major cause of blindness. abstract: Fog is a meteorological phenomenon that significantly impacts traffic safety and public health. abstract: Catfish (Clarias sp.) is an economically important freshwater aquaculture commodity in Indonesia. However, bacterial infections can compromise fish health and growth performance, highlighting the need for natural feed additives that support sustainable aquaculture. abstract: Flooding in the Lake Titicaca basin poses a critical risk to communities and infrastructure, and endangers human lives. Dikes are commonly used to protect against flooding, but their stability is essential to their effectiveness. This study examines the stability of embankment slopes on the Ilave River dams through hydraulic and geotechnical modelling, using the limit equilibrium method with specialized software. abstract: This study examined the individual and interactive effects of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) inoculation, phosphorus (P) fertilisation and gypsum levels on nutrient uptake and growth of Sorghum bicolor L. in gypsiferous soils under pot conditions. abstract: In Northern Europe, growing a mixture of shade-tolerant spruce and light-demanding birch instead of monocultures of either species is a potential way to improve forest resilience and adaptation to climate change. Planting both species at the establishment phase is a rare practice in silviculture, but it can be a viable approach for success in designing the mixture. title: Silage yield and quality of maize cultivars in central Gujarat conditions
abstract: A field experiment was conducted during kharif 2020 at the Fodder Demonstration Unit, National Dairy Development Board, Anand, Gujarat, to evaluate ten maize cultivars for fodder yield and silage quality using a randomized block design with three replications. abstract: Teaching waste poses a pedagogical difficulty: the matter that most demands critical attention is the matter students least want to touch. This article takes that difficulty as the starting point for a critical Science and Technology Studies (STS) pedagogy, asking what happens when disgust is neither managed away nor moralized, but held as a resource for learning. abstract: : Bacterial spot, caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv . pruni ( Xap ), is a major disease impacting peach production in the southeastern United States. abstract: ABSTRACT Introduced to Hawai‘i in 2016, Lema equestris has become a garden pest commonly reported on Solanum americanum , which is grown as a native and cultural plant in Hawai‘i and supports native vertebrates elsewhere across Oceania. abstract: Moringa oleifera is an important crop globally, but there is limited characterisation of maternal pod traits and progeny seedling performance. In this study, growth patterns of 10 accessions (MO-11 to MO-20) and their half-sib progeny (P-11 to P-20) were evaluated to select the best germplasm. abstract: Abstract In recent years, with the advancement of precision nutrition and biotherapy concepts, the demand for efficient and targeted delivery of functional active substances, especially probiotics, has become increasingly urgent. abstract: Nucleophilic substitutions are among the most commonly used reactions in pharmaceutical synthesis, and alkyl halides are typically used as electrophiles in these reactions. abstract: The low productivity of cowpea is primarily attributed to inadequate utilisation of genetic diversity for the improvement of local cultivars. abstract: Large mammalian herbivores (LMH) play complex roles in shaping tree cover and composition in savannas by suppressing trees through browsing and reducing competition from neighbouring trees and understory vegetation. Where LMH are declining, release from browsing and intensification of competition has unpredictable physiological consequences. abstract: Abstract This article examines how regime type shapes the politicisation and depoliticisation of intervention behaviour in intrastate conflicts. Focusing on external interventions across the wider Mediterranean region, it explains why democratic and hybrid-authoritarian states employ different intervention repertoires. abstract: La creciente demanda alimentaria induce a la degradación de los recursos naturales, posicionando al sistema silvopastoril (SSP) como una alternativa de mitigación ambiental. abstract: Brain lateralization is a widespread feature of vertebrate nervous systems, yet evidence from reptiles remains limited. abstract: Cet article analyse l'évolution historique du système éducatif malgache, depuis les pratiques d'éducation traditionnelle et orale précoloniales jusqu'aux tentatives contemporaines d'intégration des technologies de l'information et de la communication (TIC) dans l'enseignement. title: Development of time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy using heralded emission spectroscopy for organic light-emitting materials
abstract: Organic light-emitting materials are widely used in optoelectronics and bioimaging, but sometimes conventional fluorescence spectroscopy techniques can be limited by scattering, background fluorescence, photon pile-up and photobleaching. title: Circular interval-valued regression with application to wind direction: A cylindrical approach
abstract: Many real-world datasets are inherently interval-valued, yet standard statistical methods are typically designed for point observations. Furthermore, intervals that are circular in nature may naturally exist. In this paper, we introduce a cylindrical regression framework for interval-valued circular data, addressing the joint challenges of the periodical nature and measurement uncertainty within the observed circular intervals. title: Bouncing or Merging in Drop-Bath Impacts
abstract: When a liquid drop impacts a liquid surface, it deforms the surface, trapping a thin layer of air between drop and bath. The drop then either bounces off the bath or, if the gas film ruptures, merges with it. We present a model for drop-bath impacts that can accurately predict whether a drop will bounce or merge, and compare it to theory-driven experiments. abstract: Entanglement-based quantum key distribution from ground to satellite has been proposed as a scalable primitive for global quantum networks and will be demonstrated as part of the imminent QEYSSat mission. title: Galactic-Scale Distribution of 10Be and Its Implications for the Early Solar System 10Be/9Be
abstract: Meteoritic inclusions indicate that the early Solar System contained a substantial abundance of the short-lived radionuclide 10Be.
